headline: 'No Material Impact': Infosys On Trump's Suspension Of Green Cards For Tech Firms
content: The company said it remained committed to its employees, clients and communities in the US and to complying with all applicable laws and regulations. Indian IT services major Infosys said it does not expect any material impact on its operations from the US administrations decision to suspend new and pending applications under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme. In a regulatory filing to stock exchanges, the Bengaluru-headquartered company said it welcomed the opportunity to work with the US Department of Labor and other relevant government agencies to address any queries. - TCS Says US Green Card Programme Suspension Wont Affect Hiring Strategy, Plans 15,000 Local Jobs - PERM Vs H-1B: What Is The Difference, And Which One Does The US Suspension Affect? - US Green Card Crackdown: Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Microsoft Among 8 Firms Suspended | N18 - US Suspends Microsoft & Infosys From PERM? Indian Workers Face Green Card Uncertainty | News18 We do not anticipate yesterdays announcement of such suspension to have a material impact on the organisation," Infosys said, adding that it had invested in building a strong local workforce and technology and innovation hubs across the United States. The company said it remained committed to its employees, clients and communities in the US and to complying with all applicable laws and regulations. The statement comes after the US administration suspended eight major technology companies, including Indian IT services firms Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and HCL Technologies, from the PERM programme. The move was justified on the grounds that the programme had excluded American workers from the domestic job market. Global technology and consulting firms Capgemini, Cognizant, Microsoft and Adobe were also named in the directive. PERM certification, issued by the US Department of Labor, is the first major requirement for employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers for permanent employment in the country. It serves as a key step towards obtaining an employment-based green card. The potential impact of the suspension could be limited by the sharp decline in PERM applications filed by Indian IT companies in recent years. According to industry data, TCS filed just two PERM applications in the US financial year 2026, compared with 513 in 2025 and 1,804 in 2024. HCL Technologies submitted 59 applications in 2026, down from 323 in 2025. Infosys recorded 87 PERM applications in 2024, while Wipro filed 257 in 2024 and 523 in 2025. Of Wipros 257 applications in 2024, 169 were denied and 88 were withdrawn by the company. Indian IT companies accounted for less than 1,400 of the 1,17,849 PERM certifications last year, less than 2 per cent. The direct impact may therefore be smaller than it first appears," Vineet Nayar, former chief executive officer of HCL Technologies, said in a post on X. TCS has also sought to play down concerns over the suspension, saying its PERM applications had fallen to single digits in the last two years" and that the move was not expected to affect its client commitments or talent strategy. The company said its US workforce strategy was centred on hiring local talent, backed by a strong campus recruitment model. TCS operates across 31 offices and delivery centres in the country. It has also announced plans to hire an additional 15,000 employees in the US over the next five years to expand its local workforce. Infosys stated that it does not expect any material impact on its operations from the US administration's decision to suspend new and pending PERM applications. The company highlighted its prior investments in building a strong local workforce and innovation hubs across the United States.

headline: Smart investment or monopoly? Woman's ₹20 crore parking space bet sparks legal feud in China
content: A calculated real estate investment by a woman in China who bulk-purchased 196 parking spaces for nearly $2 million ( 19.36 crore) has triggered severe backlash from neighbours after she drastically raised rental and sale prices. The dispute over the parking spots, located in a residential community in Changsha, Hunan province, ultimately led to a lawsuit when disgruntled residents accused her of monopolising essential infrastructure, according to a report by the South China Morning Post. The origins of the dispute date back to 2018, when the Changsha housing project first entered the market. At the time, the development lacked essential public facilities, including schools, shops, and transport links, leading to widespread scepticism among prospective buyers, as reported by Hunan TV. As a result, flats and parking spaces saw very little interest. However, a woman surnamed Wu saw an opportunity after analysing regional development plans published by local authorities. Confident in the area's future growth, she struck a deal with the financially struggling developer to purchase 196 parking spacesamounting to 40 per cent of the community's total parking inventoryin a single transaction worth 14 million yuan (approximately 20 crore). Wus market foresight paid off as the neighbourhood rapidly developed. Residential units sold out quickly, and demand for parking spaces surged. To secure her assets, Wu installed parking locks to prevent unauthorised use. Capitalising on the newfound demand, Wu began renting out spaces for $75 ( 7,258) per month, effectively doubling the developer's original 2018 rental rate. She also listed several spaces for sale at roughly $15,000 ( 14.52 lakh) each, representing a markup of up to 80 per cent over their original value. The steep price hikes incensed the community's residents, who were already struggling with a lack of available parking. When they demanded that Wu lower the monthly rent to 300 yuan ( 4,334) and sell the spots at their original 2018 rates, she refused. Following a failed mediation attempt by a local government official, a group of residents banded together to sue Wu. The plaintiffs argued that parking spaces constitute essential community infrastructure and should not be monopolised by a single individual for outsized profit. They formally requested the court to cancel the initial purchase contract between Wu and the property developer. In February 2024, a local Changsha court ruled decisively in Wu's favour. In its judgment, the court noted that when the developer initially listed the parking spaces, all residents were given an equal opportunity to purchase them but chose to abstain. The court highlighted that Wu arranged her own funding and bore the entire market risk, while others waited to see how the local property market would perform. Concluding that her bulk purchase was entirely legal, the court also clarified that current laws do not impose any restrictions on the number of parking spaces an individual citizen may own. headline: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Heads Home For Grandmother's Last Rites After Release
content: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke returned to Maharashtra following his grandmother's death, after being released from detention in Delhi. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said he was heading back to his village in Maharashtra to be with his family following the death of his grandmother, after being released from detention in Delhi. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Abhijeet Dipke said his party colleagues Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka would address a press conference in the national capital shortly. - 'Undeclared Emergency': Kharge, Rahul To Meet CJI Tomorrow Amid CJP Protests - YouTuber Dhruv Rathee Posts First Message After His Release: 'Not Arrested Or Detained, I Was...' - Delhi Metros, Trains Should Run Until: SCs Directives On Internet, Barricades & Detentions After Saturday's Curbs - Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Rolls Out Red Carpet For PM Modi At Chennai Airport Heading back to my village to be with my family during this moment of grief. Saurav and Ashu will address a press conference shortly in Delhi. The CJP will neither back down nor be intimidated," he wrote. Abhijeet Dipke also described October 10 as the beginning of the end of this dictatorship", referring to the day CJP leaders were detained in Delhi. His paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died at 11.30 am on Saturday at her home in Santuk Pimpri village in Maharashtras Hingoli district following a prolonged illness. She had been unwell for about a month and had earlier been hospitalised in Hingoli. Her last rites were scheduled for 10 am on Sunday. Abhijeet Dipke, Das and Ranka had travelled from Mumbai to Delhi to participate in a protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Delhi Police detained the three leaders inside their aircraft soon after it landed in the national capital on Saturday. Abhijeet Dipke headed home to his village in Maharashtra's Hingoli district to be with his family and attend the last rites of his 85-year-old grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, who passed away following a prolonged illness.

headline: 'Significant Risks For India': Beyond Elon Musk's Erratic Conduct, Starlink Is Unmanageable In Myriad Ways
content: Retail use of Starlink's services undermines India's ability to regulate internet access for internal security purposes. Paired with Musk's conduct, this poses significant risks. In 2025, three years into the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Musk boasted that his Starlink system was the backbone of the Ukrainian army". Two years earlier, he had claimed to possess more real-time global economic data in one head than anyone ever", referring to the data available to him through Tesla, Starlink and Twitter, now known as X. These statements raise a fundamental question: should one individual or company have such extensive control over communication systems and access to data? Musks public interventions in the domestic politics of other countries, including his backing of political opponents of governments in the UK, France and Germany, add another dimension to the concern. Against this backdrop, Starlinks growing reach could pose a significant challenge to Indias internal security. - From Musk's Political Clout To Past Conduct: What Makes Starlink A Security Risk For India - What If Starlink Won't Switch Off? Study Flags Data And Security Risks India Faces With Musk's Network - What Is Starlink? How It Works & Why India Is Raising Security Concerns | | - Starlinks Privacy Policy Raises Surveillance Concerns: What Indian Users Need To Know The issue is not merely the discovery of Starlink terminals in Manipur, where ethnic tensions remain high, or their use by smugglers in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It is also about how the company responded when the Indian government sought information about the devices. This is false. Starlink satellite beams are turned off over India," Musk said on X in December 2024, after reports emerged that security forces had recovered Starlink equipment in Manipur. But the reality is more complex, as a research paper by the Takshashila Institution points out. Because of the imperfections in geofencing, the devices may have worked in parts of the state bordering Myanmar," the paper says. Starlinks low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites operate much closer to Earth than conventional geostationary satellites, making their signals harder to block through traditional methods. The challenge is technical as well as regulatory. Starlink terminals use electronically steered antennas that maintain narrow, constantly shifting connections with satellites. Jamming these links requires a jammer to target the signal precisely, potentially from close to the terminal. And even if one connection is disrupted, the terminal can switch to another satellite within milliseconds. Unlike a geostationary satellite, which remains in a relatively fixed position in the sky, Starlinks satellites move across different orbital paths, making them much harder to target consistently. Musks Erratic Conduct The Manipur and Andaman and Nicobar Islands incidents, along with Starlinks response to the Indian governments request for information, also raise questions about how the company handles security concerns flagged by national authorities. After Musk responded on X, Starlink cited data privacy laws and directed Indian authorities to channel their requests through US law enforcement or established international protocols. The company declined to provide the requested details of the users and usage history of the devices. The concern extends beyond the companys response to individual incidents. Musk also has considerable influence in Washington, while SpaceX occupies a strategically important position in the US governments space and defence programmes. His relationship with US President Donald Trump has survived a public spat in 2025. Musk played a prominent role in Trumps 2024 presidential campaign and later became the de facto leader of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Meanwhile, SpaceX launches satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office and the US Space Force, including those supporting missile-warning and tracking capabilities. It is also a crucial partner for NASAs human-spaceflight programmes, including its efforts to maintain a continuous human presence in low Earth orbit and undertake the Artemis lunar exploration programme. This combination of political influence and strategic importance makes Musks control over Starlink a concern for India, the Takshashila paper argues. The relationship also works in reverse as SpaceX depends on US government contracts and regulatory approvals for its commercial and national-security launches, spectrum allocations and orbital licences. Washington therefore has considerable leverage over Trumps pal Elon. In a scenario where American strategic interests demand it, the US government could potentially pressure SpaceX to share data from Starlinks Indian operations, maintain or deny coverage over particular regions, or otherwise act in ways that serve American rather than Indian interests. Ultimately, Starlinks operations remain under the control of a company subject to the authority and interests of a foreign government. The paper points to Musks conduct in Ukraine as a warning. Starlink became central to Ukrainian government and military communications after Russias full-scale invasion in 2022. Yet Musk reportedly restricted access to the service on multiple occasions and denied a Ukrainian military request to activate Starlink near Crimea, affecting operations on the ground. The concern, therefore, is not simply that Starlink is a foreign service. It is that a system on which governments and security forces might come to depend can remain subject to the operational decisions of a private company and its owner. Allowing widespread retail use of Starlink could result in loss of the states ability to regulate internet access for reasons of internal security. Relying on Starlink for critical applications could mean the loss of connectivity when it is needed most, especially during a disaster, crisis, or conflict," the paper says. Ungovernable Satellite Systems The limits of government control become clearer when attempts to block Starlink are examined. Its LEO architecture makes the service difficult to disable through conventional jamming, while its operator retains the ability to determine where the service is available. Iran offers a striking example. During protests in 2022, Musk activated Starlink over the country, allowing people with terminals to bypass government restrictions on internet access. In June 2025, amid the Iran-Israel conflict, he again indicated that Starlinks satellite beams were active over Iran. The paper says Iran responded to the use of Starlink during the protests that intensified in January 2026 with GPS and radio-frequency jamming, including attempts to disrupt the Ku-band and Ka-band frequencies used by satellite communications. These measures caused localised and temporary disruptions rather than a comprehensive shutdown. Iran also reportedly used long-range jammers, drone surveillance to identify terminals on rooftops and door-to-door raids to seize devices. Yet the difficulty of disabling the service persisted. Tehran subsequently complained to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), arguing that Starlink was violating Iranian sovereignty. The ITUs Radio Regulations Board expressed grave concern" over the situation. According to the Takshashila paper, the board noted that Starlink had claimed its terminals were not marketed, sold or activated in Iran, but had not made efforts to disable all unauthorised terminals. The board also noted that Starlink had demonstrated the ability to disable terminals en masse according to their geographic location in other countries, but had chosen not to do so in Iran. The episode illustrates the dilemma for governments: a satellite operator may possess the technical ability to restrict access in a particular territory, but the state where the terminals are operating may not be able to compel it to act. As the Takshashila paper puts it, Starlink services may remain illegally active when the Government wants them to be halted in an area. Conversely, Starlink services may be halted when the Government needs them to be operational." For India, this creates a two-way risk. Starlink could remain active in an area where the government wants communications restricted for security reasons. Conversely, connectivity could be withdrawn during a crisis when authorities need it most. What The Indian Government Wants India has attempted to address these concerns through a set of security conditions imposed on satellite communications providers. In May 2025, the Department of Telecommunications issued additional requirements for operators holding a Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) licence. The rules require operators to provide real-time monitoring facilities to security agencies and ensure that traffic to and from Indian users is routed through gateways located in India. They prohibit the use of inter-satellite links to route Indian user traffic, including in the event of a gateway failure, and require operators to support metadata collection by the Department of Telecommunications Telecom Security Operation Centre. Licensees must also undertake not to copy or decrypt Indian telecom data outside the country. The conditions extend to border security. Areas within 50 kilometres of international and coastal borders, including the Exclusive Economic Zone up to 200 nautical miles, are designated as special monitoring zones. Operators must support user-activity monitoring by law enforcement agencies and restrict or deny service to individuals, groups or areas during hostilities or when directed by authorities. The rules also prohibit location spoofing and require blocked websites to remain inaccessible through satellite services. India has sought to exercise control over the technologys development as well as its use. The licence conditions call for operators to submit a phased manufacturing programme aimed at indigenising at least 20% of the satellite networks ground segment within five years of commercial launch. Operators are also encouraged to integrate Indias indigenous satellite navigation system, NavIC, into user terminals, with a transition plan for full implementation by 2029 on a best-effort basis. Separately, the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) rejected Starlinks application for its Gen 2 satellite constellation in January 2026. The Gen 2 system incorporates direct-to-device (D2D) capability, which allows satellites to connect directly to mobile phones without conventional ground terminals. India currently has no regulatory framework for D2D satellite services, and the Department of Telecommunications is still considering its policy approach. But the paper authored by Ashwin Prasad Rao, Aditya Ramanathan and Col. Das (Retd.). argues that stringent conditions on paper do not necessarily translate into effective control in practice. The restrictions on inter-satellite links are a case in point. Starlinks architecture relies on these links to route traffic across its satellite constellation. Under Indias conditions, traffic originating from an Indian terminal must travel through a satellite and return directly to an Indian gateway, rather than pass through the orbital network. If an Indian gateway fails, the connection cannot be rerouted through another satellite or gateway; it simply stops working. That requirement undermines one of the key advantages of a satellite constellation: the ability to maintain connectivity by routing traffic through an interconnected network. More importantly, Indian authorities can monitor activity at domestic gateways but cannot independently verify what happens between satellites in orbit. The paper argues that ground-based monitoring cannot reliably establish whether a packet has travelled through an inter-satellite link before reaching an Indian gateway. Other requirements also rely heavily on undertakings and self-certification rather than independent technical verification. The rules require operators to make commitments on data handling, while the NavIC integration requirement is framed on a best-effort basis. Geofencing, on which several security safeguards depend, has already raised questions in the Manipur and Andaman and Nicobar Islands incidents. The Iran case presents a further complication: the ITU found that Starlink had the capability to disable terminals in bulk based on their location, but had not done so in that country. The proposed D2D technology could create another regulatory challenge. A mobile phone connecting directly to a satellite would not need a conventional ground terminal, potentially bypassing the gateway-dependent architecture on which Indias current rules are built. Depending on how such a system is designed and routed, Indias existing requirements on traffic routing and data localisation could become harder to enforce. The central problem, the paper argues, remains unresolved: operational control of the constellation rests with SpaceX. India can impose conditions and revoke a licence for non-compliance, but it cannot necessarily compel the company to keep services running during a crisis or to shut them down when national-security requirements demand it. A research paper by the Takshashila Institution warns that Starlink's growing reach and reliance on foreign-controlled LEO satellite systems could challenge India's internal security and strategic autonomy, citing potential issues like unmanageable network access, geofencing imperfections, and operational control remaining outside India.

headline: CJP Protest: Supreme Court directs no illegal detention — what SC said on Delhi metro, internet 'shutdown'
content: The Supreme Court on Sunday directed that there shall be no detention of any individual except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly with respect to the assembly of peaceful and unarmed people beyond the area where prohibitory orders are in operation. A bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana also issued direction related to the closure of Delhi metro station in the wake of the CJP protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The Supreme Court was hearing a contempt petition that was filed against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, IPS, alleging that Delhi Police personnel resorted to indiscriminate violence against citizens during the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in the national capital on October 10, in violation of the principles laid down by the Court. Quick answers to key questions 1What did the Supreme Court say about detaining protesters during the CJP protest? The Court directed that no individual be detained except according to the procedure established by law. It highlighted peaceful, unarmed gatherings outside areas covered by prohibitory orders. 2What did the Supreme Court say about Delhi Metro closures during the CJP protest? The Court had advised against a blanket shutdown of public transport and directed that movement should not be completely prohibited. A contempt petition later alleged that entry and exit gates at 45 metro stations were closed. 3Why was a contempt petition filed against the Delhi Police Commissioner over the CJP protest? content: led demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was detained from his Gurugram residence ahead of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protests in Delhi, on Sunday claimed that he was kidnapped" in a video posted on social media after his release late on Saturday night. Delhi Police had said Rathee could be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders". He was detained from his Sector 56 residence ahead of the planned demonstration. - Abhijeet Dipke, Other CJP Leaders Produced Before Executive Magistrate - Delhi Police Files 20 FIRs Over Attempts To Hold Protests Day After Mass Detentions, Internet Shutdown - CJP Leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka Released With Maintain Peace Condition - Dhruv Rathee To Attend CJP Protest In Bengaluru, Prakash Raj Calls Him 'Voice With A Spine' The Delhi Police has imposed prohibitory orders and denied permission for the protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The rumours and the justifications being offered for my detention and arrest and that I was a foreign passport holder, are all lies. I am an Indian citizen and I have the same rights as any ordinary citizen," he said. The remarks come after former Bengaluru Police Commissioner Bhaskar Rao earlier this week sought the Union Home Ministrys intervention to verify Rathees citizenship, immigration status and compliance with visa conditions following his participation in an anti-SIR protest here on October 8. In the video, Rathee claimed he was dragged" out of his home and taken away like a criminal". He said around 20 people entered his house and that more than 50 people were present outside. His allegations could not be independently verified. Rathee said he was subsequently taken to a police station, where officials told him he would be released. More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, police sources told PTI. headline: No Supporter To Receive Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka & Saurav Das: 'No Gatherings' Clause To Hurt CJP?
content: Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das Released: What were the charges under which they were arrested? What are the conditions? Will they hurt CJP? In what may come as major blow to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), top leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das, who were released on Sunday morning, are now bound by a Delhi Executive Magistrate court to maintain peace. Sources said the trio was forced to sign a 50,000 surety bond each along with a one-year peace bond. Under the strict conditions of their release, the leaders have to maintain absolute peace, law, and order. The court has strictly ordered them not to hold any public gatherings or instigate unrest. - CJP Leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka Released With Maintain Peace Condition - CJP Protest Highlights: All Detained Protesters, Except CJP Leaders, Released; All Delhi Metro Stations Now Open - Three CJP Leaders Detained From Flight, To Be Kept Separately, Say Police Sources | Exclusive - 'Are Protesters Chambal Dacoits? Real Dacoits Are In Parliament': Abhijeet Dipke's Parents On CJP Stir Crackdown Any violation of this bond will attract immediate re-arrest and heavier criminal charges. What were the charges under which they were arrested? What are the conditions? Will they hurt CJP? Dipke, Ranka and Das, leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), were released on Sunday morning. The Delhi Police had placed the CJP convenor and co-convenors under preventive arrest on October 10, 2026, under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). They were intercepted and detained directly from an Air India flight immediately after landing in Delhi from Mumbai. Their detention was part of a massive security clampdown by the Delhi Police to prevent a planned large-scale protest at Jantar Mantar. The CJP, alongside several opposition parties, called for the protest to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls. CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das were released on Sunday morning. The trio was forced to sign a 50,000 surety bond each along with a one-year peace bond. The court ordered them not to hold any public gatherings or instigate unrest. The Delhi Police placed the CJP convenor and co-convenors under preventive arrest on October 10, 2026. Their detention was under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India.Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully. Abhijeet Dipke (@abhijeet_dipke) October 11, 2026 The security clampdown resulted in the detention of over 7,000 protesters across Delhi, including prominent opposition leaders like Arvind Kejriwal and Mamata Banerjee, who attempted to join the demonstration. Following their release from the Delhi Cantt Police Station court, the CJP acknowledged the development on social media and renewed its calls to continue the protest demonstrations. ALONE AT THE GATES In a striking development, top police sources confirmed that the high-profile trio left the police station completely alone after completing their legal formalities. Despite the partys loud online rhetoric, not a single follower or supporter arrived at the station to receive the leaders upon their release. Senior police officials stated that the swift legal action sends a clear message that no one is above the law." | Delhi: CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das have been released after they were produced before the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station.CJP National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka says, We will hold a press conference at 2 PM." ANI (@ANI) October 11, 2026 WHAT ARE SECTIONS 126 AND 170 OF THE BNSS? The Delhi Police and the judiciary had invoked specific preventive clauses under the new Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to defuse the planned unrest: Section 126 of the BNSS (Power of Executive Magistrate): This section empowers an Executive Magistrate to act immediately if they receive credible information that a person is likely to commit a breach of peace, disturb public tranquillity, or execute any wrongful act that could trigger public unrest. The magistrate can legally compel the individuals to execute a bond to maintain peace. Section 170 of the BNSS (Preventive Arrest): This clause grants a police officer the authority to arrest an individual without a warrant and without a Magistrates order if they have knowledge of a design (plan) to commit a cognizable offence. This power is exercised strictly when it appears to the officer that the commission of the offence cannot be prevented otherwise. Following their release from the Delhi Cantt Police Station court, CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das were bound by an Executive Magistrate court to maintain absolute peace and order. Each leader was forced to sign a 50,000 rupee surety bond and a one-year peace bond, and they were strictly prohibited from holding public gatherings or instigating unrest. Any violation will result in immediate re-arrest and heavier criminal charges.

headline: India condemns attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh
content: India on Sunday (October 11, 2026) strongly condemned a major attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured more than 300. New Delhi said the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Gulf nation were "completely unacceptable and must cease immediately." "We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement. "We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons," it said. Saudi Arabia has blamed Houthi militants for the attack. "We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy return to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.

headline: Tiger kills man who entered big cat enclosure at English wildlife park
content: A man died Saturday (October 10, 2026) after he entered the tiger enclosure at a wildlifepark in northern England and was attacked by one of the animals, police said. Emergency medical personnel responded to the Yorkshire Wildlife Park near the city of Doncaster after the incident was reported at about 1:35 p.m., but the victim died at the scene, South Yorkshire Police said in a statement. The tiger was not injured and remained inside the enclosure during the incident, the force said. The wildlife park was evacuated after the attack, and officers remained at the scene Saturday night (October 10) as they investigated. We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened,'' the wildlife park said in a statement posted on its website. Yorkshire Wildlife Park began operations in 2009, with its Land of the Tigers attraction opening in 2011. The attraction is a purpose-built two-acre reserve for endangered Amur tigers, also known as Siberian tigers. The enclosure includes a 300-meter (yard) raised walkway that allows visitors to watch the big cats roam through woodlands and grasslands or playing in a waterfall pool, the park says on its website.

headline: Former Japanese PM's wife Akie Abe meets RSS general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale
content: Akie Abe, wife of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, and Tomohiko Taniguchi, chairman of Nippon Kaigi, a right-wing organisation in Japan, met Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale at the organisations office in New Delhi on October 8. A communique issued by the RSS said the meeting focused on ways to strengthen IndiaJapan relations, with particular emphasis on civilisational ties, cultural cooperation and people-centric initiatives. Also Read : The Saffron Empire The meeting lasted over an hour and featured an exchange of views on deepening engagement between the two countries, the communique said. Ms. Abe, Chairperson, Foundation for Social Contribution and Sh. Tomohiko Taniguchi, Chairperson Nippon Kaigi, a prominent Japanese non-governmental organisation, interacted over an hour, reflecting a shared interest in deepening engagement between the two countries, Sunil Ambekar, the RSS publicity in-charge, said in a post on X. The RSS said the participants would explore avenues for collaboration to strengthen cultural ties between India and Japan.

headline: India rejects UN rights body remarks on Delhi protests, cites 'double standards'
content: A day after the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Office expressed concern over the mass detention of demonstrators, civil society members, lawyers, and journalists in Delhi, India said on Sunday that concerns are unwarranted and constitute an unacceptable interference in the internal affairs of India. This is the second time in the last 12 hours that India has responded to the UN offices remarks on Saturday. Earlier, Indias permanent mission in Geneva called the concerns misplaced, saying they caused unwarranted interference in internal affairs. This time, the Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, We have seen certain remarks by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) about yesterdays events in New Delhi. India is the worlds largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media. As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances, he said, defending the action by the police in Delhi. The MEA spokesperson said, The OHCHRs concerns are therefore unwarranted and constitute an unacceptable interference in the internal affairs of India. We also note that the OHCHR has an approach of extreme selectivity when it comes to public positions. Violent responses to protests in our neighbourhood have gone uncommented, as indeed have law enforcement actions in its own vicinity. Such double standards only erode the credibility of its standing and contribute to the loss of faith in multilateralism, the MEA spokesperson said, referring to police and law enforcement agency actions in Pakistan and France. Respect right to peaceful assembly: UN rights body The UN Human Rights spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan called on Indian authorities to respect and fulfil the right to peaceful assembly, noting that restrictions must meet strict tests of necessity and proportionality. We are concerned by reports of mass detentions in India of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during todays large-scale demonstrations in Delhi, he said in a statement on Saturday evening, as reports of thousands of protestors being detained came in. We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled. Restrictions on peaceful protests must meet strict tests of necessity and proportionality, the UN office said. The Indian authorities should also ensure law enforcement forces exercise utmost restraint in response to peaceful protesters, consistent with the countrys democratic traditions and human rights obligations. All those arbitrarily detained must be immediately and unconditionally released. We also urge the authorities to engage in meaningful dialogue to address the broadly held concerns expressed, it said.

headline: India condemns 'dastardly attack' on Saudi Arabia airport that killed 12; Pakistan calls Houthi strikes 'heinous'
content: India strongly condemned repeated strikes by the Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabian airports and civilian infrastructure. In a statement on Sunday (October 11), the Ministry of External Affairs called the attacks unacceptable and said the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian targets must cease immediately. We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property, the ministry said. We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons, it added in its statement. Quick answers to key questions 1What happened in the attack on Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport? A missile struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4. The attack killed 12 people and injured more than 300, according to the reports cited in the article. 2Who did Saudi Arabia blame for the Riyadh airport attack? A Saudi-led coalition blamed Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen for the attack. 3Why did India condemn the attacks on Saudi Arabias airports? India said repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure were unacceptable and called for them to cease immediately. It also expressed condolences to the victims families and solidarity with Saudi Arabia. 4How did Pakistan respond to the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia? Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called the strikes heinous and said attacks on civilians and vital infrastructure were unacceptable. He reaffirmed Pakistans commitment to Saudi Arabias sovereignty and territorial integrity. 5Were flights operating at Riyadh airport after the attack? Airport operations were suspended, and the closure was later extended until 9 pm Sunday. Flights were diverted or cancelled, and passengers were advised to check their flight status with airlines. The Ministry of External Affairs said India stands in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest. The ministry's remarks came as Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also condemned the Houthis' strikes in Saudi Arabia. In a post on X, Sharif said, I strongly condemn the heinous attack carried out by the Houthis militia on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. We extend our deepest condolences to the families of the victims, and we pray to God for the prompt and complete recovery of the injured. Attacks targeting civilians and vital infrastructure are utterly unacceptable and pose a serious threat to regional peace and stability. These violent acts, which constitute a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately, Sharif added. He said Pakistan stands firmly and with steadfast solidarity alongside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its leadership, and its brotherly people. He also mentioned the Mecca Al-Mukarramah Joint Defense Agreement, while emphasising the deep fraternal ties that bind our two countries. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the integrity of its territories, and its security, Sharif said. The defence pact, of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. As many as 12 people were killed, and over 300 others were injured in the latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh, civil aviation authorities were quoted by the Associated Press as saying early Sunday. A missile struck a King Khalid International Airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights on Saturday, a source claimed. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen for the attack, describing it as a "full-fledged war crime" that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile. Saturday's attack was the deadliest in the kingdom since May 2015, when a suicide bombing by the Islamic State (IS) jihadist group killed 21 worshippers in a Shia mosque in the eastern Qatif governorate. It was also the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. The attack came during an unprecedented wave of Houthi strikes on the kingdom since a truce in the group's long-running war with Yemen's Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July. The Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals. Saudi civil aviation authorities on Saturday said airport operations were suspended. The closure was later extended by 24 hours until 9 pm Sunday, according to the flight tracking platform Flightradar 24.

headline: 40,000 paramilitary personnel proof that Delhi protest was successful: Prashant Kishor
content: Deployment of 40,000 paramilitary forces in Delhi was a good enough proof that the protest in the national capital on Saturday was successful, Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder and Bankipur MLA Prashant Kishor said as he joined the Opposition in demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He said the credibility of the Election Commission of India (EC) had eroded in the last 8-10 years. Delhi CJP Protest News Live Updates: CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ranka and Saurav Das released from detention Reacting to media questions on the protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Kumar, Kishor said: Many people are looking at how many people attended the protest, but the fact that the government had to deploy 40,000 paramilitary forces to stop it shows how powerful it was. He said the protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was a reflection of peoples diminishing faith in the ECI. In last eight to 10 years, there have been serious questions on the credibility of the ECI. CEC Kumar should resign, Kishor said. He pointed out how ECI had not stopped the Bihar government from distributing Rs. 10,000 each to Jeevika workers during the 2025 Assembly elections. Panic in NDA ahead of MLC polls The JSP founder also targeted an NDA meeting held in Bihar on Saturday, viewing it as sign of growing vulnerability of the ruling alliance. Just as their panic was visible from the meeting of 480 leaders in Bankipur (ahead of the bypoll in August), there is a similar panic regarding the MLC elections. Whether the NDA calls a meeting of the legislature or the legislative council, the educated teacher and graduate voters of Bihar have made up their mind to defeat the ruling alliances candidates, said Kishor. Notably, JD (U) MLA Anant Kumar Singh has openly expressed support for JSP Patna Graduate seat candidate Anuj Singh against his own partys candidate, Neeraj Kumar, in the poll scheduled on October 23. In August, Kishor had scripted history by winning Bankipur, a BJP bastion, by a margin of over 19,000 votes in the bypoll. The seat had been represented by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin for five terms.

headline: U.S. military says it disabled cargo vessel trying to run Iran blockade
content: The U.S. military said on Saturday (October 10, 2026) it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after the ships crew ignored warnings and attempted to run a naval blockade against Iran. A U.S. military fighter jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also known as the Arika Sun) with a precision munition, fully disabling the ships propulsion without harming the crew, the U.S. Central Command posted on X. CENTCOM said the cargo vessel had attempted to transit regional waters after leaving an Iranian port. Reuters was not immediately able to reach the bulk carriers operator for comment. CENTCOM warned mariners in the Gulf of Oman and the approaches to the Strait of Hormuz to heed blockade warnings, monitor notice-to-mariners broadcasts and contact U.S. naval forces. The number of vessels transiting the vital strait fell to the lowest in more than two months after attacks on tankers reached their highest level last week since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, raising concerns over shipping disruptions and supporting crude prices. Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz carried 20% of the worlds oil consumption.

headline: Delhi Police Files 20 FIRs Over Attempts To Hold Protests Day After Mass Detentions, Internet Shutdown
content: The Delhi Police has registered over 20 FIRs over attempts to hold protests over the controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Saturday, October 10 The Delhi Police has registered over 20 FIRs over attempts to hold protests over the controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Saturday, October 10, according to sources. ANI (@ANI) October 11, 2026 Ratna Singh, head of the CJPs legal team, confirmed the development in a post on X, stating that the Executive Magistrate court had released Abhijeet, Saurav and Ashutosh. Executive Magistrate court releases Abhijeet, Saurav and Ashutosh", she said. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was also detained ahead of the planned protest, was released at 3 AM on Sunday. The detentions were part of a widespread police clampdown on the proposed agitation. Those detained also included four former chief ministers: AAPs Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress founder Mamata Banerjee, and the Lefts Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar. Fresh Call For Protest A day after mass detentions and internet suspension in parts of the capital, CJPs organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde gave the call for a fresh protest at Jantar Mantar over the SIR issue. The Delhi Police registered over 20 FIRs against individuals for taking the law into their own hands, obstructing government work, and assaulting police personnel during protests over the Special Intensive Revision exercise on October 10, 2026.

headline: Delhi CJP protest: Dipke, Das, and Ranka released, but with a condition. What do BNSS Sections 126, 170 say? Explained
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were released from detention on a special courts order on Sunday, a day after they were placed under preventive arrest by the Delhi Police. The trio was among thousands of protesters detained by the Delhi Police ahead of Saturday's Jantar Mantar protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Dipke, Das, and Ranka were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate court in Delhi Cantt on Sunday, CJPs legal head Ratna Sinha informed in a post on X. A Delhi police official informed me about this in the morning. As CJP's Legal Head, I will be at the police station along with other advocates representing us," Singh said in a post on X. She said they were charged Sections 126 and 170 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Sinha later informed that the Executive Magistrate court released Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on a condition: no breach of peace for one year." The Delhi Police said a surety bond of 50,000 wa also signed. Soon after, the Delhi Police also confirmed the development, saying, Preventive arrest u/s 126/170 BNSS of Sh. Abhijeet Dipke, Sh. Ashutosh Ranka and Sh. Saurav Das was done on 10.10.2026." All due legal procedures were followed, and they were produced before the SEM Court, Delhi Cantt, on 11.10.2026, police said. They added that a bail bond as "Surety Bond of 50,000/- was filled for maintaining peace and good behaviour, for a period of one year, and they were released by the SEM Court." BNSS Sections 126 and 170 were reportedly invoked against the CJP leaders. Section 126 pertains to the security for keeping peace, and Section 170 allows arrest to prevent commission of cognisable offences. Under Section 126(1) BNSS, if an Executive Magistrate receives information about a person likely to commit a breach of the peace or disturb the public tranquillity or to do any wrongful act, they can require the person to show cause why they should not be ordered to execute a bond to keep the peace for up to a year. If the person fails to show cause, or if the Magistrate is satisfied there are sufficient grounds, they will order the person to execute the bond. If a person fails to furnish the bond, the Magistrate shall hold an inquiry into the matter, according to Vidhikarya Law Chambers. Section 170, meanwhile, provides a provision to arrest an individual to prevent the commission of cognizable offences. Under Section 170 of the BNSS, police must have a legally required basis to believe that an offence is being planned or might occur and that an arrest is necessary to prevent it. Section 170 o BNSS says: 1. A police officer knowing of a design to commit any cognizable offence may arrest, without orders from a Magistrate and without a warrant, the person so designing, if it appears to such officer that the commission of the offence cannot be otherwise prevented. 2. No person arrested under sub-section (1) shall be detained in custody for a period exceeding twenty-four hours from the time of his arrest unless his further detention is required or authorised under any other provisions of this Sanhita or of any other law for the time being in force. CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained immediately after their plane from Mumbai landed in Delhi. A video also emerged on social media showing police personnel entering the aircraft Dipke was on board at Delhi airport. "Aray mai arrest hone ke liye hi aaya hun. Karlo arrest [I have come here to be arrested; arrest me]," Abhijeet Dipke told Delhi police personnel as they asked him to cooperate. "No, this is not an arrest. Please cooperate," the Delhi Police personnel told Dipke. The video shows Dipke joining hands and asking officials if he could at least take his bag along. The detention came amid an unprecedented security clampdown in Delhi, where more than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, foiling protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar, police sources told PTI. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest. The CJP has renewed its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday as police continued their heavy security arrangements with over 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel to be deployed in the city. The CJP and opposition parties have been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of

headline: Isaias Leaves Thousands Without Power, Kills at Least 4 People
content: Bloomberg) -- Downpours spread across the Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic as Isaias remnants headed north after knocking out power to hundreds of thousands in three states and killing at least four people in Florida and Alabama. Two people died after trees fell onto their homes Friday night one in Birmingham, Alabama, according to Jefferson County Emergency Management Officer Shea Hess, and another in Escambia County, Florida, according to Governor Ron DeSantis. A third person died inside their garage from apparent carbon-monoxide poisoning after they were found with their generator running indoors, DeSantis said Saturday afternoon. Alabama Governor Kay Ivey said another person from her state died as a result of the hurricane, but didnt give further information. Remnants of the former hurricane were expected to produce widespread moderate to heavy precipitation from the Upper Ohio Valley, Central Appalachians, Mid-Atlantic, Northeast and coastal North Carolina, the US Weather Prediction Center said Saturday. Isaias was expected to put about 12.6 million people from Florida to Virginia at a level two risk for severe thunderstorms, which can bring downpours and spawn tornadoes, through the weekend, the US Storm Prediction Center said. The storm also hit energy production across the Gulf of Mexico during the week and 685,000 homes and businesses remain without power as of Saturday 3:30 p.m. New York time, according to PowerOutage.com. Thats 22% fewer homes without power than Saturday morning. Oil output in the Gulf of Mexico plummeted as the storm approached the US coast, as companies evacuated crews from platforms as a precaution and drillers sailed rigs out of its path. The Category 2 storm made landfall at 8:30 p.m. Friday near Destin, Florida, with top winds of 105 miles (169 kilometers) an hour. It quickly degraded into a post-tropical cyclone, according to the US National Hurricane Center. It was the first hurricane to hit the US in almost two years and was expected to bring widespread rain of as much as 8 inches (20 centimeters) across the region, with as much as 15 inches seen in some localized areas. While the tropical risks subside in the east, western Mexico and the US Southwest face twin threats from Tropical Storm Rachel and Hurricane Simon. Rachel is forecast to strike near the US-Mexico border in northern Baja California late Saturday and then bring flooding rains across the US Southwest, including parts of California, Arizona and Nevada, the US National Hurricane Center said. There are rare tropical storm watches up across Southern California, including for San Diego. Further south, Simon is forecast to strike near Manzanillo, Mexico, the countrys busiest Pacific port, overnight as Category 4 hurricane on the five-step, Saffir-Simpson scale, packing winds of 155 miles per hour. As much as 20 inches of rain may fall widely, with isolated spots getting up to 40 inches. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, the US hurricane center said. The rains will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides. More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com 2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Trump says Ukraine should get new President as he blames Zelenskyy for U.S. diesel prices
content: President Donald Trump said on Saturday (October 10, 2026) it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end his country's war with Russia and blaming him for high diesel prices in the U.S. I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does, Mr. Trump said. The President, who on Friday (October 9, 2026) struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to buy diesel from Russia in an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, has been urging Mr. Zelenskyy for weeks to stop strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. He has also sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than the U.S.-led war in Iran, which has elevated world energy prices. He wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel, Mr. Trump said, before departing for Tennessee where he was set to rally Republican voters. An Associated Press-NORC Centre for Public Affairs Research poll conducted last month and published October 1 found that Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran, and blame him for higher prices. Mr. Trump also suggested that if he had been U.S. President in 2022, that war would have never started. There was no reason that that war with Ukraine and Russia started. It started due to incompetence. Mr. Zelenskyy has lost 30% of your country, and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Mr. Trump said. Independent estimates are that about 20% of Ukraine's territory is under Russian control. British defence officials recently estimated that about half a million Russian soldiers have been killed in the war; there are no reliable recent estimates about how many Ukrainians have died. Mr. Trump's extraordinary intervention came after Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026). Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said on Saturday (October 10, 2026). At least 18 people were wounded. Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days. Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote Saturday (October 10, 2026) on X. He said the attacks show Moscow understands any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities." Russia's choice is war, Mr. Zelenskyy said in a later Telegram post, after drone attacks on energy facilities and a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. He said every additional billion dollars Russia earns from exports would help pay for weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production, and the recruitment of mercenaries, and that Moscow would only be ready to stop when its ability to fight diminished. Moscow received from diesel deal "signals that it is apparently permissible to continue attacking. And this needs to be corrected, he said, urging the U.S., Europe and other partners to limit Russia's capacity to wage war. Mr. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was coordinating steps to counter the extra revenue Russia will receive, and that he had spoken to French President Emmanuel Macron about shoring up air defences, warning of an increased risk of further missile strikes in the coming days. He also said he had discussed the developments with Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and that Ukraine would receive ammunition in the coming days for the F-16s it uses to intercept Shahed drones. Mr. Trump had been set to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia with President Vladimir Putin in a phone call. Instead, the American leader announced Friday (October 9, 2026) that Russia will immediately supply more than 3,00,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 5,00,000 tons in November and 1 million tons immediately thereafter. Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons within a short period of time after that, he wrote. In Kyiv, people gathered at a memorial to fallen soldiers on Independence Square greeted the deal with a mix of anger and resignation. Trump has once again shown his true face, said Oleksandr Petrenko, 26. He didn't care about the situation, the shelling or the destruction of our homes. All he's interested in is oil or the fuel prices and how much Americans have to pay. Knowing Trump, he tries to manipulate the markets. He's got an election coming up soon, Mr. Petrenko said. So he needs to emphasise to his voters that gasoline will be cheap. But it won't be effective. For Oksana Yakunina, a financial adviser from the central city of Kropyvnytskyi, the announcement didn't really come as a surprise. Trump has been working with Putin for a long time, she told The Associated Press. Ukraine's European allies expressed dismay at the deal and said they stood by their commitment to sanctions. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said Stockholm regretted the agreement, as energy revenues are central to the Russian war chest, and noted that the European Union would adopt its most comprehensive sanctions package yet on Monday (October 12 2026), with 1,600 listings targeting Russia's military-industrial complex. The German government remains committed to the sanctions imposed on Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions, spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said, adding that support for Ukraine remains unwavering. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski questioned whether Russia could deliver at all. headline: India condemns attack on Riyadh airport, expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia
content: India Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for an immediate end to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. Repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement hours after at least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on the airport. The latest attack is the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said. The MEA statement said, We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property. We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons. We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy return to the region at the earliest, it said. On October 8, following the attacks by the Houthis on two airports in Saudi Arabia over the previous two days, India strongly condemned these actions. The Indian government stated that targeting civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable and issued an advisory urging its nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain alert and vigilant. The two previous attacks on King Khalid International Airport killed four and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac. The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as it wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the Iran-backed group. The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for the attack, but a Saudi-led military coalition vowed to respond. Indian community in Saudi Arabia The Indian community in the Saudi Kingdom numbers approximately 2.74 million, including skilled and semi-skilled professionals. This is not the first time in the last seven months since the war in West Asia began that Delhi has issued condemnatory statements and security advisories to warn its citizens to stay safe. In the past seven months, at least four such occasions have warranted such statements, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi has spoken to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman about the evolving conflict in March and August this year.

headline: 'Every Failed Marriage Cannot Be...': Allahabad High Court Quashes Dowry Harassment FIR
content: The Allahabad High Court emphasised the need to distinguish matrimonial discord from criminal conduct. The Allahabad High Court cautioned that routinely converting every distressed or failed marriage into a criminal case could affect the institution of marriage at its core, while quashing an FIR alleging dowry harassment, physical assault and attempted strangulation in a case involving a brief period of cohabitation. A division bench of Justices Chandra Dhari Singh and Tarun Saxena quashed the FIR registered at the Hari Parvat police station in Agra under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Dowry Prohibition Act. The court allowed a writ petition filed by Gaurav Jain and his family members. - Delhi Hit-And-Run: Elderly Couple Flung Into Air After Car Hits Them, Woman Driver Arrested - UP Woman Catches Husband On Date With Girlfriend, Clings To His Car Bonnet As He Drives Away | Video - Karnataka BJP BLA Booked Over Attempt To Delete Names Of 7,561 Voters - 'Mard Jaat Haye Haye': UP Woman Catches Husband With Girlfriend, Ends Up Clinging To His Car Bonnet As He Drives Away In its judgment dated October 8, the high court emphasised the need to distinguish matrimonial discord from criminal conduct and cautioned against the potential misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages. According to the case details, the couple married on November 12, 2024, and the wife left the matrimonial home on February 3, 2025, after approximately two-and-a-half months of cohabitation. The husband subsequently filed a divorce petition on May 3, 2025. The FIR was registered on June 30, 2025. The allegations in the FIR included dowry demands and harassment, denial of food, threats, retention of the wifes stridhan and an attempt to strangulate her. The court noted that no complaint of domestic violence, police control room (PCR) call or contemporaneous police intervention concerning the alleged incidents during the period of cohabitation had been brought on record. The high court acknowledged that protecting women from dowry-related violence and cruelty was a statutory and constitutional imperative. However, it observed that the possibility of criminal law being misused could not be overlooked. It stressed that matrimonial discord could not automatically be equated with criminality and that criminal proceedings could not be used as a substitute for adjudication before a matrimonial court. The court warned that if every distressed or failed marriage were routinely converted into an FIR and subjected to the coercive machinery of criminal law, the institution of marriage will inevitably be affected at its core". The high court clarified that its decision did not adjudicate the merits of the pending matrimonial proceedings. Both parties remain free to pursue their remedies before the competent matrimonial court. It further stated that the complainant could pursue any independent remedy available under the law in respect of a distinct cause of action, subject to the applicable statutory requirements. The Allahabad High Court quashed a dowry harassment FIR involving a brief cohabitation period, cautioning that routinely converting failed marriages into criminal cases could undermine the institution of marriage at its core and misuses criminal law.

headline: Murray & Co and its Sunday auction: the famous 'hammer' of Madras nears the century mark
content: Any popular music consumer who scours the decades for earworms would be familiar with the phrase Hammer time, sung elegantly by M.C. Hammer in his U Cant Touch This. In Madras and now Chennai, a different form of Hammer time has been playing out since February 10, 1927 when Murray & Co saw the light, having been founded by brothers A. Vedantam and S. Rajam. In the 99 years plus a few months of its existence, the auction house has not given that hammer a break except for a couple of times due to inescapable situations. What does the continuity mean to those at the helm of Murray & Co? Hemant Srivatsa, partner, Murray & Co., responds: We are very proud of it. We have conducted Sunday auctions almost without fail since our inception. There were a few weeks during our relocation when we had to pause, and of course, the pandemic was the longest period we could not hold auctions. Other than that, we have kept the tradition going. Enterprises can dig their feet in, take over a place by imprinting their character on it. And one cannot think of that place anymore without that enterprise popping up in the mind. And then enterprises take over peoples mindspace, becoming a household name. Murray & Co has done both. After being identified with one space for a long time, a bungalow behind the iconic LIC building on Mount Road, it has had to change addresses, but its hold on the mind space of the citys residents has been unchanging and firm. Hemant throws light on the addresses the auction house has had to its name. Our original auction room was located behind the LIC Building until 2012. We then briefly operated from Mandaveli before moving to our current premises at Gemini Towers, near the Gemini Flyover. On how the business has evolved over the years, he observes: We started with real estate auctions. From there, we expanded into retail auctions of household goods and furniture, followed by industrial auctions. There has always been a transition as the business adapted to changing times. Hemant continues: Within the retail space, the categories have changed significantly. We sell far more electronic items today than when I joined the business in 1992. The market has evolved, and so have the items. Online auctions are becoming increasingly popular. Where does Murray & Co stand in cyberspace? Our industrial auctions are already completely online. Our retail auctions have not fully transitioned yet, though our online portal is currently being developed. Even after it is launched, we want to continue our physical auctions because they have a charm of their own that no technology can replace, says Hemant. And when prodded to name one transaction that has been hugely memorable for Murray & Co in the almost 100 years of its existence, Hemant refuses to take that route. Every single item is memorable. Every transaction is special, not just for us, but for the person who entrusted it to us and, hopefully, for the person who eventually bought it. Have grand plans been etched to celebrate the centenary when it arrives? Yes, the plans are still in the works. Over the next few months, we will come up with concrete ideas to celebrate the centenary. As Murray and Co. looks forward to its hundredth year, its greatest achievement is probably not merely its longevity but its ability to evolve without losing sight of what makes an auction special; its people, the stories, and the bustling sounds of bids. A century on, a tradition continues, one bid at a time.

content: The Supreme Court is convening a special Sunday sitting today, October 11, to address urgent legal challenges arising from the sweeping transit restrictions and preventive detentions enforced during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in New Delhi. A special Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will assemble at 10:30 AM to hear the matters, according to legal news portal Bar & Bench. Here is everything you need to know about today's special hearing and the events leading up to it: Quick answers to key questions 1What was the Supreme Court's special Sunday sitting on the CJP protests about? The Supreme Court scheduled a special sitting for October 11 at 10:30 AM to hear petitions concerning alleged disobedience of its directions, police action and preventive detentions linked to the protests. 2Why was a contempt plea filed over Delhi Metro closures during the CJP protests? The plea alleged that the DMRC closed entry and exit gates at 45 stations despite the Supreme Court's October 9 direction against a blanket shutdown of public transport. 3What did the contempt petition allege about Delhi Police action at Jantar Mantar? It alleged that police used indiscriminate violence against unarmed demonstrators on October 10, including detaining and assaulting people. It also raised claims about officers without name tags and the alleged manhandling of women protesters. 4Who challenged the preventive detention of opposition leaders during the CJP protests? Trinamool Congress MP and Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy approached the Supreme Court. Her petition argued that preventive detention should not be used to suppress the fundamental right to peaceful protest. 5Were Delhi Metro stations expected to close again on October 11? The related report said the DMRC had not issued an update about station restrictions for Sunday. It reported that all station entry and exit gates had reopened by 10 AM on Saturday. The primary focus of today's hearing is a contempt of court petition alleging that authorities wilfully disobeyed the Supreme Court's prior directives. Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi filed the plea seeking contempt proceedings against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara. According to Bar & Bench, the petition contends that despite the Court's October 9 order advising against a blanket shutdown of public transport, the DMRC closed entry and exit gates at 45 metro stations. Tripathi claimed that he personally verified these closures at the GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya stations on the night of October 9. The plea argued that this "deliberate recalcitrance" severely crippled public life in the national capital and stranded essential travellers, with no adequate traffic advisories. According to a LiveLaw report, a contempt of court petition has been filed in the Supreme Court against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar. The petition alleged that personnel under his command resorted to indiscriminate violence against unarmed citizens during the October 10 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar. The petitioner contended that these actions explicitly violated the principles of minimum force and proportionality previously outlined by the Supreme Court. According to the allegations detailed by LiveLaw, the police detained and assaulted multiple unarmed individuals during the demonstration. The petition also claimed that participating officers were operating without name tags and that several women protesters were manhandled by male officers during the crackdown. In tandem with the transport issues, the Bench will hear a petition challenging the sweeping police action against political figures and citizens. Trinamool Congress MP and Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy has approached the top court challenging the preventive detention of opposition party leaders, including four former Chief Ministers who were participating in the protests. According to Bar & Bench, Guruswamy argued that preventive detention cannot be weaponised to suppress the fundamental right to peaceful protest. Her plea also highlights alleged police excesses against legal professionals, bringing focus to the detention of lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Today's contempt plea directly stemmed from a hearing on Friday, October 9. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, alongside Justices Bagchi and Mohana, reviewed earlier petitions regarding the transit curbs ahead of the CJP's demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. During that hearing, the Court criticised the widespread closures of metro stations and the cancellation of over 200 trains. The Court had directed the government to ensure there was no "complete prohibition" on movement, recording an assurance from Solicitor General Tushar Mehta that the restrictions would be reconsidered. According to a recent Hindustan Times report, CJI Surya Kant recently defended the Courts decision to invoke Article 142 of the Constitution to quash FIRs against student protesters involved in earlier Jantar Mantar demonstrations. Refusing to order an independent probe into those protests, the CJI noted the need to protect the futures of the young students involved, stating, We have to see their parents, their future. We don't want them to come to court.
