headline: Trump's Newfound Obsession: He Wants Pacific Or Atlantic Ocean Renamed 'Trump Ocean'
content: US President Donald Trump has a newfound obsession. He has floated the idea of renaming either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean as 'Trump Ocean' or 'Ocean of the Americas' US President Donald Trump has a newfound obsession. He has floated the idea of renaming either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean as Trump Ocean or Ocean of the Americas. This is yet another push to extend US dominance over geographical names. - 'I Should Have Won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes: Trump Lashes Out After Navi Pillay Wins 2026 Award - Trump Says Putin Agreed To 'Immediately' Supply Russian Diesel To US, Global Markets - Trump May Announce Executive Order Seeking To Slash Diesel Prices Ahead Of US Midterm Elections - Trump Rules Out Iran Strike Before Midterms, Cites 'Productive' Talks As Oil Prices Surge Trump made the remarks during a campaign rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, on Saturday, October 10, while he was addressing the crowds ahead of the November midterm elections. We need a river. We need an ocean," Trump said. We call it Trump Ocean or Ocean of the Americas, something like that," he said, drawing chuckles from the audience, The Washington Post reported. Trumps remarks came as he invoked his earlier decisions to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America and Lake Ontario as Lake America. According to The Washington Post, the US President stressed that he wanted an ocean and a major river to be renamed before leaving office. Before I get out, I think we should have an ocean. And we need a great river," Trump said. Trumps Earlier Renaming Decisions Last year, Trump announced renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America last year, a move that triggered a diplomatic row with Mexico. Back in August, Trump also renamed Lake Ontario, which sits between the US state of New York and Canada, as Lake America. The move came amid trade tensions between the two countries. This is not the end of the story. Amid the war with Iran, Trump had said in a post on Truth Social that the strategic Strait of Hormuz should be renamed as the Trump Strait. The Strait of Hormuz emerged as a key flashpoint between the US and Iran, after the latter blocked the waterway in the wake of joint US-Israeli strikes, a move that sent shockwaves through global economies. During a campaign rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, US President Donald Trump floated the idea of renaming either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean to 'Trump Ocean' or the 'Ocean of the Americas' before leaving office.

headline: Nepal On Flood Alert: Budhi Gandaki River Swells After Landslide, Bridges Swept Away In Gorkha
content: Fresh flooding along Nepal's Budhi Gandaki River swept away two suspension footbridges and a steel bridge in Gorkha district. Flooding destroyed three bridges and damaged houses in Nepals Gorkha district, raising fresh concerns over flooding risks weeks after deadly floods and landslides killed more than 1,400 people across the country. Fresh flooding along Nepals Budhi Gandaki River swept away two suspension footbridges and a steel bridge in Gorkha district, damaged houses and put several settlements at risk, according to Nepal Police. - Woman Says Bengaluru Is No Longer For The Middle Class, Says Dont Come If Youre Not Earning 1 Lakh Monthly - Gomti Floods Lucknow: Water Reaches Ekana-Palassio, Disrupts Roads, Temples And Cremations - Lucknow Floods: Has Urbanisation Left The Gomti With Too Little Room To Breathe? - When The Bridge Becomes A Wall: Srinagars Vanishing Photographic Memory The flooding followed a landslide that blocked the river between Lokpa and Chumling in Chumnubri Rural Municipality-6, police said. The incident raised concerns about the risk of further flooding in settlements along the river. An old suspension footbridge connecting Nyakchet and Sirdibas in Chumnubri-3 was swept away by the floodwaters. A mud house belonging to Ram Bahadur Gurung in Sirdibas was also washed away, while water entered another house belonging to him. In a separate incident, floodwaters destroyed a suspension footbridge connecting Machhakhola in Dharche Rural Municipality-5 with Kerauja. Water entered five to seven houses and a similar number of sheds in the lower settlement of Machhakhola, police said. Around 20 to 22 houses in Salleri, Dharche-3, were also reported to be at risk. The steel bridge at Soti, which connects wards 2 and 3 of Aarughat Rural Municipality, was swept away as the river surged. The latest incident comes weeks after catastrophic flooding and landslides struck Nepal on August 26, triggering widespread destruction across several districts. The disaster affected areas along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems, destroying homes and critical infrastructure, including roads and bridges. By October 5, Nepal had recorded at least 1,455 deaths from the August disaster, while 5,285 people remained missing, Reuters reported. Search-and-rescue operations had officially ended, with authorities shifting their focus towards rehabilitation and reconstruction. The August disaster caused extensive damage across Nepal, with communities facing the loss of homes, livelihoods and vital transport links. Houses And Bridges At Risk In Gorkha The destruction of the three bridges has disrupted local connections between settlements, while the risk to houses in Salleri and the flooding of homes in Machhakhola added to concerns for residents. The landslide that blocked the Budhi Gandaki River is a key factor in the latest incident, according to police. A landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki River between Lokpa and Chumling in Chumnubri Rural Municipality-6, causing the river to swell and put several settlements at risk.

headline: Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico coast
content: The U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC) said Simon was located about 115 miles (185 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, on Saturday (October 10, 2026) morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph) as it moved northward. Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane late on Saturday (October 10, 2026) or early Sunday (October 11, 2026), and some additional strengthening remains possible before landfall, the NHC said. A hurricane warning was in effect for portions of Mexico's Pacific coast south of the beach resort of Puerto Vallarta, including the area around Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port. A tropical storm watch was in effect farther south toward Lazaro Cardenas. The NHC urged residents in the warning area, which also includes the Islas Marias archipelago offshore, to rush preparations to protect life and property. Simon has strengthened incredibly quickly, and thats what makes storms like this so dangerous, said AccuWeather meteorologist Dan Pydynowski. Strong winds could damage homes and businesses, while flooding and mudslides could wash out roads and make it difficult for emergency crews to reach some communities. Even after the storm passes, power outages and damaged infrastructure could make recovery challenging. PREPARATIONS UNDER WAY IN MANZANILLO In the early afternoon on Saturday (October 10, 2026) in Manzanillo, residents appeared largely calm despite the approaching storm, with little sign of panic buying at supermarkets, according to a Reuters reporter on the ground. Some stores had begun boarding up their windows, while businesses were closing and streets were relatively empty. Rain had been falling intermittently since late on Friday (October 9, 2026), and rising seas were pushing waves almost to the entrances of beachfront hotels, although strong winds had yet to arrive. Civil protection workers had closed beaches, erected barriers and raised red and black warning flags, urging residents to stay away from the shore. Marines, soldiers, National Guard officers and emergency personnel were patrolling areas vulnerable to flooding and landslides, while authorities had begun precautionary evacuations in parts of Cihuatlan, a flood-prone municipality in neighboring Jalisco state, near Manzanillo. Rivers in some areas were already running high, raising concerns they could overflow if heavy rains intensified. Mexican authorities warned that heavy rainfall was expected in the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. UP TO 30 INCHES OF RAIN EXPECTED The NHC said Simon was expected to produce 10 to 20 inches (25 to 51 cm) of rain across portions of southwestern Mexico through Sunday (October 11, 2026), with isolated totals of up to 30 inches (76 cm) possible in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. The rainfall could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in mountainous areas. A storm surge is expected along the coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall, accompanied by large and destructive waves, the NHC said. Swells generated by Simon are expected to affect portions of Mexico's southwestern and west-central coast over the coming days, creating dangerous surf and rip current conditions. Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday (October 11, 2026). Last week, Hurricane Polo made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.

headline: Shashi Tharoor invokes Modi's 2015 Emergency remarks to slam 'war-like' Delhi security, says Gen Z deserves better
content: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor hit out at the Narendra Modi-led Union government claiming that Delhi witnessed war-like deployment during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest on Satuday. Tharoor, a parliamentarian, said GenZ deserved better than an 'undeclared' Emergency. Tharoor also tagged Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 2015 post about the Emergency and said, "Thanks for teaching today's youngsters many of the same lessons, Modiji!" In the June 2015 post, PM Modi had said how personally, the Emergency brought back many memories." As youngsters, we learnt a lot during the anti-Emergency movement," he had said. Quick answers to key questions 1What did Shashi Tharoor say about security in Delhi during the CJP protest? Tharoor described Delhis security deployment as war-like and said Gen Z deserved better than what he called an undeclared EmerGenZ. He criticised the checkpoints, barriers, detentions and internet suspension. 2Why did Shashi Tharoor refer to Narendra Modis 2015 Emergency remarks? Tharoor tagged Modis post recalling lessons from the anti-Emergency movement. He used the reference to compare the 197577 Emergencys authoritarian associations with what he viewed as restrictions on young peoples political expression. 3What was the CJP protest in Delhi demanding? The CJP-led protest sought the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. It was linked to concerns raised by critics about the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. 4How did Delhi authorities respond to the planned CJP demonstration? Police denied permission for the proposed Jantar Mantar demonstration, citing security considerations and procedural requirements. Authorities deployed police and paramilitary personnel, set up barriers and detained protesters. 5What did Shashi Tharoor say the government should do instead of using force? Tharoor said the government should provide answers rather than use lathis, and allow expression instead of repression. He argued that answering questions about the elections could help restore public confidence and calm. In another post, Tharoor wrote, As I said this morning, our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared EmerGenZ, The Emergency in India was a 21 month period from 1975 to 1977 when prime minister Indira Gandhi declared a state of emergency across India by citing internal and external threats to the country. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other top leaders of the BJP have often used Emergency to target the Congress party. June 25, 2025, marked the 50th anniversary of the imposition of the 1975 Emergency. The Modi government marks the day as Samvidhan Hatya Diwas to remember the victims and the suspension of constitutional rights during the 21-month Emergency period. By combining 'Emergency' with Gen Z, Tharoor invoked the authoritarian associations of the 197577 Emergency while suggesting that young Indians are confronting restrictions on their political expression today. Delhi Police on Saturday detained more than 4,000 protesters and the leaders Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) as security forces locked down parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India's election chief. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended in the central business district and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a demonstration organised by the CJP-led movement. The protest was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The movement had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, but the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began. In an earlier post, Tharoor said the government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression. Tharoor, who was in Berlin this week, said he returned to the national capital after 2 am and has rarely seen anything like what Delhi is witnessing now. "Checkpoints every few hundred metres, concrete barriers and spike strips laid across our roads, a "war-like" deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the city, 250 trains cancelled and 45 metro stations closed, and reports of young people being detained from their own homes and the streets in and around Delhi - all to prevent citizens from peacefully raising questions about the integrity of our elections," he said on X. "Most regressive (as well as repressive) is the suspension of the internet in the heart of the national capital," the former Union minister said. Freedom of movement stands completely shackled, he added. Jantar Mantar was designated precisely so that citizens could voice dissent in the centre of Delhi, and today even the roads leading to it have been declared out of bounds, the MP from Thiruvananthapuram said. "One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection," Tharoor said. A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress, he said. "The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression," Tharoor asserted. Barricades will do nothing to restore faith in the Election Commission, and the sooner it answers the public's questions, the sooner calm will be restored, he said. "The strength of a democracy is measured by how it treats those who question its working, and by that measure, what we have seen today is utterly shameful and unconscionable," Tharoor said. The Jantar Mantar protest had prompted heightened security measures in the national capital, with police maintaining a strict vigil to prevent any breach of peace. Delhi Police had denied permission to the CJP to hold its proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing security considerations and procedural requirements.

headline: Uncertainties loom over her fate as Christa Pike returns to prison after botched execution attempt: What we know
content: Convicted murderer Christa Pike, the 50-year-old woman who survived a botched execution attempt in Tennessee last week, was discharged from the hospital and returned to prison on Saturday (local time), her lawyers said. Pike was administered two doses of pentobarbital on 30 September after the court approved her execution by lethal injection. However, the doses, usually considered fatal, failed to kill her, making her the only inmate ever to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs, AFP reported, citing the Death Penalty Information Center (DPI). She was convicted in 1995 of carrying out the brutal murder of her classmate, a 19-year-old woman named Colleen Slemmer. Pike, who was then 18, tortured and killed Slemmer, slashing her with a meat cleaver and box cutter for around an hour in a wooded part of the University of Tennessee campus, with help from her boyfriend and a friend. On Saturday, she was transferred back to Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville, where she had been held before her botched execution attempt. In a statement, her lawyers said, "Christa Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years," and added, "She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances." The statement further said that Pike "is continuing to receive medical care at the prison, and we will continue to track her recovery." On Tuesday, her lawyers said she had regained consciousness and was able to speak from her hospital bed. On Wednesday, according to her team, she began "taking limited steps" with help. On Thursday, her attorneys reported further progress, stating that she was walking "with some assistance." As Pike returns to the rehabilitation center in Nashville, her future remains uncertain. Her legal team had challenged the execution IV protocol and requested execution by firing squad. After that request was denied and the subsequent execution attempt was botched, her lawyers renewed their appeal to Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison without parole, which would prevent a second execution attempt. According to CBS News, her attorneys said commutation is the usual course of action after an inmate survives a botched execution. The Eighth Amendment to the US Constitution prohibits cruel and unusual punishments, but whether Tennessee will attempt to execute Pike again remains unclear. On Wednesday, one of her attorneys told the court, "The state has made no promises that Ms. Pike will not be subject to a future execution." For now, Pike continues to receive medical care in prison as her lawyers seek clemency and await clarity on whether the state will pursue another

headline: Two seats and Tamil Nadu's return to a political duopoly
content: As the cliche goes, one week is a long period in politics. And five months, therefore, would technically be very long. The political changes that Tamil Nadu witnessed in the past five months since the assumption of office by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government have been reflected in the byelections to the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies, both reserved for the Scheduled Castes (SCs). Internally, the two Dravidian parties the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) witnessed high drama soon after the TVK emerged as the single largest party in the Assembly election held in April-May. Three days after C. Joseph Vijay became the Chief Minister (on May 10), a group of 25 AIADMK MLAs broke ranks with party general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami and voted in favour of the TVK in the Assembly during the trust motion. By then, most of the allies had deserted the DMK and jumped on to the TVK bandwagon. Four MLAs two from the Congress and one MLA each from the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi and the Indian Union Muslim League were later made Ministers. The States first multi-party Council of Ministers was in place. Meanwhile, the AIADMKs six MLAs, who cross-voted in favour of the TVK in the Assembly in violation of the partys direction, had quit their Assembly seats and joined the ruling party. A number of former Ministers and functionaries of the party followed suit. On expected lines It was against this backdrop that the byelections were held on October 6. When the results were out on October 9, they were along expected lines as byelections in the State have always gone in favour of the ruling party. In that sense, the victory of the TVK in the two constituencies was not surprising. However, while it was definitely among the probabilities, it was nevertheless not considered a certainty for a couple of reasons: first, the TVK did not secure a majority of its own in the April-May Assembly election, though it had a vote share of about 35%. Second, given a high degree of SC representation in the Cabinet, the talk had been doing the rounds in political and bureaucratic circles about the possible consolidation of intermediary castes, accounting for a substantial section of the population in the two constituencies. Factors that were also expected to impact the elections included old caste and political alignments. In Dharapuram, the ruling party came third five months ago, securing around 23% of the votes polled. Besides, the constituency, where the intermediary community of Kongu Vellala Gounders accounts for around 40% and the SCs around 30% of the electors, is the AIADMKs traditional stronghold in the western belt. In a conversation a few weeks ago, a TVK Minister sounded more confident about his partys prospects in Madurantakam than in Dharapuram. Another factor in the mix was that the two TVK candidates had been victors in the Assembly election, as AIADMK candidates. A significant feature of the byelections was that the number of complaints about money distribution was fewer than in the past. Apart from the changes in political alignments, the big change that was noticed in the byelections was the manner Mr. Vijay had campaigned in the two places. In a stark contrast to his propaganda work during the Assembly election, when he made personal appearances only in a handful of areas, he devoted two days each to Madurantakam and Dharapuram, taking along his nominees with him on the campaign vehicle. His campaign tour was packed with drama: he had a cup of tea at a roadside shop; drove a tractor; had a bullock cart ride; and even plucked drumsticks at a farm. Mr. Vijay staked his personal image and aura to overcome widespread dissatisfaction with the partys candidates, particularly in Dharapuram. He literally sweated through intense public outreach and campaigning across these constituencies, while his Ministers and party workers left nothing to chance, says R. Kannan, a former diplomat-turned-writer. Notably, in the course of his campaign, Mr. Vijay did not make any grand announcements or perceptive observations. However, both in Madurantakam and Dharapuram, he sought to project the TVK as the true inheritor of the legacies of AIADMK stalwarts M.G. Ramachandran and Jayalalithaa. He came down heavily on the AIADMK for getting closer to its traditional adversary, the DMK. Shorn of theatrics Comparatively, the campaigns of his political rivals seemed shorn of theatrics. Mr. Vijays key challengers former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin of the DMK and Edappadi K. Palaniswami of the AIADMK stuck to the conventional style of campaign. Both his opponents criticised Mr. Vijay for not being serious in matters of governance. Both attacked him and the TVK for having forced the byelections, which were held only to ensure that their government kept going. Mr. Stalin charged the ruling party with being more interested in purchasing MLAs to protect the government. The AIADMK leaders repeated message to the electors was to teach a befitting lesson to the nominees of the TVK, who had crossed over from his party and were in the fray again. The Naam Tamilar Katchi and the Left were present, but their performance did not make any qualitative difference. For all the intense campaigning by the Chief Minister, the results were not one-sided. In both constituencies, the TVKs vote share did not exceed the 40% mark, despite the ruling party adding many parties to its alliance this time, unlike in April-May when it was on its own. The ruling party must have had its moments of anxiety when AIADMK nominee K. Banumathi was ahead of TVK candidate P. Sathyabama in the initial four rounds of counting in Dharapuram. Subsequently, the latter overtook her and DMK nominee S. Suganya finished as the runner-up. Encouraging for the DMK As far as the DMK is concerned, I would say the result is, in a sense, encouraging, as we faced the electorate virtually single-handedly, barring the support of the Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK). In both places, our vote share is about 30%, which is an achievement, says A. Subburathinam, who was elected in 1991 to the Assembly from Palani on AIADMK ticket and crossed over to the DMK early this year. Despite the reduction in his partys vote share, former AIADMK Minister Pollachi V. Jayaraman does not feel that the partys base has been eroded. He also contends that the TVK does not mean what it says. Referring to the Chief Ministers statement during the campaign on how the previous governments did not follow up properly with Keralam regarding the Anamalaiyar-Nallar scheme, a project to provide water to the western belt, the AIADMKs functionary points to reports that suddenly surfaced in the media about a group of Ministers who would go to Thiruvananthapuram on the eve of polling day to discuss the scheme. Eventually, the visit did not materialise. Another former Minister of the AIADMK, R.B. Udhayakumar, is quick to restate that traditionally in Tamil Nadu, byelections have been favourable to the ruling party. You have to view the outcome only that way. I do not think this will have serious implications for our party, he says. It remains to be seen how the rebels in the party, including former Ministers S.P. Velumani and C.Ve. Shanmugam, make their next move, as they have not been able to corner Mr. Palaniswami within the organisation. More dissidents There is a perception that the outcome may encourage the TVK to attract more dissidents from the AIADMK to its fold. What would cranes do in a dry pond? asks S. Semmalai, Health and Education Minister in Jayalalithaas Cabinet during 2001-04, who joined the TVK at Dharapuram on September 30, 2026. We do not have to do anything, as the AIADMKs volunteers would have seen the writing on the wall when their party finished third at both the places, he explains. Despite the TVK government being seen as one that is being propped up by diverse social groups, including the SCs, Mr. Vijay did not refer in his speeches in a significant way to his governments work and plans for the welfare of the community. After all, it is his government that has eight Ministers from the SCs. On the other hand, in the run-up to the byelections, the Chief Ministers visit to the Vanjiamman temple near Dharapuram, a place of worship dear to the Gounders, and Public Works Minister Aadhav Arjunas reported statement about his party having 17 legislators from another intermediary community, the Vanniyars, did not go unnoticed. A seasoned leader of the SCs from northern districts says, It looks that the TVK, just like the DMK while in power, is of the view that there is no necessity to woo the community in a deliberate manner, as the votes of the SCs will go to it even otherwise. However, Mr. Semmalai, who hails from Salem and belongs to the Vanniyar community, says, In the reserved constituencies, only the SCs can contest. But electors are from all communities. Besides, Mr. Vijay respects all communities, apart from representing all of them. In a nutshell, the results, though favourable to the TVK, have not provided any overwhelming support to the ruling party and the nature of the verdict should keep Mr. Vijay and his colleagues on toes. As Dr. Kannan says, it is still too early to declare the State is shifting back to a bipolar political landscape, though current trends point to that possibility.

STATEMENT OF SOLIDARITY WITH THE YOUTH OF INDIADhaka, Bangladesh | 10 October 2026 To the youth and democratic forces of India, We stand in firm solidarity with the young people of India demanding electoral accountability and defending their democratic rights. Recent detentions of peaceful protesters, organizers, and journalists in New Delhi, alongside internet suspensions and restrictions at Jantar Mantar, directly threaten fundamental freedoms. Concerns regarding electoral integrity and institutional independence require transparent answers, not barricades and censorship. This struggle is not yours alone. From Dhaka, we stand with you as friends bound by a common demand for accountable power, democratic institutions, and human dignity. We know this struggle intimately, because we have lived it. In July 2024, our student led movement against recruitment quotas transformed into a nationwide uprising against 15 years of authoritarian rule. The state responded with live ammunition. The United Nations later estimated that as many as 1,400 people were killed during the uprising and its suppression. We deeply remember and honor the solidarity shown by Indian students, writers, and independent voices during our uprising. We recognize Indias rich traditions of democratic resistance. The women of Shaheen Bagh defended equal citizenship through a Delhi winter, while generations of students at JNU and Jadavpur University have sustained organised dissent. These remain invaluable democratic inheritances. Today, we once again see the courage of young Indian women on the streets. In Bangladesh, women were also at the forefront of the July Revolution; their courage and sacrifices helped secure our victory. Hindutva majoritarianism, fascism, and every form of religious supremacy must not define the future of South Asia. We reject authoritarianism, communal hatred, and political intolerance in India just as we reject them in Bangladesh. Our shared future must rest on communal harmony and social justice, irrespective of religion, caste, gender, or class. No society is truly democratic while minorities live in fear, dissent is criminalized, and citizenship is conditional on identity. We call upon Indian authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly, disclose the whereabouts and legal grounds for detaining protest organizers, immediately release those held for exercising their rights, and ensure journalists can report without intimidation or equipment seizure. Today, many young leaders have been unjustly detained. Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid continue to be kept behind bars for years without trial. We regard all of Indias young protesters and prisoners of conscience as comrades. Their courage inspires young people across South Asia. Our struggles are interconnected, extending to unresolved issues of border killings, water sharing, environmental protection, and national sovereignty. We seek a South Asia where nations treat each other as equals, governments remain accountable, and sovereignty is never an excuse for domination. Our struggles are interconnected, extending to unresolved issues of border killings, water sharing, environmental protection, and national sovereignty. We seek a South Asia where nations treat each other as equals, governments remain accountable, and sovereignty is never an excuse for domination". To the democratic people of India: from Dhaka, and from the unfinished democratic aspirations of our July generation, we stand with you. Stand firm, protect one another, reject communal hatred, and refuse to surrender the future of South Asia to fascism and division", he added. headline: 'Time For Ukraine To Get New President': Trump Lashes Out At Zelenskyy For Strikes At Russian Oil Refineries
content: Trump urges Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and calls for new leadership in Ukraine amid a controversial diesel deal with Moscow. US President Donald Trump has called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacks on Russian oil refineries and suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader capable of reaching a deal. His remarks have added to tensions between Washington and Kyiv as the US moves forward with an arrangement allowing Russia to supply diesel to global markets. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Saturday, Trump issued a blunt warning over Ukraines strikes on Russian energy facilities. - Trump Strikes Oil Deal With Putin, Zelenskyy Calls US Move Weak, Unworthy - Donald Trump Strikes Diesel Deal With Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky Blasts Move | News18 - False Information: Russia Rejects Reports Of Second Plague Case After Lab Workers Death - 33 Killed In Russian Strike On Ukraine Buses; Lithuania Moves Troops Near Russias Kaliningrad He better damn well stop," Trump said, referring to the attacks on Russian oil refineries. He also questioned Zelenskyys leadership, saying, I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal." The comments followed Trumps announcement of a diesel supply arrangement involving Russia, a move that has drawn criticism from Kyiv. Zelenskyy has warned that easing restrictions on Russian diesel exports could provide Moscow with additional funds to continue its war against Ukraine. According to an Axios report citing a US official familiar with the matter, Trump decided to proceed with the arrangement after Zelenskyy did not comply with six US requests to halt attacks on Russian refineries. The development has exposed differences between the two governments over how to end the war. While Washington is seeking to reduce pressure on fuel prices, Kyiv argues that easing restrictions on Russian energy exports would strengthen Moscows ability to continue its military campaign. Trump Says Refinery Strikes Are Affecting US Consumers The US administrations push to stop Ukrainian attacks is partly linked to concerns over rising fuel prices in America, the official told Axios. According to the report, Trump wanted Kyiv to stop targeting Russian refineries without making the decision conditional on Moscow agreeing to halt attacks on Ukrainian power plants. During discussions with Trump and his envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Zelenskyy had offered to suspend the refinery strikes if Russia stopped targeting Ukraines electricity infrastructure. However, the US president wanted Ukraine to halt the attacks regardless of whether Moscow made a similar commitment, the official said. The administration believes that strikes on Russian energy facilities are adding to the financial pressure on American consumers. The attacks on the refineries cause pain in Russia, but it causes pain for the US, too," the official said. The official also indicated that Trump did not view Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries as equivalent to Russian strikes on Ukraines electricity infrastructure. Ukrainian attacks have disrupted Russias energy sector in recent months. Moscow subsequently banned diesel exports, tightening global supplies at a time when the war in Iran had already put pressure on energy markets. US Envoys Hold Eight-Hour Talks With Ukrainian Officials The dispute was also a key issue during talks between US and Ukrainian representatives in Miami on Friday. Witkoff and Kushner held eight hours of discussions with Ukrainian negotiators as diplomatic efforts to end the war continued. During the meeting, the US envoys informed the Ukrainian side that Trump was expected to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin and move ahead with easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. They also explained that the decision followed repeated US requests for Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries, according to the official cited by Axios. A Ukrainian official alleged that Witkoff and Kushner warned that continued defiance could lead Trump to suspend US intelligence support for Ukraine. However, the US official rejected that account. According to the official, the envoys instead highlighted the importance of Washingtons support, including weapons and intelligence, and urged Kyiv to avoid actions that could increase costs for American consumers. The disagreement presents another challenge for the Trump administrations efforts to negotiate an end to the war. Washington wants Ukraine to stop the refinery strikes, while Kyiv maintains that Russia should not receive financial benefits from the relaxation of sanctions. Zelenskyy Calls Diesel Deal A Gift To Putin Zelenskyy has strongly criticised the US decision, arguing that allowing Russian diesel exports would give Moscow more resources to sustain its military campaign. The Ukrainian president described the arrangement as a gift" to Putin, warning that easing sanctions would allow Russia to continue fighting for longer and result in more deaths. He also accused Moscow of responding to the easing of restrictions with further attacks on Ukrainian civilians. Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskyy said in a social media post on Saturday. Ukrainian officials said Russian strikes in the countrys south-east early on Saturday killed 15 people, including three children. The reported casualties came hours after Zelenskyy warned that reducing pressure on Moscow could encourage further military action. Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed," he said. Meanwhile, large-scale power outages were reported in Kyiv, according to Ukraines largest private energy provider. The latest exchange of remarks has further widened the gap between Washington and Kyiv over the path towards peace. Trump has defended the diesel arrangement amid concerns about fuel prices, while Zelenskyy argues that easing restrictions on Russian exports would provide Moscow with the resources to prolong its invasion. US President Donald Trump criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and suggested a new leader was needed because Ukraine continued targeting Russian oil refineries despite US demands to halt the strikes. According to reports, Trump proceeded with a diesel supply arrangement involving Russia after Zelenskyy failed to comply with six requests to stop the refinery attacks.

headline: Riyadh airport attack: At least 12 killed, over 300 injured, Trump says strikes 'not acceptable' | Top Updates
content: backed Houthis launched their third attack of the week against Saudi Arabia, killing 12 people and leaving more than 300 wounded, US President Donald Trump on Saturday (local time) condemned the attack, saying it was "not acceptable." He made these remarks while addressing reporters and said he "will be speaking" with the kingdom's leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, following the attack blamed on Yemen's Houthis. He added, "What happened in Saudi Arabia is not acceptable." Quick answers to key questions 1How many people were killed and injured in the Riyadh airport attack? At least 12 people were killed and 309 injured, according to the reported latest count. The victims included people of several nationalities. 2Who was blamed for the attack on Riyadh airport? The Saudi-led coalition blamed pro-Iranian Houthi fighters in Yemen. A related report said there was no immediate Houthi claim of responsibility for the latest incident. 3Why were flights to Riyadh diverted or cancelled? Saudi Arabias civil aviation authority temporarily suspended operations at King Khalid International Airport after the attack. Flights bound for Riyadh were diverted or cancelled. 4Will the United States join Saudi strikes against the Houthis? President Donald Trump said the United States might join the strikes and that Washington would consider the decision. No immediate announcement of additional US military support was reported. 5Should passengers travel to Riyadh airport after the attack? US, Canadian, German and other diplomatic missions urged their citizens to avoid the airport or warned against travelling there. Passengers were advised to check their flight status with their airline. The attack on Riyadh comes amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, including the war between the US and Iran and Israeli attacks in Lebanon aimed at disarming the Tehran-backed Hezbollah. 1. When asked whether Washington planned to support Saudi Arabia by joining strikes against the Houthis, Trump said, "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly." Additionally, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks against Riyadh and said they demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. 2. On Saturday (local time), the Houthis launched their third attack of the week on Riyadh's international airport, leaving at least 12 people dead. The attack came as the Iran-backed group escalated the campaign it launched earlier this year against the kingdom. Among those killed were four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh, and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. According to the latest count, 309 people were injured, Reuters reported. 3. The attack on Riyadh airport is being called the deadliest in the kingdom in over a decade. It occurred without warning, and the country's threat warning system issued no alert. The two previous attacks this week on King Khalid International Airport killed four people and caused severe damage to one of the kingdom's commercial planes parked on the tarmac. 4. All flights bound for Riyadh were diverted or cancelled on Saturday, according to Flightradar24, which at one point showed only a helicopter hovering above the airport. Saudi Arabias civil aviation authority said operations at the airport, which serves a city of around eight million people, had been temporarily suspended. 5. The Saudi-led military coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government blamed pro-Iranian Houthi fighters in Yemen for carrying out the deadly attack at Riyadh airport, adding that the kingdom would respond "decisively," AFP reported. In a statement, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the attack a "war crime" and pledged that the coalition "will respond decisively to this terrorist attack". 6. The Saudi-led international coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen said it intercepted a missile on Sunday southeast of Riyadh, in the area where Prince Sultan Airbase is situated. A statement issued hours after the attack on Riyadh airport said, "Interception and destruction of a ballistic missile in Al-Kharj, launched by the Houthi terrorist militia." 7. Following the attack, the head of the Houthi media office wrote on X that the group had "shut down Riyadh international airport". The Houthis also warned airlines against entering Saudi airspace, designating it a military operations zone after Yemens Saudi-backed government began an offensive against them on Monday.

headline: 2010-batch IAS officer appointed Deputy Election Commissioner
content: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet on Saturday appointed 2010 batch IAS officer Prakash Rajpurohit as Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India, filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of then-DEC in-charge of electoral roll and IT division Sanjay Kumar to his parent cadre in August. Rajpurohits appointment was one among 27 Joint Secretary or Joint Secretary equivalent appointments approved by the ACC, as per the order by the Department of Personnel and Training. The Rajasthan cadre officer has been serving as Joint Secretary in the Department of Defence Production under the Ministry of Defence since May this year. As per the order, he has been appointed till April 2030. Kumar had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, when he was prematurely repatriated to his parent cadre and posted in the Delhi government. He had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECIs June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country. According to ACC order, Vivek Khare, a 1996 batch Indian Telecom Service officer, will be the Joint Secretary, National Testing Agency (NTA), and Varnali Deka, a 2009 batch IAS officer of Assam-Meghalaya cadre, will be the Joint Secretary, National Health Authority.

headline: Cheating The Needle: US Death Row Inmate Christa Pike Out Of Hospital, Back In Prison After Bungled Execution
content: Pike is believed to be the first inmate in modern American legal history to survive after the full administrative infusion of lethal execution chemicals Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from the hospital and returned to prison custody following an unprecedented botched lethal injection procedure. Pike, who was scheduled for execution on September 30, survived after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital, forcing correctional officials to halt the procedure and rush her to an off-site medical facility for emergency stabilisation. Her defence attorneys confirmed her transfer back to the Debra K Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville, noting that while she remains under ongoing prison medical observation, her condition has stabilised sufficiently for prison housing. - Angry And Confused: Tennessee Death-Row Inmate Christa Pike Wakes Up After Failed Execution Attempt - Botched Execution: Prison Chief Resigns After US Death Row Inmate Christa Pike Survives 2 Lethal Injections - US To Livestream Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasans Execution By Firing Squad, First Since 1945 - 'Every Woman Should Feel Safe, Even At 10 PM': Supreme Court's Tough Talk On Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR Medical Complications and Evidence Preservation Orders Legal filings presented during emergency hearings in Davidson County Court revealed that Pike suffered severe post-procedure complications following the failed execution. Her legal team disclosed that she developed severe respiratory issues, including pneumonia, alongside motor impairment affecting her upper extremities. Presiding judges granted immediate defence motions ordering the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve all physical evidence, medical logs, chemical samples, and internal communications linked to the botched execution. The directive ensures independent forensic experts can analyse the purity, dosage, and administration protocols of the pentobarbital used during the execution attempt. Legal Framework and Clemency Requests Pike, 50, remains the only woman on Tennessees death row, sentenced for the 1995 murder of classmate Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville. Her survival marks an extraordinary anomaly in modern capital punishment, as she is believed to be the first inmate in modern American legal history to survive after the full administrative infusion of lethal execution chemicals. Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike was discharged from the hospital and returned to prison custody. Pike survived after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital during a botched lethal injection procedure. Pike suffered severe respiratory issues, including pneumonia, and motor impairment affecting her upper extremities. Presiding judges granted motions ordering the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve all evidence related to the botched execution. Pike, 50, remains the only woman on Tennessees death row. In light of the execution failure, her defence attorneys submitted renewed clemency petitions to Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, urging the administration to commute her sentence to life imprisonment without parole. Defence counsel argued that subjecting Pike to a secondary execution attempt after surviving lethal chemical administration constitutes cruel and unusual punishment under constitutional guarantees. Administrative Pauses and Policy Re-evaluations The failed procedure has triggered immediate fallout across state correctional policy, with state authorities temporarily halting all scheduled capital executions to allow for an internal administrative review. State legal representatives have avoided making definitive commitments regarding whether Tennessee will seek a new execution date once investigations conclude. As state authorities conduct technical reviews into protocol failures, civil rights groups and legal analysts continue to scrutinise protocol oversight, highlighting systemic risks inherent in chemical execution procedures. During the September 30 execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution, officials struggled with intravenous lines, spending over an hour and using at least seven needles. The pentobarbital entered surrounding tissue instead of the bloodstream, prompting a second dose before the procedure was halted and Pike was rushed to the hospital.

headline: Gunman shoots dead 7 relatives, family friend in Pennsylvania
content: A 45-year-old man shot and killed seven relatives and a family friend at a home in Pennsylvania, U.S., before apparently taking his own life, authorities said on Saturday (October 10, 2026). The victims in the city of Erie included two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant. Police responded on Friday evening to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told reporters. Video evidence showed the pair arriving at the residence appearing distressed, then attempting to contact neighbours and enter the house, Mr. Lorah said. The gunman exited the house, shot them, and returned inside, he said. The man barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit. He was later found inside with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah said. The shooter and seven of his victims were related, Mr. Lorah said. The eighth victim was a family friend. Dead inside the home were a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. The others were men and women ranging in age from 19 to 51. One of the women was eight months pregnant. Local news outlet Erie News Now said responding officers were being offered counselling over the horrifying incident. Many people across our community are hurting today: the neighbours who witnessed what happened, the families and friends of those who were killed, the officers and first responders who answered these calls, and others struggling to make sense of something so terrible, Erie Mayor Daria Devlin told reporters on Saturday. We cannot undo what happened last night, and we cannot take away the grief that these families are carrying, but we can make sure that they dont have to carry it alone, she said. Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber people and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.

headline: Anthropic's Claude AI submits false tip on Philadelphia unsolved homicide case
content: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website in the U.S. about an unsolved homicide case, authorities and Anthropic said. It's the latest example of AI models acting in unintended ways and manipulating government and other websites during tests. In a report on Friday, Anthropic also disclosed a separate incident in which its AI model submitted forms to an undisclosed government website instead of stopping before submission. The incident in Philadelphia occurred on July 18 when the AI model Claude Haiku 4.5 was tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said. Claude filled out a form on the police site PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, indicating it might have information regarding an unsolved murder listed on the site. Philadelphia Police said in a statement they were unaware of the incident until Anthropic notified them on Wednesday. Then they found the submission in the websites tip records and confirmed it was marked spam and never forwarded to police. There are rising concerns about AI companies unchecked AI agents meddling with everything from U.S. government websites to healthcare data. Critics have been calling for more regulation. In September, another AI company, OpenAI, disclosed six reports of unexpected or concerning behaviour in artificial-intelligence models. Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the Philadelphia Police Department said in a statement. Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement. Anthropic said in its report that most of the reported behaviors are forms of what it calls persistence" in which Claude, when it cannot complete a task as given, works around a restriction instead of stopping. The company said it was modifying its training to reduce the likelihood of further misbehavior. Anthropic said it briefed the White House on cases that involved U.S. government agencies at the federal, state and local levels, and notified each agency involved.

headline: Missile strikes passenger terminal at Riyadh airport; 12 killed, over 300 wounded
content: An attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabias capital killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday (October 11, 2026), with some in critical condition. The attack was the deadliest in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi-backed government forces there. The statement, which did not assign blame for the attack, said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals. The attack the latest of several in the past week on King Khalid International Airport is expected to increase Saudi pressure on allies including the United States to provide military support for the kingdom. Shortly after the attack on Saturday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he was evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis. The Houthis claimed attacks earlier in the week on King Khalid International Airport that killed three Saudis, including a pilot. On Saturday, a missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they werent authorized to speak to the media. We may. Were going to look at it, Trump said of intervening. We just found out about the recent attack. So well make a decision. We move very quickly. The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis. There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital. Riyadh airport operations suspended Saudi civil aviation authorities earlier said airport operations were suspended and the extent of injuries and damage was being assessed. An official notice to aviators said the suspension was through midnight. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed. Flights diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport. The attacks on Saudi Arabia, the worlds top oil exporter, have rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry hours after the latest one was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday. Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships. Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign sharply limited that. Saudi Arabia has run low on interceptors, officials say Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told the AP last month, with one noting that the U.S. has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran. Officials have said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive against the Houthis. On Saturday, Saudi Arabia said its foreign minister and Omani counterpart spoke by phone about the importance of supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions in the region. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region. Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability.

headline: Rampage In Riyadh: Deadly Houthi Attack At Saudi Airport Kills 12 People, Leaves 300 Injured
content: The strike triggered massive blasts across the domestic terminal area, sending thick plumes of black smoke over the capital A major strike targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has left 12 people dead and over 300 injured, marking one of the most severe aerial escalations directed at Saudi aviation infrastructure in recent years. The strike triggered massive blasts across the domestic terminal area, sending thick plumes of black smoke over the capital and causing severe structural damage near passenger boarding gates. Emergency medical services were deployed en masse to transport victims to regional medical facilities. Civil aviation authorities confirmed that flight operations at the kingdoms busiest transit hub were immediately suspended while security forces secured the perimeter and cleared falling debris. - Riyadh Airport Targeted By Houthi Missile: Air India Express, Akasa Air Cancel Flights - Loud Explosions Heard In Riyadh, Houthis Claim They Fired Missile At Airport - Saudi Says Airport Attacks In Riyadh, Abha Kill 3, Injure 36 After Houthis Claim Strikes - Stay Indoors: Indian Embassy Issues Advisory For Nationals In Saudi Arabia As Houthis Escalate Attacks Sudden Terminal Explosion and Chaos Witnesses inside the terminal described scenes of utter panic as projectile impacts shattered glass panels and caused structural collapses across departure areas. Passengers waiting at adjacent gates reported hearing massive detonations followed by shockwaves that sent shrapnel flying through crowded seating zones. Shattered glass and flying metal accounted for a majority of the casualties, with doctors treating numerous passengers and airport staff for deep lacerations and trauma. Security teams quickly evacuated thousands of travellers to lower-level concourses and surrounding parking structures to mitigate further risk. Regional Escalation and Claims of Responsibility The attack follows a series of cross-border long-range missile and drone strikes targeting key infrastructure across the region. Representatives from Yemens Houthi movement claimed responsibility for launching heavy barrage attacks, framing the offensive as retaliation for ongoing military operations along strategic coastal corridors. A strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh left 12 people dead and over 300 injured. The strike caused massive blasts across the domestic terminal area and severe structural damage. Emergency medical services transported victims to regional medical facilities. Flight operations at the airport were immediately suspended. Yemens Houthi movement claimed responsibility for launching heavy barrage attacks. The assault comes amid heightened geopolitical volatility and intense fighting over vital maritime transit routes, including the Bab al-Mandab strait. Defence analysts note that the deployment of heavy ballistic capabilities against civilian transit hubs represents a sharp escalation in regional warfare tactics. International Reaction and Emergency Response In the immediate aftermath, regional allies and global powers strongly condemned the targeting of international civilian infrastructure. International leaders expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, with discussions quickly turning towards potential defence evaluations and retaliation frameworks to safeguard regional airspace. Saudi security forces have heightened alert levels across all major airports, energy installations, and urban centres. Engineering and bomb disposal teams continue inspecting the facility grounds to evaluate structural safety and clear unexploded ordnance before permitting any partial resumption of air traffic. The missile and drone strike targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh left 12 people dead and over 300 injured, while causing massive structural damage near the domestic terminal's passenger boarding gates and departure areas.
