Rai also urged authorities to prevent a repeat of the incident and protect the independence and safety of lawyers. At the same time, I strongly urge the concerned authorities to ensure that no such incident occurs in the future and that the dignity, safety and professional independence of members of the Bar are always respected. Lawyers must be able to discharge their professional duties without fear or intimidation." Lawyers Detained Amid CJP Protest The incident took place as Delhi witnessed extensive security measures ahead of the CJPs proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The party has been demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Delhi Police had denied permission for the gathering, citing security and law-and-order concerns. The reported detention of lawyers added another layer to the wider security operation, which also saw CJP leaders and other protesters detained at different locations in Delhi. The SCBA has called for the circumstances surrounding the lawyers detention and reported use of force to be examined in accordance with law. Several Supreme Court advocates were detained amid heightened security arrangements ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Rights group says paramilitary drone strike in Sudan killed 41 near Ethiopian border
content: A drone strike blamed on Sudans notorious paramilitaries hit a gathering of displaced people on the border with Ethiopia and killed 41, a rights group said. Fridays strike by the Rapid Support Forces took place in the Abu Shandi area in Sudans Blue Nile province, according to Emergency Lawyers, which tracks the war in the northeastern African nation. Among the dead were eight children and many women, the group said. A spokesperson for the RSF didnt respond to a request for comment. The U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said it was appalled by the reported strike that also wounded dozens. Condemning these senseless killings is essential, but there must also be accountability for this flagrant disregard for international humanitarian law, said Denise Brown, the U.N. resident and humanitarian coordinator in Sudan in a statement. As each day goes by in this war, the world continues to accept the suffering of the people of Sudan. Sudans war started in April 2023 when tensions between the military and the RSF exploded into open fighting in the capital, Khartoum, and spread across the country. The conflict has killed at least 150,000 people, according to conflict monitor ACLED, though aid groups say the real number is likely higher. It has forced more than 12.4 million to flee their homes, according to UN figures, creating what aid groups call the worlds largest humanitarian crisis. Across Sudan, 33.7 million people, including 17.3 million children, urgently need aid this year, and an estimated 825,000 children face severe acute malnutrition.

headline: Saudi airport attacked again: Missile strike reported, many wounded; passengers evacuated, flights diverted
content: Saudi Arabias King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was attacked again on Saturday (October 10)prompting an evacuation and widespread flight disruptions, as the kingdom faces an escalating campaign of strikes linked to Yemens Iran-aligned Houthi rebels. A missile struck a passenger terminal and several people were wounded, one of two regional officials told The Associated Press. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly. The airport had already been targeted earlier in the week. Quick answers to key questions 1What happened at Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport on October 10? A missile reportedly struck a passenger terminal, and several people were wounded. The airport was evacuated, and flights bound for Riyadh were diverted. 2Did the Houthis claim responsibility for the October 10 Riyadh airport attack? No. At the time of reporting, the Houthis had not officially claimed responsibility for the latest attack, although earlier attacks during the week had been claimed by the group. 3Why has King Khalid International Airport been targeted repeatedly? The attacks come amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis. Saudi Arabias military-backed campaign against the Houthis in neighbouring Yemen has intensified during the same period. 4What should passengers do if they are due to fly from Riyadh airport? Passengers were advised to check their flight status with their airline before travelling to the airport. Several embassies also urged their citizens to avoid the airport and surrounding areas. 5Were flights to Riyadh diverted after the airport attack? Yes. Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 reported that flights heading to Riyadh were diverted to other airports, and the airport asked passengers to confirm their flight status with airlines. There was no immediate statement from the Houthis claiming responsibility for Saturdays incident. The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed it was aware of attacks on the airport and urged American citizens to stay away from the facility and surrounding areas. The U.S. Mission is aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10 and strongly recommends all U.S. citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas, the embassy said in a statement posted online. The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies also warned their citizens against travelling to the airport. Spains embassy described the incident as a new attack by Yemens Iran-backed Houthis in a message on X. A diplomatic source separately told AFP that a missile had struck the airport at around 1200 GMT. Canadas embassy cited ongoing military activity affecting the airport, while Germanys mission referred to the prevailing situation without providing further details. Frances embassy had urged its citizens on Friday to exercise utmost care in Saudi Arabia following Houthi strikes in recent days. It also warned French nationals against recording images of affected areas or sharing them online. Saudi Arabias government-run Centre for International Communication, which oversees foreign media in the kingdom, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reported attack triggered major disruptions to air travel, with flights heading to Riyadh diverted to other airports, according to flight-tracking service Flightradar24. The airport also issued an alert asking passengers to check their flight status with airlines before leaving for the facility. The latest incident comes amid an escalation in attacks attributed to the Houthis, who have opened a new front in the wider Middle East conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran. King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times over the past week, following the launch of a major military offensive by a Saudi-led coalition against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen. The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks, including one on Wednesday that killed a Sudanese national. Saudi Arabia backs Yemens internationally recognised government and has provided military support in its fight against the Houthis. Fighting between Houthi forces and Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops has intensified, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support to help government forces reverse recent rebel gains along the Red Sea. The Houthis advances have also increased their ability to monitor shipping along the Red Sea corridor, an important alternative route for maritime traffic amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships. However, responsibility for the latest attack had not been officially confirmed by the Houthis at the time of reporting.

headline: 'Can Rural India Afford It?': Experts Question Elon Musk's 'Oligarch' Charge Amid Starlink Row
content: Addressing the claim that Starlink could bring connectivity to underserved regions, experts argued that India already had extensive telecom and internet coverage. After tech mohul Elon Musk claimed Starlinks India entry was being stalled by oligarchs", CNN-News18s Editorial Affairs Director Rahul Shivshankar questioned his assurances about the potential of the satellite internet service to connect remote communities in India. Rahul Shivshankar raised concerns over affordability and the billionaires allegations that Indian oligarchs were allegedly stalling the satellite internet services entry into the country. - Baseless, Misconceived: Govt Refutes Elon Musks Oligarch Claim Over Starlinks India Hurdles - In Elon Musk's Own Words: Why Starlink Could Be A Security Risk For Any Country - Definitely Not Elon Musk: Indian User Questions Billionaires Writing Style In Viral Starlink Post; Internet Reacts - Starlink And India: Inside The Security Concerns Shaping Policy | Elon Musk | Jyotiraditya Scindia During a panel discussion on Saturday, Shivshankar challenged Musks claim that powerful Indian business groups were blocking Starlinks entry, pointing to the companys reported costs and the existing telecom network in India. During the discussion, Rahul Shivshankar was joined by Anand Narasimhan, Managing Editor, Special Projects, and Senior Anchor at CNN-News18; Shawan Sen, Executive Editor at CNN-News18; Senior Anchor Shivani Gupta; and Nalin Mehta, Managing Editor of Moneycontrol, among others. Now tell me, Shivani, people in the back of beyond, in rural India, can pay Rs. 8,600 monthly plus towards internet usage and consumption, plus Rs. 24,500 for hardware? Im asking this question legitimately," Shivshankar said, referring to Starlinks reported Indian pricing in December 2025. He also questioned Musks criticism of the Indian establishment, citing a Washington Post investigation that reportedly found Musks businesses had received at least $38 billion in US government contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits over the years. Rahul Shivshankar questioned Elon Musk's assurances about Starlink's potential to connect remote Indian communities. Shivshankar raised concerns over Starlink's affordability, citing reported Indian pricing of Rs. 8,600 monthly plus Rs. 24,500 for hardware. He cited a Washington Post investigation reporting Musk's businesses received at least $38 billion in US government contracts, loans, subsidies, and tax credits. Shivshankar argued India already has extensive telecom and internet coverage, including in remote areas. Shawan Sen pointed to Starlink's role in Ukraine to highlight the strategic importance of satellite communication control during conflicts. Have we forgotten how close he was and continues to be with Donald Trump?" Shivshankar asked, questioning Musks comments about the relationship between commercial enterprises and the government. Addressing the claim that Starlink could bring connectivity to underserved regions, Shivshankar argued that India already had extensive telecom and internet coverage, including in remote areas. He also maintained that the government was evaluating three companies for satellite-based connectivity: Starlink, the Ambani Group and Airtel. The discussion followed Musks allegations that Indian oligarchs were preventing Starlink from entering the market. Shivshankar described these as unverified allegations and argued that questions surrounding security, affordability and the approval process needed to be examined alongside Musks claims. His remarks placed the spotlight on whether Starlinks proposed services would be financially accessible to rural households, even if the company secures permission to operate in India. Starlink Took Pre-Orders Before Authorisation In India Further, Nalin Mehta rejected the claim of an oligarchic takeover", saying all three satellite internet players are at the same stage in the regulatory process. Mehta said the process was not about singling out one company and argued that Starlink was not the only player awaiting regulatory clearances. He (Elon Musk) is a commercial actor, who is looking out for commercial interest over here, right? By the way, PM Narendra Modi had met him at the White House when he met TrumpBy the way, (Musk) hes not the only person waiting for a licence," he said. So if you look at it, everybody is at the same stage in the regulatory processStarlink actually began taking pre-orders in India before beginning the required authorisation In India," he added. According to Mehta, the key issue that remains is security clearance, which is required before the licensing process can be completed. Why Starlinks Role In Wars Has Raised Questions Meanwhile, Shawan Sen pointed to Starlinks role in Ukraine to explain why control over satellite communication can become strategically important during conflicts. Its almost like a private company serving customers and providing them the timeline. It would be like, If you want a connection, youll get the fastest internet. That is what hes trying to tell you." Sen said he was in Ukraine in 2022 and had spoken to officials from the countrys Ministry of Defence. He referred to an episode in which Starlink connectivity became a subject of controversy. He said Musks position was that the service had not been switched off, but that an extension had not been provided. According to Sen, the episode showed the importance of understanding who ultimately controls critical satellite infrastructure. Starlink's reported placeholder pricing for India included a monthly cost of Rs. 8,600 or more for internet usage, alongside an upfront charge of Rs. 24,500 for hardware equipment.

headline: India-U.S. trade pact to be finalised keeping changed circumstances in mind: Piyush Goyal
content: The U.S. and India announced in February that they had reached a framework for an interim trade agreement, but circumstances have changed, and the pact will be finalised accordingly, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Saturday (October 10, 2026). He also said trade pact negotiations are on with number of regions including Israel, Chile, GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) and Russia-led group Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). "USA (trade pact) February me announce hua. Thodi paristhitiyan badli hain, usko abhi madde nazar rakhte hue final hoga. (It was announced in February. Some circumstances have changed; the final decision will be made keeping that in mind)," Mr. Goyal said in New Delhi while addressing members of industry chamber PHDCCI. India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods than its competitors in the American markets. The Minister did not elaborate about those circumstances, but the changing tariff landscape in the U.S. has led to further negotiations about the first phase of bilateral trade agreement (BTA) between India and the U.S. Mr. Goyal earlier this month met U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on the sidelines of G20 trade Ministers meeting in Milwaukee. Both discussed trade pact-related issues. Further, the Minister said that negotiations for a trade pact with Canada are moving at a faster pace and talks for an agreement with South Africa-led SACU group will start soon. Several countries are keen to negotiate trade agreements with India, he said adding talks with Mexico will be launched next week. Mr. Goyal informed that the trade Ministers of the U.K. and Canada will be visiting India next week. India and the U.K. implemented a trade agreement in July. The U.K. Minister will be here for the India-U.K. Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) meeting. Piyush Goyal criticises Opposition The Union Minister slams Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his claims and statements after meeting President Droupadi Murmu. "It was an objectionable behaviour ... He has insulted the President ... This is a sense of anarchy," Mr. Goyal said, adding that the Opposition leaders have misbehaved with security personnel. A delegation of INDIA bloc leaders met President Murmu on Friday evening (October 9, 2026) and handed her a memorandum on the alleged "vote chori". After the meeting, Mr. Gandhi said he was shocked and stunned that the President did not deny the "election theft" charge and "accepted" what the Opposition leaders stated.

headline: Earthquake Today: 4.2-magnitude quake hits Uttarkashi, second tremor above 4 in Uttarakhand in four days
content: A 4.2-magnitude earthquake struck Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district on Saturday evening, triggering panic among residents in Uttarkashi town and the Yamunotri valley. The National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said the earthquake occurred at 8.07 pm, with its epicentre located 2 km northwest of Uttarkashi. The tremor originated at a depth of 11 km. Residents felt strong shaking, with some rushing out of their homes as the tremors struck. Purushottam Uniyal, a priest from Kharsali village, the winter seat of Yamunotri, said the shaking was intense enough to make televisions inside houses tremble. The sudden tremors alarmed residents, prompting them to step outside as a precaution, he said. Saturday's earthquake was the second tremor measuring above magnitude 4 to hit Uttarakhand in four days. A 4.9-magnitude earthquake struck Chamoli district on October 6, raising concerns among residents in the hill state. Officials from the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) said no damage had been reported following Saturday's earthquake as of the latest update. headline: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin
content: Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraines Zaporizhzhia region, officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026), a day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscows war in Ukraine. Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraines State Emergency Service said Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded. Missiles also struck Kyiv in a daytime attack on Saturday (October 10, 2026). Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said four people were wounded. Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war, while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4.5 years since Moscows full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days. The latest attacks came a day after Mr. Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a sharp reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine, and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. Mr. Trump said on social media on Friday (October 9, 2026) that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he had been expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Mr. Trump announced that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November 2026, and 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter. Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes within a short period of time after that, he wrote. Mr. Trumps announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month, which aimed to clamp down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russias war against Ukraine. In a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia would repay it with further terror and perfidy. He described it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged. It plays into Russias hands allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world, he said. According to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, Mr. Zelenskyy called it a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners. Mr. Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the war. I believe our team is simply being used as a smoke screen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other, Mr. Zelenskyy said.

headline: Centre brings about major bureaucratic reshuffle: Prakash Rajpurohit made Dy Election Commissioner | Check complete list
content: The Centre on Saturday appointed senior bureaucrat Prakash Rajpurohit as Deputy Election Commissioner as part of a wider reshuffle involving senior-level officials. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has cleared the appointments of 27 civil servants to joint secretary-level and equivalent positions as part of the administrative changes, according to PTI. Rajpurohit, an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Rajasthan cadre, will hold the position until April 8, 2030. He succeeds Sanjay Kumar, according to an order issued by the Personnel Ministry. Meanwhile, Vivek Khare, an Indian Telecom Service (ITS) officer, has been appointed Joint Secretary at the National Testing Agency (NTA), the order said. Prakash Rajpurohit is a 2010-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre. He reportedly holds a BTech degree in Electrical Engineering from IIT Delhi and belongs to Barmer, Rajasthan. Vivek Khare is a 1996-batch ITS officer. He has been serving as Director at the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) since June 2019. Before joining the CVC, he worked as Director at the Election Commission of India (ECI). Ravi Shankar, Chittaranjan Dash, P Manoj Kumar and Abhishek Bhagotia have been appointed Joint Secretaries in the Ministry of Home Affairs. Mohammed Y Safirulla K and Ritu Sharma will take up Joint Secretary positions in the Department of Health and Family Welfare. Varnali Deka, a 2009-batch IAS officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, has been appointed Joint Secretary at the National Health Authority (NHA), while Ashish Madhavrao More will serve as Additional Chief Executive Officer at the NHA at the Joint Secretary level. Nikhil Varma has been appointed Additional Director General of Foreign Trade in Delhi. The other appointments include Tanvi Sundriyal as Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Inderjeet Singh as Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Culture, according to the order. Senior IAS officer Tamboli Ayyaj Fakirbhai has been named Executive Director at the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) at the Joint Secretary level. Rajesh Malik will serve as Executive Director at the Food Corporation of India, while Navin Agarwal has been appointed Joint Secretary in the Department of Legal Affairs. Brijesh Pandey will be Joint Secretary in the Department of Capital Development, M Ramachandrudu in the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Sonia Pant will serve as Adviser at the Joint Secretary level in NITI Aayog. Nitin Kumar has been appointed Additional Secretary at the Joint Secretary level in the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). C Muruganas will take up the post of Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, while Rajneesh Kumar Tomar has been named Chief Executive Officer of National Highways Logistics Management Ltd. Nishtha Tiwari has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Development and Welfare Board for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. Manisha Trighatia will serve as Joint Secretary in the Department of Urban Development, Avinash Jain in the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, and Pawan Kumar at the National River Conservation Directorate. Anita Shah Akella has been appointed Joint Secretary at the National Commission for Women. headline: Kuwait Airways cancels Riyadh flights due to 'airport closures', 'security situation'
content: Kuwait Airways said on Saturday (October 10, 2026) that it had cancelled two flights in and out of Riyadh, citing the closure of the airport and the security situation there. Kuwait Airways announces that flight KU775 from Kuwait to Riyadh and flight KU776 from Riyadh to Kuwait have been cancelled today, Saturday, October 10, 2026, due to the closure of the airport as a result of the security situation, read the statement posted online.

headline: Man held after 20 years in ₹37 lakh bank fraud case
content: Oct 10, 2026, 21:34 IST Chennai: Central Crime Branch of the Chennai Police arrested a 60-year-old man in Bengaluru on Friday, nearly 20 years after he helped mortgage another persons property using forged documents to obtain a 37 lakh bank loan, police said. Harinarayanan, son of Parthasarathy, was wanted in a case registered in 2007 on a complaint from Philomina Rani, wife of Ponnusamy. The case involved a 6,772-square-foot plot at Kamaraj Avenue in Sridevi Garden, Valasaravakkam. Police said a co-accused, Leemaraj, obtained a fake legal heir certificate and forged documents for the property. He colluded with Harinarayanan to mortgage the plot with a private bank in New Delhi and secure a 37 lakh loan, they said. On Friday, a special CCB team traced him to Bengaluru and arrested him.

headline: UN Human Rights body expresses concern over detentions during Delhi, Mumbai protests; calls for release of detainees
content: The United Nations Human Rights office on Saturday (October 10), expressed concern over reports of mass detentions of protesers, leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists in Delhi ahead of and during large-scale demonstrations. The protests were linked to demands by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and others for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The UN body called on Indian authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly, exercise restraint in dealing with protesters and immediately release those who had been arbitrarily detained. We are concerned by reports of mass detentions in India of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during todays large-scale demonstrations in Delhi, UN Human Rights said in a statement. Quick answers to key questions 1Why were protesters demonstrating in Delhi? The Cockroach Janta Party called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision. The planned demonstration was at Jantar Mantar. 2What did the UN Human Rights office say about the Delhi protest detentions? It expressed concern over reports of mass detentions and called on Indian authorities to respect peaceful assembly, use restraint and immediately release people arbitrarily detained. It also urged meaningful dialogue with demonstrators. 3How many people were detained during the Delhi and Mumbai protests? Reports said more than 7,000 people were detained across Delhi. Around 400 people were detained at different locations in Mumbai. 4What is preventive detention, and how is it different from an arrest? Preventive detention is confinement based on a reasonable apprehension that someone may threaten public order or security. An ordinary arrest is generally linked to an alleged offence and the legal process that follows. 5Can police detain someone without a warrant during a protest? A warrant is not always required, but police must have a lawful basis to detain someone. Under Section 170 of the BNSS, detention under that power is limited to 24 hours unless further detention is authorised under another applicable law. Restrictions on peaceful protests must meet strict tests of necessity and proportionality, it added, urging the authorities to engage in meaningful dialogue to address the concerns raised by demonstrators. The UN Human Rights office urged Indian authorities to ensure that law enforcement personnel exercised utmost restraint in responding to peaceful protesters, in keeping with India's democratic traditions and human rights obligations. It also called for meaningful dialogue to address the demonstrators' concerns. The statement came as an extensive security operation across the national capital thwarted a planned mobilisation at Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid a controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. More than 7,000 protesters were detained across Delhi, according to reports, as police and paramilitary personnel were deployed at key locations to prevent demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar. The security operation involved more than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel, according to the supplied reports. Barricades were erected across Lutyens' Delhi, while authorities carried out checks at border points, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations. Several metro stations were also closed, disrupting movement across parts of the capital. Police made repeated announcements at Jantar Mantar, instructing people and mediapersons not to gather in groups. Despite the heavy deployment, some protesters attempted to breach barricades. Around 1 pm, a group allegedly hurled stones at security personnel near Akashwani Bhawan on Imtiaz Ali Marg, injuring two police personnel. The protesters were detained, and police were likely to register multiple FIRs in connection with the incident, a senior officer said. Police also detained people at several locations, including Hanuman Temple, Safdarjung Flyover and Kerala House, as well as some protesters who managed to reach Jantar Mantar. CJP convener Abhijit Dipke and party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained at Delhi airport after arriving from Mumbai, according to the reports. In a video shared by the CJP, Dipke could be heard telling police officers who entered the aircraft: We are here to be arrested, come and arrest us. Before the detentions, police personnel told CJP leaders that they did not have permission to hold the protest at Jantar Mantar. Dipke criticised the action, saying party leaders were being treated like criminals. He also alleged that the detentions reflected authoritarianism. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who lives abroad and had travelled to India to join the demonstration, was detained by police from his residence in Gurugram's Sector 56, the reports said. Authorities also monitored social media platforms for attempts to mobilise people for the protest. More than 200 content creators were reportedly under scrutiny as police examined online posts and messages linked to the proposed gathering. Several opposition leaders were among those detained as they attempted to join the demonstration from different parts of the capital. They included former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal of the Aam Aadmi Party, West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee of the Trinamool Congress, Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan of the CPI(M), and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar of the CPI(M). The detentions triggered sharp criticism from opposition parties, which accused the government of suppressing dissent. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the Modi government of turning the mother of democracy into a muzzled democracy, alleging that the BJP and RSS were displaying cowardice through the crackdown. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi expressed solidarity with the protesting youth and urged them to continue their demonstrations. Gandhi also challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to arrest all the protesters, asserting that they would continue their fight to defend the Constitution and protect the voice of the Indian people. Activist Sonam, if those detained were not released within 24 hours. Wangchuk had previously joined a 36-day CJP agitation at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak issue. That protest ended on July 25 following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, according to the supplied account. The earlier agitation had also witnessed unrest during a march towards Parliament on July 20, when security personnel attempted to stop protesters. The demonstrations also triggered detentions in Mumbai, where police detained around 400 people at different locations for allegedly protesting without permission in solidarity with the Delhi mobilisation. Those detained reportedly included actor Imran Khan, activist Tushar Gandhi and CPI(M) workers. Demonstrations took place at August Kranti Maidan, Hutatma Chowk and other locations. Across Delhi, the authorities maintained heightened security, including the deployment of more than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces to assist the police. Mock drills were conducted at several locations to assess preparedness, while liquor shops across the capital were closed as a precautionary measure.

headline: Rs 3.4 crore fraud trail leads police to 8,574 bank accounts, one arrested
content: City cybercrime police have uncovered a complex network behind an online investment fraud that cost a 69-year-old retired bank employee Rs. 3.4 crore. Police arrested a 52-year-old man from Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and froze Rs. 21 lakh in his account.The victim received a WhatsApp message from a person posing as Rajiv Mehta, chief investment officer of a Bengaluru-based investment firm. The person added him to a group called FYERSHNIVIP and promised high returns, police said.The fraudsters posted fabricated messages showing group members earning profits. Believing their claims, the victim transferred about Rs. 3.4 crore in 13 instalments to bank accounts in different states .He realised he had been cheated when the promised returns did not arrive and the contacts became unreachable. He alerted the cybercrime helpline at 1930 and filed a complaint with the Chennai Police Commissioners office.A special team, acting on the directions of Commissioner A Amalraj, traced the transactions to Visakhapatnam. It arrested Konathala Krishna, 52, of Merudi in Anakapalli mandal. A court remanded him in judicial custody.Investigators found that the money had passed through 20 layers involving 150 banks and 27 payment applications before reaching 8,574 bank accounts. Police froze the recipient accounts and recovered about Rs. 21 lakh.Police said cyberfraud networks often use bank account holders to route illicit funds. They warned current account holders not to share their bank accounts, SIM cards, mobile phones or online banking credentials in return for commissions or other benefits.The Cyber Crime Wing urged people to verify investment offers received through WhatsApp and social media. Victims of online financial fraud can call 1930 or report the offence through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.

headline: TNPDCL to hire contract workers to install smart meters
content: Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation will hire additional contract workers to install smart meters and repair faulty distribution transformers for low-tension current transformer (LTCT) services.Each of the 45 electricity distribution circles can hire up to eight workers for 60 days. We want to install smart meters for all 60,000 LTCT services by the end of this month. We have covered about 30% so far, a senior official said. We also need to repair faulty transformers quickly so they are ready when failures occur during the monsoon. That is why we need more workers.The additional workers will help special maintenance teams repair failed distribution transformers from the field, the circular said. Overseeing the overhauling of distribution transformers in the special maintenance repair shed and assisting the special maintenance outdoor section works, particularly the periodical and breakdown maintenance of sub-station equipment, so as to ensure timely and quality power supply to consumers, the circular said.Superintending and executive engineers can invite tenders to hire workers at a daily wage of 965. TNPDCL recently allowed field officers to hire contract workers for six months to repair faults and restore power. It also instructed officials to outsource meter reading across the state. This is its third order to outsource work to private contractors.Consumers, however, said these measures had not improved the quality of power supply. They urge officials to look at complaints of power cuts, delay in restoration of power supply and poor quality of power supply and ensure remedial measures are yielding results.

headline: The Volatility Trap: Why Elon Musk's X Rants Over Starlink Prove He Can't Be Trusted
content: The SpaceX CEO has demonstrated a pattern of erratic communication that raises serious questions about his reliability as a long-term corporate partner A sudden, highly public wave of social media commentary from Elon Musk alleging that domestic interests are deliberately blocking Starlinks commercial launch in India has once again brought executive volatility into global focus. By choosing to launch aggressive public broadsides rather than navigating standard statutory procedures, the SpaceX CEO has demonstrated a pattern of erratic communication that raises serious questions about his reliability as a long-term corporate partner. The public ranting centres on Starlinks pending final security clearances and spectrum assignment. While global technology firms routinely push for swift administrative approvals, using personal digital megaphones to attack local processes reveals a fundamental impatience with predictable, rule-based governance. - Streamline Your Workflow: Multi-Device Bluetooth Keyboards and Mice Under Rs. 2,500 - Musk Accuses Indian Oligarchs Of Blocking Starlink Launch, Centre Rejects Claim | News18 - With Elon Musk, It's Not Just About Business: From India To US, There's Politics Involved - Ghar Mein Ghus Ke Marenge: Elon Musk Questions Starlinks India Entry, Gets Fact-Checked And Trolled On X Erratic Communication Over Diplomatic Dialogue Bypassing official regulatory dialogue in favour of hostile online posts reflects a volatile approach to international business relations. Standard market entry demands steady institutional coordination, transparent compliance, and respect for administrative checksparticularly when establishing critical satellite communications infrastructure. When a high-profile corporate figure repeatedly uses a social media platform like X to pressure regulators and bypass established protocols, it signals an unguided reliance on public outrage over formal diplomacy. This inclination to create digital media spectacles during delicate administrative evaluations undermines commercial credibility and alienates essential institutional partners. The Risk of Unpredictable Executive Behaviour Critical telecommunications and national infrastructure projects require long-term stability, adherence to statutory frameworks, and mutual trust between corporate leadership and regulatory authorities. Musks habit of turning complex administrative steps into sensationalised online battles highlights the risks of relying on executive leadership that operates on personal impulse rather than structured corporate policy. When executive decision-making is routinely subject to social media outbursts, global partners are left dealing with constant unpredictability. Foreign investments and technology integration demand absolute dependability, making erratic public posturing a liability for long-term strategic alliances. Why Trust Requires Institutional Respect Building sustainable international partnerships requires patience, regulatory alignment, and consistent adherence to local statutory requirements. Attempting to force administrative outcomes through viral digital pressure demonstrates a profound disregard for standard operational norms. As global enterprises expand into complex international markets, executive temperament becomes as critical as technological capability. Musks latest flurry of online posts shows that when faced with routine administrative procedure, he prefers public escalation over dependable corporate engagementproving once again why his volatile public conduct makes him an unpredictable global actor. Elon Musk alleged on social media that unnamed powerful business interests and oligarchs were obstructing Starlink to protect a monopolistic chokehold over India's internet market. The Indian government rejected these claims, stating that its satellite communication approval process is fair, non-discriminatory, and applies equally to all licensed operators.

headline: IRCTC wallet money stays locked when Tatkal tickets are sold out
content: Christopher Miltus / Oct 10, 2026, 21:14 IST Chennai: Passengers who load money into their IRCTC wallets for Tatkal bookings cannot transfer unused balances back to their bank accounts if tickets sell out or bookings fail. They often use the wallet to avoid payment failures when heavy traffic strains payment gateways and servers during peak booking hours. But unused money remains in the wallet and can be used only for future railway bookings. Passengers have asked IRCTC to allow them to withdraw the balance. Railway officials said they would escalate the issue and address the passengers concerns.

content: Uttarakhand CM targets Rahul Gandhi over his exchange with Elon Musk on Starlinks delayed India launch, stressing national security requirements. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Elon Musk and Starlinks delayed commercial launch in India, accusing him of supporting foreign interests while targeting domestic industrial groups. Dhami alleged that Gandhis repeated criticism of Indian business groups, alongside his support for foreign entities, raised questions about his intentions. - Starlink vs India: Elon Musks Security Standoff and the Battle for Satellite Internet | Raw Report - Insulting Institutions Won't Strengthen Democracy: Kiren Rijiju Hits Out At Rahul Gandhi Over CEC Protest - Starlink vs Modi Government: Elon Musk Hits Back as India Pushes Rules | JD Vances H-1B Row |News18 - 'No Monopoly In India': Jyotiraditya Scindia Dismisses Elon Musk's Starlink Claims He said companies seeking to operate in India must follow the countrys regulatory procedures and comply with security requirements. What Rahul Gandhi Said To Elon Musk The controversy followed Musks criticism of the delay in launching Starlinks satellite internet services in India. However, it must complete the required security clearances and other regulatory procedures, including spectrum-related requirements, before beginning commercial operations. Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami accused Rahul Gandhi of supporting foreign interests and continuously criticizing domestic industrial groups, alleging a conspiracy to weaken the country.

headline: Putin informs Trump Iran's position on peace deal, reports Kremlin; what has Tehran proposed?
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin has conveyed Irans position on a possible resolution to the US-Iran conflict to US President Donald Trump, the Kremlin said on Saturday, October 10, as diplomatic efforts to end the war remain stalled. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin relayed Tehrans views during a phone call with Trump on Friday, in coordination with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Reuters reported, citing Russias Interfax news agency. In coordination with the president of Iran, Putin conveyed to Trump the Iranian sides view on a possible resolution of the conflict, Peskov was quoted as saying. The Kremlin did not disclose the details of Irans position or say how Trump responded to the message. It also did not provide further information on the possible terms of a settlement. Putin offers to help broker US-Iran peace deal Putins latest outreach comes amid a prolonged diplomatic impasse over the conflict, which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Earlier this week, Putin met Pezeshkian on the sidelines of a summit in Turkmenistan. During the meeting, the Russian leader expressed Moscows interest in helping broker peace, signalling a possible diplomatic role for Russia in efforts to end the hostilities. However, it remains unclear whether Putins communication with Trump will lead to renewed negotiations or a breakthrough in the stalled peace process. Why have US-Iran peace talks stalled? Efforts to end the conflict have been at an impasse since the summer, despite an earlier understanding between Washington and Tehran. The United States and Iran agreed to a memorandum of understanding in June that outlined a framework for ending the conflict. However, Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz prompted a resumption of US military operations, undermining the diplomatic effort. More recent indirect talks between Washington and Tehran, held on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, failed to produce a breakthrough.

headline: 'Will Return Stronger Tomorrow': CJP Calls Protest 'Half Win' As Delhi Police Detains Hundreds
content: CJP leader Ajinkya vows to continue the Delhi protest, calling Saturdays action a 'half win'. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday described its protest in Delhi as a half win" and said it would continue its campaign on Sunday, despite a major police crackdown and detention of several of its leaders. In a statement, CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde alleged that the government had attempted to shut down the national capital out of fear of the protest movement. He said the group would return to the streets stronger tomorrow" and continue its protests until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media - Being Pressured...: Abhijeet Dipke Says CJP Volunteers Getting Police Notices Ahead Of Delhi Protest - CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Live: Over 7,000 Protesters Detained; Police Likely To File FIR Over Alleged Assault Of Cops - 35,000 Cops, Mass Detention Centres, High-Tech Body Cams: Delhi Police's Massive Plan For CJP Protest The CJP had planned a demonstration at Jantar Mantar demanding Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had denied permission for the protest, citing security, traffic and law-and-order concerns. Several CJP leaders were detained after arriving in Delhi, including founder Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. CJP Raises Concerns Over Dipkes Detention The party also raised concerns over the whereabouts of Dipke, Ranka and Das. It claimed that the detained leaders were not being allowed to communicate freely. The CJP particularly raised concerns over Dipke after his grandmother, Savitribai Dipke, died in Maharashtra on Saturday. The party alleged that Dipke had not been allowed to speak to his grandmother and accused the government of subjecting him to emotional atyachar" following her death. The party reiterated its resolve to continue its campaign against the government. Ajinkya said, This is a long fight", while also maintaining that the CJP would return to the streets stronger tomorrow." Dipkes grandmother died at her home in Maharashtras Hingoli district on Saturday. Dipke was detained at Delhi airport earlier in the day along with Ranka and Das. Delhi Police Refutes Claims, Says Dipke Was Informed Delhi Police rejected the claims surrounding Dipkes communication with his family. In a statement posted on X, the force said information about his grandmothers death had been conveyed to Dipke promptly" and with due sensitivity". Police also said he had been informed about the scheduled funeral and offered all possible assistance to travel to his hometown on humanitarian grounds". The police response came after social media claims alleged that Dipke had not been informed about the death. The CJP, however, has continued to demand information about the location of its detained leaders and their release. Meanwhile, Ajinkya Shinde has been named to lead the groups protest after Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained on arrival in Delhi. The Cockroach Janta Party protested to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and differences within the Election Commission.

headline: What is a preventative detention? How is it different from arrest? What to know amid police crackdown in Delhi protests
content: Parts of Delhi witnessed heightened security on October 10 as protesters gathered to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Several protesters reportedly faced difficulties reaching Jantar Mantar, where the demonstration was planned, amid police barricades and restrictions. Delhi Police detained several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee and Pinarayi Vijayan, along with CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Dhruv Rathee and All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora were also reportedly detained. According to the Press Trust of India (PTI), more than 7,000 people, including lawyers and students, had been detained while attempting to reach the protest site. Actor Imran Khan was also detained during a demonstration in Mumbai. Quick answers to key questions 1What is preventive detention? Preventive detention is the confinement of someone based on a reasonable apprehension that they may engage in activity threatening public order or security. Under Section 170 of the BNSS, police must have the required legal basis to believe an offence is planned or may happen and that detention is necessary to prevent it. 2How is preventive detention different from an ordinary arrest? Preventive detention is intended to stop an anticipated threat. An ordinary arrest is generally connected to an alleged offence and the legal process that follows. 3Can police detain someone without a warrant under Section 170 of the BNSS? Yes. Police may arrest without a warrant or magistrates order if they believe a cognisable offence is being planned and it cannot otherwise be prevented. Detention under this power is limited to 24 hours unless further detention is authorised under another applicable law. 4Can police use preventive detention based only on suspicion? No. The article says preventive detention does not give police unrestricted power to detain people merely on suspicion. Whether a detention is lawful depends on the facts and the legal grounds relied upon. 5What safeguards apply to arrest and preventive detention in India? Article 22 of the Constitution of India provides safeguards relating to arrest and detention. The article also notes that the legality of a detention depends on the provision invoked and the circumstances. The detentions have raised questions about the legal powers of the police during protests, including when they can take someone into custody without a warrant and what safeguards apply. Criminal lawyer Swagata Biswas of Metropolitan Magistrate Court at Kolkata tells Live Mint, A warrant is not always required to detain a person. An absence of a warrant does not mean that the police can detain anyone without a lawful basis. The legality of an arrest or detention depends on the provision invoked and the circumstances of the case. Under Section 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, the police can arrest a person without a warrant or an order from a magistrate if they believe a plan to commit a cognisable offence and that the offence cannot otherwise be prevented. The provision also limits detention under this power to 24 hours unless further detention is authorised under another applicable law. Preventive detention refers to the confinement of a person based on a reasonable apprehension that they may engage in an activity that threatens public order or security. Under Section 170 of the BNSS, the police must have the legally required basis to believe that an offence is being planned or might happen and that arrest is necessary to prevent it. However, it doesn't give the police an unrestricted power to arrest people merely on suspicion. Whether a particular detention is lawful depends on the facts and the legal grounds relied upon by the authorities. Preventive detention that allows authorities to hold a person to prevent anticipated threats is not the same as an ordinary arrest. An arrest is generally associated with an alleged offence and the subsequent legal process. Laws providing for preventive detention include the National Security Act (NSA), 1980; the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act (COFEPOSA), 1974; the Prevention of Black-marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980; and the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988. Article 22 of the Constitution of India provides safeguards relating to arrest and detention. Sneha Biswas specialises in covering entertainment and pop culture, with a specialisation on Bollywood, Hollywood, OTT platforms, K-pop, K-dramas, and major developments in the US entertainment industry. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: Goondas Act invoked against couple in Guduvanchery murder case
content: Tambaram City Police Commissioner invoked the Goondas Act against Manik Uddin Laskar, 22, from Assam, and his wife, Bhagawati Majhi. Police had arrested the couple in connection with the murder and dismemberment of a 38-year-old woman in Guduvanchery.The commissioner issued the detention orders on Friday. Guduvanchery police handed copies to officials at Puzhal Central Prison.The case came to light on Aug 5, when police found an unclaimed suitcase aboard the Tamil Nadu Express after it travelled from Chennai Central to Agra. The suitcase contained a headless human skeleton and other body parts.During the investigation, police examined surveillance camera footage from several locations and searched a house on Mosque Street in Guduvanchery. They found human flesh in a large vessel used for preparing biryani.Police identified the victim as Hayathun Nisha, 38, from Odisha. Investigators later arrested Laskar and Majhi on charges of murder and dismemberment. A court remanded them to Puzhal Central Prison.

headline: Meet Rakesh Kumar: Indian Oil executive recommended for CPCL's Director of Operations post
content: Sounak Mukhopadhyay Rakesh Kumar, a senior Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) executive, has received a board-level recommendation. The Public Enterprises Selection Board recommended him as Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limiteds Director of Operations. Rakesh Kumar currently serves as General Manager of Technical Services at Indian Oil Corporation Limited. His professional background covers oil refining, technical operations and management of downstream petroleum activities. The recommendation could bring a major step forward in his career. However, his appointment still needs final approval from the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet. The selection boards recommendation will now go before the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet. This committee must give final approval before Kumar takes charge. Once approved, he will become CPCLs Director of Operations. For now, his selection remains a recommendation awaiting that decision. Rakesh Kumar is a petroleum sector professional with experience in the industry. His work has focused on refinery operations, engineering and improving technical processes. These areas form a part of his profile. His experience includes work with Indias government-owned energy companies. At IOCL, he holds a position in technical services. The proposed CPCL role would take him into the companys board-level leadership. The selection followed a competitive panel interview conducted by the Public Enterprises Selection Board. Kumar was chosen from among nine candidates representing major public-sector oil and gas companies, according to PSU Connect. The panel also interviewed senior executives from IOCL, CPCL and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation. Their roles covered operations, production, human resources, planning and other business functions. Among the IOCL candidates was Kondapalli Siva Rama Rao, Chief General Manager and CEO of IOLPL. M Sankar, Chief General Manager in the Chairmans Secretariat, also appeared before the panel. Muralidhar S represented IOCL as Chief General Manager for LPG at its Karnataka State Office. Om Prasad Chetry, General Manager in charge of human resources, was another IOCL candidate. CPCL candidates included Purushotham, Chief General Manager for Corporate Planning and Business Development. Thullibilli Kishor Babu, General Manager of Operations, was also interviewed. ONGC candidates included Bhishmadev Mandal, Chief General Manager of Production. Om Prakash, General Manager overseeing Operations and Maintenance Contracts, also appeared for the interview. Director of Operations is a Schedule A board-level position at CPCL. The director oversees the refinerys operations and related company functions. CPCL is an IOCL subsidiary and a petroleum refining company in South India. The position comes under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. headline: Chennai airport raises vehicle parking charges
content: Vehicles will pay up to Rs. 35 more for the first 30 minutes and up to Rs. 110 more for parking for 24 hours at Chennai international airport from Sunday. Authorities last revised the charges in 2024.Airport authorities said the contract allows a 5% increase in parking charges. The new rates will take effect at 1am on Sunday. The charge for cars will rise from Rs. 85 to Rs. 90 for the first 30 minutes. For 30 minutes to one hour, it will increase from Rs. 110 to Rs. 115. A car parked for two hours will cost Rs. 380, up from Rs. 360.Vans with up to 16 seats will pay Rs. 345 for the first 30 minutes and up to Rs. 1,155 for 24 hours. Vehicles with more than 16 seats will pay Rs. 695 for the first 30 minutes and up to Rs. 2,315 for 24 hours.Two-wheeler parking charges will remain largely unchanged. Those who lose their parking tickets must pay a penalty of Rs. 580 for cars and Rs. 175 for two-wheelers, besides the parking charge. Cabs and taxis will continue to pay an entry fee of Rs. 45 to pick up passengers.

headline: Anti-CEC protests in Chennai: AISF, AIYF cadres arrested on Anna Salai; over 40 protesters detained in Besant Nagar
content: More than 100 cadres of the All India Students Federation (AISF) and the All India Youth Federation (AIYF) were arrested by Chennai police on Saturday (October 10, 2026) while attempting to take out a procession to the Tamil Nadu Secretariat, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The members had gathered to march to the Secretariat and lay siege to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Tamil Nadu. Led by AIYF State secretary K. Bharathi and AISF State president K. Ibrahim, the protesters assembled near the Periyar statue on Anna Salai and proceeded along Sivananda Salai. The police stopped them and prevented them from moving further. Anti-CEC Delhi protest LIVE updates: CJP urges youth to take charge of movement as leaders detained; protesters being taken away from Jantar Mantar, nearby areas The protesters accused the CEC of orchestrating vote theft and called for criminal proceedings and other action against him. They also raised slogans demanding his removal and condemning the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government for allegedly supporting those accused of stealing votes. Our vote, our right! and Do not steal our right to vote! were among the slogans raised by the protesters. The police forcibly bundled the protesters into vehicles despite their resistance and heated arguments. They were detained at a community hall. During the scuffle, Kavin, a protester from Mylapore, sustained a head injury and was taken to hospital for treatment. Over 40 detained in Besant Nagar Meanwhile, a gathering of about 40 youngsters from different walks of life, including advocate Ra. Shhiva and social activists Sachin George and Radhika Ganesh, protested at Elliots Beach in Besant Nagar, urging the revocation of the provision of the law that gives life-long immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and the halting of the SIR exercise. They demanded the resignation of the CEC. The police spoke with the protesters, but the talks failed to resolve the situation. The police said the group had not secured permission to stage a demonstration at the beach. When the protesters declined to leave, the police detained them. Arguments and scuffles broke out as officers tried to clear the area. Some protesters lay on the ground and continued chanting before being taken to the Urur Kuppam Corporation Community Hall. Later, DMK leaders A. Raja, Ma. Subramanian, and Thamizhachi Thangapandian, along with the party supporters, reached the hall and sat in dharna, demanding the immediate release of protesters. The protesters were released by the police around 12 noon.

headline: Judges of Supreme Court and high courts are appointed directly by Modi, says former judge of Madras high court K Chandru
content: Judges of Supreme Court and high courts are, in effect, being appointed directly by Prime Minister Narendra Modi rather than the collegium, said former judge of Madras high court K Chandru on Saturday.He said the Modi govt, after coming to power in 2014, attempted to introduce the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), but Supreme Court struck down the legislation. Since then, all Supreme Court and high court judges were directly appointed by Modi, not the collegium, Justice Chandru said. He said the govt had made no attempt to revive the NJAC as it had found ways that were more profitable than the commission.Criticising the collegium system of judicial appointments, he said the process lacked transparency and was not recognised by the Constitution. There are 38 judges in Supreme Court and about 1,000 judges in high courts. The appointment process takes place without anyone knowing anything through a collegium system which is not recognised by the Constitution. It is the best ever secret kept in the country, he said in his keynote address at a colloquium titled Who Will Judge the Judges, organised by Asian College of Journalism (ACJ).He added that nowhere in the world did judges themselves appoint judges, except in India, not in any elected democracy such as our country. Earlier, delivering a keynote address on the title Primus inter pares: A Critique of the office of the Chief Justice of India, former Chief Justice of Odisha high court S Muralidhar said the country was slated to have a slew of chief justices who had never headed a high court.Pointing out the lack of an adequate number of woman judges in Supreme Court, Justice Muralidhar said, Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was in office for two years. But he could not find a single woman judge suitable to be elevated to Supreme Court. Diversity is only for public consumption.Raju Ramachandran, senior advocate, Supreme Court, spoke on the title Unwillingness or Inability? Why Impeachments Fail, while Justice K Kannan, former judge of Punjab and Haryana high court, addressed the gathering on the title Preparing the Judges to Judge. Senior advocate of Madras high court R Vaigai delivered a keynote address on How Fair is the Quality of Justice: lack of diversity in appointments.

headline: CJP protests: Supreme Court to hold special Sunday sitting on contempt plea over Delhi Metro shutdowns during protests
content: The Supreme Court is set to hold a special sitting on Sunday to hear a contempt petition filed against the shutting down of Delhi Metro stations as well as the cancellation of train services. The petition alleges that the cancellations were in effect despite the apex court's 9 October order directing that there should be no complete closure of transport services on Saturday, 10 October, in connection with the anti-Chief Election Commissioner protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party. The matter will be heard by a bench comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana. The petition was filed by Shailendra Mani Tripathi, who was among the petitioners who had sought an independent investigation into the violence at the July Jantar Mantar student protest. The petition has sought for contempt proceedings against Govind Mohan, IAS, who is the Union Home Secretary; Anurag Kumar, IPS, who is the Delhi Police Commissioner, and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara, IAS. The petitioner has said that the authorities went ahead with their allegedly arbitrary closing down of metro stations as well as unwarranted cancellations of railway services despite the apex court having issued directions to ensure public transport remains operational in a regulated matter on Saturday. "This brutal assault on the fundamental rights of the citizens and sheer disregard to the orders of this court amounts to deliberate, intentional attempt on the part of Delhi Metro, Delhi Police and the Union government which must be dealt with an iron hand," the plea, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, said. The protest call was given by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission. While hearing the separate petition on Friday, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Bagchi and Mohana had directed the Centre to ensure that there was no "complete prohibition" of the movement of metro and trains coming to Delhi on October 10 due to the protest, saying they cannot bring everything to a halt. Though law enforcement agencies have the right to take steps to restrict unruly movement, citizens should not be unduly harassed, the top court had said. After the top court's order, Delhi Metro decided to shut down the entry and exit of 45 metro stations on Saturday, which is set to remain in effect till 10 pm.
