headline: 9 Killed, Including Pregnant Woman And Suspect, After Gunman Opens Fire At Pennsylvania Home
content: At least nine people were killed in a Pennsylvania home shooting, with the suspected gunman later dying from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. At least nine people, including two children and a pregnant woman, were killed in a shooting at a house in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday evening, police said. The suspected gunman later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Police were called to a home on the 700 block of Perry Street at around 5 pm local time on October 9 after receiving reports of gunfire, according to local media reports. Officers found two women dead outside the house, while other victims were found inside the property, according to Erie News Now and KBTX News 3. - Woman Says Bengaluru Is No Longer For The Middle Class, Says Dont Come If Youre Not Earning 1 Lakh Monthly - Two Killed, Up To 35 Injured In Shooting At Homecoming Party In US - Facing Difficulty Breathing: Pregnant Womans Terrifying Call From Under Seemapuri Building Debris - Yeh Wali Jagah Par...: Govinda, Sunita Ahujas Daughter Dodges Question About Komal Rani | Video Investigators said the suspect allegedly entered the home after shooting the two women and then opened fire on several people inside. He later barricaded himself in the residence, leading to a standoff involving SWAT teams. Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described the scene as one of the most difficult incidents officers and investigators had faced. He said the scale of the loss was devastating and that the circumstances surrounding the shooting were still being investigated. The suspect was eventually found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah confirmed. Police have not yet determined what led to the shooting. Authorities are also yet to establish the relationship between the suspect and the victims. The identities of those killed have not been publicly released. There are no words that can adequately express the magnitude of the loss of life here," Lorah said, adding that investigators would need time to establish what happened. Images from the scene showed several police vehicles outside the property as officers dealt with the standoff. Erie News Now photographer Chris Peterson, who was at the scene, described a chaotic situation as gunfire was heard and people ran from the area. Officials later said the situation had been brought under control and there was no continuing threat to the public. The City of Erie, in a Facebook statement, expressed condolences to the victims, their families and others affected by the shooting. Officials said they were working with the Erie Police Department and would release further information after details had been confirmed. A gunman opened fire at a home on Perry Street, killing nine people including two children and a pregnant woman. The suspect initially shot two women outside before entering the house to shoot others inside, and later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound following a SWAT standoff.

headline: Panama earthquake: Is the tsunami warning still in place? Have aftershocks been detected? Here's what we know so far
content: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Panama on Friday (October 9), collapsing buildings and roads, damaging historic structures and injuring at least 27 people. Authorities reported no deaths, although President Jos Ral Mulino cautioned that the toll could change as rescue and damage assessments continued. The shallow earthquake triggered panic across the Central American country, with residents evacuating buildings in the capital, Panama City. Authorities also issued a tsunami warning for parts of the eastern Pacific before lifting it later in the day. The earthquake was followed by dozens of aftershocks, including one measuring above magnitude 6.0, according to local geosciences authorities. Here's what we know so far about the earthquake, the tsunami warning, the aftershocks and the damage. No. The tsunami warning issued after the earthquake was later lifted, according to reports. The warning had covered the Pacific coasts of Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala. Alerts issued by El Salvador and Chile for Easter Island were also lifted. Nstor Luque, director of the Geosciences Institute at the University of Panama, said waves measuring between 3 and 10 feet (1 to 3 metres) were expected around Isla Caas and the southern coast of Los Santos province. He said major waves were not expected beyond those areas. Seawater had already reached some homes near the coast on Isla Caas, according to Luque. Yes. More than 80 aftershocks were recorded by Panama's local geosciences institute, including one measuring above magnitude 6.0. Several aftershocks measured magnitudes of 5.8, 5.5 and 5.2, according to reports. The tremors prompted some residents to evacuate buildings more than once. The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the earthquake struck at 12:56 pm local time on Friday (1756 GMT), with its epicentre around 10 kilometres (six miles) from Pitaloza Arriba, a small community in central Herrera province. The tremor occurred at a shallow depth of approximately 10 kilometres, increasing the potential for strong shaking near the epicentre. The USGS initially estimated the earthquake's magnitude at 8.0 before revising it to 7.6 and subsequently to 7.7. The shaking was felt across Panama, including in the capital, which is about 200 kilometres (120 miles) from the epicentre. Residents reported objects falling inside homes and buildings, while people rushed outdoors as a precaution. Damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Herrera, Cocl, Los Santos and Veraguas, according to officials. At least 27 people suffered minor injuries, the National Civil Protection System said. President Mulino described the situation as a major disaster and said some roads had completely collapsed. Among the reported damage: - Collapsed buildings and roads: Sections of roads developed large fissures, while some structures were partially or completely damaged in affected provinces. - Historic church damaged: The Church of San Atanasio, a colonial-style Catholic church in Los Santos province, was reported to have collapsed. The church was declared a National Historic Heritage Site in 1938. - Damage in Penonom: The cathedral in the town suffered a partial collapse and cracks. Damage was also reported at the governor's office and the Dos Continentes hotel. - Town cut off: Health Minister Fernando Boyd said Tonos, in Los Santos province, had been cut off because of road damage. Authorities were exploring whether access could be restored by air. - Damage to homes: Former president Ricardo Martinelli shared photographs showing his house in the town of Son, in Veraguas province, had collapsed.

headline: Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Imran Khan detained in Mumbai; Prakash Raj says 'Frands how long will you stop river'
content: Trisha Bhattacharya As protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified on 10 October, several Bollywood personalities, including Imran Khan, Prakash Raj, Anurag Kashyap and Vishal Dadlani, voiced their reactions. While Khan was detained in Mumbai, others criticised the police crackdown and expressed solidarity with demonstrators opposing the electoral roll revision. Actor Imran Khan was detained by Mumbai Police on Saturday, 10 October, during a demonstration at August Kranti Maidan in support of the protest movement. Quick answers to key questions 1Why are people protesting against CEC Gyanesh Kumar? Protesters are opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleging irregularities in how it was carried out. They have demanded Gyanesh Kumars resignation and accountability over the process. 2What is the Special Intensive Revision at the centre of the protests? The SIR is an Election Commission exercise to verify electoral rolls. The Commission has described it as a verification exercise, while critics have questioned its implementation and raised concerns about voter-list changes. 3Was actor Imran Khan detained during the Mumbai protest? Yes. Mumbai Police detained Imran Khan during a demonstration at August Kranti Maidan on 10 October. He shared a selfie from inside a police van, captioned, Apparently I'm going for a drive. 4How did Bollywood personalities react to the anti-CEC protests? Prakash Raj condemned the detentions and called for the SIR process to be scrapped. Anurag Kashyap and Vishal Dadlani voiced support for demonstrators, while several other film personalities criticised the police response or expressed solidarity. 5Would Gyanesh Kumars resignation be enough to end the CJP protests? Not according to CJP co-convenor Saurav Das, who said the agitation would continue until the groups demands were addressed. Those demands include an inquiry into the SIR and changes to the electoral process. The actor shared a selfie from inside a police van with the caption, Apparently I'm going for a drive. The incident became one of the day's most prominent developments involving the film industry. Several other film personalities criticised the police response. Actor Prakash Raj condemned the detentions and called for the SIR process to be scrapped. Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap backed the demonstrators on Instagram, writing, Do Darpok, 40,000 ghulam, Lakhon bahadur, while directing followers towards coverage of student leader Neha Bora before her detention. Actor Richa Chadha shared a satirical make-up tutorial about evading facial recognition cameras. Filmmaker Shirish Kunder wrote on X, When even the kids start mocking you, it's time to realise that absolutely no one is scared of you anymore (sic). Singer-composer Vishal Dadlani also criticised the crackdown in an Instagram video, questioning the scale of the security response and its impact on citizens' right to protest. Filmmaker Vikramaditya Motwane shared posts condemning the detentions, while actor Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub posted a Hindi translation of a poem by German playwright Bertolt Brecht in solidarity with protesters. Comedian Vir Das shared a screenshot explaining the Streisand Effect, suggesting that attempts to suppress attention can instead amplify it. Veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah had also attended the movement's 2 October demonstration at Mumbai's Shivaji Park, where he met organiser Abhijeet Dipke and expressed support. His participation, alongside that of other film personalities, had brought wider attention to the campaign. The demonstrations were organised against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with participants demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities. The Election Commission has maintained that the revision is a verification exercise, while critics have questioned its implementation In Delhi, police denied permission for the planned 10 October gathering at Jantar Mantar, citing public-order concerns. Authorities imposed extensive security restrictions, detained organisers and demonstrators, restricted access to Metro stations and suspended mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi. Train cancellations and transport curbs also disrupted commuters. Reuters reported that more than 2,000 people were detained in Delhi amid the security operation. Police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the capital, while organisers maintained their demand for accountability. The scale of the response drew criticism from protesters and public figures, intensifying the debate over the handling of demonstrations and citizens' right to assemble. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Sabotaging Regional Ties? NIA Probes If Flydubai Attack Aimed To Damage India-UAE-Israel Relations
content: An NIA team could travel to the UAE to record the statement of Captain Smit Machchhar and is also expected to meet UAE investigators to seek access to the attacker The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has begun its probe into the Flydubai incident, registering an FIR under sections of the Anti-Hijacking Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) on Saturday. While international probes are focused on the motivation of the Omani co-pilot, identified as Hammam al-Hammami, who attacked Captain Smit Machchhar, the NIA investigation is also examining whether damaging Indias relations with friendly countries like Israel and the UAE was part of a larger international conspiracy. - VanDyke, Cybercrime, Hawala: India Tightens Rules To Blacklist Foreign Nationals | Exclusive - VanDyke, Cybercrime, Hawala: India Tightens Rules To Blacklist Foreign Nationals | Exclusive - Flydubai Incident: NIA Invokes Anti-Hijacking Act, UAPA Over Mid-Air Cockpit Attack | Exclusive Details - 'I'd Stomp On Your Head': Flydubai Co-Pilot Supported Beating Women, Killing Jews In Social Media Posts The NIA stated in its FIR, And whereas, the Central Government is of the opinion that a scheduled offence under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 has been committed and the case is related to attack on an Indian National Pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with an apparent attempt to hijack or crash the plane FlyDubai Flight No. 1073 on 30.09.2026, and having regard to the gravity of the offence, its grave national and international ramifications, and the need to unearth the larger conspiracy, the matter requires thorough investigation by the National Investigation Agency in accordance with the provisions of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008." Thankfully, the quick thinking and bravery of the Indian pilot saved the day, but if the co-pilot had succeeded in his motive of crashing the plane, there would have been no survivors and fingers could be pointed at India since the captain is Indian," a government official told News18. Israeli intelligence agencies have claimed that the co-pilot, al-Hammami, confessed he wanted to avenge Gaza, while Donald Trump has alleged an Iranian hand in the conspiracy. However, Indian agencies are also looking closely at the excellent relations India shares with Israel and the UAE and whether damaging those ties was part of al-Hammamis motivation. Nothing is being ruled out at this stage," an investigator said. The probe so far has revealed that in July this year, al-Hammami first planned to hijack an aircraft to target Israeli assets and interests. Reports suggest he abandoned that plan because one of the crew members was known to him. He subsequently carried out meticulous planning to target a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv. Whether he specifically chose a flight with an Indian captain remains a key question for Indian investigators. Sources said Indian agencies have been in touch with their UAE counterparts since al-Hammami was taken into custody. An NIA team could travel to the UAE to record the statement of Captain Smit Machchhar once medical clearance is given and is also expected to meet UAE investigators to seek access to al-Hammami. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) registered an FIR under sections of the Anti-Hijacking Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in the Flydubai case. The NIA investigation is examining whether damaging India's relations with friendly countries like Israel and the UAE was part of a larger international conspiracy. The case is related to an attack on Indian National Pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with an apparent attempt to hijack or crash Flydubai Flight No. 1073 on 30.09.2026. Israeli intelligence agencies claimed the co-pilot, al-Hammami, confessed he wanted to avenge Gaza. The NIA invoked Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and Section 16 read with Section 15(1)(a) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967. The NIA has invoked Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and Section 16 read with Section 15(1)(a) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, in its FIR. The National Investigation Agency registered an FIR under Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and sections 15(1)(a) and 16 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) to investigate the incident.

headline: CJP protests: Why were the Supreme Court lawyers released by Delhi Police? Here's what CJI Surya Kant said
content: The Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, had to intervene on Saturday after a significant number of advocates were detained by the Delhi Police amid protests in New Delhi. Yes, on my verbal intervention, I believe they have been released. I am out of town, the CJI told ANI. This came after the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) sought the inteference of the CJI on an urgent basis over the detention of a number of advocates, which included senior lawyers and women advocates as well. The SCBA alleged that those detained had been subjected to excessive police force as they were peacefully protesting in the Supreme Court area. Quick answers to key questions 1Why were Supreme Court lawyers detained by Delhi Police during the CJP protests? The lawyers were detained amid protests in the Supreme Court area during the wider security measures for the CJP demonstration in Delhi. The SCBA said they had been peacefully protesting and alleged that police used excessive force. 2Why did Delhi Police release the detained Supreme Court lawyers? The CJI intervened after the SCBA, SCAORA and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta brought the detentions to his attention. He said he spoke to the authorities, after which the lawyers were released. 3What did CJI Surya Kant say about the release of the detained lawyers? CJI Surya Kant told ANI that the lawyers had been released following his verbal intervention. He also said he was out of town. 4What did the Supreme Court Bar Association ask the CJI to do? The SCBA urged the CJI to intervene with the authorities, establish the whereabouts and safety of every detained advocate, and ensure legal assistance. It also sought the release of those held without lawful grounds. The SCBA, the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta apprised the CJI of the situation, who then spoke to authorities, following which the lawyers were released. SCBA Honorary Secretary Pragya Baghel wrote a letter to the CJI on Saturday, urging him to take up the matter with concerned authorities and ensure that the whereabouts and safety of all detained advoates be ascertained. The Association has also called for swift legal assistance for those lawyers who have been detained and the release of those against whom there is no lawful ground for detention. The Supreme Court Bar Association resolves to request the Chief Justice of India to intervene urgently and take up the matter with the concerned authorities, the resolution stated. The resolution further emphasised the need to ascertain the whereabouts of every detained advocate, ensure their safety and provide them with legal assistance. The incident comes amid protests in Delhi linked to the proposed demonstration by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, which had led to security measures and disruptions concerning public transport. More than a thousand protestors have been detained today by the Delhi Police, including leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Sourav Das, and others. Four former chief ministers - Pinarayi Vijayan, Manik Sarkar, Arvind Kejriwal, and Mamata Banerjee were also detained. AISA president Neha Bora was also detained. Mamata Banerjee claimed she and her party leaders were "kidnapped" by police and "driven around in a prison van for two hours" before being brought to Dwarka North Police Station. headline: Northeast monsoon likely to set in around October 17 or 18: RMC
content: As the State prepares for the onset of the NE monsoon later next week, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has forecast a gradual dip in the temperatures from October 16. With the Southwest monsoon expected to retreat completely from the south peninsula by October 15, conditions could turn favourable for a reversal in wind patterns and arrival of NE monsoon in the following days. An upper air cyclonic circulation may emerge in Andaman Sea around October 11 and influence a low pressure area to form over the southeast Bay of Bengal around October 13. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said the weather system was being monitored for its intensity and path. If it moves towards land or the Tamil Nadu coast, it will help enhance conditions for a reversal of wind pattern to northeasterlies, potentially accelerating the onset of the monsoon, he said. However, the weather models indicate that the system is unlikely to intensify beyond a low pressure area. The RMC expects temperatures to gradually fall across the State after October 16 as moisture incursion and cloud cover would begin to increase. With the State still undergoing monsoon transition phase, some parts of the State, particularly north interior Tamil Nadu, may continue to experience above normal temperatures till October 14. On Saturday, Erode and Madurai airport recorded the States highest maximum temperature of 37 degrees Celsius for the day. Many other weather stations also recorded day temperature of two degrees Celsius above average. However, a weather system over Gulf of Mannar and adjoining south Tamil Nadu would trigger wet spell over south and interior parts of the State. Rainfall of light to moderate intensity may continue over south Tamil Nadu till October 16. Despite the rainfall, temperatures could remain elevated in some areas in the absence of sustained cloud cover during the monsoon transition period, officials said.

headline: Pennsylvania shooting: 9 killed in Erie mass shooting, including children; suspected gunman found dead
content: Nine people, including children, were killed in a mass shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday evening, October 9, according to multiple media reports citing officials. The suspected gunman was also found dead inside a residence, with investigators believing he died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. According to NBC Philadelphia, police responded to a home on Perry Street in Erie at around 5 pm on Friday after witnesses reported seeing a gunman firing shots outside the house before entering the residence. When officers arrived at the scene, they found two women who had been shot dead on the street. The news outlet stated that the incident subsequently escalated into a standoff, with Erie Police and SWAT teams surrounding the residence. More gunshots were then heard from inside the house, according to the report. When officers entered the home, they reportedly discovered the bodies of seven more people, including children, along with the suspected gunman. The identities of the victims and the suspect have not yet been released. The City of Erie Government confirmed the incident in a statement, describing it as a tragedy that had resulted in multiple deaths. Tonight, a terrible tragedy occurred near 7th and Perry Streets in Erie, resulting in multiple deaths, the city said. The statement added that the situation had been contained and there was no ongoing threat to the public. The shooter is deceased, and there is no ongoing threat or danger to the public at this time, the city said, extending its condolences to the victims' families and others affected by the shooting. The city said it would continue working with the Erie Police Department and provide updates as verified information became available. Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described the incident as one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes he had encountered, NBC Philadelphia reported. The loss of life is devastating and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing, Lorah said. He confirmed that the suspect was dead and reiterated that, based on the information available to investigators, there was no ongoing threat to the public. Our hearts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected by this tragedy, the police chief said, adding that words could not adequately express the magnitude of the loss of life. Investigators are working to establish what led to the shooting and the circumstances surrounding the deaths. Authorities have not announced a possible motive, and the identities of the victims and the suspected gunman remain unknown. Police have not released further details about the sequence of events inside the residence or the circumstances that preceded the shooting. The investigation is ongoing.

headline: Govt school heads told to submit details on hi-tech lab equipment, requirement
content: Heads of govt and aided schools across the state must submit a list of computers and other equipment in their schools and flag deficiencies by Oct 12.The headmasters must also list the monitors, UPS units and other accessories required for the labs, along with the estimated budget. They must upload the details on the state-run Education Management Information System portal. Respective chief/district education officers must take stock of the list and coordinate with the school heads to deploy the systems. We are yet to decide on how much equipment will be given to the schools. The first step is to identify deficiencies, an official from the chief education officers office said.On Oct 4, TOI reported that the govts flagship spoken English programme, Mozhigal, for Classes VI to X had become defunct in several schools. Schools accessed the classes through hi-tech labs, which were poorly maintained after the contract with L&T ended in May last year. Several school heads reported poor internet connectivity and a shortage of working computers, mouse devices and UPS units.Officials said the department was likely to appoint a new agency. A few middle schools were given the contract to Keltron last year, but not all schools have been covered. Once HMs submit the list, the department will set aside a budget and improve the labs, an official with the elementary education office said.

headline: Constable detained after black-flag protest over daughter's treatment
content: A head constable attached to the Avadi Tank Factory police station staged a black-flag protest and raised slogans against Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday, a day before Modis visit.Muthapudupet police detained Kothandapani, near his home in Muthapudupet. He said he was protesting against the treatment given to his 10-year-old daughter at the Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children in Egmore. Kothandapani accused the hospital of medical negligence. He said his daughter had received treatment for kidney disorder, nephrotic syndrome at the hospital since she was three. He said the doctors had misdiagnosed her condition as brain fever when she suffered a seizure in Oct 2021. Complications of this led to the amputation of her leg, he said.When the hospital denied the allegations, Kothandapani sought state government intervention. He said he was denied entry to secretariat when he and tried to submit a petition.

headline: AAP Protests In Chandigarh, Demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's Resignation
content: AAP leaders Manish Sisodia and Harpal Singh Cheema were detained during a Chandigarh protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged electoral irregularities. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) held a protest in Chandigarh on Saturday in support of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral process. Senior AAP leaders Manish Sisodia, the partys Punjab in-charge, and Punjab Cabinet Minister Harpal Singh Cheema were among those detained by Chandigarh Police during the protest, according to the partys press release. AAP leaders and workers raised the slogan Vote Choro, Kursi Chhodo" and called for transparency in electoral rolls. - AAPs Big Guarantees For Goa Ahead Of Polls: Free Electricity And Bus Travel For Women, Rs. 10 Lakh Health Cover - Delhi HC Orders Virtual Hearings At Two Court Complexes Ahead Of CJP Protest - 35,000 Cops, Mass Detention Centres, High-Tech Body Cams: Delhi Police's Massive Plan For CJP Protest - CJP Protest in Delhi: More Than 200 People Detained, Security Tightened at Jantar Mantar | News18 Manish Sisodia Calls For CECs Resignation Addressing protesters, Sisodia said the demonstration was aimed at raising concerns over alleged electoral irregularities. He criticised the detention of protesters and maintained that people should be able to express their concerns about the electoral process. I am here to support the CJPs protest on behalf of the AAP, Arvind Kejriwal and CM Bhagwant Singh Mann. Our demand is clear: Gyanesh Kumar must resign," Sisodia said. He also questioned the outcome of the Delhi Assembly elections, citing alleged deletions from voter lists in the constituencies of AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal and himself. Sisodia claimed that 40,000 votes had been deleted from Kejriwals constituency, where he lost by around 4,000 votes. He further claimed that 28,000 votes had been deleted from his own constituency, where he lost by around 600 votes. AAP Raises Concerns Over Electoral Rolls Sisodia also raised concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the process had led to questions about voter registration and the deletion of names. Referring to Uttar Pradesh, where elections are due, he claimed that 13 lakh new votes had been added without the required forms being filled. He called for greater scrutiny of electoral rolls and accountability in the registration process. The allegations were part of the AAP leaders arguments in support of the demand for the CECs resignation. Harpal Singh Cheema Supports Youth Protest Punjab Cabinet Minister Harpal Singh Cheema also backed the protest, saying young people should be encouraged to participate in democratic processes and raise concerns about electoral transparency. Cheema criticised the detention of protesters and said Punjabs youth would continue to support democratic rights and the Constitution. He also expressed support for the demand for Gyanesh Kumars resignation, reiterating the partys position that concerns over the electoral process should be addressed. AAP Reiterates Demand For Transparency AAP Punjab said the right to vote was central to democracy and called for measures to ensure transparency in electoral rolls and protect voters rights. The party reiterated its support for the CJP-led movement and maintained that the allegations raised by protesters warranted attention. Its demand for the CECs resignation remained the central issue of the Chandigarh demonstration. The AAP held a protest in Chandigarh to support the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party movement, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged electoral irregularities, transparency concerns in electoral rolls, and controversial voter list deletions.

headline: Social Security $90 checks: Why Trump is sending extra money to millions of seniors
content: More than 20 million Americans enrolled in Medicare may be receiving an extra $90 from the Social Security Administration (SSA) this month as part of a rebate announced by US President Donald Trump's administration to help eligible seniors pay their Medicare Part B premiums. The one-time payment, announced by the White House in early October, is intended to provide financial relief to older Americans facing rising healthcare and household expenses. According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), approximately 20.8 million Americans qualify for the rebate. Most eligible beneficiaries are expected to receive the $90 payment through direct deposits, while those without direct deposit arrangements will receive paper checks by mail, according to the administration. The payments come less than a month before the November midterm elections, as rising costs for groceries, fuel and other essentials remain a major concern for American households. Trump's economic policies have also faced scrutiny amid voter dissatisfaction over affordability. Not every Medicare beneficiary is eligible for the payment. The administration has outlined specific criteria for receiving the rebate. To qualify, beneficiaries must live in the United States and must not receive Medicaid assistance to pay their Medicare premiums. Higher-income beneficiaries who pay an additional amount on top of the standard Medicare Part B premium are also excluded. People enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans are not eligible for the rebate. Eligible beneficiaries who want to check their status can contact Medicare at 1-800-633-4227. The $90 payment is intended to help cover Medicare Part B premiums, which pay for services such as doctor visits, outpatient treatment and preventive care. The standard monthly Part B premium is approximately $202 in 2026, meaning the rebate covers less than half of the monthly cost. The money is coming from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which Congress established in 2008 to support improvements to Medicare Parts A and B. Trump announced the initiative on his social media platform Truth Social, describing the payments as assistance for older Americans. My Administration will, immediately, begin sending 'Checks' of nearly $100 to over 20 MILLION wonderful Seniors to help pay for their Medicare Part B premiums, the president said. Trump also criticised the Medicare Improvement Fund, claiming that it had been misused by Democrats in Congress. In a separate part of his announcement, he said the Medicare payments were distinct from refunds being issued to Americans enrolled in the Affordable Care Act (ACA), commonly known as Obamacare. The president said his administration was fulfilling his pledge to protect Medicare and Social Security, while linking the payments to his broader economic agenda. The Medicare rebate is separate from another payment initiative announced by the Trump administration for certain ACA enrollees. The White House said it had begun sending one-time $500 refund checks to approximately one million Affordable Care Act enrollees whom the administration says were overcharged for their health insurance coverage. The payments began going out on September 30, with the initiative expected to cost nearly $500 million. The two programmes cover different groups of beneficiaries and have separate eligibility requirements. Trump has also proposed distributing $5,000 checks to Americans if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress following the November midterm elections. The proposal, referred to as a Trump Dividend, has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, although some Republican lawmakers have expressed support. Unlike the Medicare rebate and the announced ACA refunds, the $5,000 payments remain a proposal rather than an approved, broadly implemented payment programme. Questions remain about how the plan would be funded and administered. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, making the midterm elections significant for the administration's legislative agenda. The $90 rebate comes as the cost of living remains a central concern for American voters. Higher fuel and energy prices, alongside the economic consequences of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, have added pressure on household budgets. Trump is not personally on the ballot in November, but the elections will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress for the remainder of his term. The administration's payment announcements come against a backdrop of voter concerns about affordability and the President's handling of the economy.

content: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta accuses Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal of attempting to disrupt peace in the capital, alleging political motives behind their actions. headline: M K Stalin slams centre, TVK govt over detention of SIR protesters

headline: 'Are Protesters Chambal Dacoits? Real Dacoits Are In Parliament': Abhijeet Dipke's Parents On CJP Stir Crackdown
content: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained from an aircraft at Delhi airport ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys planned protest Following extensive preventive detentions across the national capital, the parents of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke issued a sharp public response regarding the scale of security measures used by authorities. Speaking with reporters in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, Dipkes parents questioned the intense law enforcement deployment activated in Delhi to prevent assemblies at Jantar Mantar. Questions Raised Over Scale of Police Force Addressing media representatives, Abhijeet Dipkes father, Bhagwan Dipke, raised sharp questions regarding the massive security presence deployed across the city to manage youth-led demonstrations. He expressed astonishment at treating university students and young civic campaigners like extreme security risks. "I dont understand why so much police force is deployed in Delhi? It is an agitation of students. Have dacoits from Chambal gathered in Delhi? Dacoits are sitting in Parliament," he said. Bhagwan Dipke maintained that peaceful public engagement remains a core aspect of civic participation. Addressing official statements regarding the lack of formal protest permissions, he argued that citizens naturally seek accountability from public institutions, asserting that constitutional mechanisms exist to balance public order with civic expression. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's parents issued a public response in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra. Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka were detained from an aircraft at Delhi airport. Abhijeet Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, questioned the massive security presence in Delhi. Dipke's mother, Anita Dipke, addressed the circumstances of her son's detention on a commercial aircraft. Law enforcement officials maintain strict measures are essential to prevent traffic paralysis and protect government installations. Mother Condemns In-Flight Custody Actions Echoing concerns over administrative proportionality, Dipkes mother, Anita Dipke, addressed the specific circumstances surrounding her sons detention. Detailing reports that law enforcement personnel boarded commercial aircraft to intercept campaign leaders before they entered arrival terminals, she questioned the necessity of high-intensity operations against non-violent student organisers. She contrasted the rapid deployment used during preventive transit operations with standard law enforcement procedures for major routine crimes. Stating that the family stands firmly behind their sons civic engagements, she urged authorities to distinguish between peaceful public advocacy and security threats. Security Protocol vs Civic Rights The familys remarks come amid the ongoing debate between security enforcement and constitutional protections as capital authorities continue managing large-scale public assemblies. Law enforcement officials maintain that strict measures, including drone monitoring and Section 163 BNSS restrictions, remain essential to prevent traffic paralysis, protect critical government installations, and maintain public order in sensitive zones. Despite administrative disruptions across key transit hubs, reactions from civil society and family members ensure that discussions surrounding student rights, procedural clearances, and the scope of police powers remain at the forefront of the capitals news cycle. Authorities enforced multi-tier police perimeters, road blockades, and metro access restrictions across Delhi to prevent assemblies and non-permitted gatherings at Jantar Mantar ahead of a planned Cockroach Janta Party protest.

headline: Delhi protest: Sonam Wangchuk warns of fresh fast if detainees not released
content: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday condemned the detention of student leaders and activists in New Delhi, calling the situation a state of undeclared emergency and warning of another fast unless the detenus are released. Several political leaders and protesters including Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav and Prashant Bhushan were detained in the national capital ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Wangchuk had expressed his inability to join the protests in Delhi on Friday. Adapting Faiz Sahabs words I would say Aur Bhi Gham Hain Zamaane Main Siyasat Ke Siva Rahaten aur bhi hain wasl ki raahat ke siva (There are sorrows in the world other than politics and governance, and comforts other than the joy of union with a beloved), he wrote on Friday, adding, Hence, I send my best wishes to all and urge the leaders of different groups to stay united and show statesmanship. Meanwhile, I urge all the Gen Z friends to once again stay absolutely peaceful at all costs. This was the gift of Baapu that I tried to bring to Jantar Mantar in June; I hope we wont let Baapu down. MUST READ: Thousands detained amid police crackdown: What happened in Delhi today Condemning Saturdays detentions, Wangchuk said he hoped the government would resolve the issues through dialogue. I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared Emergency. I was happy there were so many leaders to lead the movement, but I now learn that they have all been arrested. I hope those arrested will be released soon. I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast or Padyatra March if they are not released by tomorrow. Several youth leaders, MPs, journalists and activists were arrested in Delhi today. Yesterday, when I appealed for peace ahead of todays protests, I believed the worlds largest democracy would allow peaceful protests. But it now feels like an undeclared emergency. I condemn this in the strongest terms. If the detainees are not released within 24 hours, I will consider another peaceful protest, whether a hunger strike, sit-in or protest march, in Leh or Delhi. I hope these issues are resolved before we take these steps, he said in a video. Wangchuk was at the forefront of the June protests at Jantar Mantar, where he went on a fast demanding the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. His fast drew support from students, activists and opposition leaders, bringing wider attention to the agitation. On July 18, authorities took Wangchuk to hospital, citing health concerns, on the 21st day of his fast. The move came ahead of a planned march to Parliament on July 20. Pradhan resigned on July 25, after weeks of protests and mounting pressure over the examination controversy.

headline: Sharjeel Imam Flouted Bail Conditions, Says Delhi Court; Interim Bail Revoked
content: A Delhi court held that Sharjeel Imam violated the conditions of his interim bail by interacting with a media person during his temporary release to attend his cousins weddings. A Delhi court has held that Sharjeel Imam violated the conditions of his interim bail by interacting with a media person during his temporary release to attend his cousins weddings. A Delhi court on Saturday held that student activist Sharjeel Imam had violated the conditions imposed while granting him interim bail in the 2020 Northeast Delhi riots larger conspiracy case. The courts finding came while hearing a Delhi Police plea seeking cancellation of the interim bail granted to Imam. - Loved Drishyam 3? 7 Bollywood Thrillers On OTT That Deserve A Rewatch - Journalist Who Alleged Sexual Assault By Delhi Police Official Detained With 16 Others Over FIR Demand - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured - Delhi Braces For Weekend: Barricades, Dry Days, Hotel Checks | Should You Step Out At All? The police had alleged that Imam interacted with a media person during the seven-day period for which he was released on interim bail. According to the police plea, a video circulating on social media showed Imam speaking to journalists, allegedly in breach of the condition that barred him from coming into contact with media persons. The plea was taken up by Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai at the Karkardooma Courts. The court had earlier granted Imam interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to enable him to attend the weddings of two of his cousins in Delhi and Bihar. The Among the conditions attached to the interim bail was a restriction on contacting people or witnesses connected with the case and a bar on using social media. Reports on the police application said the restriction also prohibited Imam from interacting with media persons, as reported by Live Law. The latest development came on the day Imam was scheduled to surrender before jail authorities. The Delhi court subsequently revoked his interim bail after finding a violation of the condition concerning contact with the media. Sharjeel Imam was arrested in January 2020 and is an accused in the larger conspiracy case relating to the February 2020 Northeast Delhi riots. The violence, which occurred amid protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act, left 53 people dead and hundreds injured, according to prosecution figures. Imam faces charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), among other provisions. His interim bail was granted specifically for attending his cousins weddings and was separate from his regular bail proceedings. A Delhi court revoked Sharjeel Imam's interim bail after finding that he violated conditions by interacting with a media person during his temporary release.

headline: 'Chilling reminder of Kashmir': Valley leaders liken Delhi clampdown to post-2019 restrictions
content: With several political leaders and protesters detained in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janata Partys planned protest, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and Peoples Democratic Party leader Mehbooba Mufti drew parallels with Kashmir, calling the scenes a chilling reminder of the Valley. Several political leaders and protesters including Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav and Prashant Bhushan were detained in the national capital ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Mufti compared the security and communication clampdown to Kashmir, stating: Todays Delhi is a chilling reminder of Kashmir after the unconstitutional abrogation of Article 370. People were locked in their homes, the internet was shut down, and an entire region was placed under siege. The BJP then brazenly claimed that nobody had protested. With Delhi under siege, trains halted, and roads to Jantar Mantar sealed, she added: They may repeat the same lie, claiming that nobody protested against Gyanesh Kumar. First crush the protest, then deny it ever happened. This is how enforced silence is passed off as consent. MUST READ: Thousands detained amid police crackdown: What happened in Delhi today Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah drew a similar comparison late Friday evening, saying the Kashmir model had been exported to Delhi amid stringent security measures ahead of Saturdays CJP protest. Central Delhi has been placed under a 24-hour mobile internet blockade from 10 pm Friday. [The] Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi. Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on New Jammu & Kashmir, Omar wrote on X, referring to J&Ks long history of internet shutdowns over security concerns, particularly in the Valley. Speaking to reporters in Delhi, where he had arrived for the INDIA bloc leaders meeting with President Droupadi Murmu, Omar said elections were the foundation of a democracy. If elections arent fair, then how is it a democracy? he said. Both Omar and Mufti were among several political leaders detained under the Public Safety Act during the 2019 lockdown. The Centre snapped internet, mobile, and telephone connections in J&K when it abrogated the erstwhile states special status under Article 370 on August 5, 2019, triggering the regions longest internet shutdown. 4G services were not fully restored until February 2021, while broadband and low-speed internet services on postpaid mobile phones were permitted earlier.

headline: Chennai Metro Phase 2: PM Modi to inaugurate Poonamallee-Vadapalani line today – Check stations, timings
content: The 15-km-long stretch has 11 elevated metro stations. It is part of Corridor 4 of Chennai Metro Phase 2, also known as the Yellow Line. The new metro service is expected to reduce travel time for commuters and make daily journeys easier.
