headline: 'Police picked us up without saying anything': Economist Jean Dreze detained from Jantar Mantar
content: Economist and activist Jean Dreze, along with some scholars and artists, was detained by Delhi Police on Saturday near Jantar Mantar after they gathered with posters to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Dreze, who is currently based in Jharkhand, was among four people who had gathered near Kerala House, close to Jantar Mantar. The others were filmmaker Aban Raza, scholar and researcher Paran Amitava, and scholar and artist Anjali S. We were standing there with posters and speaking to the media when the police picked us up without saying anything, Dreze said over the phone from Adarsh Nagar police station, where he was being held. He said the group reached the area early, but several others were unable to reach the protest site because roads were blocked. We thought we should make our presence felt. We were standing there with posters, speaking to the media and doing nothing. Then the police came and detained us, he said. Dreze said he had never witnessed such an incident before. He also questioned the extensive preventive measures taken ahead of the protest, including restrictions on movement that he said prevented people from reaching the venue. Dreze said he had left Jharkhand for Delhi two days earlier and reached the capital on Friday morning, just before train services were affected by cancellations. He said several trains, including those connecting Ranchi to other parts of the country, had been cancelled, making it difficult for people travelling to Delhi to attend the protest. He alleged that several people who had come to Delhi for reasons unrelated to the protest had also been detained. Around 30 to 35 such people were being held, and they belonged to working-class and minority communities. They have been mistreated and manhandled, he said. They took my phone and put me on a bus. They also broke my phone, he alleged. Gulfam, 24, who said he was from Hapur in Uttar Pradesh, said he was on his way to Bangla Sahib Gurdwara to perform seva when he was stopped by police. He said he was walking towards the gurdwara when police personnel directed him to take another route. After he stopped briefly near the protest site, he alleged, police personnel asked him where he was going and offered to show him the way. When he agreed to walk with them, he said, he was taken to a bus. Another man, Saurabh, 22, who said he was from Delhis Karol Bagh, said he was trying to reach New Delhi railway station after visiting a friend near R K Ashram when police personnel stopped him. He said he was told to board a bus and assured that he would be dropped off and released within 15 to 20 minutes after answering a few questions. His phone was taken, he alleged. It did not look as if the people being held had come for the protest. Some were going to eat, some were trying to get a ride. They were there for their own work, he said. Paran Amitava, a JNU scholar who had gathered near Kerala House, said the group had been holding posters and giving media interviews for only a few minutes when police personnel arrived. They did not tell us anything. They pushed us into a bus and tore our posters. Even inside the bus, they did not allow us to speak to the media, she said. Amitava said police personnel had initially taken the group to another police station before bringing them to Adarsh Nagar. She alleged that several people at the facility had their phones confiscated.

headline: NIA to probe 'larger conspiracy' in mid-air attack on pilot Smit Machchhar
content: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered an FIR into the mid-air attack on Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard flydubai flight 1073, with the Centre directing the agency to probe a larger conspiracy behind the incident in which an Omani first officer allegedly stabbed the captain in an attempt to hijack or crash the aircraft. The case was registered on Friday under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008, after the Centre said the matter carried grave national and international ramifications. According to the complaint, the information before the Centre states that Flight 1073 departed Dubai at 7.05 am on September 30, carrying 174 passengersmost of them Israelisand six crew members, with Captain Machchhar and an Omani first officer at the controls. At around 9.21 am, while flying near the JordanSaudi Arabia border, the aircraft dived rapidly and turned back into Saudi airspace, it said. According to the passengers accounts set out in the FIR, the first officer stabbed Captain Machchhar during the flight in an apparent attempt to hijack or crash the plane, before being overwhelmed and restrained by passengers and crew. The captain sustained deep cuts to his head and hands in the attack. Other flydubai pilots on board subsequently landed the aircraft safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, in Northwestern Saudi Arabia, at 10.45 am. The first officer was arrested by Saudi authorities following the landing, the complaint said. The FIR records that the information discloses the commission of offences against Machchhar, an Indian national, under the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967both scheduled offences under the NIA Act. The Centre said the gravity of the offence, its grave national and international ramifications, and the need to unearth a larger conspiracy required a thorough investigation by the NIA. The registration of the FIR marks the formal launch of the federal agencys investigation into the incident, which will examine whether the first officer acted alone or as part of some module, an official said.

headline: Bangla Sahib Becomes Protesters' Refuge, Then Sees Detentions As CJP Protest Draws Heavy Security
content: BJP MLA Vikram Singh, says she was detained near Bangla Sahib for sitting in a park, adding she is held at Keshav Puram police station. Any visuals from near Bangla Sahib? Getting troubling reports," an X user asked on Saturday. The replies soon pointed to the gurdwara, where protesters had sought shelter amid the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) Delhi demonstration, and where a BJP leaders daughter said she was held for sitting in a park. Visuals from the area showed protesters raising slogans near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, with a banner reading Scrap SIR; CEC Must Resign". - Delhi Traffic Chaos Ahead Of CJP Protest, Commuters Forced To Walk Amid Jams - Opinion | Guess Who Gains The Most From The Cockroach-Congress-AAP Street Show - Delhi Police Vs CJP At Jantar Mantar Again: Cops Ready With Facial Recognition Systems, Drones & Thousands Of Personnel - Delhi Turns Into A Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest: 35,000 Personnel, Metro-Rail Curbs, Internet Suspended | Protesters raise slogans near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib amid the anti-CEC protest in New Delhi on Saturday, October 10, 2026 @Cockroachisback @CJP_for_India Siyaram Susawat (@Siyaram_Susawat) October 10, 2026 Other footage appeared to show paramilitary personnel detaining demonstrators in and around the gurdwara premises. People detained from Bangla Sahib Gurudwara! Mohammed Faizan Shaikh (@king7851007) October 10, 2026 More than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Force personnel have been deployed, with barricades and spike strips in place, as the Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP protest seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Who Is The BJP Leaders Daughter Who Was Detained? Yashaswinee Raje Singh, daughter of former BJP MLA Vikram Singh, who represented Fatehpur Sadar in Uttar Pradesh, was among those detained. She posted a photo on X saying she had been detained near Bangla Sahib for sitting in a park" and was being held at Keshav Puram police station. detained near Bangla Sahib for sitting in a park. currently being held in Keshav Puram police station. Yashaswinee Raje Singh (@ywineethepooh) October 10, 2026 She gained prominence during the June-July student protests seeking then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhans resignation over alleged paper leaks, and had backed the CJP campaign at the time. What Happened At The Gurdwara? For many protesters, Bangla Sahib has long been a place of refuge, The Print reported. A 24-year-old demonstrator, who did not want to be named, said she has joined protests since she was 20, from the anti-CAA-NRC agitation to the farmers movement. Earlier, in July, the gurdwara had also sheltered student protesters demanding Dharmendra Pradhans resignation as Union education minister, The Print noted. Protesters took shelter at the gurdwara overnight after citywide restrictions were announced on October 9, ready to join Saturdays demonstration. The young protester said she and others had been at the gurdwara since 9 am. After finding Jantar Mantar barricaded, they came back here", she told the publication, raising slogans intermittently and dispersing whenever police appeared. At around 1 pm, the report stated, Delhi Police personnel arrived in large numbers from behind the gurdwara walls and took away demonstrators gathered at the entrance. Slogans of Inquilab Zindabad" and Jai Bhim" rang through the lane, and within 10 minutes the protesters had been detained. What About Devotees And Gurdwara Itself? On X, a user said police had reached the gurdwara to detain young people and questioned the sanctity of a place of worship. Another posted a map showing blocked roads around the shrine, hoping devotees would face no trouble in visiting. Yet another described Bangla Sahib as the sole haven" for protesters. Not everyone agreed: one user cautioned against using sacred places for political ends. What Does The Wider Picture Look Like? Jantar Mantar, the intended focal point, was sealed off even to media personnel. Connecting roads were barricaded, while loudspeakers at three key entry-exit points warned against gatherings, processions and road blockades under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). According to The Print, more than 200 protesters had been detained so far and taken to makeshift detention centres, among them YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and the CJPs Ratna Singh. Dipke and spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained at Delhi airport as their flight from Mumbai landed. AISA national president Neha Bora was also detained after police blocked her march from Dilli Haat. The joint protest, called by the CJP and Left organisations and dubbed Jantar Mantar 2.0, also drew farmers from Haryana and Punjab. One from Sonipat told The Print that voters rights were on his mind. What Should Those Heading That Way Know? For devotees and commuters, the Delhi Traffic Police advisory warned that movement could be affected around the Jantar Mantar vicinity, listing diversion points that include the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout and the Jai Singh Road-Ashoka Road T-point. Commuters were asked to avoid non-essential travel and check live updates. Demonstrators took shelter at the gurdwara overnight after citywide restrictions were announced ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party protest calling for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

headline: From AAP Youth Leader To CJP's Frontman: Who Is Ajinkya Shinde, The Man Leading Jantar Mantar Protest?
content: Ajinkya Shinde, a former AAP worker from Maharashtra, has been tasked with leading the CJPs protest after founder Abhijeet Dipke and two senior leaders were detained. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has handed over the responsibility of leading its protest movement to Ajinkya Shinde after the detention of its founder, Abhijeet Dipke, and two other senior leaders. Shinde, a former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) worker from Maharashtra, will lead the partys agitation against alleged electoral illegalities until its detained leaders are released. - Ajinkya Will Lead Now: CJP Releases Abhijeet Dipkes Pre-Recorded Video Before Detention - CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Live: Arvind Kejriwal, Other AAP Leaders Detained Amid Clampdown On CJP Stir - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media - Being Pressured...: Abhijeet Dipke Says CJP Volunteers Getting Police Notices Ahead Of Delhi Protest The announcement came through a video shared on the CJPs official handle. In the video, Dipke said he, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had been arrested and asked supporters to follow Shindes leadership in their absence. If you are watching this video, it means that I, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka have been arrested. In our absence, Ajinkya will lead the protest and the CJP movement. Please follow him," Dipke said. Following the announcement, Shinde called on supporters to continue their march towards Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He urged them to protest at any location where the police stopped them. The government is scared of our unity. Please come to Jantar Mantar. If the police stop you, turn that very spot into Jantar Mantar," he said. Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained from the aircraft they arrived on from Mumbai earlier in the morning. The detentions came amid police efforts to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. Who Is Ajinkya Shinde? Ajinkya Shinde, 35, is a computer science graduate from Maharashtra who previously worked with an international IT company in Pune. He later left his corporate job to become a full-time worker with the Aam Aadmi Party. According to reports, Shindes parents were farmers in Alibaug before the family moved to Latur. He has been associated with Dipke for several years, with the two reportedly meeting in Goa in 2016. Since then, they have worked together on political activities. Before leaving his job, Shinde served as the AAPs convener in Pimpri-Chinchwad. After resigning, he spent a year working on the partys election campaign in Goa, although the AAP failed to win a seat there. He subsequently joined the AAPs Maharashtra team, taking up responsibilities as a social media coordinator and convener of the partys youth wing in the state, according to multiple reports. Shindes Role In The CJP In August, Dipke inducted Shinde into the CJPs national team and appointed him as the national organisation in-charge. However, his inclusion in the partys national executive committee also attracted criticism. Two volunteers from Gujarat accused Dipke of favouring people close to him while making appointments within the organisation. Within the CJP, Shinde is considered a senior figure, ranking below Dipke, Ranka and Das. The three leaders had been among the partys prominent faces during the paper leak protests in July this year. His appointment to lead the movement following the detention of the top leadership reflects his position within the organisation. Shinde is now expected to steer the CJPs protest campaign while Dipke, Das and Ranka remain in detention. Following the detention of founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) placed its protest movement under the leadership of Ajinkya Shinde.

headline: Can Foreign National Protest In India? What Law Says Amid 'German' Dhruv Rathee's Detention
content: Dhruv Rathees detention ahead of a Delhi protest has raised questions about whether foreign nationals can join political demonstrations in India. Here is what the law says YouTuber Dhruv Rathees reported detention in Gurugram ahead of a planned protest in Delhi has brought a legal question into focus: can a foreign national, including a German citizen, participate in political demonstrations in India? The development comes two days after Rathee joined an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Bengaluru on October 8. Former Bengaluru Police Commissioner and BJP leader Bhaskar Rao has since approached the Union Home Ministry, seeking verification of Rathees citizenship, passport, immigration status and compliance with visa conditions. Rathee was among several people reportedly detained ahead of a demonstration planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi on October 10. The protest was organised around demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commissions revision of electoral rolls. - VanDyke, Cybercrime, Hawala: India Tightens Rules To Blacklist Foreign Nationals | Exclusive - VanDyke, Cybercrime, Hawala: India Tightens Rules To Blacklist Foreign Nationals | Exclusive - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured - DELHI OCT 10 PROTEST | Supreme Court Urges Continuation Of Train Services Amid Planned Protests The reported detention and the demand for an immigration inquiry have raised questions about the rights of foreign nationals in India, the conditions attached to their visas and the extent to which they can participate in political activity. Does The Constitution Allow Foreigners To Protest In India? The Constitutions fundamental rights provisions draw an important distinction between Indian citizens and other people residing in the country. Article 19 guarantees citizens the right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a), and the right to assemble peacefully and without arms under Article 19(1)(b). These specific protections are available to Indian citizens, not foreign nationals solely by virtue of being in India. However, this does not mean that foreigners are outside the protection of the Constitution. Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to any person within India, while Article 21 protects the life and personal liberty of any person. Foreign nationals can invoke applicable constitutional protections, subject to the legal framework governing their presence in the country. The distinction is therefore between having the same fundamental right to protest as an Indian citizen and being subject to the law while participating in a public gathering. Foreign nationals do not have the same Article 19 entitlement, but their conduct and any action taken against them must still be assessed under applicable law. Jean Drze And Student Activists Picked Up At Jantar Mantar The distinction between a persons country of birth and their citizenship is also relevant in the case of economist and activist Jean Drze. Born in Belgium, Drze became an Indian citizen in 2002. He is therefore not an example of a foreign national participating in a protest while in India. In Delhis Jantar Mantar, Drze and other student activists were reportedly picked up shortly after they began their demonstration. Recalling the incident, one account stated: We witnessed a rare moment of protest inside fortress Jantar Mantar: the economist and activist Jean Dreze and other student activists picked up moments after they began their protest." We witnessed a rare moment of protest inside fortress Jantar Mantar: the economist and activist Jean Dreze and other student activists picked up moments after they began their protest. Sreenivasan Jain (@SreenivasanJain) October 10, 2026 Drzes case highlights why it is important to establish a persons actual citizenship before drawing comparisons with foreign nationals such as German YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. Being born abroad does not, by itself, mean that a person remains a foreign citizen, and the legal position of an Indian citizen participating in a protest differs from that of a foreign national whose activities may be subject to visa conditions. Can A Foreign National Face Action For Joining A Political Protest? A foreign nationals participation in a demonstration can raise questions about whether the activity is permitted under the conditions of their visa or other authorisation to stay in India. The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, which came into force on September 1, 2025, provides the current statutory framework for immigration and the regulation of foreign nationals. Visa conditions and other applicable rules can restrict the activities a foreign national may undertake in India. The legality of a particular persons participation depends on the relevant facts, including their immigration status, the conditions attached to their permission to enter or remain in India, and the nature of the activity. It would therefore be inaccurate to conclude that every foreign national who attends a protest has automatically violated the law. Authorities may investigate suspected breaches of visa or immigration conditions. Depending on the applicable provisions and the findings, consequences can include cancellation of permission to stay or removal from the country. Any such outcome depends on the circumstances and the relevant legal process. What Happened During The CAA Protests? There is a precedent for foreign nationals facing immigration action after participating in political demonstrations in India. During the 2019-2020 protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, several foreign nationals faced questioning or were asked to leave India over alleged breaches of visa rules. In December 2019, Norwegian tourist Janne-Mette Johansson was asked to leave India after participating in an anti-CAA march in Kochi. In March 2020, the Union government told Parliament that five foreign nationals had been asked to leave the country for participating in anti-CAA protests in violation of visa norms. These cases demonstrate that participation in a political demonstration can have immigration consequences for a foreign national. They do not, however, establish that every form of protest participation by a foreigner is automatically illegal; the applicable visa rules and individual circumstances remain relevant. Why Has Bhaskar Rao Sought An Inquiry Into Dhruv Rathee? In a representation to the Union Home Ministry, Bhaskar Rao sought verification of Rathees citizenship and nationality, the passport he used to enter India, the category of visa or other permission under which he was staying, and the duration and stated purpose of his visit. Rao also asked the ministry to examine whether Rathee had participated in political demonstrations during earlier visits to India, as reported by Aaj Tak. He sought legal action if an investigation established violations of the applicable immigration law, visa conditions or other rules. The request followed Rathees participation in an anti-SIR demonstration at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on October 8. The event, described as a peoples tribunal, was organised by civil society groups and the CJP to oppose the revision of electoral rolls. Actor-activist Prakash Raj and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke were also present. Rathee criticised the Election Commission over transparency and accountability during the protest. The demand for an inquiry into his immigration status has since brought his participation under scrutiny. The representation by Rao is a request for verification and investigation; it is not, by itself, proof that Rathee has violated any law. Nor does the available reporting establish that his reported detention ahead of the Delhi demonstration was officially ordered because he is believed to hold German citizenship. So, Can A German Citizen Protest In India? The short answer is that a German citizen does not enjoy the same fundamental right to freedom of speech and peaceful assembly under Article 19 as an Indian citizen. Foreign nationals must also comply with the immigration rules and conditions governing their stay. But the legal position is not simply that foreigners can never attend a protest. Whether a particular foreign nationals participation breaches the law depends on their immigration status, the applicable visa conditions and the circumstances of the event. In Rathees case, the immediate issues are his reported detention ahead of the Delhi protest and Raos request for an investigation into his citizenship and visa status. Until the relevant authorities establish the facts and identify any applicable violation, the request for an inquiry should not be treated as a finding of wrongdoing. Foreign nationals do not enjoy the same fundamental rights to freedom of speech and peaceful assembly under Article 19 as Indian citizens. While they are protected by other constitutional provisions like equality before law and personal liberty, their participation in political demonstrations must comply with the immigration rules, visa conditions, and laws governing their stay in India.

headline: Flydubai Incident: NIA Invokes Anti-Hijacking Act, UAPA Over Mid-Air Cockpit Attack | Exclusive Details
content: The NIA intends to investigate the larger conspiracy behind the attack, including the possibility of an attack on India and how the plot was planned, according to sources. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered an FIR over the Flydubai incident, where an Omani pilot attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar and attempted to crash the Israel-bound plane. The NIA has registered the FIR under Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016 and relevant sections of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act to investigate the conspiracy. The FIR includes Sections 16, 18, and 20 of the UAPA to investigate potential lone-wolf terror motives, conspiracy and radicalisation networks behind the attack. Sources told CNN-News18 that the NIA intends to investigate the larger conspiracy behind the hijacking attempt, including the possibility of an attack on India and how the plot was planned. - Captain Smit Machchhars Heroic Fight: How Passengers Helped Stop Flydubai Attack | News18 - 'His Positive Spirit Is A Huge Boost': Captain Smit Machchhar Eager To Return To Skies After Attack - 'Co-Pilot Got Up To Pray, Then Hit Me On The Head': Smit Machchhar Reveals New Details Of Flydubai Incident - A Pilot's Surname, A Protest Party's Name: How A Pune Poster Turned Two Insects Into A Row Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who is currently in Dubai, averted a major disaster" after he was stabbed by his co-pilot inside the cockpit of a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday. Despite suffering serious injuries, the Indian pilot managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The NIA action provides India with a legal basis to investigate and prosecute foreign-soil offences when an Indian citizen is targeted in an act of air piracy under the Anti-Hijacking and special NIA mandates. Indian Agencies Given Full Legal Rights According to sources, Indian agencies have been given full rights to investigate the incident, as an Indian pilot was attacked. Hammam Al-Hammami has been named as the prime suspect in the case. Captain Machchhar was directly assaulted during the hijacking attempt. As such, Indian agencies now have full legal rights to register a case and request mutual legal assistance from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Investigators are probing the suspects background for links to extremist networks, digital footprint and ideological motivation to determine whether the attack was pre-planned or backed by an overseas terror entity. NIA source leaks indicated that the agency is seeking access to the aircrafts Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) Flight Data Recorder (FDR), and the suspects electronic devices through formal diplomatic and international police channels. What Happened? On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai Flight 1073 experienced a hijacking attempt when the Omani co-pilot attacked Captain Machchhar with an emergency crash axe before attempting to sabotage the controls. The incident sent the aircraft into a sudden, steep descent from 33,000 feet. Despite suffering serious injuries, Captain Machchhar triggered the electronic cockpit door override, enabling passengers and off-duty crew members to rush in and subdue the attacker. The plane turned back into Saudi airspace and landed safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, where the suspect was arrested. The National Investigation Agency registered an FIR under Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act of 2016 and relevant sections of the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, specifically Sections 16, 18, and 20, to investigate potential lone-wolf terror motives and larger conspiracies.

headline: Mettur dam level falls below 65 feet
content: The water level in the Stanley Reservoir in Mettur fell below 65 feet and stood at 64.79 feet, against its full reservoir level (FRL) of 120 feet, at 8 a.m. on Saturday (October 10, 2026). According to Water Resources Department officials, the storage was 28.38 tmc ft, against the reservoirs full capacity of 93.47 tmc ft. The inflow was 1,021 cusecs, while 15,000 cusecs was released into the Cauvery for delta irrigation. No water was released through the canal. The reservoir received 0.4 mm of rainfall. Water was not released for delta irrigation on the customary date of June 12 this year owing to the low storage level and delayed monsoon. It was subsequently released on September 1 for 45 days, until October 15. With the water level declining and inflow remaining low, officials said the release for delta irrigation might not be extended beyond the scheduled date.

headline: 'Flop Show Of Anarchists': BJP's Sambit Patra Says CJP Protest At Jantar Mantar Failed
content: BJP MP Sambit Patra said that Rahul Gandhi had failed to demonstrate the responsibility expected of someone seeking a high constitutional position. BJP national spokesperson and MP Sambit Patra described the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in Delhi as a flop show", accusing opposition leaders of spreading fake news and attempting to create anarchy over alleged electoral irregularities. Today, we witnessed the flop show of the anarchists," Sambit Patra said, claiming that attempts to create disturbances through arson and physical violence had failed. He described the developments as a victory of democracy over mobocracy". - Being Pressured...: Abhijeet Dipke Says CJP Volunteers Getting Police Notices Ahead Of Delhi Protest - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media - BJP vs INDIA Bloc News: Sambit Patras Anarchy Charge, Gyanesh Kumar Row | Oppositions Protests - Karnataka SIR Row : BJP Workers Detained Over Protest Against Form 7 FIRs | Gyanesk Kumar| News18 Sambit Patra also targeted Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee and West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee over their posts on X (formerly Twitter) concerning alleged irregularities during vote counting at Booth No. 109 in Rejinagar, West Bengal. Subsequently, the Chief Electoral Officer also tweeted that the figure was 1,109 registered voters. The claim that there were only 772 voters was false," Sambit Patra said. He said that the opposition leaders were aware that the claim was false but had continued to circulate it. Look at the Chief Electoral Officers tweet. He knows this is fake. Arvind Kejriwal, Abhishek Banerjee and Mamata Banerjee also know that it is fake. Yet, Kejriwal and his associates allegedly conspired to spread anarchy using fake news," he said. The BJP leader also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his meeting with the President of India, questioning why the opposition had not submitted evidence alongside its memorandum concerning alleged electoral irregularities. Rahul Gandhi does not even understand basic protocol. When you take a memorandum to the President of India, the President accepts the memorandum. This is the basic protocol of the Indian Constitution and Indian democracy," Sambit Patra said. He questioned the oppositions claim that the President had asked them to provide evidence at a later stage. But you said the President accepted it, and in the same breath, you are saying that the President asked you to provide evidence. Why didnt you take the evidence along with you?" he asked. Sambit Patra also referred to the Election Commissions invitation to political parties to participate in a hackathon to demonstrate alleged vulnerabilities in electronic voting machines (EVMs). When the Election Commission invites you to participate in a hackathon and challenges you to try tampering with EVMs, saying that if you can demonstrate it, they will make improvements to the machines, you disappear," he alleged. He added that the opposition had offered to submit evidence to the President later, questioning the purpose of the meeting if the supporting material was not presented at the time. Sambit Patra further said that Rahul Gandhi had failed to demonstrate the responsibility expected of someone seeking a high constitutional position. Sambit Patra also referred to the legal proceedings initiated by the Congress and other opposition-linked petitioners in the Supreme Court, alleging that they had sought facilities, including toilets and medical assistance, in connection with the protests. Why didnt they say that? They went to seek facilities for toilets, but why didnt they seek justice over the alleged theft of votes?" he said. The BJP MP also cited recent election results, claiming that the BJP and its allies had won all four seats whose results were declared the previous day. He referred to Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, as well as Puducherry, while discussing the electoral outcomes. Sambit Patra accused opposition leaders of dragging the President into a political dispute, saying the language used after their meeting at Rashtrapati Bhavan had brought a constitutional office into a political confrontation. CJP Founder Names Successor Before Detention Sambit Patras remarks came as CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police after officers boarded their flight from Mumbai as it landed in the national capital. The leaders had travelled to Delhi to lead a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Anticipating his detention, Abhijeet Dipke had released a pre-recorded video naming Ajinkya Shinde, the partys organisation in-charge, to lead the movement in the absence of its top leadership. If you are watching this video, it means that I, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been arrested. In our absence, Ajinkya will lead the protest and the CJP movement. Please follow him," Abhijeet Dipke said in the video shared on the partys X account. Shinde was designated to lead the protest until the detained leaders were released. BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra described the Cockroach Janta Party-led demonstration at Jantar Mantar as a flop show because he claimed attempts to create disturbances through violence failed, calling it a victory of democracy over mobocracy

headline: Delhi Traffic Chaos Ahead Of CJP Protest, Commuters Forced To Walk Amid Jams
content: Police searches at several locations and along key routes leading to the protest site have further contributed to congestion. Heavy security arrangements by the Delhi Police to prevent large gatherings ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest have led to severe traffic congestion in Central Delhi. The area is a key part of the security perimeter as the demonstration is scheduled to take place at Jantar Mantar. Despite advance advisories about traffic diversions, commuters travelling for work and other purposes continued to face difficulties due to the deployment of security personnel. - Delhi Police Vs CJP At Jantar Mantar Again: Cops Ready With Facial Recognition Systems, Drones & Thousands Of Personnel - Delhi Turns Into A Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest: 35,000 Personnel, Metro-Rail Curbs, Internet Suspended - CEC Protest Updates: Dipke To Land In Delhi At 9.30 AM On Saturday For CJP Protest - Delhi Police Use Spike Strips, Barricades To Restrict Movement Amid CJP Protest | Video The traffic disruptions come ahead of the CJPs fresh agitation at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged deliberate changes to Form 6 and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police searches at several locations and along key routes leading to the protest site have further contributed to congestion. While senior officials said they were taking steps to ensure the smooth movement of regular commuters, traffic in Central Delhi continued to move at a sluggish pace. The Delhi Traffic Police also issued an update on X, stating that vehicular movement around the General Post Office (GPO) on Baba Khadak Singh Marg remained affected. Traffic Update Traffic around GPO is affected on Baba Khadak Singh Marg, Ashok Road and from Pandit Manth Marg to Mahadev Road," the post read. Heavy traffic congestion was also reported at Kalindi Kunj on the Noida-to-Delhi route. In Seelampur, barricades and increased surveillance led to bumper-to-bumper traffic, while security checks further slowed movement. With commercial vehicles barred from entering the area, some commuters were forced to travel on foot. I have been walking from there. I have already walked nearly a kilometre. The traffic jam is so severe that I could not find a bus, so I had to walk. I need to go to the New Delhi" a local said. Police Say Diversions In Place To Ease Commuter Movement Dinesh Kumar Gupta, Additional Commissioner of Police (CP), Traffic Zone-II, said traffic personnel had been deployed across the area, with a focus on 30 key stretches. If any obstructions arise, we will implement proper diversions. We are fully facilitating the public to ensure they face no problems and are working to keep traffic regulated and flowing smoothly. Currently, traffic is moving smoothly, and we are patrolling the area; there are no issues at the moment. Should any diversions become necessary for any reason, we will manage the traffic flow accordingly If a blockade occurs due to a demonstration, our staff is deployed to implement proper diversions, and we are monitoring the situation personally" he said. Joint Commissioner of Police (Jt CP/HQ, Traffic) Sanjay Kumar Tyagi said certain roads in the New Delhi district had been diverted due to law and order considerations. He added that the police were making efforts to minimise inconvenience to commuters. Appropriate traffic advisories are being issued. Our entire staff is deployed at diversion points, guiding people on the alternate routes they can take to reach their destinations" he added. CJP Members Detained Ahead Of Protest The extensive security deployment has restricted protesters movement at several locations across Delhi. CJP members Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained from an aircraft after it landed at Delhi airport. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained from his residence in Gurugram. All four have reportedly been taken to different locations. Other detained protesters have been taken to Chhatrasal Stadium. The CJP said the demonstrations would continue nationwide despite the detentions, with or without leaders". In a video statement recorded inside the aircraft as police personnel entered, Abhijeet Dipke said, This is not something even Indira Gandhi did during the Emergency; this is a worse situation than that, and we are all prepared for arrest." Saurav Das alleged that the authorities were attempting to stall a constitutional movement through brute force. Heavy security arrangements and police deployment by the Delhi Police ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar led to severe traffic congestion. Barricades, increased surveillance, and checks along key routes further slowed vehicular movement.

headline: Woman says hung upside down in police custody, 2 Jharkhand cops suspended
content: Two policemen in Jharkhands Latehar have been suspended following an Adivasi womans allegations that she was assaulted and hung upside down in custody during questioning over alleged poppy cultivation. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has directed the police to take action in the matter. The 33-year-old woman alleged that she was assaulted by Bariyatu police station officer-in-charge Prabhat Kumar Das and other personnel on October 5 while grazing goats near Bagnadi Mahua in her village. According to her complaint, the policemen, who were in plain clothes, accused her of involvement in poppy cultivation and assaulted her. I was taken to the police station, tied up and hung upside down and beaten with sticks. They touch me inappropriately and forced green chillies inside my mouth, she said, adding that she was subjected to sexual harassment. Puniya further alleged that she was made to record a video statement before her release and asked to say that she was involved in poppy cultivation. I was threatened that my motorcycle and mobile phone would not be returned if I did not make the statement as instructed, she added. She also alleged that the police searched her house before taking her into custody and took away Rs. 80,000 in savings. Despite our home coming under the Herhanj police station limits, bada babu of another police station came and took me to that station to assault, she said. Taking cognisance of the allegations, Chief Minister Hemant Soren directed the Latehar police to take action in a post on X. The Latehar police subsequently said that Das and Constable Manish Kumar Ram, a CCTNS operator at Bariyatu police station, had been suspended and departmental proceedings initiated against them. According to the police, a joint inquiry team has been formed to investigate the complaint submitted by Puniya and other women. The complaint was also forwarded by the village head and the mukhiya. The police said that, according to preliminary findings, Das received information on October 5 that Puniyas husband, Mukesh Ganjhu, and another man were allegedly involved in the illegal sale of opium. A team was subsequently formed to conduct a raid near Bagnadi Mahua to verify the information and make arrests. The police claimed that Puniya was present at the spot along with her husband and Yadav, and that opium was allegedly found in her possession. According to the police, Puniya bit Constable Rams hand during the raid and snatched a packet of opium, handing it to Yadav, who allegedly fled with it. The police also acknowledged a procedural lapse, stating that the raid and recovery proceedings were conducted in the absence of a gazetted officer or magistrate, which it said was required under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The police said the allegations made by Puniya in her complaint were still being investigated and that the inquiry report was awaited.

headline: Vasan urges Tamil Nadu government to secure release of fishermen's boats from Andhra Pradesh
content: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) leader G.K. Vasan on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) urged the Tamil Nadu government to take steps to secure the release of the fishing boats of Tamil Nadu fishermen, which were recently confiscated by the Andhra Pradesh government. In a statement, Mr. Vasan said that seven fishing boats of fishermen from Tamil Nadu were confiscated by officials of the Andhra Pradesh government on June 16. They have not been released as yet, and it has affected the livelihood of the fishermen, he said. The Tamil Nadu government should hold talks with the Andhra Pradesh government to find a durable solution that would not affect the livelihood of fishermen from Tamil Nadu, the former Union Minister said. All-party meet on Cauvery Mr. Vasan, while speaking to reporters in Bhavani, Erode, expressed hope that the State government would convene an all-party meeting at an appropriate time to discuss the Cauvery water issue. He said the government had taken the right step by approaching the Supreme Court to secure the States share of Cauvery water. He also urged the DMK to effectively articulate the States concerns in Parliament on the proposed delimitation of constituencies. Strengthening of party Mr. Vasan, who was in Bhavani to attend a meeting of TMC(M) regional presidents from nine districts, said the party was strengthening its organisation in weaker areas and identifying constituencies where it had a good chance of winning in the upcoming local body elections. He urged the government to provide immediate electricity connections to the 50,000 farmers who had applied under the Tatkal scheme. He also called upon the Centre to act on the Chief Ministers request for linking the Godavari, Cauvery, and Gundar rivers. The State government should take steps to ensure that students receive education loans in full and increase Aavins milk procurement price, he said. Mr. Vasan said the Congress and like-minded parties had begun working together at the national and State levels.

headline: CPM condemns Centre's crackdown on CJP protesters, announces demonstrations across Tamil Nadu
content: The CPM on Saturday strongly condemned the Union governments crackdown, including the alleged siege of Left party offices and the detention of senior leaders on their way to participate in the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The protest demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Condemning the alleged assault on democratic rights and the detention of senior leaders and students, the party announced demonstrations at all district headquarters across Tamil Nadu. According to a post on X, the CJPs protest at Jantar Mantar received widespread support from various political parties, student groups and youth organisations. However, the Union government allegedly resorted to severe repressive measures, deploying Delhi Police and paramilitary forces. Left party offices were placed under siege, and protesters were prevented from gathering, the post claimed.Several senior Left leaders were detained while on their way to the venue. Those detained included CPM general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja, CPI(ML) leaders, Politburo members Pinarayi Vijayan and U Vasuki, Tamil Nadu state secretary P Shanmugam, and Central Committee member John Brittas. In what the party described as an attempt to intimidate protesters, Delhi Police allegedly kept the detained leaders, including former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, inside police vehicles and drove them around the capital for more than an hour without formally processing their detention.Strongly condemning the police action and what it described as the suppression of democratic dissent, the CPI(M) announced immediate demonstrations at all district headquarters across Tamil Nadu, demanding an end to the Union governments coercive measures.

headline: PM Modi to inaugurate 5 Amrit Bharat stations, dedicate Rs 750 crore rail projects in Tamil Nadu today
content: These railway projects, worth around Rs. 750 crore, is set to improve passenger facilities, strengthen rail connectivity and increase the capacity of the rail network in the state. The five redeveloped stations have been upgraded under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme at a total cost of over Rs. 70 crore. The 23-km Karaikal-Peralam railway line has been developed at a cost of more than Rs. 550 crore, while the three rail flyovers have been built for over Rs. 120 crore. Passengers to get modern facilities at these 5 Amrit Bharat stations According to SN Narain, Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO), Southern Railway, the five stations to be inaugurated are Ambasamudram, Palani, Namakkal, Paramakkudi and Vellore Cantonment. The redevelopment work includes improvements to station buildings, waiting areas, platforms, parking facilities and passenger information systems. The stations have also been equipped with facilities to improve accessibility for persons with disabilities, including ramps, lifts and accessible toilets at designated locations. - Ambasamudram railway station Located in Tirunelveli district on the Tirunelveli-Tenkasi section, Ambasamudram station has been redeveloped at a cost of Rs. 13 crore. The station serves as a rail gateway to tourist attractions such as Papanasam, Agasthiyar Falls and Manimuthar Falls and Dam, situated near the Western Ghats. The redevelopment includes a renovated station facade, a new entrance porch, covered parking, improved waiting halls and platform shelters. A new six-metre-wide foot overbridge, two lifts on the existing foot overbridge and upgraded passenger information systems have also been provided. Facilities for persons with disabilities include ramps with handrails, accessible toilets and booking counters. Redeveloped Ambasamudram railway station (Image: Southern Railway) Palani station in Dindigul district has been redeveloped at a cost of around Rs. 20 crore. Located on the Dindigul-Pollachi section, it serves as an important rail gateway for devotees visiting the Arulmigu Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple, one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan. The station attracts pilgrims throughout the year, particularly during festivals such as Thai Poosam and Panguni Uthiram. The redevelopment includes a renovated station building, a new entrance arch, covered parking, an upgraded waiting hall and toilet block, and improvements to the booking counter and concourse. A new six-metre-wide foot overbridge, lifts, platform shelters and passenger information systems have also been provided. Accessibility features and artwork reflecting local culture form part of the upgrades. Redeveloped Palani railway station (Image: Southern Railway) Namakkal station in Salem division has been redeveloped at a cost of Rs. 17 crore. Located on the SalemKarur section, it serves an important commercial and transport centre known for its temples, historic rock formations and access to the Kolli Hills. The station building has been renovated and expanded, with an improved entrance, waiting hall, executive lounge and two booking counters. The circulating area has been widened, and parking facilities for two-wheelers and four-wheelers have been improved. Platforms have been upgraded with tactile tiles, granite surfaces, shelters and LED lighting. A new six-metre-wide foot overbridge with lifts, passenger information displays and accessible facilities has also been provided. Redeveloped Namakkal railway station (Image: Southern Railway) - Paramakkudi railway station Paramakkudi station in Ramanathapuram district has been redeveloped at a cost of Rs. 14 crore. Located on the Madurai-Manamadurai-Rameswaram route, it serves as an important rail gateway for passengers travelling towards Rameswaram. The station is a key transport point for Paramakkudi, one of the districts major towns and commercial centres. The redevelopment includes an improved station facade, a new entrance arch, wider vehicle lanes, a separate pedestrian pathway and around 1,250 square metres of covered parking. A new waiting hall, upgraded toilets, an improved booking counter and concourse, and a new six-metre-wide foot overbridge are among the other additions. Lifts, upgraded platform surfaces, shelters and passenger information systems have also been provided. The project also incorporates local art and cultural elements. The improved connectivity and facilities are expected to benefit passengers and support the towns handloom sector. Redeveloped Paramakkudi railway station (Image: Southern Railway) - Vellore Cantonment railway station Vellore Cantonment station in Vellore city has been redeveloped at a cost of Rs. 8 crore. Located on the Katpadi-Villupuram section, the station serves passengers travelling for healthcare, education, tourism and business. The redevelopment includes an improved station facade, a new portico, an upgraded approach road, pedestrian pathways and better parking facilities. The waiting hall has been improved, with a reserved lounge and retiring room. Other additions include an upgraded booking office and concourse, a new toilet block and platform shelters. Redeveloped Vellore Cantonment railway station (Image: Southern Railway) Passenger amenities include coach guidance displays, train arrival and departure information boards, public announcement systems and digital clocks. Accessibility facilities have also been provided. Karaikal-Peralam railway line to boost connectivity The KaraikalPeralam new railway line will provide a direct rail link between Karaikal and the Mayiladuthurai-Tiruvarur railway corridor. It will improve connectivity for passengers travelling in the region. The project is also important for freight movement as it provides rail connectivity to Karaikal Port. This is expected to facilitate the movement of commodities such as coal, fertilisers and food grains to industries and markets. The new line is expected to support regional trade and economic activity while improving access to religious and tourist destinations, including the famous Saneeswarar Temple at Thirunallar. Three rail flyovers to ease congestion The Prime Minister will also dedicate three rail flyovers built at a total cost of over Rs. 120 crore. The projects are aimed at improving train movement, increasing line capacity and reducing congestion on busy railway routes. They are also expected to ease congestion at level crossings in Coimbatore and surrounding areas, reducing waiting times for road users and improving commuter safety. By allowing trains to move more smoothly, the flyovers will help improve the operational efficiency of the railway network.

headline: 'Annadata' Foundation Of UP's Economic Strength And Prosperity: CM Yogi Adityanath
content: The chief minister said irrigation projects that had remained pending for decades had been completed. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday highlighted the changes in the states agricultural sector since 2017, describing farmers, or annadatas, as the foundation of its economic strength and prosperity. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Yogi Adityanath said the double-engine government, under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was ensuring facilities for farmers from seed to market. - Uttar Pradesh Has Become A 'Swastha Pradesh-Saksham Pradesh': CM Yogi - 'Producer Of Technology': Yogi Adityanath Showcases Uttar Pradesh's Progress To People Of State - Yogis 80-20 Jibe At Akhileshs Election Math: 'UP Rajya Sabha Contest Sets Tone For Assembly Polls' - Noida International Airport Renamed Narendra Modi International Airport, UP Cabinet Approves Proposal He said that before 2017, farmers were burdened with debt and distress and had to run from pillar to post to deal with middlemen. The situation had changed, he said, citing access to improved seeds, irrigation facilities, minimum support price (MSP) payments through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and the PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi scheme. The chief minister said irrigation projects that had remained pending for decades had been completed. He also highlighted Uttar Pradeshs contribution to the countrys foodgrain production, stating that the state accounts for 21 per cent of the national total. The states agricultural growth rate had risen from 8 per cent to 18 per cent, Yogi Adityanath said, adding that Uttar Pradesh ranked first in the country in the production of milk, sugarcane and wheat, among other agricultural commodities. Over Rs. 1.03 Lakh Crore Paid To Farmers For Paddy Procurement Highlighting the governments efforts to ensure remunerative prices for farmers, Yogi Adityanath said more than 519 lakh metric tonnes of paddy had been procured from over 80 lakh farmers in Uttar Pradesh between 2017 and March 2026. Payments exceeding Rs. 1,03,833 crore were made directly to farmers, he said. The chief minister added that the minimum support price for paddy had been increased by Rs. 71 per quintal this year, reiterating the governments commitment to supporting farmers. Yogi Adityanath said protecting farmers rights and ensuring their prosperity remained among the highest priorities of the states double-engine government, describing them as central to Uttar Pradeshs economic strength and development. Between 2017 and March 2026, over 519 lakh metric tonnes of paddy were procured from more than 80 lakh farmers in Uttar Pradesh, with payments exceeding Rs. 1,03,833 crore made directly to them.

headline: Detained At Delhi Airport, Mourning At Home: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke Loses Grandmother Before Protest
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was reportedly held at Delhi airport as his grandmother died in Maharashtra. His father has also questioned the legal basis. As Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke reached the national capital for Saturdays protest at Jantar Mantar, grief struck his family back home in Maharashtra: his grandmother died this morning after a long illness. Dipke and his colleagues were reportedly detained by Delhi Police on landing at the airport. The CJPs protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 targets the alleged misconduct of the Election Commission, with youths from across the country converging there. Dipke, who is leading the agitation, and his associates were taken into custody as they arrived at Delhi airport. While he was in police custody, the news from home arrived: his grandmother had passed away. - CJPs Dipke Says Jantar Mantar March Must Continue Even If He Is Detained, Shares Delhi Arrival Time - I Am Not Afraid Of You: High Drama On Plane As Cops Detain Abhijeet Dipke Ahead Of CJP Protest | Video - Protesters Cant Inconvenience Public Everywhere: Passenger On Abhijeet Dipkes Detention From Flight - Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka Detained From Plane At Delhi Airport Ahead Of CJP Protest Where Did Dipkes Grandmother Pass Away? Dipkes native village is Santuk Pimpri in Maharashtras Hingoli district, and his grandmother breathed her last there this morning. His family lives in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, having moved there for his fathers job, but she had stayed on in the ancestral village. She had been unwell for the past few days. Who Has Been Detained Before The Protest? Before the agitation began, Delhi Police detained Dhruv Rathee, Tushar Gandhi, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. The CJP has condemned the police action. What Has Dipkes Father Said? Dipkes father reacted angrily to his son being detained from a flight. Taking someone who raises his voice for the nations interest off a plane, he said, goes against democracy. Asking whether terrorists and drug smugglers escape attention, he demanded that the agencies concerned explain under which law Dipke was detained from the aircraft. He also claimed it was the first time in history that a student had been detained in this manner. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) organized a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 to target the alleged misconduct of the Election Commission and to call for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: 'Undeclared Emer-GenZ': Shashi Tharoor Slams Centre Over Extensive Curbs In Delhi, CJP Leaders' Detention
content: Tharoor, an MP from Thiruvananthapuram, pointed out what he described as a "war-like deployment" of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the capital Congress MP Shashi Tharoor questioned the Central Government over the extensive security measures and restrictions rolled out in Delhi in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row. Tharoor, an MP from Thiruvananthapuram, pointed out what he described as a war-like deployment" of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the capital. He also expressed concern over the cancellation of 250 trains and suspension of metro services. - 'Spectacular Act Of Self-Emasculation': Tharoor Warns Election Boycott Will Make Opposition Irrelevant - 'Horrified, Disgraceful': Tharoor Condemns Govt Over Rahul Gandhi's Detention At EC March - All Routes To Jantar Mantar, ECI Office Barricaded As Security Beefed Up Ahead Of INDIA Bloc Sit-In - CJP Protest Today: Delhi Traffic Diversions From 6 AM, Check Affected Roads And Alternate Routes I returned to the national capital after 2 am and have rarely seen anything like what Delhi is witnessing now, with checkpoints every few hundred metres, concrete barriers and spike strips laid across our roads, a war-like deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the city, 250 trains cancelled and 45 metro stations closed, and reports of young people being detained from their own homes and the streets in and around Delhi all to prevent citizens from peacefully raising questions about the integrity of our elections", wrote the Congress leader. News18 Also Covered: CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Live I returned to the national capital after 2 am and have rarely seen anything like what Delhi is witnessing now, with checkpoints every few hundred metres, concrete barriers and spike strips laid across our roads, a war-like deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the city, 250 trains cancelled and 45 metro stations closed, and reports of young people being detained from their own homes and the streets in and around Delhi all to prevent citizens from peacefully raising questions about the integrity of our elections. Most regressive (as well as repressive) is the suspension of the internet in the heart of the national capital.Freedom of movement stands completely shackled. Jantar Mantar was designated precisely so that citizens could voice dissent in the centre of Delhi, and today even the roads leading to it have been declared out of bounds. One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection. Those detained will hvre to be released .And if the protesters simply return on Monday, will the authorities lock down the national capital all over again? Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ. A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress. The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression. Barricades will do nothing to restore faith in the Election Commission, and the sooner it answers the publics questions, the sooner calm will be restored. The strength of a democracy is measured by how it treats those who question its working, and by that measure, what we have seen today is utterly shameful and unconscionable. @INCIndia Shashi Tharoor (@ShashiTharoor) October 10, 2026 Shashi Tharoor highlighted that freedom of movement is restricted, with roads leading to Jantar Mantar standing closed. Most regressive (as well as repressive) is the suspension of the internet in the heart of the national capital. Freedom of movement stands completely shackled. Jantar Mantar was designated precisely so that citizens could voice dissent in the centre of Delhi, and today even the roads leading to it have been declared out of bounds", he said. Questioning the detention of CJP members, Tharoor continued: One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection. Those detained will have to be released. And if the protesters simply return on Monday, will the authorities lock down the national capital all over again? Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ." A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress. The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression. Barricades will do nothing to restore faith in the Election Commission, and the sooner it answers the publics questions, the sooner calm will be restored. The strength of a democracy is measured by how it treats those who question its working, and by that measure, what we have seen today is utterly shameful and unconscionable", he said. CJP Members Detained At IGI Airport CJP members, including Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport as soon as their flight landed. The three leaders have been taken to an undisclosed location. A CJP member told CNN-News18 that they were not able to contact them and that they were decentralised". We have been decentralised. Our founder and co-convener have been detained. We dont know where to go now. We are not able to contact our members. We do not know whats happening", said the person. Authorities deployed 22,000 police and paramilitary personnel across Delhi, set up checkpoints every few hundred metres with concrete barriers and spike strips, suspended internet services in the city center, cancelled 250 trains, and closed 45 metro stations.

headline: Shashi Tharoor slams Delhi crackdown on CJP protest, calls it an 'undeclared Emer-GenZ'
content: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Saturday criticised the security restrictions imposed across Delhi amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. He described the arrangement in the national capital as as unprecedented and likening it to an undeclared Emer-GenZ. In a strongly worded statement, Tharoor flagged checkpoints every few hundred metres, concrete barriers and spike strips laid across our roads, a war-like deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the city, 250 trains cancelled and 45 metro stations closed, and reports of young people being detained from their own homes and the streets in and around Delhi. Tharoor particularly criticised the suspension of internet services in parts of the national capital, calling it one of the most regressive and repressive measures. Quick answers to key questions 5 QUESTIONS 1Why was the CJP protesting at Jantar Mantar? The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) organised the protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Protesters raised allegations of voter-list irregularities and called for Kumars resignation. 2Why did Delhi Police impose restrictions ahead of the CJP protest? Delhi Police cited law-and-order concerns, public safety, traffic management and the need to protect local residents. It also said Jantar Mantar has limited capacity and denied permission for the planned demonstration. 3What did Shashi Tharoor say about the Delhi crackdown on the CJP protest? Tharoor described the restrictions as an undeclared Emer-GenZ and criticised the barricades, security deployment, transport disruptions and internet curbs. He said those detained should be released and urged the government to answer protesters concerns. 4Were CJP protesters detained ahead of the Jantar Mantar demonstration? Yes. The reports said several demonstrators were detained, including CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke and others. CJP also said content creator Dhruv Rathee had been detained. 5How did security restrictions affect travel in Delhi during the CJP protest? Restrictions included closures at many metro stations, train cancellations, traffic checks and limits on movement around Jantar Mantar. Internet services were also restricted in parts of the area. Freedom of movement stands completely shackled, he said, questioning why authorities had restricted access to Jantar Mantar, a designated site for citizens to express dissent. He also questioned whether the government would impose similar restrictions if protesters returned on Monday, and called for those detained to be released. A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress, Tharoor said. He urged the government to provide answers to protesters concerns rather than resort to force, adding that barricades would not restore public faith in the Election Commission. The criticism came as security was tightened across Delhi ahead of the CJP-led protest against the Election Commission. Earlier in the day, CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke, who was travelling from Mumbai to Delhi to participate in the demonstration, claimed in an Instagram video that police were detaining him and his associates as they disembarked from their flight at Delhi airport. The organisation also claimed that content creator Dhruv Rathee had been detained, posting that the government was TERRIFIED of young people who question its wrongdoings and refuse to stay silent. Police said the New Delhi district had been divided into 20 operational zones, with dedicated detention centres established for each zone as part of the security arrangements. Several demonstrators were detained after gathering at Jantar Mantar and Sansad Marg, amid extensive barricading and heightened security at entry points to the national capital. According to the details provided, 46 metro stations remained closed as security personnel were deployed at multiple locations across the city.

headline: Russian attack on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia kills seven, governor says
content: Seven people were killed by a Russian attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday (October 10, 2026) morning, the regional governor said, as rescuers searched for more people under the rubble. Ten others were wounded in the attack, which the governor Mykhailo Semikin said hit several locations at once in the early hours of Saturday (October 10).

headline: CJP Protest at Jantar Mantar: Why is Delhi under 'shut down'? How police explained strict curbs amid criticism
content: The Delhi Police defends the move to impose strict restrictions in the wake of the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday. On Friday, police issued a statement titled, "What is the rationale for the restrictions being put in New Delhi?." The statement came as the Centre drew criticism for "shutting down" Delhi ahead of the massive demonstration, likely to be attended by several political parties. More than 200 trains were cancelled, 45 Delhi metro stations were shut, and mobile internet services were also restricted in areas around Jantar Mantar on Saturday. The protest on October 10 was organised to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar amid allegations of irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Exercise (SIR) of the electoral roll. Quick answers to key questions 1Why did the CJP organise a protest at Jantar Mantar? The CJPs October 10 protest opposed the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities. 2Why did Delhi Police impose strict restrictions before the CJP protest? Police cited safety and law-and-order concerns, pointing to violence and injuries during a previous Jantar Mantar protest. It also said the site can accommodate only about 1,000 people and that restrictions would help manage crowds and traffic. 3What restrictions were imposed in Delhi ahead of the CJP protest? Authorities restricted entry and exit at 45 metro stations, cancelled more than 200 trains and limited mobile internet services around Jantar Mantar. Police also set up barricades and checks in parts of the city. 4Did Delhi Police grant permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar? No. Delhi Police denied permission, citing possible law-and-order concerns and inconvenience to residents. It also said the CJP communication was an intimation rather than a formal application for permission. 5What did the Supreme Court say about transport restrictions during the CJP protest? The Supreme Court directed the Centre to ensure there was no complete prohibition on metro and train movement to Delhi on October 10. A contempt plea later alleged that station closures and transport restrictions continued despite the direction. In a sharp post on X shortly before boarding his flight at the Mumbai airport on Saturday, Dipke wrote that the shutdown of Delhi and "crackdown" on supporters were "not signs of strength", but of a leader terrified of his own people. He posted, [PM Narendra] Modi has accepted defeat even before our protest has begun. The mass crackdown on protesters and the shutdown of Delhi are not signs of strength, but of a leader terrified of his own people." Left parties also condemned restrictions imposed ahead of the October 10 protest and demanded that the Delhi Police allow protesters to assemble at Jantar Mantar. CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby said that barricading and the deployment of security personnel were creating an atmosphere of intimidation. CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said with trains cancelled and metro services stopped, the government has "laid a siege around themselves and turned the whole of Delhi into a huge police camp or paramilitary cantonment". He said, "Meanwhile, the CJI has advised the government not to use a hammer to kill a fly! Does that leave room for using hammers for cockroaches?" He questioned, Has independent India ever witnessed such fear of democracy and peaceful mass protest? The issue even reached the Supreme Court. A plea filed in the court on Saturday alleged that authorities continued with the closure of metro stations in Delhi despite the Supreme Court's October 9 direction. The Supreme Court had directed the Centre to ensure that there was no "complete prohibition" of the movement of metro and trains coming to Delhi on October 10 due to the protest. The plea filed on Saturday sought initiation of contempt proceedings against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan IAS, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar IPS and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara IAS for allegedly wilfully disobeying the Court's directions, according to Live Law. The Delhi Police cited the events of the July 20 protest, organised by the CJP over irregularities in the NEET examination and students' deaths, to justify the imposition of strict curbs ahead of the protest on October 10. Police said the proactiveness stems from "what happened last time in July protests at Jantar Mantar". They said in a statement posted on X, "Permission was taken for a one-day protest at Jantar Mantar, but it continued for a month. More than 200 police personnel were injured. More than 2000 persons having criminal antecedents came to those protests, contributing to the violence. As the situation went out of control, there were clashes, and innocent students were injured too." "Now, the same group wants to gather at the same place again," police said. "Given that experience, permission cannot be given without addressing how safety will be ensured. Already, in the past week, women constables of Delhi Police have been molested and assaulted by those protesting at Jantar Mantar. That is deeply troubling, and it has to be taken seriously," the statement claimed. "Nobody wants to see that happen again. The people who come to a protest, the police personnel on duty and the people passing through the area all need to be safe," police said in its statement. Police said people have the right to protest, but at the same time, "important establishments and the offices of the constitutional bodies are in New Delhi." "People living and working in Delhi should be able to go about their day safely too. Delhi police have a responsibility towards all of these," police said. The Delhi Police also highlighted a "practical issue". They said Jantar Mantar is a small area that can accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. "Delhi is a small city-state, and there are limits to how many people a particular location can safely accommodate. Delhi being capital of the fastest growing economy of the country cannot be brought to halt every time there are protests. Delhi Police has to look after well-being of citizens and economic interests alongside the interests of those who want to protest," police added. "Balancing these responsibilities requires planning, and that planning starts with organisers seeking permission and sticking to them. Seeking permission to protest is not anti-democratic.
