headline: Caste discrimination during SC man's burial: Commission seeks report from Erode Collector, SP
content: The Tamil Nadu State Commission for Adi Dravidar and Tribal Communities has directed the Erode Collector and the Superintendent of Police (SP) to submit a detailed report by October 30, 2026, on the alleged caste discrimination during the burial of a Scheduled Caste (SC) man at Perumbali village near Perundurai. In a notice issued on Friday (October 9), the Commission said it had taken note of video footage of the incident published as newspaper reports and circulated on television and social media, as well as petitions submitted by representatives of various organisations. What happened? Chenni, a resident of Perumbali, died of age-related ailments on October 5. According to the notice, members of another community, a dominant caste in the village, allegedly objected to the burial of his body in the villages public cemetery, claiming that a person belonging to a Scheduled Caste community should not be buried there. The Commission said an argument broke out when the deceased mans relatives maintained that the public cemetery was open to people of all communities. Members of the other community allegedly insisted that they fall at their feet as a condition for allowing the burial. Subsequently, two members of the SC community allegedly fell at their feet in the presence of police and Revenue Department officials. Expressing concern over the alleged failure of the officials to intervene, the Commission said the incident raised serious human rights concerns. It observed that the obstruction of the burial was illegal and that the alleged acts attracted provisions of the Constitution and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The Commission directed the Collector and the Superintendent of Police to take appropriate action against those involved under the Act and submit a detailed report by October 30. It also sought a report on disciplinary action taken against the police and Revenue Department officials who allegedly failed to take preventive measures during the incident.

headline: 'Protesters Can't Inconvenience Public Everywhere': Passenger On Abhijeet Dipke's Detention From Flight
content: The passenger said they did not know who Abhijeet Dipke was, adding that the protest had caused inconvenience to fellow travellers. A passenger travelling on the Air India flight from Mumbai on which Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was onboard criticised the protesters for inconveniencing the public, after Delhi Police personnel entered the aircraft at the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport and detained three party leaders ahead of their planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar. We were travelling from Mumbai. We had to wait even after the flight landed. After the flight landed, we could hear sloganeering of Inquilab Zindabad from the front of the aircraft," the passenger told news agency ANI. - I Am Not Afraid Of You: High Drama On Plane As Cops Detain Abhijeet Dipke Ahead Of CJP Protest | Video - CJPs Dipke Says Jantar Mantar March Must Continue Even If He Is Detained, Shares Delhi Arrival Time - Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka Detained From Plane At Delhi Airport Ahead Of CJP Protest - CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das Say They May Be Arrested Before Oct 10: Timeline Of The Escalating Protest The passenger said they did not know who Abhijeet Dipke was, adding that the protest had caused inconvenience to fellow travellers. They were on a protest for 36 days earlier. But will they create inconvenience everywhere? Public is inconvenienced due to a few people like this," the passenger said. Questioning the protesters approach to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the passenger said that those who believed their names had been wrongfully deleted from electoral rolls could approach the Supreme Court. If the names of people have been wrongfully deleted, Supreme Court will look into it. They (protesters) are not going to look into it. Shut down courts if public will do everything. There is a system which we follow," the passenger said. If there is a problem, we will protest- will that help?" the passenger asked. CJP Leaders Detained From Aircraft At Delhi Airport Abhijeet Dipke, along with fellow CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police after Air India flight AI 2428 from Mumbai landed at Delhis IGI Airport on Saturday. Police personnel entered the aircraft as the leaders prepared to travel to the national capital for the CJPs planned protest at Jantar Mantar against the SIR exercise and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. A video shared by Abhijeet Dipke on Instagram showed a commotion inside the aircraft as the party leaders questioned the police action and asked why officers had entered the plane instead of waiting for them to disembark. You can see where the nation is heading. They are here to arrest us directly from the flight. This is something not even Indira Gandhi had done. This is dictatorship. Delhi Police have entered the flight and are trying to arrest us," Abhijeet Dipke said. Please come, I have come here to be arrested; arrest me," he added. In another exchange captured on video, Abhijeet Dipke was seen telling women police personnel, You could have waited till we came out. Come arrest us; we are not afraid." The police personnel responded, No, this is not an arrest. Please cooperate." The detentions came ahead of the CJPs planned protest at Jantar Mantar. The party had called on supporters to gather for what it described as a final call to save democracy", opposing the SIR exercise and seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police had denied permission for the proposed demonstration. Delhi Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke along with leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka inside an Air India flight from Mumbai before their planned protest at Jantar Mantar. The demonstration was organized to oppose the Special Intensive Revision exercise and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after authorities had denied permission for the event.

headline: Jantar Mantar Protest: Top leaders including Abhijeet Dipke detained in Delhi, CJP says nationwide agitation to continue
content: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday alleged a crackdown on its leaders and supporters ahead of its proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, saying its nationwide agitation demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would continue despite the detentions, CJP said in a press release. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police after their flight from Mumbai landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport, according to reports. The detentions came amid heightened security arrangements in the national capital ahead of the planned demonstration. Quick answers to key questions 1Why did the Cockroach Janta Party plan a protest at Jantar Mantar? The CJP planned the demonstration to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. 2Why did Delhi Police deny permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar? Delhi Police cited possible law-and-order concerns, procedural requirements and inconvenience to local residents and the public. 3Who was detained ahead of the CJP protest in Delhi? CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were reported detained after arriving in Delhi. The party also said influencer Dhruv Rathee, legal cell head Ratna Singh and spokesperson Mehr were detained. 4Will the CJPs nationwide protest continue after its leaders were detained? Yes. The CJP said its nationwide agitation would continue despite the detentions and that its central demand for Gyanesh Kumars resignation remained unchanged. 5What allegations about voter rolls prompted the CJP protest? The CJP cited allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and called for Gyanesh Kumar to resign. The supplied articles describe these as allegations, not established findings. In a video statement recorded aboard the aircraft as police personnel moved in, Dipke criticised the action and said he was prepared to be arrested. "This is not something even Indira Gandhi did during Emergency; this is a worse situation than that and we are all prepared for arrest," he said. Co-convenor Saurav Das alleged that the authorities were attempting to stop a constitutional movement through force. The group maintained that the planned nationwide protest would proceed with or without its leadership, reiterating its demand for the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The outfit said influencer and social activist Dhruv Rathee was detained from his residence in Gurugram's Sector 56. CJP legal cell head Ratna Singh was also detained from her Delhi residence, while group spokesperson Mehr was picked up from her home early on Saturday, according to the statement. The group further claimed that more than 1,000 volunteers, activists and other citizens had been detained across the National Capital Region, including at borders, transit hubs and surrounding streets. It alleged that local stadiums had been converted into temporary detention centres. The figures and claims about detention facilities were made by the outfit and were not independently established in the supplied statement. The CJP has called for a demonstration demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over allegations concerning voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed protest, citing security considerations and procedural requirements. Authorities also imposed restrictions and stepped up security arrangements across parts of the capital ahead of the demonstration. CJP urged young people and citizens to take part in the movement, invoking the principles of Mahatma Gandhi and Dr B.R. Ambedkar. It argued that the detention of its leaders would not change its central demand: Kumar should resign as chief election commissioner. "When the state uses mass detentions to silence democratic dissent, the public must take charge to save democracy," the CJP said in its statement. headline: 'Changing Colours To Suit Convenience': Maharashtra BJP Chief Takes Swipe At Congress
content: Invoking Amit Shahs criticism of the Congress, Chavan accused Rahul Gandhi and his party of selectively questioning electoral outcomes while ignoring their own political setbacks. Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan has launched a fresh attack on Rahul Gandhi and the Congress, accusing the party of political double standards. Sharing Union Home Minister Amit Shahs remarks on the Congresss electoral decline, Chavan took aim at its leadership and questioned its political credibility. In a social media post, Chavan accused the Congress of changing its political position according to convenience. Taking a swipe at Gandhi and other Congress leaders, he questioned their allegations of electoral malpractice while pointing to states where the party had failed to install its own chief minister for decades despite being part of governing alliances. - Tensions Rise in National Capital as Protests Against Election Commissioner Escalate | News18 - Three CJP Leaders Detained From Flight, To Be Kept Separately, Say Police Sources | Exclusive - Lucknow-Delhi Fare Row: Cheaper Trains Cancelled, Costlier Ones Open? Railways Face Questions - High Drama at Delhi Airport: Leaders of Cockroach Janta Party Detained Ahead of Protests | News18 Changing colours according to convenience is Congress politics! In states where the Congress has been unable to have its own chief minister for as long as 40 years, its own alliance partners were in power. Rahul Gandhi and Congress leaders, who make allegations of vote theft, will not utter a single word about this. This is exactly what the saying the thief cries foul means," he said. ! - . . ! Ravindra Chavan (@RaviDadaChavan) October 9, 2026 Amit Shah Questions Congresss Electoral Record Chavans remarks followed Home Minister Amit Shahs address to the BJP legislative party in West Bengal, where he questioned the Congresss electoral record and drew attention to states where the party has remained out of power, even as its alliance partners have governed for extended periods. Shah also questioned the Congress leaderships response to repeated electoral setbacks, arguing that the party needed to examine the reasons behind its declining political fortunes. His comments targeted Gandhis leadership and portrayed the Congress as struggling to rebuild its electoral base. The Home Minister also criticised the opposition INDIA bloc, questioning its cohesion under Gandhis leadership. The attack comes amid a continuing political confrontation between the BJP and the Congress over allegations of electoral malpractice, particularly the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Congress and other opposition parties have raised concerns about the exercise, questioning its implementation and warning that genuine voters could face difficulties in retaining their names on electoral rolls. The BJP, meanwhile, has defended SIR as a necessary exercise to identify discrepancies, including duplicate registrations and names of deceased voters. Chavans Earlier Challenge To SIR Opponents Chavan had earlier stepped up his attack on parties opposing SIR, asking them to clarify their position on duplicate voter registrations, names of deceased persons and alleged illegal immigrants. Sharing a video of Shahs remarks in Parliament on SIR, the Maharashtra BJP chief asked, Should infiltrators decide who the Prime Minister of the country and the Chief Minister of the state should be? If that happens, will democracy remain safe?" He also questioned whether voters should be allowed to cast ballots at multiple locations and whether names of deceased citizens should continue to appear on electoral rolls. Should a voter be allowed to vote at more than one place?" Chavan asked. Should deceased citizens have a place in the electoral rolls?" , ? ? ? ? SIR ! Ravindra Chavan (@RaviDadaChavan) October 4, 2026 The issue has also brought together political rivals in Maharashtra. Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray, along with the NCP (SP), held a joint rally called Garjana Morcha against SIR. The two Thackeray brothers, who have been political rivals for years, came together over the issue, giving the opposition campaign against the exercise greater political prominence in the state. While the BJP has sought to keep the debate focused on the accuracy of electoral rolls, opposition parties have questioned whether the revision process could affect legitimate voters. Against this backdrop, Chavans latest attack seeks to shift attention from the Congresss allegations against the BJP to the opposition partys own electoral record, political consistency and dependence on alliance partners. Maharashtra BJP President Ravindra Chavan criticized Rahul Gandhi and the Congress following Union Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks on the party's electoral decline in West Bengal. Chavan accused the Congress of political double standards and changing positions for convenience.

headline: ₹1,200 for 8 km? How Delhi's protest clampdown triggered 300% cab surges, WFH scrambles, festive weekend business loss
content: Delhi is facing a weekend of transport disruptions and business uncertainty as the Cockroach Janata Party is scheduled to hold its planned 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' protest in Central Delhi today. Here's a look at how the protest-related restrictions are affecting commuters, businesses and festive shopping across the city. An 8-km journey costing 1,200 captures the transport headache that Delhi commuters are facing amid the Cockroach Janta Party protest at Jantar Mantar. Surge pricing on Ola and Uber is practically close to three or four times the normal fare in parts of South Delhi, Noida and Gurugram. In fact, some drivers are even reluctant to accept trips towards central Delhi, leaving commuters either to pay a humongous fare for a cab or to wait. Quick answers to key questions 5 QUESTIONS 1Why are cab fares surging in Delhi during the CJP protest? Traffic restrictions around central Delhi and drivers reluctance to accept trips towards the area have reduced cab availability. The article reports fares in parts of South Delhi, Noida and Gurugram reaching three or four times normal levels. 2Which Delhi markets are closed during the CJP protest? Connaught Place, Palika Market, Janpath, Khan Market and Karol Bagh were expected to close or advised to shut over security concerns and possible disruption. Lajpat Nagar, Sarojini Nagar and Chandni Chowk traders said their markets would remain open, though individual shops may decide for themselves. 3Are Delhi Metro stations closed during the Jantar Mantar protest? Entry and exit gates at 45 stations, including Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat and Kashmere Gate, were scheduled to remain closed from 9 pm Friday until 6 pm Saturday. Interchange facilities were to remain available at the affected stations except New Delhi. 4Should commuters avoid travelling through central Delhi during the protest? Delhi Police advised people to avoid unnecessary travel, allow extra time and plan ahead when heading to airports, railway stations or bus terminals via New Delhi and central Delhi. Traffic restrictions may change depending on the situation. 5How are the protest restrictions affecting work and delivery services in Delhi? Some offices around Barakhamba Road and Connaught Place issued work-from-home advisories for Saturday morning shifts. Delivery operations by Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy were reported suspended in central pincodes 110001 and 110002, potentially causing delays and lost restaurant orders. For those travelling to work, shopping or meeting family over the weekend, getting across the city is becoming an expensive affair. The timing could not have been worse for traders. With the festive shopping season picking up pace ahead of Durga Puja and Diwali, footfall was expected to be high at the markets. However, several prominent markets in Delhi Connaught Place, Janpath and Khan Market will remain closed on Saturday, October 10, due to the CJP protest in Jantar Mantar. Chandni Chowk markets might also be impacted if customers avoid the area because of travel uncertainties. The actual revenue impact, however, will depend on how long restrictions remain and how easily shoppers can reach these markets. It has been reported that the delivery operations of Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy have been suspended in the central pincodes (110001, 110002). That means if delivery partners cannot travel through these zones to enter certain neighbourhoods or must take longer routes, customers may face delays and restaurants could lose orders. Companies with offices around Barakhamba Road and Connaught Place have already issued emergency "Work From Home" advisories for Saturday morning shifts. The CJP, in a statement issued on Saturday, urged participants to maintain peace, avoid violence and vandalism, follow lawful instructions and ensure that emergency services were not obstructed. CJP has also called on participants to remain peaceful, alert and united. The demonstration, scheduled to be held at Jantar Mantar today, has been described as an effort to seek accountability over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. CJP has called for a large mobilisation despite the Delhi Police denying permission for the protest. In its statement, CJP has urged protesters not to engage in physical confrontations, threats or intimidation, irrespective of provocation, and warned against damaging public or private property through vandalism, stone-pelting, arson or the destruction of barricades.

headline: Taiwan's leader says increasing defence spending to 'deter war'
content: Taiwan aims to "deter war" by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island's leader said on Saturday (October 10, 2026), as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims. Taiwan's 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it. "Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war," President Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan's National Day. Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion and to show the United States it is serious about its own defence. Mr. Lai's government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) in defence spending for 2027, which accounts for more than 3% of GDP. "We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others," Mr. Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered. "However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further," Mr. Lai said, noting that China continued to "apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait". Mr. Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted "there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist". Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that U.S. policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times. 'U.S. support is extremely important' The United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei's most important security backer. Mr. Trump's suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that U.S. arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world. Taiwan is waiting for Mr. Trump's signature on $14 billion worth of weapons, including the U.S.-made Patriot air defence system. Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Mr. Lai's wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population. "You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society," said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances. Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Mr. Lai's speech was "relatively moderate" and unlikely to be met with "overt reaction from Beijing". Saturday's (October 10, 2026) celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China's Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China. The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong's communist fighters. Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favours closer ties with China, said, "U.S. support is extremely important to Taiwan's security, but he noted the historical and cultural links with China. "The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges," Mr. Han said at the National Day event.

headline: From a meme handle to shutting down the capital: The anatomy of Cockroach Janta Party's digital rebellion
content: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical political outfit whose name was reportedly inspired by a remark by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, is set to hold another protest at Delhis Jantar Mantar today against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The Saturday protest, which comes days after the outfit held a protest in Bengaluru, marks another step in the CJP's journey from online satire to street mobilisation. As authorities detain around 500 people as a preventive measure, including 50 with criminal antecedents, heres a look at CJPs origins and how a meme handle grew into a movement whose protest call has prompted sweeping restrictions across Delhi. In May this year, CJI Kant pulled up a lawyer who was seeking a direction for designation as a Senior Advocate and likened some unemployed activists to "cockroaches" and "parasites" who attack the system after being unable to find employment. Kant noted, "There are already parasites in the society who attack the system, and you (Lawyer) want to join hands with them? There are youngsters like cockroaches who don't get any employment or have any place in the profession. Some of them become media, some of them become social media, RTI activists, and other activists, and they start attacking everyone." After facing backlash over his statement, the CJI issued a clarification, saying the media had misquoted him and that his criticism was directed at people entering professions with fake or bogus degrees. By then, the remark had already sparked an online response. Abhijeet Dipke posted, "What if all cockroaches come together?" and subsequently created a website and social media accounts for the Cockroach Janta Party. Dipke's initial post, a response to Kant's remarks, went viral, with millions of Indians joining the satirical outfit to voice their frustration over the NEET-UG paper leaks and the high unemployment rate in the country. Much like the Gen Z protesters in Nepal, who organised a movement using social media platforms and succeeded in bringing down the government in Kathmandu, Dipke's CJP is mobilising Indian youth using the one tool that is available to almost everyone today and has garnered much of our attention: social media. From Discord and Reddit to Instagram and X, the satirical outfit has left no stone unturned when it comes to mobilising young people seeking structural reforms in the country. Further, the outfit has drawn attention to issues such as unemployment and exam paper leaks, taking its campaign from online discussions to street protests. While many thought that Dipke and the CJP's online anger would soon fade and have no consequences in the offline world, the outfit moved from online mobilisation to holding protests in the national capital that continued for over a month into July, gaining students' support over exam paper leaks and demanding educational reforms. Since returning in June from the United States, where he was pursuing a master's degree, Dipke had been present at Jantar Mantar in the national capital as demonstrations continued, urging protesters to remain peaceful. As the outfit held demonstrations for almost a month, it gained support from climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who began an indefinite hunger strike in solidarity with the students. People across age groups also extended their support to Dipke and the outfit. On 20 July, protesters held a "Chalo Sansad" march, coinciding with the first day of the monsoon session. Delhi witnessed chaotic scenes as scores of protesters were detained, and the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) used tear gas and resorted to a lathi charge to stop the march towards Parliament. Amid growing backlash, the Centre agreed to meet CJP founders. Days later, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister. After Pradhan's resignation, the outfit called off its protests but continued seeking reforms, including those in schools under a School Thik Karo campaign. The 10 October CJP protests come as opposition parties and several student wings join hands to seek Gyanesh

headline: Lawyer who represented Mehul Choksi faces rape charges in U.K.
content: Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal, behind bars in London on charges of sexual assault, has also been accused of rape, it emerged after a court hearing in the U.K. on Friday (October 10, 2026). The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) referenced the new charges against the 57-year-old along with a charge of arranging or facilitating travel of another person with a view to exploitation. While his assistant Manpreet Kaur, also in a London prison, faces a similar charge, a third accused in the case appeared before Westminster Magistrates Court here on Friday charged with a similar offence, which he denies. Hara Tibrewala spoke to confirm his name and plead "not guilty" as a three-judge bench granted him bail under strict conditions. Aggarwal, Kaur and Tibrewala are now due to appear before Southwark Crown Court on November 6 for a pre-trial hearing. At a bail hearing in Southwark last month, Aggarwal who has represented fugitive businessman Mehul Choksi in fraud and money laundering proceedings was denied bail by Justice John Milne. In details that emerged in court, the Delhi advocate is accused of non-consensual sexual touching of a female and facilitating the travel of women with a view to exploitation allegations the judge described as deeply disturbing. The judge said he cannot accede to the request for bail as there is a risk that he would leave the country to avoid trial which has been set for March 15, 2027. Justice Milne pointed to a planned and sinister recruiting campaign" by Aggarwal to draw young women to apply for the sham post of personal assistant (PA) in search of "sexually pliant candidates. He said it was indicative of the fact that the accused was prepared to abuse his senior position for his own ends. As a native and citizen of India, the judge noted that his family, business and life were based there with no community ties" in the U.K. a country he extensively travelled to recruit despite having no legitimate basis for him requiring a PA in London. Aggarwals barrister, Sasha Wass, described her client as a man of outstanding character and reputation who has been forced to share a prison cell at Wandsworth in south-west London since his arrest in August. All the women referenced in court as the key witnesses in the sexual assault case have anonymity under UK law. Aggarwal and Kaur, 41, were arrested at a property on Brick Street in the posh Mayfair area of London on August 11 over alleged sexual offences on May 26 and August 9. The 29 Brick Street property is listed online as a Mayfair Residence Townhouse, made up of multi-storey luxury apartments that are available for rent.

The three CJP leaders were detained while they were aboard Air India flight AI 2428 at Delhis IGI Airport. Police sources said the leaders would be kept separately. Were Not Afraid Of You: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Following his detention, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke posted a video on Instagram in which he objected to the police action, saying the party had intended to hold a peaceful protest. All we wanted to do was a peaceful protest, and theyre picking us from the flight like were criminals," Abhijeet Dipke said in the video. Were not afraid of you. Come, arrest us," he added. Security Tightened Ahead Of CJP Protest The detentions come as the CJP called on supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar on October 10 for a protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing the possibility of serious law-and-order issues and alleged violations of conditions agreed upon for an earlier protest in July. Authorities introduced several security measures across Delhi, including restrictions affecting markets and Metro stations, train cancellations and internet curbs in parts of the city. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs has also directed states and Union Territories to coordinate with the Delhi Police and take measures to prevent protesters from travelling to the national capital. Police sources said the situation remained under control and personnel had been instructed to handle the developments calmly. Delhi Police detained three Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leadersAbhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Rankafrom Air India flight AI 2428 at Indira Gandhi International Airport on October 10, 2026.

headline: Lucknow-Delhi Fare Row: Cheaper Trains Cancelled, Costlier Ones Open? Railways Face Questions
content: Railwaymens Federation general secretary Shiv Gopal Mishra said trains havent stopped on this scale since Covid-19, with patients, workers and families among those affected. A journalists X post comparing Lucknow-Delhi train options has drawn attention as the Railways cancelled over 250 services ahead of Saturdays Delhi protest. For travellers from Lucknow, Mumbai and Patna, the question is simple and urgent: with their train gone or retimed, how do they reach Delhi now, and when? The post said two prominent Lucknow-Delhi trains, Lucknow Mail (12229) and the LKO-NDLS AC Express (12429), were cancelled, while seats remained on the costlier Shatabdi and Vande Bharat at nearly Rs. 1,500, against Rs. 300-800 on the cancelled services. - 7 best Bluetooth party speakers under Rs. 10,000 for Diwali celebrations - Delhi HC Orders Virtual Hearings At Two Court Complexes Ahead Of CJP Protest - CEC Protest Updates: Dipke To Land In Delhi At 9.30 AM On Saturday For CJP Protest - Delhi Protesters Bus-Stopping 'Stunt' Goes Viral As Internet Mocks Model Pose': 'Everyone Wants A Ticket To Bigg Boss' Tagging the Railways Ministry, the journalist added a pointed remark. Replies were divided. Some users said these fares are simply what the trains charge every day. Another said the cancellation circular covered only trains reaching Delhi by 2 pm, which the two trains do not. There is availability in trains with high fare Shatabdi and Vande Bharat. Well played @RailMinIndia! Piyush Rai (@Benarasiyaa) October 9, 2026 What Has Railway Board Decided? The Railway Board has cancelled more than 250 trains linked to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations ahead of a protest planned today by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which seeks the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The cancellations cover trains leaving their originating stations after 2 pm on October 9, those due at the two stations between 4 am and 2 pm today, and services departing from them, including local trains. What Are Experts And Passenger Groups Saying? Several voices have raised concerns about the scale. Subodh Jain, former Member (Engineering) of the Railway Board, noted that earlier agitations led to one or two cancellations, never so many at once. All India Railwaymens Federation general secretary Shiv Gopal Mishra told PTI he could not recall such a large stoppage outside the Covid-19 lockdown, adding that patients, workers and families heading to events were among those inconvenienced. Basant Kumar Shukla of Nagpurs Bhartiya Yatri Kendra said many passengers book 60 days ahead for urgent journeys, and urged special arrangements or booking priority on alternate dates. M Jameel Ahamed of the Coimbatore District Railway Passengers Welfare Association said reservation availability could stay tight for days. Some experts suggested terminating trains at stations nearest to Delhi, and a retired railway official asked whether trains passing through New Delhi or Nizamuddin would stop there at all. How Are Mumbai, Lucknow And Patna Faring? In Mumbai, the Mumbai Central division said the 12951 Tejas Rajdhani, scheduled at 5 pm on October 9, was rescheduled to 10 pm, and the 12953 Tejas Rajdhani to Nizamuddin from 5.10 pm to 10.10 pm, citing operational reasons". The notice did not mention the protest. In Lucknow, the comparison reflects what many travellers are weighing: a pricier seat or a longer road trip. One user suggested sleeper buses or a car. In Patna, passengers at Patna Junction were reported to be anxious, with some saying they had exams or medical visits to make, as trains were cancelled ahead of the October 10 protest. A rail-news portal reported that four pairs of Patna-Delhi trains, including the Tejas Rajdhani, Sampark Kranti, Amrit Bharat and Magadh Express, were cancelled. What Should Affected Passengers Do? Check your trains status before leaving for the station, especially if it passes through New Delhi or Nizamuddin, and confirm refund and rebooking options with IRCTC or the Railways. With reservations likely to remain tight, a bus or a flexible plan may be the safer bet. Keep your PNR and SMS alerts handy, and allow extra time at both ends, since Delhi Traffic Police has advised commuters to keep extra time in hand for railway stations on Saturday. The Railway Board cancelled more than 250 trains connected to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations due to a planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Could Bengaluru-Mumbai Get A Faster Overnight Train? Inside Vande Bharat Sleeper's 2AC Coach | WATCH
content: Mumbai journey significantly shorter? A look inside Vande Bharat Sleeper reveals the features passengers could find onboard Indian Railways Update: The Vande Bharat Sleeper is drawing attention for the facilities it brings to overnight rail travel. A recently shared video tour of its AC 2-Tier coach gives passengers a look at the berth design, onboard technology and everyday conveniences that could shape the experience on long-distance journeys. The train is also in focus as Indian Railways plans a Vande Bharat Sleeper service linking KSR Bengaluru with Mumbai CSMT. The proposed connection could bring the journey time down to under 16 hours, compared with roughly 24 hours on the existing Udyan Express. - Breathe Easier In The City: Effective Air Purifiers Under Rs. 15,000 For Compact Bedrooms - Mumbai To Bengaluru To Become India's Second Vande Bharat Sleeper Train: Timing, Cost, Route, etc - Mumbai's 'First' Heatwave Alert: Thane Swelters, Solapur Hottest In October Since 2002 | Will Schools Shut? - Full List Of Vande Bharat Express Trains In 2026: Check Routes, Timings, How To Book And Whats Coming Next The final launch date and operating details are still awaited. What Passengers Can Expect Inside The 2AC Coach The coach walkthrough highlights several features designed around individual passenger needs. The berths have cushioned surfaces, while ladders provide access to the upper berths. Passengers also have dedicated charging points for phones and laptops, a phone holder and room to keep their belongings. Air circulation is another feature showcased in the video. Each berth has its own automotive-style AC vent, allowing passengers to adjust the airflow around their sleeping space. Individual reading lights and curtains add to the convenience, particularly for those travelling overnight. The coach also has large, sealed panoramic windows. Inside, a GPS-linked information screen displays details including the trains speed and upcoming station, giving passengers updates during the journey. Toilets, Wash Areas And Meal Services The video also offers a look at the trains aircraft-style, vacuum-sealed toilets. These bio-toilets feature sensor-operated flushing and are designed to support improved hygiene onboard. A wash basin and mirror are located nearby. The trains pantry area is intended to support scheduled catering services through the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), giving passengers access to meals during their trip. Bengaluru-Mumbai Sleeper Train: Route And Expected Schedule The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service would connect Bengaluru and Mumbai overnight, with a planned journey time of less than 16 hours. The existing Udyan Express takes around 24 hours, so the new service could provide a quicker rail option for passengers travelling between the two cities. Tentative schedules have indicated late-evening departures from both ends, with arrivals the following afternoon. The proposed service is also expected to operate six days a week, although its timings and frequency have not been formally finalised. The anticipated route includes Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan. These stops would allow passengers from several locations across Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh to use the service, rather than limiting its reach to the two terminal cities. The final list of halts and the timetable will be determined by the official railway announcement. Travellers should treat the published schedules as provisional until confirmation is issued. How Many Berths Does The Train Have? The Vande Bharat Sleeper is configured as a 16-coach train, with accommodation across three air-conditioned classes. Its stated total capacity is 823 berths. Vande Bharat Sleeper Fares Explained Ticket prices depend on the class selected and the distance travelled. The supplied fare structure uses a minimum chargeable distance of 400 km, with the listed minimum fares excluding GST. As the distance increases, the fare rises accordingly. The supplied estimates put the highest fare at Rs. 13,300 for an AC First Class journey of up to 3,500 km, compared with Rs. 960 for a minimum-distance AC 3-Tier ticket. On some longer journeys, the Vande Bharat Sleeper may cost more than a Rajdhani Express ticket. Passengers will therefore need to weigh the fare against the time saved and the facilities offered onboard. When Will The Bengaluru-Mumbai Service Begin? The inaugural Vande Bharat Sleeper service between Kamakhya, near Guwahati, and Howrah began regular operations in January 2026. A Bengaluru-Mumbai connection would extend the sleeper train offering to another major travel corridor. However, the proposed services launch date, final departure and arrival times, stoppages and operating frequency remain subject to official confirmation. Passengers should rely on announcements from Indian Railways before booking or planning around the proposed schedule. The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service is expected to reduce the journey time between Bengaluru and Mumbai to under 16 hours, compared to roughly 24 hours on the existing Udyan Express.

headline: What's on the agenda as Home Ministry meets Ladakh stakeholders this month?
content: The next round of meetings between the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ladakh representatives is scheduled to take place on October 15, officials have said. The discussions, which come over a month after the last round of talks in Delhi, are set to take place against the backdrop of deliberations on an additional constitutional provision and a proposed UT-level elected body for Ladakh. After last months meeting, the Ladakh administration proposed a new governance arrangement for the Union Territory that would be neither a state nor a UT with a legislature, but a unique constitutional amendment requiring Parliaments approval. The MHA had also sent a set of questions to representatives of the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance the two bodies spearheading the movement for greater democratic representation in Ladakh. The questions, raised at a meeting between MHA officials and Ladakh representatives on September 9, urged them to deliberate on the shape, form and composition of a UT-level governance body with executive and financial powers. The talks took place after the Centre offered to introduce an additional constitutional provision, Article 371(K), for Ladakh. The questionnaire from the MHA seeks specifics from the representatives on seven key issues, from the formal name, composition and representation of the UT-level legislative body to its relationship with the existing Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. The MHA has also asked Ladakhi representatives to consult each other on the functions that should necessarily be exercised by the UT-level body in the interest of uniformity, coordinated development and effective administration, and those that should remain at the district level to protect local interests. The ministry has also sought clarity on a broad spectrum of concerns, including the principles that would guide the allocation of powers between the UT-level body and the LAHDCs. Members of the sub-committee have also been asked to specify which subjects should fall within the domain of the UT-level elected body, in tune with the basic structure of the Constitution, and whether such a unique model for Ladakh would require a legal opinion. These concerns are likely to form part of the deliberations between the two groups on October 15. In September, the KDA and ABL had submitted a list of non-negotiables to the MHA outlining their key demands, including a directly elected, constitutionally empowered UT-level legislature. Since the agitation for greater democratic control over Ladakh by its people took hold, representatives from the region have pushed a four-point agenda: statehood for Ladakh, safeguards under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, reservation of jobs for Ladakhs youth, and separate parliamentary constituencies for the two parts of the region. This agenda has driven agitations over the last three years.

headline: Delhi Protest Today: CJP says no one allowed to hijack peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar | Full guidelines
content: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) issued a set of guidelines ahead of its planned massive protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday (October 10) against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The CJP urged protesters to "maintain peace at all time" and avoid engaging in violence, carrying weapons or dangerous objects. It also advised them to know your emergency contacts. Stay with your group." The organisation strictly said, No individual can be allowed to hijack a peaceful protest. Quick answers to key questions 1What were CJPs guidelines for the Jantar Mantar protest? CJP urged protesters to remain peaceful, avoid violence and dangerous objects, respect barricades and keep emergency routes clear. It also advised verifying information, staying with their group and following lawful instructions. 2Why was CJP planning a protest at Jantar Mantar? The protest was against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Groups were also demanding his resignation. 3Did Delhi Police grant permission for CJPs October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar? No. Delhi Police denied permission, citing possible serious law-and-order concerns and inconvenience to residents and citizens. 4What should protesters do if someone tries to provoke violence? CJP advised protesters not to participate in violence or unlawful activity. They should alert a designated CJP coordinator and, where safe, the police. 5How should protesters prepare for an emergency? CJP advised staying with your group, agreeing on a meeting point and carrying identification, necessary medicines and a charged phone. If tensions rise, move away and help vulnerable people reach safety. The organisation said, Our protest, our responsibility. Stay peaceful. Stay alert. Stay united. Here's what the CJP's 12-point guidelines stated: 1. Maintain peace at all times. Do not engage in violence, physical confrontations, threats or intimidation, irrespective of provocation. 2. Do not damage public or private property. Vandalism, stone-pelting, arson and destruction of barricades can endanger lives and undermine the purpose of the protest. 3. Do not obstruct emergency services. Keep access clear for ambulances, fire engines and other emergency vehicles. Do not block hospital entrances or emergency routes. 4. Do not carry weapons or dangerous objects. Avoid carrying sticks, stones, inflammable substances or anything that could be used to injure someone. 5. Do not threaten or abuse anyone. Avoid communal slurs, hate speech, threats and personal attacks against officials, police personnel, journalists or members of the public. 6. Do not force your way through barricades. Follow lawful directions, respect designated boundaries and do not attempt to enter restricted areas. 7. Beware of provocation and infiltration. Do not judge people by their political affiliation or appearance. If anyone encourages violence, vandalism or unlawful activity, do not participate. Inform a designated CJP coordinator and, where safe, the police. 8. Verify before sharing. Do not circulate unverified claims, misleading videos, rumours or messages designed to incite panic or hostility. 9. Record incidents responsibly. If safe and lawful, document relevant incidents without interfering with police duties, obstructing others or putting yourself at risk. Do not publish unverified allegations against individuals. 10. Protect fellow protesters. If tensions rise, move away from the confrontation, alert a coordinator and help vulnerable people reach safety. Never put yourself in danger to confront a suspected provocateur. 11. Know your emergency contacts. Stay with your group, agree on a meeting point and carry essential identification, necessary medicines and a charged phone. 12. Follow lawful instructions and know your rights. Remain calm during police interactions. Do not resist physically. If detained, ask for the reason and seek legal assistance. Remember: No individual can be allowed to hijack a peaceful protest. Our conduct must reflect our cause. Peaceful protest. Constitutional rights. Responsible citizenship, the CJP's guidelines read. The CJP, which led the Jantar Mantar protest against Education Minister Pradhan in June-July, will hold a massive demonstration in Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10. Several political parties, including the AAP and Left parties, are likely to join

headline: Mallikarjun Kharge's pitch to dissolve assemblies puts own Congress government in Kerala in a spot
content: The BJPs Kerala unit appears to have found a new weapon in Congress president Mallikarjun Kharges recent statement on election irregularities. Days after Kharge demanded the dissolution of all state assemblies following the protests against the Election Commission of India, the BJP is trying to turn his statement on its head, accusing the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) of double standards on the legitimacy of elections in the state. The UDF swept the Assembly elections held this year, winning 102 of the states 140 seats and reducing its principal Opposition, the Left Democratic Front, to 35. In his speech last week, Kharge called all elections illegal and demanded the dissolution of the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, saying fresh polls should be conducted using ballot papers. For years, the Congress has alleged irregularities in electronic voting machines. But as the Opposition chorus against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar grows, the BJP, which won three seats, is seeking to portray the demand as evidence of Congresss duplicity, particularly given the partys own victory in the Assembly polls. Significantly, neither the Congress nor the CPI(M), which was then in power, raised serious allegations against the SIR in Kerala. Their main objection was to the timing of the exercise, which was scheduled for February, around the time of the local body polls. The Kerala Congress also finds itself in a peculiar position amid mounting allegations against the SIR, as the exercise was completed while Chief Minister V D Satheesans private secretary, Rathan U Kelkar, was serving as the states Chief Electoral Officer. As a result, while the national capital is rife with Opposition protests, the streets of Kerala have remained largely silent. The only protest in the state was against the police action against the Gandhi siblings, Rahul and Priyanka. It is against this backdrop that the BJP is seeking to frame its allegations. In a post on X, BJP state president Rajeev Chandrasekhar questioned the legitimacy of the Kerala elections in light of the protests. Is this an illegal Assembly or a legal one? Congress National President says all these elections were illegal and all Chief Ministers are illegal. So, the first thing to be discussed in the Assembly is whether all of us MLAs are illegal, Nemom MLA Chandrasekhar said in his post. Meanwhile, in a letter to Chief Minister V D Satheesan, BJP MLA B B Gopakumar, the partys leader in the Assembly, said the Congress presidents statement also covered the Kerala Assembly. If what the Congress president said is correct, Keralam Chief Minister came into power through rigging of the elections. At the same time, the chief minister was also seen participating in a protest in Delhi against the SIR. By taking part in that protest, he has brought humiliation upon the people of Kerala, he said. The BJP also held a core committee meeting on Thursday to discuss the Congress double standard. Why is Congress selectively questioning the outcome of elections held after the SIR? If the results are doubtful, is that not applicable to the results of Keralam elections too? The BJP will hold protests demanding the resignation of Satheesan as the chief minister, senior BJP leader M T Ramesh said.

headline: Indian man jailed in Paris over leading online child abuse ring
content: A 29-year-old Indian man has been sentenced to 20 years in prison by a Paris court for leading a masculinist group that forced young girls, many of them minors, to perform sexual acts, authorities said. The trial of Rohan Rane began on Monday (October 5, 2026) in Paris before a special criminal court and is being held behind closed doors, the State-owned France 24 television network reported. On Friday (October 9), the Paris court sentenced Rane, who came to France to study, to 20 years in prison over his involvement in an international criminal network that targeted vulnerable children in the U.S., Britain and Canada and coerced them into producing violent and sexual videos, the report added. Prosecutors had sought a 30-year jail term for Rane, who they described as a neo-Nazi lover of sadism and macabre ultra-violence. Most of the dozens of victims of the group led by Rane were American girls, the court was told. Many were under 15. Other young male members of the masculinist group were from the United States, India, Germany and New Zealand, the France 24 report added. Six of the girls, now aged between 18 and 21, made official complaints. About 20 victims were identified, but others could not be contacted, prosecutors said. After five days of hearings, mainly behind closed doors, the court found Rane guilty of offences, notably extortion committed as part of an organised gang, with the aggravating circumstances of acts of torture and barbarity perpetrated on the victims. Prosecutors said all of the girls were lured by the "CVLT" group that was driven by nihilism, racism, anti-Semitism, Nazi aesthetics and values, and the hatred of feminists and the LGBTQ+ community. The group became active ahead of the Covid-19 pandemic on the Discord platform with Rane as its leader. Rane went to France to study at a commercial school in the southern town of Antibes before becoming a sports coach. Rane was first arrested in 2021 in France. US authorities passed on information about his leadership in the "CVLT" group and how he had vaunted his desire to fullfil his "sadism".

headline: ED arrests Sadhna Group MD Rakesh Gupta in Rs 168 crore money-laundering case
content: Dr Rakesh Gupta, chairman and managing director of Sadhna Group, was arrested and remanded to five days of Enforcement Directorate (ED) custody early on Saturday after his arrest in a money-laundering case involving alleged proceeds of crime worth Rs. 168 crore. Sadhna Group operates Sadhna TV and related media networks. In his order, Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler said that Gupta, 63, should be produced before the court again by 4 pm on October 15. Gupta was arrested at 10.25 pm on Friday at Ishwar Farms in Vasant Kunj and was produced before the court at 2.03 am on Saturday at a residential camp office within two hours of the grounds of arrest being furnished, and within 24 hours of arrest, the court said. Considering his age and the specific tasks shown, ED custody for five days instead of seven days is justified. The ED case was registered on the basis of an FIR registered by the Delhi Polices Economic Offences Wing on September 29 under several sections of the Indian Penal Code on charges of cheating, criminal breach of trust , etc. Gupta is named as the second accused. The ED claim against Gupta The ED has alleged that Gupta, as chairman of the group, engineered the insolvency of Sadhna Media Pvt Ltd (SMPL) through related creditors holding 99.41 per cent of the committee of creditors, so that income-tax dues of Rs. 110.10 crore were settled for Rs. 20 lakh. They received about Rs. 2.50 to Rs. 2.82 crore in cash through USDT and hawala channels on the resale of SMPL/Aryan TV, the agency alleged. It caused SMPL to pay Rs. 4.48 crore to connected creditors, including Rs. 2,99,55,042.35 to his own company, M/s Sharpline Broadcast Ltd. The ED alleged that SEBI, in a final order dated May 29 last year, identified Gupta as the mastermind behind the alleged manipulation of shares of M/s Sadhna Broadcast Ltd and held him jointly and severally liable for about Rs. 58 crore. Proceeds of crime are prima facie assessed at about Rs. 168 crore. The groups records are kept at its Gol Market office here, which falls within the jurisdiction of the court under Section 44(1)(a) of the PMLA, the agency said. Why ED sought Guptas custody Special Public Prosecutor Simon Benjamin submitted that Guptas custody was needed to trace the hawala cash, the Rs. 2.99 crore allegedly placed in Sharpline Broadcast and Rs. 8.98 crore shown as payable to Saroj Construction and Graphisads without any bank trail, as well as the liquidated assets of SMPL. The agency said it also wants to confront Gupta with data from his seized iPhone 13 Pro and iPad Pro and with statements of co-persons recorded on October 9, examine telecast receipts in Dubai and Sydney and the crypto-hawala settlement, identify books, bank and demat records at the Gol Market office, and ascertain the role of M/s Saroj Constwell Pvt Ltd. The witnesses are the accuseds employees and relatives, the ED said, giving rise to a risk of tampering.

headline: 36 people hurt after shopping mall ceiling collapses in South Korea's Daegu city
content: At least 36 people sustained minor injuries after parts of a plaster ceiling collapsed at a shopping mall in Daegu city, South Korea, fire officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026). The Daegu Fire Department said about 70 others evacuated the facility following the collapse, which was reported at 10.16 a.m. At least nine people received treatment at hospitals, but no serious injuries were immediately reported, according to officials, who said the injury toll could rise. A photo from the scene showed emergency rescuers searching through debris following the collapse, on the second floor of the four-storey building. It was not immediately clear what caused the collapse. The office of South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said he had instructed officials to make every effort to rescue people and ensure a thorough response to the collapse.

headline: Trump-Putin diesel deal: Can the US president bypass his own Russia sanctions law?
content: US President Donald Trumps decision to allow Russian diesel supplies to global markets has raised questions about how the move fits with a new law empowering him to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas. Trump announced the diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, claiming it would swiftly bring down record-high diesel prices. The announcement came just three weeks after he signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law. The legislation empowers Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian crude oil or gas, among other restrictions. However, the latest diesel arrangement has prompted criticism that Washington is easing pressure on Moscow even as it seeks to end the war in Ukraine. Congress just passed a law giving Trump the power to impose new tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil & gas, Scott Lincicome, vice president of the libertarian Cato Institute, said on X after the announcement. Can America tariff America? he quipped. Under the agreement, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tons in November. A further 1 million tons will arrive immediately thereafter, with 3 million more depending on refinery conditions, Trump said in a Truth Social post. The US Treasury Department subsequently said Trump had directed the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to issue a temporary general licence allowing Russian diesel supplies to the global market. OFAC specified that the sanctioned transactions would be authorised for about six months, until 7 April. The White House did not immediately respond to CNBCs questions about the diesel agreement with Russia. Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat from Connecticut and member of the Senate Ukraine Caucus, accused Trumps decision of being directly contrary to Congresss intent in our bipartisan sanctions bill. Peter Harrell, visiting scholar at Georgetown University Law Centers Institute of International Economic Law, said on X that relaxing Russian diesel restrictions pretty much proves the point that the Graham Russia Bill was not going to force the Trump Administration to increase economic pressure on Moscow. Criticism also came from Republicans. Representative Michael McCaul of Texas said the legislation had given Trump significant authorities and leverage against China and Russia to bring Putins war to an end with a negotiated settlement. Unfortunately, while I understand the desire to bring down diesel prices, I am concerned the lifting of sanctions on Russian oil will only fund the Kremlins war machineemboldening more violence and destruction, as we have seen in recent days, McCaul said in an X post. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the US decision to ease sanctions on Moscow plays into Russias hands. Any easing of sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious weakness, Zelenskyy said. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. Trump has previously criticised countries that continue to purchase Russian energy. In September 2025, he wrote on Truth Social: the purchase of Russian Oil, by some, has been shocking! It greatly weakens your negotiating position, and bargaining power, over Russia. Earlier this year, his administration issued limited, 30-day waivers allowing countries to buy sanctioned Russian oil that was already in transit after the Iran war began. Jeremy Siegel, professor emeritus of finance at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, described the latest move as a short-term measure. Its not a permanent solution at all. Its sort of a short-term Band Aid, Siegel told CNBCs Closing Bell. And cutting back on or eliminating sanctions on Russia for the invasion in Ukraine, I think, is a very

headline: Starlink row: Musk shares reports on Reliance-linked firm's BJP campaign role, political donations
content: Elon Musk on Saturday (October 10, 2026) stepped up his attack against industrialist Mukesh Ambani, sharing screenshots of media reports alleging that a Reliance-funded firm helped boost BJP campaigns on social media and that a Reliance-linked company made large political donations to the ruling party. The latest post by Mr. Musk on X featured an Al Jazeera report from 2022 headlined "How a Reliance-funded firm boosts BJP's campaigns on Facebook" and an archived Indian Express report from 2024 on Qwik Supply, which reported that the Reliance-linked firm donated 385 crore to the BJP and 25 crore to the Shiv Sena through electoral bonds. The latest post comes amid Mr. Musk's scathing criticism of Mukesh Ambani over a persistent delay in the launch of Starlink satellite broadband services in India. Reliance has not publicly responded to Mr. Musk's allegations, while the government has maintained that the country's authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is "fair and non-discriminatory" and that any suggestion that it was being applied selectively was "baseless and misconceived." A few hours before he made the post, Mr. Musk on X addressed Mukesh Ambani as "Prime Minister Ambani" and accused him of protecting a monopoly. Mr. Musk wondered if Mr. Ambani would consider allowing his satellite internet service to compete with his entity in the country. On Friday (October 9, 2026), Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia asserted that India does not permit monopolies in any sector, and that despite the buzz around one particular company, three players have received satcom licences and can start operations after meeting the security requirements and milestones. Mr. Musk has alleged that powerful business interests are seeking to block his service to preserve their dominance in the Indian market. He said his Starlink was being blocked by certain oligarchs seeking to "maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people." "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" he wrote. Mr. Musk also said many areas of India have no internet access, and the absence denies children education and small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better, the technocrat asserted. Within minutes of that post late Friday evening (October 9, 2026), Mr. Musk wrote another, saying Starlink has proven to be essential in saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communication systems failed. "So you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India," he added. Mr. Scindia has said India doesn't allow monopoly in any sector. "Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology-agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers," the Union minister said at a briefing at the India Mobile Congress here. Mr. Scindia said three entities - Mr. Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb - have already secured licences, while Amazon's Project Kuiper has expressed interest and will need to follow the established procedure. While there is a lot of conversation about one particular company, three have got satcom licences, he said. "We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a licence; as and when the government decides the charge system on the revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil the security conditions, they can start operations," the minister said. TRAI and the telecom department are close to a final decision on pricing regime for satcom spectrum, Mr. Scindia added. The BJP leader also hit out at the Congress in the backdrop of Rahul Gandhi and Mr. Musk's exchange on X. "As far as the Congress is concerned... I don't think they themselves know whether they're going left or right," the former member of the party said. He said the Congress initially had a problem with "a certain person getting a licence" and pointed out that "now they have a problem, and they've allied with that person in terms of why he's not getting a licence." "So I don't know whether they have clarity on where they're going, but that is the case with the Congress, which is to be expected," Mr. Scindia said. Mr. Musk's allegations came as India Mobile Congress (IMC) a grand annual telecom event - unfolded in Delhi. "Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?" Mr. Musk wrote in a post on X earlier.

headline: U.S.-Ukraine-European negotiators meet in Miami as Trump announces diesel deal with Russia
content: Negotiators for the U.S., Ukraine and Europeans held six hours of talks in Miami on Friday (October 9, 2026) with the aim of reaching agreement on a unified proposal to end the war in Ukraine, a person familiar with the talks said. The goal is to reach agreement on such a proposal in the coming weeks so it can be presented to Russia in order to seek a breakthrough before the winter, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The talks came on the same day that U.S. President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, while his administration lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for the war. The deal was criticised by U.S. lawmakers and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. "All that money goes toward the war against people, against Ukraine, against all of us. I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair," Mr. Zelenskyy said in a statement. Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Mr. Trump that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow. The talks in Miami included U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and delegations from Ukraine as well as representatives from Europe and NATO. The negotiators covered a lengthy list of topics in the discussions, including a post-war package for Ukraine that would include security guarantees from the U.S. and from Europe, the person said. Also discussed were a post-war economic plan for Ukraine and a pathway to accession to the European Union for Kyiv, the person said. In a sensitive subject, the delegations discussed "some ideas" on territory, the person said, declining to elaborate. Ukraine has been adamant that Russia cede territory it has seized during the conflict. President Donald Trump has said both sides will need to compromise. The person said the delegations also discussed a Europe-Russia security architecture that would set the stage for peaceful years ahead. The person did not provide details.

headline: Vande Bharat train manufactured in Punjab completes 180 kmph trial on Mathura-Nagda section
content: Indian Railways new Vande Bharat train has completed a high-speed trial at 180 kmph on the Mathura-Nagda section. The 16-coach Vande Bharat Chair Car trainset has been manufactured at Rail Coach Factory (RCF), Kapurthala, Punjab. According to Ministry of Railways, the trial took place on October 8, 2026, under the supervision of the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety (CCRS). The inspection assessed the trains high-speed performance, operational efficiency and safety parameters. New Vande Bharat train undergoes a high-speed trial on the Mathura-Nagda section. (Image: Ministry of Railways) Vande Bharat train undergoes high-speed trial The newly manufactured Vande Bharat trainset is equipped with an advanced propulsion system designed to support its operations. During the trial on the Mathura-Nagda section, railway safety officials assessed the trains performance at a speed of 180 kmph. The inspection covered key safety parameters and the trainsets operational performance at high speed. However, completing a trial at 180 kmph does not automatically mean the train will operate at that speed during regular passenger services. Its permitted operating speed will depend on the applicable safety clearances and operational requirements. RCF Kapurthala records highest-ever coach production In the financial year 202526, RCF Kapurthala achieved its highest-ever annual production of 2,383 coaches. It produces coaches for modern trainsets, including Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat trains. The factory also exports railway coaches to several countries in Asia and Africa. Vande Bharat train features Vande Bharat Chair Car rake features ergonomically designed reclining seats with ample legroom, large panoramic windows to provide better views and natural lighting and fully air-conditioned coaches to maintain a pleasant temperature throughout the trip. The train also has automatic sliding doors, bio-vacuum toilets, and a smooth suspension system that reduces jerks and vibrations. - Fitted with KAVACH. - Jerk Free Semi-Permanent couplers. - Centrally controlled Automatic Plug Doors and Fully Sealed wider gangways. - Emergency Alarm Push buttons and Talk Back Units on all Coaches. - Improved fire safety Aerosol based fire detection and suppression system in electrical cabinets and lavatories. - Higher acceleration with design/operating speed of 180/160 KMPH. - Driver-Guard communication with voice recording facility & Crash hardened memory. - Air conditioning units with indigenously developed UV-C lamp based disinfection system. - Better Ride Comfort. - CCTVs in all Coaches. - For Divyangjan passengers special lavatory in the driving coaches on each end. - Coach condition monitoring System (CCMS) display with remote monitoring.

headline: Jantar Mantar CJP Protest: Abhijit Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das to reach Delhi shortly — 'See you in few hours'
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has left for Delhi to stage a protest at Jantar Mantar from Mumbai. According to a PTI report, he left for the airport at around 6.50 am in the morning from the Four Seasons Hotel in Worli in central Mumbai. He is expected to reach Delhi by 10 am, a CJP functionary said. The CJPs October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar is being held against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with groups pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Quick answers to key questions 1Why is the CJP holding a protest at Jantar Mantar? The October 10 protest is against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The groups are also pressing for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. 2Did Delhi Police grant permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar? No. Delhi Police denied permission, citing possible serious law-and-order concerns and inconvenience to local residents and citizens. 3Which CJP leaders were heading to Delhi for the Jantar Mantar protest? CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had left Mumbai for Delhi. CJP co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das also said they were on their way. 4When and where was the CJP protest planned? The demonstration was planned for October 10 at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. 5Which political parties were expected to join the CJP protest? The Aam Aadmi Party and Left parties said they would participate. The listed Left parties included the CPI(M), CPI, CPI(ML), RSP and All India Forward Bloc. Kumar is confronting allegations of tampering with voter lists under the pretext of the SIR exercise, as well as sidestepping his two colleagues to modify Form 6, the vital document used for voter registration. However, the Delhi Police has denied permission for the October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar. Speaking to reporters in Mumbai before leaving for New Delhi for the protest, Dipke said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scared of the youth amid the unprecedented clampdown in Delhi, including the cancellation of several trains. He also accused the Centre of waging a war against its own people through what he described as emergency-like conditions. Narendra Modi is a dictator. He is scared, Dipke said, asking, Which is why he has shut down railways, metro, and all roads. If Narendra Modi is so afraid of the youth of this country, the people of this country, then why is he sitting on the Prime Minister's chair? Dipke also claimed that authorities were detaining people travelling to Delhi to prevent them from participating in the protest. They are catching people on trains in other parts of Mumbai; they are not letting them go. In Delhi, Dipke said, They have shut down everything. This is fear, this is nothing but fear, this is Narendra Modi's fear. And he is afraid that the people of this country will not vote for him after this. The Delhi Police is going to people's homes and saying no one should protest. Why shouldn't they go? Protesting is our fundamental right. Article 19 gives us the fundamental right to protest in a very democratic and peaceful manner, and that is what we are going to do, Dipke said. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, co-conveners of CJP, also posted a picture on social media saying they'll be in Delhi in a few hours. See you in a few hours, Delhi! Ranka wrote on X. Citing the possibility of "serious" law and order concerns as well as inconvenience to local residents and citizens, the Delhi Police has denied permission to the CJP for its planned October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar. In a formal communication addressed to CJP co-convenor Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna, the Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi district) noted that permitting the demonstration could trigger serious law-and-order issues, PTI reported. "In the larger public interest, the permission sought cannot be granted and is hereby denied," the letter stated.
