headline: Delhi Markets Hit On Festive Eve: CP, Karol Bagh Shut, And Reaching Them Is Another Ordeal
content: Connaught Place, Karol Bagh and Old Delhi traders have shut shop, 45 metro stations are closed and diversions are in place as Navratri shopping begins. Here is what to expect. Delhis busiest shopping hubs will stay shut or sluggish on Saturday, just as the festive buying rush begins. With a protest at Jantar Mantar, metro gates closed at 45 stations and traffic diversions at 30 points, traders have pulled down shutters, and shoppers face a tough journey to the markets. Several markets in and around central Delhi, including Connaught Place, Karol Bagh and parts of Old Delhi, will remain closed on October 10, with trader bodies citing police advisories and fears of damage to shops and property, The Times of India reported. The timing hurts. - Streamline Your Workflow: Multi-Device Bluetooth Keyboards and Mice Under Rs. 2,500 - Delhi Metro Update: DMRC Revises Entry, Exit Timing To 6 PM, Reduces Restricted Stations List To 45 - Delhi Protest News Updates: 57 Metro Stations May Shut, Trains Cancelled Ahead of CJP Protest - CEC Protest Updates: Dipke To Land In Delhi At 9.30 AM On Saturday For CJP Protest It is a weekend, Navratri begins on October 11, and Dussehra and Diwali follow, when families traditionally head out to shop. Which Markets Are Closed? The New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA) advised all shops, offices and restaurants in Connaught Place to close as a precaution on October 10. Its advisory urged owners to stay vigilant" and cooperate to avoid any unpleasant situation", TOI reported. NDTA president Atul Bhargava said the body would write to authorities seeking relocation of the protest from Jantar Mantar. In Karol Bagh, the Ajmal Khan Road Vyapar Mandal said traders were advised to keep shops shut until 2 pm and would review the situation after that. Delhi Vyapar Mahasanghs Devraj Baweja said a shutdown had been announced for Sadar Bazar. A letter from the New Lajpat Nagar Market Traders Association, written in Hindi, told members that, on safety grounds, Delhi Police had instructed the market to stay closed on Saturday. Saurabh shukla (@Saurabh_Unmute) October 9, 2026 Are All Traders On Board? No. Traders in Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk and other Old Delhi markets questioned the closure call during peak festive sales. Sanjay Bhargava of Chandni Chowk Sarv Vyapar Mandal said stock for festivals is bought on credit or bank loans, and that the market had received no formal circular from Delhi Police, according to TOI. How Badly Has Business Been Hit? The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has sought curbs on large protests in commercial zones such as Jantar Mantar, Sansad Marg and Lutyens Delhi until Diwali. CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal claimed Delhis overall business had dropped to around 30% of normal over the past three days, TOI reported. He said shoppers from outside Delhi had fallen from 2-3 lakh a day to 40,000-50,000, while local footfall had declined by over 50%. These figures are the trader bodys own and are not independently verified. Is The Metro An Option? Only partly. DMRC said entry and exit at 45 stations will remain closed from 9 pm on October 9 until 6 pm on October 10, with the situation to be reviewed by security agencies. Among them are Rajiv Chowk and Barakhamba Road near Connaught Place, Karol Bagh, Lajpat Nagar, Chawri Bazar, Jama Masjid and Kashmere Gate. Interchange remains available at the concerned stations, except New Delhi. What About Roads? Delhi Traffic Police said diversions will be enforced from 6 am on October 10, depending on the situation, at 30 points. These include Dhaula Kuan Flyover, Jhandewalan roundabout, Mandi House, Lodhi Road Flyover and several Connaught Place outer circle junctions. Police asked commuters to avoid non-essential travel and keep extra time in hand for railway stations, ISBTs and the airport. Restrictions are dynamic and may be relaxed or tightened as the day unfolds. What Should Shoppers Do? Check with individual markets before stepping out, since closure timings vary. Track live updates on the Delhi Traffic Police website and X handle, or call the helpline on 1095 or 011-25844444. For many families, Saturdays festive shopping may simply have to wait. Several key markets across central and old Delhi, including Connaught Place, Karol Bagh, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Bhagirath Palace, Jama Masjid, and New Lajpat Nagar, remain closed on October 10, 2026, due to police advisories and safety concerns surrounding a protest.

headline: CJP's protest in Delhi: Contempt plea filed in Supreme Court over closure of DMRC metro stations
content: A contempt petition was filed in the Supreme Court on Saturday, alleging that the authorities are continuing with their decision to shut down metro stations and limit public transport services across Delhi in violation of the courts order issued on Friday, LiveLaw reported. On Friday, the apex court directed the authorities not to impose a complete ban on transport services to manage the protest scheduled for Saturday, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Quick answers to key questions 1Why was a contempt petition filed in the Supreme Court over Delhi Metro closures? The petition alleges that authorities continued closing metro stations and limiting public transport despite the Supreme Courts order against imposing a complete transport ban to manage the CJP protest. 2What did the Supreme Court order about transport during the CJP protest? On Friday, the Court directed authorities not to impose a complete ban on transport services to manage the protest scheduled for Saturday. 3What does the contempt plea allege about Delhi Metro station closures? It alleges that authorities continued with their decision to shut metro stations, in violation of the Courts Friday order. 4What was the CJP protest in Delhi about? The protest, called by the Cockroach Janta Party and opposition parties, was against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The plea was filed against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan IAS, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar IPS, and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara IAS. Filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, the petition alleges that the officials deliberately violated the court's directions. Tripathi was also among the petitioners who sought an independent investigation into the violence during the student protests at Jantar Mantar in July. The petitioner has claimed that officials in Delhi have closed metro stations without valid grounds and cancelled train services without justification, despite the apex court directing the authorities to allow public transport to function with appropriate regulation so that residents of the national capital were not inconvenienced. The plea further claims that the ongoing restrictions have severely "crippled public life" in Delhi, causing hardship to commuters. The petitioner stated, "Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the Bench of Hon'ble the Chief Justice, the Contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories. This deliberate recalcitrance has severely crippled public life across the National Capital Territory, stranding essential travelers, and amounts to an intentional attempt to bypass and undermine the authority and majesty of this Hon'ble Court." In the contempt plea, the petitioner argued that despite the Supreme Courts order, metro station gates at GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya were closed, with passengers allowed to exit only through manually regulated gates on Friday night. The court noted that instructions had been issued to cancel Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations the following day and to close 57 Delhi Metro stations from 9 pm that evening. It observed that the "notifications are overreaching, as they impose a complete ban upon essential public transportation". As the CJP gears up for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, the national capital has turned 'khaki,' with waves of barricades lining streets, news agency PTI reported. Paramilitary personnel in green and khaki uniforms, including members of the BSF and Rapid Action Force (RAF), marched alongside city police towards Parliament Street Police Station, carrying heavy rucksacks, tactical equipment and rifles. Warnings rang out over loudspeakers as several layers of barricades sealed off major intersections. Thousands of security personnel guarded Jantar Mantar, turning the area into a heavily fortified zone. (with inputs from agencies)

AAP's Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh clarified on Friday that the October 10 protest in Delhi would be organised by the CJP and not AAP, while asserting that members of his party would participate in the demonstration. "The CJP protest is to save democracy. We also participated in the protest on October 2. A nationwide agitation is scheduled for October 10 to stop vote theft, scrap the Special Intensive Revision process, cancel state elections allegedly conducted through irregularities, involve the Chief Justice of India in the CEC selection process, and hold elections across the country using ballot papers," Singh said. He said, "It is not our protest; it is the CJP's protest. All parties had participated last time as well, including the Samajwadi Party, Left parties, the Biju Janata Dal and us. Everyone will participate in the CJP protest." The Congress distanced itself from the CJP protest in Delhi. Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, will be in Chennai on Saturday for the next edition of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'. In an Instagram post, CJP had said, "10th October. Jantar Mantar 2.0. We're coming together again to raise our voice against Gyanesh Kumar. Thousands of us are expected..." The protest is being held against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with the groups demanding Kumar's resignation. Over 250 trains connecting New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations with destinations across the country were also cancelled ahead of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Left parties on Friday condemned restrictions imposed ahead of the October 10 mobilisation against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the Election Commission's functioning, demanding that the Delhi Police allow protesters to assemble at Jantar

headline: No permission for CJP protest in Jantar Mantar — Delhi Police cites 'serious' law and order concerns
content: Citing the possibility of "serious" law and order concerns as well as inconvenience to local residents and citizens, the Delhi Police has denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) for its planned October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar. In a formal communication addressed to CJP co-convenor Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna, the Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi district) noted that permitting the demonstration could trigger serious law-and-order issues, PTI reported. "In the larger public interest, the permission sought cannot be granted and is hereby denied," the letter stated. Quick answers to key questions 1Why did Delhi Police deny permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar? Police cited serious law-and-order concerns, possible inconvenience to residents and citizens, and alleged violations of protest conditions during an earlier gathering. It also said the communication received was an intimation rather than a formal permission application. 2How far in advance must an application for a protest at Jantar Mantar be filed? Applications to hold programmes at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days before the event. The CJP application was submitted on October 7, three days before the proposed October 10 protest. 3Why was the CJP planning a protest at Jantar Mantar? The CJP planned to protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The party cited alleged irregularities in the voter-list revision. 4What security measures were planned ahead of the CJP protest in Delhi? Around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across Delhi, with more than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces slated to assist. The New Delhi district was divided into 20 zones, and police increased checks at sensitive locations. 5How could the CJP protest security measures affect travel in Delhi? Entry and exit gates at 45 Metro stations were restricted, and traffic diversions were possible at 30 locations. Commuters were advised to check official updates, allow extra travel time and avoid non-essential journeys through New Delhi and central Delhi. The police highlighted that the communication sent by the CJP served merely as an intimation rather than a duly submitted application requesting permission. Under established guidelines, applications to hold programmes at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the proposed event date. Additionally, authorities pointed to past instances where protest conditions were allegedly violated, including gatherings exceeding stipulated time limits and creating subsequent law and order complications. Delhi has been placed under an unprecedented security blanket, with roughly 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel stationed across the capital in light of the planned CJP demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, according to PTI. To aid the Delhi Police in maintaining security, more than 120 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces are slated for deployment. Forces have been positioned at key strategic locations, and mock drills were carried out across multiple spots to evaluate response readiness. For strict oversight, the New Delhi district has been organised into 20 zones supervised by senior officers, including joint commissioners, deputy commissioners, and additional deputy commissioners, while special commissioners heading various wings are closely tracking updates. Extensive contingents of police personnel have taken up positions across the city, managing barricades and monitoring vehicular traffic as security tightens ahead of the protest. Visuals from early morning revealed a dense security presence surrounding the protest site, alongside officers posted along routes and checkpoints citywide. Traffic continued to move smoothly as police kept a close watch on vehicles entering and leaving the area, stopping and checking some cars, PTI said. Entry and exit restrictions have been placed on 45 metro stations, alongside heightened surveillance across Delhi's border points, railway stations, bus terminals, and other sensitive pockets. Commuters have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel, build extra travel time into their schedules, and plan ahead if heading to airports, railway stations, or inter-state bus terminals via New Delhi and central Delhi. The traffic police stated that restrictions remain subject to real-time adjustments and may be eased or tightened depending on the situation. The CJPs October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar is being held against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with groups pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar is confronting allegations of tampering with voter lists under the pretext of the SIR exercise, as well as sidestepping his two colleagues to modify Form 6, the vital document used for voter registration.

headline: 35,000 Cops, Mass Detention Centres, High-Tech Body Cams: Delhi Police's Massive Plan For CJP Protest
content: From drones and rooftop surveillance to preventive detentions, Delhi Police has put a multi-layered security operation in place to contain Saturday's demonstration. Delhi is witnessing an extensive security operation on Saturday as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) presses ahead with its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar despite police refusing permission. With authorities anticipating a large mobilisation, elaborate arrangements made in the run-up to October 10 are now in force across the national capital. - Metro Curbs, Cancelled Trains, Extra CCTVs: Delhi Turns Into Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest Tomorrow - Delhi Traffic Advisory Ahead Of October 10 CJP Protest: Check Affected Routes, Diversions - Being Pressured...: Abhijeet Dipke Says CJP Volunteers Getting Police Notices Ahead Of Delhi Protest - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media The demonstration, dubbed Jantar Mantar 2.0, has been called to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. A few protesters have already been detained near Janpath in the Connaught Place area. Over 35,000 Personnel Deployed, 20 Security Zones Created More than 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel are deployed across the national capital, according to ANI, as authorities seek to prevent unauthorised gatherings and maintain law and order. For closer supervision, the New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones, with joint commissioners, deputy commissioners and additional deputy commissioners assigned monitoring responsibilities. Special commissioners heading various units are also overseeing the security operation. Additional women police personnel have been called in from Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. Police have also conducted mock drills to test their response to possible disturbances. According to ANI, Delhi Police teams have been instructed to detain anyone attempting to stage an unauthorised demonstration, regardless of where it takes place. CAPF units have been directed not to issue weapons for protest-related deployment, while Delhi Police personnel are authorised to carry lathis and batons. Officers have also been advised against engaging in verbal confrontations with protesters amid concerns about videos of police interactions being circulated online. Six Detention Centres Delhi Police has designated six facilities for accommodating protesters detained during Saturdays demonstration. According to ANI, the locations are Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Yamuna Sports Complex, Surajmal Stadium and community centres in Daulatpur and Pandrawal. Police have already detained a few protesters near Janpath in the Connaught Place area on Saturday. Police sources told PTI that around 30 to 40 people with criminal records were picked up ahead of the demonstration as part of efforts to prevent possible disturbances. The authorities are also monitoring individuals suspected of being able to mobilise crowds for the protest. Surveillance has been increased near their residences, and police are tracking their movements. Body Cameras, Drones And Facial Recognition Systems Technology is another major component of the security arrangements, with police using recording equipment and planning aerial and rooftop surveillance to monitor developments. Personnel deployed for Saturdays protest are wearing body cameras on their uniforms. The devices can record footage even in darkness, helping document interactions between officers and protesters. A police personnel explained that the cameras could help establish the facts if allegations of manhandling were made. These body cams are to protect us and others. In situations of manhandling, allegations are levelled against Delhi Police. So, these body cams will prove whether we did anything to anyone or not. This will record everything" the personnel said. The security plan also includes facial recognition systems, additional CCTV cameras, drones and rooftop spotters across central Delhi, according to ANI. Police are simultaneously examining social media activity linked to the proposed demonstration. More than 200 content creators are reportedly under scrutiny as authorities monitor posts and messages that could be connected to efforts to mobilise participants. The affected areas include Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Mandi House and Patel Chowk, along with major intersections on Ashoka Road, Janpath, Sansad Marg and surrounding stretches. Other locations where traffic may be affected include the Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg junction, Barakhamba Road, Lodhi Road flyover and stretches near Bhikaji Cama Place and Moti Bagh. Police personnel are stationed at barricades and checking vehicles at selected locations. The security operation also extends to Delhis borders, where additional checks are being conducted on vehicles entering the capital. Hotels, guest houses, lodges and dharamshalas are being checked, while vigilance has been increased at railway stations, bus terminals and other transit points. Delhi Traffic Police has said diversions may be tightened or relaxed depending on developments on the ground. Home Ministry Directs States To Coordinate With Delhi Police The Union Home Ministry has also asked states and Union Territories to take preventive measures amid concerns that CJP supporters may attempt to enter Delhi despite the denial of permission. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has written to police chiefs across the country, asking them to coordinate with Delhi Police and strengthen security arrangements. The communication refers to the potential implications of a large mobilisation for law and order. I write to draw your immediate attention to the grave law & order and public order implications arising from a proposed mass mobilisation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, scheduled for 10.10.2026," the letter states. It also refers to the Delhi Police order dated October 9 rejecting the request to hold the demonstration. headline: Indian Railways train cancelled? Check refund rules for IRCTC e-tickets and counter tickets
content: Indian Railways has cancelled over 240 trains on Saturday, due to expected traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations ahead of a protest by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in the national capital. The cancellations include mail and express trains as well as passenger trains. If your train is among those cancelled, you may be wondering how to get your ticket fare back. The refund process depends on whether you booked an e-ticket through IRCTC or purchased a ticket from a railway reservation counter. IRCTC refund rules for cancelled trains According to IRCTC, passengers are eligible for a full refund of their ticket fare if Indian Railways cancels a train. No cancellation charges apply, and the refund process is automatic. Passengers with confirmed or RAC e-tickets do not need to cancel their tickets online or file a Ticket Deposit Receipt (TDR). The refund will be credited directly to the same account used to book the ticket. The refund process generally takes 3 to 7 working days from the trains scheduled departure. No action required on the part of users. Users are also requested not to give response to any false call received in this regard of claiming fast refund and asking for your credentials in any form. IRCTC never asks for user credentials for making refund, it said. How to get a refund if Indian Railways cancels your train. (Image generated using AI) - How to check train cancellation and refund status on IRCTC To check the cancellation status of your ticket, log in to the IRCTC e-ticketing website and follow these steps: - For cancellation status: Go to My Account My Transactions Ticket Cancellation History. - For refund status: Go to My Account My Transactions Ticket Refund History. Indian Railways counter tickets: How to claim a refund If a passenger purchased train ticket from a railway reservation counter, then they need to visit a computerised Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counter to claim the refund. He/she should obtain information about the refund process from the PRS counter based on the payment method used. Passengers can check refund rules for e-tickets and counter tickets. (Image generated using AI) How to check whether your train has been cancelled or not? Before leaving for the station, the passengers are advised to check their trains running status and cancellation information through the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or by calling the Indian Railways helpline at 139.

Delhi is under an unprecedented security clampdown on Saturday ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) proposed march to Jantar Mantar, with 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed, 45 Metro stations shut, more than 250 trains cancelled and mobile internet suspended in parts of the Capital. More than 250 trains connected to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations have also been cancelled. Mobile internet services have been suspended within a four-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on Friday until 10 pm on Saturday, following approval from the Union Home Ministry. Internet services elsewhere in Delhi remain unaffected. Traffic diversions have been planned at 30 key points from 6 am, including around Connaught Place, Mandi House, Patel Chowk and Jantar Mantar. Commuters have been advised to avoid non-essential travel and allow extra time for journeys to railway stations, bus terminals and the airport. 35,000 Personnel Deployed The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 security zones, each monitored by senior police officers. Police may restrict vehicles entering New Delhi after 6 am, depending on the security assessment. Liquor shops across Delhi have been ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10. Home Ministry Steps In The Union Home Ministry has directed states and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police, maintain real-time intelligence sharing and take preventive measures against attempts to enter the Capital unlawfully. In a letter to all state DGPs, the ministry directed states and UTs to coordinate with Delhi Police and take immediate preventive measures amid concerns that CJP supporters could attempt unauthorised entry from various states/UTs into Delhi to disturb public peace and order". The ministry views the maintenance of law and order and public order as a non-negotiable constitutional imperative. Strict and uncompromising execution of the above is solicited to uphold the rule of law," it said. Delhi Police Joint Commissioner Nupur Prasad said the protest application was submitted on October 7, just three days before the proposed march, whereas the rules require at least 10 days notice. CJP Leaders Defiant Despite Detention Threat CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das are expected to arrive at Delhi airport on Saturday morning to lead the proposed march to Jantar Mantar. In a video message late Friday night, Dipke said Saturdays protest in Delhi should not stop even if he was detained. Tomorrow is our march. I dont know what will happen to me, whether I will be arrested from the airport or will be later arrested. I will not be cowed down because we want to save the democracy in the country. I am not scared even if I am detained. The government can slap us with NSA or UAPA," Dipke said. The CJP alleged that 15-30 supporters travelling from Pune were forced to deboard the Goa Express at Itarsi Junction in Madhya Pradesh and detained. It also claimed that activists from West Bengal, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh were intercepted, while its spokesperson Deepak Baliyan and his brother were allegedly assaulted in Rajasthan. The party demanded the release of those detained and safe passage for supporters travelling to Delhi. It also criticised the restrictions on transport and mobile internet, calling them an attack on democratic rights. (With inputs from agencies) The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) organized the protest march to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities and voter-list tampering during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

headline: Trump takes suit against Hillary Clinton over 2016 election to Supreme Court
content: President Donald Trump asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia. The Republican President filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly $1 million in sanctions against Mr. Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A U.S. appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions. Mr. Trump's lawyers wrote in the appeal that Supreme Court review of the case is needed in order to protect the Presidency. They wrote that the decisions by the lower courts reflect "a deeply troubling trend of federal courts using sanctions and disciplinary threats to punish the President and his lawyers for legitimate legal positions that those courts (erroneously) reject." In 2022, when he was out of office after losing the 2020 election, Mr. Trump sued Ms. Clinton, Mr. Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida. Mr. Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Ms. Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia. The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood, among other claims. Mr. Trump defeated Ms. Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021. U.S. government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between members of the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favor. Mr. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax. Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Mr. Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Mr. Trump regained the Presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024, and has continued to make those false claims. 'POLITICAL MANIFESTO' U.S. District Judge Donald Middlebrooks dismissed Mr. Trump's lawsuit against Ms. Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Mr. Trump waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Mr. Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him. Mr. Middlebrooks later ordered Mr. Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly $1 million in fees and costs, imposing the sanctions for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative." The judge also faulted Mr. Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts. Mr. Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories. The Atlanta-based 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions. "Many of Mr. Trump's and Ms. Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated. In Friday's filing, lawyers for Mr. Trump and Ms. Habba said the time limit for filing the lawsuit should have been extended because he chose to defer suing during his first term in office in order to carry out his constitutional responsibilities as President. "This Court's intervention is necessary to protect the Presidency, and to prevent judicial disagreement from becoming a license to punish its advocates," the filing stated. Mr. Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the Justice Department, issued a 2019 report on his investigation. The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion, but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities. Mr. Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the election in Mr. Trump's favor. Mr. Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to look into potential missteps by the FBI. In a 2023 report, Mr. Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Mr. Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Mr. Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe. Mr. Trump's Justice Department last year indicted Mr. Comey, one of several adversaries of the President hit with criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorising leaks to the news media. A federal judge subsequently dismissed the indictment, finding that the prosecutor who Mr. Trump handpicked to prosecute Mr. Comey had been unlawfully appointed. Mr. Steele, working for an opposition research firm that was hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier that alleged ties between Mr. Trump's campaign and Russia as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Mr. Trump denied.

headline: 'India has lowest data prices, lowest cost payment systems': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu responds to Elon Musk
content: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has responded to Elon Musk's criticism of India's regulatory framework for satellite internet services, citing the country's low mobile data prices, affordable medicines and low-cost digital payment systems to argue that competition has benefited consumers. In a post on X, Vembu defended the role of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani's Jio in bringing down data prices and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government had encouraged competition and the growth of startups. "These are the facts Elon," Vembu wrote, responding to the Tesla and SpaceX CEO's remarks about Starlink's entry into India and alleged monopolistic practices. Quick answers to key questions 1What did Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu say in response to Elon Musk's Starlink claims? Vembu pointed to India's low mobile data prices, affordable medicines and low-cost UPI payments as evidence that competition benefits consumers. He also said the government had encouraged competition and startup growth. 2How did Vembu say Jio helped lower data prices in India? Vembu said Reliance Jio's launch was directly responsible for the low data prices Indians enjoy. He cited the widespread use of dual-SIM phones and large data plans as signs that mobile data is affordable. 3Why did Elon Musk accuse India of blocking Starlink? Musk alleged that business interests were preventing Starlink from entering India and questioned the delay in its approval. He said Starlink had complied with India's laws and requirements. 4How did the Indian government respond to Musk's claim that Starlink was being blocked? The Ministry of Communications called the allegation baseless, saying India has a fair, non-discriminatory authorisation framework for satellite services. It said security assessments for the licensed operators were underway. 5What must Starlink do before it can begin commercial services in India? A telecom licence alone does not allow Starlink to start operations. It must meet security conditions and obtain spectrum assignment before beginning commercial services. Vembu argued that India offers some of the world's lowest data prices, pointing to the widespread use of dual-SIM smartphones and large mobile data plans. "India has the among the lowest data prices in the world. It is so good that I don't even bother to connect to local Wifi when I travel in India and just tether my phone to work on my computer. Indians routinely have dual SIM phones with large data plans because they are so affordable. Ambani's launch of Jio is directly responsible for the low data prices Indians enjoy. India has among the lowest drug prices in the world (and going lower still). People who visit India buy medicines to take home quite regularly now. India has among the lowest cost payment systems in the world in UPI. On the other hand, Tesla is protected from Chinese competition in the US market, keeping EV prices higher in America than elsewhere. Prime Minister Modi has worked hard to create a competitive economy where the benefits flow to the average Indian. His government does not tolerate monopolies. He has also actively promoted and encouraged a massive surge in startups and that is the best signal of a highly competitive economy. Directly due to Modi government policy, Indian startups are making major advances in low cost rockets and that poses a threat to SpaceX the same say the Chinese EVs threaten Tesla. These are the facts Elon." Vembu's remarks came after Musk questioned whether Indian business interests were preventing Starlink from entering the country's satellite communications market. Musk, in a post on X on Wednesday, alleged that Starlink was being blocked in India by certain business interests. "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are... This is a crime against the people of India!" the tech mogul wrote. On Thursday, Musk again questioned the delay in Starlink receiving a licence to operate in India, claiming that the company had complied with the government's requirements. "Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he wrote. Musk subsequently took another swipe at Mukesh Ambani, sarcastically referring to him as India's prime minister while questioning the role of business interests in Starlink's entry into the country. "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO wrote. "Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" he asked, adding, There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. In his Friday post, Musk also argued that Starlink had helped save lives during natural disasters when other communications systems failed. He said allowing the company to operate in India could similarly help save men, women and children across the country. The Ministry of Communications rejected the allegations in a statement issued on Thursday morning, calling the claim baseless. "A post is being circulated on social media regarding the fairness of India's regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services," it said. The government also said the security assessment required for satellite communication services was underway. Starlink, owned by SpaceX, is among three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services that have been granted telecom licences by the Centre. The other two are Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Jio Platforms. However, receiving a telecom licence does not by itself allow the companies to begin offering services. They must also demonstrate compliance with security conditions before spectrum can be assigned and commercial operations can begin. The Centre has said the security assessment, which forms part of this process, is underway. headline: Vance expresses doubts about Pentagon plan to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution
content: President J.D. Vance cast doubt on Friday (October 20, 2026) on whether the Pentagon will livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan in December but told reporters that if it is livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it. The Republican V-P said, I don't know that that's actually going to happen, when asked about the plans that the Pentagon confirmed on Thursday (October 8, 2026). But Mr. Vance then tried to set aside the controversy over the plans for a public execution and said Hasan's crimes should not be forgotten. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people and injuring 32 others in a shooting spree at the military base in 2009. So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people, Mr. Vance said. Now, that said, I mean, look, if it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it, he added. Mr. Vance is a convert to the Catholic Church, which has long opposed capital punishment. President Donald Trump had endorsed Hasan's execution by firing squad during a Wednesday (October 7, 2026) political event in Texas, suggesting he deserves it. However, Mr. Trump was noncommittal when asked on Friday (October 9, 2026) whether he wanted the execution livestreamed. "Well, they're making a determination about that, Mr. Trump told reporters before travelling to a political event in Syracuse, New York. But he again endorsed the firing squad as the method. He will be killed. He will be, through firing squad, he told reporters. I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes. And I think the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him. Mr. Trump did not answer when asked if he would watch a livestreamed execution. Earlier on Friday morning (October 9, 2026), the head of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the U.S. government's decision to livestream Hasan's execution. It is with shock and great sorrow that I have learned of the Department of War's decision to publicly livestream the execution, Archbishop Paul S Coakley, president of the conference, said in a statement. He added that the decision was a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered. Mr. Trump approved the execution by firing squad days after a failed attempt to execute Christa Pike by lethal injection late last month pushed Tennessee's governor to halt further executions in that state this year. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the military hasn't executed a service member by firing squad since World War II. The last military execution took place on April 13, 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was executed by hanging. From Congress, lawmakers from both parties, Republicans and Democrats, widely condemned what they called the gruesome and disgusting decision to livestream the execution and implored the Pentagon to reverse course.

headline: Trump, Putin diesel deal: What it means for US fuel prices, global markets and the Russia-Ukraine war | Explained
content: What it means for US fuel prices and the Russia-Ukraine war Will Russian supplies stabilise global markets? US President Donald Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase diesel supplies to global markets, as soaring fuel prices threaten to become a political liability for Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections. The agreement comes as the US temporarily lifts sanctions on Russian fuel imports, reversing measures imposed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war against Ukraine. While the move could provide some relief to a tight diesel market, analysts have questioned whether it will bring sustained price reductions. Trump said on social media that he had a highly successful discussion with Putin, during which Russia agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and global markets, equivalent to about 2.25 million barrels. He added that Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons immediately thereafter, with additional volumes depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries damaged by Ukrainian attacks. The US Treasury Department issued a licence permitting imports of Russian diesel until April 7. Diesel prices have become a growing concern for the Trump administration, with the fuel essential for agriculture, home heating and trucking. Prices have risen 70% since the US and Israel launched the war with Iran on February 28, according to the report. Average US diesel prices reached $6.28 a gallon on Thursday, according to the AAA motorist group, putting pressure on farmers, ranchers and truckers. Diesel futures fell almost 5% following news of the agreement and were trading at $4.64 a gallon. However, analysts cautioned against expecting lasting relief. Rory Johnston, an oil market researcher and founder of CommodityContext.com, called the agreement a nothing burger, arguing that Russia typically exports substantially more diesel when its refineries are not under attack. It's clearly not a fix, but another stream to aid a very tight diesel market, said Jim Mitchell, an analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie. The agreement could provide Moscow with additional revenue despite US sanctions imposed on Russian oil companies in October 2025 over the war that began in 2022. The additional income could help Putin continue the war against Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy criticised the move as a weak decision on the part of strong partners. Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world, he said on X, warning that Russia would repay the concession with further attacks. Republican Representative Don Bacon also opposed the decision, arguing that Washington should use sanctions to pressure Moscow rather than ease restrictions. The deal offers an additional source of supply as the wars in Iran and Ukraine intensify global fuel shortages. However, the promised volumes may not be sufficient to offset broader supply disruptions. Meanwhile, Trump is considering measures to boost domestic production, including using the Cold War-era Defense Production Act to expand refining capacity and bypass regulations restricting energy production. The twin approach highlights the administration's challenge: easing fuel prices quickly while reducing supply vulnerabilities without undermining its pressure campaign

headline: CJP protest: Is travel from Noida, Gurugram to Delhi affected today? Check key traffic routes, border status
content: Ahead of a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, Delhi is under an unprecedented security blanket, with around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the city. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, citing inadequate notice and concerns over compliance with rules during an earlier protest. The commute for those travelling to New Delhi from Noida or Gurugram will likely be severely affected today. Quick answers to key questions 1Is traffic from Noida to Delhi affected by the CJP protest? Yes. Heavy queues were reported on the Sarita ViharKalindi Kunj stretch, with security checks and congestion affecting travel into Delhi. 2Are there delays at the GurugramDelhi border during the CJP protest? Yes. Barricades and security screenings at the Sarhaul border have reduced road space, causing long queues and congestion on connecting roads from Cyber City, Udyog Vihar and MG Road. 3Which routes can drivers consider when travelling between Delhi, Noida and Gurugram? The advisory suggests considering the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway and MG Road where feasible. Check current traffic updates before setting out, as restrictions may change with the situation. 4Are Delhi Metro stations closed because of the CJP protest? Entry and exit gates at 45 stations are restricted, including Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat and Mandi House. The restrictions do not mean the entire Metro network is shut; check DMRC announcements before travelling. 5Should I allow extra time to reach Delhi railway stations or the airport on October 10? Yes. Traffic diversions, security checks and congestion may delay journeys, and some trains serving New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin were reported cancelled. Check your train status and allow extra travel time. As many as 45 metro stations face entry and exit restrictions, and surveillance has been increased at the national capital's borders, railway stations, bus terminals and other sensitive locations. With restrictions affecting major transport hubs and several parts of the city, commuters have been advised to check official announcements and plan their journeys accordingly. The congestion, which began building up on Friday evening, has turned major arterial routes into severe bottlenecks. The stretch between Sarita Vihar and the Kalindi Kunj border, a primary artery for Delhi-Noida traffic, witnessed bumper-to-bumper vehicle queues extending over long distances on Friday. Similarly, at the Sarhaul border connecting Gurugram to Delhi, heavy police barricading and security screenings have drastically reduced carriageway space, creating long lines of cars and buses. The spillover effect has congested connecting roads from Cyber City, Udyog Vihar, and MG Road. Personnel from the Delhi and Gurugram traffic police have been deployed at the border and nearby intersections to regulate vehicle movement. Police have also intensified vehicle checks at these border points, inspecting buses and screening groups of passengers deemed suspicious. According to reports, regular journeys that normally take 15 to 20 minutes are currently stretching into gruelling 1-2 hour waits. Motorists are being advised to remain patient and consider alternative routes such as the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway and MG Road where feasible. Inside the capital, the Delhi Traffic Police rolled out a comprehensive advisory warning of diversions at 30 key locations starting from 6 am on Saturday. Delhi Traffic Police has warned of disruptions around Connaught Place, Mandi House, Jantar Mantar, Patel Chowk and other key intersections in central Delhi. According to the traffic advisory, the affected stretches include the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Tolstoy Marg-Janpath crossing, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk, Gol Dak Khana and Windsor Place. Traffic movement may also be affected at Mandi House, the Chelmsford Road and Sansad Marg intersections with Connaught Place's outer circle, the Barakhamba Road intersection and the Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg junction. Other locations include the Chelmsford Road-Connaught Place outer circle intersection, Bharion Road-Mahatma Gandhi Marg intersection, Lodhi Road flyover, Neela Gumbad roundabout, Madarsa T-point, Samrat Hotel roundabout, Sardar Patel Marg-Panchsheel Marg crossing, the underpasses beneath the Bhikaji Cama Place and Moti Bagh flyovers, and the Ring Road-San Martin Marg intersection. Commuters have been urged to avoid non-essential travel towards railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs), and the airport via New Delhi and Central Delhi. Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Dinesh Gupta clarified that while no roads are completely closed off, real-time decisions on traffic management are being implemented based on the evolving law-and-order situation on the ground. Those hoping to rely on public transportation to bypass the road traffic will find little relief, as the transit network is facing massive operational curbs. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has closed the entry and exit gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations from Friday night. The affected stations include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, New Delhi, Patel Chowk, Mandi House, Janpath, Supreme Court, ITO, Kashmere Gate and several stations in south and northeast Delhi. According to DMRC, the restrictions will remain in place on Saturday until further notice. Interchange facilities will be available at the affected stations, except at the New Delhi metro station, where restrictions will apply. Railway passengers are also likely to face disruptions, with several trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm reported cancelled. However, Police have clarified that passengers with valid train tickets will not be stopped from travelling and that action will be taken against those attempting to breach law and order. Despite the heavy deployment of security personnel and sweeping transit bans, the Supreme Court on Friday weighed in on the situation, backing the right to protest and criticising the blanket transit bans in Delhi as over-reaching.

headline: Trump says Norway has 'indelible stain' for not awarding him Nobel Peace Prize
content: U.S. President Donald Trump reiterated his complaints on Friday (October 9, 2026) about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, calling it a disgraceful and embarrassing decision that had left a stain on Norway, which hosts the Nobel committee. Mr. Trump unleashed on Norway hours after the committee awarded this years prize to Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza. Mr. Trump called Ms. Pillay a mystery person during a campaign rally in Syracuse, New York. I never heard of the person. Nobody did. Each year of his presidency, Mr. Trump has expressed disappointment at his failure to win the prize. This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision, Mr. Trump said. He listed a number of conflicts that he claimed a role in resolving and said he has helped prevent wars from breaking out between North and South Korea, Japan and North Korea, and China and Taiwan, without providing evidence. The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization. And we will not forget, Norway, he said.

headline: 'It's Not A Good Thing': Trump 'Unhappy' With Houthi Attacks On Saudi Arabia Airports
content: Donald Trump's remarks came after a new wave of cross-border attacks claimed by Yemen's Houthi rebels, including strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. US President Donald Trump condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying he was not happy" after strikes on airports in the kingdom killed people and injured dozens amid a fresh escalation in the conflict in Yemen. Asked by reporters at the White House about the attacks, Donald Trump said, Not good. Its not a good thing. Im not happy about it." His remarks came after a new wave of cross-border attacks claimed by Yemens Houthi rebels, including strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed three Saudi citizens, according to Saudi authorities. The attacks heightened concerns over the safety of civilian aviation and the security of key transport infrastructure in the Gulf, with several international airlines suspending flights to the Saudi capital. - Trump Rules Out Iran Strike Before Midterms, Cites 'Productive' Talks As Oil Prices Surge - 'A Decision To Make': Trump Warns Iran Of 'Easy Or Hard Way' As Tensions Remain High - 'Why Leave Them There?': Trump Says US Pulled Bombers From UK Air Base Over 'Some Threats' - Targeting Civilian Infrastructure Completely Unacceptable: India Condemns Houthi Attack On Saudi Airports Three Killed In Riyadh Airport Attacks Saudi Arabias General Authority of Civil Aviation said two attacks targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday (October 8). The strikes killed three Saudi citizens, including a Saudia airline pilot, and wounded several people of different nationalities. One attack targeted airport facilities, while another struck an aircraft belonging to state-owned carrier Saudia, causing material damage. The injuries ranged from minor to serious, according to the authority. The Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes, saying it had targeted the airport with two cruise missiles. The group also claimed to have attacked an airport in Najran, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, and fired ballistic missiles towards an airbase in Khamis Mushait. The latest strikes followed separate attacks earlier in the week on airports in Riyadh and Abha that killed three people and injured 36, according to Saudi authorities. Two women, a Moroccan and an Algerian, were killed in the attack on Abha airport, while a Sudanese national was killed in Riyadh. The earlier attacks injured 28 people in Abha and eight in Riyadh. Airlines Suspend Flights As Security Concerns Grow The attacks disrupted air travel to Saudi Arabia, prompting international carriers to suspend services to Riyadh amid growing security concerns. Lufthansa Group airlines suspended flights to the Saudi capital through October 16, while Air India and other Indian carriers announced temporary suspensions following the renewed Houthi threats. Several flights were cancelled and an Air India service travelling from Delhi to Riyadh returned to India. Two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday, October 8, killed three Saudi citizens, including a Saudia airline pilot, and wounded several people of different nationalities. The strikes caused material damage to airport facilities and an aircraft belonging to state-owned carrier Saudia.

headline: Jaishankar highlights shared aspirations, self-reliance in India-Africa partnership
content: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Friday (October 9, 2026) highlighted the historic India-Africa partnership, rooted in shared solidarity and a common pursuit of fairness, representation, and the freedom to shape their own future, while outlining key areas of cooperation between the two sides. Mr. Jaishankar arrived in Ethiopia on Thursday (October 8, 2026) from Cte dIvoire on the final leg of his three-nation tour of African countries, which also included Ghana. Addressing a gathering at the Adwa Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa, Mr. Jaishankar said the development visions of India and Africa emphasised industrialisation, which should not be denied by flooding markets with cheap goods or restricting market access. He highlighted the robust trade and investment ties between India and African countries across sectors such as manufacturing, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, energy, mining, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services and information technology. Mr. Jaishankar said self-reliance was a shared conviction that provided a strong foundation for the enduring partnership between India and Africa. India's development partnership with African countries was guided by the priorities of partner nations, he said, adding that India has "supported more than 220 projects" in areas such as "power generation, electricity transmission, water, agriculture, railways, healthcare, manufacturing and public infrastructure". He also highlighted India's capacity-building initiatives, saying more than 70,000 African students and professionals had received support from India over the past decade. Emphasising the growing role of technology in bilateral cooperation, Jaishankar pointed to the transformative impact of digital governance and expanding cooperation on India Stack. "The transformative impact of digital governance, as well as growing India Stack cooperation with Africa. Space, drones, and AI are new frontiers of this cooperation," he said. Mr. Jaishankar also underlined India's efforts to strengthen Africa's health security through vaccine support, pharmaceutical investments and the gifting of Bhabhatron cancer treatment machines. In a separate post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said India and Ethiopia shared the vision of 'AI for All' and its potential to advance development and prosperity. He also visited the Ethiopia Science Museum, describing it as a symbol of the country's efforts to build a technology-driven, knowledge-based economy. Science and innovation cooperation would play a greater role in the India-Ethiopia strategic partnership, he said.

headline: Panama earthquake today: President declares 'major disaster' as buildings collapse and aftershocks rattle country
content: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and roads across the Central American nation and prompting President Jose Raul Mulino to declare a major disaster. There were no immediate reports of casualties. The shallow earthquake was felt across Panama, which has a population of around 4.5 million, according to the National Civil Protection System. The tremor lasted approximately a minute, triggering panic in several areas and forcing people to evacuate buildings, AFP reported. Here is what we know about the earthquake, the damage it caused and its impact on transport and shipping infrastructure. The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the earthquake struck at 1756 GMT, with its epicentre located 10 kilometres (6 miles) from the small town of Pitaloza Arriba in central Herrera province. The USGS initially estimated the earthquake's magnitude at 8.0 before revising it to 7.7. The tremor was felt across the country, including Panama City, which is around 200 kilometres from the epicentre. Residents reported intense shaking, prompting evacuations from high-rise buildings. "I was scared because the shaking was very strong and prolonged. Heavy objects like dressers, the bed, and all the kitchen items were shaking," Salomon Andion, 46, told AFP after evacuating his 15-story building for the second time following aftershocks. Videos circulated on social media showed water spilling from the rooftop pool of a building more than 20 stories tall. Another video showed a bridge over the Panama Canal shaking violently while remaining upright as vehicles travelled across it. Panama's President Jose Raul Mulino described the situation as a major disaster, citing extensive damage to infrastructure. "We are facing a major disaster," Mulino said, adding that some roads had "completely collapsed." Health Minister Fernando Boyd said the worst-affected areas were the provinces of Herrera and Cocle, along with Los Santos in the southeast. The town of Tonosi in Los Santos was completely cut off, complicating efforts to reach residents and assess the damage. "We are trying to figure out how to get there by air, because it's impossible by land," Boyd said. In Penonome, a town in central Cocle province, residents described frightening scenes during the earthquake. "It was horrible, like nothing we ever experienced. My daughter was trapped in school," Juana Alveo, a 38-year-old cashier at a store in Penonome, told AFP. Former president Ricardo Martinelli also posted photographs on Instagram showing his house in the town of Sona in Veraguas province after it collapsed. Images shared by local media showed extensive damage to a church and a hotel in Penonome. President Mulino travelled to Penonome to coordinate the disaster response. Authorities issued a tsunami warning for the eastern Pacific following the earthquake, but the warning was subsequently lifted. The local geosciences institute recorded more than 80 aftershocks, including one with a magnitude above 6.0. The repeated tremors prompted further evacuations, including in Panama City, where residents left high-rise buildings as a precaution. Mulino urged the public to remain calm and avoid spreading unnecessary panic. "What happened should not be used to generate alarms and disorder," he wrote on X, adding that he had requested a report on the damage. The education ministry announced the suspension of classes in schools nationwide. Panama City's international airport, a major aviation hub for the region, was temporarily closed following the earthquake. The Civil Aeronautics Authority said several flights were diverted to other airports as a precaution. Despite the damage to roads and buildings, the Panama Canal Authority said shipping through the canal remained unaffected. The authority confirmed that the waterway, which connects the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, was operating "as normal." The canal is a major international shipping route, making the status of its operations an important consideration in assessing the earthquake's wider transport and economic implications. The leaders of Colombia, Ecuador and Guatemala sent messages of solidarity and offered to provide assistance to Panama. Authorities continued coordinating the disaster response as they assessed damage and explored ways to reach isolated areas. Earthquakes are rare in Panama and typically occur in the western province of Chiriqui, which borders Costa Rica. The latest tremor is at least the fourth earthquake measuring above magnitude 7.0 in Latin America this year, following devastating back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela's Guaira in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August. The scale of the damage in Panama, the number of aftershocks and access to affected communities remained key concerns as authorities worked to assess the consequences of the earthquake.

Pakistan speaks of combating terrorism while seeking to obscure the very question that this committee must confront- What happens when terrorists are financed, facilitated, trained, sheltered, or supported from the territory of a State?" headline: All 22 Indian Crew Members Safe After Drone Attack On Panama-Flagged Tanker Off UAE Coast
content: Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said that the government was in contact with the ship management company to ensure the crew's safety and well-being. A Panama-flagged crude oil tanker carrying 22 Indian nationals was attacked by a drone near Sharjah Anchorage off the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Friday (October 9) with all Indian seafarers on board safe, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said. The vessel, MT GEM NO. 2, was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, off the UAE coast, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). The strike triggered a fire on board, which was subsequently extinguished. - 5 Indian Seafarers Rescued After Kuwait-Flagged Tanker Hit By Projectile In Hormuz: Embassy - Indian Crew Member Injured, Two Foreign Nationals Dead In Russian Drone Strike On Vessel In Black Sea - Gwadar-Bound Cargo Attacked In Balochistan, Driver May Have Been Abducted: Sources | Exclusive - India Condemns Attack On Panama-Flagged Ship Off Oman, 11 Indian Crew Members Injured | News18 I am relieved to share that all 22 of our Indian seafarers onboard are reported to be completely safe," Sarbananda Sonowal said, adding that the government was in contact with the ship management company to ensure the crews safety and well-being. What Happened To The Tanker? UKMTO said a vessel had been struck by an unknown projectile on Friday but initially did not identify the ship. Its first update said the status of the crew, the extent of the damage and any potential environmental impact remained unknown, adding that authorities were investigating the incident. Two shipping and security sources later identified the vessel as the Panama-flagged crude oil supertanker GEM NO. 2, Reuters reported. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike. The incident occurred outside the Strait of Hormuz area, according to maritime security sources cited by Reuters. Iran Warns Ships Against Unauthorised Strait Of Hormuz Routes Irans Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy renewed its warning to vessels against taking unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passage for global energy shipments. The IRGC Navy said vessels violating designated routes through the waterway would be pursued and punished. It also said maritime freight must coordinate with the Persian Gulf Strait Authority before crossing the channel. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the worlds most strategically important shipping routes, carrying a substantial share of global oil shipments. The Panama-flagged crude oil tanker MT GEM NO. 2, carrying 22 Indian nationals, was struck by an unknown projectile near Sharjah Anchorage off the UAE coast on Friday, October 9, triggering a fire that was subsequently extinguished.

headline: Hurricane Isaias Snaps Power Lines as It Nears Florida Coast
content: Bloomberg) -- Hurricane Isaias triggered blackouts as it barreled closer to the US Gulf Coast Friday evening, bringing extreme wind gusts and a dangerous storm surge to the region. Isaias weakened as it neared landfall with winds topping out at 110 miles (177 kilometers) per hour, making it a strong Category 2 storm on the five-step Saffir-Simpson scale, the US National Hurricane Center said in an advisory at 8 p.m. New York time. The storm, which earlier in the day reached the status of a major hurricane, was about 45 miles south of Pensacola, Florida. More than 380,000 homes and businesses in Florida and Alabama already had lost power by nearly 8:30 p.m. New York time, as the storms eye neared the shore, according to PowerOutage.com The hurricane is expected to come ashore along the coast of the western panhandle of Florida. Storm surge and tropical storm warnings extended west into Louisiana. In addition to its damaging winds, Isaias is forecast to push as much as 9 feet (3 meters) of water ashore at the Alabama-Florida border, the center said. This is a life-threatening situation, Robbie Berg, a warning coordination meteorologist at the center, wrote in an earlier advisory. Persons located within these areas should take all necessary actions to protect life and property from rising water and the potential for other dangerous conditions. Oil producers in the US Gulf of Mexico have shut in 1,458,814 barrels per day of crude production in response to Hurricane Isaias, the equivalent to 72% of output in the region, the Marine Minerals Administration said in a statement Friday. Shut-ins also include 1.259 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas, or 59% of regional output and 129 platforms were evacuated as of noon in New York. Several ports are also shutting ahead of the hurricane, disrupting seaborne crude deliveries. Three fuel-making facilities are in or near the projected path, including Chevron Corp.s 356,000 barrel-a-day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi. Even small production losses could trigger sharp price increases, with US gasoline and diesel stockpiles already far below seasonal norms. Natural gas production in the Gulf has also fallen, with about 57% of regional output shut in. Still, Isaiass shift east has limited the hit to Gulf oil, gas and LNG facilities compared with earlier forecasts, even as the storm intensified, according to Gary Cunningham at Tradition Energy. Isaias is remaining stronger than originally projected but its track is more east, Cunningham said in an email, limiting the impact on Gulf production and LNG export facilities. Natural gas futures fell Friday as traders weighed the production losses against the potential for storm damage to curb regional energy demand. November gas was trading near $3.14 per million British thermal units Friday morning, after settling at $3.168 Thursday. Florida suspended tolls on bridges in Okaloosa and Santa Rosa counties to help people evacuate, while Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in 27 counties. President Donald Trump said he was canceling his plans to attend Saturdays football game between the University of Georgia and the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa to avoid disrupting the emergency response. After coming ashore, Isaias is forecast to race across Alabama and into the Tennessee and Ohio valleys, bringing as much as 8 to 12 inches of rain, said Tyler Roys, a meteorologist with commercial forecaster AccuWeather Inc. On the storms eastern side, as much as 8 inches may fall across parts of the Carolinas, including areas devastated by flooding from Hurricane Helene in 2024. In Alabama, the largest provider of multi-peril homeowners insurance is State Farm, with a 26.7% market share in 2025, according to the most recent data available from AM Best. In Florida, the leading insurers of homes are state-backed Citizens Property Insurance Inc., Florida Peninsula Insurance Co., and Universal Insurance Holdings Inc., all with more than a 7% market share last year as per the same data. Duke Energys Florida utility said workers are ready to respond to outages. Our crews are prepared to restore power as soon as conditions allow, said Todd Fountain, the utilitys storm director. At the same time, Tropical Storm Rachel is forecast to strike northern Baja California late Saturday, sending heavy rain and damaging wind gusts into Southern California, Arizona and as far north as Salt Lake City, Utah, Roys said. A shift in the track could bring the storm closer to San Diego, which would be a rare event. Further south, more powerful Hurricane Simon, with top winds of 100 mph, is forecast to possibly reach Category 4 strength Saturday as it nears landfall in Jalisco and Colima, potentially threatening the key port of Manzanillo, Mexicos busiest Pacific port. In addition to container cargoes and shipping to Asian markets, Manzanillo also hosts a key LNG import terminal, fuel storage terminals and a number of power plants. Heavy rain from Simon has already caused havoc in the Mexican state of Guerrero, with residents in several cities suffering electricity outages yesterday, according to state utility Comision Federal de Electricidad. As of Friday morning, CFE had restored about 90% of electricity in the affected area, the power companys head Emilia Calleja said in a press briefing. headline: Petrol and diesel prices today, October 10: How much does fuel cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
content: Indian refiners have felt the impact of global supply disruptions. US President Donald Trump announced that he has reached an agreement to secure diesel from Russia, marking a dramatic shift from years of US efforts to isolate Moscow over its war in Ukraine as Washington grapples with high fuel prices ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. Writing on social media on Friday, Trump stated that the deal was struck during a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, which was initially anticipated to focus on a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Trump revealed that Moscow will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel, with shipments of 500,000 tons to follow in November and one million tons immediately thereafter. He added that Russia will deliver an additional three million tons within a short period of time. The announcement runs counter to a sweeping Russia sanctions law signed by Trump last month, which was designed to restrict the oil and gas revenues funding Russia's military campaign in Ukraine.
