headline: CJP protest in Delhi: Transport, schools, shops affected; check what's closed
content: Delhi police is on alert ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday (October 10), with restrictions and precautionary measures affecting public transport, road traffic, schools, shops, and internet services. The Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed demonstration, which seeks the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police have stepped up security, with extensive checks at border points, railway stations, and other sensitive locations. Quick answers to key questions 1What is the CJP protest in Delhi about? The Cockroach Janta Party proposed a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the electoral-roll revision. Delhi Police denied permission for the protest. 2Are Delhi Metro trains completely shut during the CJP protest? No. The restrictions concern entry and exit at 45 stations, not a shutdown of the entire Metro network. Interchange facilities are available at affected stations except New Delhi; check DMRC updates before travelling. 3How will trains and roads in Delhi be affected on October 10? More than 250 train services have reportedly been cancelled, and traffic diversions may affect 30 locations from 6 am. Commuters should check their train status, allow extra travel time and monitor Delhi Traffic Police updates. 4Where and when will mobile internet be suspended near Jantar Mantar? Mobile internet services are set to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10. Internet services in the rest of Delhi are expected to remain unaffected. 5Are shops, liquor outlets and schools closed in Delhi for the protest? Connaught Place businesses have been advised to close, while liquor shops across Delhi have been ordered shut on October 9 and 10. Several schools and colleges have moved classes online or rescheduled meetings; the Connaught Place advisory is not a citywide business closure. The measures include entry and exit restrictions at 45 Delhi Metro stations, the cancellation of more than 250 train services, possible traffic diversions at 30 locations, and a temporary suspension of mobile internet services within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar. Several schools and colleges have shifted classes online or rescheduled parent-teacher meetings, while the New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA) has advised commercial establishments in Connaught Place to remain closed. Here is a breakdown of what is closed, what is disrupted and what commuters, students, shoppers and residents need to know. Delhi on October 10: What is closed and what is affected? Entry and exit gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations have been ordered closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, until further notice. The restrictions will continue on Saturday, October 10, according to the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC). Major stations affected include Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Janpath, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, ITO, Delhi Gate, Khan Market, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, Hauz Khas and INA. Other stations on the list include Shaheen Bagh, Jamia Millia Islamia, Okhla Vihar, Kalindi Kunj, Lajpat Nagar, Ashram, Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin, Welcome, Shahdara, Rithala, Rohini, Azadpur and Shivaji Stadium. The DMRC has said interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except at New Delhi Metro station. Importantly, the restrictions concern station entry and exit gates; they do not amount to a shutdown of the entire Delhi Metro network. Passengers should check the latest DMRC announcements before travelling. Rail services are expected to face significant disruption on October 10, with more than 250 train services connecting New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations with destinations across the country reportedly cancelled. The cancellations cover passenger trains scheduled to depart from their originating stations after 2 pm on October 9, as well as trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10. Departures from these stations and local train services have also been affected. Separately, the Bikaner Division of North Western Railway announced the cancellation of 13 Delhi-bound train services for Saturday, most of them originating in or passing through Haryana. Among the affected trains are: Kalka-Chandigarh-New Delhi Shatabdi (12006) Una-Chandigarh-New Delhi Jan Shatabdi Express (12058) Amritsar-Delhi Shatabdi (12014) Sirsa-Tilak Bridge Haryana Express (15308) Tilak Bridge-Bhiwani Express (14738) Bhiwani-Tilak Express (14737) Rewari-Old Delhi Passenger (54414) Old Delhi-Rewari Passenger (54421) Hisar-Old Delhi Passenger (54310) Hisar-New Delhi Passenger (54424) Railway officials cited operational reasons for the cancellations. Passengers should verify their individual train status and refund or alternative travel arrangements with the relevant railway authorities before leaving for the station. The Delhi Traffic Police has warned of possible traffic disruptions and diversions at 30 locations across the capital from 6 am on Saturday. The measures will depend on the prevailing law-and-order situation. Key locations where traffic movement could be affected include: Shankar Road-Vande Mataram 'T' Point Dhaula Kuan Flyover Jhandewalan and Panchkuian Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg Guru Nanak Chowk Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar Road Lodhi Road Flyover and Neela Gumbad Samrat Hotel roundabout Sardar Patel Marg-Panchsheel Marg crossing Bhikaji Cama Place and Moti Bagh Flyover Windsor Palace roundabout Rail Bhawan and Patel Chowk roundabouts RML Hospital roundabout The traffic police has advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance, allow extra travel time and avoid non-essential travel where possible. Those travelling to railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) or the airport through New Delhi and Central Delhi should account for potential delays and additional security checks. Possible restrictions on vehicles entering New Delhi after 6 am are also being assessed, according to police sources. For traffic assistance, commuters can call 1095 or 011-25844444. They should also monitor the Delhi Traffic Police's official website and social media channels for updates. Mobile internet services are set to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10, according to sources. The Union Home Ministry has approved the decision, the sources said. The restriction applies to mobile internet services within the specified area. Internet services in the rest of Delhi are expected to remain unaffected. The suspension is part of the security measures intended to prevent unauthorised gatherings and maintain law and order during the proposed protest. Residents and visitors in the affected area should plan for possible interruptions to mobile data access during the specified period. Several schools and colleges in Delhi have shifted classes online or rescheduled parent-teacher meetings ahead of the protest. The changes come amid concerns over transport disruptions, traffic diversions and security restrictions that could affect students, teachers and parents travelling across the city. The New Delhi Traders Association has advised shops, offices, restaurants and other commercial establishments in Connaught Place to remain closed on Saturday as a precautionary measure. The association urged shop owners and occupants of commercial premises to remain vigilant and cooperate with the advisory, citing the possibility of property damage and injuries during the expected protests. The advisory applies to commercial establishments in Connaught Place. It should not be interpreted as a blanket closure order for every market and business across Delhi. Liquor shops across Delhi have been ordered to remain closed on October 9 and October 10 as a preventive measure ahead of the proposed protest. The closure is part of the broader security arrangements being implemented in the capital. The Delhi High Court has directed that proceedings at the Patiala House and Rouse Avenue court complexes be conducted virtually on Saturday, October 10. All seven district court complexes in Delhi will otherwise remain open, according to the notification. The High Court has also directed that no adverse orders be passed in district courts because of the non-appearance of litigants, advocates, witnesses or accused persons. Urgent matters are to be adjourned for a short date, and undertrial prisoners are to be produced through virtual mode. Delhi Police has denied permission for the CJP's proposed protest, citing the short notice given for the event and alleged non-compliance with directions during an earlier protest. Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the application was submitted on October 7, only three days before the proposed gathering, whereas the applicable rules require applications to be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Security arrangements include a reported deployment of tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel, with more than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces expected to be involved. The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones for closer monitoring. Police have also conducted mock drills and stepped up checks at the capital's borders, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels, guest houses and other sensitive locations.

headline: Ladakh talks on Oct 15 to focus on powers of elected body, proposed governance model
content: The next round of meetings between the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ladakh representatives is scheduled to take place on October 15, officials have said. The discussions, which come over a month after the last round of talks in Delhi, are set to take place against the backdrop of deliberations on an additional constitutional provision and a proposed UT-level elected body for Ladakh. After last months meeting, the Ladakh administration proposed a new governance arrangement for the UT that would be neither a state nor a UT with a legislature, but a unique constitutional amendment requiring Parliaments approval. The MHA had also sent a set of questions to representatives of the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance the two bodies spearheading the movement for greater democratic representation in Ladakh. The questions, raised at a meeting between MHA officials and Ladakh representatives on September 9, urged them to deliberate on the shape, form and composition of a UT-level governance body with executive and financial powers. The talks took place after the Centre offered to introduce an additional constitutional provision, Article 371(K), for Ladakh. The questionnaire from the MHA seeks specifics from the representatives on seven key issues, from the formal name, composition and representation of the UT-level legislative body to its relationship with the existing Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. The MHA has also asked Ladakhi representatives to consult each other on the functions that should necessarily be exercised by the UT-level body in the interest of uniformity, coordinated development and effective administration, and those that should remain at the district level to protect local interests. The ministry has also sought clarity on a broad spectrum of concerns, including the principles that would guide the allocation of powers between the UT-level body and the LAHDCs. Members of the sub-committee have also been asked to specify which subjects should fall within the domain of the UT-level elected body, in tune with the basic structure of the Constitution, and whether such a unique model for Ladakh would require a legal opinion. These concerns are likely to form part of the deliberations between the two groups on October 15. In September, the KDA and ABL had submitted a list of non-negotiables to the MHA outlining their key demands, including a directly elected, constitutionally empowered UT-level legislature. Since the agitation for greater democratic control over Ladakh by its people took hold, representatives from the region have pushed a four-point agenda: statehood for Ladakh, safeguards under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, reservation of jobs for Ladakhs youth, and separate parliamentary constituencies for the two parts of the region. This agenda has driven agitations over the last three years.

headline: PM Modi: Bypoll results show people have deep-rooted connect with BJP-NDA
content: EVEN AS INDIA bloc MPs took their demand to sack Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to President Droupadi Murmus doorstep, the bypoll results for five Assembly seats and one Lok Sabha seat announced on Friday came as a shot in the arm for the ruling NDA alliance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed gratitude to the people for the added strength that the BJP-led alliance received in the form of the peoples mandate. Gratitude to the people for their continuous blessings! The Lok Sabha result of Nagaon (Assam) and Assembly results of Nandigram as well as Rejinagar (West Bengal) show yet again that the people have a deep-rooted connect with the good governance agenda of BJP-NDA, he said in a post on X. I congratulate the victorious BJP candidates and also applaud the hard work of our party karyakartas. I also congratulate our valued NDA ally, the AINRC, for their win in Thattanchavady in Puducherry. This mandate will give us added strength as we work tirelessly for the welfare of the people and to fulfil their aspirations for a brighter and more prosperous future, he said. Targeting the Opposition alliance, and especially Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the NDAs victories in the by-elections of West Bengal, Assam, and Puducherry, as well as the recent municipal elections in Rajasthan and Tripura indicate that the people have completely rejected the INDI Alliance. Despite the lies, confusion, and malicious propaganda of Rahul Gandhi and the INDI Alliance, the BJP is winning one election after another under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, Shah said in a post on X. Having lost their public base, these parties question institutions after every defeat, but the people have recognized this character of theirs. That is why, once again, they have expressed their unwavering faith in the BJP by giving it a resounding mandate he added, congratulating the Chief Ministers of the respective states. BJP president Nitin Nabin, expressing gratitude to janata janardan for the spectacular victory, said: The spectacular victory of BJP on the Nandigram and Rajnagar Assembly seats in West Bengal and the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam, along with the triumph of our ally party AINRC on the Thattanchavady Assembly seat in Puducherry, has once again proven that the people of the country stand firmly with the politics of development and good governance under the leadership of the esteemed Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji. Those who were trying to mislead the countrymen have once again been given a resounding response by the people through their votes he said. Adding the BJPs victory on eight Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha seats to the list of achievements, the partys national general secretary Smriti Irani termed it the victory of democracy over mobocracy and deceitocracy. All 10 Rajya Sabha candidates from Uttar Pradesh eight from the BJP and two from the Samajwadi Party were declared elected unopposed on Friday. The unanimous election of BJPs 8 Rajya Sabha candidates in Uttar Pradesh, along with the NDAs victories in the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam, the Nandigram and Rajnagar Assembly constituencies of West Bengal, and the Thattanchavadi Assembly constituency of Puducherry, reflect the peoples faith in the democratic process, she stated.

headline: Invest in question banks, set question paper closer to examination: House panel to National Testing Agency
content: Calling for a structural overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA), the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sports has called for a series of institutional and procedural reforms to strengthen examination security and rebuild public trust in the agency. The Committee has recommended a continuously updated question bank to minimise the risk of paper leaks, permanent recruitment of specialised staff, and a mechanism to allow candidates who arrive late at examination centres for genuine reasons to take the test without any extra time. In its 382nd report Reforms and Strengthening of the National Testing Agency presented to Rajya Sabha Chairman on October 9, the Mukul Wasnik-led committee said that investment in question banks is the most viable defence against paper leaks in the long run. NTA should invest in building a large, diverse, and continuously updated question bank which can be drawn on to set papers without the advance knowledge of the question-setters in the CBT format, question papers no longer have to be printed and transported to examination centres. Therefore, there is no compulsion to set question papers long in advance, the report said. Accordingly, the final question papers should be set very close to the examination, with questions drawn from the question bank vetted by experts using digital tools. It also emphasised a strict quarantine and sequestering of the final paper-vetters until the conclusion of the examination. The Committee also recommended that the NTA must rely on bona fide experts from top institutions like IITs and AIIMS to develop its question banks and for translation. It said that the agency must also develop a system to check the track record of said experts to establish their integrity and to rule out any conflict of interest before recruiting them. The Committee said that it broadly concurs with the phased transition to computer-based testing (CBT) and recommended that NEET-UG also move to this mode. However, it stressed that the transition must be preceded by investment in secure government-owned CBT infrastructure, particularly in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and rural areas. It said that adequate government-owned infrastructure must be in place so that reliance on private centres is avoided. It also said that 1,000 secure government CBT centres must be set up with a clear and phased timeline to facilitate the examinations. It also suggested that the NTA should itself financially support the establishment of mid-sized IT labs with 100-200 nodes in schools and colleges across the country and there must be at least 1 test centre in each district to offer all exams to minimise the stress and financial burden of transport and accommodation on students. The private institutions engaged as examination centres on a sub-contracted basis have often proved to be a weak link in examination security. Therefore, all centers must be owned and operated by the Union and/or State Government, it said. The committee recommended that NTA should create and maintain a national registry of blacklisted examination vendors. Further, it said that before rolling out the CBT mode, the NTA should consider a hybrid model where the encrypted questions may be delivered to the exam centre directly and then printed there itself, which the Committee has been informed is feasible, until full CBT readiness is achieved. The committee also proposed a mechanism to allow entry to students who arrive a few minutes late at the exam centre after taking an undertaking recording their late arrival and allow them to take the exam for the remainder period with no extra time. The panel also flagged the manpower shortage and urged the agency to expedite recruitment and develop its own permanent cadre.

headline: Panama Declares 'Major Disaster' After Powerful 7.7-Magnitude Quake; 80+ Aftershocks Recorded
content: The quake shook the Central American nation of around 4.5 million people for nearly a minute. There were no immediate reports of casualties. Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino declared a major disaster" after a powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck the country on Friday, collapsing roads and damaging buildings, while triggering a tsunami warning that was later lifted. The quake shook the Central American nation of around 4.5 million people for nearly a minute, sparking panic in the capital, Panama City, as residents fled high-rise buildings. There were no immediate reports of casualties. - Seemapuri Building Collapse: 3 Dead, Including Pregnant Woman And Child, Rescue Operations Continue - Lucknow Floods: Has Urbanisation Left The Gomti With Too Little Room To Breathe? - Tremors From Afghanistan Earthquake Felt In Kashmir: Safety Precautions Travellers Should Take - LinkedIn Cofounder Reid Hoffman Defends AI Data Centre Boom, Says It Is Keeping US Out Of Recession We are facing a major disaster," Mulino said, adding that some roads had completely collapsed". He travelled to Penonome to coordinate the emergency response. The US Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before revising it to 7.7. It placed the epicentre about 10 kilometres from Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province. Tsunami Warning Lifted A tsunami warning was issued for the eastern Pacific following the quake but was later lifted. The Panama Canal Authority said shipping through the strategic waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans remained unaffected and was operating normally. Panama Citys international airport was temporarily closed, forcing several flights to divert as a precaution, according to the Civil Aeronautics Authority. The Education Ministry also suspended classes nationwide. Leaders of Colombia, Ecuador and Guatemala sent messages of solidarity and offered assistance. Roads Collapse, Buildings Damaged Panamas Health Minister Fernando Boyd said Herrera and Cocle provinces, along with Los Santos in the south-east, were among the worst-hit areas. We are trying to figure out how to get there by air, because its impossible by land," he said. The town of Tonosi in Los Santos was completely cut off, with authorities exploring ways to reach it by air because roads were impassable. Images shared by local media showed extensive damage to a church and a hotel in Penonome. More Than 80 Aftershocks Recorded Panamas geosciences institute recorded more than 80 aftershocks, including one measuring above magnitude 6.0. Mulino urged people to remain calm and warned against spreading panic as officials assessed the destruction. We thank God for protecting the Panamanian people. We will immediately activate a structural evaluation and support plan for all the affected people," he wrote on X. Earthquakes are relatively rare in Panama, which typically experiences seismic activity in western Chiriqui province, near the Costa Rican border. (With inputs from AFP) Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino declared a major disaster after a powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck the country on Friday, causing collapsed roads, damaged buildings, and sparking panic.

headline: Trump Casts Doubt On Hegseth's Livestream Plan For Fort Hood Shooter's Execution Amid Outrage
content: Trump said that a decision on the proposed livestream had yet to be made, while making clear that he supported carrying out Hasan's death sentence by firing squad. US President Donald Trump on Friday cast doubt on plans to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the US Army psychiatrist sentenced to death for killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, contradicting Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had earlier confirmed that the execution would be broadcast publicly. Trump said that a decision on the proposed livestream had yet to be made, while making clear that he supported carrying out Hasans death sentence by firing squad. - Pete Hegseth Says Fort Hood Shooter's Execution By Firing Squad Will Be Livestreamed - US To Livestream Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasans Execution By Firing Squad, First Since 1945 - Trump Says Putin Agreed To 'Immediately' Supply Russian Diesel To US, Global Markets - Trump Says He'll Speak To Putin Soon Over Reported Plague Death As US Presses For Transparency They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed," Trump said of the execution, scheduled for December 3. I really dont care how he goes, as long as he goes." Vance Questions Livestream Plan US Vice President JD Vance also expressed uncertainty over whether the execution would be broadcast, saying he did not know if the proposal would go ahead. He added that he would not watch if it were livestreamed. I dont know that thats actually going to happen," Vance told reporters while campaigning in Ohio. If its ultimately livestreamed, Im not going to be watching it." On Thursday, Hegseth had confirmed that the military would ensure the public could watch the execution. Hasans execution would be the first by firing squad in the US military since 1945, according to Hegseth. Backlash Over Public Execution The proposal has drawn criticism from across the political spectrum. Republican Representative Austin Scott backed Hasans execution but said livestreaming it was associated with jihadist groups and that the US should hold itself to a different standard. While, Democratic Senator Mark Kelly said Hasan should face justice but questioned whether the US wanted to be associated with practices used by Iran and the Taliban. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights warned that livestreaming an execution would amount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture". Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, also called for the plan to be reconsidered. Amnesty Internationals Justin Mazzola said the death penalty violated human rights and warned that broadcasting Hasans execution would only compound the cruelty". Hasan was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013 after killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at Fort Hood, Texas. (With inputs from agencies) President Donald Trump cast doubt on whether the execution of Nidal Hasan would actually be livestreamed, stating that a final determination had not yet been made. While supporting the death sentence by firing squad, Trump noted that he ultimately did not care how the execution was carried out as long as it happened.

CEC Protest Live Updates: Delhi To Suspend Internet Services From 10 PM Tonight Till 10 PM Tomorrow Internet services in parts of Delhi will be suspended from 10 pm tonight until 10 pm tomorrow, ahead of the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The move comes amid heightened security arrangements in the national capital ahead of the protest. CEC Protest Live Updates: Delhi To Suspend Internet Around Jantar Mantar From 10 PM Ahead Of CJP Protest Mobile internet services will be temporarily suspended within a 4 km radius of Jantar Mantar in Delhi from Friday night ahead of the proposed Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest on October 10, according to an order issued by the Delhi Police Special Cell. The suspension will remain in place from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10, covering the area around the JanpathKartavya Path crossing. The Ministry of Home Affairs has approved the temporary suspension, with the order directing telecom operators to implement the restrictions across mobile internet technologies. Delhi Police has asked Airtel, Vodafone Idea, Jio and MTNL to enforce the order. The decision comes amid extensive security preparations for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar, where demonstrators are expected to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police have denied permission for the protest and imposed restrictions under Section 163 of the BNSS. Wear Saffron, Carry A Mace: Mahua Moitras Jantar Mantar Call Ahead Of CJP Protest Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra on Friday called on people to wear saffron and carry a mace while heading towards Jantar Mantar on Saturday. In a post on X, Moitra wrote, Lets all wear saffron tomorrow and carry a mace and move towards Jantar Mantar. Kaun rokega humein? Her post comes ahead of the proposed Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, which is being held against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police has denied permission for the demonstration and imposed restrictions in the New Delhi area, citing law and order concerns. Security has also been tightened across the capital ahead of the proposed protest. CEC Protest LIVE: 27 FIRs Filed Over CEC Protests In 7 Days Twenty seven FIRs were registered within seven days in connection with protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. BNS Section 3(5) was invoked in 22 cases, followed by Section 223(a) in 18, while Sections 221 and 132 appeared in 17 FIRs each. CEC Protest LIVE: Delhi Schools, Colleges Shift Classes Online, Postpone Exams Ahead Of October 10 Protest Several schools and colleges in Delhi have moved classes online, rescheduled parent teacher meetings and postponed examinations scheduled for October 10 amid heightened security concerns in the national capital. The decisions come ahead of the proposed CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 and amid restrictions on public transport in parts of Delhi. With entry and exit at several Metro stations being restricted and security being tightened across the city, educational institutions have made changes to their schedules to avoid inconvenience to students and staff. Some institutions have opted for online classes, while others have postponed exams and shifted scheduled parent teacher meetings in view of the anticipated disruption. The developments come as Delhi Police has imposed restrictions under Section 163 of the BNSS and stepped up security ahead of the proposed demonstration. Authorities have also announced restrictions on liquor shops and transport services as part of the security arrangements. CEC Protest LIVE: Sanjay Singh Clarifies October 10 CJP Protest Is Not AAP Event, Says Party Will Participate AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh on Friday clarified that the October 10 protest in Delhi will be organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and not by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), while saying AAP members would participate in the demonstration. Speaking to reporters in Sikandarpur after attending the thirteenth day ritual of senior Samajwadi Party leader Ram Govind Chaudhary, Singh said the protest was aimed at raising concerns over democracy and the electoral process. Singh said a nationwide agitation has been planned for October 10 over allegations of vote theft. He said protesters would demand the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), cancellation of state elections allegedly affected by irregularities, changes to the process of appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and the return to ballot paper voting. Clarifying AAPs position, Singh said the Delhi protest should not be described as an AAP event. It is not our protest; it is the CJPs protest, he said, adding that political parties had also joined the previous demonstration, including the Samajwadi Party, Left parties and the Biju Janata Dal. This Will Continue: Renuka Chowdhury Says Opposition Will Keep Fighting Over SIR, Gyanesh Kumar Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury has said the opposition will continue its protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Speaking about the ongoing protest, Chowdhury said the fight was about protecting rights guaranteed by the Constitution. This will continue. Until justice is served, it is our duty and our moral obligation to fight, she said. Chowdhury questioned why raising concerns over unemployment, the Constitution, citizens rights and the SIR should be considered wrong. She said the opposition would continue raising its voice through different platforms and in different ways. We must keep fighting. This is our moral obligation; this is our duty, Chowdhury said when asked how long the protest would continue. Her remarks come amid continuing opposition protests demanding action over alleged irregularities in the electoral roll revision process and calling for Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The Election Commission has rejected allegations of wrongdoing surrounding the SIR exercise. CEC Protest LIVE: Delhi Police Chain Barricades On Parliament Street Ahead Of CJP March Long chains have been used to secure several police barricades together on Parliament Street ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest on October 10. | Delhi | Long chains have been attached to several police barricades to keep them together, on Parliament Street, in view of CJPs call for protest on October 10 ANI (@ANI) October 9, 2026 CEC Protest Live: DYFI, SFI Workers March To Lok Bhavan To Protest CEC In Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, DYFI and SFI workers marched towards Lok Bhavan, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters. | Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala: DYFI and SFI workers march to Lok Bhavan demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police used water cannon to disperse the protesters. ANI (@ANI) October 9, 2026 CEC Protest News LIVE: SC On Curbs In Delhi Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest The Supreme Court questioned the petitioners challenging restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned October 10 protest, asking how it could balance protesters rights with those of citizens who need access to public transport and essential services without hearing from the organisers. How do we balance if the scales are not here before us? Give us something, the court asked, seeking details about the protest organisers and the expected number of participants. CEC Protest Live: Delhi Police Registers 25 FIRs Over SIR Protests Since Oct 2 The Delhi Police have registered 25 FIRs related to the SIR protests in the national capital since October 2, with Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra among those named, sources said. The cases relate to alleged vandalism of public property, assaults and scuffles involving police personnel, obstruction of government work and violation of prohibitory orders imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the New Delhi district. Police have taken action against protesters following repeated incidents of alleged lawlessness during the demonstrations, a police source said. CEC Protest Live: Delhi Police Denies Nod For Saturday's CJP Protest At Jantar Mantar Delhi Police has denied permission for a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 10, a senior police officer said on Friday. Police cited late submission of application and rule violations during a previous demonstration as reasons for denying the permission. Police received the application seeking permission for the protest on October 7, just three days before the protest. However, according to rules, such applications have to be submitted at least 10 days in advance, said Joint Commissioner of Police, New Delhi range, Nupur Prasad. CEC Protest Live: Delhi HC Refuses To Grant Urgent Hearing To IYC's Plea For Protest At Jantar Mantar The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to grant an urgent hearing on a plea of the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) seeking permission to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise. The plea was first mentioned on Thursday and the bench allowed it to be listed on Friday. Since it did not get listed for hearing on Friday, the counsel again mentioned that the plea be heard today itself.

headline: From Maharashtra apartment to Indonesian wilds: Rescued orangutan set to return home
content: The orangutan, currently housed in the Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC) at Vantara in Jamnagar district of Gujarat, was seized by the Thane forest division along with nine other wildlife species suspected to be part of a consignment of illegally trafficked animals. Indonesian authorities and people aware of the matter in India said relevant permits and approvals, especially from India, have already been issued with a few formalities pending on the Indonesian side, and the repatriation is likely to happen in the coming days. Officials from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and the Ministry of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia have confirmed that the repatriation process is in an advanced stage. Post seizure, the primate was initially sent to the Balasaheb Thackeray Gorewada International Zoological Park, Nagpur. Later, it was transferred to the GZRRC in March 2025, on the order of a Supreme Court-appointed high-powered committee (HPC), headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Deepak Verma, according to official records. Maharashtras then Chief Wildlife Warden, M Srinivasa Rao, had directed the Gorewada Zoo on March 1, 2025, to transfer the animal to GZRCC for proper rehabilitation until its final repatriation. This directive cited the HPCs view that keeping the orangutan in a local zoo might not be suitable, according to the records. A repatriation process, in coordination with Indonesia, was already underway in 2025 when the HPC ordered the primates transfer. Indonesia had issued an import permit, the records showed. The HPC was tasked in 2023 to deal with welfare of wild animals, including, among other, procurement or welfare of wild animals by any rescue or rehabilitation centre or zoo and recommend transfer of ownership of captive animals or of seized wild animals. Under the CITES international treaty Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora which regulates cross-border trade in animals and plants, orangutans are listed under Appendix-I, restricting their trade strictly to purposes such as research, transfers between recognised zoos and for breeding projects. The treaty encourages repatriation, if it is feasible, and Indias Wildlife Protection Act too mandates the same after consultation with the likely country of origin or export. On the orangutan seized in Thane in 2024, Ristianto Pribadi, Director of the Bureau of Public Relations and International Cooperation, Ministry of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia, said preparations for the animals repatriation have advanced through continued cooperation between Indonesian and Indian authorities. The Indian authorities have shared relevant permits and approvals issued by their competent authorities for this orangutans repatriation. Indonesia is completing the required import and entry documentation in coordination with the relevant ministries and agencies. Both sides continue to coordinate the transfer arrangements to ensure that all applicable requirements are fulfilled and that the animal can travel safely and receive appropriate care upon arrival, Pribadi said.

headline: Katie Zacharia picked as White House press secretary
content: Katie Zacharia, a communications adviser for President Donald Trumps Truth Social platform, has been offered the position of White House press secretary following Karoline Leavitts departure from the role in August, a White House official said on Friday (October 9, 2026). Ms. Zacharia did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but if she accepts the role, she would fill a critical role in the Trump administration before next months midterm congressional elections. The New York Times first reported the news. Ms. Zacharia briefly served as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security before departing in March. The conservative commentator is a senior communications adviser for Truth Social and the Trump Media & Technology Group, according to her LinkedIn page. Ms. Zacharia previously worked as a legal adviser for Fix California, a conservative group that aims to address what it described as the lefts stranglehold on state politics. The group was founded by Richard Grenell, who has served as Mr. Trumps envoy to Venezuela and is the interim president and executive director of the Kennedy Center in Washington.

headline: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake shakes Panama, USGS reports
content: A second powerful 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama Friday (October 9, 2026) afternoon following a series of aftershocks, the US Geological Survey said. It came after a magnitude 7.7 quake shook the Central American country, collapsing buildings near its epicenter and prompting evacuations. The quake, which was felt as far away as neighboring Colombia, was centered about 10 kilometers (6 miles) southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, in the central province of Herrera, the U.S. Geological Survey said. It struck at a depth of 10 kilometers (6 miles). The USGS initially reported the quake as magnitude 8, then revised it to 7.6 and later to 7.7. Visibly shaken residents of Panama City gathered outside as they waited for news of the quakes impact on Friday (October 9, 2026). We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but were okay, though were very scared, Rosendo Domnguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press by phone. Everyone is outside, scared. Multiple aftershocks continued to rattle Panama, including several measuring magnitude 5.8, 5.5 and 5.2. Seismologists at the University of Panama recorded more than 45 aftershocks, though many were too weak to be felt. Calls for calm and reports of collapsed buildings Panamanian President Jos Ral Mulino called for calm on Friday (October 9, 2026), writing on X: What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder. Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said on the Telemetro Reporta news channel that damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said there were no reports of damage in the capital, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers. Mr. Smith said several injuries have been reported, including one person struck by debris from a partially collapsed structure in the city of Penonom, around 93 miles (150 km) from the capital. He confirmed a partial collapse and cracks at the cathedral in the districts main square, as well as damage in the governors office building and the Dos Continentes hotel. No casualties were immediately reported. Local news outlets also reported that the Church of San Atanasio, a colonial-style Catholic church in Panamas Los Santos province, had collapsed. The church was declared a National Historic Heritage Site in 1938. Elsewhere, including in Veraguas province, large fissures ran along roadways. Tocumen International Airport in Panama City, one of the regions busiest airports with more than 20 million travelers in 2025, said it would temporarily suspend operations and activated evacuation plans. It said operations would resume once security conditions have been checked. The Panama Canal Authority said operations were continuing normally along the key global trade route. It said its priority was the safety of employees, vessels and crews and that specialized technical teams were inspecting facilities for possible damage. Tsunami warnings as far as Chiles Easter Island The last major earthquake to cause widespread damage in Panama struck in 1991. A magnitude 7.4 quake, centered in nearby Costa Rica killed 23 people, injured 559, and left thousands of people homeless in the border Bocas de Toro region. Earthquakes are common, especially along Panamas border with Costa Rica and its Pacific coast, because of the interaction of several tectonic plates, including Cocos, Nazca, and Caribbean plates. Panama lies along the Ring of Fire, a 40,000-kilometer (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the worlds earthquakes occur. The National Weather Service issued a tsunami warning Friday (October 9, 2026) for the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala. It warned that waves ranging from 3 to 9 feet (1 to 3 meters) above tide may occur in some coastal areas of Panama. Alerts were also issued in El Salvador and as far as Chiles Easter Island, about 3,500 kilometers (2,175 miles) off Chiles mainland coast. Chiles government placed the island under a precautionary advisory. Nearby countries sent messages of support Friday afternoon. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, whose country was recently hit by earthquakes, expressed his solidarity with the Panamanian people and their government during what he called difficult times. Panama is not alone! You can count on Colombias support and our full willingness to provide whatever assistance is needed, he wrote on X. The U.S. Embassy in Panama said it was closely monitoring the aftermath of the quake and accounting for the welfare of its citizens in Panama, a well-known retirement destination for Americans.

headline: Hurricane Isaias lashes U.S. Gulf Coast with wind and rain hours before it comes ashore
content: Homeowners gassed up generators, filled bathtubs with water and bought last-minute supplies along the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday (October 9, 2026) while Hurricane Isaias gained strength as it charged toward the beaches of Alabama and the Florida Panhandle. The Category 3 storm has grown into a major hurricane the first of an unusually quiet Atlantic season and is expected to make landfall Friday (October 9, 2026) night. Forecasters warned of a significant storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and possibly even tornadoes before the storm loses steam as it moves inland and delivers strong winds and rain well north into Atlanta. Tropical storm-force winds began to lash the Gulf shoreline around midday, hours before Isaias was expected to make landfall between Mobile Bay on the Alabama coast and the city of Destin in the Florida Panhandle. The low-lying coastal area is known for its powdery white sand beaches dotted with vacation homes, waterfront bars and seafood shacks. Residents in Panama City, Florida, braved the rain while filling sandbags Friday to protect their houses. I mean, it's just the nature of the beast. It's Florida," said Corliss Stone, who works for the fire department. Many will brave Isaias at home One of the biggest concerns is a storm surge that could be as high as 6 to 9 feet (1.8 to 2.7 meters), according to the National Hurricane Center. Places most at risk include Florida's Pensacola Beach and the Gulf Islands National Seashore. Anne Petzold, who lives with her husband in the Florida beach community of Gulf Breeze, said everyone in their neighborhood planned to ride out the storm. The couple installed hurricane shutters, picked up anything in their yard that could turn into a projectile and have two generators ready if they lose power. Everybody does what they can do, everybody asks if they need help they ask for help, they offer help. All good, she said. It's just another adventure. Neighbor Jay Brazzell said he went through a checklist of things to do, including stocking up on ice and gasoline. He decided to stay put because Isaias isn't as powerful as other hurricanes he's experienced. I mean I'm not boarding up, said Brazzell, 69. I've been through, this being, the ninth hurricane. Dangerous conditions are expected throughout the western panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi, the National Hurricane Center said. Rain began falling along the coast Friday morning, and tropical storm conditions were picking up in the early afternoon. In a sign of how serious the warnings are, dozens of Waffle Houses in the Florida Panhandle were closed, according to the company's website. The beloved Southern breakfast chain is known for staying open through severe weather and often is a measuring stick of a storm's severity. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis warned residents to expect power outages, gasoline shortages and closures of bridges and highways. As of early afternoon, the storm was centered about 90 miles (145 kilometers) south of Pensacola and moving to the north-northeast, the center said. It was packing 120 mph (193 kph) sustained winds Friday morning and picking up speed. Category 3 storms are considered major hurricanes and are capable of causing devastation. The whole region could get soaked Once Isaias comes ashore, it is expected to weaken until it is downgraded to a tropical storm by Saturday afternoon, the hurricane center said. Still, heavy rain is forecast as it moves inland, with 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 centimeters) or even more expected through the weekend from southern Alabama to southwestern Georgia. Isaias, which will be the first hurricane to hit the eastern U.S. since Milton tore up the Gulf Coast of Florida in 2024, also is expected to bring heavy rain and potential flooding to much of the Southeast over the weekend, and then to parts of the Midwest and Northeast into Monday.

headline: Zuperia targets e3w growth, e2w entry; mulls South plant
content: wheeler (e3w) maker Zuperia Auto (formerly Lohia Auto Industries) is stepping up its expansion plans, targeting monthly sales of more than 3,000 vehicles by 2028. The company also plans to enter the electric two-wheeler (e2w) segment and may look at setting up a factory in south India as volumes and its dealer network expand.The company, which currently sells around 600-700 e3ws a month, expects volumes to rise to 1,000-1,200 units a month by the end of this fiscal. We have already sold more than 1,000 vehicles in the L5 e3w category, Ayush Lohia, CEO of Zuperia Auto, told TOI.Growth will be driven by new products, an expanded sales and service network, and deeper penetration into markets where e3ws are at an earlier stage of adoption, he said.Zuperia Auto currently has about 100 touchpoints nationwide and plans to increase this to 130-140 by the end of FY27. While its presence is stronger in north India, the company is targeting four to five cities across AP, Telangana, TN and Karnataka, including Chennai and Bengaluru. It could explore a manufacturing facility in south India as volumes increase, with a decision on additional capacity likely next year, depending on demand and sales growth.Zuperia currently has installed capacity to produce 100,000 vehicles a year, including 40,000 e3ws and 60,000 e2ws, at its existing facility in Uttarakhand.Our capacity is adequate for the next one to one-and-a-half to two years. If we see further traction, we will have to come up with a new unit, somewhere in the South, Lohia said.The southern market is relatively less mature in electric three-wheelers than the North and East, where e-rickshaw penetration has been much higher. However, adoption in the South is expected to accelerate as major manufacturers strengthen their electric vehicle presence in the region.The transition from conventional e-rickshaws to safer and more sophisticated L5 vehicles is expected to continue over the next few years, he added.The company also plans to launch both high-speed and low-speed e2ws, marking its return to the segment. Earlier, it was selling low-speed products in small numbers. Very soon, we will announce our new e2ws. Within a year or so, we will be coming up with those products again, Lohia said.Alongside its expansion, Zuperia Auto is working to consolidate its businesses under a single corporate entity. Vehicle sales are currently booked through two entities a partnership firm and a private limited company both of which have the necessary certification .We are already in the transition process. We would announce the merger within the next year or so, he added.

headline: Aftershocks Rock Panama Following Largest Quake in Decades
content: Bloomberg) -- Panama was struck by its strongest earthquake in more than seven decades on Friday, prompting the evacuation of the capitals international airport and sending people fleeing buildings as powerful aftershocks rattled the country. The 7.7-magnitude quake struck Herrera Province, more than 120 miles (193 kilometers) southwest of the Panama Canal, according to the US Geological Survey. Economic losses in the region are likely to exceed $1 billion, according to an early USGS estimate. The earthquake was the strongest to hit that part of Panama since at least 1951, according to the US National Earthquake Information Center. It struck at a depth of 12.6 kilometers, the USGS said. A magnitude-6.6 aftershock hit west of the initial quake late Friday afternoon, according to preliminary USGS readings. Another eight aftershocks have been recorded at magnitude 4.8 strength or higher. The first earthquake was caused by a rupture along a major plate boundary on the Ring of Fire, the seismically active zone that encircles the Pacific Ocean. The mechanism resembled a strike-slip event, in which tectonic plates grind past each other horizontally, according to Jonathan Tytell, a geophysicist at the US National Earthquake Information Center. It was a very messy event, and shallow, which is not good, Tytell said. The energy is right there at the surface and it doesnt really have time or distance to dissipate. The USGS initially registered an 8.0 magnitude before revising it. Panamas geological institute reported the quake as a 7.2-magnitude. Immediately following the quake, the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center said waves of one to three meters (3.3 to 9.8 feet) above tide level were possible along parts of Panamas coast. As of 2:42 p.m. local time, all warnings had been lifted. The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. The quake was felt as far away as several Colombian cities, including Medelln, according to local media. In Panama, people evacuated buildings, businesses, schools and homes across several regions, local newspaper La Prensa said. President Jos Ral Mulino said the government was mobilizing personnel, resources and aid for people affected by the quake, and ordered ministries and public agencies to respond immediately and take preventive measures. Emergency officials were expected to hold a news conference to provide an update on the impact. People stood barefoot or shirtless in the streets as aftershocks continued, said Cibeles De Freitas, a communications representative for the local unit of First Quantum Minerals Ltd. Theres a lot of fear because were not used to earthquakes in Panama, she said. Were OK, just very scared. First Quantum Minerals didnt immediately provide a comment when asked about any impact on its partially idled copper mine, located about 140 kilometers north of the epicenter. Tocumen International Airport temporarily suspended air operations and evacuated passengers and administrative areas as a precaution while officials assessed the safety of the airport and its control tower. Some flights are being diverted to Colombia and Costa Rica, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar. Panama Citys Metro said lines 1 and 2 were temporarily shut down because of the earthquake. Panamas firefighters said there were no reports of deaths or injuries in the immediate aftermath of the quake. AES Panama, a unit of AES Corp., the countrys top electricity supplier, said through a spokesperson that its hydroelectric, gas-fired and renewable power plants were operational. Activities at the Trans-Panama oil pipeline were continuing normally after the quake, according to a statement from its operator. Fridays quake was the latest to hit Latin America in recent months. Venezuela was struck by twin earthquakes in late June that killed nearly 6,500 people and caused widespread destruction along its northern coast. In Colombia, an Aug. 10 quake killed more than 330 and prompted an economic emergency as damage was estimated at roughly $10 billion. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella expressed solidarity with Panama and offered assistance following Fridays earthquake. Panama is not alone, De la Espriella said in a post on X, adding that Colombia was ready to provide whatever assistance was needed. --With assistance from James Attwood, Valentine Hilaire, Jose Orozco, Brian K. Sullivan, Michael McDonald and Lucia Kassai. (Updates with aftershock from fourth paragraph. A previous version corrected the name of the US National Earthquake Information Center in the fifth paragraph.) More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com 2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Beloved frozen pizza brand discontinued after nearly six decades on US supermarket shelves
content: Trisha Bhattacharya Conagra Brands has stopped producing Celeste frozen pizzas, bringing an end to a brand that has occupied a place in American grocery freezers for nearly six decades. The decision is part of a wider effort to simplify the company's product portfolio and prioritise businesses with stronger growth prospects. The announcement has prompted nostalgic reactions from longtime customers, many of whom associate the affordable frozen pizzas with childhood meals, family kitchens and quick dinners on a budget. According to TODAY.com, a Conagra representative confirmed that production had stopped as part of the company's SKU rationalisation process, which involves reviewing individual products and removing those that no longer fit its business priorities. The company had also discussed the decision during its earnings call in September. The move comes as Conagra seeks to streamline its operations and improve profitability. Chief executive John Brase has indicated that the company is prepared to discontinue smaller brands that offer limited financial returns. There are certain brands and categories where we simply just don't see a future, Brase said, according to Food Dive. Conagra's review extends beyond Celeste. The company is examining its wider range of products, including individual stock-keeping units, to reduce complexity and direct investment towards businesses with greater potential. Brase has pointed to the company's range of more than 400 single-serve meal products as an area where a more focused assortment could improve performance. The company plans to increase investment in categories such as meat snacks and popcorn, while seeking opportunities to strengthen its core businesses. The benefits of its portfolio review are expected to build over the next 12 to 18 months, Food Dive reported. Although production has ended, shoppers may still find Celeste pizzas in some supermarkets while existing stocks last. A Conagra spokesperson told Fox Business that the company would continue selling its remaining inventory, but there would be no further Celeste products once those supplies were exhausted. For consumers who have relied on the brand as an inexpensive meal option, the distinction offers little long-term comfort. Availability will depend on how quickly retailers sell through their remaining stock. The brand traces its origins to Celeste Mama Lizio, who built a food business in the Chicago area before selling it to Quaker Oats in 1969, according to Fox Business, which cited a 1988 Los Angeles Times obituary. Over the decades, Celeste became familiar to generations of shoppers looking for convenient, affordable pizza. Its departure has revived memories of supermarket promotions and family members who regularly kept the pizzas in their freezers. The discontinuation is therefore more than a portfolio decision for some customers. It marks the disappearance of a familiar product whose place in everyday life extended well beyond the freezer aisle. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Saudia Airlines Pilot Among 3 Killed In Houthi Attacks On Riyadh Airport As Yemen War Escalates
content: The airlines also said one of its aircraft was damaged while parked at the airport, but no passengers were on board. A Saudia Airlines pilot was among three people killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport, Saudi authorities said on Friday, as the conflict in Yemen intensified and spread into the neighbouring kingdom. Captain Hamoud Ali al-Kalthami was killed in the attacks carried out on Thursday, the Saudi national carrier confirmed. Saudia also said one of its aircraft was damaged while parked at the airport, but no passengers were on board. - Saudi Says Airport Attacks In Riyadh, Abha Kill 3, Injure 36 After Houthis Claim Strikes - Riyadh Airport Targeted By Houthi Missile: Air India Express, Akasa Air Cancel Flights - From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia - Loud Explosions Heard In Riyadh, Houthis Claim They Fired Missile At Airport Saudi Arabias civil aviation authority said two attacks targeting the airport and a Saudia aircraft had resulted in the deaths of three Saudi citizens. The strikes disrupted air travel, with several flights delayed or cancelled. Explosions were heard across the capital, while diplomats were instructed to shelter in place and international schools took precautionary measures. Damage Reported Across Riyadh Saudi civil defence officials said debris from intercepted missiles damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh. The attacks raised concerns about the safety of civilian infrastructure as the conflict between Yemens Iran-backed Houthis and the Saudi-supported government escalated. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree appeared to suggest that flights operating to and from Riyadh would require approval from a coordinating body in Sanaa. Humanitarian flights to and from Riyadh Airport will be permitted for all flights authorised" by the body, he said in a post on X. Meanwhile, Houthi-affiliated media reported that Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport had killed two people. Yemens civil defence agency also reported fires following Saudi air strikes, including one that it said destroyed a factory. Fighting Intensifies Near Key Shipping Route The latest attacks come as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces attempt to regain territory along the Red Sea coast, including areas near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital route for international shipping. A Yemeni military source told AFP that government forces had launched a major operation in the region with Saudi air support, but warned that fighting remained fierce and territorial gains were limited. Houthi-affiliated media said an attack by government forces had been repelled. The Houthis have also warned workers to evacuate Saudi oil facilities after striking a major refinery south of Riyadh in recent days. (With inputs from AFP) Three people were killed, including a Saudia Airlines pilot named Captain Hamoud Ali al-Kalthami, following attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport.

headline: Sexism In The Silicon: Female AI Bots Paid 10% Less Than Male Counterparts, Study Shows
content: presenting AI assistants consistently received higher monetary valuations from both male and female test subjects A study conducted by researchers from the University of Limerick, the University of Zurich, and SKEMA Business School has revealed that human gender bias is spilling over into interactions with artificial intelligence. Researchers discovered that human participants rewarded female-presenting AI assistants 10.25 per cent less financially than identical male-presenting counterparts, despite both performing the exact same tasks using identical underlying technology. The experiment examined how workers interact with digital avatars in simulated virtual office environments. The findings indicate that societal prejudices surrounding pay equity are actively being projected onto synthetic entities, even when human users are fully aware they are evaluating automated systems. - Breathe Easier In The City: Effective Air Purifiers Under Rs. 15,000 For Compact Bedrooms - 'Inspired By 9/11': Flydubai Co-Pilot Confesses To Plotting Airport Suicide Crash In Early Probe - Boots On Ground: Pakistan Shores Up Presence In Saudi Arabia. Male-presenting AI assistants consistently received higher monetary valuations from both male and female test subjects. Lead researchers noted that while technology itself is inherently neutral, human perception continues to apply historical workplace hierarchies and implicit bias to digital workers. Imperative for Ethical Interface Design The findings have sparked calls from developers and policy experts for standardised ethical guidelines governing AI avatar design and human-computer interactions. Recommendations include adopting neutral digital personas or establishing rigid, objective evaluation frameworks to prevent human bias from influencing algorithmic compensation models.
