headline: Collector inaugurates box cricket turf at District Sports Stadium in Katpadi
content: Collector P.S. Leela Alex inaugurated a box cricket turf established at a cost of 50 lakh at the District Sports Stadium in Katpadi in Vellore on Friday. Officials of Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT), which will maintain the facility, said the turf would help to boost revenue and promote sports at the grassroots-level, especially in rural areas. The new facility will help budding cricketers in rural areas to get trained in covered nets with cricket markings and floodlights, said R. Sethuraman, District Sports Officer (Vellore). The SDAT officials said that the new box cricket turf measured between 100ft and 120ft in length and 50ft to 70ft in width while the height was 20ft. The new facility with centralised lighting will remain open between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. on all days, including Sundays. Officials said that the bookings have been priced at 826 per hour, which is much less than the market costs of private players who charge 1,500 an hour. Youngsters, who mostly come in groups of 10, would be able to afford this, they said. All amenities including, parking facilities, drinking water and washrooms have been provided. Cool drinks and snack facilities within the complex will be a value addition. Spread over 36.68 acres, the 10.81-crore District Sports Complex, which was opened in November 2023, has an open air auditorium that can accommodate at least 1,500 spectators, eight separate tracks for 400 metres athletics training, separate courts for basketball, volleyball, table tennis, tennis, coco, kabadi, football and a gym. Javelin throw can also be practised at the facility.

headline: As Israel goes to the polls, settler attacks and expansion intensify in West Bank
content: While Israel continues to attack one of Palestines two non-contiguous regions, Gaza, it is slowly and violently restructuring the other, West Bank. Israels occupation of Judea and Samaria, the biblical term for West Bank used by the Israeli government, began in 1967 following the Six-Day War. Despite being considered illegal under international law, Israel has slowly been asserting sovereignty over the region with increased restrictions for Palestinians and expansion of Israeli settlements. And this has only intensified since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Nowhere is this clearer than in data on settlements and attacks on Palestinians. According to Peace Now, an Israeli activist group that tracks settlements, fewer than 5,000 Israelis lived in the West Bank in 1967. More than half a century later, the region now houses more than five lakh settlers. That is, around 5% of Israels population now live in the occupied West Bank. On the ground, this has come with significant expansion. Peace Now data show that the Israeli government officially established more than 140 settlements and went through the full planning process. While more than 40,000 housing units in West Bank settlements have been put out to tender since 2002, nearly a quarter of these were put out to tender in the past two years. Tenders refer to proposals issued by the government for the construction of housing units. However, the tender process is required only in 13 settlements and is not required in others, so the actual number of housing units being constructed could be much higher. Further, nearly 430 outposts Israeli settlements considered illegal even under Israeli law have been established since the 1990s. More than 50% of these outposts were established in the past three years alone. Israeli law also allows declaration instead of confiscation of privately owned Palestinian land to build settlements. Through this, Israel has taken over 9,00,000 dunams of West Bank land. This expansion, which undermines the two-state solution, is happening through Israeli institutions and is closely integrated with its politics. Months after the October 7 Hamas attack, in July 2024, the Israeli Parliament declared that it was opposed to the establishment of a Palestinian state west of the Jordan River. A year later, the Knesset voted in favour of a historic declaration that officially supported the application of Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria. Though it was a non-binding resolution, the Speaker of the Israeli Knesset, Amir Ohana, then said: In 1967, the occupation did not start, it ended. That is the historical truth, and the one and only way to reach genuine peace is from [a position of] power. With Israel set to go to the polls later this month, the Netanyahu government has been tightening its grip on the West Bank. Two months before the elections, Israel published tenders for construction of 1,234 Israeli homes as part of its E1 settlement project that aims to create a continuous settlement corridor between occupied East Jerusalem and Maale Adumim. It has also issued open calls for occupation. The countrys far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, on September 27, called for a full-scale war in the occupied West Bank and urged the military to use the tactics employed in Gaza. There are very specific communities who support settlement expansion and reject any settlement dismantling. And thats most of the right-wing, but the ones who are most committed to it are the firm right..., said Dahlia Scheindlin, a non-resident Senior Fellow at the Center for International Policy, an American think tank. The party of Smotrich, Religious Zionism, is polling at about five, six, even seven parliamentary seats, and many of those are people who really prioritise settlement expansion. But everybody else whos voting for any party of the coalition is doing so with the assumption that they will always support settlements and reject any sort of dismantling there, said Ms. Scheindlin. But it is not just the ruling party. Parties contesting the coming polls seem to share a similar opinion on settlements. Prominent parties like Gadi Eisenkot-led Yashar have expressed no interest in the evacuation of settlements and have proposed strengthening of the legally established settlements in the West Bank. Impact on Palestinians Meanwhile, for the nearly three million Palestinians in the West Bank, daily life has been synonymous with navigating the multiple layers of restrictions imposed by the Israeli government, such as checkpoints, road gates and other obstacles. These restrictions have divided Palestinian communities and limited their movement and access to work, school, healthcare, farmland and even aid organisations. They have also borne the brunt of settler aggression, which has starkly intensified in the aftermath of the 2023 Hamas attack. As per the UN OCHA, more than 1,200 settler attacks against Palestinians have been recorded each year since 2023. Over 1,600 attacks have been reported just between January and August this year. More than 1,000 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank in the past four years. At least 10,000 have been injured during this period. These attacks have resulted in damage or demolitions to more than 6,000 Palestinian properties and displaced several thousands since 2023. The UN noted in 2025 that displacement in the West Bank had hit levels not seen since the start of Israels occupation nearly 60 years ago. A year later, the settler attacks resulting in casualties and displacement and open calls for occupation have only surged. Ms. Scheindlin said there is a critical mass in Israel for cracking down on settler violence, which she said is increasingly being understood as terror. Part of the reason, she explained, is that many on the right think the violence harms the image of the settlement project and may draw international attention, and a crackdown will stop pressuring Israel on this issue. International reaction The mounting settler attacks have drawn sharp criticism from international actors. For instance, Israels decision to publish tenders for its E1 settlement project in the West Bank was met with trade curbs from 12 countries. The U.K., France, and Canada, along with nine other countries, namely Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden, issued a joint statement on September 8, 2026, confirming their intention to introduce new restrictions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Only two months ago, the United Nations OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani expressed concern over the Israeli governments announcement to further increase the number of settlements and open calls by Israeli leaders for revenge and collective punishment against Palestinian communities, accompanied by threats to turn the West Bank into another Gaza.

headline: 'Aur Bhi Gham Hain Zamaane Main Siyaasat Ke Siva': Why Sonam Wangchuk Is Skipping CJP's Delhi Stir Today
content: Wangchuks current absence stands in stark contrast to his central role during CJP's earlier NEET paper leak campaign Education reformer and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has confirmed he will not be joining the Cockroach Janta Partys scheduled demonstration in the national capital on Saturday. Reaffirming his presence on the ground in Ladakh, the innovator shared a video statement on X explaining that pressing environmental realities and critical seasonal preparations require his immediate focus. Addressing ongoing administrative friction, Wangchuk emphasised that despite official measures hindering local initiatives, his team remains committed to safeguarding national security through grassroots ecological resilience. His immediate operational priorities centre on tackling acute water insecurity and preparing high-altitude fragile regions before harsh winter conditions set in. - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media - Being Pressured...: Abhijeet Dipke Says CJP Volunteers Getting Police Notices Ahead Of Delhi Protest - Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use - CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das Say They May Be Arrested Before Oct 10: Timeline Of The Escalating Protest Crucial Precedent: His Role in CJPs NEET Protest Wangchuks current absence stands in stark contrast to his central role during CJPs earlier NEET paper leak campaign. During that agitation, he anchored the movement by undertaking a gruelling 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, providing moral weight to student grievances before concluding his fast upon written government assurances. His strategic participation at the time elevated the exam-reform campaign into a national talking point. Having already tested and lent his support to the CJP during that critical juncture, Wangchuk has now chosen to pivot back exclusively to his core Himalayan ecological mission. Engineering Solutions for Himalayan Climate Risks Detailing his current scientific work, Wangchuk highlighted active preparations aimed at creating artificial glaciers to secure spring water supplies for regional agricultural communities. Additionally, his team is conducting specialised experiments to manage the risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods, designed to neutralise over 200 high-risk glacial lakes across the high Himalayas. Sonam Wangchuk will not join the Cockroach Janta Partys demonstration in the national capital on Saturday. Wangchuk cited pressing environmental realities and critical seasonal preparations in Ladakh as his immediate focus. Wangchuk previously undertook a 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar during CJP's NEET paper leak campaign. His current scientific work includes creating artificial glaciers and managing Glacial Lake Outburst Floods. Wangchuk urged leaders to maintain unity and show statesmanship, and called for non-violence from younger participants. Clarifying his absence from street-level politics, Wangchuk adapted verses by poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz, remarking: Aur Bhi Gham Hain Zamaane Main Siyaast Ke Siva Rahaten aur bhi hain wasl ki raahat ke siva (There are sorrows in the world other than politics and governance, and comforts other than the joy of union with a beloved)." He commended those working to address political challenges, noting that non-political, nature-driven threats demand equal urgency and dedicated scientific action. Appeal to Youth for Peace and Statesmanship While sending his best wishes to the demonstrations organisers, Wangchuk urged leaders across various political and social groups to maintain unity and show statesmanship. He cautioned against ideological division, stressing that constructive dialogue must remain the primary vehicle for addressing national concerns. Addressing younger participants and student groups, Wangchuk issued an emphatic call for non-violence. Recalling his previous peaceful fasts at Jantar Mantar, he urged young citizens to preserve the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi by keeping all forms of public assembly strictly peaceful. Sonam Wangchuk skipped the Cockroach Janta Partys Delhi demonstration to focus on pressing environmental realities, acute water insecurity, and critical seasonal preparations in Ladakh before harsh winter conditions set in.

headline: Trump Picks MAGA 'Devoted Fan' Katie Zacharia As New White House Press Secretary
content: Trump said Zacharia had supported him from the beginning and expressed confidence in her ability to handle the high-profile role. US President Donald Trump on Friday appointed conservative commentator and lawyer Katie Zacharia as the new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter of his Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement. Announcing the decision on his Truth Social platform, Trump said Zacharia had supported him from the beginning and expressed confidence in her ability to handle the high-profile role. - Trump Mistakes Brazil For India, Claims 125 Million Voted In Presidential Election, Attacks US Voting System - IVE: Trump Rallies Ohio Ahead Of Midterms | Husted & Ramaswamy Join | Reps Vs Dems | Midterm 2026 - What's Driving Up Oil Prices? Trump Says It's Ukraine Strikes On Russian Refineries, Not Iran War - ICE Agent Shoots At Criminal Illegal Alien From Dominican Republic During New York Arrest Operation She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," Trump wrote. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the position in August following the birth of her second child. Trump praised Leavitt for her work, saying she had done a fantastic job" as press secretary. Who Is Katie Zacharia? Zacharia currently serves as a senior communications adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, which operates the presidents social media platform, Truth Social. Trump described her work at the company as outstanding". A lawyer and graduate of Pepperdine University and its Caruso School of Law, Zacharia is also a frequent commentator on conservative television networks, including Fox News and Newsmax. She previously served as a spokesperson and deputy assistant secretary for public affairs at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees US immigration enforcement. She joined the department earlier this year under then-secretary Kristi Noem but left after around two months, according to her LinkedIn profile. Zacharia has also worked with Fix California, a conservative advocacy group founded by Richard Grenell, a longtime Trump ally. Leavitt Praised As She Exits Role Trump said Zacharia had assisted his presidential campaigns in key swing states and expressed confidence that she would work well with the media, the American public and his administration. I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration," he wrote. The press secretary is one of the White Houses most visible roles, involving regular briefings with journalists, responses to questions about government policy and communicating the presidents position on key issues. Leavitt took up the post when Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, becoming the youngest person to hold the position at the age of 27. Fox News has announced that Leavitt will join the network as an on-air contributor from November. headline: Hitler Mussolini Elected Mayor In Peru—Yes, You Read That Right
content: A politician bearing the combined names of two European wartime dictators has won a municipal election in central Peru. Hitler Mussolini Simen Flores, a 45-year-old centre-left candidate, secured the mayoral seat in the small district of Queroplca after edging out his nearest rival by just 25 votes. Running under the banner of the Ahora Nacin (Nation Now) party, Flores captured 229 votesaccounting for 34.5 per cent of the total valid ballots castin the remote Andean municipality. His victory over conservative opponent Gaspar Benilde Osorio Sambrano immediately attracted global headline attention due to the unique history behind his given names. - Brazil Elections: Can Lula Hold Back Latin Americas Right-Wing Shift? | Flavio Bolsonaro | N18G - Saffron State, Splintered Rivals: Nandigram, Rejinagar Invert Bengals Historic Election Math - Brazil Election Heads To Run-Off As Bolsonaro Beats Lula. Another Rightward Turn For Latin America? - Bypoll Results 2026: BJP Wins Nandigram; TVK Wins In Tamil Nadu, NDA Wins In Puducherry A Cultural Phenomenon Surrounding Historical Names While the combination of Hitler and Mussolini raised eyebrows internationally, unique and historically charged given names are relatively common in Latin America. Parents in rural regions frequently name children after historical figures, foreign leaders, or world events without aligning with the underlying ideologies. Flores is far from the first Peruvian politician to hold a name linked to historical figures. Previously, Hitler Guesclin Alba Snchez served as mayor of the Andean municipality of Yungar, famously campaigning under slogans such as the good Hitler" to distinguish his local administrative platform from the Nazi dictator. Focused on Local Infrastructure Over Ideology Despite the international commentary surrounding his name, local media reports indicate that Flores ran a campaign focused strictly on municipal governance, agricultural development, and regional infrastructure improvements. Queroplca, located in the Hunuco region, has a population of just over 700 residents, where local issues heavily outweigh national or international political debates. Running under the Ahora Nacin party, Flores captured 229 votes. His 229 votes accounted for 34.5 per cent of the total valid ballots cast. Queroplca, located in the Hunuco region, has a population of just over 700 residents. Election officials confirmed that the voting process proceeded smoothly, validating Flores narrow victory. He is set to take office at the start of the upcoming municipal term, shifting public attention from his headline-grabbing moniker to his promises of local civic reform. headline: CJP's Dipke Says Jantar Mantar March Must Continue Even If He Is Detained, Shares Delhi Arrival Time
content: Dipke said the demonstration should not revolve around him and must continue even if he is taken into custody. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said the partys proposed march at Jantar Mantar must continue even if he is detained or arrested, urging supporters to gather in large numbers in Delhi on Saturday, October 10. Whether I will be arrested right from the airport or arrested after that Im really not sure. But one thing is for sure, I am not going to step back, I am not going to be afraid, because we have to save our countrys democracy," he said. In a separate post on X, Dipke said he would land in the national capital at 9.30 am on Saturday. Protest must not stop if I go to jail Dipke said the demonstration should not revolve around him and must continue even if he is taken into custody. He also said he was prepared for action under stringent laws, including the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the National Security Act (NSA). If this government wants to invoke the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against me, National Security Act (NSA), or whatever they want to invoke, you can do so," he said. The CJP is demanding Kumars resignation, the scrapping of SIR or an independent and neutral procedure for appointing election commissioners. Dipke alleged that free and fair elections could not be ensured without these changes. Appeals for peaceful march Urging people to reach Jantar Mantar in large numbers, Dipke called on supporters to maintain peace and follow the law. We are law-abiding citizens, we are peaceful citizens. So no mistake should be made from our end. We are not goons," he said. He also alleged that attempts could be made to disrupt the demonstration, referring to the recent release on bail of Swatantra Bharadwaj. He urged protesters not to allow any such incident to derail the march. So after I go to jail or after I get arrested, your protest should not stop," Dipke said. Delhi Police denies permission The Delhi Police has denied permission for the CJPs proposed protest, citing possible law-and-order concerns and inconvenience to the public. In a letter to the partys co-convenor Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi district, said the permission could not be granted in the larger public interest. The police also said the communication received from the party was an intimation rather than a formal application. It noted that applications for events at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance and cited alleged past violations of protest conditions. Security has been tightened in parts of the national capital ahead of Saturdays proposed demonstration. (With inputs from agencies) The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) is demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, the scrapping of the SIR, and an independent procedure for appointing election commissioners.

headline: Delhi Wrapped In Security Cocoon As Protest Looms; BJP, Rahul Clash Over Prez Murmu Meeting Claims
content: New Delhi braces for protests and strict security Saturday as protests loom over alleged voter irregularities. New Delhi was preparing for a day of protests and heightened security on Saturday, even as Opposition leaders met President Droupadi Murmu on Friday evening and submitted a memorandum raising concerns over alleged electoral irregularities. Government sources described it as unfortunate" that the Opposition was dragging the President into the controversy following the meeting, news agencies ANI and PTI reported. - 'Presented Our Memorandum': LoP Rahul Gandhi Says Held 'Unbelievable' Meeting With President Murmu; BJP Slams 'Malicious Politics' - Opposition vs CEC Gyanesh Kumar: India Bloc Seeks President Murmus Intervention | News18 - Govt Says Opposition Dragging President Of India Into Controversy After INDIA Bloc Meeting: Report - He Is Lying: BJP Hits Back At Rahul Gandhi Over Claims On President Murmu's Meeting With INDIA Bloc The BJP hit back at Rahul Gandhi over his account of the meeting, with party spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi calling his claim unfortunate and bizarre" and accusing him of lying. Trivedi alleged that Gandhi was misrepresenting the meeting with President Droupadi Murmu for political gain and questioned the evidence backing his claims. He also accused the Congress leader of drawing constitutional institutions into political controversy. The delegation, led by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, sought Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. After the meeting, Gandhi said the President had asked the Opposition to provide proof of its allegations and that the INDIA bloc was ready to submit evidence. As the political exchanges continued, Delhis preparations for Saturdays planned protest at Jantar Mantar gathered pace. Barricades were put up at key points across the capital, traffic diversions were announced for 30 locations from 6 am, and authorities tightened security around central Delhi. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, meanwhile, revised its earlier order restricting entry and exit at 57 stations, bringing the number of affected stations down to 45. The restrictions are scheduled to remain in force until 6 pm on Saturday, subject to a review by security agencies. Interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except New Delhi Metro station. The changes followed Supreme Court scrutiny of the restrictions imposed on public transport ahead of the protest called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and student groups. The demonstrators are demanding Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged electoral irregularities. Opposition leaders met President Droupadi Murmu on Friday evening to raise concerns over alleged electoral irregularities. The delegation, led by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, sought Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. Delhi announced traffic diversions for 30 locations from 6 am and tightened security around central Delhi. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation revised its restrictions to 45 stations, down from an earlier 57 stations. CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke announced he would arrive in Delhi at 9.30 am on Saturday for the planned demonstration. CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke has said he will arrive in Delhi at 9.30 am on Saturday and proceed with the planned demonstration despite Delhi Police denying permission. In a post on X late Friday, Dipke announced his arrival time alongside a photograph of himself holding a copy of the Constitution of India. The protest preparations have also affected travel plans. Delhi Airport issued an advisory for passengers, while several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations faced cancellations. Authorities have urged commuters and passengers to check the latest updates and allow extra time for their journeys. For Saturday, the immediate focus is on whether the planned mobilisation proceeds as announced and how security and traffic arrangements are managed across the capital. The police has said diversions will depend on the prevailing law and order situation, while the Metro restrictions are due for review later in the day. A delegation of INDIA bloc leaders met President Droupadi Murmu to submit a memorandum raising concerns over alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: T.N. Home Secretary transferred, Prem Anand Sinha posted as Director of DVAC
content: Tamil Nadu Home Secretary K. Manivasan has been transferred and posted as Commissioner of Land Administration in the rank of Additional Chief Secretary. Dr. Manivasan was appointed Home Secretary by the Election Commission ahead of the Assembly election. He held the portfolios of Home, Excise and Prohibition. He has been replaced by A. Karthik, Chairman and Managing Director of the Tamil Nadu Small Industries Development Corporation (TANSIDCO). Senior IPS officer and Additional Director-General of Police (ADGP) Prem Anand Sinha has been posted as ADGP/Director of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Directorate (DVAC), Tamil Nadu. He was the Tambaram Police Commissioner. The post had fallen vacant following the transfer of another IPS officer, A. Arun, in July 2026. Inspector General of Police C. Mageshwari was given the additional charge of Director. ADGP/Commissioner of Police of the Greater Chennai Police A. Amalraj has been given the additional charge of Commissioner of Tambaram City Police until further orders. Rajesh Lakhoni, Commissioner of Land Administration, has been posted as Chairman and Managing Director of TNEB and the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited. In another key transfer, V. Arun Roy, Chairman and Managing Director of TNEB and the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited, besides heading the States green energy, transmission and power generation corporations, has been posted as Secretary, Finance (Expenditure). He succeeds N. Venkatesh. Mr. Venkatesh has been appointed Agriculture Production Commissioner and Secretary to the Agriculture Farmers Welfare Department, portfolios additionally held by Dr. N. Subbaiyan.

headline: Ensure strict adherence by builders to construction waste rules: NGT
content: Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) must ensure uninterrupted processing of construction and demolition waste and enforce compliance with waste management rules, the southern bench of the National Green Tribunal has ordered.Noting that processing facilities in Kodungaiyur and Perungudi ceased operations in 2024, the tribunal directed GCC to arrange alternatives.The order came in a case the tribunal took up suo motu in 2024 following news reports that GCC had identified 25 hotspots where construction waste was dumped. The tribunal said waste generators were responsible for managing it and directed GCC to monitor compliance with the rules. Though GCC has issued guidelines for construction and debris waste management and prevention of illegal dumping, compliance with the prescribed requirements should be made mandatory for building-plan approval, the bench comprising Justice Pushpa Sathyanarayana and Prashant Gargava said.The bench said authorities should issue completion certificates only if construction projects comply with construction and demolition waste management rules. The tribunal also directed the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board to monitor the collection, transportation, processing and disposal of such waste across the state and ensure compliance with the law and guidelines.

headline: Ensure no obstruction to water flow during construction of peripheral ring road: NGT
content: Govt agencies involved in construction of the Chennai Peripheral Ring Road (CPRR) in Tiruvallur must ensure that the road-laying work does not obstruct, divert or impede the natural flow of water into the Kannigaiper Lake, the southern bench of the National Green Tribunal has ordered.Stating that all design and execution work for the project must be carried out in accordance with technical and safety standards and proper departmental clearances, the Tribunal urged the concerned authorities to strictly adhere to the recommendations of the water resources department (WRD).The orders were passed on a case taken up suo motu by the bench in 2025 on a letter petition that a 280-metre stretch on the CPRR road, passing over the lake would obstruct natural flow of water, affect its storage and result in flooding risk of nearly 50 villages on the western side of the lake. The petitioners said the WRD had accorded a no-objection certificate (NOC) to the project without assessing the impact.However, the Tribunal pointed out that a report submitted by the Tamil Nadu Road Infrastructure Development Company stated that the project involved two componentsa high-level structure for a length of 100 metres and an embankment for the remaining 180 metres. While the WRD had issued an NOC for the high-level structure, it had not sanctioned the embankment and suggested a separate structure for the embankment to prevent obstruction of water flow. Subsequently, the TNRIDC explored the feasibility of establishing such a structure. As per the proposal, a span of 25 metres between each pier is contemplated, which will provide adequate clearance for uninterrupted flow of water, the bench comprising Justice Pushpa Sathyanarayana and Prashant Gargava said, disposing of the petition.

headline: MMA to hold students' convention
content: The Madras Management Association, one of Indias premier management associations, is organising the 25th MMA All India Management Students Convention 2026 Silver Jubilee Edition on 12th October 2026 at the Valluvar Kottam Auditorium, Chennai. The theme of this years convention is Future-Ready Leadership: Reinventing Management for a Changing World, with a focus on preparing management students and emerging professionals to navigate technological advancement, economic volatility, changing workforce expectations, sustainability priorities and global uncertainty. The Hindu Group is the media partner for this event. Speaking about the convention, Vijay Kumar, Convention Chairman & Executive Director & Group CFO, Sify Technologies Ltd, said, It is a matter of great pride and honour for us to organise the Silver Jubilee, 25th Edition of the MMA All India Management Students Convention. The theme this year is highly relevant to young management students who will soon enter a business environment being reshaped by technology, AI, changing workforce expectations and global uncertainty. The key theme of the convention Future-Ready Leadership: Reinventing Management for a Changing World aims to prepare management students to manage disruption, build high-performing teams, embrace lifelong learning and contribute to organisations that are agile, inclusive, innovative and purpose-driven. The theme chosen and the business sessions are designed to help students understand how leadership itself is being redefined and why future managers need to combine digital awareness with agility, communication, resilience, empathy, professional credibility and purpose. The Convention will address sub-themes like From Campus to Startup: Choosing Entrepreneurship as a Career and Future-Ready Careers: Reinventing Skills, Employability and Leadership Presence. The Convention will feature the Grand Finale of Chanakya The Mastermind, MMAs flagship competition to identify the Best Management Student of the Year 2026. Ten finalists will compete on stage following a rigorous selection process comprising an online quiz, presentation, telephonic interview, behavioural assessment, group discussion, communication and critical-thinking rounds. The winner will receive a cash prize of 1,00,000.

headline: When BJP protested against the Election Commission in 2014; here's where and why it happened
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is set to hold what is being described as a "peaceful protest" by founder Abhijeet Dipke at Delhi's popular protest site Jantar Mantar. It is scheduled to take place on Saturday despite denial of permission by the Delhi Police. CJP and other groups have called for the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the election proceedings, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Earlier, 42 retired judges, including former Supreme Court judges and high court chiefs, via an open letter defended Gyanesh Kumar. Criticising protests led by CJP, it expressed concerns over an alleged campaign against the Election Commission of India. Interestingly, once the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) protested against the Election Commission of India (ECI). The protest dates back to May 2014 after the poll panel denied permission to Narendra Modi, who was the then prime ministerial candidate, to hold a rally at Beniabagh Maidan in Varanasi. Quick answers to key questions 1Why did the BJP protest against the Election Commission in May 2014? The protest followed the denial of permission for Narendra Modi, then the BJPs prime ministerial candidate, to hold a rally at Beniabagh Maidan in Varanasi. The party questioned the Election Commissions neutrality and alleged bias. 2Where did the BJPs 2014 protests against the Election Commission take place? Protests took place in Varanasi and New Delhi on May 8, 2014. In Varanasi, BJP leaders staged a dharna outside the Banaras Hindu University campus. 3Which BJP leaders took part in the 2014 protest in Varanasi? Arun Jaitley, Amit Shah and Ananth Kumar staged a dharna outside the Banaras Hindu University campus after permission for Modis rally was denied. 4How did the BJPs 2014 protest against the Election Commission end? The BJP called off its protest after a meeting with Election Commission officials in New Delhi. Its delegation sought the replacement of Varanasis district magistrate and an independent inquiry into the permission denial. Modi was scheduled to hold a rally at Beniabagh Maidan. The Election Commission was accused of being biased against the party. The neutrality of the poll panel was also questioned following the denial of permission. The Election Commission reportedly had dismissed allegations of biasness during the controversy. The denial of permission for the rally triggered widespread protest by BJP workers. Several senior party leaders questioned the Election Commissions neutrality ahead of the Lok Sabha elections. According to the publication, the protests took place in Varanasi, which is now PM Modi's constituency, as well as New Delhi on May 8, 2014. BJP demanded action against Varanasis district magistrate and returning officer, Pranjal Yadav, during their protests. In Varanasi, BJP leaders Arun Jaitley, Amit Shah and Ananth Kumar, staged a dharna outside the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus following the denial of permission for Modis rally. In New Delhi, BJP leaders and workers attempted to march towards the Election Commissions office in an attempt to protest against the move. However, the protesting party workers were stopped by Delhi Police before they could reach the office. Prohibitions were imposed in the area, added the report. Reportedly, the BJP called off its protest after a meeting with Election Commission officials in New Delhi. The delegation, led by senior BJP leader Venkaiah Naidu, reportedly asked the commission to replace the Varanasi district magistrate and conduct an independent inquiry into the denial of permission. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: Rahul Gandhi to address students in Chennai today
content: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore on Friday said Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi would address various issues related to students at Island Grounds in Chennai on Saturday evening. According to Mr. Tagore, 10,000 to 20,000 students, who registered and received the QR code, will be participating in the event. Mr. Gandhi will also meet Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay at his residence. Our leader will address issues related to Tamil Nadu students such as National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test, lack of jobs, education for girls and women, and the Union governments educational policy. It is going to be an interactive session. Though protests are happening in New Delhi, he [Mr. Gandhi] is coming to Chennai because he had agreed to this, the TNCC president further said. Regarding the bypoll results, Mr. Tagore said the AIADMK support base could soon shift to the TVK. In the last 25 years, this is the first bypoll to be held without money being distributed to voters, he claimed. It is possible that the AIADMKs support base could shift to the TVK because of the Chief Ministers governance in the last four months, he said. He also criticised DMK leader M.K. Stalins repeated use of the word betrayal. I welcome the results. It is a victory for the TVK and its coalition government. He [Mr. Vijay] has brought in significant change, he said.

headline: "Will Go To Dubai": Humayun Kabir After Son Loses Rejinagar Bypoll To BJP
content: The BJP registered a major breakthrough in Rejinagar, a Muslim-majority constituency in Murshidabad district, where its candidate Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) nominee Golam Nabi Azad by 75,816 votes.

headline: Units grappling with rising costs, says expert at Vettri Tamil Nadu MSME Summit 2026
content: MSMEs play a critical role in employment generation, exports, innovation, regional development, and inclusive economic growth and strengthening them is essential for achieving the vision of a $1.5 trillion Tamil Nadu economy, said S. Vasudevan, president of Tamil Nadu Small and Tiny Industries Association (Tanstia) in Chennai on Friday. According to him, Micro and Small Enterprises across the country are presently undergoing an extremely challenging phase due to the West Asia conflict and the continuous increase in production and operational costs. In particular, the steep increase in gas prices, rising raw material costs, transportation expenses, power-related challenges, labour costs, and financial constraints have placed tremendous pressure on the MSME sector, he said at the Vettri Tamil Nadu MSME Summit 2026 organised by FICCI. In this difficult business environment, we sincerely appeal to all entrepreneurs and industrial members to exercise utmost prudence in financial management, optimise operational efficiency, avoid unnecessary expenditure, and focus on maintaining business stability and long-term growth, he added. P.N. Vasudevan, managing director of Equitas Small Finance Bank said that many MSMEs are struggling, especially the micro units. He pointed out that small-scale trading units are not covered by government schemes. Government should start thinking about how to support these micro units, he said.

headline: US Is "Kicking The Ladder" After Climbing It: Ex-Amazon H-1B Insider To NDTV

headline: After two bypolls in TN, TVK 109 not out
content: TVK cleared its first litmus test barely five months after forming the govt in Tamil Nadu, winning the bypolls in two assembly constituencies. Though Madurantakam and Dharapuram presented different political terrains, TVK won both seats with comfortable margins by fielding former AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama, who joined the ruling party just 20 days after the assembly election results in May.Sathyabama won Dharapuram by a margin of 9,471 votes, while Maragatham Kumaravel secured Madurantakam by 20,040 votes. DMK finished second in both seats, while AIADMK, which had won the two segments in the April assembly election, was pushed to the third place. The results increased TVKs strength in the 234-member Assembly from 107 to 109.This is a victory for political decorum and personal decency. It is a verdict against derogatory remarks targeting women, personal attacks and betrayal, chief minister C Joseph Vijay said in an X post.This winning streak will continue, Vijay added. The ruling party has increased its vote share in Dharapuram from 23.2% in the April elections to 37%, while in Madurantakam, TVK gained roughly 9% vote share.DMK president M K Stalin called it a temporary victory for betrayal, while AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said the results were a success of money power won by murdering democracy and duping people with reels. In Madurantakam, Maragatham built a steady lead from the first round of counting and widened the margin in successive rounds, finishing with 74,048 votes, defeating DMK candidate I Paranthamen. The entire credit goes to our leaders (Vijay) good governance and his assurance of Madurantakams development, she said.Maragatham, who won the seat as an AIADMK candidate in April with 69,284 votes, increased her tally by about 4,700 votes after switching to TVK. In turn, DMKs tally fell from 59,838 to 54,008, while AIADMKs votes dropped from 69,284 to 47,450, compared to the assembly elections held five months back. The figures pointed to an erosion of AIADMKs support base, say poll watchers.In the case of DMK, the drop was attributed to absence of key allies Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK and Left parties. CPM had fielded its own candidate here, while the other former allies are now backing TVK.In Dharapuram, Sathyabama, who had faced opposition in a few villages during her campaign, was trailing behind AIADMK candidate K Banumathi in the first five rounds. The trend shifted in the subsequent rounds when Sathyabama increased her tally, finally ending up with 66,841 votes. DMKs K Suganya moved from the third spot to the second position with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK finished third with 45,280 votes."There was a conspiracy to undemocratically defeat Sathyabama. But people rejected the conspirators, said state revenue minister K A Sengottaiyan.The Left parties which contested alone in one seat each, put up a poor show forfeiting their deposits. CPI candidate in Dharapuram got 1,157 votes while CPM candidate in Madurantakam got 1,986 votes. NTK candidates too didnt fare well. The party received 2,709 votes in Madurantakam and 5,268 votes in Dharapuram.Political analysts said the results present a mixed picture for TVK. While it was no surprise for a ruling party to win the bypoll, the winning margin was modest, considering the projections of one lakh vote margin by leaders such as Aadhav Arjuna, poll watchers said.

headline: Bar leaders meet minister for law to protect advocates
content: A delegation of the Federation of Bar Associations of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on Thursday met TN law minister C T R Nirmal Kumar and submitted a draft Bill with suggestive provisions to be included in the TN Advocates (Protection) Act, an exclusive legislation for protection of advocates.Receiving the draft Bill from the delegation led by its honorary chairperson and senior advocate S Prabakaran, the minister said he would take it to the notice of chief minister C Joseph Vijay and do the needful as per his instructions.On Oct 3, the federation convened a meeting for the welfare of the legal fraternity in which the law minister participated. In the meeting, a resolution was adopted to initiate steps for the protection of the members of the Bar.While addressing the gathering, Kumar assured members of the Bar that a law protecting the interest of the lawyers will be enacted by the state assembly. He suggested the federation come up with a draft Bill as an initial step for consulting the stakeholders. In view of the same, the Federation met the minister and submitted a draft Bill.The legislation is proposed for greater protection of advocates and their functions in discharge of professional duties. The proposal was made in the background of recent incidents of assault, killings, intimidation and regular threats caused to advocates, due to proper and honest discharge of their professional duties.This often resulted in law-and-order situations and sometimes caused obstruction and deficiencies in rendering professional services by advocates to their clients; apart from instilling a deep sense of apprehension in the minds of advocates while discharging their professional duties, Prabakaran said.Yet another hurdle faced by advocates stems from their representing detainees or arrested or incarcerated persons. It has been seen in several cases that advocates are sought to be questioned about privileged communication to make detection of alleged crime easier. However, this militates against the basic tenets of the legal profession and violates the sanctity which the law enjoins the advocate to maintain with respect to such privileged communication or materials, he added.

headline: New GRAP Rules in Delhi; Restrictions in NCR October 2026: Are you aware of this parking fees update?
content: Trisha Bhattacharya Delhi motorists will have to pay twice the existing rates at authorised parking facilities from 1 November 2026, as the government rolls out its winter air pollution control framework. The measure will remain in effect until 28 February 2027, and is intended to discourage private vehicle use during the months when pollution levels typically worsen. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation's parking facilities are excluded from the increase. Electric vehicles are also exempt from the additional parking charges under the announced plan. The decision is part of the Delhi government's broader strategy to address pollution before the winter smog season intensifies. Higher parking costs are intended to make commuters reconsider unnecessary car journeys and encourage alternatives, including public transport. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) approved a revised Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) on 28 September, with the updated schedule announced on 29 September. The plan contains 48 actions across four stages, with restrictions tightening as air quality deteriorates. Under the reported framework, parking charges can also be increased as a pollution-response measure when restrictions are activated. GRAP Stage II corresponds to the very poor air quality category, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 301400. Also Read | GRAP-I restrictions imposed in Delhi-NCR The seasonal doubling of parking fees from November to February is a separate advance measure; commuters should not assume that the increase applies only when Stage II is invoked. The government has announced several additional measures that could affect residents and commuters across Delhi-NCR. Restrictions on older out-of-state vehicles: Vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards are due to face entry restrictions from 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, with exemptions for specified cleaner-fuel vehicles, including CNG and electric vehicles. No PUCC, no fuel: Fuel stations are required to deny fuel to vehicles without a valid Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC). Automated number-plate recognition cameras are being used to strengthen enforcement. Work-from-home arrangements: Government and private offices are set to operate with 50% of staff working from home during the November-February period under the announced winter framework. Restrictions on older cars: Under revised GRAP provisions, restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel light motor vehicles extend across Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddh Nagar and Sonipat when Stage III curbs apply. The measures come as authorities attempt to limit emissions from transport, construction and other sources before winter conditions trap pollutants close to the ground. For motorists, checking the latest government notifications will be important, particularly as some restrictions depend on the prevailing AQI and the GRAP stage in force. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: AAI buys 19 acres to ease truck congestion near airport cargo terminal
content: Congestion on the GST Road is expected to decrease considerably as the Airports Authority of India has acquired 19.06 acres of land behind the Meenambakkam metro station for 278 crore to enhance the parking facilities for goods carriers that make a beeline for the Chennai airports cargo terminal.Hundreds of trucks are parked daily on the roadside due to a shortage of parking space around the cargo terminal. AI Assets Holding Ltd officially transferred the land parcel to AAI on Monday. This land was once a residential colony of erstwhile Indian Airlines employees.There is a stadium in the colony, which would be immediately converted into a parking lot for vehicles that come to deliver and pick up goods from the cargo terminal. Some demolition work is needed to increase parking space further. Three different proposals are under review to develop the 19.06 acres, keeping the long-term needs of the airport in mind, said an AAI official.Chennai airports cargo terminal handles about 400 tonnes of export and 800 tonnes of import cargo daily, nearly 30% more than last year. The cargo terminal sees a rush of goods carriers between 3pm and 8pm for at least four days a week. Traffic on GST Road is affected in the evening as trucks and private buses park on both sides near the airport. The Chennai Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority (CUMTA) has been urging AAI to shift the cargo terminal to the rear side of the airport to reduce congestion.

headline: Experts call for enforcing speed limits and stricter rules to curb road accidents
content: wheelers, taking stringent action against traffic rule violators, designing better roads, and enforcing speed limits were among the key actions proposed by govt officers and researchers to curb road accidents in the state, at a conference held in the city on Friday.Organised by the Citizen Consumer and Civic Action Group (CAG), the Tamil Nadu Road Safety Conference: From Mission to Action saw road safety experts calling for the implementation of a comprehensive and effective State Road Safety Action Plan, as the state leads the country in road accidents with 67,526 cases in 2024. The state recorded 18,449 road-crash fatalities in 2024.Calling for effective road engineering, TNRERA chairperson Phanindra Reddy said, While we have well-connected roads, we also have a high volume of vehicles. The state ranks eighth in fatalities per 1,000 vehicles. Roads must be designed to enforce safe speeds, rather than relying only on signboards, he said.Additional commissioner of police (traffic), GCTP, B Shamoondeswari, said that as technology grows, people must develop civic sense to improve road safety. While we have technology such as ANPR to detect traffic violations, the number plates on vehicles are often fake, she added. She also urged people to clear pending traffic challans. From Oct 2025 to Sept 2026, more than 26,000 drunk-driving cases were registered. But only half of them have paid the fines, she added.Vignesh Dhurai from IIT-Madras said a person violating traffic rules must first be made aware of it. Instead of directly issuing challans, a person must first be warned that he/she is violating a traffic rule, and a record of it must be kept/ If the offense is repeated, fines should be imposed, he said.S Saroja, executive director of CAG, said, Collaboration between govt departments, enforcement agencies, technical institutions, researchers and civil society organisations is crucial to building a safer road transport system.

headline: 3,000-year-old writing system unearthed in Tamil Nadu
content: red ware bowl unearthed along with iron weapons, copper objects and a possible steel sword at Thelunganur in the water spread area of the Mettur dam near Salem could offer vital clues to a writing system that existed more than 3,200 years ago.The bowl, discovered by a Tamil Nadu department of archaeology team, carries five graffiti signs arranged from left to right, making it the longest sequence of such marks recorded in the state. Excavators believe this may be an early form of writing as another bowl bears the same five symbols in a different order.This, they feel, could be a precursor to the advent of the Tamil Brahmi script that dates to sixth century BCE.The recently found graffiti could be contemporary to Indus Valley Civilization as Thelunganur and Mangadu, twin Iron Age sites near Salem, have been dated to between 1,600 BCE and 1,200 BCE, the final phase of Indus Valley Civilization.In the 1960s, ASI had found three graffiti signs in different orders at Sanur near Chengalpet. Now weve found five symbols in two different orders. We have to decipher the meaning, said K Rajan, adviser to the TN department and a co-author of a morphological study of Indus signs and graffiti marks found in Tamil Nadu. Archaeologists have so far unearthed around 16,000 graffiti-inscribed potsherds across Tamil Nadu. According to a recent morphological study, graffiti marks found at sites including Kodumanal, Keeladi, Thulukkarpatti and Kilnamandi in Tamil Nadu and in Indus Valley sites have 90% similarities. Indus Valley Civilization existed between 3,300 BCE and 1,300 BCE.Researchers said Tamil-Brahmi stone inscriptions and inscribed potsherds bear symbols at the ends of letters, suggesting these could represent an earlier form of communication.Among the other artefacts that caught the excavators imagination is a 1.9m iron spear. We also found arrowheads, axes, swords, daggers, knives and iron nails, said S Paranthaman, excavation director at the site. One other object found is suspected to be an ancient steel sword.Excavators also recovered complete skeletal remains of two Iron Age individuals.We found four types of burials pit, cist, urn and sarcophagus at a single site, reflecting the composite nature of the community. This indicates that the site evolved from the Early Iron Age to the Late Iron Age, Paranthaman said.The site gained prominence after a steel sword found here was dated to 1,200 BCE, one of the worlds oldest.

headline: 'Reel culture' led to bike stunt incident: B. Shamoondeswari, Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic)
content: Among the Gen Z, reel culture is becoming so popular that many are ready to risk their lives under the pretext of taking a video or a photograph, B. Shamoondeswari, Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic), Greater Chennai Traffic Police said here on Friday. While speaking at the Tamil Nadu Road Safety Conference 2026: From Mission to Action organised by the Citizen consumer and civic Action Group (CAG) she highlighted a recent bike stunt incident in the city, in which many youths were involved. We took action, secured a lot of people and seized several two-wheelers without number plates. In todays scenario, everyone watches Instagram. Reels are becoming so common. Whether we dance, sing, travel or cook, anything can be [posted as] reels. The reel culture is what has led to last weeks incident-- the bike racing or bike stunts, she said. She said technological advancements were in place to monitor traffic congestion in the city. K. Phanindra Reddy, retired IAS officer and chairperson of the Tamil Nadu Real Estate Regulatory Authority (TNRERA) said that nearly 35% of the accidents occured on the State Highways, and 30% on the National Highways. It is important for these agencies to ascertain the reasons for these accidents, whether they are because of poor design, poor intersections, or unrestricted access at junctions, he added. Saroja S., executive director of CAG, said that the announcement of the Tamil Nadu Road Safety Mission by the State government recently is an important step in the right direction to solve the crisis at hand. It also signals the States desire to prioritise road safety. Venkatesh Balasubramanian, Professor, Department of Engineering Design, and Head RBG Labs & Centre of Excellence for Road Safety, Indian Institute of Technology-Madras, also spoke.

headline: Delhi Police steps up security ahead of CJP protest. Ola, Uber cabs to face restrictions?
content: With the New Delhi district expected to be turned into a heavily secured zone, officers are preparing to restrict entry on roads leading into the area. Cab operators are also being sensitised about the restrictions, the news outlet reported. Delhi Police has stepped up security ahead of the protest, which is being held to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Quick answers to key questions 1Will Ola and Uber cabs face restrictions near Jantar Mantar during the CJP protest? Delhi Police said it was coordinating with Ola and Uber to regulate cab movement towards Lutyens Delhi and inform operators about restrictions. Roads leading into the New Delhi district may have restricted access; the article does not announce a blanket cab ban. 2Why is the CJP planning a protest at Jantar Mantar? The Cockroach Janta Party proposed the demonstration to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. It cited alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, including claims related to voter lists and Form 6. 3Why did Delhi Police deny permission for the CJP protest? Police said the application was submitted only three days before the proposed event, although rules require applications at least 10 days in advance. They also cited alleged non-compliance with directions during an earlier protest. 4Which Delhi Metro services are affected by the CJP protest security measures? Entry and exit gates at 45 Metro stations are to be closed, while interchange facilities remain available at affected stations except New Delhi. The restriction concerns station access and does not mean the entire Metro network is shut. 5How can commuters check Delhi traffic diversions during the CJP protest? The Delhi Traffic Police warned of possible diversions at 30 locations, depending on conditions. Commuters can check its official website and social media for updates or call 1095 or 011-25844444. The security arrangements include the deployment of 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel, the closure of entry and exit gates at 45 Metro stations, heightened surveillance at Delhi's borders and a temporary suspension of mobile internet services within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar. Police have denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing the short notice given for the event and alleged violations of rules and directions during an earlier protest. The Delhi Traffic Police has warned of possible disruptions and diversions at 30 locations across the capital on October 10. Traffic diversions will be enforced from 6 am, depending on the prevailing situation, according to the advisory. Commuters have been advised to plan their journeys in advance, allow additional travel time and avoid non-essential travel, particularly when heading towards railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) and the airport through New Delhi and Central Delhi. The locations likely to be affected include Shankar Road-Vande Mataram 'T' Point, Dhaula Kuan Flyover, Jhandewalan, Panchkuian, Mandi House, Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, Guru Nanak Chowk, Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar Road. Other locations include Lodhi Road Flyover, Neela Gumbad, Samrat Hotel roundabout, Sardar Patel Marg-Panchsheel Marg crossing, Bhikaji Cama Place, Moti Bagh Flyover, Windsor Palace roundabout, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk and RML Hospital roundabout. The police said traffic management measures would remain dynamic and could be relaxed or tightened based on real-time assessments. Commuters can check the Delhi Traffic Police's official website and social media platforms for updates and alternative routes. The traffic helpline numbers are 1095 and 011-25844444. Entry and exit gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, until further notice. The restrictions will continue on Saturday, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said. The affected stations include Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Janpath, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, ITO, Delhi Gate, Khan Market, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, Hauz Khas and INA. Other stations on the list include Shaheen Bagh, Jamia Millia Islamia, Okhla Vihar, Kalindi Kunj, Lajpat Nagar, Ashram, Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin, Welcome, Shahdara, Rithala, Rohini, Azadpur and Shivaji Stadium. Interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except at the New Delhi Metro station, according to the DMRC. The list of stations to be closed was earlier reported to include 57 stations before the number was revised to 45. The restrictions could affect office-goers, students, shoppers and other passengers who depend on the Metro for their daily commute. Mobile internet services will be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10, sources said. The Union Home Ministry has approved the decision, they added. The suspension will apply to mobile internet services within the designated area, while internet services in the rest of Delhi will remain unaffected, according to the sources. The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones to strengthen security and maintain law and order. Each zone will be monitored by a Joint Commissioner of Police, a Deputy Commissioner of Police and an Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police. Special Commissioners of Police heading various units will also monitor the zones and coordinate with senior officers to respond to any law-and-order situation. More than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces are expected to be involved in the security arrangements. Delhi Police has also conducted mock drills at several locations. Liquor shops across Delhi have been ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10 as a preventive measure. Addressing a press conference on Friday, Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said permission had been denied for the proposed October 10 demonstration. She said the application was submitted on October 7, just three days before the planned gathering, whereas the rules require applications to be filed at least 10 days in advance. Police also cited concerns over compliance with directions issued by authorities during the party's July demonstration. The CJP has proposed to protest at Jantar Mantar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. The party has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Kumar is facing allegations of voter-list tampering under the SIR exercise and of bypassing his two colleagues to alter Form 6, a key document used to register as a voter. The security measures are intended to prevent protesters from staging an unauthorised sit-in at Jantar Mantar and to stop large groups from converging on sensitive locations. Rail services could also be affected on Saturday, with several trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm reportedly cancelled. Police have stepped up checks at railway stations, bus terminals, hotels, lodges, guest houses and dharamshalas as part of the preventive security exercise. Delhi's borders will face heightened surveillance, with additional security cameras installed at several locations. Bus terminals will also see increased vigilance, with personnel monitoring passengers and vehicles arriving from neighbouring states. Airport approach roads are expected to remain under heightened security, with additional checks and surveillance. Travellers have been advised to account for possible congestion and delays when planning their journeys.

headline: Elon Musk's latest tweet: 'Dear PM Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies' - Read full text
content: Elon Musk has once again ignited the debate over Starlink's pending licence to operate in India, naming Ambani in a an X post on Friday. Musk started his message with "Dear Prime Minister Ambani," and then said, "Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India." "Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" Musk added. "There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better," he also said. In a follow-up post, the richest man in the world said, "Also, Starlink has proven to be essential for saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communications systems have failed, so you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India." This is not the first time Elon Musk has claimed there is a monopoly in India's broadband sector. Telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia rejected these claims on Friday, saying that India does not allow monopolies in any sector. "Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers," the minister said at a briefing at India Mobile Congress in New Delhi. The government said on Thursday that all three licensed satellite operators including Starlink were at broadly the same regulatory stage, calling suggestions of an unfair or discriminatory process "baseless and misconceived". Scindia said that while there is a lot of conversation about one particular company, three have got satcom licences. "We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a licence, as and when the government decides the charge system on the revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, then they can start operations," the Minister said. TRAI and the telecom department are close to a final decision on pricing regime for satcom spectrum, Scindia said. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services. Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India, the Ministry of Communications said in a press release on Thursday. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data. Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived, it added. Hitting out at Congress, in the backdrop of Rahul Gandhi and Elon Musk's exchange on X, the minister said, "As far as the Congress party is concerned... I don't think they themselves know whether they're going left or right," he said. After Musk posted on X, "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" Gandhi responded by saying, "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." Musk later thanked Gandhi for his response. "Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling," Musk said in response to Gandhi's post. headline: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 3 people as Kyiv struggles to counter escalating attacks
content: Russian strikes killed three people and wounded at least eight across Ukraine, officials said on Friday (October 9, 2026), as Ukraine struggles to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 50 people over the past three days. One man was killed, and five people were wounded in Russian strikes on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region in the morning hours, said Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the regional military administration. He said the attacks hit residential areas and that a child was among the wounded. Another man was killed in Ivano-Frankivsk in western Ukraine, Svitlana Onyshchuk, head of the regional military administration, reported. A woman was also killed in a Russian attack on warehouse facilities in the district of Bucha in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's Interior Ministry said on Telegram. Her body was found while clearing rubble and fighting a fire at the site, Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration, said on Friday (October 9). Three people were wounded there. Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than four-and-a-half years since Moscow's full-scale invasion. Elsewhere, a Ukrainian attack on Russia's eastern Belgorod region killed two people on Friday (October 9), the area's regional emergency headquarters said. Regional governor Alexander Shuvayev said that 12 people had been wounded in Ukrainian strikes. Zelenskyy appeals for NATO support Russian attacks have killed dozens of civilians across Ukraine over the past three days using a mix of ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones. On Thursday (October 8), a Russian guided bomb exploded next to public buses filled with passengers in eastern Ukraine, killing 30 people. A day earlier, a Russian missile strike killed 22 people, including five children, in the northern Ukrainian town of Pryluky. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that Moscow will likely escalate daily attacks as winter approaches, putting pressure on Ukraine as it prepares for winter and hitting the infrastructure keeping its war-battered economy afloat. Recent Russian targets have included energy systems, key industries, railways, post offices, shopping centres, telecom networks, gas stations and grain exports. The Ukrainian leader held a meeting with military officials and government members on Friday (October 9) focusing on Ukraine's energy and air defence needs. Unfortunately, there is a lot of damage to the power grid and electricity transmission facilities," he wrote on Telegram. "Repairs are going on around the clock." The Kyiv city administration said via Telegram that the Ukrainian capital would again set up government-built help stations that serve food and drinks and provide warmth and power -- known as points of invincibility -- in three districts of the city where the power situation was most difficult. Zelenskyy appealed on Thursday (October 8) for additional defence support from NATO countries, saying in an online post: It is important that support in words takes concrete form in new packages for Ukraine's defence. Supplies of anti-ballistic capabilities, ammunition for our combat aircraft and investments in interceptors -- all of this is directly helping save lives every day, he said. Without ammunition for its U.S.-made Patriot air defence systems, Ukraine can't stop Russian ballistic weapons. It is racing to develop a new generation of interceptors fast enough to catch Moscow's high-flying jet-propelled drones. Ukraine targets Russian data centres Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone strike damaged a data centre belonging to Russian technology giant Yandex, the company confirmed. "As a result of a drone attack, part of Yandex data centre infrastructure in Kaluga was affected. Several data centre modules are completely out of service. This may cause some Yandex services to experience disruptions," Yandex's press service said and added it was currently assessing the full extent of the damage. It also said that nobody had been injured. It is the second time in two days that the company has been targeted, with an earlier drone attack Thursday taking a data centre in Russia's western Ryazan region offline. Mr. Zelenskyy confirmed the data centre strike in a post on X. He also said that Kyiv's forces had hit the Ukhta oil refinery in Russia's Komi region. The region's head, Rostislav Goldstein, said earlier on Friday (October 9) that there had been an attack on the town of Ukhta, but that there had been no damage. The governor of the Kaluga region, Vladislav Shapsha, said on Friday (October 9) that nine people had been wounded by drone attacks on the region. Meanwhile, Tver regional governor Vitaly Korolyov said a Ukrainian drone sparked a fire at a factory in Redkino. No casualties were reported. Russia's Defence Ministry said that its air defences downed 505 Ukrainian drones from late Thursday until early Friday (October 9).

headline: Talks with Iran can only succeed without threats, President says
content: Peace negotiations with Iran would only succeed without "pressure and threats", Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Friday (October 9, 2026), amid deadlocked efforts to end months of fighting in the West Asia. Diplomatic efforts to end the seven-month conflict, which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, have been at an impasse since the summer. The United States and Iran agreed to a memorandum of understanding in June that spelt out a framework for ending the conflict, but Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz prompted a resumption of U.S. military operations. Recent indirect talks between Washington and Tehran on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly failed to produce a breakthrough. "Dialogue holds meaning and a chance of success only when based on mutual respect and mutual commitments, and when devoid of pressure and threat," Mr. Pezeshkian said at a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in Turkmenistan. "Negotiation conducted in the shadow of force is not negotiation, it is imposition and coercion," he said, adding that sanctions on Iran would affect "regional trade, connectivity, energy, and order." Mr. Pezeshkian said on Monday that talks with the United States to end the war were worthless and only resulted in renewed attacks. "With an enemy that every day resorts to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats, and that breaks its commitments, negotiations are meaningless," he said. Washington has in recent weeks dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure and has not struck Iran since September 1. The United States and Israel have said the war was necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons a goal Tehran has long denied pursuing. The focus of negotiations has since shifted to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping lane for oil from the Gulf that has been effectively shut since the fighting. Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation. The U.S. has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it. Putin, Pezeshkian meet Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday (October 8) he would "do everything" he could to help end the war during a meeting with Mr. Pezeshkian ahead of the summit, Russian media reported. "We are ready to do everything that is in our power to contribute to the settlement of this situation," Mr. Putin said. He added that Iran had made "real efforts to end the war" since the U.S.-Israeli attacks started on February 28, according to Russian news agencies. Mr. Putin also said there had been a "positive evolution" in Iran-Russia relations. The two countries, heavily sanctioned by the West, have reinforced diplomatic and military links since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine in February 2022, becoming increasingly reliant on each other. Kyiv and Western countries have accused Iran of supplying Russia with Shahed drones and short-range missiles that Moscow uses in attacks on Ukraine. U.S. media outlets have reported Russia has supplied data to Iran for its attacks on U.S. targets in the West Asia. "We are engaged in dialogue, but every time we negotiate with the United States, they attack again," Mr. Pezeshkian said at the talks with Mr. Putin, according to Iranian state media. Tehran wanted to see a "final framework" to end the war, Mr. Pezeshkian said. But he accused the United States of "trying to impose its policies and views on all countries". "If the United States insists on pursuing a unilateral approach, a resolution will not be possible," he said, according to state media.
