Mr. Trump told the United Nations General Assembly in September that he had to choose whether to "annihilate" Iran if it failed to make a deal. But the U.S. leader has since ruled out attacking Iran again before the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, saying on Thursday that Washington was holding "productive discussions" with the Islamic republic. The CIS was established in 1991 as a platform for dialogue among the former republics of the Soviet Union. Some states have left Georgia withdrew following a 2008 war with Russia, Ukraine halted its participation after Moscow's 2014 annexation of Crimea and Moldova left in 2023 as it sought closer ties with the European Union. The summit comes as diplomatic efforts to resolve Russia's offensive in Ukraine also appear deadlocked, with both sides intensifying attacks.

headline: How can a police officer aver that accused will abscond because he is a 'North Indian?' questions Madras High Court
content: The Madras High Court has expressed its strong disapproval to an averment made by an Inspector of Police that the accused in a criminal case was likely to abscond because he is a North Indian. The court said, such an averment ought not to have appeared in an affidavit sworn by a police officer. While granting bail to Ankur Kumar Jain of FIIT-JEE in a cheating case booked by Coimbatore police, Justice N. Ramesh wrote: The averment that the petitioner is likely to abscond because he is a North Indian is not appreciated. A persons place of origin is not a ground for apprehending that he will flee. He went on to highlight that the petitioner had lived and worked in Chennai for more than two decades and said that the latter was entitled to bail for the sole reason that the police had miserably failed to furnish the grounds of arrest to him in a language that he can read and understand. The judge pointed out that an arrest memo served on the petitioner in Tamil, a language that he could not read, too did not contain the grounds of arrest. The consequences of the police failing to follow the arrest procedures scrupulously are serious and it ends up going in favour of the accused, he said. In very serious cases, accused persons are being released not because the case against them is weak but because the police did not do what the law requires at the moment of arrest. The persons who suffer are the victims... and the cause of a fair investigation, the judge wrote. Observing that it was not clear whether such lapses by the police were the result of ignorance or indifference, Justice Ramesh said, either way, the police need to be sensitised, trained and educated on this issue, and the officers who commit such lapses must be made accountable. The judge, suo motu, impleaded the Director General of Police (Law and Order) as one of the respondents to the bail petition and directed the head of the police force to explain whether any circular or standing order had been issued instructing the police officers regarding issuance of written grounds of arrest. The court also wanted to know whether any training or sensitisation sessions had been conducted in the past or were proposed to be conducted in the future regarding the need to issue grounds of arrest. It directed the DGP to warn police officers that failure to issue grounds of arrest would lead to departmental proceedings. The High Court Registry was directed to list the matter next on November 10, 2026 for the DGP to report compliance.

headline: 'Almost putting on lockdown': Dhruv Rathee arrives in Delhi, questions security clampdown ahead of CJP protest
content: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Friday accused the central government of putting Delhi under an almost lockdown ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In a video posted on Instagram, Rathee questioned the extensive security and transport restrictions imposed in the national capital, including the planned closure of metro stations, cancellation of trains and a temporary suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi. Earlier on Friday, the DMRC said entry and exit of 57 metro stations would be closed. However, it later issued a revised list, reducing the number of stations to 45, from 9 pm on Friday to 6 pm on Saturday. Quick answers to key questions 1Why was Dhruv Rathee criticising security restrictions in Delhi before the CJP protest? Rathee said metro closures, cancelled trains and the planned mobile internet suspension made Delhi feel like it was under an almost lockdown. He questioned why such extensive measures were needed if, as he claimed, social media accounts were predicting a low turnout. 2Why was the CJP planning a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10? The CJP called the demonstration to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. Organisers alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and raised concerns about the handling of Form 6 voter-registration applications. 3Why did Delhi Police impose restrictions ahead of the CJP protest? Delhi Police described the measures as precautions to maintain law and order and protect the public. It cited concerns about crowd management, previous protests and the need to keep traffic moving and emergency services accessible. 4How many Delhi Metro stations had entry and exit restrictions for the CJP protest? The DMRC revised its initial advisory, reducing the number of affected stations from 57 to 45. Entry and exit were restricted from 9 pm on Friday until 6 pm on Saturday, while interchange facilities remained available at affected stations except New Delhi. 5Where and when was mobile internet suspended ahead of the Delhi protest? The suspension covered mobile internet services within a four-kilometre radius of the JanpathKartavya Path crossing. It was scheduled to run from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10; services elsewhere in Delhi were to remain unaffected. How are you, friends? I have arrived in Delhi. And I saw what arrangements our Prime Minister has made here. More than 50 metro stations have been shut down, Rathee said in the video. Trains have been shut down. Buses have been cancelled. And they are almost putting Delhi on lockdown because of our protests, he added. Rathee also questioned why such extensive measures were necessary if, as he claimed, social media accounts associated with the BJP were predicting a low turnout at the demonstration. On one hand, your IT cell people are saying that no one will come to our protest. If there is no crowd, then why are you doing all this if there is no crowd? I don't understand, he said. I think you are actually scared. Actually, the entire country's population is awake, Rathee added, urging people to attend the demonstration. Friends, if you are watching this, do come to Jantar Mantar on 10th October, he said. The Delhi Police on Friday defended the temporary restrictions, particularly around Jantar Mantar, saying they were precautionary measures intended to maintain law and order and protect residents, commuters, businesses and police personnel. In a statement, Additional Commissioner of Police Rajeev Ranjan said the right to peaceful protest was an important democratic right, but authorities also had a responsibility to prevent violence and ensure public safety. The police claimed that a protest authorised for a single day in July continued for nearly a month, leaving more than 200 police personnel injured. They also alleged that over 2,000 people with criminal antecedents took part in the demonstrations. According to the statement, students were also injured in clashes, while allegations of molestation and assault involving women constables during protests over the past week raised serious concerns. The Delhi Police said Jantar Mantar could accommodate around 1,000 people safely at any given time. It emphasised that obtaining prior permission was essential to ensure proper crowd management, regulate traffic and maintain access for emergency services. However, the Delhi Police have refused permission for the CJP's proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. Following the decision, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has instructed police chiefs across all states and Union Territories to ensure law and order and tighten security arrangements. Delhi has stepped up security ahead of Saturdays proposed gathering, with around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed, according to reports. Authorities have also ordered intensive checks at border points, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations. Several train services to the capital have also been cancelled, as per reports. Separately, mobile internet services will remain suspended within a four-kilometre radius of the JanpathKartavya Path crossing from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10, according to ANI citing sources. The restriction will apply to mobile internet services in the designated area, while services in the rest of Delhi will remain unaffected, they mentioned. The measures come amid heightened tensions over the CJP protest and the demand for Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls under the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The protest organisers have accused the poll body of voter-list tampering and raised questions about the handling of Form 6, the application used to register as a voter. The planned demonstration follows protests in several cities, including Bengaluru, where Rathee and actor Prakash Raj joined a CJP-led gathering at Freedom Park on Thursday. (With inputs from agency)

headline: AIADMK likely to face another crisis after decline in vote share
content: With yet another electoral setback in the byelections to Madurantakam and Dharapuram Reserved Assembly constituencies, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) is lurching towards another challenging phase, perhaps the worst in its 54-year history. Possibly, around the AIADMKs Foundation Day (October 17), critics, within and outside, of the partys general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami will launch another salvo against him. They will point out how the organisation, once a dominant force in State politics, is getting weaker day by day. For quite sometime, the talk has been doing rounds in political circles that the AIADMKs general council, when it is expected to be convened in a few months, will witness a major showdown between supporters of Mr. Palaniswami and his detractors. On the face of it, the AIADMKs performance was not that bad, as the party had secured close to one-fourth of votes polled say, around 25% in the two constituencies. In Madurantakam, the Dravidian major was handicapped by the neutral stand of the Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), which was its ally in the Assembly polls five months ago. As a result, it did not get the advantage that it would have secured otherwise. This could be seen from the fact that during the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, when the AIADMKs position was as good as what it is now, the partys vote share was 37% whereas it has gone down to 25.61% this time. When the party retained the seat in the April-May election, its score was 32.58%, which was lower than what the party had secured in 2024, in spite of the alliance with the PMK. However, the presence of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the scene early this year changed the contours of the electoral battle, making it a fierce triangular contest. In Dharapuram, the erosion of the AIADMKs vote share was quite noticeable, as it fell from 32.37% in 2024 and 40% in 2026 (April-May) to about 25% now. The party had won the seat seven times. The TVK, which had a vote share of about 29% five months ago, seems to have grown at the cost of the AIADMK, as the ruling party has got close to 37%. Former Minister Pollachi V. Jayaraman, who worked for the party in the constituency, says the results have shown that the people have not yet come out of the web of illusion of the ruling TVK. He expects them to realise the reality sooner rather than later and hopes that under such circumstances, his party will bounce back. Asked whether the ruling TVK will intensify its efforts to woo the cadre of the AIADMK, the partys deputy general secretary M. Anandan says there is no need for his party to do so. The AIADMKs volunteers have been joining us, and they will continue to join us in future too, he said. Asked about the impact of the dissidents non-cooperation on the results of the byelections, Mr. Jayaraman says: One thing is certain: I am like many others who will follow the path being shown by Mr. Palaniswami. At the same time, there is a view that the rebels camp have no leader who can match Mr. Palaniswami. Needless to say, the coming weeks are going to witness several events for the AIADMK.

headline: RIDEV expands presence with Chennai hub
content: Electric mobility platform RIDEV has opened its 16th hub in Chennai. The company provides electric two-wheelers on rent to delivery and gig workers, along with battery swapping, maintenance, roadside assistance, insurance and standby EVs at no additional cost.RIDEVs hub-based model aims to reduce vehicle downtime and eliminate the upfront investment and maintenance burden of owning an EV, helping riders keep earning.Our responsibility goes beyond putting an EV on the road to ensuring riders can continue earning without being held back by ownership costs, repairs or downtime, said Manish Kumar Jain, founder and CEO, RIDEV.Founded in April 2024 with just 10 electric two-wheelers, RIDEV has scaled to more than 12,000 electric two-wheelers on the road.

headline: Japan protests Russia's extradition requests for ICC president Tomoko Akane and eight other court staff
content: Japan on Friday (October 9, 2026) slammed Russias request for the extradition from the Netherlands of the president of the International Criminal Court, a Japanese national, and eight other officials of the court based in the European country. The extradition requests came after Moscow issued warrants for the nine in response to the ICCs 2023 arrest warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin over the war in Ukraine. The Moscow City Court last year sentenced the nine in absentia to prison terms. A high-ranking Japanese official said Friday (October 9) that Tokyo has expressed its protest to Moscow over the requests. Measures targeting individuals connected to the ICC are unjust and unacceptable, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki told reporters. We regret that Russia made extradition requests to multiple countries nevertheless. Ozaki said Japan would respond appropriately, including lodging additional protests. His comments came after Russias Prosecutor Generals Office on Thursday (October 8) submitted requests to the Netherlands and a number of other countries for the extradition of the nine ICC staff, including its president, Tomoko Akane. Moscow has accused the ICC of issuing arrest warrants against Russian citizens in violation of fundamental principles and norms of international law without any evidence, according to the Russian state news agency Tass. Relations between Japan and Russia have worsened since Putin visited a Pacific Island chain claimed by Japan in August. The Soviet Union captured the islands from Japan in the final days of World War II, leading to the dispute that has kept the two countries from signing a peace treaty formally ending their hostilities. Japan has also struggled to balance its support for the ICC and ties with the United States, which does not support the court. Also, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has been criticised at home, including for balancing her close alliance with the U.S. with Japans backing of the Netherlands-based court. We have consistently supported the ICC and will continue to do so, PM Takaichi told a Parliamentary session on Friday (October 9). Washington has accused the ICC of overstepping its mandate and has imposed sanctions on Akane and about a dozen other court staffers in retaliation for investigations into Israeli officials over the war in the Gaza Strip and probes into the conduct of U.S. military personnel in Afghanistan. The U.S. measures freeze any assets held in U.S. jurisdictions by those sanctioned and prevent court officials and their families from entering the U.S.

headline: Pakistan says 'substantial' forces, resources already in Saudi Arabia under defence deal
content: Pakistan on Friday (October 9, 2026) said a substantial number of its forces and resources were already deployed in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming its commitment to protect the kingdom's sovereignty under the Makkah defence agreement, amid concerns over the Houthi threat. Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks at his weekly press briefing in response to a question on the growing threat posed by Yemens Houthi rebels to Saudi Arabia. Referring to a recent meeting of defence officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye in Riyadh, Mr. Khan said the three countries had reaffirmed their unity in ensuring deterrence and safeguarding Saudi Arabias sovereignty and territorial integrity. He said the three countries had also agreed to mobilise resources rapidly in accordance with their requirements. Pakistan already has a substantial number of forces, as well as resources, in Riyadh. It is now up to the organisation to assess the threat perception and operate in accordance with its own mandate, Mr. Khan said. He said it would not be appropriate for him to disclose operational details, including the nature and extent of any further deployment, adding that such decisions would be taken by the alliances headquarters. It is for the organisation and the alliances headquarters to decide how much deployment is required, when and where it should take place, and the countries that are part of the alliance will make the necessary contributions accordingly, Mr. Khan said. The spokesperson also rejected reports that Pakistani fighter jets were involved in cross-border operations in Yemen, describing them as speculative. As regards your question about Pakistani fighter jets being involved in cross-border operations, this is speculative news, which has also been refuted by the Minister for Information, he said. Mr. Khan said Pakistan's forces had been deployed in Saudi Arabia since 1982 in one capacity or another, sometimes under logistical arrangements and sometimes as part of training missions. He added that deployments had again taken place following the signing of the bilateral defence agreement between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia last year and the trilateral arrangement this year. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye on August 7 following a summit in Mecca. The trilateral defence pact stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be considered an attack against all. Following the escalation of Houthi attacks, the pact's Strategic Political and Defence Committee met in Riyadh on October 5 and decided on the deployment of military forces in the Gulf kingdom. Khan said the Makkah alliance is a defensive organisation intended to defend the three countries against aggression. Therefore, these forces would not cross the border into Yemen to launch attacks against the Houthis. However, they would, of course, be utilised to defend the countrys territory and safeguard its sovereignty, he said. The spokesperson said that the attacks on Saudi Arabia were indeed a matter of great concern for Pakistan, given that approximately 2.5 million Pakistanis reside in the Kingdom, and their numbers are growing. He said a Pakistani truck driver in Yemen was also killed in a drone attack, showing a risk of people falling victim to this escalation. That is why Pakistan has consistently advocated de-escalation, dialogue, and diplomacy. At the same time, we remain committed to protecting Saudi Arabias sovereignty and providing our community with all the necessary support for their welfare, the spokesperson said. He also said that Pakistan stands in unwavering solidarity with the Kingdom In line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, our commitment to Saudi Arabias sovereignty, territorial integrity and security remains resolute. We reaffirm the Kingdoms legitimate right to defend its people and protect its critical infrastructure, Khan said.

headline: 'Build here. Scale here. Die here' - Pan IIT Alumni India Chairman on US PERM, H1-B news from Trump Admin
content: Pan IIT Alumni India has now urged IITians to return to India, claiming that India now offers better opportunities amid uncertainty surrounding US immigration policies, including the recent developments related to PERM labour certification and H-1B visas under the Trump administration. Taking to X, the body which represents alumni of 23 Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), extended concerns over ongoing visa issues in the US involving the US PERM programme. Calling for fair and transparent immigration policies, the organisation warned against stereotyping Indian talent. It also commented on JD Vance referring to Indian professionals as "indentured servants". "PanIIT Alumni India notes with concern the recent developments in the United States regarding the PERM programme and the treatment of skilled Indian professionals on H-1B visas. We respect the sovereign right of every nation to shape its immigration policy. However, we urge that such policy be applied fairly, transparently, and without stigmatising a community of professionals whose contributions to the American economy and society are well documented," the statement read. Quick answers to key questions 1What did Pan IIT Alumni India say about the US PERM and H-1B developments? The organisation called for fair and transparent immigration policies and opposed stigmatising Indian professionals. It said Indian engineers and technologists have made significant contributions to US innovation and industry. 2What is the difference between PERM and an H-1B visa? H-1B is a temporary, employer-sponsored visa for foreign professionals in specialised occupations. PERM is a labour-certification step employers generally use when sponsoring eligible workers for employment-based green cards. 3How does the PERM suspension affect Indian H-1B workers at the affected companies? The suspension halts new and pending PERM applications at the affected firms, creating uncertainty for workers pursuing employer-sponsored green cards. It does not automatically cancel their existing H-1B visas. 4Why did the Trump administration suspend PERM processing at eight technology companies? The administration accused the companies of misusing the labour-certification system to replace American workers with foreign employees. It also said the suspensions were connected to ongoing federal investigations. 5Why did Pan IIT Alumni India urge IITians in the US to return to India? Chairman Prabhat Kumar said a visa was never a stable foundation for a career and urged Indian engineers to build and create impact at home. The organisation said India offers opportunities for Indian talent amid uncertainty over US immigration policies. "For over five decades, Indian engineers and technologists a large number of them IIT alumni - have been among the most productive contributors to American innovation, research, and industry. They have built products, filed patents, founded companies, and created jobs on American soil. To characterise them collectively as "indentured servants" is neither accurate nor fair," it added. Prabhat Kumar, IRS, chairman of PanIIT Alumni India, said the ongoing situation should put focus on Indian talents shifting abroad. "For decades, we celebrated when our brightest minds left for American shores. It is time we asked what we lost in the process. A visa was never a stable foundation for a career, and this week's events prove it. The IIT covenant was nation before self. The most exciting problems and the greatest impact - now await our engineers at home. Build here. Scale here. Die here," he said. Earlier, India criticised the US decision to restrict a key green-card processing programme for major tech firms, including Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Microsoft, Adobe, Capgemini and Cognizant. The Trump administration suspended the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for eight IT majors in an effort to reduce the number of foreign workers in the US and create job opportunities for Americans. The move is likely to affect Indian techies who rely on employer-sponsored green cards for permanent residency in the US after entering the country on H-1B visas. Sneha Biswas specialises in covering entertainment and pop culture, with a specialisation on Bollywood, Hollywood, OTT platforms, K-pop, K-dramas, and major developments in the US entertainment industry. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: 'Inspired By 9/11': Flydubai Co-Pilot Confesses To Plotting Airport Suicide Crash In Early Probe
content: Hammami allegedly confessed that the ambition to execute a similar aerial assault became firmly established in his mind prior to undergoing commercial pilot training An official investigation into the recent hijacking attempt on a Flydubai flight has revealed that the suspect, identified as co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, was motivated to pursue an aviation career by the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. According to statements from the United Arab Emirates Attorney General, the suspect confessed that the ambition to execute a similar aerial assault became firmly established in his mind prior to undergoing commercial pilot training. Investigators found that the 29-year-old co-pilot planned to seize control of the Boeing 737 MAX operating from Dubai to Tel Aviv and execute a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. His stated objective was to inflict maximum casualties at Israels primary international gateway. - Flydubai Co-Pilot Interrogated By Israel's Shin Bet | Gaza | Ben Gurion Target ?| News18 - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views ? | News18 - Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack On Ben Gurion Airport, Chose Airline For Israel Route - UAE Seeks Death Penalty For Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Over Cockpit Attack Mid-Air Cockpit Crisis and Subdued Threat The incident unfolded mid-flight when al-Hammami initiated an attack inside the cockpit using the aircrafts emergency crash axe. The assault caused the aircraft to enter a steep descent before Captain Smit Machchhar, despite sustaining injuries, managed to unlock the armoured cockpit door to alert crew and passengers. Several passengers and cabin crew members intervened immediately to help restrain the co-pilot. An off-duty pilot present on board assumed control of the flight alongside the captain, allowing the aircraft to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia without further loss of life. Background, Radicalisation, and Vetting Scrutiny International counter-terrorism agencies across the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand are currently scrutinising al-Hammamis background and travel history. Reports indicate he completed flight training across multiple international institutions and had previously worked for Oman Air before being dismissed due to extremist views. He was subsequently hired by Flydubai eight months prior to the incident. The revelations have prompted aviation authorities and security experts worldwide to call for stricter vetting mechanisms, improved background tracking, and enhanced cross-border information sharing regarding pilot employment histories to prevent similar security failures. According to statements from the United Arab Emirates Attorney General, Hamam al-Hammami confessed that his ambition to execute an aerial assault was inspired by the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. This motivation became established in his mind even before he began his commercial pilot training.

headline: Saudi authorities say three killed in Houthi-claimed attacks on Riyadh airport
content: An airline pilot was among three Saudi citizens killed in attacks targeting Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia aircraft, the kingdom's civil aviation authority said on Friday (October 9, 2026). Several people of different nationalities were wounded. The attacks on Thursday (October 8) were the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels last weekend. They also marked a significant escalation on the latest front in the Iran war, which has kept oil prices and financial markets volatile. UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg was scheduled to brief the Security Council on developments in Yemen later on Friday. By Friday (October 8) afternoon, at least 124 flights to and from Riyadh had been cancelled after hundreds more were cancelled a day earlier, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware. Also read: India advises nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain vigilant amid escalating regional tensions The Indian Embassy said Air India had suspended operations through to Saturday (October 10), while the Lufthansa Group said its airlines would suspend flights to Riyadh through to October 16. Pakistan International Airlines has also suspended flights to Riyadh because of the evolving situation in the West Asia, an airline spokesman said. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis' ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a greater focus on aviation infrastructure. The guidance, updated Friday, adds that recurrent missile and drone attacks, together with the activation of air-defence systems, create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft, as well as risks associated with missile and drone overflights, interception activity and falling debris. Yemen's Houthis claim the attack The first attack on Thursday (October 8) targeted airport facilities, while the second struck the aircraft, the Saudi statement said. It did not identify those responsible, though the Houthis claimed to have targeted the airport with a ballistic missile. Among the dead was Capt. Hamoud Ali Alkalthami, the Saudia Group said in a statement. It appeared to be the first confirmed attack on the Saudi national carrier since the new offensive began. A separate Saudia Group statement said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board. The aviation statement also said the injuries to citizens and people of other nationalities ranged from minor to serious. The Saudia Group statement later said operational activities at the airport had returned to normal. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms used by the rebels to threaten regional security. Saudi-led coalition bombards Yemen's Houthi-held capital Residents in Yemen's capital of Sanaa heard heavy explosions overnight into Friday as intense fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-led forces continued. Anees al-Asbahi, spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, said on X that two of the overnight strikes on Sanaa by the Saudi-led coalition injured six people, including a child. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the strikes on Sanaa. Mohamed al-Jabir, the Saudi ambassador to Yemen, in a post on X on Friday (October 8), claimed that the Bab el-Mandeb Strait had been cleansed of Houthi remnants. He didn't provide further details. Protesters gathered in several Houthi-held cities in Yemen on Friday to denounce Saudi Arabia and its backers. Meanwhile, Saudi allies, including Kuwait and Pakistan, condemned the attack on the Riyadh airport. The Kuwaiti Foreign Ministry said the kingdom's security is an inseparable part of the security of Kuwait and the Gulf Cooperation Council countries. Pakistan has said it's making its military capabilities available to Saudi Arabia to fight the Houthis under a new mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey. Foreign Ministry spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan told reporters in Islamabad that Saudi Arabia has a "legitimate right to defend its people and protect its critical infrastructure. Riyadh airport has been repeatedly targeted The airport in the Saudi capital has come under repeated attack in recent days. This week, the Houthis warned global airlines for the last time about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theatre for their military operations. On Wednesday (October 7), Saudi officials said Houthi-claimed attacks on airports in Riyadh and Abha had killed three people. Saudi Arabia faces mounting attacks from the Houthis, who declared a blockade of the kingdom earlier this year in response to one imposed on them. The kingdom has sought support from allies, including the United States. Officials said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive. But President Donald Trump has shown reluctance to expand U.S. military involvement in West Asia and, for now, has not ordered American forces to resume strikes against the rebels. The U.S. last year carried out a nearly two-month air strike campaign against the Houthis in an effort to open international shipping lanes in the Red Sea. The Houthis had disrupted the waterway for months with their own attacks in response to Israel mounting a blockade on the Gaza Strip. Trump halted strikes after the U.S. military burned through hundreds of millions of dollars in munitions. The new Saudi-led offensive aims to retake territory the Houthis seized a month ago along Yemen's western Red Sea coast and the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Their presence there threatens a crucial alternative shipping route to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian attacks on ships have curtailed traffic.

headline: DMK retains much of its vote bank despite going it alone, reinforces position as the principal rival of TVK
content: The outcome of the byelection to the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Reserved Assembly constituencies has reinforced the DMKs position as the principal alternative to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The DMKs second-place finish in both constituencies suggests it has retained much of its vote base. This is significant given that the party contested without most of its erstwhile allies, suggesting that an united alliance could improve its electoral prospects. The Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK), which joined the DMK-led alliance ahead of the Assembly election in June, was an exception. In Dharapuram, the DMKs vote count fell to 57,370 from 64,373 in the Assembly election but one needs to account for the declined voter turnout in the constituency as well compared to April 2026. Besides, the decline could be attributed to the absence of its former allies, including the Congress, the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), the Communist parties, and the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML). However, the TVK failed to match the vote count secured by the AIADMK in the general election, despite the defection of the former AIADMK legislator and the shift of the DMKs erstwhile allies to the ruling party. P. Sathyabama, who won the seat as an AIADMK candidate in the Assembly election, securing 81,100 votes. Contesting on the TVK ticket in the byelection, she polled 66,841 votes, suggesting that she was unable to retain the entire AIADMK vote base (even after adjusting for the lower voter turnout). In Madurantakam, AIADMK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel, who contested the byelection on the TVK ticket, secured 74,048 votes, more than 5,000 above her tally in the Assembly election. This was despite the TVKs candidate, Ezhil Katherine, having secured 62,090 votes in the Assembly election. The increase notwithstanding, the result raises questions about the extent to which the AIADMKs vote base remained with Ms. Kumaravel after her defection to the TVK. The DMKs vote count, too, declined. I. Paranthaman, a well-known party face but an outsider to the constituency, secured 54,008 votes, against the 59,838 polled by the partys candidate, S. Amulu Ponmalar, in the Assembly election. The decline could partly be attributed to the absence of allies such as the VCK, which has a substantial presence in the constituency. The Pattali Makkal Katchis (PMK), decision to remain neutral in the election may have divided its Vanniyar support base. The party had contested the Assembly election in the company of the AIADMK. DMK president M.K. Stalin said the combined votes polled by the parties that contested against the ruling TVK showed that the government had been rejected by a majority of voters. A senior DMK leader and former Minister described the result in Dharapuram as an honourable defeat, pointing out that the constituency was in the Kongu region, considered an AIADMK stronghold, and that former Chief Minister Edappadi K. Palaniswami remained a well-known political figure in the area. In Madurantakam too, we have retained our vote bank even though our allies have switched camps. We need to concentrate on the section of young voters who have grown fond of the TVK and the screen-crafted charisma of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. We will evolve a strategy to overcome the shortcomings, he added.

headline: Government slams Vance's remarks on Indian IT professionals as 'deeply offensive'
content: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday (October 9, 2026) slammed as unwarranted and deeply offensive U.S. Vice President J.D. Vances comments in which he called foreign workers, including Indian IT professionals, indentured servants. Hitting out at the U.S. government for its decision to suspend labour certifications from several Indian technology firms based in America, the Ministry said the steps would not advance the shared ambitions of both countries, indicating further trouble in the already difficult economic relationship between the two countries. On Thursday , Mr. Vance and U.S. Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the suspension of the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for eight IT outsourcing giants, including five Indian IT multinationals operating in the U.S., and accused them of visa fraud. The list included Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, Cognizant, and HCL from India, often called the Big 5, as well as Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe. Such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem, the Ministry said in a strongly worded statement that reminded the Trump administration that the U.S. had been shaped by generations of immigrants. Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive, the Ministry added, pointing to the use of indentured labour by American and European colonial settlers in the 19th century, including in the U.S. and nearby islands to work on their farms. The PERM programme allows companies to certify professionals who are not U.S. citizens for essential skills, qualifying them to be sponsored for a Green Card of Permanent Residency status in the country. The U.S. government said this process benefitted more than 2,30,000 H1B visa approvals and 1,00,000 permanent residencies since 2009, claiming that the eight companies had brought in hundreds of thousands of foreign workers at lower wages through a pernicious system that defrauded the American worker. About 70% of all H1B visa holders are Indian. You [the Companies] bring in indentured servants from outside the country. You lay off American workers. And if youre a corporation, you make a ton of money by undercutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldnt be in the United States of America to begin with, Mr. Vance said. The PERM programme enables a company to sponsor a foreign employee for permanent residence in the U.S., and it must prove to the Labour Department that it tried and failed to find a comparatively qualified American for the job. The Ministry said that talent mobility helps both the U.S. and India, creating opportunities for Indians and providing U.S. companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the U.S. Mr. Vances announcement came when economic ties between India and the U.S. were under strain over the lack of progress in the Free Trade Agreement talks, despite months of negotiations in Delhi and Washington and calls between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump. Last week, after talks in Washington, the U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said no deal was imminent, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman also disclosed that negotiations had plateaued with little possible give-and-take. In addition, New Delhi is awaiting the impact of the Sanctions against Russia and Iran Act that mandates up to 100% U.S. tariffs on countries importing large quantities of Russian oil. Mr. Trump is expected to take a decision on the tariffs on October 18, just ahead of the mid-term elections in the U.S. in early November.

headline: Iran claims strike on LPG tanker taking 'illegal route' through Hormuz
content: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Friday (October 9) that it had struck a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carrier attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz via what Tehran described as an illegal route, as maritime authorities separately reported a projectile strike that triggered a fire aboard a vessel off the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coast. The two reports identified different vessels, and it was not immediately clear whether the incidents were connected. In a statement carried by Iranian state media, the Revolutionary Guards said Iranian forces had taken control of the administration of the strait, reiterating Tehran's efforts to regulate shipping through the strategic waterway amid the ongoing Middle East war. In carrying out this mission, a few hours ago, a giant LPG carrier named NV Sunshine, owned by NatWit, which was attempting to transit via the illegal route south of the Strait of Hormuz, was struck, the IRGC said. Iran has sought to impose control over the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in late February, insisting that vessels obtain its permission to cross through routes designated by Tehran. However, some ships have increasingly attempted to transit through an alternative route along the strait's southern coast. Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said a vessel had been struck by a projectile approximately 13 nautical miles (24 kilometres) off Al Jazeera Al Hamra in the UAE, southwest of the Strait of Hormuz. The incident caused a fire aboard the ship, UKMTO said in a statement on Friday. The status of the crew, damage assessment and environmental impact are unknown at present. Authorities are investigating, the agency said. British maritime security firm Vanguard also reported the incident, identifying the vessel as the Panama-flagged crude oil tanker GEM NO.2. The available reports did not establish a connection between the reported strike on the NV Sunshine LPG carrier claimed by Iran and the projectile incident involving GEM NO.2 off the UAE coast. The latest reports come days after another tanker was struck off Qatar, approximately 500 kilometres (300 miles) west of the Strait of Hormuz. Ships operating in the Gulf and those attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz have faced repeated attacks since the United States and Israel launched military action against Iran in late February. The strait is the only maritime passage into and out of the Gulf and serves as a critical route for global energy supplies. Before the war, approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas shipments passed through the waterway. Iran has sought to restrict traffic through the strait, although some vessels have continued to cross. US media reports have also described American military efforts to protect ships using the southern route. The United States, meanwhile, has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and has occasionally fired on vessels linked to Tehran, further intensifying the confrontation over maritime access. The competing efforts to control shipping through the waterway have heightened risks for commercial vessels and added to concerns over the security of global energy supplies.

headline: 'Blessing In Disguise': Terminated JNU Professor Refutes 'Sex-For-Marks' Claims, Says 'Nothing To Hide'
content: JNU professor, terminated amid a sexual harassment inquiry, has challenged the action and questioned whether due process under the POSH Act was followed. Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, who has been terminated amid a sexual harassment inquiry, has strongly questioned the process followed in his case and invoked the provisions of the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, 2013. Reacting to reports surrounding his termination, the professor said he had not received the inquiry report or the recommendations allegedly made against him. He questioned how any action could have been taken without him being informed about the findings of the committee. - 'President Listened Carefully': Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Meet President Murmu, Submit Memorandum - AAPs Big Guarantees For Goa Ahead Of Polls: Free Electricity And Bus Travel For Women, Rs. 10 Lakh Health Cover - Beyond Jantar Mantar: Ahead Of CJP Stir, SC Asks Centre To Identify Alternative Delhi Protest Venue For Future - Vijay Overcomes First Poll Battle As CM: How TVK's Bypoll Brace Is A Prestige Win I dont have the report. I dont have this dismissal. But Im telling, Im reminding to the rest of the country, POSH Act is not a Chinese Act passed by the National Peoples Congress of Republic of China. This is an Indian law passed by Indian Parliament," he said. The professor argued that the law provides respondents an opportunity to know the findings of an inquiry and respond to them. Anybody who knows POSH law will know this," he said, adding that he expected the authorities to follow the prescribed procedure. He also challenged allegations reportedly linked to sex-for-marks" claims and asked that the allegations be substantiated through the inquiry record. All those allegations of sex-for marks, show me that either in their report or anywhere, show me that. Then only then you will know how this witch hunt has been going on," he said. Calling the developments a blessing in disguise", the professor alleged that he was being subjected to a witch hunt" and said the action would ultimately help expose what he described as irregularities in the process. For me, this is the best thing that could happen to expose the witch hunt. I have nothing to hide if it is true," he said. The professor further said he had taught sexuality and gender issues for decades and maintained that he was not embarrassed by the allegations. Look at my face. Do you think Im embarrassed or something? I have taught sexuality and gender issues for decades, so dont worry," he said. He also alleged that attempts were being made to silence his voice and asserted that he would emerge stronger from the controversy. The termination comes against the backdrop of a sexual harassment inquiry at JNU. The professor has questioned whether due process under the POSH Act was followed before the action was taken. His remarks represent his side of the dispute, while the findings of the inquiry and the universitys position would be necessary to establish the allegations and the procedural details. Jawaharlal Nehru University dismissed the professor from service with immediate effect following a sexual harassment inquiry conducted by the university's Internal Committee. The dismissal order was signed by Vice-Chancellor Santishree D Pandit, citing service rules and Rule 11(ix) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules.

headline: Tamil Nadu bypoll results: TVK bags Madurantakam, Dharapuram seats
content: The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) emerged victorious in the bypolls to the Madurantakam and Dharapuram reserved Assembly constituencies, by considerable margins, after the counting of votes on Friday (October 9, 2026). In Madurantakam, at the end of the final round of counting, TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel had secured 74,048 votes, defeating the DMKs I. Paranthamen, who had polled 54,008 votes. The AIADMKs S. Kanitha Sampath was in third place with 47,450 votes. Keep track: Bypoll results LIVE updates In Dharapuram, the TVKs P. Sathyabama won by securing 66,841 votes; the DMKs S. Suganya polled 57,370 votes and the AIADMKs K. Banumathi, 45,280 votes. The bypolls in the two constituencies were necessitated after Ms. Kumaravel and Ms. Sathyabama, who had won the Madurantakam and Dharapuram seats, respectively, as AIADMK candidates in the 2026 Assembly elections, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK. Held after the TVK came to power in May, the bypolls were seen as a test of the partys popularity, while the opposition AIADMK sought to win back the seats.

headline: 'President Listened Carefully': Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Meet President Murmu, Submit Memorandum
content: INDIA bloc leaders met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum over their allegations against the Election Commission. The INDIA bloc leaders, along with Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo Mamata Banerjee, on Friday met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum over their concerns regarding the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The meeting came after several days of protests by Opposition leaders against the Election Commission, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged irregularities in the electoral process. The Opposition has also been demanding Kumars resignation. - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - Gyanesh Kumars Z+ Security Upgraded Ahead Of October 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 Protest: What Does It Entail Now? - Gyanesh Kumar Resignation Row: Opposition Protest Meets Pushback From Retired Judges | News18 INDIA Bloc Submits Memorandum To President Speaking after the meeting, Mamata Banerjee said the delegation had submitted a memorandum and that the President had assured them that she would examine their concerns. We have submitted a memorandum. We have seen from a positive outlook that she said she will investigate; she will go through the details, and she needs evidence," Banerjee said. She added that the President had asked the Opposition to provide the material supporting its allegations. She has asked us to send, which we said we will. The country is very concerned, and you, as a custodian of the Constitution, should take proper care so the democracy remains," Banerjee said. She further said the President had responded that she would investigate the matter. Rahul Gandhi Says President Did Not Deny Oppositions Claims Rahul Gandhi, speaking after the meeting, said the delegation had raised its concerns directly with President Murmu. I sat in quite an unbelievable meeting. First, we took a memorandum to the President of India. In that memorandum, we clearly stated that the Prime Minister, Home Minister Amit Shah, and CEC Gyanesh Kumar had conspired to destroy Indian democracy," Gandhi said. He claimed that the President neither denied nor disputed the Oppositions statements. The President in no way denied what we said, questioned what we said, or argued what we said. She accepted our statement and then told us that we needed to provide her with proof of election chori," Gandhi said. Gandhi said the Opposition had already maintained that the alleged electoral irregularities were known across the country. I said that the evidence of election chori is known to the entire country. State after state has been stolen. The 2024 election was stolen, and yet the President wants us to submit proof to her," he said. He added that the Opposition would provide the material collected by it when the President was ready to receive it. This same group of people will be very happy to present the evidence of election chori that we have collected to the President of India when she is ready to accept it," Gandhi said. Kharge Raises EVM, Ballot Paper Demand Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Opposition delegation also raised its demand for changes in the electoral process. Leaders from our alliance met the President and submitted a memorandum. We went specifically to apprise the President of the agitation we launched four days ago regarding the theft of votes, and we presented our case fully," Kharge said. He said the delegation highlighted what it described as serious concerns over the functioning of the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. We highlighted the issue of vote theft and the grave error committed by Gyanesh Kumar. We demanded that EVMs be set aside and elections be conducted using ballot papers," Kharge said. Kharge also said the President had asked the Opposition to provide evidence supporting its allegations. Furthermore, she asked for evidence regarding the instances of vote theft; we are currently compiling this evidence and will submit it," he said. According to Kharge, the President assured the delegation that she would examine the matter. We will provide all other relevant information as well. Above all, we addressed the fact that PM Modi and Amit Shah are intent on destroying the countrys democracy and are actively taking steps in that direction. She listened attentively and stated that she would investigate the matter thoroughly, consult the concerned parties, and determine the appropriate course of action," Kharge said. Opposition Steps Up Campaign Against CEC The meeting followed a series of INDIA bloc protests in Delhi demanding action over the electoral roll revision process and the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. The Opposition has also been calling for greater transparency in electoral roll revisions and has backed a return to ballot papers instead of EVMs. The Election Commission, however, has rejected the Oppositions allegations and maintained its position on the electoral process. The political dispute has intensified in recent days, with protests and counterclaims between the Opposition and the ruling side. The INDIA bloc delegation met with President Droupadi Murmu to submit a memorandum regarding their concerns over the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

headline: Subordinate judge vacancies to be filled soon, CJ assures Bar leaders
content: Chief Justice of Madras high court Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari has assured a lawyers delegation that he will ensure that vacancies in the subordinate judiciary are filled quickly, and that infrastructure, including decent toilet facilities for women lawyers, in those courts is put in place.He gave the assurance in response to a charter of demands submitted by a delegation of Federation of Bar Associations of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, led by its honorary chairperson S Parbakaran, chairperson N Marappan and general secretary R Ayyavoo.The demands include immediate appointment of judicial officers in all vacancies in the respective subordinate courts to ensure that the administration of justice proceeds without any backlog, ensuring that members of the Bar are provided with additional chambers and infrastructural facilities such as individual chambers attached to the court premises in subordinate courts.The federation also demanded provision of a legal research database and effective Wi-Fi services within the premises of the courts, including the subordinate courts, and demanded that E-Seva booths or information centres be established to aid the members of the Bar in technological advancements related to the legal profession and administration of justice.Steps may be taken to ensure that training centers are established for the new entrants of the Bar on professional ethics and other judicial exams to enhance their legal knowledge and capability, the representation added.

headline: Boots On Ground: Pakistan Shores Up Presence In Saudi Arabia. Will Munir's Soldiers Attack Iran-Backed Houthis?
content: Pakistan signed defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August. Under this, the three countries committed to coming to one anothers aid if any of them came under attack. Pakistan has a substantial" number of military personnel and resources stationed in Saudi Arabia, but their role is to defend the kingdom and not launch attacks against Yemens Iran-backed Houthis, the countrys Foreign Ministry said on Friday. Foreign Ministry spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan told journalists that Pakistani forces already had a significant presence in Riyadh. However, he did not confirm whether the deployment had increased under a defence agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August. - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - 15,000 Troops, Fighter Jets In Saudi Arabia: Pakistan Confirms Military Deployment Under Mecca Pact - From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia From Pakistan already we have substantial number of forces as well as resources in town, in Riyadh," Khan said. He clarified that Pakistani troops would not cross the border to attack the Houthis, stressing that their responsibility was to protect Saudi territory. Pakistan Rules Out Cross-Border Attacks Khan said Pakistani military personnel stationed in Saudi Arabia would remain focused on defence rather than conducting offensive operations against the Houthis. The spokesman said the troops would not be crossing the borders of the other side for an attack on the Houthis, but of course (is acting) in the defence of the territory". His remarks come as Yemens Houthis have stepped up attacks against Saudi Arabia. The Iran-backed group has launched repeated aerial attacks on Saudi targets, including an assault on Riyadhs international airport on Thursday that killed three people. The attacks have taken place as the conflict between the Houthis and Yemens Saudi-backed government has widened. The Houthis began a lightning offensive just across the border before launching repeated attacks on targets inside Saudi Arabia. What Is The Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey Defence Pact? Pakistan signed a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August. Under the pact, the three countries committed to coming to one anothers aid if any of them came under attack. However, Khan did not specify whether Pakistan had sent additional troops or resources to Saudi Arabia since the conflict intensified. He said decisions on the number of forces to be deployed, as well as the timing and location of their deployment, would be taken by the trilateral alliance. The alliance is headquartered in Riyadh, with a retired Pakistani general serving as its secretary-general. The spokesmans remarks did not establish whether the alliance had decided on any fresh military deployments in response to the Houthi attacks. Pakistans Military Presence In Saudi Arabia Khan also pointed out that Pakistans military presence in Saudi Arabia was not new. Pakistani forces have been deployed in the kingdom regularly since the 1980s, he said. The deployments have continued over the years, including after Islamabad and Riyadh signed a bilateral agreement in 2025. While Pakistan has confirmed that a substantial number of its forces and resources are already in Saudi Arabia, it has not disclosed whether their numbers have increased under the new trilateral defence pact. Khans statement makes clear that Pakistans stated military role in the kingdom is defensive, even as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets continue. The question of any additional deployment remains unanswered, with decisions on future troop movements resting with the three-country alliance. No, Pakistani military personnel stationed in Saudi Arabia will not cross borders to launch offensive operations against the Houthis. Their designated responsibility remains strictly focused on the defense of Saudi territory.

headline: HC directs T.N. to file comprehensive report on disciplinary proceedings initiated against erring government employees
content: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Friday directed the State government to file a comprehensive report on the details regarding the disciplinary proceedings initiated against erring government employees, the status of the proceedings and the action taken. A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan took a serious view of the delay in appointing an inquiry officer to conduct departmental inquiry against erring government officials into the case pertaining to misappropriation of funds sanctioned for the welfare of Adi Dravidar Hostel students in Sivaganga district. The court was hearing the public interest litigation petition filed by A. Sakthivel of Karaikudi in Sivaganga district, who said the petition was filed with regard to the huge scam committed by government officials involving more than 2.35 crore sanctioned for the welfare of the Adi Dravidar Hostel students. The sanctioned amount was for the essential requirements of the students such as hair oil, soap and washing powder. From 2017 to 2023, the amount sanctioned by the government was swindled by the officials and the staff in charge, and no amount had been credited to the accounts of the students, he said. Following complaints lodged by an activist, Boominathan, Sivaganga Town Police had registered a case. It was transferred to Sivaganga District Crime Branch. The investigation revealed that eight Tahsildars were involved in the misappropriation of funds, he said. He said since the persons involved in the crime were revenue officials, and in the rank of Tahsildar, the District Crime Branch was reluctant to proceed with the investigation. He sought a CB-CID probe in the case. The court posted the matter for hearing after four weeks.

headline: Maragatham Kumaravel romps home in Madurantakam, this time on TVK ticket
content: time AIADMK MLA from Madurantakam (SC), retained her seat, contesting this time on a TVK ticket, as the byelection result was declared on Friday. She defeated her nearest rival, I. Paranthamen of the DMK, by a margin of 20,040 votes. Mr. Paranthamen polled 54,008 votes, followed by S. Kanitha Sampath of the AIADMK with 47,450 votes. The byelection was necessitated by Ms. Kumaravels resignation from the Assembly barely three weeks into her second term. She, along with three other AIADMK MLAs, resigned and joined the ruling TVK. Thereafter, two other AIADMK MLAs had resigned and switched over to the TVK. As counting progressed, Ms. Maragatham built up a gradual lead, working up a margin of at least a thousand votes at the end of every round. Halfway into the process, she already had a lead of well over 11,000 votes never looking back thereafter.. She received he winners certificate from Returning Officer K.R. Narendran, Revenue Divisional Officer, Madurantakam, late in the evening. Ms. Maragatham said she quit the AIADMK after she noticed certain elements colluding with the rival DMK after the general election results favoured the TVK. This goes against the principles the party stood for. So, I left, she told reporters. She felt the people have given a suitable answer to the vicious campaign launched against her by the two Dravidian parties surrounding her resignation. She said that some of the long standing demands of people of her constituency had been a government Arts and Science college, an industrial park to provide employment opportunities for the youth, a new Taluk office at Acharapakkam, and a government hospital. My previous term has been as an opposition MLA. This time, I hope I will be able to fulfil these demands, she added. As news of her initial lead tricked out, TVK supporters began gathering outside the counting centre at the Integrated Training Institute for Social Empowerment in Aathur village. With whistles in their mouths, the red-and-gold brigade began celebrations early, chanting slogans in support of their thalapathy (Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay) and the winning candidate. While the crowd kept swelling outside, inside, the counting process was by and large incident free, except for one occasion when opposition counting agents raised concern over a broken seal of an EVM machine. Counting was held up for a few minutes due to the melee inside. In all, there were objections raised over six EVM machines while five others were randomly chosen for VVPAT verification, as per the norms. Cheguvaradas and K. Vanitha, counting agents for CPI(M) candidate P. Suganthi, said that during the tenth round of counting, the agents noticed a broken seal and missing tags when an EVM machine was brought to table number 7 for counting. When the opposition agents raised objections to it, the EVM was removed from the table. The officials did not heed our objections, neither did they respond to our queries, the agents said. Gunasekaran, counting agent for the DMK candidate I. Paranthamen, said: In response to our objections, the Returning Officer only said that he will let us know later. Meanwhile, independent candidate G. Moorthy was forced out of the counting centre twice by the CAPF and Tamil Nadu police. On both occasions, he said he protested against violation of procedures laid by the Election Commission of India by the officials. Chengalpattu Collector and District Election Officer M. Veerappan clarified that the EVMs had the internal seal put on them by the Presiding Officer of the polling station, though the external seal was missing. Engineers from Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) should have placed the seal, Dr. Veerappan added. In another machine, the close button wasnt pressed by the Presiding Officer. All the four machines were subjected to VVPAT scrutiny after the counting was completed, he added. D. Sarathkumar, Minister for Human Resource Management, Pallavaram MLA J. Kamakshi, and Chengalpet MLA S. Thyagarajan accompanied Ms. Kumaravel to the counting centre for receiving the winners certificate from the Returning Officer.

headline: No surprises in byelection results in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry as voters favour the ruling party candidates
content: The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which came to power in Tamil Nadu exactly five months ago, passed its first electoral test in Tamil Nadu on Friday (October 9, 2026), bagging the Madurantakam and Dharapuram (Reserved) Assembly constituencies. In Puducherry, the ruling All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) retained Thattanchavady. Both in Madurantakam and Dharapuram, TVK nominees Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama were elected with comfortable margins of 20,040 votes and 9,471 votes respectively. They won from these constituencies in April-May 2026 as AIADMK candidates and then defected to the ruling party after resigning as MLAs. AIADMK placed third This time, they defeated the nearest rivals, I. Paranthamen and S. Suganya, both of the DMK. S. Kanitha Sampath and K. Banumathi of the AIADMK finished third. The candidates put up by the CPI and the CPI(Marxist) in Dharapuram and Madurantakam, as part of the Left bloc, fared miserably; so did the nominees of the Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK). All the four contestants forfeited their deposits. The NTK, which came fourth in both constituencies, secured 2.92% and 1.46% of the votes polled, while the CPI got about 0.6% in Dharapuram and the CPI(M) 1.07% in Madurantakam. With the victory in the two constituencies, the TVKs strength in the Assembly rose to 108, excluding the Speaker. Five seats are still vacant. The State is known for favouring the party in power in byelections. However, the Madurantakam and Dharapuram byelections, held in five months of the TVK capturing power, were watched closely. Leaders of the three major contenders were deeply involved in the campaign. TVK president and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay campaigned two days each in the two constituencies, as it was done by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami. As for the principal Opposition DMK, its leader M.K.Stalin, former Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin, and Thoothukudi MP Kanimozhi Rajathi Karunanidhi canvassed votes for the party nominees. Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran and Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant campaigned for the nominees of the AIADMK and the DMK respectively. While the TVK saw the byelections as a chance for popular endorsement of its rule, the DMK accused the ruling party of being immature in the manner in which it had been conducting the administration and the AIADMK, alluding to its former members fielded by the ruling party, called upon the electors to reject the traitors. In Thattanchavady, the AINRCs Ashok Anand outsmarted his immediate challenger, E. Vinayagam of the Congress, by 8,482 votes, almost double the margin recorded by Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy in the April Assembly election. As the Chief Minister was also elected from Mangalam and chose to retain it, the vacancy arose in Thattanchavady. This time, Mr. Anand netted 13,358 votes and Mr. Vinayagam polled 4,876 votes. The AINRC is being supported by the BJP and the AIADMK, whereas the Congress is being backed by the TVK. Tamil Nadu Minister for Public Works Adhav Arjuna spoke at an indoor meeting there. The DMK, the CPI, the NTK, and six other contestants forfeited their deposits.

headline: Almost 75% of buildings in Gaza damaged or destroyed since October 7, 2023: An Analysis
content: On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), which marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, Israel carried out new strikes in Gaza killing at least three people. Just four days before, an airstrike on an apartment building in Gaza killed five, including four women. Since October 7, 2023, Israel's total siege on Gaza has killed around 74,200 Palestinians, with about 60% of the Strip directly under the control of the Israeli military. As many as 2,45,981 buildings, which amounts to 74.5% of all buildings before the fateful day of October 7, 2023, are likely to have been damaged or destroyed, according to a satellite radar-driven structural analysis by Conflict Ecology a geospatial research lab at Oregon State University, led by Associate Professor of Geography Jamon Van Den Hoek. The analysis was conducted using satellite data from October 7, 2023 until August 3, 2026, and composed of a 12-day period of observations based on 258 Sentinel-1 radar images alongside building footprint data. The graphic below shows the damage received to buildings. If the infographic isnt visible or is incomplete, click here to exit AMP mode. The map below also shows the damage received only in the 12-day period of observation. Densely populated areas have been damaged repeatedly in the 34 months of observation. If the infographic isnt visible or is incomplete, click here to exit AMP mode. Since the U.S.-brokered ceasefire came into effect in 2025, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has killed over 1,460 Palestinians in Gaza, as per the Gaza Health Ministry. Additionally, the IDF has been destroying more buildings in the territory it controls ever since the ceasefire. Conflict Ecologys analysis shows that a total of 25,801 buildings were detected to be destroyed or damaged in the Israeli-held side of the Yellow Line (shown in the graphic below) - a demarcation line created since the October 2025 ceasefire, with almost 53% of Gaza controlled by Israel. In the rest of the Strip, the 7,643 buildings received new damage or were destroyed. Northernmost Governorates of North Gaza and Gaza have been decimated the most, with 87% of the buildings either damaged or destroyed. Densely populated areas like Gaza City, Jabalia refugee camp, and more, come under these two governorates. The scale of destruction in Gaza has been widely documented in the last three years. The graphic below offers just a snippet into how neighbourhoods have been entirely razed by the Israeli military. Apart from the first few weeks of the war, the intensity of Israeli attacks increased in different neighbourhoods thereby, damaging or destroying buildings previously undamaged in May 2024, and in the months of January, June, and July in 2025. Additionally, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs situation report from September 30, 2026 mentions that: - 92% of assessed establishments in the commerce and industry sector are destroyed or damaged. - 74% of the road network is destroyed and 13% is damaged. - 88% of above-ground Water, Sanitation, and Health assets are damaged. 76% of underground networks of the same are damaged. - 83% of the Gaza Strips coastal zone is fully or partially destroyed. - 76% of assessed cultural and heritage sites are destroyed or damaged. - 90% of energy infrastructure including electricity distribution network and associated assets are destroyed. - 82% of all structures are destroyed or damaged.

headline: Admitting 'instances of bulk Form 7 filing for voter deletion', EC sets limit
content: Noting that instances of filing of bulk Form 7s had led to avoidable inconvenience to voters, the Election Commission of India (ECI) Friday tightened limits on the number of applications that can be submitted by individuals. Form 7 is the statutory form to seek deletion of an elector or file objection to the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll. In instructions issued to Chief Electoral Officers of all states and Union Territories, the ECI has put a limit of 10 Form 7s per individual, in both online and offline mode, during the claims and objections period of the revision process, and five per month during continuous updation of electoral rolls in the normal course. While the ECI already caps the number of online Form 7s an individual can file to six at a time, there was no limit on the number of Form 7s that an individual could submit physically to Electoral Registration Officers (EROs). The commission has been facing flak over reports of targeted bulk Form 7 submissions, and in its instructions Friday, the EC referred to the same. instances have been brought to the notice of the Commission of filing of Form 7 objections in bulk by individual electors on unsubstantiated grounds, resulting in avoidable inconvenience to the elector objected upon and increased workload on field-level functionaries, it said. In recent days, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has alleged that BJP workers had been given pre-printed Form 7 applications to seek deletion of voters in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). An FIR was registered against BJP workers in the state in connection with the same. The ECI letter Friday said: Although the number of applications to be filed online by an individual elector has been fixed as 6 at a time subject to disposal, the number of physical forms presented in bulk has not been defined and has been left to the judgement of the EROs, which is creating challenges for the field functionaries. Accordingly, the Commission with the intent to discourage bulk filing of objections by an individual elector has decided to prescribe [limits] on filing of Form 7 applications in both online and offline mode. Now, individuals can file 10 Form 7s in both online and offline mode during the entire period of claims and objections, which is usually for one month following the publication of a draft roll during an exercise like the Special Summary Revision or SIR. When the revision process is not underway and the electoral rolls are in continuous updation, individuals can file a maximum five Form 7s per month, the ECI said. According to Rule 13 (2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, any objection to a name proposed to be included in the electoral roll or application for deletion of a name on the roll can only be through Form 7, and only an individual who is registered to vote in the same Assembly constituency can submit one. Apart from individual electors, Booth Level Agents (BLAs) appointed by recognised political parties can also file forms for claims and objections. For the SIR, the ECI had allowed BLAs, who are also required to be registered as voters in the same constituency, to file up to 50 forms per day with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) in the period before the publication of the draft roll and 10 forms per day after that. In its letter, the ECI reiterated the provisions of the Registration of Electors Rules, saying EROs are to issue a notice to the objector, hear the objector personally and record statements separately for each Form 7. Once an ERO is satisfied about the validity of the objections, the person objected to has to be given the opportunity of a hearing before the ERO passes an order. It may also be ensured that in case the ERO finds that the complaint is false / fabricated, he shall proceed to take action against the applicant who has knowingly made a false statement or declaration in writing in the Form 7 as per the provisions of Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. The Chief Electoral Officers are requested to bring the above to the notice of all concerned EROs / AEROs and other field-level functionaries for necessary compliance and also sufficient publicity be given to these instructions, the ECI said. Since the SIR started, political parties across states, including Jharkhand, Odisha and Telangana besides Karnataka, have levelled charges at rivals of filing bulk Form 7s to target voters. In September, the Biju Janata Dal took up the issue with the Odisha Chief Electoral Officer, after 10 Booth Level Officers appointed by the ECI filed a police complaint that Form 7s were being uploaded in their names without their knowledge. The EC had then taken action and removed the Assistant ERO concerned for allegedly using the BLOs log-in credentials to submit the bulk forms.

headline: ICC rejects U.S. sanctions, says 'history will judge this moment'
content: The International Criminal Court said Friday (October 9, 2026) that U.S. sanctions on the institution were an attack on international law and warned that "history will judge this moment". The sanctions are "an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order which strikes at the simple principle that no one stands above the law", said the court in a statement.
