U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said earlier Friday (October 9, 2026) that Washington would ban transactions with what he called a "rogue court," escalating a long-running campaign by President Donald Trump's administration against the court. The court said such actions were aimed at intimidating ICC staff and disrupting its activities, vowing it would not be deterred. "The Court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes," said ICC President Tomoko Akane in the statement. The statement called on the ICC's 125 members to side with the institution, saying: "Its fate now rests also in the hands of the states that created it." "Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an institution created to protect them came under attack," said the court.

headline: Madras HC asks DVAC not to harass ex-minister E V Velu till Oct 15
content: Madras high court on Friday instructed Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) not to harass till Oct 15 former minister and DMK MLA E V Velu and his son E V Kumaran in connection with a case registered against them for causing a 8.22 crore loss to govt by illegally excavating soil from a lake for a DMK youth wing conference in Tiruvannamalai. Justice V Lakshminarayanan was hearing the anticipatory bail applications moved by Velu and Kumaran.When the pleas came up for hearing, state public prosecutor John Sathyan sought time to file a counter to the applications. The judge said, If the matter is adjourned at the instance of the prosecutor, you must not harass the petitioners until then, and adjourned the hearing to Oct 15.On Dec 14, DMKs north zone youth wing conference was held in Tiruvannamalai. To level the conference venue, soil was allegedly illegally excavated from the nearby Malappambadi lake, covering an area of 12 acres and a depth ranging from 10ft to 23ft, causing a 8 crore loss to govt.Representing Velu, 76, advocate Rahul Balaji submitted that the case, registered on Sept 24, was based on a complaint filed by anti-corruption NGO Arappor Iyakkam on Aug 13, nearly 10 months after the alleged events in Nov and Dec 2025.The FIR did not cite order, instruction, communication, payment or other act linking him to the alleged excavation. The conclusion that he might have facilitated the alleged offence was based on his relationship with his son, Kumaran, a director of the company that owns the land, he said.

headline: AAP's Big Guarantees For Goa Ahead Of Polls: Free Electricity And Bus Travel For Women, Rs 10 Lakh Health Cover
content: Kejriwal said the AAP governments in Delhi and Punjab had introduced the facility and promised to extend it to Goa if the party came to power. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday announced six guarantees for Goa, promising 300 units of free electricity every month, a waiver of pending electricity bills, Rs. 3,000 monthly assistance for every woman and free bus travel for women if the party forms the government in the state. Addressing a public meeting in Panaji during his three-day visit to Goa, Kejriwal also promised Rs. 10 lakh in health insurance for every family, sports grounds in every village and ward, and local manifestos at the booth level to address problems in each area. - Beyond Jantar Mantar: Ahead Of CJP Stir, SC Asks Centre To Identify Alternative Delhi Protest Venue For Future - Vijay Overcomes First Poll Battle As CM: How TVK's Bypoll Brace Is A Prestige Win - 'My Friends And I Want Vada Pav Back': Tukaram Mundhe's Heartwarming Response To Kid Goes Viral - CJP Protest October 10: Mobile Internet Suspended Within 4 Km Radius Of Kartavya Path From 10 PM Tonight This is Kejriwals guarantee, and it never breaks," he said, asserting that the AAP had fulfilled its election promises in Delhi and Punjab and would do the same in Goa. Kejriwal Targets BJP, Congress Kejriwal said people in Goa were looking for a change after becoming dissatisfied with both the BJP and Congress. He alleged that Congress MLAs joined the BJP after winning elections, resulting in a government led by the party voters had opposed. Therefore, voting for the Congress means forming a BJP government. There is no benefit in doing so," he said. He also accused the BJP of corruption and blamed it for broken roads, water shortages and prolonged power cuts. Kejriwal claimed that high electricity bills had added to the difficulties faced by people, making them look towards the AAP for relief. Arvind Kejriwal announced six guarantees for Goa, including 300 units of free electricity monthly. The guarantees also include a waiver of pending electricity bills and Rs. 3,000 monthly assistance for every woman. Kejriwal promised free bus travel for women and Rs. 10 lakh in health insurance for every family. Sports grounds in every village and ward, and local manifestos at the booth level were also promised. Kejriwal stated that all old electricity bills would be reduced to zero within a week of the AAP government taking office. 300 Units Of Free Electricity Under the first guarantee, Kejriwal promised 300 units of free electricity per household every month, a waiver of all pending electricity bills and arrangements for a 24-hour power supply. He alleged that some households in Goa were receiving bills ranging from Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 1 lakh or more. According to him, residents who approached officials to correct their bills were asked to pay first, while penalties and interest continued to accumulate. Kejriwal said all old electricity bills would be reduced to zero within a week of the AAP government taking office. From April onwards, households would receive 300 units of free electricity every month. He said the party had implemented its free electricity guarantee in Delhi and Punjab and promised to introduce the same in Goa. Free Bus Travel And Rs. 3,000 For Every Woman The second guarantee is free bus travel for women. Kejriwal said the AAP governments in Delhi and Punjab had introduced the facility and promised to extend it to Goa if the party came to power. Under the fourth guarantee, every woman above the age of 18 would receive 3,000 a month directly in her bank account. Kejriwal criticised Goas Griha Aadhar Scheme, claiming its conditions prevented many women from receiving benefits. He said the proposed AAP scheme would cover women across income groups and communities, including mothers, wives, sisters and daughters from the same family. Rs. 10 Lakh Health Insurance The third guarantee is health insurance worth Rs. 10 lakh for every family. Kejriwal criticised the condition of treatment at Goa Medical College (GMC), alleging that patients faced poor services, malfunctioning machines and long waits for operations. He said families turning to private hospitals faced bills running into lakhs of rupees. Citing Punjabs health insurance scheme, he promised free treatment worth up to Rs. 10 lakh annually at private hospitals, including coverage for medicines, tests and hospitalisation. Kejriwal also criticised the Pramod Sawant-led BJP governments Deen Dayal Swasthya Seva Yojana (DDSSY). He cited an example shared by a woman at a booth meeting, whose family allegedly received only Rs. 25,000 under the scheme towards a Rs. 2.5 lakh operation, leaving them to pay the remaining Rs. 2.25 lakh. Sports Grounds And Local Manifestos The fifth guarantee is to develop a sports ground in every village and ward. Kejriwal said children in Goa had a strong interest in sports and represented the state at national and international levels, but lacked proper facilities. He cited Punjab as an example, saying the AAP government had built sports grounds with facilities for football, cricket and volleyball and provided the necessary equipment. He promised to follow the same model in Goa. Under the sixth guarantee, AAP workers would visit streets and neighbourhoods to prepare local manifestos at ward and booth levels. These would document problems faced by residents, from minor issues to major concerns. Kejriwal said AAP candidates, once elected as MLAs, would work to resolve the listed problems. He concluded by urging voters to choose the AAP, arguing that the party would deliver free electricity, health insurance, free bus travel for women and other promised benefits if it formed the government in Goa. Arvind Kejriwal announced six key guarantees for Goa, which include 300 units of free electricity every month with pending bills waived, free bus travel for women, a monthly financial assistance of Rs. 3,000 for women over 18, and Rs. 10 lakh in health insurance per family. Additionally, the party promised to build sports grounds in every village and ward and create local manifestos at the booth level to address specific area problems.

headline: Republican vs Democrat: Argument over Trump's role in Iran war turns dangerous, one shot in Ohio dog park
content: Political disagreement over US President Donald Trump at a dog park in Ohio took a violent turn. It happened at Bainbridge Township, when an altercation broke out between two men, both of whom had guns in their cars, according to a report by The New York Times. All of this took place while both men were out with their pet dogs at a dog park. The incident began with a conversation about the presidents decision and resulted in criminal cases against both men. Reportedly, one of them is now facing possible jail time. According to The New York Times, the argument went on for about 20 minutes. The incident dates back to April when David Mattai, 55, arrived at the dog park with his spaniel, Bob. Mattai, who worked as a forklift mechanic, reportedly had the week off from work. It is believed that he ended up in the dog park after he tried taking his dog on a hiking trail, but failed. As a result, Mattai drove to the park in Bainbridge Township, northeast Ohio. At the park, Mattai met Emmanuel Mathews. The 80-year-old Mathews was a retired meat distributor who was said to be a regular at the dog park with his corgi, Frankie. Mathews, alias Mike, was believed to be sitting at a picnic table with a copy of The Wall Street Journal whose headline read, Trump Grapples With Fears on War, added the report. Amid this, Jamie Jedlinsky, 70, who was at the park with his pit mix, Willow, unknowingly became the eyewitness of the confrontation. The New York Times reported that Jedlinsky had become somewhat friendly with Mathews over the years. Upon noticing the newspaper, he gestured towards the headline about the Iran war and remarked, That sucks, dont it. However, Mathews disagreed. As a supporter of Trump, Mathews reportedly began defending the President's decisions. Mattai, who had arrived shortly before the exchange, was listening to their conversation. Mattai reportedly considered himself a democratic socialist and had a collection of political bumper stickers which read, Trump Is a Felon and Hicks Dont Mix With Politics. In the predominantly Republican area of northeast Ohio where he lived, he considered it his moral duty to comfort the afflicted and afflict the comfortable, reported The New York Times. The political disagreement between the two men subsequently escalated into an argument and turned into a shouting match. Both men carried firearms in their cars, and the simple confrontation became a criminal matter. Citing details from the confrontation through interviews, records and body-camera footage, the report said that both men face the possibility of imprisonment. Jedlinsky is likely to testify in both cases as a key witness in the matter. The report described him as someone who generally avoided discussing politics as advised by his mother. Reportedly, Mattai struggled with alcoholism in his life and would later say that he was drinking on the day of the incident. According to cleveland19, Emmanuel John Matthews shot David Mattai in the back while he attempted to leave the dog park. Later, the matter reached Chardon Municipal Court, where Matthews pleaded not guilty on April 22 and posted bond, as per the news outlet. It is reported that the victim went through multiple surgeries after the shooting incident. He (Mattai) saw the guys gun. He did not reach for his. He had the door open and was trying to get Bob situated when the man shot him in the back. At that point, he did fall, but reached in and grabbed his weapon and returned fire at the mans car, said Sally Mattai, the victims wife. The defence attorney reportedly claimed that Matthews was in danger and acted in self-defence. Bainbridge Township Officer Friedrich Kaufmann testified in court. Later, the case was transferred to Geauga County Common Pleas Court. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: Delhi liquor shops open or closed tomorrow? Check government order amid CJP's Jantar Mantar protest call against CEC
content: Delhi's retail liquor shops will remain closed on Saturday, October 10, following a government order issued as a preventive measure amid heightened political activity and a planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The order mandates the shutdown of all retail liquor outlets in Delhi on October 9 and 10. An official circular said the measure was prompted by the prevailing situation and information shared by Delhi Police. "In view of the prevailing situation and inputs received from Delhi Police, as a preventive measure aimed at maintaining public order, it is hereby ordered that all retail liquor vends with licenses in Form L6, L6 & L6FG, L8, L10 and L8 & L14 operating in Delhi will be completely closed on 09.10.2026 and 10.10.2026," the circular stated, according to ANI. Quick answers to key questions 1Will liquor shops in Delhi be open on October 10? No. Delhis retail liquor shops are ordered to remain closed on Saturday, October 10, 2026. 2Why are Delhi liquor shops closed on October 9 and 10? The government issued the closure order as a preventive measure to maintain public order, citing the prevailing situation and inputs from Delhi Police amid planned protests. 3Which liquor outlets are covered by Delhis closure order? The order covers retail liquor vends in Delhi operating under the licence categories listed in the circular: L6, L6FG, L8, L10 and L14, including the combinations specified. 4For how long will Delhis retail liquor shops remain closed? The order requires covered retail liquor outlets to remain closed on both October 9 and October 10, 2026. The closure also comes against the backdrop of INDIA bloc demonstrations over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with Opposition leaders also demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On Thursday, as the protest campaign entered its third consecutive day, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Raj Ghat to pay homage to Mahatma Gandhi. Congress General Secretary (Organisation) KC Venugopal called the agitation "one of the most powerful" protests and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of "finishing" democracy through Gyanesh Kumar. Earlier, INDIA bloc leaders tried to march to the Election Commission's headquarters on Tuesday before holding a demonstration near Jantar Mantar the following day. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several other Opposition leaders were detained during Wednesday's protest. Delhi Police have filed three FIRs relating to the demonstration, citing alleged offences that include assault on police personnel, obstruction of government work, pushing, manhandling and misbehaviour with police officers. The FIR details released so far also mention Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The CJP has scheduled a youth-led demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, raising allegations of "vote theft", the purported exclusion of young voters from electoral rolls and other issues concerning the Election Commission. CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had notified Delhi Police about the planned gathering and completed the necessary formalities. According to him, young participants from different parts of the country are expected to attend. However, the Delhi Police have refused permission for the CJP's proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. Following the decision, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has instructed police chiefs across all states and Union Territories to ensure law and order and tighten security arrangements. In an official communication, Mohan asked states and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police and take preventive steps ahead of the proposed mobilisation. The letter flagged concerns that CJP members and supporters might attempt to enter the national capital despite the denial of permission. (With inputs from agency)

headline: Beyond Jantar Mantar: Ahead Of CJP Stir, SC Asks Centre To Identify Alternative Delhi Protest Venue For Future
content: Chief Justice Surya Kant pointed out that demonstrators at Jantar Mantar frequently face severe inconvenience due to a lack of proper sanitation infrastructure The Supreme Court has asked the central government to consider designating an alternative venue for peaceful demonstrations in the national capital, noting that the long-standing protest site at Jantar Mantar lacks adequate basic facilities. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant recorded that it is high time competent authorities identify a new location equipped with essential civic amenities for citizens exercising their right to assemble peacefully. The observation came during an emergency hearing regarding transit restrictions implemented across Delhi ahead of planned demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on October 10. The court emphasised that while law enforcement agencies must maintain public order, designated assembly spaces should support basic human dignity rather than causing hardship to both protesters and local residents. - 'Every Woman Should Feel Safe, Even At 10 PM': Supreme Court's Tough Talk On Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR - 'Create Fear In The Minds Of Culprits': SC's 5 Big Observations On Women's Safety In Delhi - 'Have To Draw A Line Somewhere': On Leniency To Death Row Convicts, SC Says 'Forgiving Nature Must End' - 'Will Examine, Take A Call': CJI Surya Kant Says SC To Soon Decide On Plea To Recall CEC Law Order Lack of Civic Amenities and Nearby Residential Strain Highlighting the practical difficulties associated with the current arrangement, Chief Justice Surya Kant pointed out that demonstrators at Jantar Mantar frequently face severe inconvenience due to a lack of proper sanitation infrastructure, including public toilets. The bench observed that the narrow stretch, situated in close proximity to government quarters and residences allotted to Members of Parliament, creates administrative bottlenecks and restricts access for both residents and visitors. Echoing these concerns, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submitted that the location presents significant logistical challenges for emergency medical services. In the event of a medical emergency during a large gathering, ambulances face extreme difficulty navigating the congested access roads, posing safety risks to participants. Government Agrees to Review Assembly Locations In response to the top courts directions, the central government confirmed that the competent authority will examine the suggestion and consider identifying a more suitable, purpose-built protest site. The proposed alternative is expected to offer better spatial capacity, dedicated medical access, and proper sanitation infrastructure. The Supreme Court asked the central government to consider an alternative venue for peaceful demonstrations in the national capital. Chief Justice Surya Kant noted that Jantar Mantar lacks adequate basic facilities like public toilets. The court observed that the current location creates administrative bottlenecks and restricts access for residents and visitors. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta stated that the location presents logistical challenges for emergency medical services. The central government confirmed it will examine the suggestion and consider identifying a more suitable protest site. The Supreme Court clarified that its focus remains on balancing public order, civic mobility, and fundamental rights. By directing authorities to evaluate a fresh location, the judiciary aims to establish an arrangement that accommodates peaceful public expression while preventing citywide transit gridlock and localised disruptions in central Delhi. The Supreme Court noted that the long-standing protest site at Jantar Mantar lacks adequate basic facilities like public toilets and creates administrative bottlenecks, traffic congestion, and logistical challenges for emergency medical services.

headline: Delayed power meter readings persist across Chennai despite TNPDCL instructions
content: Complaints about delayed meter readings to assess electricity consumption continue to pour in from across the city and suburbs, despite repeated instructions from Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL) to field officers to ensure prompt assessment.Roy Rosario of Pattabiram said the assessor for his neighbourhood did not turn up for five days after the scheduled assessment period. The reading should have been taken on Oct 5, he said. Rosario said this will cause consumption to jump into higher tariff slabs and consumers to lose the benefit of 200 free units if they cross 500 units in a bi-monthly period.P Bharathi of Porur said that his electricity consumption was not assessed for two subsequent cycles. The last assessment was done in June. In Aug, we did not get a bill, and the Oct assessment is due. It is unfair on the part of TNPDCL, he said. Niranjan Kumar of Mehta Nagar said his neighbourhood faced similar problems till last month. After we raised a complaint, a woman staffer has been temporarily posted to cover our area, but we are not sure how long she will continue, he said.It may be noted that TNPDCL carried out the exercise of reassessing power bills that were abnormally high last month and detected wrong assessments in about 2,000 services across the state. Though TNPDCL justified the discrepancies considering they had to assess 1.3 crore meters at households in a month, it later decided to outsource the meter reading to private contractors citing a shortage of assessors.However, officials said that tenders are yet to be floated in many areas. We have told field officers to carry out the exercise, but it may take at least a month before contractors are engaged. Meanwhile, we have instructed them to ensure prompt assessment, said a senior official.

headline: Gyanesh Kumar's Z+ Security Upgraded Ahead Of October 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 Protest: What Does It Entail Now?
content: Security outside to his homes to personal detail, what does the upgrade mean ahead of October 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 protest by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)? News18 explains The security cover for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar has been upgraded following a fresh threat perception assessment driven by escalating street protests and direct targeting of his private residences by opposition political groups. What does the upgrade mean ahead of protests, including October 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 call by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)? News18 explains. - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - From Streets To Supreme Court: CEC Gyanesh Kumar Faces The Heat | Brass Tacks With Nabila Jamal - CEC Gyanesh Kumars Z+ Security Beefed Up: CISF Adds Additional Reserve Personnel Amid SIR Protests - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC WHY THE SECURITY UPGRADE The primary factors leading to this security enhancement include: Security agencies reassessed the threat level after protesters successfully tracked down and demonstrated outside Kumars official residence in New Moti Bagh, New Delhi, with some attempting to breach the premises. Additionally, demonstrations targeted his family home in Agra, where his elderly parents reside, resulting in the defacement of property. The opposition INDIA bloc led by prominent figures like Rahul Gandhiand other political groups like the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have launched intense agitations. They are demanding Kumars resignation over allegations of vote chori" (vote theft) and irregularities tied to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, say reports. JANTAR MANTAR 2.0: THE OCTOBER 10 PROTEST Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's security cover has been upgraded following a fresh threat perception assessment. Protesters demonstrated outside Kumar's official residence in New Moti Bagh, New Delhi, and his family home in Agra. The October 10 protest, dubbed Jantar Mantar 2.0, demands the immediate resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The Delhi Police has denied official permission for the October 10 gathering and enforced prohibitory orders. The Ministry of Home Affairs deployed 23,000 paramilitary and central force personnel to secure the capital for the protest. The October 10 protest, dubbed Jantar Mantar 2.0, is a massive nationwide political mobilisation demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration is being organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), prominent student organizations like the All India Students Association (AISA), and actively supported by MPs from the opposition INDIA bloc. The agitation centres around intense political backlash over the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The CEC is also accused of unilaterally making key alterations to Form 6 (the primary document used to register as a voter) while bypassing the input of his fellow Election Commissioners. Current Situation and Security Lockdown The protest has turned central Delhi into a high-security zone: No Police Permission: The Delhi Police has denied official permission for the gathering, enforcing strict prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS (which bans unlawful assemblies). Massive Security Grid: Despite the lack of permission, organizers have vowed to march, prompting the Ministry of Home Affairs to deploy 23,000 paramilitary and central force personnel to seal off borders and secure the capital. Pre-emptive Measures: The Delhi Police has put over 2,800 individuals with past criminal track records on an active radar using Facial Recognition System (FRS) data to prevent any repeats of past street violence. Authorities have also requested the temporary closure of dozens of metro stations and liquor shops to control crowd movements. The demonstration follows similar high-profile mobilisations spearheaded by the CJP, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, and actor Prakash Raj in Mumbai and Bengaluru. WHAT DOES GYANESH KUMARS SECURITY INCLUDE? Kumar is protected under the Z+ security category, which is the countrys second-highest level of civilian protection. The recent upgrade" is not a transition to a new security tier; instead, it is a beefing up of the existing Z+ cover using additional tactical reserve personnel. What the Z+ Security Cover Includes A standard Z+ security cover provides a comprehensive, multi-layered protection protocol: Personnel Strength: It involves a rotating detail of over 55 armed security personnel working in shifts. Commandos & Personal Security: This includes a dedicated close-protection team, round-the-clock Personal Security Officers (PSOs), and highly trained commandos from the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). Mobile Protection: A dedicated vehicle cavalcade escorting him during all transit and public movements. What Does the Recent Upgrade Add? Following the fresh threat assessment, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the CISF mobilized standby reserve units to heavily fortify specific weak points: Delhi Residence (New Moti Bagh): Mobilisation of additional paramilitary staff and positioning of static police vans round-the-clock; enforced strict access control where any visitor must state their purpose and provide identification; outer perimeter sweeps conducted by roaming commandos. Family Home in Agra: Stationing of additional state and central forces to guard his elderly parents following the recent property defacement. EC Headquarters (Nirvachan Sadan): Reinforcement of inner security points handled by the CISF; strategic deployment of external defensive cordons composed of the Rapid Action Force (RAF), the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), and the Delhi Police. Personal Security Detail: Increasing the number of active, on-field close-protection commandos directly flanking Kumar during his day-to-day movements, say reports. With agency inputs Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's security was upgraded following a fresh threat perception assessment triggered by escalating street protests, direct targeting of his official Delhi residence, and the defacement of his family home in Agra by opposition groups.

headline: CJP October 10 Delhi protest news: Here's the full list of metro stations closed in Delhi ahead of protest against CEC
content: Trisha Bhattacharya The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) announced that entry and exit gates at 57 stations would remain closed from 9 PM on 9 October 2026, and throughout 10 October until further notice, citing security reasons. Interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except the New Delhi Metro station. In its service update posted on X, the DMRC said interchange facilities would remain available at all the affected stations, except New Delhi Metro station. This means passengers may still be able to change lines at the listed stations, but they will not be able to enter or exit through the affected stations while the restrictions are in force. Quick answers to key questions 1When do the Delhi Metro station entry and exit restrictions start on October 10? DMRC said entry and exit gates at 57 stations would close from 9 PM on October 9 and remain closed throughout October 10 until further notice. 2Which major Delhi Metro stations are affected by the October 10 restrictions? Affected stations include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Kashmere Gate, Mandi House and New Delhi. The restrictions cover 57 stations across several parts of Delhi. 3Will Delhi Metro trains stop running completely during the CJP protest? No complete suspension of Metro train movement was ordered. The Supreme Court said services should be regulated rather than brought to a complete halt. 4Can passengers change Metro lines at stations with closed entry and exit gates? Interchange facilities will remain available at affected stations, except New Delhi Metro station. Passengers will not be able to enter or exit through the restricted stations. 5Why are Delhi Metro station gates being closed ahead of the CJP protest? The restrictions were announced as a preventive security measure. Delhi Police cited concerns about crowds gathering near stations and moving towards the protest venue or other sensitive locations. The restrictions cover major interchange points, busy commercial areas and stations in several parts of the capital. The full list of affected stations is as follows: Central Delhi and key interchange stations: Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Lok Kalyan Marg, Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Seva Teerth (Udyog Bhawan), Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, ITO, Delhi Gate, Khan Market, R.K. Ashram Marg, Jhandewalan, Supreme Court, Indraprastha and Shivaji Stadium. South Delhi and adjoining areas: INA, Hauz Khas, Jor Bagh, Arjangarh, Sarai Kale KhanNizamuddin, Lajpat Nagar, Jangpura, Ashram, Kalindi Kunj, Jasola, Jamia Millia Islamia and Okhla Vihar. North and north-west Delhi: Chawri Bazar, Jama Masjid, Karol Bagh, Rajendra Place, Vishwavidyalaya, Vidhan Sabha, Civil Lines, Kashmere Gate, Inderlok, G.T.B. Nagar, Kanhaiya Nagar, Netaji Subhash Place, Azadpur, Adarsh Nagar, Jahangir Puri, Haiderpur Badli Mor, Majlis Park, Shalimar Bagh, Rithala, Rohini East and Rohini West. East and north-east Delhi: Seelampur, Maujpur, Jafrabad, Welcome, Yamuna Vihar, Khazuri Khas and Shahdara. Passengers should pay particular attention to the restrictions at Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Kashmere Gate, Mandi House and New Delhi, which are important points for changing lines or accessing central Delhi. Those travelling to railway stations or government offices should check their routes in advance and consider alternative access points where available. The restrictions follow a request from Delhi Police, which cited the possibility of large crowds moving towards sensitive locations during the proposed demonstration. The restrictions come ahead of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other groups at Jantar Mantar on 10 October. The demonstrators are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police sought the closure of the stations as a preventive measure, citing concerns about crowd mobilisation, unlawful gatherings and possible movement towards sensitive locations. The proposed restrictions span several parts of the capital, rather than being limited to the area around Jantar Mantar. However, the Supreme Court on Friday, 9 October, expressed concern about the impact on ordinary commuters. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said that maintaining law and order could not mean bringing public transport to a complete halt. The court made it clear that there should be no complete prohibition on the movement of Metro trains. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured the Bench that the authorities would be asked to reconsider the restrictions and allow Metro and railway services to operate in a regulated manner. The closures appear to be a preventive security measure ahead of Saturdays demonstration, which has been called over concerns about electoral-roll revisions and demands for accountability from the Election Commission. Police are concerned that protesters could gather near station entrances before moving towards the protest venue or other sensitive locations. The DMRCs announcement concerns entry and exit access at the listed stations; it should not be interpreted as confirmation that all Metro train services will stop. The Supreme Courts intervention reinforces the distinction between restricting access at selected stations and suspending the Metro network altogether. For passengers, the practical effect could still be significant, particularly for those travelling through central Delhi or relying on interchange stations. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: 'How many trains can be stopped?' BJP ally Chirag Paswan on Delhi's EC protest shutdown
content: No one can stop the youth of India, Union Minister and LJP (RV) chief Chirag Paswan said on Friday, ahead of the planned Jantar Mantar protest called by the Cockroach Janata Party on October 10. Bharat ke yuva hain ye, inko koi nahi rok sakta prabhu. Jo log aise brahm failaine ka prayaas karte hain kitni trains koi rok lega? Kitni connectivity koi rok lega? Kitni sadko koi koi jam kar dega? (They are the youth of India; no one can stop them. Those who are trying to create such illusions how many trains can one stop, how much connectivity can one disrupt, how many roads can be blocked?) Chirag, a key NDA ally, said when asked about measures being undertaken ahead of the protest. He was responding to questions by reporters in Sonipat, Haryana, on the sidelines of a convocation ceremony. The youth of India have the capacity to show the way to the world. They have been doing so for generations; no one can stop them, he said. Chirag also took aim at the opposition, saying it is not interested in solutions. In a democracy like India, transparency is a basic right, and you must certainly provide it. All I want to know and understand is: what is your objective behind these protests? Solutions come through dialogue, not through protests. How far is it justified to block Delhis roads at regular intervals, causing inconvenience to the public? You are not winning elections, and you are causing discomfort to ordinary people by taking to the streets, he said, against the backdrop of back-to-back protests by Congress and allies. If you have genuine concerns, approach the Election Commission of India. I have full confidence that the Chief Election Commissioner will respond to your queries. You cannot approach a constitutional body through street protests. Instead, you can seek an appointment, voice your concerns, and receive an official response, he said. The point, however, is that you do not want solutions. Your objective is simply to create a ruckus on the streets, which you have been doing for the last three days. Still, I strongly believe that the youth must be heard. I have already created a platform for young people that accommodates both consent and dissent. I give everyone the freedom to express their resentment, suggestions, and concerns. Whether I agree or disagree, we will engage in a dialogue that can lead to a solution, he said. Earlier, Chirag had supported students who protested against the Bihar Public Service Commissions two-tier examination structure for the upcoming Teacher Recruitment Examinations-4 (TRE-4). The state government ultimately reverted to a single-examination format. If trains and other modes of communication are stopped to control and prevent anarchy, the government is well within its rights to do so. But if protesters have valid permission to register their grievances, then it is not fair As for our alliance position, we have always believed that allies support a coalition, not submit to it, he said.

headline: 'We Now Count Peace In Years': Omar Abdullah Recounts Mufti Sayeed-Narayana Murthy Exchange As J&K Eyes GCC Investments
content: CM Omar Abdullah recalls Narayana Murthys response to Mufti Sayeeds investment appeal, drawing a contrast between Jammu and Kashmirs past challenges and its current ambition Chief Minister Omar Abdullahs recollection of a striking exchange between former Chief Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, and Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy has brought Jammu and Kashmirs (J&K) past investment challenges into focus, as the Union Territory seeks to attract Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and build new avenues of employment. Speaking at the GCC Summit in Jammu, Omar recalled an investment event organised by NASSCOM in Srinagar during Mufti Sayeeds first tenure as Chief Minister, between 2002 and 2005. Narayana Murthy, who was present at the event, had been invited by Mufti Sayeed to consider establishing an Infosys presence in Jammu and Kashmir. - J&K Cabinet Expansion: Congress Mounts Pressure On CM Abdullah For Berths; NC Camp Sees Race For 3 Vacancies - 'Omar Govt Total Failure, Won't Last Long, Will Fall Under Own Weight': BJP's Tarun Chugh In Jammu - Omar Abdullah Delaying Local Body Polls Fearing Defeat: BJP Vows To Take To The Streets To Highlight J&K Govt's Failures - United Against BJP, Divided Within: NC, Congress Spar Over Panchayat Polls In Jammu And Kashmir According to Omars recollection, Murthy responded that if he were assured six days of peace and calm, he would come and invest on the seventh day. The anecdote became a central point in Omars address, offering a historical reference against which he sought to explain the regions changing circumstances and its present ambition to attract investment in emerging sectors. Thankfully today we dont count our periods of calm in days, we dont count them in weeks, we dont even count them in months. I think its safe to say that we count them in blocks of years," Omar said. The remark placed the regions earlier investment challenges alongside the governments current efforts to position Jammu and Kashmir as a potential destination for global technology and business operations. A POLITICAL CONTRAST BETWEEN TWO ERAS Chief Minister Omar Abdullah recalled an exchange between Mufti Mohammad Sayeed and N. R. Narayana Murthy regarding investment in Jammu and Kashmir. Narayana Murthy reportedly stated he would invest if assured six days of peace and calm. Omar Abdullah stated that Jammu and Kashmir now counts periods of calm in blocks of years. Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo emphasized the potential of GCCs for investment and employment generation. Omar Abdullah identified IIT Jammu, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, University of Jammu, University of Kashmir, and Islamic University of Science and Technology as institutions producing educated graduates. Omars recollection drew attention to the different contexts in which investment opportunities have been discussed in Jammu and Kashmir over the past two decades. During Mufti Sayeeds tenure, the reported exchange with Narayana Murthy highlighted the importance investors attached to peace and stability. Today, Omar Abdullah is seeking to build on what he describes as a changed environment and encourage companies to consider the Union Territory for technology-led investment. The Chief Minister did not present the anecdote as a personal criticism. Instead, he used it to illustrate the regions evolution and the opportunity to move towards a new phase of economic development. The political significance lies in the contrast: a past investment appeal shaped by concerns over stability is now being invoked in support of an ambition to attract global businesses and create local employment. COMING LATE TO THE PARTY IS NOT ALWAYS A DISADVANTAGE Omar acknowledged that Jammu and Kashmir is entering the GCC sector later than established technology hubs such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai. However, he argued that this need not prevent the region from finding its place in the industry. Drawing an analogy with the evolution of Indian Railways, he referred to the progression from conventional trains to Mail and Express services, Rajdhani and Shatabdi trains, and eventually Vande Bharat. His point was that late entrants can benefit from the experience of others and adopt newer models instead of repeating every stage of development. Coming late to the party is disappointing, but its not always disadvantageous. We can learn from the experiences of others. We dont have to reinvent the wheel. We just have to use it better," he said. The Chief Minister identified emerging Tier 2 and Tier 3 destinations, including Jaipur, Pune and Mohali, as examples of the kind of markets alongside which Jammu and Kashmir could seek to compete. Rather than attempting to replicate the scale of established metropolitan centres immediately, the region hopes to attract an initial investment base and gradually develop the supporting ecosystem. ATAL DULLOO EMPHASISES INVESTMENT AND EMPLOYMENT POTENTIAL Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo has also highlighted the importance of the GCC initiative, expressing confidence that the changing circumstances in Jammu and Kashmir could open new possibilities for investment and employment generation. He has stressed the potential for GCCs to provide opportunities for local youth, strengthen economic activity and encourage major companies to consider establishing operations in the Union Territory. His emphasis complements Omar Abdullahs pitch for a gradual, industry-led expansion of the regions economic base. For the administration, the challenge is to translate investor interest into concrete projects, create conditions that support long-term business operations and ensure that local graduates are equipped to take advantage of the opportunities that emerge. EDUCATED YOUTH AT THE CENTRE OF THE GCC PUSH Omar identified Jammu and Kashmirs educational institutions and young talent as important assets in its effort to attract GCCs. He referred to IIT Jammu, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, the University of Jammu, the University of Kashmir and the Islamic University of Science and Technology as institutions producing educated and ambitious graduates. However, many young people continue to look outside the Union Territory for opportunities in specialised technology and corporate services. GCCs could potentially create local employment in software development, analytics, finance, research and business operations, depending on the functions companies choose to establish. For Jammu and Kashmir, the larger objective is to ensure that its young people can build careers at home while contributing to businesses operating in national and international markets. ONE CENTRE CAN LEAD TO FIVE Omar said the success of the summit should not be judged by whether Jammu and Kashmir immediately attracts a hundred GCCs. Instead, he argued that even one centre could provide the foundation for future growth. One will lead to five, five will lead to ten, and the story will grow from there," he said. He described the workshop as a learning opportunity for the government, allowing it to understand industry expectations, study successful models and identify what needs to be done to attract investment. The Chief Minister also made clear that Jammu and Kashmir wanted to be considered on merit, rather than as a charity case because of its difficult history. The message to investors was to visit the region, assess its capabilities and give it an opportunity to demonstrate its potential. FROM POLITICAL MEMORY TO ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY The GCC initiative brings together two strands of Jammu and Kashmirs current economic narrative: the political significance of changing circumstances and the practical challenge of creating employment through private investment. Mufti Sayeeds reported exchange with Narayana Murthy provides the historical backdrop. Omar Abdullahs present-day pitch seeks to turn that contrast into an argument for a new economic direction, while Atal Dulloo has highlighted the administrations expectations for investment and job creation. Whether that ambition succeeds will depend on the regions ability to attract actual investors, provide the infrastructure and skilled workforce they require, and establish sustainable business operations. The summit marks an effort to open that conversation, but future GCC establishments and employment gains remain objectives to be realised rather than outcomes already secured. From Mufti Sayeeds reported appeal for six days of peace to Omar Abdullahs ambition of attracting global capability centres, the political and economic question facing Jammu and Kashmir is whether changing circumstances can translate into lasting investment, local jobs and a stronger private sector. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah recalled that during Mufti Sayeed's tenure as Chief Minister between 2002 and 2005, Mufti invited Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy to establish an Infosys presence in Jammu and Kashmir. According to Omar, Murthy responded that if he were assured six days of peace and calm, he would invest on the seventh day.

The order instructs all federal departments and executive branch agencies to substitute Super Intelligence" (SI) for Artificial Intelligence" (AI) in all public statements, official correspondence, websites, policy documents, and reports. Trump posted this directive on Truth Social on October 89, 2026. A formal executive order signed by Trump on September 29, 2026, instructs federal departments to substitute "Super Intelligence" (SI) for "Artificial Intelligence" (AI). The Justice Department directed staff to use "SI" in court filings, and AI.gov was updated to visually display SI.gov. A new federal Super Intelligence Force (SIF) has been established, led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. The Justice Department directed staff to use SI" in relevant court filings, and the official homepage of AI.gov was updated to visually display SI.gov (though the underlying web domain remains unchanged). A new federal Super Intelligence Force (SIF), led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, has also been established to coordinate federal policy. The rebranding initiative gained momentum following a high-level White House tech summit where Trump met with prominent industry leaders, including Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, Mark Zuckerberg, Jensen Huang, and Dario Amodei. Elon Musk announced on X (formerly Twitter) that his artificial intelligence unit would be renamed SpaceXSI. Jeff Bezos voiced support during a Fox News interview, stating that he preferred SI" because artificial" is not a flattering descriptor. BACKLASH AND TECHNICAL CONTRADICTIONS The rebrand has faced severe pushback from tech experts, linguists, and fact-checkers who point out that Trump is conflating different scientific terms. Marketing professors and software developers argue that the rebrand will be difficult to enforce globally since Super Intelligence" has a distinct, established scientific definition that does not match standard commercial software available today. On September 29, 2026, President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing all federal departments and executive branch agencies to replace the terms Artificial Intelligence (AI) and AI with Super Intelligence (SI) and SI in all public statements, official correspondence, websites, policy documents, and reports.

headline: Sri Lanka says no immediate plan to help Iranian ships near its waters with depleting food, fuel
content: Sri Lanka's government says that it has no immediate plans to help 19 Iranian ships that have been anchored in the international waters near the island nation facing food, water and fuel shortages. Foreign Ministry Spokesman Thushara Rodrigo said Sri Lanka will put its national interest first before considering any help, and the companies that supply ships are aware of possible secondary sanctions from the United States. He said, however, that there hasn't been any communication from the U.S. warning of repercussions should Sri Lanka decide to help. Rodrigo said that the ships are stationed 24 nautical miles from Sri Lanka's coast and have reported shortages of food, water and fuel. The Iranian Embassy in Sri Lanka said it has no details on the matter. The latest development involving Iranian ships off Sri Lanka's waters comes nearly seven months after a U.S. torpedo attack sank Iranian naval ship IRIS Dena, killing 87 sailors. The ship was returning home after taking part in a naval exercise on invitation from India. A second Iranian ship was brought to a Sri Lankan port after its crew reported technical problems. The wounded sailors who were treated in Sri Lankan hospitals and those rescued from the second ship were safely repatriated back to Iran. Sri Lanka is emerging from an economic crisis, and both the U.S. and Iran are crucial trading partners. The U.S. played an important role in assisting with an International Monetary Fund bailout deal and helping the agricultural sector to avert a food crisis. Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told the local Sunday Times newspaper that the ships are Iranian oil tankers and that they have been anchored off Sri Lanka for the past several months after the U.S. resumed its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving dozens of Iranian vessels stranded and unable to return home. But we are caught in a difficult situation, said international affairs analyst Dayan Jayatilleka, adding that there are limits to what Sri Lanka can practically do. "It's clear to the world that we are not willingly refusing to assist, but there are reasons that we have to be careful and deliberate. What we can do is to observe international humanitarian laws. These are not warships. These are cargo ships which carried oil to China from Iran, he said. "If these ships come in for some reason to our waters because they are attacked, we have a moral obligation to assist immediately.

headline: El Nino At Record High: Japan Weather Body Warns Strong Conditions May Last Through Winter
content: El Nino has reached its strongest intensity since records began in 1949, with Japan's weather agency expecting the conditions to persist through winter. El Nino has reached its strongest intensity on record, according to Japans Meteorological Agency (JMA), which warned that the powerful weather pattern is expected to persist through the Northern Hemispheres winter. The agency said on Friday that sea surface temperatures in the monitored region of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean were 4 degrees Celsius above normal in September. - Orkut Set For Comeback? Founder Launches Petition To Challenge AI-Driven Social Media - Collective Defence Or Political Pleading? Pakistans Houthi Dilemma Under Mecca Pact | Exclusive Details - Who Is Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay, Winner Of 2026 Nobel Peace Prize? SA's First Woman Of Colour To Start A Law Practice - Navanethem Navi Pillay, South African Jurist Of Indian Origin, Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize This surpassed the previous record of 3.6 degrees Celsius, recorded in December 1997, making it the highest level since records began in 1949. The JMA said El Nino conditions had persisted in the equatorial Pacific since spring 2026 and had now reached an unprecedented intensity. It added that the phenomenon was likely to reach a record peak during the current season, with the strongest conditions almost certain to continue through winter in the Northern Hemisphere. How El Nino Affects Global Weather El Nino is a natural climate pattern that causes surface temperatures in parts of the tropical Pacific Ocean to rise. The warming affects wind patterns, atmospheric pressure and rainfall, with consequences for weather conditions across the world. Its effects can be felt thousands of miles away, increasing the risk of extreme weather events, including droughts and floods. El Nino events usually reach their peak around December. El Nino And Rising Global Temperatures The warming ocean also releases heat into the atmosphere over time, often contributing to higher global average temperatures in the following year. Several exceptionally hot years, including 1998, 2010, 2016, 2023 and 2024, occurred after major El Nino events or during periods when the phenomenon was active. The latest assessment from Japans weather agency highlights the strength of the current event and its potential to influence global weather conditions through the coming winter. Japan's Meteorological Agency reported that El Nino reached its strongest intensity on record, with sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean hitting 4 degrees Celsius above normal in September. This surpassed the previous record of 3.6 degrees Celsius set in December 1997, marking the highest level since records started in 1949.

headline: Sri Lanka appeals to Saudi Arabia to overturn migrant worker's death penalty
content: Sri Lanka is preparing to petition Saudi Arabias Supreme Court to overturn a recent Court of Appeal ruling sentencing a migrant worker to death. We are working on an appeal and are hoping to file it today or tomorrow at the Supreme Court, Presidents Counsel Upul Kumarapperuma told The Hindu from Riyadh on Friday (October 9, 2026). He is part of a team of senior lawyers and officials from the public prosecutors office sent by the Sri Lankan government to Saudi Arabia. The case, which has brought concerns about freedom of expression, migrant workers precarity, and the death penalty to the fore, stems from a social media comment posted in late June this year by Sivarasa Anojan, an engineer in his mid-twenties, employed in Saudi Arabia. It was around the annual pilgrimage to Kataragama or the Kathirgamam temple in southern Sri Lanka, which draws scores of Hindu and Buddhist devotees. According to local media reports, a Muslim man from Kalmunai, located in the islands eastern Ampara district, was filmed attacking a dog named Subramani, after the temples presiding deity which had followed Kataragama pilgrims for hundreds of kilometres. The man, who was arrested on charges of animal cruelty, was subsequently granted bail but the video meanwhile went viral on social media, provoking shrill comments from Tamils and Muslims. The two Tamil-speaking communities, living across Sri Lankas north and east have a complex, and at times tense, relationship, owing to their respective political histories during and after the civil war. Mr. Anojan too had weighed in with a comment referring to Prophet Muhammed. Although it was swiftly deleted and Mr. Anojan posted an apology, Saudi courts deemed it blasphemous, sentencing him to five years imprisonment at first, and later increasing the punishment to death. Amid recent reports of attacks on Mr. Anojan by fellow inmates, Sri Lankan Embassy officials in Saudi Arabia visited him earlier this week and found him to be doing alright in prison, according to official sources. The government is taking every possible step, in accordance with the Saudi law, to seek relief for Mr. Anojan and for the commutation of his death sentence, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told Parliament on Wednesday (October 7). Political parties across the divide in Sri Lanka both political and ethnic have come together in their appeal to Saudi Arabia to pardon Mr. Anojan. Religious leaders, media forums, and civil society networks have also written to Saudi authorities, seeking clemency for him. Some politicians have also suggested that the Sri Lankan government request Prime Minister Narendra Modis assistance to reach out to the Saudi Arabian Crown Prince. On September 21, 2026, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake met members of Mr. Anojans family, and assured them that the government will pursue every possible legal and diplomatic channel to take up his case. Earlier this week, rights watchdog Amnesty International urged Saudi Arabias authorities to urgently overturn the death sentence issued against Mr. Anojan. In a statement, Amnesty called upon Saudi authorities to release him immediately and unconditionally given his charges stem entirely from his exercise of his right to freedom of expression. According to the statement, Saudi Arabia remains one of the worlds leading executioners. As of 5 October 2026, at least 175 people had been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, including many for drug-related offences. Foreign nationals account for a majority of those executed, with at least 94 foreign nationals from more than 20 countries put to death this year alone, it further said. In Sri Lanka, calls for the abolition of the death penalty have continued, albeit sporadically. The punishment remains on the books, but the country has not carried out an execution in 50 years.

headline: Suvendu Wins Bengal Bypoll 'Khela': 4 Reasons Why Saffron Sweep In Muslim-Dominated Nandigram, Rejinagar Matters
content: News18 explains why the victories matter for CM Suvendu Adhikari The Bharatiya Janata Partys (BJP) landslide victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar by-elections serve as a major political validation and personal triumph for West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who brought the party to power after years of Trinamool Congresss domination. Coming just months after the BJP formed the government in West Bengal, these results heavily reinforce his political authority and strategy in the state. - 'Muslims Have Found A New Friend In Us': Suvendu Adhikari Hails BJP Wins In Minority-Dominant Rejinagar, Nandigram Bypolls - Bengal to Implement UCC and Combat 'Love Jihad' and 'Land Jihad' Promises Chief Minister | News18 - Faked Injury, Humiliated Nandigram: Suvendu Adhikari Orders Probe Into Mamatas 2021 Leg Injury - 'I Could Be Detained Too If...': Suvendu Adhikari Reacts To Humayun Kabir's Detention In Murshidabad FOUR REASONS WHY SUVENDU ADHIKARIS WIN MATTERS In Nandigram, Hasi Rani Rath (BJP) defeated Milan Pradhan (Congress), while in Rejinagar, Shankharavh Sarkar (BJP) beat Golam Nabi Azad (AJUP). The victories carry several critical implications for Suvendu Adhikari: 1. Validation of His Leadership and Electoral Grip Nandigram is Adhikaris core political bastion. By fielding Hasirani Raththe mother of his slain personal aideAdhikari turned the by-election into a high-stakes emotional and political test. The BJP won the seat by a record margin of over 1.22 lakh votes, completely shattering Adhikaris own previous victory margins. This massive margin cements his undisputed command over his home turf. The BJP secured landslide victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar by-elections. BJP candidate Hasirani Rath won Nandigram by over 1.22 lakh votes. BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won Rejinagar by over 75,000 votes. The BJP claimed to secure nearly 60% of the Muslim vote in Rejinagar and 80% in Nandigram. The BJP's state assembly strength increased to 209 out of 294 seats. 2. Success of His Muslim Outreach Strategy The most significant takeaway for Adhikari is the partys performance in the minority-dominated Rejinagar seat (which has a 70% Muslim population), where BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won by over 75,000 votes. Adhikari personally led a development-focused pitch to minority voters. Following the win, Adhikari claimed that the BJP secured nearly 60% of the Muslim vote in Rejinagar and 80% in Nandigram, signaling that his efforts to break the TMCs traditional minority vote bank are succeeding, according to analysts. 3. Proof of Concept for Annapurna Yojana" Adhikari directly attributed the massive voter turnout and victory margins to women beneficiaries of the Annapurna Yojana, a state social welfare scheme providing 3,000 per month to low-income households. Winning in a 70% Muslim-majority seat like Rejinagar validates Adhikaris strategy that pro-poor welfare schemes can transcend religious lines and counter the oppositions anti-minority narrative against the BJP, say experts. 4. Silencing the Fragmented Opposition The election was the first major electoral test since the BJP took power in West Bengal. The dominant victory margins demonstrate that the oppositioncomprising a fractured front of the Congress (supported by Mamata Banerjees faction), the Left, and regional groups like the AJUPis currently incapable of mounting a cohesive challenge to Adhikaris administration, say experts. With the state assembly strength of the BJP rising to 209 out of 294 seats, these twin victories firmly establish Suvendu Adhikari not just as a regional leader, but as a leader capable of engineering historic, cross-community mandates in West Bengal. In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress's Milan Pradhan by a record margin of over 1.22 lakh votes, while in Rejinagar, Shankharavh Sarkar beat AJUP's Golam Nabi Azad by over 75,000 votes.

headline: CJP Protest On October 10: Delhi Police Denies Permission, Holds High Level Meeting
content: Delhi Police has stepped up security ahead of the CJPs October 10 protest, with permission denied and extensive measures planned to maintain law and order. Senior Delhi Police officers held a high-level meeting at the police headquarters on Friday to review the law and order situation ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The meeting focused on the evolving security situation in the capital and the arrangements being put in place to prevent any disruption. Officers also discussed recent observations made by the Supreme Court, particularly its concerns over the impact of security measures on public transport and commuters. - How Do We Balance It?: SC On Curbs In Delhi Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest - Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest On October 10, Says They Did Not Follow Rules - CEC Protest Live Updates: Delhi Schools, Colleges Shift Classes Online, Postpone Exams Ahead Of October 10 Protest - CJP Oct 10 Protest: Delhi Police Step Up Vigil, Track 2,800 'Criminals', Monitor Buses, Borders The police are preparing for a potentially large turnout, with officials expecting more than 50,000 people from Delhi and neighbouring states to attend the proposed demonstration. Security has been expanded across the New Delhi district and other parts of the capital. Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest Delhi Police has denied permission for the CJP protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the application was submitted at short notice, while guidelines require advance notice for such demonstrations. Police also cited alleged non compliance with directions and undertakings during an earlier CJP protest. The authorities said the decision was also taken keeping public safety, traffic management and the prevailing law and order situation in mind. Restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita are currently in force in the New Delhi area. Police have warned that violations could lead to legal action. 37 Blocking Points, Detention Centres Planned As part of the security plan, Delhi Police has prepared 37 blocking points across the New Delhi district and plans to use dedicated detention centres across all 15 districts if required. The arrangements are aimed at preventing large groups from moving towards Jantar Mantar and other sensitive areas. Security has also been tightened at several Delhi borders, including Ghazipur, Chilla, Tikri, Singhu, Loni, Badarpur, Kapashera and Gurugram, with police monitoring movement towards the capital. 57 Metro Stations, Train Services Hit The security preparations have also affected public transport. Delhi Police has asked the DMRC to close entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9 pm on Friday and keep restrictions in place on October 10 until the situation normalises. The police have cited concerns over large groups using stations to gather and move towards sensitive areas. Several long-distance trains heading towards Delhi have also been cancelled or curtailed ahead of the protest. The Supreme Court has meanwhile asked authorities to balance security requirements with public convenience, particularly in relation to Metro and railway services. The CJP has maintained that it will go ahead with the protest despite the police denying permission. Delhi Police denied permission because the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) submitted its application at short notice instead of providing the required advance notice, alongside concerns over public safety, traffic management, and non-compliance with previous undertakings.

headline: Nandigram Bypoll Results: BJP Candidate Hasi Rani Rath Wins By Record Margin Of Over 1.22 Lakh Votes
content: Hasi Rani Rath secured 1,64,427 votes, defeating Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who received 41,674 votes. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday retained Nandigram in West Bengal, with its candidate Hasi Rani Rath winning the Assembly by-election by a record margin of 1,22,753 votes. Rath secured 1,64,427 votes, defeating Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who received 41,674 votes. The result marks a decisive victory for the BJP in one of the states closely watched constituencies. - BJPs Maharashtra Outreach: Street Plays To Spotlight PM Modis 25-Year Public Life Journey - Haldwani Shuddhikaran Row: Is Dalit Candidate BJPs Answer To Congresss Kharge-Led Narrative? - Bengal Bypoll Result: BJP's Big Win In Minority-Dominated Rejinagar Puts Spotlight On Minority Vote - J&K Statehood Row Escalates: NC Defends Resolution, BJP Opposes Autonomy & 35A References The by-election was held on October 6, while counting took place on October 9. Rath Wins Seat Vacated By Suvendu Adhikari Nandigram was vacated by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Rath, 60, was the BJPs candidate for the seat and is the mother of an aide to the chief minister who was murdered days after the BJP came to power in May. The BJP maintained its lead from the beginning of counting, eventually securing victory by more than 1.22 lakh votes. Congress candidate Pradhan finished a distant second. The result gives the BJP a record victory margin in Nandigram, consolidating its position in the constituency. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) retained Nandigram in West Bengal. BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath won the Assembly by-election by 1,22,753 votes. Rath secured 1,64,427 votes, defeating Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who received 41,674 votes. The by-election was held on October 6, and counting took place on October 9. Nandigram was vacated by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Minority Vote Shift In Focus The result also brings attention to the changing political landscape in West Bengal, particularly the voting patterns of minority communities. The BJPs victory comes amid claims that a significant section of minority voters has backed the party. During the Assembly elections, minority votes had largely consolidated behind the Trinamool Congress (TMC), led by Mamata Banerjee. However, the principal Opposition party has since fragmented and played a limited role in the bypolls. In Nandigram, the TMC backed the Congress after its own candidate withdrew from the contest. In Rejinagar, the party persuaded its candidate to remain in the race hours after he had also announced his withdrawal. The Nandigram result marks a significant electoral gain for the BJP, as the party retains the constituency with an unprecedented margin. The outcome also highlights the changing dynamics among opposition parties and the potential implications of shifting minority support in the state. BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath won the Nandigram Assembly by-election by a record margin of 1,22,753 votes, securing a total of 1,64,427 votes against Congress candidate Milan Pradhan.

headline: Three arrested for assaulting migrant workers in Ooty
content: Three men were arrested for allegedly assaulting migrant workers who were traveling home after work onboard a bus in Udhagamandalam in The Nilgiris. The three accused were identified as Arun (27), Divakar (25), and Sanjay (26), residents of Khandal in Udhagamandalam. According to police, the three men had picked a quarrel with five migrant workers who were on a bus traveling to Khandal from Udhagamandalam town a few days ago. They had allegedly demanded that the workers give up their seats, which led to a quarrel. After the five workers got off the bus at their bus stop in Khandal, Arun, Divakar and Sanjay allgedly followed them and attacked them, leading to a fight between both groups. Local residents, who noticed the scuffle, complained of the incident to the Nilgiris police, who launched a hunt for the people involved. An investigation showed that the three accused were primarily at fault for the incident. The police arrested Arun, Divakar and Sanjay, who were later remanded in judicial custody.
