headline: 'Nothing Can Stop India's Youth': Union Minister Chirag Paswan On Transit Curbs Ahead Of CJP's Delhi Protest
content: Paswan asked how many trains anyone could realistically halt or how much connectivity could truly be blocked across an interconnected nation Union Minister Chirag Paswan has firmly rejected claims that temporary transit adjustments ahead of a planned political demonstration led by the Cockroach Janta Party in Delhi on October 10 could paralyse public movement or stifle young citizens across the country. Speaking in response to reports surrounding the cancellation of select passenger trains heading toward key capital terminals, the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) leader expressed unwavering faith in the resilience and adaptability of Indias younger generation. Paswan emphasised that narrative attempts to project routine security measures as complete transit blockades fundamentally misunderstand the determination of the nations youth. He noted that physical infrastructure management can never contain the spirit or movement of a population committed to driving progress. - Metro Curbs, Cancelled Trains, Extra CCTVs: Delhi Turns Into Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest Tomorrow - CJP Claims Govt Plans To Arrest Saurav Das, Abhijeet Dipke Ahead Of October 10 Protest - Driving From Noida To Delhi Today? These Roads Could Slow You Down; Check Alternative Routes - Will Keep Fighting To Save Democracy: CJPs Abhijeet Dipke Reacts To Complaint Over Shivaji Park Protest Challenging Misconceptions Surrounding Capital Transit Addressing journalists, the Union Minister pushed back against opposition criticisms regarding travel restrictions in the National Capital Region. He challenged commentators spreading alarmist interpretations, pointing out the practical impossibility of shutting down a vast, dynamic national network. Questioning the narrative surrounding transport curbs, Paswan asked how many trains anyone could realistically halt or how much connectivity could truly be blocked across an interconnected nation. He further observed that jamming roads or restricting specific routes cannot restrict the countrys youth, who possess the intrinsic capacity to lead the world forward just as previous generations did. Balancing Public Safety and Mass Transit Continuity The Ministers remarks coincide with administrative steps taken by civil and railway authorities to manage security ahead of scheduled political gatherings in the capital. Law enforcement agencies routinely implement temporary route realignments and train schedule adjustments near major transit hubs to prevent severe crowd congestion and preserve public order. Government officials maintain that localised administrative precautions are designed to protect commuters, ensure orderly urban transit, and maintain essential services. Rather than acting as total bans, traffic advisories and regulated service windows help balance public safety with uninterrupted daily transit across the wider metropolitan region. Unshakable Faith in Demographic Strength Highlighting the transformative potential of young citizens, Paswan reiterated that democratic participation and nation-building rely on constructive energy rather than specific transit corridors. He reaffirmed that no logistics constraint could derail the collective ambition of young Indians. By underscoring the nations infrastructural resilience, the Union Minister urged observers to look past politically driven commentary, expressing full confidence in the maturity and spirit of Indias youth. Union Minister Chirag Paswan firmly rejected claims that temporary transit adjustments ahead of the October 10 political demonstration by the Cockroach Janta Party could paralyze public movement or stifle young citizens, expressing unwavering faith in the resilience and adaptability of India's youth.

headline: Annamalai hails Nobel Peace Prize winner Navanethem Pillay
content: Former BJP leader and founder of the 'We The Leaders' movement on Friday hailed South African jurist and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navanethem "Navi" Pillay on being selected for the Nobel Peace Prize. From humble beginnings in Durban, Ms. Pillay, whose parents were of Tamil descent, and whose grandfather was brought to South Africa from India to work in sugar plantations, pursued a lifelong crusade against apartheid, gender discrimination, and systemic injustice, standing as a towering beacon of resilience and courage, Mr. Annamalai said. "From serving as a fearless human rights lawyer and the first non-white woman judge of South Africa's High Court, to providing stellar leadership as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, she has shown unwavering dedication to the marginalised, making her a source of immense pride," he said.

headline: Tiruppur domestic garment exhibition to be held in January
content: The South India Hosiery Manufacturers Association (SIHMA) and the Tirupur Domestic Garments Manufacturers Association (TIDGMA) will, in January next year, organise an exhibition of garments made in Tiruppur for the domestic market. Apart from garments made for exports, Tiruppur produces T-shirts, inner wear, and apparel worth over 40,000 crore every year for the Indian market and several leading brands source garments from Tiruppur. R. Dhamodharan, secretary of the SIHMA, said the SIHMA has nearly 675 manufacturers of garments and inner wear for the Indian market and the TIDGMA has 350 to 400 manufacturers of apparels. These producers make garments and inner wear for summer and winter. We plan to hold two fairs annually - one in Tiruppur for summer wear and another in a north Indian city for winter wear. Tiruppur garment makers produce winter wear such as thermal wear, hoodies, and so on, apart from T-shirts and basic garments, he said. The logo for the event was released and stall registration began on October 9 at a meeting headed by P. Shanmugasundaram, president of the SIHMA, and M.K.M. Balasubramaniam, president of the TIDGMA. The event, to be held at the India Knit Fair complex from January 3 to 5, will have nearly 115 stalls. We plan to invite retail chains, distributors, white label buyers, corporate buyers, and uniform producers to this business event, he added.s

headline: J&K Tech Threat: How Sat Communication Infra Raises Security Concerns For Counter-Terror Ops | Exclusive
content: Security agencies have mapped the specific zones most vulnerable to this tech-driven threat Indian security agencies have issued a major security alert over a critical blind spot emerging in the Kashmir Valley. Intelligence inputs obtained exclusively by CNN-News18 reveal that unchecked satellite communication (Satcom) infrastructure is rapidly emerging as a severe threat to counter-terror operations in Jammu and Kashmir, allowing terror outfits to bypass the local security grid entirely. According to classified agency reports, Pakistan-based terror modules specifically operational cells of the Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) and Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) are leveraging small, highly portable Satcom terminals to maintain continuous command links. These light terminals are being deployed in high-altitude hideouts across the Pir Panjal ranges and dense forest belts where cellular towers do not exist. - India Defends Starlink Framework Amid Elon Musks Discrimination Claims | SpaceX | News18 - Starlink in India News: Telecom Minister Scindia Says No Monopoly, 3 Companies Get SATCOM Licences - Why India Wants Answers Before Starlink Goes Live: Lessons From Irans Unauthorised Terminals | Exclusive - What If Starlink Won't Switch Off? Study Flags Data And Security Risks India Faces With Musk's Network THE TERRAIN ADVANTAGE: BLIND SPOTS IN THE FORESTS Security agencies have mapped the specific zones most vulnerable to this tech-driven threat. The rugged, high-altitude terrain and thick forest cover provide the perfect camouflage for these devices: - Jammu Region: The Pir Panjal Arc, encompassing Rajouri, Poonch, and Reasi. - Kashmir Valley: The dense forest belts of North and South Kashmir, specifically Pahalgam, Dachigam, and Kishtwar. Intelligence sources warn that these compact terminals can easily be concealed inside remote cave hideouts or mounted directly onto unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and drones. BYPASSING THE INDIAN TELECOM GRID Indian security agencies issued a major security alert over a critical blind spot in the Kashmir Valley. Unchecked satellite communication (Satcom) infrastructure is emerging as a severe threat to counter-terror operations in Jammu and Kashmir. Pakistan-based terror modules, specifically Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) and Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), use portable Satcom terminals. These terminals bypass local terrestrial telecom infrastructure, making them untrackable by Indian security interfaces. The technology's integration into drone warfare allows cross-border operators to navigate weapon drops and surveillance runs deep inside Indian territory. The core panic within the security apparatus stems from the technology itself. These satellite terminals link directly to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations, bypassing local terrestrial telecom infrastructure entirely. Because the signals travel straight to space, traditional Indian security interfaces, local firewall monitoring, and electronic surveillance assets cannot track, intercept, or block the unauthorized communications. This allows strike outfits to sustain long-duration hideouts while commanders receive direct, real-time operational instructions from cross-border handlers in Rawalpindi and Muzaffarabadall without leaving a single trace on local Indian telecom networks. THE GLOBAL PRECEDENT AND DRONE INTEGRATION Top intelligence officials point to international conflicts as proof of concept. Indian authorities have closely analyzed case studies where Starlink terminals provided direct internet connectivity over active conflict zones in Ukraine without local government sanction, proving that LEO satellite internet can keep an asset online completely independent of local state control. Compounding the crisis is the integration of this tech into modern drone warfare. Modern insurgency in J&K relies heavily on drone-dropped payloads around border districts. By integrating satellite terminals directly into drone controllers or autonomous units, cross-border operators can now navigate weapons drops and surveillance runs deep inside Indian territory. This completely removes the reliance on standard Radio Frequency (RF) or line-of-sight signals, effectively rendering local anti-drone jamming systems and electronic counter-measures blind. With the technological landscape shifting, top security commanders are currently meeting to formulate an immediate electronic warfare response to counter this off-grid satellite threat before it alters the operational dynamics on the ground. Portable satellite communication terminals link directly to Low Earth Orbit constellations, completely bypassing local terrestrial telecom infrastructure and preventing traditional security interfaces from tracking the signals.

headline: 'Silent On JNU Harassment': Smriti Irani Attacks Rahul Gandhi After Professor's Dismissal
content: Smriti Irani criticised Rahul Gandhi over his silence after JNU terminated Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam following a sexual harassment inquiry. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National General Secretary Smriti Irani on Friday launched a scathing attack on Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of remaining silent over the sexual harassment allegations against a JNU professor. Her remarks came hours after Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) terminated Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam with immediate effect following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment complaints filed by 11 female students. Akoijam is also a Congress Lok Sabha MP from Inner Manipur. - 'Youre Doing Your Job': Rahul Gandhi Distributes Water While Supporters Deflate Cops Detention Bus | Watch - DMK U-Turn On Rahul Gandhi? Party Backs Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 'Right To Fight' - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody? Taking a swipe at Gandhi, Irani referred to his recent comments on fighting patriarchy and questioned his silence over the allegations against Akoijam. The same gentleman, referring to Rahul Gandhi, recently spoke about smashing the patriarchy. Ironically, he is extremely silent on allegations by female students against a professor who was allegedly sexually harassing them for marks," Irani said. She further said media reports had indicated that an internal committee of the university had conducted an inquiry into the allegations and that Akoijam had subsequently been dismissed. VIDEO | Delhi: BJP National General Secretary Smriti Irani on allegations of sexual harassment at JNU, says, The same gentleman (referring to Rahul Gandhi) recently spoke about smashing the patriarchy. Ironically, he is extremely silent on allegations by female students against a professor who was allegedly sexually harassing them for marks. Media reports have led us to believe that an internal committee within the university conducted an inquiry as per law, and Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam has been found guilty of the allegations of sexual harassment. What is deafening is the silence of the former Congress national president."She adds, People who have recently seen videos of the former Congress national president physically manhandling a female police officer should not be surprised by the selective posturing of the Congress leadership. Democracy has responded to the mob. It is our legal framework, not the Gandhi family, that upholds the safety and rights of Indian women. Once again, the deafening silence of the former Congress national president is nothing more than a certification of the same." Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 9, 2026 What Is Deafening Is Silence Irani questioned what she described as the silence of the Congress leadership following the universitys action. What is deafening is the silence of the former Congress national president," she said. She also referred to recent videos involving Gandhi and alleged that Congress leaders had previously criticised the handling of a woman police officer by the former Congress president. People who have recently seen videos of the former Congress national president physically manhandling a female police officer should not be surprised by the selective posturing of the Congress leadership," Irani said. JNUs October 9 order said the universitys Internal Committee had conducted an inquiry into the allegations and recommended major punishment. The university subsequently imposed dismissal from service with immediate effect. Smriti Irani attacked Rahul Gandhi for remaining silent over sexual harassment allegations against a JNU professor who was found guilty by an internal inquiry and dismissed.

headline: Built in Goa, Armed for Okha: Indian Coast Guard Commissions Indigenous ICGS Ajit
content: The Indian Coast Guard commissioned ICGS Ajit, a 52-metre Fast Patrol Vessel built by Goa Shipyard, on 09 October 2026. Based at Okha, it will handle SAR and anti-smuggling. The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) commissioned its indigenously built Fast Patrol Vessel (FPV) ICGS Ajit at Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) on 09 October 2026, adding a Make in India-built vessel to its fleet under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat push in defence shipbuilding. The commissioning ceremony was presided over by Dr. Sirish Choudhary, IDAS, Principal Integrated Financial Advisor (ICG). - INDIA Bloc CEC Protests: 27 FIRs Filed In 7 Days, Cases Include Obstruction And Disobeying Orders - Over 35 Trains Including Rajdhani, Shatabdi Cancelled In Delhi On Oct 10 Ahead Of CJP Protest: Is Your Train On The List? - BJP MP Faces Flak As Pakistani Fighter Jet Image Appears In Air Force Day Post - UP Headmaster Taps Students Shaved Head Like Tabla, Suspended After Video Goes Viral ICGS Ajit will be stationed at Okha. The 52-metre vessel displaces 320 tonnes and has a crew of 39. Its armament includes a CRN 91 30mm naval gun and two 12.7mm M2 machine guns on remotely controlled, stabilised mounts. Its systems include an integrated bridge system, a fire control system and an integrated platform management system. The vessel is designed for maritime surveillance, search and rescue (SAR), anti-smuggling and marine pollution response operations. ICGS Ajit is the seventh of eight FPVs, built in the Adamya class, that GSL is constructing for the ICG. GSL designed the vessels in-house, and more than 60 per cent of ICGS Ajits construction content is indigenous. GSL handed the vessel over to the ICG on 25 August 2026. The eight-vessel series was contracted in March 2022 for Rs. 473 crore. The first vessel, ICGS Adamya, was commissioned at Paradip in September 2025. ICGS Ajit will be stationed at Okhe to patrol the waters off the coast of Okha, Gujarat.

headline: INDIA Bloc CEC Protests: 27 FIRs Filed In 7 Days, Cases Include Obstruction And Disobeying Orders
content: 27 FIRs were registered in seven days over protests demanding action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, with cases involving allegations of obstruction. Protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar have led to the registration of 27 FIRs in seven days, with four provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) appearing most frequently in the cases. A compilation of the FIRs shows that Section 3(5) of the BNS was used in 22 of the 27 cases, making it the most commonly invoked provision. Section 3(5) deals with shared liability when an offence is committed by several people with a common intention. - Gyanesh Kumar Protest Escalates: Cops Report Injuries, FIRs Filed | Delhi Protest | News18 - Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed - Delhi Protests: 25 FIRs Registered; Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Named For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC The second most frequently cited provision was Section 223(a), which appeared in 18 FIRs. It relates to disobedience of an order issued by a public servant. Meanwhile, Sections 221 and 132 were each mentioned in 17 FIRs. What Do The Four Sections Mean? BNS Section 3(5): Deals with liability for an offence committed jointly by people sharing a common intention. BNS Section 223(a): Covers disobedience of an order issued by a public servant. BNS Section 221: Relates to obstructing a public servant while they are carrying out their official duties. BNS Section 132: Deals with assault or use of criminal force to prevent a public servant from performing their duties. Public Property Damage Provision Also Invoked The compilation also shows that Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property (PDPP/DPDP) Act was invoked in nine FIRs. The provision deals with damage to or defacement of public property. Other provisions mentioned across the FIRs include Sections 121 and 121(1) of the BNS, which deal with causing hurt or grievous hurt with the intention of stopping a public servant from performing their duties. Section 115(2), relating to voluntarily causing hurt, and Section 126(2), concerning wrongful restraint, also feature in the cases. The FIRs further include Section 127(2) on wrongful confinement or unlawful restriction of movement, along with Sections 74 and 75, which cover offences involving assault or criminal force against women and sexual harassment. Another provision, Section 118(1), concerns causing hurt using dangerous instruments or methods. The FIRs come amid a series of protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties, student groups and civil society organisations have accused the Election Commission of irregularities in the voter roll revision, allegations that the poll panel has rejected. The protests have intensified over the past week, with demonstrations and attempts by protesters to reach Jantar Mantar. Delhi Police had denied permission for some of the gatherings and imposed restrictions on public assemblies in parts of the New Delhi district. Police have also detained protesters during attempts to march towards the designated protest area. Section 3(5) of the BNS, dealing with shared liability for joint offenses, was invoked in 22 of the 27 registered cases. The second most frequent was Section 223(a) regarding disobedience of public servant orders, appearing in 18 FIRs.

content: The train cancellations are intended to prevent passengers from facing difficulties reaching railway stations amid traffic restrictions and road blockades. headline: Collective Defence Or Political Pleading? Pakistan's Houthi Dilemma Under Mecca Pact | Exclusive Details

Diplomatic observers point out that sending polite appeals without establishing clear red lines or operational deadlines risks projecting hesitation rather than strength. Domestic Pressures Limit Islamabads Manoeuvrability Islamabads cautious approach stems from severe internal constraints. The result is a hybrid stance of rhetorical solidarity backed by tactical hesitation, leaving allies and adversaries questioning whether the Mecca Pact will deliver tangible security solutions or remain confined to diplomatic declarations. The Mecca Defence Pact is a trilateral collective security alliance modelled after NATO, pledging that an armed attack on any member state will be treated as an attack on all and requiring a joint military response.

headline: Delhi's Air Improves In September, But 5 Haryana Cities Among India's 10 Most Polluted
content: Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 level of 38 g/m in September. Meanwhile, five Haryana cities featured among Indias 10 most polluted While Delhi recorded a monthly average PM2.5 concentration of 38 micrograms per cubic metre (g/m) in September, Haryana emerged as a major air pollution hotspot, with five of Indias 10 most polluted cities located in the state, according to a new analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). The report, published on October 6, found that Panipat in Haryana recorded the countrys highest monthly average PM2.5 concentration at 78 g/m, followed by Jind at 66 g/m. Panipats PM2.5 levels exceeded Indias national daily air quality standard of 60 g/m on 20 of the 29 days observed during the month. - Punjab Stubble Burning Row: Fresh Fire Visuals, Sirsa Attacks Govt Over Pollution Crisis | N18 - 4.9-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Chamoli, Tremors Felt Across Delhi-NCR - Weather Alert: Bay Of Bengal System To Trigger Rain In Several States; What Delhi-NCR Can Expect - Think Vodka Is Boring? These Bottles Might Change Your Mind Haryana Accounts For Five Of The 10 Most Polluted Cities The five Haryana cities in the top 10 were Panipat, Jind, Yamunanagar, Gurugram and Manesar. The remaining cities on the list were Khora in Uttar Pradesh, Mandi Gobindgarh in Punjab, Pithampur in Madhya Pradesh, Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh and Byrnihat in Assam. The findings highlight that elevated particulate pollution was not limited to Delhi. Several cities in neighbouring states and other parts of the country also recorded high PM2.5 concentrations during September, ahead of the winter season when pollution levels often rise in northern India. 230 Of 251 Cities Exceeded WHO PM2.5 Guideline According to CREAs analysis of data from Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS), 230 of the 251 Indian cities with sufficient monitoring data recorded PM2.5 concentrations above the World Health Organizations daily guideline of 15 g/m. Delhis monthly average of 38 g/m was below the national daily standard of 60 g/m used as a benchmark in the report, but remained above the WHO guideline. These comparisons should be interpreted carefully because a monthly average and a daily standard or guideline refer to different averaging periods. CREA also reported that 246 of the 251 cities with sufficient data for at least 80% of the month recorded PM2.5 concentrations below Indias daily national standard of 60 g/m. Only 21 cities met the WHOs daily guideline, according to the analysis. Air Pollution Concerns Ahead Of Winter Air pollution commonly worsens across Delhi-NCR and other parts of northern India during winter, when weather conditions can limit the dispersion of pollutants. Emissions from vehicles, industries and other sources contribute to pollution, while crop-residue burning can add smoke to the air during the post-monsoon period. The September findings underline the need to monitor air quality beyond the national capital, particularly in cities recording persistently elevated particulate levels. The data also point to the importance of sustained pollution-control measures before the onset of the winter season. Haryana emerged as a major air pollution hotspot in September, with five of its cities ranking among India's 10 most polluted locations according to a CREA analysis.

headline: 26,000 CAPF Personnel To 20,000 Cops: Delhi 'Fortified' Ahead Of CJP's Jantar Mantar 2.0 Against Gyanesh Kumar
content: CJPs Oct 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: MHA has authorised a massive central force presence to enforce a strict security alert in New Delhi from October 8 to 12 Abhijeet Dipke-led Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) nationwide protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft has triggered a major security clampdown and travel shutdown across the national capital for Saturday, October 10, 2026. The Ministry of Home Affairs has authorised a massive central force presence to enforce a strict security alert in New Delhi from October 8 to 12, 2026. - Metro Curbs, Cancelled Trains, Extra CCTVs: Delhi Turns Into Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest Tomorrow - Gyanesh Kumars Z+ Security Upgraded Ahead Of October 10 Jantar Mantar 2.0 Protest: What Does It Entail Now? - Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 PARAMILITARY & CAPF DEPLOYMENT SCALE The total strength of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) deployed in the national capital is scaling up to approximately 26,000 personnel. The Home Ministry cleared 221 additional companies of CAPF specifically for this mobilization window. This heavily reinforces the 110 CAPF companies already attached to the Delhi Police. The deployment comprises a diverse mix of paramilitary branches: - CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force): 85 companies (approx. 7,0008,500 personnel), with contingents mobilised from West Bengal and former Naxal-affected areas in Chhattisgarh. Units have been instructed to carry operational-scale weapons, anti-riot gear, and full ammunition scales. - SSB (Sashastra Seema Bal): 10 companies. - ITBP (Indo-Tibetan Border Police): 7 companies. - RAF (Rapid Action Force): 7 companies specialized in crowd control and riot management. - CISF (Central Industrial Security Force): 1 company. - Women Paramilitary Personnel: An additional 450 to 500 women paramilitary officers are stationed to handle the anticipated high volume of female protesters. The Cockroach Janta Party's protest is scheduled for Saturday, October 10, 2026. The Ministry of Home Affairs authorized a security alert in New Delhi from October 8 to 12, 2026. The total strength of Central Armed Police Forces deployed in the national capital is approximately 26,000 personnel. Paramilitary units are working with 20,000 Delhi Police personnel, bringing the collective security presence past 45,000 officers. Delhi Police requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation to shut down entry/exit gates or reduce train frequencies across 57 metro stations. SECURITY GRID AND OPERATIONAL ALERT Paramilitary units are working in tandem with 20,000 Delhi Police personnel, pushing the collective security presence past 45,000 officers. Command structures have directed paramilitary units to avoid unnecessary friction while strictly blocking any unauthorized mass marches toward sensitive central locations. Paramilitary forces are enforcing Section 163 of the BNSS across the New Delhi district. Because the CJPs protest permission was denied, any assembly at or near Jantar Mantar is treated as illegal. To prevent crowd aggregation, Delhi Police requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to systematically shut down entry/exit gates or reduce train frequencies across 57 metro stations starting the night of October 9. PERMISSION DENIED Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad confirmed that permission was rejected due to short notice (applications require a 10-day prior window under guidelines), past compliance issues, and law-and-order concerns. Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is active across the New Delhi district, making any unauthorized gathering or sit-in unlawful. Multi-layered barricading and CCTV monitoring are active around Jantar Mantar and critical zones. Police are using Facial Recognition Systems (FRS) to track roughly 2,800 individuals with alleged criminal antecedents. Around 150 body-worn cameras have been distributed to officers managing crowds and key transit/protest corridors. Border & Transit Surveillance: - Heightened checks and barricades are placed at key entry points from neighboring Uttar Pradesh (eastern/Shahdara borders) and Rajasthan (southwest routes). - Police are actively monitoring railway stations, bus terminals, and incoming bus operators. - Metro stations and local markets in the New Delhi area may face restricted or regulated access depending on real-time conditions. - Station house officers (SHOs) have contacted educational institutions and paying guest (PG) accommodation owners to discourage students from joining the mobilisation. Social media calls and transport bookings are also under close scrutiny. headline: JNU sacks Congress MP as professor after 11 students allege sexual harassment
content: The Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Friday dismissed Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam of the School of Social Sciences following an inquiry by the universitys internal committee into allegations of sexual harassment. Akoijam is also the Congress Lok Sabha MP from Inner Manipur. Officials said that around 10-12 students from the Centre for Study of Social Systems had filed a sexual harassment complaint against him. An order by Vice Chancellor Santishree D Pandit stated: Whereas, an inquiry was conducted by the Internal Committee (IC) against Prof. Angomcha Bimol Akoijam of Centre for the Study of Social Systems, School of Social Sciences, pursuant to allegations of sexual harassment and based on the findings, the Internal Committee (IC) recommended major punishment to Prof. Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, as per service rules and by invoking Rule 11(ix) of Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules. She said that upon following the due process and considering all available facts and as per the report of the internal committee, the punishment of dismissal from the services of the University is hereby imposed on Professor Akoijam with immediate effect. Raising the matter last month, the ABVP staged a protest against the professor and demanded his suspension and dismissal from service. Following his dismissal Friday, the ABVP, in a statement, said, In this case, 11 female students had filed complaints of sexual harassment against the Congress MP. After considering the Internal Committees report and the available facts, the university dismissed him from service. ABVP JNU secretary, Praveen Kumar Piyush, said, ABVP JNU has consistently fought for the safety and justice of female students. Our position is clear: no ones political position or influence should stand in the way of impartial action. The university administration must continue to ensure accountability so that female students receive justice, safety, and dignity. The dismissal of the Congress Lok Sabha MP from university service is not enough; strict legal action must be taken against him, and he must be sent to jail. In a post on X, BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani said, The so-called Smash the Patriarchy brigade of the Congress ecosystem stands completely exposed. Will it demand accountability from its MP, Bimol Akoijam over serious sexual harassment complaints, or will the brigade go conspicuously silent just because its convenient?

headline: 'Patience A Necessity': Rajeev Chandrasekhar Slams Musk Over Starlink, Says 'Security Rules Can't Be Wished Away'
content: Chandrasekhar, who served as Union MoS for Electronics and IT, said all three satellite communication licensees were broadly at the same stage of securing clearances Former Union minister and BJP Kerala president Rajeev Chandrasekhar hit back at Elon Musks criticism of the delay in Starlinks India launch on Friday, asserting that national security and regulatory compliance cannot be compromised in the push to introduce new technology. In a post on X, Chandrasekhar said Indias technology and telecommunications sectors operate on three principlesOpen, Safe & Trusted and Accountable"and argued that the countrys regulatory approach is different from the crony-driven system of the past. - Musk Accuses Indian Oligarchs Of Blocking Starlink Launch, Centre Rejects Claim | News18 - With Elon Musk, It's Not Just About Business: From India To US, There's Politics Involved - Exclusive | Scindia Clarifies Government's Stand, Mocks Congress Over Rahul Gandhi-Musk Exchange - 'Zero Tolerance To Terrorism': India Hits Out At Pakistan Over Cross-Border Terror; Defends Right To Respond Satellite IP services have many security implications. More so in a country like India which has faced years of Terror and insurgency supported by inimical state actors in our neighbourhood," he wrote, referring to the security challenges associated with satellite communications. Dear Elon @elonmusk You hv certainly stirred up plenty of reaction with ur posts. But this needs a response from me, as did ur Electronic Voting machines can be hacked" post from some time ago. As someone who knows a little bit abt Telecom as someone who played a decent-ish role in building Indias wireless sector as an Entrepreneur and then as a policy maker , let me share my thoughts. It is true that Indias Telecom was a sector beset with opaqueness and corruption for several decades where cronies ruled under the benevolent love and the politics of ur latest fan (name not withheld @RahulGandhi ) But under PM @narendramodi , 3 principles govern the tech (including Telecom/Internet) sector. Open, Safe & Trusted and Accountable. Open Free from any monopoly-duopoly. Free and fair competition. Infra, Network , Platforms must be safe and trusted. Accountable Every participant should be legally accountable for safety and trust. I was a MP first and then part of PM @narendramodi jis team when this framework was developed. I have more than a little experience of fighting years of political and bureaucratic opaqueness and corruption, which shaped these principles.so todays India is not that old crony driven India. I am not in govt anymore and certainly dont speak for it. But it seems to me that Govt has made it clear: all three satcom licensees are at broadly the same stage of ensuring security clearance by verifying its safety and trust first, then spectrum. Satellite IP services have many security implications. More so in a country like India which has faced years of Terror and insurgency supported by inmical state actors in our neighbourhood. From 26/11 terror attacks to recent ones in Pahalgam, satcom has been preferred comm for Terrorists. Satellite VOIP and encryption creates more challenges security wise. Not insurmountable but new capabilities and capacity hv to be built to ensure Safety and Trust. I hv used @Starlink and I think its awesome technology and represents a new era in mobility innovation. No doubt. But a country has to plan for itself and its interests before every new choice. Thats what India is doing. Patience is unavoidable and in this case is a necessity. Rajeev Chandrasekhar (@RajeevRC_X) October 9, 2026 Chandrasekhar, who served as Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, said all three satellite communication licensees were broadly at the same stage of securing the necessary clearances, with security assessments preceding spectrum allocation. He also clarified that he was expressing his personal views and did not speak for the government. I have used Starlink and I think its awesome technologyand represents a new era in mobility innovation. No doubt. But a country has to plan for itself and its interests before every new choice. Thats what India is doing. Patience is unavoidable and in this case is a necessity," he said. What Did Elon Musk Say About Starlinks India Entry? The BJP leaders remarks come amid a public exchange between Musk and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over the delay in launching Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Musks SpaceX. Musk argued that Starlink has spent years complying with Indian laws and regulatory requirements but is still waiting for the final approvals needed to begin commercial operations. The government has rejected suggestions that Starlink is being treated unfairly, maintaining that satellite communication operators must satisfy the same regulatory and security requirements. Why Is National Security Central To The Starlink Debate? Chandrasekhar argued that satellite communication services present security challenges that need to be addressed before commercial operations begin. Referring to the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks and the Pahalgam terror attack, he said satellite communications have been used by terrorists and that satellite-based voice-over-internet protocol (VoIP) services and encryption create additional challenges for security agencies. The concerns relate to the ability of authorities to monitor communications, enforce lawful interception requirements and ensure that satellite networks comply with Indias security framework. Satellite services can also operate in areas where conventional mobile networks are unavailable, making security oversight particularly important. These concerns do not mean satellite internet technology cannot be secured, Chandrasekhar said, adding that the country needs to build the capabilities required to ensure safety and trust. Starlink, for its part, has said it has built its Indian operations around local regulatory and security requirements. Lauren Dreyer, SpaceXs vice-president of Starlink Business Operations, said the company had established controls at multiple levels and was keeping Indian user data within the country. What Is Holding Up Starlinks India Launch? Starlink has secured a licence to provide satellite communication services in India and has received authorisation from the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe). However, it is still awaiting the final clearances required to launch commercial services. The government has said the security assessment process applies to the licensed satellite communication operators Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Friday that the companies could begin operations after meeting the required security protocols and completing the necessary regulatory milestones. The government has also maintained that its approach is intended to allow competition rather than create a monopoly. Starlinks entry could expand broadband access in remote and underserved areas, where laying fibre-optic cables or building conventional mobile infrastructure can be difficult. However, its launch also raises questions about spectrum allocation, competition with established telecom operators and the security obligations of satellite networks. Rajeev Chandrasekhar responded to Elon Musk by asserting that national security and regulatory compliance cannot be compromised for new technology, emphasizing that India operates on principles of being open, safe, trusted, and accountable. He noted that satellite communications have historical security implications linked to terrorism, making patience and rigorous checks a necessity.

headline: 'We Are All Human First': Delhi Police's Fresh Appeal Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest
content: Delhi Police has tightened security across the capital with over 25000 personnel deployed ahead of a planned protest by Cockroach Janta Party on October 10. With Delhi gearing up for the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest on October 10, the Delhi Police has shared an emotional appeal asking citizens to look beyond the uniform and remember the humanity shared by both the public and the force. What Delhi Police Said - Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest On October 10, Says They Did Not Follow Rules - Delhi Metro To Shut 57 Stations From 9 PM Tonight Ahead Of CJP's Planned Protest | Full List Here - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - CJP Oct 10 Protest: Delhi Police Step Up Vigil, Track 2,800 'Criminals', Monitor Buses, Borders In a post on X, the police wrote: An Open Letter to Every Citizen. Because beyond every uniform, every opinion and every disagreement, were all human first." An Open Letter to Every Citizen Because beyond every uniform, every opinion and every disagreement, were all human first. Delhi Police (@DelhiPolice) October 9, 2026 The post featured an image carrying a message in Hindi, acknowledging citizens right to raise their voices while reminding them that police personnel, too, have families and loved ones. The message read: Dear Citizen, Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki suraksha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska apna parivar hai, apne log hai. The Delhi Police shared an emotional appeal on X ahead of a planned protest on October 10. The Ministry of Home Affairs made around 23,000 Central Armed Police Forces personnel available to the Delhi Police. The additional deployment is expected to take the number of central force personnel to more than 25,000. The Delhi Police denied permission for the CJP's proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation closed entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9 pm on October 9. Farq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi. (Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is a human being, who has a family and loved ones of their own. The only difference is the uniform, not our humanity.) Also Read: How Do We Balance It?: SC On Curbs In Delhi Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest The message comes as the capital prepares for heightened security ahead of the planned demonstration, called amid demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police Chief Calls For Restraint Separately, Delhi Police Joint Commissioner Madhur Verma urged personnel to maintain restraint while handling crowds, saying the forces strength lay in managing situations with discipline and dignity. Prepare for the storm. Practise restraint. Protect the peace. Because the true strength of the police is not merely in controlling a crowd, but in doing so with discipline, dignity and minimum force," Verma, Joint Commissioner of Police (Central Range), said in a post on X. Delhi Turns Into Fortress The appeal comes amid extensive security preparations, with the Ministry of Home Affairs making around 23,000 Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel available to the Delhi Police for deployment between October 8 and 12. The additional deployment is expected to take the number of central force personnel in the capital to more than 25,000, officials said. The Delhi Police has denied permission for the CJPs proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing violations of rules during an earlier protest. A senior officer said the application was received on October 7, three days before the planned event, whereas the rules require applications to be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Metro Curbs, Train Cancellations Ahead Of Protest Security and traffic-related measures have also affected public transport. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) closed entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9 pm on October 9, citing security reasons. Also Read: Railways Cancel Mail, Express Trains Arriving At Delhi Stations Ahead Of Oct 10 Anti-CEC Protest The Railways has also cancelled certain Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10, citing the likelihood of severe road congestion around the stations. Officials said police would deploy multi-layered barricades and use CCTV cameras to monitor the situation from control rooms. Face-recognition cameras would also be installed across the capital, while vigilance has been stepped up at several Delhi border points, including Ghazipur, Chilla, Tikri, Singhu, Gurugram, Kapashera, Loni and Badarpur. The Delhi government has also ordered liquor shops to remain closed on October 9 and 10, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. With inputs from PTI The Delhi Police denied permission because the application was submitted on October 7, only three days before the planned October 10 event, whereas rules require requests to be filed at least 10 days in advance. Additionally, authorities noted that Section 163 is in force, rendering any unauthorised gathering illegal.

headline: Bengal Bypoll Result: BJP's Big Win In Minority-Dominated Rejinagar Puts Spotlight On Minority Vote
content: The win comes as the BJP seeks to position development and governance as central themes in its outreach to minority voters in the state The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)s victory in West Bengals Rejinagar assembly constituency, where more than 72 per cent of the population belongs to minority communities, has emerged as one of the key talking points in the bypoll counting on Friday. The BJP has attributed the win to its development pitch, with the party claiming that minority voters have also backed it. The BJP won Rejinagar on Friday by 72,000 votes and Nandigram by 1,22,000 votes. After the victory, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said: We have got 60 per cent Muslim votes from Rejinagar and 80 per cent Muslim voted from Nandigran. Bengali-speaking Muslims are moving towards BJP." - BJPs Maharashtra Outreach: Street Plays To Spotlight PM Modis 25-Year Public Life Journey - BJP Picks Dinesh Arya For Uttarakhand Rajya Sabha Poll, Koel Mallick Nominated From Bengal - From Nandigram To Nagaon: Key Results Of Bypoll Battle Across 6 High-Stakes Seats Arrive Today - Better Off In Dubai: Humayun Kabir Concedes Defeat As AJUP Trails BJP In Rejinagar The trend is significant given Rejinagars demographic profile and its recent electoral history. In the previous assembly election, held just four months ago, AJUPs Humayun Kabir won the seat with around 50 per cent of the votes. Speaking to News18, BJP state president Shamik Bhattacharya said, People have voted for the development model. This time, minority voters in Rejinagar have also voted for us." Development Pitch At The Centre Of BJP Campaign Adhikari had made industrial development and employment key themes during the BJPs campaign in Rejinagar. Murshidabad district has long faced concerns over limited industrialisation and job opportunities, making economic development a significant local issue. The BJPs win has therefore drawn attention to whether its development-focused campaign has resonated with voters in a constituency where the partys electoral prospects are being viewed through the lens of its minority outreach. BJPs Minority Outreach Also In Focus The Rejinagar trend comes amid the BJPs efforts to highlight its outreach to minority voters elsewhere in West Bengal. Ahead of the October 6 bypoll in Nandigram, Adhikari had appealed to members of the minority community to extend a hand of friendship, pitching development and governance as common priorities. On Friday, the chief minister flashed a victory sign and said, Friendship bana liya," echoing that appeal. The remark appeared to reinforce the BJPs message that it had made inroads among sections of the minority electorate. The Bharatiya Janata Party won the Rejinagar assembly constituency by 72,000 votes and the Nandigram constituency by 1,22,000 votes during the Friday bypoll counting.

headline: 'How Do We Balance It?': SC On Curbs In Delhi Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest
content: Sibal told the court that certain trains scheduled to reach New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10 had been cancelled at source. The Supreme Court on Friday questioned petitioners challenging restrictions in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest on October 10, asking how it could balance the rights of protesters with those of citizens seeking access to public transport and essential facilities without hearing from the protest organisers. How do we balance if the scales are not here before us? Give us something," the court asked the petitioners, seeking details about who was organising the protest and how many people were expected to attend. - CJP-AAP Link? Congress Leader Reetam Singh Makes Big Allegations | Cong Vs AAP | News18 - 'Every Woman Should Feel Safe, Even At 10 PM': Supreme Court's Tough Talk On Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR - 'Create Fear In The Minds Of Culprits': SC's 5 Big Observations On Women's Safety In Delhi - Supreme Court To Hear Pleas Seeking Suspension Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Challenging EC Decisions To strike a balance, we need two things: citizens before us who want their basic rights, and the group that wants to protest. We do not have the latter before us," the court pointed out. Train Cancellations, Metro Curbs In Capital Reach SC The matter was mentioned by senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who flagged the cancellation of certain trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, as well as a Delhi Police proposal to close entry and exit points at 57 Metro stations. Also Read: We Are All Human First: Delhi Polices Fresh Appeal Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest All trains are cancelled, metro stations are closed. You cannot move anywhere. What is happening to my country? This is a peaceful protest," Sibal told the court. The Supreme Court questioned petitioners challenging protest restrictions in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) planned protest on October 10. The court sought details about the protest organizers and expected attendance to balance rights of protesters and citizens. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal flagged train cancellations and Delhi Police's proposal to close entry and exit points at 57 Metro stations. Around 23,000 Central Armed Police Forces personnel were deployed, and preparations for detention centers were made. The CJP called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and demanded changes to the electoral process. When Solicitor General Tushar Mehta responded, It is our country," Sibal clarified that he meant the country belonged to both of them. Advocate Prashant Bhushan said, The whole of Delhi has been shut down," while senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan argued that peaceful protest should not be treated as unlawful simply because permission had not been granted. Speaking against the curbs, senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said, You cannot shut down an entire city because you are incapable." Sibal further raised concerns over reported restrictions affecting hotels and other facilities, checks at Delhis borders, the deployment of around 23,000 Central Armed Police Forces personnel and preparations for detention centres. SC Seeks Details Of Protest Organisers The bench asked the petitioners to provide details about the organisers and the expected turnout, indicating that these details would help it consider how to balance the competing interests. Justice Bagchi said the material placed before the court appeared to indicate a blanket restriction on certain common facilities, including transport access and other essential services, potentially affecting ordinary citizens. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, while upholding peoples right to protest and assemble, said that the demonstrations should be within the ambit of the law. Also Read: Railways Cancel Mail, Express Trains Arriving At Delhi Stations Ahead Of Oct 10 Anti-CEC Protest Let us look at this from the prism of law. No doubt there is a right to association, but it has to be exercised according to law," the court stated. The counsels told the apex court that the CJP, who had organised the protests, had sought permission from the police; however, it was denied. Justice Bagchi said that the court needs to first understand the protests ground reality. If the protest is held with permission, it is a legal protest. Even if it does not strictly adhere to the law, we never say that people do not have the right to protest; however, they do so at their own risk," the judge stated. Speaking about the curbs, the SC emphasised the need for balance. If we injunct this, we will also injunct the association, then will that be fair? No, because there is a right [to protest]!," Justice Bagchi said. The matter was listed for 2 pm on Friday, when the court was to consider the pleas challenging the restrictions ahead of the planned protest. The CJP has called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and has demanded changes to the electoral process. The Delhi Police has not yet granted any permission to the CJP for the planned protest. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal flagged the cancellation of trains arriving at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, along with a Delhi Police proposal to close entry and exit points at 57 Metro stations.

headline: INDIA Bloc Delegation To Meet President At 8 PM Amid Protests Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: The meeting comes as Opposition MPs continue their protests for the third consecutive day, demanding CECs resignation over alleged irregularities in the electoral process. The INDIA bloc is scheduled to meet President Droupadi Murmu at 8 pm on Friday amid the escalating row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The demonstrations have also spread beyond Delhi. In Bihar, senior RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav led a parallel protest in Patna, while Mamata Banerjee said she would join the INDIA blocs demonstrations in Delhi. CISF Strengthens Security For CEC Amid the controversy, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) has deployed additional reserve" personnel to strengthen the Z+ category security cover for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, officials said. Liquor Shops To Remain Shut On October 9 And 10 The Delhi government has directed all retail liquor shops to remain closed on October 9 and 10 as a preventive measure aimed at maintaining public order," citing inputs from Delhi Police and planned protests by the Cockroach Janta Party against Kumar. Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest Delhi Police has rejected an application seeking permission for a demonstration planned for October 10 over the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner. Officials cited the short notice, previous non-compliance and prevailing law-and-order concerns. Police also cautioned that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remains in force across the New Delhi district, prohibiting unlawful assemblies or protests. Speaking to ANI, Joint Commissioner of Police (Joint CP) Nupur Prasad said the application did not meet the requirement of giving at least 10 days prior notice under established police guidelines. An application was submitted in the New Delhi district giving intimation that they intend to hold a demonstration-a protest-on October 10 regarding the accountability of the CEC. This intimation was examined and considered, and it was found that, first of all, it was received at very short notice. As per our laid-down guidelines, we require this at least 10 days before the dharna/protest, which was not the case here," Prasad said. (With inputs from ANI) The INDIA bloc delegation is meeting President Droupadi Murmu to address the escalating row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and to press for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Satheesan should resign as Kerala CM if assembly illegal: Rajeev Chandrasekhar hits back at electoral roll claims
content: BJP state president Rajeev Chandrasekhar on Friday said the party will question the legitimacy of the Congress-led government in Keralam in the upcoming Assembly session, following Congress leaders remarks questioning the validity of elections over the SIR exercise. The Congress-led Opposition is staging protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging malpractice in the revision of electoral rolls. Chandrasekhar in a post on X, said the party would raise the issue in the Assembly, which is scheduled to meet from October 12. Our Legislative Party Leader Gopakumar is going to write a letter to the Speaker, he said. What is the legitimacy of this Assembly? Is this an illegal Assembly or a legal one, Chandrasekhar asked. BJP has three MLAs in the 140-member state assembly following the election held in April this year after the SIR in Keralam. The first thing to be discussed in the Assembly, which affects me, V Muraleedharan, Gopakumar (All BJP legislators) and 137 MLAs, is whether all of us are illegal, he said. Chandrasekhar demanded that Chief Minister V D Satheesan clarify the issue on the floor of the House. If it is illegal, he should resign, the BJP leader said. Meanwhile, KPCC president and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph dismissed the BJPs stand, saying it was coming up with lame excuses. Joseph said he had filed petitions in the Kerala High Court and later in the Supreme Court over the electoral process and obtained directions. He also said Congress leaders had repeatedly raised their concerns about SIR at meetings convened by the electoral officer in charge of the assembly elections in Keralam. As the KPCC president, I myself filed petitions in the Kerala High Court and later in the Supreme Court, obtained directions, and spoke multiple times in all the meetings convened by the Electoral Officer who was in charge of the election at that time. We were the ones who had complaints, he said. Joseph said he had attended the meetings and raised concerns over the electoral process, while questioning whether the BJP or the CPI(M) had raised similar complaints. He said the Election Commissions approach should be to ensure that eligible citizens were included in the electoral rolls rather than focus on deleting names. The stand taken by the Election Commission regarding a voter should be aimed at making the vote available to a citizen. It shouldnt be about rejecting votes, but about including votes, he said. Joseph alleged that concerns over the SIR process had also been raised at the national level, citing media reports of disagreements within the Election Commission over certain decisions. Responding to a question on the BJP winning three seats in the Assembly election, Joseph said the party had won constituencies previously held by the ruling front and had also defeated candidates of both the CPI(M)-led front and the UDF. The election in Keralam was largely peaceful, he said. Asked about the objective behind the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) questioning the validity of the elections, Joseph said the group would have to explain its position. CPI(M) leader P Rajeev, meanwhile, said unusual variations in voter numbers had been reported in several constituencies and called for closer scrutiny of their possible impact on the election results in Keralam. In some constituencies, the votes have increased unusually. In other constituencies, the votes have decreased significantly. Therefore, the issue that this was not a normal pattern has been raised, he said. He alleged that the SIR exercise has been used to advance the BJPs political interests and called for a united effort to ensure a transparent and democratic electoral process. Rajeev also said that some parties in the INDIA bloc have called for a return to paper ballots, adding that concerns about the electoral process are being discussed at the national level.

headline: Why India Wants Answers Before Starlink Goes Live: Lessons From Iran's Unauthorised Terminals | Exclusive
content: Government sources say Indias satellite internet licensing framework is about ensuring that foreign-controlled satellite networks comply with Indias security and spectrum needs Indias prolonged clearance process for Elon Musks Starlink satellite internet service is rooted in national security concerns and the need to retain sovereign control over communications networks, government sources told CNN-News18 on Friday, pointing to the satellite operators operations in Iran as a case that highlights the risks of connectivity functioning without local authorisation. According to government sources, Indias satellite internet licensing framework is designed to apply equally to all operators, with security assessments mandatory before final operational clearance. The process, they said, is not about favouring one company over another but about ensuring that foreign-controlled satellite networks comply with Indias security, licensing and spectrum requirements. - What If Starlink Won't Switch Off? Study Flags Data And Security Risks India Faces With Musk's Network - Baseless, Misconceived: Govt Refutes Elon Musks Oligarch Claim Over Starlinks India Hurdles - Elon Musks Starlink Faces Roadblocks In India: Oligarchs Claim, Security Concerns Explained - Starlink in India News: Telecom Minister Scindia Says No Monopoly, 3 Companies Get SATCOM Licences The concerns assume significance amid the ongoing dispute over Starlinks entry into the Indian market, after Musk alleged that powerful business interests were obstructing the service to protect their dominance. The government has rejected the allegation, describing claims of discrimination in the regulatory framework as baseless and misconceived". Government sources have cited Starlinks operations in Iran, where terminals were reportedly brought into the country and used to provide internet connectivity without local authorisation, as an example of the challenges satellite technology can pose to national telecom controls. An intelligence note accessed by CNN-News18 during anti-government protests in Iran reportedly detailed the activation and use of Starlink connectivity despite restrictions imposed by Iranian authorities. According to the note, between 6,000 and 50,000 terminals were covertly smuggled into the country, providing uncensored internet access to an estimated 100,000 users. Why Starlinks Iran Operations Matter To India The Iran episode has become relevant to Indian regulators because satellite internet can provide connectivity in areas where terrestrial telecommunications infrastructure is unavailable, disrupted or restricted. Unlike conventional broadband services, which generally depend on local fibre networks, telecom towers and other ground infrastructure, Starlink uses a constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit to connect user terminals to the internet. Depending on the network architecture and regulatory arrangements, satellite connectivity can reduce reliance on domestic terrestrial infrastructure. Government sources are concerned that a foreign-controlled satellite network could potentially continue providing connectivity during civil unrest, even when local authorities have imposed restrictions on terrestrial telecom services. Such a capability, they argue, raises questions about the enforcement of lawful interception requirements, compliance with emergency internet shutdown orders and the ability of security agencies to monitor communications in sensitive areas. The concerns are particularly relevant for Indias border regions and conflict zones, where unauthorised satellite terminals could potentially provide communication channels outside established domestic regulatory arrangements. The issue is not limited to Starlink alone. Government sources maintain that any satellite operator whose services can function without the necessary local authorisation must be assessed for the risks it could pose to national security and sovereign control over communications. Iran Took The Matter To The International Telecommunication Union Iran has raised the issue of unauthorised Starlink terminals before the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies. The ITUs Radio Regulations Board has examined Irans complaints concerning Starlink transmissions from within its territory without authorisation. The board has reiterated that satellite terminals operating in a country require the relevant national authorisation and has urged the administrations associated with Starlinks satellite systems to take action to disable unauthorised terminals. Article 18 of the ITU Radio Regulations provides that transmitting stations cannot be established or operated by private individuals or enterprises without a licence issued by, or on behalf of, the relevant government, subject to the regulations provisions. The ITU proceedings underscore a central issue for regulators: the terms and conditions imposed by a satellite operator on its customers do not, by themselves, replace the requirement for authorisation from the country in which a terminal is operating. For Indian authorities, the episode highlights the limits of relying solely on an operators assurances that its services will comply with domestic rules. Regulators must also consider whether unauthorised terminals can be identified and disabled, and whether the operator can enforce restrictions when required. Why India Requires Security Clearance Before Starlink Can Launch Indias satellite communication framework requires operators to meet licensing, security and spectrum-related conditions before commencing commercial services. The government has said that Starlink and other licensed satellite communication operators are subject to the same regulatory framework and must undergo security assessments before receiving final operational clearance. The Ministry of Communications has maintained that the process is non-discriminatory. The assessment is particularly important because satellite networks operate across national boundaries and rely on infrastructure that is not always located within the territory where their services are consumed. Indian security agencies are concerned about whether satellite operators can ensure compliance with lawful interception protocols, prevent unauthorised use of terminals and respond to government directions during emergencies. The ability to restrict services in specific locations, including sensitive border areas, is another consideration. Authorities must be satisfied that the necessary safeguards can be implemented before a service is permitted to operate commercially. Spectrum assignment also remains a key part of the process. Satellite operators must comply with the technical and regulatory conditions governing the use of radio frequencies to prevent harmful interference and ensure that services operate within the authorised framework. Government sources argue that the time taken to complete these assessments should be viewed in the context of due diligence rather than as evidence of an attempt to obstruct a particular company. India's prolonged clearance process for Starlink is driven by national security concerns and the need to maintain sovereign control over communications networks, ensuring foreign-controlled networks comply with local licensing, spectrum, and security requirements. Additionally, security agencies are reviewing potential risks such as signal spillover, lawful interception compliance, and data routing concerns associated with foreign-operated satellite networks.

headline: Delhi Metro To Shut 57 Stations From 9 PM Tonight Ahead Of CJP's Planned Protest | Full List Here

The proposed restrictions are expected to remain in place throughout Saturday until the situation normalises. According to a report by news agency ANI, Delhi Police have also proposed reducing the frequency of metro trains passing through the identified stations, depending on the security situation. - Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest On October 10, Says They Did Not Follow Rules - We Are All Human First: Delhi Police's Fresh Appeal Ahead Of Oct 10 CJP Protest - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - 'Absolutely Shocking': Kejriwal Hits Out At Delhi Police For Detaining AAP Leaders At Delhi Protest The request was conveyed to DMRC in an official communication dated Thursday, October 8. Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) Rajneesh Gupta requested the metro corporation to take necessary measures at the identified stations, citing the likelihood of unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations". The proposed restrictions cover metro stations in central, north, south, east and northeast Delhi. Several stations serving prominent locations in the national capital, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, New Delhi, Mandi House, Supreme Court and Kashmere Gate, feature on the list. The proposed measures come ahead of the CJPs youth-led protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The party has raised allegations of vote theft" and voter-list manipulation. The protest is linked to allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and claims that Form 6, a key document used for voter registration, was altered by bypassing the Chief Election Commissioners two colleagues. The allegations against the Chief Election Commissioner remain claims raised by the protesters. In its communication to DMRC, Delhi Police sought precautionary arrangements at the identified stations in view of the planned demonstrations at Jantar Mantar and other locations in the New Delhi district. The police also requested the metro corporation to issue the necessary directions to its officers and staff to implement the proposed measures. CJP Activist Alleges Detention Of Protesters Meanwhile, CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke alleged that several activists had been detained across the country ahead of the planned protest. In a post on X, Dipke claimed that Thousands of youngsters have been detained across the country by the BJP government ahead of our October 10 protest." He also said that the alleged detentions would not deter the protesters and reiterated his intention to march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday. Ill be landing in Delhi tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar, come what may," he wrote.
