headline: 'No Monopoly In India': Jyotiraditya Scindia Dismisses Elon Musk's Starlink Claims
content: Jyotiraditya Scindia criticised Congress over the Starlink licence row, reiterating the government's position on security clearances and spectrum allocation for satcom firms. Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia on Friday reiterated that the government had granted licences to three satellite communication companies and maintained that commercial operations could begin only after the required regulatory conditions were fulfilled. He also slammed the Congress over its position on the licensing of satellite internet services in India, saying the opposition party lacked clarity on the issue. I dont think they themselves know whether they are going left or right," Scindia said, referring to the Congress, while responding to a question on the recent exchange between Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on X. - Starlink in India News: Telecom Minister Scindia Says No Monopoly, 3 Companies Get SATCOM Licences - Rahul Gandhi Offers Drink To Priyanka, She Sniffs It And Says No; BJP Says Even Family Doesnt Trust - Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Named In FIR For 'Assaulting, Obstructing Cops' During Protest In Delhi - Congress Delhi Protest | Rahul Gandhi Pushes Women Cop; BJP Releases Video | Jantar Mantar | News18 They first had a problem initially with a certain person getting a licence. Now they have a problem, and they have allied with that person in terms of why hes not getting the licence. I dont know whether they have clarity in terms of where they are going," the minister said. Scindia added that the governments position on satellite communication services was clear and that the regulatory process applied to the three licensed companies. But that is the case with the Congress, which is to be expected. We are very clear on our stand. Three parties have got a licence," he said. Scindia Explains Governments Position On Satcom Licences The minister said the assignment of spectrum and the commencement of commercial services would depend on the completion of the prescribed regulatory processes. Jyotiraditya Scindia accused the Congress of lacking clarity over its position on satellite communication licences. The minister said spectrum allocation and commercial operations would depend on the prescribed regulatory and security requirements. The government maintains that all three licensed satcom companies are subject to the same security assessment process. As and when the government decides the charge system on a revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil the security conditions, then they can start operations," Scindia said. | Delhi: Following Rahul Gandhi and Elon Musks exchange on X, Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia says, I have already defined the governments stand and the governments policy, and I have mentioned to you that there are three parties that have the license. Theres not a single party. As far as the Congress party is concerned, I dont think they themselves know whether they are going left or right. They first had a problem initially with a certain person getting a license. Now they have a problem, and they have allied with that person in terms of why hes not getting the license. I dont know whether they have clarity in terms of where they are going. But that is the case with the Congress, which is to be expected. We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a license. As and when the government decides the charge system on a revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfill the security conditions, then they can start operations." ANI (@ANI) October 9, 2026 The governments position is that all three licensed satellite communication companies must demonstrate compliance with the applicable security requirements before proceeding towards commercial operations. The Ministry of Communications said on Thursday that security assessments were underway for all three licensees. It maintained that the authorisation framework for telecommunications, including satellite communication services, was fair and non-discriminatory. The ministry also said that a company could proceed to the next step of seeking spectrum assignment once its security assessment was completed. It added that all three entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage. Minister of State for Communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani had also said that the Department of Telecommunications had issued licences and provisional spectrum to satellite communication companies, while security clearance remained pending with the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Department of Telecom has issued licences to all satcom companies as well as provisional spectrum. Now the issue is pending with MHA for security clearance. As soon as it is cleared, they will get it. It has nothing to do with one company," Pemmasani said on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress. Scindias remarks came after Musk questioned the delay in granting Starlink approval for commercial operations in India, stating that the company had spent five years complying with Indian laws and government requirements. In a post on X on Thursday, Musk wrote, Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?" Responding to Musk, Rahul Gandhi said, Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." Musk subsequently thanked Gandhi for his response, writing, Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling." The government has maintained that the same regulatory framework and security requirements apply to all three licensees. The government also said that the necessary security clearances and spectrum-related approvals must be completed before any licensed satellite communication company can commence commercial services. Commercial operations for satellite communication companies can begin only after the government decides the revenue-based charge system to assign spectrum and each company individually fulfills the mandatory security conditions and clearances.

headline: Mahishasura, Chamundi Hills And A Clash Of Narratives: What Is The Story Behind Mysuru's Mahisha Dasara?
content: Police have blocked Mahisha Dasara at Chamundi Hills, but celebrations will continue elsewhere in Mysuru. Why is Mahishasuras legacy sparking debate? Mysuru City Police have denied permission for the proposed Mahisha Dasara celebration atop Chamundi Hills and imposed prohibitory orders around the Mahishasura statue ahead of the event on Saturday, October 10. Mysuru City Police Commissioner Seema Latkar has reportedly prohibited gatherings within a 200-metre radius of the statue. The restrictions are set to remain in effect from midnight on Friday, October 9, until 6 am on Sunday, October 11, according to the details available. The exact dates and scope of the order should be confirmed with the police before publication. The Mahisha Dasara Aacharana Samiti had planned to organise the event at the hilltop. However, the police cited the need to prevent inconvenience to tourists visiting Chamundi Hills during the Dasara season and maintain law and order. While the proposed gathering at the hilltop has been restricted, Mahisha Dasara celebrations are scheduled to take place at Town Hall in Mysuru on October 10, according to local media reports. The decision has brought renewed attention to the competing interpretations of Mahishasuras legacy, the significance of Mahisha Dasara and its relationship with the citys celebrated Mysuru Dasara festival. What Is Mahisha Dasara And Why Is It Celebrated In Mysuru? Mahisha Dasara is an alternative cultural observance centred on Mahishasura, a figure traditionally portrayed in Hindu mythology as a buffalo-headed demon defeated by Goddess Durga, worshipped in Mysuru as Chamundeshwari. The Mahisha Dasara Aacharana Samiti has been organising the celebration since 2015. Its supporters seek to challenge the conventional portrayal of Mahishasura and highlight alternative interpretations of his historical and cultural significance. Members of the Samiti have claimed that Mahishasura was a historical ruler associated with Buddhism and that his legacy should be examined beyond the traditional religious narrative of a demon defeated by a goddess. For sections of Dalit and other marginalised communities, Mahisha Dasara has also become a platform to question dominant religious narratives and assert alternative accounts of local history and identity. The celebration is sometimes described as a counter to Mysuru Dasara. However, members of the organising committee have maintained that their intention is to highlight their interpretation of Mahishasuras history rather than oppose the citys traditional festival. How Is Mahisha Dasara Different From Mysuru Dasara? Although both observances are associated with the Mahishasura story, they differ in their religious interpretations, objectives and celebrations. Mysuru Dasara: Celebrating Chamundeshwaris Victory Mysuru Dasara is Karnatakas state festival and a major religious and cultural event associated with the Wadiyar dynasty, which ruled the Kingdom of Mysore. The festival celebrates Goddess Chamundeshwaris victory over Mahishasura, symbolising the triumph of good over evil. Its traditions combine Navaratri worship, royal ceremonies and large-scale public festivities. The Wadiyar rulers developed Dasara into a prominent royal celebration, and its traditions continued after the end of princely rule. Key attractions include the illumination of Mysuru Palace, cultural performances, religious ceremonies and the famous Jumboo Savari procession. During the procession, the idol of Chamundeshwari is carried in a golden howdah atop a decorated elephant. In 2026, Mysuru Dasara is scheduled to run from October 11 to October 21, with the grand procession taking place on Vijayadashami, October 21. Mahisha Dasara: Re-examining Mahishasuras Legacy Mahisha Dasara, by contrast, focuses on Mahishasura himself and the alternative historical and cultural interpretations associated with him. Its supporters challenge the portrayal of Mahishasura solely as a demon and seek recognition for narratives that present him as a ruler or an important figure in the regions cultural past. The observance has consequently become part of a wider discussion about caste, identity, historical memory and the interpretation of cultural traditions. Unlike the state-backed Mysuru Dasara, which features royal traditions and religious rituals, Mahisha Dasara is organised by a committee and supported by groups advocating an alternative interpretation of Mahishasuras legacy. Why Is Mahisha Dasara Controversial? The disagreement centres on competing interpretations of the same figure. In the traditional Hindu narrative, Mahishasura is defeated by the goddess, an event commemorated during Navaratri and Dasara. The Chamundeshwari temple atop Chamundi Hills is central to Mysurus religious identity, while the Mahishasura statue is a prominent landmark on the hill. Supporters of Mahisha Dasara argue that alternative accounts of the figure deserve recognition and discussion. Some view the celebration as a way to reclaim histories they believe have been marginalised in mainstream religious and cultural narratives. The issue has generated debate over religious beliefs, caste identities and the interpretation of regional history. The proposed gathering at Chamundi Hills has become particularly sensitive because the location is both a major pilgrimage destination and an important tourist attraction during the Dasara season. Police have cited tourist convenience and the maintenance of law and order as reasons for restricting the gathering at the hilltop. What Does History Say About Mysurus Connection With Mahishasura? The association between Mysuru and Mahishasura is reflected in local tradition and the citys religious identity. However, the precise historical origins of the citys name and its relationship with ancient references to Mahisha remain subjects of historical discussion. The Karnataka Governments official Gazetteer records early references to Mysuru in inscriptions, including a copper plate inscription dated to 862 AD that refers to the place as Maysooru. It also notes that the identification of the ancient place called Mahishamandala with present-day Mysuru is uncertain. These distinctions are important because the religious traditions surrounding Mahishasura and Chamundeshwari, as well as the alternative claims advanced by Mahisha Dasara supporters, should be distinguished from what can be established through inscriptions and historical records. The debate therefore involves not only religious belief but also competing interpretations of the regions past. Mysuru Palace Prepares For Traditional Dasara Celebrations Meanwhile, preparations are under way at Mysuru Palace ahead of the traditional Dasara celebrations beginning on October 11. The royal familys jewel-encrusted golden throne, known as the Ratna Simhasana, has been assembled in the palaces Durbar Hall as part of the customary preparations for the private royal durbar. The assembly of the throne is accompaniedby religious rituals and follows traditions maintained by the Wadiyar family. Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar is expected to occupy the throne during the private durbar, an important part of the familys Navaratri observances. The throne is assembled specifically for the festival period and remains a prominent symbol of Mysurus royal heritage. The preparations highlight the contrast between the established royal and religious traditions of Mysuru Dasara and the alternative historical narrative advanced by Mahisha Dasara organisers. With the proposed gathering around the Mahishasura statue facing restrictions, the Town Hall celebration scheduled for October 10 is set to remain a focal point in the ongoing debate over the figures historical, religious and cultural significance. Mysuru City Police denied permission to prevent inconvenience to tourists visiting Chamundi Hills during the Dasara season and to maintain law and order, imposing prohibitory orders around the Mahishasura statue.

headline: Metro Curbs, Cancelled Trains, Extra CCTVs: Delhi Turns Into Fortress Ahead Of CJP Protest Tomorrow
content: up comes after Delhi Police denied permission for the CJPs proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, saying the organisers had not followed the rules Delhi is bracing for heightened security ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest scheduled for Saturday against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with authorities rolling out extensive measures to control crowds and prevent disruptions across the national capital. From a shutdown of entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations to the cancellation of Mail and Express trains arriving at two major railway stations, the security measures are expected to affect public transport and movement across the city. Delhi Police has also denied permission for the proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing non-compliance with prescribed rules. - Jantar Mantar Protest Highlights: Atishi, Sanjay Singh Among 700 Detained, Internet Suspended Till 9 PM Amid Section 163 Restrictions - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - 26,000 CAPF Personnel To 20,000 Cops: Delhi Fortified Ahead Of CJPs Jantar Mantar 2.0 Against Gyanesh Kumar - Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed The protest has been called to demand the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have also been protesting over the issue, keeping the Election Commission at the centre of a wider political confrontation. 23,000 Paramilitary Personnel Deployed, CCTV Surveillance Expanded Security has been significantly stepped up across the Capital, with around 23,000 Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel made available for deployment ahead of the protest. The deployment includes personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Rapid Action Force (RAF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). ALSO READ | Delhi Police Check Hotels, Hostels Ahead Of CJPs Oct 10 Protest; Occupants, Staff Members Being Questioned Delhi Police has also installed 300 additional CCTV cameras ahead of the demonstration to strengthen surveillance and monitor crowd movement. Barricades have been erected at sensitive locations, while security arrangements are being intensified around Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street and other key areas of central Delhi. Authorities are also keeping a close watch on entry points into the Capital and the movement of buses that could bring protesters into New Delhi. Police personnel have been directed to coordinate with educational institutions and paying guest accommodation operators amid concerns about student participation. The arrangements come amid fears of a large turnout, with organisers expecting support from student groups and political parties. 57 Metro Stations Shut Entry And Exit Gates In a significant move that could affect commuters across Delhi, police have written to the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), seeking the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9pm on Friday as a precautionary measure ahead of Saturdays protest. The restrictions are aimed at limiting crowd movement towards sensitive areas and preventing large groups from converging on protest locations. The final implementation of the restrictions will depend on the authorities directions. Commuters have been advised to check official Metro updates before travelling, particularly if their journeys involve central Delhi or interchange stations. Railways Cancels Mail And Express Trains Arriving In Delhi The Indian Railways has also ordered the cancellation of Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi Railway Station and Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4am and 2pm on October 10, citing the possibility of severe traffic congestion around the stations. According to the railway order, trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on Friday and scheduled to reach either station during the specified window on Saturday will be cancelled at source. The cancellations could affect passengers travelling to the Capital during the morning and early afternoon. Travellers are advised to check their train status and seek updates from the Railways before setting out. Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest The security build-up comes after Delhi Police denied permission for the CJPs proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, saying the organisers had not followed the prescribed rules. Police have maintained that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar require advance permission and must comply with the applicable conditions governing public gatherings. The restrictions come amid heightened security and prohibitory measures in parts of the New Delhi district. The CJP has announced the protest to demand Gyanesh Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. AISA and several Opposition parties are also expected to support the mobilisation. The administration is preparing for the possibility of protesters attempting to reach central Delhi despite the denial of permission. Security agencies are on alert, with deployment plans aimed at preventing unauthorised gatherings and maintaining law and order. With transport curbs, additional surveillance and a large security deployment in place, the October 10 protest is set to pose a major logistical challenge for Delhi authorities, as they attempt to balance public order with the possibility of demonstrations in the heart of the Capital. Delhi Police denied permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar because the organisers failed to comply with the prescribed rules and regulations for public gatherings.

headline: 'Better Off In Dubai': Humayun Kabir Concedes Defeat As AJUP Trails BJP In Rejinagar
content: AJUP chief Humayun Kabir conceded defeat in Rejinagar as BJP established a strong lead over AJUP and TMC. BJP also led in Nandigram. Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief Humayun Kabir appeared to acknowledge defeat in Rejinagar even before the final results were announced on Friday, saying his political calculations had failed to deliver the outcome he had hoped for. Frustrated by his party candidates performance, Kabir remarked that he would be better off in Dubai". - 'I Could Be Detained Too If...': Suvendu Adhikari Reacts To Humayun Kabir's Detention In Murshidabad - Rejinagar Bypoll Results 2026 Highlights: BJP Candidate Shankharavh Sarkar Wins Rejinagar By 75816 Votes - By-Election Results 2026 Live Updates: BJP Wins Nandigram, Leads Rejinagar; TVK Ahead In Tamil Nadu - Saffron State, Splintered Rivals: Nandigram, Rejinagar Invert Bengals Historic Election Math The remarks came as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) established a substantial lead in Rejinagar, a Muslim-majority constituency in West Bengals Murshidabad district, according to Election Commission trends. After five rounds of counting, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar had polled 48,101 votes, placing him 34,501 votes ahead of AJUP candidate Golam Nabi Azad, who had received 13,600 votes. Azad is Humayun Kabirs son. The All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) candidate, Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, was in third place with 2,516 votes, while Congress candidate Abdullahil Kafi was fourth with 2,407 votes. The BJPs lead in Rejinagar marked a significant development in the bypoll, given the constituencys demographic profile and the partys strong showing against AJUP. BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar polled 48,101 votes in Rejinagar. AJUP candidate Golam Nabi Azad received 13,600 votes in Rejinagar. TMC candidate Rabiul Alam Chowdhury was third with 2,516 votes in Rejinagar. BJP's Hasirani Rath secured 66,415 votes in Nandigram. Congress candidate Milan Pradhan polled 16,493 votes in Nandigram. BJP Also Leads In Nandigram The BJP was also ahead in Nandigram in Purba Medinipur district, where Hasirani Rath, the mother of slain personal assistant to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, Chandranath Rath, was leading after six rounds of counting. Rath had secured 66,415 votes, giving her a lead of 49,922 over Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who had polled 16,493 votes. Santi Gopal Giri of the CPI was third with 2,495 votes, followed by Ali Md Sabe Miraj Khan of the All India Secular Front with 660 votes and Ehteshmul Haque of the Democratic Trinamool Congress with 345 votes. Counting began at 8 am on Friday under tight security, with 15 rounds scheduled in each constituency. The bypolls were held on Tuesday and are being closely watched as an early indicator of West Bengals political dynamics following the BJPs victory in the Assembly elections earlier this year. The Nandigram seat fell vacant after Adhikari, who had won both Nandigram and Bhabanipur, retained Bhabanipur. Rejinagar was vacated after AJUP founder Humayun Kabir retained the Nowda seat, which he had also won. With inputs from PTI Humayun Kabir acknowledged defeat after election trends showed the Bharatiya Janata Party establishing a substantial lead over his party's candidate, his son Golam Nabi Azad, leading Kabir to remark that his political calculations had failed.

headline: Delhi Rail Shutdown For 10 Hours: Rajdhani, Shatabdi, Lucknow Mail Among Trains Cancelled; 4 Ways To Check Status
content: Several Mail and Express trains to Delhi have been cancelled for October 10. Here are four official ways to check your train status and refund eligibility Indian Railways has ordered the cancellation of specified Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, October 10, 2026, citing anticipated severe road traffic congestion around the stations. Under the order issued on Friday, October 9, trains departing from their originating stations after 2 pm that are scheduled to arrive at either station during the 10-hour window will be cancelled at source. This means the affected trains will be cancelled at their originating stations, and passengers should check their individual train status rather than assume that all services to and from the two stations have been suspended. - Travelling To Delhi Tomorrow? Rajdhani Among Trains Cancelled Over CJP Protest | Check The List - Delhi Protest News Updates: 57 Metro Stations May Shut, Trains Cancelled Ahead of CJP Protest - 57 Delhi Metro Stations May Shut Gates Tonight, Police Write To DMRC Over Jantar Mantar Protests - CEC Protest Live Updates: Railways Cancels Trains, Police Seek Closure Of 57 Metro Stations; CJP Rally Denied Nod In view of a planned protest in Delhi and the traffic advisory issued for October 10, several services scheduled to depart from their originating stations on October 9 and 10 are reported to be affected. These include trains operating to and from New Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin and Tilak Bridge. The cancellations come amid planned protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. However, railway officials have cited anticipated traffic congestion as the reason for the move and have not confirmed that the protest itself prompted the cancellation order. Reports have also emerged of student activists being detained while travelling to Delhi for the demonstration. The Times of India reported that 14 women members of the All India Students Federation were detained at Itarsi railway station in Madhya Pradesh while travelling from Pune to Delhi. The reported detentions come ahead of the planned protest. Which Trains Have Been Cancelled? Two Rajdhani Express services departing from West Bengal on Friday, October 9, are among the confirmed cancellations. - 12301 Howrah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express: Cancelled for its October 9 journey. - 12313 Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express: Cancelled for its October 9 journey. Other trains from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and several other regions have also been included in reported cancellation lists. The following services have been named in the information available, but passengers should verify individual train numbers through official railway channels before travelling. List Of Major Cancelled Trains According to the information provided, some trains have also been cancelled because of the non-availability of rakes. The list above includes services reported as cancelled in connection with the disruption. It should not be treated as a definitive, fully verified list until the individual services have been checked against official railway notices. Are Lucknow And Patna Trains Also Affected? Some services connecting Uttar Pradesh and Bihar with Delhi have also been reported as affected. Among the Lucknow services mentioned are: - 12229 Lucknow Mail - LKONew Delhi AC Express Passengers should verify the train number and cancellation status through official railway channels. Services departing from Patna that have been reported as affected include: - Tejas Rajdhani Express - Sampoorna Kranti Express - Amrit Bharat Express - Magadh Express These services should be checked individually on the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or RailOne app. The cancellation status of every train listed above could not be independently confirmed against an official cancellation notice. How To Check If Your Train Is Cancelled: 4 Official Ways Passengers travelling to Delhi on October 9 or 10 should check their train status before leaving home. The following official channels can help confirm cancellations and service updates. 1. Check The NTES Website Or App The National Train Enquiry System (NTES) provides train-running information and updates about cancellations. - Visit the official NTES website. - Select Exceptional Trains, then open Cancelled Trains. - Choose the fully or partially cancelled list, where available, and search for your train number. - Check both October 9 and October 10, as some trains scheduled to arrive in Delhi on Saturday have been cancelled at their originating stations on Friday. The same information is available through the NTES mobile app. Menu labels may vary by version. 2. Use The RailOne App Indian Railways has advised passengers to check the RailOne app or NTES for further information. Search for your train by name or number and review the journey details before setting out. If the information appears inconsistent, confirm the status through the railway enquiry service. 3. Check Your PNR On IRCTC Passengers who booked their tickets online should check their PNR status on the IRCTC website or app before travelling. A PNR check can help confirm the status of the booking, but passengers should also consult NTES or RailOne for the latest information about train cancellations. 4. Call Railway Helpline 139 Passengers can dial 139, the Indian Railways enquiry number, for information about train-running status and reservation-related queries. This can be useful if online information is unclear or a passenger does not have reliable internet access. What About Station Display Boards? Station display boards provide arrival and departure updates, but passengers should not wait until reaching the station to check whether their train is operating. Roads around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin are expected to experience severe congestion during the affected period. Checking the train status in advance can help passengers avoid unnecessary journeys to the stations. What Happens To Your Ticket If The Train Is Cancelled? The refund process depends on how the ticket was booked. - E-Tickets: Under IRCTCs published refund rules, confirmed and RAC e-tickets for fully cancelled trains are eligible for an automatic full fare refund to the account used for booking. Passengers do not need to cancel the ticket online or file a Ticket Deposit Receipt (TDR) in this situation. - Counter Tickets: Passengers holding paper tickets booked at a railway reservation counter should follow the applicable railway refund procedure. IRCTCs published rules provide for cancellation of counter-booked i-tickets at a computerised reservation counter within 72 hours after the scheduled departure of a cancelled train. Passengers should check the applicable instructions for their ticket before visiting the counter. What Passengers Should Keep In Mind The railway order applies to specified Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10, provided they depart from their originating stations after 2 pm on October 9. It does not establish that every train operating to or from the two stations has been cancelled. Passengers travelling from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and other regions should verify their train numbers through NTES or RailOne before leaving home. The reported lists include additional services, but the status of each train should be confirmed through official railway channels. Indian Railways cancelled specified Mail and Express trains arriving at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday, October 10, 2026, if they departed after 2 pm on October 9. Affected services include the Howrah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express, Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express, Magadh Express, Tejas Rajdhani Express, Sampoorna Kranti Express, and Shatabdi Express from Kanpur Central.

headline: Madhya Pradesh police remove protesters from trains to Delhi, detentions in Gujarat
content: Ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys Saturday protest in the Capital, police in Madhya Pradesh intercepted and removed Delhi-bound protesters at Bhopal, Itarsi and Gwalior railway stations, with a senior Madhya Pradesh police officer saying at least 30 people had been detained and were counselled to return to their home states. We have removed the protesters (from the trains), the officer said, adding that those intercepted included people travelling from Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra. On Friday, the detention of two of the protesters from Itarsi railway station reached the Madhya Pradesh High Court, with the states Additional Advocate General issuing an urgent communication to senior police officials after habeas corpus petitions were filed seeking their production before the court. Police sources said Additional Advocate General Bramhadatt Singh informed the Director General of Police, the Narmadapuram Superintendent of Police, the Itarsi SHO and the Superintendent of Police (Railways), Bhopal, about the petitions seeking the production of Shravani Buva and Preeti Prashant Lodhe, who were taken into police custody at Itarsi railway station. According to police, when the matters came up for hearing on Friday, the High Court directed the state counsel to produce the two women on Monday or earlier. While they refused to get off the train then, Buva and the others were deboarded at the Itarsi station. While the CJP has called for a protest at Jantar Mantar, authorities and police in Delhi have enforced curbs to stop people from gathering, citing a denial of permission. CJPs Telangana and Andhra Pradesh units also claimed that seven of their activists had been detained by the MP police while travelling to Delhi for peaceful protest. Those detained, according to the CJP, include Stanley Korani, the outfits south zone coordinator. Four volunteers from Telangana and three from Andhra Pradesh, travelling to New Delhi to participate in a peaceful demonstration organised by the CJP, were forcibly taken off their train by police in Madhya Pradesh and placed under arbitrary preventive detention, a release issued by the outfit claimed. The Telangana volunteers have been identified as Korani, Rajesh Korapaka, Rangasai Reddy and Venkatesh Goud. They were travelling from Hyderabad to Delhi when railway police boarded their coach during a scheduled halt in Bhopal, forcibly deboarded them, and detained them, the release alleged. Another activist who did not wish to be named said that several youngsters from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh have already reached Delhi. In a separate incident, three CJP volunteers from Andhra Pradesh, Baba Fakhruddin, B Venkatesh and Renjith Rajeev, were lifted off a moving train in Gwalior. According to fellow travellers, around eight people entered the coach to take them away, a press release by the outfit claimed. Several activists from Gujarat were also detained on Friday either at police stations or in their houses. Some of them alleged that police made them sign undertakings that they would not go to Delhi for the CJP protest. Ahmedabad-based social worker Ashwin Vaghela claimed he and 54 others had planned to head to Delhi on Friday to participate in the protests, but the city police detained him and three other leaders of his group in his house. In Sabarkantha district, sarpanch of Vadvasa village Satyesha Leuva, who is the all-India vice-president of the Students Federation of India (SFI), alleged she was put under house arrest on Thursday evening, prompting her to move the High Court on Friday.

headline: Uttar Pradesh Has Become A 'Swastha Pradesh-Saksham Pradesh': CM Yogi
content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday shared the story of a Swastha-Saksham Uttar Pradesh with the people through his social media account on X Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday shared the story of a Swastha-Saksham Uttar Pradesh with the people through his social media account on X. He described the shift from the compulsion of seeking treatment to the assurance of healthcare security as the new identity of a Swastha Uttar Pradesh. - 'Producer Of Technology': Yogi Adityanath Showcases Uttar Pradesh's Progress To People Of State - 'Light Of Knowledge Reaching Children': CM Yogi Highlights Rise Of Digital Libraries In UP From 76 To 57,600 - 'Merit On The Field': Yogi Adityanath Highlights Positive Sporting Culture In Uttar Pradesh - Yogis 80-20 Jibe At Akhileshs Election Math: 'UP Rajya Sabha Contest Sets Tone For Assembly Polls' CM Yogi wrote: Under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and with a commitment to Antyodaya, the BJPs double-engine government in the state has moved beyond the weak healthcare system that prevailed before 2017 and is working decisively to make Uttar Pradesh Sawastha, Saksham, and Atmanirbhar. The biggest proof of this transformation is that Uttar Pradesh, once associated with the One District-One Mafia identity, is now setting new benchmarks in healthcare with its commitment to One District-One Medical College." Similarly, the number of MBBS seats has risen from 4,690 to more than 13,600. This has not only expanded opportunities for young people to pursue medical education but also improved access to quality healthcare closer to home for the general public. More than 10 crore people in the state covered under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana and the Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan are now able to live healthier lives with dignity and respect, free from worries about the heavy costs of treating serious illnesses. The journey from the compulsion of seeking treatment to the assurance of healthcare security has become the new identity of a Swastha Uttar Pradesh", he wrote. The number of medical colleges in Uttar Pradesh has increased from 36 in 2017 to 85, while MBBS seats have grown from 4,690 to over 13,600.

headline: Delhi CJP Protest: Rajdhani, Shatabdi among 245 cancelled trains, check full list
content: IRCTC Train Cancellation List October 10: Indian Railways has cancelled 245 trains on October 10 amid the expected traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations ahead of the CJP protest in Delhi. Passengers waiting at New Delhi railway station on Friday (Express Photo by Amit Mehra) On Thursday, around 5,000 passengers reportedly missed their trains due to heavy crowds and road blockades linked to the protest. headline: Noida International Airport Renamed Narendra Modi International Airport, UP Cabinet Approves Proposal
content: Yogi Adityanath says the Cabinet has approved a proposal to rename Noida International Airport in Jewar Narendra Modi International Airport. The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet has approved a proposal to rename the Noida International Airport in Jewar as Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced in Lucknow on Friday. Making the announcement, Adityanath said the Cabinet was grateful to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the airport, which he described as a major infrastructure project for the state. - Yogis 80-20 Jibe At Akhileshs Election Math: 'UP Rajya Sabha Contest Sets Tone For Assembly Polls' - 'Producer Of Technology': Yogi Adityanath Showcases Uttar Pradesh's Progress To People Of State - Yogi Adityanath Claims 80-20 Split Ahead of UP Assembly Elections Amid SP Controversy | News18 - Swami Vigyananand On PM Modi, Mandir & Hindutva | Kashi Vishwanath Corridor| Temple Movement | TRS He said the airport is expected to become Uttar Pradeshs largest airport and a major aviation hub in the country in the future. The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet is grateful to the Prime Minister for gifting the state the Noida International Airport at Jewar, which will be the largest airport in Uttar Pradesh and is set to become the countrys largest aviation hub in the future." The Cabinet also approves a proposal to name the Noida International Airport Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar," the Chief Minister said. Alongside the announcement, Adityanath highlighted infrastructure projects across Uttar Pradesh, including highways, rail connectivity, metro networks and freight corridors. He said the development of the Noida International Airport would further strengthen the states air connectivity. The UP Cabinet has approved a proposal to name Noida International Airport Narendra Modi International Airport. Adityanath highlighted highway, metro, rail and freight corridor projects across Uttar Pradesh. The Chief Minister credited farmers for their contribution to the Jewar airport project. The Chief Minister said approximately Rs. 60,000 crore had been invested in the construction of 42 national highways spanning 2,483 kilometres in the state. He also cited the completion of the Delhi-Saharanpur-Dehradun Expressway, Delhi-Meerut Expressway and Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway. Adityanath also referred to the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat train, describing it as the countrys first high-speed Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS). He said the project had been built at a cost of more than Rs. 30,000 crore. He added that metro rail networks had expanded in Lucknow, Kanpur, Agra, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. With the Noida International Airport at Jewar, Uttar Pradesh is reaching new heights in air connectivity," he said. Chief Minister Cites Freight Corridors, Defence And Textile Projects Adityanath also highlighted other infrastructure and industrial projects that he said were contributing to Uttar Pradeshs development. He referred to Dadri as a major junction connecting the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors, adding that more than 1,050 kilometres of the corridor passed through the state. The Chief Minister also cited the development of Indias first multi-modal inland port terminal on National Waterway-1 and a 100-acre freight village in Varanasi. In the industrial sector, he referred to the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor, including the BrahMos missile assembly unit in Lucknow, as well as the PM MITRA Textile Park being developed across 1,000 acres. The Chief Minister presented these projects as part of the states wider infrastructure and connectivity development, with the Jewar airport expected to add another major component to its aviation network. The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved a proposal to rename the Noida International Airport located in Jewar to Narendra Modi International Airport, as announced following a cabinet meeting.

headline: 'Deeply Offensive': India Hits Back At JD Vance Over 'Indentured Servants' Remark, Cites 'Painful Historical Connotations'
content: The Ministry of External Affairs said Indian professionals in the US were highly educated and skilled contributors whose work had helped drive economic growth and innovation India on Friday strongly objected to US Vice-President JD Vances description of foreign workers as indentured servants", calling the terminology deeply offensive" and saying it ignores the contributions of Indian professionals to the American economy and innovation ecosystem. Responding to questions about Vances remarks, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said Indian professionals in the United States were highly educated and skilled contributors whose work had helped drive economic growth and innovation. - JD Vance Calls H-1B Visa Programme Rife With Fraud, Says It Undercuts US Workers - JD Vance Calls H-1B Workers Indentured Servants, Internet Hits Back: Good Luck - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud We believe that such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem," the MEA said. ALSO READ | JD Vance Calls H-1B Visa Programme Rife With Fraud, Says It Undercuts US Workers Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity. Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," it added. The response comes after Vance criticised American companies for employing foreign workers through the H-1B visa programme and sponsoring them for permanent residency through the Permanent Labour Certification Programme, or PERM. What Did JD Vance Say About Foreign Workers? Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, Vance accused Microsoft of exploiting the US immigration system by laying off American employees while hiring foreign workers. He claimed that Microsoft had laid off 6,000 American workers in the previous year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. In other words, if you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants," Vance said. ALSO READ | Indian IT Firms Face US PERM Suspension: NASSCOM Says Immigration, Skilled Talent Mobility Are Two Distinct Issues He also argued that H-1B workers were vulnerable because their immigration status was tied to their employment, leaving them at risk of having to leave the country if they lost their jobs. When I say indentured servants, heres what I meanwhen somebody comes in on an H-1B, they are completely subordinate to that company," he said. Vance further claimed that H-1B workers earned around $20,000 less than American citizens in comparable positions, while workers brought in through foreign outsourcing firms earned around $48,000 less. These figures were cited by Vance in support of his argument that companies were using foreign labour to undercut American wages. The US administration has maintained that its actions are aimed at protecting American workers and addressing alleged abuses of the visa system. US Suspends Eight Companies From Green Card Programme The remarks came amid the US governments suspension of eight companies from the PERM programme, which allows employers to seek labour certification as part of the process of sponsoring eligible foreign workers for employment-based green cards. ALSO READ | Infosys To Tata: Which Indian Tech Firms Are Among 8 Hit By US H-1B, Green Card Crackdown The companies include Indian IT services firms Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and HCL, along with US-based Microsoft, Adobe and Capgemini. US officials said the action was intended to address alleged abuse of the system. Vance specifically accused Microsoft of replacing American workers with foreign employees, while the administration has also raised concerns about the role of outsourcing firms in hiring foreign labour. The suspension affects the companies ability to pursue the relevant labour-certification process for permanent residency applications. Its implications for individual workers will depend on their circumstances and the status of their applications. India's Ministry of External Affairs strongly objected to JD Vance describing foreign workers as "indentured servants," calling the terminology deeply offensive and stating that it ignores the major contributions of highly educated Indian professionals to the American economy and innovation ecosystem.

headline: Who Is Devashish Sharma? Former IAS Officer Turned BJP Candidate Leading In Assam's Nagaon Bypoll
content: A total of 15 candidates are contesting the by-election, with Sharma, Bora and Ajmal being the main contenders. BJP candidate Devashish Sharma was leading by 75,248 votes over his closest rival, AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal, as counting for the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election in Assam continued on Friday, according to the Election Commission (EC). Sharma, a former IAS officer, had received 1,81,017 votes, while Ajmal polled 1,05,769 votes. Congress candidate Sibamoni Bora was placed third with 29,826 votes, the EC website showed. - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - Nagaon Bypoll Result 2026 Live: BJP Candidate Widens Gap With Over 36,000 Votes - EC Teams To Visit 5 Poll-Bound States From This Week, UP Schedule Yet To Be Finalised - Why Mathura, Why Now? CM Yogi, BJP Chief Nitin Nabin To Take Stock Of UP Poll Strategy Vote counting began at 8 am under tight security, officials said. Postal ballots were counted first, followed by votes recorded in electronic voting machines (EVMs). The counting process is being conducted at Dawson Higher Secondary School and Nagaon Government Boys School in Nagaon, with 14 tables set up at each centre. Who Is Devashish Sharma? Devashish Sharma is a former civil servant who served as the District Commissioner of Nagaon in Assam before entering electoral politics. Born in Jorhat, he studied English literature and later completed a postgraduate diploma in Public Relations from Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan in New Delhi. Sharma began his career in the Assam Civil Services in 1992. During his administrative career, he served in Barpeta, worked as Special Officer to the then Assam Governor Lt Gen S K Sinha, and held positions including Deputy Resident Commissioner at Assam Bhawan in Mumbai and Commissioner of the Guwahati Municipal Corporation. He was posted as District Commissioner of Morigaon in 2022 before moving to Nagaon, where he served from June 2025. He took voluntary retirement on September 3, 2026, joined the BJP on September 8 and was named the partys candidate for the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election on September 11. 15 Candidates In The Fray The Nagaon parliamentary constituency comprises eight Assembly segments spread across Nagaon and Morigaon districts. A total of 15 candidates are contesting the by-election, with Sharma, Bora and Ajmal being the main contenders. Security has been tightened at both counting centres. Candidates and political parties have also been instructed to obtain permission from the district administration before organising any procession. Nagaon Bypoll Records 76.19% Voter Turnout The by-election, held on October 6, recorded a voter turnout of 76.19 per cent. The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi, who successfully contested the Assembly elections from Dispur on a BJP ticket earlier this year. The outcome of the by-election will not affect the balance of power in Parliament. The Nagaon constituency has 19.05 lakh eligible voters, including 9.43 lakh women and 50 third-gender voters. They were eligible to cast their ballots at 2,312 polling stations. Devashish Sharma is a former IAS officer and BJP candidate who is leading in the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election in Assam. He took voluntary retirement on September 3, 2026, joined the BJP on September 8, and was named the party's candidate on September 11.

headline: Former DMK Minister E.V. Velu, son E.V. Kumaran seek anticipatory bail in lake bed mining case
content: Former Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Minister E.V. Velu, 76, and his son E.V. Kumaran, 48, have filed anticipatory bail petitions before the Madras High Court in a case registered against them for allegedly excavating 45,72,058 cubic feet of sand from Malappambadi lake in Tiruvannamalai district to level the venue for the partys north zone youth wing conference held on December 14, 2025. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan on Friday (October 9, 2026) accepted a request made by State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to grant time till Tuesday (October 13) for filing written objections on behalf of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC). The judge orally advised the prosecution not to take any coercive action until then, since the first petitioner was a septuagenarian. The petitioners had chosen to seek advance bail, through their counsel Rahul Balaji, after the judge, earlier this week, rejected their plea for ex parte interim relief in two other petitions filed by them, urging the court to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against them. The DVAC registered the FIR on September 24, 2026, on the basis of a complaint lodged by Jayaram Venkatesan from the anti-corruption organisation Arappor Iyakkam. The complainant had alleged that the excavation was carried out on about eight acres of the waterbody in and around November 2025 to level land belonging to a private company of which Mr. Kumaran was one of the directors. It was claimed that the alleged illegal excavation had resulted in a loss of 8.22 crore to the public exchequer. However, both petitioners claimed they were innocent and had not committed any offence as alleged by the complainant. In his petition, Mr. Velu said that there was no overt act attributed to him in the complaint and that there was no specific allegation that he had influenced any government official during his stint as Minister last year. The allegation that the petitioners son E.V. Kumaran was responsible for the alleged excavation of gravel/lake-bed material is a hypothetical allegation, the mere fact that unauthorised excavation or mining is alleged to have taken place does not, by itself, furnish any basis to attribute the commission of such offence to the petitioner or his son, his advance bail petition read. Pointing out that he was the Minister of State Highways, Minor Ports and Public Works departments during the previous DMK regime, Mr. Velu said that even according to the complainant, Malappambadi lake was under the control of the Revenue, Corporation, and geology and mining authorities, none of whom were under his portfolio.

headline: A bank robbery, a murder, and a case that took Kerala police 19 years to crack
content: In 2007, two migrant workers vanished after the murder of a sawmill manager, leaving behind fake names and few clues. Now, an old photograph and new AI software have led police to one of them When Kerala Police entered the dusty, weather-beaten godown of a rice mill in Assams Dhemaji district this September, they had only one question for the bald man with a grey beard found working there: Are you Dilip Rajak? On September 20, the Malappuram crime branch police arrested Rajak, a 65-year-old migrant worker from Bihar, on charges of murdering the manager of a saw mill in 2007. For investigators, the arrest, which took them some 3,600 km, meant closing a nearly two-decade-long investigation that spanned Kerala, Assam and Bihar. Another accused from Bihar, Sanichar Baita, is still on the run, police said. Dilip had always feared that one day he would be caught by police, Crime Branch Inspector Ameerali V said. We had approached him after completing the entire fieldwork. With help from the Assam police, he was taken into custody. He did not resist. According to the police, Dilip and Sanichar moved to Kerala in early December 2007 in search of a job after working at rice mills in Assam. In Keralam, the two found a job at a sawmill at Perinthalmanna, where they gave their names as Umesh and Vinod from Assam. When the sawmill closed for a few days in mid-December, the two migrants decided to stay on, as did their manager Balakrishnan. Around the same time, a bank near the sawmill witnessed a robbery attempt, police said. When the saw mill opened a week later, the two migrants and Balakrishnan were found missing. Initially, nobody at the mill thought much of it. Balakrishnan had told the people at the mill that he would leave for Coimbatore, while his family at Vadakara in Kozhikode thought he was still there, Inspector Ameerali V said. On December 27, local workers at the mill found his body, hidden under a pile of sawdust. The body was covered with a cloth given to the migrant workers to sleep on, Ameerali said. In the investigation that followed, police found the two workers, who identified themselves as Umesh and Vinod, missing, and further inquiry into their background led to dead ends. But the calls the duo made back home to Bihar allegedly led to their first major lead. The duo didnt have a phone and made calls from a public pay phone, Ameerali said. The police had then found that the calls were made to Bihar, and realised that the duo was from there and not Assam. In February 2008, investigators traced the calls to the village of Dabhra under the Tarabari police station in Bihars Araria, only to realise the names they used were fake. Police realised that they were Dilip Rajak and Sannichar Bitta, but by then, Dilip had already left the village with his wife and son, Ameerali said. Locals told the police that the two had not visited their village and did not contact families. After this, police continued to periodically visit Assam but without success. In 2015, the crime branch took over the case. Our teams went to Bihar in 2021 and even in 2025, but we found that the suspects kept away from the village, the official said. That changed recently, when the police used Gandiva, an AI-driven analytical and search engine deployed over Indias National Intelligence Grid (NATGRID), to unify, cross-reference, and analyse massive volumes of security, financial, and demographic data. An intelligence-sharing platform, NATGRID connects multiple government agencies and databases, including Railways, police and telecom, helping enable intelligence-led investigations. According to Malappuram Crime Branch Superintendent of Police M P Mohanachandran Nair, investigators fed an old photo of Dilip into AI to age him and searched the database. That allegedly helped them strike gold they found a SIM card in Dilips name. When we secured Call Data Records, our suspicion grew. We found that the person changed SIM cards at least 15 times over the years, but made few calls and had fewer messages. Later, we identified the phones tower location, Ameerali said. On September 20, a four-member crime branch team arrested Dilip in Assam with help from local police and brought him back to Malappuram on September 28. Investigators say the bank robbery could be linked to the 2007 murder. The victim, Balakrishnan, might have seen their robbery attempt. The murder happened 14 days after they joined the sawmill. In Assam and in Bihar, the duo were known by their true identity, but in Kerala, they used a fake identity. That indicates they had a criminal intention, Ameerali said.

headline: 'Does Not Advance Shared Ambitions': India Pushes Back Against US PERM Move, Cites Immigrants' Role In Shaping America
content: India criticised the US decision to suspend major tech companies from the PERM programme and objected to remarks by US Vice President JD Vance. India on Friday criticised the United States decision to suspend eight major technology companies from its Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, saying the move does not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries. The government has also strongly objected to remarks made by US Vice President JD Vance about Indian professionals, calling the descriptions deeply offensive". - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud - PERM Vs H-1B: What Is The Difference, And Which One Does The US Suspension Affect? - TCS Says US Green Card Programme Suspension Wont Affect Hiring Strategy, Plans 15,000 Local Jobs - Indian IT Firms Face US PERM Suspension: NASSCOM Says Immigration, Skilled Talent Mobility Are Two Distinct Issues In a statement responding to the US Department of Labours announcement, India stressed that the PERM programme is separate from the H-1B visa system. The suspension does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents, although it could have implications for eligible employees pursuing permanent residency, or Green Cards. Also Read: US History Shaped By Immigrants: India Rebukes JD Vance Over Indentured Servants Remark Talent mobility adds value to both economies," the MEA statement said, arguing that the movement of skilled professionals creates opportunities for Indians while also benefiting US companies through access to specialised talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation. India described professional mobility as an area of substantial mutual benefit and said it expected all stakeholders to recognise its importance. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries," it said. India criticized the US decision to suspend eight major technology companies from its Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme. The US Department of Labour suspended Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe from the PERM programme. Since 2009, these companies requested almost three million foreign workers, received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals, and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. US Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing the system, claiming it laid off 6,000 American workers while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 Green Cards. The PERM suspension does not affect existing H-1B visas but could impact eligible employees pursuing permanent residency. India Calls Remarks On Indian Professionals Deeply Offensive India also took issue with comments made by Vice-President Vance in connection with the US action, saying they disregarded the contributions of highly educated and skilled Indian professionals to the American economy and its innovation ecosystem. The history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity," the statement said. Also Read: TCS Says US Green Card Programme Suspension Wont Affect Hiring Strategy, Plans 15,000 Local Jobs India added that the use of terminology carrying painful historical and colonial legacy connotations was deeply offensive". The government said it was continuing to monitor developments. US Suspends Eight Technology Companies From PERM Programme The US Department of Labour announced on Thursday that it was suspending Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe from the PERM programme. Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the decision alongside Vance, who heads the US Anti-Fraud Task Force. Sonderling said the department would neither accept new permanent labour certification applications involving the companies nor process pending ones. Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers. Theyve received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications," Sonderling said. He alleged that the companies use of foreign-worker programmes had come at the expense of American employees, saying: Thats hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers." Vance also accused Microsoft of abusing the system. There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," he said. Vance claimed Microsoft had laid off 6,000 American workers in the previous year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 Green Cards. Microsoft said around 80% of its H-1B applications filed in the previous fiscal year were intended to extend or change the status of existing employees, rather than recruit new workers. The company also said it paid H-1B employees the same as other workers performing comparable jobs. How The PERM Suspension Could Affect Green Cards The PERM programme is a key stage in the employment-based Green Card process for many foreign workers. Under the system, employers generally have to demonstrate that hiring a foreign national will not adversely affect the wages or job opportunities of similarly employed American workers. The suspension could therefore disrupt the permanent-residency process for eligible employees of the affected companies. However, it does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas or change the immigration status of those who hold them. The decision comes amid a wider effort by the Trump administration to tighten scrutiny of immigration and employment-based visa programmes. With inputs from Reuters, PTI The US Department of Labour suspended Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies, Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe from the PERM programme.

headline: 'What happened overnight?' BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over Elon Musk reply
content: The BJP Friday accused Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi of championing Elon Musks cause after the Congress leader exchanged posts with the billionaire over delays in licensing his Starlink satellite internet service in India. Bharatiya Janata Party vice-president Ram Madhav asserted that spectrum allocation would follow a transparent and non-discriminatory process. Musk, in a post on X Wednesday, accused unnamed oligarchs of obstructing Starlinks India launch to protect their market dominance. The SpaceX founder alleged the delay was intended to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people, adding, You can guess who they are, without identifying anyone. Musk wrote another post Thursday evening. Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India? To this, Gandhi replied, saying, Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy. Musk responded with Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling. Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling. Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 8, 2026 This is the Modi Government Madhav, in response, sought to remind Musk that he is not dealing with a banana republic but a big country which is respected, whose leadership is respected globally. The BJP leader also sought to underline that when it came to spectrum allocation, everything will happen in a transparent and non-discriminatory way. You should also be respectful towards this country and its leadership. Here there is a proper system, a non-discriminatory system in place to allocate spectrumMr. Musk was seeking to ridicule some of our leaders as oligarchs. Even Jio and Airtel, along with Starlink, are also waiting. In a very non-discriminatory way, the Government of India will take its decision at an appropriate time, he said. Taking on Gandhi, he said it was surprising that he who always used to accuse us of surrendering before the American leadership, before Musk, today, he has become a big champion of Elon Musks cause. The whole country would like to know what happened overnight. He should explain to the country. As far as the spectrum issue is concerned, we have seen that under the UPA government, their leaders were involved in spectrum-related corruption cases. The spectrum was sold indiscriminately, leading to huge corruption allegations. This is the Modi Government, he added. Centres statement On Thursday, the Centre defended its satellite communications licensing policy, saying it follows a fair and non-discriminatory process, a day after Musk accused certain oligarchs of holding up Starlinks India launch to protect their monopoly. In a statement, the Ministry of Communications said no applicant had yet been cleared to launch satellite communication services in India. It added that all providers must meet the countrys security requirements before receiving authorisation. Starlinks India launch remains held up by regulatory clearances, particularly security requirements, despite the companys claims that it has adapted its operations to comply with Indian rules. Speaking at the India Mobile Congress Wednesday, SpaceXs vice-president of Starlink Business Operations, Lauren Dreyer, said the company had built its India operations around local security and regulatory requirements, with safeguards at every level and provisions to keep Indian users data within the country.

headline: Delhi Police's 37-point dragnet to block CJP protests: In graphics
content: Trains cancelled, 60 metro stations closed, and hotel bookings restricted: Delhi Police have activated a 37-point dragnet across the national capital to prevent Saturdays Jantar Mantar demonstration against alleged voter roll irregularities. Here is how the security clampdown will impact commuters and visitors across the city. Delhi is heading towards a lockdown in effect if not in name as police prepare for Saturdays Cockroach Janta Party-led protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision. The police say they have learned from the last time the CJP wagon was in town, which was in June for protests that forced then-Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign over corruption in the public examination system. Specifically, senior officers believe there were two serious lapses last time, and have prepped what they believe is a fail-safe plan for the October 10 CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. Four layers of restriction between Delhi and Jantar Mantar Delhi Police has not granted permission for the Cockroach Janta Party and AISA protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. Step through what has been announced, from the railway station to the barricade. Updated 9 October. The Supreme Court has asked the authorities not to bring the Metro and railways to a complete halt. Items tagged Under review may change. Confirmedannounced Plannedbeing prepared Under reviewquestioned in court Rail and road into the capital Trains cancelled for 10 hours All trains to and from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations are cancelled from 4 am to 2 pm on Saturday, citing severe road congestion. The Supreme Court has asked that rail services not be completely suspended. No revised railway notice had been reported at the time of writing. Cancelled at source Mail and Express trains starting after 2 pm on 9 October that were due at either station between 4 am and 2 pm on 10 October are cancelled. So are the Howrah and Sealdah Rajdhani Express trains leaving West Bengal on 9 October. Checks at the borders Police will maintain heightened vigilance at Delhis entry points. People suspected of trying to mobilise crowds could be stopped and detained there, officers say. Getting across the city Gates at 57 Metro stations The DMRC said entry and exit gates would close from 9 pm on Friday until the situation normalises, with interchange still available except at New Delhi. The Supreme Court said there shall be no complete prohibition on Metro train movement. The Solicitor General said only train frequency would be reduced. App cabs restricted Police are coordinating with Ola and Uber to regulate movement towards Lutyens Delhi, and are preparing to restrict entry on roads into the New Delhi district. Delivery apps tracked Hotels told not to take new guests Hotels, guest houses and other accommodation in and around Central Delhi are asked to stay shut or restrict fresh bookings. Paharganj owners have been briefed. Liquor stores closed Shut across the city until Sunday, under an Excise department order citing public order. 3. Near the site The New Delhi district Delhi Police has not granted permission for the protest, citing prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. Stopped in your own district Districts are told to stop would-be protesters within their own jurisdiction. Those who refuse to turn back are sent straight to detention centres. More than 37 blocking points Spread across the New Delhi district, each pinned to one district or unit, so that no two units are posted at the same place. Connaught Place to shut All shops and restaurants around the Connaught Place market are to be shut. Detention centres Set up in all 15 districts, say officers, including stadiums such as Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Bawana and Chhatrasal Stadium. An earlier report put the number at around 10. The Home Ministry has made 221 Central Armed Police Forces companies, around 23,000 personnel, available to Delhi Police from 8 to 12 October. Five are all-women companies. Women police in front A source says women police will march in front to stop senior protest leaders, with male personnel supporting from behind. Women personnel will carry small body-worn devices. Mobile internet blocked Mobile internet services are blocked from 10 pm on Friday to 10 pm on Saturday, within a 4 km radius of JanpathKartavya Path. Press and livestreamers Journalists are asked to carry and prominently display valid press cards at barricades. People recording or livestreaming could face action if they obstruct police operations or violate restrictions. The plan stretches to refusing every permission sought including refusing permission for the protest itself, citing the lateness of the application. It begins with a 37-point dragnet. And, controversially, sees cops travelling to protesters (those whom they have identified) hometowns to urge them to stay away. That measure has been decried by protesters as house arrest, though the police have not formally issued such orders. Also the Union Home Ministry to whom Delhi Police reports has made 221 Central Armed Police Forces companies, i.e., 23,000 troops, available till Monday. The approach marks a reversal from last time, when district police were told to guide students and others travelling to Jantar Mantar to join the agitation. Five of the curbs come with dates and times. Pick a moment, from Friday afternoon to Sunday, to see which are in force around Saturdays protest at Jantar Mantar. Updated 9 October. Liquor stores shut citywide, till Sunday Central forces available 221 companies, 8 to 12 Oct Mobile internet blocked 4 km radius, 10 pm Fri to 10 pm Sat Metro station gates closed 57 stations, from 9 pm Fri Trains to the two stations cancelled New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin, 4 am to 2 pm Sat Liquor stores are shut and central forces are available. The Metro gate closure was announced from 9 pm and the mobile internet block from 10 pm. Mobile internet is now blocked within 4 km of JanpathKartavya Path. Liquor stores are shut and central forces are available. The Metro gate closure was due to begin, but the Supreme Court has questioned it. Liquor stores are shut, central forces are available and mobile internet is blocked. The Metro gate closure and the 10-hour rail suspension are under review after the Supreme Court hearing. The rail suspension was due to end at 2 pm. Liquor stores are still shut and mobile internet stays blocked until 10 pm. The Metro gate closure is under review and has no announced end time. Liquor stores were shut till Sunday, and the mobile internet block ended at 10 pm on Saturday. Central forces are available until 12 October. The Metro gate closure has no announced end time and is under review. Under review after the Supreme Court hearing Times are as announced. Under review: the Supreme Court questioned these curbs on 9 October, and no revised arrangement had been reported at the time of writing. Central forces are available to Delhi Police, not necessarily on the streets throughout. Court and Metro updates as reported by Bar & Bench, National Herald and Business Today. Mail and express services starting after 2 pm today and were due at either station between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10 have also been cancelled. Also, hotels and guest houses across the city have been told not to take in new visitors who appear to be arriving for the protest, though how they might identify such individuals and not inconvenience other travellers to Delhi is unclear. Nearly 60 Delhi Metro stations will be shut from 9 pm today until the situation normalises, the authorities said. Only 16 were shut for the last CJP protest. Mapping the restrictions around the Jantar Mantar protest A schematic map of where the curbs fall. Switch between all of Delhi and the area around Jantar Mantar. Border checks at entry points Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Bawana Chhatrasal Stadium New Delhi district: heavily secured zone New Delhi station Paharganj hotels briefed Hazrat Nizamuddin station Metro gates at 57 stations: closure under review Connaught Place Centre of the 4 km radius Mobile internet blocked across this whole view Mobile internet blocked, 4 km from JanpathKartavya Path Station: trains cancelled 4 am to 2 pm Sat (under review) Hotels told not to take new guests Detention centre Delhi Police plans to keep protesters out of the New Delhi district: stopping them within their own districts and at the borders, with detention centres in all 15 districts. Only the sites shown here have been named. The Supreme Court has asked the authorities not to halt the Metro or railways completely. Mobile internet services are blocked from 10 pm on Friday to 10 pm on Saturday within a 4 km radius of JanpathKartavya Path. Shops and restaurants to be shut Mobile internet blocked District assembly point Specialised unit Each district has been told to assemble at its own point, and each of the more than 37 blocking points is assigned to one district or unit, so that no two are posted at the same place. All shops and restaurants around the Connaught Place market are to be shut. Mobile internet is blocked from 10 pm on Friday to 10 pm on Saturday within 4 km of JanpathKartavya Path, which covers the whole area shown here. Where the districts assemble Central: Ranjit Singh Flyover near Barakhamba Road red light North: Election Commission of India East: Roundabout near Gymkhana post office, Safdarjung Road North-East: Roundabout near Sunehri Bagh Masjid Shahdara: In front of Parliament Street police station Dwarka: Roundabout near Buta Singh Outer: Roundabout near Windsor Place West: Kartavya Path/Man Singh Road crossing near India Gate North-West: Janpath/Tolstoy crossing near Janpath Metro station Rohini: Jai Singh Road near the MHA building Outer North: Roundabout near Gol Dak Khana South: In front of the Registrar of Companies office, Sansad Marg South-West: KG Marg/Firoz Shah Road crossing South-East: Gate No. 1, Major Dhyan Chand Stadium Specialised units Transport Bhawan: Crime Branch; 2nd and 1st Battalions, Delhi Armed Police And liquor stores across the city have been shut till Sunday. What happened in June CJP Mantar protest Weve been here before; in June the Abhijeet Dipke-founded pressure group ignited a ferocious protest that forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as the Union Education Minister. That agitation was over corruption in the public examination system. Back then the streets of central Delhi Jantar Mantar in particular resembled war zones as cops clashed with student. There were allegations of excessive force by the cops they reportedly fired pellet guns that injured students. But authorities claimed criminal elements infiltrated the protest.
