headline: PERM Vs H-1B: What Is The Difference, And Which One Does The US Suspension Affect?
content: For thousands of Indian technology professionals working in US, there is a difference between having permission to work in America and having a pathway to settle there permanently. India says Trumps latest immigration action does not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries, warning that the suspension of green-card applications for select technology firms could affect permanent residency prospects for eligible employees. But what exactly is PERM, how is it different from an H-1B visa, and what does the move mean for Indian tech workers? For thousands of Indian technology professionals working in the United States, there is a crucial difference between having permission to work in America and having a pathway to settle there permanently. - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud - TCS Says US Green Card Programme Suspension Wont Affect Hiring Strategy, Plans 15,000 Local Jobs - Does Not Advance Shared Ambitions: India Pushes Back Against US PERM Move, Cites Immigrants Role In Shaping America - US Green Card Crackdown: Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Microsoft Among 8 Firms Suspended | N18 Unwarranted, Deeply Offensive: India Pushes Back Against US PERM Move, Cites Immigrants Role In Shaping America That distinction has come into sharp focus after the Donald Trump administration suspended Microsoft, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Adobe and Capgemini from a key employment-based green-card programme. Announced on October 8, the move targets the US Department of Labors Permanent Labour Certification programme, commonly known as PERM. The administration has said it will stop accepting new applications and processing pending applications involving the affected companies. Indias Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), in a statement issued on October 9, clarified that PERM and H-1B are separate programmes and that the suspension does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas. The ministry also questioned the broader implications of the US action, stating, The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries." Here is what the two programmes mean, how they are different and what the suspension could mean for Indian professionals. The Trump administration suspended Microsoft, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Adobe, and Capgemini from a key employment-based green-card program. The suspension, announced on October 8, targets the US Department of Labor's Permanent Labour Certification program, known as PERM. India's Ministry of External Affairs clarified on October 9 that PERM and H-1B are separate programs. An H-1B visa is a temporary, non-immigrant work visa, generally granted for up to three years and extendable to a maximum of six years. PERM is a step in employer-sponsored permanent-residency applications, particularly for EB-2 and EB-3 categories. What Is An H-1B Visa? The H-1B is a temporary, non-immigrant work visa that allows US employers to hire eligible foreign professionals for specialised occupations requiring highly specialised knowledge and, generally, a bachelors degree or its equivalent. Technology companies use the programme to recruit software engineers, data scientists, researchers and other skilled professionals. An H-1B visa is generally granted for an initial period of up to three years and can usually be extended to a maximum of six years, subject to applicable rules and exceptions. Certain workers pursuing employment-based permanent residency may qualify for extensions beyond the usual six-year limit. The programme requires an eligible job and an employer willing to sponsor the worker. Employers must also meet applicable wage and labour-condition requirements. However, an H-1B visa does not provide permanent residency. A professional can work legally in the US while still having to navigate a separate immigration process to obtain a green card. That is why a suspension affecting green-card processing does not automatically mean that an existing H-1B worker must leave the country or stop working. What Is PERM, And How Does It Lead To A Green Card? PERM stands for Program Electronic Review Management. It is the US Department of Labors process for certifying that an employer seeking to sponsor a foreign worker for certain permanent positions has met prescribed labour-market requirements. Under the process, employers generally have to conduct recruitment and demonstrate that there are not sufficient qualified, willing and available American workers for the position, and that hiring the foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers. The employer files the labour-certification application, generally using Form ETA-9089. If the application is certified, the employer can usually proceed to file Form I-140, the immigrant petition, with US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). The worker must then satisfy the requirements of the relevant employment-based green-card category and wait until an immigrant visa number is available, where applicable, before completing the final stage of the process. PERM is therefore not a visa or a green card in itself. It is an important step in many employer-sponsored permanent-residency applications, particularly those under the employment-based second-preference (EB-2) and third-preference (EB-3) categories. Not every employment-based green-card applicant requires PERM. Certain categories, including EB-1 and some EB-2 National Interest Waiver cases, have different requirements and may not need labour certification. PERM Vs H-1B: What Is The Difference? The two programmes serve different purposes, even though they can form part of the same workers immigration journey. Purpose: H-1B permits eligible foreign professionals to work temporarily in the US. PERM is a labour-market certification used in many employer-sponsored green-card cases. Authority: H-1B petitions are adjudicated by USCIS, with the Department of Labor overseeing associated labour-condition requirements. PERM certification is administered by the Department of Labor. Duration: H-1B status is temporary and subject to extension rules. PERM is a step towards permanent residency, not an immigration status in itself. Employers role: An employer sponsors an H-1B petition and is responsible for the PERM labour-certification process when pursuing a green card through that route. Effect of the latest suspension: The action affects PERM applications involving the named companies. It does not automatically invalidate existing H-1B visas. H-1B concerns the right to work temporarily, while PERM concerns an important step towards securing permanent residency. Why Has Trump Suspended PERM For Tech Firms? The administration says the action is intended to protect American workers and address alleged misuse of employment-based immigration programmes. Vice President JD Vance singled out Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vance said. Microsoft disputed the characterisation of its hiring practices, saying approximately 80% of its H-1B applications in the last fiscal year were intended to extend or change the status of existing employees rather than recruit new workers. The company has also said it pays H-1B employees the same as other employees performing comparable work. TCS, meanwhile, said it did not expect the suspension to have a material impact on its workforce strategy or client engagements. It said its PERM applications had been in single digits over the preceding two years and reiterated plans to hire 15,000 additional employees in the US over the next five years. The companies responses underscore why the number of H-1B applications should not automatically be treated as a measure of new foreign recruitment or evidence that foreign employees replaced American workers. What Has India Said? New Delhi has emphasised both the distinction between the two immigration programmes and the economic contribution of Indian professionals in America. The MEA said the suspension could affect the green-card process of eligible employees of the affected companies, while making clear that it did not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B holders and their dependants. It also argued that skilled-worker mobility benefits both countries by supporting innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation in the US, while creating opportunities for Indians. The ministry said, Talent mobility adds value to both economies." It also pushed back against comments made by the US vice president, describing them as unwarranted and saying they ignored the contributions of Indian professionals to the American economy and innovation ecosystem. Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," the MEA said. What Does This Mean For Indian H-1B Workers? Workers whose PERM applications are pending with an affected company face a disruption to that stage of their green-card journey. Employees who have yet to begin the process may also face uncertainty over employer sponsorship while the suspension remains in force. Those holding valid H-1B status are not automatically required to leave the US because of the PERM action. However, delays in permanent-residency processing could complicate long-term planning, particularly for professionals approaching the usual H-1B time limit. Nor does the suspension necessarily close every alternative route to permanent residency. Eligibility for other employment-based categories depends on individual circumstances, and changing employers or immigration categories does not automatically resolve the problem. For Indian professionals who have spent years working in America, the uncertainty extends beyond immigration paperwork. It can affect decisions about buying a home, raising a family, changing jobs and planning a future in the country. The bottom line is that the US has suspended access to a route towards permanent residency for employees sponsored by the named companies; it has not abolished the H-1B programme. But for workers who have spent years building careers in America while waiting for a green card, the distinction offers only partial reassurance. They may still be able to work in the US even as their path to staying permanently becomes less certain. PERM stands for Program Electronic Review Management, which is the Department of Labor's process for certifying that an employer has met labor-market requirements before sponsoring a foreign worker for permanent residency. While not a visa or green card itself, it is a crucial step in many employer-sponsored green-card applications, particularly under the EB-2 and EB-3 categories.

headline: India reacts to US move on IT firms, says J D Vance's remark 'deeply offensive'
content: Delhis response came hours after the US administration suspended some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme. The PERM is a key provision used by American employers to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency, with several Indian IT companies also relying on the system. In a statement, the MEA said, We are aware of the US Department of Labors decision concerning the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies. It should be noted that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme. The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies, it said. Widening of crackdown The latest US action is a clear broadening of crackdown on foreign workers that has become a central policy under Trump. Technology and IT services companies are facing greater scrutiny over their reliance on foreign workers. US authorities have stepped up their probe into alleged misuse of H-1B and PERM programmes. The MEA said movement of talent adds value to both India and the US economically this has been Delhis position for several years now, highlighting the contribution of Indian skilled professionals in the US. It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US. This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries, it said. On Vances remark labelling them as foreign indentured servants, the MEA said, We have also seen some comments in this context by the US Vice President. We believe that such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem. Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity. Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive. The latest US action is a clear broadening of the crackdown on foreign workers that has become a central policy under President Donald Trump. Technology and IT services companies are facing greater scrutiny over their reliance on foreign workers. US authorities have stepped up investigations into alleged misuse of the H-1B and PERM programmes, including claims of wage undercutting, fraudulent filings and displacement of American workers. Indian professionals account for a large share of H-1B beneficiaries and employment-based Green Card applicants. In a statement on the US announcement, TCS said it prioritises local hiring in its US workforce strategy and does not expect any major disruption or impact on its business operations or client engagements. TCS said its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years and does not expect suspension of the programme to impact its workforce strategy and customer engagements. The company said it intends to hire 15,000 people in the US over the next five years. It said it has built a significant local workforce across 31 offices and delivery centres throughout the country. Microsoft said the vast majority of its employees were Americans. We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans, it said. Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category, it said, adding, We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work. Technology industry body Nasscom said, While the decision affects a specific immigration pathway, Nasscom has consistently maintained that immigration and skilled talent mobility are two distinct issues and should not be viewed through the same lens. The H-1B visa programme has historically played an important role in addressing short-term skill gaps in the US and it will continue to be used to address short term talent gaps. However, over a number of years, Indian technology companies have significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas, while steadily expanding local hiring and building a strong domestic workforce in the US. They work with the majority of the US fortune 500 companies, enable them to innovate and grow, and generate more local jobs. Consequently, the number of employees transitioning from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the PERM process is also relatively limited, it said. Indian technology companies operate across more than 80 countries and have consistently demonstrated their commitment to complying with local laws and regulatory requirements. We are confident that they will continue to adhere to applicable regulations in the US as well, Nasscom said.

headline: Delhi Police Denies Permission For CJP Protest On October 10, Says 'They Did Not Follow Rules'
content: Delhi Police has denied permission to the CJP to hold a protest scheduled for October 10, citing the short notice given for the event and prohibitory provisions in force in the New Delhi area. CJP has not been granted permission to hold the protest scheduled for October 10," Delhi Police said, while addressing a press conference on Friday. - CJP Oct 10 Protest: Delhi Police Step Up Vigil, Track 2,800 'Criminals', Monitor Buses, Borders - Delhi Police Check Hotels, Hostels Ahead Of CJP's Oct 10 Protest; Occupants, Staff Members Being Questioned - Delhi Protesters Bus-Stopping 'Stunt' Goes Viral As Internet Mocks Model Pose': 'Everyone Wants A Ticket To Bigg Boss' - Congress Delhi Protest | Rahul Gandhi Pushes Women Cop; BJP Releases Video | Jantar Mantar | News18 Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the organisation had sought permission at very short notice, while prohibitory provisions under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) remain in force in the New Delhi area. Also Read | 57 Delhi Metro Stations May Shut Gates Tonight, Police Write To DMRC Over Jantar Mantar Protests We received a letter from CJP regarding the protest scheduled for the 10th. Their conduct during previous protests was not appropriate, and they did not follow the rules," Delhi Police said. We have received an application from Saurav Das, Co-Convener of Cockroach Janta Party. The application is regarding an intimation for a protest on 10th October at Jantar Mantar. The protest was regarding the accountability of the CEC," Prasad said. Explaining the reason for rejecting the request, she said the intimation was submitted at short notice, whereas the prescribed guidelines require it to be received 10 days before the planned protest. Further, it is also important to mention that on an earlier occasion, when the Cockroach Janta Party was given permission to hold a protest there, they did not follow the lawful directions and did not follow their own undertakings given then," she said. Prasad said the decision was taken in view of the partys alleged failure to comply with legal directions and its undertakings, as well as the prevailing law-and-order situation. Therefore, because of not following the legal directions, their own undertaking, and the prevalent law and order situation, and to maintain public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, this time the permission is rejected; it is not approved," she said. She also said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was in force in the New Delhi area, imposing preventive restrictions to maintain public order and safety. It is further important to mention that if anybody violates the provisions of Section 163 of the BNSS, then proper legal action will be taken against them," Prasad said. 57 Delhi Metro Stations May Shut Delhi Police has proposed shutting the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, until the situation returns to normal, in view of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar. Interchange facilities will remain operational, the police said. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) is yet to confirm the proposal. Security arrangements have been stepped up across the national capital ahead of the CJP protest scheduled for October 10. The measures include the Metro network, long-distance train services and surveillance in central Delhi. Delhi Police are expected to hold a press conference shortly. Delhi Police denied the permission because the Cockroach Janta Party submitted their application at very short notice instead of the required 10 days, and due to prohibitory provisions under Section 163 of the BNSS. Authorities also cited the party's failure to follow lawful directions and previous undertakings, as well as concerns over public safety, traffic regulation, and the overall law-and-order situation.

headline: From mission to action – future of road safety in Tamil Nadu
content: Road safety in India has reached a scale that warrants a sustained, coordinated, and mission-mode response. Recently published data from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) for 2024 records 4,87,707 road crashes and 1,77,175 fatalities across the country. Tamil Nadu, as per this data, reported 67,526 crashes and 18,449 fatalities. Among all the States, Tamil Nadu recorded the highest number of road crashes, underlining the magnitude and urgency of the challenge. Road safety initiatives require multiple stakeholders to work together across multiple time frames. The Citizen consumer and civic Action Group (CAG), as a member of the Road Safety Network, had earlier engaged with Tiruchi Siva, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, on the need for a National Road Safety Mission to address the road safety crisis in a coordinated and sustained manner. This proposal was subsequently raised in Parliament by Mr. Siva, earlier this year. The rationale for such a Mission is similar to the broader mission-mode approach adopted for complex public health challenges: the problem requires sustained attention, coordination across multiple agencies, dedicated resources, measurable targets, and continuous monitoring, rather than a series of isolated interventions. Recently, the Tamil Nadu government announced in the Assembly, the Chief Ministers Road Safety Mission, with a reported annual allocation of about 500 crore. This is an important opportunity to strengthen and bring together road safety efforts in Tamil Nadu. The announced measures include technology-enabled enforcement through ANPR cameras, strengthening emergency response through the upgrading of government health facilities and linking them with accident-prone locations, and other initiatives. Tamil Nadu already has multiple institutions, committees, and initiatives working on different aspects of road safety. Implementation remains spread across Transport, Police, Highways/PWD, Health, Urban Development, and other departments. The value of this Mission should be in bringing these existing efforts together under a common framework, with political ownership, shared targets, clear departmental accountability, sustained funding, and regular review. The Mission can provide the platform to drive a Safe System approach across the State bringing together policy and action on speed management, safer road infrastructure and vehicles, protection of vulnerable road users and children, effective enforcement, and post-crash and trauma care. Crucially, departments should be reviewed not only on activities undertaken, but on measurable outcomes in reducing fatalities and serious injuries. Comprehensive action plan A logical and important instrument of this Mission would be a comprehensive State Road Safety Action Plan (RSAP) that provides a clear roadmap for implementation. The Plan should recognise that road deaths and serious injuries are preventable and that responsibility for safety must be shared across the transport system, in alignment with the internationally accepted Safe System approach. It should establish clear, measurable targets for reducing fatalities and translate the safe systems approach into specific interventions covering road infrastructure, appropriate speed management, safer vehicles, effective and risk-based enforcement, protection of pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users, safer school travel, driver and fleet safety, emergency and trauma care, and post-crash response. It should clearly define the responsibilities of the concerned departments and agencies, identify the resources required, ensure sustainable funding, establish timelines, and provide for regular monitoring and independent evaluation. Importantly, the State Action Plan should not remain a broad statement of intent. It should translate State-level priorities into district-level Road Safety Action Plans, based on the specific risks and needs of each district. Each identified problem should lead to a defined intervention, with a designated agency responsible for implementation, a budget, a time frame and measurable indicators of progress. This would also help address one of the persistent weaknesses in road safety the gap between policy and implementation. Data-driven approach The Centre of Excellence for Road Safety (CoERS) at IIT Madras, a think tank on road safety under MoRTH, has developed a comprehensive implementation framework, Data Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI). To facilitate the implementation of this programme, Sanjaya, an Integrated Road Safety portal, has been deployed by CoERS. This helps key stakeholders analyse data to support decision-making and monitor implementation, providing an accountability platform with the ability to create data-driven action plans and track implementation. This approach brings together relevant data from police, transport, highways, health, and other agencies to identify and prioritise risks, support evidence-based interventions and enable the government to track implementation across districts. Most importantly, it could connect each identified risk with the proposed intervention, responsible agency, funding, timeline, and outcome. Periodic reviews could then assess not merely whether an intervention has been completed, but whether it has actually reduced risk, crashes, and serious injuries.Together, these can turn the Mission from a policy commitment into coordinated, evidence-based action, with clear responsibilities and measurable outcomes. Tamil Nadu has an opportunity to demonstrate how existing road safety initiatives can be brought together under a coordinated, measurable, and outcome-oriented Safe System Mission. The immediate priority should be to give the Mission a clear framework, including a comprehensive State Road Safety Action Plan integrated with the Sanjaya platform. The experience could also provide a model for a similar Mission approach at the national level and in other States. The larger challenge is not necessarily the absence of road safety initiatives, but bringing policy, institutions, funding, implementation, and accountability together under one sustained Mission framework to achieve the ultimate goal of reducing deaths and serious injuries on our roads. (Dr. Venkatesh Balasubramanian is Professor, Department of Engineering Design, and Head RBG Labs & Centre of Excellence for Road Safety, Indian Institute of Technology Madras; S. Saroja is Executive Director, Citizen consumer and civic Action Group, Chennai.)

headline: Weather Alert: Bay Of Bengal System To Trigger Rain In Several States; What Delhi-NCR Can Expect
content: The IMD has forecast heavy rain in Uttarakhand, Kerala and Tamil Nadu on October 9, with thunderstorms and gusty winds expected in several other states The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds across several parts of India on Friday, October 9, even as the southwest monsoon continues to withdraw from more regions. Isolated heavy rainfall is likely in Uttarakhand, Kerala, Mahe, South Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, while several states in eastern, northeastern and central India may also experience unsettled weather. The IMDs October 8 national weather bulletin warns of gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph in some affected areas, including parts of Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. Winds of 30-40 kmph are forecast in parts of Andhra Pradesh, eastern Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and Sikkim. Thunderstorms and lightning are also possible in Jammu and Kashmir, parts of the Northeast and South Interior Karnataka. - H1N1 Found In 75% Of Positive Flu Tests, Dengue Hits 15,000+ Cases: What India Needs To Watch - 4.9-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Chamoli, Tremors Felt Across Delhi-NCR - Mumbai's 'First' Heatwave Alert: Thane Swelters, Solapur Hottest In October Since 2002 | Will Schools Shut? - Why Is Mumbai So Hot In October? 37.4C Recorded As El Nio Strengthens In Pacific The forecast comes as the monsoon retreats further from parts of the country. However, its withdrawal does not mean rainfall will immediately stop. The IMD says conditions remain favourable for further withdrawal from parts of eastern India, the northern Peninsula and the Northeast over the next three to four days. Why Is The Weather Changing? The IMD has identified several weather systems influencing conditions across India, including a cyclonic circulation over northeast Bihar and a trough extending towards Telangana across Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. Another circulation is present over northeast Assam and adjoining areas, while a fresh Western Disturbance over north Pakistan and neighbouring areas could influence northwestern India. These systems are contributing to a varied weather pattern, with rainfall continuing in some regions even as the monsoon retreats. The intensity and timing of showers will differ by state and locality. Delhi-NCR Weather: Partly Cloudy Skies, No Heavy Rain Warning Delhi is likely to remain partly cloudy on October 9, with the maximum temperature forecast at around 32C, according to a Times of India report citing the IMD outlook. Brief spells of rain or lightning are possible, but no warning of heavy rainfall has been issued for the capital for Friday. The IMDs latest subdivision-wise warning page lists no weather warning for Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh on October 9. Thunderstorms and gusty winds are forecast for the region on October 10 and 11. Commuters in Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad and neighbouring areas should monitor local forecasts before travelling, particularly if showers develop. Wet roads can reduce visibility and slow traffic, even when no heavy-rain warning is in force. Uttar Pradesh Weather: Rain And Thunderstorms Possible Parts of Uttar Pradesh may experience rain and thunderstorms on October 9. The IMDs subdivision-wise warning page lists a thunderstorm and lightning warning for both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. The likelihood and intensity of rainfall may vary between districts. Residents should check local updates rather than assume that every district will experience the same conditions. People working outdoors should seek shelter during thunderstorms and avoid exposed areas. Bihar Weather: Thunderstorms And Gusty Winds Bihar is among the states under a thunderstorm and lightning warning for October 9. The IMD has forecast gusty winds of 40-50 kmph at isolated places, with rainfall expected to continue in parts of the state. The weather may change quickly during thunderstorms, creating risks for people working in fields or travelling on exposed roads. Residents should avoid standing under trees or near electricity poles during lightning and strong winds. Jharkhand Weather: Rain And Winds Of 30-40 Kmph Rain and thunderstorms are possible in parts of Jharkhand on October 9. The IMD has forecast gusty winds of 30-40 kmph at isolated places, with rainfall activity expected to continue through Friday and Saturday. Heavy showers in localised areas could lead to waterlogging and affect road travel. Residents should keep away from weak trees and temporary structures during strong winds and follow local weather advisories. West Bengal And Sikkim: Thunderstorm Alert Parts of West Bengal and Sikkim may experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds on October 9. Winds of 30-40 kmph are possible at isolated places, according to the IMD bulletin. Rainfall is expected in both Gangetic West Bengal and Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim, although the distribution will vary. People travelling in hilly areas should watch for slippery roads and follow local advisories where heavy rain is reported. Odisha: Rain And Gusty Winds In Some Areas Odisha is expected to receive isolated to scattered rainfall as the unsettled weather continues. The IMD has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph at isolated places on October 9. The broader rainfall outlook indicates that Odisha may continue to receive showers through October 14. Conditions will vary across the state, so residents should follow district-level forecasts for the latest information. Madhya Pradesh: Rain Possible In Eastern Areas Eastern Madhya Pradesh may receive isolated to scattered rainfall over the coming days. The IMD has forecast gusty winds of 30-40 kmph at isolated places on October 9, accompanied by the possibility of thunderstorms. The outlook is not uniform across Madhya Pradesh, and the national bulletin does not indicate the same rainfall prospects for every part of the state. Residents should check local updates before planning outdoor activities. Uttarakhand: Heavy Rain Raises Travel Concerns The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in Uttarakhand on October 9, along with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph at isolated places. Heavy rain can make mountain roads slippery and increase the risk of landslides, falling debris and localised waterlogging. Travellers heading to hilly areas should check road conditions and local administration advisories before setting out. People should avoid stopping near unstable slopes during heavy rain. Himachal Pradesh: Check Local Forecasts Before Travelling Rainfall was recorded in parts of Himachal Pradesh in the 24 hours covered by the IMDs latest national bulletin. However, the bulletin does not list a specific thunderstorm warning for the state on October 9. Conditions can vary considerably across the hills, so travellers should check the latest local forecast and road advisories before travelling. During heavy rain, avoid areas prone to landslides and falling rocks. Jammu And Kashmir: Thunderstorms And Lightning Possible The IMD hasforecast isolated thunderstorms and lightning in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on October 9. Rain and unstable weather may affect travel in some areas, particularly along hilly roads. Travellers should check local weather and road updates before beginning their journeys. Where rain occurs, slippery surfaces and debris may create additional hazards. Northeast India: Rain And Lightning Alerts Rainfall is expected in parts of Northeast India on October 9. The IMDs outlook covers Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, while Arunachal Pradesh may also receive showers. Thunderstorms and lightning are possible in Assam and Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Rainfall may cause water levels in smaller rivers and streams to rise quickly, particularly in hilly and remote areas. Residents should avoid open fields, isolated trees and water bodies during thunderstorms. Those living in landslide-prone areas or near streams should follow local warnings and remain alert to sudden changes in weather. South India: Heavy Rain Likely In Kerala, Tamil Nadu And Karnataka Southern India is expected to see some of the most significant rainfall activity on October 9. The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in Kerala and Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, as well as South Interior Karnataka. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph are possible in Kerala and Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Lakshadweep is also under a thunderstorm and gusty-wind warning. South Interior Karnataka may experience thunderstorms and lightning, along with isolated heavy rainfall. Rainfall is also expected in parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema, where strong surface winds are possible. The broader outlook indicates that wet conditions may continue in parts of Kerala and Lakshadweep through October 10, while heavy rain may persist in parts of Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas. Residents should take precautions during thunderstorms, avoid flooded roads and follow local weather alerts, particularly in areas prone to waterlogging. October Weather: Heat And Humidity To Persist In Some Areas Rainfall will not bring relief uniformly across India. The IMD has warned that hot and humid conditions are likely to continue in isolated parts of Konkan and Goa through October 10. The weather may therefore remain unsettled in some regions while others continue to experience warm and humid conditions. Temperatures and rainfall prospects will depend on local weather systems, and city-level forecasts should be checked separately for the latest estimates. Safety Measures During Rain And Thunderstorms The IMD has warned that heavy rain and gusty winds can affect road and rail traffic, reduce visibility, cause waterlogging and damage vulnerable structures. Residents in affected areas should: - Take shelter indoors during thunderstorms and avoid standing under trees. - Stay away from water bodies and exposed locations during lightning. - Avoid driving through flooded roads or areas with poor visibility. - Keep away from weak trees, electricity poles and temporary structures during strong winds. - Check official weather and road advisories before travelling in hilly areas. - Follow local administration instructions in areas vulnerable to landslides or sudden rises in river and stream levels. The weather outlook for October 9 remains varied across India. While the southwest monsoon continues its retreat, rainfall, thunderstorms and gusty winds are expected in several regions. Residents should follow the latest IMD updates for their districts as conditions can change. Delhi is expected to remain partly cloudy on October 9 with a maximum temperature around 32C, alongside possible brief spells of rain or lightning. While no heavy rainfall warning has been issued for Friday, thunderstorms and gusty winds are predicted for October 10 and 11.

headline: Tipu Sultan: a secular internationalist, not a bigot
content: The recent offer made by a film producer to Tamil superstar Rajinikanth to act in a movie on the >Tiger of Mysore , Tipu Sultan, has yet again opened up a Pandoras Box. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and some Hindutva groups have demanded that Rajinikanth refuse the offer. This argument is made on the grounds that Tipu, the 18th century ruler of Mysore state, was a tyrant who killed thousands of Hindus as they refused to convert to Islam. This is not the first time that Tipus name has been dragged into a controversy. It began some years back when Sanjay Khan made a tele-serial based on Bhagwan S. Gidwanis book, The Sword of Tipu Sultan. His name was once again dragged into a controversy when the Congress government intended to celebrate his birth anniversary in 2014. There was opposition when a proposal was made to establish a university named after him. Tipus very name has become contentious for two reasons: first, his controversial steps in dealing with different communities and people who rose against him. Second, different perspectives through which history was constructed and his image built. Colonial historians have projected Tipu as a religious bigot, who was instrumental in killing and converting to Islam thousands of Nayars of Kerala, Catholics of Dakshina Kannada and Coorgis of Kodagu. Even Kannada chauvinists have projected him as anti-Kannadiga as he was instrumental in changing the local names of places and introducing Persian vocabulary into administration. Marxist historians, on the other hand, have viewed him as one of the foremost commanders of independence struggle and a harbinger of new productive forces. >History is unkind to Tipu Sultan . The fact is that Tipu cannot be reduced to a singular narrative or tradition of intolerance or bigotry as he represented multiple traditions. He combined tolerant inter-religious traditions, liberal and secular traditions, anti-colonialism and internationalism. He could do this as he had strong roots in Sufism, which is not explored much by historians. He belonged to the Chisti/Bande Nawaz tradition of Sufism. In fact, Tipu was radical in more than one sense. He was the first to ban consumption of alcohol in the entire State, not on religious grounds, but on moral and health grounds. He went to the extent of saying: A total prohibition is very near to my heart. He is credited with introducing missile or rocket technology in war. He was the first to introduce sericulture to the then Mysore state. He was the first to confiscate the property of upper castes, including Mutts, and distribute it among the Shudras. He is also credited with sowing the seeds of capitalist development at a time when the country was completely feudal. He thought about constructing a dam across the Cauvery in the present-day location of Krishnaraja Sagar. He completed the task of establishing a biodiversity garden named Lal Bagh. His tolerance is reflected in his annual grants to no less than 156 temples, which included land deeds and jewellery. His army was largely composed of Shudras. When the famed Sringeri Mutt, established by Shankaracharya, was invaded by the Maratha army, he issued a firman to provide financial assistance for reinstallation of the holy idol and restoring the tradition of worship at the Mutt. His donation to the famous Srikanteshwara temple at Nanjangud; the donation of 10,000 gold coins to complete temple work at Kanchi; settling the disputes between two sects of priests at the Melkote temple; and gifts to Lakshmikanta temple at Kalale are all well-known. Interestingly, Srirangapatna, a temple town, remained his permanent capital till the end of his rule. He was also instrumental in constructing the first-ever church in Mysuru. Incidentally, well-known historian B.A. Saletore calls him defender of Hindu Dharma. The allegation of forcible conversions has to be seen in the background of political exigencies either they were with the colonialists such as in the case of Christians of Dakshina Kannada, or were waging a protracted guerrilla war as in the case of Coorg. Here, historians have distorted the facts by reducing political exigencies to the communal ideology of Tipu. A ruler, who once identified himself with the American and French Revolution and Jacobinism, has remained an enigma to many. That a man who ruled for just 16 years continues to haunt Hindutva groups obviously means that Tipu continues to exist in the political discourses, political narratives as well as in the imagination of nation-building. This is where the irony of history lies one cannot just bury Tipu in the annals of history. (The writer is chairman, department of political science at the University of Mysore. muzaffar.assadi@gmail.com.)

headline: PM Carney says Canadians will decide their future after Elon Musk expresses support for separatism
content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday (October 8, 2026) that Canada's future will be decided by Canadians, pushing back on Elon Musk's call for Quebec, Alberta and Saskatchewan to separate from Canada. The future of Canada will be decided by Canadians and the priorities of Canadians, the priorities of the people of Quebec, PM Carney said when asked about Mr. Musk's comments. Mr. Carney said Canadians should be free to live according to their languages and cultures, without interference "from foreign governments and large tech firms that think they can tell us what to do." Mr. Musk weighed in on Canada's separatist debates on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) in a post on X about Quebec Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, whose separatist Parti Qubcois won Monday's provincial election. The PQ's victory was not a mandate for independence. The party won about 28% of the popular vote and fell short of a majority of the seats in the Quebec legislature. Support for Quebec independence remains at about 30%, said Daniel Bland, a political science professor at McGill University in Montreal. He said the election was driven more by a desire to oust the Coalition Avenir Qubec government than by support for separation. Good. Quebec should separate, Mr. Musk wrote, adding that They would be better off. Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too. Alberta is scheduled to hold a vote October 19 on whether the province should remain in Canada or move toward a future referendum on separation. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has said she will vote to remain in Canada. Mr. Smith said that separatist sentiment in her province has weakened as her government and Mr. Carney's have worked to address Albertans' concerns. The federal government has changed. Their approach to us has changed and they're willing to work together on addressing those issues, Mr. Smith said in Edmonton. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe responded to Mr. Musk on X with a single word: No. MMr. musk, the world's richest man and first-ever trillionaire, is a South African-born Canadian-American.

headline: Puducherry Bypoll Result 2026: NDA's Ashok Anand Wins Thattanchavady By 8,500 Votes
content: election was necessitated after N Rangasamy, who had won from both Thattanchavady and Mangalam in the April assembly elections The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured a victory in the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll in Puducherry on Friday, with its candidate Ashok Anand winning the seat by a margin of around 8,500 votes. Anand contested on the ticket of the All India N.R. Congress (AINRC), led by Puducherry Chief Minister N Rangasamy. The victory comes as bypoll results are being declared across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Assam. - Madurantakam Election Results 2026 Live: TVK Ahead Of DMK, AIADMK By Over 11,000 Votes - From Nandigram To Nagaon: Key Results Of Bypoll Battle Across 6 High-Stakes Seats Arrive Today - By-Election Results 2026 Live Updates: AINRC's Ashok Anand Wins Thattanchavady Seat By 13,358 Votes - Bypoll 2026 Highlights: Madurantakam Leads With 85.99% Turnout, Nandigram Logs 80.67% As Polling Concludes The October 9 counting covers five assembly constituenciesNandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, and Thattanchavady in Puducherryalong with the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam. Why Was A Bypoll Held In Thattanchavady? The Thattanchavady bypoll was necessitated after Rangasamy, who won both Thattanchavady and Mangalam in the April assembly elections, decided to retain Mangalam and vacated the former seat. The contest was closely watched as a test for the Rangasamy-led AINRC government and its NDA bloc. Polling in Thattanchavady was held on October 6, with the constituency recording a voter turnout of 80.81 per cent, according to AIR. This was lower than the 87.10 per cent turnout recorded during the previous assembly election. Voting took place across 31 polling stations and passed off peacefully. Eleven candidates were in the fray, including Anand, Congress candidate E Vinayagam and DMK candidate K Sethu Selvam. The result gives the AINRC-led NDA a win in the constituency that Rangasamy had vacated after retaining Mangalam. The outcome will be watched for its implications for the ruling alliance as political parties assess the results of the bypolls across the four states and Union Territory. National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate Ashok Anand won the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll by a margin of around 8,500 votes.

headline: Indian Railways nears 100% electrification: Only 191 Route Km left across 3 states
content: The Ministry of Railways is working in a mission mode to complete the electrification of its entire Broad Gauge (BG) network. Sharing the latest progress, Indian Railways said that 99.7 per cent of the countrys Broad Gauge (BG) network has already been electrified. Out of the total 70,502 route kilometres (RKm) of BG lines, 70,311 RKm had been electrified as of September 30, 2026, with only a small portion of the network remaining to be covered. Indian Railways electrification status In India, the railway electrification began in 1925, when the countrys first electric train, operating on a 1,500-volt DC system, ran between Bombay Victoria Terminus and Kurla Harbour in Maharashtra. According to the latest update from the Ministry of Railways, 27 States and Union Territories have achieved 100 per cent electrification of their Broad Gauge (BG) railway network, with no route kilometres pending. Last month, Southern Railway achieved 100 per cent electrification of its Broad Gauge (BG) network, covering 5,068 route kilometres (RKM) across the zone. The milestone was achieved after the completion of electrification work on the final 71-km-long Pattukkottai-Karaikkudi section. Only three states still have some sections under electrification. Together, these remaining stretches account for just 191 RKm. Apart from these, all new line and multi-tracking projects are being sanctioned and constructed with electrification. These 3 states still have 191 km of non-electrified tracks According to the Ministry of Railways, only three states: Assam, Karnataka and Goa, still have Broad Gauge (BG) railway sections pending for electrification, accounting for together 191 route kilometres (RKm). STATE WISE ELECTRIFIED NETWORK (RKM) Source: Ministry of Railways Electrified (30.09.2026) 27 of 30 states/UTs are 100% electrified. Remaining: Assam (55 RKM), Karnataka (120 RKM), Goa (16 RKM). Assam has achieved 97.9 per cent electrification of its 3,743 RKm Broad Gauge network, while Karnataka has electrified 96.8 per cent of its 3,743 RKm BG network. In Goa, 171 RKm of the total 187 RKm Broad Gauge network has been electrified, leaving just 16 RKm pending. The electrification of railway network will help improve train operations, reduce dependence on fossil fuels and support its sustainability goals.

headline: Jan Shatabdi trains in Keralam set for upgrade with new LHB coaches, push-back seats
content: The Ministry of Railways is set to introduce new LHB (Linke-Hofmann-Busch) non-AC Chair Car coaches with push-back seats on two popular Jan Shatabdi train services in Keralam. The move is expected to provide passengers a more comfortable travel experience. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior official from Thiruvananthapuram Division of Southern Railway (SR) has confirmed the development. The new coaches are being introduced on two important services: train number 12075/12076 Thiruvananthapuram-Kozhikode-Thiruvananthapuram and train number 12081/12082 Kannur-Thiruvananthapuram-Kannur. According to the official, these two Jan Shatabdi services are among the popular seating-accommodation trains in the state and provide an important rail link between northern and southern parts of Keralam, connecting major destinations through the coastal Alappuzha route and the inland Kottayam route. New LHB coaches with push-back seats The new Non-AC Chair Car coaches have been manufactured by the Rail Coach Factory (RCF) and have now reached Thiruvananthapuram Division. The coaches will be commissioned and inducted into regular service after completion of the prescribed works. The formal date of induction into regular service to be announced shortly, the official said. The introduction of these coaches is expected to make the journey more comfortable for passengers, particularly those travelling on the long-distance daytime Jan Shatabdi services. Keralams Jan Shatabdi trains are set to receive new LHB coaches with push-back seating. (Image: Southern Railway) Why push-back seats are being introduced Both Jan Shatabdi services have already been upgraded from older ICF coaches to modern LHB coaches. The Kannur-Thiruvananthapuram Jan Shatabdi was upgraded to LHB coaches in September 2024. Train number 12081 started operating with the LHB rake from September 29, 2024, while train number 12082 commenced from September 30. The Thiruvananthapuram-Kozhikode Jan Shatabdi was subsequently upgraded to LHB coaches from May 28, 2026. The initial LHB non-AC Chair Car coaches had a modified fixed-seat arrangement. The change was made to improve durability and reduce damage to the seating mechanism associated with push-back seats. However, push-back seats have remained a preferred choice among passengers. In response to this preference, efforts were made to introduce LHB Non-AC Chair Car coaches with push-back seating. New LHB coaches with push-back seating are set to be inducted into Keralams Jan Shatabdi services. (Image: Southern Railway) Passengers to get modern coaches The new coaches will combine the benefits of the modern LHB coach design with the push-back seating arrangement preferred by passengers. The return of push-back seating in the upgraded LHB coaches is expected to be particularly welcomed by regular Jan Shatabdi passengers. The initiative combines the advantages of the modern LHB coach design with a seating arrangement that passengers have found comfortable and convenient over the years, the railway official said. The divisional railway has also advised passengers to use the push-back mechanism and other seating facilities carefully. Proper use will help prevent avoidable damage and ensure that the improved facilities remain available and comfortable for passengers throughout the service life of the coaches, the official said. Two important Jan Shatabdi train services in Keralam Train numbers 12075/12076 operate between Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode and run daily. On the other hand, train numbers 12081/12082 operate between Kannur and Thiruvananthapuram and run five days a week. History of Jan Shatabdi services in Keralam The first Jan Shatabdi service in Keralam was introduced on November 1, 2002, between Ernakulam Junction and Thiruvananthapuram Central via Alappuzha. The service was later extended to Kozhikode in 2009 and became the present 12075/12076 ThiruvananthapuramKozhikode Jan Shatabdi. The second Jan Shatabdi service was introduced on January 20, 2011, between Kozhikode and Thiruvananthapuram via the Kottayam route. It initially operated five days a week. The service was later extended from Kozhikode to Kannur on August 2, 2013.

headline: Who Is Nidal Hasan? Fort Hood Shooter Set For Livestreamed Firing Squad Execution In US
content: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has confirmed that the execution will be made public, with the Pentagon subsequently confirming that it will be livestreamed. The United States is preparing to carry out one of its rarest military punishments in an unprecedented manner. The country will livestream the execution of a convicted mass killer. Nidal Malik Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist sentenced to death for killing 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3, 2026. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has confirmed that the execution will be made public, with the Pentagon subsequently confirming that it will be livestreamed. The move marks a dramatic departure from the tightly controlled proceedings that have traditionally surrounded executions in the country. - Trump Approves Firing Squad Execution Of Ex-Army Major Nidal Hasan In Rare Move: Why It Matters - Pete Hegseth Says Fort Hood Shooter's Execution By Firing Squad Will Be Livestreamed - 'How Trump Feels He Is': Iran Mocks US President With Hrithik Roshan Movie Meme - ICE Agent Shoots At Criminal Illegal Alien From Dominican Republic During New York Arrest Operation Well make sure that people are able to watch it, that its public, because people need to understand that theres serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth told Jack Posobiec on Real Americas Voice. The execution is expected to be the first carried out by the US military since 1961 and the first military firing-squad execution since 1945. Who Is Nidal Hasan? Hasan, now 56, was a US Army major and psychiatrist who treated military personnel. On November 5, 2009, he opened fire inside the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, where troops were undergoing medical checks and preparing for deployment. Armed with a laser-sighted handgun, he killed 13 people, including a pregnant soldier, and wounded 32 others. Witnesses reported that he shouted Allahu akbar", meaning God is great" in Arabic, during the attack. Nidal Malik Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3, 2026. Hasan killed 13 people and wounded 32 others at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009. The execution will be livestreamed, marking a departure from traditional proceedings. This will be the first US military execution since 1961 and the first military firing-squad execution since 1945. Hasan was found guilty on 45 charges, including 13 counts of premeditated murder. The massacre shocked the country because the gunman was himself an Army officer, and his victims were fellow service members. Hasan was due to deploy to Afghanistan weeks later. During his trial, Hasan acknowledged that he was responsible for the shooting. He argued that he had acted to protect Islamic insurgents from US military forces, describing himself as a soldier who had switched sides". Why Is He Being Executed? Hasan faced 45 charges 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder. He chose to represent himself during his 2013 court-martial, an unusual decision that raised concerns among his court-appointed standby lawyers about whether he was deliberately pursuing a death sentence. On August 23, 2013, a military jury found him guilty on all 45 counts. Five days later, the jury unanimously recommended death. His sentence subsequently survived the appeals process. The US Supreme Court declined to review his conviction in March 2025. On October 2, 2026, President Donald Trump approved the death sentence, following a recommendation from Hegseth. The Army subsequently scheduled the execution for December 3 at Fort Hood. Hasan was partially paralysed after being shot by police during his arrest and has since used a wheelchair. Why Is US Making The Execution Public? Hegseth has said the timing and location were deliberate: the execution is scheduled for 1 pm at Fort Hood, broadly corresponding to the time and place of the original attack. However, the decision to livestream it has raised questions about whether public punishment risks becoming a spectacle. Geoffrey Corn, a Texas Tech University law professor and former Army lawyer, told CBS News that the plan raises significant moral questions, above and beyond the questions related to the death penalty generally". He added that turning an execution into a public spectacle echoes of the past we seem to have put behind us". The last legally sanctioned public execution in the US took place in 1936, when Rainey Bethea was hanged in Kentucky before a crowd reportedly numbering around 20,000. Other US Executions: Why This Case Is Different The last US military execution was that of Army Private John A Bennett, who was hanged at Fort Leavenworth on April 13, 1961, after being convicted of raping and attempting to murder an 11-year-old girl. The last US military firing-squad execution took place in 1945, when Private Eddie Slovik was shot in France after being convicted of desertion during World War II. He remains the only American soldier executed for desertion during that war. Firing squads have also returned to civilian executions. South Carolina carried out three firing-squad executions in 2025, the first such executions in the US since 2010. Hasans scheduled execution is therefore significant not only because of the crime for which he was convicted, but also because it combines a rarely used military punishment with an unprecedented public broadcast. Whether the livestream will deter future crimes or merely intensify the debate over capital punishment remains an open question. Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3, 2026, at Fort Hood, Texas.

headline: Delhi Protests: 25 FIRs Registered; Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Named For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission
content: Delhi Police registered around 25 FIRs over protests since October 2, naming Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in cases involving alleged vandalism, assault and obstruction. Delhi Police have registered around 25 first information reports (FIRs) in connection with a series of protests in the national capital since October 2, with cases involving allegations of vandalism of public property, assault, scuffles with police personnel and obstruction of government work, news agency ANI reported on Friday, citing sources. Several political leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, have also been named in the cases, the report mentioned. - Gyanesh Kumar Protest Escalates: Cops Report Injuries, FIRs Filed | Delhi Protest | News18 - Delhi HC Rejects Plea For Mandatory Bodycams During Protests By Delhi Police, RAF | News18 - Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use - Delhi Protest Turns Violent: Cops Dragged, Pushed & Bitten? ACP Arshdeep Speaks Out | Raw Report The FIRs had been registered up to Thursday in connection with the protests, which have continued in Delhi amid prohibitory orders imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the New Delhi district. According to police sources cited by ANI, the cases concern alleged violations of the restrictions, along with incidents involving damage to public property, physical altercations and alleged obstruction of official duties. The allegations are the subject of the registered cases. FIRs OVER ALLEGED VIOLATION OF SECTION 163 BNSS The protests in Delhi began on October 2 and have continued amid restrictions on public gatherings in the New Delhi district. According to ANI, police sources said the cases relate to alleged violations of prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. The provision has been invoked in the district, where police have maintained restrictions on demonstrations and gatherings. FIR AGAINST RAHUL, PRIYANKA GANDHI OVER AKASHVANI BHAWAN PROTEST Among the cases registered earlier was an FIR concerning Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc MPs allegedly entering the premises of Akashvani Bhavan without permission during a protest against the Election Commission of India on Tuesday. Delhi Police registered the FIR on Wednesday, according to ANI. Police said the INDIA bloc had planned a march from Parliament House towards Nirvachan Sadan, the headquarters of the Election Commission of India. However, according to the police, no official permission had been sought or granted for the proposed march. When the protesters were stopped near the Election Commission office, several opposition leaders and MPs staged a sit-in protest. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra subsequently entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises along with other leaders and continued their demonstration there. The FIR was registered in connection with the alleged unauthorised entry into the premises. POLICE WARN AGAINST PROPOSED OCTOBER 10 PROTEST Meanwhile, Delhi Police have warned against a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) scheduled for October 10, citing the restrictions imposed under Section 163 of the BNSS. Deputy Commissioner of Police Shrishti Pandey said protests were not permitted at Jantar Mantar or any other location while the restrictions remained in force. She warned that any unauthorised gathering would be considered illegal and that the police would take legal action against those involved. The warning comes as demonstrations continue in the national capital and police maintain restrictions on public gatherings in the New Delhi district. Delhi Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other INDIA bloc MPs for allegedly entering the Akashvani Bhavan premises without permission during an opposition protest. The protest and subsequent unauthorized entry occurred after authorities stopped their planned march toward the Election Commission headquarters.

headline: ICE agents shoot man in New York City; negotiations with Trump seeking his release unsuccessful, Mamdani says
content: U.S. federal immigration agents shot and wounded a Dominican man while arresting him in New York City on Thursday (October 8, 2026), in what the Department of Homeland Security called a targeted enforcement operation. The man was in his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the city police and eyewitnesses. Protesters decried it as an example of the dangers of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. The man survived and is being treated at a hospital, the agency said. It did not describe exactly what led to the shooting, saying only that during the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and that the man was injured. The agency described the man as a criminal illegal alien with a prior grand larceny conviction and a history of other arrests. He was arrested in December 2023 but was released, the agency said, blaming reckless policies in Democrat-led cities, such as New York. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called in a statement for an end to all Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids in the city. Demonstrators at the scene chanted, ICE off our streets now! Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds, he said. An FBI spokesperson said an evidence response team was responding to the scene to support our partners at the Department of Homeland Security, but offered no other details. Messages seeking further information were sent to federal authorities. The person who was shot was conscious and being treated at a hospital, the New York Police Department said in a post on X, noting that its officers didn't witness the shooting and weren't involved. The shooting happened in the Marble Hill neighbourhood, a small part of Manhattan attached to the Bronx. These actions are making city less safe: Mamdani I have been on the phone with President Trump and (Homeland Security) Secretary Mullin, negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful, Mr. Mamdani said in a press conference late in the evening. He said he demanded from the Trump administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. These actions are making the city less safe, Mr. Mamdani said. This city wants ICE out. We want ICE out of our city, ICE out of our schools, ICE out of our hospitals, ICE out of our streets, ICE away from our kids. The Mayor said the child in the car is physically unharmed. New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said NYPD has located the child with a family member after a wellness check. Pedro Almaraz, an employee at a nearby restaurant, said he heard about three or four gunshots and saw a man on the ground surrounded by several officers wearing face masks and vests with Department of Homeland Security branding. Witnesses, he said, were screaming. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, a Democrat, said in a post on social media that she had been briefed on the shooting. We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding this incident. New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why, she said. Videos and photos posted by bystanders on social media showed a man sitting on the ground with his hands behind his back, in the immediate aftermath of the shooting. Another video shows New York City police officers picking up an apparently injured man and carrying him into a police vehicle. Nearby, a damaged car sat blocking the roadway with small holes in two of its windows. The videos show agents wearing ICE badges on the scene, including one carrying a rifle. With inputs from AP, Reuters
