Al Jazeera reported that Iranian naval forces are carrying out nightly patrols in the Strait of Hormuz to target ships that violate local regulations, according to an IRGC political deputy. On the diplomatic front, US President Donald Trump confirmed that Washington is engaged in productive discussions with Iran and committed to holding off on any military strikes before the upcoming November 3 midterms. A 60-day maritime armistice brokered by the US and Iran in mid-June 2026 has disintegrated, replacing brief shipping lane stability with renewed missile strikes and mounting maritime risk. The failure of the agreement prompted both states to recommence active military operations and disband formal diplomatic channels. Consequently, fears of global energy disruption have driven a major safe-haven rally in precious metals, sending domestic and spot gold prices surging alongside foreign exchange instability and recent import duty revisions.

headline: U.K. PM Burnham's Labour fends off left-wing Greens in local election
content: Andy Burnham's Labour Party won an election for the parliamentary seat vacated by former leader Keir Starmer on Friday (October 9, 2026), fending off a strong challenge from the left-wing Green Party in a boost for the British Prime Minister. Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali, the leader of the local council, won the by-election in the central London constituency of Holborn and St. Pancras with 12,292 votes, compared with 8,928 for Zack Polanski, the Green Party leader. Labour had been widely expected to hold the seat, as Mr. Burnham seeks to repair his party's damaged appeal among core voters in big cities after two bruising years in government under Mr. Starmer. While Labour's main rival in national polls is currently the populist Reform Party, the governing party is seeking to shore up support among left-leaning voters who had turned to the Greens before a national vote due in mid-2029. The result will be a blow to Mr. Polanski, a 43-year-old former actor and hypnotherapist, who has promised to make his party "an eco-populist" movement and draw support away from Labour a strategy that had been working until Mr. Burnham came to power. Ms. Abdi-Wali paid tribute to Mr. Starmer in her victory speech and said she wanted to work with Mr. Burnham on issues such as housing. "We have a responsibility to defend what we've built and pass it on," she said. "Throughout our campaign, we chose hope, and the people of Holborn and St. Pancras chose it with us. And now it's time to deliver." BURNHAM'S ARRIVAL HAS SAPPED MOMENTUM FROM GREEN PARTY Mr. Starmer was replaced as Prime Minister in July and stood down as a lawmaker in September after losing the support of his Labour Party over a series of missteps, U-turns and disastrous local election results in May. The Green Party had made record gains in London largely at Labour's expense in May's local elections, capitalising on Mr. Starmer's unpopularity. But the Greens have fallen back in national polls since, after Mr. Burnham made several policy pitches that boosted Labour's standing among voters to the left, including a tougher line on Israel and a more ambitious approach to relations with the European Union. The result caps a damaging few days for Mr. Polanski, whose leadership of the Greens has been questioned after party members passed a Zionism is Racism motion to widespread criticism from Jewish groups, other parties and even most Green party lawmakers. After the result, Mr. Polanski, who is Jewish, said he believed the displacement of Palestinian people was racist, although he declined to say that he supported the motion after not taking part in the vote last weekend. He said that he was disappointed not to win the seat but would stay on as Green Party leader, adding that the party would continue to grow despite the setback. "So many people told me on the doorstep that they want to give Andy Burnham a chance," Mr. Polanski told broadcasters. "Well, he's got a chance now. Let's see what he does with it."

headline: 'Negative Demographic Changes Led To Partition': RSS's Sunil Ambekar Makes Case For NRC | Exclusive
content: News18, Ambekar also reiterated the Sanghs position on the Uniform Civil Code (UCC). The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sanghs (RSS) demand for a nationwide National Register of Citizens (NRC) is rooted in the need to clearly establish who is a citizen of India, while negative demographic change" remains a concern for the organisation because of its implications for national unity, integrity and security, RSS Akhil Bharatiya Prachar Pramukh Sunil Ambekar said in an exclusive interview with CNN-News18. Ambekar also reiterated the Sanghs position on the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), saying that citizenship and demographic questions needed to be viewed in the context of the countrys cultural identity. - Beyond Illegal Immigration: Why The RSS Is Bringing The NRC Debate Back - The Fuel Behind Indias Nuclear Push: UCIL To Double Uranium Production Capacity By 2036 - Opinion | From Ground Zero: Why Drug-Free Bharat Is An Imperative - 'Rahul Gandhi, Kejriwal Can't Feel For Punjab Like We Do': Sukhbir Badal On SAD's Edge | Exclusive In a democracy, we need to be very clear who are the citizens of this country. I think any country will do that," Ambekar said, adding that only citizens should have the right to participate in the democratic process and access facilities meant for citizens. Population imbalance is a very important issue because negative demographic changes were one of the factors that led to the Partition in 1947," he said. NRC, Demography And Citizenship Explaining the idea further, Ambekar said there could be different mechanisms and tools available to the government to establish citizenship. However, he stressed that the objective should be to safeguard national unity, integrity and security. Only citizens will have the right to participate in the democratic process. As citizens, if they are subscribed to any facilities that are meant for citizens, they should have access to them. For the rest of the people, they can come legally through the immigration process and be part of our development process. No problem. But it should be legal." He added, After 75 years of independence, I think any aware citizen or any very well aware country should spare a thought about this situation, that how will the government identify non-citizens, what the legal process should be for them." Ambekar, however, reiterated that the RSS concerns were not directed against any particular community or religion. So, in that way, it is not against anybody. Anyone can follow any religion or worship any God, but as a country, our commitment to our identity, culture, unity, and integrity is, I think, the ultimate priority." The argument, Ambekar said, was ultimately about the countrys cultural identity. Any country has its own cultural identity. And that cultural identity builds the foundation for our national unity, national identity," he said. Bhagwats Global Outreach Elaborating on RSS chief Mohan Bhagwats visits to the US, the UK and Canada, Ambekar said it was this broader understanding of Bharat that Bhagwat sought to communicate during his recent overseas engagements. Ambekar said the visit was different from Bhagwats earlier overseas engagements, which were largely focused on the Indian diaspora. But this time, the purpose was to meet local people, particularly those from public life. They are important opinion-makers. The idea was to communicate and convey the message to them," he said. According to Ambekar, the message was about Bharat and the countrys growing potential. Bharat is changing at every level, and it has emerged as a great source of potential, not only for Bharat but for the world as well," he said. Ambekar also emphasised the need to present Bharat as a cultural nation rather than viewing it solely through the political framework of a nation-state. Bharat is a cultural nation that has evolved over centuries through its cultural practices, traditions and way of life," he said. Hindu Rashtra: Cultural, Not Political Ambekar acknowledged that the RSS needed to do more to explain its understanding of Hindu, Hindutva and Hindu Rashtra to the world. Yes, definitely. We need to do it," he said, pointing to the global relevance of what he described as Indias civilisational values. Take yoga, for example. It is helping people even in the modern world. The same is true of meditation. These are age-old practices. I do not know when they originated, but they remain very relevant and helpful in the modern world," he said. He added, We have strong cultural values and a strong foundation, such as the family system. We also have a particular way of thinking about the environment and our relationship with it." The most politically significant clarification, however, came on the idea of Hindu Rashtra. Ambekar rejected the interpretation that Hindu Rashtra was simply a political entity waiting to be created. He has not said that he is interested in creating a Hindu Rashtra. Hindu Rashtra is already there," he said, referring to Bhagwats remarks. As long as the last person continues to follow these cultural traditions and identities, it is the Rashtra," he added. Ambekar said the idea was not about creating a new political structure but about reviving awareness of an existing civilisational identity. So, it is not a political concept. It is a cultural concept of recognising this cultural identity and these traditions," he said. He described the process as one of recovering the memory" of Bharats cultural identity. When people realise, Oh, this is our identity, this is our culture, they will embrace it and take pride in it," Ambekar said. For the RSS, then, the second century is not simply about expanding its organisational footprint. Its unfinished task, Ambekar said, remains reaching every household and every locality while building a society capable of taking responsibility for its own social and national life. Sunil Ambekar stated that a nationwide National Register of Citizens is necessary to clearly establish who is an Indian citizen, ensuring that only legal citizens can participate in the democratic process and access government facilities. He also linked negative demographic changes to concerns regarding national unity, security, and the historical context of the 1947 Partition.

headline: Another Blow To Akhilesh Yadav: 3 Rebel SP MLAs To Join BJP On October 14
content: Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh and Vinod Chaturvedi - are set to join BJP on October 14 at a programme in Gauriganj, Amethi Will the Samajwadi Party face another setback ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections? Three rebel SP MLAs Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh and Vinod Chaturvedi are set to formally join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on October 14 at a programme in Gauriganj, Amethi. A fourth rebel, Manoj Kumar Pandey, has already joined the Yogi Adityanath government as a minister, although his formal induction into the BJP has not been confirmed. The proposed induction of the three legislators marks another development in the political realignment that began during the February 2024 Rajya Sabha elections, when several SP MLAs cross-voted in favour of BJP candidates, defying their partys official position. - UP Rajya Sabha Polls: Samajwadi Party Drops Plan To Field Third Candidate, Clears Way For BJP's 8 Nominees - Only Akhilesh Can Defeat BJP: Awadhesh Prasads Big Claim Ahead Of 2027 UP Polls | n18 - BJP Announces Candidates For UP Rajya Sabha Polls, Dharampal Singh, Shruti Gangwar Among 8 Names - BJP Knows How To Win. Nitin Nabin Now Wants It To Listen | Saffron Scoop The October 14 programme is expected to be attended by senior BJP leaders, including state president Pankaj Chaudhary and national general secretary Smriti Irani, the party insiders said. Who Are The Three MLAs Joining BJP? Rakesh Pratap Singh represents Gauriganj in Amethi, Abhay Singh is the MLA from Gosainganj in Ayodhya, and Vinod Chaturvedi represents Kalpi in Jalaun district. The three legislators have been at odds with the SP leadership following their support for BJP candidates in the Rajya Sabha elections. Their proposed entry into the BJP would formalise a political separation that has been developing since the cross-voting episode. Rakesh Pratap Singh has also publicly criticised the SP leadership over several political and ideological issues. His proposed induction is particularly significant in Amethi, where local political alignments remain important to both the BJP and the opposition. Manoj Kumar Pandey, the SP MLA from Unchahar in Rae Bareli, is the fourth prominent rebel associated with the episode. He was among the legislators who cross-voted during the Rajya Sabha elections and was subsequently expelled by the SP. Pandey has since been inducted into the Yogi Adityanath cabinet. However, the distinction between joining the state government and formally joining the BJP is important: October 14 induction identify Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh and Vinod Chaturvedi as the three legislators scheduled to join the party. What Does This Mean For 2027 Elections? The developments come as the BJP and SP prepare for the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The induction of sitting legislators could give the BJP additional political networks in their constituencies, while the SP faces questions about internal cohesion following the Rajya Sabha cross-voting episode. However, the electoral implications of the defections will depend on local voter responses, candidate selection and the broader contest in 2027. The formal induction of the three MLAs on October 14, if completed as scheduled, will be the next concrete step in this political realignment. headline: Meloni's overhaul of Italian electoral system | Explained
content: With just more than a year to go before her coalition government has to step down for election, Italys Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has successfully introduced a set of reforms in parliament to overhaul the European countrys electoral system to introduce a fully proportional structure with bonus seats for the most popular party or coalition. T The approval for the reforms comes weeks after Ms. Melonis centre-right coalition, in its first term, became the longest-serving administration in the country since the Second World War, and the move has been heralded by its supporters as key to ensure political stability. However, critics and Opposition lawmakers have raised concerns, saying that the overhaul is aimed at ensuring that the ruling coalition, trailing in opinion polls, hold on to power. What was the existing system in Italy? The fact that Ms. Melonis administration made the record for the longest continuous post-war reign in its first term shows that Italian politicians have always had trouble staying in power. Following the Second World War and the end of the dictatorship of Benito Mussolini, the first republic devised the parliament in such a way that it would be difficult for a single party to consolidate power. While the whole system has gone through multiple changes thorugh the years, the complex multi-member constituencies and proportional representation at the base incentivised coalitions and ensured decentralisation. The system that brought Ms. Meloni to power in 2022 was a hybrid one, nicknamed Rosatellum after independent lawmaker Ettore Rosato, where roughly 64% of seats in both the 400-member Chamber of Deputies and the 200-member Senate were decided through proportional representation while the remaining 36% seats went to first-past-the-post winners. While first-past-the-post seats gave popular candidates entry into parliament and proportional representation, where seat allocation for a party or coalition was decided based on its vote share, ensured that smaller and regional had their voices in parliament. What are the changes under the new system? The new rules, approved by lawmakers in a secret ballot on Thursday (October 8, 2026) with 227 votes against 164, scraps the first-past-the-post seats and puts the whole parliament under proportional representation. While similar systems have existed previously, the contentious/ambitious clause guarantees up to 70 bonus seats in the Chamber, and 35 in the Senate, to the party or coalition that secure at least 42% votes. This, according to the supporters of the rules, will ensure that polls that would in other cases turn out inconclusive could still produce a majority government with enough strength to run the parliament. If several parties or coalitions go past the 42% mark, the bonus will be awarded to the entity with the most votes. The bonus seats are capped to prevent any party or coalition from getting more than 220 seats in the Chamber and 113 in the Senate. The rules have also set a bar on entry for parties or coalitions to parliament, with coalitions having to secure at least 10% votes and individual parties 3% to be considered for seat-sharing under the representation system. The reforms have also raised the number of signatures needed for new parties or those that are currently not in parliament from 1,500 to 6,000, a move critics say would make it difficult for smaller parties to enter parliament. How is the Prime Minister and her allies seeing the reform? Ms. Meloni has projected the reforms as a way to ensure that Italy will always have a stable government with the bonus seats giving popular coalitions the required majority in parliament. Stable governments and greater participation mean more continuity, more accountability, and a greater ability to provide concrete answers to Italians, the Prime Minister wrote in a social media post after the reforms were approved. Calling the changes a revolution, Giovanni Donzelli, a senior leader of Ms. Melonis party, told AFP that Italians will finally have the real weight with their vote as the will choose the coalition, the platform, and the candidate for Prime Minister. What is the Opposition reaction to the move? While the administration has touted the reforms as a step towards political stability, major Opposition parties, who are leading in opinion polls with the tenure of the current government ending in December 2027, has flagged attempts by Ms. Meloni to stay in power. Calling the reforms a mess, Guiseppe Conte, former Prime Minister and leader of opposition Five Stars Movement told the AFP that it is a convoluted scheme devised solely to find a formula to gain an advantage in the upcoming elections. The rise of a new far-right party, the National Future, led by former General Roberto Vannacci, is also eroding Ms. Melonis vote base, meaning she would find it hard to garner an outright majority for her coalition in the next general election. Opposition parties have vowed to challenge the reforms in court, where, they believe, most of the new provisions could be struck down, a possibility that could encourage Ms. Meloni to trust her odds with the new provisions and call a snap election.

headline: China to resume October fuel exports after a brief halt, trade sources say
content: China is set to resume October refined fuel exports after a brief halt during its Golden Week holiday, a move that will help ease tight global fuel markets, four traders familiar with the matter said on Friday (October 9,, 2026). China has approved October exports of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel combined at around 3.7 million metric tons, according to two separate industry participants. China began curbing fuel exports in March to safeguard domestic fuel supplies as the Iran war disrupted crude oil flows and refinery production, but relaxed controls between July and September. While Beijing typically regulates fuel exports through a quota system, it has recently tightened oversight by vetting shipments on a month-by-month basis. China's National Development & Reform Commission and its Ministry of Commerce did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

headline: From Jailer To Jailbird: The Prison Paradox Of Karnataka DIG M Somashekar
content: Once tasked with probing actor Darshan's VIP treatment in jail, M Somashekar now finds himself behind bars over alleged release of a life convict using a forged Supreme Court order An officer who once headed Bengalurus Central Prison at Parappana Agrahara a place where he was responsible for maintaining discipline, monitoring prisoners and ensuring that the prison system functioned by the book is now himself behind bars. - 'Have To Draw A Line Somewhere': On Leniency To Death Row Convicts, SC Says 'Forgiving Nature Must End' - Journalist Who Alleged Sexual Assault By Delhi Police Official Detained With 16 Others Over FIR Demand - 'I Dont Know Kannada': Bengaluru Zomato Manager Tells Staff 'Learn Hindi Or Leave Job', Video Sparks Outrage - UP Woman Catches Husband On Date With Girlfriend, Clings To His Car Bonnet As He Drives Away | Video Somashekar, who was serving as a DIG in the Karnataka Prisons and Correctional Services Department, has been arrested in connection with the alleged release of a life convict from Parappana Agrahara on the basis of a forged Supreme Court order. But there is another chapter to Somashekars association with the same prison that makes his present situation particularly striking. Just two years ago, it was Somashekar who was on the other side of an investigation when actor Darshan Thoogudeepa was accused of receiving VIP treatment inside Parappana Agrahara. He was then investigating alleged irregularities within the prison system. Now, he is the one facing allegations of corruption. The Darshan Controversy Lets go back a couple of years. In August 2024, a photograph emerged showing Darshan, then in judicial custody in the Renukaswamy murder case, sitting on a chair inside the prison with a coffee mug and a cigarette, alongside history-sheeters including Wilson Garden Naga. M Somashekar, former Karnataka DIG (Prisons), was arrested for allegedly facilitating the release of a life convict using a forged Supreme Court order. Somashekar was the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara when life convict A Shankar was released on November 13, 2018. A Shankar was serving a life sentence for a 2001 kidnapping-for-ransom case. The alleged fraud regarding Shankar's release was discovered in May 2026, nearly eight years later. Somashekar previously investigated alleged irregularities at Parappana Agrahara prison, including VIP treatment for actor Darshan Thoogudeepa in August 2024. Soon after, a video of Darshan allegedly making a video call from inside the prison also surfaced. The photograph and video triggered a political and public storm, raising serious questions about how a high-profile prisoner could allegedly receive privileges inside one of Karnatakas most closely watched prisons. And it was Somashekar, then DIG (Prisons), who filed three complaints at the Parappana Agrahara police station, paving the way for criminal cases and a detailed investigation. Five teams were constituted to investigate the alleged lapses. CCTV footage, visitor records and the conduct of prison officials were examined. Nine prison officials were eventually suspended, and Darshan was shifted from Parappana Agrahara to Ballari jail. At that point, Somashekar was the senior prison official demanding accountability from within the system. The Darshan controversy raised questions about cigarettes, coffee, chairs, mobile phones, photographs and access. The Shankar case raises a far more fundamental question who checked the court order before the prison gates were opened? A prison is built around layers of verification. Prison records are supposed to be maintained. Officials are expected to verify whether an order is genuine before acting on it. A life convict cannot ordinarily walk out simply because someone produces a document claiming to have come from the countrys highest court. There should have been checks at every stage. The Case That Led To Somashekars Arrest Today, the equation has completely changed. Somashekar is himself the subject of a criminal investigation involving another prisoner and another alleged failure of the prison system. This time, the case goes back to November 13, 2018. A life convict, A Shankar, walked out of Parappana Agrahara after prison authorities acted on what was presented as a Supreme Court order directing his release. Investigators now allege that the order was forged. Shankar was serving a life sentence in connection with a 2001 kidnapping-for-ransom case, and his conviction and sentence had been upheld by the Karnataka High Court and subsequently the Supreme Court. Yet he walked out of prison. Not on parole. Not after a sentence reduction. Not following a fresh, genuine judicial order. But on the strength of a document that investigators now allege was fabricated. And the most startling part is that the alleged fraud did not come to light immediately. It was only in May 2026, nearly eight years after Shankar walked out, that the prison authorities reportedly verified the document and approached the Parappana Agrahara police. The Supreme Court authorities subsequently confirmed that the purported order did not exist. The investigation initially led to S Srikanth, then a Second Division Assistant working in the Convict Prisoner Section. Investigators allege that he was involved in the forged document and that money reportedly around Rs. 6 lakh changed hands in connection with the release. But that only opened up a bigger question: How does a forged Supreme Court order enter a prison, pass through the official system and ultimately result in a life convict walking out of the gates? This question brought the prison administration itself under scrutiny and eventually led investigators to Somashekar. He was the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara when Shankar was released. Police allege that he had a role in facilitating the release and have questioned his conduct in connection with the case. There are also allegations relating to Shankars parole and the manner in which prison procedures were followed. The investigation has thrown up another serious allegation against Somashekar. Police have said that Shankars wife alleged that the officer sexually exploited her in connection with assurances of helping secure her husbands release. That allegation remains part of the investigation and is yet to be established by a court. From Demanding Accountability To Facing Investigation This is not simply a story about one officer and one prisoner. It is about a system where a life convict allegedly walked through the gates of a major prison on the strength of a document that did not exist. And it is about an officer who, in another chapter of his career, had himself been demanding answers over alleged irregularities inside that very prison. There is, of course, a crucial distinction between the two cases. One raises questions about the checks and safeguards meant to prevent an unlawful release, while the other concerns accountability for alleged irregularities within the prison system. M Somashekar was arrested in connection with the alleged unlawful release of life convict A Shankar from Bengaluru Central Prison in November 2018 using a fabricated Supreme Court order.

headline: Cancer Drugs In India May Get 20-70% Cheaper As NPPA Approves Price-Cutting Move
content: The NPPA's decision aims to make cancer treatment more affordable by curbing excessive trade margins, with patients expected to save around Rs. 2,500 crore annually. Many cancer medicines in India could become much cheaper, with prices falling by 20 to 70 per cent, after the governments drug pricing watchdog, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), approved a cap on how much sellers can add to the price between the factory and the patient. The authority has approved in principle a proposal to cap this difference, called the trade margin, at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price (MRP), the price printed on the pack. The government estimates that patients will save about Rs. 2,500 crore a year. - Campaign Without Evidence: 42 Ex-Judges Back EC, Hit Out At Vote Theft Claims Amid Opposition Protest - BJP's Big J&K Huddle: BL Santhosh, Jitendra Singh To Meet MLAs After Statehood Resolution Row - SC Refuses To Pass Interim Order To Suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over SIR Decisions, Issues Notice To EC - SC Stays Execution Of Terror Operative In 2008 Ahmedabad Blasts Case, Issues Notice To Gujarat Govt The NPPA has approved capping trade margins at 30 per cent of the MRP on identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. It expects the move to bring down MRPs by 20 to 70 per cent, depending on each medicines existing trade structure and mark-up. The approval is subject to the finalisation of the list of drugs to be covered. The Authority deliberated on the proposal to regulate the trade margin for identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines by capping the trade margin at 30% of MRP on the same lines as the TMR exercise undertaken in 2019," said the minutes of the NPPAs meeting held on Thursday. The authority noted that the proposed intervention is expected to reduce MRP broadly in the range of 2070%, depending upon the existing trade structure and mark-up of individual medicines, and is estimated to result in annual savings of approximately 2,500 crore." The expected benefits, it said, include a reduction in out-of-pocket expenditure, improved affordability and accessibility, a reduction in excessive trade mark-ups and greater transparency in prices applicable to patients. What Has The Authority Decided? The NPPA approved a proposal to cap the trade margin on identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30% of the MRP. This cap is expected to reduce MRPs by 20% to 70% and result in annual savings of approximately 2,500 crore for patients. The anti-cancer drug market in India has an annual turnover of around 12,500 crore, with non-scheduled drugs comprising the majority. The NPPA previously used similar powers in 2019, leading to MRP reductions of up to 91% for 526 brands. The NPPA approved the proposal under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013, which gives the government extraordinary powers to act in the public interest. The Authority unanimously agreed that, in view of excessive profiteering in anti-cancer drugs and its impact on patients, consumer interest must remain paramount." The decision follows a direction from the Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), which asked the NPPA to implement trade margin rationalisation on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, as was done in 2019. The DoP has also asked the Union Health Ministry to set up an expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to recommend which drugs should be covered. It has sought the committees report by October 14, 2026. The list can be updated periodically as the market and public health needs change. Indias National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), 2022, comprises 388 drugs, including 63 anti-cancer drugs. These scheduled medicines are already subject to price control through the ceiling-price mechanism. The anti-cancer drug market comprises approximately 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs. 12,500 crore. Of this, scheduled cancer drugs account for approximately Rs. 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs. An analysis of data from Pharmarack, a research firm, indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases. The NPPA, in its minutes, also noted substantial variations in transaction prices across retail, hospital and e-pharmacy channels, including significant differences in discounts from MRP. What Does It Mean For Patients? The trade margin is the gap between the price at which a medicine leaves the manufacturer and the price a patient finally pays, after distributors, wholesalers and retailers take their cut. Non-scheduled drugs are those outside the governments price-control list. Their prices are not fixed, but the NPPA monitors them to ensure that increases do not exceed 10 per cent a year. A trade margin cap of 30 per cent of the MRP works out to 42.86 per cent of the price to the stockist, the price at which the manufacturer sells into the distribution chain. For a drug with an MRP of Rs. 100, everyone between the manufacturer and the patient would be able to retain a maximum of Rs. 30 once the cap takes effect. The authority expects lower out-of-pocket spending, better affordability and access, reduced excessive mark-ups and greater transparency in the prices patients pay. Since the cap has not yet been notified, the actual price cuts will become clear only after the drug list is finalised and manufacturers recalculate their MRPs. Supreme Courts Recent Observations The decision comes weeks after the Supreme Court criticised cancer drug pricing. On September 22, the court described the overpricing of essential cancer medicines as daylight robbery of patients. On September 29, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta pointed to a cancer drug supplied to retailers for about Rs. 2,700 but carrying an MRP of about Rs. 27,000. It asked the Centre why the 16 per cent retailer margin used under the DPCO should not apply to all medicines. The court has listed the matter for further hearing on October 12. The NPPA used the same Paragraph 19 powers in 2019. That exercise, notified on February 27, 2019, covered 42 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. The 2019 exercise resulted in substantial reductions in MRP, including reductions of up to 91% for 526 brands, with annual savings of approximately Rs. 984 crore." Activists Say Cap Is Not Enough The Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments, represented by co-convenors Jyotsna Singh and K M Gopakumar, said the cap alone would not make many drugs affordable. The NPPAs 30% cap on trade margins for non-scheduled cancer medicines will not make many of these drugs affordable, particularly patented ones." They said prices of some cancer medicines rose even after the 2019 cap was introduced, and that pembrolizumab (Keytruda) still costs around Rs. 1,95,000 per vial. They called for the use of public health safeguards in the Patents Act: What is needed is the use of the public health safeguards in the Patents Act, especially government use license under Section 100, and compulsory license to enable generic production and set a ceiling on MRP." A pharma industry official, who requested anonymity, supported the governments move. Industry market data indicates that most non-NLEM medicines operate within normal channel-discount ranges. Unusually high margins are concentrated in a relatively small group of products, particularly certain hospital-based and specialised therapies. These distortions may be corrected at the point where they arise." The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) approved capping trade margins at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price (MRP) for non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, which is expected to lower MRPs by 20 to 70 per cent and save patients about Rs. 2,500 crore annually.

content: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian told his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, on Thursday that Tehran was "trying our best to end the war as soon as possible" Irans President Masoud Pezeshkian told his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, on Thursday that Tehran was trying our best to end the war as soon as possible", and thanked him for Moscows position on the situation in West Asia. Wed like to thank you for your position regarding the situation in the region, Pezeshkian told Putin. We are trying our best to put an end to the war as soon as possible, and make sure our rights are respected". - Trump Pulling Back From Iran? But if they (US) act unilaterally, its impossible to accomplish in near future", he said. Putin Pledges To Do Everything To Help End War During the meeting with Pezeshkian, Putin vowed to do everything" to help end the war and contribute to the settlement" of the conflict. His remarks came as talks between the US and Iran came at a standstill last month, after the two sides reported a fresh spate of strikes. We are ready to do everything that is in our power to contribute to the settlement of this situation," Putin said during the meeting, according to Russias Tass news agency. Putin said Iran had made real efforts" to end the war. Pezeshkian, meanwhile, affirmed that Iran would not walk away" from efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the conflict. The war in West Asia began on February 28 this year, after the US-Israel alliance launched joint strikes on Iran amid stalled talks over the countrys nuclear programme. In retaliation, Tehran targeted US-linked facilities across the Gulf, while also blocking the key Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway that provides for nearly 20 per cent of global energy trade. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Vladimir Putin that Tehran was trying its best to end the war as soon as possible and ensure their rights are respected, while thanking Moscow for its position on the regional conflict.

headline: No New Petrol, Diesel Car Registrations From 2031? CAQM Panel's Plan To Help Delhi Breathe Easy
content: IV vehicles should be phased out by 2030, followed by BS-VI two-wheelers by 2035 and BS-VI four-wheelers by 2040 A committee of experts constituted by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has recommended a phased transition from petrol and diesel vehicles to zero-tailpipe emission vehicles across Delhi-NCR by 2040 in a report submitted to the panel. The 15-member panel has proposed a gradual phase-out of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, with different timelines for vehicles adhering to various Bharat Stage (BS) emission standards. The recommendations are aimed at curbing vehicular emissions, a major contributor to air pollution in the national capital region. - BJP Knows How To Win. Nitin Nabin Now Wants It To Listen | Saffron Scoop - Tamil Nadus First Barrier-Free Toll Plaza Opens At Paranur: No Stopping, Automatic Toll Collection - Delhi AQI: Capital's Worst October Start Since 2020 As Pollution Worsens For Fifth Day | WATCH - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey Vehicular emissions are among the sources of air pollution in the national capital region, alongside road and construction dust, industrial emissions and pollution from other sources. The problem becomes particularly acute during the winter months, when unfavourable meteorological conditions can trap pollutants close to the ground, worsening air quality across Delhi and neighbouring areas. According to the proposed roadmap, BS-IV vehicles should be phased out by 2030, followed by BS-VI two-wheelers by 2035 and BS-VI four-wheelers by 2040. The committee has also recommended stopping the registration of new ICE four-wheelers from 2031. If implemented, the proposal would mark a significant shift in the regions vehicle policy, pushing consumers towards electric vehicles and other zero-tailpipe emission alternatives. For vehicles currently operating in Delhi-NCR that comply with emission standards below BS-IV, the panel has recommended an immediate exit from the region, in line with the guidelines of the Delhi Electric Vehicle (EV) Policy. The panel has identified electric vehicles as a key alternative to conventional petrol and diesel vehicles. Besides reducing tailpipe emissions, a transition to EVs could also help lower Indias dependence on oil imports. The committee, headed by IIT Madras professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala, was constituted by CAQM in December 2025. It includes representatives from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the Ministry of Heavy Industries, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and NITI Aayog. The recommendations outline a long-term roadmap for transitioning Delhi-NCRs vehicle fleet towards zero-tailpipe emission mobility. However, the proposed timelines are recommendations by the expert panel and their implementation would depend on the decisions taken by the relevant authorities. An expert committee has recommended stopping the registration of new ICE four-wheelers from 2031. According to the proposed roadmap, BS-IV vehicles should be phased out by 2030, followed by BS-VI two-wheelers by 2035 and BS-VI four-wheelers by 2040.

headline: Delhi Police Unlikely To Allow Jantar Mantar Protest, Multi-Agency Demobilisation Plan In Place | Exclusive
content: Intelligence agencies are monitoring social media and communications linked to the proposed protest, sharing real-time inputs to prevent crowds from gathering at Jantar Mantar. Unlike earlier, Delhi Police is in no mood to grant permission for the Cockroach Janta Partys proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, with top-level sources saying the force has already initiated a comprehensive plan to prevent a large gathering in the New Delhi area, often referred to as Lutyens Delhi. According to senior sources, the demobilisation plan has already been set in motion, with additional police deployment being arranged at Delhis borders in coordination with police forces from adjoining states. District authorities are also expected to put in place necessary restrictions and checks to prevent large groups from entering the capital. - Jantar Mantar Protest Highlights: Atishi, Sanjay Singh Among 700 Detained, Internet Suspended Till 9 PM Amid Section 163 Restrictions - Delhi Metro To Shut 57 Stations From 9 PM Tonight Ahead Of CJP's Planned Protest | Full List Here - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured Sources said intelligence agencies are closely tracking activity across various social media platforms, as well as communications involving organisations and individuals linked to the proposed mobilisation, and transferring inputs in real time for quick action. The objective, officials said, is to prevent crowds from gathering around Jantar Mantar in the first place. A senior-level source said additional forces have already been deployed, while more personnel, including the Rapid Action Force (RAF), are expected to be positioned as required. This time, officials are preparing to use a graded crowd-dispersal strategy rather than relying solely on a single large-scale deployment. The security plan also includes strengthening surveillance in areas that previously had limited or no CCTV coverage. Such grey areas" are being brought under additional camera coverage, while police personnel are expected to use various recording devices, including body-worn cameras and other wearable equipment, to document the situation on the ground. Sources described the preparations as a massive security exercise aimed at preventing the mobilisation from turning into a large-scale gathering around Jantar Mantar. Police deployment is also expected at major railway and transport stations across Delhi, while senior police formations will maintain enhanced deployment around identified sensitive locations, sources claimed. A pre-decided radius around key areas is also expected to have an increased police presence. Delhi Police unlikely to grant permission for the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. A comprehensive plan has been initiated to prevent a large gathering in New Delhi. Additional police deployment is being arranged at Delhis borders in coordination with adjoining states. Intelligence agencies are tracking social media and communications related to the mobilization. Additional forces, including the Rapid Action Force, are expected to be positioned as required. At Delhis borders, coordination with adjoining state police forces is expected to form a key component of the strategy. Officials are preparing for the possibility of groups attempting to enter Delhi from multiple directions. The overall approach, according to sources, is focused on advance deployment, surveillance, inter-state coordination and phased crowd management, with the aim of preventing a large congregation from developing around Jantar Mantar. Delhi Police has initiated a multi-agency demobilisation plan, deploying additional forces at Delhis borders, coordination with adjoining states, and positioning the Rapid Action Force.
