headline: Delhi Braces For Weekend: Barricades, Dry Days, Hotel Checks | Should You Step Out At All?
content: Central forces, barricades and shut liquor shops mark Delhis tense run-up to Saturdays Jantar Mantar protest. Here is what residents can expect, and how to plan the weekend. Delhi is bracing for a tense weekend. Ahead of Saturdays Jantar Mantar protest over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, police have called in Central forces, put up barricades and asked liquor vends to shut. Residents should expect diversions and delays in Central Delhi, though no citywide shutdown has been announced. The protest has been jointly called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the All India Students Association, and several Opposition parties are expected to join. - Jantar Mantar Protest Highlights: Atishi, Sanjay Singh Among 700 Detained, Internet Suspended Till 9 PM Amid Section 163 Restrictions - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber Delhi Police have not granted permission, citing prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Officers say intelligence inputs suggest more than 50,000 people, including from neighbouring states, could try to reach the Capital. The heaviest restrictions are around New Delhi district, but checks extend well beyond it. Why Is This Happening? The Opposition has said its protests will continue until Kumar resigns, alleging irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Demonstrations outside the Election Commissions Nirvachan Sadan have been near-daily, and Hindustan Times reported that Kumars Z+ security was upgraded after protesters traced his Delhi residence. CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das says the party informed police in writing. Trinamool Congress leader Mamata Banerjee has said she will travel to Delhi. What Has The City Put In Place? The Home Ministry has made 221 Central Armed Police Forces companies, around 23,000 personnel, available to Delhi Police from October 8 to 12, officers said, among the largest such deployments for a protest since the 2020 Northeast Delhi riots. Delhi Police strength in New Delhi district, now 5,000, could rise to 15,000. Multi-layered barricades are going up on roads leading to Jantar Mantar and Parliament, and prohibitory orders cover Rajghat. Police have asked the Excise Department to keep liquor shops shut on Friday and Saturday, and Central Delhi hotels have reportedly been asked to restrict bookings. Police are also visiting hotels, guest houses and paying-guest accommodations, officials said, questioning guests deemed suspicious". Stays between October 8 and 11, large groups in their 20s and early 30s, and rooms booked by someone else draw scrutiny. Officers say no one is being stopped or detained, only questioned. But railway police in Bhopal said they detained 21 people on the Goa Express heading to Delhi, and a Mumbai-based All India Youth Federation member alleged he was accused of travelling in a protest group. Will You Be Stuck In Traffic? Likely, if you are in or near Central Delhi. Here is how the weekend looks on current information: Should You Stay Home This Weekend? There is no curfew or stay-indoors advisory in the reports so far. Section 163 orders restrict assemblies, not ordinary movement, and the build-up is focused on Central Delhi. If your plans are elsewhere in the city, they are unlikely to change, but check advisories before leaving. If you do not need to be near Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street or Rajghat on Saturday, avoid them. What Are People Saying Online? Journalist Ifrah Mufti claimed a short drive through Connaught Place turned into a 45-minute-plus ordeal of barricades, diversions and loudspeaker appeals. It may be a regular Thursday in CP, but today driving through the heart of Delhi feels less like a commute and more like navigating a protest site. Police everywhere, barricades at every turn, traffic crawling and loudspeaker announcements following you from one block to another: Police ke kaam mein baadha na daalein", zyada log ikattha na hon" and so on.Every few metres, another diversion, another barricade, another bottleneck. What should ordinarily be a short drive between one block to another has turned into a 45-minute-plus ordeal. Ifrah Mufti (@ifrahmufti) October 8, 2026 Delhi Police, meanwhile, have posted Instagram Reels under Respect her dignity", in which women officers describe abuse during protests; DCP Shrishti Pandey also criticised self-proclaimed journalists" for allegedly provoking personnel. A video circulating on social media allegedly shows a police official at an Old Delhi mosque asking people to keep families away from the protest. Delhi Police- now offering free dont protest" sermons inside mosquesVibrant democracy loading John Brittas (@JohnBrittas) October 9, 2026 What Should You Do To Prepare? Carry valid photo ID, matching the name on any hotel booking. Add generous buffer time for trips through Central Delhi, airports and railway stations, where police are checking for large groups. Buy liquor before shutters come down, since shops are to stay shut Friday and Saturday. Postpone non-urgent Central Delhi appointments until after the weekend. Follow Delhi Traffic Police and DMRC advisories for diversions or station closures. Visiting from out of town? Expect questions at hotels if you arrive in a large group. Protesters and opposition parties are demanding the resignation or arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the handling of the electoral process by the Election Commission.

headline: US To Livestream Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasan's Execution By Firing Squad, First Since 1945
content: The decision comes amid renewed debate over capital punishment in the US following a botched lethal injection in Tennessee last week. The US military will livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the gunman who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009, the Pentagon has said. The broadcast would mark an unprecedented move in the history of US executions. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is scheduled to be executed on December 3 at Fort Hood, where he carried out the shooting at a medical facility using a laser-sighted handgun. He would be the first person executed by firing squad by the US military since 1945. - Pete Hegseth Says Fort Hood Shooter's Execution By Firing Squad Will Be Livestreamed - US Lost 81 Aircraft Including F-35s, F-15Es In Iran War; Tehran Mocks Real Toll Is Far Higher - Trump Approves Firing Squad Execution Of Ex-Army Major Nidal Hasan In Rare Move: Why It Matters - Trumps Midterm Crisis? Why 41 GOP Candidates Are Distancing Themselves From Him The decision comes amid renewed debate over capital punishment in the US following a botched lethal injection in Tennessee last week. It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," a Pentagon official told Reuters on condition of anonymity. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who backed the move to execute Hasan by firing squad, also confirmed the livestream plans in a post on X. Courts have previously blocked media efforts to televise executions in the US. Experts said they were unaware of any other country that livestreams or televises legal executions. Public executions have become extremely rare worldwide. Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan are among the places known to have carried them out in recent years. In the US, public executions were once widely attended events, particularly lynchings carried out by white mobs against Black Americans during the 20th century. Death penalty experts said the last legally sanctioned public execution in the country took place in 1936, when thousands watched the hanging of a young Black man convicted of raping a white woman. Hegseth described the decision to execute Hasan at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1 pm as a no-brainer". The timing, day, and location roughly match the circumstances of the 2009 shooting. Well make sure that people can watch it, that its public. Because people need to understand that there are serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said during an appearance on the Human Events Daily programme. When asked whether Hasan had made any final requests, Hegseth said: Dont care. Well see him on December 3." President Must Approve Firing Squad Execution A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013 after convicting him on 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. Hasan, now 56, was due to be deployed to Afghanistan just weeks after the shooting. Police shot him during his arrest, leaving him partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair. US military law requires presidential approval for an execution by firing squad. President Donald Trump authorised Hasans execution on Monday following a recommendation from Hegseth, the Pentagon said. The White House declined to comment on whether Trump supported livestreaming the execution and referred questions to the Pentagon. Death Penalty Action, an organisation that opposes capital punishment, said Hasans execution would be the first military execution since 1961. According to the Death Penalty Information Centre, that execution was carried out by hanging. The last known executions by firing squad in the US military took place in 1945, the centre reported. Eugene Fidell, a lawyer, author and military law expert who lectures at Yale Law School, said livestreaming the execution would be highly unusual. It would be extremely, extremely strange" to livestream the event, Fidell said. Although firing squads have a long history in US military law, Fidell said he knew of no precedent for televising or livestreaming an execution. He added that Hasan would need to file a lawsuit in federal court to challenge a public display of his death. The Supreme Court has never addressed this question, and its an interesting question whether the current Supreme Court would put on their originalist hat and say, Well, it was OK in 1790, so what the hell?'" Fidell said. Jonathan Lurie, an author and historian of military justice, questioned the purpose of making the execution public. Whats the point of it? Who would want to see that?" Lurie said. Firing Squads And Other Execution Methods At least five US states have provisions allowing execution by firing squad, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre. South Carolina carried out the first firing squad execution in the US in 15 years in 2025. The Trump administration recently expanded the methods permitted for federal executions involving the gravest crimes. The options now include firing squads, electrocution and gas asphyxiation. The expansion came partly in response to growing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, a method that has also presented challenges during executions. Tennessees attempt last week to execute Christa Pike marked the states first planned execution of a woman in more than 200 years. However, prison personnel failed in their attempts to administer the lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate alive and hospitalised. Pikes lawyers said on Wednesday that she had awoken angry and confused" in hospital. They added that she remained seriously ill and shackled to her hospital bed. (With input from Reuters) Former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed by a firing squad of soldiers on December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, following presidential approval from President Donald Trump and a recommendation from US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.

headline: Trump Praises Immigrant Tech CEOs While Cracking Down On Foreign Workers: The Two Sides Of MAGA Policy
content: Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, hours after JD Vance announced the suspension of Microsoft and other technology firms from a key employment-based green-card programme. From calling Google CEO Sundar Pichai a monster" to honouring Microsoft chief Satya Nadella, US President Donald Trump has celebrated Indian-origin tech leaders even as his administration tightens the screws on the immigration pathways used by skilled foreign workers. There is an unmistakable contradiction at the heart of Donald Trumps approach to immigration. The US president wants America to lead the global technology race, celebrates the immigrant executives powering some of its biggest companies, and promises a new golden age of innovation. Yet his administration is simultaneously making it harder for skilled foreign workers to secure a permanent future in the country. - Trump Honours Microsoft CEO With Top Tech Medal After Vance Drops H-1B Hammer On Firm - Trumps $100,000 H-1B Fee Blocked Again: Second US Judge Rules Against Charge - US Green Card Setback: IT Giants Face PERM Suspension Amid Fraud Probe | Trump | H-1B | News18 - 'Modern-Day Thomas Edison': Trump Gives Musk With Top US Science Medal After Bitter Fallout The contradiction was on full display on Thursday, when Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, hours after Vice President JD Vance announced the suspension of Microsoft and several other technology companies from a key employment-based green-card programme. While Vance accused Microsoft of abusing the foreign-worker system, Trump was celebrating Nadella for transforming one of Americas most influential technology companies. For more than three decades, Satya Nadella has been a key figure in the transformation of Microsoft," Trump said during the ceremony, praising his leadership in cloud computing and the development of advanced artificial intelligence. Nadella, who was born in India and moved to the US to pursue his career, thanked the president on X, saying he was humbled to stand alongside so many giants of American innovation" and looked forward to advancing technology and driving American prosperity. The ceremony honoured six technology leaders, including Nadella, Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su and Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell. Five of the six were born outside the United States. The message was difficult to miss: immigrant entrepreneurs and executives remain central to Americas technological ambitions, even as the administration intensifies its scrutiny of foreign labour. US President Donald Trump honored Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Vice President JD Vance announced the suspension of Microsoft and several other technology companies from a key employment-based green-card program. The ceremony honored six technology leaders, including Nadella, Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, and Michael Dell. Five of the six technology leaders honored were born outside the United States. The US Department of Labor suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini from the PERM program. Sundar Pichais Monster Moment To Nadellas Medal Nadella was not the first Indian-origin technology leader to receive Trumps public praise in recent days. At a White House gathering of technology executives on September 29, Trump turned to Google CEO Sundar Pichai and offered an unusual compliment. This guy is a monster, and nobody knows him," Trump said, suggesting that Pichai had managed to remain relatively low-profile despite his enormous influence. All you have to know is SUNDARR! Sundar is his name." Pichai responded with humour, Hopefully a better tagline than Im a monster!" The exchange took place during a meeting on artificial intelligence, where Trump and technology leaders discussed the industrys approach to managing the risks of increasingly powerful AI systems. The episode offered a glimpse of Trumps admiration for technology executives who can help advance Americas ambitions in artificial intelligence. Pichai, like Nadella, is an Indian-born executive leading a global technology giant headquartered in the US. But the praise for these leaders sits alongside an increasingly restrictive approach to the foreign workers who help sustain the technology industry. Trumps Green-Card Crackdown On Thursday, the US Department of Labor announced that Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini would be suspended from participating in the Permanent Labor Certification, or PERM, programme. Under PERM, employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers for many employment-based green cards must demonstrate that qualified and available American workers are not being displaced and that hiring foreign employees will not adversely affect domestic wages and working conditions. The suspension means the department will neither accept new PERM applications nor process pending applications involving the named companies, according to Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling. The administration says the move is intended to tackle alleged abuse of the system and protect American workers. Vance singled out Microsoft, arguing that the company had laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vance said. He also accused employers of advertising jobs in ways that make it difficult to find American applicants before using foreign-worker programmes to fill positions. However, the figures cited by the administration do not, by themselves, establish that foreign workers replaced those who lost their jobs. Microsoft said approximately 80 per cent of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were intended to extend or change the status of existing employees, rather than recruit new workers. The company also maintained that it pays H-1B employees comparable compensation to other employees doing similar work. An H-1B visa and a green card serve different purposes. The former permits eligible foreign professionals to work temporarily in the US, while PERM is an important step towards permanent residency for many employer-sponsored applicants. The suspension does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas. The MAGA Distinction: Talent At The Top, Scrutiny At Workplace The apparent contradiction becomes easier to understand when viewed through the administrations priorities. Trumps immigration message is built around protecting American jobs and putting domestic workers first. At the same time, his economic agenda depends heavily on technological innovation, private investment and American leadership in AI, areas where major technology companies compete for highly specialised talent from across the world. An executive who builds a globally dominant company can be presented as proof of American innovation. A foreign professional hired by that same company, however, can become the subject of scrutiny over whether the recruitment process disadvantages American workers. This distinction also reflects the political appeal of separating the achievements of high-profile entrepreneurs from broader questions about immigration. Celebrating Nadella or Pichai does not necessarily mean endorsing an open-ended system for foreign employment or permanent residency. Yet the distinction has consequences beyond corporate boardrooms. Skilled workers often accept jobs in America with the expectation that years of employment could eventually lead to permanent residency. Restricting that pathway can make the country less attractive to international talent, particularly when other destinations compete for the same engineers, researchers and technology specialists. There is also a potential contradiction in the administrations argument about worker dependence. A green card can give an employee greater freedom to change employers, whereas remaining on a temporary, employer-dependent visa can make a worker more vulnerable to job loss. As immigration policy tightens, companies may have to rethink recruitment, retention and the balance between hiring locally and sourcing talent internationally. Can US Win The AI Race While Narrowing Its Talent Pipeline? Trump has repeatedly framed technological leadership as essential to Americas economic and strategic future, particularly as competition with China intensifies. His administrations public celebration of technology executives reflects that ambition. But innovation is not produced by CEOs alone. It also depends on the engineers, scientists, researchers and other specialists who develop and deploy new technologies. The US technology industry has long benefited from international talent, including professionals from India. If immigration restrictions make it harder for these workers to build long-term careers in America, companies could face higher recruitment costs, while competing countries could gain an opportunity to attract them. For India, the stakes extend beyond individual careers. The green-card suspension affects major Indian IT services companies and could add uncertainty for employees seeking permanent residency through their employers. America may be able to celebrate its immigrant technology leaders while tightening immigration rules. But sustaining its technological advantage will require more than medals, executive endorsements and promises of a golden age. It will also depend on whether the people who power that innovation continue to see the United States as a place where they can build a future. The US Department of Labor suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini from the Permanent Labor Certification, or PERM, programme to crack down on alleged system abuse and protect domestic workers.

headline: Delhi Police Check Hotels, Hostels Ahead Of CJP's Oct 10 Protest; Occupants, Staff Members Being Questioned
content: Delhi Police are checking hotels and guest houses ahead of the CJP protest on October 10. A report has claimed that guests at some locations were being questioned. Delhi Police teams are visiting hotels, guest houses, hostels and other accommodation facilities across the national capital and questioning occupants considered suspicious" ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, Hindustan Times reported on Thursday, citing at least four police officials aware of the action. According to the report, police personnel have been directed to check accommodation records, verify the identities of guests and scrutinise the purpose of their visits to Delhi. - CJP Oct 10 Protest: Delhi Police Step Up Vigil, Track 2,800 'Criminals', Monitor Buses, Borders - Delhi Protesters Bus-Stopping 'Stunt' Goes Viral As Internet Mocks Model Pose': 'Everyone Wants A Ticket To Bigg Boss' - Jantar Mantar Protest LIVE: Delhi Police Barricades Roads Amid Anti-CEC Protest Call | Delhi News - Congress Delhi Protest | Rahul Gandhi Pushes Women Cop; BJP Releases Video | Jantar Mantar | News18 The checks are aimed at identifying people who may have travelled to the national capital to participate in the proposed demonstration. At least one guest and two hotel staff members were quoted as saying that police officers had visited their establishments and asked questions about the nature and duration of their stays. The checks come as Delhi remains on high alert ahead of the planned protest, with extensive security arrangements being put in place across the national capital, according to sources cited by ANI. Delhi Police Check Hotel Registers, Question Guests HT reported that police officials had been instructed to visit hotels, hostels, guest houses and other temporary accommodation facilities to establish who was staying in the city. Delhi Police are checking hotels, guest houses and other accommodation facilities, questioning guests and verifying booking details. Around 23,000 security personnel are expected to be deployed across Delhi between October 8 and 12. CJP founder Abhijit Dipke has called for a march demanding the scrapping of the SIR exercise and accountability for alleged voter deletions. The teams are entering the premises, checking the occupant registers or logs maintained by owners and managers and checking against a list of factors," an officer was quoted as saying. According to people familiar with the checks cited by the report, the factors being examined include the duration of a guests stay, whether people have arrived in large groups and their stated purpose for visiting Delhi. Officials are treating stays between October 8 and 11 as a factor warranting scrutiny. The report mentioned that particular attention is being paid to groups comprising people in their 20s and early 30s. If they checked into the accommodation a day or two ago and plan to leave shortly after the weekend, they are being asked about their purpose of visit because they could potentially have come for the protest," an official was quoted as saying. Police personnel have also been instructed to pay attention to rooms booked by someone other than the occupant. A senior police officer was quoted as saying that personnel were checking identification documents submitted by guests against booking details. If there is any mismatch, the personnel may question the hotel staff, the guests or the persons who booked the rooms," the officer said. The report mentioned that police teams had also been given lists of four-star and five-star hotels, taking into account what an officer described as the social profile" of some protest leaders. Special Cell, Crime Branch Tracking CJP Leaders According to the report, local police personnel have been tasked with identifying potential protest participants, while specialised units, including the Special Cell and Crime Branch, have been directed to track key members of the CJP, left-wing organisations and civil society groups. Locating the place of stay of social media influencer Dhruv Rathee and CJPs founder Abhijeet Dipke is the prime responsibility of the Special Cell and Crime Branch teams," an officer told the report. Police are also monitoring bus operators and checking bookings to identify organised movement towards Delhi, particularly the New Delhi area, ahead of the October 10 demonstration. They have been asked to keep a watch on bus operators, including bookings being made and the destination. If there is organised movement of people towards New Delhi, the local police should be aware of it and stop it," an officer was quoted as saying. Checks are also being conducted around railway stations and the airport to identify large groups arriving in the capital. CJP Plans March Against SIR, Demands Accountability The police checks come ahead of the CJPs announced protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. According to PTI, CJP founder Abhijit Dipke called for nationwide mobilisation against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and said the party would march to Jantar Mantar demanding that the exercise be scrapped and accountability fixed for the alleged deletion of voters. Addressing a press conference, Dipke criticised restrictions on public gatherings in Delhi and questioned why protests could take place in other cities but face restrictions in the national capital. Dipke alleged that large numbers of voters had been deleted from electoral records and questioned the Election Commissions role in the exercise. He also referred to testimonies of people who were allegedly declared dead in electoral records despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive. Dipke alleged that the BJP and the Election Commission were working together to delete votes of people who did not support the ruling party. These allegations were made by the CJP leader and were not independently established in the reports provided. The CJP founder said the party would proceed with its march even if its leaders were detained or arrested. He also maintained that the movement was seeking accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Centre over the alleged deletion of votes, rather than attempting to destabilise the country. The CJP has announced its protest at Jantar Mantar, with demands including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. However, permission for the proposed demonstration had not been granted. Delhi Police personnel are visiting hotels, guest houses, and hostels to verify guest identities, inspect accommodation logs, and scrutinize visit purposes ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10.

headline: ICE Agent Shoots At 'Criminal Illegal Alien' From Dominican Republic During New York Arrest Operation
content: A Dominican Republic national linked to the Trinitarios gang was wounded in the neck by an ICE agent during a Bronx enforcement operation in New York City. A 28-year-old man from the Dominican Republic was wounded after a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent opened fire during an enforcement operation in New York Citys Bronx on Thursday, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said. A five-year-old child was inside the mans vehicle when the shooting took place but escaped injury, according to a law enforcement source cited by CNN. - Trumps Islam Takeover Claim Vs Real Grievances Of Frances Student Protesters Explained - Trump Says He'll Speak To Putin Soon Over Reported Plague Death As US Presses For Transparency - 'Why Leave Them There?': Trump Says US Pulled Bombers From UK Air Base Over 'Some Threats' - Islam Wants To Take Over France: Trump Reacts To Students' Protests, Blames Out Of Control Migration This is the first shooting involving ICE agents in New York City amid an intensified immigration enforcement drive by the Trump administration. The incident occurred at around 4 pm on October 8, when officers from ICEs Enforcement and Removal Operations unit were carrying out a targeted operation, a law enforcement source told CNN. The circumstances that prompted the agent to fire have not been publicly established, and the incident remains under investigation. Man Sustained Injuries, Had Links With Trinitarios gang. DHS said the man was being targeted for arrest and alleged that he had links to the Trinitarios gang. The department also cited a previous conviction for grand larceny and earlier arrests involving assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. A 28-year-old man from the Dominican Republic was wounded by an ICE agent in the Bronx, New York City. A five-year-old child was in the man's vehicle but was not injured during the shooting. The incident occurred around 4 pm on October 8 during a targeted operation by ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations unit. The man sustained a graze wound to his neck that was not life-threatening. Two federal agents were also injured during the encounter and received treatment at a local hospital. Also Read: Mexican Man Fatally Shot By ICE Agent After Allegedly Ramming Vehicle, Trying To Run Over Officer The man sustained a graze wound to his neck that was not considered life-threatening, according to the law enforcement source. Police took him to a hospital in a patrol vehicle without waiting for an ambulance, the source told CNN. Provided His Immediate Medical Assistance: DHS In a statement, DHS said the ICE officer discharged his weapon during the encounter and that agents immediately provided medical assistance to the injured man. The department confirmed that he was alive and receiving treatment at a local hospital. On October 8, at approximately 4:00 PM ET, ICE officers were conducting a targeted enforcement operation in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a criminal illegal alien from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession. He has associations to the Trinitarios gang, the same gang who brutally shot a CBP officer last year.This criminal illegal alien was arrested by the NYPD on December 7, 2023, but was released into the community a few days later by reckless Democrat sanctuary policies that put American lives at risk. During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured. ICE officers immediately rendered aid. The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation. More information will be shared as it becomes available. When dangerous illegal aliens are released back onto the streets by radical sanctuary politicians, our officers are forced to make arrests at large in the community in unpredictable and dangerous environments. Our officers should not have to risk their lives, and innocent Americans should not have to face unnecessary danger, because sanctuary politicians refuse to cooperate with federal law enforcement. Homeland Security (@DHSgov) October 9, 2026 DHS also alleged that the man had been arrested by the New York Police Department (NYPD) on December 7, 2023, but was released days later under the citys sanctuary policies. The department argued that such policies put public safety at risk and expose federal officers to dangerous situations while carrying out arrests. Two Federal Agents Injured Two federal agents were also injured during the encounter and were being treated at a local hospital, according to a law enforcement source. A federal official said one agent may have been hurt in a vehicle accident, although it was unclear whether that incident was connected to the attempted arrest or the subsequent response. The department said the FBI and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) were at the scene as the investigation continued. Witnesses Report Gunfire, Protests Gather At Scene Witnesses told police they saw a man wearing a bright yellow construction vest and carrying a gun before hearing between five and six gunshots, followed by screams, according to police officials. Video purportedly recorded at the scene appears to show a man matching that description carrying a semi-automatic rifle and wearing an ICE badge around his neck, CNN reported. The NYPD said its officers were not involved in the incident, which took place in the Marble Hill neighbourhood, north of Manhattan. Following the shooting, the department mobilised personnel to manage crowds and assist with evidence collection. Later, HSI agents and police officers were seen working behind yellow police tape as demonstrators began assembling near the site. A federal source told CNN that HSI had taken over the investigation. NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani Calls For ICE To Leave City New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticised the incident and said he had contacted US President Donald Trump over the shooting. In a statement, Mamdani said he had called the President" and will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city." Our thoughts are with the injured New Yorker and his family tonight. We are praying for his recovery," Mamdani said. Get ICE out of our neighbourhoods," he added. The investigation into the Bronx shooting is ongoing, with federal authorities yet to publicly detail what led the ICE officer to discharge his weapon. An ICE agent discharged his weapon during a targeted enforcement operation in the Bronx on October 8, 2026, wounding a 28-year-old man from the Dominican Republic. The Department of Homeland Security stated that the man was being targeted for arrest due to alleged links to the Trinitarios gang and a prior criminal record.

headline: Can Trump Win Nobel Peace Prize While US Is At War? What The Rules Say
content: Trump himself appears to believe he has earned it. It is about that time, Trump said in the Oval Office on Wednesday. US President Donald Trump is once again making his case for the Nobel Peace Prize, just days before the Norwegian Nobel Committee is set to announce this years winner. But there is an obvious question hanging over his bid: Can a president whose country is involved in an ongoing war actually win the Nobel Peace Prize? Trump himself appears to believe he has earned it. It is about that time," Trump said in the Oval Office on Wednesday, October 7, as he renewed his claim to the award. At the same time, he acknowledged that he was not confident the Norwegian Nobel Committee would choose him. - Donald Trump Vs Mark Carney For Nobel Peace Prize? The Winner Could Literally Be From Space - Riyadh Under Houthi Attack: Why Yemens War Could Trigger A Wider Regional Crisis - Can Bharat Enforce Peace Between Russia-Ukraine? Woldgang Ischinger EXCLUSIVE | The Hard Facts - Stop Energy Strikes, Keep Black Sea Trade Moving: India's 3-Part Russia-Ukraine Truce Plan Decoded I dont know what their decision is going to be," Trump said, adding that the committee has a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me." Trump has repeatedly argued that his administration has helped settle or de-escalate multiple conflicts since he returned to the White House in January 2025. On Wednesday, he claimed he had settled eight wars" and suggested that failing to recognise his efforts could undermine the credibility of the Nobel Committee. But there is a complication that is difficult to ignore: the United States remains involved in a major conflict with Iran. US At War With Iran: Does That Disqualify Trump? There is no Nobel rule stating that a political leader or head of state involved in a war is automatically barred from winning the Peace Prize. The prize is governed by the broad criteria laid down in Alfred Nobels will. It is intended for the person or organisation that has conferred the greatest benefit on humankind in the field of peace. The Norwegian Nobel Committee also emphasises peaceful dialogue, conflict resolution and international cooperation. That means the committee does not simply ask whether a candidates country has been involved in military action. It assesses the candidates contribution to peace. And this is where Trumps case becomes controversial. Trump has claimed credit for efforts involving several conflicts, including those involving Israel and Iran, India and Pakistan, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Cambodia and Thailand. Leaders in Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have publicly said they nominated Trump, although those nominations cannot be independently verified because Nobel nominations remain secret for 50 years. At the same time, Trumps claims have faced pushback from some of the parties involved, while fighting has resumed in some areas. His pledge to end Russias war in Ukraine also remains unfulfilled. Meanwhile, the US-Israeli conflict with Iran has continued for months. Trump Has Already Received A Nobel, Just Not The One He Wants There was an extraordinary moment earlier this year that added another layer to Trumps Nobel campaign. In January, Venezuelan opposition leader Mara Corina Machado, who won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, presented Trump with her actual Nobel Peace Prize medal during a visit to the White House. Machado had dedicated her award to Trump and the Venezuelan people, crediting what she described as his historic role in Venezuela. She subsequently handed him the medal as a gesture of appreciation. Trump called it a wonderful gesture of mutual respect." However, Machado could not give Trump her Nobel Prize itself. The Nobel Institute clarified that a Nobel Peace Prize cannot be transferred, shared or revoked after it has been awarded. Trump nevertheless referred to the episode while making his latest pitch, saying he had been very honoured to receive it indirectly" from the recipient, who he said believed nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump." Who Decides If Trump Wins? Ultimately, Trump does not decide his Nobel fate, nor does the US government. The award is decided by the five-member Norwegian Nobel Committee, which is elected by Norways parliament. The committee reviews valid nominations, creates a shortlist and seeks assessments from experts before gradually narrowing down the candidates. A final decision is usually reached by consensus, although a majority vote is sufficient. And being nominated does not itself mean much. The Nobel Committee has explicitly said that a nomination is not an endorsement or honour from the committee. This years pool contains 287 candidates 208 individuals and 79 organisations but the official names are kept secret. The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced on Friday, October 9, at 11 am CEST at the Norwegian Nobel Institute in Oslo. The award ceremony will then be held on December 10. No Nobel rule automatically bars a political leader or head of state involved in a war from winning the Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee evaluates the candidate's overall contribution to peaceful dialogue, conflict resolution, and international cooperation rather than simply checking if their country is engaged in military action.

headline: Sign a bond, skip Delhi: Maharashtra police warn would-be protesters against Oct 10 agitation
content: Days before the Cockroach Janata Partys (CJP) nationwide protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, activists and would-be protesters in Maharashtra have alleged that police tracked their movements, sought their travel plans and, in some cases, detained them and told them to stay away. An official from the office of the Director General of Police (DGP) said notices had been issued in a handful of cases but denied any detentions in the state. Sadaf Raza Zaidi, a 31-year-old creative strategist from Santacruz, said police personnel came to her home and questioned her about her plans for October 10. A few officers had come to my place of residence and they had asked where I would be going on the 10th of October. When I denied that I will not be going to the protest, they asked me if I knew anyone who would be going there. They also asked me to come to the police station and sign a document which stated that I will not be attending the protest. They said that they have orders to collect the data of potential protesters. The police had asked for my live location and I did not give them, said Zaidi. She believes she was approached because she had been detained during a protest in July. When the NEET protest occurred in the month of July, I was detained. I guess they have been tracking people who were detained during the last times protest, she said. Civil society group Hum Bharat Ke Log alleged that MIDC police detained activists Feroze Mithiborwala and Salim Saboowala. Mithiborwala said the two had faced repeated summonses and harassment since October 2. Mayur Sharma, a Thane-based member of the All India Students Federation (AISF), said he got several calls from police officials in Mumbai and Delhi about his travel plans. Initially, I received calls from one woman asking about my travel plans so she could join me with her group wanting to participate in the Delhi protest. This was strange because only five-six of us friends were planning to travel together. We were not really taking any group with us, Sharma said. Suspecting the callers were police, he told them his plans had changed. Fearing he would be stopped at Bandra Terminus, he and a friend boarded the train at Borivali on Wednesday evening. Then came another call, from the Delhi Railway Police. But soon after that I received a call from Delhi railway police, again seeking details of my travel journey. The officer on call claimed that they have information from Mumbai RPF that I am taking a group of 25 persons along to Delhi, said Sharma. He got off near Faridabad instead of going on to Hazrat Nizamuddin station, where he feared police would be waiting, and took the Metro into Delhi. The SHO of Nizamuddin police station confirmed police had called some members but said it was to maintain law and order. We are maintaining an order situation, he said. In Nagpur, CJP volunteers alleged that Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel called them seeking the number and identities of those travelling to Delhi, and even offered to confirm the status of their waitlisted tickets. At least two volunteers there have been served notices under Section 168 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). One, issued by Ajni police station on October 6 to CJP worker Bharat Banait of Bhagwan Nagar, said police had confidential information that he planned to travel to the Jantar Mantar protest. Citing a prohibitory order across Nagpur city under Section 37(1)(3) of the Maharashtra Police Act, the senior inspector directed him to say when he would travel, by what mode and with whom. It warned of legal action if he went without giving the details and asked him to cooperate so that no untoward incident took place. The other went to Akshay Ramteke, a volunteer from Kuhi in Nagpur district. Its subject reads: Notice under Section 168 BNSS regarding dissuading from going to the CJP (Cockroach Janta Party) protest/march to be held in Delhi on 10.10.2026. It cited a confidential communication from the DGPs office in Mumbai, Outward No. P.O./R.P.O.N.K./CJP 2026, dated October 4, and said the protest could lead to violence, road blockades and obstruction of government work. It advised Ramteke not to go and warned that if he did and any untoward incident occurred, he could be held responsible and face preventive action under Sections 126 and 135 of the BNSS and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). He was also told to appear at Kuhi police station and submit a written bond that he would not attend the protest or disturb public peace. Harssh Poddar, Superintendent of Police, Nagpur Rural, said a Section 168 notice is issued before a protest to ensure no cognisable offence is committed. An AISF member from Pune alleged police tracked students travelling to Delhi and tried to detain them at Bhusawal railway station. We were approached by more than 10 police personnel at Bhusawal around 1.30 pm. They told us they were under pressure from higher authorities and attempted to detain us. We resisted and refused to be detained. Despite the train being diverted and delayed by more than seven hours, we are continuing our journey to Delhi. We recorded the incident and also went live on Instagram. Some of the students were later detained at Itarsi, said Comrade Preeti of AISF, Pune. The DGP office official said no detentions had taken place in the state so far. There have been no instructions given from the headquarters to take harsh measures. In some instances individual Commissionerates and district SPs have taken action in the face of possible law and order problems, the official said. Under Section 168 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the police have the power to act to prevent the commission of a cognisable offence and Section 170(1) of BNSS enables preventive arrest to prevent cognisable offence, the officer added.

headline: From Nandigram To Nagaon: Key Results Of Bypoll Battle Across 6 High-Stakes Seats Arrive Today
content: Results to be out for the assembly seats of Bengal's Nandigram and Rejinagar, Tamil Nadu's Madurantakam and Dharapuram, Puducherry's Thattanchavady & Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha seat The stage is set for a defining moment in regional politics as official results for six critical by-electionsfive Assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituencyare announced today. Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and postal ballots across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Assam are being unsealed following high-decibel campaigns and robust voter participation. From high-profile battles in Bengal to shifting alliances in the South and a fiercely contested parliamentary seat in the Northeast, todays verdict holds implications far beyond local representation. - By-Election Results 2026 Live Updates: Suvendu Adhikari Says 'Friendship Bana Liya' As BJP Leads In Nandigram, Rejinagar - West Bengal By-Elections: Why Nandigram, Rejinagar Polls Matter Beyond Four Seats | News18 - Saffron State, Splintered Rivals: Nandigram, Rejinagar Invert Bengals Historic Election Math - Let Him Contest: SC Adjourns Bengal Govt Plea Against Nandigram Congress Candidate Milan Pradhans Bail High-Stakes Showdown in West Bengal All eyes are firmly fixed on West Bengals Nandigram and Rejinagar constituencies. Nandigram, long a battleground of political prestige, went to the polls after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the seat to retain Bhabanipur. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has fielded Hasirani Rath against Congress nominee Milan Pradhanwho received backing from the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress (TMC) campalongside candidates from the CPI and a rival TMC collective. Meanwhile, Rejinagar witnessed a multi-cornered contest involving the BJP, TMC, Congress, CPI(M), and the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP). High voter turnout above 80% in both segments reflects intense local mobilisation, making todays counting a direct test of political consolidation and opposition resilience in the state. Testing New Political Equations in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry In Tamil Nadu, the reserved Assembly segments of Madurantakam and Dharapuram recorded impressive turnouts exceeding 80% and 86%, respectively. The contests serve as a vital pulse check for Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) supremo C Joseph Vijay. Both seats were vacated by former AIADMK legislators who crossed over to join TVK and are re-contesting under its banner, setting up a competitive four-way fight against the DMK, AIADMK, and CPI. Official results for six critical by-elections are being announced today. Five Assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituency are involved in the by-elections. Electronic Voting Machines and postal ballots are being unsealed across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Assam. Madurantakam in Tamil Nadu recorded a voter turnout of 86.26%. Nagaon Lok Sabha in Assam saw a 76.19% voter turnout. Across the border in Puducherry, the fate of the Thattanchavady constituency will be decided. The seat fell vacant after Chief Minister N Rangasamy relinquished it to retain Mangalam. With over 80% voter turnout recorded, the verdict will indicate public sentiment towards the territorial administrations current trajectory. Triangular Parliamentary Battle in Assams Nagaon In Assam, attention centres on the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency, which saw a 76% voter turnout. The parliamentary seat became vacant after sitting Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned from the party to join the BJP. The resulting triangular contest features former deputy commissioner Debashish Sharma representing the BJP, former MLA Sibamoni Bora standing for the Congress, and AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal entering the fray. The outcome will offer significant clues regarding changing voter alignments across demographic pockets in central Assam. Key Turnout Figures at a Glance - Madurantakam (Tamil Nadu): 86.26% - Nandigram (West Bengal): 80.89% - Thattanchavady (Puducherry): 80.81% - Dharapuram (Tamil Nadu): 80.30% - Rejinagar (West Bengal): 80.00% - Nagaon Lok Sabha (Assam): 76.19% With counting progressing through sequential rounds, initial trends are expected to settle into definitive mandates by afternoon, shaping the immediate political landscape across all four regions. The by-elections cover six critical constituencies: Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Thattanchavady in Puducherry, and the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam.

headline: Infosys To Tata: Which Indian Tech Firms Are Among 8 Hit By US H-1B, Green Card Crackdown
content: Washington said the action was linked to concerns over visa misuse and multiple ongoing federal investigations. The United States has suspended eight major technology firms, including Indian IT giants Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL and Cognizant, from a programme used to help foreign workers obtain green cards, accusing companies of undermining job opportunities for American workers. Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe are also facing suspension from the US Labour Departments Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme. Washington said the action was linked to concerns over visa misuse and multiple ongoing federal investigations. - US Suspends Microsoft & Infosys From PERM? Indian Workers Face Green Card Uncertainty | News18 - Microsoft Rejects Visa Fraud Claims, Says 80% Of H-1B Filings Were For Existing Staff - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud - US Suspends Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant From Green Card Programme; Alleges Visa Fraud Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the move on Thursday as part of the administrations anti-fraud drive. Five Indian IT Firms Among Those Hit Announcing the action, Sonderling named Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini among the firms being suspended. Microsoft and Adobe were also included. The Labour Department will not accept new applications or process pending PERM applications involving the companies, Sonderling said. He alleged that the firms had made extensive use of foreign-worker programmes at the expense of US employees. Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers," Sonderling said, adding that they had received more than 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications. Indian professionals account for more than 70 per cent of approved H-1B petitions each year, making the move significant for Indias technology sector and workers seeking opportunities in the US. Vance Accuses Microsoft Of Visa Abuse Vance singled out Microsoft, accusing it of laying off American employees while continuing to recruit foreign workers. The US vice president further alleged that Microsoft cut 6,000 US jobs in 2025 after certifying that it could not find suitably qualified American workers. The company was subsequently approved for more than 6,000 H-1B visas and filed 3,682 PERM applications, including nearly 1,000 for positions similar to those held by workers who had been laid off, he alleged. There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft," Vance said. In response to Vances claims, Microsoft said that 80 per cent of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings in the last fiscal year were for existing employees, not new hires. Universities Also Face Visa Probe The administration also announced an investigation into the J-1 exchange visitor programme at nine universities, including Harvard, Yale, Stanford and Caltech. Vance alleged that some institutions were using the programme to hire foreign researchers at the expense of American graduates and academics. The J-1 visa allows foreign nationals to enter the US for research, teaching, study and other approved exchange activities. (With inputs from PTI) The United States suspended eight major technology firms, including Indian IT giants Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL, and Cognizant, alongside Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe.

content: Although comfortably ahead of his immediate contender, BJP candidate Devasish Sharma's lead margin has fallen to 1,41,916 votes. In the evening, it was over one lakh 73 thousand. headline: Revanth Reddy backs Elon Musk, hits out at 'crony distractions' in satcom row
content: Responding to Rahul Gandhis post directed to Elon Musk on X, Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy expressed his support and stated that Congress governments have always stood for digitisation and modernisation of India. Congress governments had always stood for digitisation and modernisation of India and the stellar reform to conceptualise the UPI and adopt mobile-based digital payments infrastructure was taken up under the Congress-led UPA-2 government in 2012-13. Today it stands out as a shining example of big Indian innovation. India should welcome innovative solutions in cutting edge internet systems and cannot afford to weaken Brand India globally to appease crony distractions. Revanth Reddy (@revanth_anumula) October 8, 2026 Reddy posted, Congress governments had always stood for digitisation and modernisation of India and the stellar reform to conceptualise the UPI and adopt mobile-based digital payments infrastructure was taken up under the Congress-led UPA-2 government in 2012-13. Today it stands out as a shining example of big Indian innovation. India should welcome innovative solutions in cutting edge internet systems and cannot afford to weaken Brand India globally to appease crony distractions. This came after the Centre, in a statement, said the countrys regulatory framework for satcom services is fair and non-discriminatory. Licensees are required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions, it said, without naming Musk. Security assessment as part of this process is currently underway, it added. But, doubling down on his earlier allegation, Musk said in a post on Thursday evening: Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India? Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy. Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) October 8, 2026 Responding to this, Gandhi said in a post on X: Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy. Musk then responded with: Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling. In his earlier post on Wednesday night, Musk had said: Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are This is a crime against the people of India! In another post, he said: Starlink in India would enable high-speed, affordable Internet connectivity for those who cant afford current prices or who dont have a connection at all. Reliance Jio did not respond to a request for comment.

headline: As Jharkhand woman looks to reunite with daughter in Delhi, a court nudge
content: The Delhi High Court has asked the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) to decide on the rehabilitation of a 17-year-old Adivasi girl from Jharkhand who has been staying at a Delhi shelter home since August 1, after her mother approached the court seeking custody of her daughter. The mother alleges that the girl was taken to Delhi for domestic work without her knowledge, while a Delhi Police status report says she came to the capital with a woman she knew and with her parents consent. According to the womans petition, her daughter from Jharkhands Khunti was allegedly trafficked for domestic work in Delhi. The family claims the minor left home in July, and her mothers repeated attempts to secure her custody were unsuccessful. In its October 1 order, the High Court directed the CWC to expeditiously decide the welfare of the minor child and the measures for her rehabilitation and social re-integration. The court also directed that the decision be taken within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, and made clear that it had not expressed any opinion on the manner in which the minor child is to be rehabilitated. Advocate Abhiram Venugopal, who is representing the woman, reiterated this claim, citing a report by a Jharkhand-based social outfit on September 2. However, the Delhi Police status report gives a different account, saying the girl came to Delhi around July 10 with a woman she knew and had come with her parents consent. Venugopal questioned why the CWC had cited no reason for the girls continued custody. What have they done so far? No FIR had been registered against the alleged trafficker or the people involved in employing the girl, he asked. When contacted, Deeba Naseem, chairperson of the Delhi CWC, said the HC order would be complied with. Asked why the minor was still in Delhi, Naseem said she had no information on the matter. There is nothing to be worried about, she said.

headline: No lab, absent staff: In Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat, child deaths uncover lapses
content: Central team report flags glaring gaps; Rahul, CJP visit tribal area. * The district surveillance unit, a crucial line of defence that is meant to save children from the kind of cocktail of illnesses that are alleged to have killed them in Madhya Pradeshs Balaghat, was run by a data manager. * The post of District Epidemiologist, critical for surveillance, outbreak investigation and data analysis, was vacant. There was no District Public Health Laboratory and the post of microbiologist was vacant. * The most affected village Kundekasa has been without an ASHA worker for over a year, leading to a major gap in active case detection, community mobilisation and follow-up. While the team visited Balaghat in August, the deaths have become a political crisis for the BJP government now after Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhis visit to the affected families last week. His visit followed that of Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke to Balaghat in mid-September. The Mohan Yadav government earlier maintained that the number of deaths was eight, with around 100 children falling ill, in August in four remote, Baiga tribe-dominated villages. Yadav also visited Balaghat on August 29. However, the NJORT report, which was submitted to the Union health authorities in September, shows that the deaths were not the result of an isolated failure or one identifiable disease but of a health system weakened at almost every stage, from detecting sick children in villages to maintaining vaccination records, from laboratory coordination to tracking deaths, and from referring severely ill children to bigger hospitals, and ensuring that they actually got appropriate care. It found evidence of measles alongside malaria and smaller numbers of dengue, chikungunya and enterovirus infections, in what it called a mixed febrile illness cluster. The report, which did not put a number to the estimated deaths, also spoke of gaps in data collection, reporting and sharing between surveillance, laboratory, immunization and nutrition programmes. The lack of a common repository meant even getting a timely, well reconciled, line list was a challenge, said the NJORT. The case studies During their field visit from August 13 to 18, the NJORT examined three deaths in detail (a fourth family declined to participate). One of those who died was a four-year-old boy from Kundekasa. The report said he developed rashes, fever, oral ulcers, loss of appetite and seizures, before dying at home on August 6. This was three days after an ASHA worker visited the house, and advised the family to take him to hospital, which was not done, the report said. Similarly, the NJORT said, a three-year-old girl from Kundekasa died at her maternal grandmothers home on July 22, before she was taken to hospital. In her case too, an ASHA worker and a multi-purpose worker had visited the family and urged them to take the child for malaria testing, which they did not do. The family reportedly attributed the illness to Maata, to be treated by traditional methods. Apart from delayed formal care, the NJORT said the death was a result of such cultural beliefs, plus incomplete vaccination documentation and the absence of a laboratory diagnosis. In case of the third investigated death, the team said the three-year-old girl from Bondari was brought to District Hospital, Balaghat, on August 9, after her family sought treatment from a traditional healer approximately 35 km from their village. At admission, the three-year-old weighed only 4.9 kg, and had a height of 66 cm. She died at the hospital on August 11. The NJORT said the child was vulnerable due to marked nutritional deficit, but did not establish a cause for the death. Nutritional gaps Overall, the team recorded 604 children as severely acutely malnourished and 1,985 as moderately acutely malnourished across 357 anganwadi centres in the Birsa block sectors. While earlier field teams reported that visible wasting or severe wasting was found in roughly 20-25% of the children surveyed in Baiga, the report said only around 30-35% of children were enrolled in the Poshan Tracker, and that the weekly weighing of children by anganwadi workers was not being done regularly. (Poshan Tracker is a government digital system for monitoring nutrition and child development services delivered through anganwadi centres. It helps frontline workers identify children who are malnourished and track them over time.) The report found that joint visits by auxiliary nurse midwives, ASHA and anganwadi workers were irregular, affecting coordination of maternal, child-health and nutrition services, and that there were significant discrepancies between measurements recorded in the Poshan Tracker and those seen during the NJORT field verification. The NJORT tested 64 samples for measles, of which 25 tested positive. In the case of malaria, of the 32 samples tested by the National Centre for Disease Control, 27 were positive. Dengue testing was positive in 2 of 28 samples, chikungunya in 1 of 28 and enterovirus in 2 of 24. All five water samples tested for adenovirus (which causes a range of symptoms) were positive, while eight of nine samples tested for coliform bacteria were positive, though the report said these do not establish a single cause for the entire cluster. On the gaps identified by the NJORT, Dr Dahiya said these were of staffing, and were being addressed. Malnutrition has been one of the major issues in the area. There was a supply-chain issue, but we are now focusing on ensuring that nutrition reaches the children continuously. We have treated approximately 3,500 children at their homes. Apart from this, around 750 children who were in critical condition were treated. Overall, we have been able to save around 800 children who were in critical condition. The government earlier said four Block Women Development Officers had been posted to Balaghat, and 14 sub-health centres and community health centres were being established in the region. During his visit, Gandhi called the deaths the result of total, 100% government failure, and said the children suffered from illness and malnutrition, with even basic government support absent in the area. Sanjay Uikey, the local MLA who belongs to the Congress, said: Our estimates say the death toll is over 40. Its only after much pressure that the government has announced compensation for 30-odd families. Our hope is that the push by the Health Department is long-lasting and not a temporary fix.

headline: Trump says U.S. will not resume military strikes on Iran before Nov. 3 midterm elections
content: President Donald Trump said Thursday (October 8, 2026) that he will not order a resumption of military strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections in the United States. Mr. Trump, while stumping for Republicans this week, has hinted that he was confident that an endgame to the war could come in the days before or after the election, while also hinting that he remained open to resuming full-scale military operations against Iran. For weeks, Mr. Trump has been threatening that a post-midterm election escalation in the seven-month-old war remains a viable option, despite his initial promises to Americans of a military campaign that would last a matter of weeks. But Mr. Trump in a social media post on Thursday (October 8, 2026) said the U.S. will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. Mr. Trump added that his team has been having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The U.S. and Iran signed a short-lived interim agreement in June, intended to establish a 60-day ceasefire and framework for a permanent peace deal. The deal signed by Mr. Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian collapsed within weeks amid renewed military actions and disputes over control of the Strait of Hormuz, the critical water which one-fifth world's oil flowed through before the war. Negotiations had appeared at a standstill since Mr. Trump late last month publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the strait within seven days if the U.S. met certain conditions. Iran, however, said last week they had received a U.S. counterproposal. And Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi earlier on Thursday said he expected Tehran would offer a formal reply within days. Mr. Trump on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) during a campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas, said that his special envoy, Steve Witkoff, has continued indirect negotiations with Iranian officials. But at the same time, Mr. Trump suggested he had mixed feelings about ending the war at this point. I think the deal isn't really something that I want to do, but they're willing to offer us anything to stop, Mr. Trump said. Mr. Trump believes that America is gaining leverage as the U.S. military is having greater success in helping oil tankers traverse the Strait of Hormuz and get Gulf allies' oil to market, while a Navy blockade is shutting down Iran's own oil exports. Iran has lost its near chokehold over oil flows through the vital waterway with U.S. Central Command shepherding oil tankers through the strait at night with their location systems turned off. That with the help of Gulf pipelines that skirt the strait, has allowed Gulf countries to export oil at nearly prewar levels. But Iran has ramped up attacks on tankers passing through the strait in recent days. And overall, ship traffic remains well below prewar levels, as are shipments of liquid natural gas and fuel products. Tanker operators willing to risk running the gauntlet under Central Command's protection are in some cases charging rates of $1 million a day or more, shipping analysts say. The situation has become further complicated as Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government have launched a military campaign aimed at driving Iran-backed Houthi rebels from the Bab el-Mandeb strait, another critical West Asia trade route for oil and other goods. The Houthis, in turn, are targeting Saudi airports and key infrastructure in the kingdom with drone and missile strikes. Mr. Trump's post comes as the military has dispatched more resources to the region. U.S. officials have said a third aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, and thousands of troops aboard it and accompanying ships could arrive as early as the end of October. Mr. Trump's announcement was made the same day the USS Abraham Lincoln was due to arrive to its home port in San Diego after a record-long deployment in support of the Iran war. There have been reports of crew stress and poor mental health, as well as supply shortages, including food and hygiene products. The USS George Washington, which is usually based in Asia, relieved the Lincoln in August. The other aircraft carrier in the West Asia, the USS George HW Bush, has been deployed for about six months, but it pulled into Phuket, Thailand, for a port visit several days ago.

headline: Pentagon says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed
content: be livestreamed after Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be public. Mr. Hegseth, speaking to the conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice News on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), said the execution of Hasan will take place at Fort Hood on Dec. 3. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people and injuring 32 others in a shooting at the military base in 2009. We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public, Mr. Hegseth said. Mr. Hegseth spoke to the outlet aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier while visiting the long-deployed crew, who supported the Iran war, before their arrival at their home port in San Diego. When asked if Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to the Trump administration, Hegseth simply replied: Don't care. We'll see him on December 3rd. Officials in the Pentagon clarified Thursday (October 8, 2026) that the execution will be livestreamed and that more details would follow. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell had said Monday that President Donald Trump had approved the execution of Hasan. The White House on Thursday (October 8, 2026) immediately referred questions about the plans for the livestreamed execution to the Pentagon. Mr. Hegseth said the military hasn't executed a servicemember by firing squad since World War II. The last military execution took place on April 13, 1961, when Army Private John Bennett was executed by hanging.

headline: Targeting illegals, BJP MP Nishikant Dubey starts Jharkhand tribal student rights campaign
content: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey Thursday launched a Bangladeshi Muslim Bhagao, Aadivaasi Bachao movement with the objective of securing the rights of tribal students in Jharkhand. This comes amid the Oppositions ongoing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which the BJP claims has helped clean up the voters list by removing undocumented immigrants. Dubey met students from six districts in Jharkhands Santhal Pargana region in Deoghar to discuss a public outreach to take the movements message to people. The alleged change in the demographic composition of the Adivasi-dominated region because of alleged illegal migration was one of the key electoral planks of the BJP during the Jharkhand Assembly polls in 2024. It will culminate in a large gathering where accountability will be sought from the INDI government (comprising Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, Congress, RJD, and CPIM-L Liberation) for this loot of the rights of the tribal population bordering Bangladesh, he said. The Godda MP posted on X the pictures from his interaction with the students and youth representatives. In a post, he alleged that while the Muslim population in the country had grown at 4%, in Santhal Pargana, it had grown by 17%, meaning all these are Muslims from Bangladesh who are encroaching on our water, forests, land, and women. Opposition to Gyanesh Kumar ji is a campaign to turn Bangladeshs voters into Indias voters. Today, we met with student organisations from all districts of Santhal Pargana Dumka, Deoghar, Godda, Pakur, Sahibganj, and Jamtara to outline the Bangladeshi Muslim Bhagao, Aadivaasi Bachao movement and public awareness campaign. The land of Sido-Kano ji is once again ready for revolution. Johar, said Dubey.

headline: Madras High Court permits observance of first death anniversary of prime accused Nagendran in BSP leader Armstrong murder case
content: The Madras High Court on Thursday (October 8, 2026) directed the Greater Chennai City Police to grant permission for the observance of the first death anniversary of P. Nagendran, who was the prime accused in the July 2024 murder of former Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader K. Armstrong, on Friday (October 9, 2026). Justice V. Lakshminarayanan quashed an order passed by the police denying permission for the event since they apprehended disturbance to law and order due to possible retaliatory action. He directed them to grant conditional permission by imposing reasonable restrictions such as limiting the number of participants. Though Nagendrans family had initially sought permission for the participation of 300 members in the event planned to be conducted at their residence in Vyasarpadi, they agreed to restrict the number of participants to 60 and submit the list of names to the police by Friday morning. The judge also made it clear the event should be conducted between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. at the Vysarpadi residence of the family by singing threnodies (oppari), beating drums (parai) and serving food (annadhanam) as per the customs of the community to which they belonged. He recorded the submission of the counsel for Nagendrans wife that there shall not be any political sloganeering, erection of banners or playing of provocative songs during the event. The judge took note that Nagendran had died in judicial custody in connection with multiple criminal cases. This court is of the view that eventhough the deceased happens to be one of the fakest villains of the 21st century, his family is entitled to follow the customary observances in line with their beliefs. The accused is dead but his family members are alive. The petitioner fears if such observances are not followed, the family will be inviting disastrous consequences from their forefathers. Sometimes, rationality cannot be attached to beliefs, the judge wrote. On the apprehension of Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani that the deceased was the prime accused in the brutal murder of a leading political personality in the State and hence there could be a retaliation, especially since the son of the deceased was also an accused in the murder case, the judge said, the Tamil Nadu police was robust enough to ensure nothing untoward takes place during the three-hour event. He ordered that the participants must not consume liquor and the police could intervene if there was violation of any of the conditions imposed by the court.

headline: US Sanctions Two Mumbai-Based Firms, Five Indian Nationals Over Alleged Iran Oil Trade
content: The US said the individuals and companies would be blocked from carrying out transactions involving the targeted firms. The United States on Thursday imposed sanctions on two Mumbai-based companies and five Indian nationals over alleged involvement in the trade of Iranian petroleum products, as Washington steps up pressure on Tehrans oil revenue network.
