China's Influence Seen More Positively Than US In Latin America: Poll - Iran Oil Minister Resigns, Replaced By Top Executive Amid US Blockade On Tehrans Exports Five Indians named in US sanctions Two people linked to SSPL Solutions, Dhwani Vora and Nisarg Vora, and three associated with Samudra Marine Services Ketan Kochikar, Bhupendrasingh Sahu and Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil were also sanctioned. The US said the individuals and companies would be blocked from carrying out transactions involving the targeted firms. The measures form part of Washingtons wider campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast". The State Department said it was sanctioning 10 entities, six individuals and five vessels in connection with trade in Iranian-origin petroleum, petroleum products, and petrochemical products." It accused the targeted network of channelling millions of dollars to the Iranian government, helping support what it described as a key source of revenue for Tehran. The US government is imposing sanctions on both the buyers and sellers driving this trade in Iranian petrochemical products," the department said. US expands pressure on Irans oil trade The State Department also allowed Samudra Marine Services to wind down certain transactions until October 23. Such authorisations give sanctioned parties a limited period to complete existing business and exit affected operations. Separately, the US Treasury Department announced sanctions against 17 entities and vessels linked to Irans shadow fleet". The measures are aimed at restricting Irans ability to generate revenue through oil exports and related shipping networks. Treasury is starving the tyrannical regime in Tehran of the money it uses to wage war in the region, and we will continue exposing those who enable the regimes oil sales," said US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Bessent warned that Washington would continue targeting those it believes are helping Iran evade sanctions. No enabler of Iranian sanctions evasion is safe from the full force of Treasurys authorities," he said. (With inputs from PTI) The US sanctioned two Mumbai-based companies, SSPL Solutions Private Limited and Samudra Marine Services Private Limited, along with five Indian nationals including Dhwani Vora, Nisarg Vora, Ketan Kochikar, Bhupendrasingh Sahu, and Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil.

headline: Madras High Court Registry lodges police complaint for forging its proceedings to get Bangladesh nationals deported
content: The Madras High Court Registry has lodged a complaint with the Greater Chennai Commissioner of Police in connection with its proceedings having been forged to get five Bangladesh nationals, lodged in a special foreigners camp at Attur in Salem district, deported to their country. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the High Courts standing counsel S. John Raja Singh reported that a complaint on behalf of the Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi was lodged with the Chennai city police on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) in compliance of the court orders. Bilal alias Mohammed Bilal Syed, Y. Salim and Bimal Sutrada alias Laxman Das had filed three individual writ petitions in the High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai as well as the State police to take steps for deporting them to their country. Substantiating their claim, the petitioners had submitted copies of official proceedings supposedly issued by the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court on October 8, 2025 granting clearance for deportation of five Bangladesh nationals to their home country and insisted that they must be sent back forthwith. Shocked to come across such proceedings, Justice Lakshminarayanan had on September 1, 2026 directed the High Court Registry to verify whether it had issued any such proceedings. The Registrar (Judicial) submitted a report on September 8, 2026 stating it was a forged document. Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani told the court the petitioners had also annexed a document purportedly issued in favour of them by the Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services but the officer had confirmed that no such document had been issued by his office. Central government standing counsel M.P. Jaisha, representing the FRRO, told the court that a complaint regarding forgery of government documents had already been lodged with the Central Crime Branch police in 2025 and that a First Information Report too was registered. After recording their submissions, the judge had directed the High Court Registry to lodge a police complaint with regard to forgery of its proceedings. On being told the complaint was lodged on October 6, the judge called for a status report from the police by November 10, 2026.

headline: Pete Hegseth Says Fort Hood Shooter's Execution By Firing Squad Will Be Livestreamed
content: It will be the first execution carried out by the US military since 1961 and its first firing-squad execution since the Second World War. The execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad will be livestreamed, the Pentagon said on Thursday, after Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the punishment would be carried out publicly. Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in the 2009 mass shooting at the Texas military base. His execution is scheduled for December 3. - US To Livestream Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasans Execution By Firing Squad, First Since 1945 - Trump Approves Firing Squad Execution Of Ex-Army Major Nidal Hasan In Rare Move: Why It Matters - Trump Says He'll Speak To Putin Soon Over Reported Plague Death As US Presses For Transparency - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks It will be the first execution carried out by the US military since 1961 and its first firing-squad execution since the Second World War. Hegseth says execution will be public Hegseth said Hasan would face a firing squad made up of soldiers and that the public would be able to watch. Hes going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be, and well make sure that people are able to watch it, that its public," Hegseth said in a video posted by official Pentagon accounts. Speaking aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, he added that people needed to understand there were serious consequences" for such attacks. Asked whether Hasan had made any final request, Hegseth replied: Dont care. Well see him on December 3." A Pentagon official later confirmed that the execution would be livestreamed, saying further details would be released. Hegseth said the firing squad method would mark the militarys first such execution since the Second World War, when US Army Private Eddie Slovik was executed for desertion in 1945. Hasan sentenced to death in 2013 Hasan opened fire at Fort Hood, now known as Fort Cavazos, in November 2009, killing 13 people, including 12 soldiers, and injuring 32. A civilian police officer responding to the attack shot Hasan, leaving him partially paralysed. A military jury sentenced him to death in 2013 after finding him guilty of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. Hasan acted as his own lawyer during the trial and did not deny carrying out the shooting. The Pentagon said earlier this week that US President Donald Trump had approved the execution. The military has carried out 135 executions since 1916, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. The most recent was the 1961 hanging of Army Private John Bennett, who was executed for rape and attempted murder. (With inputs from agencies) The execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan is scheduled for December 3, 2026, and will be carried out by a firing squad of soldiers at the Texas military base, with plans for the event to be livestreamed publicly by the Pentagon.

headline: Trump Honours Microsoft CEO With Top Tech Medal After Vance Drops H-1B Hammer On Firm
content: Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation at a White House-linked ceremony celebrating leading figures in US science and technology. US President Donald Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with one of the countrys top technology awards on Thursday, hours after Vice President JD Vance announced a suspension targeting the software giant over its use of the H-1B visa system. Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation at a White House-linked ceremony celebrating leading figures in US science and technology. - Trump Praises Immigrant Tech CEOs While Cracking Down On Foreign Workers: The Two Sides Of MAGA Policy - 'Why Leave Them There?': Trump Says US Pulled Bombers From UK Air Base Over 'Some Threats' - JD Vance Calls H-1B Visa Programme Rife With Fraud, Says It Undercuts US Workers - Microsoft Rejects Visa Fraud Claims, Says 80% Of H-1B Filings Were For Existing Staff Trump praised Nadellas decades-long contribution to Microsoft, saying he had helped transform the company and expand its technology around the world. Vance targets Microsoft over H-1B visas Earlier, Vance announced that Microsoft was being suspended from a programme that allows companies to seek permanent residency for skilled foreign workers holding H-1B visas. Vance, who is leading a Trump administration task force focused on alleged fraud, accused Microsoft of abusing the visa system and said the company should employ more American workers. Our message to Microsoft is: Youre a great American company, but youve got to hire great American workers," Vance told reporters. He claimed Microsoft had laid off 6,000 US workers while securing 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards last year. Microsoft has disputed the wider criticism. The company said about 80 per cent of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it filed last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, rather than hire new workers. The company also said the remaining filings were for people already legally living in the US. Trump celebrates tech leaders Nadella was among six technology leaders honoured at the ceremony. Trump also presented the National Medal of Science to SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD chief Lisa Su. Dell Technologies chief Michael Dell received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation alongside Nadella. Five of the six recipients were immigrants, including Nadella, Musk, Brin, Huang and Su. Trump called the recipients as national treasures" and praised their role in driving American innovation, particularly in artificial intelligence. The ceremony came as Trump has sought to promote a new era of US technological growth, while his administration has also pushed for tighter scrutiny of immigration and foreign-worker programmes. The tech leaders have remained regular visitors to the White House. Musk, Huang and Su recently attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping, while Musk and Huang also joined White House discussions on AI safety and development. (With inputs from AP) Vice President JD Vance announced a suspension targeting Microsoft from a green card program because the company was accused of abusing the H-1B visa system and failing to prioritize American workers. Vance claimed Microsoft laid off 6,000 U.S. workers while securing 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards last year.

headline: DAY 3: INDIA bloc protest reaches Rajghat; next stop — Rashtrapati Bhavan
content: FOR THE third day in a row, INDIA bloc leaders hit the streets demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over allegations of vote chori. A contingent, led by Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and his Rajya Sabha counterpart Mallikarjun Kharge, staged a peaceful protest at Mahatma Gandhis memorial at Rajghat and said they would continue their protest on Friday; they are likely to meet in Parliament House in the afternoon. Speaking to reporters, Congress general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal said: We have already requested the President for a meeting with the INDIA alliance leaders. The first request letter was sent on October 2. Then Rashtrapati Bhavan office intimated us to give names. On October 5, we gave a request with the names, with all INDIA alliance leaders. We asked for an appointment for (October) 7th, 8th, 9th. Today is 8th. We will wait for tomorrow also So far, there is no response. If the appointment is granted by the President, then we will march to Rashtrapati Bhavan and the selected few MPs will meet her. If not, we will march to the Bhavan and protest there, said a source in the INDIA bloc. Sources said the delegation of leaders who will meet the President, if her office agrees, will include Congresss Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, TMCs Mamata Banerjee, RJDs Tejashwi Yadav, SPs Rajeev Rai, NCP(SP)s Supriya Sule, Shiv Sena (UBT)s Sanjay Raut, among others. On Thursday, the INDIA bloc leaders headed for Rajghat from Moets restaurant in Connaught Place, where Kharge hosted a lunch for them. Speaking to reporters after the lunch, Gandhi said around 300 MPs wanted to hold a peaceful sit-in, but on the first day of the protest (October 6), they were stopped near the Election Commissions office and on the second day, they were prevented from going to Jantar Mantar by force. The truth is that (Prime Minister) Narendra Modi, (Home Minister) Amit Shah, (RSS chief) Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar have hijacked the country through a criminal conspiracy. They have destroyed the Constitution and stolen votes. They will be brought to justice. This is our guarantee, and you will see it happen, he said. Kharge announced the decision to head to Rajghat in buses. All the MPs of the INDIA bloc are going to the Gandhi Memorial. We will stage a sit-in there and peacefully pray that Modi and Shah are blessed with wisdom. We want to tell the country that the BJP government is snatching our right to vote, said Kharge. Besides Kharge and Gandhi, Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K C Venugopal, Vivek Tankha, Manickam Tagore, Jothimani Rajiv Shukla, and Deepender Hooda participated in the protest. Himachal Pradesh and Telangana Chief Ministers Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and A Revanth Reddy were also present. Trinamool Congresss Abhishek Banerjee, Menaka Guruswamy, Samirul Islam, Samawadi Partys Rajeev Rai and Mohibbullah Nadvi, CPI(M) MP John Brittas, CPIs P Sandosh and RJDs Sudhakar Singh were also present. Thursday was the third day the INDIA bloc leaders and MPs got together to protest against the CEC, demanding his resignation. On Wednesday, the INDIA bloc contingent headed to Jantar Mantar from Janpath and on Tuesday, they held a march from Parliaments Makar Dwar to the Election Commission of India office.

headline: Europe backs Ukraine funding but tightens anti-corruption conditions
content: In late August, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned allies of a roughly 27-billion hole in his countrys defence budget for the year. On October 1, after weeks of technical talks with Kyiv, the European Commission declared that Ukraines financial and military needs for 2026 were now fully covered. Yet the manner of that reassurance has exposed a widening gap between Europes commitment to Ukraine and its comfort with how Ukrainian money is spent. The 27-billion figure referred specifically to the 2026 defence gap, not to Ukraines total needs, which the International Monetary Fund has estimated at around 137 billion across 2026 and 2027. Kyiv wanted the gap filled quickly, and asked the European Union (EU) to accelerate disbursements already promised under existing 90-billion instruments. Brussels declined to front-load those payouts. In a letter in early October, European Commissioners Valdis Dombrovskis and Marta Kos informed the Speaker of Ukraines Parliament that early disbursement had been refused, and the 2026 gap was instead closed through re-allocation and coordinated contributions, with fresh conditions attached. To release the roughly 34 billion still outstanding for 2026, the Commission required Ukraine to abolish a value-added-tax exemption on small parcels, to introduce taxation of income earned through digital platforms such as OLX, Airbnb and Bolt, and to strengthen oversight of politically exposed persons, the last an explicit anti-corruption safeguard. Conditionality and risk The practical effect is that this year has been patched rather than resolved, and the Commission itself has acknowledged that 2027, when Ukraines needs are larger and American support more uncertain, will be the far harder test. There is near-unanimous agreement among member states that Ukraine cannot be allowed to collapse financially, a position backed firmly by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron and the front line EU members of the north and east. After a brief Hungarian veto of the blocs 90-billion loan package, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen insisted in Kyiv in February that we will deliver on the loan one way or the other. Public opinion has mirrored that resolve: a Standard Eurobarometer survey in spring 2026 (March, April, and May) found 75% of EU citizens in favour of providing financial and humanitarian support to Ukraine, and 76% in favour of sustaining that support until a just and lasting peace is achieved. There is no equivalent agreement on how the money should be raised or on what terms it should flow. Taxpayer fatigue in several capitals, a parallel and contentious negotiation over the EUs 2028-2034 budget, and persistent doubts about Ukrainian governance all pull against open-handedness. The headline consensus on funding Ukraine therefore conceals a sharper disagreement about conditionality and risk. The principal financial instrument to support the war effort is the Ukraine Facility, in force since March 2024, which provides over 50 billion in grants and loans for the 2024-2027 period. Crucially, every disbursement is tied to the Ukraine Plan, a roadmap of reforms weighted heavily toward the rule of law and anti-corruption. In practice the conditionality has proved elastic. In May, the European Council released close to 2.8 billion on the Facilitys seventh tranche after Kyiv had completed only 11 of 20 required reform steps, with roughly 15 overdue indicators according to the Kyiv Post. In July, the European Council amended the Plan to add 8.3 billion and new anti-corruption benchmarks, and the IMF released a $690-million tranche the same month while expressly noting missed targets. In July 2025, Mr. Zelenskyy signed a law subordinating the two independent anti-corruption bodies, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutors Office (SAPO), to the prosecutor general, provoking the first mass protests of the war and an explicit warning from the European Commission that EU accession was at risk. Growing scrutiny Mr. Zelensky reversed course within days as subsequent reporting linked the move to investigations closing in on figures near the presidency. Those fears were then borne out: in November 2025, NABU exposed an alleged $110-million scheme at the state nuclear company Energoatom, the largest corruption case of Mr. Zelenskys presidency, which cost him his chief of staff. A further investigation in August, this year, saw a deputy head of the presidential office dismissed. Polling in September reported by the Kyiv Independent found that more than 70% of Ukrainians hold Mr. Zelensky responsible for corruption within his circle, and earlier surveys recorded a majority naming graft a greater threat than the war itself. The uncomfortable point for Europe is that these exposures are themselves evidence that NABU and SAPO work, which is precisely why their independence sits at the centre of EU conditionality. The European Council meeting in Brussels is the moment these strands converge. Ukraine funding, the contested plan to mobilise some 210 billion in frozen Russian assets for a reparations loan, and European defence readiness all sit at the top of the agenda. Most of the roughly 210 billion in immobilised Russian assets is held by Euroclear, a central securities depository in Belgium, which leaves Belgium, rather than the EU as a whole, exposed to Russian retaliation and litigation. The Russian central bank has filed a claim of around 196 billion against the depository. A reparations loan could in principle be adopted by qualified majority, requiring 15 of the 27 member states representing 65% of the EUs population, and so could not be blocked by Belgium alone. Yet Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has demanded open-ended guarantees covering any damages beyond the frozen sum should Russia prevail in court, and no member state can legally commit to unlimited liability; other capitals have been reluctant to force a vote that would leave Belgium bearing a risk it alone considers unmanageable. Whatever leaders decide in Brussels, the structural tension between the scale of Ukraines needs and Europes appetite to underwrite them will outlast the summit. (Writer is a graduate student specialising in EU external affairs at Sciences Po university, Paris)

headline: 'Unacceptable': India condemns attacks on Saudi airports
content: The Indian community in the Saudi Kingdom numbers approximately 2.74 million, including skilled and semi-skilled professionals. This is not the first time in the last seven months, since the war in West Asia began, that Delhi has issued condemnatory statements and security advisories to warn its citizens to stay safe. Since March this year, at least three such occasions have warranted such statements. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman about the evolving conflict in March and August. The latest statement came amid reports that Yemens Iran-aligned Houthis escalated their campaign of strikes against Saudi Arabia, trying to shut down the kingdoms airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that has killed three people this week. The Ministry of External Affairs issued a statement: India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries. The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack at the Abha International Airport, said Saudi Arabias General Authority of Civil Aviation. It said one person was killed and eight others were injured in the attack on King Khalid International Airport. There has been a significant escalation in hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthi group and Saudi Arabia in recent days. The Houthis have been targeting Saudi border regions, energy facilities, and civilian infrastructure using armed drones and missiles. The Indian embassy in Riyadh has advised Indian citizens to stay indoors. In view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain alert and vigilant, stay indoors as necessary, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels, the Mission said. It also advised Indian nationals against circulating or reposting videos or news related to the ongoing events. The Indian Embassy, along with the Consulate in Jeddah and its outsourced services through VFS, continues to function normally, the advisory said. The 247 helpline of the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra remains available at toll-free number 8002471234, it said. The Indian community has also been advised to follow the official social media handles of the embassy for updates. The deteriorating security situation has also affected air services between India and Saudi Arabia. Air India and Air India Express have cancelled flights to and from Riyadh until October 10, while Akasa Air cancelled its Kochi-Riyadh and Riyadh-Kochi services on Thursday. Air India Express said affected passengers have been offered complimentary rescheduling or a full refund. It operates 16 weekly flights to Riyadh from Bengaluru, Kochi, Kannur and Kozhikode. Air India has also cancelled its Riyadh services until October 10. It operates seven weekly flights to Riyadh from Delhi and Mumbai. The airline said flight AI2243 from Delhi to Riyadh returned to the Capital on Thursday and was subsequently cancelled, with full refund offered to passengers. (With agency inputs from Riyadh)

headline: Venezuela's Maduro charged in U.S. with ordering torture of opponents, Americans
content: U.S. prosecutors on Thursday (October 8, 2026) charged ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiring to torture political opponents and American citizens, adding to the drug trafficking case the couple already faced. Separately, U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, who is overseeing the case, denied a request by Ms. Flores to be released from jail due to health concerns ahead of a trial scheduled for next year. Mr. Maduro (63), and Ms. Flores, (69), were captured on January 3 in their Caracas home during a U.S. military operation ordered by President Donald Trump, and were flown to New York to face drug charges against them that were announced that same day. A superseding indictment filed in Manhattan federal court on Thursday (October 8, 2026) added the torture count to the existing criminal case. Mr. Maduro and Ms. Flores each would face a mandatory minimum 50 years in prison if convicted of all the charges. They have pleaded not guilty to the original charges, but have not yet entered pleas to the new indictment, which detailed alleged torture against nine people, including three U.S. citizens. In a statement, Mr. Maduros lawyer Barry Pollack said, President Maduro denies the charges in the new indictment and looks forward to his day in court. In her bail hearing on Thursday (October 8, 2026), Ms. Flores lawyer Mark Donnelly said he had not had time to review the new charges with his client. Since Mr. Maduros capture, Venezuela has boosted cooperation with the U.S. under the leadership of his former Vice-President Delcy Rodriguez. Relations between the United States and oil-rich Venezuela were tense during the socialist Mr. Maduros 13 years in power. U.S. officials and human rights groups have long accused Venezuelan officials of torturing detainees, but Thursdays indictment marked the first time Mr. Maduro faced criminal charges over the allegations. The indictment alleged that thousands of Venezuelans were threatened, arrested, tortured or killed at the hands of the state between 1999 and 2025. Before Mr. Maduro became President in 2013, both he and Flores held positions in the late Venezuelan President Hugo Chavezs government. A violent system Maduro, Flores and other high-ranking members of their inner circle used a violent system of torture and repression to maintain their power, Jamie McDonald, the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan, told reporters outside the courthouse after Ms. Flores bail was denied. Ms. Flores was Venezuelas attorney general and led its National Assembly before becoming first lady. Many of the incidents of alleged torture described in the indictment occurred during times of political unrest in Venezuela or in response to perceived threats against Mr. Maduro. In one instance, prosecutors said, Mr. Maduro in 2013 ordered the arrest of a Venezuelan military officer he suspected of planning a coup. Members of Venezuelas military counterintelligence directorate then interrogated the officer while shocking the individual with a live electric wire around 20 times and hung the individual by the hands and feet for several minutes at a time, prosecutors said. In 2022, an American citizen detained while entering Venezuela was accused of conspiring to assassinate Mr. Maduro and was tortured by military counterintelligence officers through beatings and shocks to the persons arms, legs and genitals, according to the indictment. Flores denied release Ms. Flores lawyers had argued their client should be released on bail because she needs a cardiac procedure and wants to recover in a more comfortable environment. The lawyers proposed moving her to a residence in the New York City area with round-the-clock private security, and said she is not a danger to the community. In denying the motion for bail, Mr. Hellerstein decided the evidence against Ms. Flores appeared strong. The judge also said Flores, who wore a dark prison T-shirt and a headset to listen to a simultaneous Spanish translation of the proceedings, appeared to be relatively healthy. For whatever its worth, her appearance today is no worse and perhaps a little better than when I first met with her on her arraignment, Mr Hellerstein said, referring to her first appearance in court on January 5. She was still bandaged up from the military invasion, Donnelly said. Prosecutors in the Manhattan U.S. Attorneys Office opposed Flores release. They said Ms. Flores has received adequate medical care at the detention center, and if released poses an extreme risk of flight and danger to the public, including possible witness intimidation. Mr. Hellersteins bail denial will not affect Ms. Flores trial or potential punishment. Mr. Maduro and Ms. Flores have been held at Brooklyns Metropolitan Detention Center since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.

headline: 'Modern-Day Thomas Edison': Trump Gives Musk With Top US Science Medal After Bitter Fallout
content: Trump praised the SpaceX and Tesla chief as a national treasure and called him a modern-day Thomas Edison during a ceremony in Washington. US President Donald Trump presented Elon Musk with the countrys top science honour on Thursday, marking a public reunion between the two after their bitter falling-out last year. Trump praised the SpaceX and Tesla chief as a national treasure" and called him a modern-day Thomas Edison" during a ceremony in Washington. - Asked Grok? Trump Reportedly Consulted Musk's AI Chatbot Before Capturing Maduro - With Elon Musk, It's Not Just About Business: From India To US, There's Politics Involved - Trump Praises Immigrant Tech CEOs While Cracking Down On Foreign Workers: The Two Sides Of MAGA Policy - Did Elon Musk Break Up With Shivon Zillis? Neuralink Executives 'Hard To Let Go' Post Sparks Rumours Six leading figures from the US technology sector received prestigious awards at the event, which was titled Science: A New Golden Age". Trump praises Musk Musk received the National Medal of Science alongside Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su. Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the countrys top award for technological achievement. Trump warmly congratulated Musk, calling him a friend and saying he was a very, very special guy". The president also patted Musk on the back as he presented him with the medal in a wooden case. The ceremony offered a sharp contrast to the pairs public clash in 2025. From White House ally to bitter rival Musk had been one of Trumps closest allies after the 2024 election and became the public face of the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, which pushed for sweeping cuts to federal spending and the government workforce. Their relationship deteriorated after Musk left the administration and criticised Trumps spending plans. Trump later threatened Musk with deportation, while Musk made allegations linking Trump to Jeffrey Epstein. The dispute quickly became a highly public clash between two of the worlds most prominent figures. Relations have since improved. Musk attended Trumps state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping in September and joined a White House meeting on artificial intelligence last week. (With inputs from agencies) President Donald Trump presented Elon Musk with the National Medal of Science, which is the country's top science honor, during a ceremony titled "Science: A New Golden Age" in Washington.

headline: Saudi Says Debris From Houthis Missile Interception Hits Riyadh Kindergarten, Medical Complex
content: led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles heading towards Riyadh. The kingdom's civil defence agency later said falling debris damaged the two civilian sites. Saudi Arabia on Thursday said that debris from the interception of missiles fired by Yemens Houthis damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh, as the Iran-backed group launched a fresh wave of attacks on the Saudi capital. The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles heading towards Riyadh. The kingdoms civil defence agency later said falling debris damaged the two civilian sites. It did not report casualties or give details of the extent of the damage. - Stay Indoors: Indian Embassy Issues Advisory For Nationals In Saudi Arabia As Houthis Escalate Attacks - Loud Explosions Heard In Riyadh, Houthis Claim They Fired Missile At Airport - Air India Flight Changes Course Midway, Returns To Delhi After Houthi Strike On Riyadh Airport - Riyadh Airport Targeted By Houthi Missile: Air India Express, Akasa Air Cancel Flights Fresh attacks target Riyadh The Houthis claimed three separate attacks on Riyadhs King Khalid International Airport. Their military spokesman, Yahya Saree, also said missiles were fired at an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. The group has increasingly targeted Saudi Arabia since fighting in Yemen intensified in July. It has threatened to strike key infrastructure and disrupt Saudi airspace. Sources briefed on the situation gave differing accounts of damage at Riyadh airport, with one saying a plane suffered severe damage and another reporting that three aircraft were hit. The claims could not be independently verified. Several flights at the airport were delayed or cancelled, while passengers were advised to check with airlines before travelling. Residents told to take precautions Explosions were heard across Riyadh after the missile interceptions. Some diplomats were instructed to remain inside their embassies, while several international schools took extra safety measures. One school reportedly moved children to a basement after the attacks. A parent told AFP that her daughter had called her, saying she was completely distraught". The United States urged its citizens in Saudi Arabia to exercise heightened vigilance following the attacks. The Houthis have also threatened Saudi oil facilities, warning workers to leave them. The latest escalation comes days after an attack on a major refinery south of Riyadh. Yemens humanitarian crisis deepens The renewed fighting has also worsened the humanitarian situation in Yemen. More than 200,000 people have been displaced since July, according to UN figures, while much of the population remains dependent on aid. Yemens government says its forces have retaken strategic areas along the Red Sea coast, but the Houthis dispute those claims. The fighting has also affected Taiz, where Houthi advances have cut key routes and contributed to shortages and rising prices of essential goods. The claims made by both sides could not be independently verified as the conflict continues to move rapidly. (With inputs from AFP) Debris from intercepted Houthi missiles damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh, according to Saudi Arabia's civil defence agency.

headline: Over 5,000 chickens killed in a poultry farm fire near Cheyyar
content: More than 5,000 chickens were charred to death in a fire at a poultry farm in Ukkal village near Cheyyar town in Tiruvannamalai on Thursday. Police said the poultry farm was set up by S. Hemalatha, 39, a few years ago in her paddy field sprawling four acres. The farm, which comprises three large tin sheet-roofed sheds, houses a total of over 5,000 chickens. Fire was reported in one of the sheds around 2 a.m. Based on an alert, firefighters from Cheyyar rushed to the spot and put out the fire after an hour. Police said that 80 bags of chicken feed were also destroyed in the incident. A case was registered by Cheyyar police.

headline: Man held for illegal sand mining from Palar river in Tirupattur
content: A 33-year-old man was arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur for illegal sand mining from the dry river bed of Palar on Thursday. Police said the arrested person was identified as G. Saravanan, a resident of Vaniyambadi. Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in the district to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances. Police said a police team was on routine patrol on Chennai-Bengaluru Highway (NH-48) in the area when they saw a bullock cart with loads of river sand. He told police that the sand was mined from the dry riverbed to sell the consignment to retail traders. The team nabbed him. Police also seized a bullock cart with sand. A case was registered. Further probe is under way.

headline: Woman held for snatching gold chain from commuter on bus
content: A 45-year-old woman was arrested by the Arani taluk police in Tiruvannamalai on Thursday for stealing eight sovereigns of gold chain from a 70-year-old commuter travelling in a government bus. Police said the arrested person was identified as K. Satya, 45, a resident of Chengam town. The victim was S. Padmavathi, 70, a resident of Chennai. Initial inquiry revealed that the Padmavathi was travelling in the government bus from Chennai to Arani. Satya was seated next to her. Police said that during the trip, both were befriended. Padmavathi gave her handbag containing the gold chain to Satya after believing her assurance to keep it safe during the journey. After some time, Satya handed over the handbag to Padmavathi and got down from the bus at Irumbedu village near Arani. Police said that Padmavathi checked her bag after reaching her relatives house and found the gold chain missing. The incident occurred on September 13. Based on the complaint, a case was registered. Special teams analysed CCTV footage along the route and mobile phone signals. A police team nabbed the suspect from her hideout near Chengam. The police also recovered the gold chain from her. Later, she was lodged at Central Prison in Vellore.

headline: Forest Department organises volleyball tournament for tribal youth in Jawadhu Hills
content: Government Forest Higher Secondary School at Jamunamarathur village in Tiruvannamalai district as part of World Wildlife Week 2026, which is celebrated between October 2 and 8. Forest officials said that the tournament was aimed at encouraging sports among youth in tribal areas. It will also help create awareness about environmental protection among the tribal populace. Divided into 32 teams, 384 tribal youth participated in the knockout matches that were held on the school campus. Forest officials said that a team from Palamarathur tribal village won the first prize that carried a cash of 15,000, followed by Thekumarathur village team with a prize money of 10,000. Erimarathur village team won the third prize with a cash award of 5,000. Forest officials said that Collector Vandhana Garg distributed the prizes and certificates to the winning teams at the Collectorate in the presence of K. Sudhagar, District Forest Officer, G. Vinothraj, Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF), and S. Gunasekaran, Forest Range Officer (FRO), Jamunamarathur range (Jawadhu Hills).

headline: Mecca Pact Is Strictly Defensive, Not For Attacks: Turkish FM Hakan Fidan Clarifies | Exclusive Details
content: Fidan firmly ruled out the deployment of Turkish combat troops to undertake offensive missions in Yemen Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has dismissed criticism surrounding the newly established Mecca Defence Pact, emphasising that the agreement is strictly a collective security mechanism designed for mutual protection rather than offensive military actions. Fidan sought to dispel geopolitical misinterpretations, clarifying that the trilateral arrangement between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan operates strictly on a defensive framework. He addressed speculation regarding potential offensive operations in regional conflict zones, firmly ruling out the deployment of Turkish combat troops to undertake offensive missions in Yemen. Fidan stressed that while member nations are bound to support one another in the event of external aggression, the pact does not serve as a springboard for foreign intervention or military escalation. - Mecca Pacts First Test: Pakistani Fighter Jets Striking Iran-Backed Houthis In Yemen, Turkey Also Joins Saudi - 15,000 Troops, Fighter Jets In Saudi Arabia: Pakistan Confirms Military Deployment Under Mecca Pact - From 'We Wont Fight' To Troops For Saudi Arabia: Pakistans Yemen U-Turn And The Mecca Pact - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive Rapid Steps Towards Full Operational Capability Countering claims that the security agreement amounts to political rhetoric, Fidan asserted that the Mecca Pact is moving swiftly toward full institutionalisation and practical execution. The Foreign Minister highlighted that strategic discussions are advancing across member capitals to set up operational structures, establish formal intelligence-sharing protocols, and build joint defence capabilities. Fidan noted that cheap political rhetoric fails to reflect the reality of the evolving security environment across West Asia. He emphasised that member states are actively coordinating to operationalise the agreement, ensuring that technical, air defence, and logistical support structures are established to safeguard regional stability and national sovereignty. Firm Commitment to Regional Peace and Stability Reaffirming Trkiyes steadfast commitment to its allies, Fidan reiterated that Ankara will stand decisively alongside pact members if they face external threats or armed attacks. He underscored that protecting Saudi Arabias territorial integrity and strategic infrastructure remains a priority within the framework of collective deterrence. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan dismissed criticism of the Mecca Defence Pact. The trilateral arrangement is between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. Fidan ruled out deploying Turkish combat troops for offensive missions in Yemen. The Mecca Pact is moving swiftly toward full institutionalisation and practical execution. Turkey will stand with pact members if they face external threats or armed attacks. At the same time, the Turkish Foreign Minister maintained that military deterrence must be paired with diplomatic engagement. Trkey continues to support peaceful dialogue, regional conflict resolution, and political solutions in Yemen, balancing its defence commitments to Saudi Arabia with a broader commitment to long-term stability in West Asia. The Mecca Pact is a collective security mechanism designed strictly for mutual protection and defense rather than offensive military actions, operating to safeguard national sovereignty and regional stability.

headline: Kakodkar urges diplomatic community to work towards India becoming NSG member
content: Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) member Anil Kakodkar on Thursday called upon the countrys diplomatic community to work towards India becoming a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), even though the country was benefitting only from a waiver. He was speaking at an international conference Building Indias Nuclear Ecosystem -- Policy, Technology & Industry organised by the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras (IIT-M) and the Deccan Centre for International Relations (DCIR) in Chennai. We get a lot of uranium now from the international market, thanks to the NSG waiver. But, it is only a waiver. It is not a membership. That waiver can be turned around without much difficulty. I request all those, who are engaged in diplomacy, to make sure that we get a membership of the NSG because that is what will de-risk the availability of uranium, which is a major risk factor in building such a large programme, Mr. Kakodkar said. He called for accelerating efforts to bring thorium into energy generation sooner. Pointing to certain limitations in the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025 (aka SHANTI Act), Mr. Kakodkar said certain aspects were restricted and was allowed only for the government. There are justifiable reasons for that. But, the question is how does one carry out a nuclear reactor design de novo under such a situation? I think we need to put our heads together. I dont find enough clarity on this. For instance, molten-salt reactor was where back-end activities took place right inside the reactor system, but SHANTI Act would not allow it, legally speaking, he pointed out. Former Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations and DCIRs chair of its steering committee T.S. Tirumurti said nuclear energy was experiencing a renewed momentum across the world. Issues such as private capital, advanced manufacturing in international collaborations were increasingly central to the nuclear landscape. India stands at a particularly important juncture in this global story. With ambitious targets for expanding nuclear capacity, a long-standing three-stage programme and a growing recognition of the need for faster, more cost-effective deployment, we need to actively shape the next chapter of our nuclear journey. Professor Manu Santhanam from the Department of Civil Engineering said IIT-M has been incubating several startups. He expected some startups would grow in the nuclear sector, given the SHANTI Act, which he said has paved the way for ideas emerging from youngsters. DCIR Senior Advisor Balasubramanian C said the global nuclear landscape was witnessing a clear revival. India stood at a pivotal moment to build a self-reliant, technology-driven nuclear ecosystem, he said.

headline: Government must heed common people, says CPI's Veerapandian
content: While it is unfair to expect positive changes within four months of a new regime assuming office, the government should also pay heed to the common persons concerns and not depend solely on bureaucrats to decide on public policies, said CPI state secretary M.Veerapandian in Hosur on Thursday. He was speaking to the media on the sidelines of a party executive meeting here. The CPI leader underlined that the Lefts support to the TVK was not for a government but for democracy and that the party would always ally with the common people. There were scores of constituencies including sanitation workers, road workers, nurses, government doctors and teacher, rural road network workers, whose demands and needs were not met but were part of the poll promises. It was incumbent upon the government to honour those promises, the CPI leader said. On the controversy over use of HIndi on medicine covers in government hospitals, the CPI leader said, while the party was open to respecting all languages, it fiercely opposed the Union governments move to impose Hindi in any form [The medicine covers were procured by the erstwhile DMK regime, according to State Health Minister Arunraj].

headline: CJP claims spokesperson picked up by Rajasthan police ahead of October 10 protest
content: Ahead of its October 10 protest in New Delhi, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said its national spokesperson and organisation co-incharge Deepak Baliyan was allegedly picked up and brutally assaulted by the Alwar Police on Thursday. It claimed that over 10,000 persons have been detained from across the country ahead of the proposed march to Jantar Mantar to demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The detained persons include CJP activists and people from various student, farmer and Dalit organisations, apart from political parties, the CJP claimed. Some police personnel from Alwars Kathumar police station allegedly reached Baliyans residence late on Thursday but left after he started recording videos and also took CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka on a call, CJP leaders claimed. However, they returned later and allegedly took him away, they claimed. Deepak Baliyan was dragged after this (live video), his brother was beaten up badly. Deepak was recovering from a leg fracture, and his father has informed that the police badly smashed his leg, Ranka claimed on X. The partys official handle asked, Are we heading towards another Emergency? Alwar Superintendent of Police (SP) Sudheer Choudhary and Kathumar Circle Officer Jogendra Singh did not respond to calls seeking a comment. Kathumar police station Station House Officer (SHO) Chander Shekhar Sharma said that he is away in Ghaziabad on an official investigation. CJP founder and convenor Abhijeet Dipke claimed on social media that Rajasthan Police has brutally assaulted CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan and his brother. Deepak has been detained and his brothers head has been cracked open. The party leaders also shared a video clip of some persons in plainclothes alighting from a police jeep and approaching Baliyan. CJP co-convenor Saurav Das claimed Baliyan has been taken to this unknown location by the Rajasthan Police. We are concerned about his life. The BJP is behaving like a mafia don party and coordinating with its syndicates in BJP-ruled states. Demanding Baliyans immediate release, Peoples Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) quoted his family members as saying that two police jeeps arrived at his home around 10 pm and forcibly took him away. It also alleged that Baliyans brother was beaten up while his mother was pushed by a policeman. Later, Ranka said Baliyan has been picked up for breach of peace under (CrPC) 151, which is now covered under BNSS 170 (Arrest to prevent commission of cognizable offences). Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) supremo and MP Hanuman Beniwal demanded Baliyans immediate release, saying, Democratically protesting is the right of every citizen, but taking someone into custody before any demonstration or movement is an insult to the democratic system.

headline: Trump Rules Out Iran Strike Before Midterms, Cites 'Productive' Talks As Oil Prices Surge
content: Trump said Iran was in a weak economic and military position, while adding that the US blockade would remain in place. US President Donald Trump has ruled out any US attack on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, saying Washington is engaged in productive discussions" with Tehran. Trump made the remarks on Truth Social on Thursday, after oil prices rose sharply on reports that the US could launch fresh strikes against Iran before the elections. - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes - Trumps Midterm Crisis? Why 41 GOP Candidates Are Distancing Themselves From Him - 'How Trump Feels He Is': Iran Mocks US President With Hrithik Roshan Movie Meme - Trump May Announce Executive Order Seeking To Slash Diesel Prices Ahead Of US Midterm Elections Trump says no attack before vote I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effectwe will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections," Trump said. He said Iran was in a weak economic and military position, while adding that the US blockade would remain in place. Trump also said Washington was holding productive discussions" with the Islamic Republic, but gave no details about the nature or progress of the talks. He reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon. Oil prices rise amid regional tensions Oil markets have remained on edge as tensions continue around the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments. Trump claimed that 22 million barrels of oil had moved through the strait in one night, while claiming none came from or went to Iran. Fears of wider conflict have also been fuelled by tensions involving Yemens Houthis and Saudi Arabia. The UKMTO maritime agency said an oil tanker off Qatars northern coast was struck by multiple projectiles on Wednesday, with an unspecified number of casualties. Rising fuel prices are also becoming a political issue ahead of the US midterms. Trump, although not on the ballot, has remained closely involved in the Republican campaign as his party seeks to retain control of Congress. (With inputs from AFP) President Donald Trump stated that the United States will not attack Iran prior to the November 3 midterm elections, citing productive discussions between Washington and Tehran.

headline: Rice millers fear steep hike in rice prices
content: Rice millers in Kangayam fear that the retail price of rice may touch 100 a kg by the end of January, 2027. Non-availability of paddy and continuous increase in paddy prices are a matter of concern to the millers, said Palaniswamy, president of the Kangayam Rice Millers Association. The retail price of rice is approximately 75 a kg now. It is likely to touch 100 a kg by the end of January. Paddy is not available for the mills and almost 50% of the rice mills in Kangayam in Tiruppur district are not operating now. The price of rice for a 26 kg bag has gone up by almost 500. However, the market is not ready to absorb this hike, he said. The price of paddy that was 24 a kg in January this year is 42 a kg for KNM variety and the cost of Amman Ponni variety was 29 a kg in January and 46.20 a kg now. Paddy is not available to millers for credit. Those who are able to pay in cash are visiting the sellers and taking the paddy in bulk. A lot of rice mills are seeing last minute cancellation of paddy supplies, he added. With reports coming in that farmers have not sown the seed for January harvest due to poor south east monsoon, arrival of paddy in January next year is likely to be delayed. This will only push up the prices as the demand is usually high after mid January, Mr. Palaniswamy said.

headline: Trump Labels Those Calling AI 'Artificial Intelligence' Instead Of 'Super Intelligence' As 'The Enemy'
content: US President Donald Trump has urged people to use Super Intelligence instead of Artificial Intelligence, warning that those who do not follow his preferred term are THE ENEMY. US President Donald Trump has warned people against using the term artificial intelligence", saying those who ignore his preferred phrase, super intelligence", will be considered THE ENEMY". Trump made the remarks in a post on his Truth Social platform on Thursday. He did not specify what action or consequences would follow for those who continue to use the term artificial intelligence". The White House considers anyone that uses the term, Artificial Intelligence, as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, Super Intelligence, THE ENEMY!" Trump wrote. Trump Pushes For Super Intelligence Trump first proposed replacing artificial intelligence" with super intelligence" during his speech at the United Nations General Assembly last month. At the time, he said the new term sounds much better". In late September, Trump also signed an executive order requiring the use of the term super intelligence" across the US government. The order, however, does not apply to private companies. Despite this, some businesses and technology figures have already started using the term. Meta, led by Mark Zuckerberg, has adopted the phrase, while Trump ally Elon Musk has also used super intelligence" in posts on his social media platform X. Political Debate Over AI Terminology The debate over the terminology comes amid growing concerns about artificial intelligence, including questions around its safety and the rapid expansion of data centres across the US. Trump has strongly supported the development of AI but has also sought to present the technology in a more positive light as concerns over its risks continue to grow. The president has also previously pushed for changes to the names of places. He now refers to the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America" and has called Lake Ontario Lake America". President Donald Trump signed an executive order requiring the use of the term "super intelligence" across the US government, though the order does not apply to private companies. He also warned on Truth Social that anyone continuing to use "artificial intelligence" will be considered "the enemy".

headline: 'Fighting for our future': France high school students vow no let-up
content: Tens of thousands of people thronged a Paris square on Thursday (October 8, 2026) demanding better education and less police brutality, as students protested nationwide despite government attempts to ease a crisis that has rocked the country for more than a week. Students have blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country, with squads of riot police deployed to control the situation occasionally resulting in violent clashes. A few fireworks streamed up into the sky as tens of thousands of students from schools and universities rallied in the French capital's Bastille Square on Thursday (October 8, 2026) afternoon. Crowds of students climbed the famous monument at its centre, some waving the French flag and singing the national anthem. A student sat with his legs dangling on the top of a bus stop, clutching a sign reading: "Reason for absence: Too busy fighting for our future." Student demonstrators many attending high schools called lycees for children aged between 15 and 18 years old have complained of absent teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures. Jeanne, a 15-year-old student from a top Paris high school, said she wanted to show solidarity with pupils in less privileged areas outside the capital. "Everyone has the right to be educated at the same level. There shouldn't be people who are more educated than others when we're all in the public education system," she said. Marianne, a 20-year-old university student who also did not want to give her second name, said she was also there to protest excessive police force in recent days of protest. "For me, that's just unacceptable," she said. 'We want action' While the rallies have been largely peaceful, some demonstrators have started fires and vandalised bus shelters. In response, police have used tear gas, batons and blast balls, prompting rights groups and the children to accuse them of using disproportionate force. A 15-year-old lost a hand on Monday (October 5, 2026) after police fired a stun grenade, and the government has suspended the use of the weapons in response. Police on Thursday (October 8, 2026) evening said they had use tear gas in Bastille to disperse some "high-risk profiles" who had come into contact with them. Education Minister Edouard Geffray was set to announce "concrete measures" to address the crisis on the evening news, the prime minister's office said. Mr. Geffray earlier in the day promised to present an "emergency plan" on teacher replacements within "a few hours or a few days". In a televised address on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu promised a plan to respond to the crisis by the end of October. Although he denied security forces had been given "orders to confront" the young people, many were unconvinced. "We don't want words, we want action," 17-year-old Camille told AFP at a student march in the western city of Nantes. Outside one high school in Rennes, 18-year-old Hanaa told AFP she was "disappointed and unconvinced" by Mr. Lecornu's remarks. "We expected more from him," agreed fellow student Salyna, 17. Fundamental issues Assane Seck, father of a 15-year-old student in a Paris suburb, told AFP that at his son's school, "a teacher in one subject or another is missing" almost every day. "There are genuine, fundamental issues that deserve reflection," he said. Economy Minister Roland Lescure said this week there was room to address demands for more school resources within the highly constrained 2027 budget, which is facing heated political debate. In the current draft, education has the second largest increase in funding after defence with a boost of 1.4% to 90.9 billion. France's spending picture on education is mixed. A report from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development found that France spends 24% more per student on upper secondary education than the OECD average but it spends markedly less at earlier stages, particularly primary schools. The country's recent PISA score an annual survey which assesses the performance of education systems by measuring the skills of 15-year-old students was France's worst since the rankings began in 2000. Hundreds of students, police and teaching staff have been injured since the protests began, and more than 6,500 people mostly children have been arrested. Police have opened 18 internal investigations into allegations of misconduct. The unrest has erupted just months ahead of the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction.

headline: Russia Reports No Health Issues Among Contacts Of Woman In Plague Case
content: Russia said medical monitoring of all contacts of a woman who reportedly died of plague has concluded, with no health issues linked to infectious disease detected. Russia has reported no health issues linked to infectious disease among people who came into contact with a woman who reportedly died of plague, the governor of Siberias Irkutsk region said Thursday. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said medical monitoring of all identified contacts had been completed, with no health problems detected during the observation period. - 'Rely On Official Statements': Russia Dismisses 'False' Plague Reports Over Suspected Second Case - Russia Plague Scare: From Symptoms To Spread, How Dangerous It Is And Could It Be Another Covid? - 'Looking At It Very Strongly': Trump Offers US Help As Russia Downplays Plague Reports - Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before? Medical monitoring of all contacts has concluded," Kobzev said on Russias state-backed social platform Max. No health issues related to infectious disease were detected." Medical Monitoring Of Contacts Concludes The monitoring was carried out after authorities traced people who had been in contact with the woman amid concerns over a possible plague infection. Kobzev said the observation of all contacts had now been completed, with authorities reporting no health problems associated with an infectious disease. No Infectious Disease Symptoms Reported According to the governor, none of the monitored contacts developed health issues linked to an infectious disease during the observation period. The latest update comes as Russian authorities continue to assess the circumstances surrounding the reported death of the woman, who was said to have died of plague. For now, authorities have reported no infectious disease-related health issues among the people monitored in connection with the case. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev stated that medical monitoring of all identified contacts has concluded with no infectious disease-related health issues detected during the observation period.

headline: Israel drastically reduces British diplomatic presence in Jerusalem
content: Israel said the British consulate in east Jerusalem ended its functions on Thursday (October 8, 2026) but seven diplomats would be allowed to remain in a limited capacity, with the U.K. saying the outpost would continue to offer "vital services". The move comes after Israel ordered the closure of the consulate in September as retaliation after London-led Western sanctions over violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said Thursday's (October 8, 2026) move to downsize the U.K. presence had followed a dialogue with the British government in order to avoid an escalation of tensions between the two countries. "As I announced, the British consulate in Jerusalem ended its role today," Mr. Saar said in a statement, adding that 20 diplomats including the consul general were ending their missions and leaving the country. Mr. Saar said the building was the property of the British government and that a "task force of only seven diplomats" would be allowed to operate from the premises, "which ceased to function as a consulate today". "Their scope of activity will be very limited," Mr. Saar said, adding the two countries had "agreed on the continuation of dialogue between the governments". The U.K. pledged to continue delivering "vital services" in Jerusalem, saying the consulate general building would remain open and would "be known as the U.K. Mission, Jerusalem". "The U.K. Mission, Jerusalem is independent, operational and will continue to deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people," Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said in a statement. Mr. Miliband said the U.K. did not accept that the Israeli government had "the legal right" to enforce the closure. "We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence and we will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible," he added. The Palestinian Authority's foreign affairs ministry denounced the move as "illegal" and said in a statement that it viewed it as "an attempt to impose Israeli sovereignty over the occupied city" of Jerusalem. Israeli settlements The British consulate was founded nearly 200 years ago, and lies in east Jerusalem, part of the historically Palestinian area that Israel captured in 1967. Israel later annexed east Jerusalem and considers the holy city its undivided capital. While Israel controls east Jerusalem, most countries including Britain do not recognise its sovereignty over the whole city. Also Read | Britain bans trade with illegal Israeli settlements The British consulate handles "political, commercial, security and economic interests between the U.K. and Palestine", according to its website, as well as consular services for British nationals in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza. An AFP photographer on Thursday (October 8, 2026) saw that the diplomatic emblem and a plaque that adorned the consulate's facade had been removed. The measure has led Britain to lose a "historic and meaningful presence" in terms of their support for the Palestinians, an Israeli diplomatic source said. "So yes, they keep the building" and a limited number of diplomats, the source told AFP, but "they have lost a historic and significant footprint". The source said they thought the recent dialogue between the British and Israeli governments would allow a "turning point" in deteriorating relations. "If until a few weeks ago, until September 8, we were on a path of spiralling down, then I think the page has turned," the source said. "Dialogue is a path towards returning to... more constructive relations." September 8 was the day Mr. Saar ordered the consulate to close. Also Read | Trade curbs on Israeli settlements in West Bank unlikely to have much bite He also said Israel would expel British representatives at a centre monitoring the U.S.-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza, bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces and ban 12 Britons, mostly members of parliament, from visiting. Mr. Saar on Thursday (October 8, 2026) said those measures had been implemented. The retaliation came after 12 countries including Britain, Canada and France announced they would sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, following a surge in settler attacks against Palestinians in the occupied territory.

headline: Thanjavur Railway Junction name board in Hindi removed following protests
content: Railway authorities removed a name board in Hindi atop the second entrance at the Thanjavur Railway Junction on October 8 following opposition to it from various organisations. Tamil organisations had called for a demonstration at the junction on Thursday. However, when the issue was brought to the notice of railway junction authorities on Wednesday night, the officials said action would be taken on Thursday after consulting senior officials. Meanwhile, the DMK registered its protest and demanded the immediate removal of the Hindi name board. On October 8, a group of DMK cadres staged a demonstration on the junction premises condemning the placing of the Hindi name board at a prominent location. Thanjavur MP S. Murasoli visited the junction on Thursday while the railway officials were busy removing the Hindi name board. The Leftists Common Platform (LCP) thanked the Southern Railway for removing the name board. Display of the name board in Hindi atop the second entrance portico, where the replica of the Big Temple tower had been set up, was an act of Hindi imposition, it contended in a statement.

headline: Delhi Liquor Shops To Stay Shut Tomorrow And Day After Amid Opposition Protests
content: The order, issued by the Delhi government's Excise Department on Thursday, comes as the city braces for another round of protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: GST Council clears big procedural overhaul, keeps rates largely unchanged
content: Banikinkar Pattanayak, Dhirendra Kumar, Vijay C Roy New Delhi: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, chaired by Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, on Thursday cleared one of the biggest procedural overhauls of the indirect tax regime since its rollout in 2017, while leaving tax rates unchanged to provide greater stability. The apex decision-making body sought to expand and expedite refunds to unlock working capital for businesses, curb the power of officers to arrest people suspected of evasion, shift verification from discretionary checks by officers to system-led risk rules, and restore certainty to day-to-day compliance, among other measures. The decisions, which have been debated for months, come at a time when India needs sustained private investment growth to supplement public capex, exporters are facing the impact of the West Asia war and a more uncertain global environment, and supply chains are being realigned worldwide. The moves, coming a year after a broad range of GST rates were mostly cut and slabs rationalised, are aimed at reducing costs, easing liquidity pressures and simplifying compliance for businesses. For a country seeking to bolster manufacturing while strengthening the principle of one nation, one market, these are crucial second-order reforms whose benefits could compound over the years. The council has decided to set up an officers committee to deliberate on the issue of allowing honest buyers to have credit in cases where suppliers have defaulted, Sitharaman said, while briefing the media about the decisions taken. So far, input tax credit was available only when the tax charged to a buyer had actually reached the government. This effectively meant that a buyers credit depended on the supplier and, in a long chain, on entities with which the buyer had no direct dealings. While the Centre was in support of the proposal to protect the honest buyers against faults of others, some states requested deliberations on the issue, which the Union government accepted, the minister said. The committee is expected to submit its report in three months and any decision in this regard is planned to be implemented from April next year. The council has also decided on a new principle aimed at widening the refund mechanism. Refunds will now extend to GST paid not only on input goods but also on input services, such as factory rent, consultancy fees and logistics, where a business claims a refund because of an inverted duty structure. Refunds will also be extended to tax paid on plant and machinery, spread over five years, against a declaration that the equipment remains in the business. Every GST refund claim will now have to be acknowledged within 10 days (against the current average of 15 days), failing which it will be deemed to have been acknowledged. For exporters and inverted-duty cases, which account for two-thirds of all refund claims, 90% of the claims will be released automatically within three days after a risk check, with the balance released after verification. The council has suggested curbing the power of GST officers to arrest merely on suspicion of tax evasion. The prosecution threshold for duty evasion, too, will be raised to 5 crore from 1 crore and general penalty will be cut to 10,000 from 25,000. It recommended common standards for GST notices and proceedings across the country. For smoother movement of goods, checks will now usually be done only in the state of origin or destination, doing away with the practice of multiple checks at multiple points. Only intelligence-based and authorised interception of goods will be allowed. The council has relaxed certain conditions that had effectively restricted export benefits. Indian firms billing or receiving payment through their own overseas branch will now qualify as exports. The condition that the supplier and recipient should not be establishments of the same person has been removed, making it clear that what matters is whether the customer is abroad. Job work in India on foreign-owned goods, such as repair, testing, storage and processing, will have the customers location as the place of supply, rather than the location where the work is done. It will qualify as an export even if the goods remain in India. GST registration through the automatic route under Rule 14A is proposed to be completed in just three working days, from more than three weeks now, without officer intervention. This will apply to applicants who do not wish to pass on monthly input tax credit of more than 2.5 lakh. The route now covers 61% of registrations. Similarly, the process of deregistration will be streamlined by scrapping the requirement for a GST officers visit if the applicant has paid the taxes and is not facing a probe. On litigation, a 10,000 minimum threshold will apply to show-cause notices under Sections 73, 74 and 74A, including pending cases. Since 2017, about 11.3 lakh notices at or below this levelabout a fifth of all cases by number but involving a negligible amount of taxhave been issued. Bipin Sapra, Partner and Indirect Tax Policy Leader, EY India, said: These are among the most significant trade facilitation reforms since GST was introduced. By extending refunds of accumulated input tax credit to input services and capital goods, and rationalising blocked credits, the Council is restoring GST's founding promise of seamless credit. Also Read | 57th GST Council meeting: What's on the agenda? Jharkhand finance minister Radha Krishna Kishore proposed keeping coal outside the GST regime and allowing states to levy VAT on it. He also proposed a complementary Resource-Origin and Ecological Equalisation Framework to recognise states that supply exhaustible minerals to the national economy, without disturbing the destination principle. Jharkhand contributes substantially to national energy integration and economic development, while the depletion of resources and the long-term environmental and social burden remain within the state. Since GST on coal is passed on to consuming states under the destination principle, Jharkhand is deprived of the revenue needed to address these costs, Kishore said. "Punjab supports the direction of reform. Our request is that facilitation should be accompanied by smarter enforcement. Punjab proposes that the Government of India, GSTN and the States jointly develop a common AI-based, data-driven enforcement architecture, supported by a national repository integrating tax, vehicle and movement data and providing actionable risk intelligence to both Central and State officers. Punjab would be happy to take the initiative in piloting this model. The objective should be simple: maximum facilitation for honest taxpayers, minimum physical intervention, and maximum precision against fraud and tax evasion," said Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.
