headline: 'Very Positive Impact': PM Modi Hails 'Greater Decriminalisation' In GST, Says Reforms Will Cut Compliance Costs
content: One of the biggest changes proposed by the GST Council is the removal of the power of arrest under GST. The prosecution threshold will also be raised from Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 5 crore. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has welcomed the new set of reforms approved by the GST Council, saying changes such as the removal of arrest provisions, greater decriminalisation and simpler procedures will have a very positive impact". The reforms were approved at the 57th meeting of the GST Council held in New Delhi on October 8, 2026. The measures include changes to GST enforcement, prosecution, penalties, notices and litigation. - GST Council Scraps Tax Officers Arrest Power, Raises Prosecution Limit To Rs. 5 Crore - GST Notices For Dues Below Rs. 10,000 Scrapped: What The New Rule Means For Taxpayers - GST Councils Big Business Push: Faster Registration, Automated Refunds And Less Paperwork - GST Council's New Goods-In-Transit Rules: Who Can Stop, Check And Seize Your Consignment? In a post on X, PM Modi said, I welcome the new round of GST reforms approved by the GST Council." He said the Councils recommendations on the removal of arrest provisions, greater decriminalisation and simpler procedures" would have a very positive impact". PM Modi said the focus of the reforms was on Faster decisions", Lower compliance costs", Automated refunds" and Trust-based administration". These are in line with our constant efforts to make GST more efficient, transparent and citizen-friendly," he said. The reforms are part of a wider set of process changes covering registration, returns, refunds, litigation, input tax credit, goods in transit and exports. GST arrest power to be removed One of the biggest changes proposed by the GST Council is the removal of the power of arrest under GST. The prosecution threshold will also be raised from Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 5 crore. The minimum punishment will be removed, while the punishment whether a fine, imprisonment or both will be left to judicial discretion in every case. The general penalty, which applies when no specific penalty is provided, will also be reduced from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 10,000. The Council said a taxpayer who files late, makes a mistake or falls behind on payment will face recovery, interest and a proportionate penalty, and nothing beyond that". Enforcement to rely on detection According to the Council, the changes are possible because the GST system can now match seller and buyer invoices and identify fake credit when it arises. The Council said this capability did not exist when the GST law was framed. Enforcement can now rest on detection rather than on deterrence," the Councils note said. The shift is part of the broader move towards simpler GST procedures and a system that uses invoice-level information to identify irregularities. No GST notice below Rs. 10,000 The Council has also proposed a common standard for GST litigation. This will cover how notices are issued and served, pre-notice intimation, when fraud may be alleged, how hearings are conducted and how orders are written. Under the proposed changes, no notice will be issued where the monetary amount involved is below Rs. 10,000. The move comes alongside the reduction in the general penalty from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 10,000. Protection for genuine buyers under review The GST Council is also examining the issue of protecting a genuine buyer who has a proper invoice, has received the goods and has paid the supplier in full. A Committee of Officers will study the issue within three months. An agenda on the matter will then be placed before the next GST Council meeting. The reforms come as the Council focuses on how GST works in day-to-day transactions, with changes aimed at simplifying procedures and reducing compliance costs while making the system more efficient and transparent. The 57th GST Council meeting held in New Delhi approved major reforms including the removal of arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 5 crore, removing minimum punishment, lowering the general penalty to Rs. 10,000, and ensuring no notices are issued for amounts below Rs. 10,000.

headline: U.S. suspends Microsoft, Adobe and other major IT firms from PERM green card programme
content: The U.S. government is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and several large IT firms from a programme that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency, senior U.S. officials announced on Thursday (October 8, 2026), citing alleged fraud, and as part of an effort to push companies to hire more Americans. Our message to Microsoft is: Youre a great American company, but youve got to hire great American workers, U.S. Vice-President J.D. Vance said. Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling added that some of the largest IT firms in the world would also be suspended from that programme, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini. We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies, Mr. Sonderling said. Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Under the Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) process, employers seek certification from the Department of Labour that there is no qualified, willing or available U.S. worker for a specific job. Its a step required before filing petitions for most employment-based green cards. Mr. Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for allegedly bringing in international students to undercut American wages. Labour Inspector General Anthony DEsposito said subpoenas had already been served. We will investigate whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships, or visa abuse are compromising federally funded research, Mr. DEsposito said. If an American university is breaking the law to save $1 while exposing American research to a foreign adversary, that is not academic excellence. Its institutional betrayal.

headline: TNPDCL goes back to short-term power purchases for Summer 2027 despite minister's criticism of high-cost deals
content: Less than four months after electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar blamed previous govts for costly short-term power purchases that caused heavy losses to the state power utility, the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL) has floated tenders for similar purchases over six months to meet demand in summer 2027.The power purchase will be between Feb and July, extending beyond the practice of signing power purchase agreements till May 15. Wind power generation typically picks up in the second half of May, while demand eases with the onset of the southwest monsoon in June. While the exact quantum is yet to be finalised, TNPDCL officials said purchases would range from 2,000 MW to 3,200 MW, depending on monthly demand and supply, officials said.With day temperatures hovering at 35C in most parts, the state is facing an extended summer in Oct. Power shortages have led to load shedding this year, with several areas, including parts of Chennai, facing frequent outages. On Wednesday, Tamil Nadus power demand peaked at 20,018 MW, while consumption stood at 439.042 million units. With extended use of air-conditioners in homes, offices and factories, the power consumption is now like what we see in May, an official said. TNPDCL expects demand to rise by at least 6% next year, making short-term purchases inevitable, officials said.The summer 2027 tender was floated a day after another tender to purchase 3,000 MW for October this year. Power will be sourced from private producers within and outside the state.However, TNPDCL has not signed any new long- or medium-term power purchase agreements despite the ministers June 25 promise, made while releasing a white paper on the state power utility, to secure cheaper power through longer contracts. Now, TNPDCL has contracts for 2,830 MW of long-term supply and 2,814 MW of medium-term supply.Nirmal Kumar was unavailable for comment on the proposed short-term purchases for summer 2027.

headline: Faeces found in government school water tank in Dindigul
content: In a shocking incident, faeces was reportedly found in a drinking water tank of a government school at Manoor near Palani in Dindigul district. This is the second such incident reported in the district in recent times. According to the police, over 120 students study at the Manoor Panchayat Union Primary School, located within the Keeranur police station limits. The incident was reported when the school reopened on October 5 after the quarterly examination break. The headmaster got the water tank cleaned. The issue was also raised during the Parent-Teacher Association and School Management Committee meeting held at the school on Wednesday. Enraged by the incident, parents staged a protest and accused the school administration of negligence on student safety. As the situation escalated, Dindigul Superintendent of Police S. Jeyakumar visited the school and inspected the water tank on the premises. He issued instructions to the police to take swift action and arrest those involved in the offence. Acting on a complaint lodged by the headmaster, the Keeranur police registered a case under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). An investigation is under way. District education officials also visited the school and held meetings with the parents and the school authorities. The headmaster said cleaning work had been undertaken to prevent students from drinking water from the contaminated tank, and the issue had been reported to higher authorities. In August, faeces was found near the water tank of a Government Higher Secondary School at Thangamapatti in the district. A notice was also found near the water tank. However, when the authorities found the notice, it was wet and the text was illegible. Dindigul Superintendent of Police S. Jeyakumar had visited the school and inspected the water tank.

headline: Lawyers' delegation meets TN law minister seeking enactment oflaw for protection of advocates
content: A delegation of the Federation of Bar Associations of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on Thursday met Tamil Nadu law minister C T R Nirmal Kumar and submitted a draft bill with suggestive provisions to be included in the Tamil Nadu Advocates (Protection) Act, an exclusive legislation for protection of advocates.Receiving the draft bill, the minister assured the delegation that he would take it to the notice of the chief minister C Joseph Vijay and do the needful as per his instructions.On Oct 3, the federation convened a meeting for the welfare of the legal fraternity in which the law minister participated. In the meeting, a resolution was adopted to initiate steps for the protection of the members of the Bar.While addressing the gathering, Nirmal Kumar assured the members of the Bar that a law protecting the interest of the lawyers would be enacted by the state assembly. He suggested that the federation come up with a draft bill as an initial step for consulting the stakeholders.In view of the same, the federation met the minister and submitted a draft bill.The legislation is proposed for greater protection of advocates and their functions in discharge of professional duties. The proposal was made in the background of recent incidents of assault, killings, intimidation and regular threats caused to advocates due to proper and honest discharge of their professional duties. This often resulted in law-and-order situations and sometimes caused obstruction and deficiencies in rendering professional services by advocates to their clients; apart from instilling a deep sense of apprehension in the minds of advocates while discharging their professional duties, S Prabakaran, honorary chairman of the federation said."Yet another hurdle faced by advocates stems from their representing detainees or arrested or incarcerated persons. It has been seen in several cases that advocates are sought to be questioned about privileged communication to make detection of alleged crime easier. However, this militates against the basic tenets of the legal profession and violates the sanctity which the law enjoins the advocate to maintain with respect to such privileged communication or materials," he added.

headline: Mecca Pact's First Test: Pakistani Fighter Jets Striking Iran-Backed Houthis In Yemen, Turkey Also Joins Saudi
content: Pakistans role is being accompanied by a Turkish military deployment to Saudi Arabia. Pakistans military role in Saudi Arabia has reportedly expanded beyond defensive support, with Pakistani fighter jets being used in strikes against Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen following the activation of the Mecca defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. Israels Channel14 reported that Pakistani fighter jets were striking the Houthis in Yemen. Reports on October 7 and 8 said Pakistan Air Force jets had been involved in attacks against Ansarallah-led Yemeni forces. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - 15,000 Troops, Fighter Jets In Saudi Arabia: Pakistan Confirms Military Deployment Under Mecca Pact - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | News18 - 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised A senior Pakistani military official told The New York Times on Wednesday that Pakistan Air Force fighter jets were being used in strikes this week against the Yemeni Armed Forces (YAF). Pakistani forces already in Saudi Arabia Pakistan has moved beyond defensive support into direct combat operations, according to the reports. A former US defence intelligence analyst estimated that around 8,000 Pakistani troops are deployed in Saudi Arabia. Pakistani military spokesman Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry also confirmed to CNN that Pakistani forces were present in the kingdom. The forces of Pakistan are already there. That I can share with you," he said. At least 8,000 Pakistani troops have been deployed to Saudi Arabia this year as part of the defence pact, along with fighter jets, according to Reuters reporting from earlier this year. The reported use of Pakistani fighter jets in strikes against the Houthis comes after the activation this week of the defence pact between Riyadh, Islamabad and Ankara. Turkey brings air defence, electronic warfare systems Pakistans role is being accompanied by a reported Turkish military deployment to Saudi Arabia. The New Arab cited experts as saying Pakistan could focus on territorial defence and military support inside Saudi Arabia, while Turkey provides capabilities including surveillance, air defence and drones. According to Turkiye Gazetesi, more than 200 Turkish military personnel, along with significant quantities of electronic warfare systems and ground- and air-defence missiles, have been transferred to Saudi Arabia since the Mecca pact was formed. Turkish defence systems are reportedly being used extensively against Ansarallah and are enhancing the combat capabilities of the Saudi-backed Yemeni army. The Turkish report also said hundreds of Syrian army fighters had been deployed to the Saudi-backed side in Yemen. Iran-backed side also sees new fighters The same report claimed that the Shia front has become active", with fighters from Lebanon, Iraq and Iran entering Yemen to join the Ansarallah-led side. The developments come amid a heavy retaliatory campaign by the Yemeni Armed Forces, involving missile and drone strikes against Saudi military and energy sites. Aramco infrastructure, including refineries and storage facilities, as well as military bases and other sites inside Saudi Arabia used to attack Yemen, have reportedly been targeted repeatedly in recent days. Heavy clashes continue in Yemen Heavy fighting is also continuing inside Yemen as Ansarallah-led forces clash with Saudi Arabias proxies. The Ansarallah-led forces are seeking to expel the Saudi-led coalition from the country, according to the information available. The reported Pakistani fighter jet operations mark a significant development following the activation of the Mecca pact, as Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey deepen their military involvement amid the continuing conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia. Pakistans military spokesman earlier has confirmed that Pakistani forces are already in Saudi Arabia. Following the activation of the Mecca defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, Pakistan Air Force jets have been deployed to carry out direct combat strikes against Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen.

headline: US suspends Infosys, Microsoft, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant, Adobe, 2 other IT firms from labour programme: Here's why
content: The United States on Thursday (October 8) suspended several major technology companies, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme, citing concerns over the hiring of foreign workers. US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the decision alongside Vice President JD Vance and the head of the US Anti-Fraud Task Force. I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini, Sonderling said. He separately announced that the Department of Labour was also suspending Microsoft and Adobe from the programme. No new applications to be accepted Under the move, the US Labour Department will not accept new permanent labour certification applications involving the companies or process applications that are already pending. We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies, Sonderling said. The Permanent Labour Certification Programme, commonly known as PERM, is a key pathway for US employers seeking to hire foreign workers on a permanent basis. Labour certification is generally required before an employer can sponsor an eligible foreign worker for certain employment-based green cards. The suspension could therefore affect companies seeking permanent residency for foreign employees through the programme. US cites foreign-worker numbers Sonderling said the companies covered by the action had collectively requested nearly three million foreign workers since 2009. Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers. They've received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications, he said. The labour secretary argued that the scale of foreign-worker hiring had come at the expense of American workers. Thats hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers, Sonderling said. His remarks signal the Trump administrations broader focus on prioritising US workers and scrutinising programmes used by companies to employ foreign nationals.

headline: DCIR, IIT Madras host conference on building India's nuclear ecosystem
content: The Deccan Centre for International Relations (DCIR), an independent think tank under the Institute for Financial Management and Research (IFMR), in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-Madras), organised a one-day international conference on Building Indias Nuclear Ecosystem: Policy, Technology an Industry at IIT Madras on Thursday.The event saw active participation from members of the strategic community, industry leaders, academics, policymakers and other thought leaders. It provided a platform for open dialogue among these stakeholders on an interconnected agenda linking academia, policy, technology, industry, regulation and finance. The conference underscored that only when these elements move together can India build a nuclear ecosystem that is safe, competitive, self-reliant and globally respected.The conference was convened at a time of renewed global momentum for nuclear energy, driven by the twin imperatives of energy security and climate action with countries worldwide revisiting nuclear power as a reliable, low-carbon source of baseload electricity. India stands at a particularly important juncture in this global story, with ambitious targets for expanding nuclear capacity, a long-standing three-stage programme, and a growing recognition of the need for faster, more cost-effective deployment. The technical sessions examined the full spectrum of challenges and opportunities in building Indias nuclear ecosystem. The legal and regulatory foundations underpinning the sector were also discussed.T S Tirumurti, chair, steering committee, Deccan Centre for International Relations and former Ambassador of India to the United Nations, New York, V Kamakoti, director, IIT Madras, spoke at the event. Anil Kakodkar, member, Atomic Energy Commission, spoke on Indias Nuclear Vision.A special address was delivered online from Vienna by Andrea Borio di Tigliole, programme coordinator, Department of Nuclear Energy, IAEA.

headline: Air India, IndiGo cancel and divert Riyadh flights after missile threat
content: Air India Group and IndiGo on Thursday (October 8, 2026) cancelled and diverted several services to Riyadh as carriers monitored an evolving regional situation, disrupting travel between India and the Saudi capital. The disruption comes after Iran-aligned Houthi rebels attacked Saudi Arabia, with a missile fired towards Riyadh International Airport. Air India said its flight AI2243, operating from Delhi to Riyadh, returned to Delhi on Thursday in the interest of passenger and crew safety. The service was subsequently cancelled, with full refunds offered to passengers. The airline also announced that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until October 10, citing the developing situation in the region. Passengers affected by the cancellations will be offered full refunds, the airline said, adding that it was closely monitoring developments. Air India Express separately announced that it had cancelled its Riyadh services until October 10. An IndiGo flight from Hyderabad to Riyadh was diverted to Dammam on Thursday. The airline did not provide further details on the diversion. Air India is learnt to have evacuated its crew from Riyadh to Dammam via road, while Air India Express crew have been told to stay put. IndiGo also cancelled RiyadhDelhi flights scheduled for Thursday and Friday, according to airline sources. Services between Riyadh and Hyderabad, as well as Riyadh and Mumbai, have been cancelled for Friday. IndiGo sources described the situation as still evolving, indicating that further changes to schedules may follow. Airlines advised passengers booked on Riyadh routes to check the latest status of their flights before travelling to the airport or making onward connections there.

headline: New GRAP Rules in Delhi; Restrictions in NCR October 2026: How AQI will decide car entry - Where to check updates daily
content: NCR's revised Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) sets out four stages of pollution-related restrictions, with stricter measures coming into force with deteriorating air quality in the capital and the adjoining regions. Haryana's Sonipat district has been added to the regions in which these restrictions will be in place. Other areas include Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budha Nagar. Noida, part of Gautam Budha Nagar district is also covered in this. For a commuter, the important thing is not whether Delhi's AQI is high but the restrictions that will be invoked after each stage of the GRAP. Vehicles would face restrictions based on factors such as fuel type, emission standard, vehicle category and also location. Here is what car owners in Delhi-NCR need to know about the revised GRAP framework and how to check whether they can drive into Delhi. The revised GRAP framework divides Delhi's air quality into four stages. The most important feature of the revised framework is that authorities will not necessarily have to wait for Delhi's AQI to actually reach a particular threshold. Different stages of GRAP can be invoked based on forecasts. If pollution unexpectedly breaches a threshold because of extreme weather or an episodic event, the relevant stage can also be imposed immediately for measures that can be implemented at once. As a car owner you should remember that there is no single AQI number at which your vehicle/s will be banned. Vehicles will start facing restrictions under Stage III, when Delhi's AQI is in the 401-450 range. Authorities are required to impose restrictions on certain categories of vehicles during this stage. This stage of GRAP specifically provides for restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard Light Motor Vehicles (LMVs) in Delhi and five high-vehicle-density NCR districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budha Nagar. At Stage IV, when Delhi's AQI rises above 450, restrictions will become stricter. At this stage heavy goods vehicles entering Delhi will also be affected. Remember, AQI is the starting point, but not the only thing to check. The AQI determines the pollution category and corresponding GRAP stage, but CAQM decides when a stage is invoked based on the prevailing air quality as well as forecasts and meteorological conditions. So, you should not simply look at an AQI reading of, say, 402 and assume that all Stage III restrictions automatically apply at that exact moment. The practical sequence you can follow: Check AQI check the GRAP stage officially in force check the restrictions under that stage check your vehicle category. Stage I - AQI 201-300: At this stage strict enforcement of pollution-control norms and PUC requirements can be enforced with authorities can be directed to stop visibly polluting vehicles. These vehicles can be impounded or can be fined. Stage II - AQI 301-400: At stage 2, the focus will be on measures such as higher vehicle parking fees in order to discourage private transport and encouraging people to use public transport. Stage III - AQI 401-450: This is the stage which as a car owner is important for you as authorities are required to impose strict restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard four-wheeled LMVs in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budha Nagar. Stage IV - AQI above 450: At this stage, the focus will be on goods vehicles. The entry of heavy goods vehicles into Delhi will be stopped, although LNG, CNG, electric and BS-VI diesel trucks can be permitted to enter. Delhi-registered diesel BS-IV and below-standard HGVs are also banned from plying in Delhi. Moreover, at each stage of GRAP, the provisions of previous stage will remain in place. For the specific Stage III LMV restriction, the revised GRAP rules identifies vehicles by their BS emission standard and fuel type -- BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard LMVs. So commuters and vehicle owners should check their vehicle's fuel type and BS classification, rather than relying only on its age. Also, Stage I requires enforcement of existing restrictions concerning overage petrol and diesel vehicles. The answer depends on the vehicle category and the GRAP stage in force. For Stage III, the restriction on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard LMVs specifically covers Delhi and the high-vehicle-density districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budha Nagar. That means a commuter travelling from Noida/Gautam Budha Nagar to Delhi, for example, needs to check whether their vehicle falls within the restricted category when Stage III is in force. While the revised GRAP measures does not specifically explain what happens to a restricted private car that is already on the road when a higher stage is invoked. What it does make clear is that once a higher stage is invoked, the restrictions from earlier stages continue. Stage III measures are therefore additional to Stage I and II measures, while Stage IV adds to the restrictions already applicable under Stages III, II and I. The revised GRAP document gives citizens a particularly clear instruction: Check the AQI on the SAMEER App and check the GRAP stage in force on the CAQM website. This is important because an AQI reading by itself does not necessarily tell you the complete current restriction status. CAQM's Sub-Committee on GRAP meets frequently to plan advance action and issue orders for invoking different provisions, based on prevailing air quality and AQI forecasts. No -- not as your only check before travelling. A weather app's AQI reading may tell you about the current pollution level, but the GRAP framework operates through official stage invocation by CAQM, including decisions based on forecasts and meteorological conditions. The revised document specifically directs citizens to use the SAMEER App for AQI and the CAQM website for the GRAP stage in force. So the safest routine is: > AQI on SAMEER + GRAP status on CAQM = check before

headline: Jantar Mantar protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation: Delhi orders liquor shops shut on October 9-10
content: Delhi will shut all retail liquor shops on October 9 and 10 as a precautionary measure ahead of a planned protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation. The Delhi government has ordered the closure of retail liquor shops across the national capital citing the prevailing situation and inputs from the Delhi Police as a precautionary measure to maintain public order. An order issued by the Excise Department on Thursday (October 8) directed all retail liquor vends operating under specified licences to remain completely closed for two days. In view of the prevailing situation and inputs received from Delhi Police, as a preventive measure aimed at maintaining public order, it is hereby ordered that all retail liquor vends with licences in Form L6, L6& L6FG, L8, L10 and L8 & L14 operating in Delhi will be completely closed on October 9 and October 10, the order said. However, hotels, clubs, bars and restaurants holding valid excise licences to serve liquor will not be affected by the order and can continue to operate. The move comes ahead of a planned October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar by CJP, and opposition parties seeking Gyanesh Kumars resignation over allegations of vote theft. Several student and farmer organisations, along with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), are expected to participate in the protest. The CJP has also issued a call for the gathering. The Delhi Police has stepped up security arrangements across the capital in anticipation of the protest. More than 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed, according to a senior police officer. Permission hads not yet been granted for any protest at Jantar Mantar. The heightened security comes after violence during a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Police sources said the Delhi government was requested to close liquor shops as a precautionary step to reduce the possibility of an untoward incident during the upcoming demonstrations. Delhi government was requested for closure of liquor shops as a precautionary measure to prevent any untoward incident, a police source said. During the July 20 protest, several police personnel and demonstrators were injured, while public property was damaged and government buildings were allegedly defaced. The Crime Branch of the Delhi Police has since registered an FIR and reopened its investigation into the violence and what it described as a possible larger conspiracy linked to the protest. The latest security measures come as political tensions in Delhi have intensified over demands for Kumar's resignation. The Congress, Left parties and AAP have continued protests alleging irregularities in the electoral process and demanding that the Chief Election Commissioner step down. Large numbers of opposition leaders and supporters participated in demonstrations over the past two days. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Vadra, along with several other MPs, were detained by police during the protests on both days and subsequently released. Rahul Gandhi has said the protests will continue until Gyanesh Kumar steps down as Chief Election Commissioner. With another major demonstration planned for October 10, authorities have increased security across the capital and taken preventive measures, including the temporary closure of retail liquor outlets.

headline: India aims to be self-reliant in shipping and shipbuilding by 2047: Sonowal
content: Subhash Narayan India aims to handle its entire export-import trade using Indian-flagged and domestically built ships by 2047 as part of plans to cut reliance on foreign shipping and become a major global maritime power, Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said on Wednesday. Speaking at the third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue in New Delhi, Sonowal said the governments Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 outlines a self-reliant maritime ecosystem across ports, shipping, shipbuilding, ship repair, maritime education, and skills. India wants to become self-reliant for shipbuilding, Sonowal said, adding that the long-term objective is to build sufficient domestic capacity to meet the countrys shipping requirements and reduce dependence on foreign-flagged vessels. India is targeting a port cargo-handling capacity of 10,000 million tonnes by 2047, a substantial expansion from current levels, as it seeks to position itself as a global maritime hub. Quick answers to key questions 1What is India's shipping and shipbuilding goal for 2047? India aims to handle its entire export-import trade using Indian-flagged, domestically built ships by 2047. It also wants to become self-reliant across its maritime sector and rank among the worlds top five shipbuilding nations. 2Why is India expanding domestic shipbuilding? Building domestic capacity is intended to reduce reliance on foreign-flagged vessels and meet Indias own shipping requirements. The government also wants Indian shipyards to compete for international orders. 3How is India developing its maritime ecosystem? The plans include expanding shipbuilding and repair infrastructure, improving ports and cargo handling, and strengthening maritime education and training. These efforts are intended to support a skilled workforce and a larger domestic shipping capacity. 4How does green shipping support India's maritime ambitions? India and European partners are exploring a green shipping corridor, with India seen as having potential to supply green fuels such as green ammonia and methanol. Ports would also need infrastructure to store, handle and export these fuels. The minister said the government was developing an ecosystem that would enable Indian shipyards to compete for international orders. Cochin Shipyard, for instance, has received shipbuilding orders from countries including Germany, the US and Norway, he said. Sonowal said India also wants to become one of the worlds top five shipbuilding nations. The government is expanding shipbuilding and repair infrastructure and strengthening maritime education and training to create the skilled workforce required to support the industry. India is already the worlds second-largest supplier of seafarers, with the number of Indian seafarers rising from around 170,000 to more than 323,000, Sonowal said. The country also accounts for more than 36% of global ship recycling, he added. The minister said improvements in port infrastructure and cargo-handling systems had reduced container turnaround time from more than 35 hours earlier to about 23 hours. About 95% of Indias trade by volume is transported by sea, making maritime infrastructure critical to the countrys external trade. The minister also disclosed the extent of the human cost of the ongoing maritime security crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, suggesting that 11 Indian seafarers have so far lost their lives amid attacks and incidents involving commercial vessels. Sonowal said there had been four incidents involving Indian-flagged ships, while 74 incidents involved foreign-flagged vessels bound for India and carrying Indian seafarers. The government has evacuated more than 4,000 Indian seafarers from the affected region, he said. It is also maintaining vessel-level monitoring and staying in contact with seafarers and their families through its maritime security and coordination mechanisms. The government had previously said it was tracking Indian seafarers irrespective of their vessels flag. The latest figures cited by Sonowal indicate that the security challenge extends well beyond Indian-flagged vessels, given the large number of Indian seafarers employed on foreign-flagged ships. India has the worlds second-largest maritime workforce, making the safety of its seafarers an important component of the countrys maritime policy. Sonowal said India was also using Sagarmanthan to deepen bilateral maritime cooperation. Discussions were held with delegations from Belgium, Myanmar, Lithuania and Bhutan, among other countries. Belgium has expressed interest in working with India on green shipping and related maritime initiatives, he said. Discussions with Saudi Arabia are also progressing towards institutional mechanisms for cooperation, including in the energy sector. Bhutan, meanwhile, is interested in using Indias river ports and inland waterways to move its export cargo, Sonowal said. India is developing a network of river ports and inland-waterway infrastructure that could provide neighbouring landlocked countries with access to maritime trade routes. The minister said Indias maritime infrastructure should not only serve domestic cargo but also provide neighbouring countries with efficient access to international markets. The third edition of Sagarmanthan has attracted participation from more than 70 countries, including ministers, maritime industry representatives and international experts. Sonowal said the growing participation demonstrated the increasing importance of the dialogue as a platform for cooperation on shipping, shipbuilding, ports, maritime security and the wider ocean economy. The governments long-term maritime strategy, he said, is aimed at combining higher port capacity with domestic shipbuilding, a larger Indian-flagged fleet, skilled manpower and stronger regional connectivity to make India a self-reliant maritime economy by 2047.

headline: Air India Flight Changes Course Midway, Returns To Delhi After Houthi Strike On Riyadh Airport
content: Riyadh flight turned back midway after reports of a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, with Riyadh flights suspended until October 10. An Air India flight travelling from Delhi to Riyadh turned back midway on Thursday after reports of a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabias capital, prompting Air India and Air India Express to suspend flights to and from Riyadh until October 10. The development came as several explosions were heard across Riyadh, including a blast near King Khalid International Airport. - Loud Explosions Heard In Riyadh, Houthis Claim They Fired Missile At Airport - Riyadh Airport Targeted By Houthi Missile: Air India Express, Akasa Air Cancel Flights - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive Yemens Iran-backed Houthis later claimed they had targeted the airport with a ballistic missile, while Saudi Arabia said its forces intercepted missiles fired towards the capital. Delhi-Riyadh Flight Turns Back The Air India flight, AI2243, had taken off from Delhi and was flying towards Riyadh when the aircraft was turned around and began its journey back to the Indian capital. The decision came amid heightened concerns over the security situation around Riyadh and its airport. Flight-tracking data lists AI2243 as a Delhi-Riyadh service scheduled on Thursday. The turnaround followed reports of explosions in Riyadh and the Houthi claim that it had launched a ballistic missile at King Khalid International Airport. Air India, Air India Express Suspend Riyadh Operations Following the incident, Air India and Air India Express suspended their operations to and from Riyadh until October 10. The airlines are taking the precautionary step amid the rapidly changing security situation in and around the Saudi capital. The suspension is expected to affect passengers travelling between India and Riyadh during the period. The move comes after the airlines Delhi-Riyadh service was forced to turn back while en route to Saudi Arabia. Houthis Claim Attack On Riyadh Airport The Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for the latest attack, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile. The Houthis claimed the missile had hit its target. However, there was no immediate independent confirmation of the claim. Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said coalition forces had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh. He also said another ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait, in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemen border, had been destroyed. Airport Advises Passengers To Check Flight Status King Khalid International Airport advised passengers to contact their airlines and check their flight status before travelling to the airport. The advisory came after multiple explosions were heard over Riyadh. A witness told The Associated Press that smoke was visible and fire and ambulance crews had been deployed in the area. Outgoing flights were also halted, with passengers reportedly asked to leave their checked-in luggage and evacuate the airport. Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said the airport had closed again" on Thursday, reporting that the last landing had taken place more than 80 minutes earlier. Fresh Attacks Add To Saudi Security Concerns The latest incident follows attacks on Saudi airports earlier this week. Saudi authorities said King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport were targeted on October 6 and 7. Three people were killed and 36 injured across the two attacks, according to Saudi officials. One person was killed and eight injured in the Riyadh attack, while two people were killed and 28 wounded at Abha. The latest escalation has also disrupted air travel and raised fresh concerns for airlines operating in the region. An Air India flight traveling from Delhi to Riyadh turned back after reports of a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabias capital and explosions near King Khalid International Airport.

headline: Singapore's Air Quality 'Worst In World': Indonesian Farm Fires Shut Schools, F1 Grand Prix Faces Threat
content: F1 organisers confirm they are closely monitoring the situation, though current operational plans remain unchanged Singapores air quality has plunged to the worst level in the world" as thick, toxic transboundary haze swept across southern Southeast Asia. Driven by agricultural land-clearing fires in Indonesia, atmospheric pollution spiked into the very unhealthy" range according to real-time global monitoring data, placing the city-state above notoriously polluted global capitals. The environmental crisis has disrupted daily life across the region, triggering school closures in neighbouring Malaysia and raising serious health and logistical concerns ahead of high-profile international sporting events in Singapore. - China, Russia, Japan, South Korea: Why Schools Are Closing Across Several Countries - Asian Games 2026, Day 13 Wrap: India Win Five Medals; Men's Hockey & Cricket Teams Reach Finals - France Student Unrest Turns Violent: 700+ Police Injured As Trump Blames Migration, Islam | News18 - Opinion | From Ground Zero: Why Drug-Free Bharat Is An Imperative School Closures and Health Warnings in Malaysia Across the border in Malaysia, worsening air quality forced authorities to mandate immediate closures for roughly 200 schools, kindergartens, and daycare centres in Batu Pahat, located in the southern state of Johor. With Kuala Lumpur ranking as the second most polluted city globally during the peak of the surge, health officials advised residents to wear protective masks and limit outdoor activities. The Malaysian government warned that additional regional closures could follow if fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations remain elevated. Dry weather conditions expected to persist across the region threaten to prolong the crisis. Formula One Threat and Diplomatic Friction The sudden deterioration in air quality comes at an exceptionally sensitive time for Singapore, which is preparing to host its annual Formula One Grand Prix weekend. Race organisers confirmed they are closely monitoring visibility and health indicators in coordination with government agencies, though current operational plans remain unchanged. Singapores air quality plunged to the "worst level in the world" due to transboundary haze. Agricultural land-clearing fires in Indonesia drove the atmospheric pollution spike. Roughly 200 schools, kindergartens, and daycare centres in Batu Pahat, Malaysia, were closed. Kuala Lumpur ranked as the second most polluted city globally during the surge. Singapore is preparing to host its annual Formula One Grand Prix weekend amid the haze. The recurring haze crisis has reignited diplomatic tensions over land-clearing practices and agricultural burning in Indonesia. Dry, warm weather patterns have intensified fire hotspots across Sumatra and Kalimantan, sending dense plumes of smoke northeast over the Malacca Strait. Agricultural land-clearing and forest fires in Indonesia sent dense plumes of smoke across the Malacca Strait, causing severe transboundary haze in Singapore and Malaysia.

headline: After speculation over political appointees, government to send senior career officer to Kathmandu
content: The governments decision to forward the name of Sudhakar Dalela, one of the most senior officers in the diplomatic service, as Ambassador to Nepal is an indication of the importance of the India-Nepal relationship, as well as the delicate situation the relationship is in at present. Sources confirmed to The Hindu that the agreement or proposal for Mr. Dalela was forwarded to Kathmandu on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) and is expected to be approved soon by the Balen Shah government. Mr. Dalela, the Secretary (Economic Relations) not only has experience at managing ties with the neighbourhood from the Centre, in both the Ministry of External Affairs and the Prime Ministers Office, but also from the ground, where he was Indias previous Ambassador to Bhutan. He also has a higher rank than former Ambassadors to Kathmandu, who were at Additional Secretary rank. More than the qualifications, the governments move suggests a change in thinking, favouring diplomatic experience over political flair. Speaking at the 11th Heads of Missions conference in April this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had, according to sources present, expressed his disappointment at the slow reaction time of missions in the neighbourhood to a series of political developments, indicating the street protests and government changes in Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Maldives in recent years. Pointing to Indias then newly appointed High Commissioner to Bangladesh, former Minister Dinesh Trivedi in the audience, Mr. Modi had said that the government would henceforth prefer Anubhavi (seasoned or experienced) diplomats in the neighbourhood- leading many to speculate that the government would also send a politician to Nepal when the term of the outgoing Ambassador Naveen Srivastava ended. In particular, the government is understood to have worried that the new Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah, known for his unorthodox style, would not deal as well with a professional diplomat. In his first few weeks in office, Mr. Shah declined to meet the Ambassadors of India and China, representatives of the two most important relationships, except in a larger group, and also would not confirm a meeting with the Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, who subsequently put off his visit. In the run-up to the decision on Indian envoy, media reports in Delhi and Kathmandu had floated the names of several senior BJP leaders, particularly from Nepal- neighbouring states Bihar and Uttar Pradesh for the position. However, since that time, relations with Bangladesh have taken a turn for the worse, and the last-minute cancellation of the visit of Bangladesh Prime Minister Tariq Rahman in August this year is being ascribed to miscommunication between the political appointee and the more protocol-bound MEA officials. As New Delhi plans for a possible visit by Mr. Rahman in November, it is also hoping to host Nepal PM Shah in November-end, and appears to have decided on a sure pair of hands rather than defying convention again. Traditionally, atleast for the past three decades, only professional diplomats have been posted as heads of missions in Indias neighbouring countries, explained Vivek Katju, former Indian Ambassador to Afghanistan, Myanmar and Thailand. These are very sensitive posts and they require quiet and deft handling which only a career diplomat can usually bring, he said. Mr. Dalela, a soft-spoken 1993-batch officer who has served as the Secretary (Economic Relations) since September 2025, was most recently in the news for his role as Sherpa and for forging a joint declaration at the BRICS Summit despite differences within the grouping over the Iran war. During his posting as Ambassador in Thimphu (2022-2025), he was instrumental in pitching for Bhutans Gelephu Mindfulness City project (GMC), often travelling to India with the Bhutanese leadership to discuss investments for the project. He also managed differences over Bhutans border talks with China, hydropower pricing issues, and Bhutans moves to curb low-end mass tourism from India. He has considerable experience at the MEAs North desk, for Bhutan and Nepal ties, first as Director (North) (2006-7), and then as Joint Secretary (North) (2016-19) and would be the first time an officer with as much experience on the desk will also have helmed the embassies in Thimphu and Kathmandu. Interspersed with Mr. Dalelas neighbourhood experience have been three stints in the U.S., including as Consul General in Chicago and two postings at the Embassy in Washington, where he was the Deputy Chief of Mission. In addition, he has worked twice at Indias mission to the World Trade Organisation and ran the Trade policy desk at the Commerce Ministry earlier.

headline: Riyadh Airport Targeted By Houthi Missile: Air India Express, Akasa Air Cancel Flights
content: Air India Express and Akasa Air cancelled Riyadh flights after explosions were heard over the Saudi capital and Houthis claimed a missile attack on the airport. Air India Express and Akasa Air on Thursday cancelled flights to and from Riyadh as the security situation in Saudi Arabias capital deteriorated following explosions near King Khalid International Airport. The cancellations came after Yemens Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed they had targeted the Riyadh airport with a ballistic missile. - Loud Explosions Heard In Riyadh, Houthis Claim They Fired Missile At Airport - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive - From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis, meanwhile, said it had intercepted two missiles launched towards the capital. There was no immediate independent confirmation of the Houthi claim. Air India Express Suspends Riyadh Flights Air India Express said it had cancelled flights to and from Riyadh until October 10, citing the evolving situation in the region". The airline said passengers affected by the cancellations would be offered complimentary rescheduling or a full refund if they opted to cancel their bookings. The decision comes as flight operations at King Khalid International Airport face fresh disruption following the latest security incident. Akasa Air Cancels Kochi-Riyadh Services Akasa Air also cancelled its QP 523 Kochi-Riyadh and QP 524 Riyadh-Kochi flights scheduled for October 8. The airline said passengers affected by the cancellations could either opt for a full refund or reschedule their travel at no additional cost. Akasa Air said it was monitoring the situation in real time and would inform passengers about any further changes. It also said the safety and wellbeing of passengers and crew remained its highest priority. Riyadh Airport Advises Passengers To Check Flight Status King Khalid International Airport asked passengers to contact their respective airlines and check their flight status before travelling to the airport. The advisory came after multiple explosions were heard across Riyadh on Thursday, with a major blast reported in the vicinity of the airport. A witness told The Associated Press that flights were halted and passengers were asked to evacuate the airport. The airport said in a statement posted on X: We would like to inform passengers of the necessity to contact their airlines directly and check their flight status before proceeding to the airport." Houthis Claim Ballistic Missile Attack Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport around midday with a ballistic missile, claiming that it had hit its target". The Saudi-led coalition, however, said its forces intercepted two missiles fired towards Riyadh. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed that a Houthi missile struck the airport. The latest incident follows a series of Houthi attacks on Saudi airports this week. Saudi authorities said attacks on King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport had killed three people and injured 36 others. Riyadh Airport Already Facing Major Disruptions The latest attack has added to existing disruption at King Khalid International Airport. According to The National, dozens of departures were affected on Thursday, with 58 flights delayed and 11 cancelled at one point. The situation has also raised wider concerns for international airlines operating through Saudi airspace as the conflict between the Houthis and Saudi-led forces intensifies. Air India Express cancelled its flights to and from Riyadh until October 10 due to the evolving regional situation, offering affected passengers complimentary rescheduling or full refunds. Additionally, Akasa Air cancelled its Kochi-Riyadh and Riyadh-Kochi services scheduled for October 8, providing similar options for refunds or free rescheduling.

headline: Houthis claim new attack against airport in Saudi capital Riyadh as witness reports evacuation
content: Several explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh on Thursday (October 8, 2026), including a large blast at the city's international airport, a witness told The Associated Press, a day after the kingdom said an attack on the airport killed one person and wounded others. headline: Geopolitics, China, and AI to test India's 2047 ambitions: CEA Nageswaran
content: The global order is increasingly characterised by power and bargaining rather than rules, requiring India to negotiate from a position of strength and build coalitions it can help influence, the governments top economic adviser said, identifying five factors that would test the countrys ambition of becoming a developed economy by 2047. These five long-term shifts, including geopolitical realignment, strategic supply-chain chokepoints, Chinas manufacturing scale, climate variability, and the interplay between demography and artificial intelligence (AI), will shape India's path to becoming a rich nation by the centenary of its independence, Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) V. Anantha Nageswaran said on Thursday. Speaking at the India Investment Seminar 2026 in Mumbai, Nageswaran said these shifts would make Indias climb harder than it was for earlier latecomers, but were reasons to move faster, not to slow down. On strategic chokepoints, Nageswaran's presentation identified energy, chips, rare earths, fertilisers and sea-lanes as potential sources of leverage, arguing that India needs buffers and redundancy because such redundancy should be viewed as insurance rather than waste, according to a press release issued by SBI Funds Management Ltd, one of the organisers of the seminar. He also highlighted the scale of Chinas manufacturing sector, noting that the country accounts for close to a third of global manufacturing and that surplus capacity can be exported cheaply. For India, the answer is to compete on capability and depth rather than cost alone, the presentation said. Climate change was identified not merely as a warming problem but as one involving greater variability in monsoons and heat, with implications for insurance. The presentation said India would need to adapt domestically while contesting measures such as carbon border taxes abroad. The fifth shift concerns demography and AI. With the workforce expected to peak as machines arrive, the presentation said India cannot rely indefinitely on the traditional cheap-labour route and needs to convert its demographic numbers into skills, making skilling part of industrial policy. Nageswarans remarks came at a two-day seminar organised by SBI Funds Management Ltd and Europe's asset management company Amundi, which brought together more than 100 international institutional investors and Amundi clients to discuss Indias growth and investment opportunities. The opening day focused on Indias ambition of becoming a developed economy by 2047, with Nageswaran highlighting structural reforms, productivity and capability building as important to sustaining long-term growth. State Bank of India (SBI) chairman C.S. Setty said Indias financial system has a role in supporting growth and financial inclusion through digital public infrastructure and by expanding access to credit, insurance and investment products. He highlighted SBIs subsidiaries across banking and financial services, including SBI Funds Management, SBI Life Insurance and SBI Card. Former G20 Sherpa Amitabh Kant discussed Indias manufacturing opportunity amid changing global supply chains, while Rahul Bharti of Maruti Suzuki spoke about the companys four-decade journey and long-term international partnerships. Dipesh Shah, executive director at the International Financial Services Centres Authority, said India was emerging as a global investment platform, with GIFT IFSC creating an internationally competitive ecosystem for global investors and institutions to access India and manage India-focused assets. SBI Funds Management managing director and chief executive officer (MD &CEO) Debasish Mishra said opportunities were expanding across manufacturing, infrastructure, technology and financial markets, while Amundi deputy CEO Olivier Marie said Indias economic transformation presented significant opportunities for long-term

headline: Traffic cop & grocery shop employee held over guest worker's death in Chennai
content: Police on Thursday arrested a traffic police constable and a 26-year-old man in connection with the death of a 24-year-old guest worker near Sriperumbudur on Wednesday. The case was initially registered as a suspicious death but was altered to culpable homicide not amounting to murder after a postmortem revealed internal injuries.The deceased, Sailesh Kumar, a native of Ghazipur district in Uttar Pradesh, arrived at Sriperumbudur Sipcot on Oct 5 along with eight others in search of work. They secured jobs at a canteen and rented a house owned by S Gnanamoorthy, 33, a constable attached to the Guduvanchery traffic wing. A grocery shop operated from the front portion of the house, where A Arif, 26, worked, while another portion was rented out to guest workers.Police said Sailesh, who was drunk, repeatedly asked Arif for gutka on Tuesday night. An argument broke out after Arif refused to sell it, following which Sailesh and three of his coworkers manhandled him.Arif complained to Gnanamoorthy, and the two allegedly assaulted Sailesh and forced the workers to vacate the premises. A company supervisor later arrived and took them away. Though Sailesh left the premises, he was found dead in the rented portion of the house on Wednesday morning. Sriperumbudur police initially registered a suspicious death case and sent the body to Kancheepuram Govt Hospital for postmortem.The autopsy revealed a liver injury and internal haemorrhage. Police said the findings established that the injuries sustained during the assault had led to his death. Based on the findings, police altered the case to culpable homicide not amounting to murder and arrested Gnanamoorthy and Arif on Thursday.
