headline: Pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia? What we know so far
content: The death of a laboratory worker in Siberia on October 2, 2026, and the subsequent quarantine of dozens of people have sparked concerns about a pneumonic plague epidemic, with Russia revealing little information publicly. The incident has revived memories of the COVID-19 pandemic and allegations that the coronavirus may have emerged at a Chinese lab. What happened at the Siberia lab? The 28-year-old woman, Darya Shipilova, employed at a research institute in Siberia, fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people and dispatch the head of Russias health watchdog to the Irkutsk region. The woman worked at the anti-plague research institute in the city of Irkutsk, where the plague occurs naturally in wild animals. She died at a hospital in nearby Shelekhov that the mayor said had been placed under quarantine. Following the incident, top Russian health officials have travelled to the region. Russian authorities say the lab worker died of what initially presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection. Russia dismisses epidemic concerns Meanwhile, Russias health regulator insists there were no risks of an epidemic breaking out in Siberia after the plague institute workers death. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias health watchdog, said on October 7 that it was winding down precautionary measures it had put in place after concluding there was no risk of an epidemic. No cases of plague had been detected among anyone who had come into contact with the deceased worker, it said, while adding that 90% of those placed in quarantine had been released after nearly 5,000 lab tests had failed to detect any dangerous pathogens. When asked about a second person in Siberia allegedly falling ill, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged caution against using media reports as a reference for what was happening. Causative agent behind death not known A top official with the World Health Organisation (WHO) said it doesnt know how the lab worker in Siberia died. Maria Van Kerkhove, WHO director of Epidemic and Pandemic Management, said the UN health agency doesnt know what the causative agent was behind the womans October 2 death. She has urged Russia to provide more information about the incident that prompted global concerns about suspected pneumonic plague. The WHO initially said it estimated the risk of the Russia case to the public as low, but told a press conference on October 7 it could not make a fuller risk assessment due to insufficient information from the Russian authorities. What is pneumonic plague, symptoms Reports blamed the womans death on pneumonic plague a less common but severe form of plague that can spread from person to person. Pneumonic plague causes a severe form of pneumonia, but recovery rates are high if it is detected and treated in time. The severe disease is less common than the better-known bubonic plague linked to the Black Death in the Middle Ages. Pneumonic plague and bubonic plague are caused by the same bacteria. The former is spread by respiratory particles while the latter is spread through bites from fleas that have jumped from infected rodents. Symptoms of pneumonic plague include shortness of breath and coughing-up blood, and they can occur in as little as 24 hours after exposure, according to the WHO. If untreated, the illness can be fatal. Not linked to a biological weapon U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (October 8) that the death of the Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon. Mr. Trump said Russia insisted it had the situation under control, but added that not much information was coming out. He, however, said that the United States will help Russia over the incident. The European Union has also called on Russia to share timely and transparent reporting about the death of the plague laboratory technician. (With inputs from Reuters, AP, AFP)

headline: US Lost 81 Aircraft Including F-35s, F-15Es In Iran War; Tehran Mocks 'Real Toll Is Far Higher'
content: Aircraft loss list includes some of the US Air Forces most advanced aircraft, among them an F-35A Lightning II stealth fighter and 12 F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets. The US military has lost or suffered damage to at least 81 aircraft since the war with Iran began, with the cost of replacing lost equipment estimated at up to $3.3 billion, according to a Congressional Research Service (CRS) report. The list includes some of the US Air Forces most advanced aircraft, among them an F-35A Lightning II stealth fighter and 12 F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets that were either destroyed or damaged during the conflict. - Trump Pulling Back From Iran? Why Military, Oil, Political Pressures Could Be Making The US Rethink - No Military Solution: Iran Warns Of Stronger Response, Keeps Door Open To Talks - 'They'll Be Hit Very Hard': Trump Warns Iran With Fresh Strikes If Linked To Flydubai Attack - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes F-35, F-15Es among aircraft losses Three F-15Es were destroyed in a friendly-fire incident over Kuwait on March 2, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM). Another F-15E was reported destroyed over Iran on April 5. Each F-15E costs more than $30 million. Eight other F-15Es sustained minor damage when Iran carried out airstrikes on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on September 9 and 10. The CRS report said those aircraft were subsequently returned to service. The largest number of losses, however, involved MQ-9 Reaper drones. At least 45 Reapers have been lost, with each unmanned aircraft estimated to cost between $30 million and $50 million. The US military uses the MQ-9 Reaper for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance operations, as well as missile strikes. The US military lost or damaged at least 81 aircraft since the war with Iran began. The cost of replacing lost equipment is estimated at up to $3.3 billion. The losses include an F-35A Lightning II and 12 F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets. At least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones have been lost. Each F-15E costs more than $30 million, and each MQ-9 Reaper costs between $30 million and $50 million. Losses could cost up to $3.3 billion The CRS report, titled U.S. Aircraft Combat Losses in Operation Epic Fury: Considerations for Congress, said the United States, in coordination with Israel, began military operations against Iran on February 28, 2026, initially under the designation Operation Epic Fury. The conflict has since involved air, maritime and missile engagements across the Middle East. Combat activity slowed during an April ceasefire before some strikes resumed within weeks. The report said the Department of Defense, which is using a secondary Department of War designation" under Executive Order 14347 dated September 5, 2025, published a Lead Inspector General report to Congress on September 14. It assessed certain equipment losses from operations against Iran between April 1 and June 30. According to the CRS, analysts and Department of Defense officials have offered different estimates for replacing equipment lost during the conflict. The Congressional Budget Office estimated in September that equipment losses could cost between $1.9 billion and $3.3 billion, depending on the Pentagons replacement plans. The CRS listed 81 fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft, including uncrewed aircraft systems, as reportedly lost or damaged in US operations against Iran since February 28. Its figures were compiled using news reports and statements from the Department of Defense, CENTCOM and the Department of Defense Inspector General, which was designated the Lead Inspector General for Operation Epic Fury. The CRS cautioned that the number could change because of factors including classification, continuing combat operations and attribution. It also noted that some damaged aircraft may have returned to active service. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reacted to the figures in a post on X, claiming the actual US losses were higher. In May, the Congressional Research Service admitted that Irans Armed Forces had taken out 42 U.S. military aircraft. Now: 81. Real toll is far higher," Araghchi said. He further claimed that CENTCOM would not allow a sitting senator to inspect bases it says are undamaged, adding: You can fool all the people some of the time" US-Iran tensions The disclosure comes as tensions across the Middle East remain high amid the fallout from the wider US-Iran conflict. Fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia, continuing violence in Gaza and questions over the security of US troops have added to concerns across the region. A Congressional Research Service report stated that the US military has lost or suffered damage to at least 81 aircraft since the war with Iran began on February 28, 2026, with replacement costs estimated at up to $3.3 billion.

headline: Section 163 In Force, Heavy Security Deployed: How Delhi Police Is Preparing For Oct 10 CJP Protest
content: Delhi Police has stepped up security ahead of the CJPs October 10 protest, tracking around 2,800 people and monitoring possible routes and transport arrangements. Delhi Police is stepping up security ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) proposed protest on October 10, with additional forces being deployed and tighter surveillance planned across the capital. As part of the security preparations, police stations across Delhi have been asked to keep track of around 2,800 people identified through the facial recognition system (FRS) as having alleged criminal antecedents. Officials said police will monitor whether any of these individuals are travelling towards the New Delhi district in the run-up to the proposed demonstration. - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - 'Absolutely Shocking': Kejriwal Hits Out At Delhi Police For Detaining AAP Leaders At Delhi Protest - Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use - CJP Oct 10 Protest: Delhi Police Step Up Vigil, Track 2,800 'Criminals', Monitor Buses, Borders The police are also monitoring transport arrangements and possible entry routes to identify any organised movement of protesters towards the capital. The force is also going back to the logistics of the CJPs earlier protest. Officers have been asked to identify bus operators and other suppliers who helped arrange transport and resources during the previous agitation and check whether they have been contacted again. Police Monitoring Buses, Entry Routes Local police have been told to check bus bookings, including who is hiring the vehicles, how many people are being transported and where they are headed. Officials said particular attention is being paid to organised movement towards Delhi and the New Delhi district. Entry points, especially the eastern and Shahdara borders with Uttar Pradesh and routes towards southwest Delhi from Rajasthan, are also under heightened surveillance. Delhi Police is increasing security for the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) proposed protest on October 10. Police are tracking 2,800 people identified via facial recognition as having alleged criminal antecedents. Nearly 4,000 security personnel have been deployed across the New Delhi area. Section 163 is in force, meaning protests are not permitted without permission. Female police personnel will handle female protesters, and male personnel will handle male protesters. Barricades will be installed at entry points," an officer said. | On preparedness for the October 10 CJP protest, Delhi Police DCP Shrishti Pandey says, We are well prepared; the necessary forces are deployed here. We are highly motivated, and all our resources and preparations are in place. I urge the general public not to get swayed by any negative influence into joining such illegal protests, andif involvednot to engage in any illegal activities. Do not destroy public property or attack police personnel. This protest is illegal; it has not been allowed. I request everyone to refrain from participating in this protest." ANI (@ANI) October 8, 2026 Police are also preparing for the possibility of large crowds reaching the capital despite the proposed protest not receiving permission. Around 4,000 Personnel Deployed Since October 1, Delhi Police has requisitioned at least 20 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF), which have been deployed around Jantar Mantar and other parts of central Delhi. Nearly 4,000 security personnel have been deployed across the New Delhi area, while several stretches around the protest site have been restricted. Officials are also considering temporary detention facilities at stadiums across Delhi in case a large number of protesters arrive, refuse to disperse and insist on courting arrest. Police have further directed personnel to prevent protesters from turning other locations into makeshift demonstration sites if they are stopped from reaching Jantar Mantar. Police Ask Colleges, PG Owners To Keep Watch Delhi Police has also reached out to educational institutions as part of its preparations. Station house officers have been asked to contact university and college heads and request them to ensure that students do not participate in the protest. Owners of paying guest accommodations in major student areas have similarly been asked to discourage students from joining the demonstration. Section 163 In Force DCP Shrishti Pandey said Section 163 is currently in force, meaning protests are not permitted at Jantar Mantar or elsewhere without the required permission. Section 163 is in effect, meaning protests are not permittedneither at Jantar Mantar nor anywhere else. Any gathering will be considered illegal, and we would be compelled to take necessary legal action against it," Pandey said. She urged people to prioritise their own safety and warned that participation in an illegal gathering could have long-term legal consequences. Pandey also said police were prepared for the October 10 protest and urged the public not to be influenced by calls for an unauthorised demonstration. Female Protesters To Be Handled By Women Personnel Addressing concerns over the treatment of women protesters, Pandey said Delhi Police has strict guidelines for handling demonstrators. She said female police personnel would deal with female protesters, while male personnel would handle male protesters. According to the DCP, officers are briefed about these guidelines before being deployed on the ground. Pandey also rejected allegations of deliberate or unnecessary action against protesters, saying police personnel were present on the ground and would ensure that legal obligations were followed. Police Warn Against AI-Generated Fake Content The DCP also raised concerns over AI-generated photos and videos being circulated on social media during protests. She said people who are not physically present at a protest site can use AI tools to create photographs or videos and potentially influence public opinion. Pandey appealed to people to verify information before believing or sharing it. | On AI-generated photos of police personnel, Delhi Police DCP Shrishti Pandey says, In todays times, using AI tools has become extremely easy. Someone who isnt even in Delhior present at the protest sitecan sit far away, create a video or generate a photo, and influence everyone with it. Therefore, I urge you not to spread such fake or false news or share it on social media. I appeal to the general public to verify any news they read on social media before believing it. The Delhi Police regularly shares information through its social media handles; we are a very transparent force and ensure that any information intended for the public reaches them in a timely manner." ANI (@ANI) October 8, 2026 Delhi Police, she said, regularly shares information through its official social media accounts. Police Say Personnel Are Being Targeted Online Pandey also alleged that police personnel, including female officers and constables, were being deliberately targeted through social media campaigns. She said videos circulating online showed what she described as defamatory campaigns against police personnel and alleged that efforts were being made to influence public opinion against the force. The CJP protest comes months after the outfits July agitation over alleged NEET UG paper leak and examination irregularities, when thousands of protesters attempted to march towards Parliament. Police said 2,873 people who attended or were present at the July protest were identified as having alleged criminal antecedents. Of them, nearly 989 were allegedly linked to heinous offences. Police claimed 101 had been booked in murder cases, including 42 allegedly involved in two or more murder cases and 12 booked in 10 or more murder cases. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das informed Delhi Police on Wednesday about the proposed October 10 protest. However, police have not granted permission for the demonstration so far. Delhi Police has deployed nearly 4,000 security personnel and 20 companies of Central Armed Police Forces across the New Delhi area, while enforcing Section 163. Authorities have established heightened surveillance at border entry points, set up barricades, and instructed local stations to monitor transport arrangements and track around 2,800 individuals with alleged criminal antecedents using facial recognition systems.

We, the Opposition, assure you that action will be taken. They will be brought to justice. This is our guarantee. You will see these four individuals brought to justice," he said. After that, we said that we wanted to go to Jantar Mantar and protest. And yesterday, you saw that we were stopped at Jantar Mantar, and our people were beaten," he said. Earlier, Rahul Gandhi, along with other INDIA alliance MPs, arrived in Connaught Place for the second lunch meeting of Opposition MPs. The leaders are now heading towards Gandhi Smarak for the planned sit-in, while Rahul Gandhi, Kharge and Mamata Banerjee are set to meet President Murmu amid the ongoing protest over the SIR exercise and the demand for Gyanesh Kumars resignation. headline: Brace for more heat: Worst of El Niño yet to come, peak likely in December
content: The ongoing El Nio is set to peak in December and lead to above-average temperatures across large parts of the world in the coming months, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned. The UN body further said that there is an increased risk of droughts and floods given that the normal rainfall patterns would see a shift under the influence of the intensifying El Nio conditions. The October-December months will see El Nio reach its peak and the event will extend well into the 2027 spring of the northern hemisphere. El Nio is a climate pattern marked by unusually warm Pacific waters that disrupts global weather. El Nio is firmly established and strengthening rapidly. WMO forecasts indicate a near-100 per cent likelihood that it will persist through February 2027, potentially being one of the strongest since at least 1950, said Celeste Saulo, WMO Secretary-General, in a statement issued on Thursday. This year, Indias southwest monsoon season ended in a 13 per cent rainfall deficit. The 2026 monsoon was the fourth driest since 2001. El Nio impacted the countrys rainfall during the second half of the season. Many states, including Maharashtra and Karnataka, have declared drought, with Maharashtra imposing a 10 per cent water cut in many of its districts. Likewise, Europe experienced one its hottest summers this year with record-breaking temperatures sweeping France, Spain, and the UK. The arid summer left major rivers, including Danube, Rhine, and Thames, dry. A naturally occurring ocean-atmospheric phenomenon recurring once between two to seven years, the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has three phases: warm (El Nio), neutral and cool (La Nia). The sea temperatures along the equatorial Pacific Ocean, the WMO said, have dramatically risen in recent months thus reflecting the intensifying El Nio event. In August, the temperature in the Nino 3.4 region (which determines the ENSO phase) was 2.5 degree Celsius above normal, WMO officials noted. El Nio is known to suppress rainfall over India and many places, globally, resulting in droughts. It also pushes temperatures to rise significantly above average. El Nio is declared when the sea temperatures recorded along the equatorial and central Pacific Ocean exceeds 0.5 degrees Celsius from normal.

headline: Khalistan Referendum Meets Alberta Independence Vote: Canada Faces New Separatist Challenge | Exclusive
content: based organisation linked to designated terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun by Indian authorities, is holding its own Khalistan referendum-related event A separatist campaign aimed at creating Khalistan in India is now unfolding alongside an entirely different separatist debate inside CanadaAlbertas push for greater autonomy and a possible future vote on leaving the country. The overlap is becoming increasingly visible as Alberta prepares for its October 19 referendum, which includes a question asking voters whether the provincial government should begin the constitutional process required to hold a future binding referendum on separation from Canada. The question itself is non-binding and would not make Alberta independent. - Trump Ditches Taxpayer Funds, Says He'll Fund Midterm Ads With His Own Money After Flak - Vijay Asked Me To Be Brave: TVKs Dharapuram Candidate On Stalin Remarks, Social Media Trolling - Irans Power Plants, Nuclear Sites Among Targets As Trump Weighs Timing For Resuming Major Combat Ops - Ohio Hindu Temple Attacked With Bricks In Presence Of Priests, Devotees; Hate Crime Suspected Against that backdrop, Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), the US-based organisation linked to designated terrorist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun by Indian authorities, is holding its own Khalistan referendum-related event in Edmonton on October 18, according to the information available to News18. The timing and use of similar referendum" terminology have created an unusual political overlap: a Canadian province debating its own future within Canada, and a separatist organisation campaigning for a separate Sikh state in India, both seeking public attention in Alberta. Two Referendums, One Alberta Albertas official ballot contains 10 questions. The separation question asks: Should Alberta remain a province of Canada, or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?" A vote to begin that process would not itself take Alberta out of Canada. It would only set in motion the legal steps towards a separate, binding referendum at a later stage. SFJs campaign, meanwhile, is centred on its long-running demand for an independent Khalistan. The organisation says it is conducting non-binding referendums among Sikh communities in different countries as part of that campaign. The Edmonton event is therefore not a Canadian referendum and has no legal bearing on Albertas constitutional status. But its proximity to the official Alberta vote, combined with the use of similar terminology and public campaigning, creates the possibility of confusion between two entirely separate separatist causes. The Manjinder Singh Link The security concerns surrounding the Khalistan campaign have also become more visible in Alberta. In August, the RCMP issued a duty to warn" notice to Manjinder Singh, an Abbotsford-based Sikh activist involved in the Khalistan campaign, warning him that his life was under a credible, serious and imminent threat. Police did not disclose the nature of the threat or identify those believed to be behind it. Another activist, Inderjeet Singh Gosal of Ontario, also received an RCMP warning. Gosal has served as a Canadian coordinator of the Khalistan referendum campaign. The warnings underline the security dilemma facing Canadian authorities: the state is simultaneously protecting activists involved in a separatist campaign, investigating threats against them and dealing with the wider criminal and extremist networks that have increasingly intersected with the issue. How Did Canada Reach This Point? The Khalistan issue in Canada has for years been a major source of friction between Ottawa and New Delhi. Canada has maintained that activists campaigning for Khalistan are protected by freedom of expression and political rights, while India has designated SFJ and Pannun as terrorist-linked entities and views the Khalistan campaign as a national-security threat. The issue escalated dramatically after the June 2023 killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Surrey, British Columbia. Canada has accused Indian government-linked actors of involvement in criminal activity on Canadian soil. The RCMP has also publicly said its investigations found evidence involving homicides, extortion, organised crime and interference in democratic processes. At the same time, India has repeatedly rejected allegations that its government is involved in such attacks. The result has been a complicated security environment in which separatist activism, organised crime and allegations of foreign interference increasingly overlap. The Gangster Connection Canadian authorities have also been dealing with a separate but related wave of extortion and violence affecting South Asian communities. The RCMP said in 2024 that it had investigated homicides, extortions and other violent crimes and had identified more than a dozen credible and imminent threats that resulted in duty to warn" notifications to members of the South Asian community, particularly those associated with the pro-Khalistan movement. Canadian law enforcement has also investigated alleged links between criminal networks and violence directed at members of the South Asian community. This is where the security challenge becomes considerably more complicated than a simple India-versus-Khalistan dispute. A New Problem For Ottawa? For Canada, the Alberta developments create another layer to an already difficult problem. The countrys security agencies have to distinguish between legitimate political activity protected under Canadian law, extremist activity, foreign interference and ordinary organised crime, even when individuals or networks may overlap. The RCMP has itself described the threat environment as involving both violent extremism and organised crime, while warning that such activity has consequences for public safety. The Alberta episode adds a striking new dimension: separatist politics is no longer confined to the India-Khalistan dispute. It is now unfolding alongside a genuine Canadian debate over provincial autonomy and the possibility of an eventual Alberta independence vote. The two movements are not the same and have no demonstrated organisational connection. But their campaigns are unfolding in the same province, around the same time, with both using the language of referendums and political separation. For Ottawa, that makes the security challenge harder, not easier. Alberta's October 19 referendum includes a non-binding question asking voters if the provincial government should begin the constitutional process required to hold a future binding referendum on separation from Canada, which would not make Alberta independent on its own.

headline: With Elon Musk, It's Not Just About Business: From India To US, There's Politics Involved
content: Musk has increasingly used his enormous personal following, X and the influence that comes with controlling strategically important companies to weigh in on global politics Elon Musks latest comments on Indias Starlink rollout have brought an old question back into focuswhere does the businessman end and the political actor begin? Musk has accused unnamed oligarchs" in India of blocking Starlinks entry into the country to protect a monopolistic chokehold" on consumers. The Indian government, however, rejected the allegation on Thursday, saying Starlink and other satellite internet operators are at broadly the same stage of the regulatory process and that security assessments are still underway. - Baseless, Misconceived: Govt Refutes Elon Musks Oligarch Claim Over Starlinks India Hurdles - 'You Can Guess Who They Are': Musk Claims 'Certain Oligarchs' Blocking Starlink In India - India Defends Starlink Framework Amid Elon Musks Discrimination Claims | SpaceX | News18 - Asked Grok? Trump Reportedly Consulted Musk's AI Chatbot Before Capturing Maduro The immediate dispute is about satellite internet and spectrum. But it also fits a much bigger pattern around Musk. Across the US, Europe, Brazil, Argentina and Ukraine, Musk has increasingly used his enormous personal following, X and the influence that comes with controlling strategically important companies to weigh in on political debates, elections and government decisions. ALSO READ | You Can Guess Who They Are: Musk Claims Certain Oligarchs Blocking Starlink In India The nature of his intervention varies from country to country. Sometimes it is an explicit endorsement of a political party or candidate. At other times, it is a clash with regulators or politicians over how his businesses should operate. And in Ukraine, Starlink has become so important to the war effort that decisions by Musks company have had direct geopolitical and military implications. So, is it simply a billionaire expressing his political opinions? Or does Musk represent something differenta businessman whose commercial interests and political influence increasingly overlap? Heres looking at some key examples: INDIA: Starlink, Oligarchs And A Fight Over Market Access The latest controversy began after Musk accused unnamed Indian oligarchs" of blocking Starlinks entry into India in order to preserve their market dominance. Indias telecom ministry rejected the suggestion, saying the regulatory framework was neither unfair nor discriminatory. It added that three companies have received initial approvals, but remain subject to spectrum allocation and security clearances. The stakes are significant. India is potentially one of Starlinks largest markets, with Deloitte estimating that the countrys satellite broadband market could reach $1.9 billion by 2030. The dispute therefore sits at the intersection of Musks commercial interests and government policy. It is also not Musks first disagreement with Indian telecom players over how satellite spectrum should be allocated. The companies later reached separate arrangements involving Starlink equipment, but regulatory and security questions have remained. The India episode is therefore a particularly clear example of how a business battle can quickly become a political argument, especially when the businessman has Musks global platform. GERMANY: An Open Political Endorsement Musks intervention in Germany went much further than a regulatory dispute. Ahead of Germanys 2025 federal election, Musk openly endorsed the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), saying that only the party could save Germany". He subsequently hosted AfD co-leader Alice Weidel in a live conversation on X and urged Germans to vote for the party. The intervention triggered accusations of election interference from German politicians. Then-Chancellor Olaf Scholz said Germanys political future should not be decided by the owners of social media platforms. French President Emmanuel Macron too questioned the influence of tech billionaires over European elections, saying: Who could have imagined, 10 years ago, that the owner of one of the worlds largest social networks would intervene directly in elections, including in Germany?" UK: From Keir Starmer To Reform UK Musk also became deeply involved in British politics. He repeatedly attacked then Prime Minister Keir Starmer, including over the handling of historical grooming-gang cases. He also called for the release of far-right activist Tommy Robinson and expressed support for Reform UK. At one point, Musk appeared to be considering substantial financial support for Reform UK, although his relationship with party leader Nigel Farage subsequently soured. Musk later said Farage doesnt have what it takes" to lead the party. Again, the important point is not simply that Musk had political opinions. His interventions were taking place on X, the social media platform he owns, while he was also publicly trying to influence the direction of British politics. BRAZIL: When Musks Platform Collided With The State Brazil provides a different version of the same story. Musk became embroiled in a major confrontation with Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes over orders to block accounts accused of spreading misinformation and hate speech. Musk accused Moraes of violating Brazils constitution and called for him to be removed, calling him an utter disgrace to justice." X initially resisted the courts orders, and Brazil ultimately blocked access to the platform in August 2024. After months of confrontation, X eventually complied with the courts demands, blocked accounts under investigation and sought to have the ban lifted. This was not an election endorsement in the German sense. It was a battle over regulation, free speech and the authority of a national government over a platform owned by one of the worlds most powerful businessmen. But the political consequences were impossible to separate from Musks business interests: X wanted to continue operating in one of its largest markets. UKRAINE: When A Business Decision Becomes A Geopolitical Decision Ukraine is perhaps the most striking example of the unusual power Musks businesses can wield. After Russias full-scale invasion in 2022, SpaceXs Starlink satellite network became critical to Ukraines communications infrastructure. Ukrainian soldiers and commanders have relied on the system for battlefield communications and drone operations. Without Starlink, the Ukrainian lines would collapse", Musk was reported as saying. That meant decisions made by a private company could have consequences on a battlefield. Musks position on how Starlink should be used in the war has repeatedly attracted attention. He has restricted Starlinks use inside Russia, while Ukrainian officials have sought greater access for operations beyond Ukrainian territory. The relationship has even spilled into Ukrainian domestic politics. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said a misunderstanding over SpaceXs position on the use of Starlink contributed to tensions involving then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov. In August 2026, Zelenskyy awarded Musk Ukraines Order of Freedom, one of the countrys highest honours, recognising his contribution during the war. At the same time, Kyiv remains dependent on a system it does not control. That is a different kind of political power: not persuading voters, but controlling infrastructure that governments and militaries have come to depend on. ARGENTINA: Political Affinity Meets Business Interest Argentina offers another interesting example, although the relationship here has been more cooperative than confrontational. Musk has openly praised President Javier Milei and his libertarian, pro-business politics. The two men have met, including at a Tesla factory in Texas. Musk subsequently said his companies were looking for ways to invest in and support Argentina, which is also the worlds fourth-largest producer of lithium, a crucial component for electric-vehicle batteries. There is no evidence that Musks support for Milei was simply a business transaction. But the overlap is notable: Musk publicly aligned himself with a political leader whose economic philosophy broadly matches his own, while his companies were simultaneously exploring commercial opportunities in the country. US: From Donor To Political Insider The most direct example of Musks political involvement is in the United States, where his role went well beyond endorsing a candidate. Musk initially emerged as an increasingly vocal supporter of Donald Trump during the 2024 presidential campaign. He endorsed Trump after the assassination attempt against the Republican candidate in July 2024 and went on to campaign publicly for him. Last time America had a candidate this tough was Theodore Roosevelt," he noted. His financial backing was even more significant. Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars supporting Trump and Republican candidates, including through his America PAC. Federal filings showed that Musk became the biggest individual donor in the 2024 US election cycle, giving roughly $288 million to Republican causes. He also used X, which he owns, to amplify pro-Trump messages and attack his political opponents. After Trump won, Musks role changed again. He became an adviser to the incoming administration and was put in charge of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), a Trump initiative aimed at cutting federal spending and reducing the size of government. That created an unusual situation: Musk was simultaneously a major government contractor, the owner of companies affected by federal policy and a political insider helping shape that policy. SpaceX, for instance, has billions of dollars worth of contracts with the US government, including work for NASA and the US military. Tesla, meanwhile, operates in an industry heavily influenced by government regulations, tax incentives and environmental policy. Musks political involvement also did not end with the Trump administration. His relationship with Trump later became strained, with the two publicly attacking each other. Musk subsequently continued to intervene in US political debates and backed candidates and causes aligned with his views. None of this means Musk is the only billionaire who enters politics. Business leaders have funded political campaigns, lobbied governments and endorsed candidates for decades. Musks case, however, is different in scale and in the number of levers available to him. Elon Musk accused unnamed Indian "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's entry into the country to protect a monopolistic chokehold on consumers and maintain market dominance. India's telecom ministry strongly rejected the claim, stating that the regulatory framework is fair, non-discriminatory, and that all licensed operators are at the same regulatory stage while security assessments continue.

headline: Saudi Arabia says 3 killed in airport attacks claimed by Houthis, vows strikes 'will not go unpunished' | What we know
content: Three people have been killed and dozens wounded in attacks targeting airports in Saudi Arabia, the countrys civil aviation authorities said on Wednesday, Reuters reported. The development comes as fighting between Iran-aligned Houthi forces and Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops intensifies. One person was killed and eight others were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while two people were killed and 28 were wounded in an attack targeting facilities at Abha airport, according to the Saudi civil aviation authorities, as cited by Reuters. The Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attacks, which came amid a wider escalation in Yemen and growing fighting around the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. A Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemens internationally recognised government vowed retaliation following the airport attacks, saying they will not go unpunished, as per Reuters. The coalition later said it had carried out strikes on more than 80 Houthi military sites across the Yemeni governorates of Saada, Hodeidah, Jawf and Marib, the report said. The latest Saudi strikes and Houthi attacks mark a sharp escalation in fighting that has increasingly drawn attention to Yemens strategic position along one of the worlds key maritime routes. The attacks on Saudi airports were part of a wider series of strikes on the aviation infrastructure. Earlier on Wednesday, the Houthis attacked Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones, according to Yemens Transport Ministry. The latest escalation follows several recent incidents around Riyadh. On September 18, Saudi-led coalition forces said they had intercepted and destroyed a suspected Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh from Yemen, according to Al Jazeera. A day later, on September 19, at least one explosion was heard near Riyadh airport, while a large plume of black smoke was seen rising from a fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport, an Al Jazeera report said. The latest fighting has also brought renewed attention to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a narrow maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. Battles in Yemen have intensified around areas close to the strait, including territory around the port town of Mocha. Yemeni government forces, backed by Saudi-led coalition air support, launched a counteroffensive this week to retake strategic areas captured by the Houthis in September. With Hormuz emerging as a major chokepoint for energy shipments, the Bab el-Mandeb has come under renewed scrutiny as the Houthis step up attacks and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces seek to regain control of territory near the strait. The latest escalation is reviving a conflict that has already devastated Yemen for more than a decade. Saudi-backed forces loyal to Yemens internationally recognised government are now engaged in increasingly intense fighting with the Iran-aligned Houthis, who control large parts of the country and territory around the strategic Red Sea corridor. The conflict has also created one of the worlds worst humanitarian crises. More than 200,000 people have been displaced since the latest round of fighting began, the International Organization for Migration said on Wednesday. With inputs from Reuters.

headline: 'Merit On The Field': Yogi Adityanath Highlights Positive Sporting Culture In Uttar Pradesh
content: Yogi Adityanath highlighted Uttar Pradesh's new sporting culture since 2017, announcing appointment letters for 470 sportspersons selected in the Uttar Pradesh Police. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has highlighted the positive sporting culture that has emerged in Uttar Pradesh since 2017, making the youth and citizens aware of the transformation. He said, Merit on the field, recognition for achievements and opportunities for talented sportspersons to serve the nation together represent the new sporting culture of the New Uttar Pradesh." The Chief Minister also spoke about the neglect of sportspersons before 2017 and the new sports policy introduced thereafter. In a post on his social media account X, the Chief Minister wrote, Taking this culture forward, appointment letters will be handed over today to a total of 470 sportspersons selected under the skilled sportsperson quota in the Uttar Pradesh Police. These include 43 Sub-Inspectors (Civil Police), 295 Constables (Civil Police) and 132 Constables (PAC). The Chief Minister wrote that the opening of the doors to government service for sportspersons today reflects the transformation witnessed by Uttar Pradesh since 2017. Before this, the sports quota was neglected, and recruitment was discussed more in terms of recommendations and influence than talent. The Chief Minister said that the double-engine government has connected sporting talent with employment and a secure future. As a result, more than 534 sportspersons have so far been directly recruited across various departments, while the recruitment process for another 866 sportspersons in the Uttar Pradesh Police is also progressing. The Chief Minister extended his best wishes to all the selected sportspersons for a bright and successful future. A total of 470 sportspersons were selected and handed appointment letters under the skilled sportsperson quota in the Uttar Pradesh Police, comprising 43 Sub-Inspectors, 295 Civil Police Constables, and 132 PAC Constables.

headline: 'Zero transparency, zero accountability from EC', alleges YouTuber Dhruv Rathee addressing SIR protest in Bengaluru
content: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Thursday alleged that there was "zero transparency and zero accountability from the EC," over the SIR exercise. Addressing a protest organised by civil society groups and the CJP over SIR at Freedom Park here, he said, "I have not come here for regime change." Actor-activist Prakash Raj, who also took part in the protest, demanded the scrapping of the SIR exercise, alleging it was not merely about deletion of votes, but an attack on the dignity and rights of citizens. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is "acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah," he alleged. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke took part in the protest on Thursday. Thousands of supporters of Cockroach movement and several student groups demonstrated in the southern city of Bengaluru on Thursday, stepping up a nationwide campaign that is demanding the election chiefs resignation over a contentious revision of voter lists that has removed over 130 million people from the rolls. This fight is not going to be easy: CJP ahead of 10 October protest Meanwhile, CJP and student organisations on Wednesday called for a united mobilisation against Kumar ahead of their October 10 protest, saying the agitation will continue until the electoral system is overhauled. At a joint press conference in New Delhi, the groups sought to put their campaign against the Election Commission (EC) on a broader political footing, backing the opposition INDIA bloc MPs' October 6 protest march and describing the confrontation as one between people defending democracy and the BJP. In July, a CJP-led agitation over the NEET paper leak had forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as Union education minister. The group is now seeking to sustain street pressure against Kumar as protests against the EC intensify ahead of October 10. Wednesday's press conference brought together the CJP, the All India Students' Association (AISA), the All India Students' Federation (AISF) and the Students' Federation of India (SFI). The Aam Aadmi Party's student wing, Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP), also participated. CJP co-convener Saurav Das urged people across the country to travel to Delhi and to come prepared for a prolonged agitation. "This fight is not going to be easy. I appeal to everyone across the country to join us, book train and flight tickets," he said. Even if Kumar resigns, the protesters will not step back because the electoral system needs to be cleaned up, Das said, alleging that the BJP's pushback reflects a "lust for eternal power". The demands outlined by Das include Kumar's resignation and initiation of criminal proceedings against him; freezing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, halting upcoming elections, restoring the January 2025 voters' list and ordering an independent inquiry; and repealing the 2023 law governing appointments to the EC to establish an independent and credible selection process.

headline: US luxury spending is falling ahead of US midterm polls: What Citi's data tells about wealthy shoppers turning cautious
content: Overall US luxury credit card purchases declined 6% year-on-year in September, following 4% declines in both July and August, according to Citi. The data is based on millions of credit card transactions. The slowdown comes as the US heads towards the November 3 midterm elections, with surveys from the Conference Board and the University of Michigan showing growing unease about the US economy. Buffeted by prolonged weakness in China and the economic fallout of the Iran war, luxury brands have pinned hopes on resilient demand from wealthy US shoppers, including a growing cohort of AI millionaires, to offset softer sales elsewhere and help lift the sector out of a prolonged downturn. While continued wealth growth among affluent consumers supported the top-end of the market in September, overall US luxury credit card purchases fell 6% from a year earlier, after declining 4% in both July and August, Citi analysts said in a research note. The luxury brands most exposed to the US include Tapestry , owner of Coach and Kate Spade; French conglomerate LVMH , known for brands like Louis Vuitton and Tiffany; and Italy's Ferragamo, they said. The broader decline in spending suggests that even wealthy shoppers are becoming more cautious. Citi's data shows a mixed picture across luxury categories. Spending on leather goods and ready-to-wear items improved sequentially in September. However, spending on watches and luxury jewellery deteriorated further. Luxury brands have also raised prices this year. Most soft luxury brands selling apparel, shoes and leather goods increased prices by low single-digit percentages. That was slightly below the low to mid-single-digit price increases implemented by watch and jewellery makers. The spending slowdown comes against a backdrop of increased economic uncertainty. The run-up to US elections is often associated with greater caution among consumers and businesses, as political uncertainty can weigh on spending decisions. Economists also point to rising US Treasury yields and mortgage rates as factors that could further cool economic activity. The weakness could make it harder for luxury companies to deliver the recovery investors have been waiting for after two consecutive years of contraction. Morgan Stanley analysts said in September that the downturn in US luxury spending leaves brands with little scope for the long-awaited return to growth. The upcoming earnings season will provide a clearer picture of whether the weakness is spreading across the luxury industry. LVMH, widely viewed as a bellwether for the sector, is scheduled to report third-quarter sales on October 12. Gucci owner Kering reports on October 22 and has already indicated that investors should expect a slowdown in the US market. headline: Kangana Ranaut moves Delhi HC over alleged misuse of personality rights, AI content
content: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued summons in a suit filed by actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut, who has sought protection of her personality and publicity rights amid concerns over alleged fake news and AI-generated content linked to her. Justice Vikas Mahajan, hearing the matter, also issued notice on Ranauts application seeking interim relief against the alleged unauthorised use of her name, image and persona. During the hearing, the court examined several web links placed before it by Ranauts counsel. The material included an animated piece and a meme, which the court observed appeared to be satirical. Ranauts counsel clarified that he was not pressing for removal of the content at this stage. Advocate Saket Sikri, appearing for Ranaut, told the court that after an advance copy of the plaint was served, some defendants had already removed the allegedly offending material. The court subsequently issued summons in the suit and notice on Ranauts application seeking an interim injunction. The Delhi High Court also directed Ranauts counsel to file an amended memo of parties, noting that some defendants had been deleted from the proceedings. The matter has been listed for further hearing on February 3, 2027. The case comes against the backdrop of a series of proceedings before Indian courts, particularly the Delhi High Court, involving the personality and publicity rights of actors and other public figures. The Delhi High Court has previously granted protection to actor Amitabh Bachchan against unauthorised use of his name, image, voice and other attributes of his personality. In another significant ruling, the court protected Anil Kapoors personality rights, including his name, image, likeness, voice and distinctive expressions. Similar reliefs have also been considered or granted in cases involving public figures including Rajinikanth, Jackie Shroff, Arijit Singh and Sonu Nigam. These cases have contributed to growing judicial recognition of personality rights in matters involving unauthorised commercial exploitation and misuse of a celebritys identity. headline: 'Deeply Moved, Grateful': Former Japan PM's Wife Akie Abe At Inauguration Of Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor
content: Akie Abe expressed gratitude at the inauguration of the Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor in Varanasi, recalling her late husbands 2015 visit and Ganga Aarti. Former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abes wife, Akie Abe, became emotional as she recalled her late husbands connection with Varanasi while expressing gratitude for the inauguration of the Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor at the Rudraksh Convention Centre on Wednesday. Akie Abe jointly inaugurated the memorial corridor with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in Varanasi, dedicating it to the memory of the former Japanese Prime Minister. - Yogis 80-20 Jibe At Akhileshs Election Math: 'UP Rajya Sabha Contest Sets Tone For Assembly Polls' - 'Outstanding Leadership': World Leaders Congratulate PM Modi On Completion Of 25 Years In Public Service - Straight Talk | Twenty-Five Years, No Defeats: What Makes Narendra Modi Invincible? - Opinion | From Lal Chowk To A New J&K: The Kashmir Connection In Modis 25-Year Journey Speaking at the event, Akie Abe said, I am deeply moved and grateful to everyone for this memorial corridor and for naming it after my husband. Seeing this place brought back memories of my husbands visit here." She thanked Yogi Adityanath for the memorial corridor and said she was happy to be part of the programme honouring Shinzo Abe. I was very happy to be invited to participate in this event," she said, while expressing her heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the people of India. Akie Abe recalled Shinzo Abes 2015 visit to Varanasi, when he accompanied Prime Minister Narendra Modi and witnessed the Ganga Aarti in Kashi. She said that she had long wished to visit Varanasi herself and experience the city and its traditions. Akie Abe expressed gratitude for the Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor in Varanasi. She recalled Shinzo Abes 2015 Varanasi visit, when he witnessed the Ganga Aarti with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Akie Abe highlighted India-Japan cultural ties, drawing parallels between Varanasi and Kyoto. She said that her husband had visited Kashi and witnessed the Ganga Aarti, adding that it had been her heartfelt desire" to visit Varanasi and see the city with her own eyes. She said her dream had now come true. | Varanasi, UP: At the inauguration of Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor, former Japan PM Shinzo Abes wife Akie Abe says, I am deeply moved and grateful to everyone for this memorial corridor and for naming it after my husband Seeing this place brought back memories of my husbands visit here" (07.10) ANI (@ANI) October 8, 2026 Akie Abe also spoke about the cultural similarities she saw between Varanasi and Kyoto. She said she had been told that Varanasi was originally called Kashi and pointed out that both Kashi and Kyoto begin with the letter K and are ancient cities. She also recalled the contributions of Shinzo Abe and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the development of the Rudraksh Convention Centre. Referring to the 108 symbolic Rudrakshas placed on the exterior walls of the centre, Akie Abe explained the significance of the number 108 in Japan. She said that on the last day of December, bells are rung 108 times at Japanese Buddhist temples. She also said that it is believed that human beings have 108 afflictions or evils. Akie Abe became emotional while recalling the close and affectionate relationship between Prime Minister Modi and her late husband. Her remarks at the event centred on her personal memories of Shinzo Abes visit to Varanasi and the significance of the memorial dedicated to him. The corridor was jointly inaugurated by Akie Abe and Yogi Adityanath at the Rudraksh Convention Centre, with the Uttar Pradesh chief minister presenting her with a memento on the occasion. The Rudraksh Convention Centre itself reflects India-Japan cooperation. According to ANI, the centre was constructed with Japanese assistance and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2021. A photo gallery at the venue features photographs from December 2015, when Shinzo Abe accompanied PM Modi to Varanasi and participated in the Ganga Aarti. The memorial corridor was inaugurated as a tribute to Shinzo Abe and also highlights the broader India-Japan connection associated with the Rudraksh Convention Centre. Yogi Adityanath, while addressing the gathering, said the memorial corridor symbolises the strategic, cultural and diplomatic relations between India and Japan. Yogi also recalled Shinzo Abes contribution to strengthening India-Japan ties and Japans support for Indias development in areas including infrastructure, technology, transportation and economic development. He referred to Japanese involvement in projects including the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Rail Corridor and metro projects, besides other areas of cooperation. The Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor was inaugurated at the Rudraksh Convention Centre in Varanasi.

headline: Trump admin proposes ₹67 lakh fee for students to work in US: How Indians could be impacted
content: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed requiring international students to pay up to around 67.7 lakh ($70,000) for certain work-training programmes if they want to work in the US, as part of the Trump administrations broader crackdown on foreign visa holders. The proposed rule would require non-immigrant students on F-1 visas to pay 67.7 lakh ($70,000) to a certified institution for on-the-job training under the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, as per a statement released by DHS. An additional work-training programme would attract a proposed fee of 29 lakh ($30,000). DHS said the proposed changes are aimed at combating fraud, strengthening the integrity of the immigration system, and protecting US workers. The proposal could have a significant impact on Indian students, who make up one of the largest international student communities in the US. Around 3.63 lakh Indian students enrolled at US institutions during the 2024-25 academic year, making India the largest source of international students in the country, according to Hindustan Times. The OPT programme is particularly important for Indian students seeking to transition from higher education into employment in the US. Participation in OPT among Indian students has risen to around 1.44 lakh, according to a report in The Times of India. However, Indian student enrolment reportedly fell by around 15% in the 2025-26 cycle, amid tighter US visa policies and proposed changes to the immigration system, The Hindu reported. Under the OPT system, F-1 students can undertake temporary work related to their field of study for up to 20 hours a week while their academic programme is in session and can also work for a limited period after graduation, according to Reuters. Students with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) can qualify for an extended period of work authorization. Students currently pay around 48,000 ($500) for OPT-related applications, making the proposed 67.7 lakh ($70,000) fee a dramatic increase, according to the report. DHS said the proposed fee is intended to ensure that employers, students, and institutions are engaging in appropriate activities consistent with F-1 nonimmigrant status. For many international students, OPT serves as a bridge between studying in the US and entering the country's skilled workforce. The H-1B visa programme has, for decades, allowed highly skilled workers, particularly engineers, scientists and technology professionals from countries such as India, to work for US companies after completing their studies. US technology companies have also relied heavily on H-1B workers to fill specialized positions and address skilled labour gaps. Doug Rand, Director of the Talent Mobility Fund, which works to attract foreign STEM professionals, criticized DHS's proposal on LinkedIn, arguing that it could face legal challenges. The proposal will first be subject to a 30-day public comment period before DHS can finalize it, as per Reuters. If finalized, DHS said it would wait another 60 days before implementing the rule, giving universities, students and employers time to prepare. (With inputs from Reuters)

headline: The Fuel Behind India's Nuclear Push: UCIL To Double Uranium Production Capacity By 2036
content: India aims to increase its installed nuclear power capacity from the current 8.8 GW, generated by 24 reactors across the country, to about 100 GW by 2047. As India looks to expand its nuclear energy capacity, the Uranium Corporation of India (UCIL) has already begun working on its plan to double uranium oxide (yellowcake) production capacity by 2036. The raw powder is processed into nuclear fuel, which is used in reactors to generate electricity. UCIL is pursuing an ambitious growth strategy to double U3O8 production capacity by 2036 through new projects in Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh," said Dr K A Rao, UCIL Chairman and Managing Director, as the corporation entered its 60th year of mining operations in India. - World Teachers' Day 2026: Indias Single-Teacher Schools Fall, But Over 1 Lakh Still Remain - Opinion | From Ground Zero: Why Drug-Free Bharat Is An Imperative - LinkedIn Cofounder Reid Hoffman Defends AI Data Centre Boom, Says It Is Keeping US Out Of Recession - Andhra Police Uncover Pakistan-Linked Spy Network In Operation Firewall; 2 Arrested | Exclusive Details The plan includes a mix of augmentation and greenfield projects five in Jharkhand and one each in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh for which nominations have already been provided by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Seven new greenfield projects three in Jharkhand, two in Andhra Pradesh and one each in Meghalaya and Karnataka are also in the pipeline, but nominations are awaited from the DAE. This would enable us to increase the production capacity by four times by 2047, subject to statutory and regulatory clearances to contribute to Indias indigenous Uranium supply," said Dr Rao. Uranium, a radioactive, silvery-grey heavy metal, is used as fuel in nuclear reactors worldwide. While India began commercial mining and processing of uranium at Jaduguda in Jharkhand in 1967, its domestic reserves remain limited, leaving the country dependent on imports. India currently has about 24 commercial nuclear power reactors with an installed capacity of 8,780 MW (excluding RAPS-1), with more reactors under construction having a combined capacity of 13 GW. UCIL plans to double uranium oxide production capacity by 2036 through new projects. India currently has 24 commercial nuclear power reactors with an installed capacity of 8,780 MW. The government aims to increase India's nuclear power capacity from 8.8 GW to about 100 GW by 2047. NPCIL targets reaching about 54 GW by 2047 and 22 GW installed capacity by 2031-32. India's uranium deposits typically contain less than 0.05% uranium, compared to a global mining average of more than 0.12%. From 8.8 GW To 100 GW However, the government has now announced a major target to increase Indias nuclear power capacity from 8.8 GW to about 100 GW by 2047. India has also recently opened the doors to its civil nuclear sector for private and foreign participation through the Shanti Act, 2025. The plan also includes the development of five Small Modular Reactors by 2033, with support from the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), backed by the Rs. 20,000 crore Nuclear Energy Mission. Nearly half of the targeted 100 GW capacity is planned to come from the Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL). The target is very ambitious, but achievable," Umed Yadav, spokesperson for NPCIL, told CNN-News18. We have 24 reactors with a capacity of about 8.8 GW, and we are aiming to reach about 54 GW by 2047. It will be possible through fleet mode additions of 700 MW Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) a set of ten reactors, and we are also aiming for co-operation with our international partners, so we can have at least 22 GW installed capacity by 2031-32." The growing focus on nuclear energy also stems from its low carbon footprint and greenhouse gas emissions, which are important as India moves towards its net-zero target of 2070. It is a clean source of energy, and a reliable baseload power source, which is essential for grid stability. It is also an all-weather source. Any country with a large industrial base or growing demand from data centers requires a highly reliable and consistent source of electricity," he added. Not An Easy Road: Challenges Ahead The challenge, however, is the low grade of Indias uranium deposits. Indian deposits typically contain less than 0.05% uranium, compared with the global mining average of more than 0.12%. In contrast, some of the worlds highest-grade deposits in Canada have grades of up to 14%. Experts say mining about 1,000 kg of uranium ore yields just 280300 grams of uranium concentrate. Indias average ore grade is equivalent to the tailings grade (waste) in other parts of the world, experts say, highlighting the bigger challenge of radioactive waste generation. This not only creates challenges in securing land but also requires additional safety and environmental safeguards, while potentially leading to conflicts with local communities living near the facilities over health hazards. A larger part of UCILs strategy is now to carry out strategic outsourcing of activities and strengthen automation. The corporation currently operates about six underground mines at Bagjata, Jaduguda, Bhatin, Narwapahar, Turamdih and Mohuldih in Jharkhand, along with the countrys only open-cast uranium mine at Bandhuhurang in Jharkhand. At Narwapahar, one of its most modern and mechanised mines, operations remain heavily mechanised, with seven jumbo drills deployed in the 12-level-deep mine. Meanwhile, at Indias only open-cast uranium mine in Bandhuhurang, 13 km from Jamshedpur, the workforce on the ground has already been outsourced. The workforce has been outsourced to a private contractor for an initial six-year period with a possible two-year extension, while the supervisory staff continues to be from UCIL. About 320 workers are deployed in three shifts," said Abhishek Anand, Mine Incharge, Bandhuhurang. It is relatively cost-effective and safer to mine Uranium ore in open cast mines compared to underground ones." The Uranium Corporation of India (UCIL) is working on a plan to double its uranium oxide or yellowcake production capacity by 2036 to support India's growing nuclear energy sector.

headline: Car falls into sinkhole as road caves in near Chennai's Tidel Park
content: A car fell into a deep sinkhole that suddenly developed after a section of Rajiv Gandhi Salai (IT Expressway) caved in near Tidel Park on Thursday (October 8, 2026). The incident occurred around 10.50 am amid peak-hour traffic on the IT Corridor. The SUV was proceeding from Adyar towards Taramani when the road caved in, causing the car to fall and then roll over in the pit. The driver, Praveen, 27, sustained minor injuries. A 52-year-old woman was also in the car. Both occupants managed to escape from the vehicle before it fell completely into the pit, the police said. Traffic police personnel on duty and other motorists rushed to their rescue. With the help of Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) contractors, they safely pulled the occupants out of the pit. The police immediately cordoned off the affected stretch and diverted traffic. Vehicular movement was affected along Rajiv Gandhi Salai and adjoining areas. In May 2025, a call taxi carrying five passengers had fallen into a similar pit that had developed on the same road after a cave-in.
