headline: Congress's Solo Act, SP's Lunch Snub: Rahul Gandhi Hogs Protest Limelight, Akhilesh Isn't Impressed
content: For two days, the Gandhis dominated the show, turning what was billed as an opposition-alliance programme into an almost all-Congress affair, with allies pushed into the second row The Samajwadi Partys decision to skip the Congress-hosted lunch on October 7 was more than just a snub. It was a message to Rahul Gandhi: dont take your allies for granted. The lunch, hosted by Congress for opposition leaders amid the ongoing protest against SIR and demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, was meant to underline Opposition unity. But the SPs absence, particularly at a time when the Congress and its allies were trying to project a united front, has raised questions over whether all is really well within the INDIA bloc. - 'If We've To Bend A Little, We Will': Congress Says It's 'As Flexible As Constitution On Seat Sharing With SP - UP Assembly Elections | Congress Seeks 200 Seats As Samajwadi Party Pushes Back | News18 - Congress Is A Shield, Remove It And You Lose: Imran Masood On Ties With SP | Exclusive - United Against BJP, Divided Within: NC, Congress Spar Over Panchayat Polls In Jammu And Kashmir For two days, the Gandhis dominated the show, turning what was billed as an opposition-alliance programme into an almost all-Congress affair, with allies pushed into the second row. Officially, Congress and its allies insist there is no rift. But the little giveaways suggest a growing clash between Congresss ambition and the alliances need for unity. It began on day one. Abhishek Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhis team were seen together on the bus. Missing, however, were the Gandhi siblings. The two leaders were detained and later released. From that point, the focus shifted almost entirely to the Gandhis and stayed there on day two. Sources say the Samajwadi Party did not take kindly to this and decided to skip the lunch. In Uttar Pradesh, the SP cannot afford to look like Congresss junior partner, particularly when Congress has little at stake. With Akhilesh Yadav positioning himself as the CM face against Yogi Adityanath as Uttar Pradesh heads to polls in 2027, his cadre would hardly welcome images of the SP playing second fiddle while Congress grabs the spotlight in a battle that is primarily about the state. Why Congress Wants To Hog The Limelight The Samajwadi Party skipped a Congress-hosted lunch on October 7. The lunch was hosted by Congress for opposition leaders amid protests against SIR and demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The SP's absence raised questions about unity within the INDIA bloc. Akhilesh Yadav is positioning himself as the CM face against Yogi Adityanath for Uttar Pradesh polls in 2027. Congress aims to reinforce its own identity with 2029 in mind. Congress has its own compulsion. And it is called the Cockroach Janta Party. The last Gen Z protests were effectively upstaged by the CJP, triggering a bitter war of words between the two. Rahul Gandhi stayed away, keen to ensure Gen Z did not begin seeing the CJP as an alternative to Congress. The credit for Dharmendra Pradhans resignation went largely to the CJP and the students not Congress despite Rahul having kick-started the Chhatron Ki Goonj campaign earlier. This time, Rahul Gandhi is taking no chances. While talking about opposition unity, he also knows Congress needs to reinforce its own identity, particularly with 2029 in mind. He wants Rahul Gandhi and Congress to be seen as the principal alternative to the BJP, not the CJP. Congress has already burnt its fingers by allowing Aam Aadmi Party to grow and eventually call the shots. It sees the CJP as an extension of that threat, and wants to put it firmly in its place. Hence, the push to make Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi the main faces. The dramatic, viral images tell the story: Priyanka lying on the road, Rahul scuffling with cops, and Rahul adopting a casual, Gen-Z-friendly demeanour. It is Congresss way of owning the protest narrative and outflanking the CJP. And if keeping that spotlight means irritating a few allies, Congress appears willing to pay the price. Because right now, for Congress, owning the moment matters almost as much as keeping the alliance together. The Samajwadi Party skipped the Congress-hosted lunch following tensions over Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi dominating the opposition protest against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, which sidelined alliance partners and left the SP reluctant to look like a junior partner ahead of Uttar Pradesh's 2027 polls.

headline: 'Values, Sanskar, Courage': Indian Diaspora In Dubai Hails Flydubai Pilot Smit Machchhar's Heroism
content: Jitendra Vaidya, president of the Indian Peoples Forum (IPF) UAE, said Machchhars decision was driven not just by his training and knowledge, but also by his values Captain Smit Machchhar, who has been hailed for his courage after the Flydubai emergency, was honoured by members of the Indian diaspora at an event commemorating Prime Minister Narendra Modis 25 years in public life. As tributes were paid to the pilot, who continues to recover at a military facility in Dubai, speakers recalled the split-second decision that helped save more than 170 passengers and crew members. - Flydubai Passengers Refuse To Free Omani Co-Pilot, Say Will Only Hand Him To Police In Video - 'His Positive Spirit Is A Huge Boost': Captain Smit Machchhar Eager To Return To Skies After Attack - 'Was Reciting Hanuman Chalisa': Pilot Smit Machchhar Speaks To 'Biggest Idol' PM Modi On Flydubai Attack - Providing All Possible Help: PM Modi Speaks To Flydubai Pilot Smit Machchhars Family, Applauds His Bravery Jitendra Vaidya, president of the Indian Peoples Forum (IPF) UAE, said Machchhars decision was driven not just by his training and knowledge, but also by his values. The decision taken in a fraction of a second was not just because of his knowledge but values and sanskar. Today, the entire world is talking about the decision taken in a fraction of a second by the brave Captain," Vaidya said. The tribute ended with the packed auditorium rising in a standing ovation for Machchhar, as members of the Indian diaspora expressed their pride and gratitude towards the pilot. There was also hope that Machchhar would be able to attend a future gathering in person once he has recovered. We wish to felicitate him in person. He has made the Indian community proud," Sudha, an Indian lawyer based in Dubai, said. Meanwhile, a multi-country investigation continues into the actions and background of Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, who attacked Machchhar with an axe, leaving him seriously injured. Local media reports have claimed that Morocco is also looking into the incident amid emerging information that al-Hammami had a brief stint with Royal Air Maroc, Moroccos national carrier. Official records show al-Hammami was born in the United Arab Emirates and is of mixed heritage, with a mother of Syrian origin. Sources close to the investigation state that he spent a significant portion of his life outside of Oman. This extended period abroad occurred during his fathers employment in the UAE, while staying with his mother in war-torn Syria, and during his subsequent university studies in Australia. What Happened In Flydubai Flight? The plot came to light after the co-pilot attacked the captain aboard the Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. The passengers were later taken to safety after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, managed to regain access to the cockpit despite suffering injuries during the assault. He said he realised the aircraft was descending rapidly and forced himself to reach the cockpit door. Passengers also intervened after the aircraft plunged sharply, losing around 17,000 feet in about a minute, according to Flightradar24. Flydubai has suspended flights between the UAE and Israel following the incident. The co-pilot attacked captain Smit Machchhar with an axe inside the cockpit at 34,000 feet, causing the aircraft to plunge sharply. Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door so passengers and off-duty pilots could intervene, and the flight was safely diverted to Saudi Arabia.

headline: 'Hinduism Inclusive, Abrahamic Religions Exclusive': Madras HC Upholds FCRA Denial To Kodaikanal Trust
content: The judges also took note of the trusts founder and "moving spirit", Rev Fr Ama Samy SJ, who is an ordained Christian priest. The Madras High Court has upheld the Centres decision to deny Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) registration to a Kodaikanal-based charitable trust, while making observations on the religious character of different traditions and organisations. A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi dismissed the appeal filed by Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust, which operates a Zen meditation centre and Montessori school near Kodaikanal in Dindigul district. - 'Rahul Gandhi, Kejriwal Can't Feel For Punjab Like We Do': Sukhbir Badal On SAD's Edge | Exclusive - India SLAMS Pakistan At UN Over Terrorism, Questions Masood Azhar Bounty | Jaish-e-Mohammed | News18 - Madras HC's Landmark Ruling: Distinguishing Religion from Culture in NGO Funding | Raw Report - Rs. 100 Earned, Rs. 30 Tax, 18% GST Still Probed: When Nana Patekar Put Taxpayer's Pain Before Shinde, Fadnavis The Bench observed that unlike Hinduism, which is inclusive, the Abrahamic religions are inherently exclusive", noting that devout Jews, Christians and Muslims believe theirs is the one true revelation. The court found that the trust had not accurately disclosed its religious character. Although it had described itself as a non-religious organisation, the Bench noted that it subscribed to Zen Buddhist philosophy. The judges also took note of the trusts founder and moving spirit", Rev Fr Ama Samy SJ, who is an ordained Christian priest. The trust had argued that Zen meditation was rooted in Indias Dhyana tradition and that its activities therefore should not be considered religious. The Bench, however, observed that Christianity is a messianic religion whose theological mission is to bring everyone within the fold of Jesus Christ. The court further held that organisations involved in religious conversion should be denied FCRA registration, while making it clear that it was not alleging that the trust itself had a conversion agenda. According to the Bench, foreign-funded conversion activities could affect Indias pluralistic character and potentially imperil national sovereignty. The judgment also stressed that the FCRA provision applies irrespective of religion. The Bench noted that a fundamentalist Hindu Organisation engaged in Ghar Wapsi cannot be registered under FCRA". At the same time, the court drew a distinction between religious activities and the teaching of Indian Knowledge Systems. Organisations engaged in teaching Vedanta, the Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads and Yoga should ordinarily be regarded as educational or cultural bodies, it said. The 14-page order was pronounced on October 6 after the judgment had been reserved on October 1. The Bench concluded the order with a play on the name of Rev Fr Ama Samy. It observed that the authority had to say Illa Samy" (No Sir) to the priest, whose name literally translates as Yes". The Madras High Court upheld the Centre's decision because the trust did not accurately disclose its religious character, identifying as non-religious while subscribing to Zen Buddhist philosophy and being founded by a Christian priest.

headline: 'Rahul Gandhi, Kejriwal Can't Feel For Punjab Like We Do': Sukhbir Badal On SAD's Edge | Exclusive
content: The Shiromani Akali Dal chief said the worsening drug crisis among Punjabs youth and the deteriorating law-and-order situation were the two biggest concerns facing the state Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab, accusing it of failing to maintain law and order and claiming that the states drug crisis had worsened under the current regime. In an exclusive interview with News18, Badal said the worsening drug crisis among Punjabs youth and the deteriorating law-and-order situation were the two biggest concerns facing the state. He alleged that drugs were being pushed into Punjab through drones and claimed that rising addiction was making young people vulnerable to criminal activity. - 48 Haryana BJP MLAs, 1 Punjab Mission: What PM Modis Saturday Meeting Was Really About - CBI Raids Bhagwant Manns Camp Office In Corruption Case; Punjab CM Claims Misuse Of Agencies - Punjab Stubble Burning: Who Will End The Parali Politics? BJP Targets Bhagwant Mann | Plain Speak - CBI Found Nothing: Bhagwant Mann Hits Out At BJP After 12-Hour Raids Across Punjab One of the most concerning issues presently in Punjab is the condition of law and order and the other big issue is the worsening drug crisis among the youth. Drugs are being pushed and sent via the border in this current regime through drones and the supply has increased, which has led to more cases of addiction. These addicted youths are now only being vulnerable to get into criminal acts, which is destabilising the states law and order situation. Criminal activities like theft, firings and killings are only seen increasing. It has made Punjab unsafe. Now, women cant go out safely in the evening. The underlying reason for this issue turning worse is the police force. The Punjab police are completely out of control; its a compromised force. In the past five years of the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government, we dont have a permanent DGP. We have a temporary DGP heading the police force. Similarly, the AAP government has started the mechanism of controlling the police force in a way that they appoint all the junior officers for conducting illegal activities and whosoever gives them the maximum benefit is being promoted in lieu of huge amounts sent to the government. Lots of money is spent by a police officer to give to the government for transfer posting. That is why, they patronise criminals." Badal also said the SAD would seek votes on the basis of its record in government, arguing that the party had greater credibility on Punjab-specific issues than national parties. We have manufactured our campaign around how we have performed during our past regimes. We are the only party which will seek support and ask for votes based on our past performances. No other party talks about their past performances now. We have credibility with us. The level of commitment that a regional party in a state has is much higher than that of a national party. What I feel for the state, Rahul Gandhi or Arvind Kejriwal cannot feel that. For them, its just one state. For us, its our homeland." Punjab Has Collapsed: Badal Targets Successive Governments Backing the SADs Fight to save Punjab" campaign, Badal claimed that the state had witnessed a decline over the past decade and levelled personal allegations against chief minister Bhagwant Mann. The sloganeering around the campaign is very apt. The situation of Punjab in the last 10 years has collapsed. During Captain Amarinder Singhs tenure, not a single big development project has been attached to his name or has his contribution. In a similar manner, Mann is known to be an alcoholic. There is a total collapse of governance in the state. The outsider vs insider narrative is right. Now, people have realised that the Shiromani Akali Dal feels for them. People know that to save Punjab, they have to get their own regional party in power. Akali Dal is not a new party. Its a 105-year-old party, the second-oldest in the country." Badal also claimed that the SADs previous governments were responsible for major infrastructure projects in Punjab, including airports, power plants and road networks. If you travel from Amritsar to Chandigarh and find a big government project, ask when it was constructed. Not even a single development project was given to Punjab by any previous governments in power in the last 50 years. All airports, power plants and road networks; everything is built by the Akalis," he said. SAD Open To Alliances, But Not Congress Or AAP With the next Punjab assembly election approaching, Badal said his immediate focus was on strengthening the SAD organisation but indicated that the party was open to alliances with like-minded regional parties. My focus today is strengthening my party. I am open to all parties who are like-minded in approach. We are open to align with any party, except joining hands with Congress or Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Last time we had joined hands with the BSP. A lot of other smaller parties like the CPIM want to align, so we will evaluate and decide accordingly before the elections. We are currently concentrating on consolidating the party in Punjab." Badal Targets Waris Punjab De Badal also alleged that Waris Punjab De was being backed and funded by the AAP and claimed that the organisation was being used to weaken the traditional Akali vote base. Waris Punjab De is a creation of AAP. They have the backing of the party and receive funds from it. All meetings of Waris Punjab De are held in government offices. Have you ever heard of anybody from Waris Punjab De talking against this government? No, they cannot. They are patronising the current government. Their aim is to break away the traditional Akali vote share. There is no background of Waris Punjab De; the leader was brought in by this government to destabilise the growth of the Akalis." Our Politics Is Not Divisive The SAD chief also sought to position the party as a nationalist force and rejected any suggestion that Akali politics was divisive. For Akalis, India is our nation. We are nationalists. My father fought radicals and anti-nationals. If the aim for any party is to disturb peace, we will stand in their way. The best part about Punjab is that every religion and community lives as a family. Even during the worst of the times, no divide was seen and this is the teaching of our Gurus. Our Guru Granth Sahib says Sarbat Da Bhalawe believe that everyone should be blessed and we speak of the interests of everyone. Even during his tenure as the chief minister, my father was the leader of every community that elected him. That was the image that he had maintained. Our politics is not divisive; we dont divide among communities and religions." Badal said he was confident that the SAD could return to power if voters chose a regional party in the state. The people of Punjab always give a decisive verdict. If they want to elect their own party, then we will come to power. We are confident of winning and forming the government on all the seats across Punjab." Sukhbir Singh Badal highlighted that the two biggest concerns in Punjab are the deteriorating law-and-order situation and the worsening drug crisis among the youth, which he claims is being fueled by cross-border drone smuggling. He also pointed out that approximately 45 percent of inmates in Punjab jails are registered for opioid-assisted treatment.

headline: Trump's Popularity Falls Across US Ahead Of Midterms: Why Are Even His Strongholds Losing Faith?
content: States that backed Trump decisively in 2024 are now showing growing disapproval of his presidency, raising questions about what the shift means for Republicans in November. Donald Trump won several Republican strongholds by comfortable margins in the 2024 US presidential election. Nearly two years later, however, some of those same states are showing signs of growing dissatisfaction with his presidency. A new survey has revealed a striking shift in Trumps approval ratings just weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, raising questions about whether his party can retain its hold over traditionally Republican territory. - UP Election 2026: Akhilesh Yadav Drops 3rd Candidate | BJPs Big Strategy For UP 2027| - Trump Administration Weighs Military Action Against Iran Ahead Of US Midterms Elections | News18 - Trump Ditches Taxpayer Funds, Says He'll Fund Midterm Ads With His Own Money After Flak - Trump Delivers Fiery Remarks at Oklahoma Rally | Durant, Oklahoma | US Midterm Elections | News18 Trumps Approval Ratings Underwater In 39 US States According to a state-by-state tracker from polling firm Civiqs, more registered voters disapprove of Trumps performance than approve of it in 39 of Americas 50 states. The findings cover Democratic strongholds such as California, New York and Illinois, alongside traditionally Republican states including Nebraska, Kentucky and Tennessee. The numbers are particularly striking in Texas and Florida, two states that backed Trump in the 2024 presidential election. In Texas, 57 per cent of registered voters disapprove of his performance, while Florida has recorded a disapproval rating of 54 per cent. Trump continues to enjoy positive net approval ratings in just 11 states: Alabama, Arkansas, Idaho, Kansas, Montana, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, West Virginia and Wyoming. More registered voters disapprove of Trump's performance than approve in 39 of America's 50 states. Trump continues to enjoy positive net approval ratings in just 11 states. Trump's national approval rating had fallen to 32 per cent, the lowest recorded during his political career. Only 17 per cent of US adults approved of Trump's handling of the cost of living. The war with Iran has cost US taxpayers more than $30 billion and resulted in 18 American service member deaths. All 11 states voted for him in each of the last three presidential elections. Whats Behind The Growing Dissatisfaction With Trump? Two issues have emerged as significant sources of voter frustration: the cost of living and the continuing US war with Iran. A Reuters/Ipsos survey released in late September found that Trumps national approval rating had fallen to 32 per cent, the lowest recorded during his political career. The decline has coincided with mounting concerns over household expenses, particularly as the Iran conflict puts additional pressure on energy prices. An AP-NORC survey released in October found that only 17 per cent of US adults approved of Trumps handling of the cost of living. His performance on the broader economy received approval from just 26 per cent. The war with Iran has further complicated the economic picture. According to the same AP-NORC survey, only 28 per cent approved of Trumps handling of the conflict, while 69 per cent said the war had not been worth fighting. The conflict, which began in February, has continued for seven months without a clear resolution. It has resulted in the deaths of at least 18 American service members and cost US taxpayers more than $30 billion. Fuel prices have also risen sharply during this period. Data from the American Automobile Association (AAA) showed that the national average price of gasoline had reached $4.36 per gallon, compared with $2.98 shortly before the war began in February. Republican Strongholds Becoming More Competitive According to a Reuters report, Democrats were showing unexpected competitiveness in Senate races across 10 states that Trump won by double-digit margins in the 2024 presidential election. These included Ohio, Alaska, Iowa, Texas, Florida, Kansas, Nebraska, Mississippi, South Carolina and Kentucky. Kansas offers a notable example. Trump won the state by 16 percentage points in 2024, but a YouGov poll showed Democrat Adam Hamilton leading Republican Senator Roger Marshall by three points, with 48 per cent support against Marshalls 45 per cent. In Kentucky, which Trump carried by 31 percentage points, internal polling for Democrat Charles Booker placed him less than 10 percentage points behind Republican Andy Barr in the race to succeed longtime Senator Mitch McConnell, according to Reuters. Similarly, Democratic candidates in Florida and South Carolina were running neck and neck with Republican incumbents. David Hopkins, a political science professor at Boston College, told Reuters that the shift appeared particularly pronounced in Republican-leaning areas. Not only is there a swing away from the Republican Party compared to 2024, but the swing actually seems to be somewhat bigger in red America than in blue America, and thats putting these states that Trump won easily very much into play," he said. Trump, meanwhile, has dismissed unfavourable polling. Speaking to reporters on September 28, he said the polls are fake." He has also expressed confidence in his partys prospects, writing on Truth Social that Republicans would do well" in the midterms and urging supporters to pretend I am on the ballot". Could Trumps Falling Approval Ratings Change The Midterm Battle? The political implications extend beyond the presidents personal popularity. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the US Senate. The November 3 midterm elections will determine control of the House of Representatives and Senate for the remaining two years of Trumps current presidential term. According to Reuters, Democrats must defend two Senate seats in states Trump won in 2024 and capture four Republican-held seats to secure a majority. At least two of those Republican gains would need to come from states Trump carried by double-digit margins. A September NBC News poll gave Democrats a nine-percentage-point advantage over Republicans on the congressional ballot, with independent voters contributing significantly to that lead. However, turning polling momentum into electoral victories remains a challenge, particularly in states where Republicans have substantial financial advantages. According to advertising-tracking firm AdImpact, Republicans had reserved millions of dollars more in advertising than Democrats in several competitive states, including Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Alaska and Kansas. Republican Senator Tim Scott, who chairs the partys Senate campaign arm, emphasised the importance of campaign funding. Cash is king," Scott told reporters. Its a powerful tool that is providing us with the firepower necessary to really share our message, and our message is incredibly important for us to win these races." For now, the latest surveys reveal a notable contrast between the electoral support that carried Trump to victory in 2024 and public assessments of his presidency in 2026. Whether that dissatisfaction translates into changes in congressional representation will become clearer when Americans vote in November. Voter frustration is primarily driven by mounting concerns over the cost of living and the ongoing US war with Iran. The conflict, which began in February, has pushed national average gasoline prices to $4.36 per gallon and contributed to negative public sentiment regarding his economic management.

headline: Bengaluru CJP protest today: Prakash Raj, Dhruv Rathee to join 'people's tribunal' in SIR protest | Key things to know
content: Bengalurus Freedom Park is set to host a CJP protest on Thursday, bringing together activists and public figures to raise concerns surrounding the ongoing electoral roll revision exercise. The protest comes just two days ahead of the CJPs planned October 10 demonstration. During a joint press conference on Wednesday, CJP co-convener Saurav Das urged people across the country to travel to Delhi and to come prepared for a prolonged agitation. "This fight is not going to be easy. I appeal to everyone across the country to join us, book train and flight tickets," he said. Even if Kumar resigns, the protesters will not step back because the electoral system needs to be cleaned up, Das said, alleging that the BJP's pushback reflects a "lust for eternal power". The protestors have been demanding the resignation of the CEC at various demonstrations across the country. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, actor-activist Prakash Raj and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee will participate in a "people's tribunal" on the SIR of electoral rolls in Bengaluru today The "victims of SIR" from across Karnataka are expected to attend. The 'people's tribunal' will be followed by a "chappal protest." Announcing his attendence, Prakash Raj said on Wednesday,People's Tribunal by Cockroaches (Cockroach Janata Party)... Dipke... Ashutosh... Sourav and all the youth organisations and the civil society... the victims of SIR from across the state will be present. "Requesting all the citizens to participate in this fight to save our democracy. Come join us tomorrow, 8th October at Freedom Park... Bengaluru," he said. In a video, Raj said Dhruv Rathee, an influencer, would attend the event. Rathee also uploaded a video on his 'X' account confirming his participation in the programme and said the fight was to save democracy. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka had also announced on 'X' on October 6 that after attending the people's tribunal on SIR, they would interact with Kannadigas who have allegedly been wrongfully removed from the voters list. headline: Car plunges into sinkhole after OMR section caves in near Tidel Park in Chennai
content: A car plunged into a sinkhole after a section of Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) caved in near Tidel Park on Thursday morning, disrupting traffic on the busy stretch. The two occupants escaped unhurt. The incident occurred close to an underground Metro construction site near Tidel Park.The white car was travelling along OMR near Thiruvanmiyur MRTS when a portion of the road near the median suddenly caved in, trapping one of its front tyres. A video showed an MTC bus attempting to squeeze past the car and a Metro barricade, after which the car plunged into the sinkhole and landed upside down.Work is under way to remove the car and fill the sinkhole. Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) officials are yet to confirm whether the underground Metro work is linked to the road collapse. Police sources, however, said underground utilities, including Metro Water pipelines, had been relocated ahead of the Metro work and ruled out a rupture in water pipelines as a possible cause of the cave-in.

headline: What If Starlink Won't Switch Off? Study Flags Data And Security Risks India Faces With Musk's Network
content: According to the researchers, the network could potentially deny connectivity when India needs it or remain operational when India wants them shut down. Elon Musk may see Starlinks delayed India entry as a case of powerful interests protecting their turf. The Indian government sees it differently. After Musk alleged that certain oligarchs" were blocking Starlink from entering India to preserve a monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people", the Centre on Thursday rejected the charge as baseless and misconceived". The government said its satellite communication framework was fair and non-discriminatory and that Starlink, along with the other licensed satellite operators, was undergoing the same security assessment process before it can obtain spectrum. - 'You Can Guess Who They Are': Musk Claims 'Certain Oligarchs' Blocking Starlink In India - Baseless, Misconceived: Govt Refutes Elon Musks Oligarch Claim Over Starlinks India Hurdles - India Defends Starlink Framework Amid Elon Musks Discrimination Claims | SpaceX | News18 - Asked Grok? Trump Reportedly Consulted Musk's AI Chatbot Before Capturing Maduro Starlink, meanwhile, says it is ready to go. The company has reportedly established around 20 gateway sites in India and says it has built its operations around Indian security requirements, including controls intended to keep Indian user data within the country. But while the current debate is largely framed around competition, regulation and spectrum, one question that deserves attention is what happens when a foreign-controlled satellite network becomes deeply embedded in Indias communications infrastructure. A research paper by the Takshashila Institution, Starlink and Risks for India, published in April 2026, argues that the concerns go well beyond the question of whether Starlink should be allowed to sell internet connections to Indian consumers. The study by Ashwin Prasad Rao, Aditya Ramanathan and Col. Das (Retd.) identifies a more fundamental issue: India could find itself dependent on a network whose ultimate operational control lies outside the country. The papers central warning is stark. It says, Starlink poses significant risks to India". According to the researchers, the network could potentially deny connectivity when India needs it" or remain operational when India wants them shut down". The Problem Of Who Controls The Switch The Indian government rejected Elon Musk's charge that "certain oligarchs" were blocking Starlink's entry as "baseless and misconceived." A research paper by the Takshashila Institution, published in April 2026, argues that Starlink poses significant risks to India. Starlink already has more than 10,000 active satellites and plans a constellation of up to 42,000 satellites. Musk stated in March 2025 that his Starlink system is the backbone of the Ukrainian army. In December 2024, security forces recovered Starlink equipment from a militant group in Manipur. Starlink is unlike a conventional internet provider. Its network consists of thousands of low-Earth-orbit satellites and can provide high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity over areas where laying fibre or building terrestrial networks is difficult. The Takshashila study notes that Starlink already has more than 10,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit and ultimately plans a constellation of up to 42,000 satellites. Its scale and launch capability give it a technological advantage over most competitors. That scale, however, also creates a strategic vulnerability for countries that depend on it. The study identifies the primary risk" as the Indian governments limited ability to control Starlinks availability. The concern works both ways: Starlink could potentially continue providing service in an area where Indian authorities want it stopped, or service could be withdrawn from an area where the government needs connectivity to continue during a crisis. This is not entirely theoretical. The study points to Ukraine, where Starlink became an important communications lifeline after Russias invasion in 2022. According to the research, Musk subsequently restricted Starlink access multiple times" and denied the Ukrainian militarys request to turn on Starlink near Crimea". Musk himself has underlined just how consequential that control can be. In March 2025, he wrote that my Starlink system is the backbone of the Ukrainian army" and that its front line would collapse if he switched it off. For India, the lesson is that control over a critical communications network can become a strategic lever. The Foreign-Government Factor The Takshashila paper also highlights the relationship between SpaceX and the US government. SpaceX has become an important contractor for US defence and space programmes, including satellite launches for the National Reconnaissance Office and the US Space Force, as well as capabilities supporting missile warning and tracking. This creates another layer of concern, the researchers argue. In a situation involving a major geopolitical crisis, Washington could potentially have leverage over SpaceX, while India would have limited ability to compel a foreign-controlled constellation to act in accordance with Indian strategic requirements. The paper puts it plainly, Starlinks operator is ultimately subject to the authority and interests of a foreign government." The Data Question Starlink does not merely transmit packets across space. Its network necessarily generates information about users and their connections, including location and IP information. The Takshashila study flags Starlinks January 2026 privacy-policy update, which allowed customer information, including location data, IP addresses and certain communication information" to be used for training artificial intelligence and machine-learning models, as well as being shared with unspecified third-party collaborators. The study notes that users were opted into data sharing by default. The researchers also point to an earlier Musk statement in which he claimed, Between Tesla, Starlink & Twitter, I may have more real-time global economic data in one head than anyone ever." For India, the concern is that as Starlink expands, the amount of data generated by the network could also grow significantly. That makes data localisation, lawful interception and independent verification critical rather than merely regulatory boxes to tick. Indias Regulations Are Stringent, But Can They Be Enforced? India has not ignored these risks. Under the security conditions applicable to GMPCS operators, satellite providers must facilitate real-time monitoring, route Indian user traffic through gateways located in India, support metadata collection and ensure that Indian telecom data is not copied or decrypted outside the country. Special monitoring requirements also apply to areas within 50 km of international and coastal borders. The government says all licensed operators are subject to these requirements. The Department of Telecommunications own framework also makes clear that a GMPCS licence does not itself amount to spectrum allocation and that security compliance is mandatory. But the Takshashila study argues that regulation has a weakness as India may not always be able to independently verify compliance. One example is the requirement restricting the use of inter-satellite links. Starlinks architecture relies heavily on satellites communicating with each other through laser links. According to the study, regulators can monitor an Indian gateway but cannot reliably determine from the ground whether traffic travelled through the orbital mesh before reaching that gateway. The paper also says several requirements rely on self-certification, including commitments concerning data handling. It argues that this becomes particularly problematic in light of Starlinks updated privacy policy. The Manipur And Andaman Questions India has already encountered situations that illustrate the challenge. In December 2024, security forces recovered Starlink equipment from a militant group in Manipur. Around the same period, authorities in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands reportedly found smugglers using Starlink devices. The study says Indian authorities sought user details and usage history from Starlink in the latter case, but the company declined and directed the authorities towards US law-enforcement or international channels. These incidents also raise questions about geofencing. The study says the Manipur equipment may have worked in areas near the Myanmar border because of imperfections in geographic restrictions. It also cites Iran, where Starlink had the technical ability to disable terminals en masse but did not do so. What Happens In A War Or Disaster? There is another paradox. Satellite internet could be extremely valuable to India during earthquakes, floods, cyclones or other disasters when terrestrial infrastructure is damaged. The government itself has acknowledged that satellite communications can help connect remote, underserved, mountainous, coastal and border regions. But the same network could become a liability if India becomes too dependent on it. The Takshashila study warns that relying on Starlink for critical applications could mean losing connectivity precisely when it is most needed during a disaster, crisis, or conflict. This is why the issue is bigger than the present Musk-versus-government spat. India may benefit enormously from satellite internet. But allowing one foreign-controlled constellation to become indispensable would create a new form of strategic dependence. The study therefore recommends expanding the Digital Bharat Nidhi to improve terrestrial broadband, diversifying satellite providers, prioritising operators where India has greater leverage, limiting general retail dependence on foreign satellite internet and developing a regulatory framework for direct-to-device satellite technology. It also calls for Indias independent satcom monitoring infrastructure to be operationalised. The Indian government and studies like the one by the Takshashila Institution highlight risks regarding foreign operational control, the potential to deny or maintain connectivity during a crisis, and privacy policy updates allowing user data to train AI models by default. Additionally, security agencies have scrutinized potential compliance gaps involving traffic routing and laser inter-satellite links.

headline: CEC Gyanesh Kumar's security beefed up amid INDIA bloc's SIR protests: What is Z+ cover?
content: Amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Centre has upgraded his existing Z+ security cover, Hindustan Times reported. The move comes after protesters reached near Kumars residence in Delhi, while another demonstration was held outside his family home in Agra, according to NDTV. Officials cited by HT said the security enhancement followed a fresh assessment of the threat perception. More personnel have reportedly been deployed outside the CECs residence, at the Election Commission office and as part of his personal security detail. A senior police officer told HT that protesters had managed to trace Kumars residence in Delhi, while another protest was held outside his family home in Agra. We had to assess all the threats and increase the security cover. We had also placed a few pickets near his house, the officer said, as quoted by the publication. The security upgrade comes as the Congress and Opposition INDIA bloc continue to demand Kumars resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition would continue its protests against the Election Commissions actions. To save the Constitution and democracy, the Congress Party and the opposition are ready to take to the streets as many times as needed, face arrests, or endure legal cases, Gandhi said in a post on X. The development comes as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is also preparing to protest against Kumar. The CJP on Wednesday called for a united mobilization ahead of its 10 October protest, saying the prolonged agitation would continue until the electoral system is overhauled, The Hindu reported. Earlier, the group also backed the 6 October protest march by INDIA bloc MPs towards the Election Commission office, describing the confrontation as part of a broader campaign to defend democracy and the Constitution. The CJP has also called for the repeal of the 2023 law governing appointments to the Election Commission and demanded an independent selection process for election commissioners. The Oppositions criticism of Kumar has intensified following an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had, on record, objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process, which they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. Z+ is the highest category of general VIP security cover provided by the Government of India to individuals assessed to face a severe and credible threat to their lives. The level of protection is not fixed permanently. Security cover is reviewed periodically based on threat assessments, and the number of people receiving different categories of central security cover can change accordingly, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). The Centre determines security arrangements based on threat perception assessments prepared by central intelligence and security agencies, including the Intelligence Bureau, as per the MHA. Z+ protection involves a large, round-the-clock security detail covering the protectees residence, workplace, movements and travel routes. Such protection is generally provided by specialized units of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and other Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), according to The Print. The deployment can include armed personnel stationed at the protectees residence and workplace, escort teams during movement and personnel responsible for access control and route security.
