headline: Meta says it is using AI to detect child sexual abuse content on Instagram and Facebook
content: After facing backlash and legal inquiries from the Indian government over the presence of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on its platforms, Instagram and Facebook-parent Meta said it was using AI to improve how it detects such illegal content. These strategies include new large language model (LLM) detection of CSAM, greater ad transparency, AI sweeps of ad content, a red-teaming AI agent to detect vulnerabilities, and detecting bad actors who make new accounts after being removed the first time. Media reports had observed that CSAM was present in the ads on social media platforms Instagram and Facebook. The Indian Union government and the National Commission For Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) had met with Meta over the issue. A few weeks ago, Meta said it would share CSAM reports with the Indian law enforcement authorities. This was in addition to reporting to the U.S.-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). Between January and June 2026, Meta actioned 5.3 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on Facebook and Instagram in India, with over 98% found and proactively addressed before anyone reported it, said the company in a press release.

headline: Nana Patekar to be accorded state funeral, Maharashtra minister Ashish Shelar confirms
content: Veteran actor Nana Patekar will be accorded a state funeral in recognition of his contribution to Marathi theatre and Marathi and Hindi cinema, Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced on Thursday. Patekar died at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest in Goa. News of his death prompted tributes from the film industry and political leaders. Announcing the decision, Shelar said the actor's last rites would be conducted with full state honours. Quick answers to key questions 1What led to Nana Patekar's death? Nana Patekar died after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. 2How long did doctors attempt to revive Nana Patekar? Doctors attempted to revive Nana Patekar for around 45 minutes after he was brought to the hospital. 3What honors will Nana Patekar receive following his passing? Nana Patekar will be accorded a state funeral with full state honors in recognition of his contributions to Marathi and Hindi cinema. 4What was Nana Patekar's impact on Indian cinema? Nana Patekar was known for his powerful screen presence and versatile performances, making significant contributions to both Hindi and Marathi cinema over several decades. 5What were the circumstances of Nana Patekar's final hours? In his final hours, Nana Patekar sent a message to a friend at around 2:30 am stating he was not feeling well; his friend arrived at 4 am to find him unresponsive. In a post on X, Ashish Shelar wrote, Considering the unparalleled contribution of actor Nana Patekar to Marathi plays as well as Marathi and Hindi cinema, we have decided to conduct his last rites 'with full state honors'. Shelar also spoke to the media following Patekar's death and expressed his condolences. "The departure of Nana Patekar ji is a profound loss for the world of art. Emerging from the lanes of Yeola, he carved out his identity in Marathi theatre, Marathi and Hindi cinema through the strength of his talent and perseverance. On his passing, heartfelt condolences from me, from the Government of Maharashtra, and from the Department of Cultural Affairs," he said. Patekar suffered a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa and was subsequently taken to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive him for around 45 minutes, but he could not be saved. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, confirmed the actor's death to ANI. According to Dr Salkar, Patekar had sent a message to a friend at around 2:30 am saying that he was not feeling well. The friend later reached his residence at around 4 am. Patekar was among the prominent actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema. He made his acting debut with the 1978 film Gaman and went on to earn acclaim for his performances in films including Parinda, Prahar, Angaar, Krantiveer, Tiranga, Khamoshi and Ab Tak Chhappan. His career spanned several decades and included work across different genres and languages. Patekar continued to appear in films in recent years. He was part of Housefull 5, which starred Akshay Kumar, Abhishek Bachchan, Riteish Deshmukh and others. The actor also appeared as a police officer in Vishal Bhardwaj's O'Romeo, starring Shahid Kapoor and Triptii Dimri. Patekar also had a cameo in Subedar, which stars Anil Kapoor and

headline: 'Rs 5 Lakh Crore Saved From Wrong Hands': PM Modi Hails Digital India, Direct Benefit Transfer
content: PM Modi said Rs. 5 lakh crore was prevented from going into wrong hands through Direct Benefit Transfer, while attacking critics at India Mobile Congress. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday launched a sharp attack on those opposing measures aimed at curbing alleged malpractices in the delivery of government benefits, saying the shift towards digital governance had prevented Rs. 5 lakh crore from going into the wrong hands". Addressing the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi, PM Modi said he remained determined to continue with such measures despite criticism. - 'We Will Do It': PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey - 'Outstanding Leadership': World Leaders Congratulate PM Modi On Completion Of 25 Years In Public Service Highlighting the role of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), the Prime Minister said government assistance was now reaching beneficiaries directly through bank accounts linked to their mobile phones. Today, hundreds of government services are available on mobile phones. Government assistance now goes directly into the beneficiaries accounts. Through Direct Benefit Transfer, a sum of 50 lakh crore rupees reached the bank accounts linked to the beneficiaries mobile phones. This resulted in a saving of about 5 lakh crore rupees," PM Modi said. Calling the amount significant, he said the money had been prevented from reaching the wrong hands". This is no small figure. Five lakh crore rupees were prevented from falling into the wrong hands," the Prime Minister said. The Prime Minister then directly questioned whether those who had allegedly benefited from the practices that were being stopped would support him. Now tell me, will those whose unearned income has stopped love Modi? Did I do the right thing or not? Should all these malpractices be stopped or not?" he said. He also made it clear that criticism would not alter his resolve to pursue the measures. No matter how much they shout or scream. I am determined to see this through; I will get it done," PM Modi said. The Prime Ministers remarks came as he spoke about the transformation brought about by Digital India, particularly the increasing use of mobile phones for governance and delivery of government services. PM Modi described the Digital India initiative as a major effort towards the democratisation of technology. He said India had faced the challenge of a digital divide, with modern technology increasingly becoming a privilege for people who had the resources to access and benefit from it. Through the Digital India initiative, we resolved to change this situation, with the mobile phone at the centre of this transformation. This has been a major effort towards the democratisation of technology," the Prime Minister said. He said that over the past 10-12 years, the mobile phone had evolved beyond being merely a communication device and had become an important tool for governance. The Prime Minister also highlighted reforms in the telecom sector and the expansion of digital infrastructure as part of the governments efforts to widen access to technology. He said the government had also focused on ensuring that mobile phones and other telecom hardware were manufactured in India. PM Modi Highlights 5G Expansion At IMC PM Modi also highlighted the expansion of 5G connectivity across the country. He said 5G technology had reached every district and that more than 5.5 lakh 5G base stations were operating across India. According to the Prime Minister, mobile internet speeds had increased tenfold compared with 2022. Recalling the evolution of Indias telecom sector through the India Mobile Congress, PM Modi noted that 5G was launched in the country from the IMC platform in 2022. In 2023, he said, the focus had moved from the rollout of 5G to expanding its reach. The Prime Minister also expressed gratitude to citizens and people across the world for their wishes and greetings on the completion of 25 years of his service as the Head of Government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the shift towards digital governance and Direct Benefit Transfer has resulted in a saving of about Rs. 5 lakh crore, preventing the funds from going into the wrong hands.

headline: Friction In Karnataka Congress: DK Shivakumar Opposes BK Hariprasad's PAC Proposal
content: charge and Congress general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala would head the committee, with Hariprasad as convenor Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has opposed KPCC president BK Hariprasads proposal to constitute a Political Affairs Committee (PAC) in Karnataka to improve coordination between the Congress organisation and the government. Sources said Hariprasad and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah recently raised the proposal during their meetings with AICC general secretary KC Venugopal. They reportedly argued that the committee was needed urgently, citing feedback from ministers seeking wider consultation on major administrative decisions. - Big Conspiracy: DK Shivakumar Alleges Bulk Form 7 Submissions To Delete Voters In Karnataka - DK Shivakumars Twin Tunnel Project Runs Into Wetland Trouble: Legal Battle Looms Over Hebbal Lake Land - Karnataka: Central Teams Begin Drought Assessment As State Seeks Rs. 7,142 Crore Relief - After Tulu, Karnataka's Urdu Outreach: Government To Host First-Ever 'Urdu Habba' At Vidhana Soudha The proposed Bidadi AI City project, which has faced opposition from farmers over land acquisition, is among the issues that have highlighted the need for greater consultation, sources said. Hariprasad is learnt to have submitted a list of around 30 state leaders for possible inclusion in the proposed PAC, including ministers and senior party leaders. Under the proposal, Karnataka Congress in-charge and Congress general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala would head the committee, with Hariprasad as convenor. The proposed members include Shivakumar, Siddaramaiah, former Chief Minister M Veerappa Moily, KPCC working presidents, senior ministers and other senior leaders. The PAC is proposed as a forum to discuss major government and party decisions before their implementation. It would also provide a formal mechanism for coordination between the Chief Minister and the KPCC president, particularly ahead of the upcoming local body elections. However, Shivakumar is learnt to have opposed the proposal when it was discussed with the Congress high command. He reportedly argued that the government and the party organisation were functioning smoothly and that there was no need for a separate political affairs committee. Instead, Shivakumar told the party leadership that he had already constituted a high-level Group of Ministers (GoM) on political affairs under his chairmanship. The panel, he said, would discuss major issues before they are taken to the Cabinet. Shivakumar also pointed out that no such PAC existed during Siddaramaiahs previous tenure as Chief Minister, a source said. The Chief Ministers camp is also concerned that the proposed PAC could become an alternative mechanism with veto powers and potentially delay key administrative decisions and their implementation, sources said. Hariprasad, who recently met central Congress leaders, is reported to have stressed the need for closer coordination between the government and the party organisation ahead of the zilla, taluk and gram panchayat elections, as well as the Greater Bengaluru Authority polls, expected in about two months. The proposal comes amid visible differences between Shivakumar and Hariprasad. At an event at Vidhana Soudha on September 10 to mark 100 days of the Shivakumar government, Hariprasad was not invited to sit on the stage, while Siddaramaiah was present. On September 30, Hariprasad led a foot march from Shikaripur to Shivamogga as part of Bharat Jodo 2.0, also known as the Janata Jodo Jagruti Yatra. Shivakumar did not attend the event. Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar argued that the government and party organisation are already functioning smoothly and that a separate political affairs committee is unnecessary. His camp is concerned that the proposed PAC could act as an alternative mechanism with veto powers, potentially delaying key administrative decisions and their implementation.

headline: India exposes Pakistan's doublespeak at UN, says world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11, Pahalgam attacks
content: Exposing Pakistans doublespeak on terrorism at the UN, India has called out Islamabads efforts to gloss over its state support for terror by announcing rewards for Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) chief Masood Azahar, underlining that the world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam attacks. India on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) exercised its Right of Reply in response to the Pakistan representatives statement in the Sixth Committee of the UN General Assembly on the Agenda Item: Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. Pakistan speaks of combating terrorism while seeking to obscure the very question that this committee must confront What happens when terrorists are financed, facilitated, trained, sheltered, or supported from the territory of a State?, First Secretary in the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Raghoo Puri said. He said India has been consistent on this question, underscoring that terrorism cannot be defeated by declarations and instead requires action against its perpetrators, organisers, financiers, and sponsors. For years, Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline State in combating terrorism and as a victim while masking the fact that the Frankensteins the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan, Mr. Puri said. Calling out Pakistans doublespeak on terrorism, Mr. Puri said the country glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country, Masood Azhar. He said the world is aware of Pakistan's financial support to terrorism. Yet, we also remember that just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation. The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different, he said. Mr. Puri said that when the media can reach Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, "surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts. In May last year, India had launched Operation Sindoor targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the dastardly April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir perpetrated by The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists were killed. Earlier this month, India had dismissed as gimmicks Pakistans fresh announcement of a bounty of seven million rupees on Azhar, demanding that Islamabad take concrete action to combat terrorism. India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar, while Pakistan has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan a claim rejected by Afghanistans Taliban government. For the last few years, Islamabad has claimed that the JeM founder has been operating from Afghanistan. However, the Taliban regime dismissed Pakistans repeated claims, with a senior Afghan Foreign Ministry official saying he is not in the country. Islamabads fresh announcement on the reward for information on Azhar came as it faces pressure from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) to crack down on terror groups and their leadership. The Paris-based global watchdog is set to review Pakistans anti-terrorism efforts at its upcoming plenary. Pakistan was placed under the FATF grey list between 2018 and 2022 for its systemic deficiencies in anti-money laundering and its failure to counter-terror financing. Mr. Puri also recalled a recent statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, daughter of former Pakistan Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, who had said, The unfortunate thing is that the threat [Punjab] faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces. Exposing this dark secret, Mr. Puri said, You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds. Reality never works like that. When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice, he said. The world has not forgotten 9/11 and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught. The world has not forgotten 26/11. The world has not forgotten Pahalgam, Mr. Puri said, adding that the list, unfortunately, is painfully long. The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation, they were asked about their religion. It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism, he said. Pakistan continues with its narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation. If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are of course welcome to enjoy it," Mr. Puri said. "Any regime against terrorism to be effective must do two things assign responsibility and ensure accountability. India will defend its people, and continued terrorism against India will have consequences, he added. In another Right of Reply, Mr. Puri said India rejected Pakistans circular economy of words and narratives. If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place. But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government, he said, referring to a term used to describe allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistans 2024 general elections.

headline: Mad Sandhu Killing: One Arrested By Ahmedabad Crime Branch, Probe Goldy Dhillon Gang Link
content: According to the police, the murder was carried out in Punjab and was allegedly executed by Goldy Dhillons gang. The Ahmedabad Crime Branch has arrested one person for allegedly being involved in the killing of Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu in Amritsar. According to the police, the murder was carried out in Punjab and was allegedly executed by Goldy Dhillons gang. - Who Was Mad Sandhu, The Popular Makeup Artist And Influencer Shot Dead In Amritsar? - Mad Sandhu Killing: Attackers Chased Him Before Shooting, Police Probe Possible Conspiracy - Punjab Makeup Artist And Influencer Mad Sandhu Shot Dead In Amritsar - Punjab Law & Order Under Scrutiny: 4 Murders In 48 Hours, BJP-AAP Blame Game | Plain Speak The arrests mark a significant development in the investigation into Mad Sandhus killing, with the police now probing the alleged involvement of Goldy Dhillons gang in the murder. Sandhu, a prominent LGBTQ personality from Punjab, was shot dead on Saturday at a car-washing point on Loharka Road in Amritsar. Police said two men on a motorcycle followed him to the location and opened fire. Sandhu was taken to a hospital but died on the way. Amritsar Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill visited the spot and said the preliminary probe indicated that Sandhu had been under surveillance before the attack. According to investigators, the two assailants followed him and waited for him to arrive at the car-washing point before shooting him. They then escaped towards Loharka Road. Gill said police had gathered information about the alleged shooters as well as individuals who may have planned the attack. He added that the investigation could reveal important details in the days ahead. Following the post-mortem examination, Sandhus body was handed over to his family. His last rites were performed in Amritsar on Sunday, with family members, relatives and close associates attending the cremation. Who Was Mad Sandhu? Madhusudan, better known as Mad Sandhu, was a Punjab-based social media influencer and makeup artist who had built a following online. He was also known for openly embracing his sexual identity and speaking about the discrimination faced by members of the LGBTQ community. Sandhu had often been subjected to homophobic trolling on social media. However, he continued to speak openly about his identity and responded to criticism by saying that he was born the way he was and had accepted himself. His death has left his family, friends and followers seeking answers, as the police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Mad Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was a prominent Punjab-based social media influencer, makeup artist, and LGBTQ personality. He was shot dead on Saturday by two men on a motorcycle at a car-washing point on Loharka Road in Amritsar.

headline: EU sends envoy to Beijing as rising exports from China raise economic anxiety
content: The European Union is bracing for a confrontation with China as a trade deficit exceeding $1 billion a day heightens anxiety over potential job losses and pushes the bloc's political leaders to take a more aggressive approach toward its second-largest trading partner. The European Commission's top trade envoy, Maros Sefcovic, will be in Beijing on Thursday (October 8, 2026) for a two-day meeting with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao. The goal is to narrow the EU's 360 billion euro ($410 billion) trade deficit with China. Earlier this year, he gave Beijing a deadline of October to provide meaningful results in doing so. Politicians and economists across the 27-nation bloc consider China's massive subsidies and exports a major threat to core industrial sectors from steel foundries to car factories. China diverted many of its exports to the EU and other markets after the U.S. raised tariffs. In a debate on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) in the European Parliament in Strasbourg, lawmakers overwhelmingly expressed anxiety alongside defiance over trade with China. On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), they voted 454 to 86 on a resolution to toughen up on China that centred on a call for economic reciprocity and a proportionate EU response if China does not open its markets. Ahead of the vote, Hilde Vautmans, the Belgian lawmaker who led the resolution, said that Europe has economic power; it's time we used it. EU options range from tariffs to a trade bazooka Despite the seeming European unity this week, it remains unclear what the EU can or is willing to do. It has already rolled out trade measures against Chinese steel imports and e-commerce small parcels. France's High Commission for Strategy and Planning in February called for swift action, like 30% tariffs on many of China's exports, and a devaluation of the euro against the Chinese currency. Sales of German autos are plummeting in China, but China is also poised to gobble up market share in Europe by undercutting European automakers on price thanks to heavy state subsidies. There have already been mass layoffs at major manufacturers like Volkswagen. A letter by France and Germany, a copy of which was seen by The Associated Press, called for a sweeping rethink of the EU's China policy. Among other actions, it proposed making it easier for the European Commission to use the bloc's so-called trade bazooka, the Anti-Coercion Instrument. This is a never-before-used raft of measures for blocking or restricting trade and investment from countries found to be putting undue pressure on EU member nations or corporations. Yet not all EU nations agree on such tough measures. Spain, the eurozone's fourth-largest economy, has been less adversarial toward China in recent years. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has visited Beijing four times in three years. The European Policy Centre in Brussels said in June that European battery producers, solar panels, steel, electric vehicles, chemicals and machinery are already haemorrhaging jobs and capacity and called for a trade investigative body modelled on Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the phenomenon another China shock for Europe, similar to what happened in the U.S. in the early 2000s when hundreds of thousands of factory jobs in the American heartland were wiped out. The EU's ailing economy requires both a domestic overhaul and a more aggressive foreign trade policy, especially with China, said Tim Ruhlig, a China analyst at the European Union Institute for Security Studies, the bloc's internal think tank. Mr. Ruhlig also said that European businesses and political leadership bear some blame. It's clear that just protecting yourself from China is not the future, Mr. Ruhlig said. But to have a chance of making yourself ready for future technologies and to remain competitive in the coming 15-20 years, you have to protect yourself. It is impossible to disengage completely with China as the EU did with Russia following its invasion of Ukraine, Mr. Ruhlig said, but there is robust momentum now to reset trade relations with Beijing. Where do we make ourselves independent or at least more diverse? And where do we still work with the Chinese? Mr. Ruhlig asked. China is ready for a long trade dispute This week in Beijing, when asked about the letter penned by France and Germany, a spokesperson at China's Ministry of Commerce said that the countries should refrain from encouraging the EU to resort to protectionist measures. Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, and decoupling or cutting off supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself, the Commerce Ministry said in a statement. China is the EU's second-largest goods trading partner after the U.S., according to European Commission data. Chinese exports to the EU rose 15.3% in the first eight months of this year, according to China's customs agency, while its imports from the EU rose 6.2%. The EU does not have the capacity to wage a trade war against China, read an editorial last month in China's state-run Global Times newspaper. If it is truly determined to do so, then let it try. China's exports to Europe, as well as Southeast Asia, Latin America and Africa, expanded after U.S. tariffs went into effect last year, but it still booked a $1.2 trillion trade surplus globally in 2025. So far, China's export machine has remained remarkably resilient despite U.S. tariffs and other trade restrictions, said Max Zenglein, Asia Pacific senior economist at The Conference Board. This past weekend, ahead of the meeting between Mr. Sefcovic and Mr. Wang, China launched an anti-dumping probe on EU exports of p-nitrotoluene, which is used in dyes and pharmaceuticals. The probe was initiated after Beijing warned last month that it would take retaliatory actions if the EU instituted tougher protectionist trade measures. China has been battle-tested by successive rounds of external pressure and, so far, has largely stared down attempts to force a change in course, said Mr. Zenglein. China's economy has been largely driven by exports as domestic demand remains sluggish. The EU imports sizable amounts of Chinese lithium-ion batteries and hybrid electric vehicles, and Chinese carmakers are also expanding production capacity in Europe. While China's trade surplus has intensified concerns among its major trading partners, trade ties between the U.S. and China appear relatively stable following a summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump in Washington, wrote Bank of America economists, turning the attention to China-EU relations. When it comes to negotiations with the EU, Chinese investment in Europe is likely to be among Beijing's bargaining chips, Mr. Zenglein added, particularly as EU member states compete to attract capital, jobs, and new manufacturing projects.

headline: Italy Parliament votes on electoral law in key test for Meloni
content: Italy's Parliament votes Thursday (October 8, 2026) on a reform of the country's electoral law that opposition parties say Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's hard-right government has designed to boost its chances of re-election next year. The proposal would introduce a fully proportional system that guarantees a parliamentary majority to any alliance winning more than 42% of the vote. Italy's current electoral model combines first-past-the-post and proportional representation, with neither the right nor the left expected to secure an outright parliamentary majority at the next election. Ms. Meloni's coalition argues a new law is needed to bring greater political stability to Italy, but experts warn it could backfire and hand the left a clear path to victory at the 2027 polls. The electoral reform would "guarantee governability", Luca Ciriani, minister for parliamentary relations, told AFP. It would also benefit voters by requiring parties and coalitions to spell out their governing programme and name their candidate for premier "well before the election", he said. That could prove problematic for the centre-left, which disagrees on key policy issues and has yet to rally around a single leader. The opposition has vowed to vote against the reform, which has already cleared the Senate and now needs approval in the lower house. Chiara Braga, lower-house leader for the main opposition Democratic Party (PD), told AFP the proposal "bends democratic rules to serve the interests of those in power". Ms. Meloni's Brothers of Italy party and its allies hold a parliamentary majority, but tensions have emerged within the coalition ahead of the next general election, and Thursday's (October 8, 2026) ballot is secret, meaning rebels could vote against it. Ms. Meloni has warned she would resign if the reform fails; however, analysts say lawmakers are unlikely to risk triggering an election now. Giovanni Orsina, a political scientist at Rome's Luiss University, said it was "extremely likely" the law would be adopted. "Meloni faces little risk" in the lower-house vote, "but the law creates a completely open competitive landscape, so she does risk losing the election," he said. Under the proposed system, an alliance winning more than 42% of the vote would automatically receive a parliamentary majority, gaining an additional 70 seats in the lower house and 35 in the Senate. Legal challenges Reaching that threshold, however, may prove difficult for either side. Ms. Meloni last month became the leader of the longest-running administration in Italy's postwar history, but her coalition has been losing support to former army general Roberto Vannacci and his new National Future (FN) party. Although Ms. Meloni has so far ruled out an alliance with Vannacci, the far-right FN is polling ahead of both Meloni's allies, the anti-immigrant League and centre-right Forza Italia, and she may yet need him. According to a recent survey by Ipsos Doxa, the centre-left coalition could surpass the 42% threshold, provided it overcomes internal divisions and persuades two small radical parties to join forces. Ms. Meloni's term officially ends in October 2027, but she could opt to bring elections forward to April or May. Opposition parties have already vowed to challenge the new electoral law in court before then.

headline: The people this year's Nobel Prizes left out
content: Winning a Nobel Prize is a matter of great prestige. Winning a Nobel Prize also means the award going to a small number of people while a large number are left out, even if they really deserved to win. This is partly because of the prizes rules. Alfred Nobels will said nothing about the number of people that can be awarded at one time but the Nobel Foundations statutes limit each prize to at most three people at a time, and no one that has died by the time a prize is announced. Also, scientists need to have been nominated by nominators who have their own eligibility criteria. A big-picture view of the science Nobel Prizes through history brings another pattern into view: a preference for singular breakthroughs rather than lifetime achievements. Boyden, Bamberg, and beyond Start with the Nobel Prize this year for physiology/medicine, to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel, for their work on optogenetics. In 2002, Austrian scientist Gero Miessenbck & co. had first sensitised to light some neurons that were not naturally light-sensitive. Miessenbck is now at the University of Oxford, where his profile page describes him as an inventor of optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel have been feted for identifying and characterising the protein channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2). The next step was to show that it could control neurons. The first author of the paper that did was Edward Boyden, who helped pioneer the application of ChR2 to neuroscience. Boyden is now a professor of neurotechnology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and the Broad Institute. Another author of this paper, Ernst Bamberg, had supervised Nagels PhD and was part of the team that established the importance of ChR2. A page on the website of the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics, Germany, where Bamberg is now an emeritus professor, says he was instrumental in translating the ChR2 finding into practical applications. Yet another author, Feng Zhang, is also at MIT now, and in 2007, he was a member of one of two teams that adapted another protein, called halorhodopsin, to silence neurons with light instead of activating them. The other team, consisting of Xue Han and Boyden, had demonstrated the same capability. These contributions together rather than only those that the laureates led turned the ability to control neurons with light into a tool of neuroscience with real-world applications, including in medicine. Next, the physics prize which this year demonstrated the brokenness of the Nobel Prizes on a whole other level. Francis Halzen won the prize all by himself for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. But IceCube is an international collaboration involving around 450 experts from 58 institutions in 14 countries. Crucially, the prize-giving committee was not constrained to give the prize to one person here. The Nobel Foundation statutes allow the committee to decide whether its prizes can be awarded to associations or organisations. But the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, which awards the physics, chemistry, and economics prizes, does not seem to have adopted this option. If it had, the physics prize could have recognised the IceCube collaboration as a whole. But even if this rule did not exist, it is hard to say why the committee picked Halzen alone. In 1988, Halzen and (today) University of Hawaii physics and astronomy professor John G. Learned reported the idea of using Antarcticas ice mass as the target in which neutrinos from outer space could interact with atoms together. Learned then focused on an underwater neutrino experiment called DUMAND while Halzen pursued a project that eventually became IceCube. Also, in 2012, while searching IceCube data for neutrinos coming from outer space with very high energies, scientists found two candidate events. The data quickly snowballed into evidence proving that neutrinos could be energised significantly by natural phenomena in space and the prize citation credits this feat to Halzen alone. But in real-life (as opposed to Nobel-life), the IceCube collaboration had credited Japanese physicist Aya Ishihara with finding those two candidate events, and for which she received an International Union of Pure and Applied Physics award in 2013. This particular oversight is oddly reminiscent of the infamous Jocelyn Bell Burnell story. Ishihara is currently a professor at Chiba University, where she continues to study high-energy neutrinos and develop the next generation of neutrino detectors. Furthermore, the 2013 Science paper that reported the high-energy neutrinos also named three scientists named Claudio Kopper, Naoko Kurahashi, and Nathan Whitehorn as its corresponding authors. The physics prize for Halzen is not misplaced. Halzen was very good but the point is so were very many others. Aside from the scientists named here, it also required engineers and technicians who could build it in one of the most hostile locations on our planet. And all these people had to work together to make the project and its subsequent achievements possible. Halzen alone could never have done it. Drawing difficult lines Finally, the chemistry Nobel Prize this year illustrates the problem with the rule that it cannot be given to people who have died by the time the prize is announced. In 1953, the British physicist Frederick Charles Frank came up with a mathematical way to explain how a small chemical imbalance in a specific kind of reaction could force the reaction to make that imbalance the norm. This way required the reaction to have three properties, called autocatalysis, enantioselective catalysis, and mutual inhibition. Between 1986 and 1995, Henri Kagan in France and Kenso Soai in Japan had reported evidence of all the conditions of Franks model, providing experimental evidence that it could work in the real world. However, Frank died in 1998, aged 87. That said, the 1995 paper by Soai et al. included Takanori Shibata, who made essential contributions to this branch of chemistry (and was second author on the paper). And whereas Kagan and Soai had demonstrated different aspects of Franks model, Shibata was the first author of a 1999 paper that extended the work of Soai et al. to demonstrate the reaction Frank had tried to model. Shibata is currently at Waseda University. And again, it is not easy to rationalise the prize-giving committees decision to not include him among this years chemistry laureates. On the other hand, the committees decision to exclude U.S. chemical engineer Donna Blackmond throws light on one possible line of reasoning. A technical statement accompanying the chemistry prize credited her with extending Kagans attempts to use mathematics to understand non-linear effects in chemical reactions. Blackmond and her team later also took big strides in making sense of the mechanism of the so-called Soai reaction. And yet, the committee elected to reward the discovery of the validity of Franks model rather than work that explained and further extended it. The S.N. Bose example In the final analysis, the citations for the Nobel Prizes should not be mistaken for the history of science. Scientists build on the work of others and science advances in these slow but steady increments. When Peter Higgs and Franois Englert were awarded the Nobel Prize for physics in 2013 for predicting the Higgs boson, there was some clamour in India for not recognising the work of Satyendra Nath Bose. The objection was fair to the extent that you cant have a fruit without the whole tree and yet petty because it is not reasonable to expect one prize to laud the entire history of a field. This is why each Nobel Prize award can be a chance to reflect on its limitations, and remember that it is not an ultimate recognition. No prize is. In that vein, we should also not confuse the number of winners every year with the number of people it takes to do excellent science from grad students who perform simple experiments to senior colleagues to discuss complicated ideas with. In fact, depending on where in the world you are and your socio-economic standing, your ability to be a good scientist may turn on something as deceptively simple as having someone to help with household chores. Perhaps most of all, while the Nobel Prizes recognise good science, not all good science wins Nobel Prizes. mukunth.v@thehindu.co.in

headline: Trump says 'we don't think' Russian plague is bioweapon
content: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (October 8, 2026) that the death of a Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon. "We don't think so. We're going to find out soon enough, but we don't think so," Mr. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked if a "bio-weapon" was involved. Russia warned earlier against "false" information as reports emerged of a second suspected case. The U.S. and UN have urged Russia to be more transparent. Mr. Trump said Russia insisted it had the situation under control, but added that not much information was coming out. "If you listen to them, it's under control. But you know, people have said that before about other things," Mr. Trump said of Moscow's response. Referring to China's initial response to the Covid pandemic, Mr. Trump added: "Well, China didn't say much, and Russia is not saying much either. But they do say they have it very much under control." Mr. Trump reiterated that he has a phone call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the issue, but would not say when. "Today is Vladimir Putin's birthday," Mr. Trump added.

headline: US Proposes Rs 67 Lakh Fee For Foreign Students Seeking Temporary Work
content: The proposed rule would set a $70,000 (Rs. 67 lakh) fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for initial Optional Practical Training (OPT) and a $30,000 (Rs. 29 lakh) fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for any subsequent OPT.

headline: Bihar govt to set up grievance cell for guest workers in TN
content: Owing to the increasing number of migrant workers travelling for employment opportunities to several states across India, the Labour Resource and Migrant Workers Welfare department of Bihar is setting up Labour Service Facilitation Centres (Shram Seva Suvidha Kendra) in three districts in Tamil Nadu: Chennai, Coimbatore, and Tirupur, to address grievances, welfare and workers rights within the next two months.Additional chief secretary of the labour resource and migrant workers welfare department of Bihar, K Senthil Kumar, said, We have more than 3 crore Biharis going out to work interstate and internationally across various industries. So, the idea of the centre is to create a database on how many workers leave the state for work to help them with their livelihoods in every possible way.The department, which has already begun this initiative in Karnataka, will address language and culture gaps by providing orientation to guest workers, workplace issues, social security scheme, access to education for the children of the guest workers, health insurance, accident and death compensation, and access to govt schemes in Tamil Nadu.After conducting an extensive survey across 12 states including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Delhi NCR, Kerala, Punjab, and Maharashtra, we will be creating 12 such centres in India. In Tamil Nadu, weve chosen Chennai, Coimbatore, and Tiruppur as these are the hotspots; with close to 2-3 lakh Biharis working in Tiruppur. The survey will also include their socio-economic conditions to see which govt schemes would be more suitable to them, he added.Talking about the mass movement of labourers from Bihar, Senthil said that the Bihar govt is working towards creating job opportunities in industries and is also setting up a cement and sugar factory.

headline: Who was Jamaal Howard? Texas man killed in first US execution after Christa Pike botch, his last words: 'enjoy life...'
content: A Texas man was put to death Wednesday evening, becoming the 30th person executed in the US this year and the first since Tennessees failed attempt to administer a lethal injection to Christa Pike a week ago. Jamaal Howard was pronounced dead at 8:03 pm after receiving a fatal dose of pentobarbital at the state prison in Huntsville, the Associated Press reported. Who was Jamaal Howard? Jamaal Howard, 46, was convicted of killing Vickie Swartout, 42, in a 2000 store robbery. The store clerks killing was caught on surveillance video. Howard, who was 20 at the time, took $114 and a carton of cigarettes from the store in Silsbee, a small, rural town about 100 miles (160 kilometers) northeast of Houston, according to court records cited by the report. He was convicted of capital murder in the killing of Swartout, who was shot once in the chest during the robbery. Evidence presented at trial included surveillance video showing Howard shooting Swartout. Howard's last words Asked by the warden if he had a final statement, Howard apologised profusely to some members of his victims family, who watched through a window just feet from the death chamber. I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness, he said, shortly before the injection got underway. Im sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days. He also thanked his friends and family and said he loved them, adding he was in a good state of mind to find peace and the Lord, so I thank yall. He concluded with: "Hey, enjoy life, and peace to yall. Howard's execution came a week after 1995 murder accused Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital on September 30 in Tennessee. Her lawyers continue to seek more information about what went wrong during her execution. Her lawyers said she was unconscious at a hospital after the attempt but was awake and speaking by Tuesday. Pike, believed to be the first person to survive after receiving lethal injection drugs during an execution, stunningly woke up as plans were being made to remove her from life support, just six days after she was strapped to a gurney in the death chamber, said attorney Randy Spivey. But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone ... Christa woke up and began talking, Spivey said. Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer, is aware of what happened to her, at least up to a point, Spivey said. Many questions remain, though, about her prognosis for recovery and whether Tennessee will make another attempt to execute Pike, now age 50.

headline: Centre denies bias after Elon Musk claims 'oligarchs' blocking Starlink in India
content: The Ministry of Communications on Thursday said Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory. This comes a day after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk alleged that certain oligarchs were blocking Starlinks plans in India. In a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau, the Ministry said that licences have been granted to three satellite communication companies and all are required to meet security conditions. Their security assessments are currently underway. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage, the ministry said, calling claims of discrimination baseless and misconceived, a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau said. Earlier, Elon Musk had alleged on X that Starlink was being blocked to protect a monopolistic chokehold over Indian consumers. His comments came in response to a post arguing that Starlink could provide high-speed internet to underserved and remote communities. Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are This is a crime against the people of India! Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 7, 2026 Starlink has a licence to offer satellite internet services in India, but it is still awaiting security clearances and spectrum band allocation before it can start commercial services, Bloomberg reported. headline: Two Friends, Eight Months Apart: The Nana Patekar-Ajit Pawar Bond Maharashtra Now Remembers
content: Nana Patekar met Ajit 'Dada' Pawar when both were young and unknown. Five decades on, the friends are gone, eight months apart, and Maharashtra is remembering their bond. Nana Patekar and Ajit Pawar were friends for nearly five decades, long before one became a screen legend and the other Maharashtras Deputy Chief Minister. Pawar died in a plane crash on January 28; Patekar followed on October 8. The friendship they kept very private is what Maharashtra now remembers. Patekar, who died at 75 in Goa after what doctors said was a cardiac arrest, never made much of the bond in public. - Irreplaceable Loss: Political Leaders Mourn Nana Patekar, Recall His Cinema And Social Work - Veteran Actor Nana Patekar Dies At 75 Of Cardiac Arrest, Was Found Unconscious At Goa Home - Nana Patekar Dies At 75: PM Modi Mourns Loss; Funeral At His Pune House At 4 PM - Nana Patekars Last Message To Friend At 2.30 AM: 'Not Feeling Well'; What Happened Next Pawar, 66, was known across the state as Dada". He was a grassroots worker when they met, and he rose to hold the states second-highest office. The friendship survived both mens fame and Maharashtras politics, and it stayed out of the spotlight. Only after Pawars death did the state see how close the two had been. By then, Patekar had been asked to speak about it. How Did Two Young Men From Different Worlds Become Friends? By Patekars own account, it began before either was known to the public. Dada was a worker," he said in Marathi, in remarks reported after Pawars death. Whenever he visited Baramati, he said, Pawar looked after everything for him. He recalled that Pawar would have been 18 or 19 then, he himself 25 and Sharad Pawar 35. Fifty years is a very long association," he said. There are so many memories." What Did Nana Patekar Call Ajit Pawar? A friend, and more than that. He was a wonderful friend," Patekar said. He was like my younger brother." He spoke of Pawars journey, from a young worker to where he reached, as a remarkable journey". He asked that politics be left aside. I will always miss him," he said. Why Did He Say It Was Better Not To Speak Of It? Because, in Patekars view, friendship is not something to display once a man is gone. When a person becomes big, people talk about his friendships," he said. But now he is no more, so it is better not to speak about it." It was typical of Patekar, who lived simply in a one-bedroom flat and a village among hills, and who said he was just an ordinary man". What Happened After January 28? According to Marathi media reports, Patekar was overcome with emotion at a condolence meeting for Pawar. He was not asked to speak at length, so he paid his respects before the late leaders portrait and stepped down from the stage. A Hindi report said he was devastated by the loss. Some weeks later, about 29 days after the crash, he visited Pawars wife, Sunetra Pawar, and the family. No one can share the sorrow she is facing," he told ANI. We are sad too, but her pain is like a mountain. She will have to bear it herself." He added that along with the loss, she would have to take on the responsibilities Pawar had carried as Deputy Chief Minister. It will take time," he said. What Do The Photographs Show? A day after the crash, Patekars son Malhar shared rare photographs of Pawar at the familys farmhouse near Pune. They showed informal, private visits. Malhar wrote that Pawar was like family". The pictures offered a softer view of a leader usually seen through the lens of power. What Would Their Next Meeting Look Like? No one can say, and we doesnt presume to. But for those who find comfort in imagining that friends meet again somewhere beyond, the picture is not hard to draw. A man known for his punctuality would already be waiting. There would be no cameras and no politics, just two old friends who had known each other since before either was famous. If there were hills on all four sides and no AC, as Patekar once described his own home, he would not have minded. Patekar once spoke a line on screen that seems to speak to them both. A character tells another that people forget you after death, and asks who stays alive. Someone does," he replies, the heart for 10 minutes, the brain for 20, and the eyes for four hours." The memory of friendship, Maharashtra is now finding, lasts longer than that. Their bond started decades before either became famous, when Ajit Pawar was an 18 or 19-year-old grassroots worker in Baramati and Patekar was 25. Whenever Patekar visited Baramati, Pawar looked after everything for him, sparking a friendship that lasted nearly fifty years.

headline: 'Cannot afford to depend on single route': EU backs IMEC to make India-Europe trade more resilient amid Hormuz crisis
content: Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) to diversify trade routes and make India-Europe connectivity more resilient, with Apostolos Tzitzikostas, European Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism, warning that global trade cannot depend on a single maritime route, port or chokepoint. Tzitzikostas made the remarks at the Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026 event being held from 7 to 9 October in New Delhi, amid renewed concerns over disruptions to global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. We cannot afford to depend on a single route, a single port or maritime chokepoint, Tzitzikostas said on the opening day of the forum on Wednesday. When one is disrupted, the consequences extend to factories, energy markets, supply chains and eventually citizens and their everyday lives. The IMEC is a planned multimodal connectivity project announced on 9 September 2023, during the G20 Summit in New Delhi. The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz amid the war in Iran has renewed attention to the IMEC, highlighting the need for alternative trade and transport routes linking India with Europe. Tzitzikostas, while addressing a session on the India-EU Green Shipping Corridor: Innovation, Action and Scale, said IMEC could help diversify connectivity between India and Europe by creating a network of interconnected transport, energy and distribution links. He emphasized that ports and maritime connections would be central to the corridor, while the EU's Global Gateway initiative could help turn the IMEC vision into sustainable and resilient infrastructure projects. Recent disruptions have shown how quickly conflict, piracy, organized crime and cyber threats at sea can affect global trade, Tzitzikostas said. Europe and India are natural maritime partners. The ocean connects our economies and our societies. Our ports are gateways to trade, energy and industrial value chains, he said. Tzitzikostas highlighted the potential for India and Europe to cooperate on sustainable maritime fuels. Europe is creating a very strong demand for sustainable maritime fuels, he said. He said that India has significant renewable-energy potential and could become a major producer of green hydrogen derivatives such as green ammonia and methanol. Europe can provide India a growing market, technology and investment. This complementarity gives our partnership real potential, he said. Tzitzikostas said green shipping corridors can turn climate ambitions into concrete investments by bringing together ports, fuel producers, shipping companies and customers, with government support. The priority now is implementation: credible projects, sustainable fuel supply, bold infrastructure, and trusted standards and certifications, he said. The EU official said sustainable shipping, resilient connectivity, maritime security and healthy oceans should form the four pillars of India-EU maritime cooperation. Tzitzikostas said recent disruptions have demonstrated the vulnerability of global maritime trade to security threats. It makes absolute sense for us to deepen our cooperation on maritime security, including port and cyber security, he said. He also stressed the importance of establishing a global framework for shipping decarbonization that is workable, enforceable and pragmatic, while providing investors with certainty and supporting zero- and near-zero-emission shipping. Tzitzikostas described India as one of the world's three major maritime nations and a major source of seafarers, saying India's voice would therefore be important in shaping global maritime rules. Our task now is to turn political ambition into concrete results: cleaner seas, more sustainable ports, safer rules and stronger global rules for our oceans, he added.

headline: Nitin Nabin calls Rahul Gandhi 'anarchist', accuses Opposition of 'spreading poison'
content: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Thursday accused Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other members of non-NDA parties in the capital of nursing an anarchist mindset and seeking to spread poison in society, even as they were booked for assaulting cops during the INDIA bloc MPs protest in Delhi on Wednesday. Nabin was addressing the media on the sidelines of a visit to the Kashi Vishwanath temple. He reiterated his previous days statement that Gandhi was seeking to shelter infiltrators by raising questions against the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls due to a foreign mindset. The BJP chief dared Gandhi to step down from his position as Opposition Leader if he did not believe in the Election Commission, which oversaw his own election as well. These people are of an anarchic mindset, who only know how to spread poison in societythe elections in Kerala were also conducted by this same Election Commission. In Tamil Nadu, where they came to power from the backdoor, the elections there too were conducted by this same Election Commission, Nabin said. The people of the country are watching the kind of game they (INDIA bloc) are playingThe Leader of the Opposition is engaged in protecting infiltrators. Efforts are being made to secure rights for those who are encroaching on the rights of Indias people by coming in from different places, he added. A charge which found significant resonance in the BJPs campaign for Jharkhand, Delhi, Bihar, Assam and West Bengal, Nabin sought to underline that only the people of India have the claim over its resources, wealth and land, which would not be allowed to be encroached upon by outsiders or infiltrators. The Bharatiya Janata Party will always fight against this attempt to settle people here with a foreign mindset, Nabin added. On Wednesday too, while addressing a programme in Varanasi on the conclusion of a motorcycle yatra as part of the BJPs Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, a month-long programme to mark Prime Minister Modis 25 years in public office, Nabin said, the Opposition leaders are concerned about those who have been snatching the rights of the people of India. Nabins statements come in response to the Opposition MPs protest that is currently underway in Delhi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Named In FIR For 'Assaulting, Obstructing Cops' During Protest In Delhi
content: Delhi Police registered FIRs against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other Congress leaders and workers over the New Delhi protest. The Delhi Police registered a total of three FIRs naming Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in connection with the Oppositions protest in the national capital on Wednesday, accusing them of allegedly assaulting police personnel and obstructing government work, police sources said on Thursday. Several other Congress leaders and party workers who participated in the protest were also named in the case. - 'Fake News': Govt Denies Home Ministry Reaching Out To Rahul, Priyanka Over CEC Dharna - 'MPs Disrespected': Rahul Gandhi Demands Meeting With CEC, To Continue Protest At Akashvani Bhavan - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - 'Youre Doing Your Job': Rahul Gandhi Distributes Water While Supporters Deflate Cops Detention Bus | Watch According to the details, the allegations included assaulting police personnel, obstructing official duty, scuffling and misconduct. The police were also examining the allegations and the role of those involved, news agency PTI reported, citing police sources. According to the FIR details, the accused column remained blank, but the names of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra appeared in the details of the case. The FIR follows a tense confrontation between Opposition leaders and Delhi Police during the protest. Rahul Gandhi led INDIA bloc leaders in the street demonstration and was detained along with several other MPs. PTI reported that 91 people were detained during the protest, including multiple MPs and leaders. Delhi Police has registered three FIRs in connection with the Congress-led protest, with Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The cases allege assault on police personnel, obstruction of official duty, scuffling and misconduct during the protest. The Opposition has vowed to continue its agitation against the Election Commission and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The confrontation unfolded after Opposition leaders had held a lunch meeting at a South Indian vegetarian restaurant on Janpath and were travelling in buses towards Jantar Mantar for a surprise sit-in. Police stopped the protesters midway, resulting in an intense face-off. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other women leaders were seen lying on the road while holding copies of the Constitution. They were subsequently removed from the spot and taken into police buses amid slogans by Opposition members demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. MPs belonging to the Congress, Trinamool Congress, CPI-M, CPI, RJD, IUML and other parties were among those participating in the protest. Protest Over SIR, Election Commission The confrontation was part of the Oppositions continuing campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. As the Oppositions confrontation spilt onto the streets, INDIA bloc MPs attempted to proceed towards Jantar Mantar. Rahul Gandhi was seen trying to open a barricaded gate as police pushed the protesters back and detained several leaders. Priyanka Gandhi later alleged that women police personnel had scratched her and thrown protesters to the ground. The Opposition, meanwhile, maintained that it was exercising its democratic right to protest and seek answers from the Election Commission. Rahul Gandhi said the Congress and INDIA bloc were prepared to repeatedly take to the streets, face arrests and legal cases in what he described as a fight to save the Constitution and democracy". The Congress leader also said the Opposition would continue its agitation until Gyanesh Kumar resigned. Congress Says FIRs Will Not Stop Protest Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal said the party would not back down following the registration of FIRs against its leaders. Let them register thousands of FIRs, who is bothered about it? We are very much proud that we are fighting for retaining the democracy of this country," Venugopal said, according to ANI. Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda, whose name was also included in the FIR, said the Opposition would not be intimidated by the police action. The Opposition has continued to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, while Congress has announced further protests at the state, district and block levels. The Delhi Police registered FIRs against Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra accusing them of assaulting police personnel, obstructing government work, scuffling, and misconduct during an opposition protest in the national capital.

headline: 'Baseless, Misconceived': Govt Refutes Elon Musk's 'Oligarch' Claim Over Starlink's India Hurdles
content: Elon Musk had claimed on X that Starlink was being blocked to protect what he described as a monopolistic chokehold on the Indian market. The government on Thursday rejected SpaceX CEO Elon Musks allegation that certain oligarchs" were preventing his satellite internet company Starlink from starting operations in India, saying the countrys regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory". The Ministry of Communications issued the clarification after Musk claimed on X that Starlink was being blocked to protect what he described as a monopolistic chokehold" on the Indian market. - 'Mujhe Kya Lena Dena': When Nana Patekar Responded To Being Called A 'Modi Fan' | Throwback - We All Have To Go Someday, Dont Know If Ill Be Here Tomorrow: What Nana Patekar Said Four Days Before Death - Nana Patekar Was About To Buy A Rs. 1.5-Crore Car. Then He Saw A Farmer Suicide Report - Hills On All Four Sides, No AC: Nana Patekar's Simple Life Across Mumbai, Pune And Goa What Govt Said In Response To Musks Accusations In a statement issued through the Press Information Bureau, the government said three companies offering Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services using non-geosynchronous satellite orbit-based technology have already received telecom licences in India. A post is being circulated in social media regarding the fairness of Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services," the statement said. The government said all three licensed operators are required to meet specified security conditions before proceeding to the next stage of obtaining spectrum assignment. Security assessments for all three companies are currently underway. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the government said. What Elon Musk Claimed Musk had earlier responded to a post arguing that Starlink could provide high-speed internet access to underserved and remote communities in India. He said the company was facing opposition from unnamed business interests. Unfortunately, we (Starlink) are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are This is a crime against the people of India," Musk said. In the post, X account DogeDesigner, had argued that Starlink could expand access to high-speed broadband in underserved parts of India. The post said the satellite-based service could connect remote villages that lack reliable internet access, allowing more people to get online, and urged authorities to complete the necessary clearances for Starlink to begin commercial operations. Starlink is among the three satellite communication companies to have received licences from the Indian government. The security assessment process for all three is currently in progress. With inputs from ANI The Indian government rejected Elon Musk's allegations as baseless and misconceived, stating that the regulatory framework for satellite communication services is completely fair and non-discriminatory.

headline: China rejects EU request for voluntary curbs on hybrid car exports as trade talks begin in Beijing: What it means
content: China has rejected a request from the European Union for voluntary curbs on hybrid car exports to the bloc, adding a new flashpoint to trade talks between Brussels and Beijing as the two sides seek to avoid a wider trade conflict, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing two diplomats briefed on the discussions. Earlier, the European Commission had asked China to voluntarily limit shipments of China-made hybrid vehicles to Europe, according to the report. The development comes as EU Trade Commissioner Maro efovi travels to Beijing for two days of talks with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao. The negotiations aim to address the EU's widening trade deficit with China, with Chinese exports of relatively low-cost electric and hybrid vehicles emerging as a key issue. The EU has been increasingly concerned about the rapid growth of Chinese vehicle sales in the European market. Chinese carmakers captured a record share of nearly 12% of Europe's new-car market in August and accounted for roughly one in three plug-in hybrid sales in the region, Bloomberg reported. Therefore, the surge has put hybrid vehicles alongside electric cars at the centre of the EU's concerns over China's growing automotive exports. The European Commission is now considering safeguard measures that could restrict imports following a surge in Chinese-made hybrids entering the European market. One option under consideration is a tariff-rate quota, under which imports would be allowed up to a specified volume, while vehicles brought in above that threshold could face additional tariffs, Bloomberg reported. The proposed restrictions would be time-limited, said the Bloomberg report. The EU's initial approach was to seek a negotiated solution rather than immediately impose new trade restrictions. The European Commission had sought China's agreement to voluntarily limit hybrid exports to Europe. The Financial Times on 17 September 17 reported that Beijing could face higher tariffs if it did not agree to such restrictions. The commission hopes to get Beijing to accept a unilateral EU mechanism to cap hybrid imports, rather than having China voluntarily restrict exports, according to FT. The issue is expected to feature prominently in the latest round of EU-China trade talks in Beijing, which are starting on Thursday. efovi and his team are scheduled to hold two days of negotiations with Chinese officials, with discussions aimed at reducing the trade imbalance without triggering a broader confrontation, according to The Guardian. The outcome could influence whether the European Commission proceeds with its proposed safeguard measures. The commission is also reportedly viewing hybrids as a potential test case. If the measures are effective, similar tools could potentially be considered for other sectors where the EU sees significant trade imbalances, according to Bloomberg. For the EU, the continued growth in Chinese vehicle exports is adding pressure to address concerns over an uneven trading relationship. China has a large trade surplus with Europe, and the hybrid-car dispute could therefore risk becoming part of a broader trade dispute.
