headline: How A Worker's Missed Security Email Led To China Getting Hold Of Sensitive US F-35 Jet Parts
content: The parts were supposed to be delivered to San Francisco, but an unexpected change in route has left Washington scrambling for answers. A missed security email and a last-minute change in shipping route led to sensitive components of the US-made F-35 stealth fighter jet ending up in China, raising concerns over possible lapses in Americas military supply chain. According to a Bloomberg report, the incident has come under fresh scrutiny after new details emerged about how the shipment was diverted despite strict US export controls intended to keep sensitive defence technology out of adversaries hands. - Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before? - Loved Air Crash Investigation? 4 Shows To Watch That Probe Real Plane Crashes - OpenAI Is Losing Nearly Rs. 4.8 Crore A Day. Reason: Its Own AI Went Rogue - Asian Games 2026 India Full Schedule, October 2: Complete List Of Events And Timings How Did The F-35 Parts End Up In China? The shipment, which originated in Australia in late May, contained an F-35 cockpit canopy and a weapons-bay door. The parts were being transported to the United States for possible repair or disposal. Bloomberg, citing a person briefed on the incident, reported that the shipment was originally scheduled to reach San Francisco through South Korea and Taiwan, both US defence partners. However, delays in its departure from Australia prompted a change in the delivery route. In an attempt to make up for lost time, the shipment was mistakenly redirected through Hong Kong. The problem was that the components were subject to strict US export restrictions that prohibited their transit through certain countries. The Security Email That Went Unnoticed Sensitive components of a US-made F-35 stealth fighter jet ended up in China. The shipment originated in Australia in late May and contained an F-35 cockpit canopy and a weapons-bay door. A missed security email and a last-minute change in shipping route led to the diversion through Hong Kong. The F-35 is considered among the world's most advanced fighter aircraft and its stealth capabilities are central to its design. The incident has prompted investigations by the US Defence Department and State Department. Freight forwarding company DSV, which was handling the shipment on behalf of F-35 manufacturer Lockheed Martin, had sent an email identifying the components as subject to the US International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). These regulations govern the export and transfer of sensitive American defence equipment and technology, with restrictions intended to prevent such material from reaching US adversaries. The email warned against routing the shipment through certain countries, but the UPS employee responsible for handling it missed the instructions, according to the person cited by Bloomberg. The source also suggested that the communication may have been sent through an IT system different from the one used by the UPS agent, potentially contributing to the oversight. Why Are The Missing F-35 Components Sensitive? The F-35 is considered among the worlds most advanced fighter aircraft and is part of the most expensive weapons programme in US history. Its stealth capabilities are central to its design, allowing the aircraft to operate while reducing the likelihood of detection by enemy radar systems. Both missing components were coated with radar-absorbing material, raising concerns about the potential exposure of sensitive military technology. China has for years targeted the F-35 programme in espionage efforts, adding to concerns about the latest incident. Diana Maurer, who oversees F-35 support reviews at the non-partisan US Government Accountability Office, described the loss as significant. Its not good the Chinese now have" an F-35 canopy, Maurer told Bloomberg, calling the loss a big deal." Im sure the Chinese celebrated and then they got busy trying to reverse engineer it and figure out how to counter it with their own technical capabilities," she added. Pentagon, State Department Launch Investigations The incident has prompted investigations by the US Defence Department and State Department, with officials examining how the shipment was diverted and what measures are needed to prevent similar lapses. At a September 29 congressional briefing, Erica Plath, the Pentagons deputy assistant secretary of defence for logistics, said a team she had assembled was taking steps to prevent another such incident, Bloomberg reported. The Pentagon, meanwhile, has sought to distance itself from responsibility for the shipping error and played down the significance of the components, describing them as unserviceable". US Transportation Command said in a statement that it was not involved in the transportation or coordination of the shipment in question." We are actively working with U.S. authorities and industry partners to retrieve these components, investigate the incident, and place safeguards to avoid a future occurrence," the Defence Department said in a statement. US Lawmakers Demand Answers Over Security Lapse The diversion has drawn scrutiny from lawmakers concerned about vulnerabilities in the international supply chain supporting American military programmes. Senator Mark Warner, the senior Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, demanded a Pentagon briefing on the incident, while the committees Republican chairman, Senator Tom Cotton, called for a review of the defence supply chain. Republican Senator Kevin Cramer, who chairs the Senate Armed Services subcommittee investigating the incident, has also questioned whether the diversion was entirely accidental. Did China have a plan all along to intercept this?" Cramer asked. What Has Lockheed Martin Said? Lockheed Martin, which manages much of the global spare-parts inventory supporting F-35 operations in the US and 19 other countries, addressed the incident when Bloomberg first reported the missing components last month. Our logistics decisions are not made unilaterally," Lockheed Martin said, adding that it selects transport providers based on their compliance with government regulations. While we cannot discuss the details of which logistics partner was involved, we are working closely with them to help develop and implement preventive measures to strengthen our collective oversight and prevent recurrence," the company said. Asked about the newly disclosed circumstances of the diversion, Lockheed Martin said on Wednesday that we have nothing to add or correct on the series of events you mentioned." A shipment containing an F-35 cockpit canopy and a weapons-bay door from Australia was rerouted through Hong Kong due to delays and a missed security email from freight forwarder DSV that warned against restricted transit countries. A UPS employee failed to notice the instructions, allowing the sensitive defense parts subject to ITAR regulations to be diverted.

headline: Trump interrupted by protesters as he fights to rally Texas voters behind Paxton in U.S. Senate race
content: President Donald Trump, facing protesters and a poor political climate, fought to rally Texas voters behind embattled Senate candidate Ken Paxton on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) night in a bid to stave off a blue wave in the nation's most populous red state. Speaking to a packed Freeman Coliseum, Mr. Trump also clarified recent comments in which he appeared to suggest the bombing of an American city would be a small price to pay for the war in Iran. He said Wednesday (October 7, 2026) that Iran might try to hit an American city with a missile. You want to see problems? Let them hit San Diego, let them in Los Angeles, Mr. Trump said. We're not going to let that happen. We protect our cities. We protect our country. The President's message was interrupted repeatedly by protesters, including by one who appeared to be close to the stage. In all, at least a dozen demonstrators interrupted the President. Some were led away by police. Mr. Trump stepped away from the microphone briefly after one interruption. He's going back home to mom, Mr. Trump said. But what he doesn't know is his mom voted for Trump. The Republican Party did not plan to devote so much money and manpower to Texas this midterm season. Texas is the nation's most populous reliably Republican state, where Mr. Trump won in 2024 by almost 14% points. But with Election Day less than a month away, Mr. Trump's poor approval ratings, the Iran war and soaring gas prices have threatened Republicans in virtually every state. Wednesday's (October 7, 2026) appearance marked Mr. Trump's third trip to Texas in less than a month, and party officials have devoted more than $300 million to elections in the State so far. In a sign of Mr. Trump's poor standing, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott did not attend the evening rally. A three-term Republican governor who won reelection in 2022 by roughly 11% points, even Mr. Abbott has been caught in the turbulent national currents. He's locked in a competitive reelection race against Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa. Instead of appearing with Mr. Trump, Mr. Abbott was scheduled to headline the dedication of a hospital about 330 miles away. Democrats seized on the governor's absence. For years, Greg Abbott has never been shy about embracing Donald Trump, calling Trump a great friend' and championing his agenda every step of the way, said Texas Democratic Party spokesperson Jacob Long. But now, as Texas families get crushed by record-high prices driven by Trump's tariffs and war with Iran, suddenly Greg Abbott has somewhere else to be. While the race for governor has drawn a sudden influx of cash from Democrats, the State's U.S. Senate race has drawn the most attention as Democrats fight for the chamber's majority. The State has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988, but candidate James Talarico's fundraising, Mr. Trump's low approval rating and nagging concerns about Mr. Paxton's character have put the race squarely in play. Mr. Trump spent most of his remarks focused on the Texas Senate contest, describing Mr. Paxton as perhaps the greatest attorney general in the United States of America. He was tough and he was with us all the way, Mr. Trump said of Mr. Paxton. He's a fantastic man. Mr. Trump made no mention of the recently leaked recording of Mr. Paxton lamenting the war in Iran and rising fuel prices, while also complaining his campaign was being run by operatives in Washington. And while Mr. Trump praised Mr. Paxton briefly at the beginning of his remarks, he spent far more time attacking Mr. Talarico, whom he referred to repeatedly as Tala-freako.

headline: Starlink row: Govt rubbishes Elon Musk's remarks on 'oligarchs' as 'baseless', hails India's 'fair' framework
content: The Ministry of Communications issued a statement on Thursday, following SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's remarks against Indian oligarchs for blocking Starlink communication services in the country. The government said it has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services. "The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said without explicitly referring to Musk's comments a day earlier. On Wednesday, a social media post by Elon Musk went viral. The SpaceX and Tesla boss had shared DogeDesigner's' post, which gave pointers on why India needs Starlink. Musk reshared the X post, saying, "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are. This is a crime against the people of India!" The Ministry of Communications did not name Musk in its statement on Thursday, but acknowledged the post, which was being circulated on social media, regarding the fairness of Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. Rubbishing Musk's claim, the minister said, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived. The ministry said, The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services. Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India, the government said. Under the terms and conditions of the license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data, the minister added. The statement mentioned that the security assessment is currently underway with respect to all three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum, the ministry stated. The government further informed that at present, all three entities are broadly at the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived, it said.

headline: Nana Patekar's Last Message To Friend At 3.30 AM: 'Not Feeling Well'; What Happened Next
content: Nana Patekar messaged a friend around 3.30 am saying he was not feeling well. The friend saw it at 4 am and rushed to his Goa residence. Veteran actor Nana Patekar had messaged a friend around 3.30 am on Thursday, saying that he was not feeling well, shortly before he suffered a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, according to information shared with doctors at the hospital. The message became the first indication that something was wrong with the 75-year-old actor in the early hours of Thursday. - Hills On All Four Sides, No AC: Nana Patekar's Simple Life Across Mumbai, Pune And Goa - Veteran Actor Nana Patekar Dies At 75 Of Cardiac Arrest, Was Found Unconscious At Goa Home - Nana Patekars Kargil Chapter: How Prahaar Training Took The Actor From Reel To Real War - Nana Patekar Dies At 75: Doctor Says '45 Minutes of CPR' Could Not Revive Actor LIVE Updates On Nana Patekars Death According to Dr Shekhar Salkar of Manipal Hospital, Patekars friend saw the message around 4 am and immediately rushed to the actors apartment in Dona Paula, near Panaji. Salkar said the friend had informed hospital doctors about the message and what followed after he saw it. Patekar was living at the apartment with a caretaker. The friend saw the message around 4 am and rushed to the apartment of Patekar, who was living with a caretaker," Dr Salkar said. Nana Patekar messaged a friend around 3:30 am saying he was not feeling well. Patekar's friend saw it at around 4 am and rushed to his Goa residence. Patekar was found unconscious on the floor. The sequence of events then moved rapidly. Patekar was found unconscious at his residence, following which efforts were made to get medical assistance to the apartment. The caretaker arrived at the private hospital at around 4.18 or 4.20 am, according to Salkar. From there, an ambulance was sent to Patekars nearby residence. Patekar Was Found Unconscious, CPR Started At Home By the time the medical team reached the apartment, Patekar was already on the ground and was unconscious and almost unresponsive, Salkar said. The medical team immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and shifted the actor to the hospital while continuing the resuscitation efforts. The treatment started in the ambulance itself," Salkar said. Patekars residence was around five minutes away from the hospital, and the actor was brought to the medical facility in roughly 10 minutes, according to the doctor. Doctors continued attempts to revive him after he reached the hospital. Salkar said CPR was administered for around 45 minutes, but the actor could not be revived. Patekar was subsequently declared dead in the early hours of Thursday. ANI, quoting Salkar, reported the time of death as 5.20 am, while PTI, quoting the same doctor, put it at 5.10 am. Doctors Say Exact Cause Yet To Be Established Salkar said the actor had suffered a cardiac arrest, although the exact underlying cause was not known at the time. He also said Patekar was a known cardiac patient and was on medication, as far as the doctors had been informed. A medico-legal case was registered following the death. Patekars body was shifted to Goa Medical College and Hospital in Bambolim for a post-mortem examination to ascertain the exact cause of death. headline: Hills On All Four Sides, No AC: Nana Patekar's Simple Life Across Mumbai, Pune And Goa
content: Reportedly worth Rs. 50-80 crore, the veteran actor kept a 1BHK flat, a Goa home and a farm near Pune. Here is where he lived, and what he said about choosing village life. Nana Patekar, who died at 75 in Goa on Thursday after a cardiac arrest, was reportedly worth around Rs. 50-80 crore. Yet he kept a one-bedroom Andheri flat, a Goa home and a Pune farm. Asked on Kaun Banega Crorepati why he chose village life, his answer was disarmingly simple. Doctors at Manipal Hospital said that Patekar was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula and could not be revived despite about 45 minutes of CPR. A medico-legal case has been registered and a post-mortem is awaited. - Nana Patekar Dies At 75: Remembering The Actors Simple Life, Love For Farming and His Pune Farmhouse - Nana Patekars Kargil Chapter: How Prahaar Training Took The Actor From Reel To Real War - Veteran Actor Nana Patekar Dies At 75 Of Cardiac Arrest, Was Found Unconscious At Goa Home - Nana Patekar Dies At 75: Doctor Says '45 Minutes of CPR' Could Not Revive Actor Born Vishwanath Patekar in Murud-Janjira on January 1, 1951, he debuted with Gaman (1978) and spent nearly five decades in Hindi and Marathi cinema, from Parinda and Krantiveer to Welcome and Natsamrat. He won three National Film Awards and the Padma Shri in 2013. Reports put his earnings at Rs. 2-3 crore per film in recent years. His way of living never seemed to follow the money. Where Did Nana Patekar Actually Live? For most of his adult life, in a single-bedroom flat in Andheri, Mumbai. The roughly 750 sq ft home was reportedly bought for about Rs. 1.1 lakh decades ago and is now estimated to be worth around Rs. 3 crore. He lived there with his mother, Nirmala, until her death in January 2019 at the age of 99. He stayed on alone, and in interviews often said his needs had never outgrown the flat. What About Goa And Pune? Reports say he also owned a more contemporary house in Goa, where he died, and split his time between Mumbai, Goa and Pune. His largest property was reportedly a 27-acre farmhouse in Khadakwasla, near Pune, with seven rooms and a large hall. Wheat and paddy grown there were reportedly sold across Maharashtra, with earnings shared among farmhands and local farmers. A separate house on Punes Law College Road is also reported. How Rich Was He, Really? Estimates range from Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 80 crore, built over five decades. Yet his garage was reportedly a Mahindra Jeep CJ4, an Audi Q7 and a Mahindra Scorpio. There was no supercar collection, and little sign of a stars usual trappings. Why Did He Choose Village Life? He answered this himself, in an exchange with Amitabh Bachchan on Kaun Banega Crorepati. Bachchan asked why, after such fame, he had left it all behind for a village. I dont belong to the industry," Patekar said, in Hindi. I come here, work and run back. Ive never gone to parties here. It never suited me. Im from the villages and Ill remain there. Thats where I feel good." He said he had received far more than he ever wished for. When your needs are limited, life becomes very easy," he said. His village home, he added, has no AC, but I enjoy it immensely." Then came the line that drew applause from the studio. In a city, he said, houses have walls. Here, we have hills: hills on this side, hills on that side, hills on all sides, and we sit in the middle." What Did He Do With His Money? Reports say he gave much of it away. In 2015, he reportedly handed cheques of Rs. 15,000 each to over a hundred drought-hit farming families in Latur and Vidarbha. Friends and colleagues have long cited this as proof that wealth was never the point for him. Wikipedia lists the Naam Foundation as his organisation. What Did His Years In Uniform Say About Him? The same discipline showed in his army years. He trained for three years with the Maratha Light Infantry while preparing for Prahaar (1991) and was given an honorary Captains rank in the Territorial Army. In August 1999, during the Kargil War, he obtained special permission from then Defence Minister George Fernandes. He then spent over two weeks near the LoC as part of a Quick Reaction Team, losing about 20 kg, by his own account to The Lallantop. Where Did The Hardship Come From? According to reports, Patekars family business was taken over by an acquaintance when he was 13, and he began painting movie posters in Chunabhatti for Rs. 35 a month. His father died of a heart attack when he was 28. He also lost his elder son, Durvasa, at two and a half. He is survived by his son, Malhar. Why Is A Film Clip Going Viral Today? A scene from one of his films has resurfaced on social media. Patekars character tells Mahie Gills: You wont drink, you wont dance. People will forget you after you die." Her character asks: Who stays alive after death?" Someone does," he replies. The heart for 10 minutes, the brain for 20, and the eyes for four hours. In those four hours, the eyes see how your own people behave. After that, death must feel like a gift to the corpse." A tribute to Nana Patekar. Three National Film Awards, four Filmfare Awards, the Padma Shri in 2013 and 23 years of service in the Territorial Army, including during the Kargil War. An actor who lived life with immense passion both on screen and in real life. Vijay Kumar (@adv_vkr) October 8, 2026 It was a monologue about how people treat you once you are gone. Patekar lived in a one-bedroom flat and a village among the hills, and he valued people over parties. For those who loved him, and for those who knew him only from the screen, the line lands differently today. Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 in Goa on Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest. He was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula and could not be revived despite about 45 minutes of CPR at Manipal Hospital.

headline: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize ,but doubts he will get it
content: U.S. President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances. "I don't know what their decision is going to be," Mr. Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday (October 9, 2026). "They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me." Since his return to the White House last year, Mr. Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world's most prestigious award. "It is about that time," Mr. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "But I was very honoured to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump." Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gave her 2025 Nobel Peace Prize medal to Trump in January as she sought U.S. support for her efforts in Venezuela. Mr. Trump said he should get the prize after wading into eight conflicts since taking office last January. The leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated Trump, though there is no way of verifying that. Parties to some conflicts Mr. Trump claims to have resolved dispute the U.S. President's diplomatic role, and fighting has flared again in some of those regions, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the border between Cambodia and Thailand. A resolution to Russia's war in Ukraine has eluded Mr. Trump, who promised to end it on the first day of his second White House term. U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran have led to a seven-month simmering conflict that has upended global energy supplies and driven gas prices up before November's midterm elections. Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, the special rapporteur for the Palestinian Territories, are among the favorites to win this year.

headline: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro, wife to face new charges in US: 'Detained Americans were tortured' — What we know so far
content: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores may face new criminal charges in the United States over allegations that Americans detained in Venezuela were tortured, a US official said on Wednesday. The official told Reuters that the new charges could come as soon as Thursday. What do we know about new charges against Maduro, wife? The possibility of new charges was first reported by CNN on Wednesday. Details of the new charges, including the identities of the alleged torture victims, were not immediately available. The US reportedly accused Maduro's government of detaining Americans as leverage to extract concessions such as relief from financial sanctions. Americans whom the US classified as wrongfully detained during Maduro's tenure included five oil executives arrested on graft charges. They were freed in 2022 in exchange for two of Flores' nephews who had been convicted in the US of drug trafficking. Others detained included two former US Army Special Forces members who were arrested in Venezuela in 2020 in connection with a botched raid aimed at ousting Maduro. They were freed in 2023 as part of another prisoner swap, Reuters reported. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney's office, which brought the charges, declined to comment. Lawyers for Maduro and Flores did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Maduro's capture Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, were captured by the US military from their home in Caracas on January 3 and brought to New York to face drug trafficking charges. They have been held in a federal jail in Brooklyn. They have pleaded not guilty and are scheduled to go on trial starting June 1, 2027. Flores is due to appear in Manhattan federal court on Thursday to urge US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to release her from jail before trial for health reasons. Prosecutors oppose her release. Since Maduro's capture, Venezuela has been led by his former vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, who has increased cooperation with the Trump administration.

headline: Pakistan Calls Retired Soldiers Back To Balochistan Amid Rising Militant Attacks | Exclusive
content: Facing mounting security pressures and a manpower shortage, Pakistan's Frontier Corps has moved to bring retired personnel back into service in Balochistan. Pakistans Frontier Corps (FC) has moved to bring retired personnel back into service in Balochistan amid a growing manpower crunch, rising militant attacks and mounting security challenges in the restive province. An official communication issued by the office of the Inspector General of Frontier Corps Balochistan (North), accessed by CNN-News18, reveals that retired personnel have been asked to report to their former units for re-enlistment. - BLA Fighters Overrun Police Station In Balochistan, 2 Security Personnel Killed: Sources - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks - Saudi Says Airport Attacks In Riyadh, Abha Kill 3, Injure 36 After Houthis Claim Strikes - Gwadar-Bound Cargo Attacked In Balochistan, Driver May Have Been Abducted: Sources | Exclusive The move comes as the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) intensifies its operations against Pakistani security forces, with the separatist group claiming to have carried out 94 armed operations across the province in September alone. Retired Soldiers Asked To Report By October 30 Retired personnel have been directed to contact their respective wing commanders before October 30 if they wish to return to service. The document also indicates that personnel who retired several years ago may be considered for re-enlistment. Those returning to duty will receive salaries corresponding to their completed years of service. BLA Claims 105 Pakistani Security Personnel Killed In September The move comes against the backdrop of sustained attacks by the BLA, which has claimed responsibility for a series of operations targeting Pakistani security forces across Balochistan. In its account of activities during September, the separatist group claimed to have carried out 94 armed operations, allegedly killing 105 Pakistani security personnel and injuring 52 others. The BLA also claimed responsibility for 63 improvised explosive device (IED) attacks, 18 incidents involving the seizure of weapons and the destruction of 46 vehicles belonging to Pakistani security forces or what it described as enemy forces. The group further claimed to have conducted 25 raids and blockades during the month, killing 37 individuals it described as Pakistani military intelligence agents and capturing 21 Pakistani personnel and alleged intelligence agents. It also acknowledged the deaths of 33 of its fighters during armed operations in September. Military Convoys, Checkpoints Among Targets In a separate statement covering September 14 to 23, the BLA claimed to have carried out 25 operations across Panjgur, Kech, Kharan, Khuzdar, Mastung, Washuk and Nushki. The group alleged that 18 Pakistani military personnel and members of alleged state-backed armed groups were killed during these operations. Its claimed targets included military convoys, checkpoints, surveillance infrastructure, supply routes and government installations. The BLA also claimed that its fighters temporarily seized control of certain areas and government facilities. The attacks have unfolded alongside continuing counter-insurgency operations by Pakistani security forces against separatist groups in Balochistan. Balochistans Worsening Security Crisis Balochistan has witnessed a prolonged separatist insurgency, with the BLA among the principal armed groups fighting the Pakistani state. The group has repeatedly targeted security personnel, government installations and infrastructure projects linked to the Pakistani government and foreign investment. In August 2025, the United States had designated the BLA as a Foreign Terrorist Organisation, citing its involvement in attacks against security forces and civilians in Pakistan. Pakistan's Frontier Corps is recalling retired personnel to address a growing manpower crunch, rising militant attacks, and mounting security challenges in Balochistan. Retired soldiers have been asked to report to their former units for re-enlistment.

They were identified as Momin Mirja, 56; a three-year-old boy; Abdul Rehman, 28; Devruddin, 28; Salma, 50; Chote, 34; Sakina, 35; and Samad, 30. Among the deceased reported earlier was a girl aged around 12 years, whose identity was yet to be ascertained. Another deceased was identified as Gulafsa, 21, who was approximately four months pregnant. The identity and details of another deceased child were also yet to be ascertained. Rescue Operations Underway Rescue machinery has been deployed at the site, with ambulances, Delhi Fire Service personnel, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) officials and personnel from other agencies involved in the operation. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Shahdara Rajendra Prasad Meena said the collapsed structure was a four-storey building and confirmed that rescue operations were underway. We received information at 3.40 pm. This is a four-storey building, which is 25 square yards in area. So far, 7 people have been rescued. They are out of danger. The rescue operation is ongoing. All agencies are present at the scene. Ambulances and Delhi Fire Service staff are deployed. MCD officials, DM, and everyone are present at the scene," Meena said. Senior Fire Officer Manish Kumar said some people were believed to be trapped underneath the debris. Our control room received information at 3.30 pm. It is being said that some people are trapped underneath. Rescue operations are ongoing," he said. DM Ajay Kumar said witnesses at the site reported that demolition work was being carried out at an adjacent building. He said the demolition work may have involved machinery that caused vibrations, which could have affected the collapsed structure. Around 3.15 pm, a four-story building located right at the corner collapsed. It covered an area of approximately 22 to 25 square yards. Witnesses present at the scene reported that the adjacent building was undergoing demolition work, possibly using machinery that caused vibrations, which impacted this building, causing it to collapse," Ajay Kumar said. He added that around seven or eight people were inside the building at the time and that two to three people could still be trapped under the debris. The rescue operation involves teams from the Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), MCD, CATS and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF). The Delhi Chief Ministers Office said rescue and relief operations were underway and that every effort was being made to safely rescue people trapped under the debris and provide prompt medical assistance to the injured. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed all concerned agencies and officers to maintain close coordination, expedite rescue efforts and ensure all necessary assistance and care for those affected. The CMO said the situation was being continuously monitored. Witnesses at the site reported that demolition work on an adjacent building may have used machinery causing vibrations that impacted the structure, while locals also claimed the building had developed cracks from tremors.

headline: 'Will Examine, Take A Call': CJI Surya Kant Says SC To Soon Decide On Plea To Recall CEC Law Order
content: The plea seeks recall of the September 23 order, which followed a split verdict on whether the challenge to the 2023 law should be heard by a larger Constitution Bench The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it would examine an application seeking recall of its September 23 order referring the challenge to the law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners to a Constitution Bench. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said the court would examine and then take a call" on the application when it was mentioned by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. - Supreme Court To Hear Pleas Seeking Suspension Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Challenging EC Decisions - 'Create Fear In The Minds Of Culprits': SC's 5 Big Observations On Women's Safety In Delhi - 'Let's Be Very Clear': Supreme Court Says It Didn't Approve Modified Form 6, Asks Who Made Changes - Supreme Court To Examine Plea To Recall Split Verdict On Law Governing Appointment Of CEC, ECs The application has been filed by Naman Sherstra, one of the petitioners challenging the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. Why Has Recall Been Sought? The plea seeks recall of the September 23 order passed by a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which followed a split verdict on whether the challenge to the 2023 law should be heard by a larger Constitution Bench. The application raises a potential conflict-of-interest issue involving Justice Sharma. It claims that his son, Siddharth Sharma, has been appearing as standing counsel for the Election Commission of India before the Madhya Pradesh High Court. According to the plea, this association was not disclosed during the five hearings before the bench. The petitioners argue that had they known about it earlier, they could have sought Justice Sharmas recusal. The plea, however, does not allege that Justice Sharma was actually biased or acted in bad faith. Instead, it raises the question of whether the circumstances could create a reasonable apprehension about impartiality. It seeks recall of Justice Sharmas opinion and the common order referring the matter to a Constitution Bench. It does not seek recall of Justice Dattas separate opinion. What Happened On September 23? The controversy stems from a split verdict delivered by Justices Datta and Sharma on September 23. The petitions challenge provisions of the 2023 law that changed the mechanism for appointing the CEC and Election Commissioners. Under the law, the selection committee comprises the prime minister, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union cabinet minister. Justice Datta held that there was no need to refer the challenge to a larger bench and that the issues could be decided on the basis of existing legal principles. Justice Sharma, however, held that the case involved substantial questions of constitutional interpretation and should be heard by a Constitution Bench of at least five judges under Article 145(3) of the Constitution. The split verdict resulted in the matter being placed before the CJI for appropriate directions on the constitution of a larger bench. The latest application is separate from a curative petition filed by another petitioner, Dr Jaya Thakur, which also raises concerns over Justice Sharmas participation in the case. The Supreme Court has clarified that the two proceedings would follow their respective courses. The Supreme Courts latest response does not mean the recall application has been allowed. The CJI has only said the court will examine it and take a decision on whether it should be entertained. The September 23 order resulted from a split verdict by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma on whether petitions challenging the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench.

headline: Shiranthi Rajapaksa arrested: What is case against Sri Lanka's ex-President Mahinda Rajapaksa's wife?
content: corruption authorities arrested the 73-year-old Rajapaksa from Colombo home on 7 September, according to BBC. Rajapaksa is being questionined her over the 10 million rupees ($30,300) of donations from a state bank received by the Siriliya Saviya charity, meant to be spent on a specialised scanner for Colombo's Lady Ridgeway Children's Hospital, news agecies said. Allegations against Rajapaksa point out that such a scanner had already been donated by the Chinese government. The then-head of the bank also was arrested for allegedly circumventing procedures in releasing the money to the charity. The court released him on bail later. Rajapaksa has denied any wrongdoing and says the money has not been appropriated. She returned to Sri Lanka this Monday from Singapore, where she was receiving medical treatment. She had filed a court petition to try to prevent her arrest, but the hearing was set for 12 October. After questioning Rajapaksa at her home police took her before a court, were she was sent for a week-long detension pending investigations. Police then escorted Rajapaksa, who had one eye bandaged from recent surgery, to a vehicle to be taken to a jail, AP reported. The former first couple's son, lawmaker Namal Rajapaksa, also has been detained on charges of bribery. Mahinda Rajapaksa's spokesperson, Manoj Gamage, has said the money is safe in Siriliya's accounts and that no fraud has occurred, BBC reported. Mahinda Rajapaksa served as president of Sri Lanka from 2005 to 2015. Rajapaksa, and his family werre adored by the country's majority ethnic Sinhala Buddhists after he and his brother Gotabhaya Rajapaksa led a military campaign to defeat the now-defunct Tamil Tiger rebels and end a 26-year civil war in the island nation in 2009, during his first term as president. However, his popularity declined after his re-election in 2010 over allegations of bribery, corruption and the stifling of freedoms, leading to his defeat while seeking a third term in 2015. His family had wielded unbridled power, with his son, brothers, nephews and nieces holding top government positions. The family made a comeback in 2019 when security emerged as a key concern following Islamic State-inspired suicide bomb attacks that killed 267 people in churches and hotels on Easter Sunday.Mahinda's brother, Gotabhaya Rajapaksa was elected president later that year. But in 2022, protests broke out across the country as an economic crash brought on by the COVID-19 crisis, a tourism downturn and his economic decisions. Gotabaya Rajapaksa, who was serving as leader at that time, was eventually toppled. In 2024, Aruna Dissanayake, a Marxist member of Parliament from Colombo representing Marxist Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP), defeated prominent names including incumbent President Ranil Wickremesinghe, who finished third with just 17 per cent of the votes and Namal Rajapaksa, son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, who managed less that 3 per cent of votes in the election. Dissanayake became president on an anti-corruption platform in 2024 promising to take action against anyone suspected of corruption in the Rajapaksa family and previous administrations. (With inputs from agencies and BBC)

headline: Trump Pulling Back From Iran? Why Military, Oil, Political Pressures Could Be Making The US Rethink
content: The clearest sign is that while US has abandoned military force, the Trump administration is also increasingly talking about negotiations, concessions and an end to the war. Ever since the US-Israel-Iran war began, US President Donald Trumps Iran policy has been built around the assumption that overwhelming military pressure would force Tehran to back down. This strategy now appears to be running into limits. The clearest sign is that while Washington has abandoned military force, the Trump administration is also increasingly talking about negotiations, concessions and an eventual end to the seven-month war even as it keeps military options on the table. - US-Iran Tensions Rise: Rubio Orders Iranian Envoys Out Of New York As Trump Issues Ultimatum - No Military Solution: Iran Warns Of Stronger Response, Keeps Door Open To Talks - 'They'll Be Hit Very Hard': Trump Warns Iran With Fresh Strikes If Linked To Flydubai Attack - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes A New York Times report described the shift as a broader pattern of retreat, pointing to the withdrawal of 12 B-1 bombers from a US base in Britain. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down the move, with Rubio saying the Pentagon was constantly reallocating resources where they need to be." But the report said the redeployment was another example of Washington pulling back forces that had been positioned as deterrence against Iran. Military Option Becoming Harder To Sustain? The first problem is that a prolonged war is consuming military resources. The US has demonstrated enormous conventional superiority over Iran. American and Israeli strikes have badly damaged Irans military infrastructure and nuclear facilities. But Tehran has shown that it can still impose costs through missiles, drones, maritime attacks and asymmetric tactics. The Washington Post reported this week that US B-1 bombers were moved away from RAF Fairford after intelligence indicated a potential Iranian swarm drone" threat. The episode highlighted how even a militarily weakened Iran can force the US to protect its bases and rethink the positioning of expensive assets. A July New York Times report said Trump had held off on a major escalation partly because of concerns about dwindling US stocks of Patriot and other air-defence interceptors. Washington has abandoned military force and is increasingly talking about negotiations and concessions. The US withdrew 12 B-1 bombers from a US base in Britain. Iran had accumulated an estimated 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to up to 60 percent before US-Israeli strikes. US Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity. The November midterm elections are approaching, creating pressure on the administration. Iran Has Not Capitulated The second problem is that military strikes have not produced the political outcome Washington wanted. Irans conventional capabilities may have been severely damaged, but Tehran has not simply accepted US demands. The nuclear question remains particularly difficult. Before the US-Israeli strikes, Iran had accumulated an estimated 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to up to 60 per cent, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency. Reuters reported this week that the whereabouts of a significant portion of that material remains unclear, while Iran has yet to allow inspectors to return to bombed sites. That leaves Washington with an uncomfortable choice of whether it should continue bombing in the hope of eliminating Irans nuclear capability, or negotiate an arrangement that places verifiable limits on it. Vances New Formulation In a recent interview, US Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful" reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity for the war to end. He questioned why Tehran would need uranium enriched to 60 per cent if it had no intention of developing a nuclear weapon. If you dont want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 per cent enriched fuel," Vance said. At the beginning of the conflict, Trumps position was presented much more starkly that Iran should have no enrichment. Vances current formulation instead focuses on a meaningful" reduction in enrichment capacity. This appeared to represent a softening of Washingtons earlier demand for zero enrichment. That does not mean Trump has suddenly accepted an Iranian nuclear programme. It suggests that Washington may be moving from an absolute demand towards a negotiable threshold. But Will Iran Agree? There is another reason the strategy is shifting: Iran and the US are negotiating from fundamentally different starting points. Washington wants nuclear concessions. Tehran has focused heavily on the US naval blockade, sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has sought guarantees that the fighting will end, sanctions and restrictions will be lifted and frozen assets released before fully reopening the strategic waterway. This creates a classic diplomatic deadlock as Washington wants Iran to concede first, but Tehran wants Washington to make the first move. Iranian officials have also insisted that recognition of its right to enrich uranium remains a red line, making the gap between the two sides substantial. Trumps Iran war has also become a domestic political problem. The November midterm elections are approaching, while higher energy prices and the wider economic consequences of the conflict are creating pressure on the administration. The Atlantic reported that the White House has been weighing military options even before the elections, but that officials are divided over whether renewed strikes would actually improve Trumps political position. Trump himself has continued to threaten further action while simultaneously signalling that the war could soon end. On Wednesday, he said the conflict would end very soon" and predicted oil prices would fall sharply once it did. The Trump administration is not necessarily giving up on Iran. It may instead be recognising that maximum military pressure has limits, and that the quickest way to turn battlefield pressure into a political outcome could now be through a negotiated settlement. For Trump, the challenge is finding a deal he can present as victory rather than retreat. For Iran, the challenge is deciding how much it can concede without appearing to have surrendered under American pressure. Prolonged military conflict has consumed significant US resources, such as dwindling stocks of Patriot air-defense interceptors and the need to reposition B-1 bombers away from potential Iranian drone threats. Additionally, domestic political pressures ahead of the November midterms and rising energy prices are pushing the administration to reconsider maximum military pressure.

headline: Isaias Poses Risk to US Energy Output at Category 2 Strength
content: The first Atlantic hurricane of the season is forecast to reach the US Gulf Coast Friday, threatening damaging winds, flooding and potential disruptions to energy production after an otherwise quiet storm season for the region. Tropical Storm Isaias is expected to grow into a strong Category 2 hurricane in the coming days, with top winds of 110 miles per hour, the US National Hurricane Center said in an 11 a.m. New York time advisory. The current forecast takes the storm well east of major oil platforms and natural gas pipelines off the coast of Louisiana and Texas. That track is partly based on guidance from newer, AI-enabled storm models. But more conventional models, typically based on physics equations, have shown the system tacking toward eastern Louisiana, said Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher at the University of Miami. That trajectory would put the storm closer to energy assets near New Orleans. Theres a little bit of wiggle room, McNoldy said. Risk modeler Chuck Watson of Enki Research said in a blog post Wednesday morning that effects from Isaias could extend eastward to Pensacola, Florida, and Eglin Air Force base in the western Florida panhandle before the storm collapses. If that comes to pass, Watson said potential damages and economic impacts could exceed $6 billion. The storm is poised to undergo rapid intensification in the next day or so as it runs through near-record-warm water and moist air. Though the storm could weaken again before landfall, NHC forecaster Eric Blake wrote Wednesday that it will likely grow in size putting more communities in the path of damaging winds and rains. Isaias arrives at a precarious time for oil markets. Amid strain from the war in Iran, theres little cushion for disruptions to diesel production, the workhorse fuel used by trucks, trains, industry and for heating. A shift westward could bring more offshore production and Gulf Coast energy infrastructure into the storms path. As of late Wednesday morning, hurricane watches and storm surge alerts had been posted from Mississippi to Florida. As much as 7 feet of water could push inland on top of high tide, the center said. Chevron Corp. is evacuating non-essential personnel from its Gulf platforms as a precaution. No changes to production or operations are expected at this time, the company said. As of Tuesday, roughly 9.24% of Gulf oil production and 3.36% of natural gas production had been shut in ahead of the storm, according to data published by the federal Marine Minerals Administration. Forecasters have warned that the risk of damaging winds is rising along the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and Mississippi. Heavy rains are expected to extend for miles, bringing a threat of urban flooding and isolated river flooding in the US Southeast. Isaias was situated 540 miles south-southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi River Wednesday morning. By Thursday, its expected to grow into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season a milestone normally reached in the second week of August. This Atlantic season has lagged well behind the usual pace, with eight named storms, none of which became hurricanes. By early October, an average season typically has produced about 11 named storms, including five hurricanes and two major hurricanes. Strengthening El Nio conditions have increased wind shear that helped suppress activity across the basin. Shear occurs when winds change speed or direction at different altitudes, disrupting a storms structure. With assistance from Brian K. Sullivan, Lucia Kassai, Joe Wertz and Mary Hui. 2026 Bloomberg L.P. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

content: Some Israeli officials said discussions about a renewed US offensive have intensified, although they played down the likelihood of such an operation before the elections. The United States military has been instructed to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, even as President Donald Trump has yet to make a final decision on whether to launch fresh strikes, according to a report published by Axios. The Pentagon directed US Central Command several days ago to complete preparations for potential military operations, according to the officials. - US Deploys Third Aircraft Carrier With 10,000 More Troops To Middle East After Trump's Warning - Watching It Very Closely: US Urges Russia To Share More Information On Plague Death - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes - 'They'll Be Hit Very Hard': Trump Warns Iran With Fresh Strikes If Linked To Flydubai Attack The order did not set a timeline for any attack, but US and Israeli officials said the possibility of renewed combat remains under consideration. If Washington decides to resume the war, the campaign could involve extensive strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, power plants and nuclear facilities, the officials said, as per Axios. Also Read: Has Trump Softened On Iran? JD Vances Shift On Uranium Enrichment Sparks Fresh Questions Attack Before November Elections? The fresh attacks can be carried out before the US midterm elections and probably a week before the Israeli elections, reported Axios, citing US and Israeli sources. The Pentagon directed US Central Command to prepare for potential military operations against Iran. The order did not set a timeline for any attack. Potential targets include Iranian energy infrastructure, power plants, and nuclear facilities. A renewed US offensive could push up oil prices and affect November midterm elections. President Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about Iran. The timing of any escalation could also carry political implications. As per Axios, a renewed US offensive within the next three to four weeks could push up oil prices and potentially affect the November midterm elections. The Departments job is to develop and present military options to the President," a Pentagon official told Axios. The possibility of strikes before the elections is being weighed, although Israeli officials said they do not consider it the most likely scenario. Some Israeli officials said discussions about a renewed US offensive have intensified, although they played down the likelihood of such an operation before the elections. The discussion about possible resumption of major combat operations in Iran has increased. The chances of it happening before the elections is not high but we dont rule it out. After the midterms, the chances of it happening increase significantly," a second Israeli official said. Also Read: Iran Has Lost Complete Control Of Strait Of Hormuz: Rubio Says Tehrans Economy In Total Freefall Trump Holds All Cards A White House official, meanwhile, said Trump retains the ability to act at any time. The U.S. is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iranian economy collapsing. Iran has been decimated, and things will go one of two ways: the easy way or the hard way," the official said. President Trump holds all the cards and will do whatever is best for the United States," he added. The developments come as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran remain stalled. Qatari mediators are still awaiting an Iranian response to a US counterproposal that includes demands for concessions on Tehrans nuclear programme. Trump, Netanyahu Discuss Iran Trumps national security team met for several hours at Camp David on Friday to discuss the war and broader foreign policy issues. An Israeli official said Iran was among the subjects discussed, including the possibility of restarting major combat operations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said after the meeting that the discussions were focused on long-term" foreign policy planning. Trump also spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday, marking their second conversation in a matter of days after a prolonged period in which the two leaders had limited contact. A US official said the conversation included discussion of remembrance and respect for the victims of the October 7 massacre." The call came after Netanyahu convened his national security team for a meeting on Iran, according to an Israeli official. Netanyahu had also spoken with Rubio on Monday. If military operations resume, US and Israeli forces are expected to coordinate closely, with Israels military likely to participate in the campaign. Iran To Launch Offensive? The officials also warned that Irans leadership, which they described as increasingly desperate and paranoid, could potentially launch an attack of its own rather than wait for another US-Israeli offensive. They said Iran has already been caught off guard by two attacks and would be determined to avoid a third surprise strike. Any renewed war could also have repercussions for Israels political landscape. The heightened security environment could benefit Netanyahu by limiting the ability of political rivals to target him during the final phase of the campaign, while a renewed conflict or prolonged state of emergency could reshape the electoral debate. If Washington decides to resume the war, the military campaign could involve extensive strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, power plants, and nuclear facilities.

headline: 'I Could Have Done Very Bad Things': Trump Targets Hillary Clinton, Biden, Obama; Says They Impeached Him Twice
content: Donald Trump said he could have done very bad things to Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Barack Obama, citing respect for the presidency. US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he could have done very bad things" to former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and former Presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, but claimed he chose not to because he believed the office of the presidency had to be treated with respect. Trump made the remarks during an Oval Office event on October 7, while responding to a question about his repeated warning that Democrats could impeach him if they regain control of Congress in the November midterm elections. - Trump Ditches Taxpayer Funds, Says He'll Fund Midterm Ads With His Own Money After Flak - Im Getting Good At It: Trump On Possible Third Impeachment If Democrats Win US Midterm Elections - 'Shove It Up Their A**': Trump's Profane Remarks Targeting Democrats Raises Eyebrows At Ohio Rally - US Deploys Third Aircraft Carrier With 10,000 More Troops To Middle East After Trump's Warning A reporter asked Trump what Democrats would impeach him for. Trump said Democrats dont know," referring to comments he said he had seen from lawmakers who could not identify what they would impeach him over. He then turned to his Democratic political rivals. With that being said, I could have done very bad things to Hillary Clinton. I could have done very, very bad things to Joe Biden. I could have done very bad things to Barack Hussein Obama," Trump said. I thought it was inappropriate to do so, because you have to treat the office of the presidency with respect," he added. Trump did not specify what he meant by very bad things." Later in the same exchange, however, he said he had had my shot and still do" at Biden, Clinton and Obama, adding that people had told him, lets go get them," but that he had declined because you cant do that to the presidency." Trump said he could have done very bad things to Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Barack Obama, but chose not to out of respect for the presidency. He made the remarks while discussing the possibility of Democrats impeaching him again, saying, They impeached me twice. Trump said he still believes he could do whatever I want but argued that the presidency must be treated with respect. Trump then connected his comments to the two impeachment proceedings he faced during his first presidency. Then I found out that they impeached me twice," Trump said. And I certainly, even to this moment, I have, I can do whatever I want, if I want. Theyve done some very bad things." Trump also described the presidency as a very sacred position" and said it had to be treated properly. Trump was impeached twice by the Democratic-controlled House during his first term. The first impeachment, in December 2019, involved charges of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress stemming from his dealings with Ukraine. The Senate acquitted him on both articles in February 2020. The second impeachment came in January 2021, when the House charged Trump with incitement of insurrection following the January 6 attack on the US Capitol. The Senate again acquitted him in February 2021. The Houses official historical record lists both impeachments and the subsequent Senate acquittals. Trump Has Repeatedly Raised Prospect Of Third Impeachment Trump has increasingly invoked the possibility of a third impeachment as Republicans campaign to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections. In January, Trump told House Republicans that they needed to win the midterms because, if they did not, Democrats would find a reason to impeach me." He also raised the prospect during his campaign appearances earlier this month. According to an Associated Press report, Trump told supporters in Oklahoma that if Republicans did not win, Democrats could end up impeaching him, adding that he had become very good at beating them in impeachment." The issue has also featured in preparations for a possible Democratic takeover of the House. AP reported last month that House Democrats were preparing an extensive oversight agenda if they regained the majority, with impeachment remaining among the constitutional tools they had not ruled out. Democratic leaders, however, have emphasised investigations and oversight rather than committing to a third impeachment of Trump. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries has said Democrats have neither ruled impeachment in nor ruled it out, saying any action would be guided by facts, law and the Constitution. During an Oval Office event on October 7, US President Donald Trump claimed he could have done "very bad things" to Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden, and Barack Obama, but chose not to because he believed the presidency had to be treated with respect.

headline: Texas carries out first execution in U.S. since Christa Pike's failed lethal injection
content: A Texas man who fatally shot a convenience store clerk was put to death Wednesday evening (October 7, 2026), becoming the 30th person executed in the U.S. this year and the first since Tennessee's failed attempt to administer a lethal injection to Christa Pike. Jamaal Howard, 46, was pronounced dead at 8.03 p.m. on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) after receiving a fatal dose of pentobarbital at the state prison in Huntsville. He was convicted of killing of Vickie Swartout, 42, in a 2000 store robbery caught on surveillance video. Asked by the warden if he had a final statement, Howard apologised profusely to members of his victim's family who watched through window a few from him. Texas has executed six people so far in 2026 and plans two more executions scheduled this year. Earlier Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Howard's attorneys unsuccessfully sought to block the execution by arguing that he was intellectual disabled and that he faced the same risks similar to those in Pike's case because both states use pentobarbital for lethal injections. Ms. Pike's lawyers are seeking more information about what went wrong after the 50-year-old woman survived two doses of pentobarbital on Sept. 30. Her lawyers said she was unconscious at a hospital after the attempt but was awake and speaking by Tuesday (October 6, 2026). Inmate remained chatty' on drive to the death chamber On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Howard was chatty during the 45-mile (70-kilometre) drive from the death row prison to the Huntsville Unit, where executions are carried out, said Amanda Hernandez, a spokesperson for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice. He made small talk with the officers through the whole trip before being taken to a holding cell near the death chamber, she said. He was asking questions and was very engaged in the process. Store clerk's killing was caught on surveillance video Howard was convicted of capital murder in the killing of Swartout, who was shot once in the chest during the robbery. Evidence presented at trial included surveillance video showing Howard shooting Swartout. Howard, who was 20 at the time, took USD 114 and a carton of cigarettes from the store in Silsbee, a small, rural town about 100 miles (160 kilometres) northeast of Houston, according to court records. Man's attorneys filed late appeals bidding to stop execution In bidding to halt Howard's execution, his attorneys filed a motion before the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals raising concerns about the quality of Texas' execution drugs. The court denied that request and a second filing involving the drugs without comment. His attorneys also argued unsuccessfully to the US Supreme Court that Howard's execution should be halted because he was intellectually disabled. The Supreme Court in 2002 had barred the execution of intellectually disabled people. But it has given states some discretion in how they determine such disabilities. The state told the court that Howard's lawyers did not present evidence that would show he meets the requirements for a claim of intellectual disability. The high court late Wednesday declined to intervene, without comment, clearing the way for the execution. Florida leads the nation in executions this year Florida has carried out 16 executions so far this year, the most of any state. Most states that allow executions use lethal injection as their primary method. Tennessee's Republican Gov. Bill Lee has halted the one remaining execution that was scheduled to be carried out in his state this year.

headline: Hedgehog Wins Contest to Replace Historical Figures on UK Cash
content: Historical figures including the UKs wartime prime minister Winston Churchill will be replaced on the countrys banknotes by images of an Atlantic puffin, a barn owl, a buff-tailed bumblebee and a European hedgehog, the Bank of England said. The decision to introduce the animals drew criticism earlier in the year, particularly from right-leaning politicians. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called it the definition of woke. Thats despite nature having emerged as the most popular theme in a public consultation the Bank held on refreshing its money last year. Among the 44,000 responses to that survey, historical figures ranked third. The BOE has proceeded with the plan and this week revealed the four creatures picked following a second consultation that took into account the views of wildlife experts and around half a million members of the public. We have chosen four distinct and inspiring animals that not only showcase the great variety of wildlife we have in the UK but will also enhance the security of our banknotes, said Victoria Cleland, the chief cashier who announced her departure in the summer. The production of the new notes will also try to make the cash more resistant to counterfeiting. A decision has yet to be made about which animal will adorn which denomination, while the process to introduce new notes will take a few years, the Bank said. Churchill has been on the 5 note for the last decade, while other notes feature the author Jane Austen, painter JMW Turner and Second World War code-breaker Alan Turing. On the reverse side all notes show the monarch King Charles III. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Petrol, diesel prices today, October 8: Check rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and more
content: Indian refiners are facing the impact of disruptions to global oil supplies. However, state-run OMC retailers have so far maintained a freeze on petrol and diesel prices. India's largest private fuel retailer, meanwhile, increased petrol prices by 5 per litre and diesel prices by 3 per litre on Saturday. Nayara Energy was also the first fuel retailer in India to pass on the impact of rising international oil prices to consumers after energy supplies were disrupted following the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February. State-run OMCs delayed passing on the higher costs until May. Retail petrol and diesel prices were subsequently raised through a series of staggered revisions, resulting in a cumulative increase of around 7.50 per litre for both fuels by the end of May. Petrol and diesel rates across major metros have remained largely unchanged since June. In Mumbai, petrol was priced at 111.21 per litre on October 8, unchanged from the previous day. The petrol rate in the financial capital has seen only marginal movement in recent days, fluctuating between 111.18 and 111.21 per litre. Global oil prices rose on Thursday as concerns over supplies from the key Middle East-producing region intensified amid an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures rose $1.33, or 1.33%, to $101.53 a barrel by 0116 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained $1.11, or 1.26%, to $89.39. Oil prices had settled lower on Wednesday after the International Energy Agency agreed to accelerate the release of oil stocks and prioritise diesel supplies under a plan launched in March. Governments are seeking to address record fuel prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war. However, risks to oil shipments through the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have increased in October as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month. Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz carried shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies. In the latest incident, a tanker north of Qatar was hit by multiple projectiles, resulting in casualties, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Wednesday. "In the past, such attacks have resulted in a reduction in shipments from the Persian Gulf. This time around, producers appear to be willing to take the risk of their vessels being damaged, as there is no alternative way to get their oil to international markets," Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at bank ANZ, said in a note on Thursday. Hynes said the IEA's oil release would likely comprise barrels that were already part of the group's original 400-million-barrel release plan announced at the start of the Middle East conflict. This means it does not appear to represent an additional draw on strategic inventories. "Ultimately, strategic stock releases can augment supply flows temporarily but do not create new production capacity," he said. US inventory data also supported oil prices. Crude stockpiles in the world's largest oil consumer and producer fell by more than expected, while diesel inventories declined marginally. Crude inventories dropped by 3.2 million barrels to 424.1 million barrels in the week ended October 2, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a decline of 1.7 million barrels. Distillate fuel inventories, which include diesel and jet fuel, fell by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels. The inventory level remains well below levels typically recorded at this time of the year over the past five years.
