headline: Organisations engaged in religious conversion shall be denied FCRA registration: Madras HC
content: A Division Bench of the Madras High Court (Madurai) has said religious organisations, whose activities would not affect the nations secular fabric and social amity, are entitled to obtain Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) registration. But organisations engaged in converting people of one religious faith to another shall be denied FCRA registration. The court was hearing the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed by Kanzeon Public Charitable Trust in Kodaikanal in Dindigul district. The appellant, a trust founded in 2021 and registered under Section 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961, sought certificate of registration under the provisions of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The appellants application was rejected. Challenging the same, the appeal was filed. The appellant submitted the trust had established a Zen Meditation Centre at Kodaikanal and its activities cannot be labelled as religious. On its part, the Centre submitted the policy of the government is to check the inflow of foreign funds that may be deployed for carrying out conversion and other activities which would harm the secular fabric of the country. In the instant case, the author of the trust was an ordained Christian priest addressed as Rev. Fr. Ama Samy SJ. A Division Bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and M.D. Sumathi said, One cannot forget the fact that Christianity is a messianic religion. Their theological and religious mission is to bring everyone within the fold of Jesus Christ. There is a saying a leopard will not change its spots. Unlike Hinduism which is inclusive, the Abrahamic religions are inherently exclusive. The devout Jews, Christians and Muslims believe that theirs is the one true and complete revelation because that is what their Holy books say of themselves. Rule 9 of FCR Rules, 2011, states the application must be in Form FC-3A. Form FC-3A requires the applicant to disclose the nature of the organisation. The appellant trust claims to The judges said te appellant need not have been so coy. Section 12 of the FCRA bars only an unregistered religious organisation from accepting foreign contributions. An organisation having a definite religious programme is entitled to apply for a certificate of registration from the central government under Sections 11 and 12 of the Act. But one has to make a clean breast of everything. One cannot keep any card up ones sleeve. This is no game of hide and seek, they added. It is necessary to make a clear distinction between a religious organisation and a cultural or educational entity. An organisation primarily engaged in the systematic teaching of Vedanta, the Bhagavad Gita, the Upanishads, Yoga and allied Indian Knowledge Systems through structured classes, residential courses, publications, research and preservation of manuscripts cannot be classified as religious institutions. Indian Knowledge Systems would fall under the category of education or culture, the bench said. Zen philosophy is of Chinese origin. Organisations like the appellant trust cannot therefore claim any right to be registered under FCRA. We are a pluralist nation. Unlike the USA, we are not a melting pot but a salad bowl, a beautiful metaphor credited to Justice Ruma Pal. This status quo would be upset, if one religious group gains ascendancy, the court said. If foreign funds are freely allowed inside to facilitate conversion activities, the sovereignty of the nation would be imperilled. We hasten to clarify that we do not accuse the appellant of having any such agenda. Section 12(4)(a)(ii) of the Act specifically refers to conversion from one religious faith to another. This provision applies to all religious organisations. A fundamentalist Hindu Organisation engaged in Ghar Wapsi cannot be registered under FCRA. The statutory regime which was put in place during UPA rule (2010) is intended to subserve secular objects, the bench said. When the statute envisages a frank disclosure of all the details, any misrepresentation would entail rejection of the application itself. Though the applicant is engaged in religious programmes, they wrongly projected themselves as non-religious. That is why, the respondent authority had to say Illa Samy (No Sir) to Rev. Fr. Ama Samy (which name literally translates as Yes), the court said. It said an application seeking FCRA registration should correctly disclose the nature of the applicant. Failure to do so will result in rejection of the application. Even if all the details are in order, the authority is still at liberty to negative the request. This is because there is no right as such to receive foreign contributions. It can at best be a privilege. The authority must however correctly classify the applicants. Persons and organisations engaged in upholding the civilisational heritage of India have to be classified as educational or cultural. If the programmes of the applicant pertain to worship and rituals, they will fall under the religious category, the court said and dismissed the appeal.

headline: IMF reaches staff deal with Pakistan, potentially unlocking $1.2 billion
content: The International Monetary Fund has reached a staff-level agreement with Pakistan on reviews of some of its lending programs, potentially unlocking about $1.21 billion in financing pending board approval, the fund said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). If the board approves the deal, Pakistan could access about $1 billion under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and $210 million under the climate-focused Resilience and Sustainability Facility, bringing total disbursements under the two programs to around $5.7 billion. Pakistan remains reliant on external financing to bolster foreign exchange reserves and meet debt repayments. Supported by the EFF, the authorities have successfully navigated the impact of the West Asia conflict, and strong policies have helped preserve macroeconomic stability," the fund said. Risks remain elevated, however, due to geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions and trade disruptions, the IMF said. Pakistan is the most vulnerable major Asia-Pacific economy to a prolonged West Asia conflict, given its dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and financing support from the region, Ahmad Mobeen, principal economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said earlier this year.

headline: Average 73% decline in wildlife population sizes between 1970 and 2022: WWF report
content: The average size of monitored vertebrate mammals, fish, birds and amphibians populations declined 73% over 52 years between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) biennial Living Planet Report, 2026. As part of the Living Planet Index (LPI), average changes in the size of wild populations of vertebrate species are measured over time, tracking variations in relative abundance rather than absolute numbers. This means that the size of these populations fell by, on average, 73% during the assessment period, and it does not reflect the number of individual animals lost, nor the number of populations lost. Habitat loss and degradation, overexploitation of resources, climate change, impact of invasive species, pollution and disease are some of the dominant drivers of changes across ecosystems and wildlife populations, the Living Planet Report stated. The way the world produces and consumes food is the single largest driver of biodiversity loss. The food and agriculture system is the leading cause of habitat destruction, overharvesting, and a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. Even as the report noted the declining trends in wild populations, it also noted that nature can recover if society follows a clear pathway to trigger positive tipping points in the energy, food and finance systems that drive biodiversity loss. The Living Planet Report 2026 is both a stark reminder of the scale of the biodiversity crisis and a message of hope. While the Living Planet Index continues to highlight significant declines in monitored wildlife populations, the report also shows that these declines are not inevitable, said Ravi Singh, Secretary General and CEO, WWF-India. Species recoveries, including those of tigers in India and globally, demonstrate what sustained conservation action, collaboration and long-term commitment can achieve, he added. The LPI, produced by the Zoological Society of London, includes 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species from 1970 to 2022. The strongest declines, 85%, were seen in freshwater ecosystems, followed by terrestrial ecosystems, at 69% and marine ecosystems at 59%. Although the overall trend is negative due to the magnitude of the declining trends, half of the populations included in the LPI are stable or increasing, WWF said. The report highlights recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and southern African elephants, which, it said, demonstrate that targeted conservation interventions can deliver proven results. The report noted rise in global wild tiger numbers between 2010 and 2025 from 3,200 to around 5,700 individuals.

headline: India plans subject-expert inspectors for homoeopathic medicine manufacturing units
content: India plans to amend its drug regulation rules to recognize homoeopathic degrees as the requisite qualification for inspectors overseeing plants that manufacture these alternative medicines, aiming to ensure safety and quality through domain expertise, according to two government officials and two documents reviewed by Mint. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation will amend Rule 49 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, to recognize a degree in homoeopathy or specialization in homoeopathic pharmacy for appointments under Section 21 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

headline: Govt weighs export floor price for cotton yarn to ensure domestic supplies
content: In a first, the government is vetting a proposal to levy a minimum export price (MEP) on cotton yarn to ensure local availability and protect domestic textile manufacturers from a sharp rise in raw-material costs, two people aware of the matter said. The move comes against the backdrop of a surge in cotton yarn prices following US restrictions on cotton originating from Chinas Xinjiang region, where Washington alleges that Uyghurs and other ethnic minorities are subjected to forced labour.

headline: Attacks on Saudi airports claimed by Houthi rebels kill 3 people, officials say
content: Two attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia claimed by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen killed three people Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Saudi officials said, as the kingdom was pulled deeper into the latest front in the Iran war. The Saudi General Authority for Civil Aviation did not blame any party for the attacks at Abha and Riyadhs King Khalid international airports, but Houthi rebels took credit earlier for the airport strikes. The attack on Abha airport killed Moroccan and Algerian residents and wounded 28 other people, while the attack on King Khalid airport killed a Sudanese national and wounded eight other people, officials said. As Riyadh has been targeted over the past week, new cage-like fences have been erected around fuel tanks and other equipment of the Saudi state-run Aramco oil company near the capitals airport. The kingdom, the worlds top oil exporter, has seen oil and military assets targeted in recent days, posing a threat to crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic has been curtailed due to the Iran war. The spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis, Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, said forces intercepted a ballistic missile north of Riyadh and destroyed a platform in Yemens capital of Sana that had been used to launch attacks on the Saudi capital. The AP could not independently verify these claims. Saudi Arabia and allied Yemeni forces launched a major ground and air offensive aimed at retaking territory that the rebels seized a month ago along Yemens western Red Sea coast and on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Those positions gave the Houthis better surveillance as they pursue a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping. On Monday, officials said forces of the Saudi-led coalition recaptured several key areas around the strait, through which about 12% of global trade transits.

headline: India's 1st High-Altitude Wildlife Safari Begins In Ladakh. Here's How To Experience It
content: Snow leopards remain notoriously difficult to spot. Their pale-grey coats blend almost completely into Ladakh's rocky mountain landscape, and traditional tracking trips can involve hours of scanning distant slopes.

headline: Tanker off Qatar reports hits from multiple projectiles: U.K. maritime agency
content: A tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck "by multiple projectiles", causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). The incident took place 51 nautical miles (94 kilometres) off the coast of the tiny Gulf state, the British agency said, adding that authorities were investigating. It did not specify the origin of the ship. The reported attack on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) was around 500 kilometres (300 miles) from the Strait of Hormuz. Ships in the Gulf and those attempting to transit the strait, the only way in or out of the oil-rich region for vessels, have come under repeated attack since the U.S. and Israel sparked the West Asia war in late February. Iran has blockaded the strait ever since and fired on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings. The United States has set up its own counterblockade of Iranian ports and occasionally fires on vessels linked to Tehran. It has also bombed Iranian targets in retaliation for Tehran's attacks on ships, although there have been no such reported strikes since September 1. Some vessels continue to ply the strait and U.S. media has reported on American efforts to protect ships on a route hugging the coast of Oman. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the war, which began with a massive wave of surprise U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran, have been deadlocked for months. Hormuz is vital to the world economy, with around a fifth of the planet's oil and liquefied natural gas passing through the strait before the war began.

headline: 'We don't distinguish between nations': Coast Guard chief on rescue operations
content: Indian Coast Guard Director General of the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Paramesh Sivamani on Wednesday underscored the forces commitment to saving lives at sea, saying it does not distinguish between nations while carrying out an effective search and rescue (SAR) operation. Speaking to the reporters ahead of the 12th edition of the national level Search and Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) to be conducted off Paradip coast on Thursday, he said several nations look up to India in the event of a crisis. We have enhanced our capacity, redefined the procedure and fine-tuned the standard operating procedure over the years. We have established a very robust system of SAR and all the nations in the Indian Ocean Region look up to Bharat in case there is a crisis or in a volatile situation that requires a SAR, said the ICG chief. Stating that they have built up the SAR capabilities from scratch, Sivamani said they have ensured that the ICGs prowess of executing a good SAR operation is there for a larger good of humanity. Whenever there is a crisis and our ships and aircrafts are required to the spot we do that immediately, he said. During the inaugural event of SAREX, the ICG chief also emphasised that the future of maritime SAR hinges on advanced technological integration, real-time information sharing, and seamless inter-agency synergy. Sivamani stressed the imperative for enhanced vessel tracking, robust distress-alert management, data-driven operational decision-making, and accelerated asset mobilisation. He also underscored that operational lessons derived from past missions and multi-agency exercises must directly translate into heightened mission readiness and response capabilities. The SAREX-2026 exercise will witness participation and observation by 32 delegates from 30 foreign friendly nations. The multi-agency exercise aims to validate operational preparedness, enhance international interoperability, test joint response mechanisms, and foster the exchange of best practices reaffirming the preservation of life at sea as the paramount objective of every mission. The 24th National Maritime Search and Rescue Board meeting was also held on the occasion and it deliberated on strengthening national and international SAR frameworks, recognising that maritime emergencies transcend geographic boundaries and necessitate synchronised coordination among global Rescue Coordination Centres and maritime safety agencies. Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth, who inaugurated the event, called upon all participating agencies and international partners to reaffirm their shared commitment to safeguarding lives at sea and to strengthen the spirit of cooperation that underpins effective search and rescue across the region. Invoking the principle of One Earth, One Family, One Future, he said collective efforts can build a safer, more resilient and more cooperative maritime community. Speaking on Indias efforts to strengthen its search and rescue capabilities, Seth said Indias journey in Satellite-Aided Search and Rescue has progressively evolved from Low Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (LEOSAR) to Geostationary Search and Rescue (GEOSAR) and now towards Medium Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (MEOSAR).

headline: US Forces in Okinawa Face Curfew After Marine's Arrest
content: Bloomberg) -- The US Forces in Okinawa paused operations for 48 hours starting at noon on Wednesday and imposed a month-long curfew on military personnel, following the arrest of a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a Japanese woman. US military personnel on Japans southernmost island of Okinawa will cease operations to undergo training on standards and discipline and will be prohibited from leaving their bases to socialize or from consuming alcohol, according to a statement. Serving on Okinawa comes with responsibility, the statement read. Every interaction with our neighbors either builds or undermines the trust that is essential to our team. When that trust is damaged, it affects the strength of our alliance and the security of this region. Following the operational pause, military personnel will be subject to a midnight curfew for a 30-day period, the statement added. Local police arrested a 20-year-old US serviceman on suspicion of killing 39-year-old Anna Yagi early Saturday at a hotel in the city of Naha. National broadcaster NHK said the serviceman denied the charges, citing police investigators. The incident threatens to reignite local opposition to the US military presence on Okinawa, where around 30,000 American service members are based. The rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US troops in 1995 triggered major protests, and serious crimes involving US military personnel since then have periodically stoked opposition to the American military presence on the island. Ahead of a meeting Wednesday with Okinawa Governor Genta Koja, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered condolences to the bereaved family and said her government had lodged a strong protest with Washington. Japan demanded full cooperation with the investigation, strict disciplinary action against US military personnel, thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents, and appropriate support for the victims family, she said. As a result, the US side announced new measures, Takaichi said. We understand that the US side intends to further scrutinize its code of conduct going forward. Koja earlier met with Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi in Tokyo. Ahead of those meetings, Koja said, This is the result of a failure of human rights training by the US military, given this happened despite repeated requests from the Okinawan side to ensure similar cases are prevented. Koja became governor only last month after a campaign in which the long-running dispute over US bases took a back seat to other issues. I feel deep frustration that such a heinous and deplorable crime has occurred, and an American serviceman was arrested in connection to it, Koizumi said. I hope to push forward discussions between Japan and the US on what measures will be effective in preventing such cases in the future. (Adds meeting between Okinawa Governor Koja and Takaichi.) headline: Second day, second Opposition protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, detentions again
content: Pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Opposition leaders staged a protest for the second consecutive day in the heart of the Capital Wednesday before they were stopped and detained by police. The Samajwadi Party, however, stayed away from the INDIA bloc protest. On Tuesday, after the Opposition protest, Congress allies had expressed concern that it had been turned into a Rahul Gandhi show. The SP skipped the lunch hosted Wednesday by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath. From the restaurant, Opposition MPs, including Gandhi, Mamata TMCs Derek OBrien, CPI(M)s John Brittas and CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, boarded three buses to head towards Jantar Mantar. Over the next couple of hours, as the buses crawled forward, Congress workers walked alongside. Police, however, blocked the way and the march came to a halt near Windsor Place. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women leaders. Congress MP along with Rahul Gandhi detained during protest against CEC near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Wednesday. (EXPRESS PHOTO BY PRAVEEN KHANNA) Later, police forcibly removed Congress workers and detained the Gandhi siblings and other senior leaders. Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan was among those who had joined the protest. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us, Gandhi said. He thanked all INDIA bloc MPs standing firm in defence of our democracy in Parliament, outside on the streets, and today near Jantar Mantar. The Congress called for more protests at state, district and block levels on Thursday. The party also played down the absence of SP MPs from Wednesdays lunch meeting, saying they had left Delhi the night before or early Wednesday. The SPs absence, it is learnt, also came up during the discussions over lunch. Later in the day, INDIA bloc leaders reached out to the SP, which agreed to send its representatives for the protest Thursday, sources said. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge coming out of Sagar Ratna with Congress leaders and other party leaders, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (EXPRESS PHOTO BY PRAVEEN KHANNA) Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, said all alliance parties were invited to the lunch. But the decision for lunch had been taken late last night and communicated. It was therefore natural that some parties could not be represented. There is needless comment in some sections of the media on it. INDIA and other Opposition parties are united and stand in solidarity against Vote Chori, SIR and Delimitation, he said. Sources in the SP said the party leadership and the MPs were upset with the Gandhi siblings for stealing the show Tuesday. It is true that we are not happy with the poor coordination by the Congress regarding the protest at Akashvani Bhavan. It was supposed to be a joint protest by the INDIA bloc, and not by the Gandhis. The next big election in the country is in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party has a bigger stake than the Congress. Akhilesh Yadav raised the concerns about SIR in Uttar Pradesh more aggressively and effectively, while the Congress leadership only took symbolic steps during the SIR in UP earlier this year. But the Congress in Delhi tried to portray that only it was serious about SIR, an SP leader said. The developments are playing out against a key backdrop: the UP Assembly elections early next year. In the politically significant heartland state, the SP and the Congress are allies and as the polls approach, a tussle over seat distribution has begun.

headline: Up to 30 per cent of cotton area under 'illegal' GM hybrids, finds study
content: More than a quarter of the total area cultivated under cotton in India comprises illegal hybrids incorporating unapproved genetically modified (GM) traits, including resistance to glyphosate herbicide. Out of the 114.8 lakh hectares (lh) area sown under cotton by Indian farmers in 2025-26, an estimated 26.2-29 lh, i.e. 24-30%, was of hybrids containing unauthorised herbicide-tolerant (HT) or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) genes, according to a field-based study commissioned by the Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) and National Seed Association of India (NSAI). India currently allows farmers to grow GM cotton hybrids/ varieties containing only two genes cry1Ac and cry2Ab that are isolated from Bt, a soil bacterium. These genes code for proteins toxic to certain bollworm insect pests. But the FSII-NSAI study shows farmers are also planting the seeds of hybrids that contain cp4-epsps and Vip3A genes. Both these are alien genes, whose harbouring in any crops has not been approved by the government. The cp4-epsps gene, sourced from another soil-dwelling agrobacterium, makes cotton plants tolerant to glyphosate. This herbicide cannot be sprayed on normal cotton, as the chemical does not distinguish between the crop and weeds. The Vip3A gene is derived from Bt, but works differently from the cry1Ac/ cry2Ab genes and is said to effectively control a broader spectrum of bollworm larvae. The FSSI-NSAI study has been based on 227 geo-tagged seed/ leaf samples collected from fields of 984 farmers across 16 districts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh (AP) and Rajasthan. The 16 hotspot districts were identified using a combination of secondary data sources, including glyphosate sale trends, farmer interactions and seed market intelligence. The testing of the samples for gene identification was conducted using dipstick/ lateral flow assays and ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay). We found the HT cp4-epsps gene to be present in 72.69% of the field samples, with this as high as 88.64% for Telangana, 70.92% for Maharashtra, 62.86% for AP and 57.14% for Rajasthan. It indicates widespread adoption of HT technology by farmers for weed management, despite the government not authorising this GM trait, said Bhagirath Choudhary, director of the Jodhpur (Rajasthan)-based South Asia Biotechnology Centre that undertook the study. The demand for the unapproved HT gene technology has been driven by the acute shortage of labour and high manual weeding costs. Farmers have decisively shifted towards glyphosate-based weed management enabled by (illegal) HTBt cotton technology. They are typically applying 2-3 sprays per season that costs Rs. 750-850 per acre, as against Rs. 12,000-15,000 through manual weeding, Choudhary noted. Laboratory analysis of samples apart, the decline in sales of legal Bt cotton hybrid seeds from 596 lakh packets in 2022-23 to 463 lakh packs in 2025-26 (each packet contains 450 grams of seeds) is also proof of the high acceptance of HT hybrids by farmers. This has been accompanied by a significant 29% jump in imports of glyphosate, from 27,721 kilolitres in 2024-25 to 35,642 kilolitres in 2025-26. The FSSI-NSAI study has estimated the unauthorised HTBt seed market in India to have expanded from around 35 lakh packets in 2017-18 to 82-88 lakh packets in 2025-26. At an average price of Rs. 1,000 per packet, this market would be conservatively valued at Rs. 820-880 crore. Equally interesting is the planting of cotton hybrids expressing the Vip3 Bt gene. We found 53.74% of our 227 field samples testing positive for this next-generation insect-resistance gene. Its presence was 58.16% in Maharashtra, 54.29% in AP, 57.14% in Rajasthan and 38.64% in Telangana. The driver here seems to be effectiveness against pink bollworm, with the first-generation Bt hybrids becoming vulnerable to this insect pest, said Choudhary. Simply put, the market for illegal GM cotton seeds is growing, with both farmers and a sophisticated supplier network bypassing the countrys established biosafety and regulatory approval system.

headline: Pakistan's unwarranted references to Kashmir part of propaganda: Harivansh Singh at IPU meet
content: Exercising Indias right to reply in response to certain references made by Pakistani delegation on J&K at an international forum in Tanzania, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh Narayan Singh on Wednesday said that Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India, and that Pakistan has no locus standi commenting on Indias internal affairs. Speaking at the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) in Arusha, Tanzania, Singh said, We deplore the attempts by a delegation to politicise the forum and to bring in unwarranted references to issues which do not fall within the purview of this forum or meeting. He added that quite habitually, this (Pakistani) delegation attempts to indulge in propaganda and makes baseless allegations against India. The Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh have been, are, and shall always remain integral and inalienable parts of India. No amount of rhetoric and propaganda from any country can override the fact that accession of Jammu & Kashmir to India was completely legal and irrevocable, he said. Pakistan has no local sustainability to comment on Indias internal affairs. In fact, it is Pakistan which is in illegal and forcible occupation of Indias territories that it should vacate, he added. Highlighting the progress Kashmir has seen over the last few years, Singh said, People of Jammu and Kashmir are progressively moving forward on the path of development and democracy. This was evident in a high voter turnout in both the general elections 58.5%, the highest in the last 35 years and 63% in the Assembly elections in 2024. Jammu and Kashmir witnessed a record surge in tourists last year. Harivansh arrived in Arusha on Sunday to head the high-level parliamentary delegation at the 153rd IPU Assembly and associated sessions.

headline: 'It Is About Time': Trump Makes Fresh Nobel Peace Prize Bid, But Doubts Committee Will Oblige
content: Trump claimed he had settled eight wars since returning to office and said his efforts had gone beyond those of previous US presidents. US President Donald Trump has made another public push for the Nobel Peace Prize, saying he believes he deserves the 2026 award while admitting he is unsure whether the Norwegian Nobel Committee will choose him. Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump said the announcement was approaching and suggested he had reason to expect recognition. - 'The Orange Plague': 8.5-Foot Naked, Golden Trump Statue Unveiled At European Parliament - 'Don't Have The Full Picture': WHO Can't Conduct Full Risk Assessment On Russia Plague Reports - Israel Refuses Flydubai's Request To Resume Tel Aviv Flights After Cockpit Attack: Report - Mecca Pact Activated: Pakistan Deploys Military Forces To Saudi Arabia As Houthi Attacks Intensify It is about that time," Trump said. But I was very honoured to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump." Trump claimed he had settled eight wars since returning to office and said his efforts had gone beyond those of previous US presidents. Ive done stuff that nobody else has ever done. Im not bragging, Im just telling you the facts. No president has probably ever settled any wars. I settled eight wars." The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize is due to be announced on Friday. Trump acknowledged that he could be overlooked, saying the committee had a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me". But, whether I get it or not, I have done far more. And I think it would be a great discredit to them. And Im not saying that out of scorn, Im saying that when you settle eight wars, and nobodys never," he added. Trump compares himself with Obama Trump also questioned the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize awarded to former US President Barack Obama. Obama got it, and he didnt do anything," Trump said. He still doesnt know what he got it for. He got it when he got elected, right at the beginning, and he had no idea why he got it." The US president also recalled that last years peace laureate Venezuelas Maria Corina Machado had handed over her prize to him at the Oval Office Last time they gave it to a young lady whos a fabulous person, and she said she didnt deserve it, that I deserved it, and she gave it to me," Trump said. Peace claims face scrutiny Trump has said his administration helped address eight conflicts and prevented others through diplomatic pressure and the threat of tariffs. Leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated him, although such claims cannot be independently verified. However, some parties to conflicts Trump says he helped resolve have disputed the extent of his role, while fighting has resumed in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the Cambodia-Thailand border. Trump has also yet to secure a lasting end to the war in Ukraine, despite previously promising to end it quickly. The US president has also pointed to his efforts involving Iran, where months of conflict have continued following US and Israeli strikes. The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded independently by the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Other names and institutions mentioned among potential contenders include Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court and the UN special rapporteur for the Palestinian territories. (With inputs from agencies) Leaders from Cambodia, Israel, and Pakistan have stated that they nominated US President Donald Trump for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

headline: Suzlon to invest ₹200cr in wind blade plant in southern TN
content: Suzlon Group, a leading wind energy equipment maker, is investing Rs. 200 crore to set up a new, large wind-blade manufacturing facility in southern Tamil Nadu, strengthening its manufacturing footprint in the state and creating about 2,000 jobs.The proposed plant, which will come up on a 40-acre site along the Tuticorin-Melakarandai National Highway, will have two manufacturing lines and produce Suzlons latest S175 wind turbine, rated at 5 MW.Over the last three decades, we have invested about Rs. 775 crore directly in Tamil Nadu and currently employ about 2,000 people directly, besides supporting around 1,500 indirect jobs. With the new facility, we expect to add more than 500 direct jobs and around 1,500 indirect employment opportunities, Girish Tanti, co-founder of Suzlon Group, told TOI.The new investment comes as Suzlon expands its manufacturing capacity to cater to the growing demand for wind power in India. The company has held initial discussions with the Tamil Nadu govt on the proposed expansion. I think the new government is pretty progressive, he said.The proposed factory will be a very high-tech facility. So, we have embraced digital technology in a very big way, primarily for three things either to enhance productivity, enhance workplace safety, or enhance performance, Tanti said. The facility, which is planned to have a manufacturing capacity of nearly 1 GW, is expected to be up and running by early 2027. So, its strategically located, which will give it the flexibility for exports also, he added.Suzlon has had a long manufacturing presence in Tamil Nadu, with the state being among the first locations where the company began its operations in the mid-1990s. The company initially established its presence in the Muppandal wind energy cluster in the southern part of the state.The company currently runs one of its largest manufacturing units at Puducherry. Spread over a 66-acre plot, the Puducherry unit now operates as an integrated plant for Wind Turbine Generators (WTG) and Nacelle Covers (NCU). It also runs a large forging operation in Coimbatore.Suzlons expansion comes at a time when Tamil Nadu is seeking to regain its position as Indias leading renewable energy state, particularly in wind power. The state has significant wind and solar resources, besides a large industrial base that is driving electricity demand.The proposed facility will add to Suzlons manufacturing footprint in Tamil Nadu and is expected to strengthen the states position in the countrys wind turbine manufacturing ecosystem.In June this year, Suzlon unveiled its 2.0 growth strategy, with a five-year capex plan of Rs. 2,500 crore and an ambitious target to quadruple annual renewable energy sales to 10 GW and expand its assets under management (AUM) to 70 GW by FY31.

headline: Cornell students stage sit-in to protest university's handling of alleged 2024 gang rape
content: in at a dining hall and vowed not to spend money on campus on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to protest sexual violence and how the university has handled complaints, in the latest expression of outrage over an alleged 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house. A handwritten sign reading Justice for Jane Doe the name under which the accuser is suing was propped on an empty table in the dining hall in the afternoon. Some students sat around the room without eating, while others lunched. Another small group sat outside holding signs with messages such as we are Jane Doe. Groups organising the demonstration intended to keep the sit-in going for seven hours. The demonstrations were meant to spotlight complaints that the university is slow to respond to reports of sexual assault while quick to protect its reputation. Among other demands, the groups want the university to retool disciplinary procedures for addressing complaints and expel or revoke the degrees of anyone involved in the alleged October 2024 sexual assault. Jane Doe, who was a student then, alleges that Chi Phi members plied her with alcohol and drugs and several sexually assaulted her. One man sent others a message inviting them to participate, according to a lawsuit she filed last month against Cornell, the fraternity, seven men who were Chi Phi brothers and others. Lawyers for two of the men have denied they participated in a sexual assault. Attempts by The Associated Press to reach the others or their representatives have been unsuccessful. Some of the men who underwent a university disciplinary hearing in 2024 told investigators that the sexual activity was consensual or said they were not involved. The woman went to Cornell police in November 2024, though no criminal charges resulted. In the wake of her lawsuit, the state attorney general is conducting a renewed criminal investigation. Cornell closed down the Chi Phi campus chapter in 2024 and says it expelled some students and suspended others after an investigation under the federal Title IX law. This week Cornell trustees brought in former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to review how the school investigates sexual assault and sexual harassment, how the disciplinary process works, campus police response and more.

headline: Brazilian students in Rio de Janeiro march against the prospect of another Bolsonaro presidency
content: Thousands of Brazilian students marched in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to protest against the possibility of Flvio Bolsonaro winning the presidency, after the far-right candidate received more votes than incumbent and left-leaning Luiz Incio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazils presidential election. A sea of red-clad demonstrators made their way between two historical squares in Rios center, chanting and holding signs referencing Brazils sovereignty and democracy in the South American country, which they said were under threat. Were fighting for Brazil, not for Lula, said Talita Amaral, a 19-year-old environmental science student at a nearby university. She was wearing Brazils yellow and green soccer jersey, often worn by supporters of Bolsonaro, which she said was a gesture aimed at reclaiming the national colors. We dont have time to be sad, we need to be doing this, occupying the streets, sending messages in WhatsApp groups, trying to convince people, Amaral said, as the chant Ol ol ol ola, Lula Lula rang out across Cinelandia square. Neither Flvio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup, nor Lula received more than the required 50% of the vote needed to become Brazils leader on Sunday. Therefore, they will face each other in an unpredictable runoff on Oct. 25. But Flvio Bolsonaro has at least two advantages: He received 2 million more votes than Lula on Sunday and the candidates who placed third, fourth and fifth are all on the right of the political spectrum. They gathered 6 million votes between them. Mr. Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion because of his ties to the failed Banco Master a case that many protesters in Rio made reference to on Wednesday. Some pointed to Jair Bolsonaro's handling of the coronavirus pandemic, during which 700,000 people were reported to have died from the disease, while others held signs emblazoned with messages such as Brazil isn't anyone's backyard and I don't vote for someone who sells Brazil. Many on the left fear a Flvio Bolsonaro presidency would fully align the Brazilian government with the United States because of the proximity in ideologies between U.S. President Donald Trump and the Bolsonaro family. Last year, Trump imposed a 50% tariff on Brazilian goods and imposed sanctions on a Brazilian Supreme Court justice, citing Jair Bolsonaros trial, which he called a witch hunt. If Bolsonaro wins, Brazil will become a colony of the United States, said Joo Victor Vieira, 20, who studies literature. He said that Bolsonaro represented a threat to minorities such as people of color, women and the LGBTQ+ community. Bolsonaro's father was notorious for homophobic remarks. Mr. Vieira said that while he was initially dispirited following the results on Sunday, he has since regained hope. This protest shows that social movements are still very much alive, he said. We will resist.

headline: I&B Ministry notifies names of 13 journalists as Press Council members
content: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) on Wednesday officially notified the names of 13 journalists as members of the Press Council of India (PCI) Indias key media watchdog. The names comprise six newspaper editors and seven working journalists (other than editors). The gazette notification has been long pending, with the PCI operating at half its sanctioned strength for nearly a year and without a single working journalist or newspaper editor. The PCI operates under the Press Council Act, 1978, which stipulates that the Council must consist of a chairperson and 28 members, each serving a three-year term. So far, only 14 of the 28 members have been appointed: five MPs, three nominees and six from among newspaper owners and management, aside from the chairperson. Earlier in the day, the Editors Guild of India also demanded the immediate reconstitution of the 15th Press Council in conformity with the Press Council Act, 1978, including the prompt filling of all 13 seats reserved for professional journalists.

headline: 9/11 families vs Saudi Arabia: Will Riyadh finally face trial? What the lawsuit alleges, what families want Trump to do
content: Nearly 25 years after the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, the families of victims are still waiting for their long-running legal battle against Saudi Arabia to reach trial. A federal appeals court in New York on Wednesday (October 7) heard arguments over whether the Kingdom should remain a defendant in a lawsuit alleging that Saudi government-linked individuals provided assistance to some of the 19 al-Qaida hijackers. The three-judge panel did not immediately rule on whether the case can proceed. The hearing, however, gave the families a fresh opportunity to press their demand for accountability and to call on President Donald Trump to put pressure on Riyadh. More than 100 relatives of 9/11 victims attended the hearing in lower Manhattan, according to the accounts provided. The judges asked really meaningful questions and challenged Saudi Arabia's lawyers, Terry Strada, whose husband Tom was killed in the attacks, said after the hearing. The civil lawsuits, first filed in 2004, involve hundreds of victims' relatives and injured survivors, as well as insurers and businesses. At the heart of the claims is an allegation that Saudi government employees or officials knowingly assisted members of the 9/11 plot and helped create an environment in which al-Qaida could operate and develop. The plaintiffs allege that individuals associated with Saudi Arabia provided support to at least two of the 19 hijackers who eventually carried out the attacks. The lawsuits also allege that extremist religious figures in Saudi Arabia assisted the hijackers and that Saudi-linked charities helped funnel money and other support to people associated with al-Qaida. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers were Saudi nationals. Saudi Arabia, however, has consistently denied that its government was involved in the attacks. The attacks killed 2,977 people when hijacked aircraft crashed into New York's World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a field in Pennsylvania. Other defendants in the broader litigation, including Iran, the Taliban and al-Qaida, have already been found in default. The latest legal battle centres on sovereign immunity the principle that foreign governments are generally protected from being sued in US courts. Saudi lawyers argue that the Kingdom should be dismissed from the case because it is a sovereign state and that the allegations do not overcome that immunity. They have also pointed to the US-Saudi relationship in the 1990s, arguing that Washington and Riyadh were partners in efforts against terrorism and al-Qaida founder Osama bin Laden. The plaintiffs' lawyers disagree. They argue that the evidence and allegations are sufficient for Saudi Arabia to face the civil lawsuit in a US court. The appeals court hearing followed an August 2025 ruling by US District Judge George B. Daniels, who allowed the case to continue in federal court. Importantly, Daniels did not rule that Saudi Arabia was liable or that the allegations had been proven; his decision concerned whether the litigation could proceed. The appeals court must now decide whether that ruling stands. The judges did not indicate when they would issue their decision. If Saudi Arabia succeeds, the Kingdom could be removed from the case before the families get their opportunity to take the allegations to trial. If the families prevail, the litigation could move forward, potentially forcing Saudi Arabia to continue defending itself against allegations that its officials or agents assisted the 9/11 hijackers. That would not mean Saudi Arabia had been found responsible for the attacks. It would mean only that the plaintiffs' claims could proceed through the US judicial process. For the families, that distinction is important: after decades of litigation, they say they want the opportunity to establish the facts in court. The families are also demanding action from President Donald Trump. After Wednesday's hearing, relatives called on Trump to pressure the Saudi government to apologise and to support the victims' efforts to hold Riyadh accountable. Aaron Sand, whose father died in the attacks, directly appealed to the president. President Trump, I love ya, but you are not doing enough, Sand said. He urged Trump to prioritise the families who lost relatives in the attacks and said Saudi Arabia's status as a US ally should not prevent the victims from seeking accountability. Brett Eagleson, whose father Bruce was killed on 9/11, also questioned where the president and Congress stand. We are about a month from the midterm elections. Where are the members of Congress? Where is the president of the United States? Will he stand with the families or with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Eagleson asked. Strada similarly said the administration could intervene politically and called for the Kingdom to be held accountable. As an American, a patriot, I want to see the right thing done, she said.

headline: Trump administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorisation
content: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security has proposed that international students pay at least $70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), part of the Trump administrations wider crackdown on foreign visa holders. Under the proposal, nonimmigrant students with F-1 visas would be required to pay $70,000 to a certified institution for on-the-job training, known as Optional Practical Training (OPT), and $30,000 for any additional work training. DHS said the new rules were meant to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers. Under the OPT system, foreign students can engage in work training for up to 20 hours per week while school is in session, as well as for a limited time after graduation, with an additional allowance for those with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Those who enroll are currently expected to pay around $500. DHS is now setting a fee to ensure employers, students, and institutions are engaging in appropriate activities consistent with admission as an F-1 nonimmigrant, the agency said. Such training programs often serve as a bridge for students seeking work under H-1B visas, which the Trump administration has also targeted with increased fees. For decades, the H-1B program has allowed young engineers and scientists from across the world, especially India and China, to turn years of study at U.S. universities into high-paying jobs and a path to permanent U.S. residency. Leading U.S. tech companies have come to rely heavily on these workers to fill skilled positions. When he was campaigning in 2024, President Donald Trump vowed he would make it easier for foreign students to remain in the country, suggesting they be automatically awarded a Green Card after graduation. Like similar DHS proposals, the rule change is likely to be met with swift legal challenges. This proposed rule isnt going to fare well in the courts, just as the 100k H-1B fee and other restrictionist policies have been struck down, Doug Rand, director of the Talent Mobility Fund, which works to attract foreign STEM professionals, wrote on LinkedIn on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). The proposal is subject to 30 days of public comment before it can be finalised. DHS said it would wait 60 days after finalisation before putting the rule into effect to allow schools, students and employers time to prepare.

content: DHS said the fees are intended to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed a steep new fee of at least $70,000 for international students seeking work training in the country, in the latest move by the Trump administration to tighten rules for foreign visa holders. Under the proposal, students on F-1 visas would have to pay $70,000 to a certified institution for Optional Practical Training (OPT), which allows foreign students to gain work experience related to their studies. Students with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics can qualify for an extended period of training. This proposed rule isnt going to fare well in the courts," Rand wrote on LinkedIn, referring to previous immigration restrictions. An additional work training programme would carry a proposed $30,000 fee, marking a major increase from the current fee of roughly $500.

headline: Dozens of soldiers, militants and miners killed in Nigeria attacks
content: Nigerian troops killed more than 25 Islamic State-aligned militants as they fought off an assault on a military position in northeastern Borno State, suffering an unknown number of casualties of their own, military sources and a member of the civilian defence force said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). In a separate, earlier incident, gunmen on motorbikes killed more than 25 soldiers and over 100 small-scale gold miners in Zamfara State, in the northwest, a military source, government official, and three residents said. The attacks underscore the persistent threat posed by Islamist insurgents in northeastern Nigeria despite years of military campaigns against Boko Haram and its offshoot, known as Islamic State West Africa Province. Meanwhile, violence is spreading in the northwest, where bandits and Islamist groups also operate. Insecurity is likely to be a key issue in Nigerias election early next year. Special forces under attack In the incident in the northeast, troops of the 101 Special Forces Battalion came under attack on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) night from four directions in Kukawa, near Lake Chad, but repelled the assault with air support, according to the military. Preliminary assessment indicates that over 25 terrorists were neutralised, with 14 bodies recovered so far, Captain Mohammed Goni, acting military information officer for Operation Hadin Kai, said in a statement. Troops seized six AK-47 rifles and ammunition during follow-up operations. The military sources said some soldiers were killed in the fighting but did not provide details. A member of the Civilian Joint Task Force, which supports military operations in the northeast, said more than three of its members were killed. The military said it would continue joint operations to prevent militants from regrouping and launching further attacks. Gunmen on motorbikes On October 5, heavily armed bandits on motorcycles attacked a military camp in Bindin, a community in Zamfaras Maru local government area, killing at least 25 troops, three eyewitnesses told Reuters. Salisu Abdu, a resident of the nearby Bindin village, said he had counted the bodies of 25 dead soldiers. A military source who participated in an operation to reinforce security in the community on Wednesday confirmed the attack, saying that he too saw 25 bodies. The gunmen looted the base after overrunning the soldiers, he said. The gunmen then opened fire in a mining pit on Tuesday where about 1,000 people were digging for gold. At least 100 people were killed, according to a village head and relatives of the victims. Reuters could not confirm the casualty figures. Neither the Nigerian military nor the Zamfara State government responded to requests for comment.

headline: Trump's $70,000 OPT fee proposal for international students explained: What is OPT and who will bear the cost?
content: The Trump administrations proposal to impose a $70,000 fee for initial Optional Practical Training (OPT) has put a spotlight on a programme widely used by international students seeking to gain work experience in the United States after completing their studies. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed charging $70,000 for each F-1 student seeking initial OPT and $30,000 for any subsequent OPT. DHS says the move is aimed at tackling fraud and abuse, strengthening the integrity of the immigration system and protecting US workers. Here is what the proposed change means and how the OPT system works. Optional Practical Training, or OPT, is a temporary employment programme for eligible F-1 international students in the US. It allows students to work in a job that is directly related to their major or field of study. The programme is designed to give foreign students practical experience that complements their academic education. Students can generally seek OPT either before completing their studies or after graduation. OPT is available to eligible F-1 nonimmigrant students enrolled at US educational institutions. Students must receive a recommendation from their designated school official (DSO) before applying for employment authorisation from US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). The work undertaken through OPT must be related to the student's field of study. Eligible F-1 students can receive up to 12 months of OPT at each education level. For example, students progressing through different levels of education may become eligible for OPT associated with each level, subject to the applicable rules. There is also a special provision for graduates in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields. Eligible STEM graduates can receive an additional 24-month extension, potentially allowing them to remain authorised to work for a longer period after graduation. Under the system described in the proposal, students currently face fees of roughly $500, making the proposed $70,000 charge a dramatic increase. The proposed initial fee would be 140 times the current amount. The proposal would also establish a $30,000 fee for subsequent OPT, creating another significant financial hurdle for students seeking additional work training. DHS says the proposed fees are intended to combat fraud and abuse, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system and protect US workers. The department has raised concerns about the way the OPT programme is being used and argues that some participants, employers and institutions have exploited existing rules. DHS says its Student and Exchange Visitor Program has identified schemes involving problematic worksites and so-called pay-to-stay arrangements, in which students may maintain their immigration status without receiving legitimate educational or employment benefits. The department argues that the higher fees would encourage schools to exercise greater oversight before recommending students for OPT. The proposal would require the SEVP-certified school to pay the fee before its designated school official recommends an F-1 student for OPT. The fee would apply when a school recommends a student for OPT rather than being tied to a specific employer. However, the financial impact could ultimately extend to students, employers and educational institutions depending on how the costs are handled. No. The proposed fee specifically concerns eligible F-1 nonimmigrant students seeking OPT. It is not a blanket $70,000 fee on every international student studying in the US. Students who do not seek OPT would not be subject to the proposed OPT charge simply because they hold an F-1 visa. The proposal is not yet final. The rule is subject to a 30-day public comment period before DHS can decide whether to finalise it. DHS has said it would wait 60 days after finalisation before implementing the rule, giving schools, students and employers time to prepare.

headline: Loanees do not mortgage their constitutional rights with banks: Madras High Court
content: The mere fact that a citizen of the country either raises a loan from a bank or stands as a guarantor for a loan availed by someone else does not mean that he has mortgaged his constitutional and legal rights lock, stock and barrel with the bank, the Madras High Court has observed. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan made the observation while dismissing an application filed by Bank of Baroda to review his August 24, 2026 order revoking a Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against Kondepati Ganga Prasad who was a guarantor for a high value loan availed by GVR Infra Projects. The judge highlighted that the right to travel freely across the world was a fundamental right enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution as declared by the Supreme Court in Maneka Gandhi Vs. Union of India (1978). In order to have a restriction of that right, it should be in accordance with law. The term law under Article 21 implies a legislation. A letter written by the Manager of the bank to the Bureau Of Immigration cannot be treated as law. If a nationalised bank is permitted to do this, then every private creditor or non-banking finance corporation would also be emboldened to approach the police for issuance of LOC to prevent their debtors from going abroad, the judge wrote. He went on to state: God forbid the debtors from being thrown at the mercy of wolves of creditors. All these observations are made only to point out that the constitutional rights of the petitioner does not come to an end with the commencement of mortgage with the review petitioners bank. In the present case, the guarantor proposes to go abroad to earn and repay the amount after returning. However, the bank was insisting upon him to repay the money first and then go abroad. This is a catch-22 situation. If the bank wants the money, the petitioner has to earn it. The petitioner, in his wisdom, has decided to go abroad to earn it. The bank says till he pays the amount, he should not be permitted to go abroad. This vicious circle has to be broken. Justice Lakshminarayanan also said, no business venture gets started with an intention to create a loss but such was the nature of life that not every business ends up successful. The bank, while issuing the loan, was well aware that all loans were not going to be repaid and some were bound to become sticky or Non-Performing Assets (NPAs). I should point out that the Bank of Baroda, for the very purpose, has a separate branch called the stressed accounts branch. This shows that the number of sticky accounts with the Bank of Baroda is so high that it requires special attention of a team of officers, he added. The judge recorded the submission of the banks counsel that it had not lodged any criminal complaint of fraud against the guarantor either with the Central Bureau of Investigation or the State police. Even the bank officials who were responsible for clearing the loan in favour of the private company had not been prosecuted. The bank has not done so because it is very well aware that it was the business decision taken by the managerial authorities at that relevant point of time to clear the loan in favour of the petitioner. When there is no fraud, either at the instance of the petitioner or at the instance of the managerial staff of the bank, for the mere fact that the petitioner is a defaulter, he cannot be forced to stay within the four corners of this country in order to ensure that the amounts are re-paid, the judge concluded.

headline: 'Rely On Official Statements': Russia Dismisses 'False' Plague Reports Over Suspected Second Case
content: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed reports of a second suspected case and urged the public to rely on official sources. Russia has rejected reports of a suspected second case of plague in Siberia, calling much of the media coverage false information" as the United States, European Union and World Health Organization sought greater clarity from Moscow. The reports centre on an employee at a plague research institute in the Irkutsk region. A 28-year-old woman working at the facility reportedly died after falling ill, with some reports suggesting she may have been exposed to the disease through a broken test tube. - Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before? - Lab Workers Mysterious Death At Russias Anti-Plague Institute: Why Has It Drawn US Attention? - Russia Plague Scare: From Symptoms To Spread, How Dangerous It Is And Could It Be Another Covid? - Why Is Plague Still A Threat? What Russia's Irkutsk Scare Reveals About The Deadly Bacteria Russian authorities, however, said the woman died from pneumonia and found no evidence linking her illness to plague. Russia urges reliance on official information Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed reports of a second suspected case and urged the public to rely on official sources. The vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information," Peskov told reporters. Russias health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said there was no epidemic risk for the population" following an investigation. The agency said more than 90% of people who had contact with the woman had completed medical observation, with no signs of infectious disease detected. It also said nearly 5,000 laboratory tests had found no dangerous pathogens. Rospotrebnadzor said it had introduced precautionary anti-epidemic measures" and shared information with the WHO under international health regulations. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said no microorganisms connected to the womans work had been found in her biological samples. WHO, US seek greater transparency The reports have nevertheless prompted concern outside Russia. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Moscow to clarify reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause". The European Commission also called on Russia to provide timely and transparent reporting" on the situation. US President Donald Trump, asked whether a biological weapon could be involved, said: We dont think so. Were going to find out soon enough." Mongolia has meanwhile increased health checks along its border with Russia. Its government said health surveillance and monitoring measures" were being implemented. The WHOs initial assessment put the risk at moderate to low for the Irkutsk region, low for Russia and very low for Europe. (With inputs from agencies) Russian authorities stated that the 28-year-old laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died from pneumonia of undetermined cause, rejecting unconfirmed media reports and rumors linking her death to a plague infection.

headline: FBI arrests teen after alleged ISIS-inspired Mall of America terror plot: Inside the undercover sting
content: The FBI has arrested an 18-year-old man accused of planning a terrorist attack at the Mall of America in Minnesota after an undercover operation in which agents allegedly supplied him with an AK-47 and ammunition. According to an AP report, Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud was arrested on Tuesday in a public park in Richfield after allegedly paying $600 to an undercover FBI employee posing as a member of ISIS for an assault rifle and 200 rounds of ammunition, according to a federal criminal complaint. Authorities said the operation disrupted an alleged plan to attack the Mall of America, one of the largest shopping centres in the United States. Here is what is known about the case. Mohamud, 18, is an American-born US citizen of Somali descent, according to US Attorney Daniel Rosen. He appeared in federal court in St. Paul on Wednesday for his initial hearing. It was not immediately clear whether he had an attorney who could comment on the allegations. According to the criminal complaint, Mohamud repeatedly discussed plans to attack the Mall of America in messages exchanged with a confidential source. Investigators allege that he intended to target non-Muslims at the shopping centre on October 24, when a Hmong arts celebration was scheduled. Rosen said the teenager had expressed an intention to kill potentially 30 to 60 people. The FBI intervened before he could allegedly carry out the plan, authorities said. The investigation involved an undercover FBI employee who posed as a member of ISIS. According to the complaint, Mohamud communicated with the confidential informant for months before the FBI supplied him with the weapon and ammunition. He allegedly paid $600 for an AK-47 and 200 rounds of ammunition. Agents arrested him immediately after the transaction in Richfield, several miles northwest of the Mall of America. The operation allowed investigators to document the alleged weapons purchase while preventing the suspect from obtaining the firearm through an independent source. The FBI first became aware of Mohamud in December 2024, according to the complaint. That was also when the confidential source began exchanging messages with him. By May 2025, investigators had become sufficiently concerned about his activities that FBI agents went to his home. According to the complaint, Mohamud's mother told agents that he was still at school and contacted his father. His father declined to speak with the agents and said he would provide their contact information to his lawyer. The investigation subsequently continued for nearly two years before the arrest. The criminal complaint alleges that Mohamud expressed admiration for recent terrorist attacks and showed interest in travelling to Somalia to join ISIS. Investigators said he ultimately decided against travelling because he could not afford the trip. Instead, according to the complaint, he allegedly turned his attention to carrying out an attack in the US, with the Mall of America identified as his target. The allegations describe an alleged progression from interest in ISIS to discussions about a specific domestic target and, eventually, an attempt to obtain a firearm and ammunition. The complaint says Mohamud intended to attack the mall on October 24, coinciding with a scheduled Hmong arts celebration. Authorities have not indicated that the event itself was the reason for the alleged targeting beyond its presence at the mall on the date identified in the messages. The Mall of America is a major public gathering place in Bloomington, Minnesota, making an alleged attack there potentially capable of causing large numbers of casualties. US Attorney Daniel Rosen praised the FBI investigation and said agents had identified the threat before the alleged plan could be executed. This was a radicalized young man who needed to be watched, Rosen said. He also urged parents to take seriously any indication that a child may be becoming radicalised, particularly if federal law enforcement has raised concerns with the family. Mohamud has been arrested and appeared in federal court, but the allegations in the criminal complaint have not been established at trial. The federal case will now proceed through the court system, where prosecutors will have to prove the charges against him. The FBI's operation is also likely to draw attention because undercover agents supplied the alleged suspect with the firearm and ammunition used to establish the final stage of the investigation. Authorities have said the intervention prevented the alleged attack from taking place.

headline: Thirumavalavan's statements on SIR sends mixed signal to cadre, party leaders
content: Contradictory statements and positions taken by the VCK on the impact of SIR of electoral rolls on the results of the recent Assembly election in the State has surprised and confused political circles, as VCK continues to be a part of the cabinet led by TVK. Participating in a protest against the Election Commission of India in New Delhi recently, VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan raised doubts over TVKs recent victory and attributed its success to the SIR process. SIR created a three-cornered contest and that is why we have this result. It is possible that TVKs victory could be due to the SIR (its impact) just as in other States, he said, surprising many. After all, Mr. Thirumavalavan threw his weight behind the TVK, which recently contested in the bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram reserved constituencies. VCK general secretary D. Ravikumar also echoed similar sentiments. Asked how VCK could justify its support for the TVK government while simultaneously questioning the Assembly election results, he said, We have raised concerns about the SIR process, not just now, but in the last many months since it was implemented. There is a serious possibility that SIR could have influenced the outcome of the Tamil Nadu Assembly poll, as it has in other post-SIR States. Major political parties and civil society organisations should conduct a survey, like the CPI(ML) did in Bihar, and verify the deletions and additions. He further said, Our leader said at the time of the results that in constituencies where there had been more deletions, TVK had won, and where there had been fewer deletions, the other parties had done better. But this does not automatically mean that TVK benefited from SIR, there needs to be a proper investigation into the SIR process in Tamil Nadu to find out the social composition of the deleted voters. A senior VCK leader said it is time for Mr. Thirumavalavan to take a clear stance with respect to alliance. Our leader needs to communicate to the cadre and the supporters where the VCK stands with respect to TVK. Statements such as these are not helping the party. We should preserve our ideological foundation, he said. Another VCK leader added, The statements perhaps reflects the fact that he is not confident about TVKs electoral fortunes in the future and its ideological commitment in opposing the BJP/RSS. We should have supported the TVK to form the government from outside.

headline: CMC to organise conference on gene therapy in Vellore
content: The 11th International Cell and Gene Therapy Conference (CGTCON 2026) will be held at Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore town on October 8. According to a press release, the conference, including a workshop, will be organised by the Centre for Stem Cell Research, a collaborative unit of BRIC-Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem), Bengaluru, and the CMC. This years conference, which will end on October 10, will showcase developments in fields of major diseases, such as haematological, ocular, diabetic and metabolic, neurological, cardiovascular, and dermatological disorders. It will also cover organoids and disease modelling, nucleic acid delivery technologies, and the industry, manufacturing, and regulatory aspects of advanced therapeutics. CGTCON 2026 aims to strengthen collaborations between clinicians, scientists, industry partners, and regulatory stakeholders, the release said.

headline: State govt. relaxes domicile clause for gold ring scheme
content: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday relaxed the eligibility criteria for the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam, amending the guidelines to include children whose mothers were born in Tamil Nadu but had moved to another State after marriage, provided their parents reside permanently in Tamil Nadu. Under the scheme, a one-gram gold ring is provided to children born in government hospitals in Tamil Nadu. The scheme was launched by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on September 28 and is being implemented retrospectively from June 22, 2026. The Government Order, issued by the Health and Family Welfare Department, prescribes the guidelines for the scheme. While implementing the scheme, it came to the governments notice that in some cases, women from Tamil Nadu who had been living in another State after marriage, but whose parents continued to reside permanently in Tamil Nadu, returned to their parental homes for childbirth and delivered their babies in the government hospitals in Tamil Nadu, said Darez Ahamed, Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, in an official release. One such case was that of Uma Maheswari, who, after marriage, has been living with her husband at Udayagiri in Mysuru district of Karnataka. Her parents reside in Karaikudi in Sivaganga district. She came to Tamil Nadu, for childbirth and delivered a baby at the Karaikudi Government Headquarters Hospital on September 17. Under the conditions that were in force, the family was initially unable to benefit under the scheme, as the mother who had delivered the child was required to be a permanent resident of Tamil Nadu. Considering this, the government has decided to expand the eligibility conditions under the scheme, the release said. As per the new guidelines, if the mother of a child born in a government hospital was born in Tamil Nadu and had moved to another State after marriage, but her parents are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu, the child will also be provided a gold ring on submission of relevant documentary evidence. Accordingly, Ms. Maheswari was provided a one-gram gold ring. The amendment will also apply retrospectively to eligible children from June 22, 2026, the release added.
