headline: Paperless registration mandatory for some family arrangement deeds from Nov. 2
content: As part of the second phase of Anywhere Registration under the STAR (Simplified and Transparent Administration of Registration) 3.0 system, the Tamil Nadu government has accorded administrative sanction for mandating paperless registration of certain documents pertaining to family arrangements from November 2. A Government Order (G.O.) to this effect was issued by the Commercial Taxes and Registration Department on Wednesday. As per the G.O., settlement deeds, release deeds, partition deeds, and revocation of settlement deeds relating to family arrangements will be registered paperless to ensure citizen convenience and transparency, and to reduce the manual handling of documents. Under the arrangement, the digitally executed deeds shall be sent to the Sub-Registrar through the online registration facility, along with the required supporting documents. The Registration Department shall process those documents, and the parties shall thereafter appear before the Sub-Registrar concerned for identification, authentication, and completion of the prescribed registration formalities. After all the formalities are completed, the registered document shall be digitally processed and sent to the citizens login. It will be preserved in the STAR system. The State government had already mandated presence-less registration of deeds relating to the first sale of plots by plot promoters and the first sale of flats by builders, along with the consecutive deposit of title deeds and for the deposit of title deeds and deeds of receipt presented by banks and other financial institutions.

headline: GCC, MSSRF discuss measures to strengthen waste management
content: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) and the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF) discussed priorities for strengthening solid waste management and environmental health systems in Chennai under the CLEAR (Clean Land, Equitable Air and Resilience) project. A meeting chaired by GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran at Ripon Buildings on Wednesday focused on the Corporations priorities for reducing solid waste and air pollution over the next two years, implementation challenges across zones, lessons from waste audits and field inspections, and wards and zones to be prioritised for pilot projects. Training and capacity-building needs of conservancy workers, engineers, and field staff were also discussed. The CLEAR project, led by MSSRF in collaboration with IIT-Madras, Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research and the GCC, examines the links between solid waste management, air pollution, climate-related risks, and public health. Participants visited the GCCs Integrated Command and Control Centre, where officials explained how solid waste management operations and air-quality information are monitored.

headline: ECI special drive till Oct 9 to enrol young, first-time eligible voters
content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) will undertake a special drive till October 9 to enrol young and first-time eligible voters in the electoral rolls in Tamil Nadu and other States where the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has been completed. An official release from Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik said special camps would be conducted in the districts for the enrolment of young and first-time eligible voters, preferably on October 10. Special focus will be given to urban areas and bigger cities to increase the enrolment of first-time and young voters. The services of Electoral Literacy Clubs in schools and colleges will also be utilised to create awareness among eligible young voters and facilitate their enrolment, the release said. The District Election Officers (DEOs) have been instructed to give wide publicity to the special drive through the media and their official social media handles. Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) will hold regular meetings with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to review and monitor the progress of the drive and ensure effective implementation of the instructions, the release added.

headline: CREDAI Tamil Nadu expands network, to add five new chapters
content: The Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India (Credai) Tamil Nadu will host the fifth edition of STATECON, its flagship event for the real estate and construction industry, on October 11 and 12, 2026. This year, Credai Tamil Nadu will also launch the first edition of FAIRBUILD 2026, a B2B expo for construction and building materials, which will be held alongside STATECON. FAIRBUILD connects vendors, suppliers and original equipment manufacturers with real estate developers, architects, and key decision makers, said W.S. Habib, president of Credai Tamil Nadu. Credai is also expanding its network to more cities and towns across Tamil Nadu. Currently, Credai Tamil Nadu has a presence in 10 cities. We will be adding five more chapters, taking the total to 15. The new chapters will include Coonoor and Ooty in the Nilgiris, Kodaikanal, Vellore, Thanjavur, and Karur. This will be the first time Credai will have chapters in hill stations, Mr. Habib said. The head of Credai in Tamil Nadu also pointed out that there is no corruption in the sector now, which is a big relief. We have a government that says no to bribes, he said. To a query on whether construction costs have gone up, Mr. Habib said: Raw material costs are rising. However, the situation is better than it was during the war. STATECON 2026 will feature focused discussions on the issues that matter most to the sector today. Sessions will examine the growth drivers of Tamil Nadus real estate market, the changing expectations of the new homebuyer and access to capital. They will also cover policy and ease of doing business, the impact of AI and PropTech, and the growing role of robotics and emerging construction technologies in how projects are planned and built. There will be discussions on issues like labor shortage, Mr. Habib said.

headline: Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital holds campaign to mark World Sight Day
content: As part of the initiative, undergraduate students pursuing optometry at the institute designed specially curated simulation glasses mimicking the visual impact of different conditions including cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy and refractive errors at four locations. More than 1,400 individuals wore these glasses and experienced how everyday vision can be affected by these conditions, said a press release. Highlighting the importance of proactive eye care, Karpagam, Dean, DAIO, said, raising awareness about silent eye diseases is crucial to motivate people to get annual examinations. Early detection is the primary defense in controlling preventable and avoidable blindness. If untreated, these eye conditions can affect independence, productivity and quality of life and, in many cases, can lead to avoidable vision loss.

headline: Centre Challenges Appointment Of Jharkhand Police Chief In Supreme Court

headline: Take tough stance on encroachers of temple properties: Minister
content: Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh on Wednesday instructed executive officers to work in tandem with officials of revenue and forest Departments to retrieve lands belonging to temples in the State. Addressing officials during a routine review of works at the department headquarters in Nungambakkam, the Minister also said that they should take a tough stance when it comes to encroachments and illegal name transfers of temple properties. If you come across any such instance, ensure that you file a complaint with the police immediately and obtain an FIR, he said. CCTV cameras should be installed and maintained properly in temples that witness heavy crowds regularly. Devotees wanting to eat the Annadhanam should not be made to wait for long periods before the food is served, he added.

headline: Syria Says Country's Northeast Oil Pipeline Damaged In "Sabotage Attack"
content: Years of civil war before the fall of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in late 2024 devastated Syria's oil, gas and electricity sectors, with the country becoming heavily reliant on imports to meet its needs.

headline: Three youths arrested for possession of narcotic tablets in Arakkonam
content: Three youths were arrested by Arakkonam Town police for possession of 113 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near a railway station in Arakkonam on Wednesday. The police said the arrested persons were identified as S. Ramkumar, 26, V. Udaya Sankar, 19, and K. Vijay, 20. They are residents of Chennai. Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Ranipet SP P. Sibin, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places such as bus terminii, railway stations, and isolated buildings in the district. During one of these checks. a police team intercepted three suspects near the railway station. They checked the trios bags and found narcotic tablets in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies in Mumbai. The tablets were sent by couriers to them. The police said the gang was on their way to Chennai, where they planned to sell these tablets in retail. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

headline: Health Minister accuses DMK of playing 'cheap politics'
content: Accusing the DMK of playing cheap politics over the brown paper covers used to dispense medicines to patients, Health Minister K.G. Arunraj on Wednesday said that TVK was the only organisation committed to following former Chief Minister C.N. Annadurais two-language policy in letter and spirit and would never compromise on it. On Tuesday, members of the DMK, including former Minister T.R.B. Rajaa, posted photographs of the pill covers distributed to patients in the government medical colleges in Karur and Coimbatore, which carried dosage instructions in Tamil, English, and Hindi, on social media. Condemning this, the Health Minister, in a statement, said that DMKs fake drama was exposed. He said at the Karur government medical college hospital, the covers given to patients were usually obtained from the Central Prison, and morning/afternoon/night was stamped on them only in Tamil. In December 2025, there was a shortage of covers supplied from the Central Prison. Following this, an emergency order was issued on December 31 during the DMK regime to print four lakh covers through the Erode district printing cooperative society. Those covers had come into circulation among the people in January 2026 when the DMK was in power. Similarly, in Coimbatore, the design was officially approved and printed through the Chinthamani Cooperative Society three years ago. Dr. Arunraj said that as soon as the issue came to the governments attention, the use of those medicine covers was immediately stopped at both Karur and Coimbatore hospitals. In Karur, it was ensured that the supply from Central Prison was restored and only Tamil was used, while in Coimbatore, steps were taken up to immediately print covers in Tamil and English. What kind of politics is it to now shift the blame onto the ruling party after having allowed Hindi during their own tenure, creating the template for it and putting it into circulation among patients, he questioned the DMK.

headline: Saudi Says Airport Attacks In Riyadh, Abha Kill 3, Injure 36 After Houthis Claim Strikes
content: Attacks on international airports in Riyadh and Abha killed three foreign nationals and wounded 36 others, Saudi authorities said. Attacks on international airports in the Saudi capital of Riyadh and the southern city of Abha killed three people and wounded dozens, the kingdoms civil aviation authority said on Wednesday. On Tuesday and Wednesday Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were subjected to attacks targeting their facilities," the authority said in a statement. - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks - From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia - 'Evil America Will End': Al Qaeda Calls For Similar Attacks, Praises Flydubai Incident - EXCLUSIVE: Pakistan to Deploy 25,000 Troops to Saudi Amid Rising Houthi Threats | Yemen Crisis-N18G Saudi authorities did not specify who was responsible despite ongoing hostilities with Yemens Houthi fighters, who claimed attacks on both airports on Wednesday. An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport and a Sudanese national was killed at the airport in Riyadh, the agency said, with 36 people wounded in both attacks. The authority said the injuries ranged from minor to severe" at both locations. All injured individuals were immediately transported to hospitals to receive necessary medical care. The attacks also caused some material damage," it said. The Saudi-led coalition that backs the pro-government forces in Yemen said on X that it destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform" used in the attack on Riyadh. The Houthis claimed a flurry of attacks on Saudi targets on Wednesday including firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh airport, as the group battled for territory in Yemen against pro-government forces supported by the Gulf kingdom. The Saudi-led military coalition that backs Yemens internationally recognised government earlier said a missile targeting Riyadh airport was intercepted. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree earlier said in a post on X that drones and missiles also targeted Saudi Arabias Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait and had hit their targets accurately". But the group was yet to comment on the latest announcement.

headline: Undercover FBI Employee Sold Teen Rifle For $600, Then Arrested Him
content: The 18-year-old had been under investigation for nearly two years, trading messages with a confidential informant, before agents sold him the rifle and ammunition and arrested him on the spot, they said.

headline: India's stakes in the Global Pandemic Agreement
content: At the United Nations High Level Meeting (UN HLM), in New York in September 2026, India made official remarks on the Political Declaration on Pandemic Prevention Preparedness and Response (PPPR). The Declaration is part of the emerging global legal regime on pandemics led by the WHO-Pandemic agreement (PA). Shaping the framework The PA was adopted by 124 member-states in 2025, including India. No country voted against it, while 11 abstained, reflecting alignment across high-, middle- and low-income countries (HICs/LICs/LMICs). The negotiations hinged on how to balance national sovereignty with international cooperation and solidarity, exposing the fault lines between the Global North and the Global South. Key issues included whether a global treaty can set binding targets for measures such as One Health without securing funding for countries with fragile health systems. Or whether national pandemic regulations can be harmonised through global frameworks. And whether private manufacturers can be required to share vaccines in real time at affordable prices. The PA is not yet open for ratification because negotiations are still ongoing for an annex concerning the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system. PABS could help ensure that, during a pandemic, LICs and LMICs receive a fair share of vaccines, medicines and other therapeutics. Even without ratification, the PA has created a first-of-its-kind global legal regime for the PPPR. Operationalisation requires countries such as India to balance interests of the HICs, LICs and LMICs. This will determine whether the PA will further entrench the inequities of the COVID-19 pandemic or make global health governance truly inclusive. Editorial | Landmark agreement: On the draft WHO Pandemic Agreement At the UN HLM, India succeeded in enshrining the multilateral components of the PA within the principle of national sovereignty. India reiterated its commitment to strengthen global pandemic preparedness but stressed that effective pandemic management requires that international coordination is demonstrated. The first is equitable access to drugs, vaccines and therapeutics and the creation of global public goods, such as digital infrastructure (which admittedly align with its own national priorities). The second is a respect for national sovereignty and the primacy of member-states in shaping global policy interventions according to national circumstance. As a contrast, the United States rejected the Declaration, calling the PABS and WHOs role in declaring pandemics as a challenge to its national interests. In its remarks, India has acknowledged the concerns of the Global North and the South. Both sides have upheld national sovereignty as paramount in several provisions. The African countries did not give consent to commitments to monitor the human-animal-environment interface, a key source of pandemic outbreaks, without significant funding, which was not guaranteed by the Global North. Similarly, countries in the Global North did not want binding targets with regard to technology transfer (and other similar provisions). But as India said at the UN HLM, Global Solidarity must be demonstrated through action; India must be an active player in the finalisation of the global PPPR regime. India is already actively engaged in the PABS negotiations and must lead the Global South in the post-PABS context. India can consider three options. First, developing partnerships on technical areas of the PA (One Health, surveillance, health workforce strengthening) to build trust with other countries in the Global South, and a store of operational solutions to tricky national sovereignty problems. Second, leveraging its leadership role within existing global political groupings. For example, the H20 summit (a health and development G-7 and G-20 partnership) will take place under the United Kingdoms G-20 leadership at the end of 2027; pandemic preparedness is one of the core health agendas. During Indias G-20 presidency in 2023, India launched the Global Initiative for Digital Health and holds considerable influence within the platforms health initiatives. Another is Partners for Multilateralism, which was launched in 2026 by the European Union (co-sponsors are Australia, Barbados, Brazil, Canada, India and Kenya). Third, strengthening and aligning domestic policy and regulatory architecture around its own priorities for the PA. Global leadership always rests on domestic strengths. India must ensure that its national policies on PPPR such as regulation of access to biological material and distribution of the benefits uphold the highest standards of equity which India can then demand at the global level. A South-South health role An equitable global regime on PPPR is in Indias interests as much as a responsibility towards the Global South. India is the pharmacy of the world, manufacturing one of the largest shares of vaccines in the world in terms of volume. Yet, it needs an equitable global vaccine distribution regime. The patents for the vaccines that India manufactures are held by global pharmaceuticals. India is also import-dependent for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). India needs access to the latest technology from the Global North to strengthen the manufacturing of high-grade personal protective equipment and medical devices. At the same time, India needs to lead South-South Cooperation and share its technological strength with other countries in the Global South. Indias health system has a continental scale, and as Indias Health Secretary stated at the UN HLM, its interventions in digital health infrastructure, laboratories networks and One Health are valuable as global public goods. An effective PA needs an engaged India, and a strong PA will strengthen Indias own pandemic management. Priyadarshini Singh is a Research Fellow at the Centre for Social and Economic Progress (CSEP). This article is based on a forthcoming CSEP working paper on the Pandemic Agreement.

headline: Trump administration proposes huge OPT fee hike from $500 to $70,000 for F-1 students seeking to work in US
content: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed requiring international students on F-1 visas to pay at least $70,000 for work-based training under the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, in the latest move by the Donald Trump administration to tighten rules governing foreign visa holders. Under the proposal, F-1 students would have to pay $70,000 to a certified institution for on-the-job training through OPT, while any additional work training would carry a fee of $30,000, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday. The proposed fees would represent a sharp increase from the roughly $500 that students currently pay to participate in the programme. The Department of Homeland Security said the proposed fees were intended to strengthen oversight of the OPT system and ensure that employers, students and educational institutions comply with immigration requirements. The agency said the measures were designed to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers. Under the current OPT system, foreign students with F-1 visas can undertake work training for up to 20 hours a week while school is in session. Students can also receive a limited period of work authorisation after graduation. Students who graduate in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields can qualify for additional OPT work authorisation. DHS said the new fee would ensure that OPT participants engage in activities consistent with their admission to the US as F-1 nonimmigrants. The proposed change could have significant implications for international students who rely on OPT to gain US work experience after completing their degrees. OPT has long served as an important bridge between studying at a US university and entering the country's skilled-worker system, including through the H-1B visa programme. The H-1B programme has been widely used by technology companies and other employers to hire highly skilled foreign workers, including engineers and scientists from countries such as India and China. The Trump administration has separately increased pressure on the H-1B programme through higher fees and other proposed restrictions. For international students, the proposed OPT fee could therefore add a substantial financial hurdle at a stage when many are seeking to transition from education into employment. The proposal also marks a significant contrast with Trump's campaign position in 2024. During his presidential campaign, Trump had said he wanted to make it easier for foreign students who graduate from US universities to remain in the country. He had suggested that students graduating from US colleges could automatically receive Green Cards. His administration has since pursued a broader crackdown on foreign visa holders and proposed changes affecting several categories of nonimmigrant workers and students. The latest OPT proposal is likely to face scrutiny from universities, employers, immigration groups and foreign students. The proposal is not yet final. DHS will allow 30 days for public comments before deciding whether to issue the rule in its final form. If finalised, the department said it would wait another 60 days before implementing the new requirements, giving schools, students and employers time to prepare.

headline: An open door is more powerful than a closed argument, Kamal Haasan tells CEC
content: Rajya Sabha member and Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) founder Kamal Haasan has appealed to chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to initiate urgent steps to restore public trust in the Election Commission of India (ECI) and urged him to meet Opposition Members of Parliament at the Samvidhan Bhavan in the Parliament complex. He sent an open letter to the CEC in this regard on Wednesday. The letter comes in the backdrop of heightened tensions following the detention of opposition leaders in New Delhi as they attempted to meet the Election Commissioners to raise grievances regarding electoral integrity and voter roll revisions.Highlighting that the credibility of the Indian depends entirely on the credibility of its elections, Kamal outlined several core issues fuelling public apprehension over electoral processes. Expressing concern over the 'rushed and erroneous implementation' of SIR, Kamal warned that stringent documentation requirements risk disenfranchising eligible voters, particularly those from socio-economically weaker sections.The letter pointed to growing worries regarding recent alterations to Form 6 (voter registration), allegations of selective enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), and the unabated flow of unaccounted money in political campaigns. The MP raised concerns over the alleged deployment of central investigative agencies in contexts that trigger political defections and undermine the independence of elected representatives.Critiquing the detention of opposition leaders who sought an audience with the Commission, Kamal stated that such measures cannot be the way forward when institutional trust is being tested. 'This is not a request on behalf of one political party. It is an appeal in the larger national interest,' he wrote, inviting the CEC and fellow commissioners to meet Opposition MPs at Samvidhan Bhavan.Concluding the letter, the actor-turned-politician emphasised that maintaining public faith requires visible impartiality, noting, 'At a time when trust in democratic institutions must be strengthened, an open door can be more powerful than a closed argument.'

headline: 'The Orange Plague': 8.5-Foot Naked, Golden Trump Statue Unveiled At European Parliament
content: Titled The Orange Plague, the copper sculpture was created by Danish artist Jens Galschit and shows Trump sitting on the shoulders of a smaller, frail figure. An 8.5-foot-tall statue of US President Donald Trump, covered in 23-karat gold leaf and depicted naked, has been unveiled at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France. Titled The Orange Plague', the copper sculpture was created by Danish artist Jens Galschit and shows Trump sitting on the shoulders of a smaller, frail figure. Trump is depicted holding a golf club in one hand and the scales of justice in the other. - France Riots Videos Go Viral As Post Links Unrest To Angry Students, Overcrowded Schools; Internet Divided - France Gripped By Violent Student Protests: Why Thousands Are On The Streets And Whats Happening - Lucknow Shocker: Stray Dog Shot Dead By Biker After It Barked At Him; CCTV Captures Killing - Diljit's AURA Tour, Guns N' Roses, Lollapalooza: Biggest Concerts Coming to India In The Next Few Months Trump likes gold,' Galschit said after the sculpture was unveiled on Tuesday. In a way, I think he would like this sculpture.' Artist says statue is a political statement The sculpture is also known as the King of Injustice'. A message on its plinth reads: I am sitting on the back of a man. He is sinking under my burden. I will do anything to help him. Except step down from his back.' Galschit said the work represents what he sees as Trumps impact on the environment and the rules-based international order. Trump is destroying all the things I believe in,' the artist said. He also said the decision to depict Trump naked was inspired by Hans Christian Andersens The Emperors New Clothes, in which a vain ruler parades through the streets without clothes. Dictators dont like you laughing at them,' Galschit said. Display approved by Parliament According to CNN, the exhibition was sponsored by Danish MEP Per Clausen. Its presence at the European Parliament does not mean the institution officially endorses the views represented by the artwork. A European Parliament spokesperson said the exhibition had been approved by the parliaments quaestors, a cross-party group responsible for administrative matters. MEPs are allowed to sponsor cultural events and exhibitions in designated areas, subject to parliamentary rules. Clausen said the display was intended to encourage debate about global power and Europes relationship with the US. I think we need to have a discussion about power in the world and how this power is used,' he said. Statue to remain on display until Thursday The temporary installation is expected to remain on display until Thursday. More than 1,000 3D-printed miniature versions of the sculpture are also being offered to visitors as protest tokens'. Galschit has previously displayed the work at events including the Munich Security Conference and the COP30 climate conference in Brazil. The artist is also known for his Pillar of Shame, a memorial linked to the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre. This is about the powerful and the powerless,' Galschit said, drawing a parallel between the two works. Trump has not publicly commented on the sculpture. (With inputs from CNN) The 8.5-foot-tall naked golden statue of US President Donald Trump unveiled at the European Parliament is titled 'The Orange Plague' and is also known as the 'King of Injustice'.

headline: Official says WHO doesn't know exactly how lab worker in Russia died in plague case
content: Maria Van Kerkhove, WHO director of Epidemic and Pandemic Management, said the agency doesnt know what the causative agent was behind the womans October 2 death and urged Russia for more information A top official with the World Health Organisation said Wednesday (October 7, 2026) the UN health agency doesnt know how a lab worker in Siberia died amid concerns about plague, and she urged Russia to provide more information. Maria Van Kerkhove, WHO director of Epidemic and Pandemic Management, said the agency doesnt know what the causative agent was behind the womans October 2 death, and this is why we need more information. In its tersely worded statements, Russias public health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, does not link the case to pneumonic plague, saying only that extensive testing found no evidence the lab workers illness was caused by any of the pathogens she worked with at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. Russia has said she died of pneumonia a typical acute respiratory viral infection and its health authorities have found no cases of plague recently, WHO has said, acknowledging that pneumonia is commonplace. We dont understand how she was infected, Van Kerkhove said. The comments suggested the UN health agency has more questions than answers about the situation at the lab, which focuses on plague and was founded about a century ago to study the disease in a region where it is endemic. Since the suspicious death of the lab worker, Russian authorities have kept a tight lid on information about it. The incident has been surrounded by secrecy and claims that it could have been caused by pneumonic plague. While the case has raised global concerns, Russian state TV and other national state-controlled media have steered clear of the subject. Some state-sponsored news outlets withdrew earlier reports about the case.

headline: Tamil Nadu Schools Face Acute Shortage of Physical Education Teachers
content: In more than 28 years as a govt school physical education (PE) teacher, S Pushparaj has not had a single promotion or pay hike. The job often costs him money, he says. Pushparaj finds grounds for his students to play at, raises funds so they can train. Sometimes I pay the auto fare to bring children from interior villages to competitions, he says.Physical education teachers across Tamil Nadu have similar complaints. According to S Sankaraperumal, president of the Tamil Nadu PE teachers association, 2,500 high and higher secondary schools and 8,500 middle schools have no physical education teacher.Colleges too, are losing ground. The state govt recently proposed a memorial for TVKs five ideological leaders (Rani Velu Nachiyar, Periyar E V Ramasamy, B R Ambedkar, Anjalai Ammal and K Kamaraj) at University Union grounds. Teachers and students have opposed the move as the ground is shared by University of Madras-affiliated colleges for sports training and meets.If this happens, no one will be able to access the ground for training, says Pushparaj, president of the Chengalpet district handball association. We approach institutions to access their facilities to train students for tournaments. At the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University, we are asked to pay `30,000 a day when we take govt school students to train. Its a govt institution. I dont understand why we have to pay so much. On the other hand, he adds, a few private institutions have given them their grounds for free and, in some cases, provide food for the students.PE teachers at govt schools say they are merely a title, frequently assigned work that has nothing to do with their subject. We are usually roped in to monitoring students and maintaining discipline and do other administrative jobs, says S Arockia Das, a govt school PE teacher. In some schools, my colleagues double up as watchmen, office assistants or clerks. Our primary role becomes assisting the headmaster with administrative work. When we get hired at a school, our duties get reduced to doing whatever work we are assigned, rather than teaching physical education.Sankaraperumal says while most schools dont have PE teachers, even where they are appointed, staffing is not adequate. A high or higher secondary school with 700 students generally has only one PE teacher, with a second teacher coming only when the strength exceeds 700, he says. Most primary and middle schools do not have playgrounds and even among matriculation schools, 70% lack them.He adds that only a third of govt schools have grounds. Sometimes portions of the ground are occupied by noon-meal centres, anganwadis or other govt departments. Only 30% of schools have facilities for sports such as athletics, volleyball, badminton, kabaddi, football and hockey.The result is that students who cannot access school grounds are left dependent on external facilities. Those who can afford it can train at sports clubs run by federations, while students in villages or from low-income families practise wherever they find space. Earlier there was a system of collecting a separate PE fee at schools. It is no longer the case. PE relies on common PTA funds, he says.Vanessa Peter, founder of Information and Resource Centre for the Deprived Urban Communities, says govt schools need to ensure access to safe, inclusive and accessible play spaces. Tamil Nadu state policy for children, 2021 allows children to participate in matters concerning them. Bala Sabhas, with children aged 12 to 18 as members, are expected to discuss issues concerning children and place resolutions before the gram sabha. A similar mechanism can be adopted in urban areas through Siruvar Mandrangal (govt-run children forums), where children can identify their education and sporting needs and participate in decisions about spaces in their neighbourhoods. Their voices should be part of planning and development, says Vanessa.But the govt is on the defensive. Students are given two compulsory periods for physical education, says Gopalakrishnan, the states chief inspector of physical education. There are playgrounds for them to play and necessary equipment is provided. Appointment of PE teachers is a govt decision based on school requirements. What more can the govt do?

headline: TN widens eligibility for gold ring scheme
content: Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme was launched by chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sept 28 Chennai: Tamil Nadus scheme to give a 1g gold ring to babies born in govt hospitals will now cover children of women who moved elsewhere after marriage, provided both their parents remain permanent residents of TN.The govt has relaxed the residency requirement under the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme, which previously required the mother to be a permanent resident of the state. The amendments to the scheme, launched by chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sept 28, will apply to babies born in govt hospitals from June 22, 2026. Families seeking benefits under the revised conditions must submit documents establishing that both maternal grandparents are permanent residents of TN.Earlier, a patient Uma Maheswari, who lives with her husband in Karnatakas Mysuru district, was not included in the scheme as she did not meet the permanent residency requirement. On Thursday, the health department said her parents live in Karaikudi in Sivaganga district and she was at their home for childbirth. She delivered a baby by C-section at a govt hospital in Karaikudi on Sept 17. Following the relaxation, the block medical officer presented a 1g gold ring to her baby on Wednesday, the release said.

headline: 'CBI Found Nothing': Bhagwant Mann Hits Out At BJP After 12-Hour Raids Across Punjab
content: Chief Minister Mann said the timing of the raids indicated that the BJP had begun preparing for the Punjab elections. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday hit out at the BJP over the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) raids conducted across the state, claiming that the agencys teams returned empty-handed after a 12-hour operation. Mann said the CBI itself had written that nothing was found" during the searches. He accused the BJP of using central agencies to intimidate political opponents and tarnish the image of an elected Chief Minister ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. - 'Rattled By Love, Support I'm Receiving': Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann Targets BJP Over CBI Raid At Camp Office - Every Mother And Sister Is Brand Ambassador: Mann Govt Distributes 3,824.87 Crore To 75 Lakh Women - 48 Haryana BJP MLAs, 1 Punjab Mission: What PM Modis Saturday Meeting Was Really About - AAP Protests Across Punjab Over ED-CBI Raids, Accuses BJP Of Targeting Mann Govt We Will Not Be Intimidated Taking to X, Mann said the raids were the result of political frustration" and asserted that neither he nor the Punjab Government would bow to pressure. The CBI raids are merely the result of political frustration. We will not be intimidated by or bow down to these petty attempts to scare or defame us. We have come here not to make money, but to serve Punjab, and Punjabis never tolerate injustice," Mann said. Speaking to the media on the sidelines of an event in Sangrur, the Chief Minister said, We are not going anywhere. We will face the central agencies and answer every question. The BJP should understand that Punjabis are not going to be frightened by threats or arm-twisting tactics." They Came With A Purpose, But Found Nothing Mann claimed that the CBI teams had conducted searches for around 12 hours but returned without finding anything. The teams that came to raid Punjab have already returned empty-handed. They came with a purpose, but what did they find? Nothing. They went back empty-handed," he said. He alleged that the raids were aimed not only at him but also at his family and the work of the Punjab Government. This is an attempt to defame me, my family and the work being done by our government. But such conspiracies will not stop us from serving the people of Punjab. The BJP is making futile and desperate attempts to harass us," Mann said. Mann Links Raids To Elections The Chief Minister said the timing of the raids indicated that the BJP had begun preparing for the Punjab elections. Whenever elections approach, a familiar pattern emerges in states where the BJP faces a political challenge. In Delhi they arrested Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, and Satyendar Jain before the elections. In Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Delhi, Haryana and other states, whenever elections approach, central agencies suddenly become active," he said. Mann also claimed that the BJP had harassed political opponents ahead of elections in Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal. He said Punjab would not be intimidated by such tactics and asserted that the BJP should apologise to Punjabis for attempting to tarnish the image of an elected Chief Minister. Raid Yatra Will Be A Flop Referring to the state governments ongoing Yudh Nashean Virudh campaign against drugs, Mann said political pressure would not weaken its resolve. We are fighting against drugs because the future of Punjabs youth is at stake. We are taking this message to every corner of the state. This fight is for the future of our children and to honour the martyrs and those who sacrificed their lives for Punjab," he said. Taking a dig at the BJPs anti-drug campaign, Mann said its Raid Yatra" would also prove to be a flop. Punjabis have never bowed before pressure, and they will not do so now. Punjab is not going to succumb to these tactics. We will stand firm and continue working for Punjab and its people," he said. Punjab Is Our Priority Mann said that while elections were important for the BJP, governance remained the AAP governments priority. For the BJP, everything may be about elections, but for us, governance is about serving the people. Elections will come and go, but Punjab and its people will remain our priority," he said. He also accused the BJP of treating Punjab unfairly on issues including Panjab University, Chandigarh, the Bhakhra Beas Management Board (BBMB), the Sutlej Yamuna Link (SYL) canal, the Harike canal, Day tableaux, RDF funds and border area funds. Mann also referred to the farmers agitation against the farm laws, alleging that more than 700 farmers from Punjab died during the protest. The hands of the BJP are drenched with the murder of more than 700 farmers of the state, who attained martyrdom during the protest against the draconian farm laws," he said. Mann Highlights Canal Irrigation The Chief Minister also highlighted the expansion of canal irrigation in Punjab, saying farmers had benefited from greater availability of canal water. Canal water is reaching farmers in a much bigger way. Because of better availability of canal water, farmers have witnessed an increase in agricultural production of up to four quintals per acre in many areas," he said. Mann said greater use of canal water was necessary to protect Punjabs groundwater and secure the future of agriculture in the state. Taking a dig at opposition parties, he said the Congress was occupied with internal infighting, while the Shiromani Akali Dal had been pushed to the margins because of its past actions. Mann said the Aam Aadmi Party would continue working for the people and script a new chapter in Punjabs political history in the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: Pointing to Indus Water Treaty, Karnataka signals intent to reopen Cauvery water consensus
content: The States response refers to international practices to revisit inter-State water allocations by agreement or adjudication in the changed circumstances, known as rebus sic stantibus The State of Karnataka on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) signalled its intent in the Supreme Court to unravel decades-old judicial consensus on the Cauvery water-sharing dispute on the grounds of inequitable allocation of water and changed circumstances. Even the Union of India has been seeking a modification of the now in abeyance Indus Treaty of 1960 on the ground of changed circumstances, the State said. Karnataka was replying to Tamil Nadus application in the Supreme Court, complaining of backlog in the allocation of the Cauvery water. The States response, filed by advocate Nishanth Patil and settled by senior advocate Mohan Katarki, referred to international practices to revisit inter-State water allocations by agreement or adjudication in the changed circumstances, known as rebus sic stantibus. In view of the looming inequity, the State of Karnataka reserves its right to apply in the changed circumstances for reopening of the inequitable allocation in the Award of Tribunal read with judgment of the Supreme Court. The normal practice is that the water allocations are periodically revisited, the 40-page reply said. The tribunal award, along with the apex court judgment in 2018, had allocated the total annual flow of the Cauvery basin assessed at 740 tmc ft (thousand million cubic feet) at 50% dependability at Lower Coleroon Anicut. This water was apportioned between Karnataka (284.75 tmc ft), Tamil Nadu (404.25 tmc ft), Keralam (30 tmc ft), and Puducherry (7 tmc ft), alongside allocations of 10 tmc ft for environmental flows and 4 tmc ft earmarked as inevitable wastage to the sea. In case the annual yield was less than 740 tmc ft in any water year due to distress caused by less rainfall, the States were directed to share distress proportionately (pro rata). But Karnataka said there was no scientific formula for sharing distress on a pro rata or proportionate manner. The present water year 2026-27 has been a distress one due to the failure of the southwest monsoon from June to September. Water-sharing was entirely based on a sense of equity, but hydrological realities have changed due to climate change, environmental degradation, shifting monsoons, etc. The water allocation and quantities decided by the tribunal, and confirmed by the apex court, followed a rigid pattern which had not taken any of these subsequent developments into consideration, Karnatakas response said. Water-sharing in a distress year has to take into consideration the absence of a scientific distress formula as admitted by Tamil Nadu. Secondly, the absence of a monthly component of annual yield of 740 tmc ft was also a factor, the response said. Moreover, the Cauvery basin has two rainfall seasons: the southwest monsoon from June to September, and the northeast monsoon from October to December or beyond. The northeast rainfall mainly benefit the lower riparian State of Tamil Nadu, while a failure of the earlier monsoon session put Karnataka in dire straits. Again, the response said Tamil Nadu was allocated the lions share of 404.25 tmc ft due to its claim of historic irrigation, while the State of Karnataka had been allocated only 284.75 tmc ft out of the 483 tmc ft available up to Biligundlu, ignoring its drought-prone areas. In a distress water year, the first priority should be given to drinking water requirements, since people cannot live without drinking water. The second priority must be given to the dry irrigation in the drought areas, since irrigation in these drought areas provides minimum income and sustenance to the farmers. Out of the present storage of 48.878 tmc ft in Karnatakas four reservoirs, drinking water requirement is 35 tmc ft. The remaining 13.878 tmc ft is wholly insufficient to meet the dry irrigation in the command of four reservoirs in Karnataka, the States response said.

headline: Seemapuri building collapse: Three dead, including pregnant woman and child, eight injured in Delhi
content: According to the latest updates, eight people have been rescued in injured condition and were sent to hospitals. The incident took place a month after a building in Delhi's Satya Niketan collapsed on September 6, killing seven people. storey residential building came crashing down in northeast Delhi's Seemapuri area on Wednesday afternoon, killing three. The body of a child, aged a year and a half with its head severed, has been recovered from the debris. A pregnant woman was also killed while at least eight people have been injured, officials said. Eight injured after building collapsed in Seemapuri According to PTI, eight injured people have been rescued and sent to hospitals. The incident came a month after Delhi's Satya Niketan collapsed on September 6. It left seven people dead and 12 injured. (this is a developing story)

headline: HC refuses interim relief to EV Velu, son in lake illegal lake soil excavation case
content: Madras high court on Wednesday refused to direct the DVAC from taking any coercive action against former minister and DMK MLA E V Velu and his son E V Kumaran in connection with a case registered against them for allegedly causing a loss of Rs. 8.22 crore to the Tamil Nadu govt by illegally excavating soil from a lake for a DMK Youth Wing conference in Tiruvannamalai.Justice V Lakshminarayanan instead directed the DVAC to file its response to the plea moved by Velu and his son seeking to quash the case by Nov 6. The Supreme Court has categorically said that the high courts must refrain from passing such interim orders in quash petitions, the judge said.On Dec 14, DMKs north zone youth wing conference was held in Tiruvannamalai. To level the conference venue, soil was allegedly illegally excavated from the nearby Malappambadi Lake, covering an area of 12 acres and a depth ranging from 10 to 23 feet causing Rs. 8 crore loss to the govt.Denying the allegations, advocate Rahul Balaji for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners was neither the applicant for the conference nor its organiser. The conference was organised by a Member of Parliament, and the authorities were aware of this.Contending that the provisions invoked in the complaint itself were questionable, he pointed out that the offences included criminal breach of trust and cheating did not arise from the facts alleged. The counsel further submitted that the conference venue was owned by a private limited company and had been used several times previously for holding large conferences. At least three conferences had allegedly been conducted at the same venue earlier.The authorities were attempting to connect a permission granted for excavation of a small quantity of silt with the allegation that material had subsequently been removed from the lakebed in large quantities. The FIR itself merely claimed that there was evidence of removal of material from the lakebed, but questioned who had determined that such removal had actually taken place and on what basis, he said.He further claimed that the FIR was a complete work of fiction and maintained that the allegations were unsupported.

headline: Iran has 'lost complete control' of Hormuz Strait: Rubio
content: The Straits of Hormuz are open. Theres almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So theyve lost complete control of the Straits, Mr. Rubio said "The Straits of Hormuz are open. There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So they've lost complete control of the Straits," Mr. Rubio told reporters during a visit to Athens. He argued that as a result of "crippling" sanctions, the Iranian economy was "about to reach a place few countries in the world have been". Every dollar received by the "radical Shia clerics" is spent on Hezbollah and Hamas, he said. "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period, end of story," Mr. Rubio said. "And anything they agree to that would be acceptable to the United States has to be something that ensures that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon." He argued that what Iran "was trying to do was build up a conventional capability so massive that they would become untouchable".

headline: Yemen's Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airports as conflict deepens
content: The Houthis claimed a flurry of attacks on Saudi targets on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) including firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh airport, as the group battles for territory in Yemen against government forces supported by the kingdom. The Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen, captured swathes of coastal land from Yemen's pro-government forces last month after the country's civil war reignited in July. The fighting has displaced more than 2,00,000 people within the country, the United Nations said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). Yemen's internationally recognised government this week declared a counter-offensive and claims to have uprooted Houthi fighters from strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha. But the Iran-backed Houthis say they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult. "Our armed forces have just targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate, by God's grace, and led to a disruption of air traffic," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) in a post on X. The Saudi-led military coalition that backs Yemen's government said the missile was intercepted. In a separate post the Houthis also said they targeted a military supply convoy near the airport in the Yemeni city of Aden, the interim capital for the government. The Yemeni government's Saba news agency reported missiles and drones targeting that airport. The agency cited transport authorities as saying one of the missiles landed near the runway minutes before the scheduled arrival of a flight from Cairo, which was forced to divert to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia. Houthi drones and missiles also targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, spokesman Saree said, claiming they had "hit their targets accurately". It is the second time this week that the Houthis claimed to have attacked the main airport in the Saudi capital. It is facing frequent temporary closures of its airspace, according to tracking website Flightradar24, but Saudi authorities have not publicly acknowledged the closures or confirmed any strikes targeting the airport. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has been fighting the Houthis since 2015, and is now trying to roll back the group's latest advance. On Monday (October 5, 2026), the coalition said it was providing air support for the counter-offensive launched by the Yemeni government forces. After a four-year ceasefire, Yemen's civil war re-erupted in July. Last month the Houthis seized the entire western coastline along the Red Sea in the country's deadliest fighting in years. On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), new clashes in Yemen's west left at least 62 combatants dead, including 37 Houthis, military sources from both camps told AFP. The government's Saba news agency also said the Houthis fired a missile at the city of Taiz, which is held by government forces, wounding five civilians. "We went out into the street to check on the wounded and saw young civilians who had been hit. The Houthi shell landed in the middle of the street, right in an area crowded with civilians," Taiz resident Al-Fateh al-Eisaei told AFP. Yemen's government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory home to most of the country's population, and much of it held for more than a decade. The war has also caused a humanitarian crisis that has left most of the nation's population dependent on aid. The UN's International Organization for Migration on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) said more than 200,000 people have been internally displaced by the latest round of fighting. It also expressed alarm at the lack of funds available to counter the crisis in one of the world's poorest nations. Mohammed, a 33-year-old charity worker who fled from Mocha to Aden, told AFP on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) that "people there are terrified". "Life in Mocha has come to a complete standstill," he said.

headline: Seemapuri Building Collapse: 3 Dead, Including Pregnant Woman And Child, Rescue Operations Continue
content: 3 Dead, Including Pregnant Woman And Child, Rescue Operations Continue Eight injured people have been rescued and shifted to Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Tahirpur, for further medical treatment. A total of 11 people have been rescued from the debris so far after a five-storey building collapsed in Delhis Seemapuri on Wednesday, a month after the deadly building collapse in Satya Niketan. Of them, eight injured people have been rescued and shifted to Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Tahirpur, for further medical treatment. They have been identified as Momin Mirja, 56; Abdaan, 3; Abdul Rehman, 28; Devruddin, 28; Salma, 50; Chote, 34; Sakina, 35; and Samad, 30. - 'Every Woman Should Feel Safe, Even At 10 PM': Supreme Court's Tough Talk On Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR - Facing Difficulty Breathing: Pregnant Womans Terrifying Call From Under Seemapuri Building Debris - CJP's Abhijeet Dipke Threatens 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' On Oct 10 If Gyanesh Kumar Doesn't Resign - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured Three people have died in the incident, including one child. The deceased include a 12-year-old girl whose identity is yet to be ascertained, Gulafsa, 21, who was approximately four months pregnant, and another child whose identity and details are yet to be ascertained. headline: TN witnesses rise in murder cases & CM is missing in action: Stalin
content: DMK president M K Stalin on Wednesday said Tamil Nadu was witnessing a `disturbing rise in murders, and alleged the chief minister was missing in action to prevent spike in violence. He said the govt was busy with publicity management instead of ensuring public safety.Listing out murders reported from various districts, Stalin in his X post said that criminals have become emboldened because they see no fear of swift investigation or punishment. He accused chief minister C Joseph Vijay of running the state like a film set with staged events. Law and order cannot be handled through slogans, social media posts, or PR-driven appearances, Stalin said alleging that Vijay was on a shooting mode.Stalin said police force has been weakened by political interference, confused priorities, and a lack of clear direction from the top, allowing criminals to operate with confidence. He said TVK regime has created a climate where criminals feel protected and victims feel abandoned.Vijay should stop offering excuses for governance failure and immediately strengthen policing on the ground, fast-track investigations, and ensure visible patrolling in vulnerable areas. Stalin also called for accountability within the Home Department, saying the chief minister cannot evade responsibility when murders continue unabated.

headline: AAP Protests Across Punjab Over ED-CBI Raids, Accuses BJP Of Targeting Mann Govt
content: CBI Raids, Accuses BJP Of Targeting Mann Govt AAP held protests across Punjab against the alleged misuse of ED and CBI by the BJP-led Centre, accusing it of targeting the Bhagwant Mann government. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Punjab on Wednesday held protests in Patiala, Amritsar, Ludhiana and Barnala, alleging that the BJP-led Central government was misusing agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against Opposition-ruled states. AAP ministers, MLAs, leaders and workers participated in the protests and accused the BJP of using central agencies to pressure political opponents and target the Bhagwant Mann-led Punjab government. - Why Mathura, Why Now? CM Yogi, BJP Chief Nitin Nabin To Take Stock Of UP Poll Strategy - BJPs 8 New Rajya Sabha Faces in UP Signal 2027 Strategy - Karnataka SIR Row : BJP Workers Detained Over Protest Against Form 7 FIRs | Gyanesk Kumar| - 48 Haryana BJP MLAs, 1 Punjab Mission: What PM Modis Saturday Meeting Was Really About AAP Accuses Centre Of Targeting Opposition Governments Addressing the protests, AAP leaders alleged that the ED and CBI were being used as political tools against governments that were not led by the BJP. They claimed that similar tactics had been used in states such as West Bengal and Jharkhand and alleged that Punjab was now being targeted ahead of the elections. The party leaders said the alleged action was aimed at defaming the Bhagwant Mann government and diverting attention from its development work. Nothing Found In CBI Raids, Says Balbir Singh Punjab Health Minister Dr Balbir Singh alleged that the CBI raids at eight locations in Punjab were conducted with the intention of damaging the image of the Mann government. The BJP got the CBI to conduct raids at eight locations to defame the Mann government, but nothing was found," he said. Dr Balbir Singh also questioned why the ED and CBI were allegedly silent on a 650-crore scam in Haryana. He claimed that the latest action was an attempt to divert attention from questions being raised against the Election Commission and the BJP. AAP Says Raids Signal Start Of Poll Campaign AAP MLA Jeevan Jyot Kaur, who led the protest in Amritsar, alleged that the BJP had effectively sounded the poll bugle in Punjab through the ED and CBI action. She claimed that the BJP could not match the development work of the Mann government and was therefore relying on pressure and intimidation against the AAP. By getting ED and CBI raids conducted in Punjab, the BJP has sounded the poll bugle for the upcoming elections," she said, adding that Punjabis would not accept such tactics. Effigy Of Modi Government Burnt In Ludhiana In Ludhiana, AAP leaders led by MLA Ashok Parashar organised a protest march. AAP volunteers and members of the public participated in the demonstration, carrying placards and raising questions over the alleged use of central agencies against political opponents. Ludhiana East MLA Daljit Singh Bhola Grewal accused the BJP-led government of trying to stop AAP and Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann through the alleged misuse of the ED and CBI. He said the BJP was rattled" by the guarantees fulfilled and development work carried out by the AAP government in Punjab. He also said Punjabis would not be intimidated by such action. Meet Hayer Says AAP Was Prepared For Such Tactics Speaking during the protest in Barnala, AAP MP Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer alleged that the BJP had a pattern of using central agencies during election periods. He claimed that the AAP had expected such action in the months ahead of the Punjab elections and said the party was prepared to counter what he described as hooliganism". Meet Hayer also alleged that similar attempts had been made in Delhi, Bengal and other states to create fear of central agencies and influence elections. He further claimed that the BJP had failed to find an issue of corruption against the Punjab government during its nearly five-year tenure and was now trying to create issues to target the AAP. Votes Will Be Cast By People Of Punjab, Not Agencies Meet Hayer also targeted the BJP over its electoral presence in Punjab, claiming that the party did not have candidates in all 117 Assembly constituencies or enough workers to deploy at polling booths. He said the BJP could not seek votes in Punjab on the basis of its work and compared its record with the AAP governments work in electricity, canal water, hospitals, sports grounds and roads. Votes will not be cast by the ED or CBI. Votes will be cast by the people of Punjab," Meet Hayer said. He added that the people of Punjab had already made up their minds to re-elect Bhagwant Singh Mann as Chief Minister. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Punjab held widespread protests across Patiala, Amritsar, Ludhiana, and Barnala to oppose the actions of central agencies.

headline: Pakistan Deploys Military Forces To Saudi Arabia As Houthi Attacks Intensify
content: The Mecca Pact was activated after intensified Houthi missile and drone attacks targeted Saudi Arabia, including areas near Riyadh and Medina. Pakistan has confirmed the presence of its troops in Saudi Arabia, with the countrys military spokesman saying the deployment is part of defence ties between the two countries that have continued for several decades. This comes amid the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistani troops have been deployed in Saudi Arabia for decades and continue to perform various roles under the newly formed Mecca Pact. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | - 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised Pakistani troops have been in Saudi Arabia for decades Chaudhry said Pakistan and Saudi Arabia share a longstanding defence relationship, with Pakistani military personnel already present in the kingdom. According to the DG ISPR, Pakistani forces in Saudi Arabia undertake various roles under the Makkah defence agreement. He confirmed that the presence of Pakistani troops is part of the decades-old defence cooperation between the two countries. The confirmation comes under the newly formed Mecca Pact, officially known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement or Makkah Al-Mukarramah Pact for Joint Defence. What is the Mecca Pact? The pact was signed on August 7, by Saudi Arabia, Trkiye and Pakistan in Mecca. It states that an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be treated as an attack on all three, creating a NATO Article 5-style collective defence commitment. Under the collective defence clause, an attack on one member is regarded as an attack on all three, leading to consultations and a coordinated response. However, the signatories have stressed that the agreement is defensive in nature. It is not intended to replace existing alliances or automatically require military intervention, with responses subject to consultation. Joint exercises, intelligence sharing The agreement also provides for the creation of a permanent secretariat in Riyadh. Lt Gen (Retd) Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the alliances first secretary-general for a three-year term. The pact envisages cooperation in areas including joint military exercises, intelligence sharing and defence-industrial collaboration. It also covers coordination on technologies such as drones, electronic warfare, artificial intelligence and air and missile defence. Experts have described the pact as an effort by three middle powers" to jointly address security concerns instead of relying solely on external guarantees. The arrangement comes amid regional uncertainty linked to the wider Iran-Israel conflict and perceived gaps in the Gulf security architecture. While the pact is officially described as non-targeted and focused on stability, it is widely viewed as a deterrence signal primarily towards Iran and Israel. Pact activated after Houthi attacks The Mecca Pact saw its first activation this month following intensified Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi targets. The attacks included claims of strikes near Riyadhs airport, an Aramco facility and power infrastructure near Medina. Saudi Arabia subsequently convened an emergency meeting of the pacts Strategic Political and Defence Committee. The three countries agreed to activate deterrence measures" and begin the rapid deployment of Turkish and Pakistani military forces and defence capabilities to Saudi Arabia. This marked the first invocation of the Mecca Pact. However, detailed troop numbers, mission mandates and command arrangements have not been fully disclosed publicly. The Mecca Pact, officially known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement or Makkah Al-Mukarramah Pact for Joint Defence, was signed on August 7 by Saudi Arabia, Trkiye, and Pakistan in Mecca. It functions as a collective defence commitment where an armed attack on any of the three member countries is treated as an attack on all of them, triggering mandatory consultations and a coordinated response.
