headline: 'Raised India To The Heavens': Ex-Serbian President Praises PM Modi, Says Attempts Being Made To 'Tear Him Down'
content: Vucic's comments surfaced in India on Wednesday as PM Modi marked 25 years of continuous service as the head of a government, first as Gujarat CM and then as Prime Minister. Former Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic has praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for elevating Indias standing on the global stage, while claiming that attempts were being made to undermine" and tear down" the Indian Prime Minister. Vucic made the remarks during an interview with Serbian journalist and television host Milomir Mari on irilica Milomira Maria, a political programme broadcast by Prva TV in Serbia. The interview, which aired on October 5, was held ahead of Serbias parliamentary elections and was centred on the theme Ne dam da srue Srbiju" (I wont let them bring Serbia down"). - 'We Will Do It': PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service - 'Outstanding Leadership': World Leaders Congratulate PM Modi On Completion Of 25 Years In Public Service - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country You have a leader like Narendra Modi. And now there is an effort to undermine him. PM Modi has raised India to the heavens. He tries to follow the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi," Vucic said during the conversation. India became so important on the world stage because of him. Became a force. He has done tremendous things, yet they try to tear him down by claiming he failed or dont know what. It has become a pattern," he added. Vucic did not specify who he believed was attempting to undermine PM Modi or identify the alleged efforts against the Prime Minister. Vucics Modi Praise Comes As PM Marks 25 Years Vucics comments surfaced in India on Wednesday as PM Modi marked 25 years of continuous service as the head of a government, first as Gujarat Chief Minister and then as Prime Minister. Vucic also congratulated Modi on the milestone in a post on X, saying few people could claim to have devoted a quarter of a century to serving their country. Congratulations, @NarendraModi, on completing 25 years of public service at the highest level. Few people can say they have devoted a quarter of a century to serving their country, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and then as Prime Minister of India," Vucic wrote. I know how deeply you care about India and its future, and the world can see how high you have raised India," he added, wishing Modi many more years of good health, strength and success" in serving the Indian people. The BJP shared a clip of Vucics remarks on Wednesday while marking Modis 25-year milestone, writing: When world leaders speak like this about our Prime Minister, it says everything. India under PM Modi is rising, and the world is taking notice." Vucic Now Campaigning For Parliamentary Polls Vucic, who served as Serbias president for two five-year terms, resigned from the presidency last month as he prepares to contest Serbias upcoming parliamentary elections. He is leading the Aleksandar Vucic United Serbia" list and has been campaigning to return to government as prime minister. During his appearance on irilica, Vucic discussed his campaign, the opposition and the political situation in Serbia. Serbian media reported that he described the countrys political situation as a moment in which the state is in danger". Vucic and Modi have maintained close diplomatic engagement in recent years. The two leaders met in New Delhi in February on the sidelines of the India AI Impact Summit and discussed strengthening cooperation in defence, manufacturing, digital public infrastructure, fertilisers and infrastructure. Vucic has also previously highlighted Indias growing role in global affairs. In February, he wrote about the India AI Impact Summit, describing it as a moment that positioned India at the centre of the global AI dialogue. Aleksandar Vucic praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for elevating India's global standing and following the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, while claiming that patterned attempts are being made to undermine and tear him down.

headline: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
content: The French government said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boys hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters accusations of police brutality. Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday (October 8, 2026). The wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron. At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school. We saw there were lots of crumbling walls, a shortage of teachers in public schools, absent teachers, said Gabriel Fillieule, who used to attend a public school but now goes to a private one. He and others said they were protesting to demand better learning conditions for all. Polices use of force being investigated While most of Wednesdays (October 6, 2026) blockades were peaceful, police used tear gas and pushed back protesters in a street barricaded by rubbish bins outside Sciences Po university in central Paris. Rights groups, labour unions, students and some opposition politicians have accused the police of using disproportionate force to quell the wave of protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said he had ordered the suspension of the use of stun grenades following an incident in the northern city of Lens on Monday (October 5, 2026) in which there was a strong possibility the firing of a stun grenade had caused a teenager to lose his hand. I am suspending their use for the high-school students movement until light has been shed on what happened in this case, said the Minister, who added that 18 incidents in total had been referred to the police inspectorate for investigation. Protesters have said they blame poor learning conditions for a sharp drop in French teenagers scores in reading and maths over the past decade. French 15-year-olds scored 43 points lower in reading in 2025 than in 2015, according to the OECDs Programme for International Student Assessment, the biggest drop among the OECD countries. Their maths scores also dropped the most. But the government, under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, has little spare cash to address students complaints of teacher shortages, ageing school buildings and inequalities between schools in affluent and poor areas. Twenty-four high schools damaged by fire or vandalism Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has acknowledged the legitimate demands of Frances students but also described the unrest as the most violent student demonstrations in decades. Education Minister Edouard Geffray told parliament that 24 high schools had been damaged by fire or vandalism to the extent that they would remain closed for weeks, meaning some 30,000 students would receive no in-person teaching until they reopened. He estimated it would cost 20 million to 30 million ($22 million to $34 million) to fix the damage. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to opinion polls, said those who damaged schools should pay for the repairs rather than taxpayers. The government has adopted a similar stance and has a bill going through parliament that aims to set up such a system. Unrest elsewhere Elsewhere in Europe, where budgets have been under pressure as governments respond to successive cost-of-living and energy crises, students in parts of Belgium staged similar protests. In the Belgian city of Liege in the southern French-speaking Wallonia region, at least 107 people have been arrested in connection with student protests this month, the Belga news agency reported. Teachers are also on strike. In Portugal, the main teachers union FENPROF launched an indefinite strike in mid-September over working conditions, with teachers refusing to do any unpaid work beyond the 35 hours a week mandated by law. And in Spain, teachers unions have been protesting conditions in state schools. Teachers in Madrid plan a strike on October 14 to press demands including a reduction in hours, smaller class sizes and higher salaries.

headline: Southwest monsoon withdrawal advances, rainfall to continue in several states
content: The southwest monsoon is likely to withdraw from more parts of Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, and some areas of Telangana and north interior Karnataka over the next 2-3 days, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The monsoon withdrawal line currently extends through parts of Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Karnataka. The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon typically starts from western Rajasthan in September before gradually progressing across northwest and central India, and subsequently moving toward the southern peninsula and eastern regions. However, the pace of withdrawal depends on prevailing rainfall and atmospheric conditions. The development is watched closely by policymakers and agricultural markets as the southwest monsoon contributes about 70% of India's annual rainfall and plays a crucial role in farm output, reservoir levels and rural economic activity. Meanwhile, several parts of northwest India are likely to receive rainfall over the coming week, with the IMD forecasting varying intensity across the region. Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Muzaffarabad are likely to experience fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on 8 October and 10 October. Rainfall activity is expected to become isolated to scattered on 9 October and 11 October. Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall during 8-13 October. The Haryana-Chandigarh-Delhi region and Punjab may also see isolated to scattered rainfall throughout 8-13 October. West Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive rain during 8-9 October, while East Uttar Pradesh could see rainfall from 8-10 October. Further west, West Rajasthan is expected to receive isolated rainfall on 11-12 October, while East Rajasthan may see rainfall on 12 October. Also, several parts of central and east India are likely to receive rainfall over the coming days. In Central India, Chhattisgarh and East Madhya Pradesh are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall from 8-9 October. Chhattisgarh could also experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 4050 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, on 8 October. East Madhya Pradesh is likely to see isolated thunderstorms and lightning on 8 October. In east India, Bihar is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall during 8-10 October, while Odisha could see rainfall through 13 October. Jharkhand and Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim are expected to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on 8 October. Gangetic West Bengal may see widespread rainfall on 8 October, with isolated showers on 9-10 October. The Andaman & Nicobar Islands are also likely to receive rainfall, with fairly widespread to widespread showers expected from 9-13 October. In south peninsular India, rainfall activity is expected to remain significant. Kerala and Mahe are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rain during 8-11 October, while Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are expected to see widespread rainfall on 9 October. Isolated to scattered rain is also likely across Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka during 8-13

headline: 24 Killed, 60 Injured In Fresh Russian Missile, Drone Strikes On Ukraine
content: Russias latest missile and drone barrage across Ukraine killed 24 civilians, including four children, and injured around 60 others. At least 24 civilians, including four children, were killed and around 60 others injured after Russia launched a fresh wave of missile and drone attacks across Kyiv and nearly a dozen other Ukrainian regions overnight, Ukrainian officials said. The strikes caused significant damage in several areas, with residential buildings among the sites hit in the latest Russian barrage. - Towering Black Smoke Seen Over Russia Coast After Ukraine Hits Tanker; All 23 Indian Crew Rescued - Russia Stood With India When It Mattered: EAM S. Jaishankar Reaffirms Moscow Ties | Breaking News - Russia Warns Diplomats To Leave Ukraine Over Fresh Strikes Threat: 'Responsibility Entirely With...' - Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridge During German Chancellor's Visit, Vows To Intensify Attacks Four Children Killed In Apartment Strike The strikes caused widespread damage, with one Russian missile hitting a residential building and killing four children. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said three of the children were just one year old, while the fourth was eight. Ukraine had been expecting a major Russian attack. A day earlier, Zelenskyy said the countrys intelligence agencies had detected preparations for a large-scale assault. Despite the warning, Ukrainian air defences were unable to prevent the strikes from causing heavy casualties and damage. Ukraine Struggles To Counter Russian Weapons The latest attacks have once again highlighted the challenges faced by Ukraine in defending itself against Russias long-range weapons. Kyiv is particularly struggling to intercept ballistic missiles and a newer type of jet-powered drone that Moscow has increasingly used in its attacks. Ukraines ability to counter Russian ballistic weapons has also been affected by shortages of ammunition for its US-made Patriot air defence systems. At the same time, Kyiv is working to develop a new generation of interceptors capable of dealing with Russias faster, high-altitude jet-powered drones. Aerial War Continues Amid Battlefield Stalemate The overnight strikes came as Russia and Ukraine continued a wider long-range aerial conflict, while their ground forces remain largely locked in a stalemate. More than four and a half years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion, repeated aerial attacks are causing growing damage on both sides, although the impact is considered far more serious for Ukraine because of its smaller resources. US Peace Efforts Yet To Bring Breakthrough Efforts led by the United States to push the two sides towards peace have so far offered little hope of an immediate reduction in the fighting. Discussions about possible low-level technical talks remain ongoing. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin continues to pursue the war, believing that sustained pressure could eventually force Ukraine to give in and weaken the resolve of its Western allies, according to Western analysts. At least 24 civilians, including four children, were killed and around 60 others injured after Russia launched a fresh wave of overnight missile and drone attacks across Kyiv and nearly a dozen other Ukrainian regions. One Russian missile struck a residential building, killing four children, three of whom were one year old and the fourth eight.

headline: Trump-backed Ken Paxton admits Iran war, fuel prices are hurting his Texas Senate bid - Report
content: Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton privately acknowledged that the Iran war and rising fuel prices are creating difficulties for his campaign, telling donors and lobbyists that several factors affecting the race were beyond his control, according to Axios. Paxton, Texas attorney general and a close ally of President Donald Trump, as per the report, made the remarks during a closed-door fundraiser in Washington, DC, last month. Axios said it has obtained an audio recording of the meeting from an attendee who opposed Paxton and was granted anonymity because the event was private. Asked what issues were weighing on his campaign, Paxton said the problem was not tariffs but the war and rising gasoline and diesel prices, according to the recording obtained by the news outlet. He specifically pointed to diesel prices of more than $6 a gallon, saying higher fuel costs were being felt by consumers and were contributing to increased food prices and other expenses. Paxton described affordability as the biggest problem facing his campaign and linked it to difficulties with his polling numbers. When an attendee noted that Paxton could not stop the war, the Republican candidate agreed and said he had no control over gas prices. He also acknowledged that several factors affecting a federal Senate race were outside his control. I dont make the decisions, Paxton said, according to the media outlet, adding that he did not know what was behind some of the decisions. Paxton pointed to his proposed tax-cut plan as a way to address affordability concerns. The plan includes new deductions related to housing and healthcare, as well as an expansion of the child tax credit, according to Axios. Im just trying to figure out ways I can help people, Paxton said, adding that his role would be to propose legislation. The Paxton campaign rejected the significance of the comments, telling Axios that the attorney general was simply acknowledging the high cost of gasoline and diesel and the pressure those prices were putting on Texans. The campaign said Trump was working to bring prices down and argued that Paxton would go to Washington to support those efforts while seeking to put more money into families pockets. Trump is scheduled to rally with Paxton in San Antonio on Wednesday. Paxton is running against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico after defeating Republican Senator John Cornyn in the May primary runoff. A Talarico victory would mark the first time a Democrat has been elected to the US Senate from Texas since the 1980s. Paxton has been among Trump's most loyal political allies. Trump backed Paxton during the Republican primary despite appeals from Senate Republicans to support Cornyn.

headline: Plague scare in Russia, tourism season in Goa, and a screening demand from opposition leader
content: With the death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in Russias Irkutsk region in Siberia sparking public health concerns about pneumonic plague during Goas tourist season, the states Opposition Leader has called for health screening of all tourists arriving in the coastal state from Russia. This comes as Goas tourist season kicks off, with the first batch of international tourists arriving last week. A woman working at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East died of plague last week. While 200 people who came into contact with her have now been quarantined, Russian authorities claim the worker died on October 2 of pneumonia of an as-yet-unestablished origin, and that there is no risk of an epidemic breaking out. In Goa, which sees a significant number of Russian tourists, the development has sparked concerns. On Wednesday, Congress leader Yuri Alemao, the Leader of Opposition in the Goa Assembly, said the government must immediately introduce precautionary health screening for tourists from Russia. The remarks come a day after the World Health Organization (WHO) sought more information on the death from Russia, saying that timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks. I demand surveillance for passengers arriving from Russia, in coordination with Central health authorities. Tourism is vital to Goa, but public health and the safety of Goans must come first. Prevention is always better than crisis management, said Alemao in a post on X. Alemao said the government cannot afford complacency regarding concerns after the death of the laboratory worker in Russia. With regular charter flights now bringing tourists from Russia to Goa, I demand the government immediately introduce precautionary health screening, he said. For his part, Kedar Naik, the Goa governments director of tourism, said the department is yet to receive any advisory from the WHO or any other health organisation regarding the issue. As of now, the [tourist] season is going well. We are welcoming all the tourists to Goa. There is no concern since we have not received any advisory from the WHO or any other organisation. If the health regulators issue any advisory in this regard, we will look into it and accordingly initiate corrective measures, Naik said. The tourism season in the coastal state officially commenced last week with the arrival of the first charter flight from Russias Yekaterinburg, carrying 162 passengers to Goa. Another charter with 285 passengers from Moscow arrived on October 4. After the arrival of the first charter flight from Russia on September 30, Tourism Minister Rohan Khaunte said the tourism departments approach is to strengthen the traditional source markets such as Russia and the UK, while simultaneously widening Goas international footprint. As connectivity grows, we also want international travellers to discover more of Goaour heritage, culture, wellness, nature, cuisine, spirituality and the diverse experiences that lie beyond our beaches. Our focus is on building Goa as a better-connected, responsible and year-round global destination, Khaunte had said.

headline: Petrol Pump Dispute Turns Deadly: Indian Oil Official Stabbed 7 Times In Maharashtra's Hingoli
content: Indian Oil Official Stabbed 7 Times In Maharashtra's Hingoli Mahesh Shelke, an Indian Oil official, was stabbed seven times with a knife, allegedly by the son of the petrol pump operator. An Indian Oil sales manager was allegedly stabbed to death in Maharashtras Hingoli after a dispute over the sealing of a petrol pump turned violent on Tuesday evening. Mahesh Shelke, an Indian Oil official, was stabbed seven times with a knife, allegedly by the son of the petrol pump operator. The petrol pump had remained shut for three months because of technical issues. The operator, Sahebrao Pandavveer, and his family reportedly requested officials to give them a month to restart the petrol pump. However, the officials refused the request, police said. The disagreement then escalated into a heated argument between the two sides. Sales manager stabbed seven times During the argument, Sahebrao Pandavveers son, Umesh Pandavveer, allegedly attacked Shelke with a knife. Shelke was stabbed seven times in the attack, according to police. The Indian Oil official died following the assault. The incident took place as Shelke and his team were carrying out the process of sealing the petrol pump in Chondhi. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the dispute and the subsequent stabbing. The case centres on the disagreement over the petrol pump, which had been closed for three months due to technical problems, and the request by the operators family for additional time to resume operations. The Indian Oil official, Mahesh Shelke, was attacked during a dispute that broke out when he and his team arrived to seal a petrol pump in Ambachondi village that had been closed for three months due to technical issues, and the operator's family requested more time to restart operations, which the officials refused.

headline: Meet Neuhof School Band from Mizoram: Winners of Yamaha Teens Rock 2026 - What maestro AR Rahman said about them
content: Winners of Yamaha Teens Rock 2026 - What maestro AR Rahman said about them Yamaha Music India held its Grand Finale of Yamaha Teens Rock 2026 The Battle of Bands at Bengaluru. Promoting young bands from several schools across India, the event was marked by a night full of talented and creative live performances as young musicians took to the stage to showcase their music. After several performances, Neuhof School Band from Neuhof English Medium School from Mizoram became the winner of Yamaha Teens Rock 2026. They were followed by CS Howlers from CS Academy, Tamil Nadu as the First Runner-up and The Apricity from Shri Hanuman Mandir Dharamshala School, West Bengal as the Second Runner-up. The winning Neuhof School Band took home a cash prize of 4.5 lakh. Neuhof School Band consists of six members, comprising three boys and three girls from Classes VIII and IX. The band features Silvya Lalmuankimi on vocals, Lalthlamuani Pachuau and Robert Van Lal Din on keyboards, Elnathan Vanlalnunzira Ralte on lead guitar, Grace Vannunmawii on bass, and Lalchhanchhuaha on drums. The event was also attended by AR Rahman, Brand Ambassador of Yamaha Music India. Talking about it, Rehman said, as quoted by ANI, Music gives young people a space to express, and platforms like Teens Rock give that expression a stage. It was wonderful to see these talented bands come together, perform with passion and bring their unique identities into their music. I congratulate all the finalists and hope this experience inspires them to continue learning, creating and developing their own musical voices. Initiatives like Teens Rock play an important role in encouraging more young people to experience the power of music and performance. Yamaha Teens Rock 2026 saw more than 680 registrations and over 270 video submissions from young bands this year. After several eliminations and multi-stage selections, six bands qualified for the Grand Finale. Out of these, five qualified as zonal winners while one was selected via public voting. The performances were judged by Yamaha Artists Mr Ranjit Barot, Mr Gulraj Singh and Mr Rhythm Shaw, alongside Mr Stuart Briner, director of music and performing arts at Trinity College in London. The initiative aims to support young musicians in their musical career by creating opportunities and providing them a platform to learn, collaborate and perform. It also contributes to the growth of India's music culture. Sneha Biswas specialises in covering entertainment and pop culture, with a specialisation on Bollywood, Hollywood, OTT platforms, K-pop, K-dramas, and major developments in the US entertainment industry. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: 'Facing Difficulty Breathing': Pregnant Woman's Terrifying Call From Under Seemapuri Building Debris
content: Block, New Seemapuri, in Shahdara district, collapsed. A five-storey building collapse in Delhis New Seemapuri left several people trapped under the rubble on Wednesday, with rescue teams racing to reach those buried beneath the debris. Among those feared trapped was a four-month pregnant woman who managed to call her family and said she was struggling to breathe. One person was reported dead after the five-storey building in E-Block, New Seemapuri, in Shahdara district, collapsed at around 3.30 pm. The collapse partially damaged two adjoining buildings and left several people trapped under the debris. - Mahalaya 2026: How To Perform Tarpan At Home, Mantras And Who Can Do It - Gujarat Shocker: Teen Alleges Father Raped Her, Mother Took Nude Photos For Talking To Male Friend - The Millennial Mom | Postpartum, Breastfeeding, And The Bittersweet Reality No One Prepared Me For - 'Something Bigger Than Me': Esteban Ribovics On Building Legacy Beyond MMA Delhi Fire Services (DFS), the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), police and civic officials launched a rescue operation at the site. The building, numbered E-401, stood on a plot of approximately 25 square yards. Eight injured people, including a three-year-old child, were rescued and taken to the GTB Hospital emergency department, which is currently operating from the Rajiv Gandhi Hospital campus. She is four months pregnant A 30-year-old resident, Sameena, told Hindustan Times that her 21-year-old sister Gulfisha managed to call from beneath the debris. She is four months pregnant. Her four-year-old daughter and owners daughter are with her too. She said she is stuck inside and is facing difficulty breathing," Sameena said, according to the Hindustan Times report. Gulfisha, a resident of D-Block, had gone to meet her mother when the building collapsed. The rescue operation was being carried out from the Eidgah premises as the lanes on the other side of the collapsed building were severely cramped. Mother feared trapped under rubble Haseena, 42, said her mother was trapped under the rubble. She was crossing the street when it collapsed. My father was walking ahead. He told me," she said, the report added. A relative of the building owner, who identified himself as 33-year-old Mohammed Akbar, said the property belonged to his father-in-law, Mohammed Anwar. The whole family lives here across four floors. The building collapsed in front of me," Akbar said. He said three members of the family, including his sister-in-law, were trapped following the collapse. According to Ameena, the owners daughter, the building adjoining their house had been undergoing demolition for the past five to six days. They were using a machine to demolish. This impacted our house," she claimed. Ameena, as quoted by HT, said the family had moved into the building around four months ago after constructing it. They had previously lived in another building owned by them in the neighbourhood. Eight injured taken to hospital Eight people rescued from the collapsed building were taken to GTB Hospital, officials said. Those injured included a woman and a three-year-old child, while the remaining injured were men. Those identified among the injured include Anwar, the owner; his wife Salma; their son Abdur Rehman; three-year-old Abdan; and Sakina, a tenant. The injured were being treated at Rajiv Gandhi Hospital. A local resident claimed that an adjoining house had been undergoing demolition for five to six days using a machine, which impacted their building. Additionally, locals mentioned that the structure had developed cracks following tremors felt in Delhi-NCR from an earthquake in Uttarakhand.

headline: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, three dead: officials
content: Israel carried out new strikes in Gaza on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) as it marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, with Palestinian officials reporting three people dead. Also read | Israelis mark three years since Hamas attack that set off Gaza assault Loud bangs across the border in Gaza were audible from the site of the Nova music festival just as family members gathered at dawn to mourn the more than 300 revellers killed three years earlier. In Gaza City, Al-Shifa hospital reported two people killed in an Israeli strike overnight. Gaza's civil defence identified one of the dead as Mohamed Tamous and said he was a volunteer for the agency, which serves as an emergency rescue service under Hamas. The Israeli military said it struck and killed "two Hamas terrorists who had exited Kamal Adwan Hospital in the northern Gaza Strip," adding that one had "planted explosives... in the area of the Yellow Line with the intention of harming IDF troops." The so-called Yellow Line demarcates the areas under Hamas and Israeli military control in the Gaza Strip. The military identified one of those killed in the strike as Tamous, whom it said was a sniper in Hamas's military wing while simultaneously working for the civil defence. In the southern city of Khan Yunis, Nasser Hospital said that a 60-year-old man, Hisham Ibrahim Abu Mustafa, was killed in an Israeli strike and that others were injured. On the third anniversary of the first day of the war in Gaza, living conditions remain dire in the coastal Palestinian territory, despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025. "After three years of siege, killing and destruction, Israel has turned the Gaza Strip into an uninhabitable place," said Gaza City resident Mahmoud Abu Hasira. Beneath the rubble Hundreds of thousands of displaced people still live in tent cities and makeshift shelters that sprawl on beaches or next to piles of rubble from bombed-out residential buildings. "We once had homes, but now we have lost our loved ones, whose bodies still lie beneath the rubble," said Bassam Nasser, a resident of Beit Hanoun, a now largely destroyed city in Gaza's north, who was displaced in the early days of the war. Israel says it controls about 60% of Gaza, on the territory's outer perimeter, including Beit Hanoun, while most of the Palestinian population lives in the remaining Hamas-controlled areas. Though Israel eased its restrictions on aid trucks entering Gaza after the ceasefire, Ahmed Nasser, another resident of Gaza City, told AFP that life remained desperately hard. "The war and the famine have left us hungry, fearful and displaced, living in tents and struggling with soaring prices," he said. Israel's military offensive has displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations. Since the ceasefire was declared last October, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,460 people in Gaza, according to the ministry.

headline: India calls for de-escalation after Black Sea ship attacks
content: escalation after Black Sea ship attacks The targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways must be restored at the earliest, the Ministry of External (MEA) official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Wednesday. We have seen a string of attacks targeting commercial vessels in the Black Sea region. We condemn such attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger the lives of our seafaring community, he said. Listing out the four incidents, he said that the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov came under attack while it was plying in the Black Sea. There were three Indian nationals onboard. One of them was injured and has since received medical treatment, he said, adding that the Indian embassy in Romania is in touch with them for their safety and welfare. We thank the Romanian authorities for their support and swift action, he said. A Togo-flagged ship, Alfa Watan, was attacked yesterday and the fate of its crew is unknown, he said. Another vessel, Palau-flagged MV ABLE, came under a drone attack, but fortunately all its 18 crew, including 7 Indian nationals, have been rescued. One Indian national suffered injuries and is under medical supervision, the MEA spokesperson said, and thanked the Bulgarian authorities for their timely help. Our Mission in Bulgaria is offering all possible assistance to our seafarers, he said. The fourth ship which came under attack is the Liberia-flagged Aframax Rio, an oil tanker. All the crew, consisting of 23 Indian seafarers, have been rescued, he said. The Liberia-flagged vessel carrying oil, with a crew of 23 Indian nationals, came under attack by drone boats off Russias Black Sea coast, Russian authorities said. The crew has been saved and evacuated to shore, a spokesman for the Russian transport ministry told state-run TASS news agency. The Aframax Rio tanker came under attack on Tuesday by unmanned surface vessels (USVs), and open fire is raging in the Black Sea waters, the Russian transport ministry said. The ministry said the vessels all Indian crew of 23 was saved and none was hurt. The incident took place near Sochi, Russias popular resort city on the Black Sea coast. When asked about the Indian proposal to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the MEA spokesperson said, On the issue of the Ukraine conflict, India has consistently maintained that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward. On Sunday, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India has moved beyond advocacy and stepped up its efforts in recent months to resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging in conversations with both Kyiv and Moscow. In Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday that India has declared its readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the Ukraine conflict and Russia is grateful to New Delhi for such willingness. Indeed, India is declaring readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the situation surrounding Ukraine, Peskov was quoted as saying by the state-run TASS news agency. His statement came days after Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described Indias proposal for a possible ceasefire with Russia as the broadest among four offers received by Kyiv. The other proposals had come from Turkiye, Egypt and the US. We have four proposals. The broadest one is Indias proposal. We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in this combination, Sybiha had told reporters in Kyiv last week.

headline: Modi calls for secure, open maritime order amid geopolitical disruptions
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order built on cooperation and mutual trust, as India seeks to expand its maritime economy, shipbuilding and green shipping capabilities. In a written message to the third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue, organised jointly by the ministry of ports, shipping and waterways and Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi, Modi said developments in one part of the worlds oceans can have consequences far beyond their shores, making global dialogue and cooperation increasingly important. Our vision is of a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order that brings greater peace, prosperity and progress for all, Modi said on Wednesday, adding that he was confident the dialogue would strengthen the larger vision. The message comes against a backdrop of growing geopolitical and economic disruptions to global shipping, including risks to trade routes and supply chains following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the US-Iran war. India has increasingly emphasised the need for secure sea lanes, resilient supply chains and greater international cooperation in the maritime domain. He linked India's maritime ambitions to its broader goal of becoming a developed economy by 2047. He said the country was looking at the oceans with a renewed sense of purpose while simultaneously seeking to protect marine ecosystems. Indias maritime vision extends across regions and oceans and is built on cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit, Modi said. We believe the oceans must become a source of shared prosperity, where every country has a voice and an opportunity to grow. The remarks come as India is seeking a larger role in global maritime trade and supply chains, including through investments in ports, shipbuilding, shipping and maritime infrastructure. Modi said Indias major ports had nearly doubled their capacity, while turnaround times had fallen significantly. The government is also preparing for what he described as a new era of shipbuilding and green shipping, alongside investments in ocean science and exploration. He also highlighted the governments efforts to modernise the regulatory framework governing the maritime sector through new-generation maritime laws, aimed at creating a contemporary framework for the industry. The government is also investing in ocean science and exploration to better understand the country's seas and use them responsibly. India has also brought in new-generation maritime laws to create a modern framework for the sector. At the same time, we are investing in ocean science and exploration so that we can understand our seas better and make responsible use of their immense potential, Modi said. Indias maritime push is also being supported by its large seafarer workforce. Modi said Indian seafarers now constitute the worlds second-largest maritime workforce, with young Indians earning recognition across the worlds oceans. He said India is protecting ocean health and coastal ecosystems as it builds a stronger maritime economy. The Prime Minister invoked Indias long maritime history, referring to the ancient port city of Lothal, the Chola dynasty and the naval traditions of Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Indian sailors and traders, he said, historically carried goods, ideas, stories and culture to distant lands. Modi said India's relationship with the ocean was also one of responsibility, with the country seeking to balance economic expansion with protection of coastal and marine ecosystems. He expressed hope that Sagarmanthan would generate fresh ideas, deepen international partnerships and create new opportunities, while reinforcing the principle that the oceans should remain a source of shared

headline: 'Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir': he sold Kashmiri Pandit land that he didn't own
content: In hot pursuit of this man, J&K Police arrived at a house in Zewan area in Srinagars outskirts on September 24. A woman who answered the door told them that he had already left. The personnel asked her to show them the room where he stayed. The woman led them and, gingerly, tapped on the door. The team instinctively spread out; some barged into the room, others secured the windows. Inside,an elderly man sat under a dim light, his favourite Urdu newspaper in hand, with little knowledge that it was this love for the broadsheet that landed police at the door of the house where he had been hiding all this while. He is Somnath Koul. Or Mohan Lal Dhar. Or Brijnath Bhat. Or Hadinath Dhar. It depends on whom you ask, or which identity document he chooses to produce. But the police department in the Union Territory already had a moniker for him: Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir. Police say that for almost a decade now, Koul, now 80, had been swindling Valley residents with promises of selling them land left behind by Kashmiri Pandit migrants like himself. To some, he would pose as an attorney facilitating the sale. In other cases, he would pose as the owner himself, beguiling the potential buyers with his story of having to leave his home due to the onset of militancy in the 1990s. None of the land that he wanted to sell belonged to him in the first place, said a police officer. Koul would identify the land left behind by the Pandits, strike a deal with prospective buyers with forged documents, collect the money and disappear, the officer added. That was until January this year when police found Kouls photograph affixed to one of the fake sale documents. It set off a nine-month-long hunt that eventually uncovered a trail of fraudulent land deals dating as far back as 2017. Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Crime Branch. (Image: Special arrangement) In November last year, a south Kashmir resident approached the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Crime Branch, stating that he had bought five kanals (a little over half an acre) of land at Drusoo village in Pulwama and 300 poplar trees planted on a parcel of land in Bijbehara after paying Rs. 93 lakh. The complainant said that when he went to court for ratification of Agreement to Sell, he was told that the land doesnt belong to the person shown as seller in the agreement. On April 1 this year, the Crime Branch registered a formal FIR against Koul, setting off an investigation in motion. It was a piece of land belonging to a migrant Kashmiri Pandit and Koul had posed as the owners attorney. In the case of the Bijbehara property, he claimed to be the owner himself, said an investigating officer. When we contacted the actual owner, he told us he had not given anyone a power of attorney. The Agreement to Sell listed Koul as a resident of a locality in Jammu with an alternate address in Bengaluru. But when police teams reached the two addresses, Koul was nowhere to be found. But the so-called agreement offered police a crucial clue. Ghulam Mohidin Dar, a resident of Budgam in central Kashmir, had signed the document as a witness. In August, Crime Branch sleuths reached his house. Dar told the officials he would change his clothes and accompany them. We were waiting for him when his family members attacked us, an officer said. In the melee, Dar managed to escape. On September 17, after a 10-kilometre chase from Rajbagh to Kanipora, Dar was nabbed. Police investigations revealed that Dar, himself an influential land broker, would lure the buyers for Koul. This is when police started learning about Kouls multiple identities. Said to be a retired Ayurvedic doctor, Kouls name in his service records is Brijnath Bhat. He owns two Voter Identity cards and two Aadhaar cards each. In one voter card, he is Brijnath Bhat. In the other, he is Hadinath Dhar. His two Aadhaar cards identify him as Somnath Koul and Mohan Lal Dhar, respectively. Of the four documents, only one could be genuine. We checked with the Aadhaar database, his name was recorded as Somnath Koul, says an officer. It was a mystery for us. If his name in so-called service records was Brijnath Bhat, how could he make an Aadhaar in the name of Somnath Koul? Search on for Dar by Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Crime Branch officials in Budgam. (Image: Special arrangement) Finger tips damaged, iris altered As the mystery about his identity deepened, police decided to go for biometrics. It threw up more surprises. He had destroyed his fingertips. When we asked him about it, he said he had accidentally burnt them, the officer said. His iris scans too failed many times. The official at the Aadhaar centre said he most likely had an eye surgery. We really had a hard time getting one of his iris scans matched. The officials went through his Aadhaar records and were left befuddled once more. In 2016, Koul applied for an Aadhaar card in the name of Brijnath Bhat, a resident of Muthi in Jammu. The name matched his service records. In 2022, he, however, changed the name on his Aadhaar to Somnath Koul. We are checking how it happened, the officer said. The Agreement to sell also showed his name as Somnath Koul. The man himself, though, remained elusive, prompting J&K police to liken him with Charles Sobhraj the famous con artist. But interrogating Dar, police came upon a curious piece of information. Koul was an avid reader of newspapers. Apart from his favourite one published from the Valley, he would also Back at the Crime Branch, officials went through its own database to check cases against different identities assumed by Koul. They found at least four other cases, the oldest one dating back to 2017 and registered at the EOW of the Crime Branch. The three other cases were registered in the EOW and Special Crime Wing from 2021 to 2026. The complainant in the first case, police said, knew him as Brijnath Bhat. In his complaint, a villager stated that Koul posed himself as an attorney for a piece of land at Goshabugh in Pattan, Baramulla. A deal was done for 11 kanals and 3 marlas, a little less than one-and-a-half acre, for Rs. 55 lakh. The parcel included some pieces of land belonging to Kashmiri Pandit migrants. After the complainant paid Rs. 9.17 lakh in advance, Koul disappeared without a trace. In 2021, Koul again posed as an attorney, out to sell one-and-a-half kanal of Pandit land at Gulab Bagh Pandach in Srinagar. This time, he again identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. After allegedly taking Rs. 47 lakh from the buyer, he disappeared. Police filed a chargesheet in absentia. Two years later, police received two more complaints. Koul allegedly promised the same piece of land to two different buyers at Humhama near the Srinagar airport. To one man, he identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. To the other, he was Hadinath Dhar. He took a combined total of Rs. 1 crore from the two men and disappeared, said police. In the latest case, he had taken Rs. 15 lakh from his buyer before doing the vanishing act, and being arrested months later. With his arrest, J&K Police have finally learnt that the man they compared with Charles Sobhraj, a criminal known for his flamboyance, is a frail former Ayurvedic doctor with a penchant for the good old newspaper. Koul, or Bhat, is now in Srinagar Central Jail serving judicial custody. It was his love for the newspapers that finally proved to be his undoing, said an officer connected with the probe. Senior Superintendent of police, Crime branch/ Economic Offices Wing Kashmir Abdul Waheed Shah said that they are taking the activities of this land mafia very seriously because it has been ruining lives and families. We ensure that every such complaint is investigated thoroughly so that the perpetrators of such crime are brought to justice. When a family buys a piece of land, they spend most of their hard earned savings. Once they are defrauded, it completely ruins that entire family, he said. We are taking strict action against the brokers as well as any officials involved in such frauds. We have been focused on exposing these fraudsters and dismantling their networks. Our law enforcement also helps raise awareness among public to stay vigilant against such fraud.

headline: Has Trump Softened On Iran? JD Vance's Shift On Uranium Enrichment Sparks Fresh Questions
content: told Reuters that Iran needed to demonstrate its commitment to not developing nuclear weapons by changing its enrichment programme. US Vice President JD Vance has called on Iran to make a meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity as part of an agreement to end the war, raising questions over whether Washington has softened its earlier demand that Tehran abandon enrichment altogether. Vances comments come alongside tougher statements from other senior US officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has reiterated that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, while President Donald Trump has warned that the war will end through either the nice way or the not-so-nice way". - 'Not Going To Trade Words For Actions': Vance Says Iran Must Cut Nuclear Enrichment To End War - 'We Knew That Guy Was A Problem': JD Vance Questions How FlyDubai Omani Co-Pilot Got Back In Cockpit - JD Vance On Iran: U.S. Demands Major Nuclear Concession To End War | U.S. Iran War | - 'How Trump Feels He Is': Iran Mocks US President With Hrithik Roshan Movie Meme Iranian officials, meanwhile, have questioned whether Washington genuinely wants negotiations as the US-Israel war on Iran enters its eighth month. Simon Mabon, professor of international relations at Lancaster University, told Al Jazeera that the prospect of Iran seeking a nuclear weapon remained remote. He said Iranian negotiators were more concerned about sanctions, frozen Iranian assets, the US naval blockade and fighting across the region, which he described as the main obstacles to a deal. What has the US said? Vance told Reuters that Iran needed to demonstrate its commitment to not developing nuclear weapons by changing its enrichment programme. If you dont want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 percent enriched fuel?" he said. If you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, dont build highly enriched fuel. Thats a very basic threshold issue," he added. US Vice President JD Vance called for a meaningful reduction in Iran's uranium enrichment capacity. The US-Israel war on Iran has entered its eighth month. The International Atomic Energy Agency reported Iran enriched uranium to 60 percent. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated negotiations with Washington were futile. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested room for talks based on justice and fairness. Uranium enrichment can make the material usable as fuel for nuclear reactors or, at much higher levels, for nuclear weapons. The International Atomic Energy Agency has reported that Iran enriched uranium to 60 percent, below the roughly 90 percent level considered weapons-grade. In its May 2025 assessment, the IAEA found no credible indications of a structured nuclear programme. Vance also said the US was speaking with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, although he added that its not totally clear how their country makes decisions". Rubio, meanwhile, accused Iran of missing several opportunities to reach an agreement while speaking to reporters in Athens. Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period, end of story," Rubio said. He also claimed Iran had lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz and that its economy was in total and complete freefall". He said Iran, under crippling" sanctions, was about to reach a place few countries in the world have been". What has Iran said? Pezeshkian said on Monday that negotiations with Washington were futile", accusing the US of using talks while pursuing Irans government. Our problem with the United States is that every time we come to the negotiating table, war is immediately imposed upon us," he said during a meeting with Armenias foreign minister. They have attacked us three times following talks so far; this demonstrates that they do not seek dialogue. On the contrary, their goal is to bring down the Islamic of Iran," he said, according to Irans official IRNA news agency. With an enemy that resorts daily to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats and breaks its promises negotiations become futile, and our nation will not accept such an approach." However, Araghchi, speaking to foreign ambassadors in Tehran on October 4, said, Only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict, suggesting there is still room for talks to continue and a deal to follow. This came after an Iranian proposal presented during the United Nations General Assembly in New York in late September to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations. However, Trump subsequently rejected the proposal. US Vice President JD Vance stated that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity and stop producing 60 percent enriched fuel to demonstrate its commitment to not building a nuclear weapon.

headline: Libraries to take digital route with online journals, co-working spaces
content: Extending online access to books and journals to upgrading reading halls into co-working spaces and introducing digital membership cards, the school education department is planning a digital upgrade of its public libraries across the state. Key proposals include introducing an open source integrated library system on the lines of Koha and D-Space software in Anna Centenary Library to other libraries in the state, allowing members to remotely access the library resources onlineThe initiatives, proposed during a recent meeting of authorities from the Directorate of Public Libraries (DPL), aim to transform libraries on a par with the departments vision for libraries outlined in the policy note.Such library management systems are currently in place in top state libraries, including the Anna Centenary Library and Kalaignar Centenary Library in Madurai. They not only provide a catalogue of library and employee resources, but also help streamline day-to-day operations from check-in/check-out. Discussions were made to expand this to other libraries, majorly full-time libraries where there is adequate footfall and space. Proposals were also given to introduce e-cards to those availing of membership, an official from DPL said.Other additions include upgradation of library reading halls into air-conditioned co-working spaces with WiFI facilities through renovations in collaboration with CMDA or the civic bodies. At present, out of 162 libraries in the city, 16 have been converted into co-working spaces. Nine more libraries are being upgraded, and they will be completed by the end of this year. Co-working space-cum-libraries will soon come up at full-time libraries in MKB Nagar, Ayanavaram and Royapettah, among others, an official with the district library office said.Director of libraries S Jayanthi said the proposals had been sent to the govt, but decisions on which library would benefit and cost were yet to be made. We will work with whatever the govt approves and follow their directives. It is a long process and nothing has been finalized yet, she added.Digitization is a tremendous advantage, which will help bring in youngsters to competitive exam aspirants to libraries. It is a step in the right direction to bring public libraries on a par with privately owned libraries, said K Nithyanandam, president, Madras Library Association.

headline: Assistant district fire officer arrested for demanding, accepting bribe in Tiruvannamalai
content: Omjasvin M D / TNN / Oct 07, 2026, 20:10 IST CHENNAI: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) arrested an assistant district fire officer in Tiruvannamalai district on Wednesday on charges of accepting a bribe of Rs. 10,000 from a doctor for issuing a no objection certificate (NOC) for a proposed clinic/hospital.The complainant, Dr Ganesh, a resident of Chengam taluk, had applied for the NOC. According to the DVAC, assistant district fire officer B Saravanan demanded Rs. 10,000 to issue the certificate.Unwilling to pay the bribe, Ganesh approached the DVACs Tiruvannamalai detachment, following which a case was registered, and a trap was organised on Wednesday.During the trap, Saravanan demanded and accepted the Rs. 10,000 from the complainant. He was subsequently arrested and remanded

headline: CPM opposes TN govt's smart meter tender, says it could pave way for power sector privatisation
content: CPM state secretary P Shanmugam on Wednesday condemned the TVK govt I Tamil Nadu for floating a tender to install smart meters under the Union govts Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) and demanded that it drop the plan, which he said would affect the interests of all sections of people.Shanmugam said the scheme was part of an attempt to privatise Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL). Though the Union govt was yet to introduce the Electricity (Amendment) Bill in Parliament, it was pressuring all the state govts to install smart meters, he alleged.The TN govt should not succumb to the pressure from the Centre and should not follow suit, Shanmugam said in a statement.He said the move could affect welfare measures, including 200 free units of electricity for domestic consumers, free power connections for farmers and subsidised electricity connections for MSMEs. It could also undermine the state govts control over TNPDCL and eventually pave the way for its privatisation, he alleged.The installation of smart meters could also result in the introduction of peak-hour tariffs for domestic consumers, he said and recalled that the previous DMK govt had attempted to implement the smart meter scheme but withdrew the plan following strong opposition from the Left parties.

headline: a sacrifice that defied the British Raj
content: The year 1932 began ominously for satyagrahis of the freedom struggle. The British Raj was no longer in any mood to keep the Congress in good humour. Amid the severe impact of the Great Depression, a national government assumed office in London in August, with Ramsay MacDonald of the Labour Party as Prime Minister and Stanley Baldwin of the Conservative Party as the virtual second in command. Liberals were also part of MacDonalds Cabinet. In a few months, it scored a landslide victory in the general elections. In New Delhi, Willingdon had become the Viceroy, replacing Irwin, who struck a pact with Mahatma Gandhi in March 1931 and adopted a conciliatory approach towards Gandhi and the Congress. Willingdon was no Irwin. By the time Gandhi returned to Mumbai on December 28 after a four-month visit to England, where he attended the Second Round Table Conference, the Raj had not only abandoned the pact but had also begun repressive measures in many provinces, including Bengal and the United Provinces (now called Uttar Pradesh). The rule by ordinance was in place, with 15 ordinances having been promulgated, under which, as recorded by Tara Chand in History of Freedom Movement in India (Volume 4), it [the government] was committing harrowing barbarities and ruthless repression. Two days before Gandhis arrival, Jawaharlal Nehru was arrested. A Civil Martial Law had been clamped. Gandhis arrest On January 1, 1932, Gandhi, after holding discussions with members of the Congress Working Committee, informed Willingdon about the resumption of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The response of the government was swift. The Congress was declared illegal. Gandhi was arrested on January 4, followed by Rajendra Prasad the next day. By January 10, leading Congressmen all over India were behind bars, wrote D.G. Tendulkar in Mahatma (Volume 3). It was on that day that in Tiruppur town of the western region of Tamil Nadu, a satyagrahi was beaten to death and his martyrdom propelled him into prominence. He was one of the agitationists who staged, like lakhs of people elsewhere in the country, demonstrations to highlight the Congress policy of boycotting foreign cloth and liquor. While accepting the blows of the police, the Tiruppur satyagrahi upheld the tricolour flag that symbolised the national movement and refused to part with it. He was N. Kumarasami, also known as Tiruppur Kumaran. As he held the flag aloft without letting it touch the ground, he came to be called Kodi Kaatha Kumaran (Kumaran who protected the flag). He went on to become a symbol of those who laid down their lives for the sake of the political freedom of their fellow countrymen. Who was Kumaran? According to a Tamil biography authored by B.S. Sundaram, a freedom fighter and the leader of the agitation team that led a demonstration in Tiruppur on the fateful day (January 10, 1932), Kumaran was born on October 4 in Chennimalai, now in Erode district, to a modest weaving family belonging to the Senguntha Mudaliar community. He could study up to the fifth standard, after which he took to the traditional occupation. In 1923, the 19-year-old married Ramayee, who was aged 14. He migrated to Tiruppur, where he worked for six years as a clerk at a cotton ginning mill. The biography, which was published on Independence Day in 1950, states that Kumaran, who wore only khadi clothes when he migrated to Tiruppur, was very eager to participate in the Vedaranayam Salt March of 1930, which was led by C. Rajagopalachari (C.R. or Rajaji) but was prevailed upon by his parents and employer not to take part in the event. However, his interest in the national movement was such that he started getting involved in various stirs. He became a member of the Tiruppur Desabandhu Youth Association. Noticing Kumarans growing interest in the freedom struggle, his friends and relatives taunted him for his acts. He continued to engage himself in the activity within a short period of the death of his father, Natchimuthu Mudaliar, in 1931.Yet, he remained unwavering in his focus. In fact, the biographer Sundaram mentioned that at the time of the fateful agitation, only his mother, Karupayee Ammal, was in town and not his wife, who had gone to Kumarapalayam. Had she been there, she would have attempted to prevent Kumaran from going ahead with his decision, the biographer pointed out. As has happened on many occasions, the person who was supposed to lead the agitationists in Tiruppur had dropped out on the morning of January 10. At about 5 a.m. that day, a couple, who had migrated from Gujarat for livelihood and were enthusiastic participants in the national movement, were picked up by the police and produced before a sub-collector in Pollachi. Eventually, the responsibility of leading the satyagrahis, numbering nine, fell on the shoulders of Sundaram. Kumaran volunteered to be in the forefront of the processionists, who went around Tiruppur, which was still a small town of Tamil Nadu then. Women at a few places had performed arati (traditional way of welcome) and provided their moral support. When the satyagrahis reached the towns police station on the main road, 30 police personnel and two officers pounced on them without giving any warning, recounted Sundaram. What followed was a rain of lathis. Kumaran, having led the processionists, bore the brunt of the attack. The portion of the brain above the left ear was fractured. Some more blows were given on that spot. Even when he fell on the ground, he held the national flag tightly in his right hand. Another satyagrahi, who also received a lethal blow, was R. Raman Nair. Talking of the other martyr, Sundaram observed that it was on Nairs suggestion that he agreed to lead the stir. Nair had also participated in the Civil Disobedience movement earlier and had been imprisoned. As Kumaran and Nair lay lifelessly on Tiruppurs main road, the policemen, using their shoes, trampled on them. As a postmortem was conducted the next day, the governments records state that the date of Kumarans death is January 11, 1932. His funeral was carried out almost in a clandestine manner, with the administration permitting only two persons to carry his body and not allowing other mourners to take it in a procession openly. Tamil scholar M.P. Sivagnanam, popularly known as Ma.Po.SI, in his seminal work on Tamil Nadus role in the freedom struggle Viduthalipporil Tamizhagam (Volume Two) pointed out that the circle inspector, Mohammed, who carried out the attack, was transferred out of Tiruppur. This was not a punishment to him. But it was protection to him from the people of Tiruppur who trembled with rage, the scholar wrote. Memorial pillar In no time, the Congress party had, in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, and many other parts of the State, begun holding events to perpetuate the memory of Kumaran. His birth anniversaries were observed as Volunteers Day and the death anniversaries as Kumaran Day. In January 1948, Cutchery Road, where Kumaran was beaten to death, was named after him and the local body decided to put up a statue too, according to a news item published by on February 5, 1948. On August 18, 1957, a pillar in memory of Kumaran was unveiled by then Chief Minister K. Kamaraj near the Tiruppur railway station. The stately column is erected near the Tirupur Railway Station at a cost of Rs.[] 8,000. It is 25 feet in height with a torch at the top and depicting the picture of a volunteer holding the Congress flag. The pillar is erected in view of the centenary celebrations of the freedom struggle, reported this daily on August 20. The event was attended by Finance Minister C. Subramaniam, Sundaram, and Kumarans nephew, Lakshmanan. In January 1965, as part of the centenary celebrations of Lala Lajpat Rai, the wives of Kumaran and Vanchinathan, who assassinated, in June 1911, the then Tirunelveli Collector and District Magistrate Robert William DEscourt Ashe, were honoured at an event at the Rajaji Hall, Chennai. A gold-plated silver medal and a white khadi silk saree were given to each of them. While Vanchinathans wife Ponnambal received the award, Ramayee did not make it, but her sister-in-law did. In October 1979, while participating in a conference of freedom fighters on the Tamukkam grounds in Madurai, then Chief Minister M.G. Ramachandran announced that his government would give a grant of 10,000 to Ramayee, besides providing her with a monthly ex gratia grant of 300 to 500. In April 1991, the State government built a memorial, containing photographs and exhibits concerning Kumaran and freedom fighters of Tiruppur district. In April 1998, Ramayee died, and her mausoleum is located on the memorial complex. On the occasion of the martyrs birth centenary in October 2004, the Postal department brought out a stamp on him. In October 2025, the foundation stone was laid in Chennimalai for a Kumaran memorial to be built at a cost of 2.5 crore. Though 95 years have gone by, the legacy of Kumaran lives on.

headline: Chaos At Jantar Mantar: Rahul Gandhi Detained; Opposition MPs Stage Dharna
content: Rahul Gandhi Detained; Opposition MPs Stage Dharna The Opposition's decision to return to the streets came less than 24 hours after Tuesday's dramatic protest. The INDIA blocs protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar escalated in Delhi as Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition MPs reached Jantar Mantar but were stopped by police barricades, with several protesters detained. The latest confrontation came a day after a high-voltage standoff in central Delhi in which Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several other Opposition leaders were detained following an hours-long sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan. On Wednesday, Opposition MPs first gathered for a strategy lunch at Sagar Ratna restaurant on Delhis Janpath, hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. The meeting was held to decide the blocs next course of action and coordinate its campaign. After the lunch, the MPs boarded buses and headed towards Jantar Mantar, where the Opposition had announced plans to stage a joint protest. However, Delhi Police put up barricades and blocked routes leading towards the protest site. The buses carrying the MPs were stopped as the police moved to prevent the demonstration from proceeding as planned. - INDIA Bloc Jantar Mantar Protest Live: Rahul Gandhi Released After Nearly 2-Hour Detention, Total 91 Opposition Leaders Held Today - 'Gyanesh, Time To Resign': Rahul Gandhi's Tricolour Wave To Detention & Release, SIR March Sees High Drama - 'Youre Doing Your Job': Rahul Gandhi Distributes Water While Supporters Deflate Cops Detention Bus | Watch - Not Going To Stop: Rahul Gandhi Vows To Continue Protests After Detention Near Jantar Mantar Want 100 FIRs Against Me: Rahul Gandhi Challenges Govt As He Leads INDIA Bloc Protest Against CEC Rahul Gandhi had earlier said the Opposition would go to Jantar Mantar after being prevented from marching to the Election Commission headquarters on Tuesday.
