headline: 19-year-old student in Poland injures 8 people in school attack
content: A 19-year-old student at a vocational school in northern Poland attacked fellow students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object Wednesday (October 7, 2026), injuring eight people before fleeing and being arrested nearby, authorities said. The attack took place about 11 a.m. local time at the Vocational School Complex No. 4 in Ostroleka, about 120 kilometres northeast of Warsaw, police said. Authorities did not provide any information about the suspected motive or details about the weapon. Four students, two teachers and two passersby were injured, Elzbieta Edyta Lukasiewicz, a spokesperson for prosecutors, told the Polish news agency PAP. None of the injuries were life-threatening, but one person was seriously wounded, and some victims were evacuated by helicopter to a hospital, she said. Authorities identified the suspect only as Jakub Z., in line with Polish privacy laws. He was arrested on a riverbank less than 1 kilometre (a half mile) from the school after fleeing the scene, according to police. He was wounded at the time of his arrest in what prosecutors said was a result of self-mutilation. The young man was taken to a hospital. Police in the Mazovia province, which includes both Ostroleka and Warsaw, posted a photo on X showing a policeman with his hand placed on the back of a person lying down with their hands tied behind their back. The person's face and hands are pixelated. Polish media published blurred photos reportedly taken by students that showed bloodstained floors inside the school. Two hours after the attack, Ostroleka Mayor Pawel Niewiadomski wrote on social media that the situation has been brought under control but that the school would remain closed while authorities investigate the circumstances of the attack. He said kids and others affected would receive psychological support and that he had asked all schools in the region to ban any unknown people from entering their premises. A spokesman for the local firefighters told Polsat television that a suspicious backpack was found in the school and that authorities were investigating its contents. School attacks are not common in Poland. However, a stabbing at a Catholic convent in southeastern Poland last month left one person dead and four others wounded. Police detained a suspect.

headline: World leaders greet Modi on completing 25 years as an elected head of government
content: Leaders from various countries across the world on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) extended greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for completing 25 years as the elected head of a government, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat from October 2001 and then as the Prime Minister from May 2014. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, through an X post, noted that Mr. Modi had dedicated himself to the development of Indian society and the nation over the years. I express my deep respect for your achievements in advancing Indias development and elevating its standing in the international community, she said. While experiencing Indias culinary culture and music, I was able to engage in concrete discussions with Prime Minister Modi on measures to advance the Japan-India Special Strategic and Global Partnership to a new stage, making my stay immensely fruitful, she said, recounting her visit to India in July. Ms. Takaichi said, To realise a Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP), Japan and India, which share strategic directions, will further strengthen our partnership through even closer collaboration with Prime Minister Modi. Avatar of our times Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever extended greetings to Mr. Modi. Following my productive visit to India last month, I look forward to further deepening the strong partnership between our two countries, he said. Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay called Mr. Modi an avatar of our times. Botswanas President Duma Gideon Boko said: We commend you for your dedication and service to the people of India. We wish you success in the years ahead and look forward to the enduring friendship between our countries. Emphasis on good governance From Gujarat to leading the worlds largest democracy, Prime Minister Modis journey has been marked by a strong emphasis on good governance, innovation, technology, infrastructure and development, contributing to Indias transformation and its growing role on the global stage, said Philippines President Bongbong Marcos. From our Strategic Partnership in 2025 to the Philippines joining the CDRI last month, our ties continue to grow from strength to strength. I look forward to welcoming Prime Minister Modi to Manila for the ASEAN-India and East Asia Summits in November, he added. Dominicas Prime Minister Roosevelt Skerrit also congratulated Mr. Modi. Inspiring leadership across the Global South Wishing Mr. Modi on the occasion, Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said: From the transformation of Gujarat to Indias emergence as one of the worlds largest and fastest-growing economies, his leadership in infrastructure, digital public goods, financial inclusion and innovation has lifted millions and inspired nations across the Global South. As fellow democracies and leading voices of the Global South, Nigeria and India share a common commitment to a fairer, more inclusive and more representative international order, he said.

headline: 200 quarantined, 5,000 tests, no confirmed cases, no epidemic risk — latest updates
content: Russias health regulator has said there is no risk of an epidemic in Siberia after a 28-year-old worker at a plague research institute died of pneumonia of unknown origin, even as the World Health Organization (WHO) continues to seek more information from Moscow. The death of Darya Shipilova, a laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, triggered international concern after reports suggested she may have contracted pneumonic plague following an alleged laboratory incident. Russian authorities have rejected those reports and said no plague has been detected. Here are the latest updates following the initial plague scare in Siberia: Russia has ruled out an epidemic risk, while the WHO continues to seek more information about the laboratory workers unexplained death. Quick answers to key questions 1What caused the pneumonia that led to the death of Darya Shipilova in Russia? The official cause of Darya Shipilova's death remains pneumonia of unknown origin, with no confirmed connection to plague despite initial concerns. 2Why were 200 people placed under quarantine after the incident at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute? Approximately 200 people were placed under quarantine as a precaution after Darya Shipilova's unexplained death raised concerns about potential infectious disease transmission. 3How did Russian authorities respond to the claims of a plague incident following Shipilova's death? Russian authorities rejected claims of a plague incident, stating that their investigations found no laboratory accident and that no plague pathogens were detected. 4Should the public be concerned about a possible plague outbreak in Siberia? According to Russian health authorities and the WHO, there is no risk of an epidemic in Siberia, and the overall risk to the public is assessed as low. 5What steps has the WHO taken regarding the pneumonia case in Siberia? The WHO has requested additional information from Russian authorities to clarify the circumstances surrounding Shipilova's pneumonia and investigate any potential health risks. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias health watchdog, said it was winding down precautionary measures introduced after Shipilovas death, after determining there was no epidemic threat to the population. Around 200 people were initially placed under quarantine or medical observation. The regulator said about 90% had since been released and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests had found no dangerous pathogens. No plague infection has been identified among people who had contact with Shipilova, according to Russian authorities. Rospotrebnadzor also said Shipilova had been vaccinated and was considered immune to the dangerous infections handled at the institute. However, authorities have not established what caused the pneumonia that led to her death. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the UN health agency had requested additional information from Russia to clarify the circumstances surrounding the case. The WHO is seeking details on the cause of the severe pneumonia, the pathogen that prompted Russia to introduce public-health measures and reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. The agency said Russia had reported that no case of plague had recently been registered in the Irkutsk region. The WHO has also mobilised experts to assess the situation. Based on the information available, it has assessed the risk as moderate to low in Irkutsk, low for Russia overall and very low for the WHO European region. The Kremlin has dismissed reports circulating about a possible second suspected plague case in Siberia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a large amount of media coverage had emerged around the incident but that most of it was false information. He urged the public and media to rely on information provided by Russian health authorities. Reuters said it was unable to find evidence in Russian media that a second person in Siberia had died of plague, although some social media bloggers had made unsupported claims. Russian authorities have said their investigation found no laboratory accident involving dangerous microorganisms. Testing of samples from Shipilova also reportedly found no microorganisms associated with the pathogens she worked with. Authorities have maintained that the epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region is stable and that the official cause of her illness remains pneumonia of unknown origin. Earlier reports from Russian outlet People of Baikal had alleged that Shipilova died of plague, potentially after exposure from a broken test tube. Russian officials have disputed those reports. The case has drawn scrutiny beyond Russia. The United States formally requested additional information from Moscow through a confidential diplomatic communication, according to a source familiar with the matter. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called for greater transparency, while President Donald Trump said he expected to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin about the incident. The European Union has also urged Russia to provide timely and transparent reporting and said reliable epidemiological and microbiological findings were needed. Mongolia has introduced additional health surveillance along its border with Russia, although its government said the current risk level remained low. Border crossings in Selenge province continue to operate normally, with health monitoring measures in place. China has also said it remains in close communication with Russia on infectious-disease prevention and control, including plague. The key unresolved issue remains what caused Shipilovas pneumonia and death. Pneumonia can result from a range of bacterial and viral infections and can also occur with pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread between people through respiratory particles, but there is currently no confirmed evidence that Shipilova had plague or that the disease has spread among her contacts. For now, Russian authorities say there is no epidemic threat, while the WHO continues to seek additional information to resolve conflicting reports and assess the potential public-health risk. (With inputs from AFP, AP, Reuters, and Bloomberg)

headline: Opposition vs Gyanesh Kumar: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi forcibly removed, detained during INDIA bloc protest in Delhi
content: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi forcibly removed, detained during INDIA bloc protest in Delhi Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, along with his sister Priyanka Gandhi, who is an MP from Kerala's Wayanad, were both removed by force on Wednesday by officials of the Delhi Police and were also detained after they, along with other leaders, staged a sit-in protest at the roundabout near central Delhi's Shangri-La hotel after they were stopped from reaching Jantar Mantar. The INDIA bloc MPs are protesting against the alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's functioning, and are also demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Priyanka Gandhi was also filmed lying on the road, with a copy of the Constitution in her hands. Quick answers to key questions 1Why were Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi detained during the protest in Delhi? Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained by the Delhi Police after they attempted to march towards the Election Commission's office, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the electoral roll revision. 2What are the allegations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar? Gyanesh Kumar faces allegations related to the controversial revision of electoral rolls, which opposition leaders claim has disproportionately favored the ruling party, leading to the removal of over 130 million names from the rolls. 3How did the protest against Gyanesh Kumar escalate? The protest escalated when police barred the opposition MPs, including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, from reaching the Election Commission's office, leading them to stage a sit-in protest that resulted in their forcible removal. 4What was the reaction from opposition leaders regarding the police's actions during the protest? Opposition leaders accused the police of using excessive force, labeling their treatment of the MPs as 'hooliganism' and asserting that their right to protest was being violated. 5What impact did the protest have on Gyanesh Kumar's scheduled visit to Chhattisgarh? In response to the ongoing protests against him, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar postponed his planned two-day visit to Chhattisgarh, which included meetings and a temple visit. Once the MPs were not allowed to proceed towards Jantar Mantar, they decided to sit in at the roundabout. Following this, security personnel gathered in the area in large numbers and forcibly removed Rahul Gandhi and put him inside a police bus. He was put inside the bus by policemen who carried him on their shoulders as he refused to cooperate. Congress leaders like Raja Warring, Amarinder Singh, and Uday Bhanu climbed on top of the bus, as per a PTI report. Mumtaz Patel sat on the bonnet. After Rahul, the attention shifted to Priyanka Gandhi, and a large posse of female police officials started removing her and other female Opposition leaders who were lying on the road. They were also forcibly put inside a bus and taken away from the site. Priyanka Gandhi said, according to the Congress, I will not move from here. This is how they treat MPs who simply want to meet the Election Commission. This is how they beat up MPs. Women police personnel have scratched me all over and thrown us to the ground. Let them call their forces back, reported ANI. Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi accused the Centre of hooliganism, while Pawan Khera said, "It is our democratic right; we are fighting for this right. Article 19 grants us permission to protest in this manner, and Jantar Mantar is a designated spot; if we cannot stage a protest here, then where else can we do it?" RJD MP Manoj Kumar, who was a part of the protest, alleged that the police were using force. Jha told reporters, "This is a launch. Not just Gyanesh Kumar; this Government is going out now. They are launching a lathi charge on the soul of India, on the democracy of India. Shame on such people." Earlier in the afternoon, the INDIA bloc MPs attended a meeting convened by Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to discuss the issue concerning the Chief Election Commissioner, after which they headed towards the Jantar Mantar protest site. With agency inputs

headline: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka hauled away again after lie-in on Delhi road
content: The Congress leaders were detained by cops in dramatic circumstances Rahul Gandhi was manhandled and bundled into a police bus, the second time in as many days. An angry-looking Priyanka Gandhi, who lay on the road with her arms crossed, was hustled away minutes later. She held on to a copy of the Constitution, her arm outstretched outside the moving vehicle. The showdown erupted after a lunch meet organised by Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge for INDIA bloc MPs. The venue was the all-vegetarian Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath, less than 2 km from the Jantar Mantar protest site. Earlier, Rahul Gandhi was trolled online by a section of X users for allegedly having a non-vegetarian roll from Khan Chacha eatery during his eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan on Tuesday. After about one-and-a-half hours, the MPs streamed out of the eatery and went and sat in three buses parked on Janpath Road and headed towards Jantar Mantar. Interestingly, the Samajwadi Party skipped the lunch meeting. Sources in the Congress said that most of their MPs had left Delhi by this morning and couldnt attend the meeting and the subsequent protest. Congress agitators stand atop a bus on Day 2 of their anti-CEC protest in New Delhi. (Express Photo by Praveen Khanna) The issue was discussed during the lunch meeting where most other INDIA bloc parties were in attendance. When Rahul spoke to reporters, he said that 45 FIRs had been lodged against him, but he considered them to be medals and wanted a 100 FIRs. Today, we feel that we will protest at Jantar Mantar, which is a designated protest site, and tell the country that for us Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate Election CommissionerAs I said yesterday, around 300 Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs wanted to meet Election Commissioners, but they did not meet us. They told us that we cannot protest here (Jantar Mantar), Gandhi said. Lunch over, the MPs were being ferried in buses to Jantar Mantar when the cops closed them down at Windsor Place, which is roughly 900 metres from the popular protest site. Some Congress leaders, including Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Imran Masood, Imran Pratapgarhi, Deepender Hooda and Srinivas B V climbed the roof of the bus in which Kharge, Rahul and Priyanka were travelling, and waved the tricolour, as the procession crawled from Janpath to Jantar Mantar, bringing the high security area to a halt for the second day. An impromptu sit-in took place at the roundabout in front of the Shangri-La hotel. The police soon moved to detain the protesters who countered the security officials. Heavy police presence ahead of the protest. (Express Photo by Praveen Khanna) Rahul kept resisting police attempts to put him inside a van for detention. The INDIA bloc leaders jostled with security personnel who tried to detain them and clear the area. The entire Windsor Place roundabout was jammed with buses, cars and Congress youth outfit workers. While he was taken away to the Barakhamba police station, Rahul released a video message, continuing to engage through his social media platforms, besides his on-ground presence. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us, he wrote in a post on his X handle along with a video message. Later, the Congress said, The bus in which Rahul Gandhi ji was being taken was punctured by Congresss Babbar lions near Agrasen ki Baoli. The leaders were then taken to a police station in central Delhi. In a video attached to an X post, Rahul Gandhi said that Prime Minister Modi, Amit Shah, (RSS chief) Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar can do all this, but we are going to bring them to justice. My guarantee that all four of them will be brought to justice. This is all a panic reaction. This is all fear. They are going to be brought to justice, mark my words, he said. The was the latest in a series of protests by political leaders and civil activists to press for Chief Election Commissioner Kumars resignation since a September 25 report that suggested irregularities in the SIR process and differences among the election commissioners. With inputs from PTI

headline: Commercial Vessels Attacked In Black Sea, 31 Indian Crew Members Safe, One Injured: MEA Condemns Incident
content: India condemned attacks on three commercial vessels in the Black Sea, with 31 Indian crew members rescued and one injured, the MEA said. India has condemned attacks on three commercial vessels in the Black Sea and called for an immediate end to such incidents, stressing that commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must not be targeted. In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the vessels Alfa Watan, Able and Aframax Rio came under attack in the Black Sea. The ministry also provided an update on the Indian crew members aboard two of the vessels. - 'Attacks On Seafarers Must End': India Condemns Attack On Ship In Hormuz That Left 11 Indians Injured - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks - Indian Crew Member Injured, Two Foreign Nationals Dead In Russian Drone Strike On Vessel In Black Sea - 5 Indian Seafarers Rescued After Kuwait-Flagged Tanker Hit By Projectile In Hormuz: Embassy Seven Indians Among Crew Of Vessel Able The MEA said Able, a Palau-flagged vessel, had a total crew of 18, including seven Indian nationals. One of the Indian crew members was injured in the attack. With assistance from the Bulgarian authorities, the crew members were evacuated and taken to Varna, Bulgaria. The injured Indian national is receiving medical treatment, the ministry said. India also thanked the Bulgarian authorities for their support in evacuating and assisting the crew. All 23 Indian Crew Members On Aframax Rio Rescued The ministry said all 23 crew members aboard the Liberia-flagged Aframax Rio are Indian nationals and have been rescued. The MEA did not provide further details about their condition in its statement. India Awaits Information On Alfa Watan Crew The third vessel named by the MEA, Togo-flagged Alfa Watan, was also attacked in the Black Sea. India said it was awaiting information about the crew members aboard the vessel. India Calls For Immediate End To Attacks The MEA said the continued attacks on commercial shipping were a matter of deep concern" for India. Targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must end," the ministry said, reiterating its call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interest of peace and stability. The statement underlined Indias concern over the safety of commercial vessels and seafarers amid continuing incidents in the Black Sea. The Ministry of External Affairs stated that the commercial vessels Alfa Watan, Able, and Aframax Rio came under attack in the Black Sea.

headline: TNPDCL to procure up to 3,000 MW of power to meet evening, mid-night peak in demand in Oct
content: Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation (TNPDCL) will go for short-term power purchase agreements for up to 3,000 megawatts (MW) in October as power demand is continuing to peak around 20,000 megawatts (MW), making uninterrupted and reliable power supply a big task. The quantum is more than what TNPDCL purchased during peak summer this year, as the discom had signed agreements only for 2,400 MW during April for the rates ranging from Rs. 6.5 to Rs. 12 per unit.The power utility has floated a tender to procure power from private generators within and outside the State till Oct 31 from next week to meet the surge in power demand in the evening and midnight hours. Once signed via the union govt's DEEP portal, the private generators will start supplying power from Oct 12. From 6 pm to midnight, TNPDCL will procure 3,000MW to meet the night peak, while the procurement will be 1,500 MW from midnight to 2 am. The rates will be known after the agreements are signed. TNPDCL is already purchasing up to 3,000 MW through short-term and swap arrangements and procure equally from exchanges to meet the peak power demand."The power requirement has been very high since last month due to extended summer conditions. Wind power generation has considerably come down and contribution from central govt plants has also reduced, making the power purchase inevitable. If the northeast monsoon sets in by Oct 20, the power demand is likely to subside after which we will have to shut down our own thermal plants for overhauling as part of the preparation for next summer. If the northeast monsoon is also poor, we may have to repeat power purchases for November too," said a senior TNPDCL official.However, the official pointed out that the shortage is only during evening hours as electricity is available in surplus during the day due to good solar power generation. Electricity and law minister CTR Nirmal Kumar blamed the reduced power supply from central generating stations to justify the short-term power purchase agreements.On Tuesday, Tamil Nadu's power consumption was 432.6 million units (Mu), which is almost equal to last year's maximum power consumption in a day, while the peak demand was 19,921 MW. Of the 432.6 MU, 80 MU was supplied by TNPDCL's thermal plants, 83.4 Mu was from central power stations. About 38.5 Mu was purchased through short-term agreements, while 36.5 Mu was purchased from power exchanges.

headline: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody?
content: Congress leaders and MP Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with several other Opposition MPs, were detained on Wednesday for the second consecutive day as they continued their protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row. The Gandhis were briefly detained on Tuesday afternoon and later in the evening, too, as they protested at Akashvani Bhavan when their plan to move to the Election Commission office in Delhi was thwarted. On Wednesday, the opposition MPs were protesting at Jantar Mantar. - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - DMK U-Turn On Rahul Gandhi? Party Backs Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 'Right To Fight' - Form 6 Row: Rahul Gandhi Says Gyanesh Kumar Will Be Held Accountable | - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police What happens when an Opposition leader or Member of Parliament is detained? The legal process explained. | Delhi: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, along with other INDIA bloc MPs, being taken away from the spot near Jantar Mantar by the Police after detention.(Video: Congress) ANI (@ANI) October 7, 2026 THE LEGAL PROCESS When a Member of Parliament (MP) or the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) is temporarily detained during a public protest, the legal framework balancing law enforcement duties and parliamentary privileges functions through distinct protocols: No Immunity Against Detention Outside Parliament: Under Article 105 of the Indian Constitution, MPs are immune from civil arrest 40 days before, during, and 40 days after a parliamentary session. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained for a second consecutive day. Opposition MPs were protesting against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row. Under Article 105 of the Indian Constitution, MPs are immune from civil arrest 40 days before, during, and 40 days after a parliamentary session. This immunity does not apply to criminal offenses or preventive detention during a demonstration. Local police must immediately inform the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha about an MP's detention. This immunity explicitly does not apply to criminal offenses or preventive detention during a demonstration. If an MP participates in an unauthorized march or sit-in outside the Parliament complex, law enforcement can legally detain them under standard provisions of the law. Physical Protocol and Separation: To disperse unauthorized assemblies and maintain public order, police physically escort the LoP or MPs into transit vehicles (like police vans or buses). Instead of being locked inside a standard cell or jail block, high-profile legislators are generally brought to nearby police stations or designated temporary holding sites. They remain in administrative custody alongside other detained colleagues. Immediate Notification to the Presiding Officer: The standard operating procedure mandates that the local police must immediately inform the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, depending on the MPs house). The police must send a formal communication stating the precise reasons for the detention, the location where the MP is being held, and the duration of custody. Failing to promptly inform the Presiding Officer constitutes a serious breach of parliamentary privilege. VIDEO | Delhi: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (@priyankagandhi) waves a copy of the Constitution as police detain her.(Full video available on PTI Videos Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 7, 2026 Brief Custody & Transition to Release: Because the objective of preventive detention during a protest is to clear the public site rather than prosecute a crime, the custody is typically brief. Once the agitation dissolves and order is restored, the LoP or MPs are usually released from the station within a few hours. A permanent criminal record is not generated unless the police file a formal First Information Report (FIR) for actions like unlawful entry, assaulting a public servant, or damaging public infrastructurewhich can transition the temporary detention into a formal criminal arrest. When MPs are temporarily detained during a public protest, police escort them into transit vehicles and bring them to nearby police stations or temporary holding sites rather than locking them in standard cells. The local police must immediately notify the presiding officer of the respective house with details of the detention, and detainees are typically released within a few hours once order is restored.

headline: India, UK agree to explore cross-border equity, bond listings through GIFT IFSC
content: border equity, bond listings through GIFT IFSC India and the UK have agreed to explore ways to boost cross-border investment and Indian firms access to international capital, including through equity and bond listings via Gujarat International Finance Tec-City International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC), according to a finance ministry statement. The agreement was part of the joint statement adopted after the fourth UK-India Financial Markets Dialogue, held in London on 29 September. The dialogue was led by senior officials from the finance ministry and HM Treasury, with participation from financial services regulatory authorities from India and the UK. The Indian participants included the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai). The UK side included the Bank of England (BoE) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). The finance ministry said participants exchanged updates on reforms in their respective jurisdictions and reaffirmed their shared ambition for sustainable economic growth, resilient and open financial markets, and increased bilateral trade and investment. The discussions covered capital markets, insurance and pensions, asset management and fintech. The finance ministry said Sebi shared how India is transforming global investor participation by streamlining market entry and operations, while RBI highlighted the significant ease of overseas access to sovereign and corporate debt. The participants discussed the growing role of GIFT IFSC in mobilizing international capital into India and agreed to continue regulatory cooperation and knowledge-sharing to support its development as an international financial centre, the ministry said. The two sides also agreed to identify priority areas to explore for future capital markets cooperation ahead of the next Economic and Financial Dialogue, according to the joint statement. The finance ministry said the UK outlined recent updates to its insurance regulatory framework as part of its Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy, as well as developments in its pensions and annuity markets. India outlined its ambitions to expand coverage, investment and market capacity, the ministry said. Both sides agreed on the importance of the Insurance and Pensions Workplan established in 2023 to support market development, bilateral trade and investment. The participants recognized the value of competitive and resilient markets, access to specialist expertise, diverse pools of capital and reinsurance capacity in managing complex risks and supporting long-term domestic development, according to the finance ministry. The two sides also discussed opportunities in reinsurance arising from India's evolving regulatory framework and from deeper cooperation between the London market and Indian insurers and reinsurers. Participants exchanged experiences on regulation, governance, coverage and long-term savings reform. They discussed measures to increase participation and support productive long-term investment and agreed to explore knowledge sharing in areas aligned with their domestic priorities, the ministry said. The UK set out work on its regulatory framework for alternative investment fund managers, while India provided an overview of key reforms undertaken by Sebi and the IFSCA. Both sides welcomed continued regulatory cooperation on asset management and discussed how mutual understanding of reforms, investor requirements and market conditions could support increased cross-border investment. The two sides also welcomed further internationalization of the Indian rupee and recognized Londons role as the leading offshore rupee trading hub, the ministry said. Participants discussed the importance of credible sustainable finance frameworks, high-quality disclosures, global standards and investor confidence in mobilizing private capital for the low-carbon and climate-resilient transition. The finance ministry said participants also reviewed progress under the India-UK Financial Partnership asset management workstream and recognized the value of industry evidence in identifying practical opportunities for deeper participation by the UK and Indian asset managers in each others markets. On fintech and innovation, India shared its experience on scaling fintech adoption and financial inclusion through digital public infrastructure, including digital identity, digital payments, central bank digital currencies and data exchange frameworks, according to the joint statement. Both sides agreed on the importance of supporting responsible innovation and competition without compromising regulatory oversight. They also exchanged perspectives on the potential opportunities and the risks of artificial intelligence in financial services and agreed on the value of continued bilateral exchange and coordination through relevant international fora. India shared its digital onboarding process for retail financial services and committed to further sharing its experiences, the finance ministry said. The two sides also noted risks posed by the criminal adoption of new technologies to financial crime, including the use of artificial intelligence to commit fraud on an industrial scale in so-called scam compounds operating in foreign countries, as well as risks to cybersecurity, data protection and operational resilience. Participants shared their experiences using technology and regulatory innovation to detect and prevent financial fraud and agreed to continue cooperation among the relevant authorities, according to the ministry. On cross-border payments, both sides reaffirmed their support for the G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-Border Payments. They discussed practical priorities for reducing frictions, improving transparency and facilitating greater efficiency in cross-border payments aligned to the G20 Roadmap. The two sides also updated each other on developments in their retail payment infrastructures and recognised the work at the G20 to continue promoting interoperability and interlinkages among electronic payment infrastructures. The finance ministry said India and the UK welcomed the constructive discussions and reaffirmed the important role of the Financial Markets Dialogue in supporting their shared ambitions for sustainable growth, deeper trade and investment, and resilient financial markets. Both sides welcomed the contribution of the India-UK Financial Partnership in identifying practical and potential solutions to deepen financial services links. The participants also reflected on a strengthened relationship, particularly in the context of the launch of Vision 2035, and the importance of driving implementation of the UK-India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, which entered into force on 15 July 2026, according to the joint statement. The two sides agreed to drive progress across the workstreams, with updates to be reviewed through the relevant bilateral mechanisms and at the next UK-India Economic and Financial Dialogue, the Ministry of

headline: TNPDCL to replace 1.7 crore electricity meters with smart meters across TN; 56.8 lakh in Chennai region
content: Around 1.7 crore consumers including households, commercial and other low-tension (LT) categories in all major corporations in the state are set to get their electricity meters replaced with smart meters, as Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd (TNPDCL) has floated tenders in seven different packages inviting service providers of advanced metering infrastructure. In Chennai region, 56.85 lakh meters will be installed.The smart meters will do away with the manual reading of power consumption at doorsteps as the meters equipped with a SIM card can generate invoices at the end of each billing cycle and send SMS to the consumers phone number about the dues to be paid. The smart meters are expected to bring down the discrepancies in power bills due to delayed and wrong assessments.In Chennais T Nagar, 1.29 lakh smart meters have already been installed as part of the smart city scheme. The smart meter can also automatically disconnect a service temporarily for default on payment.During his budget presentation in the assembly in August, finance minister N Marie Wilson announced that the entire Chennai region comprising 38.80 lakh LT services would be covered with smart meters. However, the scheme has been extended to all municipal corporations, according to TNPDCL sources. A separate tender has been floated to install 4.72 lakh smart meters in all distribution transformers to detect line loss, energy thefts and others. Chennai region has been split into two packages, and the remaining 23 corporations have been clubbed in four packages. Six corporations in Kancheepuram, Villpuram, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai districts will be part of one of the packages, while five corporations in Erode and Karur districts are part of another package. Trichy, Thanjavur, and Erode will form a package, while Madurai and Tirunelveli form another package.The very first smart meter tender was floated in August 2023 to cover all three crore electricity consumers in the state, before it was lodged in December 2024, due to poor participation of bidders and high maintenance cost quoted by them.Fresh tenders for smart meters were floated again in March 2025, and the tenders were revised again in August to cover 1.44 crore consumers, whose bimonthly consumption is above 400 units, in the first phase before it was cancelled again. TNPDCL earlier this year appointed PFC Consulting to install 6.7 lakh smart meters in all govt buildings, and the installation is set to begin shortly.While the Union govt will release 15% of the total meter cost to the service provider, the latter will install and maintain the meters for a period of 10 years for a monthly maintenance charges.The prices of smart meters have come down drastically. In Madhya Pradesh, three-phase meters have been procured for Rs. 5,400, while a single-phase meter was purchased for Rs. 2,500. The monthly maintenance charges worked out to Rs. 65 per month. For Tamil Nadu, we expect further slashing of prices, said a TNPDCL official.

headline: Sri Lanka arrests ex-First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa over graft allegations
content: First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa over graft allegations corruption body on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) arrested former First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa, wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, over alleged financial irregularities. She has been remanded until October 13. The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) said it was arresting Ms. Rajapaksa in connection with an investigation into the alleged misuse of funds at her charity Siriliya Saviya Foundation. Ms. Rajapaksa travelled to Singapore on September 16 for medical treatment. She was served with a summons at Colombo airport to provide a statement to police in connection with allegations of financial irregularities at her charity. She flew back on Monday (October 5, 2026) after filing a court petition seeking to prevent her arrest, but the hearing for anticipatory bail was fixed for October 12, news agency AFP reported. Her arrest comes about a month after the Commission arrested opposition lawmaker and her eldest son, Namal Rajapaksa. He is in remand custody following his arrest over corruption allegations in a 2013 Airbus aircraft deal signed when his father Mr. Mahinda Rajapaksa was President, and an ongoing probe into bribery allegations linked to Indian property development company Krrishs real estate project in Sri Lanka. The Rajapaksa family has denied any wrongdoing and accused the government of pursuing a political witch-hunt. Also read: Sri Lanka: chasing system change The arrests come as part of the ruling National Peoples Power governments ongoing anti-corruption drive, in which many politicians, bureaucrats and businessmen are being investigated over graft charges. Authorities appear to be expediting long-dragging investigations. Eliminating corruption was among the chief poll pledges of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, who completed two years in office recently. Addressing a rally of famers in Polonnaruwa district in Sri Lankas North Central Province last month, President Dissanayake said that he had no sympathy for anyone, and whether is the mother or grandmother everyone must face the law.

headline: Isaias landfall forecast: Tropical storm heads for US Gulf Coast; Florida declares emergency
content: Tropical storm heads for US Gulf Coast; Florida declares emergency Tropical Storm Isaias has formed over the Gulf of Mexico and is forecast to strengthen rapidly in the coming days, potentially reaching significant hurricane strength. AccuWeather expects Isaias to become a hurricane over the central Gulf before making landfall along the US Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, with the storm likely to reach Category 2 strength and possibly intensify briefly to Category 3. AccuWeather Hurricane Experts said Isaias is likely to become the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, potentially making it the latest first hurricane to form in the Atlantic basin in more than 100 years. The storm is forecast to bring a combination of storm surge, heavy rainfall and damaging winds to areas stretching from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Isaias was centered about 285 miles (460 km) west of Progreso, Mexico, and roughly 580 miles (935 km) southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi River, the AP reported, citing the Miami-based National Hurricane Center. The storm had maximum sustained winds of 40 mph (65 kph) and was moving east-northeast at 8 mph (13 kph). The exact location of Isaias' landfall remained uncertain. According to the AP, the National Hurricane Center's initial projections indicated that the storm's center could come ashore late Friday or early Saturday somewhere between eastern Louisiana and the western Florida Panhandle. Residents along the northern Gulf Coast were urged to monitor the storm's progress and prepare for potential impacts. There is an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts along portions of the northern Gulf Coast, the hurricane center said, according to AP. The agency urged residents from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle to closely follow forecast updates and ensure they had hurricane plans in place. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis also declared a state of emergency for 25 counties across the Panhandle and Big Bend regions, AP reported. The declaration activates the state's emergency management plan and allows authorities to deploy personnel and equipment to respond to potential impacts. AccuWeather currently expects Isaias to reach Category 2 strength on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale before making landfall late Friday night or early Saturday morning. But there is a possibility the storm could become a major hurricane before reaching the coast. There is a chance the storm peaks as a Category 3, or major hurricane, while over the central Gulf, AccuWeather Chief Meteorologist Bernie Rayno warned. Beyond the potential landfall zone, Isaias is expected to bring heavy rain to parts of the Gulf Coast and much of the US Southeast from Friday into the weekend, according to forecasters cited by AP. The storm was also expected to strengthen as it moved toward the Gulf Coast, raising concerns about wind and storm-surge impacts along parts of the northern Gulf Coast. The hurricane center said Isaias is pronounced ees-ah-EE-ahs. While strong winds and storm surge could cause major problems along the coast, AccuWeather said heavy rainfall and flooding may be the biggest threat from Isaias. The storm is expected to produce 14 inches of rain across a broad part of the southeastern United States, while areas close to and just east of the storm's center could receive 48 inches or 812 inches. AccuWeather's Local StormMax rainfall forecast is 25 inches. The flooding threat could be particularly serious in areas where the ground remains saturated following heavy rainfall over the past week. As Isaias approaches the north-central Gulf Coast, squally winds and rainfall are expected to increase. After landfall, heavier and steadier rain could spread inland along a north-northeasterly path. AccuWeather forecasts wind gusts of 100120 mph near and just east of the hurricane's center if Isaias reaches hurricane strength before landfall. Its Local StormMax wind gust is 120 mph. A wider area of the Southeast could experience tropical-storm-force winds of 4060 mph, particularly around the central Gulf Coast and into Tennessee. The worst wind damage and coastal storm-surge flooding are expected near and just east of where the storm makes landfall, AccuWeather said. The strengthening storm is also expected to produce higher seas and large swells, creating dangerous conditions for small craft and increasing the risk of strong rip currents along Gulf Coast beaches. Isaias could bring additional severe-weather hazards beyond flooding and hurricane-force winds. Another hazard from the storm will be the risk of severe thunderstorms, including tornadoes and waterspouts, Rayno said. The bulk of the severe weather is expected near and east of the storm's center, although the tornado and waterspout threat could extend hundreds of miles to the east this weekend, according to AccuWeather.

headline: Trump vows $5,000 cheques to woo voters: Inside Republicans' move to save midterms amid Iran war woes
content: With less than a month to go before the US midterm elections on 3 November, President Donald Trump is escalating his pitch to voters by promising $5,000 cheques if Republicans win and retain control of Congress, months after saying that he did not care about the midterms. Trump made the announcement in September at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas. "If the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000," he said. Explaining the rationale behind his proposal, the US President cited America's "tremendous economic success," adding that Washington "is making so much money". The offer comes as the Iran war and its impact on fuel prices and household expenses threaten to weigh on Republican prospects, putting affordability at the centre of the campaign. However, questions remain over who qualifies for the payments, how they will be funded and whether the $5,000 pledge can secure congressional approval. The president's promise of $5,000 payments to Americans comes months after he said that the US wanted to strike a favourable deal with Iran, adding, "I dont care about the midterms. Look what happened last night, that was a prelude to the midterms. People understand it, as he referred to his endorsed candidate winning a Texas GOP Senate primary runoff. Also Read | I dont care about the midterms': Trump According to a PBS report, he likened the proposed dividend to companies sharing profits with their shareholders and cited his administrations distribution of $1,776 payments to military personnel in December. According to a Reuters report, the US President is also sending payments worth $500 to roughly one million Americans in October. The White House has described the payments as refunds for what it called excessive fees charged to people who purchase health insurance through the Affordable Care Act. However, strategists say the payments could influence races that may determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress. The payments will be limited to eligible residents of the 30 states that use the federal HealthCare.gov insurance marketplace. Residents of the 20 states operating their own marketplaces will not receive them. According to the White House, only about 950,000 of the 19 million people covered through the Affordable Care Act will qualify. Separately, Trump has sought to withhold billions of dollars in transport funding and other federal assistance from Democratic-led states, including Minnesota and New York, but courts have blocked or stalled those efforts. Recently, he also signed an executive order to expand access to tax-exempt diesel. Speaking about the waiver, Trump said, "We are not going to need it long, I hope." The midterms are also arriving at a difficult time for Trump. According to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in September, his approval rating fell to a low 32%, while the Iran war has pushed gasoline and diesel prices sharply higher and intensified concerns over the cost of living. The conflict has now continued for months, despite Trump initially saying that it would last only a few weeks, adding to the political pressure on Republicans as they seek to retain control of Congress. The focus will now shift to the US midterms and whether Trump will announce further measures in an attempt to woo voters.

headline: India-EFTA trade pact covers 99.6% of Indian exports: commerce secretary
content: trade pact with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) offers tariff coverage for 99.6% of Indias exports to the bloc, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday. At an outreach event for major exporters in New Delhi, Agrawal urged exporters, industry bodies and state governments to draw up market-specific plans to make greater use of the agreement, according to a press statement from the commerce industry. The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), which came into force on 1 October 2025, has opened up significant market access for Indian businesses across Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, Agrawal said. The outreach event was held as part of the second India-EFTA Prosperity Summit 2026, with leaders from all four EFTA states in New Delhi to mark the first anniversary of TEPA and discuss the way forward. EFTA's commitments cover 92.2% of its tariff lines, accounting for 99.6% of India's exports, with full coverage of non-agricultural products, Agrawal said. India, in turn, has committed 82.7% of its tariff lines, covering 95.3% of EFTA exports. The commerce secretary said the agreement should not be viewed merely as a tariff-reduction arrangement, with predictability emerging as one of its key benefits for businesses. Tariffs will remain stable for the foreseeable future, with no surprises, Agrawal said, adding that this will allow companies to make investments, build supply chains, and plan for the future with greater confidence. He urged Indian companies to build partnerships with businesses in EFTA countries and develop value chains spanning inputs to final products. Such partnerships, he said, could improve reliability on both sides and help Indian businesses integrate more deeply with high-income markets. The agreement also provides opportunities in agriculture, with duties on many products coming down to zero, Agrawal said. He asked exporters to identify products where the tariff reductions create an opportunity and develop long-term supply arrangements with buyers in EFTA markets. The four EFTA countries together import goods and services worth more than $500 billion annually, providing a sizeable market for Indian exporters, the secretary said. Agrawal called on export promotion councils, industry associations and state governments to take the opportunities created by TEPA to businesses across the country and explain how companies can use the agreement to expand exports. He also called for a more targeted approach to export promotion, asking stakeholders to prepare a five-year action plan with each EFTA partner country and for individual markets. Such plans should identify how India can increase its presence in each market as well as the non-tariff barriers that need to be addressed, he said. The secretary also highlighted the investment commitments under TEPA as a key feature distinguishing the pact from other trade agreements. Under Article 7.1 of the agreement, the EFTA states have committed to aim to increase foreign direct investment from EFTA investors into India by $50 billion within 10 years of the agreement coming into force and by an additional $50 billion over the following five years. The agreement also includes an aim to facilitate the creation of 1 million jobs in India within 15 years. Agrawal said Indias expanding domestic market offers investment opportunities across sectors and that stronger partnerships between Indian and EFTA businesses could take investment beyond the levels envisaged under the agreement. He also emphasized the need for Indian businesses to view EFTA not simply as a destination for exports but as an extension of their potential market. The idea is also that businesses in India should see the market of EFTA countries as an extension of their market,

headline: 'Matter Of Deep Concern': MEA Says 259 Indians Recruited Into Russian Army, Warns Of Grave Danger To Life
content: The issue has repeatedly surfaced over the past two years, with videos and reports of Indians trapped with Russian forces appealing to the Indian government for help. Tirupati said around 30 people who wanted to leave the camp contacted Nizamabad MP Dharmapuri Arvind and sought help with their rescue and repatriation. He said more than 20 people were still in Russia, while he and two others had returned to India. headline: First Made-In-India C295 To Take 1-2 Months More; Air Chief Confirms 'Minor Issues'
content: India C295 To Take 1-2 Months More; Air Chief Confirms 'Minor Issues' The delayed aircraft holds immense significance, as it is the 17th jet in a total order of 56 transport aircraft but the very first to be completely manufactured domestically Indias push for indigenous aerospace manufacturing is facing a slight delay, as the delivery of the very first made-in-India C295 tactical transport aircraft has been pushed back. Originally anticipated to be handed over to the Indian Air Force (IAF) by September 2026, and prior to the given timelines because of the updates in the last few months, the aircraft is now expected to take an additional one to two months to join the fleet. As per Indian Air Force chief ACM AP Singh, this delay is due to minor issues encountered during the testing phase, which are currently being actively resolved. The delayed aircraft holds immense significance, as it is the 17th jet in a total order of 56 transport aircraft but the very first to be completely manufactured domestically. Under a landmark Rs. 21,935 crore contract signed in September 2021 between the Ministry of Defence and Airbus Defence and Space, the initial batch of the fleet was built in Spain. - Tejas Mk1A: Review Meeting Post Oct 15 To Decide Delivery Schedule, First Lot Expected By Year-End - From 'We Wont Fight' To Troops For Saudi Arabia: Pakistans Yemen U-Turn And The Mecca Pact - 'Losing Out On Aviation Factory': BJP Leader Vinoj P Selvam Targets Tamil Nadu Govt Over C-390 Plan - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes The first 16 aircraft delivered from outside the country have already been received, with the remaining 40 aircraft slated to be made in India. Speaking on the progress of the domestic manufacturing line, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh noted that the first Indian-made C295 is already well into the production testing phase. He said that while there are some minor issues currently being resolved, the aircraft will hopefully be ready in a month or two. In his wider update on IAF capabilities, the Air Chief also touched upon other critical aviation assets, briefly noting progress towards force multipliers like the AEW&C Mark 1A. The manufacturing of the remaining 40 aircraft is being executed by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) in partnership with Airbus at a Final Assembly Line (FAL) located in Vadodara, Gujarat. This facility, established to boost the governments Aatmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) initiative, marks the very first time a private sector company has set up a military aircraft assembly line in India. The major structural components for these aircraft are manufactured at a facility in Hyderabad before being shipped to Vadodara for final assembly, integration, and flight testing. The induction of the C295 fleet represents a critical modernisation step for the IAF, as these modern transports will completely replace the legacy Avro fleet that has been in active service since the 1960s. The first made-in-India C295 tactical transport aircraft delivery is delayed by one to two months. The delay is due to 'minor issues' encountered during the testing phase. The aircraft is the 17th jet in a total order of 56 transport aircraft. A Rs. 21,935 crore contract was signed in September 2021 for the C295 aircraft. Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) is manufacturing 40 aircraft in partnership with Airbus in Vadodara. The C295 is a highly versatile, twin-engine turboprop aircraft with a 5 to 10-tonne payload capacity. It is exceptionally well-suited for Indias varied and demanding geographical challenges. Equipped with a rear ramp door for quick-reaction deployment and the para-dropping of troops and cargo, the C295 can operate seamlessly from short, semi-prepared, and unprepared airstrips. This makes the aircraft an invaluable tactical asset for logistical operations in high-altitude terrain, particularly along the borders in Ladakh and the Northeastern sectors. Airbus was approached for a comment on the status of the aircraft, but the company did not respond to queries. The delivery of the first made-in-India C295 tactical transport aircraft has been delayed by one to two months due to minor issues encountered during the testing phase, which are actively being resolved.

headline: Gwadar-Bound Cargo Attacked In Balochistan, Driver May Have Been Abducted: Sources | Exclusive
content: to preliminary reports, the cargo convoy was en route to the strategic Gwadar Port when it was intercepted by armed men Heavily armed Baloch militants targeted a Gwadar-bound cargo convoy in Balochistans Nasirabad area near Turbat district, opening fire on the vehicles before setting two cargo trailers ablaze, security and local sources reported.
