The resulting fire completely engulfed the cargo vehicles, causing severe damage to the goods bound for the port. Local witnesses stated that Pakistan security forces failed to reach the site in time to intercept the attackers or secure the immediate area during the assault. The incident underscores a sharp intensification of targeted attacks against commercial infrastructure and logistics networks linking the rest of Pakistan to the Gwadar Port project. Security forces have launched a search and rescue operation in the surrounding mountainous terrain to track down the attackers and safely recover the abducted driver. No group has officially claimed responsibility for the ambush yet, though state authorities frequently attribute such logistical sabotage to active Baloch separatist factions operating in the region. Gwadar Port is a strategic, warm-water, deep-sea port situated on the Arabian Sea in the Balochistan province of southwestern Pakistan. It sits right at the mouth of the Persian Gulf and just outside the Strait of Hormuz, placing it directly along one of the worlds most critical international oil shipping lanes. The port represents a massive geopolitical and economic project, owned by the government-backed Gwadar Port Authority but managed and operated by the China Overseas Port Holding Company (COPHC). Heavily armed Baloch militants targeted a Gwadar-bound cargo convoy in Balochistan's Nasirabad area. The attackers set two cargo trailers ablaze and reportedly abducted at least one driver. The cargo convoy was en route to the strategic Gwadar Port when it was intercepted. Gwadar Port is a strategic, warm-water, deep-sea port in Balochistan province, Pakistan. Gwadar Port is managed and operated by the China Overseas Port Holding Company (COPHC). Heavily armed Baloch militants intercepted a Gwadar-bound cargo convoy near Turbat district, opening fire to halt the vehicles before torching two heavy trailers and abducting at least one driver.

headline: After 14 years, Tamil Nadu records lowest Cauvery realisation
content: After a gap of 14 years, Tamil Nadu has recorded the lowest realisation of the Cauvery river during southwest monsoon (June-September) in 2026. In the last four months, the State got 44.208 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft). Usually, its quota for the period is 123.14 tmc ft. Going by this yardstick, the shortfall in realisation is almost 79 tmc ft. During the monsoon of 2023-24, the State recorded around 45 tmc ft. However, statistically, the current years receipt marked the fourth low realisation since 1974-75, when certain provisions of the 1924 Tamil Nadu-Karnataka agreement on the sharing of the Cauvery river became due for review. The present storage of the Mettur dam, from which the release of water for irrigation began about a month ago, would last nearly for 18 days, in the event of the current level of discharge (15,003 cubic feet per second or 1.2963 tmc ft. in a day) getting continued. As on date, the storage is 36.639 tmc ft. (capacity: 93.47 tmc ft.). An allowance of 10 tmc ft. has to be provided for drinking water requirement, environmental flows and dead storage. This has raised concerns among farmers and water experts about the prospects of paddy coverage during the samba-thaladi cultivation season, which is picking up momentum gradually. Unless the northeast monsoon comes to the rescue of the farmers, the immediate future appears bleak. Besides, even now, Karnataka has been protesting against the Cauvery Water Management Authoritys (CWMA) prescription on the water release. Between September 24 and October 4, the State received about 3.35 tmc ft. against CWMAs order to Karnataka to provide 5.18 tmc ft to Tamil Nadu over 15 days (from September 24, 2026). The paddy coverage in the Cauvery delta region is almost one lakh acres down, compared to the previous years figure for the corresponding period. As against 2.64 lakh acres in 2025-26, the existing coverage was 1.68 lakh acres as on October 5. Of the current years figure, direct sowing accounts for nearly 1.27 lakh acres, giving an indication that farmers of the region have come to terms with the shortage of water and they have not opted for the conventional way of paddy cultivation that consumes much more water. Of the nine districts falling under the delta region, two districts alone Cuddalore and Tiruvarur account for about 72 per cent of the paddy coverage. Around 52,700 acres in Cuddalore and 68,400 acres in Tiruvarur have been covered. In the same period last year, the deltas coverage was about 2.64 lakh acres. Eventually, it touched around 13 lakh acres. It remains to be seen how much of the current years target of nearly 12.7 lakh acres is going to be met.

headline: Trump's 'Islam Takeover' Claim Vs Real Grievances Of France's Student Protesters Explained
content: 6, US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social, framing the French unrest as an existential, religious, and demographic crisis The massive student protests sweeping across France have become a flashpoint for international debate, drawing a stark contrast between US President Donald Trumps framing of the unrest and the actual structural grievances driving the students. All you need to know. - Donald Trump Vs Mark Carney For Nobel Peace Prize? The Winner Could Literally Be From Space - Islam Wants To Take Over France: Trump Reacts To Students' Protests, Blames Out Of Control Migration - US Deploys 9,000 More Troops To Middle East As Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes - Macron Calls Trump As Iran War, Hormuz Crisis Fuel Global Oil Shock; France Pushes G7 Action Donald Trumps Claim: An Islam Takeover" On October 6, 2026, US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social, framing the French unrest as an existential, religious, and demographic crisis. Trump wrote, Whats happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isnt about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country!" According to political analysts, Trumps remarks align with his long-standing narrative regarding European border control. Observers note that the comments are heavily utilized by the Make America Great Again" (MAGA) movement to reinforce immigration rhetoric ahead of competitive U.S. midterm elections. Trump did not provide any evidence linking the ongoing demonstrations to migration or religious demands. French officials have strongly pushed back, with Foreign Minister Jean-Nol Barrot explicitly dismissing external geopolitical spin in favor of a factual narrative, according to al Jazeera, Reuters and other reports. US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on October 6, 2026, framing French unrest as an "Islam Takeover." French high school and university students have been mobilizing since mid-September 2026. Over a quarter of a million demonstrators are driven by public education underfunding, austerity measures, and deteriorating classroom environments. Prime Minister Sbastien Lecornu suspended all high school classes across France for a week. Over 6,100 people have been detained since late September, with hundreds of students and over 700 police officers injured. The Real Grievances of Frances Student Protesters French high school (lyce) and university students have been mobilizing since mid-September 2026. According to French student unions, labor organizations, and domestic journalists, the movement is rooted strictly in public education underfunding, austerity measures, and deteriorating classroom environments. The primary factors driving over a quarter of a million demonstrators into the streets, according to international media, include: - Staffing Shortages: Widespread frustration over a severe lack of teachers, unfilled vacancies, and failure to replace absent educators. - Overcrowded Classrooms: Many classrooms are packed with 32 to 35 pupils, creating unmanageable student-to-teacher ratios and heavy workloads. - Dilapidated Infrastructure: Run-down buildings unable to cope with changing weather, notably classrooms reaching up to 40C (104F) during extreme European heatwaves without adequate climate control. - Systemic Pressures: Frustrations over exhausting, over-extended timetables, short lunch breaks, and high mental anxiety surrounding Parcoursupthe national university admissions application portal. - Austerity Discontent: General public anger regarding broader government budget restrictions, which initially included a proposal to raise higher education registration fees (later scrapped by the Education Ministry in a bid to placate protesters). Escalation and Government Response What began as an isolated demonstration supporting a teacher strike in a Paris suburb has snowballed into Frances largest student movement in decades. While the majority of student-led rallies march peacefully, the crisis has descended into serious clashes between youth groups and security forces, leading Prime Minister Sbastien Lecornu to suspend all high school classes across France for a week. According to Frances Interior Ministry, over 6,100 peoplemostly minorshave been detained since late September, with hundreds of students and over 700 police officers injured during blockades, tear gas deployments, and isolated instances of arson. Despite the intensity of the unrest, no evidence or demands from the student organizations have targeted immigration, integration, or religious identity. The student protests in France are driven by public education underfunding, austerity measures, severe teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, and dilapidated, uncooled infrastructure. Students are also frustrated by heavy workloads and anxiety surrounding the Parcoursup university admissions portal.

headline: 'Spectacular Act Of Self-Emasculation': Tharoor Warns Election Boycott Will Make Opposition Irrelevant
content: Tharoor cited Congress' pre-Independence electoral strategy and Hungary to argue that Opposition parties must not abandon the ballot box. Thiruvananthapuram MP and veteran Congress leader Shashi Tharoor warned that the act of boycotting elections would make the opposition irrelevant". - 'Horrified, Disgraceful': Tharoor Condemns Govt Over Rahul Gandhi's Detention At EC March - 'Credit Chori' Clash Over 'Vote Chori' Row? Congress & CJP Supporters Squabble On Social Media - Opinion | Why Oppn's Manufactured Outrage Over Electoral Rolls Is A Threat To Democracy - Right Word | A Verdict That Dismantles The Theft Of Votes Narrative Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke last month urged opposition parties to boycott elections if they believe the process is rigged" and said that continued participation legitimises allegedly unfair elections and creates a false sense of transparency". Without naming Dipke, Tharoor said that those who advocate such boycotts often point to Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian struggle for freedom from colonial rule but argued that such a strategy would not work under the current circumstances. Tharoor Cites Congress Own Election History Tharoor highlighted that the Indian National Congress itself had recognised this distinction during the Independence movement. Shashi Tharoor warned that boycotting elections would make the "opposition irrelevant." Tharoor published his remarks in an opinion piece titled "Boycott is not an election strategy." Tharoor highlighted that the Indian National Congress boycotted elections under the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms of 1919. The Congress later chose to participate in elections held under the Government of India Act of 1935. Tharoor cited Hungary as an example of an opposition remaining in the electoral arena despite an "illiberal system." He pointed out that while the Congress boycotted elections under the restrictive Montagu-Chelmsford reforms of 1919 to reject what it considered a flawed system of colonial tokenism, it later chose to participate in elections held under the Government of India Act of 1935, despite the limited franchise and communal electorates. According to Tharoor, Indian leaders at the time recognised that refusing to contest elections would hand the right of representation to less worthy forces" and leave the public under unmediated colonial authority. Tharoor argued that the same logic applies to political parties operating within Indias present constitutional system. In our contemporary constitutional system, choosing non-participation against domestic rivals is not a moral stand, but a spectacular act of self-emasculation," he wrote. Election Boycott Could Hurt Cadres Tharoor also highlighted the impact an election boycott could have on the organisational strength of political parties, particularly their cadre morale and local networks. Staying away from elections, he said, could cause cadres to disperse, local networks to weaken and financial resources to dry up. According to him, rebuilding a political organisation after years of non-participation would be extremely difficult, if not impossible, while a party that retreats from electoral contests risks becoming irrelevant to the voters it seeks to represent. Tharoor Cites Hungary Elections Tharoor also cited Hungary as an example of an opposition choosing to remain in the electoral arena despite what he described as an illiberal system" designed to entrench Prime Minister Viktor Orbns rule. He said the Hungarian opposition refused to abandon the ballot box, contested elections and exposed the governments failings before ultimately mobilising to secure a landslide victory. Tharoor argued that electoral authoritarians and dominant parties are rarely weakened by moral appeals or voluntary abstention, but instead are challenged through organised resistance at the ballot box. I think we must recognise that illiberal autocracies are dismantled through competitive endurance, not voluntary retreat," he wrote. Shashi Tharoor warned that boycotting elections would make the opposition irrelevant and described such non-participation against domestic rivals in a sovereign democracy as a spectacular act of self-emasculation rather than a moral stand.

headline: TVK govt announces roll out of 'Annan Seer" scheme; fixes annual income ceiling at ₹2.5L
content: The state govt on Monday issued an order for implementing its flagship Annan Seer scheme and allotted 812 crore as the first instalment for this year.The scheme will come into effect from Monday, said social welfare and women empowerment department secretary Pallavi Baldev in the order. The scheme is one of the key poll promises of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.The govt has, however, has fixed an annual income ceiling of 2.5 lakh for the brides family to become eligible for the scheme, as against 5 lakh ceiling promised in TVKs election manifesto. Under the scheme, eligible brides will be given an eight-gram, 22-carat gold coin along with a silk saree.The GO described Annan Seer as an expression of the govts love, affection, protection and responsibility towards young women getting married, in keeping with Tamil tradition and culture. It noted that around five lakh marriages take place in the state every year. The scheme is being implemented from the current financial year to convey the govts role as an elder brother to young women getting married, the order said.However, the reduction in income ceiling effectively excludes families earning between 2.5 lakh and 5 lakh a year from a benefit promised to them in the manifesto. The GO does not explain the reason for fixing this eligibility ceiling. The govt will float an open tender under Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 1998, for procuring the gold. The price of the gold will be determined based on the rate published by India Bullion and Jewellers Association on the day of procurement, the GO said.

headline: VCK demands basic amenities for SC/ST residents in the Nilgiris
content: The Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) have demanded that basic amenities be provided to villages populated by communities from underprivileged backgrounds in Kookalthorai in the Nilgiris. The VCK alleged that residents of Anna Nagar, Indira Nagar, Sundakkarai, Jeeve Nagar and others, in the Kookalthorai panchayat limits did not have adequate access to basic amenities such as good roads, street lights and drinking water. The VCK on Monday even staged a protest in front of the Kookalthorai panchayat office demanding better housing, a community hall and other facilities for residents in the village, a majority of whom belong to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities. The party alleged that the communities have been neglected for over 50 years and that government officials had neglected the villages because they were populated by SC/ST communities. K. Sagadevan, deputy zonal secretary of the VCK, delivered a speech at the protest and demanded that the government immediately look into the needs of the residents and take necessary steps to ensure that they have access to basic amenities.

headline: RBI to clarify forex reporting rules soon
content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will soon issue a clarification on its new foreign exchange rules, as the norms have created confusion for individuals undertaking personal transactions, deputy governor Rohit Jain said on Wednesday. The individuals are not included with respect to the reporting requirements for the contracts of a personal nature, Jain said at a press conference post the monetary policy decision. He added that the central bank would clarify the matter shortly through an FAQ. In January, the central bank overhauled its decade-old foreign exchange rules, bringing exports and imports of goods and services under a unified regulatory framework. The Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, notified on 13 January, came into force in October, replacing the 2015 regulations. The overhaul, which followed two rounds of public consultation and nearly two years of deliberations, aims to simplify procedures and reduce compliance burdens, particularly for smaller exporters and importers. It also gives authorized dealer banks greater responsibility for managing routine trade-related matters. However, the norms triggered concerns among freelancers, content creators and small service exporters over whether they now need to file additional export declarations for payments received from overseas. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said individuals subscribing to television channels, apps, journals or newspapers, as well as those providing services abroad such as tutoring or small software services, would not be required to comply with the reporting requirements aimed at exporters and importers. According to the RBI notification, exporters of goods will continue to declare shipment values through the Export Declaration Form (EDF) embedded in shipping bills at EDI ports. Service exporters will now have a defined 30-day window from invoice issuance to file declarations, with flexibility for consolidated monthly filings and bank-approved extensions. Software exports have been explicitly brought under the definition of services, with authorized dealers and Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) recognized as specified authorities. For smaller transactions of up to 10 lakh, exporters and importers will be allowed to close outstanding entries in RBl's export and import monitoring systems based on self-declarations, including quarterly bulk submissions, easing procedural burdens for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and service exporters, according to the order. For small, even the exporters, if the amount is small, up to 10 lakh per bill, not annually, per bill, 10 lakh, then a self-declaration will suffice and an invoice. There is some concern about uploading and giving invoices, but up to 10 lakh, an alternative has been given, which is in the form of a self-declaration, Malhotra said. Jain described the broader changes as a step forward in simplifying trade regulations and reducing the burden on authorized dealers as well as exporters and importers. The new framework retains the existing 15-month timeline for realization and repatriation of export proceeds for goods and services, while extending it to 18 months where exports are invoiced or settled

headline: 'Iran Has Lost Complete Control Of Strait Of Hormuz': Rubio Says Tehran's Economy In 'Total Freefall'
content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran has lost control of the Strait of Hormuz, while describing the countrys economy as being in total and complete freefall. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday claimed that Iran no longer has full control over the Strait of Hormuz, saying the key oil shipping route remains open despite the ongoing conflict. Theres almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began," Rubio said. He argued that the situation showed Iran had lost complete control" of the strategically important waterway. The Strait of Hormuz is a major route for global oil shipments, making developments around the waterway closely watched by energy markets and governments. Rubio Says Irans Economy Is In Freefall Rubio also described Irans economic situation as being in total and complete freefall". He attributed the pressure to what he called crippling" US sanctions. According to Rubio, the sanctions were pushing Iran towards an economic situation that few countries in the world have experienced. US Says Iran Must Not Obtain Nuclear Weapon Rubio reiterated Washingtons position that Iran must not be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon. Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period, end of story," he said. He added that any agreement with Iran that could be acceptable to the United States would have to provide assurances that Tehran would never obtain a nuclear weapon. Rubio Raises Concern Over Irans Conventional Military Capability Rubio also accused Iran of seeking to build a conventional military capability on such a large scale that it would become difficult to challenge. He said Irans aim was to develop a force so massive" that the country would effectively become untouchable". US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open and that oil shipments have recovered to near pre-conflict levels, indicating that Iran has lost complete control over the waterway.

headline: Four-storey building collapses in Delhi's Seemapuri, several feared trapped
content: residential building in northeast Delhi's Seemapuri area collapsed on Wednesday. Several people are feared trapped inside, prompting a rescue operation by the Delhi Fire Services (DFS). The incident took place in the afternoon when the front portion of the four-storey building came crashing down, according to a DFS officer. The DFS received a call regarding the collapse at 3.30 PM. Fire tenders have reached the spot. "Search and rescue operation is ongoing," the DFS officer told PTI. In the latest development, five to six people have been rushed to a nearby hospital as a major rescue operation gets underway. Heavy machinery, including JCB excavators, was spotted at the accident site. Speaking to PTI, Shahdara DCP Rajendra Prasad Meena said, So far, around five to six people have been taken to the hospital. The rescue operation is still underway. We will know once all the information is compiled. At present, two to three people can still be seen inside, and they are also communicating with us. Local resident Saleem, who claimed to reside in the collapsed building, told PTI, This was our house. It suddenly collapsed. We managed to get quite a few people out. My own son-in-law was trapped inside, but he was safely rescued. My daughter was also inside, and she has been rescued as well. Two children have also been rescued. Three others are still trapped inside, and they are being rescued by removing the roof with the help of a crane. Pankaj Luthra, Municipal Councillor, Jhilmil, added, We received information that an old building, around 4050 years old, had collapsed" "Four to five people have already been rescued from the debris. The entire police force, MCD and administration are involved in the rescue operation. We are making every possible effort to ensure that no further incident occurs and are doing our best. Meanwhile, the Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory for commuters after the accident. Traffic has been affected in areas such as Seemapuri Gol Chakkar, DLF Bhopura and nearby places due to the incident. The Delhi Traffic Police posted on X, "A multi-story building has collapsed in Seemapuri and rescue teams are working at the site. Traffic is affected around Seemapuri Gol Chakkar, DLF Bhopura and adjoining roads. Every clear lane gives an ambulance and rescue vehicle a faster way through. Please avoid the area if possible. Do not stop, park or gather near the site, and follow the directions of traffic personnel." The latest incident occurred a month after the Delhi Satya Niketan PG collapse. On September 6, a boys' PG in the area collapsed, killing seven people and injuring many. headline: J&K Cabinet Expansion: Congress Mounts Pressure On CM Abdullah For Berths; NC Camp Sees Race For 3 Vacancies
content: Congress Mounts Pressure On CM Abdullah For Berths; NC Camp Sees Race For 3 Vacancies The cabinet expansion is proving to be a tightrope walk for Omar Abdullah as he has to maintain regional, religious and caste balance Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday said that his much-anticipated cabinet expansion will take place after the GST Council meeting in Delhi and subsequent consultations with National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah, even as the Congress has again mounted pressure for inclusion of its two legislators in the council of ministers. Speaking to reporters in Srinagar, Omar Abdullah said administrative changes have been carried out after a lot of thought and that the cabinet expansion will be finalised only after his Delhi visit. - Omar Abdullah's Claim On Rohingyas Factually Wrong Since India Does Not Recognise Them As UNHCR Refugees, Say Experts - 'Omar Govt Total Failure, Won't Last Long, Will Fall Under Own Weight': BJP's Tarun Chugh In Jammu - United Against BJP, Divided Within: NC, Congress Spar Over Panchayat Polls In Jammu And Kashmir - 'If We've To Bend A Little, We Will': Congress Says It's 'As Flexible As Constitution On Seat Sharing With SP The statement comes at a time when the nine-member council of ministers capped under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 is functioning with only six members, leaving three vacancies. With two berths already being demanded by the alliance partner Congress, the race within the National Conference for the remaining slot or slots has intensified. Sources in the Congress said the party leadership has once again conveyed to the NC high command that it must get its due share in the government. We fought the election together. Congress has six MLAs supporting the government from outside. We must get our due share in the cabinet. Two berths for Congress is a genuine and minimum demand," a senior Congress leader told on condition of anonymity. The Congress leader said the party high command in Delhi has also been briefed and the issue is likely to be taken up when Omar Abdullah meets senior Congress leaders during his Delhi visit for the GST Council meeting. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced cabinet expansion will occur after the GST Council meeting in Delhi. The nine-member council of ministers is currently functioning with six members, leaving three vacancies. The Congress party is demanding two ministerial berths for its legislators. At least a dozen senior National Conference legislators are lobbying for the remaining cabinet berths. The cabinet expansion is expected to take place between October 12 and 15. The Congress, which contested the 2024 Assembly polls in alliance with the National Conference, has been supporting the Omar Abdullah government from outside. The party has been demanding at least two ministerial berths one for Jammu region and one for Kashmir ever since the government formation in October 2024. However, the National Conference has so far maintained that the Congress should first join the government formally. Congress, on the other hand, has said that without a concrete assurance on cabinet berths, joining the government would be meaningless. A senior NC leader admitted that the pressure from Congress is real this time. The GST Council meeting will be attended by Finance Ministers of all states. J&Ks representative will be there. But on the sidelines, Omar Sahib will meet Congress leadership. That meeting will be crucial," the leader said. NC ASPIRANTS: EEK ANAR, SOU BEEMAR" While the Congress is staking claim from outside, inside the National Conference, there is no dearth of aspirants a classic case of Anaru sou beemaar" (one pomegranate, hundred sick). According to party sources, at least a dozen senior NC legislators are lobbying hard for the remaining cabinet berths. Among them, a seven-time senior legislator from Srinagar has made it clear that he must be included in the cabinet this time. I have served the party for four decades. I have won seven times from Srinagar. My seniority, my experience, and my contribution to the party cannot be ignored. I must be included," the veteran legislators close aide quoted him as saying. Similarly, another influential legislator from North Kashmir has conveyed his disappointment in advance. If I am not given a share this time, I will be hugely disappointed. The people of North Kashmir have overwhelmingly voted for NC. North Kashmir must get representation in the cabinet," the legislator from Baramulla/Kupwara belt told his supporters, according to sources. Apart from these two, several other names are doing the rounds, including two former ministers from South Kashmir, one senior Shia face from Central Kashmir, and a young legislator from Jammu region who is seen as close to Omar Abdullah. CASTE, REGION, RELIGION BALANCE A CHALLENGE The cabinet expansion is proving to be a tightrope walk for Omar Abdullah as he has to maintain regional, religious and caste balance. At present, the six-member cabinet includes: - Omar Abdullah (Chief Minister) - Surinder Kumar Choudhary (Deputy CM Jammu) - Sakeena Masood (Itoo) - Javid Ahmad Dar - Javid Ahmad Rana - Satish Sharma (Independent MLA from Chhamb, supporting NC) Out of the six, three are from Jammu (Surinder Choudhary, Javid Rana, Satish Sharma) and three from Kashmir (Omar, Sakeena, Javid Dar ). DELHI VISIT CRUCIAL The Chief Minister is scheduled to leave for Delhi tomorrow for the GST Council meeting chaired by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. J&K Finance Ministers concerns over GST compensation and funding for the Union Territory are likely to be raised. But more than GST, the political consultations in Delhi are being watched closely. Party insiders said the expansion is likely to take place between October 12 and 15, after Omar returns from Delhi. Meanwhile, the opposition BJP has taken a jibe at the delay in cabinet expansion. BJP MLA Sunil Sharma said, It has been almost a year since NC government came to power, but they are still running a headless cabinet. Congress is blackmailing them and NC MLAs are fighting among themselves. This shows lack of leadership." The NC has rejected the charge, saying the government is stable and expansion will be done at an appropriate time. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced that the cabinet expansion will take place after the GST Council meeting in Delhi and following consultations with National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah. Party insiders indicate the expansion is likely to occur between October 12 and 15.

headline: Chevron CEO warns 'unwise' US diesel export ban could worsen global fuel crunch | What it means
content: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth has warned that a US ban on diesel exports would be unwise, arguing that restricting supplies to the global market could worsen the fuel crunch and undermine Washingtons reputation as a reliable energy supplier, CNBC reported. Export bans, be they in the US or in other countries, actually take supply off the global market and they run the risk of making the situation worse, Wirth told CNBC. The US has been a reliable supplier to the world at a time when it needs it, he said, warning that an export ban could create doubts among US allies and partners about the reliability of American energy supplies during periods of crisis. The debate comes as diesel prices have surged amid disruptions to global energy markets linked to the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz crisis and reduced Russian fuel supplies. US President Donald Trump had threatened to restrict diesel exports unless European countries released more of their own fuel reserves. The move was aimed at easing pressure on US consumers, farmers, truckers and businesses facing sharply higher fuel costs ahead of the November midterm elections. However, Trump later said that a diesel export ban was never really on the table and, following the G7 agreement, said the US would not impose the ban. The Group of Seven has agreed to coordinate the release of 100 million barrels of oil and petroleum products from emergency reserves over four months through the International Energy Agency (IEA). The plan includes a substantial, front-loaded release of diesel within the first 20 days. The G7 has also committed to avoiding energy export restrictions among its members and called on other producers to refrain from export bans that could worsen market tensions. The move followed pressure from Washington on European countries to tap their reserves as diesel prices climbed. The G7's action is intended to increase market supply and ease price pressures in the short term. The US is an important supplier of refined petroleum products to the international market. Restricting exports could therefore redirect supplies towards the domestic US market while tightening availability elsewhere, particularly in Europe. That could push up diesel prices outside the US even as American consumers receive some short-term relief. Analysts in a CNBC report warned that an export ban could ultimately discourage refining and reduce overall fuel availability. For now, the immediate threat of a US diesel export ban has receded after Trump backed away from the proposal and the G7 agreed to a coordinated release of reserves. The IEA is expected to coordinate and monitor the stock releases, with G7 countries leaving open the possibility of additional diesel releases if needed, as per the .

headline: Nobel Prize 2026: When will the awards be announced, date and timings in IST
content: Nobel Prizes 2026 will be announced between October 5 and 12, 2026, to honour outstanding contributions in the fields of medicine, literature, arts, chemistry, physics, economics and peace. They are regarded among the worlds most prestigious awards and are highly anticipated each year. Indians who have won a Nobel Prize are Rabindranath Tagore, C.V. Raman, Mother Teresa, Amartya Sen, and Kailash Satyarthi. A visual guide to 2026s Nobel Prize winners Nobel Prizes: Areas of recognition Nobel Prizes are awarded for outstanding achievements in medicine or physiology, physics, chemistry, literature, economic sciences, and peace. According to a Reuters report, the Nobel Prize now comes with a recently increased amount of 12 million Swedish crowns or $1.21 million. The awards are highly coveted and bestow instant international fame on the recipients. Date and timings of Nobel Prize announcements in I.S.T. Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine The prize was announced on October 5, 2026, at 3 p.m. IST, at the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institute. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel won the award for discoveries leading to a technique called optogenetics, which allows scientists to control select nerve cells using light. 2026 Nobel medicine prize: Trio wins for optogenetics work Nobel Prize in Physics The prize was announced on October 6, 2026, at 3.15 p.m. IST, at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. It was won by Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Physics Nobel 2026 goes to Francis Halzen for discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin Nobel Prize in Chemistry The prize was be announced on October 7, at 3.15 p.m. IST, at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won it for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Nobel Prize in Literature The prize will be announced on October 8, 4.30 p.m. IST, at the Swedish Academy. Nobel Peace Prize The prize will be announced on October 9, 2.30 p.m., IST at the Norwegian Nobel Institute. Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2026 (Nobel Prize in Economics) The prize will be announced on October 12, 3.15 p.m. IST, at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. How to watch the Nobel prize announcement ceremonies? The announcements of the prestigious prizes can be watched live on YouTube. They can be streamed through the Nobel Prize YouTube channel. Nobel Prize Winners 2025 The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret and John M. Martinis for the discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit. Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar M. Yaghi for the development of metalorganic frameworks. The prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi for their discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance. Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Lszl Krasznahorkai for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art. Maria Corina Machado was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her tireless work promoting democratic rights for the people of Venezuela and for her struggle to achieve a just and peaceful transition from dictatorship to democracy Who founded the Nobel Prize? A Swedish chemist and entrepreneur, Alfred Nobel created the award and dictated in his will that the bulk of his sizable estate be used to fund prizes to those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind. Nobel is best known as the inventor of dynamite and was also a businessman, poet, and linguist. Mr Nobel spent much of his career developing weapons. He died in 1896, and the first prizes were awarded in 1901, following a legal battle over his will. A private institution called The Nobel Foundation is responsible for fulfilling the intentions of Alfred Nobels will. According to the Nobel Prize website, the main mission of the Nobel Foundation is to manage Alfred Nobels fortune in a manner that ensures a secure financial standing for the Nobel Prize over the long term and that the prize-awarding institutions are guaranteed independence in their work of selecting recipients. Nobel selected the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences to award the prizes for chemistry and physics, the Swedish Academy for literature, Swedens Karolinska Institute medical university for physiology or medicine, and the Norwegian parliament for peace. All timings mentioned are based on the information displayed on the official Nobel Prize website. With inputs from Reuters

headline: The seven Shiva temples of Mylapore
content: Of late, cult of the Sapta Sthana circuit is growing in Mylapore. It involves seven Shiva temples in the area. If social media is to be believed, the tradition is a 1000 years old! And yet until the early 2000s, none of us Mylaporeans had even heard of it, familiar as we were with the temples. Also Read: Sketching Meenakshi: Learn to draw temple sculptures and architecture Before we get on with Sapta Sthanam in Mylapore, we need to know that such a tradition exists elsewhere and for centuries. In the Thanjavur region is a group of seven Shiva temples, all of them of great antiquity, adored in the Tevaram. These are Thiruvaiyyaru, Thirpazhanam, Thiruchotruthurai, Thiruneithanam, Thiruvedikudi, Thirupoonthuruthi and Thirkandiyur. In the month of April/May (Chithirai), the Lord at Thiruvaiyyaru sets out in a palanquin and visits each of the other six temples. At each, the deity of that temple joins in a palanquin and this way, there are seven palanquins by the end of the festival. The temples are all by the Cauvery, on whose dry bed the procession progresses. In sharp contrast, the seven temples of Mylapore are not linked by a common legend, and they are also not shrines of the same antiquity. Among these, the Kapaliswarar temple is certainly the oldest. Though its inscriptional records are weak, its history is well established by way of Tamil poetic works the Tevaram (7th century CE), the Periya Puranam (12th) and the Tirupugazh (15th). The lack of inscriptions is attributed to the destruction of the older shrine by the sea. This is most likely to have been by the Portuguese though we dont have any written evidence of this, their record at Shiva temples in Sri Lanka supports the theory. The present temple is said to be around three hundred years old, and as we have been saying this for around a hundred years, let us add a century to it. The relocated precinct today owes a lot to the dubashes of the East India Company. Of perhaps equal antiquity is the Virupakshiswarar temple of Mylapore, with its vast tank. Inscriptions from the 11th century have surfaced here. It is believed that Sivanesan Chettiar, the father of Poompavai, at whose invitation Sambandar came to Mayilai in the 7th century, was associated with this temple. But it is significant that Sambandar in his Tevaram hymns sings only of Kapaliswarar. The Periya Puranam of the 12th century does not mention Sivanesans connect with this temple either. Madras is, as we all know, an agglomeration of villages, populated by migrants. Apart from the truly ancient temples of the city that predate the founding of the colonial metropolis, most shrines here were constructed by the well-to-do, wanting some symbols of their places of origin in the city in which they had settled. That accounts for practically all the remaining five Shiva temples of Mylapore. Government records however add to the confusion. The Karaniswarar temple was 300 years old as per the government census of 1961. It is likely that when migrants moved to Mylapore from Saidapet, a weavers colony, where there is an older temple to Shiva by the same name, they built a shrine here. But we also have a claim that inscriptions from the 12th century have been found here! The Valeeswarar temple, as per the HR&CE is 1300 years old but as per the 1961 census dated back 400 years. It is very likely inspired by the temple of the same name in Kanchipuram, with which it shares a legend. The Teerthapaleeswarar temple according to the 1961 census again is of Pallava origin but the same record says that the present shrine dated to 500 years prior. The two most recent ones have of late begun to claim the greatest antiquity. The Velleeswarar temple began life dedicted to Ganesa by the weavers of Mylapore around 300 years ago. The shrines to Velleeswarar and Kamakshi came up in the 1850s, inspired no doubt by Mangadu and funded by the Sengunthar community. A tale now circulates that it predates the Kapali temple! The Malliswarar temple was constructed in the 1850s by a Chidambara Mudaliar and now claims to date back a thousand years! When challenged on their historicity, most shrines have a common answer they were so thoroughly destroyed by invaders that there was nothing left. What is inexplicable is the silence of Tamil sacred poetry. Beyond a point, like the legend of St. Thomas, it is best to respect faith and keep facts to ourselves. Lastly, on the Sapta Sthanam circuit it is my hunch that it was the slim booklet Siva Temples of Mylapore, published in 2002 by Kalamkriya, the publication wing of the Sanmar Group, that first gave the devout such an idea. From there, it has travelled back a 1000 years. (Sriram V. is a writer and historian)

headline: Henri Kagan And Kenso Soai: Meet The Scientists Behind 2026 Nobel Prize In Chemistry
content: Meet The Scientists Behind 2026 Nobel Prize In Chemistry The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai the prize for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. French chemist Henri Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. The two changed the way scientists think about asymmetric chemical reactions and how tiny differences between molecules can be amplified into overwhelmingly one-sided outcomes. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded them the prize for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis." Who Is Henri Kagan? Henri Kagan is a French chemist whose work has been central to one of the biggest challenges in asymmetric chemistry. He focused his work on finding ways to make a chemical reaction produce predominantly one of two molecules that are mirror images of each other. Henri Kagans work showed that it was possible to control this molecular handedness" during a chemical reaction rather than simply ending up with a mixture of both forms. His research on asymmetric synthesis became particularly important because the three-dimensional arrangement of atoms can determine how a molecule behaves, especially when it interacts with the highly shape-specific molecules found in living organisms. One Molecule Can Heal, Its Mirror Image Can Harm: Chemistry Behind 2026 Nobel Prize Who Is Kenso Soai? Kenso Soai is a Japanese chemist whose work took this question further by examining what happens when chemistry can effectively amplify its own small differences. His research focused on autocatalysis, a process in which a product of a chemical reaction helps drive the formation of more of that same product. In the context of mirror-image molecules, this creates a remarkable possibility that an extremely small imbalance between the two forms can be amplified through repeated chemical reactions until one form becomes overwhelmingly dominant. Kenso Soai became particularly well known for the reaction that now bears his name, the Soai reaction, which provided one of the clearest demonstrations of how autocatalysis can amplify molecular handedness. French chemist Henri Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

headline: CBI Summons Punjab CM Mann's OSD In 'Cash-For-Favours' Case: What FIR Says | Exclusive
content: The summons came after the CBI registered a First Information Report (FIR) on October 5 and conducted coordinated raids across eight locations in Punjab and Chandigarh The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has issued a summons directing Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, to appear for questioning at its Chandigarh office. The summons came after the federal agency registered a First Information Report (FIR) on October 5 and conducted coordinated raids across eight locations in Punjab and Chandigarh. The extensive searches targeted Chief Minister Manns Camp Office, Ghumans residential premises, and the homes of his close associates, alongside raids across Mohali, Patiala, Ludhiana, Jalandhar, and Gurdaspur districts. Simultaneously, the state government is set to mention its urgent petition before the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Court order that directed the CBI probe. - CBI Raids Bhagwant Manns Camp Office In Corruption Case; Punjab CM Claims Misuse Of Agencies - BREAKING | CBI Raids Bhagwant Manns Camp Office, Aides Residence Post Corruption Claims | - Punjab CBI Probe: CM Manns OSD Faces Corruption Allegations | Cash-for-Transfers | Punjab News - Punjab Govt Panel On Sacrilege Law Amendments To Meet On October 6, Discuss Akal Takht Suggestions Core Allegations Uncovered in ED Money Laundering Probe The foundation of the CBIs FIR stems from communications sent by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the Director General of Police (DGP), Punjab, under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). During money laundering raids conducted in May on an individual named Nitin Gohal and his associates, the ED uncovered extensive documentary and digital evidence detailing a widespread corruption network. Recovered WhatsApp conversations and internal ledgers indicate that Gohal operated as an active intermediary, leveraging his access to CMs OSD Rajbir Ghuman to influence state government decisions. The ED alleges Gohal collected crores of rupees in proceeds of crime to manipulate government transfers, tender specifications, departmental rule amendments, and the procurement of arms licences. Evidence cited in the FIR includes leaked confidential policy drafts, discussions on illegal cash payments, and records showing Gohal funded air travel and hotel stays for key government associates in cash. Seven Accused Named Under Criminal Conspiracy and Cheating Charges The CBI issued a summons for Rajbir Singh Ghuman, OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, for questioning. The summons followed an FIR registered on October 5 and raids across eight locations in Punjab and Chandigarh. The CBI's FIR stems from communications sent by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the DGP, Punjab. The CBI FIR formally names seven accused, including Rajbir Singh Ghuman and Nitin Gohal. The agency invoked penal provisions under IPC Section 120B and 420, and BNS Section 61(2) and 318(4). The CBI FIR formally names seven accused alongside unknown public servants and private individuals. The named individuals include Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal (alias Raja), Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, and RS Nagra. The agency has invoked penal provisions under both the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): - Criminal Conspiracy (IPC Section 120B / BNS Section 61(2)): Applied for entering into an illegal agreement to perform unlawful acts, including taking bribes to manipulate state policy, administrative approvals, and government decisions. - Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property (IPC Section 420 / BNS Section 318(4)): Invoked for deceiving individuals and dishonestly inducing the delivery of money or property through fraudulent promises of government favours. Scope of Institutional Corruption Outlined in FIR According to the official communication sent to the Punjab Police and detailed in the CBI FIR, the accused conspired to take bribes across vast areas of state administration. The documented illicit activities include influence over Change of Land Use (CLU) matters, land demarcation proceedings, property disputes, housing scheme approvals, and sensitive revenue records. The FIR emphasises that the syndicate misused access to confidential state information to manipulate government procurement, tweak departmental rules, and influence postings and transfers across departments in exchange for illegal gratification. The CBI issued a summons directing Rajbir Singh Ghuman, OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann, to appear for questioning after registering an FIR on October 5 in a 'cash-for-favours' corruption case.

headline: How Fight Over Seating Arrangement At Qawwali Event Left Sena Councillor, NCP Worker Dead, 10 Injured
content: Buldhanas Deulgaon Raja Qawwali Seating Arrangement Row: The deceased are Anwar Sheikh, a Shiv Sena councillor, and Arif Pathan, the husband of an NCP councillor A fatal clash over qawwali seating arrangements in Deulgaon Raja, Buldhana district, Maharashtra, resulted in the deaths of two local political figures and left at least 10 others injured. All we know so far. - Wont Hold Back On Relief: Eknath Shinde Assures Farmers Of Loan Restructuring Amid Maharashtra Drought - Indian Man Slaps Canadian Kick Streamer After Heated Clash Over Filming: You Are F*ing Racist | Video - 'They Have Become Ghajinis': Fadnavis Takes Swipe At Uddhav, Raj Thackeray Over Mumbai Protest - Bigg Boss 17s Anurag Dobhal Arrested In Dehradun After Allegedly Assaulting His Brother-In-Law The deceased have been identified as Anwar Sheikh, a Shiv Sena (Eknath Shinde) councillor, and Arif Pathan, the husband of an Nationalist Congress Party (Ajit Pawar) (NCP) councillor. The two men belonged to rival local factions. Following the incident, the Deulgaon Raja police registered two separate FIRs mapping the conflict. According to Buldhana Superintendent of Police Nilesh Tambe, 20 individuals from both factions have been arrested as investigations continue. WHAT CAUSED THE FIGHT? The root cause of the fatal seating row was a petty dispute involving children and youth sitting at a locally organized qawwali programme near the Bholeshah Dargah in Pratap Nagar, Deulgaon Raja. During the musical performance, some young children and youth from two separate local groups got into an argument over who got to sit where at the venue. Elders and senior members from both groups originally intervened to stop the minor argument. However, instead of cooling the situation down, the confrontation escalated as the adult memberswho belonged to rival political networkstook sides. Two local political figures died in a clash over qawwali seating arrangements in Buldhana district, Maharashtra. At least 10 individuals were injured in the incident. The deceased were identified as Shiv Sena councillor Anwar Sheikh and NCP councillor's husband Arif Pathan. Buldhana Superintendent of Police Nilesh Tambe reported that 20 individuals from both factions have been arrested. Deulgaon Raja police registered two separate FIRs, including charges of murder, attempt to murder, rioting, and unlawful assembly. The disagreement lingered throughout the day. Later that evening, both factions arrived at the Deulgaon Raja police station to file complaints against each other, where they came face-to-face and the deadly brawl began. CHARGES FILED IN FIRS The Deulgaon Raja police have registered two separate First Information Reports (FIRs) based on cross-complaints from both sides one filed by Sheikh Mujahid Sheikh Ali and the other by Sheikh Atik Sheikh Umar. The cases invoke strict provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). These charges include murder, attempt to murder, rioting, and unlawful assembly. Following the deaths of the Shiv Sena councillor and the NCP worker, heavy tension gripped the area. Buldhana Superintendent of Police Nilesh Tambe deployed heavy police reinforcement and special units from the Local Crime Branch (LCB) across Deulgaon Raja. The funerals of both deceased individuals were conducted back-to-back under strict, heavily armed police monitoring to ensure no further flare-ups. The town has since returned to a state of tense but controlled calm. With Marathi inputs The fatal clash was triggered by a petty dispute over seating arrangements among children and youth at a qawwali programme near the Bholeshah Dargah. The minor argument escalated when adult members from rival political factions took sides, leading to a deadly brawl outside the police station.

headline: One Molecule Can Heal, Its Mirror Image Can Harm: Chemistry Behind 2026 Nobel Prize
content: The difficulty is that when a chemical reaction can produce two mirror-image molecules, it will often produce both. Nobel Prize In Chemistry: What if two molecules had exactly the same atoms, the same chemical formula and almost exactly the same structure but behaved very differently simply because one was the mirror image of the other? This seemingly strange problem lies at the centre of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, which was awarded to French chemist Henri B. Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai for their discovery of nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. What Does It Mean When A Molecule Has A Mirror Image? Start with your hands. Your left hand and your right hand look almost identical and both contain the same fingers, joints and bones but there is no way to rotate one hand so that it becomes exactly the other. They are mirror images of each other but they are not superimposable. Chemists call this property chirality, a term derived from the Greek word for hand". Molecules can have the same kind of handedness, meaning that a molecule can exist in two different forms that are mirror images of each other. These two forms are called enantiomers. This distinction becomes particularly important in biology because the molecules inside living organisms are themselves three-dimensional structures with specific shapes. A molecule therefore does not interact with another molecule simply because the two have compatible chemical formulas; their shapes have to fit together in the right way, much as a left hand fits differently into a glove designed for a right hand. That is why two molecular mirror images can behave very differently when they encounter the machinery of the human body. So Can The Mirror Image Of A Medicine Really Do Something Completely Different? It can and this is one reason why controlling molecular handedness is so important in pharmaceutical chemistry. Many drug molecules exist in two mirror-image forms but the two versions do not necessarily produce the same biological response. One form may interact with a particular target in the body and produce the therapeutic effect a drug was designed to achieve while its mirror image may be less effective, inactive or capable of producing unwanted effects. This means that making a drug molecule is sometimes only half the problem. Scientists also need to control which handed version of that molecule they make. Why Cant Chemists Simply Make The Version They Want? The difficulty is that when a chemical reaction can produce two mirror-image molecules, it will often produce both, rather than naturally choosing one over the other. Imagine tossing a perfectly balanced coin: heads and tails should appear in roughly equal proportions. A chemical reaction can behave in a similar way when it has no particular reason to favour one molecular hand" over the other, leaving chemists with a mixture of two mirror-image products. For many applications, however, that mixture is not what scientists want. They need a reaction that strongly favours one enantiomer, allowing them to obtain a product with a particular three-dimensional arrangement. This is the problem known as asymmetric synthesis: finding ways to make a chemical reaction produce predominantly one of two possible mirror-image forms. Henri Kagan made a major breakthrough in this area in 1986, when he developed a method that could produce a large excess of one mirror-image form rather than an equal mixture of both. His work demonstrated that chemists could exert much greater control over molecular handedness than had previously been possible. But another stranger question remained which was that what would happen if a tiny preference for one molecular form could somehow grow larger by itself? How Can A Tiny Molecular Advantage Become A Huge One? This is where Kenso Soais work enters the story. Soai studied chemical reactions in which the products could influence the reaction that produced them, a phenomenon known as autocatalysis. In an ordinary catalytic reaction, a catalyst helps a reaction proceed without being consumed in the process; in an autocatalytic reaction, the product itself can help promote the production of more of that same product. This creates the possibility of a chemical feedback loop. Suppose a reaction begins with an extremely small imbalance, in which one mirror-image form is present just slightly more than the other. If the molecules produced by that reaction then encourage the formation of more molecules with the same handedness, the original imbalance can be amplified. A tiny difference can therefore become a much larger difference. Soais research eventually produced what became known as the Soai reaction, demonstrating a remarkable form of asymmetric autocatalysis. By 2003, his experiments had shown that a reaction could produce essentially one of two possible mirror-image forms, something that had previously been observed as a characteristic of living systems rather than something that chemists could reproduce in the laboratory. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to French chemist Henri B. Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai for their discovery of nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

headline: India slams OIC's 'willful blindness' at UN, defends action against terror infrastructure in Pakistan, PoK
content: India on Tuesday slammed the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly, rejecting its remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and New Delhis actions against terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK). Responding to the OIC chair's statement, BJP MP Biplab Kumar Deb accused the group of being unable to differentiate between the victim and the perpetrator. I now respond to the statement made by the OIC Chair regarding India's focused and measured action against terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, from where terrorist attacks against India have been planned and directed, Deb said at the UN General Assembly. It is unfortunate that the speaker is unable to distinguish between fact and fiction and cannot differentiate between the victim and the perpetrator, he said. India has the full right to protect its people against terrorism on the border coming from Pakistan. The consequences of being involved in terrorism will not be tolerated, Deb added. Deb, the Lok Sabha MP from West Tripura, delivered Indias national statement at the UN General Assembly Sixth Committee on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. He is part of a 15-member parliamentary delegation that arrived in New York for a UN familiarisation week. Deb said India understands from bitter experience that terrorism is not a theoretical threat but a persistent and daily reality. This threat has serious implications for international peace and security, economic progress, democratic institutions and human rights. It attacks the most fundamental right of every human being the right to life, he said. For decades, our people have suffered from cross-border terrorism, Deb said, referring to the long-standing security challenge faced by India. He also cited the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year, in which 26 tourists were killed, as an example of the devastating human cost of terrorism. The Pahalgam terror attack was a calculated assault on our sovereignty, planned and executed by networks that continue to enjoy state patronage, safe havens, and material and logistical support from across our western border, he said. Terrorism is contrary to the values of the United Nations. Deliberately targeting civilians can never be justified in any manner. There is no distinction between good and bad terrorism. India considers terrorist attacks as crimes against humanity, Deb said. As India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, We consider that even a single attack is one too many and even a single life lost is one too many, he added. Deb also criticised the OICs position on Jammu and Kashmir, urging the group to focus instead on Pakistans control over territory that India claims. The OIC chair would do better to focus on Pakistan's illegal occupation, especially in Rawalakot, where wanton killings, brutal violence and the denial of basic rights to the people living there are so visible, Deb said. Such willful blindness only speaks of bigotry and intolerance, he added. His remarks came a day after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) rejected references to Jammu and Kashmir made by the OIC Contact Group, calling them unwarranted and factually incorrect. In a statement shared on X, the MEA said the OIC had no locus standi to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India. The Indian response followed a meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir in New York, comprising Azerbaijan, Pakistan, Trkiye, Saudi Arabia and Niger. During the meeting, the group reaffirmed its support for what it described as the Kashmiri peoples right to self-determination.

headline: Christa Pike awake after failed execution, her attorneys seek more information
content: U.S. death row inmate Christa Pike has regained consciousness after Tennessees failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection last week, and her attorneys are set to head to court Wednesday to seek more information about what went wrong. Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital as executioners attempted to put her to death on September 30 for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. Pike is believed to be the only person to survive after lethal injection drugs were administered. Pikes attorneys are set to appear in court Wednesday as they are seeking more information from the Tennessee Department of Correction. Chancery Court Judge IAshea Myles has scheduled a Wednesday morning (October 7, 2026) status conference in Nashville in the case. Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care, attorneys for Pike said in a statement. Pikes prognosis remains unclear and, at a minimum, she faces a lengthy recovery, the attorneys said. They said Pikes arms were burned and blistered after the attempted lethal injection and that she is handcuffed to the hospital bed. Pikes attorneys are seeking a court order to require the prison system to preserve information from the attempted execution including drug lot numbers, needles, execution logs and other information. Attorneys with the Tennessee attorney generals office wrote in a Tuesday court filing that the court order is unnecessary because the prison system is obliged to maintain this evidence in other cases and must assure it is preserved. They said state officials have taken the necessary steps to obtain medical care for Pike and ascertain what occurred. Republican Governor Bill Lee called what happened deeply disturbing and ordered a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred. The governor postponed the states only other execution scheduled for this year. Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on the possibility that a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue rather than entering her bloodstream. Pikes attorneys wrote in their court filing that apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown. The attempted execution got underway around 7:30 p.m. on September 30, when Pike was given a chance to make a final statement. About five minutes later, Pike raised her head and said her arm was hurting. At some point, she appeared to lose consciousness, but she could be heard audibly breathing until media were escorted from the witness room at 8:53 p.m. An ambulance arrived at the prison at 9:14 p.m. to take Pike to a hospital.

headline: 'Even Your Father Can't Stop Us': Pakistan CM Sohail Afridi's Warning To Shehbaz Govt, Military
content: next phase of the march comes amid a security lockdown around Islamabad, with the federal government warning protesters against entering the capital Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi has issued a defiant warning to Pakistans federal government and military establishment, saying no one can stop the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march from reaching Islamabad. Speaking exclusively to CNN-, Afridi also accused Pakistans courts and authorities of failing to implement orders related to meetings with jailed former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, as well as his medical treatment. - 'No Guns, But I Have People's Power': Sohail Afridi Leads PTI March, Rejects KP Military Action - KP CM Opposes Pak Military Operations, Says Pashtuns Wont Shed Blood For Americas Dollar Wars - Pakistans Rs. 5,300-Billion Corruption, If This Is Wisdom: KP CM Afridi Attacks Naqvi | Exclusive - 'No Guns, But I Have People's Power': Sohail Afridi Leads PTI March, Rejects KP Military Action I challenge the whole of Pakistan. I challenge the entire world that out of those seven points, if even a single demand is proven to be unconstitutional or illegal, then at that very moment, I will cancel my long march," Afridi said. The PTI leader was referring to the partys seven demands as its convoy, which began its march from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 4, moves towards Islamabad. The march is being led by Afridi and is centred on demands including the release of Imran Khan. Even Your Father Wont Be Able To Stop Us Afridi, who has repeatedly said the march will continue towards the federal capital, delivered a direct warning to the government and those attempting to block the protesters. When we say that we will reach Islamabad and show you, then forget about you, even your father wont be able to stop us," he said. The comments come amid heightened tensions between the PTI-led provincial government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the federal government of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Islamabad has deployed security forces and warned that protesters would not be permitted to enter the capital. The march began after negotiations between PTI and the federal government failed to resolve their differences. Pakistan Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has accused Afridi of sabotaging the talks, while PTI has maintained its demands linked to Imran Khan and other political issues. Afridi Questions Courts Over Imran Khan Orders Afridi also launched a sharp attack on Pakistans judicial system, alleging that court orders concerning Imran Khan have not been implemented. Kohat residents, the chief justice of Pakistan is from your city, yet my hearing hasnt taken place," he said. I told the chief justice of the Islamabad High Court, but he didnt even respond to my greeting." Afridi claimed that an order issued by three judges of a high court directing that he be allowed to meet Imran Khan had not been implemented. An order comes from three high court judges that I should be allowed to meet my leader, but it isnt implemented," he said. He made a similar allegation regarding Khans medical treatment, saying a three-judge Supreme Court bench had ordered that the former prime minister be treated at Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad. An order comes from three Supreme Court judges that Imran Khans treatment should be carried out at Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, but it isnt implemented," Afridi said. The dispute over Khans medical treatment has been a major flashpoint between PTI and the government. In August, Pakistans Supreme Court ordered Khans transfer to Shifa International Hospital, but he was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences before being returned to prison. The government subsequently sought a review of the Supreme Court order. I Know About Your Lack Of Honour Afridi also launched a personal attack on a government leader, questioning his political standing and using the term coward" while referring to him. That coward who has lost his election against an elderly woman. If this shameless persons father had been a man, he wouldnt have sat on the seat of an elderly woman," Afridi said. I know about your lack of honour, and I also know about the honour of that coward who is your leader," he added. Afridi did not soften his rhetoric as the PTI convoy continued its journey towards Islamabad. The march had begun at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat on October 4, with Afridi saying he would personally lead the movement. The convoy subsequently moved through parts of southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and reached the Mattani area on the outskirts of Peshawar on October 6. The next phase of the march comes amid a security lockdown around Islamabad, with the federal government warning protesters against entering the capital. For Afridi, however, the message remains unchanged: unless even one of the PTIs seven demands is proved illegal or unconstitutional, he says, there will be no turning back. No one can stop us from reaching Islamabad," his message to the government was. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi issued a defiant warning that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf long march toward Islamabad would not be stopped. The march, which began on October 4, is centered around seven core demands, including the release of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.
