headline: Madras High Court denies interim relief to DMK's ex-Minister E.V. Velu, his son in lake bed excavation case
content: Madras High Court on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) refused to grant interim relief to DMKs former Minister and incumbent Party Whip in Tamil Nadu Assembly E.V. Velu (76) and his son E.V. Kumaran (48) in a case booked against them for allegedly excavating 45,72,058 cubic feet of sand from Malappambadi lake in Tiruvannamalai district for levelling the venue of the partys north zone youth wing conference held on December 14, 2025. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan rejected the plea for an ex-parte interim stay and ordered notice, returnable by November 6, to the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption (DVAC) on individual petitions filed by the father and son to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against them on September 24, 2026. Jayaram Venkatesan of Arappor Iyakkam, the anti-corruption NGO was the complainant. The complainant had alleged the illegal excavation from about eight acres of the waterbody, in and around November 2025, to level the lands, belonging to a private company in which Mr. Kumaran was one of the directors, resulted in a loss of 8.22 crore to the public exchequer. However, both petitioners claimed they were innocent and had not committed any offence. Highlighting that the FIR had been registered only after a change of government in Tamil Nadu, Mr. Velu, in his petition said this was the second criminal case booked against him at the instance of Arappor Iyakkam after the formation of the TVK government in May 2026. The first FIR, also booked by the DVAC, in connection with laying of highways had already been challenged before the High Court. Senior counsel Sidharth Luthra, assisted by Rahul Balaji, contended the FIR under challenge had been registered entirely on surmises, political conjecture and general statements without attributing any overt act against the petitioners. The court was told that even if the contents of the FIR were taken to be true on face value, still they do not disclose commission of any offence. Mr. Luthra also pointed out since the FIR dates back to the period when Mr. Velu was the State Highways Minister, the FIR does not disclose whether any approval required under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 had been obtained. In any event, the FIR does not contain any allegations attracting the provisions of the PC Act, except making bald and sweeping allegations of abuse of official position, he added.

headline: '13.39 Crore Voters Deleted Through SIR': EC Responds To Oppn's Claim, Says Those Eligible Can Get Name Added
content: gives out ASDD data, says if a voters name is not included in final electoral roll despite prescribed process, they can appeal before District Magistrate or CEO The Election Commission has clarified its position on the Oppositions allegation that more than 13 crore voters were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. According to ECI data, a total of 95.40 crore voters were reviewed during the three phases of the SIR exercise. Of these, 13.39 crore voters were categorised under ASDD and other categories during the revision process. - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - How Convenient, Pookie: Posters Taking Potshots At Rahul, Akhilesh Splash Delhi Ahead Of INDIA Bloc Meet - Will Wait Till I Get Justice: Shivakumar Protests Outside Karnataka CEOs Office Over Voter Deletions - 'Congress Believes In Creating Ruckus, Exposed Again': BJP After EC Denies Oppn's Meeting Request Claim ASDD refers to voters who were found to be Absent, Permanently Shifted, Dead or Duplicate. As per the Election Commissions figures: - Absent / Not Traceable: 3.01 crore - Permanently Shifted: 6.30 crore - Dead: 2.80 crore - Duplicate: 1.02 crore - Other Categories: 0.26 crore - Total: 13.39 crore THE CLARIFICATION The Election Commission official said the ASDD lists were prepared after an extensive verification exercise by more than 10 lakh Booth Level Officers across the states. The ASDD lists were also provided booth-wise to more than 22 lakh Booth Level Agents of political parties. The ECI official said voters were given one month to file claims and objections after the draft electoral rolls were published. During this period, eligible voters could seek inclusion of their names, while objections could also be filed against the inclusion of ineligible voters. The Commission clarified that if a genuine voters name was inadvertently left out during the SIR process, the voter could seek inclusion through the claims and objections process and subsequently through Form 6. The ECI further said that if a voters name was not included in the final electoral roll despite the prescribed process, the person could appeal before the District Magistrate or the Chief Electoral Officer, as applicable. The Election Commissions position comes amid Opposition allegations over the deletion of more than 13 crore names during the SIR exercise. The ECI maintains that the figures represent voters identified under different categories during the verification process and that eligible voters have been provided mechanisms to get their names included in the electoral rolls. ASDD refers to voters who were identified as Absent, Permanently Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate during the revision process.

headline: News18 DEFCON 2026: Decoding India's Next Defence Transition
content: import dependence remains important, but the larger test is whether self-reliance can translate into technological ownership, industrial depth, and operational readiness Indias defence transformation is entering a more demanding phase. Reducing import dependence remains important, but the larger test is whether self-reliance can translate into technological ownership, industrial depth, operational readiness and the ability to build capabilities at scale. That transition was at the centre of DEFCON 2026, in association with The Chanakya Dialogues, which brought together military leadership, policymakers, diplomats and industry to examine the capabilities India will need as warfare, technology and global security relationships evolve. - PTI Vs Shehbaz: Pakistan Government Weighs Emergency, Governor's Rule In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa - From Hormuz To Bab-El-Mandeb, Who Is Protecting Indian Seafarers In Conflict Zones? - 'US Becoming Lonelier Power By Choice': Jaishankar Flags 'Radical Repositioning' Of America - Opinion | From Corridor To Network: Why IMEC Must Be Built For A World Of Disruption Delivering the Keynote Address, Shri Rajnath Singh, Union Minister for Defence, placed self-reliance firmly within the national security framework. National Security Is Truly Resilient When It Is Self-Reliant." He connected that resilience with domestic capability creation: Design, develop and manufacture in India is a vision we are working with." But the discussions through the day also made clear that domestic production alone cannot define the next phase. General NS Raja Subramani, PVSM, AVSM, SM, VSM, Chief of Defence Staff, pointed to the speed at which the nature of conflict is evolving. The character of war is changing faster than we are able to adapt," he said. The challenge, therefore, is not simply to develop new technologies, but to ensure that industrial acquisition and operational systems can absorb and deploy them quickly enough. That need for adaptation is closely linked to integration. Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Defence Secretary, GoI, emphasised jointness not merely at the operational level, but throughout capability development: You should be able to plan your capabilities jointly, do acquisitions jointly and ultimately apply power jointly." It signals an important shift, from building capability service by service towards thinking about how military power is planned, acquired and applied as a whole. For the Indian Navy, resilience extends beyond acquiring platforms. Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, PVSM, AVSM, VSM, Chief of the Naval Staff, highlighted the importance of being able to maintain, repair, replenish and upgrade ships, submarines and aircraft. In a crisis, when supply chains or access to critical technologies may be constrained, sustainment becomes part of combat capability itself. DEFCON 2026 also widened the definition of preparedness. Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (Retd.), PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, SM, VSM & Bar, Governor of Bihar, examined information warfare and the growing importance of narratives and perception in contemporary conflict. General (Dr) Vijay Kumar Singh (Retd.), PVSM, AVSM, YSM, Governor of Mizoram, brought military diplomacy into the discussion, underscoring how security relationships increasingly extend beyond the battlefield. The industrial conversation, meanwhile, showed why states matter to the national defence ecosystem. Shri Sanjay Jaju, IAS, Chief Secretary, Govt. of Telangana, discussed aerospace, defence and space capabilities within Telanganas longer-term industrial vision; while Dr G Satheesh Reddy, AP State Defence Advisor & Director of the Aeronautical Society of India, highlighted the role regional ecosystems can play in expanding Indias manufacturing base. Together, the discussions pointed to a more complex definition of self-reliance. Production is one measure; ownership of critical technologies, integrated planning, resilient supply chains, faster adaptation and the ability to sustain capability during a crisis are equally consequential. Indias journey from self-reliance to global leadership, therefore, is not simply about making more at home. It is about building the technological depth, operational integration, industrial scale and strategic partnerships required to compete, collaborate and contribute at a global level. Know more at DEFCON Summit 2026, in association with The Chanakya Dialogues | State Partners Government of Uttar Pradesh, Government of Andhra Pradesh & Government of Uttarakhand | Associate Partners: Suzlon, LIC, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Paras Defence & Space Technologies Limited, Jaykay Enterprise Limited & Reliance Industries Limited. Defence production reached a record level of 1.78 lakh crore in FY202526, while defence exports reached an all-time high of 38,424 crore.

headline: Israelis mark three years since Hamas attack that set off Gaza assault
content: Israelis on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) mark three years since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, triggering a military assault that destroyed much of Gaza, where conditions remain dire despite a year-old ceasefire that is meant to halt the war for good. The attacks, during which militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages to Gaza, marked the deadliest day in Israels history. Israels subsequent bombardment and ground operations have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza, health authorities there say. On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Israelis will hold a vigil at the site of the Nova music festival near the Gaza border, where 348 young people were killed by militants during the attack. They will also hold an event commemorating the anniversary at Hostage Square in Tel Aviv. Israeli election 20 days away The anniversary is the first for Israelis without any hostages still held in Gaza, with those dead and alive exchanged in swaps with Hamas for Palestinians held in Israeli jails. The remains of the last Israeli hostage were recovered in January. It also comes just 20 days ahead of Israels first election since the attack, a vote that is viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus long tenure in power. Mr. Netanyahu has rejected blame for the security breach and resisted calls for an independent investigation. That has frustrated many in Israel, including families of those killed in the attacks, some of whom have joined the election race. A poll by the Israel Democracy Institute showed that 68% of Jewish Israelis said that the events of October 7 were a very central or fairly central element in their decision of which party to vote for. Election polls show neither Mr. Netanyahu nor his main competitors would muster enough seats in parliament to form a coalition if a vote were held today. U.S.-backed ceasefire fails to halt Israeli attacks, disarm Hamas The anniversary is also the first since an October 10, 2025, U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that halted major fighting but has failed to stop Israeli attacks in Gaza or secure the disarmament of Hamas and other militant groups. The deal left Israel in control of some 53% of Gaza, since expanded by Israeli forces to nearly two-thirds. Hamas controls the remaining third, where the 2 million population mostly live in makeshift tents and bombed out buildings. US President Donald Trumps so-called Board of Peace has proposed several plans that would see Gaza rebuilt. But those plans, which fail to account for the property rights of Palestinians whose homes were destroyed, have failed to gain the buy-in of Israel or Hamas, which are still deadlocked in ceasefire talks. The two have yet to agree on the terms of a deal that would see Hamas lay down its weapons in exchange for Israeli troop withdrawals. Israel says it will not pull back until Hamas fully disarms; Hamas says it has agreed to a phased process but will not disarm so long as Israeli attacks continue. Israel has kept up a bombing campaign in Gaza that has killed a number of Hamas militants in recent months but has also killed many civilians, say Gaza health authorities, whose death figures do not distinguish between civilians and combatants. More than 1,400 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, the health authorities say. During the same time, five Israeli soldiers have been killed by militants or in combat, the military says.

headline: Pakistan security forces kill 18 terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan
content: Pakistani security forces have killed 18 terrorists in separate operations in the restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces, state media reported on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). According to Radio Pakistan, the security forces killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The federal government uses the term 'Fitna al-Khawarij' for terrorists belonging to the banned terror outfit Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan. Separately, five terrorists were killed in Balochistan's Mastung district, according to state-run Pakistan Television. Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain terrorists, while clearance and search operations were underway in the area, the report said. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended the security forces for the operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, according to Radio Pakistan. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces have witnessed a surge in militant attacks in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

headline: 7 policemen injured in attack in northwest Pakistan
content: Seven police personnel sustained injuries after militants attacked a police checkpost in northwest Pakistan on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), an official said. The incident occurred in the Shadipur area of Kohat district in the restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. No individual or group has claimed responsibility for the attack. According to District Police Officer (DPO) Mazhar Iqbal, the attack on the police checkpost was foiled after police personnel returned fire. The attackers fled the scene following the retaliation from the police, DPO Iqbal said, adding that the injured personnel were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital. A search operation has been launched, and an investigation into the incident is underway. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and provincial Information Minister Shafi Jan condemned the attack. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province has faced recurring unrest over the years driven by militant violence, cross-border movement of fighters from Afghanistan and repeated military operations. The federal government accuses the banned terror outfit Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan of carrying out attacks in provinces bordering Afghanistan after its ceasefire deal ended in November 2022.

headline: Nobel Prize 2026: How JNU scientist Suneel Kateriya helped lay the groundwork for optogenetics
content: A tiny freshwater alga and an Indian scientist's doctoral research in Germany are part of the scientific journey behind the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. In 2001, Suneel Kateriya was working in Professor Peter Hegemann's laboratory in Regensburg, Germany, when he searched the genes of Chlamydomonas, a single-celled alga that can detect and move towards light. Kateriya identified two light-sensing proteins. The genes were later named channelrhodopsin-1 and channelrhodopsin-2. Quick answers to key questions 1What is optogenetics and how does it work? Optogenetics is a technique that allows researchers to control specific cells using light. It works by introducing light-sensitive proteins into neurons, enabling the use of light to alter the electrical activity of those neurons precisely. 2Why is Suneel Kateriya's research on Chlamydomonas significant for optogenetics? Suneel Kateriya's research identified light-sensing proteins in the alga Chlamydomonas, which laid the groundwork for optogenetics, enabling precise control of neuron activity and opening new avenues for neuroscience research. 3How have advances in optogenetics impacted research on neural circuits? Advances in optogenetics have allowed scientists to study neural circuits more precisely, linking specific neurons to behavior, such as learned fear responses in animals, which enhances our understanding of brain functionality. 4What challenges does optogenetics face in its clinical application? Optogenetics faces challenges like effective gene delivery, long-term safety, precise cell targeting, and the necessary light intensity for practical application in clinical settings. 5Should researchers consider optogenetics as a viable option for future therapies? Yes, researchers should consider optogenetics, given its potential for targeted control of cells in various neurological conditions, although it remains primarily a research tool at this stage. More than two decades later, Kateriya is a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), while his work forms part of the scientific foundation behind optogenetics a technique that allows researchers to control selected cells, including neurons, using light. The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2026 medicine prize to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for the discovery of light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Kateriya has described his contribution as part of a broader collaborative effort. "Fundamental science and academic excellence are needed for bigger innovations," he told India Today Digital. The original research was not aimed at understanding the human brain. "We had a fundamental question: how is this alga sensing light, and where are the genes?" Kateriya said. "We never thought it would be used for controlling the human brain." The researchers found gene sequences encoding rhodopsin proteins and proposed that they could function as light-driven ion channels. Experiments that followed showed that these proteins act as tiny molecular gates: light causes them to open, changing a cell's electrical activity. The first findings involving channelrhodopsin-1 appeared in Science in 2002, followed by research on channelrhodopsin-2 in PNAS in 2003. Neurons communicate through electrical signals involving the movement of charged particles, or ions. Channelrhodopsin combines a light sensor with an ion channel. When its gene is introduced into a neuron, light can effectively be used to switch that neuron on or influence its activity. Professor Nishith Gupta of BITS Pilani's Hyderabad campus explained why that was significant. "We could stimulate the brain long before optogenetics," he said. "What we lacked was the ability to choose a particular population of neurons and control its activity on the millisecond timescale at which the brain communicates." Dr Santhosh Sethuramanujam of IIT Madras said older approaches could affect multiple cell types across a brain region, whereas optogenetics allows more targeted control. "By simply shining light on brain tissue, scientists can switch targeted cells on or off with pinpoint, millisecond precision," he said. Optogenetics has since been used to study neural circuits and memory, including experiments in mice that linked specific neurons to learned fear responses. The technology has also entered early-stage human research. In a 2021 trial, a patient with retinitis pigmentosa received a gene carrying a channelrhodopsin called ChrimsonR. Special goggles then projected light onto the retina. With the goggles, the patient could perceive, locate, count and touch objects using the treated eye. Without them, the patient could not detect them. It was a partial recovery in one patient, not restoration of normal sight. "Blindness is furthest along because the retina is accessible both to gene delivery and to light," Gupta said. Despite the promise, optogenetics remains largely a research technology. Scientists still face challenges involving gene delivery, long-term safety, cell-specific targeting and the intensity of light required. "If I had to name the biggest barrier, it would be achieving safe, durable control of precisely the right cells in the human brain," Gupta said. Indian laboratories are also using optogenetics to study vision, glioblastoma and genetic diseases. For Kateriya, the journey has come full circle: from identifying light-sensitive genes in a microscopic alga as a PhD student to using related tools at JNU to study disease. "Peter taught me hours and hours, as a PhD student," he said. "That is very important."

headline: What happens to 'energy drinks' after Campa, PepsiCo get interim court relief against FSSAI label ban? | Explained
content: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of Indias (FSSAI) action against potentially misleading claims suffered a temporary setback on Tuesday after the Delhi High Court granted interim relief to Reliance Consumer Products in its dispute with the regulator over the use of the term energy drink on high-caffeine Campa beverages. With PepsiCo, Reliances Campa and Monster now receiving interim relief, questions remain about what happens to products already in stores, as well as stocks that were withdrawn or seized following FSSAIs direction. Can they continue to be sold or automatically return to shelves? On Tuesday, Reliance Consumer Products moved the Delhi High Court, seeking relief from the FSSAI order prohibiting the company from marketing products under its Campa brand as energy drinks. The court questioned the food safety regulator over its directive and asked why the company had not been issued a notice before the order was passed. Further, the court told FSSAI that it was never too late to correct its mistake. The court clarified that the temporary relief applies only to products already manufactured and does not permit the companies to produce new batches carrying the energy drink label. The stay will continue until the next hearing on 5 November. According to its petition, Reliance argued that state authorities had seized Campa stock and directed e-commerce platforms to delist the products. Both Reliance and PepsiCo informed the court that they would suffer huge losses due to FSSAIs order. Reliance Consumer Products told the Delhi High Court that its existing stock included 168 million cans and 120 million plastic bottles marked as energy drink. The company also had packaging carrying the same description ready for a further 400 million cans and 360 million bottles. PepsiCo said that 492 million bottles and 26 million cans bearing the disputed label were in circulation as of 31 July. In the present case, the Delhi High Court has allowed the companies to sell their existing stock carrying the disputed label. However, they cannot manufacture new batches bearing the description while the interim arrangement remains in force. Ashwin Bhadri, founder and CEO of Equinox Labs, explains that food packaging is planned months in advance, and by the time a dispute reaches the courts, products may already be sitting in warehouses, with distributors or on retail shelves. Businesses must then determine whether the stock should be held, recalled, reworked, relabelled or allowed to remain in circulation, with substantial costs potentially passing through the supply chain. The dispute between the beverage brands and the food safety regulator stemmed from a 30 June order in which FSSAI directed companies selling high-caffeine beverages to stop using energy drinks and related terms. Further, it gave the companies three months to revise their product labels and packaging accordingly. The disagreement centres on whether drinks containing high levels of caffeine may be promoted and labelled as energy drinks. headline: CEC appointment law row: SC to examine plea seeking recall of September split verdict
content: SC to examine plea seeking recall of September split verdict The Supreme Court on 7 October agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench, news agency PTI said. On September 23, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger Constitution bench. It had said due to a difference of opinion, the matter be placed before CJI Surya Kant on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication. On Wednesday, a bench comprising the Chief Justice of India and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. "We will examine and take a call," the CJI said. Sankaranarayanan told the bench that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, but the matter had subsequently been released from that bench and he was asked to mention it before the CJI. "There is a split verdict on the Chief Election Commissioner issue. We have mentioned an application for recall of the judgment," the senior advocate said. When the CJI asked whether there was any other interlocutory application (IA), Sankaranarayanan said that a curative petition had also been filed, but added that the recall application was a separate plea. "A curative petition has been filed. That, I think, will have to go in its own form. Whether it is maintainable, I don't know. Ours is an IA seeking recall of the judgment. Curative often requires a review," he said. The development comes after a two-judge bench of Justices Datta and Sharma delivered split opinions on September 23 on the Centre's plea seeking reference of the challenge to the 2023 law to a larger Constitution Bench. Justice Datta declined the Centre's request for such a reference, while Justice Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench. In view of the difference of opinion, the matter was placed before the Chief Justice for the constitution of an appropriate bench. The petitions had challenged the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which replaced the selection mechanism laid down by the Supreme Court in its March 2, 2023 judgment. In that judgment, a five-judge Constitution bench had directed that the CEC and ECs be appointed by the President on the advice of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 law, under which the selection committee comprises the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. The CJI is now not part of the statutory selection panel. (With PTI inputs) - The new law alters the established selection process for Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. - The Supreme Court's involvement raises questions about the laws constitutional validity and electoral governance. - Differences in judicial opinions highlight ongoing tensions in the judiciary regarding election oversight. headline: INDIA Bloc Huddle At Delhi Restaurant Amid High-Voltage CEC Protest, Police On Standby
content: Mallikarjun Kharge hosts an INDIA bloc lunch in Delhi a day after Rahul Gandhi-led protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the ECI. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday hosted a lunch meeting for INDIA bloc MPs at Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath in Delhi, a day after the Oppositions high-voltage protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission of India (ECI). The meeting comes amid heightened political tensions over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Oppositions allegations of vote chori". - Kharges Lunch Meet With INDIA Bloc MPs After Rahul Gandhi Sit-In Has A South Indian Twist - INDIA Bloc Protest: Opposition MPs To March From Makar Dwar To EC Headquarters Over Voter Rolls - Opposition Takes To Streets Against EC | INDIA Bloc March Targets CEC Gyanesh Kumar | - Gyanesh Kumar Is Scared: Rahul Gandhi Questions EC At Oppn Protest, Says 'Standing Here To Save Democracy' The INDIA bloc is expected to discuss its next course of action and ways to intensify its campaign demanding answers from the poll panel and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The lunch was scheduled for 1.30 pm at Sagar Ratna, Janpath. Several senior Opposition leaders gathered for the meeting, including Congress leaders and representatives of INDIA bloc allies. Security was heightened around the restaurant, with police cordoning off the area following Tuesdays confrontation between Opposition MPs and Delhi Police. Delhi Police On Standby As Opposition Meets The heightened security comes against the backdrop of continuing protests in central Delhi over the CEC and the SIR exercise. Delhi Police had already stepped up deployment in the New Delhi district, with barricades placed at several intersections and stretches leading towards Parliament and Jantar Mantar. Paramilitary and local police personnel were also deployed along protest routes. The police response remained a key feature of Tuesdays protest, with security arrangements being strengthened after Opposition MPs marched towards Nirvachan Sadan. The developments have prompted heightened vigilance around central Delhi, particularly locations connected with Opposition activity. Multiple reports mentioned that Delhi Police was on standby at the Janpath restaurant on Wednesday. What Happened During Tuesdays INDIA Bloc Protest On Tuesday, INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards Nirvachan Sadan, demanding action against the Election Commission and seeking the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over their concerns regarding the SIR of electoral rolls. The march was stopped by heavy police barricading. Rahul Gandhi was seen climbing a barricade as police attempted to halt the advancing protesters. Several Opposition MPs were detained, while Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress leaders later entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises and staged a sit-in. The sit-in continued for several hours. Delhi Police eventually removed the protesters and detained them, saying the action was necessary to maintain law and order. Police said around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained during the day. The Opposition, however, maintained that it wanted to meet the Election Commissioners and raise its concerns directly. Rahul Gandhi had said that around 300 Opposition MPs wanted to meet the poll panel and submit their concerns. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hosted a lunch meeting for INDIA bloc MPs at a Delhi restaurant to discuss their next course of action and how to intensify their campaign demanding answers from the poll panel and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Piyush Goyal courts US firms for investments across key sectors
content: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal held meetings with senior executives of leading US companies in New York this week to discuss strengthening India-US trade and investment ties and invite them to explore opportunities in India, the commerce ministry said on Wednesday. Goyal met Blackstone president and chief operating officer Jonathan Gray and chairman of Blackstones international private equity business Prakash Melwani to discuss expanding the company's investments and partnerships in India across key sectors. He met Neuberger Berman chairman and chief executive George Walker and senior members of its leadership team. The discussions covered opportunities to deepen investment linkages and strengthen engagement in financial and wealth management services, the ministry said. In a meeting with Este Lauder Companies president and CEO Stphane de La Faverie, Goyal discussed growth opportunities in India, including increased manufacturing and sourcing, as well as the country's growing beauty and personal care market. Goyal met IBM chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna, with discussions focusing on further strengthening IBM's engagement in the country and expanding collaboration in artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, quantum computing and other emerging technologies. In his meeting with MetLife president and CEO Michel A. Khalaf, discussions focused on the company's growth opportunities in the country and the expansion of the insurance and financial services sector. Goyal also met General Atlantic chairman and CEO William E. Ford to discuss opportunities to further deepen the company's investment and business engagement with India. Separately, Goyal met AIA Group non-executive chairman Mark Tucker. The discussions focused on AIA's engagement in India and opportunities in the insurance and financial services sectors, including in the context of India's vision of Insurance for All by 2047. The meetings provided an opportunity to discuss India's growth prospects and investment opportunities across financial services, manufacturing, energy, technology, artificial intelligence and other sectors, as well as ways to further strengthen India-US economic and commercial ties, the ministry said. Bilateral trade between India and the US rose to $140.77 billion in fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26) from $132.14 billion in FY25, according to data from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). Indias exports to the US edged up to $87.31 billion from $86.51 billion, while imports rose to $53.45 billion from $45.63 billion. As a result, Indias trade surplus with the US narrowed to $33.86 billion from $40.89 billion. headline: 3 years of October 7 attack: 'Never take the enemy lightly' — What went wrong for Israel? Expert weighs in
content: Israel on Wednesday marked three years since the Hamas-led October 7 attack, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. The assault, the deadliest attack in Israels history, exposed major gaps in the countrys intelligence assessment and security preparedness. It also triggered the war in Gaza, which has since killed more than 74,200 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry. People also gathered at the site of the Nova music festival in southern Israel, where hundreds were killed during the Hamas attack. Reports have pointed to prior intelligence warnings from other countries and other signals that Israel did not act on adequately, as well as a broader failure to assess Hamas intentions and capabilities. Prof. (Dr.) Khinvraj Jangid, Professor and Director of the Jindal Centre for Israel Studies, said the failure went beyond a single intelligence lapse. Jangid, who specialises in Israeli society and politics and the Israel-Palestine conflict, said one failure was at the intelligence level, where Israel did not adequately respond to signs of Hamas activity and preparations. There are two levels of failures here. There was one failure at the intelligence level, in a way where they did not take serious note of the movement of Hamas forces, Jangid told Livemint. But he argued that the intelligence failure was closely linked to a deeper problem: Israels assessment of the threat posed by Hamas. I think it came from this over-reliance on the assumption that Hamas cannot really hurt Israel more than shooting rockets, he said. For five, seven years before October 2023, whenever Hamas attacked Israel, it attacked by launching some rockets or balloons, fire balloons. I think this is the maximum Israelis anticipated. Jangid said this created a bit of lethargy and an overconfidence about what nature of the threat Hamas can really be capable of. Jangid said the second failure was political, arguing that Israels intense domestic crisis in 2023 distracted attention from the external security threat. The second thing is a bigger failure of political attention, he said. Israel, in the year 2023, was in a civil-war kind of situation. Israel was then engulfed in mass protests over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus judicial overhaul, with strikes and widespread disruption. Because of Netanyahus judicial reforms, the positions where he wanted to change the appointment of the judges, the whole country was on fire, Jangid said. There was a national strike, and the airport was shut. Jangid recalled that Israels then-defence minister had warned the government that the internal political crisis could have security consequences. We are so much in a civil war that our enemies will take benefit of us, that we need to really come out of this kind of domestic instability, he said, recalling the warning. I would say the failure is not only of intelligence. The failure is also because Israel was deeply caught in a civil-war kind of situation in the domestic setting. Jangid said the scale and nature of the October 7 assault represented a profound shock for Israel. Israel, in a way, survived, very brutally, a massive terror attack of the kind that, after the state of Israel was established, no civilians really witnessed such a massacre, he said. What happened on October 7th, actually for the next three days, was a very, very terrible massacre at a large level. Think of it, more than 21 communities were attacked. He described the assault as an unprecedented security shock for a country that has long placed intelligence, surveillance, and military preparedness at the heart of its national security strategy. Such a thing was extremely brutal for the state of Israel, Jangid said. Jews have seen such atrocities, but those were in the time of the Holocaust. The October 7 attack also transformed the conflict from a Hamas-Israel confrontation into a wider regional war, with Iran-backed groups opening additional fronts against Israel. After 7th of October, and I remember this, from 8th of October, Hezbollah from Lebanon started attacking Israel in the north, Jangid said. He said the attacks forced Israel to evacuate large numbers of residents from communities near the Lebanese border. More than 100,000 people of the north were evacuated, and they remained evacuated for the period of two years, all of 2024 and all of 2025, he said. Jangid argued that Irans role was central to the wider regional confrontation. I think Iran participated in this war from the 8th of October, by allowing and encouraging Hezbollah to attack Israel from the north, he said. The northern front added another layer to Israels post-October 7 security calculations, forcing it to confront not only Hamas in Gaza but also Hezbollah in Lebanon and the wider network of Iran-backed armed groups in the region. The Houthis in Yemen also launched missile and drone attacks towards Israel. Why Israel eventually turned its focus towards Iran According to Jangid, Israel increasingly concluded that confronting Irans regional network required addressing what it viewed as the source of that network. Thats why Israel, when it could really get its head out of the waters in the south of Israel, and in the north of Israel, it realised that in order to deter these proxies, it would have to attack the source of the proxies, which is the Islamic Revolutionary Guards in Tehran, he said. Iran is not a Ukraine, and Israel is not a Russia. I think Iran participated in this war very actively. The war upon Iran was, in a way, inevitable, because Israel really wanted to fix the problem for its national security once and for all. It doesnt matter that it has failed to do so. But the rationale, the logic of the war is absolutely in self-defence, as I understand it. For India, Jangid identified two broad lessons from Israels experience. The first, he said, is not to underestimate an adversary. Never take the enemy lightly, he said. Too much self-assurance and too much overconfidence can really bite back. Jangid argued that adversaries closely watch a countrys domestic situation and may seek to exploit periods of political or institutional weakness. Hamas attacked Israel in October of the year 2023 because Israel was completely absorbed, consumed in its domestic civil-war kind of situation, he said. If a country is internally unstable, if a country is internally going through a deep crisis, then thats the weakest a country can come to. I think one lesson is that our enemies take note of how we are doing domestically. Are we coherent? Are we nationally resilient? Are we united? Are we politically moving ahead? Or are we attacking each other and fighting over the fundamental issues, rather than working through our disagreements in a peaceful manner? October 7 also demonstrated the limits of technological superiority and intelligence capabilities, Jangid said. Having the best of the Mossad, having the best of the nuclear weapons, and having the best of the regional and American alliances doesnt save Israel from this kind of shaking. Its an irony, right? Its a country known for its intelligence. For Jangid, the central lesson is that no intelligence system can eliminate uncertainty or guarantee that an adversary will behave in accordance with established assumptions. All of this tells us also this thing that the notion of security is extremely slippery and confusing, he said. All of these things were, in a way, useless on the day Hamas really caught Israel by surprise.

headline: It Just Won't End: How A Google Map Glitch Is Adding To Traffic Woes On Barapullah Phase-III Flyover
content: While it was built to cut the travel time between East Delhi and Central Delhi, commuters are now facing hours of traffic congestion, with travel time exceeding an hour Delhis much-awaited Barapullah Phase-III flyover has turned into a headache for commuters since the day of its inauguration on September 29. The stretch is designed to connect Mayur Vihar to Sarai Kale Khan and ultimately to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). While it was built to cut the travel time between East Delhi and Central Delhi to around 20 minutes, commuters are now facing hours of traffic congestion, with travel time exceeding an hour. - Delhis Barapullah Faces Big Traffic Test: New Flyover, 3-Km Jam And 55-Minute Waits On Day 2 - Heavy Rain Brings Bengaluru Traffic To A Standstill, Commuters Share Videos: Mahadevapura Beach - Mumbai Traffic Alert: Overturned Dumper Blocks Magathane Flyover, Ghatkopar And JVLR Hit | Key Updates - Jantar Mantar Protest Today: 11 Metro Stations Shut, Traffic Restricted | Is Your Route Affected? According to the Delhi Traffic Police, the issue stems from a design flaw that results in two stretches of three lanes each merging into a single-lane road. Then A Google Maps Goof-Up At the heart of the concern lies a Google Maps goof-up, as a result of which traffic data on the newly opened Barapullah Phase-III stretch is not being reflected. With the traffic situation unclear on the Google Maps app, commuters continue to choose the route, contributing to the volume of vehicles on the stretch and adding to the traffic woes. While it remains unknown how long Google Maps will take to resolve the issue, a response given on Googles support forum states that search features and navigation for newly opened roads and routes can take around a week to stabilise. The Bigger Problem: Design Of The Route The design of the stretch creates a bigger trouble: the Phase-III flyover has three lanes. However, where it meets the existing Barapullah corridor, it meets another road consisting of three lanes. Both roads then narrow into a single lane, leading to a sudden traffic chaos. Adding insult to injury is another route of three lanes located just further ahead that brings traffic from the Ashram and DND side onto the stretch. The Delhi Traffic Police and Public Works Department (PWD) officials on October 1 addressed the issue, and a drone survey showed multiple traffic streams narrowing into a limited road width. The traffic police has asked the PWD to redesign the merger rather than counting on traffic diversions and curbs. The traffic congestion is caused by a design flaw where two stretches of three lanes merge into a single-lane road, compounded by a Google Maps glitch failing to show real-time traffic data.

headline: 'When An Army Allows Its Soldiers To Grow Beards': Ex-Singapore Envoy Takes Aim At Asim Munir
content: Kausikan argued that the original idea behind Pakistan - a homeland for Muslims in South Asia - was fundamentally altered after Bangladesh broke away in 1971. Former Singapore diplomat Bilahari Kausikan has launched another sharp critique of Pakistan, this time questioning the ideological direction of its military under Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and even asking what purpose Pakistan serves after the creation of Bangladesh. But once Bangladesh split off from it, that rationale disappeared. So what is Pakistan today? Except that it is not India," Kausikan said. His most pointed criticism, however, was reserved for Pakistans military, which he described as the institution that is keeping the country together, albeit precariously. Kausikan said the Pakistani military was once a largely secular institution but has undergone a significant ideological transformation. The only thing holding Pakistan precariously together is its military. But that military used to be a secular force. It is now a religious military. When an army allows its soldiers to grow beards, it is in trouble," he said. The remarks amount to a particularly direct assessment of the military leadership under Munir, who has emerged as the most powerful figure in Pakistans political and security establishment. Kausikans argument is that the institution that has traditionally been viewed as Pakistans principal source of stability is itself changing in ways that could deepen the countrys problems. He also questioned Pakistans attempts to retain strategic relevance through its ties with Saudi Arabia. Referring to the Mecca pact and Pakistans relationship with Riyadh, Kausikan said Islamabads efforts to position itself as a key security partner had not necessarily translated into influence. Former Singapore diplomat Bilahari Kausikan questioned the ideological direction of Pakistan's military under Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir. Kausikan argued that the original idea behind Pakistan was fundamentally altered after Bangladesh broke away in 1971. He described Pakistan's military as the institution precariously holding the country together, noting its ideological transformation from secular to religious. Kausikan questioned Pakistan's attempts to retain strategic relevance through its ties with Saudi Arabia, citing the Mecca pact. But it never quite falls over. It is trying to make itself relevant with the Mecca pact. But when Saudi Arabia was attacked by the Houthis, did they call on Pakistan? No!" he said. The latest remarks build on Kausikans earlier criticism of Pakistan in July this year, when he acknowledged that the countrys military had demonstrated considerable diplomatic agility but warned that foreign-policy successes could not solve its domestic problems. Diplomatic success doesnt feed people thats the hard reality," he said at the National Press Foundations International Reporting Fellowship, while discussing Pakistans improved diplomatic engagement with the US. Kausikan had also described Pakistan as a country teetering on the brink of failure" and argued that its fundamental problems were internal, including economic mismanagement and the failure to contain jihadist groups. Pakistans problems are not diplomatic; Pakistans problems are much more fundamental within Pakistan," he said. His earlier warning also carried a stark nuclear dimension. Kausikan said international concern over Pakistan was driven largely by the fact that it possesses nuclear weapons. If Pakistan did not have nuclear weapons, no one would care," he said. Bilahari Kausikan criticized Pakistan's military for undergoing an ideological transformation from a secular force to a religious military, noting that allowing soldiers to grow beards indicates the army is in trouble.

headline: Trump says he has call scheduled with Putin to discuss possible case of pneumonic plague in Russia
content: President Donald Trump on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Mr. Trump said he would be talking with Mr. Putin about the case very soon. Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause. Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Mr. Trump said the U.S. is in very deep discussions on the topic. Well be able to report about it, probably tomorrow, Mr. Trump said. The World Health Organization on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) said the case presents a very low risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. On Monday (October 5, 2026), Mr. Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation. Its a rough disease. You know, thats a disease we used to be able to control, but somehow those microbes have gotten stronger and smarter. Theyre like an army, Trump told reporters at the White House. The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18. Ukraine has given the administration and Congress a wish list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals it would like to see hit with U.S. sanctions under that law.

content: Some opposition leaders reportedly felt mistreated because Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi effectively took over the spotlight by staging the sit-in inside Akashvani Bhavan What began as a joint INDIA bloc protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday ended with an unexpected flashpoint within the opposition alliance. - 'MPs Disrespected': Rahul Gandhi Demands Meeting With CEC, To Continue Protest At Akashvani Bhavan - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - 2006 Corruption Case: What Led To Vigilance Probe Against CEC Kumar Ordered By Kerala Home Minister The Gandhi siblings move helped keep the Opposition protest alive for several hours after several INDIA bloc leaders had been detained and taken away in buses. ALSO READ | Rahul Gandhis SIR Dharna: Why AAP, DMK Skipped INDIA Blocs Sit-In Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar The episode has added to concerns among INDIA bloc parties about coordination within the opposition alliance, with some allies feeling that the Congress and the Gandhi siblings ended up taking centre stage in what was meant to be a joint protest. The INDIA bloc MPs had marched towards the Election Commission office in Delhi on Tuesday, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over their allegations of vote chori". As police detained opposition leaders and put them into buses, the protest appeared to be winding down. Rahul Gandhi, however, returned towards a bus parked near Akashvani Bhavan, where Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was seated. The two then walked past the police and entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises. The move caught not only the police but also several Congress leaders by surprise. ALSO READ | No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM: ECI Flags Unusual Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation had reported earlier that Congress leaders too were unaware of the siblings plans and noted that the initial idea was to get inside the Akashvani Bhavan premises and potentially use its rear exit, which is located towards the Election Commission side. With routes to the poll panel blocked, the diversion offered an unexpected way to keep the protest going. Once inside, the Gandhi siblings turned what had appeared to be the end of the opposition protest into another standoff with the police. Why Are INDIA Allies Unhappy? While the move gave the Congress protest renewed momentum, some INDIA bloc allies were reportedly unhappy with the manner in which it was carried out. The issue was not merely the decision to enter the premises. Some allies were also unhappy that the Congress had decided to seek a meeting with the Election Commission without consulting them. The Congress subsequently moved to contain the fallout. According to the report, Congress leader KC Venugopal conveyed to INDIA bloc parties that the party leadership had acted on the spur of the moment and expressed regret over the mistrust" caused by not keeping the allies in the loop. Not The First Coordination Problem The latest episode has also revived concerns among INDIA bloc partners about the Congress taking unilateral decisions during joint opposition programmes. The alliance parties have repeatedly attempted to project unity in their campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and Rahul Gandhis allegations of vote chori". Tuesdays protest saw participation from several opposition parties, including the Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress, RJD, CPI(M) and others. The BJD, which has maintained equidistance from the NDA and INDIA bloc, also sent two MPs to participate in the march. However, the DMK and AAP stayed away from the protest. The Gandhi siblings dramatic Akashvani move ultimately ensured that the protest continued for hours, with several opposition leaders later joining them inside the premises. But the episode has also exposed the continuing challenge before the INDIA bloc: maintaining a common political line while ensuring that individual partiesparticularly the Congress as the alliances largest opposition forcedo not appear to dictate the agenda. The Gandhi siblings' impromptu decision to enter Akashvani Bhavan caught allies by surprise and left some opposition leaders unhappy, as they felt mistreated and believed the Congress leadership took over the spotlight without prior consultation or coordination.

headline: Rubio, in Greece, set to call for the West to restore founding democratic principles and values
content: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to call for the nations of the West to return to their civilisational roots and restore the values that drove the rise of Europe and North America to global dominance for centuries. In Athens to discuss deepening economic, energy and security cooperation with Greece, Mr. Rubio will deliver a speech later on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) near the ruins of the Acropolis, a widely recognizable symbol of the city's ancient civilisation associated with the creation of popular participatory government and the social contract. The State Department, which is billing the speech as a major address on democracy and its future, says Mr. Rubio will call upon Americans and Europeans alike to join together in a great renewal of the Western spirit an inheritance stretching from Athens and Rome to Christendom to the founding of the American . Mr. Rubio is seen by many as the gentle face of the Trump administration and has been frequently dispatched to clarify or otherwise address concerns about the Presidents frequently undiplomatic statements. In some quarters, however, Mr. Rubios Athens speech may be seen as a follow-on to the blistering address Vice-President J.D. Vance gave at last years Munich Security Conference, in which he excoriated Europeans for allowing unchecked immigration and accused them of overreliance on America and inattention to their own security. Mr. Vance and Mr. Rubio are the leading contenders to assume Trumps mantle at the top of the Republican Party, which faces stiff challenges in next months congressional midterm elections. Mr. Rubio intends to remind listeners of qualities he says were born in Greece and later defined the West, such as curiosity, courage, ambition and a restless spirit of exploration and discovery of the unknown. He will warn that too much of our civilisation has forgotten these essential qualities, and urge our allies across the West to join the United States in rejecting decline, defending our shared heritage, and confronting a new era of great-power competition together, the department said. The Trump administration has repeatedly accused countries in Europe of backsliding on their traditional values and democratic principles by stifling the free speech of conservatives and falling short on commitments to international partners like the United States. Many of those countries have rejected the complaints and accused the U.S. under Mr. Trump of being guilty of similar behaviour and worse with its staunch anti-immigration stance that some believe is racist. Ahead of his visit to Athens, about 1,500 people gathered to protest Mr. Rubios presence and the war in Iran, chanting American killers! The demonstration was organised by a communist labour union and other left-wing groups and was held ahead of extensive road closures planned in Athens on Wednesday (October 7). Organisers said similar protests were held in at least 12 other Greek cities. Mr. Rubio is on the second leg of a three-nation tour of NATO allies that has already taken him to Iceland and will end in Portugal on Thursday (October 8). The trip is aimed at reassuring U.S. partners that the Trump administration is committed to their success and security despite what has been an often brusque and sometimes rude approach to traditional friends that has stirred unease. Mr. Rubio began emphasising historical themes on Thursday (October 8), when he met Iceland's foreign minister at the site of the landmark 1986 summit between former President Ronald Reagan and then Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, a meeting that many believe marked the beginning of the end of the Cold War and was a catalyst for the eventual dissolution of the Soviet Union. It remains unclear what impact Mr. Rubio's visits will have, although on Tuesday (October 6) in Reykjavik, he sought to reassure Iceland that President Donald Trumps administration has no designs on the island. Rather, he said the U.S. shares Iceland's deep concerns about Arctic security as tensions between the U.S. and Russia rise in the High North and elsewhere. Iceland has been uneasy about Mr. Trumps intentions toward it after he posted a map showing the colours of the U.S. flag sprawling across all of North America and extending to Iceland and Greenland. That wariness has persisted despite an agreement last month to increase the U.S. presence in the neighbouring Danish territory of Greenland that appears to have ended Mr. Trumps demands for the U.S. to take full control of the island. But after Mr. Rubios talks in Reykjavik, those tensions appeared to be on the wane. Mr. Rubio said the United States would not do anything in Iceland without Icelands consent. Before delivering his speech in Athens, Mr. Rubio will likely be asked about allegations of misconduct levelled at U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle. The top Democrats on the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs committees, Sen. Jeanne Shaheen and Rep. Gregory Meeks, have initiated probes into claims reported last month by the Wall Street Journal that Guilfoyle acted improperly while serving as the top U.S. envoy to Greece. The Journal reported that Guilfoyle told guests at a reception that the U.S. could undermine the Greek government if it chose to, promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company, and allowed its lobbyist into private diplomatic meetings. Mr. Guilfoyle, a former Fox News Channel host and California prosecutor who was once engaged to Mr. Trumps son Donald Jr., has denied any wrongdoing, and Mr. Rubio has defended her before. Mr. Guilfoyle, Mr. Rubio said after the Journal story appeared, has been an incredible advocate for the Presidents agenda in Greece and across Europe. He said he and Trump greatly value the ambassadors pivotal work and leadership, notably on energy issues. The Trump administration sees Greece as key to advancing the promotion and export of U.S.-produced liquefied natural gas to Southeastern and Central Europe.

headline: Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use
content: Delhi High Court refused a PIL seeking mandatory body cameras for Delhi Police and RAF during protests, saying there was no grey area on the issue. The Delhi High Court on Wednesday refused to entertain a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed during protests and crowd-control operations, and asked the Centre to consider the petition as a representation. A bench headed by Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre questioned the need for judicial intervention on the issue, saying there was no grey area" concerning the use of body cameras. - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - 'Absolutely Shocking': Kejriwal Hits Out At Delhi Police For Detaining AAP Leaders At Delhi Protest - Delhi's Rape Cases Have Dipped Since 2023, But Supreme Court Called Ground Reality 'A Systemic Failure': Heres Why - | Journalist Seeks FIR Against ACP Vivek Bhagat Over Alleged Misconduct | Gyanesh Kumar The court said the matter involved policing as a whole and not just the Delhi Police. Why should we direct them to legislate? It cannot be said that it is a grey area you want us to deal with. They have provided measures by incorporating a statutory provision, as and when the legislature had some intention. Why do you feel that it is necessary to have some judicial order?" the bench observed. The court further said, We are not concerned with Delhi police only, but we are concerned with entire policing." The observations came as a PIL seeking directions to make body-worn cameras mandatory for police and RAF personnel deployed for crowd-control duties and protests was submitted to the court. Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner, told the court that body cameras were already being used by police personnel, but their deployment appeared to be very haphazard". Delhi HC refused to entertain a PIL seeking mandatory body cameras for Delhi Police and RAF during protests. The Acting CJ Nitin Sambre-led bench said there was no grey area and asked why the court should direct authorities to legislate. The court asked the Centre to consider the petition as a representation. Sibal submitted that body cameras were essential during protests because allegations of violence often arise from such situations. According to his submission, protesters accuse police personnel of excesses, while police blame protesters for creating violence. The court asked Sibal whether the petition cited any instances of misuse of body cameras by police. Sibal replied that his concern was not misuse but the lack of consistent deployment of the cameras. He said wider use would benefit the entire process and stressed that the plea was not partisan in any way". Sibal also submitted that courts had intervened in matters relating to policing and investigation. He referred to provisions under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), under which searches and seizures are required to be recorded. The bench, however, asked Sibal to specify the provision under the new law that provides for such recording. The PIL was filed by Chahat Raghav seeking directions to make body-worn cameras mandatory for Delhi Police and RAF personnel deployed for crowd-control duties. The petition was moved in the wake of protests held at Jantar Mantar in July 2026, including demonstrations linked to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk. The petitioner claimed that incidents involving the use of force during the demonstrations were largely documented through mobile-phone recordings made by bystanders. The plea sought directions to authorities to frame appropriate rules, regulations or a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) requiring police and RAF personnel deployed for crowd-control duties to wear body cameras. It also sought a comprehensive mechanism for the storage, integrity, retention and evidentiary use of footage recorded through such cameras. According to the plea, such a framework would ensure that recordings could serve as an authenticated record of events during protests and other crowd-control operations. The petitioner argued that mandatory body cameras would help establish accountability and provide an objective record of interactions between law-enforcement personnel and protesters. The plea acknowledged that allegations of excessive use of force had been levelled against police personnel, while also pointing to allegations of attacks on police personnel and vandalism by some protesters. The petition specifically referred to the events of July 21, 2026, alleging the use of force by Delhi Police and RAF personnel during protests. It claimed that footage available in the public domain showed injuries to both police personnel and protesters. It further referred to a review meeting held on July 23, in which, according to the petition, the Inspector General of RAF acknowledged that certain force used during the deployment was not in accordance with prescribed standards. The petitioner also relied on a 2022 Delhi Police Standing Order concerning the regulation of rallies and processions. According to the plea, the order provides for recording of protest-related policing through third-party videography. The petitioner argued that while third-party videography could provide useful documentation, it had limitations, particularly in capturing events from the perspective of personnel directly involved in crowd-control operations. Body-worn cameras, the plea contended, would provide a more continuous and comprehensive record. Delhi Police Had Floated Tender For 1,500 Cameras The petition also pointed to steps already taken by the Delhi Police towards procuring body-worn cameras. According to the plea, Delhi Police had floated a tender through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for procurement of 1,500 body-worn cameras at an estimated total value of around Rs. 7.4 crore. This works out to approximately Rs. 49,333 per unit. The petitioner also relied on observations of the Supreme Court concerning the use of body-worn cameras and referred to provisions of the BNSS, 2023, relating to audio-video recording of search and seizure operations. The respondents in the petition include the Union of India, the Commissioner of Delhi Police, the Director General of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D). The plea ultimately sought a comprehensive framework governing the deployment and operation of body-worn cameras during protests and crowd-control situations, including provisions to ensure footage is securely preserved and remains available for appropriate scrutiny or evidentiary purposes. The petitioner contended that an authenticated audiovisual record could assist authorities, courts and other stakeholders in determining the sequence of events and examining competing allegations arising from protests. The Delhi High Court refused to entertain the PIL because it determined there was no "grey area" in the use of body cameras, noting that the issue involves policing as a whole rather than just the Delhi Police and that the legislature has already incorporated relevant statutory provisions.

headline: KP CM Opposes Pak Military Operations, Says Pashtuns Won't Shed Blood For 'America's Dollar Wars'
content: during PTIs long march, Sohail Afridi accused Pakistans military establishment of pursuing policies that have repeatedly cost Pashtun lives. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has stepped up his attack on Pakistans military establishment, accusing it of pursuing dollar wars" at the cost of Pashtun lives and warning that his government would resist any policy that leads to further bloodshed in the province. We were, are and will remain with Pakistan," Afridi said, while making it clear that his support did not extend to policies that, according to him, came at the cost of his people. He warned that Pashtuns would resist any such policy and said his government would stand up for the lives and rights of people in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Afridi has repeatedly opposed fresh military operations and drone strikes in the province, arguing that decisions concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cannot be taken behind closed doors without taking its people into confidence. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi accused Pakistans military establishment of pursuing dollar wars. Afridi Warns Of Resistance To Military Operations The KP chief minister also drew a red line over any future policy involving military action in the province, saying he would oppose measures that put Pashtun lives at risk. His remarks come amid a broader dispute between the PTI-led provincial government and the Centre over Pakistans counter-terrorism strategy.
