Afridi has maintained that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cannot simply accept decisions on military operations made elsewhere, and has sought a greater provincial say in policies affecting areas facing militant violence. PTI Long March Moves Through Khyber Pakhtunkhwa The remarks were made against the backdrop of the PTIs long march, being led by Afridi and aimed at building pressure over the continued imprisonment of Imran Khan. The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 before moving through Karak and Kohat. Afridis convoy subsequently headed towards Peshawar, with protesters scheduled to move through Charsadda before assembling at Khairabad, where the next phase of the protest is expected to be announced. The federal government has warned against attempts to force entry into Islamabad, while PTI has maintained that its protest will continue. KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi criticized the military establishment for pursuing what he termed "dollar wars" at the cost of Pashtun lives, warning that his government would resist policies leading to further bloodshed in the province.

headline: Highly educated professionals are vulnerable to financial cybercrime, finds IIT-Madras study
content: A study led by researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-Madras) has found that financial cybercrime victims in India are often highly educated professionals, challenging the perception that victims are primarily careless, financially unaware or greedy. The study found that high digital literacy does not necessarily protect individuals from cyber fraud. Victims included IT professionals, bankers, doctors, management and finance professionals, public-sector officers and individuals with cybersecurity certifications. Why growing trust in digital payments may be leaving Indians more exposed to cybercrime The researchers found that victims were often targeted during periods of stress or life disruption, including illness in the family, retirement, job searches, or workplace pressure. Fraudsters exploited fear, financial expectations, and reputational concerns to create an engineered brain freeze, with victims describing a state of mind arrest that impaired their ability to think clearly. Financial losses ranged from a few thousand rupees to more than 1 crore, while victims also reported shame, insomnia, depression, and damaged family trust. The study also found that institutional responses varied, with some banks and cybercrime cells responding quickly while others lacked the required technical capabilities and coordination. The study was led by retired IPS officer P. Kandaswamy and Nandan Sudarsanam, from IIT Madras in collaboration with Akanksha Jaiswal, Associate Professor, The University of Western Australia, Chennai Campus and Ameeta Fernando from Loyola Institute of Business Administration, Chennai. The research received support from the Wadhwani School of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at IIT Madras. The study sample comprised victims of financial cybercrime residing in various Indian cities including Chennai, Bengaluru. Hyderabad, New Delhi and Mumbai. The team contacted the cybercrime cells in these cities, sharing the studys purpose with police officers who, in turn, shared victims contact details and provided an initial brief to the victims about the research study. The final details included 11 females and 22 males, mostly married with dependents. Among them, 12 were senior citizens, including one visually impaired individual. Mr.Kandaswamy IPS (Retd), Adjunct Faculty, Department of Data Science and Artificial intelligence, Department of Management Studies, IIT Madras said, The response to cybercrime must move beyond blaming victims. Banks and law-enforcement agencies need stronger systems for early detection, rapid intervention, and coordinated response, along with better support for victims. Nandan Sudarsanam, Wadhwani School of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, IIT Madras, said, Our findings show that financial cybercrime is not simply a problem of inadequate digital literacy. Even highly educated and digitally experienced individuals can become vulnerable when fraudsters exploit fear, stress, and urgency. Understanding these factors is essential to designing more effective prevention strategies. Indias rapid digital transition near-universal mobile access, UPI, and the wider Digital India push has brought hundreds of millions of first-generation users into digital finance within a decade, opening an unusually wide attack surface for investment and stock-trading frauds, task and job scams, digital payment frauds, malware attacks, and the distinctly Indian digital arrest scam. While official statistics from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) record the transactional breach, they remain silent on the human trauma behind the numbers, prompting the research team to ask a human question rather than a technical one.

headline: South India pins hope on northeast monsoon for rainfall relief
content: After recording a 24.3% rainfall deficit during the JuneSeptember southwest monsoon, South Peninsular India is now banking on the northeast monsoon, or retreating monsoon, which typically sets in October. Southern states receive a significant share of their annual rainfall during OctoberDecember. Mint explains. How did the southwest monsoon perform? Indias southwest monsoon rainfall in 2026 was 87% of the long-period average (LPA), with cumulative rainfall of 759.4mm during June-September, making it the fourth-lowest since 2001 and 13th-lowest since 1901, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). South Peninsular IndiaAndhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telanganaexperienced a significant rainfall deficit during the season. With 542.0 mm of rainfall, 76% of the LPA, the region recorded its fourth-lowest monsoon rainfall since 1901 and second-lowest since 2001. In contrast, Central India received normal rainfall at 97% of LPA, while North-West India and North-East India recorded 94.1% and 74%, respectively.

headline: Manipur Seeks 30 Additional CAPF Companies As Anti-Militancy Operations Intensify | Exclusive
content: The request includes specialised CoBRA and RAF units as security agencies step up operations against militant groups across the state. The Manipur administration has sought additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), including specialised units such as the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) and the Rapid Action Force (RAF), as security operations against militant groups intensify across the state, according to sources. Sources said the state has sought 30 additional companies of CAPFs to strengthen security arrangements and sustain operations against militant groups involved in violence and other security-related activities. - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use - How Fight Over Seating Arrangement At Qawwali Event Left Sena Councillor, NCP Worker Dead, 10 Injured - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks The request for additional forces comes amid heightened security concerns in Manipur, where the administration is seeking to maintain a sustained security presence in vulnerable and sensitive areas. The additional deployment is expected to support counter-insurgency operations, area domination, protection of vulnerable locations and maintenance of law and order. The security situation in the state remains particularly sensitive following the prolonged ethnic conflict between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei communities, which has resulted in deaths, displacement and continuing tensions in several parts of Manipur. Emerging tensions between Naga and Kuki-Zo groups have added another layer of complexity to the security situation, particularly in the hill districts. Authorities are consequently keeping a close watch on areas considered vulnerable to further escalation of violence. The government has also recently notified a number of areas as sensitive from a security perspective, underlining the continuing challenges faced by the administration in maintaining peace and preventing further violence. The proposed deployment of additional CAPF personnel is expected to give security agencies greater operational capacity in these areas. Specialised forces such as CoBRA could be utilised for operations against armed groups in difficult terrain, while other CAPF units may be deployed for area security, protection duties and maintaining law and order. The request comes amid heightened security concerns in Manipur. The security situation is sensitive due to ethnic conflict between Kuki-Zo and Meitei communities. Emerging tensions between Naga and Kuki-Zo groups add complexity to the security situation. The administrations request for 30 additional companies comes as security agencies seek to step up coordinated operations against militant groups and prevent further incidents of violence in the state. headline: All 23 Indians aboard Liberian-flagged oil tanker rescued after attack off Russia's Black Sea coast
content: vessel carrying oil, with a crew of 23 Indian nationals, came under attack by drone boats off Russias Black Sea coast, Russian authorities said. The crew has been saved and evacuated to shore, a spokesman for the Russian Transport Ministry told the state-run TASS news agency. The Aframax Rio tanker came under attack on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) by unmanned surface vessels (USVs), and open fire is raging in the Black Sea waters, the Russian transport ministry said. The Ministry said the vessels all Indian crew of 23 was saved and none was hurt according to preliminary data. The incident took place near Sochi, Russias popular resort city on the Black Sea coast. Russias Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin held a headquarters meeting on eliminating the consequences of the attack on the tanker Aframax Rio off the Black Sea coast. According to the report, the fire was so intense that firefighting could not begin initially. Open burning of oil is currently taking place in the Black Sea area. Firefighting can begin only after the intensity decreases, when it becomes possible for rescue vessels to approach the tanker safely, the report said. As a precautionary measure, Sochi Mayor Andrey Proshunin temporarily banned access to the citys beaches. The citys emergency response centre has made a decision to temporarily ban access to the beaches and sea embankments. Sochi residents and guests are kindly requested not to expose to risks and wait for an official decision regarding their reopening, Mr. Proshunin wrote on his Telegram channel. The Black Sea is a critical global trade choke point facing severe disruption due to escalating attacks on commercial shipping and port infrastructure from the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. The attack comes two days after at least two people were killed and some crew members, including one Indian, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire on a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea. India said it viewed these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern. The targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world, the Ministry of External Affairs said. We continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. On Sunday (October 4, 2026), External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said India has moved beyond advocacy and stepped up its efforts in recent months to resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging in conversations with both Kyiv and Moscow.

headline: 'Election Commission Should Respond With Facts': Ex-CEC OP Rawat On SIR, Gyanesh Kumar Row
content: Asked about the demand for Kumars resignation, Rawat said he would not comment on a political demand. Former Chief Election Commissioner OP Rawat has weighed in on the escalating confrontation between the Election Commission of India (ECI) and Opposition parties over electoral roll revisions, saying the poll panel should answer allegations of large-scale voter deletions with facts and evidence. Rawats remarks come amid a fresh political flashpoint over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with the Opposition demanding his resignation and accusing the ECI of undermining the integrity of the electoral process. - Opposition Takes To Streets Against EC | INDIA Bloc March Targets CEC Gyanesh Kumar | - Kharges Lunch Meet With INDIA Bloc MPs After Rahul Gandhi Sit-In Has A South Indian Twist - INDIA Bloc Huddle At Delhi Restaurant Amid High-Voltage CEC Protest, Police On Standby - 'Fake News': Govt Denies Home Ministry Reaching Out To Rahul, Priyanka Over CEC Dharna Asked about the demand for Kumars resignation, Rawat said he would not comment on a political demand. I do not comment on political demands. Whether to resign or not is a personal decision," he said. His comments came a day after a major Opposition protest in Delhi. Opposition MPs, led by Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, sought to march towards the Election Commission headquarters and meet the poll panel. The delegation was stopped by police, with several leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, detained during the confrontation. The Opposition has maintained that it wants to present its concerns directly to the Commission. On the proposed delegation of 200-300 MPs seeking a meeting with the poll panel, Rawat said the ECI should meet them regardless of their numbers. The Election Commission will not go outside, but there is enough space at the Commission to meet all the MPs," he said. At the heart of the dispute is the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have alleged that more than 13 crore names were deleted from draft electoral rolls across states and Union Territories, raising concerns over eligible voters being disenfranchised. Former Chief Election Commissioner OP Rawat commented on the escalating confrontation between the ECI and Opposition parties. Opposition MPs, led by Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, sought to march towards the Election Commission headquarters. More than 13 crore names were allegedly deleted from draft electoral rolls across states and Union Territories. The ECI recently ordered a special drive in 20 states and Union Territories to identify and enrol genuine voters. Rawat said the ECI should directly address the allegation. The Election Commission should respond to such allegations with facts," he said, stressing that the poll panel must provide a fact-based clarification on the reported deletion of more than 13 crore voters. The issue has gained further traction after the ECI recently ordered a special drive in 20 states and Union Territories where SIR has been completed to identify and enrol genuine voters who may have been left out. The Commission has also directed officials to compare pre-SIR and post-SIR rolls and identify voters who may have been wrongly excluded. The ECI, however, has maintained that the revision exercise is aimed at cleaning electoral rolls and identifying ineligible entries, while the Opposition has questioned the transparency and implementation of the process. The dispute centers on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with Opposition parties alleging that over 13 crore names were deleted from draft lists across states and Union Territories. While the Opposition has questioned the transparency of the exercise, the ECI maintains that the revision aims to clean the electoral rolls and identify ineligible entries.

headline: Blood-tainted ice cubes and a famine in Madras
content: the sweltering heat of colonial Madras, British rulers and the citys elite raised glasses of Scotch whisky, chilled by ice cubes floating in their drinks. The huge blocks of ice were naturally formed in the lakes of New England in the U.S. and imported to India. In Madras (now Chennai), the ice bars were brought to the Ice House in Triplicane, where they were stored and cut into smaller pieces for evening drinks.

headline: Sand mining scam in Tamil Nadu: ED's 2024 communication to DGP challenged before Madras High Court
content: EDs 2024 communication to DGP challenged before Madras High Court The Madras High Court on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) ordered notices to Tamil Nadu government and Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption (DVAC) on a writ petition filed by the partner of a private construction company challenging the Directorate of Enforcements (ED) 2024 communication regarding an alleged 4,730-crore sand mining scam during the erstwhile DMK regime. First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan, however, refused to grant an interim stay of all further proceedings pursuant to the EDs 2024 communication to the then Director General of Police/Head of Police Force or prevent the DVAC, which had now begun a detailed inquiry on the basis of the communication, from taking coercive action against the petitioner. A. Rajkumar, partner of R.S. Constructions based at Nanganallur in Chennai, had filed the petition urging the court to quash the EDs communication sent to the DGP/HoPF on June 13, 2024 and consequently forbear the DVAC from registering either a First Information Report (FIR) or taking any coercive action against the petitioner on the basis of the two-year-old communication. Senior counsel AL. Somayaji, representing the petitioner, told the Division Bench that the ED had initiated proceedings against a host of individuals before 2024 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 solely on the basis of some unconnected FIRs registered by the State police regarding sand mining and in the absence of any substantial predicate offence for suspecting money laundering. The High Court had quashed all the proceedings initiated by the ED and also set aside provisional attachment of several properties by the central agency. The Supreme Court too had refused to entertain an appeal filed by the ED challenging the High Courts order. Those court orders were passed after taking into consideration the 2024 communication of the ED to the then DGP/HoPF, the senior counsel said. However, now, it appeared the DVAC was planning to act on the basis of the 2024 communication and hence the petitioner had approached the court with a plea to quash that communication. State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan told the court the DVAC manual provides for two types of inquiries a preliminary inquiry and a detailed inquiry into the complaints received by it. ED had shared the information, available with it regarding the alleged sand mining scam, with the DGP/HoPF in compliance of the statutory obligation imposed upon it under Section 66(2) of the PMLA which mandates the central agency to share such information with the other law enforcing agencies. Hence, the DVAC had now begun a detailed inquiry on the basis of the EDs dossier, the SPP said. Justice Murugan wondered how could the petitioner urge the court to quash a communication sent by a central agency in compliance of its statutory obligation. The Bench, nevertheless, decided to order notice to the State government, DVAC and ED on the petition but refused to pass any kind of interim order in favour of the petitioner.

headline: Supreme Court To Examine Plea To Recall Split Verdict On Law Governing Appointment Of CEC, ECs
content: The Supreme Court will examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict on the 2023 law governing CEC and EC appointments. The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench, news agency PTI reported. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was informed about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. - INDIA Bloc To Jointly Move Supreme Court Over Legal Protection To CEC Gyanesh Kumar Under 2023 Law - Why Has No Chief Election Commissioner Ever Been Impeached In India & What Does It Actually Take To Remove CEC? - 'Let's Be Very Clear': Supreme Court Says It Didn't Approve Modified Form 6, Asks Who Made Changes - Supreme Court To Hear Pleas Seeking Suspension Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Challenging EC Decisions Responding to the plea, the CJI said, We will examine and take a call." The development comes after a two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered separate opinions on September 23 on the issue of whether the challenges to the 2023 law should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench. Recall Plea In Split Verdict Case According to PTI, Sankaranarayanan told the CJI-led bench that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta. However, the matter was subsequently released from that bench, and the counsel was asked to mention it before the CJI. Supreme Court agrees to examine a recall plea against the September 23 split verdict on the CEC-EC appointment law. Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma differed on whether challenges to the 2023 law should go to a larger Constitution Bench. The 2023 law excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. There is a split verdict on the Chief Election Commissioner issue. We have mentioned an application for recall of the judgment," the senior advocate told the bench. When the CJI asked whether there was any other interlocutory application (IA), Sankaranarayanan said a curative petition had also been filed. He, however, clarified that the recall application was a separate plea. A curative petition has been filed. That, I think, will have to go in its own form. Whether it is maintainable, I dont know. Ours is an IA seeking recall of the judgment. Curative often requires a review," he said. September 23 Split Verdict The recall plea relates to the split opinion delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on the Centres plea seeking reference of the challenges to the 2023 law to a larger Constitution Bench. The batch of pleas challenges the validity of the 2023 law governing the appointment of the CEC and ECs. A key issue in the challenge is the exclusion of the Chief Justice of India from the panel for selecting the CEC and Election Commissioners. The two judges differed on whether the matter should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench. Justice Datta declined the Centres request for such a reference, while Justice Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench. Following the difference of opinion, the two-judge bench had said that the matter should be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength. The bench said this was necessary for an effective and authoritative adjudication" of the issue. The latest development before the CJI-led bench therefore comes against the backdrop of that split verdict. The recall application seeks recall of the September 23 judgment, while a separate curative petition has also been filed, according to the submission made by Sankaranarayanan. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan informed a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant about a recall application regarding the September 23 split verdict delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. In response to the filing, CJI Surya Kant stated that the court would examine the matter and take a call.

headline: Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Cyprus keen to join: 'Multiple routes' key for IMEC amid Hormuz crisis, says French envoy
content: Multiple routes key for IMEC amid Hormuz crisis, says French envoy Mestrallet, in India from 5-7 October to advance the IMEC project and France-India cooperation on connectivity, said that multiple routes are key for IMEC as disruptions and risks are affecting existing trade links, reinforcing the importance of developing alternative connectivity options linking India, the Middle East and Europe. We have eight signatories, and they are heads of state. Any potential extension will only be decided by the eight governments. We hope that in the ministerial meeting we could decide to extend the perimeter of IMEC, Mestrallet said at the press conference hosted by the French Embassy at ITC Maurya in New Delhi. Mestrallet said an IMEC ministerial meeting is expected to be held by the end of this year, where the eight existing signatories could consider expanding the corridors membership and geographical scope. IMEC is now considered a network of complementary routes in order to be more resilient. If on one particular route there is a blockage, an accident, a technical problem or even a local crisis, the other routes will be available, Mestrallet said. Mestrallet named Egypt, Lebanon and Oman among countries interested in working with or joining IMEC. He also identified Greece and Cyprus as European countries that could be particularly interested in becoming full members. Any formal expansion would require a decision by the eight existing signatories, he said. Mestrallet also clarified the position of Jordan and Israel, saying both countries were mentioned in the original agreement but did not sign it. They have not signed because they were not present. Its Jordan and Israel, although they were mentioned, he said. IMEC was announced in September 2023 during the G20 summit by India, the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, France, Germany, Italy and the European Union. The corridor envisages connecting India with Europe through the Middle East using shipping, rail and other connectivity infrastructure. Mestrallet said that since its creation, IMEC discussions have taken place at the steering committee level, but there has not yet been a ministerial-level meeting. We hope that by the end of this year there will be a ministerial meeting because in the meantime, since the creation of IMEC, there was only a steering committee, not a ministerial committee, he said. He emphasized that the ministerial meeting could therefore provide an opportunity for the participating governments to consider expanding the corridor. Mestrallet said IMEC would need to work with countries and ports outside the existing group, regardless of whether they eventually become full members. In any case, members or not members, we will have to work with them because they want to work positively, and so we have to work with them to find the best possible method being a full member, an associated member or something else, he said. Mestrallet said the geopolitical crises in the Middle East have increased the need for a resilient connectivity corridor. The difficulties 7 October, Gaza, Iran, Hormuz have even increased the necessity to have a resilient corridor, offering several possibilities to the market, Mestrallet said at the event. He said the disruptions and risks affecting existing trade routes have reinforced the importance of developing alternative connectivity options linking India, the Middle East and Europe.

headline: Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission
content: The FIR comes a day after Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders were detained from Akashvani Bhavan during their protest against the Election Commission. Delhi Police on Wednesday registered an FIR in connection with Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with other INDIA bloc MPs and leaders, entering the Akashvani Bhavan premises without permission during an Opposition protest a day earlier. The FIR comes after Delhi Police detained around 260 protesters, including 10 MPs, on Tuesday as Opposition leaders protested against the Election Commission of India (ECI). - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody? - DMK U-Turn On Rahul Gandhi? Party Backs Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 'Right To Fight' - Form 6 Row: Rahul Gandhi Says Gyanesh Kumar Will Be Held Accountable | - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police What Happened At Akashvani Bhavan? According to Delhi Police, INDIA bloc leaders had planned a march from Parliament House towards Nirvachan Sadan, the headquarters of the Election Commission. Police said no official permission had been sought or granted for the proposed march. After the protesters were stopped near the Election Commission office, several Opposition leaders and MPs staged a sit-in. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra subsequently entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises along with other leaders and continued their protest there, police said. According to the police, the protesters were asked to vacate the premises but refused to comply, insisting that they would not leave until a delegation of MPs was allowed to meet Election Commission officials. Delhi Police registered an FIR against Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for entering Akashvani Bhavan without permission. Around 260 protesters, including 10 MPs, were detained by Delhi Police during the protest. The protest was organized over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were removed from Akashvani Bhavan and detained after refusing to vacate the premises. The FIR triggered a political face-off between INDIA bloc leaders and the BJP. Delhi Police said it eventually intervened to maintain law and order and prevent the situation from escalating. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other protesters were removed from the premises and detained. Around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained during the days protest. They were taken to New Police Lines, Kingsway Camp, and subsequently released. Why Were INDIA Bloc Leaders Protesting? The Opposition protest was organised over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police had said on Tuesday that Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders were detained from the Akashvani Bhavan premises to maintain law and order" and prevent the situation from deteriorating. According to a police statement, the action was taken after Gandhi refused to vacate" the premises, stating that they would not move until a delegation of MPs was granted time to meet officials of the Election Commission of India." Opposition Defends Rahul Gandhi The FIR triggered a political face-off, with INDIA bloc leaders defending Rahul Gandhi and accusing the Centre of adopting dictatorial" measures, while the BJP accused the Congress leader of trying to create anarchy" and targeting constitutional institutions. Congress MP Imran Masood rejected the allegation that Gandhi had forcibly entered the premises, maintaining that he was accompanied by other parliamentarians. Rahul Gandhi is the LoP and was accompanied by MPs. He did not enter anywhere forcibly We will fight till the very end. We will not back down just because of an FIR," Masood told ANI. Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Manoj Pandey also backed Gandhi and accused the Centre of being intimidated by the Oppositions mobilisation. What can you expect from a dictatorial government? Dictatorial people are in power today. The Leader of the Opposition, a leader who is on the streets for public issues. He has the ability to fight, the courage to fight," Pandey said. Today, the central government is scared. Whatever is being seen is an extreme, and the end of the extreme is certain," he added. BJP Hits Back At Congress The BJP, meanwhile, accused the Congress leadership of creating hurdles in the countrys development and questioned the Oppositions agitation. BJP MLC Parinay Fuke said, Rahul Gandhi is carrying out these protests to defame the country, and I do not see any substance in his issues. At a time when India is rapidly developing, advancing on multiple fronts, expanding industrialisation and attracting large-scale foreign investment, I believe such efforts create hurdles to the countrys progress" BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan accused Gandhi of targeting constitutional institutions and compared him to a spoilsport". Rahul Gandhi is similar to an unstable spoilsport who flips the game board when they are losing, and Rahul Gandhi has now become a democracy wrecker unleashing anarchy and chaos because Rahul Gandhi has failed and is unable to win elections democratically," Kesavan said. Rahul Gandhi is engaging in dubious drama, trying to play the victim card by vilifying our constitutional institutions Rahul Gandhi, instead of behaving like a responsible leader of the Opposition, is engaging in misconduct that resembles anti-national forces and anti-national elements" he added. Delhi Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other INDIA bloc leaders for entering the Akashvani Bhavan premises without permission during an opposition protest.

content: The prime minister said the pessimism was not limited to economic indicators and that India needed to regain confidence in itself Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday recalled the economic challenges he said India was facing when he began his journey in government, saying there was widespread pessimism about the country and its prospects. People around the world would say our economy is a gone case," PM Modi said, adding that growth was not stable, inflation was through the roof". - 'We Will Do It': PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country - 'Those Who Opposed Me Showed Me Power Of Democracy': PM Modi Reflects On 25-Year Journey - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey The prime minister said the pessimism was not limited to economic indicators and that India needed to regain confidence in itself. The country that was drowned in negativity needed a new belief," he said. Then I did what I know," Modi added. ALSO READ | We Will Do It: PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service The remarks came as PM Modi marked 25 years in government. He took oath as the chief minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, beginning a quarter-century journey that would later take him to the Prime Ministers Office. When I took oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I never thought that I would ever reach this milestone," PM Modi said. Reflecting on the journey, Modi credited the people of the country for his continued stint in public life. Today, I have completed 25 years of continuous service. This is the result of the peoples constant blessings and support," he said. I express my gratitude to all the people of the country," Modi said, adding that he bowed before the people of the country. He also thanked all the parties that are part of the National Democratic Alliance. Those Who Brought Me Down Taught Me How To Rise Again PM Modi also reflected on the role played by his political opponents and setbacks in shaping his journey, saying that difficult experiences had taught him important lessons. Those who brought me down taught me how to rise again," he said. Those who opposed me showed me the power of democracy," Modi added. He said that, in retrospect, none of his experiences had been wasted. Nothing that happened in my life went to waste; every experience taught me something," he said. PM Modi marked 25 years in continuous public service on Wednesday, commemorating his journey that began when he took the oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001.

headline: Chemical leak at dyeing unit leaves 50 people with breathing difficulties in Salem
content: More than 50 people, including workers and residents, reportedly suffered eye irritation and breathing difficulties following a chemical leak at a dyeing unit in Gugai, in Salem on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) night. The unit, owned by Mr. Badrinathan, is located on Muniyappan Kovil Street in Ward 47 of the Salem Corporation. More than 10 workers were engaged in dyeing textile yarn at the unit. According to the police, the workers were mixing hydrochloric acid, which is used in the dyeing process, when they noticed a leak in the dyeing room. The workers reportedly rushed out of the unit after experiencing breathing difficulties. As the unit is located in a residential area, people in nearby houses were also affected by the fumes. They complained of eye irritation and shortness of breath and alerted the Fire and Rescue Services. A team from the Shevapet Fire and Rescue Services station reached the spot and entered the dyeing room. The firefighters sprayed water and took steps to contain the leak. The situation was brought under control in less than 30 minutes. The Shevapet police also visited the spot and conducted an inquiry. Residents alleged that chemical leaks from the unit had occurred on earlier occasions, causing discomfort to people living nearby. The police are investigating whether the unit has the required permissions from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board and how the hydrochloric acid leaked from the dyeing room.

headline: What is the economic mileage of a free ride?
content: Vettri Payanam, which alone is expected to cost an additional 1,600 crore a year and a total of 6,000 crore for free travel, has brought to focus social return on investment (SROI) versus fiscal cost. Actor-turned-Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay seems to have mastered the art of welfare politics by accommodating the gratis within an about 4 lakh crore revenue-spending framework. However, the real test is whether the government can convert 84 lakh daily journeys into measurable gains in female employment, productivity, household income and mobility. Going by Tamil Nadus Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), estimated at 40.67 lakh crore for 2026-27, it is large enough to afford Vetri payanam in a narrow accounting sense. Nevertheless, the States outstanding liabilities are projected at about 27% of GSDP in 2026-27. Besides, debt servicing is about 1.28 lakh crore or 37% of the states estimated revenue receipts. The latest initiative, launched on Gandhi Jayanti Day, is an extension of the existing womens zero-fare bus scheme, Vidiyal Payanam, covering a much wider range of government buses. The scale is substantial, as 12,692 buses, about 69% of the 18,413 scheduled buses operated by the eight state transport undertakings, have been brought under Vettri Payanam. Of the 1.95 lakh scheduled single trips, around 1.65 lakh, or 85%, will operate under the scheme. The government expects approximately 84.32 lakh women to benefit every day. Cost to exchequer The annual allocation for the free travel scheme, including Vetri Payanam, is reportedly estimated to cost around 6,000 crore annually. Before expansion, the annual allocation was about 4,400 crore, implying an additional burden of approximately 1,600 crore a year. Tamil Nadus 2025-26 Budget allocated up to 3,600 crore as a subsidy for Vidiyal Payanam (launched by the previous DMK regime), along with 1,782 crore for concessional student fares and 1,857 crore for diesel subsidies. The expanded Vettri Payanam scheme accounts for only 1.7% of revenue receipts and 0.15% of GSDP in isolation, but the States budgeted 55,775-crore revenue deficit indicates that current revenues are insufficient to meet current expenditure. Citing studies that found economic rationale in such populist schemes, at 6,000 crore a year, the State is effectively betting that cheaper mobility will produce higher female labour participation, higher household disposable income, better access to education and healthcare and stronger use of public transport. Converting mobility into employment is one of the biggest advantages. If transportation costs are a hindrance to women accepting jobs, particularly in urban and industrial clusters, free travel can expand the geographical radius of the employment market. It has the potential to become a complementary policy to skilling, industrialisation and womens employment initiatives. Its economic impact will be much larger and wider if the government connects bus routes with industrial estates, IT parks, textile clusters, markets and educational institutions. It could also ensure a public transport multiplier as higher occupancy on the existing services translates as low marginal cost of carrying an additional passenger, provided capacity is available. The environmental benefit, however, depends on whether buses actually replace private-vehicle trips rather than merely generate additional trips. Rising concerns The recurring burden on the State budget, which may appear to be small in terms of GSDP, is not targeted, which means part of the subsidy goes to those who may not need financial assistance. The higher the ridership, the larger the reimbursement needs will be. In order to ensure sustainability, the State should have a clear formula linking reimbursement to actual passenger journeys and route costs. Otherwise, it may put pressure on transport funding if reimbursement does not fully compensate TN State Transport Undertakings (STUs), which already have weak finances and incur daily average losses of 19 crore. On an all-India basis, too, the picture is the same as they cannot run like conventional commercial bus companies because of their public-service mandate. Apprehensions are that the scheme will create market distortion, crowding out private bus operators, who are already up in arms. A writ petition has been filed in the Madras High Court challenging the constitutional validity of the scheme. Economics behind A Tamil Nadu State Planning Commission study found that women in Madurai, Tiruppur and Nagapattinam were able to save an average of 888 a month through free bus travel. For those earning less than 12,000 a month, these savings represented a meaningful proportion of monthly income; farm and construction workers, street vendors and domestic workers were reported to save 14% of their monthly income. The State 2025 Assembly documents say the scheme has facilitated more than 571 crore journeys, with female daily ridership rising from about 32 lakh in 2021 to 57 lakh. It also cites the Planning Commissions findings that the scheme improved womens workforce participation. An independent 2024 study by the Citizen Consumer and Civic Action Group (CAG), which surveyed 3,000 women across six Tamil Nadu cities, similarly found monthly savings of 601-800. It reported that women frequently redirected the savings towards family health and education. As per the existing arrangement, the State compensates transport undertakings for zero-fare journeys. CAG reported that the government reimbursed MTC at 16 per zero-value ticket, implying that the revenue loss is effectively shifted from the transport corporation to the State Budget. Several States have already adopted or are in the process of allowing free or highly subsidised bus travel for women. Karnatakas Shakti scheme, launched in 2023, is a large, universal scheme with the State initially budgeting 4,000 crore annually. Research by Azim Premji University covering January 2023-March 2025 found a substantial increase in bus usage following implementation. Telanganas Mahalakshmi scheme, which began in December 2023, offers free travel to women, girls and transgender persons on specified TGSRTC services. Womens share of its bus passengers has risen from 40% to more than 67%, with more than 35 lakh women travelling free every day. Punjab introduced its free bus travel scheme in 2021. More than 3 lakh women use it daily, and nearly 11 crore women's journeys were recorded in FY23-24. However, PRTC reported a severe cash crunch, seeking 151 crore in pending reimbursements, as the free-travel scheme was costing it around 30 crore a month. Delhis women-free-travel scheme has generated enormous usage. DTC data showed 8.25 crore free journeys between April and July 2026 alone. In August 2025, Andhra Pradesh launched Stree Shakti, providing free travel to women, girls and transgenders in the State on specified APSRTC services. Kerala and Himachal Pradesh have had women-focused free travel/fare concessions, but their scale and design differ. A yearly 6,000-crore commitment is not a one-off theatric; rather, the State government has to transparently quantify the benefits of an unstinted subsidy to show mobility efficiency, labour market efficiency, income generation efficiency, cost-benefit ratio and long-term sustainability (at the end of the current term of TVK). The ultimate fare for its success is measurable SROI, not the electoral mileage.

headline: Mumbai CEO flags India airport entry hassles, sparks debate over immigration, customs: 'Forget tourism'
content: Monk Entertainment CEO Viraj Sheth has criticised the airport arrival experience in India, citing multiple forms, immigration and customs queues and what he described as a frustrating process for passengers entering the country. Sheth made the comments in a post on X after arriving in India. The post, published on October 6, has received 286,000 views and triggered a debate among users, with some agreeing with his concerns while others said India's airport entry process has become more streamlined. Just landed in India. the second you enter, it just feels like they want to make it as difficult as possible for its citizens to enter. arrival form, self declaration form, ebola form, never ending immigration and customs lines, frustrated people. forget tourism, makes a regular citizen want to think twice to enter. Several users responding to Sheth's post disputed the suggestion that India's immigration and customs procedures necessarily result in long delays. One user wrote, I travel at least once a year to India. Never ever had a problem. In New Delhi they have so many immigration counters. Never experienced more than 10 minutes delay. In New Delhi, since 1990s unless you have something to declare, you just pass thru the Customs from green channel. There are no lines at all. Now you can fill up the immigration online form 36 hours before you land in India. Another user pointed to the availability of digital options and smart gates, writing, Self declaration forms are in every country .rest all can be done online . Smart gates are in place . Nothing will be served u on plate dear u have to make effort to get convenience. The responses highlight a broader split over the arrival experience: while some passengers view documentation and checks as routine border procedures, others argue that queues and the number of steps involved can make the process cumbersome. Some users also raised concerns about what happens after passengers clear immigration and customs. One user wrote, All that is still tolerable but scammers just outside the arrival posing as taxi drivers are the real nuisance. No sense of behaviour or hygiene, with only goal to loot people and oggle at women. Disgusting people, Another commenter described the experience of returning to India as stressful, writing, Our tension start the day we think about coming to India. They treat us like we have done some crim leaving India. India is our home and they ask 100 questions why we are here today?! What the hell! We feel so good after leaving India from our vacation. The comments point to concerns that extend beyond formal immigration procedures, including interactions with people offering transport services and the experience passengers encounter immediately after exiting the airport. Not all responses were critical. One user said India's immigration process compared favourably with those in other countries, writing, I found Indian immigration to be a lot better than other countries except for customs dept at airport who would like to scan too many bags again wasting too

headline: The China-U.S. rapprochement
content: U.S. rapprochement The world, understandably, has been watching carefully the unfolding summitry between the United States and Chinese Presidents over the last several months. It had been a long time between drinks: just under a decade in the case of President Donald Trumps last visit to Beijing in late 2017; and just over a decade since President Xi Jinping stood on the White House lawns in 2015 with President Barack Obama. Editorial | Superpower summit: On the Trump visit to China Whereas now it is four summits in little more than six months: Beijing, Washington, Shenzhen and then Miami. Now it is everything, everywhere, all at once, with some speculating that we are seeing the birth of a new G-2. More a new phase It is natural for the world to wonder what, if anything, has fundamentally changed in the strategic architecture of the U.S.-China relationship. It is always hard to parse the difference between the language and theatre of politics and diplomacy, and what is actually happening on the ground. Despite the pomp and circumstance in both the Beijing and Washington summits, the reality is that nothing much has changed in the fundamentals of the relationship. Whatever public language might be used, the U.S. and China remain fully engaged in an all-pervasive strategic competition on which of them will emerge as the dominant Indo-Pacific and then global power for the 21st century militarily, in the economy, technology, foreign policy as well as the underlying ideological contest between democratic capitalism and Chinas alternative authoritarian model. Whatever the diplomatic surround sound might be, core decision-makers in both Washington and Beijing continue to have a deeply realist view of this ongoing strategic contest or what the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)has long called the struggle for the future of the international order. Strategic competition is not going away. The real question is whether that competition can be managed within the framework of some mutually acceptable rules of the road. Or whether it is left unmanaged with a rolling risk of crisis, conflict or even war. What the U.S. and China appear to be doing is moving towards an imperfect form of bilateral management mechanism. This process began in May last year with the regularisation of the political channel between U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng. This followed the imposition of trade-destroying tariffs of 125% in April 2025 by Mr. Trump, which were then promptly matched by 125% from Mr. Xi. To preserve their respective national economic interests, both sides then walked back from the brink of a full trade war. Since then, Mr. Bessent, Mr. He and their teams have now met eight times on average every two months. And after a tumultuous decade across every dimension of the relationship, the Bessent-He channel has indeed had a stabilising effect. Beijings push for stability China in particular has sought stability as it moves into 2027. Later next year, the CCP convenes the 21st Party Congress when Mr. Xi will be appointed to a record fourth term as General Secretary and where he hopes to appoint a fresh phalanx of personal loyalists to the partys most senior positions. While Mr. Xis authority remains unchallenged, he will want as benign a domestic economic environment as possible. Chinas dilemma is that the domestic drivers of economic growth are performing poorly. Private domestic consumption is in the doldrums. Private residential construction is into its sixth year of recession. Private fixed capital investment is also flat-lining. That leaves public investment (i.e., Chinas gargantuan techno-industrial strategy) and net exports as the two primary pistons driving the Chinese growth engine. The last thing Beijing wants is for the U.S. to resume a full-scale trade war which Mr. Trump is perfectly capable of doing. Just look at what he did in 2018 and in 2025. China therefore has been doubling down on its stability narrative with the U.S. Its new concept of constructive strategic stability is about maximising cooperation, managing competition within defined bounds, while also managing strategic differences, which is code language for Taiwan. In Chinas conceptual universe, if these three pillars are properly attended to, then the cardinal objective is achieved: stability. It is an elegant schemata. It is Chinas effort at managed strategic competition with the U.S. Moreover, the U.S. has formally accepted this framework in official readouts from the Beijing Washington Summits. But the U.S. has added the explicit caveat that any such bilateral framework be both fair and reciprocal. For Washington realists, that is enough to drive a bus through any constructive strategic stability narrative on any day of the week. Furthermore, Beijing would be wildly optimistic if it concluded that Donald Trump is likely to be constrained in his future freedom of manoeuvre because of some grand, overarching foreign policy narrative. The President just does not operate that way. A fragile truce What concerns China most is if what is called the Busan Tariff Truce agreed to last October falls apart. That original 12-month truce has only been extended two months. If the U.S. concludes that China has not been helpful on U.S. agricultural exports, or in the normalisation of the critical minerals and rare earths trade with the U.S., there is a real risk that the Busan Truce collapses. And if the European Union were to move in the same direction on tariffs given the crisis in European manufacturing, the consequences for an export-dependent Chinese economy would be large. For all these reasons, both tactical and strategic, the U.S.-China relationship remains deeply fragile. Even if the Busan Truce extends beyond December, the effective general U.S. tariff rate against China will remain much, much higher than, for example, Indias. Beyond trade, there also remains a formidable array of export controls on critical technologies, including world-class chips where China remains several years behind the U.S. And that leaves to one side a bilateral foreign investment regime which remains deeply restrictive at both ends of the relationship. Therefore, breathless reporting about an emerging G2 between the U.S. and China in some sort of global strategic condominium is fanciful. Whatever tactical accommodations may occur in the trade relationship, the fundamental nature of the strategic competition between Washington and Beijing continues. Remember it was Donald Trump, on the very eve of Mr. Xis state visit to Washington DC, who stated, Whoever wins in AI, wins. That is Xi Jinpings view too. That does not exactly sound like an emerging G-2 to me. Kevin Rudd is Global President and CEO of Asia Society, New York, and the 26th Prime Minister of Australia

headline: 'World Is Talking About Indian Pilot, One Day It'll Talk About Made In India Planes': PM Modi
content: PM Modi referred to Captain Smit Machchhars bravery while speaking about Indias journey towards self-reliance as he completed 25 years in service. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday linked the global recognition earned by Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar after the Flydubai cockpit attack to a larger ambition for India a day when the world will not just talk about Indian pilots, but also about aircraft made in India. Today the entire world is talking about the Indian pilot. There will be a day when the entire world will talk about the Made in India planes," PM Modi said, referring to Machchhars bravery while speaking about Indias journey towards self-reliance as he completed 25 years in service. - Providing All Possible Help: PM Modi Speaks To Flydubai Pilot Smit Machchhars Family, Applauds His Bravery - 'Was Reciting Hanuman Chalisa': Pilot Smit Machchhar Speaks To 'Biggest Idol' PM Modi On Flydubai Attack - Captain Smit Tells PM Modi How Hanuman Chalisa Gave Him Strength During Flydubai Cockpit Fight - Smit Machchhars Wife Sonal On His Recovery, PM Modis Call And Flydubai Cockpit Attack | Full Interview We Will Do It: PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service The remarks came days after Captain Machchhar, the commander of Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was seriously injured after being attacked by his co-pilot inside the cockpit on September 30. The aircraft, carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabias Tabuk. Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchhar managed to get the cockpit door open, allowing passengers to intervene and helping prevent what could have been a catastrophic crash. PM Modi had earlier called Machchhar a hero and said his courage and quick thinking had prevented a potential tragedy on the scale of 9/11. His bravery and presence of mind have saved hundreds of lives," Modi had said. During his subsequent conversation with Machchhar from his hospital bed, Modi again praised the pilot, telling him that Indians are not those who take lives, but those who are willing to risk their own lives to save others." He also said Machchhar had enhanced the prestige of the Indian pilot community. The pilot told PM Modi that his 17 years of flying experience, including 11 years as a captain, helped him understand the gravity of the situation and react immediately. Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot on Flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30. The aircraft, carrying 174 passengers, made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. PM Modi linked Captain Machchhar's recognition to India's ambition for 'Made in India' aircraft. India has a significant step in military aviation through the Tata-Airbus C295 programme. A final assembly line for the C295 aircraft was inaugurated in Vadodara in 2024. PM Modis Made in India plane" remark also fits into a broader push to build an indigenous aerospace manufacturing ecosystem. India has already taken a significant step in military aviation through the Tata-Airbus C295 programme. A final assembly line was inaugurated in Vadodara in 2024, becoming the countrys first private-sector aircraft final assembly facility. Of the 56 C295 aircraft ordered for the Indian Air Force, 40 are to be manufactured and assembled in India, with deliveries planned through 2031. The programme goes beyond assembly: more than 13,000 parts are to be manufactured in India, with Indian suppliers forming part of the aircrafts production ecosystem. Airbus says the first C295 to be made in India is scheduled to roll out from Vadodara in September 2026. For PM Modi, therefore, Machchhars story represents one side of Indias aviation ambition: Indian talent earning global admiration. The next challenge is to ensure the machines they fly can carry the same Made in India" stamp. Captain Smit Machchhar commanded Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30, where he was seriously injured after being attacked by his co-pilot. Despite his severe injuries, he managed to open the cockpit door, enabling passenger intervention and preventing a catastrophic crash during an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
