headline: 23 Indians rescued after Ukrainian drone strike sets oil tanker ablaze off Russia's Black Sea | What we know
content: many as 23 Indian crew members were rescued after a Ukrainian drone attack targeted an oil tanker off Russias southern coast on Tuesday evening, putting the sailors at risk, Russias Transport Ministry said, according to AFP. The ministry said the tanker was attacked by naval drones and that crude oil was burning in the waters of the Black Sea. Firefighters will make another attempt to bring the blaze under control once the fire's intensity decreases. The incident took place near Sochi, the Russian resort city on the Black Sea coast with a population of nearly 500,000, according to AFP. Videos and images circulating on social media showed bright orange flames burning at sea, with a thick column of black smoke rising near the coastline. The tanker attack came a day after another commercial vessel caught fire and sank off the Romanian coast in the Black Sea, leaving two foreign nationals dead. Several crew members were injured, including three Indians, according to AFP. The vessel, MV Royad Mammadov, was involved in an incident off the Romanian coast. Romanian authorities rescued the injured crew members and provided them with medical treatment. The incident has added to growing concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in and around the Black Sea amid the Russia-Ukraine war. Russia and Ukraine have increasingly targeted infrastructure linked to commercial shipping and energy since the conflict began in 2022. Russia has, in recent days, struck grain vessels carrying Ukrainian goods near Romania, a member of the European Union. Meanwhile, Ukraine has defended its attacks on Russian oil infrastructure as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian towns and cities. Both sides have signalled an escalation in attacks in recent weeks. Russia has also intensified strikes on Kyiv, including attacks on key bridges and daytime drone strikes in the capital, disrupting traffic and daily life. Previous Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities have caused oil spills, beach closures and other environmental damage, as per reports. India has expressed concern over continued threats to commercial shipping and called for dialogue and diplomacy to end ongoing conflicts. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that Romanian authorities had rescued the injured crew members from the recent incidents and that they were receiving medical treatment, as per ANI. India also thanked Bucharest for its swift assistance, according to the news agency. Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra visited the three injured Indian nationals undergoing treatment at Constana County Hospital and assured them of continued assistance, the Indian Embassy in Romania said. The MEA also highlighted Indias role in co-launching the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers at the United Nations. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar had previously raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels during his address to the UN General Assembly.

headline: CEC Gyanesh Kumar and 2006 Keralam bribery case: What happened then, why is probe being reopened – Explained
content: led government in Keralam directed the states Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to reopen a 2006 probe into an alleged bribery claim against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), Gyanesh Kumar. The case is about the death by suicide of Malaysian civil engineer Lee See Been, who was associated with the PATI-BEL consortium involved in the upgradation of road construction project under the Kerala State Transport Project (KSTR). The development came as Opposition leaders, including Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, demanded the CECs resignation over allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Quick answers to key questions 1What is the CEC Gyanesh Kumar bribery case from 2006 about? The CEC Gyanesh Kumar bribery case from 2006 involves allegations against Kumar related to a Malaysian engineer's suicide and claimed corrupt practices regarding a World Bank-aided road construction project. 2Why has the Kerala government decided to reopen the 2006 bribery investigation? The Kerala government has reopened the investigation in response to renewed public pressure and opposition demands for accountability surrounding Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of irregularities in electoral processes. 3How did Malaysian engineer Lee See Been's suicide relate to Gyanesh Kumar's case? Lee See Been's suicide is linked to Gyanesh Kumar's case through a suicide note that allegedly accused PWD officials, including Kumar, of soliciting bribes for clearing payment bills related to a construction project. 4What actions were taken by the Kerala government following Lee's suicide? Following Lee's suicide, the Kerala government removed Gyanesh Kumar from his position and initiated a probe through the Vigilance Bureau, which later did not progress until recently. 5Should Gyanesh Kumar resign amid the allegations against him? The question of Gyanesh Kumar's resignation is contentious, with opposition leaders advocating for his ouster due to ongoing allegations, while Kumar has not publicly resigned. Delhi police on Tuesday night temporarily detained Rahul Gandhi in the national capital to end an almost nine-hour standoff during a protest seeking Kumars resignation. Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were escorted by the police toward a bus from Akashvani Bhawan premises, after they were barred by hundreds of officers from marching to the election office earlier in the day. The Congress leaders were later released at night. In 2006, Kumar, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre, served as Secretary of the state Public Works Department (PWD). During his tenure, a bribery claim had emerged after a suicide note of a Malaysian engineer, who was part of a World Bank-aided Road work project executed by a Malaysian and Indian joint venture called PATI-BEL. The Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) has been a flagship project of the state PWD. At a cost of 1,600 crore, the project aimed to renovate select major roads totalling 1,600 km under the PWD with a World Bank loan. The Keralam-based Bhageeratha Engineering and Malaysian firm PATI joined hands for the bidding. The joint venture took up works worth 216 crore, mainly involving the modernisation of the main central road from the state capital of Thiruvananthapuram in the south to Angamaly in Central part of the state. The project would build the states first road designed with novel surfacing techniques. PATI-BEL began work on the project in December 2002 after entering into a final agreement with the then Congress-led government. In October 2006, the contractor informed the government that they could not complete the work within the original deadline, citing the delay in land acquisition. As construction costs escalated, PATI-BEL demanded a 30% increase in the contract amount. The finance department, led by Thomas Isaac under the CPI(M) government, refused the demand and sought the World Banks permission to re-tender the work. Lee See Been, 54, was the chief project manager of the works executed by PATI-BEL. In 2006, the company submitted bills worth 18 crore for payment. According to Legislative Assembly documents from 2007, PATI-BEL officials visited the ministers several times to seek payment. As the chief project manager, Lee was reportedly under pressure from subcontractors and construction material vendors seeking payment. As the work got delayed, the Congress-led Opposition also put pressure on the CPI(M) government. It was the former alliance that had awarded the work to the venture. On 11 November, 2006, Lee, who had by then returned to Malaysia, died by suicide in Kuala Lumpur. He reportedly left a suicide note addressed to the company director and his wife, alleging that PWD officials had sought bribes for clearing the bills. Reports suggested that the suicide note had included the name of the then PWD secretary, Gyanesh Kumar. The suicide note was never made public. A month after Lees death in 2006, the then CPI(M) government removed Kumar from his post. A probe by the Vigilance Bureau to examine the allegations was also ordered. The government cancelled the contract with PATI-BEL because the work could not be completed by the deadline. Subsequently, the government re-tendered the work. In March 2010, then Keralam Home Minister Kodiyeri Balakrishnan, a CPI(M) leader, informed the Legislative Assembly that two Vigilance probes concerning the KSTP were ongoing. However, the probe did not proceed. Kumar, who was removed as the PWD secretary in December 2006, was not given any fresh posting in the state, according to a report in . He then went on central deputation to New Delhi, when the Congress-led UPA government was in power. In 2007, the CPI(M) government in Keralam cancelled the contract with PATI-BEL. A year later, the government agreed to renew the contract with PATI-BEL itself. PATI-BEL took over the project again after the government allotted an additional 72 crore, in addition to the original 216 crore. Congress veteran and Keralams Opposition leader Oommen Chandy had then demanded Finance Minister Thomas Isaac clarify the circumstances of the renewal, given that Isaac had demanded blacklisting of PATI-BEL when the work

headline: AI appears to have been used in bank hacks: South Korean President Lee
content: South Korean President Lee South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks and called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era. In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used, causing considerable public concern and anxiety, Lee said during a cabinet meeting. Please establish the circumstances swiftly and clearly, and concentrate personnel and resources on minimising the damage. South Koreas police have launched a full-scale investigation into the hacking attacks against commercial banks that led to a breach of customers personal information, the Yonhap news agency reported on Tuesday. Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, the Financial Services Commission (FSC) said on Friday, while Yonhap reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank also suffered breaches. Authorities have not yet disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used in the hacking incidents or the full scale of the breaches. On Sunday, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance. Financial watchdog the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Financial Security Institute shared data about 28 unique IP addresses and some country information linked to the recent hacking attempts with the financial sector, the FSS said on Tuesday. In September, Australia said an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files, in what could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. An artificial intelligence research firm said last week that AI agents tried to hack into a Canadian government website, casting the effort as a failed hacking attempt, while Canada said there were no indications its systems were compromised.

headline: 'Those Who Opposed Me Showed Me Power Of Democracy': PM Modi Reflects On 25-Year Journey
content: PM Modi also sought to frame his 25-year milestone as something larger than a personal achievement, saying his political journey has been driven by a sense of purpose Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who completed 25 years in government on Wednesday, looked back at a political journey that began with his swearing-in as Gujarat chief minister on October 7, 2001, and said that even those who opposed him and tried to bring him down ended up teaching him important lessons. Those who brought me down taught me how to rise again," PM Modi said, reflecting on the experiences that shaped his 25-year journey in public life. - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey - 'We Will Do It': PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service - 'Our Economy Was A Gone Case': PM Modi Recalls India's Challenges As He Marks 25 Years In Govt He also said those who opposed him helped him understand the strength of Indias democratic system. Those who opposed me showed me the power of democracy." ALSO READ | We Will Do It: PM Modi Reaffirms Viksit Bharat 2047 Resolve As He Marks 25 Years In Public Service Modi, who became Gujarat chief minister in 2001 and went on to become prime minister in 2014, said he had never imagined reaching the milestone when he first took oath in Gujarat. When I took oath as the chief minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I never thought that I would ever reach this milestone," he said. Marking 25 years of continuous service, PM Modi credited the people of the country for his journey. Today, I have completed 25 years of continuous service. This is the result of the peoples constant blessings and support," he said. I express my gratitude to all the people of the country," Modi said, adding that he bowed before the people of India. He also thanked the parties that are part of the National Democratic Alliance. I want to thank all the NDA parties," Modi said. Nothing That Happened In My Life Went To Waste Looking back at the setbacks and challenges he encountered during his political career, Modi said every experience had something to teach him. Nothing that happened in my life went to waste; every experience taught me something," he said. His remarks came as he reflected on a journey that has taken him from the Gujarat government to the Centre and through three consecutive terms as prime minister. PM Modi also sought to frame his 25-year milestone as something larger than a personal achievement, saying his political journey has been driven by a sense of purpose rather than personal ambition. If I had wanted to shine in electoral politics, I could have entered the political arena much earlier," he said. I am a person to live for mission, not ambition," Modi said. My Duty Is My Dharma Modi also invoked the idea of duty and action while reflecting on his years in public life. My focus is always on karma," he said. My duty is my dharma," he added, saying his karma was for the country and its people. He also went on to say that his 25-year milestone is not personal". The milestone marks 25 years since Modi first took charge as head of a government in Gujarat. He served as Gujarat chief minister until 2014, when he moved to national politics after leading the BJP to a majority in the Lok Sabha elections. He was sworn in as prime minister on May 26, 2014, and has since completed two full terms and is currently serving his third term. PM Modi first took oath as the Gujarat chief minister on October 7, 2001, marking the beginning of his 25-year journey in government service.

headline: New GRAP Rules in Delhi; restrictions in NCR Oct 2026: These 8 states; older buses to be impacted - Imp for commuters
content: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has tightened Delhi-NCR's Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), bringing some restrictions into force at an earlier stage and removing exemptions for certain vehicles. Among the key changes, restrictions on inter-city and inter-state buses below BS-VI, CNG or electric vehicles, as well as diesel generator sets, will now apply from Stage I of GRAP, instead of Stage II. The revised framework also changes rules for commercial vehicles carrying essential goods and expands public advisories under the citizen charters issued for each GRAP stage, reported. The latest changes mark the fifth modification to GRAP since 2022, with a greater focus on vehicular emissions and dust-control measures. Under the earlier GRAP framework, restrictions on certain inter-state buses entering Delhi came into effect at Stage II. The revised rules bring these restrictions forward to Stage I and expand their geographical coverage. During Stage I, inter-city and inter-state buses from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and the adjoining states of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir will not be allowed to ply in Delhi-NCR if they are not electric, CNG or BS-VI diesel vehicles. The revised rule also removes the earlier exclusion for buses and tempo travellers operating under an All India Tourist Permit. For commuters travelling into Delhi-NCR from neighbouring states, this could affect the availability of older buses once Stage I GRAP restrictions are imposed. Restrictions on diesel generator sets have also been moved from Stage II to Stage I of GRAP. The change brings generator use under the initial stage of the pollution-control framework, reflecting CAQM's tighter approach to sources of emissions during periods of deteriorating air quality, the TOI reported. The revised GRAP removes an earlier exemption for certain BS-IV goods vehicles carrying essential commodities during the more stringent stages. Following a Supreme Court order, BS-IV goods vehicles carrying essential commodities will no longer receive the earlier exemption under Stages III and IV. This includes light goods vehicles and medium goods vehicles under Stage III and trucks or high goods vehicles under Stage IV. The revised framework also specifically addresses restrictions during Stage III on diesel-operated BS-IV and below-standard light and medium goods vehicles registered outside Delhi entering the capital. CAQM has expanded the geographical scope of restrictions on certain older passenger vehicles. SD Attri, member technical, CAQM, said restrictions under Stage III on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard light motor vehicles have now been extended to Sonipat. The restrictions already applied to Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar. This means vehicle owners and commuters in the affected areas will need to keep track of the GRAP stage in force before travelling during periods of severe pollution. The revised framework introduces a limited relaxation under Stage III. While construction and demolition activities remain restricted, pothole repair work will be allowed. The change distinguishes essential road maintenance from broader construction and demolition activity during the more stringent pollution-control stage. CAQM is also moving towards greater public visibility of pollution levels at construction and demolition sites. SD Attri told TOI that construction and demolition sites measuring more than 500 square metres will be required to display PM10 and PM2.5 levels. Attri said, "We have decided to make it mandatory for construction and demolition sites measuring over 500 square metres to display PM10 and PM2.5 levels. Currently, only the state pollution control board can check these levels, but we want the public to be able to see the concentrations as well. We will issue an order soon to implement this." CAQM has also amended its 2021 directions concerning the monitoring of dust-control measures at construction and demolition sites across NCR. The revised GRAP contains 48 action points, covering measures to be implemented across the different stages of the pollution-control plan. CAQM has also expanded the citizen charters associated with each GRAP stage. These charters provide public-facing guidance on the measures and precautions applicable during different levels of air pollution. For commuters, transport operators and businesses in Delhi-NCR, the key change is that several restrictions that previously came into effect at later GRAP stages will now be triggered earlier. The revised rules therefore make it important for residents and businesses to track the GRAP stage declared by authorities, particularly during the winter

headline: Your gender dictates your path to work: men use two-wheelers, women walk or take a bus
content: wheelers, women walk or take a bus A working woman in India is more likely to walk to her workplace in rural areas and take a bus or other public transport in urban areas. A working man, meanwhile, relies heavily on two-wheelers in both rural and urban areas. These are the findings of the recently released National Household Travel Survey by the statistics ministry, covering 492,000 households and 1.8 million individuals. The first-ever nationally-representative survey reveals how gendered commute to workplace can be in India. Mint explores the data in detail.

headline: JUI-F Chief Backs PTI Long March, Says Force No Answer To Pakistan's Political Crisis | Exclusive
content: also called for talks between the government and opposition, saying broader political consultation was needed to find a way forward. Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has called for dialogue between Pakistans government and opposition, arguing that political and security challenges cannot be resolved through force or military-style measures. Rehman made the remarks after meeting a delegation of Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz Ainey-e-Pakistan at his residence. The delegation included Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former National Assembly Speaker Asad Qaiser. - 'As Directed By Patnaik': BJD Joins Opposition Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over SIR, Voter Deletions - Opinion | Why Oppn's Manufactured Outrage Over Electoral Rolls Is A Threat To Democracy - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - Insulting Institutions Won't Strengthen Democracy: Kiren Rijiju Hits Out At Rahul Gandhi Over CEC Protest The opposition leaders also invited Rehman to participate in an All Parties Conference (APC) as efforts continue to bring opposition parties onto a common platform. PTI Has A Right To Protest, Says Fazlur Rehman Rehman backed the PTIs right to hold its long march, saying peaceful political activity should not be obstructed by the government. A long march is a democratic right and PTI should be allowed to exercise that right," he said. When political parties announce that they will remain peaceful, they should be trusted," Rehman added. His remarks come amid heightened tensions between the government and opposition, with the PTIs protest campaign adding to an already strained political environment. Calls For Dialogue, Political Moderation Rehman said Pakistans political situation was suffering from an imbalance and called for broader consultations among political parties to move the country towards political moderation. We were not a part of the negotiations, but in principle, we do not oppose the process of dialogue," he said. The JUI-F chief has opposed a force-based approach to political and security problems, arguing that military operations and excessive use of force cannot provide a lasting solution to the countrys crises. He has also called for the release of political prisoners and criticised political intolerance and pressure on opposition parties, while stressing the need for equal political rights. Rehman rejected the idea that any one political force could claim exclusive ownership of patriotism and called for political disputes to be settled through talks and consensus. Behind-The-Scenes Forces And Negotiations Rehman also addressed the role of forces operating outside the formal political process, saying their involvement in negotiations could be crucial to reaching a settlement. He observed that if forces operating behind the scenes became part of the negotiations, it would be possible to reach a conclusion through dialogue. The JUI-F chief has maintained that political parties should be able to determine the countrys political course without allowing confrontation among the government, opposition and state institutions to deepen. Invited To All Parties Conference Rehman confirmed that he had been invited to the proposed APC but said the JUI-F would consult internally before deciding its position. We have told the opposition to consider this matter in detail, while we will also consult our party. A joint agenda should emerge through consultation among all political parties at the APC," he said. The proposed conference is aimed at developing a broader opposition approach as Pakistan grapples with political confrontation, economic pressures and continuing security challenges. JUI-F Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman backed the PTI's right to hold its long march, stating that peaceful political activity is a democratic right and should not be obstructed by the government. He emphasized that when political parties announce they will remain peaceful, they should be trusted.

headline: Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modi's Political Journey
content: first 25 years were about building political power, from Gandhinagar to Delhi. The next phase is being framed around what that power can deliver by 2047 On October 7, 2001, Narendra Modi took oath as the chief minister of Gujarat. Twenty-five years later, on October 7, 2026, he completes an uninterrupted quarter-century as head of an elected governmentfirst in Gandhinagar and then in New Delhi. The number 25 itself is therefore the starting point, but it does not tell the entire story. - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country - PM Modis 25-Year Political Journey: Gujarat To The Prime Ministers Office | BJP | - PM Modi News Live Updates: PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says Peoples Blessings Made It Possible - PM Modi Completes 25 Years Of Public Service As Head Of Government, Wishes Pour In Over these years, PM Modi has gone from a relatively new state-level leader to Indias longest-serving head of an elected government. He has won three successive Lok Sabha elections, overseen the expansion of schemes ranging from Jan Dhan to Jal Jeevan Mission, and pushed a political-economic agenda built around digitalisation, infrastructure, manufacturing and a more assertive global role for India. PM Modis Political Career: A 25-Year Journey By The Numbers 1. 25 Years: The Journey From Gujarat To Delhi Modis 25-year run began on October 7, 2001, when he became Gujarats chief minister. He remained in the post until May 2014, before becoming prime minister on May 26 that year. The Union Cabinet, in a resolution passed on October 6, 2026, described October 7 as the completion of 25 years of continuous leadership" as head of government. 2. 8,931 Days: Indias Longest-Serving Head Of An Elected Government In March 2026, PM Modi crossed 8,930 days, the cumulative tenure previously held by former Sikkim chief minister Pawan Kumar Chamling. The 8,931-day figure combines his years as Gujarat chief minister and prime minister, making Modi the longest-serving head of an elected government in India. 3. 4,399 Days: His Record As Prime Minister On June 10, 2026, PM Modi became Indias longest-serving elected prime minister in continuous tenure, crossing Jawaharlal Nehrus record of 4,398 days. The figure refers specifically to his uninterrupted tenure as prime minister since May 26, 2014. 4. 13 Years: Gujarat Before Delhi Before becoming prime minister, PM Modi spent more than 13 years as Gujarat chief minister. He took over in October 2001 and remained chief minister until May 2014, winning successive assembly elections during that period. His Gujarat years also became the political foundation for the Gujarat model" that became central to his 2014 national campaign. 5. Three Successive Lok Sabha Victories PM Modi has led the BJP/NDA to power at the Centre after the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections. But the three victories have not been identical. In 2014, the BJP won 282 seats on its own; in 2019, that rose to 303. In 2024, the BJP fell to 240 seats, meaning the third Modi government depended on NDA allies for a majority. 6. 282: The 2014 BJP Breakthrough The BJP won 282 Lok Sabha seats in 2014, giving PM Modi the first BJP single-party majority at the Centre since the partys formation. It was the election that transformed Modi from a powerful state leader into a national political force. 7. 303: The 2019 High Point Five years later, the BJP improved its tally to 303 seats. The result gave PM Modi a larger standalone mandate than in 2014 and made the 2019 election the high-water mark of BJP parliamentary strength under his leadership. 8. 240: The 2024 Reset The BJP won 240 seats in 2024, 63 fewer than its 2019 tally and below the 272 seats required for a simple majority in the Lok Sabha. Modi nevertheless returned as prime minister for a third consecutive term, heading an NDA government. The change is significant because it marks the first Modi government at the Centre in which coalition partners became numerically essential to the governments majority. 9. 59 Crore: Jan Dhans Financial-Inclusion Footprint One of the defining early initiatives of the Modi government was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. By August 2026, more than 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts had been opened. Government data shows that about 56 per cent of the accounts belonged to women and 78 per cent were in rural and semi-urban areas. Jan Dhan also became a key part of the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile architecture through which subsidies and other benefits could be transferred directly to bank accounts. 10. Rs. 53.26 Lakh Crore: The Scale Of Direct Benefit Transfers Digital welfare delivery has become one of the most visible changes in the architecture of the Indian state. Cumulative Direct Benefit Transfers had reached Rs. 53.26 lakh crore by September 2026, according to a government release. DBT is designed to transfer benefits directly into beneficiaries bank accounts, reducing intermediaries in welfare delivery. 11. 24,509 Million: UPIs August 2026 Transactions The clearest example of Indias digital transformation may be UPI. UPI recorded 24,509 million transactions, about 2,450.9 crore, in August 2026 alone, according to government data. What began as a digital-payment system has become a defining part of everyday commerce, from street vendors and small shops to large retailers and online businesses. 12. 1.65 Crore: GST Taxpayers The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was one of the biggest structural tax reforms of the Modi era, coming into effect on July 1, 2017. The number of GST taxpayers increased from 66.5 lakh in 2017 to 1.65 crore in May 2026, according to the finance ministry. The government presents the increase as evidence of a wider formal tax base, although taxpayer growth also reflects changes in the economy, compliance systems and registration requirements. 13. 15.89 Crore: Rural Homes With Tap-Water Connections When the Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019, only 3.23 crore, or 16.71 per cent, of rural households were reported to have tap-water connections. By July 18, 2026, the government reported that the number had risen to 15.89 crore households, or 82.09 per cent of rural households. The government itself notes that drinking water is a state subject and that implementation involves both the Centre and states. 14. More Than 4 Crore: Houses Under The Housing Push Housing has been another major component of the Modi governments welfare pitch. The Union Cabinets October 2026 resolution says more than four crore houses have been delivered under the governments housing programmes. The number brings together a larger political promisemoving welfare beyond cash transfers towards visible assets such as houses, toilets, electricity and water connections. 15. 25 Crore: Governments Multidimensional-Poverty Claim The Modi government says more than 25 crore Indians have moved out of multidimensional poverty over the past decade-plus. This figure needs an important qualification: it refers to the multidimensional-poverty methodology and should not be presented as 25 crore people simply crossing an income-poverty threshold. The figure is cited by the government and is based on NITI Aayogs multidimensional poverty estimates. 16. Rs. 4.09 Lakh Crore: PM-KISAN Transfers Since its launch in 2019, PM-KISAN has become a major pillar of the governments direct support to eligible landholding farmers. As of March 2026, the government said more than Rs. 4.09 lakh crore had been transferred through 21 instalments. The scheme provides Rs. 6,000 a year to eligible farmers in three instalments through DBT. 17. 1,46,560 Km: Indias National Highway Network Infrastructure is another area where the numbers show a dramatic change. Indias national highway network stood at 1,46,560 kilometres by the end of 2025, compared with 91,287 km in 2014an increase of about 61 per cent, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The more revealing number may be the quality of the network: four-lane-and-above national highways increased from 18,371 km in 2014 to 43,512 km. 18. Rs. 12.2 Lakh Crore: Capital Expenditure The Modi governments infrastructure strategy has increasingly relied on public capital expenditure. For 2026-27, the Centre budgeted about Rs. 12.2 lakh crore in public capital expenditure. Government data puts public capex at around Rs. 2 lakh crore in 2014-15, showing how dramatically the allocation has expanded over the period. This shift towards capital spending has been one of the central features of the governments post-pandemic economic strategy. 19. Rs. 1.78 Lakh Crore: Defence Production Indias defence production reached a record Rs. 1.78 lakh crore in FY2025-26, according to the defence ministry. That was nearly four times the Rs. 43,746 crore recorded in FY2013-14. Defence exports also reached Rs. 38,424 crore in FY2025-26. The figures form a central part of the governments argument for a more self-reliant defence-industrial base. 20. Rs. 13.11 Lakh Crore: Electronics Production Electronics manufacturing has been another major Make in India success story claimed by the government. Production of electronic goods increased from about Rs. 1.9 lakh crore in 2014-15 to Rs. 13.11 lakh crore in 2025-26, a seven-fold increase, according to MeitY. Electronics exports rose from around Rs. 38,000 crore to Rs. 4.24 lakh crore over the same period. Mobile-phone production alone increased from around Rs. 18,000 crore to Rs. 6.27 lakh crore. 21. $860 Billion-Plus: Indias Exports Indias combined merchandise and services exports reached an estimated $860.09 billion in FY2025-26, according to the commerce ministrys April 2026 estimate. A later government update put the FY2025-26 total at $863.1 billion, making it a record year for Indias overall exports. The figure captures a broader shift in the PM Modi years: the attempt to make manufacturing, services and global trade central to Indias growth story. 22. 3.5 Crore: Lakhpati Didis The governments women-focused rural livelihoods programme has also produced a number that has become part of the Modi governments political vocabulary. The Union Cabinets October 2026 resolution says approximately 3.5 crore women have become Lakhpati Didiswomen in self-help groups whose annual household income reaches at least Rs. 1 lakh. The governments broader rural-livelihood data shows the programme operating through millions of self-help groups across the country. 23. 60 Crore-Plus: Ayushman Bharats Reach Healthcare became another major welfare pillar through Ayushman Bharat. The Union Cabinet says free medical treatment has been provided to more than 60 crore people under the governments health initiatives. The figure illustrates the scale at which the government has tried to shift welfare delivery from individual subsidies towards large national entitlement programmes. 24. 36: Countries That Have Conferred Top Honours On Modi PM Modis foreign-policy story can also be measured through the number of international honours he has received. The Union Cabinets October 2026 resolution says Modi has received state honours from 36 countries. The government cites this alongside Indias G20 presidency, the inclusion of the African Union in the G20 and initiatives such as Vaccine Maitri as evidence of Indias expanding diplomatic footprint. 25. 2047: The Deadline For The Modi Vision Perhaps the most important number for understanding PM Modis third term is not a number describing the past at all. It is 2047: the centenary of Indias Independence and the deadline around which the governments Viksit Bharat" vision is framed. The political pitch has therefore moved from measuring what happened between 2014 and 2024 to defining what India should look like by the time it turns 100. And that is perhaps the clearest way to read PM Modis 25-year journey. The first 25 years were about building political power, from Gandhinagar to Delhi. The next phase is being framed around what that power can deliver by 2047. From 8,931 days in office to 1.46 lakh km of national highways, from 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts to 2,450 crore-plus monthly UPI transactions, the numbers tell a story of a state that has become more digital, more infrastructure-focused and more directly involved in welfare delivery. Twenty-five years after he first took charge in Gujarat, the Modi story is therefore no longer simply about longevity. It is about the scale, reach and durability of the political and economic model he has spent a quarter-century building. Narendra Modi began his 25-year run on October 7, 2001, when he took oath as the chief minister of Gujarat.

headline: Coimbatore Medical College Hospital changes medicine covers after instructions in Hindi spark controversy
content: The Coimbatore Medical College Hospital (CMCH) administration on Tuesday replaced the brown paper covers used to dispense medicines to patients with fresh ones after instructions printed in Hindi on the former triggered a row, with many criticising it as contradicting the two-language policy of Tamil Nadu. DMK leader and former Minister for Industries T.R.B. Raja was among those who criticised the inclusion of Hindi instructions on the covers. (It) seems like the three-language policy is being implemented in Tamil Nadu hospitals too! First Karur... Now the same situation in Coimbatore as well, he posted on X, along with a photo of a pharmacy cover purportedly issued by CMCH, with instruction in Tamil, English and Hindi. He had posted earlier that similar covers with instructions in three languages were being used in Karur. A senior official from CMCH said the covers with instructions in three languages were printed and supplied by Chinthamani Cooperative Society and no one had flagged any issue with the instruction in Hindi. We replaced these covers with new ones on Tuesday evening, said the official, adding that such covers had been in use for a long time. A source from the pharmacy section of the hospital claimed that similar covers with instructions in three languages had been in use during the previous regime as well. Meanwhile, pharmacists were instructed not to use the covers with instructions in three languages and use the new ones, containing Tamil and English. According to CMCH authorities, the hospital handles around 3,000 to 4,500 outpatients a day, and a large number of migrant workers working in the city and nearby areas seek treatment at the hospital.

headline: Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhi's Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police
content: Ins With Police For more than 15 years, Gandhi's political journey has repeatedly intersected with police barricades, preventive arrests and detentions A small gate, a police cordon, a flying kiss and a long sit-in inside Akashvani Bhavan. By the time Tuesday night ended, Congress MP and Leader of The Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had once again turned a confrontation with the police into the defining image of an Opposition protest. The LoP was among INDIA bloc leaders who attempted to march towards the Election Commission on October 6, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and protesting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - DMK U-Turn On Rahul Gandhi? Party Backs Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 'Right To Fight' - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody? - Form 6 Row: Rahul Gandhi Says Gyanesh Kumar Will Be Held Accountable | Police stopped the march near the poll panels office. Gandhi climbed a barricade, waved the Tricolour and was taken towards a police bus. But that was not the end of the drama. Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra managed to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises, where they and other Opposition leaders staged a dharna for hours. Police eventually removed and detained them. They were released later last night night. Gandhi said he was standing there to protect democracy", while the BJP dismissed the protest as theatrics and accused him of attempting to create anarchy and politically relaunch himself. But Tuesdays spectacle was not an isolated episode. For more than 15 years, Gandhis political journey has repeatedly intersected with police barricades, preventive arrests and detentions, often when he has tried to physically reach farmers, protesters, victims families or government institutions. In some ways, the most recent episode looked remarkably similar to the very first major confrontation of this kind. Rahul Gandhi was among INDIA bloc leaders who attempted to march towards the Election Commission on October 6. In May 2011, Rahul Gandhi arrived at Bhatta Parsaul in Greater Noida, the epicentre of a violent farmers' agitation. In November 2016, Gandhi was detained after going to Delhi's Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. In June 2017, five farmers were killed in police firing during an agitation in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh. In October 2020, Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra travelled towards Hathras after the death of a 19-year-old Dalit woman. 2011: Bhatta Parsaul The Beginning Of The Template Long before he was Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi was a young Congress general secretary and Amethi MP. In May 2011, he arrived at Bhatta Parsaul in Greater Noida, the epicentre of a violent farmers agitation against land acquisition for the Yamuna Expressway project. The administration had deployed a heavy police presence. Gandhi nevertheless managed to enter the village at around 4 am, riding pillion on a motorcycle. Police were reportedly caught off guard and recognised him only after he began meeting farmers. He spent the day meeting farmers, listening to their grievances and sitting on a dharna. I feel ashamed to call myself Indian after seeing what has happened here," Gandhi said, accusing the then Mayawati government of unleashing atrocities on villagers. He also told the protesters: I am with you till your demands are met." The confrontation ended late that night when Uttar Pradesh Police arrested Gandhi under Section 151 of the CrPC, a preventive provision. He was taken away from the protest site and later released. The BJP called his intervention a political drama" and a political stunt". BJP leader Rajnath Singh argued that if Congress genuinely wanted to help farmers, the then UPA government should push through the pending Land Acquisition Bill. It was an early example of a political pattern that would return repeatedly: Gandhi gets around a police cordon, reaches the people at the centre of a controversy, sits with them, and the eventual detention becomes part of the political message. Fourteen years later, at Akashvani, the method looked strikingly familiar. Only, the motorcycle had been replaced by a small gate. 2016: OROP, A Hospital And Another Detention In November 2016, Gandhi was detained after going to Delhis Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital to meet the family of Ram Kishan Grewal, a retired soldier who had died by suicide amid a dispute over One Rank One Pension. Gandhi was stopped near the hospital and taken into custody. The episode became particularly dramatic when Grewals family members were also detained. Inside Mandir Marg police station, Gandhi confronted an officer over the treatment of the veterans relatives. Sharm nahi aati aapko? Aap ek jawan jo mar gaya hai uski family ko utha kar laye hain. Kya jurm hai unka?" he asked. Gandhi was subsequently detained again while participating in protests over the issue. Gandhi and thed Congress portrayed the police action as an attempt to prevent him from standing with veterans; the government and BJP maintained that the law-and-order situation justified restrictions. 2017: Mandsaur Riding Into Another Farmers Flashpoint The following year, Gandhi again headed towards a farmers protest. In June 2017, five farmers were killed in police firing during an agitation in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh. Gandhi attempted to enter the district to meet the families of those killed. The local administration had denied him permission. He was arrested at the Rajasthan-Madhya Pradesh border near Neemuch under Section 151 of the CrPC. I just want to meet the farmers," Gandhi said after being detained. BJP spokesperson GVL Narasimha Rao accused Gandhi of opportunistic and cynical politics" and said Gandhi was indulging in political tourism" and trying to create a photo-op". 2020: Hathras Confrontation Caught On Camera If Bhatta Parsaul established the pattern, Hathras produced one of its most powerful visual moments. In October 2020, Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra travelled towards Hathras after the death of a 19-year-old Dalit woman who had been allegedly gang-raped and assaulted. Their convoy was stopped on the Yamuna Expressway. The siblings continued on foot. Police tried to stop them. Gandhi fell during the confrontation and was eventually detained. I am standing here peacefully. I want to march alone to Hathras. Section 144 talks about public assembly. I will go alone to Hathras. On what basis are you detaining me?" Gandhi asked police. After the confrontation, Gandhi said, Can only Modi-ji walk in this country? Cant a normal person walk?" The BJP described the visit as political tourism". Union minister Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi said: There should not be political tourism" over the case, while BJP leaders accused the Congress of attempting to politicise the tragedy. For Congress, however, the images of Gandhi being stopped and detained became central to its attack on the Uttar Pradesh government. 2022: From ED office To Vijay Chowk The National Herald case brought another form of confrontation. Gandhi appeared before the Enforcement Directorate in June 2022 for questioning in the money-laundering case linked to the National Herald. Congress workers and leaders protested outside, with several leaders being detained during attempts to march towards the ED office. A month later, Gandhi himself was detained during a Congress protest against the questioning of his mother, Sonia Gandhi, by the ED. On July 26, Gandhi and other Congress MPs staged a sit-in at Vijay Chowk and planned to march towards Rashtrapati Bhavan. Delhi Police stopped them and detained several leaders. Congress alleged misuse of state power. The BJP, meanwhile, portrayed the protests as an attempt to pressure an independent investigative agency. The confrontation had once again moved from the legal issue itself to the politics surrounding Gandhis physical resistance to police restrictions. 2026: PM Residence, Parliament, Protests And Akashvani By 2026, Gandhis position had changed dramatically. He was no longer simply a Congress leader leading street protests; he was now the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha. Yet the street-politics playbook remained. In July 2026, Gandhi took his protest directly to Prime Minister Narendra Modis doorstep after police action against students protesting alleged examination irregularities and paper leaks. Accompanied by Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Opposition leaders, he staged a sit-in outside 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, demanding accountability, the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a discussion in Parliament. The move reportedly caught Delhi Police off guard, as arrangements had been made for a possible protest at Vijay Chowk instead. After nearly three hours, police detained Gandhi and several Opposition leaders and took them away in buses. Gandhi later explained his strategy bluntly: If the youth are on the streets, the Opposition should be too." Tuesdays protest offered the most theatrical version yet. The INDIA blocs march towards the Election Commission was stopped by police. Gandhi climbed the barricades, waved the national flag and carried a placard declaring: Gyanesh, its done bro!" Then came the unexpected twist. As police began detaining Opposition leaders and moving them towards buses, Gandhi and Priyanka entered Akashvani Bhavan. What followed was an hours-long sit-in inside the premises before police finally removed the protesters. Gandhi and Priyanka were among those detained and were released later in the night. Gandhi defended the protest in sweeping terms, saying, I am not interested in what the BJP says. I am standing here to protect democracy in the country." The BJP offered the exact opposite interpretation. Union minister Kiren Rijiju called the protests drama" and told Gandhi to learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and BJP workers rather than rely on such tactics. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra accused the Congress of trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary" and alleged that the Opposition was willing to undermine democracy to do so. BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi was equally scathing, saying the protest was theatrics" and questioning why Gandhi had not simply sought a formal meeting with the Election Commission. The Rahul Gandhi Protest Playbook There is a striking visual continuity running through these episodes. In Bhatta Parsaul, Gandhi slipped past the police on a motorcycle. In Mandsaur, he tried to cross a state border despite restrictions. In Hathras, he continued on foot after his vehicle was stopped. During the ED protests, he sat down at Vijay Chowk and refused to simply disperse. And at Akashvani Bhavan, he found another route after police had apparently brought the march under control. The locations, political battles and Gandhi himself have changed. The instinct to cross the barricade has not. Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders attempted to march towards the Election Commission on October 6, 2026, to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and protest the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. After police stopped the march, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi entered Akashvani Bhavan premises and staged an hours-long dharna before being removed and detained by police.

headline: FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka over Delhi All India Radio sit-in
content: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have been booked on trespassing charges for allegedly entering Akashwani Bhawan in Central Delhi during Tuesdays protest march against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. A police officer said the FIR under relevant sections has been registered at Parliament Street Police Station and an investigation has been launched. On Tuesday, around 200 MPs of the INDIA bloc had called for a protest march from Makar Dwar of Parliament to the Election Commission headquarters. The march, led by Congress leaders, was stopped at Akashwani Bhawan after the protesters had covered around 700 metres on Parliament Street, where barricades had been put up. Rahul Gandhi climbed over the police barricades. As police began detaining MPs and party workers, he entered Akashwani Bhawan, asking a security guard to allow him inside. According to police sources, the main gates of the All India Radio office were shut, but a smaller gate used for entry remained open. Following Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other leaders, including KC Venugopal and Deepender Hooda, also managed to enter the building and demanded to meet the Election Commissioner. Akashwani Bhawan is located around 200 metres from the Election Commission headquarters. Senior Delhi Police officers entered the building and tried to convince Rahul Gandhi and the other leaders to come out. However, they staged a sit-in protest inside the premises for around seven hours before being detained by the police at 7 pm. They were taken to the New Police Lines in Kingsway Camp in Northwest Delhi.

headline: Barricades, Sting, and 'Khan Chacha': How the Gandhis kept protest going
content: What appeared to be the end of the INDIA blocs protest to the Election Commission took an unexpected turn after Gandhi siblings found a way past the police barricades and into the Akashvani Bhawan premises. The Opposition leaders had set out from Parliament Street to the Election Commission headquarters, barely 300 metres away, demanding action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. But the march was stopped by Delhi Police, with barricades put up on the routes. Several Opposition MPs were also detained and taken away in buses. As the detentions mounted, only a few Congress leaders remained at the protest site. The drama began around noon when Rahul Gandhi climbed atop a police barricade near the NITI Aayog office on Sansad Marg. He was seen holding and waving the Tricolour flag as cameras captured the moment. He later climbed down as police began detaining MPs who were sitting on the road and protesting. But the question is, was Rahul done with that? No. As detained MPs were being taken away, he suddenly moved towards a bus parked near Akashvani Bhawan, where Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was seated. As Rahul Gandhi was about to get into the bus, he and Priyanka exchanged a glance. Priyanka then got down. The two siblings, along with their supporters, walked past the policemen and entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises, taking the protest to a new location and leaving the police confused and scrambling to respond. Rahul was seen with Congress leaders K C Venugopal, Deepender Singh Hooda, Charanjeet Singh Channi, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi and Praniti Shinde. The leaders settled under a tree inside the premises and insisted that they be allowed to meet the Election Commission. We represent the people of the country we are their voice, Rahul told reporters. I am not interested in what the BJP says. I am standing here to protect democracy in the country. Along with me, 300 Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs had come and they are also trying to protect democracy, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha added. Even as the confrontation with police continued, the Gandhi siblings were seen taking a breather during the prolonged protest. At one point, Rahul offered Priyanka Sting energy drink. She was seen smelling it before taking a sip. Later during the protest Rahul was seen eating a roll from Khan Chacha while Priyanka sat beside him. The informal breaks came as the Congress leaders continued their sit-in and maintained that they would not leave until they were allowed to meet the Election Commission. View this post on Instagram On claims that they are disrupting traffic and causing inconvenience, Rahul Gandhi said the police should then tell them where can we stage a sit-in, and we will sit there. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also told a police officer that the inconvenience to commuters was being caused by the Delhi Polices repeated barricading of roads and routes across the city. She argued that since the protest began, police had been blocking multiple routes and even restricting access around metro stations, leading to traffic snarls and disruptions. The inconvenience, she said, was not being caused by Congress workers or those protesting on the streets, but by the police arrangements put in place to contain the agitation. View this post on Instagram Their protest eventually escalated, with police moving in to remove Rahul and other leaders from the Akashvani Bhawan premises. Rahul was forcibly removed and briefly detained as the protest continued elsewhere. But Priyanka remained at the centre of the agitation. At one point, she was seen climbing the gated premises at Kingsway Camp, where Rahul had been taken after being removed from the protest site. She opened the gates, after which Congress workers entered the premises. View this post on Instagram As the protest stretched till late evening, Rahul said the Opposition MPs would continue to press for a meeting with the election commissioners. They will have to meet us The MPs were disrespected. We have not done anything wrong. We want to go to the election commissioners and ask questions of them and tell them that they have done vote chori, Gandhi said. But on the other hand, according to EC it had not received any request from Congress or any political party seeking a meeting. By then, what had started as an INDIA bloc march from Parliament Street to the poll panel had turned into a day-long confrontation, with the Gandhis repeatedly defying police attempts to contain the protest.

headline: T.N. records highest Southwest monsoon temperatures in the last nine years
content: Tamil Nadu experienced unusually warm weather during the Southwest monsoon this year, with temperatures remaining elevated for a sustained period, according to an analysis by the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC). The State recorded its highest temperatures during the season compared with the 2018-25 period. This assumes significance particularly against the backdrop of 2023, 2024, and 2025 being the three warmest years on record globally. According to the Regional Weather Forecasting Centre (RWFC), RMC, the State registered a mean temperature of 29.45C during the season (between June and September) this year, which is nearly 1.21C above the 2018-25 average. The assessment of temperatures during Southwest monsoon showed a sustained period of above readings across the States weather stations network. Both maximum and minimum temperatures remained above the 2018-25 average, with the strongest warming signal observed between July and September. The maximum mean temperature was 34.25C, with an anomaly of 1.40C compared to the 2018-25 average. The mean minimum temperature was 24.64C (+1.02C). V.R. Durai, Head, RWFC, said it was not just isolated hot days in different locations, but elevated temperatures persisted over the months. This seasons mean temperature was 0.72C higher than the previous highest temperature recorded in 2023. We found that Tamil Nadu recorded a marked rise in mean temperature this season compared with each of the previous years, he said. The warming trend strengthened from July this year, after widespread rainfall in June helped keep temperatures under control. This years July, August, and September were the warmest months compared to corresponding months in the 2018-25. Vellore, Puducherry, Palayamkottai, Meenambakkam in Chennai, Kodaikanal, and Tiruttani were among the weather stations that recorded above normal mean temperatures during the Southwest monsoon. The weather station-wise assessment also showed that the warming weather trend was widespread across the States network. Citing the three warmest years globally, Mr. Durai said the trend pointed to an overall warming of weather conditions with every passing year. The spike in temperatures had intensified since 2020. While global warming was a major factor behind the soaring mercury level in the State during the Southwest monsoon, a strong El Nio this year also contributed to the increasing warm trend. The results include the first and second rounds of Shillong Teer and other scheduled games such as Juwai Teer, Khanapara Teer, Shillong Morning Teer and Shillong Night Teer. Shillong Teer is an archery-based number game conducted in Meghalaya under local regulations. Participants select numbers from 00 to 99, with the winning numbers determined according to the arrow counts recorded during the scheduled rounds. The first and second-round results for October 7 will be added below once they are officially released. Readers are advised to verify the numbers with authorised result announcements before claiming any prize. headline: 'Committed To Welfare': India Backs Afghanistan's Sovereignty As Taliban, Pakistan Clash At Moscow Talks
content: India backed Afghanistans sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity at the Moscow Format talks, reaffirming its commitment to the Afghan people. India has voiced support for Afghanistans sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity at the eighth Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan in Moscow, reiterating its commitment to the welfare of the Afghan people. An Indian delegation led by Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar and Joint Secretary (PAI) Dr M Suresh Kumar conveyed New Delhis position at the meeting hosted by Russia. - Pakistan-Taliban Rift Moves To Moscow; India, China And Iran Join Key Afghanistan Talks | Exclusive - Incompetence, Negligence Or Worse? UN Rapporteur Questions Pakistan Airstrikes In Afghanistan - Russia Reaffirms Full Support For Afghan Taliban Regime During High-Level Moscow Talks | Exclusive - Russia Voices Concerns Over Civilian Deaths In Pakistani Strikes On Afghanistan, Calls Situation Serious The consultations brought together officials from Russia, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi led Afghanistans delegation, while Belarus and Egypt participated as guests. Based on its long-standing friendship with Afghanistan, India remains committed to the welfare of Afghan people and supports Afghan sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity," the Embassy of India in Russia said in a post on X. The reiteration of Indias position came as Pakistan has carried out cross-border military strikes into Afghanistan. New Delhis position at the Moscow consultations was conveyed against the backdrop of those cross-border actions. During the meeting, participants reaffirmed that there was no alternative to developing cooperation with Kabul on an equal and mutually beneficial basis and supporting Afghanistans integration into the global economy, the Russian Foreign Ministry said. India backed Afghanistans sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. India reiterated its commitment to the welfare of the Afghan people at the Moscow Format talks. The consultations called for equal and mutually beneficial engagement with Kabul. The participants also called on the international community to provide regular humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people, stressing that such aid should not be politicised. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the forum brings together countries that have a stake in establishing and maintaining an equal and mutually beneficial partnership with the Afghan people. It offers an opportunity to hold a substantive discussion of matters related to providing international assistance to Afghanistan and, importantly, to do so in conjunction with Kabul," Lavrov said. Lavrov also said August 2026 marked the fifth anniversary of Afghanistans liberation from two decades of Western occupation". He said the military presence of the US and its NATO allies had ended after what he described as the Afghan peoples fighting spirit and determination". Lavrov also lauded Afghanistans uncompromising fight against ISIS and other terrorist groups" and its efforts to combat drug trafficking. He said hundreds of militants had been eliminated and several high-profile terror attacks had been foiled. According to Lavrov, strengthening Kabuls counterterrorism capabilities through material and expert assistance, along with maintaining contacts between intelligence and law enforcement agencies, serves the interests of all countries involved. On Afghanistans economy, Lavrov said it continued to develop despite what he described as harsh sanctions pressure from Western countries. The Moscow Format was established in 2017, with the participation of special representatives from 11 countries, including Russia, Afghanistan, India, Iran, China and Pakistan. Its main objective is to promote national reconciliation in Afghanistan and facilitate the establishment of peace in the country. At the eighth Moscow Format Consultations, India voiced support for Afghanistan's sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity while reaffirming its commitment to the welfare of the Afghan people.

headline: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Orders Probe Into Missing 45 Acres in Erravalli; Notices To Be Issued To KTR, Family
content: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy ordered officials to trace 45 missing acres in Erravalli after holding a review of the land records pertaining to the village Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy directed the officials to identify the missing 45 acres of land in Survey No. 325 at Erravalli village in Markook mandal of Siddipet district. According to official records, Survey No. 325 comprises 388 acres. However, a recent survey reportedly identified only 343 acres, leaving 45 acres of land unaccounted. - Kerala Lottery Result Today Live: DhanaLekshmi DL-72 Winning Numbers For October 7, 2026; First Prize Rs. 1 Crore - 'Game Up For Kejriwal, Mann': Delhi Minister Reacts As People Shower Flowers On CBI Car After Chandigarh Raid - PM Modi Performs Aarti At Delhis Sri Vinayak Mandir As He Marks 25 years Of Public Service | - 'Zero Tolerance To Terrorism': India Hits Out At Pakistan Over Cross-Border Terror; Defends Right To Respond The Chief Minister held a review of the land records pertaining to Erravalli and neighbouring Venkatapuram villages. During the meeting, officials briefed Revanth Reddy on the survey findings and the discrepancies in the recorded extent of land. Chief Minister Revanth Reddy directed officials to issue notices to BRS chief and former Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) and his family members, whose lands are located adjacent to Survey No. 325, seeking submission of their revenue and land records to the government. Revanth Reddy also said the government plans to distribute the land available in Survey No. 325 to eligible local farmers. The Chief Minister further ordered the establishment of a Telangana Martyrs Colony" within Survey No. 325 for the families of those who sacrificed their lives during the Telangana statehood movement. Officials were directed to identify and allocate housing plots to the martyrs families and develop the colony with all necessary infrastructure and amenities. Revanth Reddy suggested that the Housing Department be entrusted with the responsibility of constructing the colony and directed officials to complete the project by June 2.
