headline: The status of the U.S. blockade on Cuba
content: It has been nearly nine months since the U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order threatening tariffs on any country that supplies Cuba with oil, and the U.S. Coast Guard began intercepting tankers and ships bound for the island. Power cuts in Cuba have since become very common, often lasting beyond 12 hours a day and even close to 20 hours in some provinces. Independent UN human rights experts condemned these actions, calling them energy starvation and an unlawful blockade of the island country, as the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights reported. In July 2026, the UN General Assembly voted 136-9 (with 30 abstentions) to debate the blockade despite U.S. objections. Mr. Trump, meanwhile, has threatened a takeover of the island nation a threat that is unlawful according to the UN Charter, which prohibits the threat or use of force against a countrys political independence. The new blockade is over and above a 64-year-old embargo by the U.S. Embargo or blockade? Following the 1959 Cuban revolution, the Cuban government led by Fidel Castro nationalised U.S.-owned property in 1959-60. The U.S. responded, imposing a partial embargo on Cuban trade in October 1960 and making it full-fledged in 1962. Cuba terms the measures el bloqueo, or a blockade, as it goes beyond mere bilateral trade and is exemplified by further measures taken by the U.S. on Cuban foreign trade. The Cuban Democracy Act of 1992 barred foreign subsidiaries of U.S. firms from trading in Cuba, and the Helms-Burton Act of 1996 wrote the embargo into law, so that only the U.S. Congress can lift it. It also allowed lawsuits against foreign firms using property in Cuba that was confiscated from the Americans. After coming to power, Mr. Trump expanded further on these punitive measures by bringing Cuba back on the State Sponsors of Terrorism list (without any justification after it was briefly removed by the outgoing Biden administration in January 2025). This has meant that banks find it difficult to deal with Cuban entities. In May, the Trump administration imposed secondary sanctions on foreign firms dealing with the Cuban state and its military conglomerate, GAESA. It has also indicted former Cuban President Raul Castro on problematic charges, besides the January 29 order, which declared a national emergency and authorised extra duties on goods from any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba. Year after year in the UN General Assembly, since 1992, there has been near-unanimous demand to end the embargo, but the resolutions are not binding, and this has allowed the U.S. to continue it. Havana claims that the cumulative damage of the embargo has been to the tune of $178.7 billion and $8.08 billion in the year up to February 2026 itself, which includes just one month of the fuel blockade. These costs are not just lost U.S. trade, but also the impact on Cubas overall trade because of what the embargo imposes. For example, ships docking in Cuba are barred from U.S. ports for 180 days, which has led to increased freight costs. With the U.S. imposing financial sanctions, banks refuse Cuban payments, and imports of medical equipment and machinery have also been affected. Has this hostility against Cuba always been the case? U.S. policy towards Cuba has been motivated largely by the lobbying efforts of Cuban exiles based in Miami, Florida, who fled the island following the Revolution. These hardliners include those born to Cuban-immigrant parents, such as current Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who have sought the collapse of the communist system in Cuba. They have also strongly backed the Trump administrations actions, as making conditions that are ripe for regime change, according to the International Crisis Group. The hostility against Cuba experienced a brief thaw during former President Barack Obamas second tenure. In December 2014, he and Raul Castro announced a normalisation of ties, which led to embassies reopening, Cuba being taken off the terrorism list, and culminating in a visit to Havana by Mr Obama. Travel and remittance rules were eased, but the embargo still stayed. Mr. Trump reverted much of it during his first tenure before imposing stronger restrictions in his second tenure, which intensified after U.S. forces attacked Venezuela and abducted its president, Nicolas Maduro and took control over the Latin American countrys fuel and energy resources since then. Why was Venezuela an important lifeline for Cuba? Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, which affected the Cuban economy severely, leading to what was called a special period, Fidel Castro and Hugo Chavez signed an oil-for-services agreement in 2000. This led to the Barrio Adentro health missions (neighbourhood medical services) provided by Cuban doctors in Venezuela. Some 40,000 Cuban doctors, teachers and other professionals worked in Venezuela, while the country supplied about 1,00,000 barrels of oil a day on relatively easy terms. Cuba also resold some of the oil for hard currency, according to U.S. officials, to mitigate the impact of the U.S. financial sanctions. Meanwhile, mismanagement of the state oil company PDVSA, the 2014 crash in oil prices and later U.S. sanctions cut Venezuelas oil output to a third by the late 2010s, leading to lowered shipments to Cuba. The imports met, by late 2025, only about a quarter of Cuban demand for oil and about a third of its oil imports. In January 2026, that came to naught too after the U.S. took control of Venezuelas oil sector. Mexico, which had supplied about 44% of Cubas oil imports, then suspended deliveries. Russia has not been able to step up and fill in the gap either, with just sporadic ships managing to deliver supplies to Cuba since the naval blockade. What was the impact of the fuel blockade? The International Crisis Group lists severe disruption to transportation, food distribution, health care, water systems and communications in the country. On May 7, three UN Special Rapporteurs said fuel scarcity was keeping people from hospitals and children from school. They cited a backlog of more than 96,000 surgeries, 11,000 of them for children, and delays in infant immunisation. The scale of the impact is shown in satellite imagery data. An index of night-time light intensity built from NASA satellite data, a proxy for electricity use, fell from about 1012 in 202125 to around six by mid-2026. Ships reaching Cuba have been reduced from 100-120 a month to just 50-60 in early 2026 and oil cargoes have become sporadic. The impact of the sanctions has also meant a large drop in employment in industries such as tourism which the Cuban government sought to utilise to shore up its dollar reserves and mining and shipping. The naval blockade has also occurred at a time when one in five Cubans have emigrated in the past five years due to the weak economy. How is China helping Cuba mitigate the fuel shortage? On September 23, President Miguel Diaz-Canel said that Cuba has installed 1,418 MW of solar capacity in 144 parks and would pass 1,500 MW by the end of 2026. He said that renewables already generate 21.4% of the countrys electricity. Much of the equipment for these installations have arrived from China. Data from the energy think tank Ember show Chinese exports of solar panels and cells to Cuba being minimal till 2024 and then going up to a cumulative 2,200 MW by mid-2026. In September, reports showed that a third batch of 5,000 standalone solar systems donated by China arrived for public buildings and isolated homes, after shipments in August and November 2025. But power blackouts persist because solar power is not generated after sunset, when demand peaks and battery storage is inadequate in Cuba. The power grid also relies on aging oil-fired plants. Chinese customs data also show Chinas imports from Cuba rising from about $50 million in 2015 to $320 million in 2022, with commodities such as zinc ores, nickel products, lead and silver ores, lobsters, cigars and rum. But this trade fell to $230 million in 2025 and $145 million roughly in 2026 so far. What other reforms has Havana embarked upon? Havana approved 176 reforms in June to expand private enterprise and foreign investment, but the blockade continues to stymie these. Back-channel talks with the Trump administration have continued but there is little progress because the latter demands regime change while Havana insists that it will not compromise on its sovereignty or political constitution, according to ICG. With inputs from Gauri Singavarapu who is interning with Data Team

headline: The protests and polls in Spain
content: The last two days have been extremely eventful for Spain, the European nation that has been rocked by mass movements demanding a solution to a housing crisis. What began as a response to the eviction of a senior citizen in Madrid snowballed into protests across the country, forcing Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to first put together emergency legislation to address the situation and, following the failure of the emergency measures to get the nod from the parliament, call snap elections. The announcement of the national election, to be held on November 29, 2026, eight months ahead of schedule, came hours before a demonstration in Barcelona, the capital of the Catalunya province, which has a long-standing separatist ambition, which attracted thousands and turned violent. Following this, the government has put together a fresh 21-point proposal to tackle the crisis, opening the door to a temporary settlement. What prompted the protests? At the centre of the events that led to the snap elections, which some analysts see as a blessing in disguise for Prime Minister Sanchez heading a fragile coalition, is an 87-year-old woman, Maria del Carmen Abascal, who was evicted from the apartment which was rented by her father in 1956. After the death of her parents, Ms. Abascal continued as a tenant in the building, located in the now upscale Retiro neighbourhood in the Spanish capital, Madrid, until she was taken out on a stretcher last month. The eviction, which was previously blocked by courts three times, angered people across the country and made Ms. Abascal, who was hospitalised after her eviction, a symbol of the imminent housing crisis in the country. The eviction was later reversed by the investment fund, which had acquired ownership of the building she was living in, but the dominoes could not be stopped. People began gathering in large numbers, seeking protective measures for those renting apartments, anti-fraud rules, and a ban on evictions without alternative housing. Spaniards were already angry with the rising rents across the country, which have surged more than 80% within the last decade, making housing one of the biggest concerns for people. According to the Youth Council of Spain, the average rent in the country was more than 98% of the average salary for people under 30, an exorbitant figure. What happened in Barcelona? People in the second-largest city in the country, who have historically fostered animosity towards the Spanish administration, had scheduled a demonstration for the weekend after a legislation to address the crisis was voted down by the extremely divided parliament, but was postponed due to inclement weather. While the announcement of the snap election was projected to be an option for the people to express their dissatisfaction through the ballot, the Catalonians decided to go ahead with the demonstration. However, the demonstration, with thousands of people, which began as a peaceful march, turned violent when some groups allegedly threw stones at the police and set containers on fire. Around 30 police personnel reported minor injuries, while at least 13 people were arrested following the incident, which, according to visuals circulating online, resembled nothing less than a fiery street fight. What does the emergency legislations propose? The initial legislation put forward by the Socialist-led government in two Bills proposed, among other measures, a ban on evictions till 2030. It also sought to regulate short-term rentals and proposed automatic contract renewals, while Health Minister Monica Garcia indicated the imposition of a ban on the purchase of housing by vulture funds, without elaborating. However, both the Bills failed to garner a majority of votes in parliament, with the major blow coming from the Catalan separatist party Junts, which supports the ruling Sumar coalition of left parties, voting against. However, following the protests in Barcelona, the Sanchez government rushed to put together another piece of legislation to address the issue, which the government approved on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). The 21-point proposal includes measures to facilitate easier renting or buying of houses, extension of protection against eviction for vulnerable residents, regulation of room rentals, a new tax on seasonal rentals, prohibition of speculative real estate purchases, and tax breaks for owners and tenants who are punctual with payments. While most of the provisions are similar to those that were voted down in parliament last week, this time the government is optimistic about getting legislative approval as it only needs to pass an interim body of 69 members instead of the full 350-member parliament after the announcement of election. What advantages does the Prime Minister have in the situation? The November 29 election will see Spaniards go to the polls for the fifth time in 10 years, with Mr. Sanchez trying to leverage the situation to establish a stronger government. The socialist leader returned to office for a second term in 2023, scraping together a fragile last-minute coalition after the conservative Peoples Party won the most without getting a majority. However, he has been on the back foot from the beginning, facing criticism for agreeing to amnesty demands by Catalan parties to secure their backing and later when allegations of corruption rose against his family members. However, with less than a year left for his term to end, the protests and the subsequent voting down of a relief measure have given him a silver lining. Even though his government failed to pass the legislation to quell peoples dissatisfaction, Mr. Sanchez now has the narrative to push for a landslide mandate and has legislation favourable to the protesters to give the people in return. The failure of the legislation to pass parliament has, in a way, kicked off the Prime Ministers campaign even before calling the election.

headline: 'Zero Tolerance To Terrorism': India Hits Out At Pakistan Over Cross-Border Terror; Defends Right To Respond
content: At the UNGA Sixth Committee, Biplab Deb accused Pakistan of fuelling cross-border terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir and defended India's right to respond. India has reiterated its firm position against cross-border terrorism at the United Nations General Assembly, with BJP MP and national general secretary Biplab Kumar Deb accusing Pakistan of actively fuelling terrorist activities in Jammu and Kashmir and asserting Indias right to defend its people and borders. Speaking at the Sixth Committee of the 81st UN General Assembly, which deals with international legal matters, Deb stressed the need for stronger international action against terrorism, including those who organise, finance and sponsor terror attacks. - Unity In Peril? Before INDIA Bloc's 'Save Democracy' March, NC-PDP Rift Spills Out In Jammu - INDIA Bloc Announces Massive Protest Against Modi Govt From Oct 7 In J&K Over SIR, ECI & Statehood Issues - Omar Abdullah Delaying Local Body Polls Fearing Defeat: BJP Vows To Take To The Streets To Highlight J&K Govt's Failures - They Oppose SIR As They Don't Want To Lose Rohingya Votes: J&K BJP President Sat Sharma Hits Out At INDIA Bloc Deb said Pakistan had established base camps for terrorist organisations along the border and was actively supporting terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir. He strongly reiterated Indias right to defend itself against cross-border terrorism. The remarks came as India pressed for an international legal framework to hold accountable those responsible for terrorist attacks, including the perpetrators, organisers, financiers and sponsors of terrorism. Referring to the Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 innocent civilians last year, Deb said it was essential to ensure that all those behind such cross-border terrorism were held accountable. The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba, had taken responsibility for the attack. India has maintained that Pakistan is a state sponsor of cross-border terrorism. Following the Pahalgam attack, India retaliated against terrorist bases operating from Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, according to the position outlined in the report. At the UN, Deb reiterated Indias position that its right to protect its people against terrorism cannot be questioned. The BJP leader also underlined Indias rejection of any distinction between different forms of terrorism. There can be no distinction between good and bad terrorism," was the thrust of Indias position, with Deb stressing that there could be no justification for targeting civilians. India Pushes For Comprehensive Convention On International Terrorism A major focus of Debs address was Indias long-standing demand for the early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT). India proposed the convention in 1996, but it has remained pending for nearly three decades amid differences between countries over its provisions, including disagreements over the treatment of groups described by some as freedom fighters". Deb argued that a stronger international legal framework was necessary to ensure accountability for those involved in terrorism. The call assumes significance in the context of Indias demand for legal action against everyone involved in attacks such as Pahalgam, including those who provide financial, organisational or logistical support. Deb also drew attention to the changing nature of terrorism and the use of emerging technologies by terror organisations. He highlighted concerns over the use of technology for recruitment, radicalisation, propaganda, operational planning and terrorist financing. According to the priorities outlined by Deb, countering the misuse of emerging technologies is part of Indias broader approach to combating terrorism. Other priorities include ending terrorist financing, putting victims at the centre of counter-terrorism efforts, strengthening nationally owned capacity-building, confronting terrorist ideology and impeding terrorist infrastructure. The intervention placed Jammu and Kashmir and the threat of cross-border terrorism at the centre of Indias broader argument for stronger international action against terror networks and their sponsors. Following his UNGA engagement, Deb also posted on X about his participation in the Sixth Committee. Delivered Indias National Statement at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (), Sixth Committee, on the agenda item Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism," Deb said. He said India, under Prime Minister Narendra Modis leadership, continued to follow a firm zero-tolerance approach to terrorism" and called for decisive global action against terror networks, their financing and those providing them safe havens. Deb said Indias resolve reflected Modis commitment to a secure, peaceful and rule-based world order". India has been pressing for the early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT), which it originally proposed in 1996 to establish a stronger international legal framework for holding perpetrators and sponsors of terror accountable.

headline: A Small Gate, A Flying Kiss And Samosas: How Rahul Gandhi Stumped Cops At Akashvani Bhavan
content: How Rahul Gandhi Stumped Cops At Akashvani Bhavan According to Congress sources, the move was not part of the plan and the idea was to get inside the Akashvani Bhavan premises and use the rear exit located towards the EC side For a protest that was supposed to be over, Rahul Gandhi had other ideas. The buses had begun rolling out from outside Akashvani Bhavan, carrying opposition leaders who were detained after the INDIA blocs march towards the Election Commission was stopped. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were inside one of them. Even members of Rahul Gandhis staff, including Alankar Sawai, were on the bus. - Form 6 Row: Rahul Gandhi Says Gyanesh Kumar Will Be Held Accountable | - Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Detained During Protest Against CEC At Akashvani Bhawan; Released After 2 Hours - Will Rahul Gandhi Be INDIA Blocs PM Candidate In 2029? Heres What Mamata Banerjee Said - 'MPs Disrespected': Rahul Gandhi Demands Meeting With CEC, To Continue Protest At Akashvani Bhavan And then, just as the bus moved, came the surprise. The Leader of Opposition was suddenly spotted not inside the bus, but on the road divider, waving at the crowd gathered around Akashvani Bhavan. He blew a flying kiss towards those watching, before making an unexpected move towards the premises. - Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) October 6, 2026 Before the guards could control the melee, Rahul Gandhi spotted a small gate and squeezed through. He turned right and walked into the Akashvani Bhavan premises, leaving the police and even some of his own people trying to make sense of what had just happened. Priyanka Gandhi, meanwhile, followed him in quietly. ALSO READ | No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM: ECI Flags Unusual Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation The timing could hardly have been more unusual. People inside the premises were getting down and preparing for their lunch break when the two Gandhis suddenly appeared among them. Soon, the mood inside changed. The siblings moved around the premises, waving at people and stopping for selfies. Their staff, who had initially been left behind with the buses, eventually came running in and made their way through. The duo continued to walk around, waving occasionally at those gathered outside the railings. The protest, which had looked like it was headed towards an abrupt end, had acquired a second act. And it was a decidedly less formal one. ALSO READ | Insulting Institutions Wont Strengthen Democracy: Kiren Rijiju Hits Out At Rahul Gandhi Over CEC Protest At one point, food became part of the impromptu sit-in. Samosas were ordered from a shop next door. Then came a Kathi roll. There was even a Sting energy drink that Rahul Gandhi offered to his sister. Priyanka Gandhi, however, smelled it, took a small sip and returned the bottle to her brother, prompting a jibe from the Bharatiya Janata Party. For a while, there seemed to be no clear scriptor at least, not one that everyone had been told about. The Congress MPs began arriving later, one by one. KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera joined the scene after roughly an hour, as more opposition leaders made their way into the premises. What had begun as a march to the Election Commission had turned into an unexpected occupation of the neighbouring Akashvani Bhavan and Rahul Gandhis sudden detour appeared to have caught almost everyone, including his own team, by surprise. According to Congress sources, the move was not part of the original plan. The idea, sources said, was to get inside the Akashvani Bhavan premises and potentially use its rear exit, which is located towards the Election Commission side. With routes to the poll panel blocked, the diversion offered an unexpected way to keep the protest going. ALSO READ | Rahul Gandhis SIR Dharna: Why AAP, DMK Skipped INDIA Blocs Sit-In Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar For those watching from outside, however, the sequence was much simpler: the buses left, Rahul Gandhi disappeared from one of them, and moments later he was inside the premises; waving, taking selfies, eating a samosa and keeping a protest alive that had appeared to be over. What Happened On Tuesday The day had begun with the INDIA blocs planned march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, with opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and raising allegations linked to the revision of electoral rolls. The march did not get very far. Security personnel stopped the MPs near the NITI Aayog area, putting up multiple layers of barricades between the protesters and the Election Commission office. The opposition leaders wanted to proceed to Nirvachan Sadan and meet the Election Commissioners. As the standoff grew, Rahul Gandhi climbed onto a barricade and waved the tricolour, drawing cheers from the crowd. Several MPs were detained and taken away in buses. Priyanka Gandhi was also briefly taken towards a waiting bus before joining her brother again near Akashvani Bhavan. By then, the protest appeared to be breaking up. That was when the Gandhi siblings made their unexpected move into Akashvani. What followed was an hours-long sit-in. Rahul Gandhi said the protesters were comfortable inside, with mattresses, toilets and tea available, and that they were prepared to stay for as long as necessary. More opposition leaders subsequently joined them. The protest continued for nearly nine hours before Delhi Police moved in during the evening to clear the premises and detain Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other leaders. They were later taken to the Kingsway Camp police lines and released. The Election Commission, meanwhile, said it had not received a request for a meeting from a political party until 4pm, and later said when a delegation of MPs sought a meeting, it considered the proposed format and venue unusual. The INDIA bloc staged a march from Parliament toward the Election Commission headquarters to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and raise concerns regarding the revision of electoral rolls.

headline: 4 injured at stir against Sangh leader at Keralam varsity event

headline: India News Highlights, 7 October 2026: Maharashtra CM meets Amit Shah in Delhi to seek special assistance for drought
content: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday met Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi and sought special financial assistance from the Centre for the state, where nearly 80 per cent of the talukas have been affected by severe drought. During the meeting, Shah assured the Centre will provide maximum possible drought assistance to Maharashtra, he stated. Every FIR medal for me: Rahul Gandhi says he aims for 100 amid CEC protests Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hosted a lunch for INDIA bloc MPs at Sagar Ratna in Janpath, New Delhi, on Wednesday. Several Opposition MPs, including Karti Chidambaram, Charanjit Singh Channi, Imran Pratapgarhi and Mukul Wasnik, attended. Police were heavily deployed outside Sagar Ratna, cordoning off the footpath around the restaurant. Additional barricades were also being brought in. After lunch, Opposition MPs started leaving Sagar Ratna and boarded two buses arranged by the INDIA bloc. The buses carrying the MPs then left Janpath for Jantar Mantar, where the bloc is scheduled to hold a protest. Speaking to the media outside the restaurant, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition planned the protest after the Election Commissioners did not allow 300 MPs to meet them on Tuesday. Like I said yesterday, 300 MPs wanted to meet the ECs yesterday, but we were not allowed to meet them. So today, our plan is to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. We want to tell the country that Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate CEC. These people are desh-drohi. Gyanesh Kumar has to resign, Gandhi said. There are 45 FIRs against me. But my aim is for 100 FIRs, he added. 5-floor Delhi building collapses, several feared trapped A five-storey building collapsed in Delhis northeast Seemapuri area on Wednesday afternoon. The incident took place at around 3:30 pm. Four fire tenders have been rushed to the spot, located behind a fish market. Several people are feared trapped under the debris. INDIA bloc protests in Patna, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation INDIA bloc parties, including the RJD, Congress and Left, held a protest march in Patna on Wednesday over their allegations of vote theft and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters burned effigies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Kumar. RJD leaders alleged that the CECs role in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process had benefited the BJP, while calling for his removal under the slogan Gyanesh Hatao, Loktantra Bachao (Remove Gyanesh, Save Democracy). Im still a student: PM Modi at event to mark 25 years of public life Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday marked 25 years since he first took oath as Gujarat Chief Minister on October 7, 2001, saying he never imagined he would reach this milestone and credited the people for his journey. Speaking at the culmination of the Seva Sankalp Yatra in Delhi, Modi said he still considers himself a student and seeks to keep learning. He also pledged to achieve a developed India by 2047, make India a top-three economy and a global manufacturing hub, and strengthen self-reliance. FIR against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi over Akashvani Bhawan sit-in Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have been booked for alleged trespassing after entering Akashvani Bhawan during Tuesdays INDIA bloc protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Around 200 Opposition MPs had marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission but were stopped at Akashvani Bhawan, around 200 metres from the poll panels office. The Gandhis and other leaders then staged a sit-in inside the premises for nearly seven hours before being detained around 7 pm. The FIR was registered at Parliament Street Police Station and an investigation is underway. Telangana books BJP booth agent over 30 illegal Form 7s Telangana Police have registered an FIR against BJP booth-level agent S Balachander for allegedly filing 30 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters in Hyderabads Musheerabad constituency, all against Muslim voters. The forms were submitted on September 28, but the booth-level officer and supervisor refused to accept them; a field verification on October 1 found all 30 voters were residents of the constituency. The FIR comes a day before the end of the claims and objections phase of the electoral-roll Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the final voter list due on November 9. Balachander has denied wrongdoing through the BJPs broader denial of attempts to delete voters.

headline: CM alleges oppn destroyed over 100,000 Form 7 applications
content: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday alleged that BJP and JD(S) workers had withdrawn and destroyed more than one lakh Form 7 applications after submitting them in bulk during the revision of electoral rolls, while BJP demanded that the Election Commission act against him for making what it called unsubstantiated allegations.

headline: RBI repo rate news LIVE: RBI raises GDP growth forecast to 7.1 per cent for FY27
content: RBI raises GDP growth forecast to 7.1 per cent for FY27 Financial markets were bracing for the hike in interest rates amid mounting global and domestic headwinds. A hike in the short-term lending rate (repo) by the RBI in its upcoming monetary policy would mark a stance reversal, following four rate cuts totalling 125 basis points in 2025 and a prolonged pause thereafter, the agency reported. The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 25 basis points to 6.50 per cent. Markets fall ahead of MPC decision, rise later Equity benchmarks began Wednesdays trading session on a weak note as investors remained cautious in anticipation of a rate hike. Sentiments remained cautious as investors sought clarity on the central banks review on economic growth and inflation. The BSE Sensex slipped 102.43 points, or 0.14 percent, to open at 72,965.38, while the Nifty 50 shed 85.65 points, or 0.38 percent, to start at 22,690.45. Selling pressure intensified shortly after the bell across both benchmark indices. However, soon after the repo rate announcement, markets marginally picked up. Global instability, rising CPI big concerns The central banks MPC review comes at a time when the economic policy faces fresh pressures from geopolitical instability and rising prices. Key drivers influencing the committees stance include geopolitical tensions, rising Consumer Price Index (CPI), and increasing domestic food price pressure, among other factors. The prolonged conflict in West Asia and higher crude oil costs are stoking broader macroeconomic concerns with microeconomic consequences they are pinching the common mans pocket every day. Moreover, concerns over persistent food inflation have kept retail price growth volatile.

headline: Saffron State, Splintered Rivals: Nandigram, Rejinagar Invert Bengal's Historic Election Math
content: Nandigram, Rejinagar Invert Bengals Historic Election Math For the first time in 15 years, the state voted under a BJP govt, with CM Suvendu Adhikari leading the saffron government following their historic victory in May 2026. West Bengals Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls are not merely two Assembly contests. Unlike typical localised bypolls that serve as minor mid-term evaluations, the October 6 elections carry the weight of a fundamental but systemic shift, putting the new regimes grip and a shattered opposition to an immediate litmus test. What makes Bengal different from most by-poll-bound states is that this is not simply a contest over the performance of a government. It seemed like a contest over the collapse of an old electoral grammar. - Suvendus Nandigram, Vijays Tamil Nadu Test: Why These Bypolls Matter Beyond The Seats - Faked Injury, Humiliated Nandigram: Suvendu Adhikari Orders Probe Into Mamatas 2021 Leg Injury - Faked Injury, Humiliated Nandigram: Suvendu Adhikari Orders Probe Into Mamatas 2021 Leg Injury - 'I Could Be Detained Too If...': Suvendu Adhikari Reacts To Humayun Kabir's Detention In Murshidabad The by-elections in Nandigram and Rejinagar mark a completely unprecedented chapter in West Bengals current political situation. For the first time in 15 years, the state voted under a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) administration, with chief minister Suvendu Adhikari leading the saffron government following their historic victory in May 2026. The polls took place after Adhikari announced that the government would soon implement Uniform Civil Code, anti love-Jihad and anti land-jihad laws. The constituencies Nandigram and Rejinagar that voted on Tuesday have 30 per cent and 70 per cent Muslim population respectively. In Nandigram, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (Mamata Banerjees faction) did not have a candidate, as the partys candidate withdrew nomination and it led former chief minister Mamata Banerjee to extend support to the Congress candidate. Meanwhile, Rejinagar in Murshidabad, appears to have witnessed an election in which the Opposition, though splintered, has participated as both offshoots of the erstwhile Trinamool Congress fought the polls. An Erasure and Splintering of the Opposition The defining characteristic of these bypolls is the structural collapse of the traditional opposition. Chief Minister Adhikari confidently claimed that the iconic twin-flower symbol of the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) has been effectively erased from the ballots. Following intense internal friction after their state election defeat, the TMC split into warring factions months back. In Nandigram, the epicentre of Bengals historical land agitations, the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction failed to even field a candidate after their nominee withdrew. Left with no options, Mamata Banerjee explicitly backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan under a tactical survival alliance. Meanwhile, a rival rebel TMC faction under Ritabrata Banerjee fielded its own candidate under a temporary envelope symbol. Combined with contestants from the CPI, the Left, and the Indian Secular Front (ISF), the non-BJP vote seems to be fragmented. The West Bengal bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar took place on October 6. The state voted under a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) administration for the first time in 15 years. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari leads the saffron government after their victory in May 2026. Nandigram has a 30 per cent Muslim population, and Rejinagar has a 70 per cent Muslim population. The All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) split into warring factions after their state election defeat. A New Political Equation West Bengal bypolls historically featured unified ruling party machineries dominating fragmented regional challengers. These two seats completely invert that model. For decades, Bengals politics was governed by a familiar binary. The Left once dominated the political space, the Trinamool Congress then emerged as the principal vehicle of anti-Left consolidation. Voters largely knew where the principal battle lay. The BJPs rise disrupted that arrangement. But the latest churn is doing something more significant it is fragmenting the Opposition space itself. Minority Outreach vs Hardline Governance What makes this double-bypoll functionally unique is how it forces the Adhikari administration to balance its ideological posturing with immediate electoral math. Nationally, the BJP government is actively advancing major legislative shifts, including a draft committee for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) and promises of strict legislation targeting religious conversions. Yet, the ground realities of these specific segments have forced a tactical shift in campaign rhetoric. Rejinagar holds an estimated 70 per cent Muslim voter demographic, while Nandigram maintains roughly 30 per cent. Rather than depending entirely on polarising themes, chief minister Adhikari spent the final days of the campaign actively wooing minority voters too, framing his party as a stable governance alternative for all communities. Ultimately, these choices will dictate the template for Bengals future. If the BJP retains Nandigram and makes deep incursions into Rejinagars minority blocks, it will prove that a splintered opposition can hardly counter the states rewritten political order. If the loose Congress-Mamata alliance strikes back, it may provide the first blueprint for how anti-BJP forces can survive under the new regime. The by-elections were necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the Nandigram seat in Purba Medinipur district, while AJUP founder Humayun Kabir did the same for the Rejinagar seat in Murshidabad.

headline: 'We Need To Land, He Doesn't Have Time': Dentist Reveals 45-Minute Battle To Save Smit Machchhar Mid-Air
content: According to Dr Musaev, the captain told him, Please help me. My God is with me. I want to live. I dont want to die here. For 45 minutes inside the stricken Flydubai aircraft, Israeli dentist Dr Shota Musaevs priority was to keep Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar alive until the plane could land. Machchhar had been brutally attacked by his co-pilot during Flight FZ1073, which was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30 with 174 people on board. The UAE authorities have described the incident as an attempted terrorist attack". The co-pilot, Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked Machchhar inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft. - Headphone Cords, Zip Ties & A Chokehold: How Passengers Subdued Flydubai Flight Attacker - Pilot, Plumber And An Ordinary Father: Meet The Heroes Who Saved 174 Lives On Flydubai Flight - First Visuals Of Injured Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar Surface After Flydubai Cockpit Attack - Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar Reveals Cockpit Attack: One Last Fight To Save Flight What followed was a desperate struggle involving the injured captain, passengers, crew and two off-duty pilots who helped prevent what could have been a catastrophic crash. Israel Was Prepared To Shoot Down Flydubai Plane With 150 Israelis Aboard After Cockpit Attack: Report Musaev, 47, was travelling with his wife on the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after connecting from China when he heard screams and a call for a doctor. Speaking to The National and ABC News, he recalled rushing towards the cockpit and finding Machchhar badly injured. There was heavy bleeding from his head and left hand," Musaev told The National. He initially used T-shirts to press against the wounds, but the bleeding continued. He then asked the cabin crew for ice. He had very, very deep cuts," Musaev said, describing how he kept pressure on the wounds while repeatedly applying ice. Every time he lifted the makeshift dressing to check the injuries, the bleeding worsened. Dr. Shota Musaev kept Captain Smit Machchhar alive for 45 minutes after an attack. Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv had 174 people on board. The co-pilot, Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, attacked Captain Machchhar with a crash axe. Captain Machchhar suffered a skull fracture, serious head and hand injuries, and damaged vision. The aircraft landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All through the 45 minutes, I kept the pressure on," he said. But controlling the bleeding was only part of the challenge. Musaev knew the badly wounded pilot also had to remain conscious. I told him, Please dont sleep, we need you," the dentist recalled. He asked Machchhar about his children and their names, trying to keep him talking and reassure him that he would see his family again. Machchhar, despite his injuries, was desperate to survive. According to Musaev, the captain told him, Please help me. My God is with me. I want to live. I dont want to die here." He complained repeatedly of intense pain in his head and a burning sensation in his hands. At one point, Machchhars condition deteriorated sharply. His pulse became dangerously low, prompting Musaev to raise his feet. The pulse returned. Later, when the pilots lips turned blue, Musaev realised there was little time left. We need to land quickly. He doesnt have much more time," he told a steward. Musaev also resisted attempts to give Machchhar pain medication. With the pilot suffering heavy blood loss and lying on his back, the dentist feared moving him or administering medicines could worsen the situation. Meanwhile, the crisis in the cockpit was still unfolding. Passengers helped restrain the co-pilot using headphone cables, while two standby pilots entered the cockpit with another passenger and helped stabilise the aircraft. Other passengers remained vigilant, fearing there could be additional attackers on board. The aircraft eventually landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where Machchhar was handed over to medical teams. He was later transferred to the UAE for specialised treatment. Smit Machchhar Health Update: Skull Fracture, Damaged Vision, Memory Problems The extent of Machchhars injuries has emerged gradually. Fresh details indicate that the captain suffered a skull fracture, serious injuries to his head and hand, and damage affecting his vision. His vision remains blurred, while he has also struggled to recall parts of the incident, describing his memories as being in bits and pieces". Reports also indicate that Machchhar underwent emergency surgery in Saudi Arabia to treat the severe skull injury before being moved to the UAE. He is now recovering at a specialised medical facility, with doctors closely monitoring his vision and neurological condition. Despite the ordeal, he remains determined to return to flying. For Musaev, the episode has also left deep psychological scars. He said he and his wife struggled to sleep after the incident and that he lost weight in the days that followed. Yet he rejects the idea that he alone was responsible for saving the captain. Smit saved our lives. Smit is a hero," Musaev said, adding that what happened on the plane was an example of passengers coming together in an extraordinary crisis. He saved our lives and we saved his life." The dentists account offers a glimpse into those tense 45 minutes between the attack and the emergency landing, when a wounded pilot fought to stay alive, passengers fought to regain control of the aircraft, and a dentist with no expectation of becoming part of the story used whatever he had at hand to keep a fellow passenger alive. On September 30, Flydubai Flight FZ1073 carrying 174 people experienced an attempted terrorist attack when the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, brutally attacked Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit. Passengers, crew, and off-duty pilots intervened to restrain the attacker, stabilize the aircraft, and execute an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

headline: Trump says nobody knows who is running Iran
content: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) that nobody knew who was running Iran during the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its eighth month. Their leaders are gone, their second group of leaders is gone, and the biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country, Mr. Trump said. Irans Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Sunday (October 4, 2026) Washington knows very well who its counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in Iran works. The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials, Esmaeil Baghaei said in a news conference. Irans Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which began on February 28. His son, Mojtaba Khamenei, succeeded him but has not been seen in public since he was injured in the same strike that killed his father. Iran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host U.S. bases. U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have killed thousands and displaced millions. Fuel prices that have risen in response to the war are also a risk to Mr. Trumps Republican Party ahead of the November U.S. midterm elections in which control of Congress is at stake. Mr. Trump, whose approval rating has held at a record low amid concerns of high cost of living spurred by soaring gasoline and diesel prices, has offered shifting timelines and goals for the war.

headline: Munich Security Conference CEO Benedikt Franke: 'India has said right things for years… not often lent its weight… It's finally walking the talk'
content: India has said right things for years not often lent its weight Its finally walking the talk Im absolutely thrilled that India is finally walking the talk. Prime Minister Modi has said the right things for a while on this issue, that there is a need for dialogue, for negotiations However, India didnt vote accordingly in the UN Now, not just the Ukrainian foreign minister but also President Putin (have) has said that the proposals received from the Indian side were the only ones he was seriously considering I hope more countries take note of this development We (Europe) believe that our best hope lies with countries like India and China that have a special relationship with Russia These countries are now finally ready to (use) their diplomatic weight and their relationship to support efforts to bring this war to an end We hope it doesnt lead to a situation in which the aggressor (Russia) is rewarded and the victim (Ukraine) is punished We, Europeans, will do everything we can to ensure that the Ukrainians end up in the strongest possible negotiation position I just hope India sort of doubles down on these very promising signs. * Why do you think the needle has moved for India? The Ukraine-Russia war comes at a cost for everyone. Countries like India need stability and predictability in global trade and relations India needs to continue on its growth trajectory, to pull hundreds of millions out of poverty Another (reason) is that multi-alignment is great on paper. It also comes to a natural limit at some point. Civilians are dying every day in Ukraine, civilian infrastructure is destroyed How can you be a liberal democracy, position yourself as a leader in this world on inter-State cooperation, on development, and not act on blatant breaches of international law? And then, India is becoming more ambitious in a lot of fields, putting stuff in space, being an economic or technological powerhouse. But, on the diplomatic front, I dont think Indias actions to date matched its self-perception. * Critics in Europe and the West say India is still buying Russian energy. India argues that it is acting in self-interest. Its perfectly okay to buy Russian oil and gas, but I wish that when you go into the shop to buy it, you dont kiss the shopkeeper Why do we need selfies at the BRICS summit? Why do we need the embrace between Modi and Putin? Maybe we are underestimating the close emotional ties between India and Russia We just hope that this special relationship can be, in a way, used to end the stalemate we are seeing. And by putting a little pressure on its favourite shopkeeper, India could make a major difference in the war. * What do you make of US President Donald Trumps efforts for peace in the Russia-Ukraine war? I have been criticised in the past for praising President Trump for trying. I think trying is better than not trying, and I wish there were a European-led effort, but there is not. And so, everyone that tries to solve this without throwing the Ukrainians in front of the bus deserves praise. I am not 100% sure that President Trumps efforts and the focus on or connection to business interests of the United States in Russian resources was very helpful It is perfectly okay for the United States to do business with Russia. At some point, I hope the European Union and India will do more business with Russia. At the end of the day, we want a stable, prosperous and constructive Russia. No one wants a tumbling giant like Russia But first, (it is) based on an expectation that this war comes to an end, that aggression ends, that the sovereign territory of Ukraine is restored If we have no agreement on that, having an agreement on business sends the wrong signal But I could imagine that if you Indians broke the ice now, the US joining such an effort would make a huge difference. * Is it still a stalemate after four-and a-half-years of the Ukraine war, and what does it mean for European security? For Ukraine, to be perfectly honest, its quite a success that they are still there. Europe has not done enough to help Ukraine win. Hence, it has not won. But we have done a lot to help them survive, get their house in order, and become a leader in defence technology. They are now producing most of the stuff they need themselves We need to appreciate that this country, which is only a quarter of the population of Russia and only a fraction of its economic potential, has held out for four years I dont want to paint a rosy picture. The winter will be terrible. The Russians have destroyed so much energy and other infrastructure But they (the Ukrainians) are still there on a lot of sovereign territory, and here and there, they actually win battles, produce what we call iconoclastic victories and deep strikes into Russian territory. They, by the way, never attack civilian infrastructure Now the question is, will Europe step up its effort to bring Ukraine into a good negotiating position? Will the US realise once again who the actual aggressor is? Will India and other powerhouses put a little pressure on Putin? I have no answer. * How do you see the energy security issue playing out given the war in West Asia, on top of the Russia-Ukraine conflict? I am quite pessimistic that without a larger alliance of countries working, this conflict will be solved any time soon. I do not believe in some American predictions. I do not believe in the miraculous disappearance of the Houthis. I do not believe in a sudden end to Iranian ambitions I wish for a stronger European role, a stronger American role, and a stronger Asian role in finding a diplomatic solution. I fear there is an implicit assumption of a division of labour globally in these conflicts. Europeans believe that is American-caused and it needs to be American-solved. Americans believe that Ukraine is Europes problem. If we continue this silo thinking I dont think we will see a solution (The Iran conflict) is also driving up prices in Germany at a time when our domestic politics are in a difficult place, when our industry is in a difficult place. That increases the chances of the right or the left fringes of the political spectrum to win. * Do you think the rise of the right and the extreme right is here to stay, especially in Germany? As long as the political centre doesnt find clear answers to some of the worries that the population in Germany, but also across the world, has personal security, job prospects, prosperity for their kids, crime, migration, culture and enters into a national debate on these, the political extremes will be further empowered Global governance, global multilateralism, will not be revitalised How many Indians believe that the UN is their best chance? How many Indians put real faith into the World Bank and the IMF? Take their worries, justified or not, seriously, and provide real, value-added solutions. If we dont, the extreme ends will win, and whether its left or right really makes no difference. In Germany, the extreme left is pretty close to the extreme right. * Germany has a very close relationship with China, and the recent meeting between US President Trump and President Xi Jinping indicates some kind of rapprochement. The two superpowers need to de-escalate, need to clear the air occasionally. Hence it is to be welcomed Its perfectly okay to be friends with China and the US at the same time, as it is perfectly okay for India to try to be friends with everyone at the same time. I mean, if multi-alignment works for you, why shouldnt it work for us? There is still an issue with human rights. But, at the end of the day, we want a strong, prosperous China that engages constructively in international relations. * You have been coming to India for at least a decade now. How do you see Indias perception about itself, and its perception from where you sit in Germany? I love coming to this country because the feeling of dynamism, of optimism, is just infectious and great Indian interlocutors have become more confident. They see their economic growth rate. They see the many Indian success stories, the space programme. (But) With superpower status come responsibilities. At some point, multi-alignment will come to a natural limit. You will have to choose sides on certain issues at some point India has said the right things for many years. It hasnt necessarily put its full weight behind these statements.

headline: Suspected Toxic Gas Kills 4 Students Cleaning Underground Water Tank In UP's Vrindavan
content: The incident took place after students noticed a foul smell coming from the tank, which was around 12 to 14 feet deep. Four students died and another was injured after they were exposed to suspected toxic gas while cleaning an underground water tank at a residential Sanskrit school in Vrindavans Chaitanya Vihar, officials said on Wednesday. The incident took place after students noticed a foul smell coming from the tank, which was around 12 to 14 feet deep. The students first used a motor to remove water before attempting to clean the remaining water and sludge. - Doda Medical College Hijab Row: Students Protest After Abaya Removal Claim | - France Gripped By Violent Student Protests: Why Thousands Are On The Streets And Whats Happening - Ambedkar University Delhi Revises Attendance Rules For PhD Scholars Receiving Fellowships - The Right Tablets Under Rs. 25,000 for Students, Streamers, And Multitaskers According to officials, one student entered the tank but soon became unconscious. Four others went inside in an attempt to rescue him, but they too collapsed. All five were pulled out and taken to hospital. Four Students Die, One Survives District Magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh said four students, aged between 17 and 20, died in the incident. Their bodies were sent to the mortuary and their families were being informed. The fifth student, identified as Rudra, survived and was receiving treatment. SSP Shlok Kumar said he was conscious and able to speak. He was initially taken to the district hospital before being referred for closer monitoring. The Mathura Police said the incident occurred at Vrindavan Gurukulam, where students live and study. Probe Ordered Into Tank Cleaning Singh said a magisterial inquiry would be held to establish how the incident occurred and whether the gurukulam had the required recognition. A magisterial inquiry would be conducted to ascertain how the incident occurred, whether the gurukulam had the required recognition and under what circumstances the students were made to clean the water tank," he said. The inquiry will also examine why students were made to clean the underground tank and whether proper safety measures were in place. Officials said CCTV footage from the premises would be examined as part of the investigation. The police will also take further legal action based on complaints filed by the families of the deceased students. The district administration has also decided to conduct fresh checks of other gurukulams in the area. Their buildings and facilities will be inspected to identify possible safety risks and prevent similar incidents. The Chief Minister has taken cognisance of the incident and directed officials to ensure rescue efforts and proper medical treatment for the surviving student, officials said. (With inputs from ANI) Four students died after being exposed to a suspected toxic gas while cleaning an underground water tank at a residential Sanskrit school in Vrindavan's Chaitanya Vihar.

headline: Three with Bhatti links held in J&K, one in Punjab; items 'drone-dropped from Pakistan' seized
content: The Jammu & Kashmir Police on Tuesday claimed to have arrested four people, including a Punjab resident, for allegedly being members of a cross-border narco-terror module with links in Pakistan. Police claimed the accused had links with Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti. The arrested persons included two residents of Talhar, both called Ajay Kumar who went by the aliases Rabb and Sam, respectively, and one Rahul from Treva. Police claimed they have seized an Italian-made Bretta pistol along with two magazines and four live rounds, besides 500 grams of heroin and opium each from them. The seized items were reportedly dropped by drone from Pakistan, a police official said. Police said all three accused are in their early 20s and are drug addicts. Following their interrogation, a man called Jaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi was arrested from Punjab. The lid was taken off the module after a police party apprehended Rabb and Rahul on October 3 and seized a pistol along with ammunition and nearly 500 grams of heroin. On their disclosure during preliminary questioning, police nabbed Sam and seized nearly 500 grams of opium from him, officials said. Shahzad Bhatti link Officials said that the accused had links with Bhatti, a Pakistani handler operating under the patronage of ISI, who used to send them consignments of arms, ammunition and narcotics through drone from across the international border for further delivery to members of the module in Punjab. During questioning, they admitted having received two drone-droppings the first one containing nearly half-a-dozen pistols a few months ago. While delivering that consignment to some people who had come to the region from Punjab, Rahul had kept one of the pistols for himself, which later led to his arrest, a police official said. The second drone-dropping, this time containing narcotics, was received a few days ago, which the accused had buried near a tubewell to avoid detection, police added. A case has been registered under relevant sections, and further investigation is in progress to unearth a wider network and members of the cross border narco-terror module. Security agencies have already raised concern over the use of drones by terrorist handlers and cross-border smugglers in Pakistan to send weapons and narcotics into Jammu and Kashmir. The agencies, in a massive pre-Independence Day operation launched simultaneously across 14 states, detained nearly 250 people allegedly linked to the Bhatti network. Arms, grenades and surveillance material were collected from them. The operation followed intelligence inputs, warning of attempts by terror operatives of strikes ahead of I-Day celebrations.

headline: French riot police fire tear gas as more than 2,50,000 rally nationwide for school funding
content: Police fired tear gas to control crowds in Paris and elsewhere in France on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) as more than a quarter of a million people rallied nationwide to support high school students demanding more education funding, according to government figures. The protests increased pressure on the administration of outgoing President Emmanuel Macron. As pupils blockaded high schools, large crowds waving flags and placards gathered in Marseille, Strasbourg and other cities. The demonstrations showed how protests that began at a high school in the Paris region in mid-September have grown into a nationwide movement the latest of many that have marked Macron's nearly decade-long tenure. We need to listen to them, said La Monimart, an adult demonstrator in the northern city of Lille. They are 17 years old; they are not completely clueless, and they know what they are talking about. It's important to show that there are adults who support them. The Interior Ministry estimated that 2,66,000 people took part in demonstrations across the country on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), including 56,000 in Paris, where small groups of protesters clashed with riot officers at a city square at the end of a largely peaceful march. Nearly 500 people were detained Tuesday (October 6, 2026), the Ministry said. The widespread use of arrests, tear gas and riot-control weapons against teenagers is fueling defiance and angering some parents and teachers. Some student groups called for new protests Thursday (October 8, 2026). Interior Minister Laurent Nuez said the police response had been proportionate in almost all cases and that the protests had at times turned into riots, requiring police intervention. French Prime Minister Sbastien Lecornu said the government and school leaders must listen to students' concerns and find solutions. Questioned in parliament on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) about the protest movement, Mr. Lecornu denounced ultra violence threatening schools. Responding to criticism of police tactics, he pledged that any accidents would be investigated and described allegations that the police are racist as a lie.

headline: 'Not Going To Trade Words For Actions': Vance Says Iran Must Cut Nuclear Enrichment To End War
content: Vance said the US was still open to a deal but would seek concrete action from Tehran rather than promises about future nuclear limits. US Vice President JD Vance has told Reuters that Iran must make a meaningful" reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity for Washington to agree to an end to the seven-month war between the two countries. In an exclusive interview, Vance said the US was still open to a deal but would seek concrete action from Tehran rather than promises about future nuclear limits. - Has Trump Softened On Iran? JD Vances Shift On Uranium Enrichment Sparks Fresh Questions - JD Vance On Iran: U.S. Demands Major Nuclear Concession To End War | U.S. Iran War | - US-Iran Tensions Rise: Rubio Orders Iranian Envoys Out Of New York As Trump Issues Ultimatum - No Military Solution: Iran Warns Of Stronger Response, Keeps Door Open To Talks If you dont want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?" Vance said. If you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, dont build highly enriched fuel. Thats a very basic threshold issue." I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity," he added. US Seeks Concrete Nuclear Concessions Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy shipments. US President Donald Trump has rejected Tehrans latest proposal and warned that military operations could intensify after the November midterm elections. Vance, who has played a central role in efforts to negotiate an end to the conflict, said Washington would not accept verbal assurances alone. Were not going to trade words for actions," he said. The war has disrupted energy markets and increased pressure on the Trump administration as higher fuel prices become a political issue ahead of the US midterms. Vance Questions Irans Decision-Making Vance also said Washington remained uncertain about who ultimately makes key decisions in Tehran. The US has been negotiating with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, but Vance questioned how much authority they have within Irans political system. One of the things we picked up on is its not totally clear how their country makes decisions," he said. Iran rejected that assessment. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said US officials know who their Iranian counterparts are and understand Irans decision-making system. The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Baghaei said. Vance also told Reuters that he had spoken with US field commanders about the war and dismissed concerns over shortages of critical munitions. He said Iranian forces could still strike commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz but were largely unable to stop energy exports through the waterway. Vance said he had not decided whether he would run for president in 2028, saying: Im inherently a procrastinator. I really havent thought about it much." (With inputs from Reuters) US Vice President JD Vance stated that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity, specifically questioning why they need 60 percent enriched fuel if they do not want a nuclear weapon.

headline: Trump Says He'll Speak To Putin Soon Over Reported Plague Death As US Presses For Transparency
content: Trump said he had a call scheduled with Putin. The development came a day after Trump said the US was ready to help Russia if needed. US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he would speak to Russian President Vladimir Putin very soon" over the reported death of a laboratory technician at an anti-plague institute in Russia, as Washington pressed Moscow for more information. Trump said he had a call scheduled with Putin when asked whether he had discussed the case with the Russian leader. The development came a day after Trump said the US was ready to help Russia if needed. - 'Was In A Very Bad Shape But Still Had Sense': Trump Calls Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar A 'Hero' After Flydubai Incident - 'Looking At It Very Strongly': Trump Offers US Help As Russia Downplays Plague Reports - 'Why Leave Them There?': Trump Says US Pulled Bombers From UK Air Base Over 'Some Threats' - 'Sooner Or Later It Must Go Off': Putin Says World Cannot Rule Out Nuclear Weapons Use US Seeks Transparency US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Moscow to share more details about the incident, saying greater transparency would help countries respond appropriately. We encourage Russia to be transparent and share more information with the world so that all of us could react accordingly and appropriately," Rubio said during a visit to Iceland. The Wall Street Journal reported that the US State Department had sent Moscow a confidential diplomatic communication warning that withholding information could conflict with international health obligations. Russia Rejects Plague Reports Russian authorities have denied reports of a confirmed plague case or special anti-plague measures in the Siberian city of Irkutsk. Reports said a 28-year-old technician, identified as Darya Shipilova, may have contracted pneumonic plague after a laboratory accident. Russian officials, however, said tests had not detected the disease. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said an inspection found that the woman had died from pneumonia, while the cause remained undetermined". He added that no microorganisms linked to her work were found in her samples and that no other institute employees had sought medical care. Russias health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor also said an online document claiming special measures had been introduced was not genuine. We wish to clarify that the document and information in question do not originate from official sources and are untrue," it said on Telegram. WHO Calls For Clarity The World Health Organization said Russia had reported no confirmed plague case in Irkutsk and had launched an investigation into a case of community-acquired pneumonia involving an employee of the institute. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for timely, complete and transparent information sharing" to resolve conflicting reports and assess any possible public health risk. The WHO said the risk to Irkutsk was currently moderate to low" based on available information and that it was monitoring the situation. Plague is a bacterial disease, with pneumonic plague being the most contagious form. It can spread through respiratory droplets and can be fatal if treatment is delayed. (With inputs from agencies) US President Donald Trump announced plans to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin following the reported death of a laboratory technician at an anti-plague institute. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Moscow to share more details to help other countries respond appropriately, while the State Department warned that withholding information could breach international health obligations.

headline: MPs wanted a meeting in Parliament Annexe against protocol, says Election Commission
content: Saying that no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm Tuesday, the Election Commission (EC) said it was later informed by police that the Opposition Members of Parliament (MPs) wanted a meeting at Parliament House Annexe. It said this request was unusual, because, as per protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India. The EC said it still offered to send a senior officer to receive their memorandum, but the MPs rejected its proposal. Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some MPs wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to todays developments, it is clarified that, till 4 pm today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission, the poll panel said in its statement on Tuesday evening. The EC said it was informed by the Delhi Police, around 4 pm that a delegation of MPs led by the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the Commission to submit a memorandum. After 4 pm today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the above-mentioned meeting with the Honble MPs, it was informed by the DCP, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request as unusual and therefore, could not be accepted, as, in accordance with ECI protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India, it said. The EC said it still proposed to send its most senior officer on duty to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum, which in itself would have been an unprecedented step. However, this offer was also declined by the Honble MPs, the Commission said. ECI respects the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country, as well as its own protocols and conventions, which are of utmost importance. Any political party may, at any time, request for a meeting with the Election Commission; and the Commission, keeping in view the suitability of time, schedules a date and time for the meeting. This is a regular practice, it said. It pointed to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties. All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides, it said.

headline: North Korea warns U.S. over Taiwan while Kim pledges support for Russia
content: North Korea criticised the United States over its arms sales and military support for Taiwan, accusing Washington of fuelling tensions in the Taiwan Strait, state media KCNA said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). A KCNA commentary citing North Korean international affairs analyst Kim Myong Chol said U.S. policy on Taiwan was undermining peace and stability in the region. The commentary condemned the appearance of U.S.-sold fighter aircraft in Taiwan, saying the U.S. should think twice whether it is ready to stand in frontal confrontation with the powerful national power of the Peoples of China for the security of Taiwan and whether it can cope with its consequences. The first two of a batch of 66 new F-16V Block 70 fighter jets ordered in 2019 arrived in Taiwan last week, as Taiwan faces a rising military threat from Beijing which claims the democratically governed island as its own territory. Meanwhile, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pledged continued support for Russia and its war effort in a birthday message to President Vladimir Putin, state media KCNA said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). Mr. Kim said Pyongyang would continue to expand joint work under the countries comprehensive strategic partnership, saying he was convinced that Russias sacred war of justice to defend its sovereignty, security interests and territorial integrity would end in victory, KCNA said. The message did not explicitly mention Russias war in Ukraine. North Korea has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 troops to support Russias war in Ukraine since 2024, according to Ukrainian and South Korean estimates. North Korea and Russia have strengthened ties sharply since Putin and Kim signed a mutual defence pact in June 2024.

headline: Press Council of India operating at half strength, without a single working journalist or newspaper editor
content: THE COUNTRYS key media watchdog, Press Council of India (PCI), has been operating at half its sanctioned strength for nearly a year now and without a single working journalist or newspaper editor. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) has not yet formally notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, six of whom should be newspaper editors and seven should be working journalists other than editors, despite the PCI nominating them earlier this year. Ironically, the PCI remained without a chairman for nearly four months until Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, a retired Supreme Court judge, was reappointed to the post in April this year. Justice Desai had completed her previous tenure in December last year, resulting in a prolonged vacancy before her reappointment. The PCI operates under the Press Council Act, 1978, which stipulates that the Council must consist of a chairperson and 28 members, each serving a three-year term. The members include six newspaper owners, one representative from news agencies, five Members of Parliament and three persons with special knowledge or practical experience in education, science, law, literature and culture, nominated by the University Grants Commission, the Bar Council of India and the Sahitya Akademi, respectively. In addition, the Council includes six newspaper editors and seven working journalists. The Act therefore mandates the appointment of 13 newspaper editors and working journalists. However, after the 14th Press Council completed its term in October 2024, the 15th Press Council has yet to be fully constituted. At present, only 14 of the 28 members have been appointed: five MPs, three nominees and six from among newspaper owners and management, aside from the chairperson. The documents further show that the PCI sent three communications to the I&B Ministry separately dated May 25, July 2 and September 9 requesting it to issue the Gazette notification under Section 5(5) of the Act. The section states that the Central Government shall notify the names of persons nominated as members in the Official Gazette, and that each nomination shall take effect from the date of notification. In its latest communication to the Ministry, dated September 9, the PCI requested that the Gazette notification for the 13 members be issued at the earliest. It said it had received communications from nominees expressing concern over the delay in officially notifying their appointments as PCI members. In the earlier communication dated July 2, the PCI asked the Ministry to expedite the notification of the 12 individuals it had nominated to the Council by that date. This is essential to enable the 15th term of the Council to become fully representative and functional so that it can discharge its regular responsibilities, the letter stated. The matter, it is learnt, is under process at the Ministrys end. The PCI has continued to hold meetings despite functioning with half its sanctioned strength. It held its last meeting in June, and another is scheduled for later this month. The issue was also raised in Parliament in February by BJD legislator Sasmit Patra, who highlighted the serious implications of the absence of a duly constituted Council and a chairperson. He urged the government to treat the matter with the seriousness it deserved and take immediate steps to appoint a chairperson and constitute the 15th Press Council. Restoring the full functioning of the PCI is essential to uphold democratic values, strengthen media accountability and reaffirm the governments commitment to a free, fair and responsible press, he said.

content: Zelenskyy particularly called for political backing from the United States and Europe, urging countries with the necessary defensive capabilities to provide support. Weve got updated intel on Russias preparations for a massive strike. I ask you, please, to take care of yourselves and respond to missile threat alerts," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address on X. - Towering Black Smoke Seen Over Russia Coast After Ukraine Hits Tanker; All 23 Indian Crew Rescued - India Steps In To Mediate Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire; Kyiv Calls Indian Proposal 'Most Comprehensive' - 24 Killed, 60 Injured In Fresh Russian Missile, Drone Strikes On Ukraine - 15,000 More Troops, $202.58-Bn Defence Spending For 2027: Decoding Putin's Moves Amid War With Ukraine He said Ukrainian forces and the air force were ready to respond, but stressed that their ability to defend against the Russian assault would depend on the weapons available to them.
