Two crew members were killed and 11 were rescued. The Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew. One of them was injured and receiving medical treatment. (With inputs from agencies) Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that fresh intelligence indicates Russia is preparing a "massive attack" on Ukraine, urging citizens to monitor missile threat alerts and take necessary safety precautions.

headline: 'Entire Career Ahead': Delhi Court Grants Bail To 17 Youths Arrested At Jantar Mantar Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: The court observed that the majority of the accused students and journalists are young individuals with non-habitual criminal records A Delhi court has granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists who were arrested during high-voltage demonstrations at Jantar Mantar targeting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Judicial Magistrate First Class Animesh Kumar at Patiala House Court ordered their immediate release, noting that the right to peaceful protest remains fundamental, provided it does not cross into violence. The ruling provides significant relief following a tense standoff in the capital, where security forces clashed with student activists and media personnel. - Jantar Mantar Protest Highlights: Atishi, Sanjay Singh Among 700 Detained, Internet Suspended Till 9 PM Amid Section 163 Restrictions - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC Court Cites Age and Non-Habitual Status In four separate orders, the court observed that the majority of the accused are young individuals with non-habitual criminal records. The bench emphasised that the charges invokedprimarily relating to obstructing public spaces and resisting police officers under Section 132 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)carry a maximum sentence of two years and are largely bailable. Highlighting that the accused have their entire careers lying ahead", the magistrate ruled that continued detention was unwarranted. Each demonstrator was granted bail upon furnishing a personal bond with one surety. Judicial Directives on Injuries and Police Charges Addressing claims raised regarding physical scuffles during detentions, the court directed the jail superintendent to ensure immediate medical care for those injured during the protest or subsequent police action. The order specifically mandated that proper medical evaluation be conducted as advised by official medical officers. A Delhi court granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists. Judicial Magistrate First Class Animesh Kumar at Patiala House Court ordered their immediate release. The court observed that the majority of the accused are young individuals with non-habitual criminal records. The charges invoked carry a maximum sentence of two years and are largely bailable. The court imposed specific compliance conditions on all 17 individuals for their release. While granting relief, the court acknowledged the severity of police allegations regarding physical resistance, manhandling of personnel, and disruption of transit routes. The bench reiterated that while expressing opposition is legally protected, assaulting officers on duty remains a grave concern that cannot be countenanced under the guise of agitation. Conditions Applied for Release To ensure smooth judicial proceedings moving forward, the court imposed specific compliance conditions on all 17 individuals. The released students and journalists must maintain active mobile contact numbers, refrain from committing further offences, regularly attend all scheduled court dates, and seek prior judicial permission before travelling outside India. With the bail orders dispatched to the New Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police for compliance, the decision marks a critical legal juncture in the ongoing political friction surrounding the Election Commission. A Delhi court granted bail to 17 students and freelance journalists, citing that they were young individuals with non-habitual criminal records who had their entire careers ahead of them, and that the charges of obstructing public spaces carried a maximum sentence of two years and were bailable.

headline: Omar Abdullah's Claim On Rohingyas Factually Wrong Since India Does Not Recognise Them As UNHCR Refugees, Say Experts
content: The J&K Chief Minister had said that Rohingyas got shelter in Jammu after international conventions were violated in Myanmar, and driving them out is wrong Chief Minister Omar Abdullahs statement that Rohingyas in Jammu are living under international conventions and as UN-recognised refugees is factually incorrect and against Indias official position. Top defence experts and former DGP Dr SP Vaid, while speaking with , have clarified that India has no agreement to give refugee status to Rohingyas and that, under Indian law, all foreigners without valid passports are treated as illegal migrants, on par with economic immigrants. - Why Stop At Padma Bhushan?: Omar Abdullah Bats For Bharat Ratna For CEC Gyanesh Kumar - Omar Abdullah Delaying Local Body Polls Fearing Defeat: BJP Vows To Take To The Streets To Highlight J&K Govt's Failures - United Against BJP, Divided Within: NC, Congress Spar Over Panchayat Polls In Jammu And Kashmir - Unity In Peril? Before INDIA Bloc's 'Save Democracy' March, NC-PDP Rift Spills Out In Jammu Omar Abdullah had said that Rohingyas got shelter in Jammu after international conventions were violated in Myanmar and driving them out like this is wrong. But experts say there is no such binding convention on India. Omar Abdullah on Tuesday said, This is a humanitarian issue. They are not here illegally. They got shelter after international conventions were violated. If you can send them back, send them. But till they are here, we cannot let them die of hunger or cold." But this claim does not stand on facts. spoke with prominent defence expert and former DGP of Jammu & Kashmir Dr SP Vaid on this issue. Dr Vaid said, Indias position on this is very clear. We have no agreement to treat Rohingyas as refugees. India does not register Rohingyas as refugees. UNHCR may give them cards, but the Government of India does not officially recognise those UNHCR cards. Under Indian law, all foreigners without a valid passport/visa are treated as foreigners, as illegal migrants, just like economic immigrants and tourists. What Omar Abdullah is saying is wrong." India does not register Rohingyas as refugees. India is not a signatory to the 1951 UN Refugee Convention. Around 40,000 Rohingyas are living in India, with UNHCR registering about 22,500. The Government of India stated in May 2025 that UNHCR cards offer no protection from detention. The MHA issued an advisory in 2017 to states to identify and deport Rohingyas as illegal immigrants. Defence experts also said that India is not a signatory to the 1951 UN Refugee Convention. Therefore, the so-called international convention argument does not apply to India. The Government of India in the Supreme Court in May 2025 itself said that UNHCR cards offer no protection from detention and Rohingyas are liable to be dealt with under the Foreigners Act and the new Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. According to MHA data, around 40,000 Rohingyas are living in India, out of which UNHCR has registered around 22,500 and given them identity cards. But those cards only help to get access to some basic services; they do not give legal right to stay in India. Experts say Omar Abdullahs attempt to link Rohingyas with Bangladeshis is also misleading. If a Bangladeshi is staying illegally, he is also an illegal immigrant. Rohingyas cannot be given separate treatment. Both are foreigners without valid documents. The BJP has hit back strongly at Omar Abdullahs humanitarian pitch. BJP President for J&K Sat Sharma said that Rohingyas living in Jammu are a major security threat. Jammu is a border city, just a few kilometres from the Pakistan border. Their settlement here is not humanitarian; it is a political conspiracy. Sharma said, How can the Chief Minister defend Rohingyas? Intelligence inputs have time and again said that Rohingyas are involved in terror funding, drug peddling and changing demography. They have been found involved in illegal activities in Jammu, Hyderabad and Delhi. To give them water and electricity connections on humanitarian grounds when Jammu people face power cuts is appeasement." BJP has demanded a CBI probe into who brought Rohingyas to Jammu and settled them in colonies like Bhatindi, Sunjwan, Narwal, which are sensitive from a security point of view. BJP says in 2017, MHA had issued an advisory to all states to identify and deport Rohingyas as they are illegal immigrants. It is worth mentioning that Omar Abdullah has been taking this stand since 2017. In 2017, when the BJP demanded their deportation, Omar had said that till 2014, in Unified Headquarters meetings, Rohingyas were never flagged as a security threat; this narrative came after 2014. But security agencies refute it. They say threat assessment changes with time. In recent years, many Rohingyas have been found with fake Aadhaar and PAN cards and have been involved in human trafficking networks operating from the Bangladesh-Myanmar border to Jammu. On the ground, Jammu Municipal Corporation has started a drive to disconnect illegal water and electricity connections of Rohingya colonies on the directions of MHA, after a verification drive found that many are living on encroached JDA land without any valid document. But with the Chief Minister himself calling it a humanitarian issue and saying we cannot treat them like animals, they are humans", a clear Centre vs State confrontation is emerging over Rohingyas again. Political observers say Omar Abdullah is trying to balance his vote bank, as his statement came just a day before INDIA Blocs Save Democracy rally in Jammu, where he will share the stage with Congress and PDP, both of whom have a soft corner for Rohingyas. But the fact remains, as confirmed by Former DGP Dr SP Vaid and the legal position of the Government of India: India does NOT register Rohingyas as UNHCR refugees; India has no agreement to give them refugee status, and under Indian law they are treated as foreigners / illegal migrants, the same as economic immigrants. So Omar Abdullahs argument that international conventions give them the right to shelter in Jammu has no factual basis. Under Indian law, all foreigners without valid passports or visas are treated as illegal migrants and economic immigrants. India is not a signatory to the 1951 UN Refugee Convention and does not officially recognise UNHCR refugee cards, meaning they offer no protection from detention under the Foreigners Act.

headline: 'Begani Shaadi Mein Mera Kya Kaam?': Owaisi On Why AIMIM Gave INDIA Bloc's EC March A Miss
content: The AIMIM chief, however, said he had his own concerns about the Election Commission and the appointment process for the CEC. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Tuesday said he did not join the INDIA blocs protest march to the Election Commission in Delhi because his party is not part of the alliance, while calling for changes to the process of selecting the Chief Election Commissioner. Speaking to reporters in Hyderabad, Owaisi said, I did not go there because I am not a part of that (alliance). Begani shaadi mein mera kya kaam?" - 'Muslims Not Your Personal Property': Owaisi Targets Samajwadi Party, Offers Alliance To Stop BJP's Third UP Term - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - Opposition March To Election Commission Turns Dramatic | Gyanesh Kumar | SIR Row | - How Convenient, Pookie: Posters Taking Potshots At Rahul, Akhilesh Splash Delhi Ahead Of INDIA Bloc Meet The AIMIM chief, however, said he had his own concerns about the Election Commission and the appointment process for the CEC. The INDIA bloc march in Delhi was aimed at pressing its demands over the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police detained around 260 protesters, including 10 MPs, after stopping the march. Owaisi Wants CJI On CEC Panel Owaisi called the existing process for selecting the CEC as the biggest problem", saying it gives too much influence to the executive. Under the 2023 law, the selection committee consists of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister. Owaisi called for the law to be changed so that the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition jointly select the CEC. The process for the selection of Chief Election Commissioner, which is wrong. It is completely in favour of the executiveThe process needs to be changed," he said, adding that the present system needed to be corrected. SIR Is NRC Through Backdoor Owaisi also renewed his criticism of the SIR exercise, saying he had raised concerns about it during the process in Bihar. This SIR is wrong. I believe that SIR is an NRC through the backdoor," he said. His comments came as opposition parties stepped up their campaign against the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul, Priyanka Detained The INDIA bloc protest in Delhi ended after a prolonged standoff with police. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other opposition leaders staged a sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan after police stopped them from marching towards the EC office. Delhi Police later detained the protesters, saying the march had not been granted permission and that restrictions were in place in the area. The opposition has been protesting over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and has demanded action over its concerns regarding the SIR exercise. (With inputs from PTI) Asaduddin Owaisi stated that he did not join the INDIA bloc's protest march to the Election Commission because his party is not part of the opposition alliance, famously remarking, "Begani shaadi mein mera kya kaam?"

headline: Residents of western suburbs call for regulation of spaces beneath flyovers
content: Residents of the western suburbs, including Pattabiram, Thandurai, and Thiruninravur, have urged the Highways Department to regulate the spaces, beneath flyovers and service lanes, which are mostly encroached upon by vendors. Poor maintenance Motorists also complained about the lack of maintenance, such as the painting of rail overbridges in Thiruninravur, Veppampattu, Thandurai, and Pattabiram. Thandurai resident K.S. Gopalakrishnan said that several shops occupied space on the service lanes of the flyover that replaced the LC-10 railway gate in their area, creating traffic bottlenecks during the morning and evening hours. Several two-wheelers belonging to customers take up the remaining space, causing inconvenience to residents of these localities, including Gopalapuram and Vallalar Nagar. Ambulances, cars, and even autorickshaws struggle to navigate these roads. Commuters taking trains from the nearby Pattabiram station also park their vehicles here, he said. These encroachments under the bridge and along the service lanes were there for nearly 15 years without any interference from an agency, said another resident. Jayaraman of Pattabiram said that the recently completed flyover at Veppampattu and the one under construction at LC2 Pattabiram Railway Siding also had encroachments. Lighting under these bridges is not much, which leads to all kinds of unwanted activities. Food joints come up without any permissions. People are scared to go to such spaces after dark as there is absolutely no police presence, the resident said. Road users rights Consumer activist T. Sadagopan said that it is necessary to regulate the shops and the parking spaces beneath the flyovers and the service lanes. People talk of the rights of the vendors, then what about that of the road users for whom these facilities were primarily created? We would like some greenery and walking spaces under these flyovers, not illegal shops. The flyovers should also be decorated with wall art and murals like those inside the city. There are shops constructed by the Avadi Corporation that remain empty as the rents are exorbitant. Street vending zones must be created like in the case of Greater Chennai Corporation. Sources in the Highways Department said that steps would be taken, along with the local body, police and Revenue department, to remove the encroachments.

headline: Forest Department destroys 125 illegal country-made guns in Tiruvannamalai
content: The Forest Department destroyed 125 illegal country-made guns using a road roller at the Office of the District Collector in Tiruvannamalai town on Tuesday, as part of Wildlife Week Celebrations. Forest officials said that the drive was aimed to prevent illegal hunting and to protect wildlife under the provisions of Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Forest officials approached tribals living on the fringes of forests to voluntarily surrender illegal country-made firearms in their possession. General amnesty to volunteers who surrender country-made guns have helped recover these illegal firearms from the public. Support from the public is key to prevent such possession of firearms, S. Gunasekaran, forest range officer (FRO), Jamunamarathur range (Jawadhu Hills), told . Collector Vandana Garg launched the drive to destroy seized illegal firearms at the Collectorate in the presence of R. Udhayakumar, Superintendent of Police, K. Sudhagar, District Forest Officer, A. Sivasubramania Pillai, District Revenue Officer, and G. Vinothraj, Assistant Conservator of Forests. Among the forest ranges, Nadanur forest range has the highest number of firearms (41) that were destroyed at the Collectorate, followed by Santhavasal (22), Melpattu (19), Polur (17) and Jamunamarathur (15). Forest officials reach out to tribal elders in the hills to convince residents in hamlets to give up country-made guns, said S. Vembu, a resident. Forest officials said that traditionally, tribals possessed illegal country-made guns to guard themselves from wild animals, thefts, and hunting purposes. These guns also helped farmers transport their produce from the hillock to foothills and safely return home with their earnings. With better roads, policing, and transport facilities, such possession of illegal arms is no longer required, said Mr. Vinothraj. Forest officials said that the general amnesty that was offered by the Forest Department and the district police in 2016 and 2021 have helped many people, especially tribals in the hills, to voluntarily surrender illegal firearms. Awareness, including door-to-door meetings with residents, about the voluntary surrender of illegal firearms were to be continued.

headline: Vellore police hands over missing phones to owners
content: The district police in Vellore have handed over 300 lost and found mobile phones, worth 60 lakh, to its respective owners on Tuesday. These phones were recovered by the Vellore district cybercrime. The initiative comes after the formation of a Cyber Crime police unit at the SP office in the district, and the introduction of a cell tracker application where for complaints to be registered. Superintendent of Police N.U. Sivaraman handed over the phones to its owners at his office in Vellore town. So far, the police have returned 2,588 mobile phones worth around 5.05 crore. The cybercrime team had been monitoring the missing mobile phone handsets through their IMEI number at periodical intervals. Lost phones were tracked using IMEI numbers. The police said that whenever the missing phones were activated, either by those who find them on the road or by those who bought these phones second-hand without proper verification, the cybercrime police team alerts the user. The users either hand them over to the police or send them through courier from other districts and States. Using cybercrime cells, all complaints of snatching or missing mobiles phones were taken up for investigation.

headline: RPF, Nemili police seize 16 kg of ganja in separate cases; four persons held
content: Four drug peddlers were arrested, and 16 kg of ganja was seized in two separate surprise checks by the Railway Protection Force (RPF) and the Nemili police in Ranipet on Tuesday. The police said that in the first incident, K. Vikram, 26, B. Deepak Kumar, 22, I. Yabesh, 24, and S. Anjanappa, 27, were arrested by Nemili police near Arakkonam town. Initial inquiry revealed that Nemili police were conducting a surprise check on Panapakkam Main Road, when they saw a gang attempting to flee after they noticed police on the stretch. However, they were nabbed. The police team also seized 6 kg of ganja from them. The drug peddlers were allegedly selling small quantities of ganja at public places in surrounding villages near Nemili and Arakkonam towns. A case was registered. and the arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. In a separate incident, surprise searches by a team of RFP and GRP personnel on express trains at Arakkonam railway station was conducted on Tuesday, when the team found 10 kg of ganja. The police said that a gang of three persons had alighted from the train when they noticed the team. They abandoned the consignment. A case was registered by RPF Arakkonam. The police were analysing CCTV camera footage to nab the gang that was involved in the smuggling. A probe is under way.

headline: Burglars decamp with 30 sovereigns of gold, ₹5 lakh in Ranipet
content: Burglars decamped with 30 sovereigns of gold jewellery, 1 kg of silver objects and around 5 lakh cash from the house of a retired railway officer in Arakkonam town on Tuesday. The police said that the victim, Moindeen Sharif, 68, was a retired railway official. Initial inquiry revealed that along with family members, Moindeen had gone to visit his son in Chennai for a week. When he returned, he found cupboards broken in the living room and bedroom. The police said that gold ornaments and cash that were kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was also damaged. On being informed, Arakkonam Town police inspected the spot. CCTV cameras in the house and along the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. A probe is under way.

headline: DMK seeks ECI probe into TVK candidate's poll expenditure in April poll
content: DMK deputy organisation secretary and MLA S Austin on Tuesday petitioned Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik seeking an urgent inquiry into an alleged cover-up of election expenditure and violation of the model code of conduct by TVK candidate for Dharapuram P Sathyabama. TVK general secretary Aadhav Arjuna had dismissed the video as an AI generated clip, while Sathyabama told reporters that she would initiate action on those who spread the video.He cited a video which was circulated on social media and alleged the woman seen in the video was Sathyabama. Austin said the woman was heard claiming to have spent Rs. 31 crore during the April Assembly election.After meeting CEO at the state secretariat, Austin said ECI should summon and scrutinise Sathyabamas election expenditure accounts and audit the expenses incurred during the April poll. He submitted a pen drive containing the video along with his complaint.If the expenditure was found to have been concealed, action under Representation of the People Act and other applicable laws should be taken against her, Austin said.He also sought an inquiry into complaints of distribution of cash and gifts, including lamps, sarees and tiffin boxes, to voters in Dharapuram.Asked about the TVK camps claim that the video was morphed, Austin said, No one will accept that it is them. That is what she is also saying.

headline: Madras HC sets aside ₹3 lakh compensation order for failed tubectomy
content: Madras high court has set aside an order of a single judge directing the state govt to pay Rs. 3 lakh as compensation to a woman who became pregnant after undergoing a family planning (tubectomy) surgery and free education for the child.This court could understand the sympathy expressed by the single judge towards the petitioner, who would have difficulty raising the child alone after losing her husband. However, since a govt order was already in place providing compensation of Rs. 60,000 in cases involving failure of tubectomy, the single judges order could not be sustained, the first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan said.Citing a judgment rendered by a division bench of the court in Dhanam case, the court said, the standards and quality assurance in sterilization services state that female sterilization carries a small risk of failure, about 5 in 1,000 in the first year.It is also stated that a woman who misses her period should report to the health facility within two weeks, and that she should then be offered free termination of pregnancy and repeat sterilization, the court said. This apart, the Supreme Court has made it clear that the issue of negligence cannot be decided in a writ petition, the judges pointed out.The apex court emphasized that in cases where there are disputed questions of fact, the high court may decide to decline exercising writ jurisdiction and that negligence in such cases had to be established first by the claimants, the court said.This does not leave the woman without a remedy. The govt has a scheme for exactly this situation providing Rs. 60,000 compensation. If the woman believes she has a claim for more, because of negligence on the part of the doctor or the hospital, she must prove it before a civil court, where both sides can lead evidence, the bench said.

headline: 'No, He Didn't, You Buffoons': White House Denies Trump Told Iran To 'Take Out' US Cities
content: Trump made the comments at a midterm election rally in Nebraska on Monday while defending high oil prices linked to the war with Iran. The White House on Tuesday rejected claims that US President Donald Trump was suggesting Iran should attack Los Angeles and San Diego, saying he was talking about the threat posed by Iran. Trump made the comments at a midterm election rally in Nebraska on Monday while defending high oil prices linked to the war with Iran. He said the higher prices were a small price" to pay for keeping the US and the world safe. - 'Let Them Destroy Los Angeles, San Diego': Trump's 'Deranged' Invitation To Iran Surprises Americans - No Military Solution: Iran Warns Of Stronger Response, Keeps Door Open To Talks - 'A Decision To Make': Trump Warns Iran Of 'Easy Or Hard Way' As Tensions Remain High - Has Trump Softened On Iran? JD Vances Shift On Uranium Enrichment Sparks Fresh Questions Its a little bit high. Its a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe," he said. A Very Small Price They can take out a city. Let them take, let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay," Trump said, adding that the situation would be over very soon". The remarks quickly drew criticism from Democrats, who accused the Republican president of appearing to suggest that Iran could target the two major California cities. California Governor Gavin Newsom called Trump deranged and dangerous" over the remarks, while House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said the nuclear annihilation of an American city is no laughing matter". After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should take out" Los Angeles and San Diego.He is deranged and dangerous. Gavin Newsom (@GavinNewsom) October 6, 2026 White House Hits Back The White House rejected that interpretation and accused the media of creating a freakout" that was not rooted in reality". He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadnt been stopped," White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said. The White House Rapid Response account also directly criticised a Los Angeles Times headline that said Trump had suggested letting Iran take out Los Angeles and San Diego". No, he didnt, you buffoons," the account said, adding that Trump was referring to the US effort to stop Iran from gaining the ability to attack Los Angeles and San Diego with nuclear weapons. No, he didnt, you buffoons. He was saying the U.S. is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon which they would if they had the chance. Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) October 6, 2026 Which they would if they had the chance," it added. Trump Defends Iran War Costs Trump has been campaigning ahead of the midterm elections as his administration faces pressure over the economic impact of the conflict with Iran. High oil prices have become a key concern for voters, with Republicans facing questions over the war and its effect on household costs. Trump has argued that the economic pressure is justified by the need to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, saying the conflict could end soon. (With inputs from agencies) During a midterm election rally in Nebraska, Donald Trump defended high oil prices linked to the war with Iran by stating that letting Iran take out cities like Los Angeles and San Diego was a small price to pay to keep the country safe.

headline: Rare Japanese sparrowhawk sighted in Adyar estuary
content: A rare visitor has again turned up on Chennais coastline. Three birders recorded a Japanese Sparrowhawk at the Adyar estuary a couple of days ago, marking only the second time the species has been seen at the same spot.The first sighting at the estuary came in Nov last year. Then, in March this year, the small raptor was spotted at Auroville near Puducherry, said Kumaresan Chandrabose. He, along with Balakrishnan and Bharath, jointly recorded it in Adyar estuary two days ago. This is the third sighting recorded in the country and second in Chennai, Kumaresan said.What makes the records remarkable is the birds usual range. The Japanese Sparrowhawk is found only in Japan, Mongolia and China, far from the Indian coast.The individual spotted this time is an adult female. Available information showed that adult females are larger than their male counterparts, weighing around 111g193g. They have brown upperparts but no red-brown barring on their underparts or sides. Adult females have white bodies and wing linings with brown-grey barring. They have yellow eyes and, like adult males, yellow legs and a stripe over the throat, but it is more obvious on adult females. T Murugavel, a raptor expert and project coordinator for Environment Monitoring and Action Initiating, said that, on and off, birders spot such vagrants in Chennai, especially in the Adyar Estuary, the Theosophical Society, and Guindy National Park (GNP).The Brown Hawk-Owl that I sighted on The School campus a couple of decades ago was spotted in GNP a few years later. Hence, these habitats must be preserved with minimal anthropogenic pressures, he added.

headline: Bypoll turnout dip points to voter fatigue
content: The fall in voter turnout in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram bypolls on Tuesday suggests that roadshows by TVK leader C Joseph Vijay could not offset voter fatigue.At the end of the day, Madurantakam registered 86.26% and Dharapuram 80.3% voting. The constituencies had registered 93.22% and 89.89% voting in the assembly election in April this year.The decline is significant as the bypolls followed the defection of sitting AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama to TVK. Vijay had organised roadshows in both the constituencies, in contrast to his relatively limited campaigning during the April polls.The low turnout is consistent with the pattern observed in several by-elections triggered by disqualification or resignation of MLAs over the past decade. Of the 18 bypolls held in 2019 after AIADMK MLAs were disqualified for switching sides and aligning with expelled party leader T T V Dhinakaran, at least 12 recorded a decline in turnout compared with the previous assembly election or its equivalent.The seats where turnout declined in 2019 include Andipatti (to 75.9% from 78.25% in 2016); Harur (82.3% from 84.3%) and Pappireddipatti (to 83.8% from 85.78%). Periyakulam recorded a turnout of 72.9%, down from 74.9%, while Sattur saw a decline to 76.2% from 78.22%. In Thanjavur, the turnout fell to 67.3% from 69.41%.The Vilavankode bypoll held after the resignation of Congress MLA S Vijayadharani in 2024 recorded a turnout of 65.39%, compared with 67.12% in the 2021 assembly election.In contrast, the turnout rose when the election was necessitated by the death of an MLA. In the 2023 Erode East bypoll following the death of Congress MLA E V K S Elangovan, polling rose to 74.5%, from 66.56% in 2021. Similarly, the turnout in the 2017 Dr Radhakrishnan Nagar bypoll held after the death of former chief minister J Jayalalithaa was 77.5%, up from 68.36% in the previous election.This time, the Left parties criticism of the defections and alleged voter inducements by the parties have added another dimension to the bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram. There is widespread anger that the elections were imposed unnecessarily, said Madurantakam DMK candidate I Paranthamen.However, TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel cited a local public holiday unlike the general holiday during the assembly elections as one of the reasons for the lower turnout. She dismissed allegations of betrayal. When EPS tried to form a govt with the support of DMK, we had to leave, said the two-time MLA. My voters are convinced about my decision and will stand by Annan Vijay. Oct 9 will be a day of celebration for us.

headline: AC mechanic hacked to death in Mylapore, 3 college students detained
content: A group of men killed a 21-year-old AC mechanic with machetes in Mylapore on Monday night. Police suspect a feud linked to ganja sales led to the attack. They have formed three special teams to trace the suspects and have detained three students of a city college in Adyar.Police said Sathyaseelan previously lived with his family on Veerapathiran Street in Mylapore. He received treatment at a drug rehabilitation centre, and later, his family moved to Balaji Nagar in Velachery. He had studied till Class IX.Sathyaseelan continued to visit Mylapore to meet his friend Sabari. On Monday, he was chatting with friends on Veerapathiran Street when a group of men arrived on two-wheelers and attacked him with machetes.He suffered deep injuries to his head, arms, and thigh and collapsed at the scene. He died at Government Royapettah Hospital and police sent his body for postmortem. Mylapore police registered a murder case and examined CCTV footage from the neighbourhood.Police detained four youths in connection with the murder and questioned them. Teams were also searching for three other suspects believed to have been involved in the attack. Preliminary inquiries indicated that Sathyaseelan has a history of ganja consumption and had shared some information about the local drug trade during his rehabilitation. Police were investigating whether the attack was linked to a dispute over the ganja sales.Police said Sathyaseelan recently threatened one of the assailants, after which they attacked him as a warning.

headline: 'Congress Believes In Creating Ruckus, Exposed Again': BJP After EC Denies Oppn's Meeting Request Claim
content: The BJP slammed Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission, calling it a "political drama" and denying any meeting request was made. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday criticised the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, over the INDIA blocs protest against the Election Commission, accusing him of creating a political drama" and making false claims about seeking a meeting with the poll panel. Addressing a press conference, BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the Election Commissions statement that no request for a meeting had been received from any party until 4 pm. - A Small Gate, A Flying Kiss And Samosas: How Rahul Gandhi Stumped Cops At Akashvani Bhavan - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police Rahul Gandhi, an expert in political drama, spent the entire day creating a spectacle. Now, the facts officially released by the Election Commission through its press release have exposed his lies," Trivedi said. Political Drama: BJP Slams Oppn Protest He claimed the Election Commission had informed Gandhi around 4 pm that it was ready to meet the delegation under its prescribed procedure. Trivedi said Gandhi instead insisted on taking around 300 MPs to the Commissions office, calling the demand unprecedented. However, he insisted on meeting in a different manner. He was claiming that there were 300 MPs and that he would go to the Election Commission premises along with all 300 MPssomething that has never happened in the history of India," the BJP leader added. BJP Tears Into Congress Trivedi also alleged that the Opposition refused the ECIs offer to send a senior official to receive their memorandum at the protest site. Therefore, it is clear that their objective was not actually to present their concerns before the Election Commission," he said. Questioning the Oppositions claim about the number of MPs participating, Trivedi said the Congress had 129 MPs across both Houses and alleged that several major INDIA bloc parties did not participate in the protest. What an enormous lie!" he said, questioning where the figure of 300 MPs came from. Trivedi also questioned the absence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and senior lawyers from the protest, alleging that the Oppositions objective was political rather than to raise concerns before the poll panel. The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi for creating political drama and making false claims that the Opposition had sought a meeting with the poll panel. According to BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi, the Election Commission stated that no meeting request had been received from any party until 4 pm.

headline: 'Islam Wants To Take Over France': Trump Reacts To Students' Protests, Blames 'Out Of Control' Migration
content: France is currently facing a nationwide student-led protest movement over underfunded schools, teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating infrastructure. US President Donald Trump has reacted to the student-led protests in France, linking the unrest to what he described as out of control mass migration" and alleging that Islam was seeking to take over the country. Whats happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isnt about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country! President DJT," Trump wrote on X. - 'Morally Binding' But Not Legally Enforceable: Tech Giants Sign Trump's AI Self-Policing Pact - 'Super Intelligence Force': Trump Names Intel Chief Jay Clayton To Lead New AI Task Force - 'How Trump Feels He Is': Iran Mocks US President With Hrithik Roshan Movie Meme - France Riots Videos Go Viral As Post Links Unrest To Angry Students, Overcrowded Schools; Internet Divided France is currently facing a nationwide student-led protest movement over underfunded schools, teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating infrastructure. The demonstrations began in the Paris region in September and spread to more than 30 cities on October 6, with trade unions and other public-sector workers joining the rallies. Students blockade schools, campuses High-school students have blockaded hundreds of lyces and university campuses as part of the protests. Demonstrations have been reported in Paris, Marseille, Lille, Lyon, Nantes, Strasbourg, Rennes and other cities. While some protests remained peaceful, others involved burning barricades, vandalism and clashes with riot police. Police used tear gas and other crowd-control measures at several locations. The protests are centred on demands for more resources and better conditions in Frances education system. The demonstrations began in the Paris region in September and spread to more than 30 cities on October 6. High-school students have blockaded hundreds of lyces and university campuses as part of the protests. French authorities say more than 5,000 people have been arrested, with around 87% of them minors. The government has reported injuries to approximately 215 students and 715 police officers. The high-school union Union Syndicale Lycenne has reportedly demanded 10 billion for urgent school reconstruction. What are students demanding? Students are calling for more teachers and replacement staff when teachers are absent. They are also demanding smaller classes and reduced workloads. Other demands include the renovation of ageing or unsafe school buildings and better teaching materials and support staff, including nurses and social workers. Students are also seeking more higher-education places and increased funding for education. The high-school union Union Syndicale Lycenne has reportedly demanded 10 billion for urgent school reconstruction, 150,000 additional higher-education places and large-scale teacher recruitment. Over 5,000 arrested French authorities say more than 5,000 people have been arrested, with around 87% of them minors. The government has reported injuries to approximately 215 students and 715 police officers, although figures and descriptions of individual incidents vary by source. One particularly serious incident was reported in Lens, where a teenager reportedly lost a hand after a grenade exploded during the unrest. Police-watchdog investigations are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident. Protests take on political significance The protests are taking place as Prime Minister Sbastien Lecornus government attempts to advance a politically contentious 2027 budget that involves major spending reductions. The student movement has therefore become linked to wider public-sector anger over austerity, wages and pressure on public services. The unrest is also unfolding months before Frances next presidential election. This has increased pressure on the government and given both the left and far right an opportunity to frame the crisis politically. Trump, meanwhile, has framed the protests differently, linking them to migration and Islam rather than the education-related demands being raised by students. Government promises consultations The immediate government response has been to promise consultations with students. Ministers have also been asked to prepare proposals on teacher replacement, school hours and renovation of school facilities by the end of October. The student movement, however, continues to focus on demands for greater education funding, more teachers, improved infrastructure and additional support for schools and universities. Students are calling for more teachers, replacement staff, smaller classes, reduced workloads, and better teaching materials. Additional demands include 10 billion for urgent school reconstruction, 150,000 extra higher-education places, and large-scale teacher recruitment to address underfunded schools and deteriorating infrastructure.

headline: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Detained During Protest Against CEC At Akashvani Bhawan; Released After 2 Hours
content: We want to meet the CEC. We have no hope from the government," Priyanka Gandhi said while speaking to CNN-. Congress Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and his sister, Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday evening amid the Oppositions protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, according to Congress sources. Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, the outgoing chief of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC), was also seen with Rahul Gandhi as police officers urged the protesters to end their dharna. He was released two hours later. Police had earlier announced that the sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan would not be allowed to continue overnight and asked the protesters to disperse. - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police - Will Rahul Gandhi Be INDIA Blocs PM Candidate In 2029? Heres What Mamata Banerjee Said - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Booked: FIR After I.N.D.I.A. Bloc Protest At Akashvani Bhawan | Detention would follow if they refused to vacate the premises, according to the announcement. Congress had earlier claimed that Delhi Police was trying to detain Rahul Gandhi and other MPs from Akashvani Bhawan. Meanwhile, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said the government was incompetent" and asserted that Gyanesh Kumar will not be spared". We want to meet the CEC. We have no hope from the government," Priyanka Gandhi said while speaking to CNN-. The Opposition leaders are protesting over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, along with other MPs, were earlier stopped on Parliament Street in front of Akashvani Bhawan and the NITI Aayog office as they attempted to proceed towards the Election Commission. After being prevented from moving further, the leaders sat on the road in protest. Rahul Gandhi and TMCs Abhishek Banerjee were subsequently seen climbing atop a police barricade, while Priyanka Gandhi was taken to a waiting bus for detention. She, however, soon got off the bus and joined Rahul Gandhi at the Akashvani gate. Despite being stopped by police, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and Congress MP Deepender Hooda entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises through the reception gate. The leaders were later seen sitting under a tree. Congress leader Pawan Khera told CNN- that all the protesters had been detained and taken to an undisclosed location. We were not allowed to meet the EC and were suddenly detained by Delhi Police," Khera said, adding that Rahul Gandhi had requested police to provide them a place to protest. Khera said the Congress would organise more protests, adding that the party had a history of protesting for the country". He also said all Opposition parties had realised what is going on in the EC". Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained by Delhi Police during an opposition protest at Akashvani Bhawan against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Tamil Nadu byelections: Madurantakam and Dharapuram record 86.26% and 80.3% polling
content: Madurantakam and Dharapuram record 86.26% and 80.3% polling The Assembly byelections in Madurantakam in Chengalpattu district and Dharapuram in Tiruppur district in Tamil Nadu went off peacefully on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). Barring some glitches in the EVMs that were attended to immediately, polling in Madurantakam district was peaceful, with 86.26% voters exercising their franchise. While the final polling figures are still awaited, the turnout was lower than the 93.22% that the constituency had registered during the Assembly election in April-May this year. The by-election was necessitated by the resignation of Maragatham Kumaravel, who won on AIADMK ticket in the Assembly election and then switched to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which has fielded her now. Follow live updates on the bypolls here. Polling began on a sluggish pace but picked up pace from 9 a.m., elections officials said. In polling booth number 26 at Sithandi, the control unit of the EVM malfunctioned and had to be replaced twice. This led to a delay in the start of polling. Similarly, in booth number 55 at L. Endathur, the ballot unit of the EVM had to be replaced after polling agents objected to a mark visible on the name of a candidate. The ruling TVK lodged a complaint against DMK candidate I. Paranthamen for allegedly violating the Model Code of Conduct when he spoke to reporters, alleging horse-trading by the TVK, pointing at a complaint filed by two Opposition MLAs with the DVAC. Denying any violation, Mr. Paranthamen said his party was in possession of screen shots of a message that many voters in Madurantakam received on Monday, containing details of their EPIC and polling booths, with the picture of the TVK candidate. This happened during the silent period. We have given a written complaint with proof, he told . AIADMK candidate S. Kanitha Sampath said young voters might not have voted for the TVK in large numbers this time because of several reasons, including the increase in the prices of essential commodities and electricity tariff. CPI(M) candidate P. Suganthi alleged that the lack of basic facilities such as drinking water, wheelchairs, and shamiana at certain booths caused hardship to the voters. Among the voters at one of the booths at Mamandur was Divya Priya, a final-year anaesthesiology student, who was voting for the second time in six months. She said she turned up to vote so that the political party of her choice would win. Miles away at Pallipettai, Monishasree, an employee of an IT company in Chennai and a second-time voter, entered the polling booth with her mother to vote. She has taken a days leave to come here and vote, says Bhagyalakshmi, 64, her mother. For reaching Pallipettai, one has to reach Acharapakkam where government buses mostly do not stop. I wasnt surprised when they stopped today, perhaps because of the election. Else, I get down six kilometres away at Melmaruvathur and wait for my father to pick me up, Monishasree said. Outside the polling station, Senthamarai, 93, was seen walking past. Asked if she had voted, she said she had cast her vote through postal ballot and was out for a mid-day stroll. The district election officials had received 434 postal ballots from from voters aged above 85 and 459 postal ballots from people with disabilities. Chengalpattu Collector M. Veerappan said the polling was peaceful. The EVMs have been moved to the strong room at the Integrated Training Institute for Social Development, Athur. 80.3% polling in Dharapuram The Dharapuram (reserved) constituency, which has 2,23,306 voters, recorded 80.3% polling. The voting was disrupted for a while at a couple of booths. The turnout that was sluggish in the morning hours picked up as the day progressed. However, the turnout was lesser in the byelection than in the April-May Assembly election which recorded 89.9%. A larger number of the State police and CISF personnel was deployed at 18 of the 320 booths identified as sensitive. Officials said polling went off without any untoward incident, and the disruption at two booths was addressed immediately. Polling was halted at the Kolinjivadi booth (137) in Dharapuram town for half-an-hour in the morning hours after a voter, Jaithun Beevi, 75, alleged that she was prompted by an election worker to press the TVK symbol on the EVM. DMK agents demanded action against the worker. They relented after officials assured them of follow-up action. At the booth at Kavundachipudur in Dharapuram town, the presence of a TVK agent, Saravanan, triggered a protest by DMK workers, leading to the disruption of the voting. The DMK workers argued that Saravanan, who was previously with the DMK, did not belong to the particular ward of the Dharapuram Municipality where the booth was located. Returning Officer and Dharapuram Revenue Divisional Officer Felix Raja intervened and explained to the DMK workers that there were no restrictions on candidates appointing party agents anywhere in the constituency, provided the candidates had submitted Form 10 applications for them. The voting resumed, only to be disrupted again by DMK workers, who demanded that Saravanan be removed from the booth. TVK functionary and former Minister K.V. Ramalingam met the RDO and sought his intervention. Subsequently, Saravanan was permitted to continue as the TVKs agent at the booth. At an urban booth in Dharapuram, Pavithra, a first-time voter in the April-May Assembly election, opined that the byelection was an opportunity for the people to choose a better candidate. In the byelection, there was no pressure from my daughter to vote for any particular party, her father Saminathan said. P. Sathyabama of the TVK, who had won earlier as the AIADMK candidate by securing 40.56% of 1,99,944 votes, is pitted against S. Suganya of the DMK and Banumathi of the AIADMK. In the April-May election, Gowri Chitra of the TVK came third, with 46,438 votes, securing 23.23% of the votes polled. The DMK, whose candidate T. Indirani polled 63,336 votes accounting for 32.2%, is testing its strength without the support of allies in the byelection. After polling came to a close, officials sealed the EVMs and the VVPATs for moving them to the strong room at LRG Government Arts and Science College at Tiruppur. A total of 384 EVMs were utilised for the byelection. The votes will be counted on October 9.

headline: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi detained after hours-long anti-CEC protest, released later
content: CEC protest, released later Led by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, leaders of INDIA bloc Tuesday stepped up their attack on the Chief Election Commissioner, demanding his resignation before they were detained late in the evening after staging a protest for hours near the Election Commission office in the heart of New Delhi. The leaders were released later in the night. Parliament Street shut down as Gandhi and others tried to march towards the EC office with their supporters, and climbed atop police barricades, before finding their way into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. Through much of the day, Gandhi and Vadra were holed up inside the AIR premises, demanding they be allowed to meet the CEC. They were joined by SPs Akhilesh Yadav, TMCs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, and CPI(M)s John Brittas. All I want to do is meet the Chief Election Commissioner and tell him that he has done vote chori. I can continue to sit here. I am comfortable here. If they dont want us to sit here, give us some other site, Gandhi said. Targeting the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the RSS chief, Gandhi alleged that the country had been hijacked with the vote chori. What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape, he said. The day-long protest began with the march being stopped soon after it started from Parliament House around 10 am, following which the opposition MPs sat on the street outside Akashvani Bhavan, very close to the EC office. As MPs were being detained, Gandhi spoke to his sister seated inside one of the buses and both went inside the Akashvani Bhavan, taking all by surprise. Besides the Gandhi siblings, the Congress leaders who joined them inside the AIR premises included Deepender Hooda, Charanjit Singh Channi, Praniti Shinde, K C Venugopal and Pawan Khera. Several MPs returned to the protest site after being released from detention. In a post on X, Gandhi said, Gyanesh its done bro. Time to resign. MPs from the BJD, which has not been part of the INDIA bloc, also joined the march. DMK and AAP leaders stayed away from the protest.

headline: Trump Approves Firing Squad Execution Of Ex-Army Major Nidal Hasan In Rare Move: Why It Matters
content: Why It Matters The US military has not carried out an execution since 1961, when Pvt. John Bennett was hanged after being convicted of raping an 11-year-old girl. US President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of former Army major Nidal Malik Hasan, who was convicted for the 2009 Fort Hood massacre in Texas that left 13 people dead and 32 wounded. The decision is significant because executions under the US military justice system are extremely rare. The US military has not carried out an execution since 1961, when Pvt. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said Hegseth would decide the time and location of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," Parnell wrote on X. 60 Years Later, US Military Execution Set To Return? Hasan, former Army psychiatrist, opened fire inside a medical facility at Fort Hood where soldiers were undergoing examinations. He used a laser-sighted handgun and shouted Allahu akbar" during the attack. He later said he carried out the shooting to prevent US troops from being deployed to Afghanistan and killing fellow Muslims. During his trial, Hasan made little attempt to defend himself and described himself as a soldier who had switched sides." Trumps approval sets the military execution process in motion, but it does not necessarily mean Hasans death sentence will be carried out soon. He could challenge the execution through a habeas corpus petition in the civilian federal courts, a legal route that could potentially delay his execution for years. Former President George W. Bush approved the execution of Army Spc. Ronald Gray in 2008, but a judge later stayed it. Trumps decision also comes days after a failed lethal-injection execution in Tennessee prompted the state governor to halt further executions this year and order an independent review. Asked about the incident, Trump called it an interesting situation." It shouldnt be very difficult," Trump said of carrying out lethal injections.
