headline: Storm In Pakistan Over Mecca Pact: Ishaq Dar Evades Question On Houthi Military Action | Exclusive Details
content: Exclusive Details The Foreign Ministers silence highlights deep-seated constitutional sensitivities inside Pakistan regarding overseas military commitments Pakistans Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar abruptly terminated a media interaction following sharp questioning over whether parliamentary approval would be sought before committing Pakistani forces to kinetic operations against Houthi rebels in Yemen. The abrupt departure has sparked intense political speculation regarding Islamabads operational involvement in the escalating Gulf crisis. The dramatic press briefing follows an October 5 defence commitment in which Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey activated the Mecca Joint Defence Pact. Under this agreement, the three nations agreed to prepare military units and assets for rapid deployment within Saudi territory to counter ongoing Houthi missile and drone strikes. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive - 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | Mecca Pact Activation and Rapid Deployment The trilateral alliance shifted rapidly from a strategic framework to operational deployment following an emergency session of the strategic political committee in Riyadh. With Saudi-backed forces launching wide-scale offensives along Yemens Red Sea coast, allied nations agreed to accelerate force integration. While Pakistans military leadership previously asserted that commitment to Saudi Arabias territorial integrity remains absolute, the prospect of direct offensive engagements has drawn intense domestic scrutiny. Questions over whether deployment mandates extend into offensive kinetic actionor remain strictly defensivehave placed significant pressure on the ruling coalition. Constitutional Friction Over Foreign Military Deployments The Foreign Ministers silence highlights deep-seated constitutional sensitivities inside Pakistan regarding overseas military commitments. Opposition figures and legal experts maintain that any combat deployment outside national borders requires explicit parliamentary debate and authorisation, citing precedent set during previous Gulf conflicts. By skipping the question and ending the press conference, Dar triggered widespread criticism from opposition legislators who accuse the government of bypassing democratic oversight on critical national security decisions. Regional Escalation and Multi-Nation Strategy The joint deployment plan unfolds against the backdrop of widening Red Sea hostilities and severe disruptions to international shipping routes. While Islamabad continues to explore diplomatic channelsincluding dialogue proposals with regional stakeholdersallied operational preparations are proceeding rapidly. As Saudi Arabia and its allies fortify key strategic positions, the Pakistani government faces growing demands to clarify the exact mandate, scope, and constitutional backing of its troops deployed under the Mecca pact. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar abruptly ended a press briefing and evaded questions on whether parliamentary approval would be sought before committing Pakistani forces to military actions against Houthi rebels.

headline: Ganga Water Treaty is 'flawed', needs to be updated: Bangladesh river expert
content: The 1996 India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty is flawed as it lacks a guarantee clause and does not account for factors like climate change impact, a leading Bangladesh river water expert has said. Speaking to on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), Manjur A. Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission (NRCC) of Bangladesh said the Treaty will expire in December and should be replaced by a short-term treaty of three years. This should be followed by a better researched trilateral treaty that also brings in Nepal since that nations rivers carry Himalayan snowmelt to the Ganga. The Ganga Water Treaty is three decades old and flawed as it does not include a guarantee clause. It also does not have ecological flow and environmental flow considerations. In addition, the treaty does not include factors that are related to climate change. It simply divides the water of the river. That is not a right approach, said Mr. Chowdhury who believes that the Ganga Water Treaty should include Nepal. A good treaty, he added, should take into account the health of the river so that the Ganga is not overexploited. Before the treatys expiry in December this year, ideally, we should opt for a short-term treaty of three years during which time we will conduct further research and negotiations to draft a new and lasting Ganga Water Treaty that will incorporate technological and environmental developments, said Mr. Chowdhury, speaking exclusively to . Treaty expires in December India always looks at the Ganga treaty as a bilateral treaty but in the lean months it receives a lot of snowmelt from Nepals Ghaghara, Gandaki, and Koshi rivers; they also need to be monitored if we have to care for the Ganga, Mr. Chowdhury said. He argued that the Ganga water treaty requires a fresh approach as environmental factors of the twenty-first century will have to be considered while drafting the text of the treaty. His comments came a day after he made similar remarks at a conclave in Dhaka calling for a fresh treaty. The Ganga Water Treaty will expire in December this year unless the two sides agree to renew the treaty for another three decades. Earlier, former Foreign Secretary Farooq Sobhan, who had negotiated the treaty during the first prime ministerial tenure of Sheikh Hasina in 1996 said that the absence of an arbitration clause is a problem for the treaty. Speaking with , Mr. Sobhan further said that there are unfulfilled Indian promises related to the Ganga Water Treaty that will have to be revisited. India had promised to build a barrage for Padma (Ganga) in Bangladeshi territory at that time, but it was not followed up. That was the quid pro quo for not including the arbitration clause. But that barrage was not built, said Mr. Sobhan. He added that Bangladesh carried out surveys in the 1990s regarding the building of a barrage but did not receive the help it needed. Discussions on the renewal of the Ganga Water Treaty have been ongoing in both India and Bangladesh though important technical consultations are yet to be held ahead of the expiry in December this year. Earlier JD(U) MP Sanjay Jha had called on the Government of India not to renew the Ganga Water Treaty saying that the treaty with Bangladesh had negatively impacted Bihar. Subsequently, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar had written to Mr. Jha on August 28, We fully understand your concerns regarding the Ganga Water Treaty. I would like to bring to your attention that under the leadership of the Jal Shakti Ministry, inter-ministerial consultation involving relevant stakeholders have taken place to ensure broad-based consultation on the future of the treaty. (The Correspondent was in Dhaka as the guest of Centre for Governance Studies (CGS) to participate in the Bay of Bengal Conversation.)

headline: 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hits Uttarakhand, tremors felt in Delhi-NCR
content: A 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhands Chamoli on Tuesday night, with its tremors felt in the Delhi-NCR region. The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology, which characterised its status as reviewed. Nearby seismicity (Credits: National Center for Seismology) Delhi-NCR has experienced several noticeable earthquakes this year. On January 19, 2026, a mild 2.8-magnitude earthquake struck New Delhi, with its epicentre in North Delhi at a shallow depth of about five kilometres. Brief tremors were felt across parts of the capital, but no damage was reported. On April 3, 2026, tremors were felt in Delhi-NCR after a 5.9-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan. The epicentre was near Darawan, and mild shaking was also reported in Punjab, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir and Kargil. No casualties or property damage were immediately reported. And on June 27 a stronger 6.2-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan, causing tremors in Delhi-NCR and other parts of northern India. The National Centre for Seismology placed its depth at approximately 215 kilometres. What to do during earthquake Here is a quick refresher from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) on how to stay safe when the ground shakes. If youre indoors: - Drop, cover and hold on. Get down on the floor, take shelter under sturdy furniture and hold on until the shaking stops. - If there is no shelter nearby, crouch in an inside corner and shield your head and face with your arms. - Keep away from windows, glass, exterior walls and anything that could topple, such as shelves or light fixtures. - If you are in bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow. If a heavy fixture hangs above you, move carefully to a safer spot. - Use a doorway only if it is close by and structurally strong. - Stay inside until the shaking stops completely. Most injuries happen when people try to move around or rush out during a quake. - Be prepared for power cuts, and for fire alarms and sprinklers to go off. If youre outdoors: - Stay where you are, but move away from buildings, trees, poles and wires that could collapse or fall. - Remain in the open until the shaking ends. Many injuries occur near exterior walls and exits because of falling debris. If youre in a vehicle: - Pull over as soon as it is safe, avoiding overpasses, power lines and buildings. - Stay inside the vehicle until the shaking stops. - Afterwards, drive carefully and avoid damaged roads and bridges. If youre trapped under debris: - Do not light matches or kick up dust. - Cover your mouth with a piece of clothing. - Signal for help by tapping on a pipe or wall, or by blowing a whistle. Shout only as a last resort, since it can make you inhale dust.

headline: Bypolls held in five Assembly seats, one Lok Sabha constituency
content: Bypolls were held on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) in five Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Puducherry, and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam. The Madurantakam Assembly constituency in Tamil Nadu recorded the highest polling percentage of 86%. The other Assembly seat which went to the polls in Tamil Nadu was Dharapuram, which saw a turnout of just over 80%. Both seats in the State were reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. Keep track | Byelections 2026 highlights: Bypolls to five Assembly seats, one LS seat conclude with high voter turnout; minor incidents reported Switched loyalties The byelections to these two seats were necessitated by the resignations of Magaratham Kumaravel from Madurantakam (SC) and P. Sathyabama from Dharapuram (SC), who both won on All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) tickets in the 2026 State election and subsequently switched to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) after resigning their Assembly memberships within three weeks in May 2026. They are both in the fray, this time as TVK nominees. The two constituencies are witnessing a multi-cornered contest, with Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), AIADMK, and Naam Tamilar Katchi candidates also in the fray. Significantly, the Communist Party of India (CPI) and CPI-Marxist, which are extending outside support to the TVK-led government, have jointly put up a candidate in the two seats. In Puducherry, where the bypoll was held in the Thattanchavady Assembly segment, there was 80.8% voting. The election was caused by the resignation of AINRC chief and Chief Minister N. Rangasamy, who retained the Mangalam Assembly seat. W.B. bypoll amid SIR drama In West Bengal, where bypolls were held in the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly seats, there was a voter turnout of almost 80%, despite the fact that many were not able to vote as their inclusion in the electoral roll is under appeal in Appellate Tribunalds. Opposition parties raised allegations of electoral malpractice, with the Congress seeking a repoll in both the constituencies. Voter polling trends till 5:30 p.m. showed Nandigram at 79.4% and Rejinagar at 78.4%. West Bengals Chief Electoral Officer received 97 official complaints through designated portals on the polling day. The bypolls were needed as West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari won two seats and then vacated Nandigram to retain Bhabanipur, where he had defeated former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. The Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) MLA Humayun Kabir, had also won in both Rejinagar and Nowda in Murshidabad, later giving up the Rejinagar seat. Alleged voter intimidation, booth capturing Nearly 19,000 members of the electorate from these two seats who could not vote in the last Assembly election were also unable to exercise their franchise in the bypolls. Their names were put under adjudication, and still remain in that state. Leaders from the Congress, the Mamata AITC, and the CPI-M have raised allegations of voter intimidation, fake voting, booth capturing, and other issues in both constituencies. Congress State president Subhankar Sarkar submitted a memorandum to the West Bengal CEO office, asking for the bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar to be cancelled, calling for repolling to take place. West Bengal Congress leaders have made allegations of voter intimidation, booth capturing, proxy voting, and EVM malfunctioning. The Congress candidate for Nandigram, Milan Pradhan, who was arrested before the election, also alleged that booths were captured. They are not letting people vote because then it will make history, Mr. Pradhan said. Our Rejinagar Assembly constituencys byelection, constituency number 70, is being controlled by the police. Vote looting is taking place at every booth, the Congress candidate from Rejinagar, Abdullahil Kafi, said. Altercation in Rejinagar Noada MLA Humayun Kabir got into a physical and verbal altercation with the police, who then used force to remove him from the AJUP party office in Rejinagar. He broke the law, so he was arrested, I will not make any further comments, Sub-Divisional police officer Anandajit Hore said after Mr. Kabirs arrest. During the verbal altercation, police had told him he could not be there on the day of polling. Do not work as their middleman. Do not do vote chori. You are doing work for the thieves. I will not go home, said Mr. Kabir. He was taken to the Rejinagar Police Station in a police vehicle. Mr. Kabir had won the Rejinagar seat on May 4, but since he also won from Noada, he recused himself from Rejinagar and his son was nominated from there. However, since campaigning began, Mr. Kabir has alleged intimidation against the AJUP candidate. The BJP candidate for Nandigram, Hasirani Rath, is also the bereaved mother of a deceased aide to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. She offered prayers on polling day. Our Honourable Chief Minister, who has been Chief Minister for five months, has already completed most of the development work in Nandigram. This time, after I am elected, we will think about what more we can do for development, Ms. Rath said. Three-cornered fight About 76% of 19.05 lakh electors voted in the byelection held in Assams Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency, which was necessitated after Pradyut Bordoloi, who won the constituency for the second successive term in 2024, quit the Congress to contest and win the Dispur Assembly seat on a BJP ticket. Though 15 candidates are contesting in the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, which comprises eight Assembly segments in Morigaon and Nagaon districts. However, the contest is expected to be primarily among the BJPs Devasish Sharma, a former bureaucrat; the Congresss Sibamoni Bora, a former MLA; and the All India United Democratic Front chief Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal, an MLA and three-time former MP. All three exuded confidence about winning the seat. Barring a minor confrontation over alleged vote-switching at a polling booth in Nagaon districts Juria, the polling process was largely peaceful.

headline: Tear Gas, Water Cannons And School Blockades: 250,000 Take To The Streets As France's Education Crisis Explodes
content: 250,000 Take To The Streets As France's Education Crisis Explodes The weeks-long movement began against severely under-resourced classrooms, chronic teacher shortages, and crumbling educational infrastructure French riot police have deployed tear gas and water cannons against student blockades as over 250,000 protestersincluding high school pupils, university students, teachers, and parentsmarched across France. The nationwide day of action represents the largest escalation yet in a weeks-long movement against severely under-resourced classrooms, chronic teacher shortages, and crumbling educational infrastructure. The widespread disruptions forced the partial or total closure of hundreds of secondary schools and university campuses nationwide, with major urban centres including Paris, Lille, Marseille, Lyon, and Rennes seeing heavy police deployments. - France Riots Videos Go Viral As Post Links Unrest To Angry Students, Overcrowded Schools; Internet Divided - France Gripped By Violent Student Protests: Why Thousands Are On The Streets And Whats Happening - Teen Loses Hand After Picking Up Police Grenade As France School Protests Spiral Out Of Control - Islam Wants To Take Over France: Trump Reacts To Students' Protests, Blames Out Of Control Migration Street Clashes and Escalating Police Tactics The nationwide demonstrations turned volatile as security forces moved to clear improvised blockades composed of wheelie bins, wooden pallets, and metal barriers outside school gates. In Paris, small groups of demonstrators hurled projectiles and set rubbish bins alight, prompting heavy-handed tactical responses from riot units who fired tear gas canisters into dense crowds of teenage protesters. Public outrage over police tactics has intensified following a series of severe injuries on the front lines. Authorities confirmed that a 15-year-old student lost a hand after an incident involving a police sting-ball grenade during demonstrations, while hundreds of officers and protesters have sustained injuries since the start of the agitation. Overcrowding, Shortages, and Heatwaves The anger stems from what student unions describe as a systemic crisis in French public education. Protesters point to overcrowded classrooms reaching up to 40 pupils per teacher, the non-replacement of absent staff, and a lack of basic health and support staff in public institutions. Over 250,000 protesters marched across France in a nationwide day of action. Hundreds of secondary schools and university campuses were partially or totally closed. A 15-year-old student lost a hand after an incident involving a police sting-ball grenade. Classrooms are overcrowded, reaching up to 40 pupils per teacher. Pupils faced examinations in unventilated classrooms reaching 40C. Environmental conditions have further fueled the movement. Following extreme heatwaves earlier in the year, pupils faced examinations in unventilated classrooms reaching 40C, highlighting long-standing failures to modernise ageing school infrastructure. Political Fallout as Government Calls for Calm The growing unrest presents a severe political challenge for Prime Minister Sbastien Lecornus administration. Facing intense questioning in Parliament, Lecornu denounced instances of ultra violence" surrounding the protests while promising investigations into controversial police incidents. With major trade unions joining the student movement and political opposition figures accusing the government of heavy-handedness, student leaders have vowed to maintain school blockades until concrete funding commitments and structural reforms are delivered by the ministry. Protesters are demonstrating against severely under-resourced classrooms, chronic teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms reaching up to 40 pupils per teacher, and crumbling educational infrastructure.

headline: 3 children suffer head injuries as ceiling collapses at government school in Udaipur
content: Three children suffered head injuries after the ceiling of their classroom collapsed at a government primary school in Udaipur on Tuesday. Two other students sustained minor injuries in the incident that took place in the Bhindar area. The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) whose members visited campuses in different parts of Rajasthan in August. Tuesdays incident took place around 11 am at Government Primary School, Narada, under Vaniyatalai gram panchayat in the Bhindar police station area, when a portion of the plaster from a classroom ceiling suddenly came down. There were 32 children in the classroom at the time. The school, which runs up to Class 5, has 37 students in all, which is why it is common for students of different classes to study in the same room. Authorities were informed of schools condition Shaktawat said the education department had earlier been informed about the poor condition of the building. The building was constructed in 2001 and had become dilapidated. We had already informed the education department about its condition. The last time the school building was repaired was in 2020, he said. Following directions from the education department and the local administration, the school building has now been locked as a precautionary measure. Classes will be shifted to a temporary location near Matajis mandir nearby. The incident comes just over a year after one of Rajasthans worst school-building tragedies. On July 25, 2025, the roof of a government school in Piplodi village of Jhalawar district collapsed, killing seven children and injuring 28 others. The National Human Rights Commission subsequently took cognizance of the incident and sought a report from the Rajasthan government, noting allegations that authorities had been informed about the buildings dilapidated condition. The safety of government schools has again emerged as a major issue in Rajasthan in recent months following the School Thik Karo campaign by the CJP. Its teams visited government schools across the state and highlighted problems ranging from unsafe and dilapidated buildings to schools functioning without proper infrastructure. Some CJP workers were also attacked while visiting a government school in Bagru. The government school at Rampura-Kanwarpura in Jaipurs Bagru area, which had been declared unsafe, was demolished after the CJP campaign highlighted its condition. The government sanctioned around Rs. 18 lakh for construction of a new building.

headline: Cornell sexual assault case: Why the investigation has been reopened | Explained
content: Explained The 2024 alleged Cornell University sexual assault case in the U.S. has resurfaced now after the woman involved filed a civil lawsuit in September 2026 against the university, the fraternity and the seven accused men. The alleged incident involved seven members of Cornell Universitys Chi Phi fraternity. The universitys independent student newspaper, The Cornell Daily Sun, broke the story on September 18, publishing reports that brought the universitys Title IX disciplinary proceedingsand the way university handled the case to public attention. Title IX proceedings are initiated by federally funded educational institutions to resolve allegations of sex-based discrimination, sexual harassment, and sexual assault In September 2026, the District Attorney announced that the investigation would be reopened. New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor. What happened? The alleged incident took place at the Chi Phi fraternity house in Ithaca, New York, on the night of October 19, 2024. The woman, referred to as Jane Doe in legal documents, was a 20-year-old Cornell student at that time.In her complaint, she said that she had been heavily intoxicated and was incapacitated and was unable to consent to any sexual activity. In November 2024, Jane Doe reported the incident to the Cornell University Police Department (CUPD), and Cornell subsequently started its own Title IX investigation. The university also referred the case for a criminal investigation to the Tompkins County District Attorneys Office. But that initial investigation resulted in no charges. Matthew Van Houten, the Tompkins County District Attorney, maintained that the statement provided to his office did not establish a criminal offence under New York law. In a statement, the DAs office said that Jane Does sworn statement in November of 2024 did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped. On the contrary, Jane Does statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual. My office obviously did not and could not have based our November 2024 decision on the allegations in a civil lawsuit that would not be filed until nearly two years later. However, Jane Does lawyers disputed that and pointed to interviews conducted by CUPD in November 2024, in which Jane Doe described her alleged incapacitation and said that she had been raped. That raised several questions about what information CUPD provided to the District Attorneys office. The Cornell Daily Sun reported that Cornell released an FAQ page addressing the Universitys response to the alleged 2024 Chi Phi gang rape in an email sent to the Cornell community. The page contradicts a claim made by the Tompkins County District Attorney. What evidence was actually provided to prosecutors is now one of the main issues being examined as the criminal investigation is being reopened. How did the university deal with it? Cornell conducted its own disciplinary process Title IX in January 2025, separate from the criminal investigation. The university stated that The universitys Title IX investigation was conducted over several months and included hearings where a panel of trained faculty and staff heard evidence over multiple days. The complainant and respondents had the opportunity to testify and present evidence in the universitys investigation. At its conclusion, the hearing panel issued a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell. Of the seven accused men, two were expelled and two received suspensions lasting multiple semesters. Another student, who had graduated before the process was completed, was barred from entering campus for three years. In two other cases, the students were found not responsible for sexual misconduct, although they still received various administrative and educational sanctions, including to write reflection papers. Cornell also permanently revoked its recognition of the Chi Phi chapter and closed it. The universitys disciplinary measures, particularly references to written assignments given to some of the accused students gained public outrage. Cornell has strongly denied that students accused of sexual assault were simply told to write essays as punishment. The university said in a statement that the written assignments were part of broader educational sanctions and were not the sole consequence in cases where more serious disciplinary measures had also been imposed. The case continued to receive wider attention among Cornell students and around the world as required from timely reports by The Cornell Daily Sun. That attention led to protests, statements from alumni and calls from the Cornell Student Assembly for greater transparency and changes to the universitys policies on sexual violence. Cornell has emphasised that the universitys process was focused on determining whether its own policies had been violated, while the district attorneys office was responsible for deciding whether there was sufficient evidence to pursue criminal charges. What happens next? The criminal investigation has now been reopened. District Attorney Van Houtens role in the case was replaced after Governor Hochul appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor. Ms. James will oversee the criminal investigation and determine whether the evidence supports bringing criminal charges. Meanwhile, Jane Does civil lawsuit is still ongoing. It names Cornell, the fraternity organisations and the seven men as defendants and lays out her allegations concerning the assault and Cornells handling of her complaint. Cornell has said it will cooperate with the reopened criminal investigation and support an independent review of how it handled the case. The university reiterates in its statement that We will continue to examine and strengthen our policies to ensure we are doing all we can to foster a culture where sexual misconduct is never tolerated, those who come forward are supported, and individuals found responsible through our processes are held accountable.

headline: Byelections 2026 highlights: Bypolls to five Assembly seats, one LS seat conclude with high voter turnout; minor incidents reported
content: This live blog has been closed Bypolls were held on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) in five Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Puducherry, and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam. The Madurantakam Assembly constituency in Tamil Nadu recorded the highest polling percentage of 86%. The other Assembly seat which went to the polls in Tamil Nadu was Dharapuram, which saw a turnout of just over 80%. Both seats in the State were reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. In Puducherrys Thattanchavady Assembly segment, there was 80.8% voting. Also read | 19,000 West Bengal voters to miss bypolls as appeals remain pending in tribunals In West Bengal, where bypolls were held in the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly seats, there was a voter turnout of almost 80%, despite the fact that many were not able to vote as their inclusion in the electoral roll is under appeal in Appellate Tribunals. Opposition parties raised allegations of electoral malpractice, with the Congress seeking a repoll in both the constituencies. Voter polling trends till 5:30 p.m. showed Nandigram at 79.4% and Rejinagar at 78.4%. West Bengals Chief Electoral Officer received 97 official complaints through designated portals on the polling day. Bye-election was also held for Assams Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency. About 76% of some 19.05 lakh electors voted in the polls. The bypoll was necessitated after Pradyut Bordoloi, who won the constituency for the second successive term in 2024, quit the Congress to contest and win the Dispur Assembly seat on a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ticket. headline: 'Watching It Very Closely': US Urges Russia To Share More Information On Plague Death
content: Marco Rubio said the US had measures available to help Russia if the plague situation proved more serious than Moscow had indicated The United States is closely watching the situation in Russia following the death of a 28-year-old lab worker at a plague research centre in Siberia. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has urged Moscow to share more information about the case, which has triggered speculation over the circumstances of the womans death. Russian officials have said they are still investigating the cause of death. They have also said that people who came into contact with the woman tested negative for pneumonic plague. - Lab Workers Mysterious Death At Russias Anti-Plague Institute: Why Has It Drawn US Attention? - US Embassy Issues Health Alert, Warns Americans To 'Have A Plan To Depart' Amid Plague Scare In Russia - 'Looking At It Very Strongly': Trump Offers US Help As Russia Downplays Plague Reports - WHO Says Siberia Plague Risk Is Low As Dozens Quarantined After Suspected Lab Worker Death I think its incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world," Rubio told reporters. Were watching it very closely, hour by hour." Reports first emerged on Friday that almost 200 people had been placed under observation in Siberias Irkutsk region following the womans death. What happened to the lab worker? The lab worker was named in Russian media as Darya Shipilova. She had reportedly fallen ill a couple of days before her death. Reports suggested that she may have fallen ill after breaking a test tube containing the pathogen or after a field trip to an area where plague occurs naturally among wild rodents. Russian officials, however, have played down those reports. Russias health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said Shipilova had died of pneumonia of an undetermined etiology". A 28-year-old lab worker died at a plague research center in Siberia. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Moscow to share more information about the case. Almost 200 people were placed under observation in Siberia's Irkutsk region. The lab worker was identified in Russian media as Darya Shipilova. Russia stated that no case of plague had been recorded in Irkutsk. In a statement read out on Tuesday by World Health Organization spokesman Christian Lindmeier, Russia said no case of plague had been recorded in Irkutsk. No case of this dangerous disease has been recorded in the city of Irkutsk," the statement said. Russia also said all contacts of the patients had been identified and were being monitored. All of the patients contacts have been reportedly been identified and are being monitored for illness, and none to date have shown symptoms of illness," the statement added. US offers help as speculation grows The case led to a back and forth between Russia and the United States on Tuesday, amid questions over whether the disease could spread beyond Russia. Speaking during a visit to Iceland, Rubio said the US had measures" available to help Russia if the situation proved more serious than Moscow had indicated. Rospotrebnadzor responded by offering assistance to the United States. The Russian Federation is ready to assist the US in combating infectious disease outbreaks," it said in a statement. US President Donald Trump also echoed Rubios comments, saying he was looking very strongly" at the case. According to the Washington Post, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the State Department and the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response are working on the US response. Russia says disease not detected Asked about the death following Rubios remarks, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov cited the findings of Rospotrebnadzor. Asked about the Russian offer of assistance to the US, Peskov said it was a good thing when mutual assistance is offered". Rospotrebnadzor also sought to counter speculation surrounding a document circulating online that allegedly detailed special anti-plague measures. We wish to clarify that the document and information in question do not originate from official sources and are untrue," the watchdog said on Telegram. Why is pneumonic plague a concern? The plague bacterium, or Yersinia pestis, is found among rodents such as marmots in the region. The disease killed up to half the population of Europe in the 14th century, when it was known as the Black Death. The Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East was founded more than 100 years ago in response to an outbreak in the 1920s. Dr Simon Clarke, associate professor in cellular microbiology at the University of Reading, told Radio 4s PM programme that the pneumonic form of Yersinia pestis was nearly always fatal if left untreated, but could be overcome with antibiotics. Pneumonic plague can transmit from person to person and that is why there is the concern around this," Clarke said. He added that while people may immediately think of lockdowns and Covid when an infectious disease outbreak occurs, that is just not whats going to happen here". People think, Oh the plague, thats gone, that went hundreds of years ago, but it hasnt," Clarke said. Its a threat to human health and thats why they need to study it." The US urged Russia to share more details following the death of a 28-year-old lab worker named Darya Shipilova at a plague research centre in Siberia, which sparked global speculation and prompted nearly 200 people to be placed under medical observation.

headline: 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation
content: The Election Commission said no political party had sought an appointment with it until 4 pm on Tuesday. Amid the Oppositions protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the deletion of voters names, the Election Commission on Tuesday said it had not received any request from political parties for a meeting until 4 pm. The poll body said at around 4 pm, it was informed that a delegation led by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi wanted to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum. - Opposition March To Election Commission Turns Dramatic | Gyanesh Kumar | SIR Row | - 'Congress Believes In Creating Ruckus, Exposed Again': BJP After EC Denies Oppn's Meeting Request Claim - Opposition Protests Intensify as Rahul Gandhi Attempts to Reach Election Commission Amid Barricades - How Convenient, Pookie: Posters Taking Potshots At Rahul, Akhilesh Splash Delhi Ahead Of INDIA Bloc Meet 240-Member Delegation Sought Meeting After 4 PM: EC Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to todays developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," the ECI said in a statement. The ECI said it was subsequently told that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe. The Commission described the request as unusual", saying its established protocol requires delegations seeking such meetings to visit the poll panels premises. Unusual: EC On Opposition Meeting Request After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the above-mentioned meeting with the Honble MPs, it was informed by the DCP, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request as unusual and therefore, could not be accepted, as, in accordance with ECI protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India," the statement read. As an alternative, the ECI offered to send its senior-most officer to the Parliament House Annexe to receive the memorandum. The Commission said this was itself an unprecedented step, but the offer was declined by the MPs. The development came as INDIA bloc MPs staged a protest against the SIR exercise and sought the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Opposition has alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. The protest march was planned from Parliament House towards the Election Commission headquarters. However, police stopped the march in central Delhi and detained several MPs. During the action, the Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra made an unexpected detour into the nearby Akashvani Bhawan premises after police began moving protesters into buses. The siblings later sat in protest inside the premises, while other Congress leaders joined them. What Rahul Gandhi Had Said Earlier in the day, Gandhi demanded a meeting with the Election Commissioners, alleging that Opposition MPs have been disrespected." He alleged that the Election Commissioners had disrespected" the voice of the people by not meeting MPs. He demanded that the poll panel meet opposition leaders and answer questions over the allegations of vote theft". The MPs will meet the Election Commissioners; they will have to meet usWe all are very comfortable hereThey have disrespected the voice of the nation by disrespecting the MPs; we just want to meet the Election Commissioners and ask questions and tell them that they have done vote theft," the Congress MP said. The Congress leader had indicated he would continue the sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan before being detained along with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The Election Commission stated that it received no meeting request from political parties until 4 pm, after which it was informed that a delegation led by Rahul Gandhi wanted to submit a memorandum. The ECI deemed the request unusual since the 240 MPs wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe instead of the poll panel's premises.

headline: 'Sudden action seems bit strange': Omar Abdullah after 150 flown out of J&K for deportation
content: A day after 150 alleged Bangladeshi nationals picked from across the Union Territory were airlifted to West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday said the sudden action seemed a bit strange. If you look at it, their presence here has not really caused us any particular harm. However, it is also true that they cannot stay illegally, he said. Omar said that Rohingyas are being unfairly targeted, adding that it is not in the hands of the UT government but the government at the Centre, who are using the police to move them out. We gave them (Rohingyas) refuge here, a little space, and allowed them to stay here until conditions in their country improved. Now, suddenly taking action against them seems a bit strange to me, he said. The 150 people airlifted to Bagdogra, from where they will be deported, are among 500 who were detained from different parts of the Union Territory during a survey to identify illegal immigrants. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, Omar commended the Supreme Court for raising questions on the issue of deletion of names from voter lists. Omar said, The good (thing) is that questions are being raised in the Supreme Court as well, especially the deletion of names from voter lists. The SC has sought answers regarding this from the EC and the Government of India. We will have to see how far this can be corrected by the courts. The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a petition accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting in violation of the law that governs his terms of office by functioning in a unilateral manner, and seeking his removal. The notice issued by a three-judge bench, presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, was also directed at Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, and ECI Director General (Information Technology) Seema Khanna. On INDIA blocs Delhi march, he said that after the leaders met in New Delhi, a calendar was drawn out for this month. The beginning of that was for the members of Parliament from the INDIA bloc to march toward the Election Commission, and this will go on, he added. UCC will never be implemented in J&K In response to a query regarding the implementation of the UCC in Jammu and Kashmir, the CM said, A Uniform Civil Code is not truly uniform until it is implemented everywhere. It will never be implemented here. He also pointed out Bihars resistance to its implementation, stating that, Similarly, there are other governments too that have said the UCC will not be applied in their states. So, this is only being implemented by the BJP. He said it is wrong that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is trying to implement this step by step in states where they are in power. These matters are not handled from state to state. If you have the courage, bring a legislation in Parliament, debate it and then lets see whether it passes or not. If you look at it in the true sense of a democracy, this has to be debated at the Centre. They will not introduce this law in Parliament because they do not have the numbers, he said.

headline: Rajnath Singh stresses on self-reliance in aerospace sector as HAL delivers its 2,000th aero-engine
content: reliance in aerospace sector as HAL delivers its 2,000th aero-engine Singh, who witnessed the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Koraput division at Sunabeda, noted that indigenisation of components and reduced turnaround time are contributing to operational readiness and extended service life of critical defence assets. Aerospace self-reliance must extend to indigenous aero-engine capability, particularly for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme. A sovereign aerospace ecosystem requires indigenous capabilities across materials, design, manufacturing, testing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO), said Singh. He also highlighted proposed investment of around Rs. 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI), and establishment of Indias first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility. Urging the HAL Koraput division to raise standards in quality, productivity, indigenisation, innovation and delivery timelines, Singh described the 2,000th engine as a significant milestone and called for using it as a foundation to build an Indian aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems. Emphasising the need for reliable indigenous propulsion for Indias helicopter ecosystem, the defence minister stated that forces require engines that are available when needed, supported throughout their lifecycle, and upgraded with evolving technology. Aero-engine development is a long-term endeavour requiring sustained investment, specialised testing, skilled manpower and a strong industrial ecosystem, with focus on repeatable, reliable and scalable production, design, critical materials and superalloys, he added. Singh, on the occasion, hailed HALs contribution to military aviation, noting that its engines have powered frontline aircraft, including the MiG-21, MiG-27, MiG-29 and Su-30MKI since establishment of the unit in 1964. The defence minister announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP engine production capacity from 30 to 50 engines annually with an investment of Rs. 335 crore. He also announced a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of Rs. 218 crore. The new line will manufacture up to 100 engines annually and is scheduled to be fully established by 2028-29, catering to indigenous helicopters including Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter (LCH), added Singh. He also called for greater integration of MSMEs, start-ups, private industry, academia and research institutions into the propulsion ecosystem.

headline: Stop daily drama, learn from Modi to win people's support: BJP to Congress
content: the Congress protest against the Election Commission of India as drama, the BJP Tuesday slammed the principal Opposition party and leaders of non-NDA parties who had joined it of abusing the Commission after failing to secure the mandate of the people. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, should learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP on securing peoples support on the basis of work instead of relying on drama. It is time to stop the drama that Rahul Gandhi ji and his colleagues keep doing daily against the Election Commission and the Supreme Court. It has been going on since 2014 In a democracy, serve the people and you will get their mandate, he said. You call the Election Commission a thief, the government a thief. This will neither serve democracy nor the rise of the Congress party again. I especially want to tell Rahul Gandhi ji: Learn from Modi ji, from BJP karyakartas who continue to serve, not for their own sakes but selflessly. If you serve them, you will earn the trust of the people. Doing this drama will not help, he said. Asking the Congress to stop peddling the narrative of anti-national forces, Rijiju sought to underline that the party which ruled the country for 55 years, including two years of the Emergency, was now talking of democracy. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the Opposition leaders were venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the Opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand. Were those victories illegitimate? he said. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he said. Lok Sabha MP and former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad said Rahul Gandhi, Congress, and the Opposition alliance were attempting to create an atmosphere of anarchy in the country. He said the Supreme Court had held the SIR to be legally valid yet the Congress was insulting the voters of the country by blaming the Election Commission for its repeated electoral defeats. Instead of accepting the peoples verdict, the Congress is trying to undermine democratic institutions and create confusion and disorder through unfounded accusations, Prasad said. The question is whether Rahul Gandhi, the Congress party, and the Opposition alliance want anarchy in the country. Opposition leaders have gathered in Delhi and surrounded a sensitive area of the national Capital. Opposition leaders are claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mohan Bhagwat have Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar under their control. This is extremely irresponsible, and we strongly condemn it, he said. He said Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had gone even further and said that all elections should be cancelled and conducted again through ballot papers which reflects their real intention and desire. Congress leaders cannot win fair elections and, therefore, they now want a return to booth capturing, stamping, and winning elections through pressure by pouring ink into ballot boxes. They want to prevent the poor, Dalits and marginalised sections from voting in villages. This is how the Congress used to win, whether in Bihar or Uttar Pradesh, he said. Addressing the media at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. In the evening, after the Election Commission issued a statement saying no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm Tuesday and that it was later informed by police that Opposition MPs wanted a meeting at Parliament House Annexe, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Gandhi: It is clear that telling the EC anything was not his intention Neither did he seek any appointment, and when time was given, he did not go. After that, when it was said that a representative would be sent to collect a memorandum from him, he was not ready.

headline: 'Extraordinary Courage': US House Honours Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar For Foiling Flydubai Terror Attack
content: US House honours Indian pilot Smit Machchhar for foiling the attempted terrorist attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The US House of Representatives has passed a resolution honouring Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, while condemning the attempted terrorist attack on the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight. The resolution honours Machchhar for his role in thwarting the attack onboard the Flydubai flight on September 30, 2026. - Smit Machchhar Hailed By PM Modi | Speaks To Pilots Parents After Flydubai Crisis | - First Visuals Of Injured Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar Surface After Flydubai Cockpit Attack - Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar Praised After Flydubai Cockpit Attack; Wishes Pour In For Recovery - Who Is Smit Machchhar? The Indian Pilot Who Saved 174 Passengers | Flydubai Hero Story | According to the resolution, Flydubai Flight 1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, Israel, carrying approximately 174 passengers. The majority of the passengers were Israeli citizens, while four were United States citizens and 27 were children. First officer attacked captain The resolution states that midway through the flight, the first officer attacked Machchhar on the flight deck with the aircrafts emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls. The aircraft lost more than 14,000 feet of altitude in under 30 seconds following the incident, according to the resolution. It said Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack despite suffering grave injuries. Whereas Captain Smit Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and, despite grave injuries, used his remaining strength to unlock the cockpit door so that off-duty pilots could enter and land the aircraft and so that crew and passengers could restrain the first officer," the resolution reads. Aircraft landed safely in Saudi Arabia The resolution said the aircraft subsequently landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia, with all passengers and crew accounted for. It also referred to an announcement made by the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates on October 3, 2026. Whereas, on October 3, 2026, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the Emirati investigation had determined that the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act," the resolution said. The House resolution also commended the actions of the off-duty pilots, cabin crew and passengers who helped secure the flight deck and bring the aircraft safely down. US condemns attack as act of terrorism The resolution said the House of Representatives honours Machchhar for his extraordinary courage" in protecting everyone aboard the aircraft. It also commends the heroic actions of the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down". The resolution further wishes Machchhar and all those injured a full recovery. It condemns the attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 as an act of terrorism and as an attack on the safety of international civil aviation". The House resolution also calls for a full and expeditious investigation" by the governments of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. It further calls for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed. The resolution was submitted by Mr Gottheimer in the House of Representatives. The US House of Representatives passed a resolution honouring Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary courage in thwarting an attempted terrorist attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 on September 30, 2026.

headline: Andhra Police Uncover Pakistan-Linked Spy Network In 'Operation Firewall'; 2 Arrested | Exclusive Details
content: Linked Spy Network In Operation Firewall; 2 Arrested | Exclusive Details Targeted defence officials were allegedly engaged through chats, voice calls, and video calls before being honeytrapped and induced to share sensitive information In exclusive information accessed by CNN-, the Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence (AP CI) Cell has uncovered an alleged Pakistan-linked espionage operation targeting Indian Defence personnel as part of its ongoing investigation into the suspected sharing of sensitive and classified information related to defence establishments, strategic locations, and naval assets. The operation, designated Operation Firewall2026", has reportedly exposed a modus operandi in which female Pakistan Intelligence Operatives (PIOs) allegedly used fake social-media profiles to target Defence personnel. - NEET UG Paper Leak Case: CBI Probe Nears Final Stage, Charge Sheet Likely Soon - Gyanesh Kumar Faces Kerala Vigilance Enquiry Over 2006 PWD Allegations | CEC Under Scrutiny | - Rs. 657-Crore Love Affair: Chandigarh Officers Dancer Girlfriend, House, Luxury Trips Under CBI Probe - Multi-State NIA Crackdown: Arrests Across Bengal, Assam & Kerala Over IMK Links | According to officials, the operatives initially approached the defence personnel through platforms such as Facebook and Instagram, and after establishing trust, shifted communications to WhatsApp. The targets were allegedly engaged through chats, voice calls, and video calls before being honeytrapped and induced to share sensitive information. The information allegedly sought included details about the movement and number of naval ships and submarines, photographs, videos, details of Commanding Officers, and other classified information. One of the alleged PIOs, Joshita Pall, reportedly established contact with a target through Facebook before shifting the communication to WhatsApp. She allegedly introduced herself as an employee of a ship-building company in Mumbai and sought information on the movement and number of ships and submarines, photographs, and details of their Commanding Officers, besides offering monetary inducements for sharing such information. Another alleged Pakistan Intelligence Operative, Anvi Mehta, reportedly introduced herself as a psychologist based in Delhi and allegedly attempted to honeytrap naval personnel through voice and video calls. Officials stated that Anvi Mehta allegedly sought photographs of naval ships and sensitive establishments and attempted to induce personnel to show sensitive areas of naval establishments and ships or submarines during video calls. The Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell uncovered an alleged Pakistan-linked espionage operation targeting Indian Defence personnel. The operation, designated Operation Firewall2026, exposed female Pakistan Intelligence Operatives using fake social-media profiles. The investigation led to the arrest of two persons and involves 18 suspects, including 13 naval personnel. Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contract driver, was arrested for allegedly sharing sensitive information and receiving money. Pradeep Mukharjee, a naval employee, was arrested for allegedly sharing an OTP and sensitive information with PIOs. The PIOs also induced Indian personnel to share WhatsApp OTPs, offering monetary incentives through cryptocurrency or other intermediaries. Such OTPs are subsequently used to activate WhatsApp accounts in Pakistan, which are then allegedly utilised for further communication, honeytrapping, and collecting sensitive defence information. Investigators further suspect that financial inducements were facilitated through cryptocurrency channels and other intermediaries originating from Pakistan, establishing an alleged financial link between the PIOs and the targeted personnel. As part of the investigation of Operation Firewall2026 launched on October 1, officials say the Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence cell has arrested two persons in connection with an alleged Pakistan-linked espionage network involving 18 suspects, including 13 naval personnel. The operation involved 12 AP CI teams deployed across 10 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, and Bihar. The teams worked in coordination with State ATS units, naval officials, and local police, and seized electronic devices from the suspects. According to the AP CI Cell, Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contract driver engaged for naval officers, was arrested in Visakhapatnam for allegedly sharing sensitive/classified information about naval and defence establishments with a Pakistan-based intelligence operative and receiving money in return. He is currently in judicial custody at Visakhapatnam District Jail. The second accused, Pradeep Mukharjee, a naval employee at the Visakhapatnam Naval Base, was arrested in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. He is accused of sharing an OTP for activation of a WhatsApp account by a Pakistan Intelligence Operative (PIO), communicating with PIOs, and allegedly sharing sensitive information concerning naval and defence establishments. He was subsequently produced before a court in Vijayawada and remanded to judicial custody. Operation Firewall-2026 is an ongoing investigation launched on October 1 by the Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell that uncovered an alleged Pakistan-linked espionage network targeting Indian Defence personnel.

headline: Teacher arrested under POCSO Act for sexually harassing a 13-year-old boy
content: The Colachel All Women Police have arrested a teacher on charge of sexually harassing a teenaged boy. The police said teacher Vedhakkann, 52, of Paalapallam near Colachel sexually harassed a 13-year-old boy when he was in the bible class being conducted by a church there. When the boy refused to go to the school on Monday, his parents asked him the reason. As the boy revealed about the sexual harassment by the teacher, who is also taking bible class, his father filed a complaint with Colachel All Women Police, who arrested Vedhakkann on Tuesday under the POCSO (Protection of Children against Sexual Offences) Act.

headline: Bypoll 2026 Highlights: Madurantakam Leads With 85.99% Turnout, Nandigram Logs 80.67% As Polling Concludes
content: Bypoll 2026 Highlights: Voting has concluded in all six constituencies across three states and the Union Territory of Puducherry that went to the polls on Tuesday. Voting was held in four Assembly constituenciesNandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, and Thattanchavady in Puducherryalong with the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam. Polling remained brisk across the constituencies, with voter turnout crossing 79 per cent in all the five assembly seats by 6 pm. Madurantakam recorded the highest turnout at 85.99 per cent, followed by Thattanchavady at 80.81 per cent and Dharapuram at 80.31 per cent. Nandigram recorded 80.67 per cent turnout, while Rejinagar registered 79.85 per cent by 6 pm. The bypoll results are being closely watched as they may provide an early indication of the political mood and the direction of politics in the respective states. In West Bengal, attention is particularly focused on Nandigram and Rejinagar. The BJPs performance is being watched after its victory in the April Assembly elections and its subsequent formation of the state government. Nandigram has also drawn attention due to the BJP fielding Hasirani Rath, mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who was killed shortly after the Assembly election victory. The Opposition remains fragmented in both constituencies, with multiple parties and factions in the fray. In Tamil Nadu, Madurantakam and Dharapuram are witnessing four-cornered contests involving the TVK, DMK, AIADMK and CPI. Former AIADMK MLAs K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama are contesting on TVK tickets. The counting of votes will take place n October 9. headline: CBI Raids Bhagwant Mann's Camp Office In Corruption Case; Punjab CM Claims 'Misuse Of Agencies'
content: to the CBI action, CM Mann alleged that the central agencies were being misused ahead of the Punjab elections. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Tuesday registered a corruption case involving an Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and other senior officers, and conducted searches at three premises linked to the Punjab chief minister across the state. The searches included Manns camp office" at Kothi No 50 in Mohali, the native village of his OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman at Gharcho in Sangrur, and another location in Chandigarh, according to officials. Raids are also being conducted in Kharar where bag full of cash was thrown from a flat previously during the ED raids in a dramatic visual in the month of may. So far, in total four locations are being raided by the agencies against Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. - Punjab Govt Transfers Rs. 1,262 Crore To 36.87 Lakh Women Under Satkar Scheme: Mann - 48 Haryana BJP MLAs, 1 Punjab Mission: What PM Modis Saturday Meeting Was Really About - Punjab Stubble Burning: Who Will End The Parali Politics? BJP Targets Bhagwant Mann | Plain Speak - Economy Destroyed, Chitta Flows Freely: Amit Shah Attacks Punjab AAP Govt Over Drugs, Corruption The CBI action followed directions from the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which ordered the federal agency to conduct the probe. What Punjab HC said The High Court directed the CBI to investigate the matter after noting that material shared by the Enforcement Directorate prima facie indicated the involvement of the OSD and other senior officers in acts of corruption. The High Court order came on a public interest litigation filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who had sought an independent probe into the matter raised by the ED with the Punjab Police through letters to the Director General of Police. Following the courts directions, the CBI registered the corruption case and carried out searches at the locations linked to Mann and his OSD. Mann alleges BJP is nervous Reacting to the CBI action, Mann alleged that the central agencies were being misused ahead of the Punjab elections. In a post on X, Mann said the BJP had started preparing for the elections. CBI raided my camp officenow ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab, so that Punjab govt and me can be defamed. The BJP is nervous seeing the love from people," he posted. Punjab Minister Harbhajan Singh ETO also alleged that the BJP was using central agencies instead of approaching voters ahead of the elections. While preparing for the elections, instead of going to the people in Punjab, BJP started misusing the central agencies. The CBI raid on the camp office of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann ji is proof of this," ETO said. He alleged that efforts were being made to defame the Mann government but claimed that people in Punjab were aware of the truth. Efforts are being made to defame the Mann government, but the people of Punjab are aware of the truth. No matter how much pressure you apply, you cannot break peoples trust," he said. Kejriwal backs Mann AAP Convenor Arvind Kejriwal also reacted to the CBI searches, linking the action to the upcoming elections. The CBI raid on the Punjab Chief Ministers office two months before the elections is the result of the BJPs frustration," Kejriwal said in a post on X. He alleged that the BJP-led government at the Centre had repeatedly pushed Punjabis around", referring to the farmers movement, the issue of Punjabs water and the Punjab University issue. And now, its even pushing around their elected Chief Minister," Kejriwal said. He further alleged that the BJP could not win the Punjab elections by contesting them directly and was therefore seeking to fight them with the help of the ED and CBI. But Punjabis have made up their minds, and they will respond to the BJPs CBI raid in the upcoming elections by electing Bhagwant Mann with 100+ seats and making him Chief Minister again," Kejriwal said. Punjab is scheduled to go for Assembly polls early next year. The CBI registered a corruption case involving the Chief Minister's OSD and other senior officers following direct orders from the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

headline: Union Cabinet hails 25 years of Modi at helm, flags 'mandate, trust, his governance'
content: The Union Cabinet adopted a resolution Tuesday, hailing the enduring trust that the public have reposed in Narendra Modi and his governance achievements over the last 25 years, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and later as Prime Minister of the country. Briefing reporters on the decisions of the Union Cabinet at its meeting Tuesday, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution covers Modis unbroken public service record, spanning the period from October 7, 2001, when he first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat, to his continuous tenure as Prime Minister up to October 7, 2026. Vaishnaw said the Prime Minister received a standing ovation from all Cabinet colleagues during the meeting. The resolution congratulated Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. An official statement on the resolution stated: Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by the principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that the public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi. The statement listed ten salient features of his leadership of Gujarat and India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarats successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigrams separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarats experience across India. His sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels, it stated. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity, it stated. His determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for womens reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs. 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind, it stated. The resolution lays particular emphasis on Modis willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose, it stated. Under Modis leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs. 2 lakh crore to over Rs. 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs. 2 lakh crore to more than Rs. 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen Indias ability to meet its needs, it stated. Modis faith in technology, it said, emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing Indias own Covid vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moons south pole demonstrated PM Modis vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights Modis ability to give India direction through global upheavals. During Covid, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times. The resolution cited the 2016 surgical strikes, the 2019 Balakot air strikes and the 2025 Operation Sindoor as national security red lines established under Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staffs post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust, the statement said. The resolution links Indias rising stature with Modis ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Unions G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how Indias capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and Indias growing influence and contribution to shared solutions, it stated. Modis vision, it said, unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarats dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lallas consecration strengthened Indias connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047, it stated. Modis approach to disaster management was also hailed Tuesday. Gujarat was recovering from the devastating Bhuj earthquake that struck just months before Modi became Chief Minister. He set a three-year recovery target and a move towards mitigation. An Institute of Seismological Research was established in 2003. As Prime Minister, he released the countrys first National Disaster Management Plan in 2016. He articulated a 10-point agenda for Disaster Risk Reduction at the Asian Ministerial Conference in New Delhi, calling for technology and mobile-based warnings, wider risk coverage and greater international cooperation. The governments focus also moved to early warnings and zero casualty. A multi-hazard early warning system was launched under Modis tenure and the India Meteorological Department has been providing district-level, impact-based and risk-based warnings while an indigenous multi-hazard decision support system has been operational since 2023. At the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019, India also launched the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, which today has 59 member countries and 13 partner organisations. India has also deployed search and rescue teams at disaster sites, notably in Nepal in 2015 and 2026, in Turkiye and Syria after the 2023 earthquake.

headline: Who Is Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit? Operation Sindoor, Safed Sagar Veteran Set To Be New IAF Chief
content: With nearly four decades of service, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has held several key operational and senior command positions. The government has appointed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, the Defence Ministry announced on Tuesday. Air Marshal Dixit will take charge in the rank of Air Chief Marshal from the afternoon of October 31, 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, who is set to retire the same day. - Kargil War, Operation Sindoor Veteran Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit Appointed New Indian Air Force Chief - Video: F-35A, Tejas Aircraft Fly Together During Joint Exercise Tarang Shakti - Mohsin Naqvi Loses Asian Council Support, Bangladesh's Tamim Iqbal Raring To Replace Him - Ram Temple Donation Counting Staff To Wear Pocketless Saffron Jumpsuits, Mobile Phones Banned In Sanctum Who Is Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit?
