headline: Supreme Court Strength Grows To 37 Judges; CJI Administers Oath To Three New Justices
content: The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended their names to the government on September 28. Before the three elevations, the top court had a working strength of 34. A day after Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal announced that the government had cleared the names of three judges for elevation to the Supreme Court, Chief Justice Surya Kant on Tuesday administered the oath of office to Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh. With their elevation, the Supreme Courts working strength rose to 37, one short of its sanctioned strength of 38. - 'Create Fear In The Minds Of Culprits': SC's 5 Big Observations On Women's Safety In Delhi - 'Strikes At Heart Of Constitution': Justice Ujjal Bhuyan Calls SIR 'Disenfranchisement Of Indian Citizens' - SC Stays Execution Of Terror Operative In 2008 Ahmedabad Blasts Case, Issues Notice To Gujarat Govt - 'Justice Not Only About Conviction': Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Orders Child Online Safety Framework The three new judges took oath at the auditorium of the new Supreme Court block in the presence of all sitting Supreme Court judges, judicial officers and officials from various high courts. Their family members and lawyers from the Supreme Court and high courts were also present at the ceremony. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended their names to the government on September 28. Before the three elevations, the top court had a working strength of 34. Supreme Court Now Has Three Women Judges With Justice Sunita Agarwals appointment, the number of women judges in the Supreme Court has risen to three. She joins Justices BV Nagarathna and Venkita Subramani Mohana. Justice Nagarathna has been a Supreme Court judge since August 31, 2021, while Justice Mohana was appointed to the top court on June 2, 2026. While Justices Agarwal and Nagarathna came to the Supreme Court after serving in high courts, Justice Mohana was elevated directly from the Bar. She had been a senior advocate in the Supreme Court. Justice Nagarathna is also set to become Indias first woman Chief Justice of India in 2027, although her tenure as CJI will last less than a month. Who Are The New Supreme Court Judges? Justices Agarwal and Upadhyaya hail from the Allahabad High Court, while Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh is from the Jharkhand High Court. Justice Agarwal was Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, Justice Upadhyaya was Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, and Justice Singh was Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court before their elevation to the Supreme Court. Justice Sunita Agarwal Justice Sunita Agarwal was born on April 30, 1966, and enrolled as an advocate with the Uttar Pradesh Bar Association on December 16, 1990. After 21 years of practice, she was elevated as an additional judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011. She was sworn in as a permanent judge on August 6, 2013. After serving as an Allahabad High Court judge for 12 years, Justice Agarwal was appointed Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court on July 23, 2023. Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya was born on June 16, 1965, in Muskarai village of Ambedkar Nagar district in Uttar Pradesh. He graduated in law from Lucknow University in 1991 and enrolled as an advocate on May 11 that year. He was appointed Chief Standing Counsel for Uttar Pradesh in May 2007 and continued in the post until his elevation to the Allahabad High Court. He was appointed a puisne judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011, and became a permanent judge on August 6, 2013. Justice Upadhyaya took oath as Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court on July 29, 2023, and was transferred as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court on January 21, 2025. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh was born on July 7, 1965, and obtained his LLB degree from the University of Delhi. He enrolled as an advocate in the Patna High Court in 1990 and practised there until 2000. He then practised in the Jharkhand High Court from 2001. He was appointed an additional judge of the Jharkhand High Court on January 24, 2012, and was confirmed as a permanent judge on January 16, 2014. He served as Acting Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court from December 20, 2022, to February 19, 2023. He took oath as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court on April 17, 2023, and was transferred as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court on July 19, 2025. Chief Justice Surya Kant administered the oath of office to Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh.

headline: 'You need partners for strategic autonomy, you can't do everything by yourself': Finland envoy to India
content: protectionism rising from big powers like the US, what would be Finlands priorities in terms of the India-EU FTA, set to be operationalised in the coming months? The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) sends a clear and strong message that when it comes to international trade, rules-based trade is still beneficial for all of us. This applies to all the FTAs that both India and the European Union (EU) are signing with other partners as well. So, there is a strong signal that there are several countries that want to have rules in international trade. The US has imposed steep reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods and even on several EU goods. So, how does Finland assess the impact of all of this on global supply chains and on small, open economies? We are living in quite a turbulent time, when it comes to geopolitics and geoeconomics. Everybody is looking at partners and diversifying things to make sure you have the freedom of manoeuvre, and also certain (amount of) predictability. We are all doing that be it India, the EU or Finland. That is one of the lessons learned. India has been seeking from the EU to ease the CBAM, visa norms for professionals and even data protection. What is Finlands position on this? We are part of the EU, so we have been part of the decision making on the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and the same applies to the EU data protection laws. But we believe it is about level playing field, and sustainability in the long run. Many Indian companies are already adapting; something I personally noticed is that sustainability issues are more on the agenda in India. Should India and Finland collaborate more on critical minerals and batteries? Because Finland has large reserves, India has demand. That is also part of the EU-Finland-India partnership. Again, it all comes down to the supply chain and strategic autonomy. And in that context, the EU and India see each other as trusted partners. And you need partners when it comes to strategic autonomy. You cannot do everything by yourself. With navigation disrupted due to war, especially in the Red Sea and the Black Sea, is there a scope for cooperation on alternative routes, maybe IMEC, mooted by India in 2023? Definitely, one of the consequences of the recent geopolitical, geoeconomical changes in the world is that, again, it all comes down to the supply chains and strategic autonomy. All the countries are looking for new logistic routes. They want to cut down dependencies. When it comes to this particular corridor, we all understand that there are several geopolitical issues at the moment. We have been supporting it from the beginning, but one has to be realistic. And when it comes to logistic routes, it must be feasible. For the time being, there are certain geopolitical issues in West Asia that are hindering it at the moment. You have been talking about resilient supply chains and strategic autonomy. Do you think globalisation, as we know, will change forever? I hope not. For a small country like us, we would like to see sort of rules and institutions when it comes to the international order. We would also like to see that world trade would be free. So, we are partnering with countries that have similar views. Finland, India and the EU have similar views when it comes to international order, as well as on multilateralism. India and Finland are definitely natural partners when it comes to multilateralism, the UN charter and the UN-based multilateralism. We would like to see India as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, and we believe that the Council needs to be reformed. India said that it is in touch with Russia and Ukraine to find a solution to the ongoing war, and the Ukrainian Foreign Minister has said they support Indias proposal. Have there been discussions between Kyiv and other EU partners on the proposal? Yeah, sort of two remarks on that. Firstly, all the attempts to bring the war to an end are highly appreciated and needed. As we all know, it has been underway, and it is already the 5th year. The global consequences are clear. Your External Minister has talked about the consequences multiple times, so that is clear. We are in a situation where everybody else is ready to negotiate to stop the war except the Russians. So basically, what we need is that the global community incentivises Russia to come to the negotiation table, and then to have the war ended. Incentivise, as in how would that work? To incentivise in terms of sanctions, or trade? Incentivise that they would understand it is also for their best to stop the war because it is clear that the consequences for the Russian economy and the society are huge. At the end of the day, too many human beings are being lost in the war. You have arrived in New Delhi at a time when the India-EU relations are getting stronger, and the India-EU FTA is in the last leg before being signed. What do you think about the collaboration between New Delhi and Helsinki at this point? We have been witnessing record-high activities this year: Finland Prime Minister Petteri Orpo visited India, President Alexander Stubb made a state visit to India, as well as we also had the Nordic-India Summit in Oslo. Then a few weeks ago in Gandhinagar, there was the 10th edition of the World Circular Economy Forum organised for the first time in South Asia, by the governments of Finland and India. And when you add to that the FTA and the perspective of the agreement to be enforced next year, this creates a great momentum to deepen our collaboration. And therefore, our task here will be to turn this framework into concrete activities.

headline: District Collector inspects rain-hit areas in Ooty
content: hit areas in Ooty The Nilgiris District Collector, Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru, inspected the Boat House Road adjoining the Udhagamandalam Railway Station after a brief spell of heavy rain led to the area becoming waterlogged on Monday and Tuesday. According to the district administration, Udhagamandalam town received around 58 mm of rainfall till Tuesday morning. The Collector, following her inspection, said that waterlogging had been reported along the Boat House Road, Karnataka Garden and Fingerpost, and that immediate work was undertaken to drain the areas. She said that the flooded areas were quickly cleared of standing water soon after the rains stopped, except at the railway station and under the railway bridge that spans the Kodappamund Channel and Boat House Road. The Collector said that the bridge was extremely old and that the design of the road infrastructure underneath it leads to inundation. Steps were being taken to permanently fix a motor system that can pump out water from the bridge following spells of heavy rain in the future. She added that earth movers, pumps and equipment for clearing blocked drains and tree cutting are kept ready to deal with any emergencies arising from rains during the Northeast monsoon. The Collector also said that further dredging of the Ooty Lake is to take place at a cost of 2.5 crore. Ms. Tanneeru said that dredging works had already been undertaken two years ago at a cost of 7.51 crore, but water hyacinth had taken over a large part of the lake. The hyacinth will be removed when dredging works restart from Thursday onwards. She also appealed to the public to stay indoors and avoid unnecessary travel during spells of heavy rain, that can increase risks of trees becoming uprooted and power lines getting snapped.

headline: 'Targeting of commercial shipping must end': India condemns latest attack on vessels
content: The Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) condemned the targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, and civilian infrastructure following two separate attacks in the Black Sea and off Oman that left two foreign seafarers dead and several Indian crew members injured. Eleven Indian crew members were injured on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) after a Panama-flagged commercial vessel MT On Peace was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Thanking the Omani authorities for their support, MEA said that the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Omans Khasab. In another attack in the Black Sea, two crew died and 11 were rescued on Monday (October 5, 2026) after a fire broke out on commercial ship MV Royad Mammadov, Romanian authorities said. The Black Sea has become an increasing battlefield for drone attacks in the Russia-Ukraine war. MEA said two foreign seafarers were killed and some members of the crew, including Indian nationals were injured in the attack, adding that, the injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. Thanking the Romanian authorities, the Ministry said that the three Indian nationals, who were part of the crew of the ship, are safe. Expressing grave concern for the safety of global commerce, MEA mentioned that it will continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. MEA stated that navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest, saying that targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end

headline: NLC India Limited gets new Director for Power
content: PLSS Chaitanya Prakash assumed office as the Director (Power) of NLC India Limited (NLCIL) on Monday. According to an NLCIL press release, Mr. Prakash had earlier served as Executive Director (Operations) at Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), overseeing strategic operations and advancing capital projects. He had also served in Green Valley Renewable Energy Limited (GVREL), a joint venture of DVC and NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) and DVC-CIL Power Private Limited (DCPPL), a joint venture of DVC and Coal India Limited.

headline: 'Mulling Legal Action Against Mahua Moitra': Chief Electoral Officer Who Conducted Bengal SIR Responds To Allegations | Exclusive
content: I am seeking legal opinion and preparing a defamation case...We need to know what documents she is relying on to make these allegations, Manoj Kumar Agarwal said Manoj Kumar Agarwal, the Chief Electoral Officer under whom Bengals Special Intensive Revision took place and who is the present Chief Secretary of Bengal, said he is seeking legal opinion and preparing to initiate defamation proceedings over allegations made by Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra in connection with the SIR. I am seeking legal opinion and preparing for a defamation case. She is trying to malign me. He termed the allegations baseless" and defended the electoral-roll revision process, asserting that the deletion and addition of names are governed by the prescribed legal framework. 2 biggest architects of Bengal SIR committed every illegality under the planet. Subrata Kaku & Manoj Uncle watch out. India is coming for you next. Bachh nahi paoge. Mahua Moitra (@MahuaMoitra) October 3, 2026 Manoj Kumar Agarwal is seeking legal opinion to initiate defamation proceedings against Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra. Moitra alleged that Agarwal and Subrata Gupta were the "2 biggest architects of Bengal SIR" and committed "every illegality under the planet." Agarwal stated that the Chief Electoral Officer does not have the power to suo motu add or delete names from the electoral roll. Electoral-roll data covering all 80,681 booths has been uploaded on the website for public verification. Judicial officers from West Bengal and Odisha were appointed under High Court supervision to oversee the process. According to Agarwal, the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) has the authority to add or delete names from the electoral roll. The District Election Officer (DEO) and the designated appellate authorities have their respective roles in the process, he said. As far as I understand the prevailing law, the Chief Electoral Officer does not have the power to suo motu add or delete names from the electoral roll," Agarwal said. He added that where an appeal is received through the DEO, the CEO can exercise appellate authority, but there is no provision for the CEO to suo motu delete a voters name. Agarwal also questioned the evidence supporting the allegations. I do not know on what basis these allegations are being made or what evidence has been produced in support of them," he said. Referring to the electoral-roll data available on the Chief Electoral Officers website, Agarwal said voters could verify information relating to deceased, duplicate, shifted and absent electors for booths across the constituencies concerned. He said the draft electoral roll had already been published online and that voters had been given an opportunity to file Forms 6, 7 and 8 for inclusion, deletion or correction, as applicable. Agarwal said electoral-roll data covering all 80,681 booths had been uploaded on the website and was available for public verification. On the subsequent judicial oversight of the process, Agarwal said the matter had been placed under the supervision of judicial officers following the Supreme Courts intervention. He said judicial officers from West Bengal and Odisha were appointed under High Court supervision to oversee the process. Agarwal also rejected any allegation that he had personally or illegally deleted voters names. I discharged my responsibilities transparently and in accordance with the law. I did not illegally delete anyones name and I have not done anything wrong," he said. On Subrata Gupta, whom Moitra also named in her post, Agarwal said Gupta was an observer and did not have statutory powers to add or delete names from the electoral roll. His role, Agarwal said, was to monitor the process and report any irregularities to the Election Commission of India. Agarwal said he was prepared to provide an explanation to anyone seeking clarification regarding his role. I am very clear about the limits of my authority. I am not someone who acts without restraint. Whatever I do will be done strictly in accordance with the law," he said. On the ongoing protests and controversy surrounding the SIR exercise in Bengal, Agarwal declined to comment, saying the matter was sub judice. He, however, maintained that the exercise was not conducted either in favour of or against any political party. There were fictitious voters, but at that time this MP did not raise the issue. We do not fear anything. We know exactly what we have done and are confident that our actions were in accordance with the law," Agarwal said. Manoj Kumar Agarwal is seeking legal advice and preparing a defamation case against Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra over her social media allegations claiming he and Subrata Gupta committed illegalities during Bengal's Special Intensive Revision.

headline: 'Annan Seer' scheme: Tamil Nadu government allocates ₹812 crore
content: The Tamil Nadu government on Monday (October 5, 2026) issued an order allocating 812 crore in the first phase for the Annan Seer scheme, under which eligible brides will be given eight grams of gold and a silk saree. Women from families with an annual income not exceeding 2.5 lakh will be eligible for the scheme. The order, issued by Pallavi Baldev, Secretary, Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, said detailed guidelines for implementing the scheme would be issued separately. The gold and sarees would be procured in accordance with the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 1996. The price of gold would be based on the rate fixed by the Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA), it said. Marriages taking place on or after the date of issue of the government order would be covered under the scheme. Applications will be received online.

headline: Rahul Gandhi's stand-on-barricade moment came with a Led Zeppelin track
content: led INDIA opposition bloc protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Ok. So they werent actually there. But Congress MP Rahul Gandhi served up some Led Zeppelin spirit in an Instagram reel; the clip showed the Leader of the Opposition standing astride Delhi Polices yellow metal barricades, hands on hips while a sea of protesters swarmed around. At 6.45 pm three hours after it was posted the reel had been viewed over 2.7 million times. And if you want to check out the full song (its a banger!) you can do so here: But the day began with less hard rock and more political sloganeering; opposition MPs led by Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, as well as Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and the Trinamool Congress Abhishek Banerjee, set off on a march from parliament to the EC office. The purpose? To confront CEC Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision of state/UT voter rolls. The substance of these allegations that the EC helps the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party win elections have been made frequently by Gandhi and other opposition MPs, though there was little by way of public response. The Express investigative reports prompted a furious response from the opposition and democracy activists, including the Abhijeet Dipke-founded Cockroach Janata Party, all of whom are now demanding Gyanesh Kumar resign as the CEC and the voter lists be rolled back. On Tuesday afternoon those protests led to tense showdowns between Delhi Police and the protesters, with dozens of the latter group herded away into police buses and detained. Both Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were also briefly detained. She was sitting in a bus, parked outside Akashvani Bhavan the headquarters of All India Radio and Rahul was about to get in. Suddenly, they looked at each other and walked past the cops and into that compound. The move seemed off-script and the police were caught flat-footed. This sort of off-the-cuff thinking seems to have become part of Rahul Gandhis personal gameplan in cornering the government during public protests. Remember the impromptu sit-in outside Prime Minister Modis home in July to protest police violence against NEET protesters? In fact, till they walked into Akashvani Bhavan, most Congress leaders said they thought the protest was over squashed by the authorities who seemed better prepared this time than last, when the CJP protested at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG exam paper leak. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, one of them said. Clearly Rahul had a plan, though.

headline: Kargil War, Operation Sindoor Veteran Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit Appointed New Indian Air Force Chief
content: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is known for pushing the indigenous LCA Tejas and other indigenous aircraft projects in the force. Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the new Chief of the Indian Air Force. He will succeed the current Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh. Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh superannuates office on October 31. Air Marshal Dixit is majorly known for pushing the indigenous LCA Tejas and other indigenous aircraft projects in the force. He is expected to further promote the governments Aatmanirbharta initiative in defence. - Who Is Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit? Operation Sindoor, Safed Sagar Veteran Set To Be New IAF Chief - IAF Cheif: India May Seal 114-Rafale Jet Deal With France By March 2027 | BREAKING | - Tejas Mk1A: Review Meeting Post Oct 15 To Decide Delivery Schedule, First Lot Expected By Year-End - We Possess Necessary Capabilities: IAF Chief On Pakistan-China Fifth Gen Fighter Plans Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force on December 6, 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Defence Staff Service College in Bangladesh and National Defence College. He has more than 3,500 hours of flying experience on various aircrafts including to name a few; Mirage-2000, variants of Mig, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, HAWK and Tejas. He is an Experimental Test Pilot and a Qualified Flying Instructor. During his service career spanning approximately four decades, he has been actively involved in numerous operations and exercises including Op-Safed Sagar, Op-Rakshak and Op Sindoor. Who is Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit? Air Marshal Dixit, service number 18558 F(P), belongs to the fighter stream and was commissioned as part of the 138 Course. According to reports, he was promoted to Flight Lieutenant on December 6, 1991, Wing Commander on May 5, 2003, Group Captain on March 1, 2009, and Air Commodore on June 17, 2013. He became Air Vice Marshal on June 11, 2019, Air Marshal on October 1, 2022 and Commander-in-Chief on September 1, 2024. His training includes the 69th National Defence Academy course as a cadet and the 57th National Defence College course as an Air Commodore. During his illustrious career, the Air Marshal has held a number of significant field and staff appointments. He commanded a front-line fighter air base in Western Sector and a premiere fighter training base in Southern Sector. Held key operational and project posts Dixit served as Commanding Officer of No 9 Squadron in Gwalior between December 15, 2003 and January 15, 2006. He also served as Principal Director, Air Staff Requirements, at Air Headquarters in Delhi. He was Air Officer Commanding at Air Force Station Bidar from January 2018 to May 2019 and later served as Air Defence Commander with Southern Air Command in Trivandrum. From October 2020 to September 2021, he was Assistant Chief of Air Staff, Projects, at Air Headquarters. He then served as Assistant Chief of Air Staff, Plans, from October 2021 to September 2022. As an Air Marshal, Dixit served as Senior Air Staff Officer at South Western Air Command, Deputy Chief of Air Staff at Air Headquarters and Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Central Air Command in Allahabad. He later served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee, from May 2025 to June 2026. Since July 2026, he has been serving as Principal Staff Officer, Operations, at Air Headquarters, Delhi, and Vice Chief of Air Staff. Air Marshal Dixit has received three awards, as per reports the Vayu Sena Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal and Ati Vishisht Seva Medal. He was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal in 2006 for devotion to duty. As Commanding Officer of a fighter squadron, Dixit oversaw its rejuvenation and re-equipping with Mirage-2000 aircraft. He also played a key role in the acceptance flights and ferrying of 10 new Mirage-2000 aircraft from France to India. The Vishisht Seva Medal was awarded to him in 2011. He has flown 3,200 hours on more than 20 types of aircraft and had served as a Qualified Flying Instructor and Experimental Test Pilot. he ahs also worked on indigenous upgrade projects for Jaguar and MiG-27 aircraft, as well as his role in the technical evaluation and field trials of aircraft under the Medium Multi Role Combat Aircraft programme. He was awarded the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2023. Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the new Chief of the Indian Air Force. He succeeds the current Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, who superannuates from office on October 31.

headline: Students, teachers march in France on biggest day of school protests
content: In Marseille, Nantes and Lyon, the street protests began peacefully mid-morning, with the largest demonstration expected in Paris in the afternoon. Youngsters held aloft smoke flares and placards reading Under our school books, anger and Where are the politicians? Do they even know we exist? Tuesdays demonstrations come after a fortnight of protests which began in Pariss deprived suburbs before spreading across the country. The government responded with riot police, saying the movement had now morphed into urban violence. A teenagers hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday. Franois-Xavier Lauch, prefect of Pas-de-Calais, declined to comment on the exact circumstances, saying some 200 to 250 protesters had been hurling objects at police. The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police dispersal grenade. The High School Students Union said 1,800 high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online. The education ministry did not immediately make numbers available. When the answer is violence, it means democracy is no longer working, said Hugo Vetzel, a high school leaver in Strasbourg now taking classes for the entrance exams to Frances top-tier universities. There is such a gap between the elites and us. Prime Minister Lecornu promises response Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has ordered his ministers to tackle the students leading demands. Those include ensuring absent teachers are replaced, reviewing the length of the 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. school day and the need for longer lunch breaks. The government would also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings, said Lecornu, who demanded ministers send in their first proposals by the end of October. But finding spare cash will be difficult. The protests have piled pressure on a government trying to narrow a ballooning budget deficit as investor concerns about Frances growing debt pile, weak growth and reluctance to rein in spending push bond yields higher. The yield on Frances 10-year bonds briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5% last week. The surge in French borrowing costs has started to spill into the broader euro area, with the sliding euro currency the latest alarm bell for policy makers. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Tuesday there was no need for the European Central Bank to step in. Marine Le Pen, the far-right euro-skeptic populist leading the presidential race ahead of next springs election, set out plans to slash public spending if elected, seeking to establish her fiscal credibility as the bond market crisis deepens. Thousands of arrests Frances interior ministry said 6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said, without specifying the crimes. At least 715 police officers and 215 teenagers have been injured in clashes, according to Lecornus office. Six months before an election to replace Macron, his government and Le Pens National Rally party have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the protests. The LFI denies the accusation. Bally Bagayoko, the LFI mayor of Saint-Denis, a poor Paris suburb, said he opposed violence but stood beside the protesting students. I stand by being on the side of my residents, and high school students are my residents, he said.

headline: Ex-spy chief is arrested in Germany on suspicion of trading state secrets, treason
content: former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service was arrested on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) on suspicion that he had passed state secrets to a foreign intelligence service, the federal prosecutor's office said. August Hanning, who led the Federal Intelligence Service, known by its German acronym BND, from 1998 to 2005, is strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets, attempted treason, and espionage, the federal prosecutor's office said in a statement. Mr. Hanning, 80, was arrested in Bad Toelz-Wolfratshausen in southern Germany. A former aide, identified as Manfred D., was also arrested in Steinfurt in western Germany and has been charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage. The statement did not reveal who the two men were suspected of spying for. The premises of both men were searched on Tuesday (October 6). Former aide allegedly supplied Hanning with BND documents The prosecutor's office said Manfred D. worked as Hanning's chief of staff and later served as chief of staff for several subsequent BND presidents from 2012 until 2026. In his role, he had access to confidential information, the prosecutor's office said. Both suspects are believed to have agreed in 2010 to have Manfred D. continuously transmit valuable intelligence from the BND to Hanning in exchange for payment, the statement said. The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D. provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the federal intelligence service for internal purposes, particularly for executive intelligence briefings, the statement said. Mr. Hanning used the information in private consulting work and, on one occasion, "used classified intelligence provided by Manfred D. to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service. Manfred D., who, in line with German privacy rules, cannot be identified by his full name, provided Mr. Hanning with classified information for several years, the statement said, but it was not immediately clear if the collaboration continued until their arrests on Tuesday. The office did not say which country the foreign agent worked for and said it has yet to be determined if the material reached the intended recipient. The statement added that Hanning was in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D., for several years. Hanning is suspected of involvement in a prominent child abduction case Mr. Hanning came under scrutiny in a separate investigation into the abduction of Hamburg businesswoman Christina Block's children from her ex-husband in Denmark in January 2024 in a custody battle that had been going on for several years. The investigation into that case led to Tuesday's (October 6) arrests. The current proceedings stem from evidence found during a search of Mr. Hanning's residence in connection with that case, the federal prosecutor's office stated. Mr. Hanning and a retired official from the Hamburg State Criminal Police Office are suspected of having accepted a contract from Block in 2022 to abduct her children while serving as executives of a security firm, the public prosecutor's office announced in the fall of 2025, according to German news agency dpa. The Blocks are a prominent Hamburg family best known for their popular national steakhouse chain Block House. The custody trial has received a lot of attention in the country, with German tabloids offering heavy coverage from the court. A message to the BND for comment was not immediately returned. German opposition lawmaker calls for a quick probe German opposition lawmaker Konstantin von Notz expressed shock about the allegations against Hanning and called for a quick investigation. This is a hard-hitting and deeply troubling story," said von Notz, a member of the Greens party and also the German parliament committee overseeing the intelligence services. "We expect a swift and thorough investigation into the egregious allegations levelled against former BND chief Hanning, von Notz told Spiegel Online. "We have been criticising the dubious and wide-ranging lobbying activities of former top officials and those with the highest security clearances in Germany for years, he said and called for banning former officials with security clearances from engaging in private consulting work after leaving office, Spiegel Online reported.

headline: 'Tech-savvy' fighter pilot, who's flown Mirage and Tejas, set to be next Air Chief
content: Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is set to become the next Chief of the Air Staff at the end of this month, the Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday. The announcement comes nearly three weeks before the current Air Chief, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, is due to retire on October 31. Air Marshal Dixit is currently serving as the Vice Chief of the Indian Air Force (IAF). Popular among his colleagues, Air Marshal Dixit is described by officers as a thorough professional, soft-spoken, balanced and a grounded individual. An Experimental Test Pilot and Qualified Flying Instructor, he has more than 3,500 hours of flying experience on aircraft including the Mirage 2000, various MiG variants, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. At the same time, he is known to be an avid reader, highly tech-savvy and a visionary leader. This is also evident from his public speeches. He has consistently emphasised the need for a balanced mix of traditional and modern weapon systems in the militarys inventory, arguing that conventional aircraft must be complemented by emerging technologies such as drones and missiles to ensure long-term operational effectiveness. In a separate speech, he highlighted the lesson from Operation Sindoor that technology has fundamentally altered the relationship between distance and vulnerability in modern warfare, underscoring the importance of real-time surveillance. Over a distinguished career spanning four decades, the decorated officer has held several critical appointments, including Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Central Air Command and Deputy Chief of Air Staff. As CISC, he consistently worked to promote jointness and integration among the three services, according to an earlier government statement. As a commanding officer, he re-equipped No. 9 Squadron with Mirage-2000 aircraft and later commanded a frontline fighter base in the Western Sector and a premier fighter training base in the Southern Sector. He has also served as Directing Staff at the Air Force Test Pilots School and as Principal Director, Air Staff Requirements, at Air Headquarters. The Air Marshal has served as Air Defence Commander of Southern Air Command and held the appointments of Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Projects), Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Plans) at Air Headquarters, Vayu Bhawan, and Senior Air Staff Officer at Headquarters South Western Air Command. During his four-decade-long service career, he has been actively involved in several operations and exercises, including Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak and Operation Sindoor. Born on December 9, 1966, he was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force on December 6, 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, the Defence Services Staff College in Bangladesh and the National Defence College.

headline: The Nobel Prize 2026: An interactive guide
content: Explore this years Nobel winners, and their achievements with this interactive guide. The prizes are being announced from October 5 to 12, 2026. Published: October 6, 2026 | Updated: October 7, 2026 Published: October 6, 2026 | Updated: October 7, 2026 - Physiology & Medicine U.S. U.S. James A. Robinson U.S. For studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson are currently Professors at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Cambridge, U.S. James A. Robinson serves as a Professor at University of Chicago, U.S. Their work examines the reasons for the differences in prosperity between countries, one of them being institutions introduced through colonisation. It focuses on extractive and inclusive colonial institutions that have reversed the fortunes of colonies, making poor colonies richer and rich colonies poorer. Japanese Organisation For its efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons and for demonstrating through witness testimony that nuclear weapons must never be used again. Nihon Hidankyo is the only nation-wide organization of A-bomb survivors of Hiroshima and Nagasaki (Hibakusha). It has member organizations in all 47 Japanese prefectures, thus representing almost all organized Hibakusha. Its officials and members are all Hibakusha. The total number of the surviving Hibakusha living in Japan is 174,080, as of March 2016. There are several thousands of more Hibakusha living in Korea and other parts of the world outside Japan. HIDANKYO is cooperating with those organizations in their work for the defense of the living and rights of these people. For her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life. Han Kang was born in 1970 in the South Korean city of Gwangju before moving with her family to Seoul. She comes from a literary background, her father Han Seung-won being a reputed novelist. Alongside her writing, she has also devoted herself to art and music, which is reflected throughout her entire literary production. Han Kang began her career in 1993 with the publication of a number of poems in the Literature and Society. Her prose debut came in 1995 with the short story collection. Han Kangs major international breakthrough came with the novel The Vegetarian in 2015. In her oeuvre, Han Kang confronts historical traumas and invisible sets of rules and, in each of her works, exposes the fragility of human life. Henri B. Kagan, born 1930 in Boulogne-Billancourt, France, is a renowned French chemist known for his pioneering work in stereochemistry the study of how the three-dimensional arrangement of molecules affects their behaviour. He earned his Ph.D. in 1960 from the Collge de France and later became Professor Emeritus at the Universit Paris-Sud, France. Kenso Soai, born 1950 in Hiroshima, is a Japanese chemist known for his pioneering work in asymmetric autocatalysis, a process in which a chemical reaction can produce more of the same type of molecule and amplify its handedness. He earned his Ph.D. in 1979 from the University of Tokyo, Japan, and is Professor Emeritus at Tokyo University of Science, Japan. The prize was awarded for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discoveries that helped scientists control the "handedness" of molecules. This advance has become important in making medicines. Some molecules come in two versions that are mirror images of each other, much like our left and right hands. These are called chiral molecules. Although the two versions may look almost identical, they can behave very differently inside the body. Our bodies naturally use only one version of many important molecules. This preference for one form is called homochirality. But how does this one-sided chemistry arise? When scientists make chiral molecules in the laboratory, they normally produce both versions. For a long time, it was difficult to make a reaction favour just one. Henri Kagan made a breakthrough in 1986, finding a way to make a chemical reaction produce more of one version than the other. Kenso Soai took the next big step. In 1995, he designed a reaction that could favour one version. In 2003, he succeeded in producing only one of the two mirror-image forms. Their discoveries helped explain how one-sided chemistry can emerge and laid important foundations for asymmetric synthesis a method that allows scientists to make medicines containing the specific form of a molecule they need, rather than producing a mixture of both forms. U.S. Francis Halzen, born 1944 in Tienen, Belgium, is a Professor of Physics at the University of WisconsinMadison, USA, where he has played a leading role in the study of high-energy neutrinos and their cosmic sources. He earned his Ph.D. in 1969 from KU Leuven, Belgium. Francis Halzen's work has helped advance our understanding of some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe through the study of particles known as neutrinos. Neutrinos are tiny, elusive particles that pass through the Earth and our bodies almost unnoticed. But because they can travel vast distances without changing direction, they can reveal clues about the most powerful events in the universe. Halzen recognised this potential, and in 1988, he proposed an ambitious idea: use the enormous volume of Antarctic ice at the South Pole to detect high-energy neutrinos. When a neutrino collides with an atomic nucleus in the ice, it can produce a faint flash of light. Sensors embedded deep in the ice can detect and track these flashes. The idea eventually became IceCube, a neutrino observatory occupying about one cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice. Completed in 2011, IceCube soon detected high-energy neutrinos originating far beyond our Solar System, opening a new way to investigate the universe's most powerful cosmic particle accelerators. Halzen's vision and leadership helped establish neutrino astronomy as a new field of science. Hegemann, born in 1954, is the Hertie Senior Professor of Neuroscience at Humboldt University of Berlin, Germany. He earned his Ph.D. in 1984 from the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsried, Germany, where the discoveries were made. Nagel, born in 1953, is a Professor of Molecular Plant Physiology at the University of Wrzburg, Germany. He earned his Ph.D. in 1988 from the University of Frankfurt, Germany. The prize-recognised discoveries were made at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt, Germany. Karl Deisseroth U.S. Deisseroth, born in 1971, is the D.H. Chen Professor and Professor of Bioengineering and Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences at Stanford University, USA, and an Investigator at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. He earned his Ph.D. in 1998 and M.D. in 2000 from Stanford University. The prize was awarded for their discoveries of light-gated ion channels and optogenetics a revolutionary technique that allows scientists to study how nerve cells control memories, emotions and behaviour in the living brain. It began with a simple question: How does a single-celled alga know which way to swim when it senses light? Peter Hegemann became fascinated by Chlamydomonas, a microscopic alga that moves towards a light source. In the early 2000s, his research led to the discovery of channelrhodopsin, a light-sensitive protein found on the surface of the algal cell. When exposed to blue light, channelrhodopsin opens a channel that allows charged ions to flow into the cell, generating an electrical impulse. Hegemann and his collaborators discovered that the protein could make other cells sensitive to light, laying the foundation for a revolutionary way of controlling cells with light. Working alongside Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel helped reveal the remarkable properties of channelrhodopsin. The discovery showed that this protein could act like a light-controlled switch. When blue light hits channelrhodopsin, a channel opens and charged ions flow through it, producing an electrical signal. Crucially, the researchers found that the protein could make different types of cells respond to light. This insight would prove transformative for neuroscience: if a light-sensitive protein could be introduced into nerve cells, scientists could potentially switch their activity on or off with light. Karl Deisseroth took the discovery of channelrhodopsin from algae into the world of neuroscience. He introduced the gene for channelrhodopsin into nerve cells from rats. When he illuminated these cells with blue light, the cells generated nerve signals. Published in 2005, the breakthrough demonstrated that light could be used to control the activity of nerve cells with remarkable precision. Two years later, Deisseroth took the technique a crucial step further, showing that this light-controlled switch could work in the brains of living mice. The method became known as optogenetics. It gave researchers an unprecedented way to control specific groups of nerve cells and investigate how neural circuits shape memories, feelings and behaviours. For example, you could select "Category" in the 'group by' filter and "Gender" in the 'shade by' filter.

headline: Rahul Gandhi Held Dharna, Abhijeet Dipke's CJP Took To The Streets, INDIA Bloc Moved SC, What Next?
content: SIR Row & Gyanesh Kumar's resignation demand: Rahul Gandhi's dharna, Abhijeet Dipke's CJP stir, Opposition INDIA Bloc's SC plea, what next? The Congress-led Opposition and the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) are actively fighting against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, aggressively demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. They launched a high-intensity protest march from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters. Security personnel heavily barricaded the route and stopped the march near the NITI Aayog and Akashvani Bhavan stretch on Parliament Street. Denied further passage, Rahul Gandhi climbed atop a police barricade, waved the Tricolour, and subsequently sat on the road with other opposition leaders to stage a dharna (sit-in protest). Gandhi was seen holding a placard and posted a message directly targeting the CEC, stating: Gyanesh, its done bro. Time to resign." Following the confrontation and road blockade, Delhi Police briefly detained Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav, and several other senior opposition lawmakers. Following their brief detention, they remained seated near the gates of Akashvani Bhavan to continue their demonstration. Gyanesh, its done, bro.Time to resign. Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) October 6, 2026 THE CORE CONFLICT The friction stems from the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The poll panel stated that the exercise aimed to clear duplicate entries, which resulted in striking off 130 million names. However, the CJP and the INDIA bloc opposition alliance allege that the process was manipulated to delete genuine, eligible voters without due process. Internal cracks within the Election Commission also surfaced when it was reported that two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, formally objected to the SIR decisions multiple times. Thank you, Mumbai Police, for your cooperation today. Salute to all the police personnel who were on duty! Jai Hind Delhi Police, seekh lo kuch Mumbai Police se. Abhijeet Dipke (@abhijeet_dipke) October 2, 2026 Mass protests erupted on October 2, 2026, across major hubs. The CJP, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, held massive rallies at Shivaji Park in Mumbai despite being denied official police permission. Demonstrations have simultaneously hit New Delhi, where police detained around 150 activists. The CJP has officially announced a massive Jantar Mantar 2.0" march scheduled for October 10, 2026. The Supreme Court of India stepped into the fray to hear petitions against the SIR. While the top court refused to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Chief Justice Surya Kant issued formal notices to the Central Government and the Election Commission regarding controversial modifications made to voter enrollment forms (Form 6) during the revision. The SC stated it would reconsider or recall any decisions found to have been taken without required unanimity or majority approval. Petitions and critics challenge 14 specific decisions made during the SIR processincluding modifications to Form 6 and voter deletionsfollowing reports that the other two Election Commissioners (Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi) recorded internal objections. The ECI has rejected claims of an internal rift, maintaining that differing views are routine in a multi-member body and that major decisions had consensus approval. WHAT THE RULING PARTY SAID The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has strongly defended the Election Commissions autonomy. It has accused the opposition of backing fake or bogus voters". It has termed the protests a fake narrative" and stating that the dynamic cleanup represents democracy in action". Fact CheckThe statement made in this post is misleading 1) The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026 2) In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court." Election Commission of India (@ECISVEEP) October 5, 2026 EC REBUTS RAHUL GANDHIS CLAIMS The Election Commission of India has hit back against allegations made by Gandhi over the use of Form 6 in the voter enrolment process, seeking to clarify what the form is meant for and how applications are processed. It stated in a post on X: The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026. In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court." The statement made in this [Rahul Gandhis] post is misleading." WHAT NEXT? ECI and Government Submissions: The ECI and the Centre are expected to formally file their responses and records defending the legality and unanimity of the SIR decisions before the Supreme Court bench. Judicial Review of Records: If the court reviews the administrative files and finds decisions were made without proper concurrence, it may issue an injunction or recall those specific procedural orders. On-Ground Protests: Opposition parties (including INDIA bloc constituents) and groups like the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) are continuing street demonstrations and demands for the CECs resignation or an independent SIT probe. On Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Rahul Gandhi and around 150 INDIA bloc MPs marched toward the Election Commission of India headquarters to protest the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and demand the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, leading to brief detentions by Delhi Police after police barricades stopped them near Parliament Street.

headline: Pakistan Recycles Kashmir Rhetoric To UN Chief Even As Country Faces Economic Collapse, Local Tension | Exclusive
