Headline inflation remains stubbornly high, driven primarily by a 33% surge in electricity tariffs and a 39% hike in domestic fuel prices, which have severely crushed household purchasing power. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar briefed UN Chief Antnio Guterres on the Jammu and Kashmir issue. Pakistan is experiencing a macroeconomic crisis with a 33% surge in electricity tariffs and a 39% hike in domestic fuel prices. The power-sector circular debt in Pakistan has breached PKR 1,675 billion. The IMF projects Pakistans current account deficit to widen up to $4 billion. The Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has led protests in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The countrys energy sector is under intense structural stress, with the power-sector circular debt breaching PKR 1,675 billion, directly violating strict fiscal targets agreed upon with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Compounding these domestic woes are external vulnerabilities; the IMF projects Pakistans current account deficit to widen up to $4 billion, leaving the national exchequer highly exposed to external geopolitical shocks and rising global oil import costs. Simultaneously, this economic strangulation has triggered explosive civil unrest and severe local tensions within Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has spearheaded sustained regional protests and mass mobilisations against the central government. While initial public fury focused on the denial of basic wheat and electricity subsidies, the agitation has evolved into a broader political movement against the systemic dilution of local representation, particularly opposing the allocation of legislative seats to non-local refugees. Locals are actively demanding greater regional autonomy, direct control over their natural resources, and the dismantling of Line of Control (LoC) trade barriers to establish direct economic links with India to alleviate severe local shortages of food and medicine. In response to this growing instability, the Pakistani state has deployed aggressive counter-measures, drawing sharp international condemnation at forums like the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC). The government has attempted to crush the dissent through heavy paramilitary deployments, localized communications blackouts, and the controversial deployment of anti-terror laws against civil rights activists. Observers and intelligence sources note that this combination of regional political alienation, aggressive state crackdowns, and a collapsing national economy has created a volatile security environment, which Islamabad frequently attempts to mask on the global stage by rehashing its traditional, decade-old diplomatic rhetoric regarding the broader Kashmir dispute. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar used the meeting with UN Chief Antnio Guterres to brief him on the Jammu and Kashmir issue, reiterating Islamabad's demand for a peaceful resolution according to UN Security Council resolutions. However, intelligence sources note this rhetoric acts as a political smokescreen to divert international attention from domestic governance failures.

headline: At least 12 Indian sailors injured in attacks in Black Sea, Hormuz; MEA condemns
content: With Indian seafarers being injured in two separate attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Tuesday condemned the incidents and expressed deep concern over the targeting of commercial shipping. Eleven Indian crew members were injured after a Panama-flagged vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. In the other incident, at least two foreign crew members were killed and some others, including an Indian, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire on a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Monday. We condemn the attack earlier today on a Panama-flagged commercial vessel, MT On Peace, off the coast of Oman, where it was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the MEA said in a statement. Of the total crew of 19, 17 are Indian nationals. It is learnt that 12 crew members have been injured, including 11 Indian nationals, it said. With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman. We thank the Omani authorities for their valuable support, it said. The MEA said the continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a cause of deep concern for India. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interests of peace and stability in the region, it said. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest, the MEA said. In the other incident, the Indian Embassy in Romania reported that there were three Indian nationals among the crew members and one of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties (foreign nationals) while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members, the mission posted on X. It said all three Indians are safe and in good health. We condemn the attack on MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea in which two foreign seafarers were killed and some members of the crew, including Indian nationals, injured. The injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. The three Indian nationals, who were part of the crew, are safe. We thank Romanian authorities for their swift action in this incident, the MEA said. India views these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern, it said. The targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world. We continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. Indian seafarers account for almost 12 per cent of the global maritime community. According to sources, at least nine Indian seafarers have died, one is presumed dead, and seven have been injured since the start of the West Asia crisis, until July this year. There have been at least 29 incidents of attacks on vessels carrying Indian seafarers four involving Indian-flagged vessels and the rest involving foreign-flagged vessels. In the Black Sea, too, Indian seafarers have been victims of attacks from both Russia and Ukraine. In fact, India started actively pushing for Russia-Ukraine peace after Indian seafarers were hit by such attacks. In September 2026, India and Liberia launched a 25-nation Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the UN General Assembly to ensure safety and security of merchant crews and commercial shipping against targeted attacks, the MEA said. (With PTI, London)

headline: Tukaram Mundhe Makes Headlines In US Too: NYT Report Hails Maharashtra FDA Chief's Food Safety Crackdown
content: NYT Report Hails Maharashtra FDA Chief's Food Safety Crackdown The NYT piece details how Tukaram Mundhe's surprise inspections have captured public attention and turned him into an unlikely viral celebrity The New York Times featured Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe in an October 2026 report highlighting his aggressive, zero-tolerance food safety crackdown in Mumbai. All you need to know. - FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe EXCLUSIVE: Defends His Actions, Responds To Bribery Claims - Tukaram Mundhe Bans Infant Formula Ads, Mother-Child Photos On Baby Food Packets - 'If You Know...': Tukaram Mundhe Responds To Sanjay Rauts FDA Bribery Claims, Says Infant Nutrition Next Target - Man Finds Rat In Dosa At Mumbai Hotel, Vomits In Shock; Tukaram Mundhe's Team Suspends Licence THE NEW YORK TIMES COVERAGE Published under the title, In India, a Food Inspector Sparks Fear in Mumbai Restaurants, the piece details how Mundhes surprise inspections have captured public attention and turned him into an unlikely viral celebrity. Since taking charge in May 2026, Mundhes team conducted over 12,000 inspections, issued thousands of notices, and suspended hundreds of establishment licenses for severe hygiene and safety violations. The international coverage explores the Tukaram Mundhe Effect", examining how visible routine regulation, strict enforcement, and social media have turned standard bureaucratic governance into headline news. WHO IS TUKARAM MUNDHE? Tukaram Mundhe became Maharashtra FDA Commissioner in May 2026. His team conducted over 12,000 inspections since May 2026. Mundhe is a 2005-batch Indian Administrative Service officer. He has been transferred 25 times across 21 years of service. Mundhe secured an All India Rank of 20 in the 2004 UPSC Civil Services Examination. Tukaram Mundhe is a prominent 2005-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Maharashtra cadre. He is widely recognized for his strict, no-nonsense administration style, zero-tolerance policy toward corruption, and an aggressive, public-welfare-driven execution of his duties. He currently serves as the Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of Maharashtra, a position he assumed in May 2026. Since taking over the Maharashtra FDA, Mundhe has spearheaded a massive statewide crackdown on food safety and hygiene violations. His team has conducted thousands of surprise raids on iconic restaurants, local dairies, and modern quick-commerce warehouses. The aggressive drive has shut down non-compliant kitchens and resulted in the seizure of large caches of adulterated items, turning him into a viral social media figure. Publicly nicknamed Singham IAS," Mundhes rigid enforcement of the law often pits him against powerful local interests, including sand mafias, illegal establishments, and corrupt systems in previous tenures. One of the most talked-about facets of his career is his 25 transfers across 21 years of service. While critics point to his confrontational style creating administrative friction, his supporters view his short tenures as a byproduct of political pushback against his uncompromising honesty. Born on June 3, 1975, in a farming family in Tadsonna village (Beed district, Maharashtra), he attended a local Zilla Parishad school. He went on to secure an MA in Political Science and cleared the UPSC Civil Services Examination in 2004 with an impressive All India Rank (AIR) of 20. Over his career, he has served in various leadership capacities, including District Collector of Solapur (where he earned praise for drought mitigation) and Municipal Commissioner of Navi Mumbai and Nagpur. He is a recipient of the Best Collector Award and the National Award for Social Justice and Empowerment. The New York Times featured Tukaram Mundhe in an October 2026 report highlighting his aggressive, zero-tolerance food safety crackdown and surprise inspections across Mumbai restaurants.

headline: 'MPs Disrespected': Rahul Gandhi Demands Meeting With CEC, To Continue Protest At Akashvani Bhavan
content: Gandhi alleged that the poll commissioners had "disrespected" people's voice by not meeting MPs.He demanded that the poll panel meet opposition leaders & answer their questions. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday held a protest inside the Akashvani Bhavan premises, demanding a meeting with the Election Commissioners and alleging that Opposition MPs have been disrespected." The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha alleged that the Election Commissioners had disrespected" the voice of the people by not meeting MPs. He demanded that the poll panel meet opposition leaders and answer questions over the allegations of vote theft". - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody? - DMK U-Turn On Rahul Gandhi? Party Backs Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: 'Right To Fight' - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police The MPs will meet the Election Commissioners; they will have to meet usWe all are very comfortable hereThey have disrespected the voice of the nation by disrespecting the MPs; we just want to meet the Election Commissioners and ask questions and tell them that they have done vote theft," Gandhi said. Rahul Gandhi To Continue Protest At Akashvani Bhavan The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said he and other Congress leaders had no objection to continuing the demonstration at the venue. He also said the party would move elsewhere if the Delhi Police arranged another location. We dont have any problem with protesting hereWe will continue our protests hereIf they (Delhi Police) are uncomfortable with us protesting here, they can provide us with another place to protestThe Constitution allows us to lodge a protest," Gandhi added. The protest is part of the Congress-led oppositions campaign against alleged irregularities in the electoral process. The party has repeatedly raised allegations of vote theft" and demanded greater transparency from the Election Commission. Gandhi and other party leaders have been seeking a meeting with the poll panel to present their concerns and seek responses to their allegations. The Election Commission has previously rejected allegations of wrongdoing and maintained that electoral processes are conducted according to established rules. Opposition Stages Sit-In At Akashvani Bhavan The LoP, accompanied by Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several Opposition leaders, staged a sit-in outside Akashvani Bhavan after being stopped from marching towards the Election Commission office. The protest led to a complete shutdown of Parliament Street as Gandhi, along with hundreds of supporters and Opposition MPs, attempted to proceed towards the poll panels office located nearby. Opposition March To EC Office Halted The demonstration began around 10 am when the march, which had started from Parliament House, was halted. Following this, Opposition MPs gathered on the road outside Akashvani Bhavan, around 200 metres from the Election Commission office. Several leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress leaders Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, and CPI(M) MP John Brittas, were detained by the police. They were taken away in buses and released later. BJP Slams Congress Protest Meanwhile, the protest has drawn criticism from the BJP, which accused the Opposition of targeting constitutional institutions over its electoral setbacks. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, targeting the INDIA bloc, said the march was aimed at venting their frustration" over electoral defeats by making baseless allegations against constitutional bodies and attempting to damage their credibility. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also criticised Gandhi, alleging that he was attempting to create confusion" and boost his politics" by misrepresenting the Supreme Courts position. Another BJP spokesperson, Sudhanshu Trivedi, attacked the Opposition over what he described as theatrics on the streets". He questioned the Congress on whose interests it was serving by seeking voting rights without verification of voters classified as absent, shifted, dead and duplicate". Rahul Gandhi held a protest inside the Akashvani Bhavan premises to demand a meeting with the Election Commissioners, alleging that they had "disrespected" opposition MPs and the voice of the nation.

headline: When The Bridge Becomes A Wall: Srinagar's Vanishing Photographic Memory
content: Srinagars Vanishing Photographic Memory Fencing installed along historic bridges in Srinagar has made the Jhelum river and the buildings beyond increasingly difficult to photograph For centuries, the bridges of Srinagar have offered more than a way across the Jhelum. They have been vantage points from which the city has looked at itself. From these bridges, photographers have recorded the river, wooden houses, shrines, markets, boats, mountains, and the everyday life of the old city. Some of the earliest surviving photographs of Srinagar were made from these very vantage points, turning the bridges into accidental archives of the city. Today, however, those same vantage points are slowly disappearing behind metal. - Tremors From Afghanistan Earthquake Felt In Kashmir: Safety Precautions Travellers Should Take - Delhis Barapullah Faces Big Traffic Test: New Flyover, 3-Km Jam And 55-Minute Waits On Day 2 - Indian Man Spots Narrow Lanes, Garbage Piles, Wall With Ads In China, Questions Why Is Only India Called Dirty? - 20 Lakh Indians Upskilled For AI, But Only 3 Lakh Have Advanced Skills: Which Jobs Should You Target? A walk through downtown Srinagar, including Zaina Kadal, offers a glimpse of what may become a larger problem. Fencing installed along historic bridges has made the river and the buildings beyond increasingly difficult to photograph. In places, the chain-link fencing used is so closely knitted that even a mobile phone camera struggles to find an unobstructed opening. The fences may be designed to keep people from jumping into the Jhelum and to prevent the throwing of waste into the river. The intention, particularly where human lives are concerned, is difficult to dispute. Srinagar has been fencing vulnerable bridges precisely because of concerns over suicide attempts and pedestrian safety. But there is another consequence, quieter and less immediately visible. What happens when the very places from which Srinagar has historically been photographed can no longer be used to photograph Srinagar? The bridge as a camera Consider Zaina Kadal. Built by Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin in 1427, the bridge has for centuries been part of the physical and cultural fabric of the old city. It was not merely a crossing over the Jhelum. It stood amid markets, river traffic and the dense urban life of downtown Srinagar. And the bridge has been part of the photographic memory of that city for well over a century. Srinagar's bridges have historically served as important vantage points for photographing the city. Early photographs of Srinagar, including those by Samuel Bourne and Frederick Bremner, were taken from these bridges. Zaina Kadal, built in 1427, has been a significant photographic subject and vantage point for over a century. Fencing installed on historic bridges in downtown Srinagar is now obstructing photographic views of the river and buildings. Authorities cite suicide prevention, garbage dumping, and pedestrian safety as reasons for installing fences on vulnerable bridges. In 1868, photographer Samuel Bourne photographed Zaina Kadal, capturing the bridge and its surroundings at a time when shops lined the structure. That image survives today as evidence of a Srinagar that no longer exists in quite the same form. A later account of the photograph notes the bridges distinctive cantilever construction and its use as a market. Another historic image in the British Library archive is titled Srinagar from Zeina Kadal 4th Bridge", photographed by Frederick Bremner. The camera looks along the Jhelum towards Shah Hamadan Shrine. The bridge was not simply appearing in the photograph. The bridge was the place from which the photograph was possible. Remove that viewpoint, and an entire category of photographs disappears with it. The same story can be found elsewhere along the Jhelum. Samuel Bournes 1864 photograph of Srinagar was probably taken from the Old Fateh Kadal bridge. From there, the frame brought together the Jhelum, Shah Hamadan Mosque and Hari Parbat, creating precisely the kind of layered cityscape that today forms part of Srinagars historical visual vocabulary. Another Bourne photograph records a bridge over the Jhelum, small boats and the Maharajas palace. These are not merely pretty old photographs. They are documents of a vanished city. They tell us what the river looked like, where boats travelled, how buildings related to the water, what the skyline looked like and how the bridges fitted into the urban landscape. They allow todays Srinagar to be compared with yesterdays Srinagar. A city remembered through its viewpoints The importance of these vantage points becomes even clearer in photographs from the twentieth century. Collections of old Srinagar photographs contain images of houseboats along the Jhelum near Budshah Bridge in 1969, boats moving through Zaina Kadal in 1985 and people crossing Amira Kadal in 1962 on bicycles, on foot and in tongas. Each photograph freezes something that was otherwise destined to disappear. The boat disappears. The shop disappears. The house changes. The bridge is reconstructed. The river changes. The people grow old. But the photograph remains. That is why the seemingly mundane act of looking over a bridge railing has historical importance. A person standing on Zaina Kadal today, holding up a phone to photograph an old wooden building across the river, may not realise that they are participating in the same long tradition of looking that produced some of Srinagars earliest visual records. The difference is that the nineteenth-century photographer had an open frame. The twenty-first-century photographer may now have a wall of metal between the camera and the city. There is an important distinction to be made here. The question is not whether Srinagar should have safety barriers. It should. Authorities have cited suicide prevention, garbage dumping, pedestrian safety and public demand as reasons for fencing vulnerable bridges. In 2024, fencing was initiated at several major bridges specifically to prevent suicide attempts. The more difficult question is how those barriers are designed. There is already evidence that safety and visibility need not necessarily be treated as opposites. The treatment of Budshah Bridge, for instance, shows the possibility of designing a barrier that provides protection while retaining some visual permeability. In May, the administration said the proposed fencing of Budshah Bridge and Cement Kadal should strengthen safety while maintaining aesthetics, surrounding visibility and heritage value. That principle deserves to be applied consistently. A safety fence does not necessarily have to become a visual barricade. There is a difference between preventing a person from climbing over a railing and preventing a camera from seeing through it. A difference between making a bridge safer and making it photographically blind. What will Srinagar look like in 50 years? This may sound like a small concern in a city dealing with much larger problems. Cities are remembered not only through official heritage records, maps and government documents. They are remembered through millions of informal photographs taken by residents, visitors, journalists, artists and families. Someone photographing the wooden faade of an old house from Zaina Kadal today may unknowingly create the only easily accessible record of that building before its faade is altered. Someone photographing a row of riverside houses, a shrine, a boatman or the changing skyline may create a visual reference that becomes invaluable decades later. The photograph does not have to be famous to become historical. It simply has to survive. Instead, something subtler will happen. The city will become harder to photograph from the places where it has historically been photographed. Future generations may possess thousands of photographs of Srinagars monuments, but fewer photographs of how those monuments actually sat within the city: the angle of the river, the neighbouring houses, the bridges, the boats, the markets and the ordinary visual relationships that make a historic city recognisable. There may be a simple principle worth considering while the remaining fencing projects are designed and reviewed: If a bridge is historic, its safety infrastructure should protect people without unnecessarily blocking the historic view. That could mean wider visual openings, transparent or less visually obstructive sections, carefully positioned viewing points, designated photographic apertures, or sections deliberately designed to preserve important sightlines. Authorities have installed fencing along vulnerable bridges primarily to prevent suicide attempts, stop garbage dumping into the Jhelum, and enhance pedestrian safety.

headline: 'Insulting Institutions Won't Strengthen Democracy': Kiren Rijiju Hits Out At Rahul Gandhi Over CEC Protest
content: Rahul Gandhi was among several Opposition leaders who marched towards the EC office as protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar entered their fifth day. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday hit out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc MPs protest against the Election Commission, urging him to stop this drama" and learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and BJP workers. Reacting to the protest, Rijiju said the Congress and Rahul Gandhi had been repeatedly attacking institutions such as the Election Commission and the Supreme Court. - 'Congress Believes In Creating Ruckus, Exposed Again': BJP After EC Denies Oppn's Meeting Request Claim - Everyday Congress, Rahul Gandhi Doing Drama: Kiren Rijiju On CEC Protest | "Democracy Will..." - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - BJP vs INDIA Bloc News: Sambit Patras Anarchy Charge, Gyanesh Kumar Row | Oppositions Protests The time has come to put an end to the daily drama orchestrated by the Congress partyspecifically Rahul Gandhi and his associateswho constantly attack institutions like the Election Commission and the Supreme Court," Rijiju said. He questioned how long such a situation would continue, saying, This drama has been ongoing since 2014; how long will it continue?" Rahul Gandhi marches towards EC office Congress MP Rahul Gandhi was among several Opposition leaders who marched towards the Election Commissions office on Tuesday as protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar entered their fifth day. The INDIA bloc MPs marched towards Nirvachan Sadan in an attempt to reach the Election Commission office. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc MPs' protest against the Election Commission. Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders marched towards the Election Commission's office on Tuesday. The protests are against alleged irregularities in the poll body's decisions, specifically the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The previous march from Parliament to the Election Commission was held on August 11, 2025. The current protests began on October 2. The Opposition parties are protesting alleged irregularities in decisions of the poll body, particularly the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, described as a clean-up drive of electoral rolls. The previous march from Parliament to the Election Commission was held on August 11, 2025, against the SIR. The current protests began on October 2, when Opposition parties and civil society groups called for a gathering over the revision of electoral rolls. Opposition leaders detained during march Several Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, were briefly detained during their march towards the Election Commission office. Congress MPs have also claimed that police and security personnel stopped them from moving towards Nirvachan Sadan as part of the protest, which includes a demand for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The BJP has dismissed the march. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called it another attempt to relaunch Rahul Gandhi" and accused the Congress of wanting to spread anarchy" across the country. What Rijiju said about Rahul Gandhi Rijiju said that in a democracy, serving people earns a political mandate. He alleged that when the Opposition failed to secure such a mandate, it attacked the Election Commission. He also referred to the Supreme Court and said that when the court asks for an apology, the Opposition then attacks the court and says it has no faith in it. Rijiju said the Congress had labelled the Election Commission and the government as thieves". Such behaviour will neither strengthen democracy nor lead to a resurgence of the Congress party," he said. He specifically urged Rahul Gandhi to learn from Modi and BJP workers, who, according to Rijiju, serve society and the country selflessly and continuously". If you engage in service, the public will place their trust in you; mere theatrics will not suffice," Rijiju said. CEC row and protests Since October 2, the protests have involved hundreds of security personnel, barricades and other restrictions, along with detentions. The protesters include activists and civil society members such as All India Students Association president Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, Prashant Bhushan, Nikhil De and Nandita Narain. They had visited Parliament Street police station over the protest call at Jantar Mantar last Monday but were denied permission. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), whose previous protest at Jantar Mantar in July against alleged examination irregularities led to the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, also launched a parallel protest on October 2 at Shivaji Park in Mumbai. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a mobilisation" at Jantar Mantar on October 10. On Monday, the CJP welcomed the INDIA blocs proposed protest and said its own October 10 mobilisation should be viewed as a broader youth call rather than that of a particular organisation. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Monday declined to pass an interim order restraining Gyanesh Kumar from functioning over allegations that he took several decisions unilaterally despite objections from the other two election commissioners. The court said it could not proceed on assumptions" without first verifying the facts. Separately, Assistant Commissioner of Police (Connaught Place) Vivek Bhagat was promoted to Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police in a routine Delhi Home Department order on Monday. The order was later put on hold at his request. This came two days after he was named in a police complaint filed by a female journalist alleging sexual harassment while she was reporting on a protest near Jantar Mantar. The allegation led to a protest near Parliament Street Police Station, with protesters seeking an update on the complaint. Opposition leaders and INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission's office to protest against alleged irregularities in decisions made by the poll body, particularly targeting the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

headline: Russia says nearly 900 Ukrainian drones downed, Moscow region fuel depot reportedly burns
content: Russian air defences intercepted nearly 900 Ukrainian drones overnight over multiple regions of the country, as well as the occupied Crimean Peninsula and the Sea of Azov, the Defence Ministry in Moscow said on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). Unconfirmed media reports said a major fuel depot in the Moscow region was on fire after the attack, which killed two people. Ukraines domestically developed long-range drones and, increasingly, missiles have allowed Kyiv to hit Russian soil over the more than 4.5 years since Moscows forces launched a full-scale invasion. Russias bigger military has maintained air superiority during the war, making aerial attacks on civilian areas of Ukraine routine. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 650 drones flew towards the Moscow region between Monday (October 5, 2026) evening and Tuesday morning. Most were destroyed far from the city, and 105 were downed as they approached it, he said. Mr. Sobyanin later reported that 68 more drones targeting Moscow were downed during daylight on Tuesday. Ukraine has regularly targeted Russian oil refineries and storage depots, claiming last weekend that it had disabled 51% of Russias oil refining capacity. The claim could not be independently verified. Russian President Vladimir Putin said last week that the attacks had cost Russia about 1% of its gross domestic product (GDP). Russia has traditionally been the worlds third-largest producer of refined fuel products from crude, after the U.S. and China. The Kremlin has banned diesel exports because of the Ukrainian strikes, pushing global prices higher, which prompted U.S. President Donald Trump last month to urge Ukraine to stop hitting Russias refineries. After several days of targeting bridges in the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, as part of a campaign to make civilian life difficult, Russia attacked one of the bridges over the Dnipro river in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the regional military administration chief. Traffic across the bridge was temporarily suspended as a result of the attack, he said. A night-time Russian attack on a Zaporizhzhia residential building wounded five people, and a daylight strike on a warehouse in the city caused a large fire, Mr. Semikin said. Russian forces are also trying to choke shipping in Ukrainian ports in the Black Sea, denying Kyiv vital grain export revenue. The Russian Defence Ministry said its forces had struck targets overnight in Ukraines southern Odesa region on the Black Sea coast with drones. An ammunition depot was hit, as were a bulk carrier in the Chornomorsk port carrying dual-use goods, and port infrastructure in Izmail, the Ministry said.

headline: Cabinet Passes Resolution Congratulating PM Modi On 25 Years Of Continuous Leadership
content: The resolution outlined 10 aspects of Prime Minister Modis tenure, tracing his journey from Gujarat to the national stage. The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. The resolution described the milestone as more than a customary tribute, highlighting what it called Modis leadership guided by the principles of Nation First" and Citizen First". It also cited three mandates in Gujarat and three successive Lok Sabha elections as reflecting public support for his leadership. - 'Outstanding Leadership': World Leaders Congratulate PM Modi On Completion Of 25 Years In Public Service - 'Those Who Opposed Me Showed Me Power Of Democracy': PM Modi Reflects On 25-Year Journey - PM Modi Marks 25 Years In Public Service, Says 'I Bow Down In Front Of People Of My Country - Modi@25: 25 Years, 25 Numbers That Tell The Story Of Narendra Modis Political Journey The resolution outlined 10 aspects of Prime Minister Modis tenure, tracing his journey from Gujarat to the national stage and highlighting initiatives and policies across development, welfare, reform, technology, national security, diplomacy and cultural heritage. From Gujarat To India The resolution highlighted initiatives such as SWAGAT, through which PM Modi personally heard citizens grievances, and said it later inspired PRAGATI, which brought governments together to review stalled projects and resolve implementation bottlenecks. It also cited Gujarats Jyotigram scheme, which provided separate electricity feeders for agriculture, as an example of an initiative that was subsequently taken to the national level. Welfare And Empowerment The resolution linked Modis focus on poverty with schemes providing housing, water, banking and healthcare. It cited nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, more than 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty. It also highlighted womens empowerment, citing approximately 3.5 crore Lakhpati Didis and the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for reservation for women. The resolution also pointed to PM-KISAN transfers exceeding 4 lakh crore, along with startups, skilling and education reforms and PM-JANMAN for particularly vulnerable tribal communities. Reforms And Self-Reliance The resolution cited GST, welfare-delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial-era laws as examples of major reforms undertaken during Modis tenure. It said public capital expenditure had risen from 2 lakh crore to more than 12 lakh crore, while highway expansion and railway electrification had also progressed. Electronics production, according to the resolution, increased from around 2 lakh crore to more than 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing were also cited as part of the push for self-reliance. Technology And Science The resolution highlighted Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity as having strengthened welfare delivery, while citing UPI as a major transformation in digital payments. It also pointed to the development of Indias Covid-19 vaccines and the Chandrayaan-3 landing near the Moons south pole. Private participation in space and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology were also highlighted. Leadership During Crises The resolution highlighted the governments response to the Covid-19 pandemic, including domestic vaccine development and rapid vaccination. It also cited measures taken during the West Asia crisis, saying timely decisions and steps related to energy security helped India withstand disruption. On national security, the resolution cited the 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot air strikes and 2025 Operation Sindoor. It also mentioned the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension, creation of the Chief of Defence Staffs post, action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast. Indias Global Role The resolution highlighted Indias role in the G20 and BRICS, its advocacy for the Global South and the inclusion of the African Union in the G20. headline: DRDO Conducts Successful Trial Of Indigenously Developed High-Altitude Airship At 21 Km
content: The experimental flight attained an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level (AMSL) and remained at an altitude of 20 km AMSL for more than 30 minutes. The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Tuesday carried out the successful flight trial of an indigenously developed High-Altitude Platform (HAPS), the Ministry of Defence said. The trial has marked a significant step towards developing long-endurance stratospheric airship technology in India. - AAP Protests Across Punjab Over ED-CBI Raids, Accuses BJP Of Targeting Mann Govt - Petrol Pump Dispute Turns Deadly: Indian Oil Official Stabbed 7 Times In Maharashtra's Hingoli - 'Youre Doing Your Job': Rahul Gandhi Distributes Water While Supporters Deflate Cops Detention Bus | Watch - Facing Difficulty Breathing: Pregnant Womans Terrifying Call From Under Seemapuri Building Debris DRDOs Airship Maintained A Height Of 20 Km For 30 Mins During the experimental flight, the platform reached an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level (AMSL) and maintained a height of 20 km for over 30 minutes. It was subsequently commanded to descend and was successfully recovered, while flight performance data was analysed. The Ministry said real-time video feeds and vehicle parameters were continuously transmitted to a Ground Control Station throughout the flight. The data indicated that the platform performed as intended. The HAPS was equipped with several instrumentation and control systems, including an inertial measurement unit, a Global Positioning System (GPS) receiver, onboard cameras and an altitude control mechanism, along with other subsystems. The trial was conducted in coordination with the Indian Air Force, Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification (CEMILAC), Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Airports Authority of India (AAI) and other civil authorities, the Ministry said in a statement. What Is High-Altitude Platform? DRDO successfully conducted a flight trial of an indigenously developed High-Altitude Platform (HAPS). The platform reached an altitude of 21 km and maintained 20 km for over 30 minutes. Real-time video feeds and vehicle parameters were continuously transmitted to a Ground Control Station. The HAPS was equipped with an inertial measurement unit, GPS receiver, onboard cameras, and an altitude control mechanism. The trial was coordinated with the Indian Air Force, CEMILAC, DGCA, and AAI. The High-Altitude Platform is a lighter-than-air system being developed by DRDOs Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE) in Agra for long-duration surveillance in the stratosphere. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh congratulated DRDO, the Indian Air Force, public sector undertakings and industry partners involved in the trial. He described the achievement as an important milestone in Indias Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative towards developing a long-endurance stratospheric airship. Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D, and DRDO Chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh also congratulated the teams involved in the successful flight trial. During the experimental flight, the high-altitude platform reached an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level and successfully maintained a height of 20 km for over 30 minutes.

headline: Switching Brain Cells On Or Off With 'Light' Touch: Why Optogenetics Won 2026 Nobel Prize For Medicine
content: 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine: Optogenetics is a technique that allows scientists to use pulses of light as a remote control to switch specific brain cells on or off Optogenetics, the method for controlling brain cells with light, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, awarded jointly to scientists Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel. How does it work? WHAT IS OPTOGENETICS? Optogenetics is a biological technique that allows scientists to use pulses of light as a remote control to switch specific brain cells (neurons) on or off with millisecond precision. The technology works by bridging genetics and optics: The Light Switch (Algae Proteins): Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered that certain single-celled green pond algae contain special proteins called channelrhodopsins. These proteins act as light-gated ion channelsmicroscopic doors" that fly open when hit by specific colours of light (like blue light), allowing electrical current to flow. The Delivery: Karl Deisseroth took the genetic code for these light-sensitive proteins and successfully inserted them into the DNA of specific nerve cells in animals. Optogenetics won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. The Nobel Prize was awarded jointly to scientists Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel. Optogenetics uses pulses of light to switch specific brain cells on or off with millisecond precision. Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered channelrhodopsins, light-gated ion channels in algae. Karl Deisseroth inserted the genetic code for light-sensitive proteins into animal nerve cells. BREAKING NEWSThe 2026 in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics." The Nobel Prize (@NobelPrize) October 5, 2026 The Control: Once the target neurons express this protein, researchers can shine a tiny fiber-optic light onto the brain tissue. A flash of light instantly forces the channel open, triggering the neuron to fire a signal. Other engineered proteins can similarly turn neurons off using a different colour of light (like yellow). WHY DID IT WIN THE NOBEL PRIZE? The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet honored this breakthrough because it fundamentally revolutionized neuroscience, moving the field from just observing the brain to actively controlling it. Before optogenetics, scientists relied on drugs or electrical shocks to stimulate the brain, which messy and unselectively activated all surrounding cells. Optogenetics allows scientists to single out one exact type of neuron while leaving neighboring cells untouched. By flashing a light to turn specific brain circuits on or off, researchers have been able to map exactly how neural networks shape memories, feelings, movement, and complex behaviours in living animals. The technology is providing crucial insights into what goes wrong in neurological and psychiatric conditions such as Parkinsons disease, schizophrenia, depression, addiction, and Alzheimers. It has already moved into clinical human trials, where researchers have used the algal proteins to successfully restore partial vision in individuals suffering from genetic blindness (retinitis pigmentosa). The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

headline: 11 Indian crew injured after ship hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz; India condemns attack
content: Eleven Indian crew members were injured on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) after a Panama-flagged commercial vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a strong condemnation from India. The vessel, MT On Peace, carried 19 crew members, including 17 Indian nationals. In total, 12 crew members 11 of them Indians sustained injuries in the strike, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). "We condemn the attack earlier today on a Panama-flagged commercial vessel MT On Peace off the coast of Oman, where it was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz," the MEA said in a statement. "Of the total crew of 19, 17 are Indian nationals. It is learnt that 12 crew members have been injured, including 11 Indian nationals," it said. The MEA said continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a "cause of deep concern" for India. "We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interests of peace and stability in the region," it said. "The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest," it added. The MEA said the sailors of the vessel were evacuated with the help of Omani authorities. "With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman. We thank the Omani authorities for their valuable support," it said.

headline: From LoC To LAC, Census Teams Complete Population Enumeration In Snow-Bound Areas Of J&K, Ladakh
content: The exercise covered a total of 5,292 Enumeration Blocks (EBs), including 4,597 in Jammu & Kashmir and 695 in Ladakh The population enumeration exercise for Census 2027 has been successfully completed in the designated snow-bound areas of the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, marking a significant operational milestone ahead of the national census. The exercise covered a total of 5,292 Enumeration Blocks (EBs), including 4,597 in Jammu & Kashmir and 695 in Ladakh. In Ladakh, the entire Union Territory was covered during the September exercise, with 695 Enumeration Blocks completed 367 in Leh and 328 in Kargil. The exercise covered 5,292 Enumeration Blocks (EBs), with 4,597 in Jammu & Kashmir and 695 in Ladakh. Ladakh became the first Union Territory to complete population enumeration for Census 2027. Kishtwar district became the first district in the country to complete population enumeration for Census 2027. Doda recorded the highest number of completed enumeration blocks at 798, followed by Kishtwar with 602, Ramban with 418, Anantnag with 377, Baramulla with 359, Reasi with 345, and Udhampur with 313. Kishtwar district, which was declared fully snow-bound, has become the first district in the country to complete population enumeration for Census 2027. Amit Sharma appreciated the coordinated efforts of district administrations, Census officials, special charges, enumerators and supervisors, besides acknowledging the cooperation extended by local residents. He said the successful completion of the exercise across difficult and remote terrain demonstrated the preparedness of the Census machinery and the effectiveness of field-level arrangements put in place for areas where geographical and climatic conditions require a separate enumeration schedule. The operation was supported by an extensive preparatory exercise, with nodal officers and district coordinators deployed across districts for field training, preparation and demarcation of enumeration blocks, distribution of Census kits and ensuring that prescribed manuals reached the concerned Charges. The exercise also received close attention from the senior leadership of the Census organisation, including Shri Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, IAS, Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India. The successful completion of the snow-bound enumeration is expected to provide an important foundation for the next stages of Census 2027 in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Ladakh became the first Union Territory in the country to complete population enumeration for Census 2027 after covering all 695 Enumeration Blocks across Leh and Kargil during the September exercise.

headline: Kenya confirms first Ebola case imported from Congo after patient dies in Nairobi
content: Kenya's Health Ministry on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) confirmed the country's first imported Ebola case from Congo. Health Minister Aden Duale said a Kenyan citizen who arrived in the country on Saturday (October 3, 2026) from Congo, via Uganda, had been isolated and treated at Nairobi Hospital. The patient tested positive for the Ebola virus after developing symptoms associated with haemorrhagic fever. The patient died late on Monday (October 5, 2026) while receiving treatment. Health authorities have placed the country on high alert and are monitoring for possible additional cases. Mr. Duale said 28 contacts, including family members and health workers who had cared for the patient, had been identified. Another 23 passengers who had travelled on the same flight from Uganda were being traced. The contacts will remain in isolation for 21 days, and will be released after testing negative for the virus, Patrick Amoth, the Ministry's Director, said. The patient will be buried within 24 hours, in accordance with recommended public safety protocols. Kenya is the fourth country to record an Ebola case in the current outbreak, which was declared in eastern Congo in mid-May. Uganda recorded 20 cases, and France one. Before Kenya reported its case, there had been no active cases outside Congo since Uganda declared its outbreak over in late August. This is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned it could become the deadliest, as it continues to outpace efforts to track and contain it. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Vaccine and treatment trials are under way in Congo's Ituri province, the outbreak's epicentre.

headline: Unity In Peril? Before INDIA Bloc's 'Save Democracy' March, NC-PDP Rift Spills Out In Jammu
content: Farooq Abdullah said the PDP was most responsible for the abrogation of Article 370 in J&K and alleged that the party had helped the BJP, drawing a sharp reaction from the PDP The INDIA bloc is set to hold a joint Save Democracy protest rally and padyatra in Jammu and Kashmir on October 7, part of a nationwide campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). The decision for joint protests across states and Union Territories was taken at the alliances September 30 meeting in Delhi, where leaders, including PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, National Conference leader Omar Abdullah and senior Congress leaders, projected a united front. But as the Jammu and Kashmir unit prepared for the October 7 rally, the alliances internal differences quickly came to the fore. - INDIA Bloc Announces Massive Protest Against Modi Govt From Oct 7 In J&K Over SIR, ECI & Statehood Issues - Omar Abdullah Delaying Local Body Polls Fearing Defeat: BJP Vows To Take To The Streets To Highlight J&K Govt's Failures - They Oppose SIR As They Don't Want To Lose Rohingya Votes: J&K BJP President Sat Sharma Hits Out At INDIA Bloc - Congress Frustrated After 12 Years Out Of Power: Telangana BJP Chief On Election Commission Row A joint meeting of the local INDIA Blocattended by the National Conference, PDP, Congress, Panthers Party and other constituent partieswas held in Jammu three days ago to work out the blueprint for the padyatra. Within 24 hours, however, the National Conference and PDP were publicly at odds again. The development is significant because the two parties are among the key constituents of the INDIA bloc in Jammu and Kashmir, but have long been political rivals. Their latest confrontation has also brought the strain between the National Conference and Congress into focus. Farooq Abdullah Targets PDP, Congress The latest round of friction began with a statement by National Conference president Dr Farooq Abdullah, who directly attacked the PDP. Farooq Abdullah said the PDP was most responsible for the abrogation of Article 370 in Jammu and Kashmir and alleged that the party had helped the BJP. He said Jammu and Kashmir was not getting its rights and that its powers and identity had been taken away, alleging that the PDP had helped the BJP in this process. Farooq Abdullah also targeted his alliance partner Congress. He said Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru had made a major mistake by not making the Election Commission autonomous, a statement that was seen as a direct reference to Congress. PDP Hits Back: NC Has Forgotten Article 370 The PDP did not remain silent. PDP leader Waheed-ur-Rehman Para and other party leaders hit back at Farooq Abdullah, saying his claims were wrong. Para said Article 370 remained the core issue of the PDPs ideology, but alleged that the National Conference had now forgotten it. According to Para, the NC was now focusing only on statehood and had moved away from the Article 370 issue. Cracks In NC-Congress Relationship Too? The friction, however, is not limited to the NC and PDP. All is not well between the National Conference and Congress either. In Jammu and Kashmir, the NC and Congress are alliance partners, while the PDP is not part of that direct alliance. However, differences have emerged between the NC and Congress as well. Congress had made two key demands. The first was the formation of a coordination committee to ensure that the government functioned smoothly. Omar Abdullah did not constitute that committee. The second demand was for two ministerial berths for Congress in the Cabinet. That demand was also not accepted. As a result, Congress had to extend outside support to the government. Congress also wanted one secure Rajya Sabha seat to be given to the party, but that demand was not accepted by the NC either. This has also created friction within the alliance. Another bone of contention is Omar Abdullahs meetings with Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Delhi or Prime Minister Narendra Modidialogues that Congress is not comfortable with as it feels the National Conference is cosying up to the BJP. Political experts say this is the biggest weakness of the INDIA Bloc in Jammu and Kashmir: while the parties remain united against the BJP and PM Modi at the national level, their political rivalry continues in Jammu and Kashmir. The NC and PDP draw from the same vote base and both are seeking to protect their political space and existence at the expense of the other. That is why, according to political observers, the unity visible in Delhi does not necessarily translate to Jammu and Kashmir. The October 7 rally will take place. There will be a photo session and the slogan of Save Democracy will be raised. But the statements emerging even before the slogan has been raised have already put a bigger question before the INDIA blocCan the alliance save its own unity in Jammu and Kashmir? Farooq Abdullah blamed the PDP for the abrogation of Article 370 and alleged that it helped the BJP, while PDP leaders countered that the National Conference had forgotten Article 370 and was only focusing on statehood instead.

headline: France test-fires new nuclear-capable missile: Defence Ministry
content: Defence Ministry France on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) test-fired for the first time its new M51.3 nuclear-capable ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine, the Defence Ministry said. It was not carrying a warhead. The missile, a variant of Frances M51 missile, was fired from the Le Vigilant submarine off Brittany and impacted in the North Atlantic, hundreds of kilometres from any coastline, it said. President Emmanuel Macron witnessed the firing from a French warship, an official told AFP. The launch was conducted without a nuclear warhead and in strict compliance with Frances international commitments, the defence ministry said. The test once again demonstrates the excellence of the high-tech solutions employed by French industry in the field of nuclear deterrence, it added. This test came against a backdrop of increased tensions in Europe with Mr. Macron warning of a shift in the nature of Russian aggression and threats against European nations following a series of hybrid attacks blamed on Moscow. He vowed in mid-September that these actions would not go unanswered. The French President also proposed this year that European partners join the advanced nuclear deterrence framework of France, the European Unions sole nuclear weapons power.
