Reuters, citing the regional newspaper La Voix du Nord, reported that the teenager lost his hand as well as part of his lower arm. The incident took place during the latest round of protests, as clashes between students and police continued amid the wider agitation over conditions in French schools. Why are students protesting in France? The demonstrations are taking place at lycees, the schools where French teenagers aged between 15 and 18 complete their final years of school. Students have raised several grievances, including teacher absences, classroom conditions and overloaded school timetables. They have also complained about school days that can run from 8 am to 6 pm. As the protests have grown, demonstrators have reportedly blocked entrances to hundreds of schools across France. The government has sought to address the grievances raised by students. However, it has also accused hard-left activists of hijacking the movement, according to the report. Videos show clashes, protests intensify Visuals shared by AFP on X showed demonstrators dragging bins and other objects through streets. On Friday, October 2, Reuters reported on X that protesters had thrown firecrackers at riot police in Pantin, near Paris. The latest protests have continued to intensify, with hundreds of schools affected across the country. More than 500 of Frances 3,700 high schools, or lycees, were shut down or partially disrupted on Monday, according to AFP. Demonstrators are also preparing for what has been described as Act III" protests expected on Tuesday. The French government said the unrest has so far left 215 students and 715 police officers injured, AFP reported. The education system isnt working Students involved in the demonstrations have continued to voice their concerns over the state of the education system. Alma, a pupil at the Lycee Charlemagne in central Paris, told AFP, Its clear the education system isnt working." Another student, Simon, said protesters would not stop simply because they were being given a platform to express their views online. They think that just because theyre letting us express ourselves on a platform, on the internet, well stop blocking access and being angry, but this anger has been here for years," Simon said. With more than 500 lycees disrupted and further demonstrations planned, the protests over classroom conditions and the wider education system continue to intensify across France. Students are protesting over grievances including teacher absences, poor classroom conditions, overloaded school timetables, and long school days running from 8 am to 6 pm.

headline: 'Influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj Gets Bail In Jantar Mantar Assault Case
content: Bhardwaj allegedly assaulted a 38-year-old man during a Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest in June. Self-styled right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj was granted regular bail by a Delhi court in connection with the Jantar Mantar assault case on Tuesday. Bhardwaj is accused of assaulting the father of a student activist during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in July. - Jantar Mantar Protest Today: 11 Metro Stations Shut, Traffic Restricted | Is Your Route Affected? - Prohibitory Orders In Force, Metro Stations Shut: Delhi Beefs Up Security Ahead Of Jantar Mantar Protest - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured - Jantar Mantar Protest LIVE: Delhi Police Barricades Roads Amid Anti-CEC Protest Call | Delhi News The order was passed by Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of Patiala House Courts. The Judge passed the order after earlier giving Bhardwaj interim bail for three weeks and observing his conduct during the period. The detailed bail order is awaited. The court had on September 15 granted Bhardwaj interim bail for three weeks, observing that his conduct during this period would be considered while deciding his regular bail plea. The relief came with several conditions. Bhardwaj was barred from posting, publishing or discussing the case, his defence or the complainants family on social media or any other media platform. He was also directed to stay away from the complainant, his daughter and all witnesses, and was warned against tampering with evidence. While granting interim bail, the court emphasised that bail was an expression of its trust and not a trophy to be displayed". It also cautioned Bhardwaj against holding or participating in any public celebration following his release. The case stems from the alleged assault of the father of a student activist during protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar. The influencer was detained in Uttar Pradeshs Bulandshahr on September 4, shortly after the Delhi Police told CJP protesters that he would be arrested within 72 hours over an alleged assault. No response found Bhardwaj Boasted About Cracking Skull Of Student Activists Father The case gained attention after a video of Bhardwajs interview circulated widely on social media. In the clip, he allegedly claimed to have cracked Kumars skull during the protest. The influencer allegedly escaped from Naithla village on a Bullet motorcycle heading towards Khurja shortly before the police team arrived to detain him, officials said. He was reportedly wearing a helmet, which police suspect was intended to hide his identity. The viral video triggered severe public backlash, prompting an outpour of support from opposition leaders including Rahul Gandhi, and leading members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to march to the Parliament Street police station demanding immediate action on Friday. What Happened During CJP Protest? The physical altercation took place during a CJP-led protest against the alleged NEET-UG exam paper leaks at Jantar Mantar. Sanjay Kumar, who was accompanying his student-activist daughter Nishu Azad, was struck on the head during a scuffle and had to be taken away in an ambulance to receive stitches. Bhardwaj openly boasted about cracking Kumars skull . He claimed that an alleged phone call from BJP leader Kapil Mishra helped him escape prison and named prominent leaders as his elder brothers" who supported him. What Swatantra Bhardwaj Said In Podcast? Nishu ke baap ko hum sar faade Aapko pata hai, isko kaun sa dhaara lagta hai? Half murder. Section 307. Sar pe saath taka laga hua tha. Banda marne ke sthiti pe ambulance mein ja raha tha. Uski beti thana ke baahar khade hoke keh rahi thi ki agar mere baap ko insaaf nahi mila to hum zehar khaake mar jaayenge?" he said in the podcast. [I cracked the skull of Nishus father. Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in a serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didnt get justice.] Following the outrage, Bhardwaj backtracked on Friday, stating that his comments about political intervention were entirely sarcastic" and meant to mock his critics . He claimed the video was heavily edited and that he acted in self-defense" after being surrounded and pushed by protesters at the site. Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of the Patiala House Courts granted regular bail to Swatantra Bhardwaj after observing his conduct during a prior three-week interim bail period.

headline: Direct DVAC to register FIR against Finance Minister Marie Wilson, insists PIL plea before Madras High Court
content: An advocate has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register a First Information Report (FIR) on the basis of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilsons claim in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly that he was a victim of corruption in the School Education Department during the previous DMK regime. The plea is expected to be listed for hearing before the first Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan since it had been filed as a public interest litigation (PIL) petition. K. Sivasubramaniam of Chennai had filed the petition seeking a direction to register an FIR against the Minister, as the payment of a bribe was also a criminal offence. The petitioner stated that Mr. Wilson, during a debate in the Legislative Assembly on August 24, 2026, confessed to being a victim of corrupt practices during the previous regime, when bribe money was allegedly demanded and collected forcibly from educational institutions. The Minister also said that he was a witness to the payment of a bribe and that he knew exactly how much was paid. Highlighting that not only the receipt of a bribe but also the payment of one to public servants was an offence under Sections 8 and 12 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the PIL petitioner said he lodged a complaint with the DVAC on August 27, 2026, as a result. However, he complained that the law enforcement agency had, so far, not taken any action on his plea to register an FIR against the Minister. An open confession of a criminal act made by a Minister inside the Legislative Assembly cannot be dismissed as mere political rhetoric, the petitioner said and contended that the constitutional immunity granted to legislators, under Article 194(2) of the Constitution, from civil or criminal proceedings with respect to their actions in the House would not provide a shield of immunity for criminal acts. While the speech inside the Assembly is recorded in the official transcript, the act of giving a bribe took place outside the Legislative precincts. The official speech serves as a voluntary, unequivocal evidentiary admission of a completed pre-existing criminal act under Section 8 of the PC Act. Privileges under Article 194 cannot be weaponised to bar law enforcement from investigating independent cognisable crimes admitted by public functionaries, his affidavit read. Further, claiming that former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi had subsequently levelled certain allegations of irregularities against Mr. Wilsons educational institutions, the petitioner insisted that the allegations against the sitting Minister, too, must be probed by the DVAC.

headline: Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive
content: Sources said Pakistan is preparing to provide Saudi Arabia with additional military support as Riyadh faces an escalation in attacks from the Houthis Pakistan is moving towards a significantly expanded military role in Saudi Arabia as the conflict with Yemens Houthi rebels intensifies, with sources indicating that Islamabad is preparing a broader mobilisation of its armed forces under the newly activated Mecca defence pact. The development comes as Saudi-backed Yemeni forces have launched a major offensive against the Houthis around the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, backed by Saudi air power. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | - 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised - From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia Sources said Pakistan is preparing to provide Saudi Arabia with additional military support, including personnel and military capabilities, as Riyadh faces an escalation in attacks from the Houthis. The sources claimed that the mobilisation could involve forces from across Pakistans military, including the Army, Air Force and Navy, as well as missile and rocket capabilities. Details of the deployment, including the numbers and precise roles of the forces involved, have not been publicly disclosed. The development follows an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Mecca Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on October 5. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Trkiye agreed at the meeting to move immediately towards implementing their collective defence commitments and take steps to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities for rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia. The joint statement did not specify the number of troops to be deployed or identify the individual military units and weapons systems involved. Pakistans Military Role According to sources, Pakistans military footprint in Saudi Arabia could now expand considerably as Riyadh seeks additional support amid the Houthi escalation. Sources claimed that Pakistani military assets could be positioned to protect Saudi territory and strategic installations, while Pakistani naval assets could also be involved in safeguarding Saudi interests around the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab. There have also been claims that Pakistan could provide artillery, rockets, drones and short-range missile capabilities. These details, however, have not been publicly confirmed by Islamabad or Riyadh. The sources further claimed that Pakistani Air Force assets could support Saudi operations against Houthi threats. Any direct Pakistani participation in airstrikes inside Yemen would represent a major escalation, but no such role has been officially announced. Pakistans public position so far has focused on defending Saudi Arabias sovereignty and territorial integrity. Islamabad has repeatedly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and backed Riyadhs right to defend itself. What The Mecca Pact Says The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Trkiye in August and provides a framework for collective defence. The three countries have now agreed to translate that framework into practical military measures. The October 5 joint statement said the alliance would take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities" and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, in accordance with existing arrangements and the national laws of the three countries. The agreement also states that the security of each member is an integral part of the collective security of all three. Why The Timing Matters The activation of the pact comes as Yemens Saudi-backed government has launched a major counteroffensive against the Houthis. The offensive is focused in part on areas around Bab al-Mandab, the narrow waterway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and one of the worlds most important maritime chokepoints. Saudi Arabia has provided extensive air support to the operation, with the Saudi-led coalition saying around 100 fighter jets were involved. The Houthis, meanwhile, have continued missile and drone attacks against Saudi targets, including oil infrastructure and other strategic sites, according to reports. The latest developments therefore mark a potentially significant expansion of Pakistans military commitments in the Gulf. Pakistan is moving towards a significantly expanded military role as the conflict with Yemens Houthi rebels intensifies, following an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Mecca Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on October 5.

headline: 730 Days Of Childcare Leave: How NCW's New Proposal Seeks To Change Parenting For Working Couples
content: The NCW has proposed transforming the existing women-centric Child Care Leave (CCL) system into a gender-neutral framework, under which either parent could take leave For years, Indias childcare leave framework has largely been built around one assumption that when a child needs extended care, it is the mother who is expected to step away from work. The National Commission for Women now wants to change that. In a set of 37 recommendations submitted to the Centre, the NCW has proposed transforming the existing women-centric Child Care Leave (CCL) system into a gender-neutral framework, under which either parent could take leave to care for their child. It has proposed splitting the existing 730-day entitlement between working parents, introducing shared caregiving, extending the benefit to private-sector employees and creating a broader ecosystem of workplace childcare. - The Millennial Mom | Postpartum, Breastfeeding, And The Bittersweet Reality No One Prepared Me For - 'Something Bigger Than Me': Esteban Ribovics On Building Legacy Beyond MMA - 17-Year-Old Kills Mother In Lucknow After Dispute Over Returning Home - Your Child Is Not Meant To Carry Your Emotions: The Parenting Lesson Many Learn Too Late What Is The Existing 730-Day Child Care Leave Rule? Under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, eligible female government employees can currently avail themselves of up to 730 days of Child Care Leave during their entire service for taking care of their two eldest surviving children, up to the age of 18. There is no age limit for a disabled child. CCL is subject to conditions, including limits on the number of spells in a calendar year and prior approval from the competent authority. The framework has evolved over the years. The government has also highlighted measures such as reducing the minimum period of CCL from 15 days to five days and allowing employees to leave headquarters or undertake foreign travel during CCL, subject to rules. However, CCL is not a universal parental benefit. Government rules were amended in 2020 to allow male government employees to avail CCL, but only where they are single male parents, such as widowers, divorcees or unmarried fathers who are raising children on their own. The NCW wants to move beyond this. The National Commission for Women (NCW) submitted 37 recommendations to the Centre. The NCW proposes transforming the existing 730-day Child Care Leave (CCL) system into a gender-neutral framework. Currently, eligible female government employees can avail up to 730 days of CCL for their two eldest surviving children up to age 18. The NCW proposes dividing the existing 730 days equally between working parents, with 365 days for each. The NCW also proposes mandatory paid paternity leave across all sectors, including private and unorganised sectors. What Is The NCW Proposing? The commission has proposed that the existing 730 days be divided equally between both working parents 365 days for each. Alternatively, where both parents work for the same organisation, they could potentially have access to a common pool of 730 days. The proposal goes further for children in the crucial early years. For those aged zero to two, the NCW has suggested a 60:40 shared-care model between primary and secondary caregivers. In practical terms, this could mean that childcare does not automatically translate into a long career interruption for the mother. A father could take a substantial period of leave when the child needs him, while the mother could return to work without having to shoulder the entire burden of caregiving. That is also the thinking behind another major recommendation: mandatory paid paternity leave across sectors, including the private and unorganised sectors. CCL Is Different From Maternity Leave Child Care Leave (CCL) is different from maternity leave because it is meant to allow an employee to take time off to look after an existing child, rather than for pregnancy, childbirth or the immediate post-delivery period. Under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, eligible female Central Government employees can avail themselves of up to 730 days of CCL during their entire service for caring for their two eldest surviving children, subject to prescribed conditions. Importantly, this 730-day CCL provision is a benefit under Central Government service rules and does not apply to private-sector employees. While certain single male Central Government employees can also avail CCL under specified conditions, there is currently no equivalent statutory 730-day childcare leave entitlement for employees in the private sector. Maternity leave, on the other hand, is a separate benefit linked to pregnancy and childbirth and is governed by applicable maternity benefit laws and service rules. The Supreme Courts Paternity Leave Push The NCWs proposal comes months after a significant intervention by the Supreme Court. In March 2026, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan, while hearing Hamsaanandini Nanduri v Union of India, dealt with the rights of adoptive mothers but also devoted considerable attention to the importance of fathers in childcare. The court urged the Union government to introduce a legal provision recognising paternity leave as a social security benefit, saying its duration should be determined keeping in mind the needs of both parents and the child. The judgment made an important point: the absence of paternity leave can reinforce traditional gender roles because even fathers who want to participate meaningfully in early childcare may not have a genuine opportunity to do so. The court noted that existing Central government rules do provide male government servants with 15 days of paternity leave in specified circumstances. But it observed that the concept remains relatively limited and less recognised compared with maternity protection. Private Sector: The Bigger Test The most consequential part of the NCW proposal is its push to extend gender-neutral CCL to the private sector. The commission has suggested a phased approach, beginning with large industries before extending it to medium and small enterprises. It has also proposed incorporating CCL into the Social Security Code, along with financial incentives and tax support for employers that adopt childcare policies. The NCW has specifically flagged recruitment discrimination, stalled promotions, salary consequences and perceptions that women who take childcare leave are less committed to their jobs. It has said that motherhood should not become a career penalty". The commissions recommendations recognise that parents need more than leave. It has proposed a National Childcare Infrastructure Mission aimed at creating five lakh creche seats by 2030, through on-site creches, shared or cluster facilities and contributions to a State Childcare Fund. It has also called for minimum national standards for creches and greater workplace flexibility, including work-from-home and flexible workload arrangements. The recommendations also attempt to address a much larger gap: women outside formal employment. The NCW has pointed out that more than 90 per cent of women workers remain outside effective coverage and has called for maternity and childcare benefits for informal, gig and platform workers. So, the 730-day proposal is not simply about giving fathers more leave. It is about changing the architecture of caregiving in India. If implemented, the idea would be that having a child should not automatically mean a womans career takes the larger hit, while a fathers role is reduced to a few days of paternity leave. Instead, childcare could become a shared entitlement, backed by leave, creches and workplace flexibility. The NCW has proposed transforming the existing women-centric 730-day Child Care Leave system into a gender-neutral framework. Under this proposal, the 730 days could be divided equally between both working parents or accessed as a common pool if they work for the same organization, while also extending the benefit to the private sector.

headline: 'Gyanesh Kumar Is Scared': Rahul Gandhi Questions EC At Oppn Protest, Says 'Standing Here To Save Democracy'

INDIA bloc MPs protested against the Election Commission in Delhi on Tuesday. Rahul Gandhi questioned why elected MPs were not allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. All MPs are here standing to save the democracy," he said. Gandhi went on to target Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that they had undermined democracy. PM Modi, Home Minister Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar have finished the democracy," the Leader of Opposition said. Not even a single person can run away. Nobody can escape. This is treason against the country," he added. INDIA Bloc March Stopped Near Akashvani Bhawan The protest began after opposition MPs assembled at Parliaments Makar Dwar and set off towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters. The demonstration was organised amid the oppositions demand for Kumars resignation over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other opposition leaders subsequently sat on the road after being prevented from moving ahead. She later got off the bus and joined her brother near the Akashvani gate. The Gandhi siblings, along with Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda, later entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises through the reception gate. Police asked the protesters to vacate the area, but they remained there and insisted that they wanted to proceed to the Election Commission office. The protesting MPs carried cutouts depicting Kumar in an RSS uniform and raised slogans such as BJP hi CEC hai", Vote chor, gaddi chhod" and Democracy not for sale." Gandhi had earlier targeted the CEC in a post on X, writing: Gyanesh, its done bro. Time to resign". Several opposition leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained after police stopped the march. BJD MPs also joined the demonstration. Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the participation reflected opposition solidarity against what the party calls irregularities in the electoral process. With inputs from PTI Opposition MPs marched towards Nirvachan Sadan to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and irregularities in the electoral process.

headline: Rahul Gandhi's SIR Dharna: Why AAP, DMK Skipped INDIA Bloc's Sit-In Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: after an opposition meeting where Rahul Gandhi's strategy regarding CEC Gyanesh Kumar was approved by other partners, but AAP and DMK were sidelined The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) skipped the INDIA blocs October 6 Save Democracy" march and Rahul Gandhis subsequent sit-in following deep-seated political friction and strategic disagreements over how to target the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). WHY AAP SKIPPED THE PROTEST According to AAP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, the party has its own approach to addressing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row and voter list irregularities. AAP claimed they have been actively running their own persistent ground protests on the issue. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) skipped the INDIA bloc's October 6 "Save Democracy" march. Tensions escalated after Rahul Gandhi's strategy regarding CEC Gyanesh Kumar was approved, sidelining AAP and DMK. AAP leader Sanjay Singh stated the party has its own approach to addressing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) row. The DMK criticized the Congress party and accused Rahul Gandhi of "political immaturity." Tensions between DMK and Congress peaked after Congress aligned with actor-politician Vijay's party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). AAP explicitly stated it chose to skip the joint march because it believes the issue concerns the public directly. They preferred to protest without using their formal party banner, opting out of the Congress-led joint political framing, according to reports. During previous sit-ins staged by Rahul Gandhi outside the Prime Ministers residence, AAP leaders like Saurabh Bhardwaj had publicly accused Congress of attempting to hijack" and weaken youth-led student movements. AAP had even questioned in the media how Congress leaders easily managed to hold high-profile sit-ins in high-security zones near the PMs residence while ordinary student protesters faced heavy police action. AAP alleged that Congresss theatrical demonstrations were designed to steal the spotlight away from organic grassroots campaigns. WHY DMK SKIPPED THE PROTEST Local political friction in Tamil Nadu severely fractured relations between the two parties. The DMK strongly criticised the Congress party and accused Rahul Gandhi of political immaturity". Tensions peaked after Congress aligned with actor-politician Vijays party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The DMK viewed this move as an opportunistic betrayal of coalition principles, leading them to formally distance themselves and skip the INDIA blocs joint activities. While other alliance leaders such as Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav (SP), and Arvind Sawant (Shiv Sena UBT) joined the sit-in demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, both AAP and DMK chose to chart their own course away from Congress leadership, say reports. The Aam Aadmi Party and the DMK skipped the march and Rahul Gandhi's sit-in due to deep-seated political friction, strategic disagreements over targeting the BJP, and being sidelined from the core strategy group by Congress's unilateral decision-making.

It stated in a post on X: The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026. In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court." The statement made in this [Rahul Gandhis] post is misleading." Opposition leaders staged a sit-in protest after security personnel blocked their "Save Democracy" march toward the Election Commission headquarters, following outrage over alleged voter roll discrepancies linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

headline: Samajwadi Party Drops Plan To Field Third Candidate, Clears Way For BJP's 8 Nominees
content: The Samajwadi Party has decided not to field a third candidate in the UP Rajya Sabha elections. Akhilesh Yadav said the party's focus is now on all 403 Assembly seats. The Samajwadi Party (SP) has decided not to field a third candidate in the Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha elections, removing the possibility of a contest for the 10 seats and clearing the way for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to elect all eight of its nominees if the nominations are found valid. The decision came on Tuesday, the final day for filing nominations for the biennial Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh. - BJP Announces Candidates For UP Rajya Sabha Polls, Dharampal Singh, Shruti Gangwar Among 8 Names - Akhilesh Yadav Has Announced Only 2 Names, Can SP Chief Still Pull Off A Surprise For BJP In UP Rajya Sabha Polls? - Hardeep Singh Puri, BL Verma Among 8 Sitting MPs Dropped From BJP's Candidate List For UP Rajya Sabha Polls - BJP Knows How To Win. Nitin Nabin Now Wants It To Listen | Saffron Scoop The Samajwadi Party has fielded two candidates, party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, both of whom filed their nomination papers in the presence of SP president Akhilesh Yadav. The development follows speculation that the SP could field a third candidate after the BJP announced its eight nominees on Monday. The BJP has the numbers to comfortably win seven seats, while the SP has the strength to secure two seats based on the existing composition of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly. Akhilesh Yadav Puts Focus On 403 Assembly Seats Akhilesh Yadav appeared to signal the partys decision through a cryptic post on X on Tuesday. The SP chief said the partys focus was not on three Rajya Sabha seats but on all 403 seats of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly. Samajwadi Party has decided not to field a third candidate for the UP Rajya Sabha elections. Akhilesh Yadav said the party's focus is now on all 403 Uttar Pradesh Assembly seats. With eight BJP and two SP candidates for 10 seats, an unopposed election is now likely. Now, our focus is not on three, but on 403," Yadav said in his post. The remark created a stir in political circles and was seen as an indication that the SP had decided against challenging the BJP for an additional Rajya Sabha seat. The SP had earlier been considering a third candidate for the Rajya Sabha elections. However, with the party ultimately nominating only Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, the immediate possibility of a contest has been eliminated. The party has 101 lawmakers in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly. Its decision to stick to two candidates means the party is now set to focus on securing those two Rajya Sabha seats rather than attempting to stretch its numbers for a third seat. BJPs Eight Candidates File Nominations The SPs decision came on the same day that all eight BJP candidates filed their nominations for the Rajya Sabha elections. The BJPs nominees are Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. The BJP candidates were accompanied by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak during the nomination process. With eight BJP candidates and two SP candidates now in the fray, the number of candidates matches the 10 available Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. The biennial elections for the 10 seats are scheduled for October 16, while the terms of the sitting members expire on November 25. The SPs decision not to field a third candidate has effectively removed the prospect of a direct contest between the BJP and SP for the additional seat. Since the number of candidates is currently equal to the number of seats, all 10 candidates could be elected unopposed. However, the process is not yet formally complete. The nomination papers will have to undergo scrutiny, followed by the withdrawal process. If no additional candidate enters the contest, all 10 nominations are found valid and no candidate withdraws, voting will not be required on October 16. The Samajwadi Party decided to drop its plan to field a third candidate in the Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha elections, which removes the possibility of a contest and clears the way for all eight BJP nominees.

headline: 'Rockstar' FDA Chief Tukaram Mundhe Gets NYT Spotlight: 'Diners Revere Him, And Owners Fear Him'
content: Maharashtra FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe gained international attention in a New York Times report for his rigorous food safety crackdown across the state. Tukaram Mundhe, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner known for his uncompromising approach to enforcement, has drawn international attention for his crackdown on food safety violations. The New York Times recently put the IAS officer in the spotlight, describing him as a rockstar" in a front-page report on his campaign against restaurants and food businesses across Maharashtra. - Tukaram Mundhe Bans Infant Formula Ads, Mother-Child Photos On Baby Food Packets - 'If You Know...': Tukaram Mundhe Responds To Sanjay Rauts FDA Bribery Claims, Says Infant Nutrition Next Target - 'Something Bigger Than Me': Esteban Ribovics On Building Legacy Beyond MMA - Man Finds Rat In Dosa At Mumbai Hotel, Vomits In Shock; Tukaram Mundhe's Team Suspends Licence Also Read: Tukaram Mundhe Bans Infant Formula Ads, Mother-Child Photos On Baby Food Packets No business appears to escape Mundhes attention," the newspaper wrote, under the strap Diners revere him, and owners fear him". The report also referred to Mundhe as a food safety celebrity", pointing to the unusual public interest generated by what would ordinarily be routine regulatory inspections and enforcement action. What Tukaram Mundhe Said After NYT Report Mundhe shared the New York Times report on X, but played down the attention he has received. NYT calls Tukaram Mundhe a rockstar and food safety celebrity. The report says his raids have made him popular with diners and feared by food business owners. Reacting to report, Mundhe says, Good governance is not about making headlines, but about making a difference. The IAS officer cleared UPSC in 2004 with an All India Rank of 20. His latest drive seized 50,601.78 kg of food stock worth Rs. 1.19 crore. Good governance is not about making headlines, but about making a difference," he said. Good governance is not about making headlines. It is about making a difference.Food safety is ultimately about protecting people, upholding standards and building public trust. When enforcement is fair, fearless and consistent, institutions earn credibility and citizens begin to believe that the system works. The New York Times captures one such story from Maharashtra. Tukaram Mundhe (@Tukaram_IndIAS) October 5, 2026 In a separate post, he explained what he believes effective enforcement should achieve. Food safety is ultimately about protecting people, upholding standards and building public trust. When enforcement is fair, fearless and consistent, institutions earn credibility and citizens begin to believe that the system works. The New York Times captures one such story from Maharashtra," he wrote. Who Is Tukaram Mundhe? A 2005-batch Maharashtra-cadre IAS officer, Mundhe has developed a reputation over the course of his career for taking a hard line on administrative enforcement and resisting political or institutional pressure. His journey into the civil services began in modest circumstances. Mundhe grew up in a farming family, with his father working as a marginal farmer and his mother managing the household amid financial difficulties. He helped with farm work while studying at a Zilla Parishad school. Also Read: A Star Spreads Light, Not Darkness: Inside Tukaram Mundhes Latest Warning To Bollywood He subsequently pursued higher education in Political Science at Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University before clearing the UPSC Civil Services Examination in 2004 with an All India Rank of 20. His administrative career has taken him through several districts and civic bodies in Maharashtra, including Nanded, Washim, Jalna, Solapur, Navi Mumbai, Nashik, Nagpur and Pune. Over the years, he has served as Assistant Collector, District Collector and Municipal Commissioner, besides holding positions including Chairman and Managing Director of the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Ltd (PMPML). His tenure as Solapur Collector brought particular recognition for work related to water management and administrative transparency. He received the Maharashtra governments Best District Collector Award for 2015-16 and was also honoured as the Waterman of Maharashtra." Mundhes style of functioning has also made him one of Maharashtras most frequently transferred bureaucrats. He has reportedly been transferred more than 24 times during nearly two decades in government service. Mundhes Food Safety Crackdown His current assignment as Maharashtra FDA commissioner has given that reputation a new focus, with the department stepping up inspections and action against food businesses across the state. The enforcement drive intensified ahead of the festive season. Between September 23 and 27, the FDA suspended licences and seized 50,601.78 kg of food stock valued at Rs. 1.19 crore, according to department data. The action extended across several divisions. The FDA said licences or registration certificates of 13 establishments in Mumbai, six in Konkan, eight in Pune and three in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar were suspended. Among the establishments facing action were well-known Mumbai businesses including Kyani & Co, Colaba Sweet Mart, Arun Vilas Farsan and Subway, among others. The New York Times featured Tukaram Mundhe on its front page for his uncompromising food safety crackdown against restaurants and food businesses across Maharashtra.

headline: TVK-led government backstabbed nurses, alleges M.K. Stalin
content: president M.K. Stalin on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) alleged that the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government had backstabbed nurses after promising to fulfil their demands. In a social media message, he condemned the arrest of nurses (on Monday [October 5] night), who had been fighting for job security, equal pay, and permanent employment. How could the government bring itself to arrest nurses when it is not able to hold talks with them? The legal adviser of the nurses has alleged they were arrested after being invited for talks on the pretext of holding discussions, he said. Mr. Stalin said before coming to power, the TVK had extended support to the protesters, but had taken police action against them after becoming the ruling party. What do the TVK Ministers say about this incident when they have been defending Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, a bundle of contradictions? The nurses continued their protests with the help of the lights on their mobile phones after the power was cut. They were arrested overnight. Is this the change the TVK is talking about? he asked. Mr. Stalin also recalled the warning by the woman police officer, who was gesticulating with her fingers and saying, Your life is important. Will the Chief Minister, who holds the police portfolio, respond to it? Or will he make reels of the woman police officers action and advertise it as an achievement? he asked. EPS condemns police action AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami said the police brutality unleashed by the TVK government against nurses, who were staging a peaceful protest, is the height of cruelty. The police force under the Chief Minister has committed this fascist atrocity against nurses who are engaged in the vital duty of saving lives. How will this Reels Chief Minister justify it? he asked in a social media post. Before coming to power, do you remember what your party functionaries and those who are Ministers today said while standing in front of these very same nurses? Is this the change you promised: saying one thing before coming to power and doing the exact opposite after assuming office? he further asked. He urged the government to immediately release all the arrested nurses and ensure that no cases are filed against them. Arbitrary action Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran also criticised the State government for what he called arbitrary action against the agitating nurses. In a post on social media, Mr. Dhinakaran recalled how the ruling party, while not in power, had supported the nurses demands. He pointed out that during the COVID-19 pandemic, the nurses had rendered their services, even unmindful of their lives, and that the government should meet their demands on job security and equal pay for equal work.

headline: Has Urbanisation Left The Gomti With Too Little Room To Breathe?
content: Lucknows latest flood has revived questions over development along the Gomti. As the riverfront itself goes under water, experts warn about the shrinking floodplain LUCKNOW: The latest flooding in Lucknow may have begun with rain falling hundreds of kilometres upstream, but the damage being seen in the city is raising a more difficult question: What happens when a river is denied the space it needs to spread? The Gomti rose in Lucknow days after the heaviest rain had passed because runoff from its upper catchment took roughly eight to 10 days to travel downstream. Yet the inundation of low-lying neighbourhoods such as Faizullahganj, Ghaila and Daud Nagar has also put the spotlight on a longer-term transformation of the rivers landscape the steady urbanisation of areas that once functioned as the Gomtis floodplain. - Gandak Swallows Homes On Camera, Cow Dung 'Flies' At MP As Bihar Floods Drown 200 Villages - Delhi's Rape Cases Have Dipped Since 2023, But Supreme Court Called Ground Reality 'A Systemic Failure': Heres Why - Indian Man Spots Narrow Lanes, Garbage Piles, Wall With Ads In China, Questions Why Is Only India Called Dirty? - Bengalurus Hebbal Tunnel Under Scrutiny: IIT-Bombay Study Faces Questions Over Data And Traffic Claims The issue is particularly relevant in a city that has invested heavily in turning its riverfront into an urban public space. The Riverfront Question Lucknows Gomti Riverfront was conceived as a major urban renewal project, with promenades, parks and public spaces along an 8.1-km stretch of the river. But the project also involved straightening the river and constructing reinforced diaphragm walls along both banks. Studies cited in recent environmental assessments and reporting found that the floodplain along the developed stretch was narrowed from about 450 metres to 240 metres, while the clear waterway was reduced from roughly 250 metres to between 100 and 125 metres. The project reclaimed around 200 hectares of land. That change matters during extreme flows. A floodplain is not simply unused land beside a river; it is part of the river systems natural storage space. When water levels rise, the river can spread into these areas, slowing and distributing the flow. Constricting that space with roads, walls and construction can leave less room for the river to accommodate sudden increases in discharge. A 2019 study also found a significant ecological difference between channelised and relatively undisturbed sections of the Gomti. Researchers identified eight habitat types for fish and other aquatic organisms in undisturbed stretches, compared with just two in the channelised sections. What About Lucknows Marine Drive? The citys so-called Marine Drive has become another prominent piece of infrastructure along the Gomti corridor. But the current flooding does not by itself establish that Marine Drive caused the inundation. What it does show is the vulnerability of infrastructure built close to the river. The Marine Drive underpass was among the stretches severely affected during an earlier spell of heavy rain, with vehicles getting stranded in floodwater. The larger concern, therefore, is not one road or project in isolation. It is whether a series of roads, embankments, walls and developments along the river has progressively reduced the space available for water to move and disperse during high-flow events. This Years Flood Has Exposed The Contradiction The contradiction is now visible on the ground. The Gomti Riverfront, built partly to bring the city closer to its river, has itself been inundated as the river swelled. Large low-lying portions of the waterfront were submerged even as local rainfall had eased, with authorities opening barrage gates to manage the rising water. At the same time, several neighbourhoods located in low-lying areas have remained vulnerable to flooding. This does not mean that the Riverfront alone explains the current inundation. Officials have attributed the immediate rise in the Gomti to exceptionally heavy rainfall across its upstream basin. Between September 25 and 27, Lakhimpur Kheri recorded 268.3 mm of rain, Shahjahanpur 263.9 mm, Hardoi 147.2 mm, Sitapur 144.1 mm and Pilibhit 119.9 mm. Lucknow itself recorded 180.5 mm during the same three-day period. The runoff from those districts continued moving towards Lucknow after the skies cleared over the city, producing the delayed flood pulse now being witnessed. But unusually heavy rain is only one part of the flood equation. When The Floodplain Becomes Real Estate Principal secretary of the irrigation and water resources department Anil Garg has pointed to three factors behind the present inundation: exceptional rainfall across the basin, smaller rivers and streams reaching their carrying capacity, and urbanisation and encroachment over the Gomtis floodplain. Historically, Garg told TOI, the river could spread across a wider floodplain during high flows. Urban development has reduced that space, meaning water is increasingly confined to a narrower corridor and low-lying settlements can bear the consequences. The concern is particularly acute because the citys development has not stopped at the existing riverfront. The Green Corridor project is being constructed along the Gomti, including an embankment intended partly to protect flood-prone areas. The LDA says sections of the embankment have already protected parts of Gomti Nagar Extension and adjoining areas from rising water. That creates an important policy dilemma: should the response to a river with less floodplain be more embankments and more barriers, or should more of its natural flood-storage capacity be restored? More Embankments Or More Room For The River? The answer is already moving towards more flood protection infrastructure. Following inspections of flood-hit areas, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered a survey for a proposed embankment system extending from Bakshi Ka Talab in Lucknow towards Naimisharanya in Sitapur. Officials are also examining vulnerable stretches and possible pumping stations. Separately, the LDA has proposed a Rs. 182-crore embankment along the Gomti from IIM Road towards Hardinge Bridge via Khadra to protect areas including Faizullaganj and Daud Nagar. These measures could protect settlements already exposed to flooding. But they also underline the central challenge facing Lucknow: the city has increasingly built around and along a river whose behaviour depends on having space to expand. The present flood is therefore not simply a story of rain falling upstream and water arriving late. It is also a reminder that when extreme rainfall sends a delayed surge downstream, the amount of floodplain left open to the river can determine where that water ultimately goes. For Lucknow, the question is no longer just how high the Gomti will rise. It is how much room the city is still willing to give the river when it does. The flooding in Lucknow was primarily triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall across the Gomti's upstream basin between September 25 and 27, with runoff taking eight to ten days to travel downstream. Additionally, officials cited smaller rivers reaching capacity and the steady urbanisation and encroachment over the river's natural floodplain as major contributing factors.

headline: Flydubai's Omani Co-Pilot Wanted 'Revenge For Gaza', Jordan Military Base Was 'Plan B': Report
content: Investigators believe the suspect, identified as Omani national al-Hammami, had prepared the attack well before the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. An Omani co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a Flydubai flight allegedly planned to crash the aircraft at Israels Ben Gurion Airport and was motivated by a desire to take revenge for Israels actions in Gaza, according to findings from the investigation cited by Israeli media outlet Ynet. According to the investigators, the accused co-pilot also had a plan B ready, in case the first plan failed, which included targetting a US military facility in Jordan. - Can A Pakistani Pilot Fly Into India? Flydubai's Omani Co-Pilot Case Raises Questions - BREAKING NEWS | Israel Was Ready To Shoot Down FlyDubai Plane After Captain Attack | CBS Report - Flydubai Cockpit Horror: UAE Orders Probe Into Possible Terror Link, Prior Planning | - Israel Was Prepared To Shoot Down Flydubai Plane With 150 Israelis Aboard After Cockpit Attack What Omani Co-Pilot Had Planned? Investigators believe the suspect, identified as Omani national al-Hammami, had prepared the attack well before the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Israeli officials said he had initially planned to carry out the attack in July but abandoned that attempt because of a personal connection with a crew member. According to the investigation, his primary objective was to bring down the aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv. If reaching Israel became impossible, investigators believe he intended to target a US military facility in Jordan instead. Israeli officials say al-Hammami had travelled to Israel as early as June and was preparing himself to become a martyr", according to Ynet. Other reports citing officials familiar with the investigation have also said he had previously considered attacking an Israel-bound flight before abandoning the plan. An Omani co-pilot allegedly planned to crash a Flydubai flight at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport. The co-pilot had a plan B to target a US military facility in Jordan if the first plan failed. The alleged plot came to light after the co-pilot attacked the captain aboard the flight on September 30. The aircraft lost around 17,000 feet in about a minute during the incident. Flydubai has suspended flights between the UAE and Israel following the incident. Also Read: Israel Was Prepared To Shoot Down Flydubai Plane With 150 Israelis Aboard After Cockpit Attack: Report No Link With Terrorist Organisation At present, investigators have not found evidence that the suspect was operating under the direction of a terrorist organisation or foreign government. The current assessment is that he acted alone, although authorities are examining his travels and contacts in several countries. Investigators are also looking into visits he made to countries regarded by Israel as hostile or enemy states. Officials are examining whether he encountered anyone during those trips who could have recruited, instructed or influenced him. Authorities in Australia and New Zealand are separately examining his background. Australian officials have confirmed that a joint counterterrorism team involving the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation is looking into his links to Australia, where he held a student visa and studied between 2015 and 2017. What Happened In Flydubai Flight? The alleged plot came to light after the co-pilot attacked the captain aboard the flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. The mostly Israeli passengers were later taken to safety after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, managed to regain access to the cockpit despite suffering injuries during the assault. He said he realised the aircraft was descending rapidly and forced himself to reach the cockpit door. Also Read: Flydubai Passengers Refuse To Free Omani Co-Pilot, Say Will Only Hand Him To Police In Video Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience, said he relied on his understanding of the aircraft and the situation despite being badly injured. Passengers also intervened after the aircraft plunged sharply, losing around 17,000 feet in about a minute, according to Flightradar24. One passenger, Miryam Shira Ohayon, described the plane as pretty much out of control" during the incident. The incident has been described by UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash as a terrorist act". Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also said the suspect had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination". The attacker, he calls out to the aircrew, Kill me, kill me," Netanyahu said, adding it was clear he was suicidal". Flydubai has suspended flights between the UAE and Israel following the incident. The passengers were subsequently flown back to Israel on a replacement aircraft. With inputs from AFP Investigators revealed that the Omani co-pilot, identified as al-Hammami, intended to crash the aircraft at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport as revenge for Israel's actions in Gaza. His plan B was to target a US military facility in Jordan if reaching Israel failed.

headline: When Brazil Became India And Nepal Became 'Nipple': Looking Back At Trump's Most Memorable Gaffes
content: up came this week, when Trump appeared to confuse Brazil with India while commenting on Brazils presidential election US President Donald Trump has a long history of verbal slips, geographical mix-ups and memorable mispronunciations. The latest came this week, when Trump appeared to confuse Brazil with India while commenting on Brazils presidential election. In a Truth Social post, he initially wrote that 125 Million People" had voted in the first round of Indias presidential election, even though it was Brazil that held its presidential election on October 4. The figure of around 125 million voters also matched Brazils election. Trump later changed India" to Brazil" in the post. - Brazil Elections: Can Lula Hold Back Latin Americas Right-Wing Shift? | Flavio Bolsonaro | N18G - Trump Mistakes Brazil For India, Claims 125 Million Voted In Presidential Election, Attacks US Voting System - Brazil Election Heads To Run-Off As Bolsonaro Beats Lula. Another Rightward Turn For Latin America? - Putin Praises PM Modi's Ukraine Peace Efforts, Hails India's Diversity: 'Never Fails To Amaze' It is only the latest in a long list of memorable Trump gaffes. Here are some of the most notable ones: Invented A Country Called Nambia During a speech at the United Nations in 2017, Trump referred to Nambia" while praising African countries. Unfortunately for the US President, there is no country called Nambia and he appeared to be referring to Namibia. The slip immediately became one of his most widely mocked geographical gaffes. Nepal Became Nipple, Bhutan Became Button Trump reportedly struggled with the names of Nepal and Bhutan during a 2017 briefing ahead of a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. According to a report by The Washington Post, he pronounced Nepal as nipple" and Bhutan as button". The report also said Trump did not initially realise that Nepal and Bhutan were separate sovereign countries and thought they were part of India. Belgium Is A Beautiful City At a 2016 rally, Trump said Belgium is a beautiful city." Belgium, of course, is a country and the capital is Brussels. The remark became another frequently cited example of Trumps geographical slips. Iran Became The Islamic Of Japan At a NATO summit in Ankara in July 2026, Trump referred to Iran as the Islamic of Japan" while discussing an Iranian missile attack. Zelenskyy Became Putin During the same NATO summit, Trump referred to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as President Putin" before attempting to correct himself. He subsequently explained that he had been posing a question for Russian President Vladimir Putin, but the slip was widely noted. Turkey Became A Company While speaking during the NATO summit, Trump also referred to Turkey as a great company", before correcting himself and saying country". TikTok Became Tic Tac During the same NATO appearance, Trump referred to TikTok as Tic Tac". The social media platforms name is TikTok; Tic Tac is the brand of breath mints. Though it was another small slip, it quickly made its way into the list of gaffes from his NATO appearance. Greenland Became Iceland At the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026, Trump repeatedly referred to Greenland as Iceland" while discussing the territory and his long-running interest in acquiring it. The mix-up was particularly notable because Greenland itself was central to the subject of his remarks. Finland And Raking Forests While discussing California wildfires, Trump once claimed that Finland did not face the same kind of forest-fire problems because Finns spend a lot of time raking" their forests. The comment drew widespread attention, with Finlands president subsequently clarifying that he had discussed forest management with Trump, but not that Finns routinely rake forests. Prince Of Whales During a 2019 meeting with then-British Prime Minister Theresa May, Trump referred to Prince Charles as the Prince of Whales" rather than the Prince of Wales. The slip was quickly picked up because Wales is one of the constituent countries of the United Kingdom, while whales are marine mammals. Two Corinthians At Liberty University in 2016, Trump referred to the biblical passage 2 Corinthians as Two Corinthians". The pronunciation became a talking point because the traditional English pronunciation is Second Corinthians". It was a small verbal slip, but it became memorable because of the religious setting in which he made it. Donald Trump initially confused Brazil with India in a Truth Social post regarding a presidential election.

headline: 'As Directed By Patnaik': BJD Joins Opposition Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over SIR, Voter Deletions
content: The BJD has joined Opposition protest in Delhi against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged SIR irregularities and voter deletions across India. The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) on Tuesday joined the Opposition parties protest march in New Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the deletion of voters names across the country. The BJD had announced earlier in the day that its Members of Parliament would participate in the protest at the direction of party president Naveen Patnaik. - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - From Streets To Supreme Court: CEC Gyanesh Kumar Faces The Heat | Brass Tacks With Nabila Jamal - BJD MPs Invited By Congress To Join INDIA Bloc March Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar | - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC The party has now joined the Oppositions mobilisation against the Election Commission, even as it reiterated that it maintains an equal distance from both the INDIA bloc and the NDA. BJD Parliamentary Party leader in the Rajya Sabha Manas Mangaraj had said the decision was taken following Patnaiks direction. As directed by our party president Patnaik, our MPs will participate in the protest march," Mangaraj said. The Opposition MPs began their march from Parliaments Makar Dwar towards Nirvachan Sadan, the headquarters of the Election Commission of India, demanding Kumars resignation. The protest is centred on allegations of irregularities in the SIR exercise and concerns over the deletion of voters from electoral rolls. BJD MPs joined the Opposition march in Delhi demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation. BJD raised concerns over the alleged deletion of over 13 crore voters nationally and more than 25 lakh voters in Odisha. The party reiterated that it maintains equal distance from the INDIA bloc and NDA, saying its participation is aimed at protecting electoral integrity. BJD Says Participation Is To Protect Electoral Integrity The BJD said it has been demanding Kumars resignation over his alleged role in the SIR exercise. Mangaraj maintained that the partys participation in the protest should not be viewed as an alignment with the INDIA bloc. As a responsible political party committed to protecting democratic institutions and the integrity of the electoral process, the BJD will participate in todays programme," Mangaraj said. The party also said a BJD delegation would visit a police station in Delhi and submit a memorandum demanding Kumars resignation. The BJD has raised concerns over the alleged exclusion of more than 25 lakh voters in Odisha and over 13 crore voters across the country in the name of SIR, according to the party. Mangaraj also referred to the situation in Dhamnagar in Odishas Bhadrak district, which he said had further strengthened the partys apprehensions about the electoral roll revision exercise. The deletion of 227 votes belonging to members of a minority community from a particular area (Dhamnagar), allegedly without the knowledge of the BLOs, raises serious questions about the integrity of the SIR exercise," he said. The BJD further flagged the alleged deletion of thousands of voters from electoral rolls in the Dhamnagar Assembly constituency and the sudden voluntary retirement application submitted by Odisha Chief Electoral Officer RS Gopalan. Opposition March Gains Momentum The BJDs participation has added to the Oppositions show of strength during Tuesdays protest. Leaders of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, respectively, besides TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, were expected to join the march. CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the Supreme Courts observations on the modified Form 6 had further strengthened the Oppositions position ahead of the protest. We will start our march by 10.30 am from Makar Dwar to the Chief Election Commissioners office. Then, almost all MPs who belong to the INDIA bloc will join," he said. He added that the Opposition was more charged" after the Supreme Courts observations and asserted that the protest would be a historic march". Security was tightened around Parliament and the Election Commission headquarters ahead of and during the protest, with barricading and deployment of security personnel in central Delhi. The BJD joined the opposition protest march in New Delhi to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and the deletion of millions of voters' names across the country. Party leaders emphasized that the participation was aimed at protecting electoral integrity and democratic institutions rather than aligning with the INDIA bloc.

headline: Yemen, Saudi Arabia strike Houthis as counteroffensive gets underway
content: Yemen's military backed by Saudi jets attacked Houthi targets including in the capital on Monday (October 5, 2026) as they launched an ambitious counteroffensive to recapture all territory held by the group following its recent lightning gains. The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn. Also Read: Yemens Houthis say struck Riyadh airport, other Saudi sites The government announced the lofty goal of retaking all Houthi territory home to most of Yemen's population, and much of it held for more than a decade on Sunday (October 4, 2026). Last month the Iran-backed group seized swathes of coastline along the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for oil and cargo shipping, in Yemen's deadliest fighting in years. The Houthis have also been attacking neighbouring Saudi Arabia since Yemen's civil war flared back to life, and have declared a maritime blockade on its ships. A source in the Saudi energy sector told AFP that an attack Sunday (October 4, 2026) had again halted pumping by the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, a key conduit for the kingdom's exports since Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the wider West Asia war. Later on Monday (October 5, 2026), the Houthis agency that liaises with airlines warned that Saudi airspace was not safe for civilian flights as it "will be the theatre of operations of our armed forces", but it carved out exceptions for the skies over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Crude prices had already been soaring as a result of West Asia war, before the Houthis began targeting the tankers and infrastructure of the world's largest oil exporter. Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser warned on Monday (October 5, 2026) that global oil stockpiles were "scarily thin" owing to the U.S.-Iran war, days after G7 nations agreed to release more of their inventories to ease supply concerns. "The system is already straining," Nasser told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London. The Houthis have accused the Saudi-led coalition of carrying out hundreds of strikes since the renewed fighting began. On Sunday (October 4, 2026), Yemen's military spokesman announced over 1,000 strikes against targets including artillery and rocket launcher positions, combat reinforcements and supply lines. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said 100 jets flew at daybreak as part of an operation dubbed "Dawn of Yemen", providing "round-the-clock air support for the Yemeni armed forces on the ground". Yemen's military also announced a "strategic offensive" against Sanaa, which has been in Houthi hands since 2014. The Houthis' official Saba news agency said a girl and a woman were killed in Sanaa governorate on Sunday. The strikes have yet to blunt ongoing Houthi advances on the ground, however. On Sunday, the group effectively encircled the city of Taiz after cutting the main supply route linking it to the interim government capital of Aden. Taiz residents remained defiant, vowing to stay and defend their city. "We cannot leave the city. It is impossible for us to leave. We will stay and die inside this city," Fahmi Ahmed Ghaleb told AFP. Humanitarian crisis Taiz city remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters. The Houthis' surrounding of Taiz "is a significant development, but I think it is still too early to say that we are witnessing a decisive turning point", Ahmed Nagi, a senior analyst for Yemen at the International Crisis Group, told AFP. While the war in Yemen predates the broader Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, it has become its most active front in recent weeks. The Houthis launched a rapid offensive around the Red Sea coast in September that killed hundreds of combatants on both sides. According to UN figures, the fighting has displaced more than 184,000 people. The Houthis took control of Sanaa in September 2014, forcing out the government and prompting Saudi intervention the following March at the head of an international coalition. The ensuing civil war caused hundreds of thousands of deaths and a spiralling humanitarian crisis that left a majority of the population relying on aid.

headline: Can Ladakh grow saffron? First-ever mass plantation drive begins in Leh
content: Indias saffron cultivation is set to expand beyond Kashmir, with a mass plantation drive underway in Ladakhs Leh district as the Union Territory makes its first attempt to cultivate the high-value spice on a large scale. Vinai Kumar Saxena, Governor, UT Ladakh, on Sunday announced the planting of 90,000 saffron corms, weighing 800kgs, in this region that has unique high-altitude agro-climatic conditions suitable for saffron. This pioneering project has immense potential to strengthen our local economy, creating lucrative and sustainable new livelihood opportunities for our hardworking farmers, youth, and self-help groups, he said. The experiment, spread across 4,000 square metres area in Leh, is a part of Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative to reclaim lost agrarian land in Ladakh. Saffron, the dried stigma of the flower, is often used in cooking, cosmetics, and for medicinal purposes. Pampore in Kashmir is well known for cultivating the finest saffron in India. The plant can be cultivated between autumn and winter, with the ideal location having minimum temperatures ranging from 8C to 10C and benefitting from light to moderate snowfall. Only corms weighing more than 10 grams bear saffron flowers, and the number of flowers depends on the size of the corm, directly affecting saffron production. On average, an acre of saffron cultivation in Pampore is known to yield a maximum of up to 2 kg of saffron. The present cultivation exercise in Leh comes in the wake of a successful experimental attempt at growing saffron in Ladakh two years ago, led by researchers at the CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM), Jammu. Botanically known as Crocus sativus, IIIM scientists had succeeded growing saffron in open fields in Leh. In 2024, the institute inked an MoU with the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Leh, towards setting up demonstration farms for the cultivation of medicinal, aromatic and flowering plants in Leh. Since then, the institute has been developing protocols for cultivation, processing, and post-harvest management extendable to these crops to the farmers field and is planning to introduce more crops. John had led a team that succeeded in growing saffron under greenhouse conditions in the Pune lab and has worked with farmers across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Sikkim for experimenting and increasing the acreage of saffron cultivation in India.

headline: Far-right election win leaves migrants questioning their future in eastern Germany
content: immigrant Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won a regional election last month, not a day goes by without Ola Akhras and her husband discussing whether they should go back to Syria. The couple live with their two young daughters in Magdeburg, where Saxony-Anhalt's newly elected State legislature was set to meet on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), for the first time since the AfD surged to its best result yet, putting it in a strong position to form Germany's first far-right regional government since the Second World War. During its first sitting, the 83-seat legislature will elect its Speaker, a post that traditionally goes to the largest party, and the AfD hopes for an initial symbolic victory. The State's next Governor is unlikely to be chosen before December 2026. "It's bad we've built our lives here, we really loved being here, but now we don't feel welcome anymore," said Ms. Akhras, who fled Homs for Germany in 2018. She speaks fluent German and works as a doctor at the local hospital, where she is completing her specialist training in internal medicine. Ms. Akhras, who wears a hijab, said she felt appreciated at work, but had lately encountered hostility while shopping and no longer felt safe leaving home in the evening. "Our children will never be recognised as Germans here," she said. The mood toward migrants has soured since 1 million arrived in 2015 The mood in society is very different from a decade ago, when Germans welcomed more than a million migrants from war-torn countries such as Syria, Iraq and Afghanistan, under Chancellor Angela Merkel. Many built new lives, learned the language and found work. However, as Germany's economic problems slow growth, high inflation, rising energy prices have worsened, public sentiment towards the newcomers has deteriorated. The AfD and other critics of immigration have blamed migrants for the country's problems. The 13-year-old party has gained support particularly rapidly in Germany's formerly Communist and economically weaker eastern States, including Saxony-Anhalt, though it also continues to gain at the national level; it is the strongest Opposition party in parliament and leads recent polls. The AfD's victory in Saxony-Anhalt last month underlined the party's skill in capitalising on discontent with issues well beyond its core theme of curbing immigration, as Chancellor Friedrich Merz's unpopular national government struggles to turn around Germany's stubbornly sluggish economy. The party's strong showing has unsettled migrants and those Germans who thought the nation was immune to nationalism after the horrors of the Nazi past. Many migrants fear AfD's campaign will lead to more deportations It remains uncertain whether the AfD will form the next government in Saxony-Anhalt it fell three seats short of a majority in the September 6, 2026, election. But many immigrants and refugees fear that if the far-right party succeeds in heading the State government, it could try to implement its campaign promises, which include more and faster deportations, as well as restrictions on the admission of asylum seekers. There are no figures yet showing whether racist incidents have increased since the election, but "counselling centres are extremely busy, the phones are ringing off the hook, counselling appointments are fully booked, and people are in great need of counselling and support," said Undra Dressler, Executive Director of the Saxony-Anhalt State Network of Migrant Organisations. "We know of people who have left, people who are considering it, and people who have made a conscious decision against it and say: 'I'm staying. I won't accept these conditions. Now more than ever, I'm going to get involved,'" Ms. Dressler said. One of those determined to stay is Mohamad Aldabagh, a pharmacist from Homs who fled to Germany in 2015, at the height of Syria's civil war, when hundreds of thousands crossed the Mediterranean on flimsy rubber boats in hopes of finding a safer future in Europe. "It's been a very good experience living in Germany over the past 10 years," said Mr. Aldabagh, 34, a father of two young children who works at a pharmacy in Magdeburg. "I've rebuilt my life here, and I won't let anyone take that away from me." While he said he had also experienced racism, he believes that skilled workers like himself, or the many foreign doctors working in Germany, are needed, and that society cannot afford to treat them badly. AfD wants no culturally foreign workers despite skilled labour shortage While the AfD's programme for Saxony-Anhalt does not reject labour migration altogether, it takes a highly selective approach to recruiting foreign workers. The party explicitly proposes refraining from recruiting workers it describes as "culturally foreign," and ending a State programme designed to support the integration of foreign skilled workers, said Rahim Hajji, a professor of social and health services at Magdeburg-Stendal University of Applied Sciences. "This raises a fundamental question," Mr. Hajji said. "How is a state with an ageing population and growing labour shortages supposed to meet its demand for skilled workers if it substantially restricts the pool of international workers it is willing to recruit?" As of August 2026, more than one in four doctors, or 27.1%, in Saxony-Anhalt's hospitals did not hold German citizenship, according to a survey by the Mediendienst Integration group, which researches migration in Germany. "We want to contribute to the well-being of society here," Mr. Aldabagh said. "We are needed. We are not the black sheep in this country." He paused, and added: "But if we don't get respect anymore, then we'll move to another state where AfD isn't as strong."

ALSO READ | Remember His Name: Israelis Hail Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar After Flydubai Attack Doctors, according to sources, are working overtime to ensure that his vision is fully restored and does not prove to be an impediment to the captains plans to fly again. His positive spirit is a huge boost. He continues to smile through the ordeal," a source said, adding that Smit in Gujarati means smile" and Captain Machchhar is living up to his name.
