headline: Naveen Patnaik's BJD joins Opposition's Election Commission protest
content: sent Manas Mangraj and Sulata Deo to join protests that have erupted in central Delhi Tuesday, led by Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who were briefly detained by police before being released. There is little love lost between the BJD and the Bharatiya Janata Party in power at the centre and in Odisha today, after the BJP thumped the BJP in the 2024 Assembly election, a loss the state party is now questioning. In the past, though, the BJD was a member of the BJP-led national alliance, i.e., from 1998-2009. Protests against CEC Kumar and the Election Commission have gathered pace since the Express report last month. An Express investigation found that Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had objected formally and on record 14 times in 10 months to the manner in which decisions were taken regarding the SIR. Among the 14 points raised were the allegedly illegal modification of Form 6 to include questions about the voters parents or grandparents and a push to centralise control of the ECINET software that manages the lists. BJD demands Gyanesh Kumars resignation On Monday BJD spokesperson Lenin Mohanty told reporters in Bhubaneswar that Gyanesh Kumar has no option but to resign (and) take moral responsibility. Mohanty insisted Kumar had to quit because he had lied about changes to Form 6 that the alterations during the SIR had been approved by the Supreme Court. The court this week said it had not approved any modifications to Form 6 and sought a response from the EC and the government. Now, Kumar has no option as Gyanesh Kumar had lied that Form 6 was approved by the Supreme Court, he has no moral right to continue but to step down, the BJD said in a statement. BJD leader Lekhashree Samantsinghar underlined that demand, declaring voters across the country, including those in Odisha, had lost trust in the EC. They (EC) must have done similar manipulation during the 2024 elections in Odisha by tampering with EVMs to make a particular party win the election, Samantsinghar alleged. INDIA bloc protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Security was stepped up across the New Delhi district, and opposition MPs were stopped on the way, after which they sat on a dharna. headline: Israel puts military on alert for October 7 anniversary, warns Gazans
content: Israel's Defence Minister on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) said he had put the military on high alert before the anniversary of Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, warning Gazans would pay a "heavy price" if forces were harmed. Also read: 10 key moments in the Israel-Hamas war The office of Defence Minister Israel Katz said the instruction came "in light of intelligence regarding Hamas's intentions to attempt to carry out attacks and terror operations against our forces in Gaza on that day". "If, heaven forbid, our forces are harmed, the ones who will pay the heavy price will be Hamas and the population of Gaza beyond all proportion," the statement added. Hamass October 7, 2023 attack was the deadliest day in Israels history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead. Also Read: Palestinian death toll in Gaza war crosses 74,000: Health Ministry In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gazas Health Ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations. Since a ceasefire was declared last October, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people in Gaza, according to the Ministry. On Monday (October 5), during a state ceremony to mark three years since the attack, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza and vowed to continue targeting anyone who was involved in the attack or who held hostages.

headline: Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
content: U.S. President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan for the 2009 shooting rampage at Fort Hood, Texas. The U.S. military has not carried out the death penalty since 1961. The Army secretary will decide a time and place for the execution, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell wrote in a post on X. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come, Mr. Parnell wrote. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist, walked into a medical building where soldiers were getting medical checkups, shouted Allahu akbar Arabic for God is great! and opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun. Thirteen people were killed and more than 30 injured. He said it was an effort to stop them from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims and made almost no effort to defend himself at trial. He told jurors that evidence would show he was the shooter and described himself as a soldier who had switched sides. Mr. Trump's approval triggers a series of procedural steps toward carrying out the execution, but Hasan could put them on hold potentially for years with a habeas corpus appeal in the civilian federal court system, according to an article published in May in the magazine Army Lawyer. Death sentences are extremely rare in the military justice system, and executions even rarer. Four men, including Hasan, are currently on the military's death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. President George W. Bush approved the execution Army Spc. Ronald Gray in 2008 but it was put on hold by a judge and he remains at Leavenworth. The last man executed in the military system was Pvt. John Bennett, hanged in 1961 for raping an 11-year-old girl. Mr. Trump approved the firing squad execution days after a failed attempt to execute Christa Pike by lethal injection pushed Tennessee's governor to halt further executions this year and order an independent review. Mr. Trump resumed the federal death penalty after an informal moratorium during previous administrations. The federal government executed 13 people between 2020 and early 2021, contributing to making Trump the most prolific execution president in over 130 years. Asked whether the botched execution in Tennessee would lead him to seek changes to capital punishment, Mr. Trump said it was an interesting situation. It shouldn't be very difficult, Mr. Trump said of carrying out lethal injections.

headline: Trump says his super PAC will pay for taxpayer-funded ads that sparked backlash for glorifying him
content: funded ads that sparked backlash for glorifying him President Donald Trump said Monday (October 5, 2026) that he will stop using taxpayer funds for television advertisements glorifying himself that sparked a major backlash, and instead tap his super PAC to cover costs going forward. In a post on his social media site, Mr. Trump defended the ads, which cost at least $1.5 million in federal funds and have drawn intense criticism. Mr. Trump said they were positive promotion for our Great USA. This is a rather standard thing to do, the president wrote, while blaming intense criticism for using taxpayer funds on the ads on the Radical Left. But the president added that he'd decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc." That is Mr. Trump's political war chest, which had amassed more than $400 million by the end of July. Mr. Trump has begun to tap it to boost Republican candidates around the country ahead of midterm elections. Mr. Trump provided no details on reimbursing taxpayers for ads that had already aired, nor on how he would go about having his political organisation pay for such future advertising. The White House which had fiercely defended using taxpayer money on spots meant to promote the President said Monday (October 5, 2026) night that MAGA Inc. will pay for such ads going forward. It did not answer questions about how it or Mr. Trump might prove that his political funds were being used on such future advertising. Mr. Trump's abrupt about-face came after leaders from both parties criticised using taxpayer funds for the ads. Legal experts said the ads might even violate federal statutes, including a law against congressionally appropriated funds being used for publicity or propaganda and one limiting the partisan political activities of government employees. The spots began airing in late September The first ad featured clips of Mr. Trump talking about defeating communism interspersed with onscreen text promoting the largest tax cuts in history, reigniting American manufacturing and a call to defend law and order and police. Later the same week, a second ad began running. It showed scenic videos of Mount Rushmore with quotes and clips from Mr. Trump's Fourth of July weekend speech there honoring the country's 250th anniversary. A third, more recent one was virtually identical to an ad for Mr. Trump's Republican reelection campaign in 2024 and showed him walking down a hallway as his voice can be heard warning of a final battle against globalists and warmongers. All ended with a message: Paid for by the U.S. Government. According to AdImpact, which tracks media spending, the spots had cost at least $1.4 million by the end of September. The actual amount spent could be far more, depending on whether networks classified the ad as a political ad.

headline: Yemen's Houthis say struck Riyadh airport, other Saudi sites
content: Houthis said on Monday (October 5, 2026) they had struck Riyadhs international airport, an oil refinery and other sites in Saudi Arabia, as the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said they had destroyed Houthi targets on the Red Sea coast. Pakistan and Turkiye have pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a new mutual defence pact following weeks of Houthi attacks, as Riyadh and its Yemeni government allies began an ambitious push aimed at retaking all territory held by the group. The fighting in Yemen has become the most active front in the West Asia war in recent weeks, displacing more than 1,84,000 people, the United Nations says, and deepening the conflict that has engulfed the wider region. The Houthis previously controlled much of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa and the western city of Hodeida, but seized swathes of coastline last month along the Red Sea and key Bab al-Mandab Strait, in Yemens deadliest fighting in years. The Houthis have also been attacking neighbouring Saudi Arabia since Yemens civil war flared back to life and have declared a maritime blockade on its ships. The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn. Turki Al-Malki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, said on X that its naval forces had hit military targets belonging to the Houthis in Hodeida on the Red Sea coast. They destroyed weapons depots, facilities storing booby-trapped boats and naval mines and had thwarted a planned attack targeting waterways in the southern Red Sea, he said. Later, the military said it had driven the Houthis from the area surrounding the Bab al-Mandeb Strait a vital route for maritime traffic including the port city of Mocha, Dhubab airport and Al-Omari military camp. They also said they expelled the Houthis from several areas in Taiz in the southwest, where deadly fighting has surged in recent days. Military sources stopped short of confirming an official announcement of Mochas recapture, saying that pro-government forces had cut off the only supply route to the port. UN deeply concerned Loud explosions rattled the Saudi capital on Monday (October 5, 2026) evening, with a Houthi spokesman saying the group had hit King Khalid International Airport, a refinery belonging to state oil giant Aramco and other targets in the kingdoms south. It came a day after Yemens government announced the lofty goal of retaking all Houthi territory home to most of the countrys population, and much of it held for more than a decade. Representatives of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye held an emergency meeting in Riyadh on Monday (September 5, 2026) under the auspices of a joint defence agreement signed in August committing them to come to each others aid in the event of any attack. They also agreed to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom. The statement did not specify what role the troops would fill once in Saudi Arabia. A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting, and condemned the continued Houthi cross-border attacks on Saudi Arabia. Houthi attacks have repeatedly targeted Saudi oil infrastructure, as well as its tankers in the Red Sea. A source in the Saudi energy sector told AFP that an attack on Sunday (October 4, 2026) had again halted pumping by the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, a key conduit for the kingdoms exports since Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the wider West Asia war. Crude prices had already been soaring as a result of the West Asia war before the Houthis began targeting the worlds largest oil exporter. Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser warned on Monday (October 5, 2026) that global oil stockpiles were scarily thin owing to the war. The system is already straining, Mr. Nasser told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London.

headline: IIT Bombay Student Death: Prof Doolla Denies Allegations Of Caste-Based Harassment, Use Of Derogatory Words
content: Based Harassment, Use Of Derogatory Words Mumbai Crime Branch has recorded around 60 statements in the Sahil Wakode case. IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayan Doolla has denied caste harassment allegations. The Mumbai Crime Branch has so far recorded statements of around 60 people in connection with the death of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, with the statement of professor Suryanarayan Doolla also recorded as part of the ongoing investigation. Doolla has denied all allegations levelled against him, according to crime branch sources. He also denied using any caste-based or derogatory words during his interaction with the student. Doollas Account Of The Examination Hall Incident According to crime branch sources, Doolla told investigators about the circumstances in which he allegedly saw Wakode copying from his mobile phone during an examination. Doolla reportedly said that when he noticed Wakode using the phone, the student attempted to hide it. Mumbai Crime Branch has recorded statements of around 60 people in the Sahil Wakode case. Doolla denied caste discrimination allegations and said he saw Wakode using a mobile phone during an exam. Investigators are examining statements, digital evidence and CCTV footage to reconstruct events surrounding Wakode's death. The professor told the crime branch that he did not say anything to Wakode and instead handed him his examination paper and asked him to leave the examination hall. The examination episode is a key part of the investigation because Wakode died later that day. According to news agency PTI, the 22-year-old second-year student was found hanging in his hostel room on the evening of September 18, hours after he was allegedly caught using his mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. Doolla also denied allegations that he discriminated against Wakode on the basis of caste. Doolla also told investigators that throughout his tenure at IIT Bombay, he had never discriminated against any student or any other person on the basis of caste. He reportedly said that he was a teacher and that his responsibility was to teach students, adding that all students were equal to him. The professor further denied the allegations made against him and maintained that he had acted in accordance with institutional guidelines, ANI reported. The allegations against Doolla had been raised by Wakodes family following the students death. Wakodes father had alleged in his complaint that his son had told him during their last meeting that Doolla had subjected him to casteist abuse over the preceding three months and had expressed fear of being implicated in a false case. Crime Branch Probes Events Before Students Death The crime branch is examining Doollas statement alongside statements recorded from students, faculty members, hostel staff and others connected with the case. PTI reported that more than 25 people had already been questioned by September 28, including IIT Bombay students, faculty members and hostel staff. Investigators are also examining what happened between the examination incident and Wakodes death. Police officials said Wakode made calls to several friends after the examination hall episode. According to PTI, Wakode spoke to a female friend and expressed regret over his performance in the mid-semester examination. Investigators said he told her that he had made a mistake during his thermodynamics paper and lamented the subsequent examination malpractice episode. Digital Evidence Under Examination The crime branch is also examining digital evidence to reconstruct the sequence of events before Wakodes death. According to PTI, Wakodes iPhone was sent to the Kalina Forensic Science Laboratory for technical analysis to retrieve digital logs and device history. Authorities indicated that they could seek assistance from Apple if forensic experts were unable to unlock the device. A formal request was also made to WhatsApp for relevant account information. CCTV footage recovered from the IIT Bombay campus is also being examined. The footage was forwarded to the Kalina laboratory for certification under the Information Technology Act so that it can be used as court evidence. The Mumbai Crime Branch recorded statements, including Professor Suryanarayana Doolla's, following the death of 22-year-old second-year student Sahil Wakode. Wakode was found hanging in his hostel room on September 18, hours after he was allegedly caught using his mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester thermodynamics examination.

headline: Who Is Nadeem Ahmed? The 24-Year-Old YouTuber At The Centre Of Delhi Police's AI Deepfake Allegations
content: Police allege Ahmed used AI tools to fabricate the objectionable material and circulate it on social media in an attempt to create tension and disturb public order. Delhi Police have arrested 24-year-old Nadeem Ahmed, accusing him of creating and circulating an AI-generated video that purportedly showed Additional DCP Vivek Bhagat sexually harassing a woman journalist. Police allege that Ahmed used artificial intelligence tools to fabricate the objectionable material and circulate it on social media in an attempt to create tension and disturb public order. Investigators are now probing whether he acted alone and whether other people were involved in the alleged conspiracy. Ahmed, who has around 24,000 followers on Instagram, describes himself as an independent journalist. According to authorities, he started his YouTube channel during the protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). His digital footprint and activities on the platform are now under scrutiny as investigators try to establish whether he acted alone or was part of a larger network. - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - ACP Bhagat Under Fire: 3 Women File Harassment Complaints, AI Video Case Deepens Row | - Delhi Police Officer Accused Of Molesting Female Journalist Promoted To Additional DCP Amid Probe - Considering The Enquiry: Delhi Cop Asks To Put Promotion On Hold After CJP Accuses Him Of Sexual Harassment The arrest comes against the backdrop of a separate controversy over allegations of sexual harassment involving Delhi Police personnel during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Three women journalists had alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering the demonstration. Their complaints are being examined by the Delhi Police Crime Branch. Police have stressed that the AI-generated material is separate from those allegations and have registered a case over the creation and circulation of the purportedly fake content. Who Is Nadeem Ahmed? According to Delhi Police, Ahmed is a 24-year-old resident of Haryana who describes himself as an independent journalist". Police said he started a YouTube channel around April this year. Investigators have also shared details about his educational background, saying Ahmed had studied at a madrasa in Saket and had failed his Class 10 examination. Police are examining his digital activities as part of the investigation into how the allegedly fabricated content was created and disseminated. The bigger question for investigators is whether the video was the work of an individual acting on his own or whether there was a wider network behind it. Police have said they are probing whether Ahmed received any funding and whether others were involved in producing or circulating the material. Delhi Police allege that Ahmed created the material using AI tools and subsequently circulated it on social media. According to police, Ahmed himself told investigators that he used an AI tool to create the disputed footage. He also allegedly admitted that his objective was to tarnish the image of the Delhi Police and create an atmosphere of unrest. Based on his statement, authorities have begun looking into his sources of funding and associates, raising the possibility that the investigation could extend beyond the 24-year-old YouTuber. The Delhi Police have separately denied allegations that women protesters were assaulted and described some of the claims as baseless and misleading". Meanwhile, the Crime Branch is examining the complaints made by the journalists. Bhagat himself has since stepped aside from an additional charge following the allegations. The Delhi government said the arrangement involving 12 officers had been initiated before the allegations emerged, but Bhagat requested not to take up the additional responsibility until an inquiry was completed. What Charges Does Ahmed Face? Police have invoked several provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against Ahmed, including Sections 353, 352 and 336, besides other provisions. Section 353 deals with statements conducing to public mischief and covers the publication or circulation of false information, rumours or reports, including through electronic means, in circumstances specified by the law. Section 352 deals with intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace. Section 336 relates to forgery. Its use in an AI-generated-content case is significant because it illustrates how existing criminal provisions can be applied to digitally fabricated material. In another recent Delhi case involving an AI-generated video targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, police had also invoked Section 336 along with provisions concerning forged electronic records, intentional insult, defamation and criminal conspiracy. The exact application of these provisions in Ahmeds case will ultimately depend on the evidence collected during the investigation and the prosecutions case. Nadeem Ahmed is a 24-year-old YouTuber and independent journalist who was arrested by the Delhi Police for allegedly creating and circulating an AI-generated deepfake video. The fabricated footage purportedly depicted Additional DCP Vivek Bhagat sexually harassing a woman journalist, which authorities state was done to create public unrest and tarnish the image of the police.

headline: U.S. moves to strip 40 persons of American citizenship
content: The U.S. launched the largest denaturalisation effort in modern history by moving to strip 40 individuals, including one of Indian origin, of their American citizenship, the Department of Justice said. The 40 individuals facing denaturalisation actions in multiple U.S. courts have been accused of serious offences, including acting as an agent for a foreign government, committing voluntary manslaughter, and aggravated sodomy against a man with special needs. Balwinder Singh, of California, is facing denaturalisation action in the States Eastern District court for using a fraudulent identity to gain admission to, and acquire, U.S. citizenship. Todays announcement marks the largest denaturalisation effort in modern history, Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Monday (October 5, 2026). Under the Immigration and Nationality Act, a naturalised U.S. citizens citizenship may be revoked and certificate of naturalisation cancelled, if it was procured illegally, or by concealment of a material fact, or by wilful misrepresentation. Every single one of these individuals lied their way into U.S. citizenship, said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate, of the Justice Departments Civil Division. This administration will continue to pursue the largest denaturalisation effort in department history to restore trust and integrity in U.S. citizenship. Our message is clear: the United States will not tolerate deception in the naturalisation process, Mr. Shumate said. According to the Department of Justice, Mr. Singh, in 1992, submitted an immigration application under the identity of Balwinder Singh. In 2003, he sought and received permanent resident status under a second identity. Fingerprints establish that Singh submitted both applications. In 2009, Singh naturalised under his second identity. The complaint alleges seven counts for his numerous misrepresentations and unlawful acts that adversely reflect his moral character, the Justice Department said. The department said it was also seeking to revoke the citizenship of Jinchao Wei, a China-born former U.S. Navy sailor convicted of espionage-related offences. According to the Justice Department, Mr. Wei enlisted in the Navy in 2021, and by February 2022 had begun conspiring to sell military secrets to China. He became a U.S. citizen in May 2022, under provisions designed to expedite naturalisation for people serving honourably in the U.S. armed forces. Mr. Wei was convicted in August 2025 of conspiracy to commit espionage, espionage, and unlawful export of technical data related to defence articles. He was sentenced to 200 months in prison and discharged from the Navy. Among those against whom denaturalisation actions have been initiated are people from Pakistan, Mexico, Cambodia, Nepal and Afghanistan.

headline: U.S. accuses California woman of spying for China, surveilling Taiwan leader's son
content: U.S. authorities arrested a California woman on Sunday (October 4, 2026) and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan's President at the behest of Chinese officials, the FBI said. The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday (October 4) before her planned departure to China, the agency said in a statement. Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent. Zhang surveiled a son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, the FBI said. The agency did not directly name Zhang's alleged target, but later shared a New York Post report identifying him as Lai Ting-yu, a U.S. resident. The Justice Department said Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and subsequently sent them photos, video and license plate information of the Taiwanese leader's son and his family. Zhang used tradecraft to avoid detection and never notified Washington that she was acting for a foreign government, Bill Essayli, the first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, said in a statement. The Chinese embassy in Washington and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It was not immediately clear whether Zhang has a defense attorney. She will appear on Monday (October 5) in a Los Angeles federal court, Essayli said. Mr. Lai and his Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan's separate identity from China, a position that frequently angers Beijing, which views the island as Chinese territory. Washington does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but the United States is the island's most important international backer and weapons supplier.

headline: Women With Guns, Highways Under Siege: BLF's New Female Strike Force Emerges In Balochistan
content: BLFs New Female Strike Force Emerges In Balochistan A BLF video shows female fighters undergoing weapons and combat training, receiving briefings from a female commander and participating in field operations. The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has released footage purportedly showing the training and field activities of its newly formed female combat unit, the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD), as the separatist group seeks to project an expanded armed presence in Pakistans restive Balochistan province. The video shows female fighters undergoing weapons and combat training, receiving briefings from a female commander and participating in field operations. The BLF has claimed that KAAD was created to formally induct women into its armed ranks, with roles extending beyond combat to intelligence, communications, medical support and logistics. The unit is named after Karima Baloch, the former chairperson of the Baloch Students Organisation-Azad. - BLA Fighters Overrun Police Station In Balochistan, 2 Security Personnel Killed: Sources - Gwadar-Bound Cargo Attacked In Balochistan, Driver May Have Been Abducted: Sources | Exclusive - Asim Munir Vows To 'Defeat' Terrorism, But Pakistan Sees 12-Year High In Militant Attacks - 'Evil America Will End': Al Qaeda Calls For Similar Attacks, Praises Flydubai Incident The footage comes after the BLF attributed a series of recent attacks on Pakistani military and security forces to KAAD. According to the group, the unit carried out its first armed operation near Turbat, where its fighters allegedly ambushed a Pakistani military convoy on the CPEC highway in the Jusak area. The BLF later claimed that nine Pakistani military personnel were killed across two operations, although the casualty figures have not been independently verified. The BLF also claimed that its female fighters conducted snap checks and search operations in the Manguchar area of Kalat, stopping vehicles and targeting military convoys travelling to reinforce security forces in the area. The group alleged that several military vehicles were damaged or disabled. Pakistani authorities did not immediately confirm the claims. Meanwhile, the latest reports from Chagai district point to renewed armed activity along the strategically important Quetta-Taftan route. Armed fighters reportedly entered Yakmach, with women among those seen in the group, and established a blockade on the Quetta-Taftan highway. Reports also said the fighters attacked and set fire to a National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) office in Yakmach. Authorities had not publicly confirmed the incident or reported casualties at the time of reporting. The highway has repeatedly emerged as a flashpoint. Security-monitoring data records earlier incidents this year involving armed groups blocking the route, conducting vehicle checks and attacking security posts and convoys in Chagai. In August, suspected Baloch insurgents also carried out attacks on commercial and security convoys around Yakmach and other parts of the Quetta-Taftan corridor. The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) established its new female combat unit named the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD), honoring Karima Baloch.

The INDIA alliance, a grouping of more than two dozen opposition parties led by the Congress, said it would begin protests on October 6 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. All opposition lawmakers plan to march to the Election Commission office in Delhi, the alliance has said. The central allegation, made by protesters and opposition parties, is that the commission manipulated voter rolls to favour the BJP. The commission and the government have denied this. What Is Cockroach Janta Party Protest About? The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) launched a nationwide campaign on Friday with a demonstration in Mumbai. The partys target is a nationwide voter-verification exercise launched last year. Critics say it has removed millions of eligible voters. The Election Commission says the exercise is meant to weed out duplicate, deceased or ineligible entries. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the protests would continue until Kumar resigns, with Goa, Kolkata and Bengaluru among the cities targeted this month. Delhi Traffic Police regulated and diverted traffic due to a planned protest march by opposition lawmakers from the INDIA alliance to the Election Commission office. Protesters were demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter roll manipulation.

headline: 'Complete Catch-22 Situation': Bombay HC Questions Voter Deletion Under SIR
content: The petitions argue that deleting voters from draft electoral rolls without individual notice violates statutory provisions as well as constitutional safeguards. The Bombay High Court on Monday flagged a complete Catch-22 situation" for voters who have changed their residences, questioning how they can update their electoral details when their applications for address modification are rejected during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. A division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar was hearing a batch of petitions challenging the Election Commission of Indias automated rejection of Form 8 applications submitted by voters in Goa seeking to change their addresses. - Why Reject Form 8?: Bombay HC Questions ECI On Voter Forms During SIR - Supreme Court To Hear Plea Raising Doubts Over ECI Decisions Under Gyanesh Kumar Next Week - Can Supreme Court Suspend Gyanesh Kumar? The Constitutional Question Behind The Unprecedented Plea - Election Commission Of India Orders Comparison Of Pre-SIR And Current Electoral Rolls The petitions argue that deleting voters from draft electoral rolls without individual notice violates statutory provisions as well as constitutional safeguards. The Bench noted that voters who have shifted residences are effectively left without a legitimate route to retain or update their registration. While Form 8 is meant for changing an address, voters whose applications are rejected are being directed towards Form 6, which is used for fresh enrolment and requires a declaration that the applicant is not already registered elsewhere. The Form 6, it is a false declaration. He gives you Form 8; you say I cannot touch your Form 8; you must give the enumeration. He says, I do not want to give the enumeration, I am giving you Form 8. But section 21 says you have to hear him before removing his name, not from the draft, from the original roll," the Court said. The Bench also questioned whether the SIR exercise was intended to determine the presence of voters on electoral rolls or to establish their citizenship. The entire SIR procedure was on the basis that it had to find out whether an elector is actually an Indian citizen or not. The basis of the SIR was not to see whether the voter is there or not. It is to find out whether he is an Indian citizen or not," the court said. Advocate Gauresh Agni, appearing for the ECI, submitted that the exercise was also aimed at identifying illegal immigrants. There were illegal immigrants also," he said. The Bench questioned whether directing voters to submit Form 6 or Form 8 would actually address that objective, while referring to the Supreme Courts judgment on the Bihar SIR. So, will this subserve the purpose by a Form 6 or a Form 8? Judgment [of the Supreme Court on Bihar SIR nowhere says that the manner of doing this is going to be by Form 6. Law is either by the legislature or, if it is delegated, or a rule-making power," the court stated. The Court also raised concerns over the constitutional implications of the exercise, particularly if eligible citizens end up being excluded from the electoral rolls. If, by this process, citizens are excluded, then how do we read this mandate?" it added. The Bench stressed that the ECIs constitutional responsibility includes ensuring that eligible citizens are not deprived of their right to vote. ECI Defends Deletion From Draft Rolls The ECI, meanwhile, argued that an intensive revision under Section 25(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, involves preparing electoral rolls afresh. According to the poll body, voters who do not receive or submit enumeration forms would consequently not figure in the draft rolls. Whoever is not given the enumeration form, the name has to go off the draft roll, and if you are not in the draft roll, there is no entry which can be transferred to another place," Agni argued. On the question of individual notice, the ECI said notices had also been displayed publicly because authorities may not have updated information about voters who had moved. There is a notice put up even on the notice board because the voters fresh details may not be available with us before removal. There were instances where people had shifted; there were no details of where they had shifted available," Agni clarified. The Bench, however, questioned the ECIs reliance on the draft roll at this stage of the exercise. Draft roll will not come into picture until the SIR is complete. Here the SIR is not complete. You are in the process." The case comes days after the same Bench, on October 1, raised concerns over the ECIs automated software-based rejection of Form 8 applications submitted by voters seeking to update their addresses. The Court had questioned whether automatically rejecting such applications could undermine the larger objective of maintaining an inclusive and accurate electoral roll. The Bombay High Court pointed out that voters who changed residences face a Catch-22 when their Form 8 address modification applications are rejected and they are redirected to Form 6, which requires a false declaration that they are not registered elsewhere, while draft rolls omit them without proper prior hearings.

headline: Delhi Police Steps Up Security Ahead Of Oppn Protests: Over 3,000 Cops Deployed, Barricades Placed
content: Security has been intensified at several key locations, including the Parliament of India, the Parliament Street roundabout and the gates of the Election Commission. The Delhi Police has stepped up security across the New Delhi district ahead of the proposed Opposition protests, with more than 3,000 personnel being deployed to maintain law and order. The protests are being held in Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. As part of the security arrangements, 27 companies of male personnel and four companies of female personnel have been deployed in the district. A police company typically comprises around 100 to 115 personnel. - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - 'Lathi Can Stop Crowd, But Not A Question': Rahul Gandhi Slams Centre Amid Protests Against CEC - Abusing His Position: Rahul Gandhi Targets Gyanesh Kumar After SC Denies Approving Modified Form 6 - From Streets To Supreme Court: CEC Gyanesh Kumar Faces The Heat | Brass Tacks With Nabila Jamal Security has been intensified at several key locations, including the Parliament of India, the Parliament Street roundabout and the gates of the Election Commission. Additional personnel have also been positioned at various Metro station gates in the area. The heightened security comes against the backdrop of a series of protests in the national capital in recent days, including demonstrations by political parties, student organisations and civil society groups. Also Read: Journalist Who Alleged Sexual Assault By Delhi Police Official Detained With 16 Others Over FIR Demand FIR Registered Amid Anti-CEC Protests Delhi Police had on Monday registered FIRs following protests by student groups, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to reach Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. headline: Both Engines Of Flydubai Plane Had Failed During Steep Dive, Had To Be Restarted, Says Ex-US Pilot
content: Captain Steve Scheibner said both engines of the flydubai Boeing 737 MAX 8 appeared not to be operating during its steep 16,000-foot dive. Retired US Navy and American Airlines pilot Steve Scheibner, commenting on the flydubai flight incident, said it appeared that both engines of the Boeing 737 MAX 8 were not operating while the aircraft was in the midst of its steep dive. Scheibner linked the assessment to the activation of the aircrafts emergency evacuation lights, saying there was only one way those lights could illuminate in flight. - Flydubai Pilot Under Probe, Hijack, Crash Or '9/11-Style Attack' Suspected, Say Israeli Officials - Flydubai Co-Pilot Studied in Australia Between 2015-2017: Probe Launched Into Omani Pilots Links - Why Did Flydubai Flight FZ1073 Have Two Extra Pilots On Board During Cockpit Attack? - Flydubai Attack: What Happens If A Pilot Cuts Fuel To Both Engines Mid-Flight? It seems as though both engines were not operating while they were in the midst of this dive," Scheibner said. According to Scheibner, the apparent engine failure added another major challenge to an already chaotic situation inside the cockpit. He said the off-duty pilots who eventually helped regain control of the aircraft not only had to arrest the dive but also had to deal with the possibility that both engines had stopped operating. Not only was it a miracle that the off-duty pilots who got into the cockpit saved the plane from the dive, but they also had the further issue of having to relight the engines while they were in the midst of that melee," he said. Flydubai Flight Plunged 16,000-Foot In About 30 Seconds Both engines may have stopped operating during the flydubai flights steep dive, Captain Steve Scheibner said. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds, before passengers overpowered the co-pilot. Scheibner hailed Captain Smit Machchhar and the passengers as heroes. Reuters reported that flydubai flight FZ1073 plunged around 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) in approximately 30 seconds before it was levelled out and eventually landed safely. Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in southern England, recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters and described what passengers would have experienced as similar to a very, very vertical roller coaster." Paduanelli said the sudden descent would have subjected passengers and crew, as well as the Boeing 737 MAX 8, to substantial forces. For passengers who were not strapped in, he said their bodies would literally lift from their seats because of the negative G-force. His simulation indicated that the aircrafts autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, allowing the jet to accelerate rapidly. The aircraft was ultimately levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, while a reserve crew member took control and landed the plane. Meanwhile, Reuters quoted some Israeli officials as saying that the co-pilot had told UAE interrogators that he had planned the attack before being hired by flydubai. Flydubai Captain Attacked Inside Cockpit Scheibner also described the extraordinary actions of Captain Smit Machchhar, who was attacked inside the cockpit. He called the Indian pilot an absolute hero" and said Machchhar managed to reach back and open the cockpit door while fighting for his life. Scheibner explained that the 737 cockpit door opens inward. Once it opened enough for a woman and her daughter near the front toilet to see what was happening, the woman raised the alarm. Her husband rushed to help, followed by other passengers who moved towards the cockpit. He said the passengers response reflected how aviation security and passenger behaviour changed after the September 11, 2001 attacks. Rather than remaining passive and waiting for authorities to intervene, passengers moved to take control of the situation themselves. They worked through that rather quickly," Scheibner said, describing how passengers pulled the captain out and began getting him medical attention while simultaneously fighting with the co-pilot as the aircraft remained in a steep dive. The aircraft was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew, most of them Israeli. After passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, a reserve flydubai pilot travelling onboard took control of the aircraft and landed it at a regional airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia. The co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, was detained and later transferred to UAE custody. The incident remains under investigation, with Reuters reporting that authorities in Australia and New Zealand have also examined the co-pilots links to those countries. New Zealand police said he had been in the country from November 2018 to May 2019 to complete part of his flight training for a UK-based company. According to retired pilot Steve Scheibner, it appeared that both engines of the Boeing 737 MAX 8 failed and stopped operating during the steep dive, requiring the off-duty pilots to relight them.

headline: 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised
content: Khawaja Asif said an urgent meeting was held primarily to settle its organisational framework and not specifically to coordinate battlefield operations against the Houthis The organisational structure of the Mecca Pact has been formally finalised, with the appointment of its secretary-general ratified, Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said, as Saudi Arabia continues direct military operations against Yemens Houthi rebels. Asif said an urgent meeting related to the pact was held primarily to settle its organisational framework and not specifically to coordinate battlefield operations against the Houthis. The structure of Mecca Pact has been formalised, the Secretary-General appointed for Makkah Pact has been ratified, and all related matters have been fully ratified," Asif said. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive - From 'We Wont Fight' To Troops For Saudi Arabia: Pakistans Yemen U-Turn And The Mecca Pact Mecca Pact Kicks In: Pakistan, Turkey To Send Forces To Saudi Arabia As Houthi Attacks Mount His comments come amid heightened military activity involving Saudi forces in Yemen. According to the Pakistani defence minister, Saudi Arabia is directly engaged in combat with the Houthis, while Pakistan and Turkey are providing support to Riyadh under the broader security arrangement. As for the Houthi situation, Saudi Arabia has engaged in combat against the Houthis," Asif said. He said the Houthis had adopted a defensive posture while also making territorial gains in parts of Yemen over the past month. The Yemeni government, he added, now wants to regain those areas. The Houthis have adopted a defensive stance, and over the past month, they captured certain areas in Yemen which the government now wants to recapture," Asif said. Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role The organizational structure of the Mecca Pact has been formally finalized. The Secretary-General appointed for the Makkah Pact has been ratified. Saudi Arabia is directly engaged in combat with Houthi rebels in Yemen. Pakistan and Turkey are providing support to Riyadh under the broader security arrangement. The armed forces of Pakistan and Turkey are playing a supportive role, not directly conducting combat operations. Asif stressed that Pakistan and Turkey have a presence in Saudi Arabia but are not leading the ongoing combat operations against the Houthis. Pakistan and Turkey both countries have their presence there. However, Saudi Arabia is fighting its own battles against the Houthis where combat is active, while we are present and providing whatever type of assistance and support is needed," he said. The minister also sought to distinguish between the military engagement and the institutional work being undertaken through the Makkah Pact. The meetings were not held for this specific combat purpose; rather, it was our organizational structure that was formalised today," Asif said. The pact, involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, is being positioned as a framework for closer security and defence cooperation among the three countries. Its formalisation comes at a sensitive time for the region, with instability in Yemen continuing to have wider implications for Gulf security. Asif said the armed forces of Pakistan and Turkey are currently playing a supporting role rather than directly conducting combat operations. We are currently at a position where the armed forces of Turkey and Pakistan are playing a supportive role," he said. He added that the scope of the engagement extends beyond military assistance and includes reconstruction. Definitely, reconstruction and all those things are areas where we are involved, but combat is practically being carried out by Saudi Arabias own forces, and they are the ones reclaiming those areas," Asif said. The clarification is significant as it indicates that, despite the formalisation of the pact and the presence of Pakistani and Turkish personnel in Saudi Arabia, Riyadhs forces remain at the forefront of the current fighting against the Houthis. The organisational structure of the Mecca Pact has been formally finalised, and the appointment of its secretary-general has been fully ratified.
