headline: From 100 To 14,000: AIIMS Obesity Clinic Charts India's Rising Burden, States Begin To Follow
content: 100 patients in its first year to 2,300 so far this year, the clinic shows the scale of need, as Gujarat and Telangana follow suit As obesity climbs the public health agenda and state governments begin opening dedicated clinics in public hospitals, the oldest among them is already seeing patients in thousands. Every Wednesday, the obesity clinic at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi sees 50 to 60 people, many from weaker economic backgrounds. They come, says Dr Naval K Vikram of AIIMS, not for cosmetic reasons but after facing physical problems". - Captain Smit Machchhar Suffers Depressed Skull Fracture: How Serious Is The Head Injury? - 'Deeply Worrying': World Medical Body Flags Attacks On Doctors In Bangladesh, Writes To Tarique Govt - Tax Junk Food, Make Healthy Food Affordable, Train ASHAs: Experts Outline Plan To Fight Obesity - H1N1 Cases Rising: Infection Is Gone, But You Are Still Unwell? Understanding Long Flu Symptoms Since it opened in October 2017, the clinic has registered 14,000 patients. It saw about 100 in its first year, and 2,300 have come this year alone, till September. Since we opened, we have seen a constant increase in patients because the prevalence of obesity keeps rising," Dr Vikram, who conceived the clinic, told . More recently, falling prices of generic semaglutide have made more patients willing to buy a class of drugs that was long too expensive for most of them, and the clinic has now been prescribing more of it. AIIMS Obesity Clinic" opened on October 11, 2017, the day then observed as World Obesity Day, which is now marked on March 4. It joined a line-up of specialised clinics at AIIMS, among them the chest clinic, the institutes oldest, and others for sleep disorders and infectious diseases." A Clinic Built Around The Whole Patient The obesity clinic is a multicomponent one. A nutritionist prepares a personalised diet plan for each patient, and the team also includes a physiotherapist, a psychiatrist, a bariatric surgeon and metabolic physicians." Over time, it has added state-of-the-art equipment, including a body composition analysis machine, a FibroScan, which shows how obesity affects the liver, and a handgrip strength machine. When patients need cardiac, orthopaedic or other evaluations, they are referred to other doctors at AIIMS." The OPD runs once a week on Wednesdays. It sees an average of 50 to 60 patients every week, about 20 of them new registrations." Cheaper GLP-1 Drugs Change The Equation The biggest recent change has been cost. GLP-1 drugs, the newer class of obesity medicines, were long out of reach for most of the clinics patients, who could not afford the expensive injections. With generic semaglutide now on the market, prices have fallen, and more patients are willing to buy it. Prescriptions of GLP-1 analogues at the clinic have gone up over the past few months," Dr Vikram said. Patients still have to pay for these medicines themselves. They are free only for limited beneficiaries, such as those under the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) panel." Other States Follow AIIMS is no longer the only public institution taking this approach. In March 2025, Gujarat began opening free obesity treatment clinics in civil hospitals in three cities, offering diet plans, exercise guidance and complete health support. In May this year, the Department of Endocrinology at the Nizams Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Hyderabad, inaugurated a dedicated Comprehensive Obesity Clinic. It aims to provide scientific, evidence-based and multidisciplinary care for people living with obesity and related metabolic disorders, and runs from Monday to Saturday. Public Health System Needs Training" Public health experts say the AIIMS model is what the country needs more of, and that the bigger gap is people. Similar to AIIMS, India needs more such obesity clinics offering prevention and management of obesity. For this, we need health workforce training, which is one of the main gaps today," said Prof Monika Arora, vice president, (Research and Health promotion) at the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI). India has run maternal and child health programmes and programmes on communicable diseases for decades, she noted, so the workforce on the ground is trained for addressing those challenges. Till now we talked about undernutrition, but the nutrition landscape is changing, and the time has come to give obesity the attention it deserves as a risk factor, a chronic disease and major public health challenge. With Poshan 2.0 increasingly recognising obesity, we must also strengthen the capacity of our health system to respond. This means training medical officers, NCD clinic teams and counsellors to prevent, identify and manage overweight and obesity effectively. Equally important is empowering our frontline health workers with the knowledge and skills to recognise obesity early, counsel families and communities, and support healthier behaviours." Another public health expert, Dr Arun Gupta, said the rise in the need for treatment of obesity is a worrying trend as AIIMS clinic data shows. It would be terribly expensive if we rely and continue to treat obesity and fail to prevent it. There are many steps India needs to take to prevent obesity right from birth onwards including to protect and promote breastfeeding, after six months to avoid commercial ultra-processed foods in the diet of children. One significant step would be to regulate marketing of ultra-processed food products high in sugar, salt and fats." Since it opened in October 2017, the obesity clinic at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi has registered 14,000 patients.

headline: Election Commission Rebuts Rahul Gandhi's 'Misleading' Form 6 Claims, Issues Fact Check
content: The exchange between Gandhi and the EC comes amid a broader political confrontation over electoral rolls and the SIR exercise The Election Commission of India has pushed back against allegations made by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the use of Form 6 in the voter enrolment process, seeking to clarify what the form is meant for and how applications are processed. Gandhi has repeatedly raised questions over the addition of voters and alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, particularly in the context of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. His latest claims have brought Form 6, the application used by eligible citizens to seek inclusion of their names in the electoral roll, into focus. - Delhi Police Books Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi For Entering Akashvani Bhavan Without Permission - Form 6 Row: Rahul Gandhi Says Gyanesh Kumar Will Be Held Accountable | - Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra Detained At Jantar Mantar: What Happens When An MP Is Taken Into Preventive Custody? - Bhatta Parsaul To Akashvani: Rahul Gandhis Most Dramatic Protests And Run-Ins With Police The EC, however, has disputed the interpretation of the process and sought to set the record straight on several points raised by the Congress leader. What Is Rahul Gandhis Form 6 Allegation? Gandhi has questioned how Form 6 applications could be used to add voters to electoral rolls and has alleged that the process could facilitate the inclusion of ineligible voters. ALSO READ | Lets Be Very Clear: Supreme Court Says It Didnt Approve Modified Form 6, Asks Who Made Changes The Congress has argued that the scale of voter additions and the manner in which applications are processed warrant greater scrutiny, particularly in states where the party has flagged discrepancies in electoral rolls. What Does Form 6 Actually Do? Form 6 is the prescribed application for a person seeking inclusion of their name in the electoral roll. It can be submitted by eligible citizens who are not already registered as voters. But filing the form is not, by itself, the final step in enrolment. An application goes through the prescribed verification process before an electoral registration officer takes a decision on whether the applicant meets the eligibility requirements. What Is The ECs Response? The EC called Rahul Gandhis claim misleading" and gave two points: The Bihar SIR order was not a unilateral decision by Gyanesh Kumar: The commission said the June 24, 2025, order launching the Bihar SIR was issued with the unanimous approval of the commission" and was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in its May 27, 2026, judgment. Fact CheckThe statement made in this post is misleading 1) The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026 2) In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court." Election Commission of India (@ECISVEEP) October 5, 2026 The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court, according to the EC: The commission referred to its September 26, 2026, Press Note No. 120, specifically Point 1(iii), which said: The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court." However, the EC did not directly say Gyanesh Kumar did not change Form 6" or explain who actually introduced the modified online Form 6. That remains the issue the Supreme Court has now asked the commission to clarify. The Supreme Court was explicit on Monday as it said: Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Lets be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified it." Why Does Form 6 Matter In The SIR Debate? Form 6 has assumed greater significance amid the ongoing debate over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. ALSO READ | Why Has No Chief Election Commissioner Ever Been Impeached In India & What Does It Actually Take To Remove CEC? During the revision exercise, the commission has been focusing not only on identifying voters who may need to be removed from rolls but also on ensuring that eligible citizens who were left out can get themselves enrolled. This is where Form 6 becomes important. People who are eligible to vote but whose names are missing from the electoral roll can use the form to seek inclusion. The political disagreement, therefore, is not simply over the form itself but over how applications are scrutinised and whether the safeguards are sufficient to prevent wrongful additions. The exchange between Gandhi and the EC comes amid a broader political confrontation over electoral rolls and the SIR exercise. While the Congress has alleged that the revision process could result in legitimate voters being excluded and has questioned the addition of voters, the Election Commission has maintained that the exercise is intended to clean up electoral rolls while ensuring that every eligible voter gets an opportunity to be registered. Form 6 is the prescribed application form that eligible citizens who are not already registered can file to seek the inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. However, simply filing the form is not the final step, as every application must go through a mandatory verification process before an electoral registration officer makes a final decision.

headline: Jeffrey Archer's Life Was Stranger Than Fiction: Bankruptcy, Prison And 300 Million Books
content: Archer died suddenly and peacefully at his home on October 5, 2026, aged 86, just a day before the global release of his final novel - Adam & Eve. Jeffrey Archer spent five decades writing about ambition, betrayal, wealth, power and people who refused to stay down. In the end, his own life contained enough twists to fill one of his bestselling novels. The British novelist and former Conservative politician died suddenly and peacefully" at his home on October 5, 2026, aged 86, according to his publisher HarperCollins. His death came just a day before the global release of Adam & Eve, the 31st and final novel of a career that saw him sell more than 300 million books worldwide. - Jeffrey Archer, Bestselling British Novelist And Former Politician, Dies At 86 - Inside Jeffrey Archers Final Novel Adam & Eve: A Love Story With A Twist Of History - He Wrote About Abba In A Quiver Full Of Arrows: Soha Ali Khan Remembers Jeffrey Archer - Jeffrey Archer Spent 2 Years In Prison, These Are 4 Lessons He Learnt As A Jailbird It was an almost perfectly Archer-like ending: a celebrated storyteller finishing his final story just as another chapter of his life closed. But Archers career was not built simply on literary success. It was shaped by financial disaster, political ambition, public scandal, imprisonment and, most remarkably, repeated reinvention. Political Ambition To Financial Ruin Archers ambitions began early. He once recalled that at three he wanted to be four, and at four he wanted to become prime minister. He eventually entered British politics, becoming a Conservative MP for Louth at the age of 29. He spent five years in Parliament and later became deputy chairman of the Conservative Party under Margaret Thatcher. Then came a financial crisis that would dramatically alter the course of his life. Archer had invested heavily in a Canadian company, Aquablast, which later collapsed. According to his official biography, the failure left him with debts of 427,727. Facing bankruptcy, he resigned from Parliament and turned to writing as a way of repaying his creditors. Jeffrey Archer died on October 5, 2026, at the age of 86. His final novel, Adam & Eve, was released a day after his death. Archer sold over 300 million books worldwide during his career. He was convicted of perjury in 2001 and sentenced to four years in prison. His breakthrough novel, Kane and Abel, sold over 34 million copies across 119 countries and 47 languages. That decision produced his first novel, Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less, published in 1976. The premise itself sounded remarkably close to the circumstances surrounding him. It spoke about how four men are cheated out of their money and devise an elaborate plan to recover it. Archer had found his escape route through fiction. Then Came Kane and Abel His breakthrough came with Kane and Abel, published in 1979. The novel followed two men born into dramatically different circumstances one the son of a wealthy American banking family, the other born into poverty in Poland whose lives become intertwined through rivalry, ambition and power. The story became an international phenomenon. According to Archers publishers, it eventually sold more than 34 million copies across 119 countries and 47 languages. It also revealed the formula that would define Archers career. There were characters driven by enormous ambition, dramatic reversals of fortune and the promise that a persons starting point need not determine where they end up. The irony was that Archer knew something about all three. The Scandal That Changed Everything For all his success as a novelist, Archer could never completely escape politics. In 1992, he was made a life peer and entered the House of Lords. But his political ambitions eventually collided with one of the biggest scandals of his life. The roots went back to 1987, when Archer sued the Daily Star for libel after the newspaper alleged that he had paid a sex worker. He won the case and was awarded 500,000. Years later, however, evidence emerged suggesting that Archer had fabricated the alibi he had used in that trial. In 2001, an Old Bailey jury convicted him of perjury and perverting the course of justice. He was sentenced to four years in prison. The judge described the offence as an exceptionally serious case of perjury. The fall was spectacular. Archer, who had once appeared to be on the path towards the highest levels of British politics, was now a convicted prisoner. Yet even prison became material for his writing. Archer spent more than two years behind bars before being released early in 2003. Rather than allowing the experience to end his public life, he turned it into another literary project. His three-volume A Prison Diary Hell, Purgatory and Heaven documented his experiences in Britains prison system, including his time at high-security Belmarsh and the open prison North Sea Camp. In a final interview shortly before his death, Archer reflected on what prison had taught him, saying he had learnt a lot" and that we all make mistakes". His prison experience did not erase his political career entirely. He eventually returned to the House of Lords as a non-affiliated peer and remained there until retiring in 2024. A Life Stranger Than Fiction So many chapters of Archers life seemed to echo the subjects he repeatedly explored in his books. His characters chased money, status and power. They suffered reversals, fought their way back and often found themselves trapped by decisions they thought they could control. Archer lived through versions of many of those experiences himself. Even his final novel carried themes that had long fascinated him: class, social expectations, love, war and inequality. Adam & Eve begins with two children born on the same day in 1918 a shepherds son and an earls daughter whose lives become intertwined. Archer called it the most satisfying thing I have ever written." In January, when announcing that it would be his final novel, Archer explained that he realised while writing it that, at 85, he could not hope to surpass it. And so, after more than 300 million books sold, decades on bestseller lists, a political career that rose and crashed, a prison sentence and one of the most remarkable literary comebacks in modern British publishing, Archers final story arrived almost simultaneously with his death the most Jeffrey Archer ending of all. Jeffrey Archer passed away suddenly and peacefully at his home on October 5, 2026, at the age of 86.

headline: Tribunal Judges Flag EC Portal Glitches, Say Deleted Voters Unable To Get Notices, Hearings
content: The portal does not allow tribunals to upload additional documents sought from appellants, conduct virtual hearings or restore a voters name after an appeal has been decided. More concerns have emerged over the Election Commissions digital infrastructure for handling appeals by voters affected by the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal, with judges of more than a dozen appellate tribunals flagging several gaps in the system. - 13.39 Crore Voters Deleted Through SIR: EC Responds To Oppns Claim, Says Those Eligible Can Get Name Added - 'No Meeting Sought Till 4 PM': ECI Flags 'Unusual' Request By Rahul Gandhi-Led Delegation - EC Teams To Visit 5 Poll-Bound States From This Week, UP Schedule Yet To Be Finalised - Why Reject Form 8?: Bombay HC Questions ECI On Voter Forms During SIR The judges said the EC portal does not provide a mechanism to directly serve notices to parties. There is no mechanism till date in spite of several requests and reminders," the minutes reportedly said. A notice format approved by some tribunals in May had also not been implemented. The portal also does not allow tribunals to upload additional documents sought from appellants, conduct virtual hearings or restore a voters name after an appeal has been decided. Nor can appellants download certified copies of tribunal orders to understand why their names were deleted or included. Another major concern relates to appeals submitted physically to district authorities. The judges said there was no proper mechanism to digitise and track such cases, warning that injustice will be done to such citizens" if these appeals do not reach the appropriate channel. The tribunal process was created to provide a legal remedy to the 27.16 lakh electors whose names were ultimately deleted after judicial officers examined 60.06 lakh voters flagged by the EC for logical discrepancies" or as unmapped". The Supreme Court had ordered the appointment of judicial officers in February and later directed the creation of appellate tribunals comprising retired High Court judges. Nineteen single-member tribunals were notified on March 20. Two judges have since resigned and were replaced. The Bengal SIR process remains far from fully settled even after the Assembly elections. As of September 10, the ECI told the Supreme Court that 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed, but only 1.26 lakh had been disposed of. Of these, 22.21 lakh appeals were filed by deleted voters seeking inclusion, while 16.10 lakh challenged inclusions. Appellate tribunal judges flagged that the Election Commission portal lacks mechanisms to directly serve notices, upload additional documents, conduct virtual hearings, or restore voter names after an appeal is decided. Appellants also cannot download certified copies of tribunal orders.

headline: Rs 50,000 Cr Assets? BRS Seeks ED Probe Into Revanth Reddy's Family Businesses, Congress Rubbishes Charge
content: Krishank alleged that CM Reddy was using his office to promote business interests connected to his family while avoiding questions about their assets and business activities. Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) former Corporation Chairman Manne Krishank has sought a comprehensive Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation into the alleged business interests, assets and financial transactions of Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and his family members, evoking a sharp reaction from the Congress which dismissed the allegations. Speaking at a press conference at Telangana Bhavan, Krishank alleged that the Chief Minister was using his office to promote business interests connected to his family while avoiding questions about their expanding assets and business activities. - 'If We've To Bend A Little, We Will': Congress Says It's 'As Flexible As Constitution On Seat Sharing With SP - Even 50 Would Be A Big Deal: Samajwadi MP Snubs Congress 150-Seat Demand For UP Polls - Kharge Calls CEC Gyanesh Kumar Govt's 'Puppet' At CWC Meet, Lists 5 Demands On Voter Rolls - INDIA Bloc Meet Today: As AAP, DMK Skip And Akhilesh Stays Away, Oppn Faces A Bigger Problem Than BJP BRS raises questions over Medicover, Maxbien Krishank questioned Revanth Reddys repeated participation in the inauguration of private healthcare establishments, alleging that government hospitals and public healthcare infrastructure were being neglected. He alleged links between Maxbien Pharma, Medicover Hospitals and people connected to the Chief Ministers family. He demanded an independent investigation into the ownership structures, shareholdings, investments and financial transactions of the companies. Krishank also questioned the alleged increase in the financial potential of Sahrudaya Healthcare and raised questions about the business interests and shareholding patterns involving companies associated with the Chief Ministers family. These are not questions being raised in the air. We are placing documents, company records and financial details before the public and the investigating agencies," Krishank said. Rs. 13,000 crore allegation Krishank alleged that Rs. 13,000 crore of alleged black money had been converted into legitimate funds through Medicover-related transactions. He demanded a detailed ED investigation into the claim. He said investigating agencies should examine the source of funds, beneficial ownership, shareholding patterns, related-party transactions and the movement of money across the companies concerned. Krishank also raised questions about Geetha Automotive, alleging that five Hyundai showrooms were established in Hyderabad after Revanth Reddy met senior Hyundai representatives in South Korea. He questioned the companys ownership and investment structure and alleged that Dumpa Sirisha, whom he described as an investor, had interests across multiple companies. Who are the real investors? Who are the beneficial owners? What is the source of the investment? These questions can be answered only through an independent financial investigation," Krishank said. Private businesses expanding while public institutions ignored Krishank alleged that the Chief Minister was promoting private businesses associated with members of his family while not giving adequate attention to government hospitals and schools. Government hospitals and schools are not being built at the required pace, but private hospitals and educational institutions associated with the Chief Ministers family are expanding," he alleged. He further alleged that Revanth Reddy was actively promoting companies and businesses linked to his family members. Krishank challenged the Chief Ministers family members to participate in a public discussion on the allegations. If the members of Revanth Reddys family come for a discussion and prove that my allegations are wrong, I will withdraw them, apologise and never speak about the Chief Ministers family again," he said. Rs. 50,000 crore assets claim Krishank further alleged that the Revanth Reddy family had accumulated assets and business interests worth more than Rs. 50,000 crore over the last two years. He demanded that complete details of their assets, investments, companies and business transactions be made public. He also asked whether Revanth Reddy and his family were ready to face an independent investigation into their businesses, assets, investments and financial transactions. Krishank said the BRS would submit details and documents relating to the alleged business interests of the Chief Ministers family to the President of India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and leaders of all political parties in Telangana. Congress Denies Allegations Telangana government whip Ramachandra Naik rubbished the allegations made by the BRS, with Congress saying Revanth Reddys family has no business connection with Medicover Hospital. Naik said Medicover existed before the Congress government came to power and later sold a stake to a foreign entity as part of its expansion plans. Congress rejected the allegations against Reddys family as politically motivated, arguing that BRS is raising the issue to divert attention from questions surrounding the assets and business interests of the KCR family. Naik also challenged KCR, KTR and other members of the Kalvakuntla family to agree to a comprehensive inquiry into their assets. BRS demands ED probe Krishank demanded a comprehensive and independent investigation by the Central Government and the ED into the alleged business dealings, assets, investments, shareholding patterns and financial transactions involving Revanth Reddy and his family members. The law must be the same for everyone. If the BJP-led Central Government is serious about tackling corruption and black money, it must order an impartial ED investigation into these allegations," Krishank said. He also said that he had already been arrested twice and that his residence had previously been subjected to police action. I have already been sent to jail twice. My house doors have been broken open. What more can they do? I will continue to question those in power and demand accountability," Krishank said. BRS former Corporation Chairman Manne Krishank alleged that Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and his family members accumulated assets and business interests worth over Rs. 50,000 crore, raising questions about companies like Maxbien Pharma, Medicover Hospitals, and Geetha Automotive. He demanded an independent Enforcement Directorate investigation into these financial transactions and ownership structures.

headline: Separatists win Quebec election in test for Canada PM
content: Separatists won provincial elections in Quebec on Monday (October 5, 2026), with a promise to hold a vote on leaving Canada after U.S. President Donald Trump leaves office, testing Prime Minister Mark Carney's message of national unity. But the Parti Quebecois fell short of a majority government in Canada's French-speaking province, offering some solace for the federalist camp. The PQ win still upends Canada's political landscape as the country confronts a trade war and annexation threats levelled by the United States. It also comes just two weeks before Canada's oil-producing province of Alberta, an economic powerhouse, holds a separate vote on whether it wants to begin the process of leaving Canada. The results make PQ leader Paul Saint-Pierre Plamondon, a 49-year-old lawyer known by his initials as PSPP, Quebec's next premier. At a jubilant victory party in Montreal, his supporters chanted a famous separatist slogan declaring that "Quebec is a country". The partial results indicated that the separatists won only about 30% of the vote, but vote-splitting among the federalist parties tipped the result in the PQ's favour. "We have the right in a democracy to pose the question (to leave Canada)," 26-year-old oil worker Felix Marineau said. "Being against an independence referendum is being against democracy." Independence after Trump? PM Carney congratulated PSPP, saying that "building a stronger Quebec is core to our mission of building a stronger Canada." The Prime Minister is popular in Quebec, and the separatist win was not seen as a repudiation of his stance toward Mr. Trump, whose trade war and annexation threats have infuriated Canadians. Instead, the PQ's rise after more than a decade in opposition has been tied to frustration over affordability and an enduring desire to protect the French language in an increasingly anglophone country. Surveys suggest that only about 30% of Quebecers want independence, but PSPP has maintained he will call a referendum on leaving Canada, just not while Trump is in office. He has said a decision on Quebec's independence "requires conditions that allow for an informed and calm debate." That shouldn't be "hijacked by the theatrics of an unpredictable president," he added, ruling out a referendum until at least 2029. Quebec has held two previous votes on leaving Canada. Federalists won comfortably in 1980, but the 1995 result was excruciatingly close, with just 50.58 percent voting to stay in Canada. First-time voter Alexia Gomez, 19, invoked tensions with the United States when she told AFP she opposed an independence referendum. "If Quebec becomes independent it would make us politically, economically and militarily vulnerable," she said. Lydie Periard, a 22-year-old student, said she was "very worried" by the PQ's victory, condemning what she termed the party's "populist" stance on immigration. The PQ has backed immigration cuts, particularly for non-French speakers. 'Abolish the monarchy?' PSPP may not have majority backing for an independent Quebec, but his plans to target the British monarchy appear far more popular. Canada is part of the British Commonwealth. King Charles III, Canada's head of state, is represented in Ottawa by the governor general. Lieutenant governors represent the monarchy in the provinces, including Quebec. In a 2025 Leger poll, 87% of Quebecers said they felt no attachment to the British monarchy, and only 31% expressed a favorable view of King Charles. PSPP has said his government could cut off funds for the lieutenant governor, calling it a "masquerade that wastes money."

headline: 'No Contacts Showing Symptoms': WHO Probes Suspected Plague In Russia After Lab Worker Dies
content: WHO is seeking details from Russia on the circumstances of the death, laboratory tests and their results, contact tracing and the health status of those identified as contacts. The World Health Organization (WHO) is in contact with Russian health authorities after a laboratory worker in the Irkutsk region died of severe pneumonia, amid reports that the death could be linked to suspected pneumonic plague. The WHO spokesperson told in an email that the worker died on October 2 and that the cause of death has not been officially confirmed. Also, laboratory testing is reportedly underway. - Kenyas First Ebola Case Ends In Death: From Fever To Vomiting, Know The Symptoms Of The Virus - WHO Says Siberia Plague Risk Is Low As Dozens Quarantined After Suspected Lab Worker Death - Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before? - US Embassy Issues Health Alert, Warns Americans To 'Have A Plan To Depart' Amid Plague Scare In Russia All of the patients contacts have reportedly been identified and are being monitored for illness," the WHO spokesperson said, adding that none of the contacts had shown symptoms so far. The United Nations Health arm, WHO, is seeking details from Russian authorities on the circumstances of the death, laboratory tests and their results, contact tracing and the health status of those identified as contacts. It is also assessing whether there could be any international public health implications. In accordance with Articles 9 and 10 of the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR), WHO is in contact with the Russian health authorities to verify the event, its circumstances, the laboratory tests underway, and their results, the rationale for contact-tracing and the health status of contacts, as well as any potential international public health implication. WHO has offered support if needed." For now, WHO says the risk to the general public appears low. But the assessment could change as more information becomes available. Based on unofficial information available, the public health risk to the general population appears to be low. The risk assessment will be updated once more information is available." What Triggered Panic Across Globe? A laboratory worker in Russia's Irkutsk region died of severe pneumonia on October 2. The WHO is in contact with Russian health authorities regarding the death and potential links to suspected pneumonic plague. The deceased worker was identified as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova. Russian public health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor stated the woman was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown origin. Local reports indicate close to 200 contacts have been identified and are under medical observation. The case has triggered concern because the deceased woman reportedly worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, near Irkutsk in Siberia. Local reports have identified her as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova. Reports have claimed that she may have been exposed to Yersinia pestis", the bacterium that causes plague, during laboratory work. However, Russian health authorities have not confirmed that she had plague or that there was a laboratory accident. has reached out to the Ministry of Health of Russian Federation for further details and confirmation. The story will be updated if a response is received. Russias public health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, has said the woman was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown origin. It also said expanded testing of her samples did not detect microorganisms associated with her professional activities and that the epidemiological situation in Irkutsk and nearby Shelekhov remained stable. As a precaution, people who may have come in contact with the woman have been placed under medical observation. Local reports have put the number of contacts at close to 200, while several healthcare facilities have introduced quarantine measures. Authorities have said no contacts have developed symptoms so far. What Is Pneumonic Plague? The latest reports have raised particular concern over pneumonic plague, the form of plague that affects the lungs and can spread from person to person through respiratory droplets. The disease is caused by Yersinia pestis and can become severe rapidly. However, experts believe it is treatable with antibiotics when diagnosed and treated early. The current incident, however, should not yet be described as a confirmed plague outbreak. The WHO said it has offered support to Russian authorities and will update its risk assessment when more information becomes available. The United States has also said it is monitoring reports of a suspected pneumonic plague case in Irkutsk, while stressing that many details remain unconfirmed. According to Indian Medical Association Kerala State Research Cell convenor, Dr Rajeev Jayadevan, there is no need for panic as health authorities in Russia are actively tracing the contacts and there is no immediate threat to India. Yersinia pestis is the bacterium that causes plague. But calling this an outbreak at this stage would be premature. This is still an evolving story. What we know so far from media reports is that a laboratory worker died of pneumonia and that the laboratory apparently had a test tube with Yersinia pestis." The WHO opened an investigation after a 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died of severe pneumonia on October 2 amidst unofficial reports linking her death to a suspected pneumonic plague exposure.

headline: Brazil lurches to the right as Lula falters in the first round of presidential election
content: Sunday night was supposed to be historic for Luiz Incio Lula da Silva, who was seeking a record fourth term as Brazils president. But when the results came in, the night looked gloomy. Instead of winning in the first round, as his supporters had expected, Lula trailed his challenger Flvio Bolsonaro by about 1.8 percentage points, or 2.2 million votes. With Flvio also falling short of the 50% needed for an outright victory, the election now moves to a second round on October 25 leaving Lulas campaign facing a tougher contest than anticipated, while Bolsonaro heads into the runoff with the momentum of having finished first. The two candidates struck sharply different notes as the results became clear. Flvio, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, declared that Brazilians were demanding change. It is the end of the era of the Workers Party (PT); it is a big change in our country, he told reporters in Braslia. Lula, speaking to supporters in So Paulo, acknowledged that the result had been unexpected. I confess to you that I was convinced I would win the election in the first round, he said. But Lula insisted that the contest had now entered a new phase. The second round is a new campaign, he said, arguing that the runoff would give voters a direct choice between the two candidates and their visions. Political pundits agree that the second round is a new election and can go either way. But there is little doubt that, for now, the momentum is with the right. As if Flvio staying ahead of Lula in the presidential election was not shocking enough for Brazils left, the results for Congress, the Senate and state governors came as a big jolt too. Candidates from the Bolsonaros Liberal Party (PL) broke voting records in the Congress, while the party emerged as the dominant force in the Senate and made significant gains in state assemblies. Flvios supporters also account for a majority of the governors elected in the first round, pointing to a broad rightward shift that extends beyond the presidential race. But the most significant feature of the rightward shift may be that the PL has not grown at the expense of Lulas party. The far-right party has expanded its base by eating into the traditional conservative and centre-right political space. With 19 senators elected, the PL will increase its representation from 15 to 28 seats from February 2027, giving it the second-largest single-party bloc in the Senate since Brazils return to democracy. While the left has maintained its position in the Chamber and Senate, the far right has grown by devouring much of the right a trend also seen in other Latin American countries. Another factor behind Flvios strong performance was the evangelical vote, which has increasingly consolidated behind the Bolsonaro family, while Lula failed to translate Brazils large Catholic population into the electoral advantage his campaign had expected. The contrast was particularly striking after the controversy surrounding Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Brazils patron saint, which became a political issue during the campaign. In municipalities with an above-average concentration of evangelicals, Flvio won 52% of the valid votes. The contrast was even sharper in municipalities with the highest concentration of Catholics. Lulas share there fell by 11 percentage points compared with his previous performance. Now, the second round will force both campaigns to broaden their appeal beyond their core constituencies. Flvios is expected to make anti-PT sentiment the central theme of its strategy, with his team hoping to attract the supporters of other right-wing candidates who failed to move to the second round. Flvio will also seek to reach the roughly 40 million Brazilians who either abstained or cast blank or invalid ballots. His campaign has already secured political support in five states where gubernatorial races will go to a second round, compared with four for Lula, giving the Bolsonaro camp an additional network of state-level allies in the runoff. Lula, too, has identified abstention as one of his biggest targets for the second round. More than 33 million Brazilians did not vote in the first round, the highest abstention rate since 1998. We are going to appeal to the people who did not vote, Lula said, calling on them to return to the polls because their vote would be crucial in deciding the countrys future. For Lula, the challenge now is to prevent the election from becoming a referendum on the PT while rebuilding the broader coalition that carried him back to the presidency in 2022. But there are murmurs of some criticism of his campaign within the presidents party. Some reports on Monday suggested that in his seventh presidential campaign, Lula was surrounded by people who, according to former PT campaign insiders who had worked with him in previous elections, were reluctant to challenge him or tell him what he did not want to hear. If the account is accurate, the problem with the campaign was not a lack of experience at the top, but the absence of people around Lula who were willing to tell the veteran of seven elections when his strategy was no longer working. That assessment may be a little harsh for a politician who has built his career on being seen as a man of the people and on his ability to understand the pulse of the country. I know how to speak to the poor, I know how to speak to ordinary Brazilians, Lula had said a day before the first round of elections. As the Sundays result puts his instinct to its biggest test, Lula will now have to draw on all his experience to reconnect with voters beyond his traditional base. The Brazilian president will also need to deploy all his political expertise to win the contest that could determine not only his presidency but also his political legacy.

headline: India News Highlights, 6 October 2026 | Delhi Police release Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi from detention hours after Opposition's anti-CEC protest
content: leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka, and other MPs have been released from detention following their protest at Akashvani Bhawan in Delhi over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police on Tuesday night released Opposition leaders, including Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, after a nearly nine-hour protest at Akashvani Bhavan in Delhi. The INDIA bloc leaders had been detained after staging a protest inside the All India Radio premises next to the Election Commission office. They were taken away in buses before being released later in the evening. The Opposition leaders, who had earlier climbed atop barricades during the protest, had vowed to continue their demonstration until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and tell him that he had committed vote theft. The protest was held over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. These detainees included Akhilesh Yadav, Abhishek Banerjee, Kalyan Banerjee, Derek OBrien, Imran Masood, P Santosh and A Rahim. As the protest escalated, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with some supporters, entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises while attempting to reach the Election Commission headquarters. Congress leaders Pawan Khera and other party workers also remained at the premises. Rahul Gandhi, speaking to media persons from inside Akashvani Bhawan, said the opposition was fighting to save democracy. We are not only countering them. headline: nuclear archaeology finds Werner Heisenberg mistook how close he was
content: Hans Bethe. Felix Bloch. Niels Bohr. Albert Einstein. Enrico Fermi. James Franck. Otto Frisch. Samuel Goudsmit. Lilli Hornig. Rolf Landshoff. Maria Goeppert Mayer. Rudolf Peierls. George Placzek. Eugene Rabinowitch. Joseph Rotblat. Leo Szilard. Edward Teller. Stanislaw Ulam. John von Neumann. Victor Weisskopf. Eugene Wigner. These are just some of the scientists who had emigrated from Europe, many of whom later made critical contributions to the Manhattan Project the American effort to build the worlds first nuclear weapon. Many of these scientists had seen firsthand the horrors Nazi Germany was perpetrating in Europe; many were Jews who were escaping persecution themselves. They showed their contempt for Adolf Hitler and his armies by bringing a sense of urgency to their research on the bomb, and were often motivated by what they believed the stake was: the fate of the world itself. The Manhattan Project tested its first atom bomb on July 16, 1945, and delivered two to the U.S. military in July-August. Part of their sense of urgency was rooted in doubts about whether Nazi Germany was also building a bomb, including an effort led by physicist and Nobel laureate Werner Heisenberg. Their anxieties were not unfounded: in April 1945, only weeks before Germany surrendered to Allied forces, Heisenbergs team had assembled a nuclear reactor in a cellar beneath a church in Haigerloch, in the countrys south. The setup, called the B8 pile, had 664 cubes of uranium suspended on chains in around 1,400 litres of heavy water. A 40-cm-thick shell of graphite surrounded the core, and was itself surrounded by a layer of aluminium and a 60-cm-thick layer of (ordinary) water. Heisenbergs team had taken six years to build B8 but had little to show for it. When a few neutrons were shot into the reactor, the uranium multiplied them into more but no chain reaction followed. Far from critical After the war ended, Heisenberg said the team had come very close; he wrote in a 1947 article in Nature that Haigerloch didnt have enough resources and that just a little more quantity of uranium would have done the trick. According to a new study in PNAS Nexus, by researchers from the U.S., Heisenberg & co. were actually way off the mark. Only around 14 of the 1,100 or so uranium cubes made for Heisenbergs efforts still survive. Using a pycnometer, the team found the density of one cube to be 18.535 g/cm3, lower than the 19.01 g/cm3 of solid uranium, indicating the cube was porous. Another cube contained 0.724% of uranium-235 (by mass), meaning it was natural rather than enriched uranium. In March 1944, a German physicist named Karl Wirtz had reported that Nazi Germanys stocks of heavy water had accidentally been diluted to 98.85% purity. A post-war sample from Haigerloch in 1947 found only 96.8% purity. The team also started from the records of aluminium giant Norsk Hydro to estimate that Nazi Germany had a maximum supply of 1,836 kg of pure heavy water during the war. When the team worked upwards from here, including the design of the B8 pile, they concluded it had a neutron multiplication factor of 0.942. A reactor needs to have a factor of 1 to be critical, and a difference of 0.058 is actually large. The team found that the uranium cubes in B8 were arranged too close together, preventing the heavy water from efficiently slowing the neutrons. The researchers estimated that increasing the heavy waters purity to 100% would improve the factor to only 0.95. They also simulated over 1,200 combinations of uranium and heavy water and found that the B8 pile would have required at least 2,994 kg of uranium and 3,411 litres of heavy water to become critical. B8 however, contained 1,538 kg of uranium and 1,549 kg of heavy water when it was dismantled. More importantly, the team also estimated all German facilities at the time combined possessed only 2,572 kg of uranium and 1,890 kg of 96.8%-pure heavy water a significant shortfall and which could support a factor of 0.959 at best. Industrial capacity The first U.S. reactor, called Chicago Pile-1, first became critical on December 2, 1942, using natural uranium as fuel and graphite, rather than heavy water, as the moderator. So some nuclear historians have opined that Heisenberg et al. had simply picked the wrong moderator. A 2025 study in The European Physical Journal H demurred, however: while the U.S. was able to source petroleum coke extremely low in boron and turn it into reactor-grade graphite, the graphite made from metallurgical coke in Germany was high in boron, which absorbs neutrons. The B8 pile used the graphite from the predecessor B7 pile, and the new study also found that it contained 3.4 weight-parts per million (wppm) of equivalent boron contamination. The Siemens graphite from earlier contained around 6.6 wppm. On the other hand, the Manhattan Project used graphite with around 1.4 wppm of boron. In simulations, it didnt matter how far apart the uranium cubes in the B7 pile or in any previous piles could have been: the contamination made criticality impossible. The significant difference between the Nazi German and the Manhattan Project programmes, then, seems to have been industrial capacity. The Americans developed and built multiple technologies to enrich uranium, set up reactors and chemical separation units, and a weapons laboratory, which together created 1.3 lakh jobs and invested $2.2 billion at the peak. Nazi Germany had nothing of similar scale. Understandable concerns According to a 2015 study in Angewandte Chemie, some uranium from the Nazi nuclear programme had not experienced a significant neutron flux and had probably come from Joachimsthal in todays Czechia, indicating (in a limited sense) the absence of an industrial uranium enrichment programme. Many questions about the Nazi nuclear programme still remain open, often rooted in different interpretations of common data. Some important ones are centered on whether German scientists deliberately delayed the bomb project. Some technical questions are open, too. For example, the purity of the heavy water at Haigerloch itself is unknown and the graphites boron content is based on archival rather than direct, firsthand information. The overall picture today is neither that German physicists were incompetent nor that they were tantalisingly close to building a bomb. Their base of materials fell short of what a nuclear programme required and their supply chains were not good enough. Ultimately, given the information available at the time, and more so given Germany was also home to many of the worlds best nuclear physicists, the Manhattan Project scientists concerns were understandable. mukunth.v@.co.in

headline: UN chief calls for Gaza ceasefire ahead of October 7 anniversary
content: United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Monday (October 5, 2026) called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza ahead of the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. It is time for the ceasefire to become permanent. It is time to allow humanitarian assistance at scale. And it is time to respect international law, Mr. Guterres said in a statement, calling for a political path to lasting peace across the whole region. Let this anniversary mark not only another year of mourning, but also a renewed determination to build a different future: one in which Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace and security, with their rights, dignity, and aspirations fulfilled, Mr. Guterres said. The UN chief acknowledged Israels casualties in the statement, calling the Hamas attack abhorrent for killing more than 1,200 Israelis and foreign nationals and the hostage-taking of another 251 people. Mr. Guterres also said Palestinians in Gaza have faced a massive loss of life, displacement and destruction, without specifying their death toll. Their suffering, too, demands an end, now, Mr. Guterres said. Israels years-long military campaign in Gaza has killed more than 74,200 people according to the Palestinian Health Ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are deemed reliable by the UN. Mr. Guterres acknowledged that a brief ceasefire, announced by U.S. President Donald Trump in October 2025, brought some relief. But it has yet to deliver security, adequate humanitarian assistance or a credible path to recovery and peace. Israel, which still controls most of Gaza, refuses to withdraw its soldiers until Hamas disarmament has been verified. Hamas, for its part, has advocated for gradual disarmament rather than immediate and unilateral surrender of its arsenal. Since the 2023 attacks, Israel has waged military attacks on several fronts, notably invading southern Lebanon to confront Hezbollah, the Islamist movement backed by Tehran, and launching war against Iran in late February alongside the United States.

headline: Indian Crew Member Injured, Two Foreign Nationals Dead In Russian Drone Strike On Vessel In Black Sea
content: MV ROYAD MAMMADOV was attacked in the Black Sea, leaving two foreign nationals dead and crew members injured. Three Indian crew members are safe, the Indian embassy said. A commercial vessel, MV ROYAD MAMMADOV, came under attack in the Black Sea, leaving two foreign nationals dead and some crew members injured, the Embassy of India in Romania said. Three Indian nationals were among the crew members aboard the vessel, and the embassy later confirmed that all three were safe, with one of them injured and receiving medical attention in Romania. The Indian mission said it had learnt of the attack and was in contact with relevant authorities to ascertain further details about the incident and the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals. - 'Nothing Conclusive Yet': JD Vance Says US Probing Iran Link In Flydubai Hijacking Attempt - Commercial Vessels Attacked In Black Sea, 31 Indian Crew Members Safe, One Injured: MEA Condemns Incident - India Condemns Attack On Panama-Flagged Ship Off Oman, 11 Indian Crew Members Injured | - Ship Carrying Indians Sinks In Black Sea After Catching Fire, Captain Killed; Zelenskyy Blames Russia Embassy Confirms 3 Indians Safe In its first update on the incident, the Embassy of India in Romania said, We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea." As per preliminary information, there have been two casualties (foreign nationals), while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members." The embassy added, The mission is in close contact with the relevant authorities to ascertain further details about the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals." In a subsequent update, the mission confirmed that all three Indian nationals were safe. It said one of them had been injured and was receiving medical attention. MV ROYAD MAMMADOV was attacked in the Black Sea, the Indian Embassy in Romania said. The embassy said two foreign nationals were killed and some crew members were injured. Three Indian nationals were among the crew; all three are safe, while one is injured and receiving medical attention. All three Indian nationals are safe. We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members." The embassys statements put the number of casualties at two foreign nationals and said some crew members were injured. It did not provide further details about the identities or nationalities of those killed. Ambassador Speaks To Indians At Constana Hospital Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constana County Hospital, the embassy said. Mohapatra also spoke with the hospitals Chief Physician, who confirmed that the three Indians were in good health and receiving necessary care. Amb Manoj Mohapatra spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constana County Hospital. He also spoke with the hospitals Chief Physician, who confirmed that all three are in good health and receiving necessary care. The Ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support." The mission said it remained in close contact with hospital authorities and was extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members. Zelenskyy Says Russian Drones Hit Vessel Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, according to news agency PTI, said the vessel was struck by two Russian drones while it was in neutral waters. Zelenskyy said the civilian vessel was carrying corn and was owned by Turkiye. He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard and that the ships captain had been killed. He added that the fate of another person was still being established. Zelenskyy said 11 crew members were rescued, one of them injured. He also said Ukraine had repeatedly proposed concrete steps to de-escalate the situation and ensure security in the Black Sea. The incident comes amid heightened risks to commercial shipping in the Black Sea due to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. Commercial vessels and port infrastructure in the region have faced repeated disruption as the conflict has continued. Jaishankar Raises Safety Of Seafarers The attack also comes against the backdrop of Indias concerns over the safety of commercial vessels and seafarers. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, in his address to the 81st United Nations General Assembly, said attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers had taken place across maritime routes from the Gulf and the Red Sea to the Black Sea. New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations. This is completely unacceptable." Jaishankar also said India had joined Liberia and 23 partner nations in an international coalition to mobilise global public opinion and defend commercial shipping routes. We must ensure that the safety and security of shipping and seafarers is never compromised. Scrupulously observing international law is an integral element of that endeavour," he said. The External Affairs Minister also called for restraint and de-escalation in the Gulf region to protect civilian crews and ensure uninterrupted energy supplies and global trade. Three Indian nationals were among the crew on the vessel when it was struck by Russian drones, and the Embassy of India in Romania confirmed that all of them are safe. One of the Indian crew members sustained injuries and received medical treatment at Constana County Hospital.

headline: By-Elections 2026 Live Updates: TN's Madurantakam tops bypoll turnout at 83.86%, Bengal's Nandigram records 79.39% until 5 PM
content: polling station in Nandigram, Purba Mednipur during Nandigram constituency assembly By-Election. (Express photo by Partha Paul) By Elections 2026 Voting Live Updates: Polling in the Madurantakam Assembly byelection in Tamil Nadu recorded the highest voter turnout among the constituencies reporting figures by 5 pm, with 83.86% of voters casting their ballots, according to the Election Commission. In West Bengal, the Nandigram Assembly constituency saw 79.39% voter turnout till 5 PM. In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll recorded 78.83% turnout, while the Nagaon Lok Sabha byelection in Assam saw nearly 76% of voters exercise their franchise. In Tamil Nadus Dharapuram, the figure stood at 78.53%. Both Dharapuram and Madurantakam are reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. Polling in Bengal will continue till 6 pm, while voting in Assam will end at 5 pm. Counting of votes in all the constituencies will take place on October 9. Tamil Nadu: The bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram were necessitated by the resignation of then AIADMK MLAs K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Satyabama, who later joined the ruling TVK. Both have been re-nominated from their respective seats. The DMK and AIADMK are also contesting both constituencies. In West Bengal: Nandigram is the more closely watched contest, with BJP candidate Hasirani Rath facing Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, rival TMC faction candidate Mohammad Eteshamul Haque and CPIs Santigopal Giri. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who was killed in May. In Rejinagar, the candidates include Golam Nabi Azad of the Aam Janata Unnayan Party, BJPs Sakharav Sarkar, TMCs Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh, Congress Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi and CPI(M)s Syed Asad Ali. In Assam: The Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll is an important contest for the BJP, Congress and AIUDF. The BJP is trying to increase its support in the Muslim-majority seat, while the Congress is working to hold on to its minority voters. AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal is also trying to regain the partys influence after it won only two Assembly seats in April, down from 16 earlier. Fifteen candidates are contesting, but the main fight is expected to be between BJPs Devashish Sharma, former Congress MLA Sibamoni Bora and Ajmal In Puducherry: Bypoll is being seen as a test of the four-month-old NDA government led by Chief Minister N Rangasamy. The election was necessitated by Rangasamys resignation from the seat. While 11 candidates are in the fray, the main contest is expected to be between the ruling AINRC-led NDA, the Congress and former ally DMK.

headline: 32 Killed As Nigerian Air Force Plane Crashes, President Tinubu Declares Three-Day Mourning
content: Tinubu declared three days of national mourning for the Air Force personnel who died in the crash, while ordering flags to be flown at half-staff nationwide. A Nigerian Air Force aircraft crashed in southwestern Nigeria on Monday, killing all 32 people aboard, including 25 passengers and seven crew members, President Bola Tinubu said. The aircraft was travelling from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact with it at 0813 GMT, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. The wreckage was subsequently found near Igbokoda in Ondo State, where rescue teams were sent to the crash site. - Russia's Nuclear-Capable Bomber Aircraft Crashes During Training Flight, Six Killed - Dual UK-Iranian National Arrested Over Suspected Terror Offence Linked To Airbase Incident - Flydubai Attack: Co-Pilots 2-Year Stay In Australia On Student Visa Under Security Scanner - Why Two People Must Be In The Cockpit At All Times: The Crashes That Changed Aviation Rules The Air Force said the aircraft had been undertaking a routine mission. The presidency and Keyamo identified it as an ATR-42, a twin-engine turboprop aircraft capable of carrying between 30 and 50 passengers, according to its manufacturer. Painful Moment For Our Armed Forces: President Tinubu The president extends his deepest condolences to the family of the 25 passengers and seven crew members involved," Tinubus office said in a statement. This is a painful moment for our armed forces and for the entire nation," it added. Tinubu later ordered an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash. A Nigerian Air Force aircraft crashed on Monday, killing all 32 people aboard. The aircraft was travelling from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact at 0813 GMT. The wreckage was found near Igbokoda in Ondo State. The aircraft was identified as an ATR-42, a twin-engine turboprop. President Tinubu declared three days of national mourning for the Air Force personnel. The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences," Tinubu said in a statement. The aircraft came down near a naval base, according to the presidency and Keyamo. Footage shared on social media showed people gathered near a river as rescuers searched the surrounding area by boat. Three-Day National Mourning Declared Tinubu declared three days of national mourning for the Air Force personnel who died in the crash, while ordering flags to be flown at half-staff nationwide. The identities of those killed will be released after their families have been informed, the presidency said. Residents near the crash site reported hearing the aircraft shortly before it went down. Dayo Akinte, a 39-year-old firewood seller who lives about a kilometre from the site, told AFP she heard a noise that sounded like thunder" around the time of the crash. Since the accident, three aircraft have also been flying over the scene", she said by phone. Akinte said a person fishing in the nearby swamp alerted the naval base and residents after discovering the crash. The incident occurred in Igbokoda, in Ilaje, an oil-producing area of Ondo State. The crash is among Nigerias deadliest aviation accidents involving a military aircraft in recent years. With inputs from AFP/Reuters An ATR-42 military aircraft crashed in southwestern Nigeria while traveling from Benin City to Lagos, killing all 32 people on board, which included 25 passengers and seven crew members. President Bola Tinubu has ordered the Nigerian Air Force to immediately conduct a thorough investigation to determine the cause of the crash.

headline: 'No Longer In Politics': Pabitra Kar Missing From Election Scene, Not In Nandigram Ahead Of Bypoll | Exclusive
content: Kar had emerged as a prominent political figure in the constituency after switching from BJP to TMC and taking on Suvendu Adhikari in the election. Pabitra Kar, the Trinamool Congress candidate who contested against West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari in Nandigram, is conspicuous by his absence from the election scene ahead of polling. On the eve of polling, a visit to Kars residence in Nandigram found that he was not at home and was not in the constituency. His wife, Shiuli Kar, told Bangla that Pabitra is currently no longer active in politics. - Faked Injury, Humiliated Nandigram: Suvendu Adhikari Orders Probe Into Mamatas 2021 Leg Injury - 'I Could Be Detained Too If...': Suvendu Adhikari Reacts To Humayun Kabir's Detention In Murshidabad - Faked Injury, Humiliated Nandigram: Suvendu Adhikari Orders Probe Into Mamatas 2021 Leg Injury - Suvendus Nandigram, Vijays Tamil Nadu Test: Why These Bypolls Matter Beyond The Seats Kars absence is notable given his recent political journey in Nandigram. He had emerged as a prominent political figure in the constituency after switching from the Bharatiya Janata Party to the Trinamool Congress and taking on Suvendu Adhikari in the election. From BJP to TMC, then a contest against Adhikari Pabitra Kar had been associated with the BJP. Ahead of the 2024 election, however, he left the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress. The TMC subsequently fielded him against Adhikari in Nandigram. Kar lost the contest, after which his political presence in the constituency appeared to diminish. Now, just ahead of another election in Nandigram, Kar is not present on the ground. Pabitra is no longer in politics Speaking to Bangla, Shiuli Kar said her husband is no longer involved in active politics. Shiuli, who herself has held the post of panchayat pradhan, also spoke about her relationship of respect with Suvendu Adhikari. Recalling an earlier conversation with Adhikari, she said, Many years ago, I had told Suvendu Babu that one day he would become the Chief Minister." Hopeful about Nandigrams development Shiuli Kar also expressed confidence that Suvendu Adhikari, in his capacity as Chief Minister, would work for the development of Nandigram. Her comments come at a significant political juncture in the constituency, where Adhikari has maintained a strong political presence since defeating Mamata Banerjee in the 2021 Assembly election. For Pabitra Kar, however, the current election marks a sharp contrast to the spotlight he occupied just months ago. Once at the centre of Nandigrams political contest, he is now away from the constituency and, according to his wife, has stepped away from active politics. Shiuli Kar stated that her husband is no longer active in politics and was absent from the constituency ahead of the polling in Nandigram.

headline: U.S. envoy holds rare meeting with Sudan's top general in push to seek end to fighting
content: U.S. envoy met over the weekend with Sudan's top general as the Trump administration pushes for diplomatic efforts to end a war that has created what many describe as the world's largest humanitarian crisis. Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump's senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, met Saturday (October 4, 2026) with Sudanese General Abdel-Fattah Burhan at a luncheon hosted by Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi on the sidelines of the mid-year coordination meeting of the African Union, according to a social media post. These efforts aim to enable Sudan to restore its security and stability, embark on reconstruction and development, and, through an inclusive Sudanese-owned and Sudanese-led national dialogue, transition toward a civilian-led government, Mr. Boulos wrote on X. The rare meeting between Mr. Boulos and Mr. Burhan comes as the U.S., Egypt and other intermediaries seek to renew pressure on the warring parties in Sudan to negotiate an end to the fighting that has killed at least 59,000 people, displaced some 13 million and pushed many parts of the African nation into famine. It also took place less than two weeks after Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim Ahmed Ibrahim accused the U.S. of denying a visa for Burhan to attend the high-level week of the UN General Assembly last month in New York, saying it was a betrayal of Washington's host country obligations. The State Department declined to comment at the time, citing visa privacy laws. The war in Sudan, which has entered its fourth year, has been overshadowed over the past year by the conflicts in the West Asia. The African country first plunged into chaos in April 2023 when a power struggle between the military and the powerful paramilitary Rapid Support Forces exploded into open fighting in the capital, Khartoum, and elsewhere in the country. Although repeated attempts at peace talks in recent months have failed to end the war, Mr. Boulos and other Trump administration officials have said they believe there is still a chance for a regional agreement to secure an immediate humanitarian truce, including certain withdrawals and the establishment of safe humanitarian corridors. The United States stands ready to support all efforts leading to a comprehensive dialogue among the Sudanese political forces, leading to a preliminary road map of the future of the Sudan, Mr. Boulos said in his post.

headline: Plaque in tribute to Indian Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
content: Two years after the BMCs decision, the road was officially named as Freedom Fighter Ramnath Goenka Marg on November 25, 1995. It was inaugurated by then Vice-President K R Narayanan, with then Chief Minister Manohar Joshi and municipal commissioner JD Jadhav. The name of the lane has now been engraved upon the new plaque along with Goenkas portrait and his words that define the newspapers motto of Journalism of Courage. Remembering our founder Ramnath Goenka On his 35th death anniversary, a plaque was unveiled on the corner of Ramnath Goenka Marg, Nariman Point, Mumbai in the presence of Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan of the Bombay High Court and Anant Goenka, Executive Director, Group. Express Photo by Sankhadeep Banerjee The plaque of 8.5 feet width and 12.5 feet height, was constructed over four months. While the plaque was constructed in four months, the intricate engravings were executed over a period of 25 days. The plaque rests on a platform, which takes the total height of the structure to 14 feet, said urban planner Hardik Sankhe, who worked on its design. The project work was executed by the contractor, Aditya Interiors. The final nod for constructing the commemorative plaque was granted by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporations A ward office in July 2025, following which permissions from traffic police, BEST and the Mumbai Heritage Conservation Committee were obtained.

headline: Married into Bihar and want to be a teacher? New domicile rule may pose hurdle
content: On September 22, days before applications opened for teacher recruitment, Bihar introduced a new rider women married into the state must produce documents with their parents address, not their husbands. For these candidates, it effectively nullifies reservation benefits. A year after it passed its Domicile Policy 2025 to leave only 15% of seats for candidates outside the state, the Bihar government has introduced a new policy rider women married into the state must produce documents with their parents and not their husbands address. This effectively means that women from outside Bihar married into the state are not eligible for any reservation benefits. In a notification it issued on September 22, the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) said: Married women, who wish to avail quota, will have to produce their caste, residence and non-creamy layer certificates, from [the] address of their parents, not of their husbands. The notification was issued around the time when the BPSC opened applications for its 32,388 teacher posts through the Teachers Recruitment Examination (TRE)-4. The notification comes as the policy passed in August 2025 comes into effect this year for the first time. For applicants, it adds another layer of filtering. Said a BPSC official: Since Bihar had not introduced its domicile policy in our past three examinations, women candidates were free to use their husbands address. We had to ensure foolproof implementation of our domicile policy, and needed to clarify rules on married women, applicable for women married into Bihar. In TRE-I, held in August 2023, around 1.20 lakh teachers were appointed against 1.70 lakh advertised vacancies. In TRE-II, held in December 2023, around 96,000 teachers were selected against 1.22 lakh advertised posts across primary, middle, secondary and higher secondary cadres. TRE-III, originally held in March 2024, was cancelled after a paper leak and re-conducted in July 2024 for 87,774 vacancies. The BPSC subsequently selected around 70,000 candidates across the four school cadres According to officials, about 50,000 out-of-state teachers have been appointed across TRE-I to TRE-III since 2023 nearly one-fifth of BPSCs 2.68 lakh teacher appointments. Of the 5.68 lakh teachers hired since 2006, a good number of candidates came from other states. This upset Bihar candidates. When the Bihar Teacher Recruitment Rules were first notified in March 2023, a mandatory Bihar domicile policy implementation clause was added. But the Bihar cabinet scrapped it in July 2023, which effectively means that the Bihar domicile policy was never enforced for any examinations, said an education department official. Notified in August last year, the BPSC TRE Domicile Rules introduced a 40% quota for candidates who passed matriculation or intermediate from institutions in Bihar. Under the new policy, no direct quota exists for candidates from outside Bihar, and they must compete exclusively for 15% open seats. Non-domicile candidates also dont receive state reservation benefits such as womens quota and other relaxations, and, like other general candidates, require 60% in central and state teacher eligibility tests to qualify the highest qualifying mark among the categories. Bihar reserves 85% of state teacher recruitment posts directly for permanent residents of Bihar through various reservation quotas. The BPSC, which has invited applications for the TRE-4 examination, has not yet announced its examination schedule. Of the total 32,388 vacancies, 3,847 positions are for Class 1 to Class 5, 8,563 posts for Class 6 to Class 8, 3,878 posts for Class 9 to Class 10, and 16,101 posts for Class 11 to Class 12 teachers. According to the UDISE+ 2024-25 report, Bihar has a total of approximately 94,339 schools, both government and private. About 80.84% to 80.90% of these, roughly 76,000 to 76,300 government-managed schools, operate in the state. These government schools are served by a total of approximately 7.07 lakh (707,000) teachers.

headline: Ukraine or West Asia, India backs all meaningful peace efforts: PM Modi
content: In his statement after the bilateral meeting with visiting Swiss President Guy Parmelin, Modi said: Both India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. We will continue to work together for global peace and stability. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace. His statement came a day after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India has got a little more involved beyond advocacy and is having conversations with both Russia and Ukraine, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. Last week, Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha had said that India has put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war, for the first time since the war began in February 2022. Elaborating on the context and rationale behind Indias move, Jaishankar said on Monday that Delhi started the latest round of conversations with Russia and Ukraine in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. Speaking at an interactive session at the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Jaishankar said: In the month of July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. And we started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that. Jaishankar said those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo being carried. And there was concern over grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain So it got linked to energy. So it became a somewhat broader conversation, he said.
