He said those conversations are ongoing including during Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on August 31, after which Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Vlodymyr Zelenskyy in early September, followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit on September 11-12. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its obviously not an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, Jaishankar said, adding that resolving concerns pertaining to grain, fertiliser and fuel are in the interest of India, as well as the Global South. We have the interests of the parties themselves, that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. From the very beginning, he said, India has held the view that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties there were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in a reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he said, India has always believed that there wasnt any point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. On October 1, Putin had said that Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha had said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He had said Ukraine was prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and was also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea. Modi has been raising the issue with Putin since 2022, when he first said this is not the era of war. In a meeting with Putin in Moscow in July 2024, Modi said peace talks do not succeed amid bombs, guns and bullets, and a solution cannot be found on the battlefield. On August 31 this year, Modi had urged Putin to move from endless war to end of war, when they met in Bishkek on the sidelines of the summit of SCO leaders.

headline: Rahul Gandhi says abuse of position by CEC Gyanesh Kumar proven, BJP calls remarks 'full of lies'
content: As Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said that the Supreme Court didnt approve any of the modifications to Form 6, the Opposition hit out at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saying that the courts observation was proof that he was abusing his position to help the BJP. In response, the ruling party stated that the top courts notice to the poll panel and the Centre was democracy in action. The Election Commission had included a new section in Form 6 that seeks the status of the applicants parents vis--vis the last Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended. Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi said it is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP, he said. In a post on X, Rahul said that Kumar and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable. Taking on Rahul Gandhi, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra termed Rahuls post on X full of lies, an attempt to spread anarchy in the country by propagating lies. The CJI did not say that the Form 6 was illegal. Rahul Gandhi is lying that the Supreme Court said so There is punishment for lying, he said. Patra alleged that Rahul is trying to mislead the country on what transpired during the Supreme Court hearing and on the statement issued by the Election Commission on September 26. On both the issues, Rahul Gandhi is trying to create anarchy in the country by misleading people so that is (political) rallies gain some strength, he said. The fact that this entire matter was taken to the Supreme Court and the apex court issued notices is also democracy in action, Patra said. Responding to Rahuls post on X, the Election Commission of India called his remarks misleading. The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026, said the ECI. In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court, the ECI said on X. Congress general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal said it was yet another instance where Gyanesh Kumar overruled other ECs to perpetuate illegality for the BJP. During the Modi-Shah regime, the Election Commission has truly become a cheating commission which deprives the ordinary citizen of their inalienable right of franchise. Based on todays proceedings, we reiterate our core demand Gyanesh must go, he said. TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee said that the contradiction is glaring. The ECs own press note of 26 September says Form 6 was upheld by the SC, while the Supreme Courts statement now says otherwise. Who is misleading the country? These contradictions go to the heart of our democracy. If the institutions meant to protect our vote contradict each other, who protects the voter? This is how elections are stolen, he wrote on X. CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the SC categorically stated that it never approved the modified Form 6. How many lies will Gyanesh Kumar tell The ECI, under Gyanesh Kumar, claimed in its September 26 press release that the top court had approved the changes. Now that press release has mysteriously disappeared from the ECI website. This is not a minor discrepancy it is a grave assault on institutional credibility, said Kumar. CPIM MP John Brittas said: I had written to the EC months ago pointing out that the modifications to Form 6 are illegal and unconstitutional. I am glad that the Supreme Court, after an inordinate delay, has finally clarified that these changes never had its sanction or clearance. Citizens were deeply anguished by the Courts prolonged reluctance to step in and protect their most fundamental right the right to belong to and participate in the electoral process

headline: Karnataka CID probe puts forest dept in the dock over killing of three 'poachers'
content: A CID investigation into the killing of three alleged poachers in Karnatakas Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, bordering Tamil Nadu, by forest officials in the early hours of August 15 this year, has raised several questions: autopsy reports indicate shots were fired at close range; videography of crime scene does not show weapon alleged to have been found with the victims; bodies were removed and crime scene not preserved. The CID has cited some of these findings, based on forensic and field evidence, in its plea to the Karnataka High Court for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the three forest officials Shivaraja Sasalavada (29), beat forester to whom the shotgun used in the killings was issued by the forest department; Shivalinga Nayaka (51), anti-poaching forest watcher; and Girisha R (29), anti-poaching camp watcher. The HC registered the CIDs plea on September 24, and the first hearing was held on September 30, when the court issued notice to the accused. The state forest department had said the three who were killed Anthony Swamy (50), John Rose Peter (43) and Sebastian David Kumar (35), residents of villages on the fringes of a forest in Hanur in Karnataka were poachers. It had said the men were armed and had first opened fire on the forest team, leading to retaliatory firing. A fourth person, Joseph Mahima Das alias Benjamin (45), had managed to escape. Based on his account, a police complaint was filed by Anthony Swamys wife, Lourde Mary. The police complaint had said the four men had gone to find lost cattle and were sleeping in the forest when forest officials opened fire on them. A CID investigation was ordered on August 24, after post-mortem reports found the shooting happened at close range, and, contrary to the forest departments claims, indicated that the victims were probably on the ground facing upwards when they were shot. On September 10, a local court in Hanur granted anticipatory bail to the forest officials, saying that the prosecutions case was based on circumstantial evidence. Opposing the bail, the CID, in its plea before the HC, has raised the following points: * It has cited the post-mortem report which said the cause of death was shotgun injuries, and the range of fire of shotgun injury (was) at close range. * Citing the crime scene video recording by the forest department, the CID has said it does not disclose the existence of a weapon alleged to have been found with the deceased at the crime scene. * The very fact that the dead bodies have been removed from the scene of the offence, that the crime scene was not preserved, and that the accused did not inform the nearest police as early as possible discloses that the officers have breached, the norms prescribed in a 1991 notification for incidents of firing by armed forest personnel, it has said. * There is no material to indicate the deceased caused a threat or danger to the forest personnel to justify the action of killing three people at close range, the CID has said What autopsy reports said * According to the autopsy report, Sebastian David Kumar, had two shotgun bullet entry wounds on his body. A shot on the left side of his chest revealed burning/scorching and singeing of chest hair, indicative of a close range gunshot. The shot was fired front to back, above downwards and left to right, the report said. A second shot on his right thigh found burning/ scorching present and charring singeing and soot deposition within and around the wound margins, indicating it was also fired at close range and in a below upwards direction, it said. * Antony Swamy had a gunshot wound on the right side of his lower rib cage from a close range, the report said. The direction of the gunshot was above downwards, front to back and right to left. * John Rose Peter had a single shotgun wound on his neck above the collar bone, fired at close range, with a top down direction. At the time of the incident, the hunters were at a higher point than the department staff at the Karadikalu rocks. Since the hunters were not visible to the department staff they were shot in the upper part of the waist when the staff retaliated. The staff did not act with any malicious intent, Karnataka Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy had said on August 17. The forest department had said the firing incident was the culmination of a night-long search to find poachers on the basis of actionable intelligence. They were conducting searches and when they chanced upon the persons who had come with the intent of poaching, both groups became alert. They have fired and we have fired, Hanur Assistant Conservator of Forest Mariswamy had said. Around 75 metres from the place where they were found, two bags of deer meat were found. It was the meat of the animal they hunted in the night, the Hanur ACF had said. Based on the evidence, it is certain that those who entered the forest were poachers, the Chief Conservator of Forests for Chamarajanagar district, Dr Malathi Priya, had said. A September 20, 1991, order grants immunity to forest personnel whenever they open fire to protect government property and life, but the immunity is subject to conditional use of firearms and reporting norms for shooting incidents.

headline: He stood beside his mahout's body. Five years later, Kerala bids him farewell
content: decades, Pallatt Brahmadathan was a constant presence in temple festivals across Kerala. Only last year, the tusker had carried the thidambu or sacred replica of presiding deity Paramekkavu Devi during the Thrissur Pooram last year. On Monday, scores of people gathered at the premises of its owner, Pallattu Rajesh, at Erattupetta in Kottayam to pay their last tributes to the gentle giant known for its calm demeanour. Brahmadathan, the 54-year-old male elephant, died after being struck by lightning on Sunday evening. As Brahamadathan lay motionless at the Pallatt family compound, flowers and wreaths piled up and sandalwood sticks burned as grieving admirers stood around. Brahmadathans owner Rajesh, his family members, and mahout Sarath grieved inconsolably near the carcass when a crane lifted it for post-mortem examination. Brahmadathan was brought to Kerala 28 years ago from Arunachal Pradesh. His first owner in the state was Pappalaparambil Pothen Varghese of Puthuppally in Kottayam. At that time, it was known as Puthuppally Brahmadathan. Sixteen years ago, the Pallatts, another family of traditional elephant owners in the city, took over its guardianship. Ever since, Brahmadathan had been carrying their family name. Brahamadathans imposing presence at many annual festivals in Keralam had made him a social media star of sorts with a number of its reels being shared widely. Like a family member Recalling his relationship with the elephant, owner Rajesh said, My three brothers and I were managing Brahmadathan. After the festival season, we used to tether him at our house compound. Each time, before he left for a festival procession, Brahmadathan used to greet my aged mother. He had become a member of our family over the years. Rajesh said Brahmadathan was loved by both young and the old alike. I can proudly say that Brahmadathan had never attacked any person in his 28 years of life in Keralam, he said. As Brahmadathan passes into the lore of Keralas domestic elephants, its bond with its mahouts was fondly recalled by elephant lovers. In 2021, when his previous mahout Damodaran Nair alias Omanachettan died, Brahmadathan had stood beside his body. It was seen raising its trunk towards Omanachettan, giving a final farewell to the man who had been his shadow for 25 years.

headline: Trump Ditches Taxpayer Funds, Says He'll Fund Midterm Ads With His Own Money After Flak
content: Trump said he would fund the ads with money raised for his political organisation, MAGA Inc., rather than public funds. US President Donald Trump on Monday said he would pay for political advertisements ahead of Novembers midterm elections with his own money, backing away from the use of taxpayer funds after facing criticism from both Republicans and Democrats. Trump said he would fund the ads with money raised for his political organisation, MAGA Inc., rather than public funds. - 'Shove It Up Their A**': Trump's Profane Remarks Targeting Democrats Raises Eyebrows At Ohio Rally - Im Getting Good At It: Trump On Possible Third Impeachment If Democrats Win US Midterm Elections - Opinion | How Communists Have Started Losing The Culture War In West Bengal - 'They'll Be Hit Very Hard': Trump Warns Iran With Fresh Strikes If Linked To Flydubai Attack This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The move follows criticism over a $20 million advertising campaign run through the US Department of Homeland Security, with critics accusing Trump of using government money to promote himself and his political message. Trump defends patriotic ads The White House has defended the advertisements as public service announcements aimed at promoting patriotism and national pride. One recent advert, aired during an NFL game, showed Trump warning of a final battle" against what he described as communists, Marxists and fascists. Another featured Trump declaring that America would never be a communist country". The adverts carry an onscreen message saying they were Paid for by the US Government". The White House has argued that the campaign is not political because Trump is not on the ballot and the adverts contain no direct call to vote. Bipartisan backlash over taxpayer money The use of public money has nevertheless drawn criticism from both sides of the political divide. Republican Senator John Kennedy had said the government could not use public funds to promote the president, while Democratic Senator John Hickenlooper described the adverts as propaganda". Democratic Representative Mike Levin also criticised the campaign, saying taxpayers were being made to pay for it. Trump has previously urged Republican voters to pretend that Im on the ballot" during the midterm elections. The White House has compared the adverts with public information campaigns run by previous administrations, including Covid vaccination messages under former President Joe Biden and wartime campaigns under Franklin Roosevelt. (With inputs from agencies) President Donald Trump announced he will pay for political advertisements ahead of the November midterm elections using his own money raised for his political organization, MAGA Inc., instead of relying on public funds.

headline: Jeffrey Archer, Bestselling British Novelist And Former Politician, Dies At 86
content: Archer died "suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions", his publisher said. British novelist and former Conservative politician Jeffrey Archer, whose best-selling books made him a household name while his political career was overshadowed by scandal and a prison sentence, died suddenly at 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday. Archer died suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions", the publisher said. His editor, Kate Elton, described him as a master storyteller and an editors dream". - Inside Jeffrey Archers Final Novel Adam & Eve: A Love Story With A Twist Of History - Jeffrey Archers Life Was Stranger Than Fiction: Bankruptcy, Prison And 300 Million Books - He Wrote About Abba In A Quiver Full Of Arrows: Soha Ali Khan Remembers Jeffrey Archer - Jeffrey Archer Spent 2 Years In Prison, These Are 4 Lessons He Learnt As A Jailbird He had been due to appear at the Cheltenham Literary Festival this week to discuss Adam and Eve, which he had called his final novel after five decades of writing. The book was due to be published Tuesday. From MP to best-selling author Archer entered politics early, joining the Conservative Party while studying at Oxford University. In 1969, aged 29, he won a by-election and became one of Britains youngest MPs. His parliamentary career ended in 1974 after the collapse of a Canadian investment left him facing financial ruin. He turned to writing, publishing Not A Penny More, Not A Penny Less in 1975. The book launched a hugely successful literary career. His novels, often centred on politics, money, ambition and betrayal, eventually sold more than 300 million copies worldwide, according to his website. His political fortunes also recovered. In 1985, then-prime minister Margaret Thatcher appointed him Conservative deputy chairman. He later became a member of the House of Lords. Scandal and prison sentence Archers career was repeatedly hit by controversy. In 1986, he resigned as deputy chairman after admitting paying 2,000 to prostitute Monica Coghlan, while insisting the money was intended to help her leave the country. His political comeback ended in 1999 when he abandoned his campaign to become the first elected mayor of London after allegations that he had arranged a false alibi in his earlier libel case against the Daily Star. In 2001, Archer was convicted of perjury and perverting the course of justice and sentenced to four years in prison. He was released on parole in 2003. Despite the scandals, he continued writing and publishing until his death. Archer retired from the House of Lords in 2024. (With inputs from agencies) Jeffrey Archer died suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions at the age of 86, according to his publisher HarperCollins.

headline: From Riyadh Airport To Aramco Refinery: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia
content: Yemen's Houthis Claim Strikes Across Saudi Arabia Houthis said the strikes targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Aramco refinery in Rabigh and military sites and smaller airports in southern Saudi Arabia. Yemens Iran-backed Houthis on Monday claimed a wave of drone and missile attacks on targets across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadhs international airport and an Aramco refinery. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had used drones as well as ballistic and cruise missiles in the attacks. He said the strikes targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Aramco refinery in Rabigh and military sites and smaller airports in southern Saudi Arabia. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat - Pakistan Expands Military Footprint In Saudi Arabia As Houthi Conflict Escalates | Exclusive Loud explosions were heard over Riyadh late Monday, shortly after earlier blasts were reported in the Saudi capital, AFP reported. Saudi authorities have yet to comment on the Houthi claims or confirm any damage. Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets The claims came as the Saudi-led coalition intensified its military campaign against the Houthis in Yemen. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said Saudi naval forces had carried out strikes on military targets" in the Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast. He said the operation destroyed weapons depots, facilities holding booby-trapped boats and naval mines, while also preventing a planned attack on shipping routes in the southern Red Sea. The escalation follows a major offensive by Yemens internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia. Yemeni forces said they had carried out more than 1,000 strikes and begun an operation towards Sanaa, the Houthi-held capital. Pakistan, Turkey pledge Saudi military support The latest fighting comes after the Houthis seized large areas of territory along Yemens Red Sea coast and near the Bab al-Mandab Strait last month. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has secured military backing from Pakistan and Turkey under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, with Islamabad and Ankara agreeing to deploy forces to the kingdom under the pact to help defend its territory. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government has vowed to retake Houthi-held territory, much of which has remained under the groups control for more than a decade. (With inputs from agencies) Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched a wave of drone and missile attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Aramco refinery in Rabigh, and military sites and smaller airports in southern Saudi Arabia.

headline: 'Age Of Flux': Jaishankar Warns Of Turbulent Times, Says India Will 'Rise To Challenges'
content: Jaishankar said geopolitical tensions were creating new challenges for countries, from energy and food security to fertilisers and trade. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday said the world was entering an age of flux", marked by conflicts, uncertainty and tariff volatility, but expressed confidence that India would be able to navigate the choppy waters" ahead. Speaking at the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave, Jaishankar said geopolitical tensions were creating new challenges for countries, from energy and food security to fertilisers and trade. - 'Moving Beyond Advocacy': Jaishankar Confirms India-Led 'Ongoing Discussions' To End Ukraine War - 'Can't Pretend Things Are Normal With Oil Prices Hitting $100': Jaishankar On Global Energy Shock - 'Moving Beyond Advocacy': Jaishankar Confirms India-Led 'Ongoing Discussions' To End Ukraine War - 'US Becoming Lonelier Power By Choice': Jaishankar Flags 'Radical Repositioning' Of America This is going to be an age of flux, as you call it. And it is going to be turbulent and volatile, with uncertainties. We are seeing two major conflicts, we are seeing other frictions. As I said, there is the pressure of non-market factors, there is tariff volatility," he said. India backs dialogue on Ukraine Jaishankar said India continued to engage with both Russia and Ukraine and maintained that the conflict could not be resolved on the battlefield. From the very start, we have always held that this conflict in Ukraine is unlikely to be resolved in the battlefield," he said, stressing that dialogue and diplomacy" remained the best path towards a settlement. He recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modis meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his own visit to Kyiv, where he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Ukrainian officials. We still keep in touch with both sides," Jaishankar said, adding that efforts to promote peace were worth pursuing because of the concerns of the Global South. He also criticised peace gatherings that exclude Russia, asking: What is the point of having a gathering on the Ukraine conflict, where Russia is not there?" Choppy waters need careful response Jaishankar said India had faced major disruptions before, including the Covid pandemic and the impact of global conflicts on energy, food and fertiliser supplies. Yes, these are choppy waters," he said. We need to factor them into our thinking, plan and respond that in a sense is the task before us." I am very confident that we will rise to the challenge," he added. He also highlighted Indias role in representing the Global South, saying it expects India to articulate on the world stage". On Indias foreign policy, Jaishankar backed a multi-aligned approach, saying New Delhi should avoid a black-and-white view" of its relationships with major powers. He called the US as a key strategic and defence partner, while stressing the importance of managing ties with China, Russia and Europe. Every relationship net-net is a plus-plus. And therefore, we should really have the confidence of pushing it at every front, knowing that progress on any front makes it easier on other fronts. So it is kind of oppositive of a zero-sum game," he said. (With inputs from PTI) External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar warned that the world is entering a turbulent age of flux defined by conflicts, uncertainty, and tariff volatility. However, he expressed full confidence that India will navigate these choppy waters and successfully rise to the challenges.

headline: 'Why Leave Them There?': Trump Says US Pulled Bombers From UK Air Base Over 'Some Threats'
content: The Pentagon confirmed that all US bombers deployed to RAF Fairford had returned to their home stations in the United States. US President Donald Trump said Monday that Washington had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain after receiving warnings of some threats", without giving details about their nature. There were some threats, and rather than tempting the enemy well capture the enemy and beat the enemy, but why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit," Trump told reporters at the White House, adding that the bombers had been moved not very far". - US Bombers Leave UK Base After Suspected Iran-Linked Terror Plot: What We Know About RAF Fairford - Trump Says He'll Speak To Putin Soon Over Reported Plague Death As US Presses For Transparency - Trump May Announce Executive Order Seeking To Slash Diesel Prices Ahead Of US Midterm Elections - 'How Trump Feels He Is': Iran Mocks US President With Hrithik Roshan Movie Meme The Pentagon confirmed that all US bombers deployed to RAF Fairford had returned to their home stations in the United States. The move came after a security scare near the base and amid reports of a fresh threat linked to Iran. Security scare triggers bomber withdrawal RAF Fairford was placed under heightened security after British police arrested five men near the base on September 27. The arrests followed a report from a local farmer who saw several vans and men acting suspiciously. Counter-terrorism officers found no explosives in the vehicles but recovered petrol. The suspects were later released on bail as the investigation continued. A sixth man, a British-Iranian dual national, was also arrested and released on bail. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there were strong indications" of Iranian involvement, while Tehran has denied any role. US Vice President JD Vance said the decision to move the bombers was taken out of an abundance of caution". Secretary of State Marco Rubio, however, said there was no confirmed direct link between the withdrawal and the suspected plot. Fairfords role in Iran war RAF Fairford has been a key staging point for US heavy bombers during the conflict with Iran. Its location allows American aircraft to operate closer to the Middle East than they could from bases in the US. US officials have not publicly detailed the latest threat. The New York Times, citing American officials, reported that commanders had received new warnings about an Iran-backed plot targeting the base. Iran has previously warned that British bases used to support attacks on Iranian territory could be considered legitimate targets. Tehran has nevertheless rejected allegations that it was behind the suspected plot. (With inputs from agencies) President Donald Trump stated that Washington withdrew all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford after receiving warnings of some threats. The Pentagon confirmed that the aircraft returned to their home stations in the United States following a security scare and reports of a fresh threat linked to Iran.

headline: Pakistan, Turkey To Send Forces To Saudi Arabia As Houthi Attacks Mount
content: The decision was announced after an emergency meeting in Riyadh on Monday attended by senior officials from the three countries. Pakistan and Turkey will move towards the rapid deployment of troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, as the kingdom faces escalating attacks from Yemens Houthis. The decision was announced after an emergency meeting in Riyadh on Monday attended by senior officials from the three countries, including Pakistans Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif. - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat - Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat | - 'Pakistan, Turkey Playing Supportive Role, Saudi Leading Houthi Combat': Mecca Pact Structure Formalised In a joint statement, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey reaffirmed their unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the Kingdoms security and territorial integrity." They also agreed to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom". The trilateral mutual-defence agreement, signed in August, commits the three countries to support one another if any member comes under attack. The pact brings together Turkey, which has NATOs second-largest military, Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed country in the Muslim world, and Saudi Arabia, a key Gulf power. Troop role remains unclear The three countries said they would take the necessary steps to provide agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment" in Saudi Arabia. However, they did not specify how many troops would be sent or what role they would perform once deployed. The move comes as Saudi Arabia faces repeated attacks from the Houthis, who have targeted cities, oil facilities and shipping routes since fighting in Yemen intensified again. The security situation has also worsened in recent months. In September, the Houthis launched an offensive that captured large areas from Yemens Saudi-backed government. Riyadh-backed forces launched a counteroffensive on Monday, seeking to recover territory held by the Houthis, including areas under their control for more than a decade. (With inputs from AFP) Pakistan and Turkey are swiftly deploying troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement following escalating attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement against the kingdom's cities, oil facilities, and shipping routes.

headline: Chief Secy should ask District Collectors to instruct officials to follow Union Govt.'s guidelines on protocols: MP
content: Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi general secretary and Villupuram M.P. D. Ravikumar, on Monday urged the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary to ensure that the instructions issued by the Union Government regarding how Members of Parliament should be treated be followed and that District Collectors should instruct Officials of Revenue and other departments to follow them. In a statement, Mr. Ravikumar said that an order issued on January 12, 2026, states that MPs representing the area must be invited to public functions organised by a Government office. In accordance with the Protocol, due consideration should be given to the fact that Members of Parliament rank above officers of the level of Secretaries to the Government of India and accordingly, proper and convenient seating arrangements should be made for them at public functions, and the appropriate order of seating on the dais should be followed, he pointed out. He added, In invitations and media events organised for functions taking place within a constituency, the names of the Members representing that constituency who have confirmed their participation in the events may be included. If the constituency of any Member of Parliament extends across more than one district, the Member of Parliament must invariably be invited to all functions held in the districts that form part of his or her constituency.

headline: Veeramani's drivers held on charges of abetment
content: Central Crime Branch (CCB) on Monday arrested three drivers working for Gem Granites Veeramani for alleged abetment in connection with the sexual offences cases against the industrialist, the police said. Four cases had already been registered against Veeramani, and another case was registered on October 2. Investigation is under way in all five cases. During the investigation, the police identified Veeramanis drivers Lazar, Parthiban, and Babu as allegedly having assisted him by bringing minor girls to him. The police said Lazar had worked for Veeramani for 23 years, while Babu had been employed for eight years. Parthiban was working as his driver. The police also conducted searches at the residences of the three accused in connection with their alleged role in facilitating Veeramanis offences. Eight mobile phones and 55 documents were seized. Further investigation is on

headline: There should be no GST on MDR for UPI transactions: C. Rangarajan
content: The GST Council should come out with a clear statement that it would not levy tax on the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) fees to be paid by the merchants for UPI transactions above 2,000, C. Rangarajan, former Governor, Reserve Bank of India, said here on Monday. I would urge that the GST Council, which is meeting in one or two days from now, must clearly come out and say that GST should not be levied, he said, at the launch of a book on 10 years of UPI roll out. The new UPI Payment Rules 2026 stipulates a 0.4% MDR fee for person-to-merchant transactions above 2,000 from October 15, 2026. While maintaining that there were no ground rules over pricing of public good, Dr. Rangarajan wondered whether it was the correct time to levy MDR, when 75% of the UPI transactions were below 2,000. Perhaps one could have waited for some more time and then levied charges after it has completely taken roots, he said. In the 10 years of its existence, UPI has progressed well in the country through the good work put up by the National Payments Corporation of India (NCPI). He, however, said that there was a cost involved in running the system and it must be recouped. It can be recouped at a time when it is really considered to be appropriate. Soumya Swaminathan, Chair, M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation, and former Chief Scientist, World Health Organisation, cautioned about financial exclusion of people due to the digital divide. She said it was well known that the gender divide was quite high in terms of digital access, especially among the lower socio-economic groups. While AI brings with it scope in several disciplines, such as education, health, agriculture, or climate resilience, we have to keep in mind are we reaching everybody or are we further excluding those who are excluded from the system. Deep divides on gender and social equity exist today and it was important to track those metrics as the country expands its digital public infrastructure, she added. V. Kamamoti, Director, IIT-M, said that the roll out of UPI demonstrated three things scale, equity, and democratisation of opportunity. The book Cashless Nation: How UPI Changed Everything is authored by Santanu Paul, computer scientist and entrepreneur and an IIT-M alumnus, and B. Sambamurthy, a retired banker and former Chairman of NPCI. It throws light on the various institutional, policy, and regulatory aspects of UPI as also the contestations, between banks and fintechs for example, and how the NPCI resolved all those. Sundaraman Ramamurthy, MD and CEO, Bombay Stock Exchange, and Ashwin Mahalingam, Dean Alumni and Corporate Relations, IIT-M, also spoke.

headline: SC Quashes HC's Rs 5 Lakh Compensation Order Against Maharashtra FDA In Pune Sweet Shop Case
content: The Supreme Court set aside a Bombay High Court order directing the Maharashtra FDA to pay Rs. 5 lakh compensation to a Pune dairy, ruling the food safety action was lawful. The Supreme Court has set aside a Bombay High Court direction requiring Maharashtras Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to pay 5 lakh compensation to a Pune-based dairy and sweets establishment, holding that the food safety action was taken in the interest of public health and within the statutory framework. The case concerns State of Maharashtra & Ors. v. M/s. Gurunanak Dairy & Sweets, arising from action taken by the FDA after a complaint of food poisoning. The dispute centred on the suspension of the establishments food licence following an inspection in which officials found deficiencies relating to hygiene, maintenance of records, labelling and personal hygiene of employees. The State maintained that the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, after a sample of Malai Pedha was found to be unsafe. On June 12, 2026, Food Safety Officers from the FDAs Pune unit inspected the establishment following the complaint and collected the food sample for analysis. The licence was subsequently suspended. The proprietor challenged the action before the Commissioner, FDA, through a statutory appeal filed on June 15. The establishment later submitted a compliance report on July 9. According to the State, the FDA conducted a reinspection just four days later, on July 13, after receiving the compliance report. The matter then reached the Bombay High Court through Writ Petition No. 9905 of 2026. On August 17, the High Court revoked the suspension of the food licence and also directed the FDA to deposit 5 lakh as compensation for the business losses allegedly suffered by the establishment. The Maharashtra government challenged the compensation direction before the Supreme Court. It argued that the FDA had acted after an unsafe food sample was detected and that the inspection had revealed several regulatory deficiencies. The State also submitted that the statutory appeal filed by the establishment was pending before the Commissioner and had been reserved for orders. The government further argued that there was no material to show that the FDA had acted maliciously, arbitrarily or with an intention to cause financial loss to the business. It maintained that the time taken during the statutory process could not, by itself, justify imposing compensation on the government. After considering the submissions, the Supreme Court set aside the Bombay High Courts direction requiring the FDA to pay 5 lakh and quashed the compensation order. The ruling leaves the compensation direction against the Maharashtra FDA set aside while recognising that regulatory action taken on the basis of food safety deficiencies and an unsafe food sample was within the statutory framework. The Supreme Court set aside the 5 lakh compensation order, holding that the Maharashtra FDA's food safety action against the Pune sweet shop was executed within the statutory framework and in the interest of public health.

headline: Animal welfare groups seek clarity over transfer of five Assam elephants to Tamil Nadu
content: A group of 53 animal welfare, wildlife, and conservation organisations has urged the Tamil Nadu government to examine the ownership, acquisition, and age records of five young elephants transferred from Assam to temples and religious institutions in Tamil Nadu. In a joint representation to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and other authorities, the organisations sought clarity on whether the elephants Durga, Rupsing, Shiva, Hiralal, and Bijuli were gifted, purchased or transferred. They also sought the verification of their birth dates, Ownership Certificates, acquisition documents, no-objection certificates, and identification records. Ownership Certificates The groups have raised questions over the chronology of the records, noting that the Ownership Certificates for three elephants were issued only in October-November 2025, despite their recorded dates of birth being several years earlier. They have also questioned the validity of Rupsings Ownership Certificate, which they claim is about seven years old, despite a five-year renewal requirement. The organisations said they had also been informed that six more young elephants would soon be transported from Assam to Tamil Nadu, and called for such transfers to be paused until the five existing cases are examined. Veterinary assessment They have sought an independent veterinary assessment of the elephants following their 3,000-km journey, as well as a scrutiny of their proposed use in temple rituals and processions. The signatories include People for Cattle in India, Animal Welfare Board-linked groups, wildlife conservation organisations, and animal protection groups from Tamil Nadu, Assam, Karnataka, Keralam, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Goa, and Haryana.

headline: Madurantakam, Dharapuram go to polls for second time in six months
content: Madurantakam (SC)and Dharapuram (SC) Assembly Constituencies will go to polls for the second time in six months on Tuesday. Over 2.13 lakh voters will exercise their franchise in Madurantakam (SC) constituency. Out of the 2.13 lakh electors, 1.08 lakhs are women. The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of AIADMK MLA Maragatham Kumaravel, who is now contesting as the TVK candidate. The DMK has put up its former Egmore MLA I. Paranthamen, while the AIADMK has brought back S. Kanitha Sampath, who had won the seat in 2011. The CPI(M), although extending outside support to the TVK-led government, is contesting independently and has put up P. Suganthi of the Tamil Nadu Untouchability Eradication Front. Chengalpattu Collector M. Veerappan said polling materials and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) have been dispatched to all 285 polling stations on Monday. A mock poll would be held at 5.30 a.m. on Tuesday before polling begins at 7 a.m. Sixty polling stations have been identified as vulnerable. There would be a micro-observer deputed by the Election Commission (EC) in each of the polling stations. The Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel have been stationed at 60 locations in the constituency, Dr. Veerappan added. Till Monday, polling officials seized cash, precious metals such as gold, freebies such as saris and towels, and liquor bottles, worth 2.53 crore in total. All 167 polling locations will have wheelchair facility for persons with disabilities, the Collector said. Besides, pandals have been set up at polling locations for shade, and drinking water facilities have been made available. Each polling station will have live web streaming through two cameras, one inside the station, and another outside facing the queue. Out of 931 postal ballots dispatched to persons with disabilities and those aged above 80, 893 have been received. Elaborate arrangements have been made for the byelection in the Dharapuram (SC) constituency, with 320 polling stations set up at 186 centres. Polling will be held from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. The constituency has 2,23,306 voters 1,07,285 men, 1,16,013 women, and 27 service voters. Voter information slips have been distributed to 2,21,365 voters, accounting for 99.13% of the electorate. Of the 1,236 applications received from voters aged above 85 and persons with more than 40% disability for home voting, 1,201 have exercised their franchise through postal ballots. A total of 1,536 polling personnel have been deployed. Security and surveillance have been intensified for the bypoll. General, Expenditure, and Police Observers have also been deployed by the Election Commission. The constituency has 18 vulnerable polling stations spread across nine locations. CCTV cameras will be used for live monitoring at these stations, with additional Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel deployment and micro-observers to oversee polling. The 384 EVMs being used for the election have been prepared with the symbols and photographs of the contesting candidates. Officials said non-voters from outside the constituency, who had come to campaign for candidates, were required to leave the constituency by 6 p.m. on Sunday, when campaigning ended. The police have been checking hotels, marriage halls, and other accommodations, while checkposts have been set up on the constituencys borders. After polling, the EVMs and election records will be moved to the strongroom at the LRG Government Arts and Science College in Tiruppur and will be put under a three-tier security arrangement. Counting will take place at the college on October 9, with 14 tables for EVM counting and two for postal ballots. The counting centre will have three-tier security involving the local police, State Armed Police, and the CISF. The State government has declared a public holiday in both constituencies on Tuesday on account of the byelection. An order issued by Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar said employees working in Chengalpattu, Tiruppur, and neighbouring districts, but registered as voters in Madurantakam and Dharapuram, should also be given a paid holiday.

headline: Ram Madhav takes part in meeting of BJP functionaries in Chennai
content: BJP leader Ram Madhav, who has been named as State in-charge for Tamil Nadu, took part in a meeting of party functionaries at the partys State unit head office in Chennai on Monday. BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran, and State and district-level functionaries were also present. Talking to reporters, BJP leader Pon. Radhakrishnan said Mr. Madhav and the partys co-in-charges for the State Nirmal Kumar Surana and D.K. Aruna took part in the meeting, on the directions of the partys national leadership. Mr. Radhakrishnan was hopeful that his party would emerge successful in all the upcoming elections. The BJP will organise events in all State district headquarters on October 7 to mark BJP leader and Prime Minister Narendra Modis 25 years in public service, Mr. Radhakrishnan said. He also hailed the leadership of Mr. Modi.

headline: Families of three labourers who died while cleaning septic tank in Ariyalur refuse to accept bodies
content: Families of the three labourers, who suffocated to death on October 2 after entering a septic tank in a house under construction at Sendurai in Ariyalur district, have refused to receive the bodies after an autopsy and demanded 30 lakh as compensation for each victims from the State government. The CPI(M), Tamil Nadu Untouchability Eradication Front (TNUEF), and the Annihilation of Hazardous Sewerage Killings, a people science movement, have extended their support to the families. The deceased were identified as K. Bhaskar, 42, of Srinivasapuram in Tiruvarur district; K. Dhinakaran, 60, of Alivalam village in Tiruvarur district, and K. Ramachandran, 45, of Nakkambadi village in Ariyalur district. Dhinakaran who entered the septic tank first to remove wooden planks/supporting framework fixed inside fell unconscious and died. Bhaskar and Ramachandran who went to his rescue, one after another, also died. The Sendurai police arrested the building owner M. Subramanian of Sendurai. He was remanded in judicial custody. The autopsy was conducted at the Government Hospital, Ariyalur, but the victims families have refused to receive the bodies, said police and CPI(M) sources. The party, along with the TNUEF, has been holding talks with officials demanding 30 lakh as compensation for the families. However, no headway has been made. The three labourers hail from a poor background and hence the State government should provide each family a sum Rs. 30 lakh as compensation, said Udhayan, State organiser of the Annihilation of Hazardous Sewerage Killings-Sarinigar. Mr. Udhayan said he visited Ariyalur on Saturday and Sunday and interacted with the family members of the victims. Citing a Supreme Court judgment of 2023, Mr. Udhayan said the compensation for sewer deaths shall be Rs. 30 lakhs and shall be paid by the Union, Union Territory or the State government as the case may be. Their other demands include government jobs for one of the family members of the labourers, for the government to bear the educational expense for the labourers children, and grant either a free house or a house site patta to the three families. Mr. Udhayan said a fact finding team would soon be sent to Ariyalur, and a report would be submitted to the State government. A group of CPI(M) and TNUEF members, who allegedly tried to stage a protest at the Ariyalur Collectorate, on Monday were detained, the police said.

headline: Trump May Announce Executive Order Seeking To Slash Diesel Prices Ahead Of US Midterm Elections
content: Trump may promote the measures during a campaign appearance in Nebraska. Earlier on Friday, Trump said he would not move ahead with a proposed ban on diesel exports. US President Donald Trump is expected to unveil executive measures aimed at easing fuel costs, which have emerged as a political concern for Republicans ahead of the midterm elections, Politico reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. Trump is set to promote the measures during a campaign appearance in Nebraska. High diesel prices, along with his decision to boost foreign beef imports ahead of November, have sparked frustration among farmers and ranchers during the crucial harvest season. The issue has gained attention in both Republican strongholds and battleground states. - 'I Offered Them Nothing': Trump Rejects Report On Iran Sanctions Relief, Frozen Funds; Calls It 'Hoax' - One Of The Most Important Things We Did: Trump Says Iran War Will End Very Soon - Trump Says US Will Win Iran War 'Very Soon', Inflation Will Be 'Eradicated' Once It Ends - US-Iran War Live Updates: Iran Says It Received US Response To Latest Ceasefire Proposal The announcement follows weeks of mixed signals from the administration over diesel prices. On Friday, Trump said he would not move ahead with a proposed ban on diesel exports, despite repeatedly indicating that such a step was under consideration, the report mentioned. The measures include a Treasury Department review of certain diesel-related taxes and an order directing states to expand access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is widely used by farmers and construction workers. States would also be encouraged to suspend some fuel taxes. Some Republican governors have already introduced similar measures. The White House has been considering the steps as fuel prices rise amid the war involving Iran and Israeli forces and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. Higher diesel costs have added pressure on farmers and contributed to inflation. However, some Republicans oppose suspending fuel taxes, arguing that states rely on the revenue to fund infrastructure projects. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said Trump would announce additional short-term assistance for farmers in Nebraska. Ten states representing about a third of US diesel sales had expanded access to dyed diesel by Friday, while some had also waived taxes on fuel used by agricultural vehicles. AAA said average diesel prices fell to $6.32 a gallon on Monday, but remained significantly above last years level. Fuel analyst Patrick De Haan said federal action could benefit road users but would offer limited relief to farmers already using tax-exempt diesel. It could save on-road users ~60c/gal," De Haan said in a social media post on X. But farmers already use dyed diesel and are still paying record prices. Taxes arent the problem, supply is." Denton Cinquegrana, chief oil analyst at Dow Jones Energy, warned that suspending fuel taxes could hurt transportation funding in the longer term. When youre not collecting taxes, youre just kicking the can down the road, because you have to fix roads and stuff like that," Cinquegrana said. The proposed executive measures include a Treasury Department review of certain diesel-related taxes and an order directing states to expand access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel used by farmers and construction workers. States would also be encouraged to suspend specific fuel taxes to help lower costs.

headline: Israel Was Prepared To Shoot Down Flydubai Plane With 150 Israelis Aboard After Cockpit Attack: Report
content: After the plane plunged 14,000 feet after the cockpit attack, the Israeli Air Force tried to contact the cockpit but got no answer, prompting Israel to scramble fighter jets. After an Omani pilot stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight last week, Israeli authorities faced a tough choice of shooting down the flight despite having more than 150 Israelis aboard. Two Israeli sources with direct knowledge of the situation told CBS News that Israel was prepared to shoot down the flight after the captain was attacked with a crash axe in the cockpit. Israel has a long-practised procedure for this kind of possible 9/11-style event, they said. - Opinion | 34,000 Ft Terror: Israels Victim Or Aggressor Question Returns - Smit Machchhar Hailed By PM Modi | Speaks To Pilots Parents After Flydubai Crisis | - It Couldve Been: Trump Says Iran Could Be Linked To Omani Pilot Who Stabbed Capt Smit - First Visuals Of Injured Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar Surface After Flydubai Cockpit Attack After the plane plunged 14,000 feet following the attack, the Israeli Air Force tried to contact the cockpit but got no answer. A command centre was established and Israels airspace was closed, while fighter jets were scrambled to take stock of the situation. Israel called back its jet once the plane turned towards Saudi Arabia, prompting Riyadh to scramble its own jets. Eventually, the captain managed to unlock the cockpit door, and a group of Israeli passengers and Flydubai staff restrained the co-pilot. What Were Israels Options? As per the CBS News report, if the flight had gotten within a certain distance of the Ben Gurion International Airport, Israel would have sent jets into Jordanian airspace to investigate. The Israeli fighter pilots would have gotten as close as possible to inspect the cockpit and try to make visual contact with the pilot to assess the situation. If there appeared to be panic in the cabin, the pilots would relay their findings to the Air Force and a pre-established committee. If it was determined that the plane was hijacked and the potential hijackers maintained radio silence, the committee would contact the Israeli Prime Minister and Defence Minister. Israel has a policy of shooting down a rogue aircraft, but only the Prime Minister is authorised to make that decision. The Israeli sources said that shooting down the passenger jet would be considered better than many hundreds being killed if the plane slammed into Israels prominent Azrieli buildings, the airport or another high-value target." The Omani co-pilot, identified as Hammam Al-Hammami, is currently in the United Arab Emirates, where he is undergoing a second round of interrogation after first being questioned by Saudi authorities when the plane made its emergency landing. Israel has sent its own representatives to the UAE to participate in the investigation. The Jerusalem Post reported that al-Hammami had researched airlines flying to Israel and had even visited the country months before the cockpit attack. I tried to get hired by all the airlines," he reportedly told investigators. I checked which ones flew to Tel Aviv. Thats why I chose flydubai. I planned [the operation] even before I was hired." Mossad and Israels security agency, Shin Bet, have faced criticism over an alleged failure to properly vet the pilot. Israel and Oman do not have diplomatic relations. According to the reports, only pilots holding passports from countries with which Israel has diplomatic relations can land at Israeli airports. Israel prepared to shoot down the Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight after the Omani co-pilot stabbed the Indian captain in the cockpit and the plane plunged 14,000 feet. Authorities feared a 9/11-style attack targeting high-value locations such as the Azrieli buildings or Ben Gurion International Airport.

headline: British Airways Flight To Chicago Declares Emergency, Dumps 30 Tonnes Fuel, Returns To Heathrow
content: tracking data showed the Boeing 777 descend suddenly from around 37,000 feet to approximately 9,000 feet before turning back towards London. British Airways flight BA295 has just landed at London Heathrow after burning 30 tonnes of fuel, according to aviation news network AIRLIVE. SQUID 38 and SQUID 43, Heathrow Airports emergency ground vehicles, met the British Airways aircraft at the terminal immediately after landing. The flight, which was travelling from London Heathrow to Chicago, earlier declared an emergency while flying over Ireland and transmitted the 7700 emergency code. Flight-tracking data showed the Boeing 777 descend from around 37,000 feet to approximately 9,000 feet in 9.5 minutes in a stable descent before turning back towards Heathrow. - British Airways Flight BA295 Emergency Over Ireland | London-Chicago Flight | Emergency | - British Airways London-Chicago Flight Declares Emergency Over Ireland, Descends To 9,000 Feet - Pilot Attacked Mid-Air: FlyDubai Flight Plunges, Terror Motive Under Investigation | Raw Report - First Images From Flydubai Flight Show Passenger In Blood-Soaked T-Shirt After Cockpit Fight The initial ACARS message from the crew stated, WE ARE RETURNING TO LHR DUE PRESS PROBLEM. CAB ALT REACHED 10500. NO MEANS OF JETT FUEL 30T OVER MLW" . This means the flight crew is returning to London Heathrow Airport (LHR) because they are experiencing a cabin pressurization issue. The cabin altitude has reached 10,500 feet, and they cannot dump (jettison) fuel, meaning the aircrafts current weight is 30 metric tonnes over its Maximum Landing Weight (MLW)." However, the crew has somehow been successful in jettisoning its fuel over the Bristol Channel. What is an ACARS Message? An ACARS message is a short digital text message sent between an aircraft and ground stations via ACARS (Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System). now making its way back to Heathrow after lowering fuel weight. Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) October 5, 2026 According to Flightradar24, the aircraft circled over the Bristol Channel for around 45 minutes. London Heathrow is preparing for the aircrafts emergency landing. The flight is now making its way back to Heathrow after reducing its fuel load, with the aircrafts current position over Cardiff, United Kingdom. The flight departed London Heathrow at 12.14 pm GMT. The reason for the emergency has not yet been officially confirmed. More details are awaited. The British Airways flight that declared an emergency while en route to Chicago was flight BA295.

headline: TVK MLA causes a flutter, upset at Congress MP getting to light the lamp ahead of him at community baby shower ceremony in Tiruchi
content: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagams Tiruverumbur MLA, Navalpattu S. Viji, caused a flutter when he seemingly tried to take away a candle from Congress Rajya Sabha Member Christopher Tilak while he was about to light a traditional lamp at a Samuthaya Valaikappu (community baby shower) organised here on Monday (October 6, 2026) by the Department of Social Welfare. Upset at Mr. Tilak being handed the candle ahead of him, after HR&CE Minister S. Ramesh, the District Collector, and other TVK MLAs had lit the lamp, Mr. Viji tried to get hold of the candle held by the MP, while gesticulating and making a point. In the melee, the wax candle with flame fell down. Mr. Ramesh and officials quickly intervened and pacified Mr. Viji and asked him to light the lamp. Speaking to reporters after the event, Mr. Ramesh tried to downplay the incident, claiming that the MLA was only insisting on following the protocol. He dismissed suggestions that there was a rift among the TVK members and those who joined the ruling party from the AIADMK or its allies. You should have seen us work [in the byelection campaign] in Dharapuram. We all worked together as siblings, and we are united by love. Do not try to create unnecessary confusion, he said in response to a question. He denied that the TVK had distributed cash to voters in the run-up to the byelections. I do not want to respond to unsubstantiated charges, Mr. Ramesh said, commenting on CPI(M) State secretary P. Shanmughams allegation that the TVK had distributed cash to voters. If there is proof, let them take action. Are there any complaints from the public? he wondered, when pressed further. He maintained that the TVK had sought the votes of the people honestly. He dismissed DMK president M.K. Stalins and AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswamis claims that the public mood had turned against the TVK owing to the rise in the prices of essential commodities and power tariff. He recalled that Mr. Stalin had said the TVK would not even win a single seat in the 2026 Assembly election. The Opposition leaders were claiming that the party would get 3%-5% votes at best, but the TVK was voted to power. There is no public sentiment against the TVK; the people are keen to ensure the victory of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay again and again, he said, claiming that the Opposition had tried to set a narrative by orchestrating a few instances of sloganeering.

headline: 'We Knew That Guy Was A Problem': JD Vance Questions How FlyDubai Omani Co-Pilot Got Back In Cockpit
content: The FlyDubai incident has also raised broader questions about how different aviation security systems operate when a pilot moves between airlines or countries. US Vice President JD Vance has raised questions over how the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a FlyDubai flight, Smit Machchhar, was allowed to return to the cockpit despite previous concerns about him. Vance said the case raised questions about aviation security and pilot screening. If you look historically, that person should not have been flying an airline," he said. - 'Circumstances Being Probed': Flydubai Refuses To Divulge Identity Of Smit Machchhar's Omani Co-Pilot - Stabbed Flydubai Indian Pilot Stable After Surgery At Saudi Hospital Following Cockpit Attack - Flydubai Passengers Refuse To Free Omani Co-Pilot, Say Will Only Hand Him To Police In Video - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views | The remarks came as more details emerged about Hamam al-Hammami, who attacked the captain of the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight with a cockpit axe and attempted to bring the aircraft down. Co-pilot had reportedly been grounded in Oman According to the information provided, Oman had previously grounded Hamam al-Hammami over concerns about extremist views. He later left Oman Air and was hired by FlyDubai. He subsequently ended up flying an aircraft carrying 182 people to Israel. The sequence has raised questions over how concerns that had earlier resulted in him being grounded were dealt with when he moved to another airline. Vance directly addressed the issue while discussing the FlyDubai incident. We KNEW that guy was a problem not the U.S., but historically, that person should NOT have been flying an airline," Vance said. The comments put the focus on whether information about the co-pilots previous history was adequately shared or considered before he was allowed to fly for FlyDubai. Nobody made sure he stayed out of one The FlyDubai incident has also raised broader questions about how different aviation security systems operate when a pilot moves between airlines or countries. The information provided on the case states that someone had previously identified enough concerns about Hamammi to take him out of a cockpit, but he was later able to return to commercial aviation. He allegedly attacked the captain with a cockpit axe after boarding the Israel-bound flight and allegedly attempted to bring the aircraft down. The incident has therefore shifted attention towards the pilot vetting process and how previous security concerns were handled. Vance also said the US was reviewing procedures to prevent people considered flight risks from getting control of an aircraft. Thats the story of the 9/11 terrorist attack, is that we brought a lot of people into the United States of America who shouldnt have been here and certainly shouldnt have been flying plane," Vance said. Vance says no conclusion on Iran link Vance was also asked about a possible connection between the FlyDubai co-pilot and Iran. He said he did not want to get ahead of any announcements and would defer to John Ratcliffe and intelligence officials on the issue. In terms of involvement with Iran thats something I defer to John Ratcliffe and some of the intelligence folks on. I dont want to get ahead of any announcements there, but its certainly something were looking at, but I wouldnt say Ive seen anything conclusive just yet," Vance said. His remarks indicate that the US is examining a possible Iran connection, but that no conclusion has been reached. Hamam al-Hammami had previously been grounded in Oman due to concerns regarding his extremist views before eventually being hired by FlyDubai and flying a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.

headline: Keralam to install Rs 10 sanitary napkin vending machines at public places
content: Sanitary napkins will soon be available through vending machines at select public places in Keralam, with the Women and Child Development Department launching an initiative aimed at improving access to menstrual hygiene products for women and girls during travel. The initiative, called WOMN Women on the Move & Menstrual Need-s, will begin on Tuesday as part of the state governments 100-day action programme, according to an official press release. As part of the pilot project, sanitary napkin vending machines and incinerators will be installed at 14 KSRTC terminals and depots across the state, the release said. Each packet will contain three sanitary napkins and will cost Rs. 10. Incinerators will be provided at the locations to facilitate the disposal of used sanitary napkins, it said. The project will subsequently target major tourist destinations, KSRTC terminals and depots and other public places across the state, according to the department. Women and Child Development Minister Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the project at the Thampanoor KSRTC Bus Terminal in Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday. (With PTI inputs)
