headline: Why Has No Chief Election Commissioner Ever Been Impeached In India & What Does It Actually Take To Remove CEC?
content: According to Article 324(5) of the Constitution, a CEC can only be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge A Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) has never been impeached in India because the constitutional bar is set exceptionally high, deliberately designed to protect the independence of the Election Commission of India (ECI) from political or executive interference. While controversies surrounding past CECs like T.N. Seshan and current political friction involving the current CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, have led to extreme political heat and unprecedented formal removal motions by opposition groups, the rigorous legal hurdles have ensured that no removal has ever crossed the finish line. - SC Refuses Interim Stay on CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Opposition Gears Up for Protests | - INDIA Bloc Meet Tomorrow: Whos Attending, Whos Skipping As Opposition Plans Joint Fight Against SIR - INDIA Bloc To Jointly Move Supreme Court Over Legal Protection To CEC Gyanesh Kumar Under 2023 Law - Breaking News | TVK Breaks With Congress Over CEC Gyanesh Kumar Demand, Calls It Diversionary Furthermore, from a strict legal standpoint, the term impeachment" is technically reserved by the Constitution of India exclusively for the President of India (under Article 61); for a CEC, the process is formally termed removal. WHAT IT ACTUALLY TAKES TO REMOVE A CEC According to Article 324(5) of the Constitution, a CEC can only be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge. The statutory process is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, and breaks down into the following stringent steps: 1. Valid Grounds Only A CEC cannot be removed due to unpopular policy decisions or political disagreements. A Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) has never been impeached in India. The term "impeachment" is reserved for the President of India under Article 61. A CEC can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge, according to Article 324(5). The removal process requires a formal motion signed by at least 100 MPs in Lok Sabha or 50 MPs in Rajya Sabha. A CEC's removal requires a Special Majority in both Houses of Parliament and a Presidential Order. The Constitution restricts the grounds strictly to two specific charges: - Proved misbehaviour 2. Initiation in Parliament The process must begin with a formal motion signed by a significant number of Members of Parliament (MPs): Lok Sabha: Requires at least 100 MPs to sign the notice. Rajya Sabha: Requires at least 50 MPs to sign the notice. The motion must be admitted by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, who has the discretion to accept or reject it. 3. Independent Judicial Inquiry Once admitted, the charges are not voted on immediately. A three-member judicial committee is set up to investigate the allegations. The committee consists of: - A Supreme Court Judge - A High Court Chief Justice - An eminent jurist This committee conducts a formal investigation and submits a report finding the CEC guilty or not guilty of the specified charges. If the committee finds no proof of misbehaviour or incapacity, the process drops entirely. 4. The Special Majority" Voting Hurdle If the committee finds the CEC guilty, the motion goes to a vote in both Houses of Parliament. To pass, it requires a Special Majority in each house separately: Absolute Majority: Support from more than 50% of the total membership of the House. Two-Thirds Majority: Support from at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. 5. Presidential Order Only if both Houses pass the motion with a special majority in the same session will the resolution be sent to the President of India, who then issues the official removal order. CEC VS. OTHER ELECTION COMMISSIONERS It is important to note that this massive constitutional shield only applies to the Chief Election Commissioner. Under Article 324(5), the other two Election Commissioners (ECs) in the multi-member body can be removed much more easily by the President simply upon the recommendation of the CEC. This distinct lack of parallel protection for ECs remains a major point of debate for structural electoral reforms in India. SECTION 16 PROTECTION Section 16 protection refers to the legal immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023. This provision protects serving or former election commissioners from civil or criminal court proceedings for any official actions taken in good faith. The statute explicitly states that no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings" against a person who is or was a CEC or EC for any act, thing, or word done or spoken in the course of discharging their official duties. The protection is significant because it extends to the commissioners even after they leave office. It is designed to cover official electoral taskssuch as voter roll preparation, constituency boundaries, or election schedulingshielding commissioners from frivolous or politically motivated lawsuits. The Ongoing Controversy & Current Debate This legal shield has become a focal point of immense public and political debate: While proponents argue that this immunity is essential to prevent political harassment and ensure the independent functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI), critics and opposition groups argue that it creates an unprecedented lack of accountability. Critics highlight that even Supreme Court judges do not enjoy this specific level of statutory immunity from the filing of proceedings. Legal experts and former officials have noted that the protection is not absolute. It does not protect against malafide (bad faith) actions or conduct that occurs entirely outside the scope of their official duties. Furthermore, the text of the law does not explicitly bar police investigations or arrestsit strictly bars courts from entertaining or continuing legal proceedings. The constitutionality of Section 16 is actively being examined. Legal challenges brought before the Supreme Court of India argue that the provision undermines institutional transparency and user voting rights, particularly amid disputes over internal disagreements within the multi-member commission. A Chief Election Commissioner has never been impeached in India because the constitutional threshold is set exceptionally high to protect the Election Commission's independence from political interference, and legally, the term impeachment applies exclusively to the President.

headline: Less than two years after massive clean-up, water hyacinth takes over large swathes of Ooty lake
content: up, water hyacinth takes over large swathes of Ooty lake In addition to the ineffectual exercise, local bird watchers have noted a drastic reduction in the bird population in the lake due to the unscientific clean-up that led to the destruction of sand banks and reed beds on which the birds had become dependent. Clean-up of lake The project to clean the lake was inaugurated in October 2024, with 7.51 crore being sanctioned for the exercise across 24 hectares, as well as to modernise the sewage treatment plant with additions to keep debris, including solid waste, from entering the waterbody. However, less than two years after the work began and less than a year after it was completed, pollution in the lake remains comparable to previous levels, leading to the proliferation of water hyacinth across a substantial portion of the waterbody. Conservationists said that the presence of water hyacinth is a telltale sign of eutrophication or nutrient-pollution caused by the uncontrolled runoff of pollutants, including fertilisers, manure, and untreated sewage that leads to the rapid growth of plant life, choking whatever little aquatic life that remains. N. Mohanraj, a Nilgiris-based conservationist, said that until the 1980s, the Ooty lake hosted a rich array of biodiversity due to its high water quality, but the continued discharge of untreated waste has severely polluted it. He said that the proliferation of water hyacinth soon after the desilting of the lake has showcased a lack of understanding of the lake ecosystem, with the clean-up also completely ridding the lake of its reed beds and sand banks that helped filter out a portion of the toxins entering the waterbody. Mr. Mohanraj said that the problem is most visible in the Ooty lake and Thalakundha, while the Sandynallah Reservoir, which lies between the two, is relatively clear of water hyacinth due to reed beds that still exist in some form, though highly degraded, in Khandal. Decline in bird population The cleaning of the lake has also led to a drastic reduction in the lakes bird population, especially among wetland species, said bird watchers. In 2023, prior to the desilting work, more than 600 birds across 25 different wetland species were recorded, the highest in the Nilgiris, while the numbers fell drastically in 2025, with only 13 species and 270 birds being recorded. Local birdwatchers said that the numbers have remained the same in 2026. The birds had been dependent on sand banks around the lake for food and for the surrounding foliage to nest. However, due to the unscientific and destructive clean-up operation across the lake, much of these areas were destroyed, said a wildlife researcher who spoke to . He said that the government had wasted money trying to clean up the lake when the causes of the pollution remained unaddressed. The main cause of pollution of the lake is the illegal dumping of sewage and agricultural runoff into the Kodappamund channel. Any clean-up plan that failed to address the underlying, fundamental cause of pollution of the channel is doomed to fail, he said. We have also been calling for the setting up of a lake protection committee that can work with the district administration and the myriad agencies that have some jurisdiction over the lake, so that we can educate them about wildlife and biodiversity and projects such as the lakes cleanup can be conducted without affecting the local wildlife. However, our repeated pleas have consistently been ignored, he said. Mr. Mohanraj also said that the district administration or local NGOs must conduct regular, yearly tests of the water quality in the lake to scan for heavy metals and toxins, as water from the lake flows downstream into the ecologically-sensitive Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR).

headline: 'Dream Was To Crash Into Israel': Flydubai Omani Co-Pilot Likely To Face Death Penalty In UAE
content: Hammami wanted the terror attack to happen so quickly that the Israeli military would not have enough time to scramble fighter jets. The accused Flydubai hijacker could face the death penalty in the United Arab Emirates after allegedly planning to crash an Israel-bound passenger plane into Tel Avivs Ben-Gurion airport, according to reports cited by New York Post. Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, 29, reportedly told investigators that he had a dream" of crashing the aircraft into the Israeli airport. The Jerusalem Post reported that al-Hammami had researched airlines flying to Israel and had even visited the country months before the cockpit attack. - UAE Seeks Death Penalty For Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Over Cockpit Attack - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views ? | - Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack On Ben Gurion Airport, Chose Airline For Israel Route - Flydubai Terror Plot Unraveled: Chilling Confession Of Omani Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami | I tried to get hired by all the airlines," he reportedly told investigators. I checked which ones flew to Tel Aviv. Thats why I chose flydubai. I planned [the operation] even before I was hired." The dream was to crash into Ben-Gurion Al-Hammami had reportedly worked with Flydubai for eight months. According to the Jerusalem Post, he had been intent on crashing a plane in July but changed his mind because he was close to a crew member. However, his reported plan to crash an aircraft on Israeli soil allegedly continued. The dream was to crash into Ben-Gurion [Tel Aviv] airport," he reportedly said. According to the report, al-Hammami wanted the attack to happen so quickly that the Israeli military would not have enough time to scramble fighter jets. Investigators suspect that al-Hammami acted as a lone wolf" rather than carrying out instructions from a terror organisation, a source told the Jerusalem Post. His interrogation in the UAE is continuing. A senior Emirati source told Ynet that the co-pilot is expected to face the death penalty. Prosecutors are seeking the harshest possible punishment after al-Hammami allegedly attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with a crash axe. Israeli, US, Saudi officials join probe The investigation has expanded with the arrival of Mossad investigators and Israeli aviation experts in Abu Dhabi. According to Ynet, the Israeli investigators will take part in the interrogation of al-Hammami. The report also said that two US intelligence agents had travelled to Abu Dhabi. It remains unclear whether the US authorities will participate in the interrogation process. Saudi and Omani officials are also expected to continue questioning al-Hammami, according to the report. The investigation comes amid questions over how the accused pilot was cleared to operate an Israel-bound flight. Questions over pilot vetting Mossad and Israels security agency, Shin Bet, have faced criticism over an alleged failure to properly vet the pilot. Israel and Oman do not have diplomatic relations. According to the reports, only pilots holding passports from countries with which Israel has diplomatic relations can land at Israeli airports. Shin Bet has said the Transportation Ministry is responsible for vetting passenger lists. Transport Minister Miri Regev, however, has said security agencies are responsible for flight security. Regev claimed that her department had not been given a list of the passengers or any warnings about the pilots. The issue of how al-Hammami was able to operate an Israel-bound flight is therefore also being examined as part of the wider investigation. Alleged social media posts under scrutiny Al-Hammami has also come under scrutiny over social media posts that have emerged since the incident. The posts allegedly show him expressing hatred towards Jewish people and making comments promoting violence against women. The Telegraph reported that, in an exchange with a woman while he was studying aviation management remotely at Buckinghamshire New University, he allegedly wrote, Id stomp on your head, wipe the floor with you, make you an example to others, and then divorce you." The alleged posts are now part of the scrutiny surrounding the accused co-pilot as investigators continue to question him in the UAE. The accused Flydubai co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, is likely to face the death penalty in the United Arab Emirates following his alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound passenger plane into Ben-Gurion airport.

headline: Delhi's Rape Cases Have Dipped Since 2023, But Supreme Court Called Ground Reality 'A Systemic Failure': Here's Why
content: Delhi Police statistics show a marginal dip in registered rape cases, the top court emphasised that absolute numbers do not reflect the ground reality of citizen safety The Supreme Court of India on Monday called the recent spate of horrific, recurring sexual assaults exposed fundamental, administrative breakdowns in public safety, lax police patrolling, and unmonitored public spaces in New Delhi a systemic failure". While Delhi Police statistics show a marginal dip in registered rape cases 1,901 cases in 2025 compared to 2,076 in 2024 and 2,141 in 2023 the top court emphasized that absolute numbers do not reflect the ground reality of citizen safety. - Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea On Mandatory Body Cams For Police, Says 'No Grey Area' In Their Use - SIR Row: Rahul Gandhi Held Dharna, Abhijeet Dipke's CJP Took To The Streets, INDIA Bloc Moved SC, What Next? - High Drama At Jantar Mantar: Over 500 Detained, Internet Suspended, 12 Metro Stations in Delhi Shut - Journalist Who Alleged Sexual Assault By Delhi Police Official Detained With 16 Others Over FIR Demand Taking suo motu cognisance on September 28, 2026, a bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran noted that public spaces cannot be allowed to turn into zones of high risk" due to preventable administrative deficiencies. WHY IS IT A SYSTEMIC FAILURE? The Supreme Court identified several critical administrative and institutional lapses behind this systemic failure: 1. Failure to Secure Vulnerable Public Spaces The court pointed out that severe gaps in urban administration directly compromise safety. A key factor was the absence of a visible police presence in areas known to be dangerous. For instance, a 17-year-old girl was gang-raped by men posing as police personnel in Southeast Delhis Aastha Kunj Parka location already designated as a dark spot" by the Delhi Police where lighting gaps had still not been resolved. The Supreme Court of India called the recurring sexual assaults in New Delhi a "systemic failure." Delhi Police statistics show 1,901 registered rape cases in 2025, 2,076 in 2024, and 2,141 in 2023. The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance on September 28, 2026. A bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran noted public spaces cannot be "zones of high risk." The court ordered time-bound safety measures to be implemented across Delhi-NCR within four weeks. Poorly lit roads, broken streetlights, and non-functional CCTV cameras continue to plague vulnerable stretches, rendering safety tech infrastructure ineffective. 2. Lack of Law Enforcement Interception The bench drew painful parallels to the 2012 Nirbhaya case, highlighting a glaring lack of highway and transit monitoring. The court specifically cited an incident where a minor girl was sexually assaulted inside a moving private sleeper bus that traveled over 47 kilometers from Greater Noida to Delhi without being intercepted or checked by any police patrol or checkpoint. 3. Institutional Inertia vs. The Right to Life The Supreme Court clarified that its focus is not on individual culpability or a single case, but on the broader institutional failures that transcend them. The bench firmly stated that the right to live with dignity and free from the fear of violence is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental Right to Life under Article 21 of the Constitution. A minor drop in annual statistics does not absolve the state when basic public infrastructure leaves women exposed to recurring violence. DIRECTIVES ISSUED BY THE SUPREME COURT To address these institutional gaps, the court ordered strict, time-bound safety measures to be implemented across the Delhi-NCR within four weeks: - The police must map vulnerable areas (bus stands, parks, metro stations) and deploy dedicated, accountable patrolling teams. - A complete overhaul and audit to fix broken CCTV cameras and streetlights based on local data and citizen complaints. - Authorities must submit a detailed status report on the actual on-ground functionality of fast-track courts, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) courts, the emergency response number 112, and the 181 womens helpline. The Supreme Court noted that recent horrific sexual assaults exposed fundamental administrative breakdowns, including unmonitored public spaces, lax police patrolling, poor illumination, and broken CCTV cameras. Despite a marginal drop in registered rape cases, the top court stressed that absolute statistical dips do not reflect the ground reality of citizen safety.

headline: Journalist Who Alleged Sexual Assault By Delhi Police Official Detained With 16 Others Over FIR Demand
content: Around 17 people, including a journalist who alleged sexual assault by a police officer, were detained after protesting outside a Delhi police station demanding an FIR and action. Around 17 people, including one of the female journalists who alleged sexual assault by a police officer, were detained in Delhi on Monday morning after spending the night outside the Parliament Street police station. They were demanding registration of an FIR and action against police personnel accused of assaulting three female journalists during a protest. The protesters were seeking an update on the complaints filed by the women, who alleged that they were assaulted while covering a protest against the Chief Election Commissioner near Jantar Mantar on October 3. The group included freelance journalists, YouTubers, and one of the alleged victims. - Protesters Detained Outside Parliament Street Police Station Amid Allegations of Misconduct - 'Wanted To Spread Anarchy': Delhi Police Call Viral 'Groping' Video AI-Generated, Arrest 24-Year-Old YouTuber - Delhi Protest Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Turns Tense: 110 Detained, 15 Cops Injured - Bihar Cop Suspended After Video Shows Him Brandishing Pistol At Flood-Hit People, Oppn Slams Abuse Of Power A senior police officer said Section 163 had been imposed across the New Delhi district. The officer said Parliament Street was not an authorised location for protests, and therefore the gathering could not be allowed. What Happened To The Journalists? The Delhi Police said on Sunday that it had received three separate complaints from female journalists alleging sexual assault by police personnel during the October 3 protest. The complaints have been handed over to the Crime Branch for investigation. Police said the statements of the three women were recorded on Sunday and CCTV footage from the protest site would also be examined. Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said protesters had been informed about the restrictions under Section 163. The provision prohibits gatherings of five or more people, demonstrations and other activities without prior written permission. According to Yadav, police personnel acted on Saturday after protesters refused to leave the area despite being asked to do so. She said the three women later approached police with complaints of manhandling during their detention. Their complaints were recorded, medical examinations were conducted and the cases were subsequently sent to the Crime Branch. Yadav also appealed to anyone having video footage related to the alleged incidents to share it with investigators. What Did The Journalists Allege? One of the journalists said in her complaint that she had seen All India Students Association president Neha Bora and other women protesters being detained. She alleged that there was no female police officer at the spot. According to her complaint, she raised the issue with a police officer, who allegedly pushed and shoved her. She said the officer left the spot after she confronted him. Another journalist said she was covering the protest on Ashoka Road around 3 pm. She alleged that she was recording the detention of activist Yogendra Yadav and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan when she felt someone touch her back. She said she turned around and found a police officer standing very close to her. According to her complaint, when she questioned him about the alleged inappropriate touching, the officer dismissed her allegation. Over 150 Detained On Saturday The controversy comes after more than 150 people were detained on Saturday for allegedly trying to return to Jantar Mantar. Those detained included AISA president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan. The latest group remained outside the Parliament Street police station overnight, demanding that an FIR be registered and action be taken against the police personnel named in the complaints. CJP Supports Journalists The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has backed the women journalists and demanded action against the police personnel facing the allegations. Ratna Singh, head of the CJPs legal team, said on X that the woman who had accused an ACP of molestation was among the 17 people detained while demanding registration of an FIR. Singh also alleged that some of those detained were assaulted by police, claiming that two people were brutally beaten". Instead of protecting the victim and registering an FIR, why are those demanding justice being detained and assaulted? Shame on you, Delhi Police. Release all of them immediately. They are currently detained at Delhi Cantonment police station," she wrote. The police, meanwhile, have said the complaints are being investigated by the Crime Branch and that CCTV footage and other evidence will be examined They were detained after spending the night outside the police station demanding the registration of an FIR and action against police personnel accused of assaulting three female journalists during an earlier protest.

headline: 'Defeating BJP more important': DMK, Akhilesh Yadav's UP poll message
content: speculation of tensions between INDIA bloc allies Samajwadi Party and Congress over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the DMK backed SP president Akhilesh Yadavs statement, emphasising that alliance victory is more important than seat-sharing, and urged parties to unitedly defeat the BJP. Following reports on the rift within the INDIA boc allies, Yadav took to the social media platform X on Sunday to assert that the primary focus should be on defeating the BJP and protecting democracy, the Constitution, and reservation. DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan said the party backs SPs stance. The alliance should win and defeat the BJP. One party getting two or three seats more is not the question. Everybody should stand united to defeat the BJP, he said. The Election Commission is a neutral body. But after Gyanesh Kumar had come, it is not a neutral body, he claimed, alleging that Kumar was functioning under the influence of the ruling party at the Centre. Speculations over the rift between SP and Congress come amid Opposition parties clarion call to protest against the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls and the Election Commission. Key INDIA bloc leaders met last week to chalk out ways to organise a joint protest seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, halt the SIR process following Express Investigation revealing the rupture within the EC and Form 6 irregularities. As Uttar Pradesh is headed for Assembly polls in February 2027, the Congress party has undergone a leadership revamp, reportedly drawing the ire of SP members. The appointment of Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president of its Uttar Pradesh Congress has been reportedly perceived as a pressure tactic to bargain for more seats in the polls. Masood, 56, a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics, had rejoined Congress in 2023 following brief stints with BSP and SP. Masood, triggered row on September 21 as he told ANI that Akhileshs political activity was meaningless unless the alliance was finalised. Finalise the alliance if you have to have an alliance. If it (the alliance) is not to be done, we (Congress) are going ahead with our preparations. Akhilesh ji should finish this work (alliance finalisation) immediately. If you have to lead, the responsibility is on you. Dil bhi aapko bada karna padega (You will have to have a large heart), Masood said. He said the SP should not think of moving ahead without the Congress. Because if you are going ahead without the Congress, defeating the BJP is not in your mind. Only the Congress can fight the BJP, he said. In June 2025, Masood had also stirred the alliance debate by saying the 62-17 formula would not work in the 2027 Assembly polls, referring to the seat-sharing arrangement between the two allies for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. With inputs from PTI

headline: 'Your Place Is In Jail': Supreme Court Rebukes Rajpal Yadav In Rs 5 Crore Cheque Bounce Case
content: In May 2024, a sessions court convicted Rajpal Yadav and sentenced him to six months in jail. The Delhi HC later suspended his sentence. The court noted that Yadav had undertaken to deposit Rs. 5 crore with the court registry by Monday but had failed to do so. The actor produced a copy of a Rs. 50 lakh demand draft and said it was being processed by the bank. Is this genuine or not? We dont know," the bench said. - Supreme Court To Hear Pleas Seeking Suspension Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Challenging EC Decisions - 'Let's Be Very Clear': Supreme Court Says It Didn't Approve Modified Form 6, Asks Who Made Changes - Minimum Threshold Of 18 Years: SC Asks Centre To Frame Rules To Bar Social Media Platforms From Allowing Minors - Can Supreme Court Suspend Gyanesh Kumar? The Constitutional Question Behind The Unprecedented Plea When Yadavs counsel said the draft was with the bank, the complainants counsel alleged that the actor had no respect for the majesty of the institution". Justice Bagchi then said, They may be richer than you, but they are poor to the extent you have swindled them. This arrogance needs to be put in its right place. You should know when to open your mouth. Your place is in jail." How the Rs. 5 crore dispute began The case concerns Rs. 5 crore received by Yadav and his wife from Murli Projects in connection with a film being produced by the actor. The parties entered into four agreements after the film could not be completed within the agreed timelines. Under the third agreement, Yadav gave eight security cheques to Murli Projects. The third agreement was later replaced by a fourth agreement, described as a consent agreement dated April 21, 2013. According to Yadavs plea, the agreement provided for the return of the eight security cheques and issuance of four fresh cheques of Rs. 10 crore each. The Supreme Court rebuked Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav for failing to deposit Rs. 5 crore in a cheque bounce case. The Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the payment by Tuesday. The case involves Rs. 5 crore received by Yadav and his wife from Murli Projects for a film. In May 2024, a sessions court convicted Yadav and sentenced him to six months in jail. The Supreme Court had previously granted extensions, with the latest deadline for deposit being October 5. Yadav alleges that Murli Projects did not return the eight security cheques and instead presented seven of them, which were dishonoured. This led to criminal complaints against Yadav and his wife. From conviction to jail In May 2024, a sessions court convicted Yadav and sentenced him to six months in jail. The Delhi High Court later suspended his sentence after his counsel assured the court that the dispute would be settled. The matter was also referred to the Delhi High Court Mediation Centre. However, the High Court later observed that despite repeated assurances and several adjournments, Yadav had failed to make promised payments. It noted that he had not deposited amounts he had undertaken to pay, including Rs. 2.5 crore that he had sought permission to pay in instalments. In February 2026, the High Court directed Yadav to surrender before jail authorities. His plea seeking more time was rejected. He surrendered on February 5 and remained in jail until the High Court granted an interim suspension of sentence after he deposited Rs. 1.5 crore with the complainant. He was later sentenced to three months imprisonment for failing to deposit the remaining amount despite several undertakings. Yadav has challenged this before the Supreme Court. SC gives one more deadline According to Yadavs plea, the subsequent consent agreement made the earlier cheques invalid and therefore the complaints based on those cheques were not maintainable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The Supreme Court had on September 8 exempted him from surrendering, subject to depositing the money by September 9. On September 15, it granted another two-week extension and asked him to deposit the money by October 5. When the matter was heard on Monday, the court was told that the amount had still not been deposited. Yadavs counsel cited the closure of banks for three or four days. Why? You were given 16 days on September 15. Today we are on October 5. You are out of time by seven days. You could have filed an application seeking extension of time," the court said. The complainants lawyer said the total amount was Rs. 7.5 crore and argued that Yadav should be liable for contempt. The court, however, did not dismiss his appeal as the complainant might then be unable to recover the money. We want to dismiss it, but we also want to balance equities to ensure that your client gets some money," the bench remarked. The court directed that the payment be made by Tuesday and listed the matter for compliance. The Supreme Court strongly rebuked Rajpal Yadav because he failed to comply with his legal undertaking to deposit Rs. 5 crore with the court registry by Monday. The Bench noted that the actor had repeatedly missed deadlines and failed to honour his commitments regarding payments owed to Murli Projects.

headline: Telangana CEO orders action against Form 7 misuse to delete eligible voters
content: The Chief Electoral Officer of Telangana, C Sudarshan Reddy, has issued an order to the Commissioner of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, the District Education Officer, Hyderabad, and all collectors and DEOs of districts across the state, asking them to take appropriate action against individuals who submitted Form 7s to falsely delete eligible voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The CEOs memo, issued on Monday, reads, It has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing bulk applications in Form 7 before the EROs (electoral registration officers) and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine. The memo added that officials, including collectors, DEOs and EROs, should take action against the applicants, who have made knowingly false statement or declaration in writing in form 6, 6A, 7 and 8 as per the provisions of section 31 of the Representation of People Act 1950. The memo further states that such action shall be preceded by an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The CEOs instructions come against the backdrop of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committees (TPCC) electoral office filing a complaint with the Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad, seeking FIRs over alleged Form 7 misuse. The first alleged instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a booth-level agent (BLA) of the BJP, seeking the deletion of 31 electors, including a Congress BLA and his family members, the Congress claimed. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. The third instance brought to the notice of the commissioner was from Goshamahal assembly constituencys booth number 173. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO [booth-level officer] refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader claimed. The Congress is in power in the state. What is Section 31 Section 31 of Representation of People Act -1950 refers to making false declarations. It reads, If any person makes in connection with(a) the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll, or (b) the inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll,a statement or declaration in writing which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 pertains to inquiry into claims and objections. As per the rule, The registration officer shall hold a summary inquiry into every claim or objection in respect of which notice has been given under Rule 19 and shall record his decision thereon. The rule further states, At the hearing, the claimant or, as the case may be, the objector and the person objected to and any other person who, in the opinion of the registration officer, is likely to be of assistance to him, shall be entitled to appear and be heard. The registration officer may in his discretion-require any claimant, objector or person objected to, to appear in person before him; (b) require that the evidence tendered by any person shall be given on oath and administer an oath for the purpose.

headline: Flydubai Co-pilot May Be Holding Dual Citizenship, Appointment Shows Screening Gaps: Omani Sources To News18
content: the radicalisation flag, Omani authorities had permanently banned Hamam al-Hammami from working in the aviation sector, say sources Investigating authorities are tracking a complex web of international background details regarding the 29-year-old Omani national, Hamam al-Hammami, who carried out the mid-air assault on Flydubai Flight FZ1073. New biographical information and regulatory disclosures reveal critical gaps in aviation screening and raise the strong possibility that the suspect holds dual citizenship, according to sources from Oman. - UAE Seeks Death Penalty For Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Over Cockpit Attack - Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack On Ben Gurion Airport, Chose Airline For Israel Route - EXCLUSIVE: FLYDUBAI PILOTS PAST EXPOSED | Barred in Oman Over Extremist Views, Then Hired | - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views | International Upbringing and Syrian Roots Official records show al-Hammami was born in the United Arab Emirates and is of mixed heritage, with a mother of Syrian origin. Sources close to the investigation state that he spent a significant portion of his life outside of Oman. This extended period abroad occurred during his fathers employment in the UAE, while staying with his mother in war-torn Syria, and during his subsequent university studies in Australia. Prior Blacklisting and Failure to Check Backgrounds Al-Hammamis history with aviation security dates back to his time as a trainee at an Omani airline. Security agencies in Muscat identified his interest in accessing extremist websites on the internet at an early stage. Acting on this radicalisation flag, Omani authorities took swift action, permanently banning him from working in the aviation sector. Hamam al-Hammami, 29, carried out a mid-air assault on Flydubai Flight FZ1073. Al-Hammami was born in the United Arab Emirates and has a mother of Syrian origin. Omani authorities banned al-Hammami from aviation due to his interest in extremist websites. Omani authorities never received requests for background checks on al-Hammami from foreign entities. The aviation agreement between Israel and the UAE restricts flight crews to specific nationalities. Following the flight ban, al-Hammami left Oman. Crucially, Omani authorities confirmed that they never received any requests from foreign governments or airlines to conduct background checks on al-Hammami for employment purposes. Omani officials emphasized that had any information been requested prior to his hiring by Flydubai, the sultanate would have immediately shared his security red flags, as it is doing now in the active counterterrorism investigation. Nationality Anomalies Under Bilateral Agreements The disclosure has put immense pressure on the regulatory framework governing flights between the UAE and Israel. Under the explicit terms of the aviation agreement between Israel and the UAE, air routes between the two nations may only be operated by flight crews holding UAE nationality or the nationality of a state that has formalized and normalized diplomatic relations with Israel. Because Oman does not maintain formal diplomatic ties with Israel, al-Hammamis presence in the cockpit strongly indicates that he may hold a second nationality that allowed him to bypass the restriction. Systemic Negligence and Oversight The details highlight a breakdown in standard operating procedures. Investigators are focusing on how an individual flagged for extremist ties could seamlessly enter a major regional commercial carrier. The security failure points directly to a vulnerability in the verification procedures established under the bilateral aviation agreement. Analysts state that the suspects ability to clear screening suggests a combination of procedural negligence, severe oversight, or a deliberate disregard for protocol by vetting parties. Investigating authorities revealed that 29-year-old Omani national Hamam al-Hammami was previously flagged by security agencies in Muscat for accessing extremist websites as an airline trainee. This radicalisation flag resulted in him being permanently banned from working in Oman's aviation sector before he was later hired by Flydubai.

headline: Madras High Court permits DMK to file ₹1-crore defamation suit against Ministers Aadhav Arjuna, Nirmal Kumar
content: The Madras High Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) granted leave (permission) to the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) to file a 1-crore defamation suit against Ministers Aadhav Arjuna, C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar, and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) Information Technology wing. Justice K. Govindarajan Thilakavadi allowed an application filed by the DMK, through senior counsel J. Ravindran, seeking the leave of the court, as the TVK IT Wings office, as well as the headquarters of social media giants such as X Corp, Meta Platforms, and YouTube, were located outside the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court. The plaintiff party, represented by its general secretary Duraimurugan, had filed the defamation suit seeking damages from the two Ministers as well as the TVKs IT wing for reportedly accusing the DMK of having shielded child sexual abuse case accused R. Veeramani of Gem Granites during the partys previous regime. In its plaint, the plaintiff party said that the First Information Report (FIR) in the case registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, was promptly registered during its rule on October 7, 2025, just a day after a child rights activist had handed over a video clipping of the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl child to the police. Thereafter, the investigation proceeded in accordance with the law on the basis of the available evidence. Making it clear that the DMK, being the then ruling party, had not interfered with the investigation in any manner whatsoever, the court was told that the party had no connection or connivance with the accused. On the other hand, the two Ministers vehemently opposed the plea for grant of leave on the ground that the suit, in its present form, was not maintainable for want of adherence to procedures prescribed under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). The Ministers said that the DMK had failed to issue notices to them under Section 80 of the CPC. Claiming they had been sued in their official capacity as members of the State Cabinet, the Ministers said that the plaintiff party ought to have issued notices to them under Section 80(1) of the CPC or in the alternative obtained the leave of the court under Section 80(2) for dispensing with the statutory requirement of issuing such notice.

headline: Farmer murdered after his police complaint on harassment of minor daughter in Tiruttani; one arrested
content: A 45-year-old farmer was murdered by two persons in Tiruttani of Tiruvallur district on Sunday (October 4, 2026). A senior police official from Tiruvallur district said the victim, Yuvaraj, was a resident of Periyar Nagar in Tiruttani. He had given a complaint to the Tiruttani police against a youth of the same locality for persistently harassing his minor daughter. Enraged by this, the youth, identified as Sanjay Lawrence, along with a friend, who remains unidentified, hacked Yuvaraj to death. headline: Nobel Prize 2026 In Medicine Awarded To Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann And Georg Nagel
content: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries in light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on Monday for their discoveries in neuroscience. The three scientists were recognised for their research into light-gated ion channels, a type of protein that helped establish the field of optogenetics, a pioneering technique that uses tiny lights to activate specific groups of neurons in the brain. - Spain Housing Crisis Triggers Snap Election: Why Pedro Sanchez Is Betting On Angry Renters To Fight The Right - Your Next Date Could Be Chosen By The Government. It has also provided clues that could contribute to the treatment of conditions including blindness, depression, addiction and dementia. How optogenetics changed neuroscience Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel researched light-gated ion channels and their role in controlling neural activity. Their work established optogenetics, which allows researchers to activate discrete groups of neurons in the brain using tiny lights. The technique has helped illuminate how specific neural circuits function. The Nobel Committee member said the research could provide clues for treating a range of conditions, including blindness, depression, addiction and dementia. When will the other Nobel Prizes be announced? The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine is the first of six Nobel Prizes being awarded this year. Each prize recognises groundbreaking contributions by an individual or organisation in a specific field. The Nobel Prize in Physics will be awarded on Tuesday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. Last year, John Clarke, Michel H Devoret and John M Martinis shared the prize for work that made the behaviours of the subatomic world observable in a system large enough to see with the naked eye. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry will be awarded on Wednesday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. Last year, the prize went to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for developing molecular building blocks with spaces large enough for gases and other chemicals to flow through them. The Nobel Prize in Literature will be awarded on Thursday by the Swedish Academy in Stockholm. Last year, Laszlo Krasznahorkai, a Hungarian novelist known for his dystopian themes and relentless prose, received the award. The Nobel Peace Prize will be awarded on Friday by the Norwegian Nobel Institute in Oslo. Last year, Mara Corina Machado, who built a powerful social movement in Venezuela challenging the nations authoritarian president, won the award. Next week, the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences will be awarded on Monday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. Last year, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt were honoured for research explaining the relationship between technological progress and sustained economic growth. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries in neuroscience.

headline: Spain Housing Crisis Triggers Snap Election: Why Pedro Sanchez Is Betting On Angry Renters To Fight The Right
content: Why Pedro Sanchez Is Betting On Angry Renters To Fight The Right Public anger over housing intensified following the eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman who had lived in the same Madrid home for 70 years. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Snchez has called a snap general election for November 29, betting that growing anger over high rents and the rejection of his governments housing measures will help his Socialist party mobilise left-wing voters. Snchez, who has led a left-wing minority government since 2023 and has been prime minister since 2018, announced the early election on Monday in a televised address. The election was called three days after right-wing parties rejected emergency legislation aimed at tackling Spains housing crisis. The next general election was due to be held before the end of next summer. - The Royal Palace In India That Has Its Own Golf Course, Stadium And 170+ Rooms | Video - 'We Were Very Close To Winning. What Happened?' Rahul Gandhi Asks Kanhaiya Kumar After DUSU Defeat - Why Are Tens Of Thousands Protesting Over Rent In Spain? Defending his governments social and humanitarian record, Snchez acknowledged that it had made mistakes but said it was now time for voters to decide. Its up to you now," he said, according to his televised address. He also referred to a period of global tension, the climate emergency and social and technological changes, including disruptive advances in artificial intelligence. Snchez said Spanish voters must decide what role they wanted Spain to play in this changing world. He again portrayed the political choice as one between his progressive government and the Spanish right. You, the men and women of Spain, must decide whether you want to join the far-right wave that drives regression wherever it governs, or to ensure that Spain remains a bastion of openness, social justice, and environmental responsibility," Snchez said as quoted by The Guardian. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Snchez called a snap general election for November 29. Snchez has led a left-wing minority government since 2023 and has been prime minister since 2018. Right-wing parties rejected emergency legislation aimed at tackling Spains housing crisis. An 87-year-old woman's eviction in Madrid sparked protests. Snchez's brother was banned from public office and his wife faces trial for corruption allegations. Housing measures rejected by right-wing parties The snap election comes as Spain faces growing anger over high rents and insecure tenancies. Snchezs government had proposed two decrees containing measures intended to improve access to housing. These included a ban on evictions until 2030 and regulations covering temporary rentals and rentals by room. However, the measures were rejected in Congress on Friday by the conservative Peoples Party (PP), the far-right Vox party and the right-wing Catalan pro-independence party Junts. The PP, which is leading in polls, argued that construction rather than regulation was the better way to address the housing crisis. The party could need support from Vox to form a government. The rejection triggered an angry response from crowds outside Congress, with protesters shouting shame" and Your profits; our misery". The PP welcomed Snchezs decision to call an early election, saying Spaniards would now have the opportunity to rebuild our country". 87-year-olds eviction sparks protests Public anger over housing intensified following the eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman who had lived in the same Madrid home for 70 years. Abascal said she could not afford a 230% increase in rent demanded by the investment fund that had bought her apartment. Her eviction prompted tens of thousands of people to protest. A large tent camp also appeared in Madrids central Puerta del Sol square, recalling the 2011 indignados movement. Large demonstrations were held across Spain over the weekend as protesters demanded urgent action on the housing crisis. Authorities said 70,000 people participated in a protest in Madrid on Saturday, while organisers estimated the crowd at 500,000. Can housing help Snchez against the right? Polls have consistently put the PP ahead of Snchezs Spanish Socialist Workers Party, while support for Vox has also been growing. Snchez is now betting that housing will become a defining election issue and that anger over rents, combined with opposition to the rejection of his governments housing measures, will encourage left-wing voters to turn out. The housing crisis has also helped shift attention away from the governments much-criticised handling of the continuing crisis in Spains North African enclave of Ceuta. The crisis began after around 70,000 people crossed into the territory from neighbouring Morocco within 48 hours. Corruption allegations add pressure Snchezs government and his inner circle have also faced corruption allegations over the past two years. In July this year, his brother, David Snchez, was banned from holding public office for nine years after being found guilty of administrative misconduct linked to his hiring by a Socialist-led council in Extremadura. Meanwhile, Snchezs wife, Begoa Gmez, is due to face trial after a judge charged her with embezzlement, influence peddling, corruption in business dealings and misappropriation of funds following a two-year investigation. David Snchez and Begoa Gmez have denied any wrongdoing. Snchez has previously accused his political and media opponents of carrying out a harassment and bullying operation" against his family. Pedro Snchez called a snap general election for November 29 after right-wing parties rejected his government's emergency housing measures. He is betting that public anger over high rents and housing will mobilize left-wing voters.

headline: Kainchi Dham drowns in tourists after Hanuman Ansh release, district may act to ease pressure
content: We usually expect about 25,000 people visiting the shrine every day, but the long weekend saw a crowd of more than 35,000 every day, the DM told Express. For kilometres, cars crawled through the Kumaon hills towards Kainchi Dham over the long weekend, bumper-to-bumper on the mountain road. Pilgrims got out and walked along the roadside and families waited for hours, while vehicles heading towards Mukteshwar were caught in the same gridlock as those arriving for darshan. Videos circulating online over the weekend showed long lines of cars, buses and two-wheelers around Bhimtal, Bhowali and Kainchi, with reports of journeys that ordinarily take a few hours stretching much longer. The congestion has prompted the Nainital administration to consider opening an alternative route to ease pressure on Kainchi Dham. The district administration will meet temple authorities, police and other stakeholders on Tuesday to finalise crowd-control measures, he said. We usually expect about 25,000 people visiting the shrine every day, but this weekend, since October 2, we have seen a crowd of more than 35,000 every day. Both the pilgrims and the locals use the same road to Kainchi, which also goes up to Mukteshwar, causing a traffic jam for hours, Lalit Mohan said. He said traffic had been cleared from the Mukteshwar side on Sunday. What explains the surge? Mohan attributed the latest surge to two factors: the end of the monsoon, when travellers who had avoided the hills because of rain and landslides return, and the release of Hanuman Ansh, the film based on the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba. It is learnt that 24.34 lakh people visited Kainchi Dham in the first six months of 2026, compared with around eight lakh visitors in the entire previous year. The surge has even prompted Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi to urge devotees to check the situation before travelling to Kainchi Dham. There is a huge crowd at Kainchi Dham at the moment we should all check the situation there before going, he said, adding that visitors should avoid a situation where children and women in your family are suffocating in the crowd or are stuck in a traffic jam. He also suggested that devotees consider other sites associated with Neem Karoli Baba if Kainchi remains overcrowded. The hills are choked The proposed diversion comes as Uttarakhand is already building an 18.15-km Kainchi Dham bypass from Sanatorium to Ranighat. Eight kilometres were completed and hot-mixed earlier this year, and hill-cutting on another 10.15 km is done too. A motor bridge is also being built to connect the bypass with the Bhowali-Almora highway. The state has separately built the Bhowali bypass and a 30-metre double-lane bridge over the Shipra River to ease congestion in the area. The states Public Works Department has also identified the Talla Ramgarh-Ratighat road as an alternative route connecting Kainchi with Ramgarh, Mukteshwar, Lohaghat and Champawat, saying its strengthening could significantly reduce traffic pressure. A state planning document notes that Uttarakhand receives tourists equivalent to roughly 300 per cent of its resident population, compared with 185 per cent in Himachal Pradesh, and warns that hill destinations once known for walking and trekking are increasingly being choked by vehicles. The National Green Tribunal has recently taken on record a scientific carrying-capacity study covering major pilgrimage sites including Kedarnath, Hemkund Sahib, Gangotri and Yamunotri, reflecting a wider debate over the limits of tourism and pilgrimage in the fragile Himalayas. Kainchi has already had its own carrying-capacity study. A Tourism Department study conducted in 2025 found that 64 per cent of devotees came only for darshan and returned the same day, while 82.4 per cent were from outside Uttarakhand. Nearly two-thirds were aged between 15 and 30. Parking was the biggest infrastructure complaint, with 74 per cent of respondents dissatisfied with parking facilities. At the temple, authorities said the situation remained manageable. Pradeep Bhatt, who works in Kainchi Dhams accounts section, said authorities have deployed additional police personnel inside and outside the temple. The crowd has swelled due to the long weekend. Police are taking extra precautions. The police force is now being placed inside and outside the temple too. So far it has been managed all right, he said. By Monday, the immediate crisis had eased. Dheeraj Tiwari, 27, who runs his familys business beside the temple entrance, said the worst congestion lasted a day or two. The administration has now cleared everything out. Today everything looks normal. It was the long weekend that created a lot of flow of pilgrims, he said. For residents, however, the problem is measured differently. Mani Bharadwaj, who formerly worked at Hotel Monal, about 500 metres from the shrine, and lives in Bhowali, said the disruption extended beyond tourists. Today things seem to have gone back to normal, but over the weekend the locals faced a lot of problems. When thousands of vehicles are stuck on the same road, it affects everyone people going to work, bringing supplies, travelling for medical needs or simply trying to get home. Locals have no separate road. The same infrastructure has to serve pilgrims and local residents. Every time there is a huge rush, locals bear the disruption. There needs to be a permanent solution rather than waiting for every long weekend and then putting more police on the roads, he said.

headline: BJP's list of 8 for Rajya Sabha poll: 2 women candidates, 1 big name dropped
content: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Monday announced its eight picks for the October 16 Rajya Sabha poll in Uttar Pradesh, fielding two women candidates. Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, whose term in the Upper House is at an end, was not on the list of nominees, which party insiders indicated shows the Central Council of Ministers is due for a shakeup. Former Lok Sabha MP Priyanka Singh Rawat and Shruti Gangwar, Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwars daughter and a prominent member of the Uttar Pradesh BJP, were among the partys nominees in the politically important state. Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, and Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan were the others. Ten Rajya Sabha seats are falling vacant in Uttar Pradesh, eight of which are currently held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) hold one each. How the numbers add up Currently, the BJP-led NDA holds 150 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, while non-NDA parties account for just over 100 seats. The road to 294: the NDA is two votes short of eight Rajya Sabha seats in UP MLAs in the 403-member House after seven deaths in 11 months seats at stake in the October 16 polls first-preference votes needed to win each seat Beyond the BJPs own 255 MLAs 294: NDAs effective strength The bar starts at the BJPs own 255 MLAs, so it is not drawn from zero. The six who take the NDA from 288 to 294 Unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh, expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik) The UP Assembly currently has 396 members in the 403-member House, following the death of seven MLAs in the past 11 months. Each Rajya Sabha candidate, therefore, will require 37 first-preference votes to win. The October 16 polls is going to be a tough contest between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP). The BJP and SP have the numbers to win seven and two seats respectively out of the 10 at stake. The timing of the polls adds to the intrigue as they come months before the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections likely to be held early next year. The BJP has 255 MLAs and its NDA allies add another 33: Apna Dal (S) 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. This takes its tally to 288. With the support of Puja Pal; unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls; and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik), the NDAs effective strength reaches 294, two short of the required 296 (37 for each) first-preference votes to ensure victory of eight candidates. Of the 10 seats that will go to polls, the BJP holds eight at present.

headline: Madras High Court dismisses as withdrawn case against building Tamil Nadu's new Secretariat at Pattinapakkam
content: Madras High Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) dismissed as withdrawn a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by a lawyer, seeking a direction to the Tamil Nadu government to abandon its plan to construct a new Legislative Assembly-cum-Secretariat complex on 25.55 acres of Tamil Nadu Housing Board (TNHB) land at Pattinapakkam (Foreshore Estate) in Chennai. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan permitted the petitioner, R.S. Tamilvendan of Chennai, to withdraw the case without granting any kind of liberty. The litigant took the call after the judges said that the case had been filed casually and for publicity with no research on the matter and without raising valid grounds. What did the Bench say? During the course of the hearing, the Chief Justice asked: How can you say that it is wastage of public money? It is for the government to construct [the Secretariat] wherever it wants. Please tell us, what is the power of the court to direct the government to construct a particular building at this place or that place? Where is that power? There may be hundreds of reasons, but where is the power? Justice Murugan said: You have filed a public interest litigation petition to stall a project. See your affidavit. It runs for just two pages and has only two relevant paragraphs. You should have done some research, collected proper materials, and explained to the court why you are challenging the governments decision; only then can this court consider your plea. Here, there are just two paragraphs. The Division Bench also recalled that it was not the first time that a case had been filed in the High Court challenging the governments decision to shift the Legislative Assembly and Secretariat to a new location. They pointed out that the High Court had dismissed a similar case filed about a decade ago on the ground that courts could not interfere with the governments policy decisions. Even the Supreme Court had categorically held the same. Therefore, we are asking the very first question as to from where do we get the power to issue a writ of mandamus to the government to abandon its plan? the Chief Justice asked the petitioners counsel and said, the petitioner would have known about the previous decisions had he done some research. You have not even made an attempt to do any research. When you come up with a public interest litigation petition, is it not your duty to work on all this? Justice Murugan asked. The Chief Justice said: In fact, such cases require the imposition of costs. You just want publicity, thats all. However, the Bench refrained from imposing costs, since the petitioners counsel chose to withdraw the case.

headline: Does RAC guarantee a seat in Indian Railways? What Reservation Against Cancellation means for your train ticket
content: When booking a train ticket, passengers often come across the term RAC and wonder what it means for their journey. Does an RAC ticket allow them to board the train? Will they get a seat, or will they have to wait for a berth to become available? In Indian Railways, RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation. An RAC ticket allows a passenger to board the train and travel with reserved seating accommodation, but it does not guarantee a full sleeping berth. If a berth becomes available, the RAC passenger may get it based on the applicable rules. Here is how the RAC system works and what passengers can expect when travelling with an RAC ticket. What Reservation Against Cancellation means Speaking to .com, a senior railway official said that RAC is a reservation status used by Indian Railways when confirmed berths in a particular class have already been allotted but limited accommodation is still available for passengers. The official explained that a RAC passenger is permitted to board the train and is provided reserved seating accommodation. In classes with sleeping berths, two RAC passengers may initially be allotted seating on a berth designated for RAC passengers. This means that while the passengers journey is assured, a full sleeping berth is not necessarily assured at that stage, the official stated. Can RAC ticket become confirmed? According to the railway official, an RAC ticket can move to confirmed status if a berth becomes available. For example, if passengers holding confirmed reservations cancel their tickets before chart preparation, the available berths can be allotted to RAC passengers according to the applicable reservation system. So, a passenger whose status was RAC 25 at the time of booking may see it improve to RAC 10, RAC 2 or eventually CNF before the journey. Once the ticket becomes confirmed, the passenger is allotted a full berth, the official said. What happens if the ticket remains RAC after chart preparation? When asked about whether a passenger can travel with RAC ticket after chart preparation, the official replied that the passenger can still travel. If the ticket remains RAC after the final reservation chart is prepared, reserved seating accommodation remains available, but a full berth may have to be shared as per the RAC arrangement, the official added. The official further said that there is also a possibility of getting a full berth during the journey. If a confirmed passenger does not turn up, cancels at a stage permitted under the rules, or a berth otherwise becomes available, the vacant accommodation may be allotted to an RAC passenger by the travelling ticket checking staff as per applicable rules and priority. RAC vs WAITING LIST: WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE? The passenger can travel and has confirmed accommodation, normally including a full berth where applicable. Reservation Against Cancellation The passenger can travel and has reserved seating accommodation, but a full berth is not guaranteed until it becomes available. Reserved accommodation has not yet been allotted. For fully waitlisted e-tickets, the applicable Indian Railways rules determine whether the passenger can travel after chart preparation. Why does Indian Railways have RAC system? As per the official, the RAC system helps Indian Railways make better use of available accommodation while giving more passengers certainty about their journey. Instead of keeping passengers entirely on the waiting list, RAC allows a limited number of passengers to travel with seating accommodation while keeping them in line for full berths that may become vacant due to cancellations, the official added.

headline: Lab Worker's Mysterious Death At Russia's Anti-Plague Institute: Why Has It Drawn US Attention?
content: people were reportedly placed under observation after the 28-year-old workers death, as questions remain over whether pneumonic plague was involved. A death at a specialised anti-plague research institute in Siberia has triggered questions over what happened inside the facility and drawn the attention of health authorities beyond Russia. The case emerged from Shelekhov, near Irkutsk, where an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute fell ill under circumstances that are still being investigated. As Russian authorities sought to contain concerns, the United States said it was closely following developments. - Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before? - Lab Worker's Death From 'Unknown Infection' Sparks Plague Fears In Russia, Hundreds Quarantined - Why Is Plague Still A Threat? What Russia's Irkutsk Scare Reveals About The Deadly Bacteria - Russia Plague Scare: From Symptoms To Spread, How Dangerous It Is And Could It Be Another Covid? But what happened at the institute, why has pneumonic plague entered the conversation, and what has prompted Washington to watch the case? What Happened At The Anti-Plague Institute? The incident centred on the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Shelekhov, near Irkutsk. Russian authorities were responding to an incident in which a suspected dangerous infection was released as a result of a laboratory accident. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias consumer health watchdog which handles infectious diseases, did not specify what was released. One of the institutes employees later died after being diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown etiology", or cause. An employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov died after being diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown etiology. The deceased employee was identified as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova. Nearly 200 people were placed under observation at a hospital in Shelekhov. The US State Department and CDC are closely monitoring reports of a suspected pneumonic plague case in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia. Rospotrebnadzor stated that the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region is stable. Local media identified the employee as 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova. Rospotrebnadzor said special measures had been carried out in connection with the case of an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute". The agency also expanded testing of samples taken from the patient and found no microorganisms associated with her professional activities, according to Russian state news agency TASS. Why Did Plague Enter The Picture? The possibility of plague was publicly raised by Alexei Tsydenov, head of neighbouring Buryatia. In an October 3 Telegram post, Tsydenov said a woman in the neighbouring Irkutsk region had died, maybe of the plague". He also stressed that there are no plague outbreaks" in Buryatia. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev subsequently said an extraordinary meeting of the regional anti-epidemic commission had been held with Russias chief state doctor. The meeting, he said, was related to a suspected case of a particularly dangerous infection affecting a resident of the region". Russian health authorities have stopped short of identifying the infection as plague. Rospotrebnadzor officially described the womans illness as pneumonia of unknown cause. Gennady Onishchenko, a former head of Rospotrebnadzor, also told TASS that the infection was most likely not the plague, but even if confirmed, there will be no spread of this disease". Nearly 200 People Reportedly Placed Under Observation As questions mounted over the infection, precautionary measures were taken in Shelekhov. Independent regional news outlet Liudi Baikala reported that nearly 200 people were placed under observation at the hospital where the laboratory technician had been taken. The outlet also reported that quarantine was imposed at at least one maternity hospital in the city. An aluminium plant near the laboratory instructed its employees to wear masks as a precautionary measure. Artem Fominikh, director of the Irkutsk Aluminum Plant, acknowledged that there are many rumors and conflicting reports circulating". All identified close contacts are under medical supervision. At present, they show no signs of the disease, and their laboratory test results are negative," Fominikh said. Rospotrebnadzor, meanwhile, sought to allay concerns about the possibility of a wider health emergency. The sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region, the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable," the agency said. Why Is The US Watching Closely? The developments in Siberia have also caught the attention of the United States, which is specifically monitoring reports that the worker may have died from pneumonic plague. We are aware of reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia. We are monitoring the situation closely with the CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] and our other interagency partners," a US State Department official told Al Jazeera. Washington also made clear that it was seeking greater clarity over what had happened. Many details have not been confirmed. We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly," the official said. The US Department of Health and Human Services told CNN that the CDC was closely monitoring the situation in Russia, adding that the safety and security of U.S. citizens is our highest priority." What Is Pneumonic Plague? Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which is usually found in small mammals and their fleas. There are three forms of plague. Other forms typically spread through contact with infected fleas, animals or infected tissues. Pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread from person to person through respiratory particles. According to the US CDC, patients with pneumonic plague can develop fever, headache and weakness, followed by rapidly developing pneumonia. Symptoms can include shortness of breath, chest pain and cough, sometimes accompanied by bloody or watery mucus. The World Health Organization says plague has a high fatality rate, but it can be treated with antibiotics. Precautions can also be used to prevent infections from spreading. The ability of the pneumonic form to pass between people makes identifying and monitoring close contacts particularly important when such an infection is suspected. An incident involving a suspected dangerous infection release occurred at the institute, following which a 28-year-old laboratory technician named Darya Shipilova fell ill and died after being diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown cause.

Shehbaz Govt Holds Talks As Crisis Deepens In Pakistan - 'No Guns, But I Have People's Power': Sohail Afridi Leads PTI March, Rejects KP Military Action The development comes a day after KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the PTIs long march, defying warnings from the federal government and leading thousands of supporters as the party renewed its campaign for the release of jailed PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.
