headline: Russian Lab Worker Dies After Suspected Pathogen Leak: Have Research Accidents Caused Outbreaks Before?
content: Laboratory accidents involving dangerous pathogens are rare but they have happened. One of the clearest examples came in 2003, after the SARS outbreak had officially ended. A 28-year-old laboratory worker at a Russian anti-plague institute in Siberia died after developing severe pneumonia, with US officials now monitoring reports that she may have contracted pneumonic plague in what could be a laboratory-related incident. The woman, identified by local media as Darya Shipilova, worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, in Russias remote Irkutsk region. Reports about her death raised concerns over a possible exposure to the bacterium that causes plague, although Russian health authorities have not officially confirmed pneumonic plague as the cause. - Lab Worker's Death From 'Unknown Infection' Sparks Plague Fears In Russia, Hundreds Quarantined - Dual UK-Iranian National Arrested Over Suspected Terror Offence Linked To Airbase Incident - 65-Year-Old Kerala Man Stabs Wife To Death Over Suspicion Of Affair, Then Dials Son To Inform Him - Woman Claims Rs. 450 Pizza Ordered On Zomato Arrived Half-Eaten And Stale; Company Responds Russias consumer and public health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said the employee was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown aetiology. The agency said expanded testing of samples from the patient had found no microorganisms associated with her professional activities. Nearly 200 people who may have had contact with the woman have reportedly been placed under medical observation as authorities carry out preventive measures. Lab Accidents Have Caused Infections And Outbreaks Laboratory accidents involving dangerous pathogens are rare but they have happened. One of the clearest examples came in 2003, after the SARS outbreak had officially ended. A 27-year-old researcher working in a virology laboratory in Singapore contracted SARS-CoV. The World Health Organization later concluded that the researcher most likely acquired the infection through accidental contamination in the laboratory. The investigation identified inappropriate laboratory practices that had contributed to the accident. Fortunately, the Singapore case did not lead to further transmission but WHO warned that an accidental laboratory exposure could potentially restart SARS transmission, given the number of laboratories around the world handling the virus or retaining samples from SARS patients. There were also other laboratory-associated SARS infections around the same period, including cases reported in Taiwan and China. WHO subsequently strengthened its guidance on handling and storing SARS coronavirus material. Deadly Soviet Anthrax Accident An even more serious example occurred in 1979 in Sverdlovsk, now Yekaterinburg, in the former Soviet Union. An outbreak of inhalational anthrax killed dozens of people after anthrax spores were accidentally released from a military microbiology facility, according to US government and scientific assessments. A CDC review said that the accidental release of Bacillus anthracis spores resulted in 68 deaths among 79 patients with inhalational anthrax. Another CDC account describes the Sverdlovsk incident as the largest outbreak of inhalational anthrax in the 20th century. A scientific reconstruction published in Science concluded that an aerosol release from the Soviet facility caused the outbreak, with cases concentrated along a zone extending from the facility in the direction of the prevailing wind. Smallpox Escaped From A Laboratory Smallpox provides another striking example. The last naturally occurring case of smallpox was recorded in Somalia in 1977. But one year later, a laboratory accident in Birmingham, England, caused the disease to reappear. According to the WHO, the 1978 laboratory accident caused a limited outbreak and killed one person. It remains the only known human smallpox cases after the diseases natural eradication to have been caused by a laboratory accident. What About COVID And Lab Leak Question The Russian case is also likely to bring back memories of the debate over the origins of COVID-19. Although, there is no established evidence that SARS-CoV-2 caused the COVID-19 pandemic because of a laboratory accident. The origin of the virus remains an area of scientific investigation. In its latest major assessment, published in 2025, the WHOs Scientific Advisory Group for the Origins of Novel Pathogens said the available evidence favoured zoonotic spillover, meaning transmission from animals to humans. However, WHO also said that important information needed to fully evaluate all hypotheses had not been provided and that the laboratory-related hypothesis could not be completely ruled out. Could The Russian Case Become An Outbreak? That remains unknown. The key question is not simply whether Shipilova had plague, but whether she was infected with a pathogen capable of spreading to other people and, if so, whether anyone else was exposed. Pneumonic plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and affects the lungs. Unlike the more familiar bubonic form, pneumonic plague can spread between people through respiratory droplets. It can be extremely serious, but early antibiotic treatment can be effective. This is why the reported monitoring of nearly 200 contacts is significant even though Russian authorities have not officially confirmed plague as the cause of Shipilovas death. A 28-year-old laboratory worker named Darya Shipilova at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia died from severe pneumonia, sparking US concerns that she may have contracted pneumonic plague in a potential laboratory-related incident.

headline: Trump Mistakes Brazil For India, Claims 125 Million Voted In Presidential Election, Attacks US Voting System
content: Donald Trump appeared to confuse Brazil with India while commenting on Brazils presidential election, claiming 125 million voted in India. Voting in America is CORRUPT!!!" Trump added, signing off as President DJT". The election Trump was referring to was Brazils presidential vote, in which right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro emerged ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the first round. Bolsonaro secured around 47 per cent of the vote, while Lula received about 45 per cent, according to Reuters. Trump appeared to confuse Brazil with India, referring to Brazils presidential election as Indias Presidential Election. The Bolsonaro family and its Liberal Party made strong gains, with the party becoming the largest force in Brazils Senate. Flavio Bolsonaro Beats Lula In First Round Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, performed more strongly than most private surveys had predicted. Reuters reported that pre-election polls had forecast Lula leading the first round by around three percentage points. The pollsters missed badly," Robert Muggah, cofounder of the Igarape Institute, said, according to Reuters, adding that runoff polls showing a dead heat could also underestimate Bolsonaros support. The election campaign centred on the cost of living, corruption and insecurity. Despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has faced difficulties winning over voters dealing with high living costs, household debt and concerns over crime and gang activity. Bolsonaro sought to capitalise on those concerns, while Lula expanded welfare measures and proposed fresh debt relief for families. Brazils public finances also remained a major issue, with public debt above 82 per cent of GDP and concerns over sluggish economic growth. Bolsonaros stronger-than-expected showing could also have economic implications. Reuters reported that Brazils currency and stock market had risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger. Bolsonaro Family Scores Multiple Wins The presidential result was accompanied by a strong showing by the Bolsonaro family and its Liberal Party. According to AFP, the Liberal Party became the largest force in Brazils Senate, winning 19 of the 54 Senate seats up for grabs, although it fell short of an outright majority. The party will also be the largest in the Chamber of Deputies. Jair Bolsonaros wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, secured more votes than any other Senate candidate in Brasilias Federal District. AFP reported that commentators believe the 44-year-old could be considering a presidential bid of her own in 2030. Former President Jair Bolsonaros second son, Carlos Bolsonaro, was the second most-voted Senate candidate in the southern state of Santa Catarina. His youngest son, Jair Renan Bolsonaro, 28, was elected a federal deputy in the same state. US President Donald Trump mistakenly claimed that 125 million people had voted in "India's Presidential Election" while commenting on Brazil's first-round vote, before using the incorrect figure to attack the US voting system.

headline: Florida Designates CAIR, Muslim Brotherhood As Terror Groups, Imposes Sweeping Curbs | Exclusive
content: The DeSantis administration has cut state funding and campus access for the designated groups under Floridas new terrorism law, HB 1471. Florida has designated the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and the Muslim Brotherhood as domestic terrorist groups, opening the way for sweeping restrictions on their activities across the state, top Indian intelligence sources told CNN-. The move, approved by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet on September 29, comes under the states new terrorism law, HB 1471, and places restrictions on funding, contracts and access to state institutions. - 34% Teaching Posts Vacant In Centrally Funded Institutions: SBI Research - LPU University Descends Into Violence: What Can Justify Destroying Campus? | Plain Speak - 'Ghost', 'Rape' And 'Suicide': Why Punjab's LPU And Chitkara Universities Saw Unrest Within 48 Hours - LPU Unrest: No Batons, Pellet Guns Used On Students, Says AAPs Baltej Pannu Florida authorities have cited alleged historical ties to Hamas and CAIRs status as an unindicted co-conspirator in the 2007 Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing trial among the primary grounds for the decision. Florida Moves To Shut Down CAIR Activities Under the designation, CAIR and affiliated groups will be barred from receiving funding from state and local governments, while existing state contracts involving designated entities will be terminated. The action also seeks to shut down their activities in Florida and imposes penalties on affiliates under the states new legal framework. The restrictions extend to educational institutions, with designated groups barred from university campuses and student funding linked to them set to be cut off. Florida designated CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as domestic terrorist groups. The move was approved by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Cabinet on September 29. The designation comes under the state's new terrorism law, HB 1471. CAIR is barred from receiving funding from state and local governments. Florida authorities cited CAIR's alleged historical ties to Hamas and its status in the 2007 Holy Land Foundation trial. Students found promoting designated organisations could also face expulsion under the measures outlined by state authorities. Hamas Links, 2007 Case Cited Florida authorities have cited what they describe as CAIRs historical links to Hamas-linked networks while laying out the grounds for the designation. They have also pointed to CAIRs status as an unindicted co-conspirator in the 2007 Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing trial. The two factors form a central part of the states case for bringing CAIR under the ambit of HB 1471 and imposing restrictions on its activities. CAIR has strongly rejected the designation, calling it unconstitutional and unfounded. Why The Florida Move Is Significant Top Indian intelligence sources told CNN- that the move demonstrates how individual US states can create independent legal frameworks, such as HB 1471, to impose state-level terrorist designations without relying on federal enforcement. The decision also significantly expands the consequences of such a designation by taking it beyond funding and contracts and into universities and other state institutions. By restricting CAIRs operations in Florida and imposing consequences for the promotion of designated groups on campuses, the policy could reshape the boundaries of legal, campus and civil rights advocacy across state institutions, according to the sources. The Florida decision also comes amid wider action against Muslim Brotherhood branches and networks, including US federal measures involving branches in Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon and Sudan. The September 29 action therefore marks a significant expansion of Floridas state-level counter-terrorism framework, with the DeSantis administration using the newly created legal mechanism to target funding, institutional access and operations of groups designated under the law. Florida authorities cited alleged historical ties to Hamas-linked networks and CAIRs status as an unindicted co-conspirator in the 2007 Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing trial as the primary grounds for the decision.

headline: Brazil Election Heads To Run-Off As Bolsonaro Beats Lula. Another Rightward Turn For Latin America?
content: Off As Bolsonaro Beats Lula. Another Rightward Turn For Latin America? Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula in the first round but without an outright majority, meaning Brazilians will vote again on October 25 to decide who becomes the next president. Brazils presidential election is headed for a run-off after right-wing Senator Flvio Bolsonaro finished ahead of incumbent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva in the first round, but fell short of the majority required for an outright victory. Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, secured about 47% of the vote, compared with Lulas 45%. The two will now face each other in a second round on October 25. - Brazil Elections: Can Lula Hold Back Latin Americas Right-Wing Shift? | Flavio Bolsonaro | N18G - 'Something Bigger Than Me': Esteban Ribovics On Building Legacy Beyond MMA - Full Schedule Of ODI World Cup 2027: Tournament To Start On October 2, Final In Johannesburg On November 21 - Pranavi Urs Becomes First Indian Woman To Win Asian Games Golf Gold, Team Takes Silver The result came as a surprise after opinion polls during the campaign had generally put Lula slightly ahead. It also sets up another sharply polarised contest in Latin Americas largest country and economy, with the 80-year-old Lula seeking a fourth term and Bolsonaro attempting to bring Brazils conservative movement back to power. Flvio Bolsonaro Outperforms Expectations Flvio Bolsonaro, 45, entered the presidential race after his father endorsed him as his political heir. Jair Bolsonaro had already been barred from running and is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup attempt following his defeat in the 2022 election. Despite having a relatively limited national profile before his candidacy, Flvio consolidated support among Brazils conservative base and finished ahead of an incumbent who had been polling slightly higher during the campaign. The senator said he was very happy" with the first-round result and expressed confidence ahead of the October 25 contest. Flvio Bolsonaro secured about 47% of the vote in the first round. Luiz Incio Lula da Silva received 45% of the vote in the first round. The run-off election between Bolsonaro and Lula will take place on October 25. Lula first won the presidency in 2002, was re-elected in 2006, and returned in 2022. I am very happy with the real possibility that, three weeks from now, Brazil will give a definitive answer by choosing a modern government," he said, according to AFP. The first-round results also indicated a strong showing for Bolsonaros Liberal Party (PL), which had the most governors, senators and federal deputies elected in the results reported so far, according to the . Jair Bolsonaros wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, was also elected to the Senate on Sunday. Lula Admits Result Was Unexpected For Lula, the first-round outcome fell short of his expectations. I admit I was convinced I would win in the first round," he said on Sunday. The game is about to start. We are in extra time. In extra time, we will win over the Brazilian people." During the campaign, Lula cast the election as a choice between democracy and barbarism", while also putting Brazilian sovereignty at the centre of his pitch. The veteran leftist is seeking a fourth term in office. He first won the presidency in 2002, was re-elected in 2006 and returned for a non-consecutive term in 2022, when he defeated Jair Bolsonaro by less than two percentage points in the closest presidential election in Brazils history. That election was followed by unrest on January 8, 2023, when supporters of Jair Bolsonaro vandalised government buildings in Braslia. Flvio Bolsonaro has pledged to grant amnesty to his father and supporters held responsible for the January 8 unrest if he becomes president. What Happens In The October 25 Run-Off? Neither Lula nor Flvio Bolsonaro crossed the threshold required to settle the election in the first round, sending the contest to a head-to-head vote. The first-round votes do not carry over. Brazilians will vote again on October 25, this time choosing only between the two finalists. Lula draws stronger support from Brazils poorer northeast and among lower-income voters, Catholics and women, while Flvio Bolsonaro has greater support in the south and among wealthier voters and evangelical Christians, according to the . The contest also comes as several Latin American countries have elected right-wing presidents aligned with US President Donald Trump. The run-off will determine whether Brazil, the regions largest country and economy, follows that broader political shift. Crime And Economy Among Key Election Issues Crime and insecurity emerged as major concerns for voters during the campaign. While Brazils homicide rate has fallen, street crime, violence and drug trafficking remain prominent issues. Flvio Bolsonaro has pledged to designate Brazilian gangs as terrorist organisations and build maximum-security prisons similar to those in El Salvador. Lula has criticised the US designation of Brazilian gangs as terrorist organisations, while pursuing measures aimed at disrupting the financial networks of organised crime, improving homicide investigations and investing in prisons. The economy has also been central to the campaign amid high levels of personal debt and slowing growth. Lula has leaned on the social welfare programmes associated with his previous governments, particularly Bolsa Famlia, which provides financial assistance to families while linking support to requirements including childrens education and healthcare. Flvio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has proposed a public debt ceiling, government spending cuts and a revision of social welfare programmes. US-Brazil Relations In Focus Foreign policy has emerged as another dividing line between the candidates. Lula made sovereignty" a central campaign theme and at times accused the United States of trying to interfere in Brazils election. The president of Brazils Supreme Electoral Court, however, said on Sunday that no evidence of international interference had been found. Flvio Bolsonaro has built closer links with Washington and earlier this year successfully lobbied the United States to designate Brazils two biggest gangs as terrorist organisations, according to the . Tensions between Braslia and Washington had also risen after Trump used Jair Bolsonaros coup trial as justification for imposing tariffs on Brazil and sanctioning some Brazilian officials and judges. Flvio Bolsonaro has nevertheless pledged to maintain an economically pragmatic" relationship with China, which has overtaken the US as Brazils largest trading partner and remains a crucial market for Brazilian soy and beef exports. The October 25 run-off will now decide whether Lula secures a fourth term or Flvio Bolsonaro takes the political movement built around his father back to Brazils presidency. Right-wing Senator Flvio Bolsonaro finished ahead of incumbent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil's presidential election, securing about 47% of the vote compared to Lula's 45%.

headline: Pakistan Government Weighs Emergency, Governor's Rule In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
content: Sources say major decisions could be taken within the next couple of days if the deadlock with PTI administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa continues. Pakistans political crisis has deepened amid failed negotiations between the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government and the federal government, with Islamabad now weighing a range of constitutional and security options to deal with the escalating standoff. Sources said Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi held a detailed meeting with the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to discuss the prevailing political and security situation in the province. The discussions reportedly focused on possible constitutional measures, including the imposition of an emergency or Governors Rule, as the federal government assesses its options. - Governor's Rule In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? A top government source indicated that major decisions could be taken within the next couple of days, suggesting that the federal government is moving towards a possible response if the deadlock with the PTI provincial administration continues. Sources said the federal government is prepared to consider tough measures if Afridi refuses to cooperate with the Centre or continues with the protest mobilisation. Among the options being discussed are the imposition of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa or Governors Rule. Sources indicated that the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and President Zardari are reportedly supportive of constitutional measures to address the situation. The political confrontation is unfolding alongside a serious security challenge in the province. Sources said Pakistans security forces are preparing for a major operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa aimed at eliminating terrorists, with a large-scale military operation reportedly being planned. The convergence of the political standoff and security situation has added urgency to the federal governments deliberations. The Centre is now examining whether constitutional intervention, tougher action against the PTI-led provincial government, or a broader security response could be required. For now, the situation remains fluid, with the federal government, military establishment and political leadership weighing their next move. With negotiations having failed and PTI continuing its confrontation with Islamabad, the coming days could prove crucial for the future of the PTI government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The federal government is considering imposing an emergency or Governors Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid an escalating political standoff and failed negotiations with the provincial administration. Federal legal experts are examining Articles 232 and 234 of Pakistan's Constitution to address the worsening law and order situation and friction with the Centre.

headline: Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack On Ben Gurion Airport, Chose Airline For Israel Route
content: Hammami, who is under arrest in the United Arab Emirates, allegedly told investigators that he intended to kill Machchhar inside the cockpit The Omani co-pilot who attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv had allegedly planned to crash the aircraft into Israels Ben Gurion Airport in a 9/11-style attack, according to reports citing his interrogation by UAE investigators. Hamam al-Hammami, who is under arrest in the United Arab Emirates, allegedly told investigators that he intended to kill Machchhar inside the cockpit, continue flying the aircraft normally and secure the necessary landing clearances before deliberately crashing the plane into a building or an aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport, Israeli media outlet Ynet reported. - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views ? | - UAE Seeks Death Penalty For Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Over Cockpit Attack - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views | - EXCLUSIVE: FLYDUBAI PILOTS PAST EXPOSED | Barred in Oman Over Extremist Views, Then Hired | According to the report, al-Hammami allegedly waited until the aircraft was over Jordan before launching his attack. The timing, he reportedly told investigators, was intended to leave little time for authorities to detect or stop the plot before the aircraft reached Israel. ALSO READ | Did Israel Ignore A Red Flag? UAE Shared Flydubai Crew List Before Journey, Yet Omani Pilot Got Clearance He also allegedly said that if he could not reach the airport, he would crash the plane into a skyscraper in Tel Aviv or a US military base in Jordan. I Chose Flydubai Because It Flies To Tel Aviv In another revelation, Israeli Channel 13 reported that al-Hammami had selected Flydubai specifically because the airline operated flights to Tel Aviv. I looked into which airline flies to Tel Aviv. Thats why I chose Flydubai. I planned it even before I was accepted," he allegedly told investigators, The Times of Israel reported. The reports suggest the alleged plot was not conceived during the September 30 flight but had been planned before al-Hammami joined Flydubai. He had reportedly flown to Ben Gurion Airport several times in the months before the attack. During a visit to Israel in June, he allegedly used the trip to gather information and work on the plan, according to Israeli media reports. ALSO READ | UAE Attorney General Confirms Flydubai Co-Pilot Attacked Captain With Cockpit Axe, Calls It Terrorist Act Channel 12 reported that al-Hammami had initially planned to carry out the attack in July but abandoned it at the last moment because he had developed a friendship with one of the crew members. How The Plot Was Foiled The plan, however, collapsed after Machchhar survived the initial assault and managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering serious injuries. According to reports, al-Hammami attacked the Indian captain with a cockpit crash axe after asking to pray. Machchhar subsequently managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to enter and restrain the attacker. Two off-duty pilots then helped take control of the aircraft before it made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. During the attack, the aircraft reportedly plunged around 16,000 feet in less than a minute after al-Hammami interfered with the controls. Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera reported that he switched off the engines and pushed the rudders forward, sending the aircraft into a rapid descent. Machchhar later recounted the attack to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying al-Hammami had asked to pray shortly before striking him. The captain initially thought the aircraft itself had been hit before realising that the blows were coming from the co-pilot. Questions Over Pilot Vetting The latest revelations have added to questions over how al-Hammami was cleared to fly commercially, particularly on a route to Israel. ALSO READ | Al Qaeda-Linked Images, Videos Put Flydubai Co-Pilots Posts Under Scanner; Radicalisation Suspected Al-Hammami, 29, had previously been barred from flying in Oman amid concerns over his extremist views, according to reports. He had earlier been associated with Oman Air, and investigators are examining how information about those concerns was handled when he later sought employment elsewhere. The case has also raised questions over the sharing of information between aviation authorities and security agencies in Oman, the UAE and Israel. Netanyahu has ordered a review of security arrangements for foreign civil aviation following the incident. Israeli authorities are also examining whether anyone else was involved in the alleged plot. Hamam al-Hammami allegedly planned to crash the Flydubai aircraft into Ben Gurion Airport in a 9/11-style attack, or alternatively into a Tel Aviv skyscraper or a US military base in Jordan.

headline: UAE Seeks Death Penalty For Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Over Cockpit Attack
content: Hammami to face the maximum punishment for the September 30 attack, in which the Omani co-pilot allegedly assaulted Indian Captain Smit Machchhar. The United Arab Emirates is seeking the harshest possible punishment, potentially including the death penalty, for Hamam al-Hammami over the alleged terrorist attack on the cockpit of flydubai Flight FZ1073, Israeli news outlet Ynet reported. A senior Emirati source told the outlet that Abu Dhabi wants Hamam al-Hammami to face the maximum punishment for the September 30 attack, in which the Omani co-pilot allegedly assaulted Indian Captain Smit Machchhar with a crash axe and attempted to seize control of the aircraft. The report also said Israeli intelligence officials and aviation experts are assisting the UAE-led investigation. The Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, carrying more than 170 people, was forced to make an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after the cockpit attack. Passengers and crew members intervened and helped overpower Hamam al-Hammami, while other pilots helped stabilise the aircraft. He was detained in Saudi Arabia before being transferred to the UAE. - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views ? | - Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack On Ben Gurion Airport, Chose Airline For Israel Route - EXCLUSIVE: FLYDUBAI PILOTS PAST EXPOSED | Barred in Oman Over Extremist Views, Then Hired | - Flydubai Co-Pilot Hamam Al-Hammami Was Banned From Flying In Oman Over Radical Views | The UAE has officially described the incident as a terrorist attack. Prosecutors said Hamam al-Hammami attacked Smit Machchhar with an emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft. Hamam Al-Hammami Said He Wanted To Crash The Plane The investigation has taken a more serious turn following statements Hamam al-Hammami allegedly made during questioning in Saudi Arabia. According to The Wall Street Journal, citing a Saudi official briefed on his interrogation, Hamam al-Hammami told investigators that he wanted to crash the aircraft and was not afraid of dying. Other reports have alleged that investigators are examining whether he intended to crash the plane into a prominent location in Israel. Those claims remain part of the ongoing investigation and have not been independently established. Investigators are also trying to determine whether Hamam al-Hammami acted alone or had support from a wider extremist network. Israeli Officials Join UAE Probe Ynet reported that Israeli intelligence officials, including Mossad personnel, along with Israeli aviation experts have joined the investigation in the UAE. The probe also involves authorities from Saudi Arabia and Oman, while investigators are examining Hamam al-Hammamis background, online activity and previous aviation career. The investigation is also examining how Hamam al-Hammami was able to work as a commercial pilot despite earlier concerns about his conduct. Before joining flydubai, Hamam al-Hammami had worked with Oman Air. According to The Wall Street Journal, people familiar with his background said Oman Air had barred him from flying after authorities became aware of his interest in extremist websites. He was subsequently placed in a deradicalisation programme and assigned a desk job. He later sought employment elsewhere and reportedly joined flydubai in February this year. The United Arab Emirates is seeking the harshest possible punishment, which could potentially include the death penalty, for co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami following the cockpit attack on flydubai Flight FZ1073.

headline: 'No Guns, But I Have People's Power': Sohail Afridi Leads PTI March, Rejects KP Military Action
content: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa CM said the provincial government would not accept decisions taken behind closed doors and policies concerning KP must reflect the will of its people Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insafs (PTI) long march towards Islamabad, defying warnings from the federal government and declaring that his province would reject any policy he believes goes against the interests of its people. Afridi, who reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead the march, addressed thousands of PTI supporters at Gandi Chowk before the convoy moved towards Karak. The protest has been organised primarily to demand the release of jailed PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi Announces Long March for Imran Khan's Release - PTI Long March For Imran Khans Release To Begin From Lakki Marwat On October 4: KP CM - Governor's Rule In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? Shehbaz Govt Holds Talks As Crisis Deepens In Pakistan - Pakistan Political Crisis Deepens As Govt Talks Hit Deadlock; Imran Khan's Supporters Refuse To Call Off Today's March In a strongly worded address, Afridi said the provincial government would not accept decisions taken behind closed doors" and insisted that policies concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa must reflect the will of its people. I have no guns or rocket launchers. I have the power of the people," Afridi said, according to remarks reported from the rally. He also declared that his government would say absolutely not" to military operations and drone strikes in the province, while reiterating his opposition to what he described as policies imposed without consultation with KP. We will say absolutely not to any policy against the people of KP," he said. Afridi linked the march not only to Imran Khans imprisonment but also to what he described as a wider struggle over the political and security direction of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This is not just a Pashtun war, it is the war of all Pakistan," he said, urging people to come out in support of the movement. The KP chief minister also claimed that policies pursued over the past 22 years had contributed to the rise of terrorism in the province. He has repeatedly criticised the federal governments counterterrorism approach, arguing that it has failed to deliver lasting peace and calling for a policy shift involving provincial stakeholders. Afridi claimed that KP had witnessed peace during Imran Khans roughly three-and-a-half-year tenure as prime minister and alleged that subsequent policy decisions had contributed to renewed instability. These remain political claims by the PTI leadership. He also accused those making decisions behind closed doors of selling the blood of Pashtuns" and said decisions affecting the province should be made with the participation of its people. Only Imran Khans rule will prevail here," Afridi said, reiterating his allegiance to the jailed former prime minister. The chief minister further claimed that Imran Khan remained resilient despite the imprisonment of his wife and sisters, describing the former prime minister as a guarantee of national unity and the future of Pakistans youth. The march comes after negotiations between the federal government and PTI failed to produce an agreement that would persuade the opposition party to call off the protest. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has accused Afridi of changing an agreed draft and said talks broke down over issues including counterterrorism cooperation and implementation of the National Action Plan. PTI, meanwhile, has maintained demands linked to Imran Khan and greater consultation between the federal and provincial governments on security policy. The federal government has warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad, while Section 144 restrictions have been imposed along several routes in KP citing security and public-safety concerns. Afridi had earlier insisted that the October 4 march would go ahead under all circumstances" and urged supporters to keep the protest peaceful. He had also said PTI workers would march with their bare hands" and hand over anyone carrying objects capable of causing unrest to police. The convoy is expected to move through KP over several days before heading towards Islamabad. The PTI has said the march is part of its broader campaign for Imran Khans release and against what it describes as political and constitutional violations. The primary objective of the long march is to demand the release of jailed PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, alongside protesting against policies imposed without provincial consultation and opposing potential military operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

headline: Pakistan-Taliban Rift Moves To Moscow; India, China And Iran Join Key Afghanistan Talks | Exclusive
content: Moscow Format was established in 2017 as a regional mechanism for consultations on Afghanistan Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions will take centre stage as Russia hosts the eighth round of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan in Moscow on Monday, bringing together senior officials and special representatives from Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, China, Iran, Russia and Central Asian countries. The talks come amid a sharp deterioration in relations between Islamabad and the Taliban-led government in Kabul, with Russia signalling that it wants to use the regional forum to encourage dialogue between the two sides. - Incompetence, Negligence Or Worse? UN Rapporteur Questions Pakistan Airstrikes In Afghanistan - Russia Voices Concerns Over Civilian Deaths In Pakistani Strikes On Afghanistan, Calls Situation Serious - Afghan Taliban Minister Warns Pakistan, Claims Kabul Can Raise Flag In Peshawar In Two Days - Message For Pakistan? Russia Is Training Afghan Taliban Fighters With Advance Skills & Equipment Russias Special Presidential Representative for Afghanistan Zamir Kabulov said last week that the Pakistan-Afghanistan situation would be discussed during the consultations and that Moscow was ready to use the platform to encourage the two sides to reach a reasonable compromise". The meeting is expected to bring Pakistans Special Representative for Afghanistan, Ambassador Mohammad Sadiq, and Pakistans Ambassador to Kabul together with the Afghan delegation led by Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi. Pakistans foreign ministry has confirmed Sadiq and the countrys ambassador to Kabul will represent Islamabad at the consultations. However, there is no confirmation yet of a bilateral meeting between Sadiq and Muttaqi. A report citing Pakistani diplomatic sources said no such meeting had been scheduled, while the Taliban side has not indicated that it requested one. Muttaqi is, however, scheduled to hold a separate meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the Moscow Format gathering. According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the two are expected to discuss bilateral cooperation and current issues in Afghanistan-Russia relations. The broader Moscow Format consultations will cover political and economic cooperation between Afghanistan and regional countries, along with efforts to strengthen regional cooperation against terrorism and drug trafficking. A joint statement is expected at the conclusion of the meeting. India is among the countries participating in the consultations, alongside China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Belarus and Egypt have been invited as guest participants. The Moscow Format was established in 2017 as a regional mechanism for consultations on Afghanistan. The seventh meeting, held in Moscow in October 2025, brought together the same broad grouping of regional stakeholders and focused on political, economic and security cooperation. This years meeting assumes greater significance because of the worsening Pakistan-Afghanistan dispute. Islamabad has repeatedly raised concerns over militant groups operating from Afghan territory, while the Taliban government has rejected Pakistans allegations and accused Islamabad of violating Afghan sovereignty. Recent cross-border violence has added to tensions between the two neighbours. With both Pakistan and Afghanistan represented in Moscow, the consultations offer another regional platform for discussions on border security, terrorism and the wider political and economic situation in Afghanistan, even as the possibility of a direct Sadiq-Muttaqi meeting remains uncertain. The eighth round of the Moscow Format Consultations in Moscow focuses on addressing Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions, encouraging a reasonable compromise between Islamabad and Kabul, and discussing political, economic, and regional counter-terrorism cooperation.

headline: CBSE 'hack', IIT gig and US recognition: Nisarga Adhikary's incredible year at 19
content: September 22. It was almost an hour past midnight. Nisarga Adhikary was sitting in the Starbucks caf at IIT Kanpur. An email notification flashed across his screen. It was a message from the US Department of Justice, acknowledging his work in finding and reporting a security flaw within their systems. I was having my second cup of coffee when I received the email, he recalls. Nisarga Adhikary is only 19 years old. On paper, this recognition stood as one of the most prestigious accolades he could have ever imagined. Yet, surprisingly, he remained unfazed, showing no trace of excitement. I love to break stuff, Nisarga says. Hacking things is a part of me trying to understand how things work. The security flaw was not something he had been assigned to find. There was no college project or professional brief behind it. He was simply trying to understand how the system worked. Still, the recognition was the latest turn in a remarkable five months for this 19-year-old. In February, he first drew public attention for identifying alleged security flaws in the Central Board of Secondary Educations digital examination system and has since landed a job at IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity hub. Nisarga is from Siliguri, West Bengal. His parents, both senior government officers, wanted him to take the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) and he was preparing through a FIITJEE South Delhi programme. Then, his work began attracting attention. His parents were worried, Nisarga says, before they gradually became more accepting of it. Earlier this year, Nisarga began examining publicly accessible parts of CBSEs On-Screen Marking (OSM) system, the digital platform used to evaluate scanned answer sheets. He claims he found several weaknesses in the system. One, its One-Time Password (OTP) checks could be bypassed, allowing an unauthorised user to access examiner accounts without receiving an actual code. Two, poorly configured storage on Amazon Web Services (AWS) allegedly gave him access to about 1.8 million scanned answer sheets. Nisarga also demonstrated the account-takeover risk by accessing the account of a physics teacher on the live CBSE system. Asked about the ethics of accessing a real persons account, he says hed blurred the teachers details and used the access only to demonstrate the vulnerability. He reported his findings to the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), the government agency that coordinates responses to cybersecurity incidents, in February. By May, he had published a detailed account of what he had found. He had also come on television to describe and explain his findings. His revelations quickly attracted attention as students, teachers, and parents were already raising concerns about glitches, evaluation inconsistencies, and operational problems linked to the OSM rollout. The board initially denied that its OSM portal had been compromised, but later acknowledged that cybersecurity issues had been flagged in the public domain. Subsequently, on May 31, CBSE stated that it had been closely monitoring the vulnerabilities in the OnMark portal and that a team of cybersecurity professionals drawn from various arms of the government as well as the IITs had been deployed over the last few days to fortify the system. Nisargas findings soon became part of a wider political debate. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was among those who publicly praised him for raising questions about the CBSE system. Nisarga also participated in protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the NEET-UG paper leak and posted a photograph with CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke. He says he was invited to meet Rahul Gandhi alongside Sarthak Sidhant, who had separately flagged alleged irregularities in CBSEs tendering process, but chose not to go. Sarthak, an 18-year-old student from Jharkhand, had known Nisarga before they became publicly associated with the CBSE controversy. He says they met around three years ago on Reddit and credits Nisarga with supporting him during CBSE times. Kshitij Kapoor, a software engineer at AI research lab Nous Research, says he has known Nisarga since he was 14. He met him through Capture The Flag (CTF), competitive cybersecurity exercises where players find hidden text strings called flags inside vulnerable systems or programmes. Hes always had a knack for poking holes in systems. The curiosity hasnt changed much but the scale definitely has, Kshitij says. I was happy to see him get recognition. Having known him since so early on, it felt very personal to me in a way. Nisarga describes himself as a nerd all his life. He says he spends almost all his waking hours glued to a screen, claiming that he has no non-technical friends. Outside cybersecurity, he reads young-adult fiction, like The Fault in Our Stars. He is also a big fan of Japanese animation such as Tokyo Ghoul. He reads books about activism and says he is interested in activism for the rights of neurodivergent people, queer rights and internet freedom. His views on technology and society are shaped, he says, by what he calls neoliberal technocratic biases. He describes himself as socially very left and economically right. He looks up to the likes of Sam Altman and Mark Zuckerberg, the heads of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI and technology company Meta, respectively, for their drive to build things. Around the same time, Nisargas views on technology and government brought him to the attention of IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal. When the Centre moved to restrict Telegram before the NEET-UG re-exam, Nisarga criticised the decision, arguing that authorities had failed to prevent paper leaks while trying to restrict a messaging platform that could still be accessed through proxies. IIT Kanpur director Manindra Agrawal responded to his comments, saying he would need to sit Nisarga down and explain. He had already reached out to the teenager earlier, and the interaction eventually led to Nisarga joining C3iHub, IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity-focused technology innovation hub, as an Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Threat Intelligence Engineer. His job involves identifying and understanding potential security threats. Nisarga, however, remains sceptical of an educational system that measures people through examinations and credentials alone. You can have a PhD and still produce low quality research and do worse than your peers with no degree. It depends on talent and curiosity, he says. For now, he is settling into life at IIT Kanpur. He says the transition has not been difficult, although he describes Kanpur as a bit bad compared with places he has lived before. Eventually, he wants to work across technology, defence and artificial intelligence and may eventually return to formal education, possibly in the US or another country. For someone whose curiosity began with figuring out how computer systems work, the question now is what he will choose to explore next. But when that email from the US Department of Justice arrived, Nisarga did not see it as a defining moment for him. I was unamused. It was like any other normal Hall of Fame mention for me, he says. I think I work a lot and put all my time into research because thats the only coping mechanism I have. Why is he unmoved by this latest recognition? Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir once said that one cannot have a great social life at age 20 and achieve extraordinary career success at the same time, he says. It might sound toxic but hes kind of right, I feel.

headline: Lab Worker's Death From 'Unknown Infection' Sparks Plague Fears In Russia, Hundreds Quarantined
content: A laboratory worker has died after being diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown origin in Siberia, as Russia responds to a suspected dangerous infection. Russian authorities are responding to a suspected laboratory accident in Siberia in which a potentially dangerous infection may have been released, after a laboratory worker died following a diagnosis of pneumonia of unknown" origin, CNN reported. The incident took place at the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, near Irkutsk, according to Russian state media TASS. - Al Qaeda-Linked Images, Videos Put Flydubai Co-Pilots Posts Under Scanner; Radicalisation Suspected - Man Jumps Off 43rd Floor In Noida, Body Split Into Two; Had Checked In A Day Earlier - Russia's Nuclear-Capable Bomber Aircraft Crashes During Training Flight, Six Killed - 65-Year-Old Kerala Man Stabs Wife To Death Over Suspicion Of Affair, Then Dials Son To Inform Him However, it remains unclear exactly what infection, if any, was released, with Russias federal agency for infectious disease control, Rospotrebnadzor, saying the employee had been diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown etiology," meaning pneumonia of an unknown cause. The sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region, the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable," Rospotrebnadzor said, according to CNN. The agency said it had taken special measures in connection with the case of an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute." The death has nevertheless raised concerns over a possible case of pneumonic plague. Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighbouring of Buryatia, had said that the employee, a 28-year-old woman, had died possibly from the plague." A laboratory worker died after being diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown origin at an anti-plague institute near Irkutsk. Nearly 200 people were reportedly placed under observation, while quarantine was also imposed at a maternity hospital. Russian authorities said the epidemiological situation in Irkutsk, Irkutsk city and Shelekhov remained stable. He also stressed that there are no plague outbreaks" in Buryatia, CNN reported. Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev urged people to remain calm on Friday after an extraordinary meeting of the regional anti-epidemic commission was held with Russias chief state doctor. Kobzev said the meeting was linked to a suspected case of a particularly dangerous infection affecting a resident of the region," according to CNN. Quarantine And Medical Monitoring Precautionary measures have also been introduced around Shelekhov. An aluminium plant near the laboratory instructed its staff to wear masks. Artem Fominikh, director of the Irkutsk Aluminium Plant, urged people to remain calm, saying that there are many rumours and conflicting reports circulating." All identified close contacts are under medical supervision. At present, they show no signs of the disease, and their laboratory test results are negative," Fominikh said, according to CNN. CNN also reported that unofficial reports from the independent regional outlet Liudi Baikala said nearly 200 people had been placed under observation at the hospital in Shelekhov where the laboratory worker had been taken. The outlet also reported that quarantine had been imposed at at least one maternity hospital in the city. The reports of quarantine have added to concerns surrounding the incident, although the Russian authorities have maintained that the epidemiological situation remains stable. Gennady Onishchenko, a former head of Rospotrebnadzor, said the infection in the Irkutsk region was most likely not the plague." Even if plague were confirmed, he said, there will be no spread of this disease." Pneumonic plague is one of three forms of plague caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Unlike the other two forms, which typically spread through contact with infected fleas, animals or infected tissues, pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread from person to person through respiratory particles, according to the information cited by CNN. Patients with pneumonic plague can develop fever, headache and weakness, followed by rapidly developing pneumonia, shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing and, in some cases, bloody or watery mucus, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. A 28-year-old laboratory worker at the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov died following a diagnosis of pneumonia of unknown etiology.

Zhang is a licensed California realtor with JC Pacific Capital Inc. and has 130 sales and listings on her Zillow profile. Ting-Yu, an engineer in his 30s, studied at universities in the United States and has a young U.S.-born son with his wife, Hsiao Chen, according to Taiwanese media reports. He currently works for Dutch multinational electronics company Philips. If the PRC [Peoples of China] wish to obtain leverage over the President of Taiwan during any potential conflict, the location and pictures of the close relatives of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official, including pictures of their homes and cars, could be useful to the PRC," FBI Special Agent Kevin Holt wrote in the October 3, 2026, criminal complaint. Taiwan-China Tensions Taiwan has remained at the centre of high geopolitical tensions for decades. The island maintains that it is independent, while the Chinese government claims it is part of China. Taiwan is also strategically located along major shipping routes and is home to manufacturing facilities producing some of the worlds most advanced semiconductor chips. FBI Details Alleged Surveillance Mission The complaint alleges that Zhang and a man identified only as Individual 1" flew from Las Vegas to Seattle on September 1, 2025. The pair then rented a black Nissan Rogue and drove to the residence they were allegedly targeting. Images from a neighbours security camera included in the complaint allegedly show the two appearing to film" Ting-Yu, his wife and their child as they arrived home that evening. CBS News said it matched the images to an address near Seattle owned by Ting-Yu. According to the complaint, Zhang allegedly sent messages to a Chinese government handler through the Chinese messaging app WeChat. She wrote: Saw him. Young male. Its that young one," and I am videorecording," before sending two licence plate numbers. The FBI said the messages were obtained through a search warrant for Zhangs iCloud account. Zhang was in contact with at least two people whom she appeared to acknowledge worked for the PRC government," Holt wrote. Zhang Allegedly Received Assignment In China The complaint alleges that Zhang was introduced to one of the Chinese government officials in June 2025 by a classmate from Beijings University of International Relations. Holt said the university has close ties to Chinas Ministry of State Security. During a June 2025 trip to Changsha, China, Zhang allegedly booked a private room where she met the government official and received the surveillance mission, according to Holts affidavit. She later sent a message to the official saying: I can take care of this thing," the complaint said. On August 26, 2025, Zhang allegedly wrote: I will be busy with work in L.A. this week. I will probably go to Seattle next week," while the official replied: Ok. Thank you for your hard work," according to the complaint. Zhangs Background As a California Realtor Zhang is a licensed California realtor with JC Pacific Capital Inc. Her Zillow profile lists 130 sales and listings across Los Angeles and neighbouring counties. Ting-Yu earned a bachelors degree in electrical engineering from Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, Ohio, in 2012. He then obtained a masters degree in Bioengineering Innovation and Design from Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore in 2013, followed by a PhD from the Department of Bioengineering at the University of Washington, according to a profile from one of his academic publications. Taiwanese television news station SETN reported that Ting-Yu met his Taiwanese wife while studying for his doctorate. They married in 2018 and had a child in the United States in 2020, according to Taiwans national news agency CNA. Previous Cases Involving Chinese Agents In US Chinese government agents have previously been accused of spying on and harassing Chinese dissidents and pro-democracy activists in the United States. Federal prosecutors said Shujun Wang, 75, infiltrated a Chinese pro-democracy group in Queens, New York, and provided information about it to Chinas Ministry of State Security for 17 years. He was convicted in 2024 of acting as a covert foreign agent. Two people were arrested in April 2023 over their involvement in an unofficial Chinese police station in Manhattan that was allegedly established to monitor Chinese dissidents. The Justice Department has also warned about a Chinese security operation known as Operation Fox Hunt, which seeks to repatriate wanted Chinese nationals around the world and targets opponents of the Chinese government. New York-based Quanzhong An, whom prosecutors described as a leader of the U.S. wing of Operation Fox Hunt, was sentenced in March 2025 after allegedly harassing a Chinese dissident in an effort to bring the person back to China. In California, former Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang was charged in May with acting as a Chinese agent. She admitted to receiving payment to promote Chinese government propaganda in the United States, including publishing an essay on her blog denying forced labour" in China. Wanying Zhang was arrested by the FBI at Los Angeles International Airport on charges of acting as an unregistered agent of a foreign government. According to a federal criminal complaint, she allegedly surveilled and filmed the U.S.-based son of Taiwans president near Seattle.

headline: US Bombers Leave UK Base After Suspected Iran-Linked Terror Plot: What We Know About RAF Fairford
content: What We Know About RAF Fairford The withdrawal comes amid renewed security concerns following an alleged plot targeting RAF Fairford. The US Air Force pulled all its bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire following an investigation into an alleged terror plot targeting the British base. The bombers were redeployed to their home bases in the United States, a Pentagon official told the . A Pentagon spokesperson confirmed the withdrawal, saying: While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States." - '3 Vans, Masked Men': How A Farmers 999 Call Helped Foil Suspected Terror Plot Near UKs RAF Fairford - UK Sees 'Strong Indications' Iran Involved In RAF Incident; Tehran Says 'Barking Up Wrong Tree' - US Deploys Third Aircraft Carrier With 10,000 More Troops To Middle East After Trump's Warning - If Iran Had Nuclear Weapons, No One Could Stop It From Controlling Hormuz: US At least 10 of the 12 B-1 bombers stationed at Fairford flew out on Sunday. Some had arrived less than a week earlier as part of a regular rotation, highlighting how quickly the US moved to remove the aircraft from the base. Why Did US Pull Its Bombers? The withdrawal comes amid renewed security concerns following an alleged plot targeting RAF Fairford. US media reports said commanders received new or more urgent intelligence about a potential threat in recent days. The New York Times reported that the information was linked to threat warnings that had first emerged around three weeks ago but that the level of urgency increased sharply over the previous 24 hours. American officials have not publicly disclosed the precise nature of the intelligence that prompted the sudden departure. The move came after a dual British-Iranian national was arrested in central London last week on suspicion of plotting a terror attack. The arrest followed a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September. Six people have reportedly been taken into custody and subsequently released on bail as part of the investigation. British authorities have linked the suspected plot to Iran. Tehran has denied any involvement. What Is RAF Fairford? RAF Fairford is a Royal Air Force station in Gloucestershire, around 100 miles (160 km) west of London. Although operated by the British military, it has long been an important base for US air operations. The base has been used by American bombers during military operations in the Middle East and other conflicts for decades. Its importance has increased again amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Former British prime minister Keir Starmer had granted Washington permission to use British bases for what the UK described as defensive" strikes against Tehran. The US Air Force pulled its bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into an alleged Iran-linked terror plot targeting the British military base, which prompted heightened security concerns and urgent intelligence warnings.

content: A major fire broke out at the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertakings Anik bus depot in central Mumbai on Monday evening, officials said. headline: Donald Trump Vs Mark Carney For Nobel Peace Prize? The Winner Could Literally Be From Space
content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has emerged as a name in the wider Nobel Peace Prize discussion, particularly because of his international diplomacy. US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are among the names attracting attention ahead of the announcement of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize which will be announced on October 9 in Oslo, with the Norwegian Nobel Committee set to choose the winner from hundreds of nominations. The committee has confirmed that 287 candidates- 208 individuals and 79 organisations- were nominated this year but their identities have not been made public. Trumps Nobel Push - 'We're Leading Over China': Trump Hints He Doesnt Want To Work With Xi On AI, Cites US Secrets Risk - 'Super Intelligence Force': Trump Names Intel Chief Jay Clayton To Lead New AI Task Force - IVE: Trump Rallies Ohio Ahead Of Midterms | Husted & Ramaswamy Join | Reps Vs Dems | Midterm 2026 - 'A Decision To Make': Trump Warns Iran Of 'Easy Or Hard Way' As Tensions Remain High Trump has repeatedly expressed his desire to receive the Nobel Peace Prize and has reportedly been nominated this year by the leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan. However, his chances remain low, particularly as his administration wages war with Iran and faces criticism over its approach to international conflicts. Last years prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado after Trump had repeatedly lobbied for the award. Weeks later, Machado handed her Nobel medal to Trump in an apparent effort to win his support for her campaign for democratic change in Venezuela. The episode could influence how the five-member Norwegian Nobel Committee approaches this years decision. Haakon Gjerloew, acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO), told Reuters that the committee could consider whether awarding a particular candidate might expose them to pressure from Trump. One consideration, he said, could be whether giving the prize to someone could put them under pressure from Donald Trump" and whether the award would do more harm than good". What About Mark Carney? Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has also emerged as a name in the wider Nobel Peace Prize discussion, particularly because of his international diplomacy and Canadas role in discussions around global security and multilateral cooperation. However, the Nobel Committee does not publish its shortlist, meaning speculation around individual candidates cannot be treated as confirmation that they are being seriously considered. The same applies to Trump and other political figures whose names have appeared in public predictions. Nobel For International Space Station? One of the most unconventional names to appear in the 2026 prediction debate is the International Space Station. PRIOs updated prediction list, released in September, included the ISS alongside individuals and organisations involved in humanitarian work, human rights and conflict resolution. The space station could be recognised not for a conventional peace initiative but as a symbol of international cooperation. The ISS brings together astronauts and space agencies from countries that have frequently been geopolitical rivals on Earth. Despite those tensions, the station has provided a platform for scientific cooperation spanning decades. PRIO has argued that the ISS represents what countries can achieve when they work towards a shared objective despite political differences. Other Names In Nobel Peace Prize Prediction Race The PRIO prediction list also includes Ukrainian child-rights activist Mykola Kuleba, the Save Ukraine organisation, Sudans Emergency Response Rooms and the Committee to Protect Journalists. Other potential candidates include Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court (ICC), the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and Francesca Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Occupied Palestinian Territories. When Will The Nobel Peace Prize Be Announced? The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced at the Norwegian Nobel Institute in Oslo on October 9 at 11 am local time. The identities of the official nominees will remain confidential for 50 years under Nobel rules, meaning public lists and predictions cannot establish who is actually under consideration by the committee. The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced on October 9 at 11 am local time at the Norwegian Nobel Institute in Oslo, with the committee selecting from 287 nominated candidates.

Following the acceptance of Mohsen Paknejads resignation, Hamid Bovard", the CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company", has been appointed as acting Minister of Oil by a decree from the president", the statement carried by state broadcaster IRIB said. The official said Paknejad had offered to resign some time ago due to personal issues", but his request had initially been rejected. According to the official, Pezeshkian had asked Paknejad to remain in office. However, the president eventually accepted his resignation after the minister insisted on leaving.
