headline: Ujjain is preparing for 40 crore pilgrims. What will the ancient city lose?
content: With the state government approving 128 projects worth Rs. 13,851 crore, Ujjain is being transformed at a pace rarely seen in the temple towns modern history as it races to prepare for the 2028 Simhastha from new highways, bridges and ghats to five-star hotels. Ujjain has always resisted the march of time, clinging to its ancient city of temples, ghats, bazaars and British-era offices. Now, as Ujjain prepares for Simhastha 2028, its maps are being redrawn, hurtling the sleepy temple town towards a new modernity carved through its old streets with bulldozers, widened roads and concrete. On September 27, a crowd gathered outside the Shahi Masjid, where the administration was preparing to remove the portion of the mosque within the proposed road alignment, as protests raged over road-widening projects in Ujjain ahead of the 2028 Simhastha. Hours later, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav took an axe to his grandfathers ancestral home in Abdalpura. The demolitions came as the administration raced against time for the Simhastha Mela 2028, for which the government has approved 128 projects worth about Rs. 13,851 crore across 10 departments. For Yadav, Simhastha has become his governments defining project, with the administration effectively mobilised around a single task: transforming the ancient temple town before pilgrims arrive. On the ground, the transformation is unfolding on a scale rarely seen in Ujjains modern history. Highways are being carved into the citys approaches, railway lines and bypasses are being built, roads and bridges widened, kilometres of new ghats taking shape along the Shipra, and water and sewerage networks being laid underground. What is taking shape is not simply a city preparing for a festival, but a centuries-old temple town being physically remade into a modern pilgrimage city. Simhastha Mela Authority director Jagdish Aggarwals office in Kothi Road, a leafy neighbourhood, is less a conventional government chamber these days than a control room for one of Madhya Pradeshs biggest infrastructure exercises. Project officers come in with updates, meetings are held with swamis and other stakeholders, and meetings with the chief minister are woven into a schedule dominated by Simhastha. Every Thursday, Aggarwal sits with the collector and deputy collector for a review devoted to the same question: how to get Ujjain ready for 2028? We are preparing keeping in mind the possibility of around 40 crore people coming to Ujjain, Aggarwal said, explaining why projects that would otherwise appear excessive for Ujjain are being taken up simultaneously. But theres also a human cost involved: the eroding trust among residents. Yasin Khan, a local, welcomed the road-widening project but frowned upon the speed at which the administration proceeded. When the houses were marked in my neighbourhood, both Hindu and Muslim families came out and demolished portions of the houses ourselves. But the administration barely took us into confidence. Its better to demolish on your own than wait for the administration to come with a bulldozer. Changing Ujjain The most visible changes are on Ujjains roads. The Ujjain-Indore six-laning project, estimated at Rs. 1,692 crore, is under construction, while a separate Indore-Ujjain greenfield four-lane corridor, estimated at Rs. 2,935 crore, is also being developed, SMA officials said. A 98.73-km Ujjain-Jaora greenfield four-lane corridor, costing about Rs. 5,017 crore, received its foundation stone in July. Planned with seven flyovers, three railway overbridges, eight major bridges, 22 medium bridges, 36 underpasses and 430 culverts, it is targeted for completion by December 2027. It is intended to provide an east-west connection towards Jaora and the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway while taking long-distance traffic away from the city, SMA officials said. More than 80 percent of road and connectivity works had reached the ground, with the road component around 70 percent complete. Around 15 bridges are under construction, and we expect five or six to be ready for inauguration by December, Aggarwal said. More than 10 five-star hotels are either coming up or planned in Ujjain, Aggarwal said, alongside smaller hotels and guest houses. Along the Shipra, the government is building approximately 29.2 km of new ghats and associated works, stretching from the Shani temple area towards the Nagda bypass. The Rs. 778-crore project is intended to spread bathing and pilgrim movement over a longer stretch of the river, officials said. At Gaughat, Akram Khan, a project supervisor for a private company, said they would meet the deadline for the restored ghat by December. The restoration is taking place against an old British water works department office, built in the 1930s. Only the old English chimney remains as the Madhya Pradesh government races ahead with the modern ghat. We began work in May and employed over 100 workers per day, paying them at least Rs. 800 per day to finish this work. The reason we can race through the project is that the governments fully focused on this. From making roads to providing us with electricity and water connections, they raced through all that to help our project, Akram said. The second major riverfront project is the Rs. 919.94-crore Kanh closed-duct diversion scheme, intended to prevent polluted water carried by the Kanh River from entering the Shipra. The scheme involves a 30.15-km diversion system, including an 18.15-km cut-and-cover section and a 12-km tunnel. Inside Ujjain, the road programme is being executed through municipal packages, with roads widened around the old city and Mahakal area. One of the most contentious stretches is the road from Khajurwali Masjid towards Ganesh Chowk, where widening work has now moved to the ground and brought the Shahi Masjid within the road alignment. Protests and race against time Across Ujjains old neighbourhoods, the transformation is not happening only behind construction-site barricades. It is happening at peoples front doors. Hindu and Muslim families alike have been taking hammers and pickaxes to portions of homes, shops and religious structures marked for demolition under the new road alignments. Lokendra Nigam, a cloth merchant from Chattri Chowk, lamented the removal of a small portion of his shop. We are doing it for the Simhastha. Of course, we understand the devotees need space to move. But we should be adequately compensated. We feel the authorities dont listen to us. At the Simhastha division of the Madhya Pradesh Public Works Department, Executive Engineer Praful Jain studies the map of Ujjain on his computer, tracking projects for Simhastha 2028. The PWDs Simhastha division has 20 works underway, Jain said, including an underpass, a bridge and road and connectivity projects. Among the most significant is the 629-metre Hari Phatak underpass, intended to provide an alternative route towards Mahakal Lok. More than 100 structures, on average, have been identified for impact across the underpass and elevated-corridor projects, Jain said. The focus, he said, is on resource and manpower planning, machinery planning and resolving issues on multiple fronts simultaneously, so that construction can begin at the appropriate time rather than waiting for one project to finish before another starts. Jain said the department is increasingly relying on precast technology to compress timelines. Beams, columns and girders can be prepared in advance and brought to sites for assembly. The road network is also intended to create capacity beyond the festival. Four-lane and six-lane interconnected roads are being developed at different locations, Jain said. The Simhastha works, in that sense, are being designed as infrastructure that can continue to serve the city after the festival. We want to develop international-level infrastructure across the world, like the Temple Mount in Israel or Mecca in Saudi Arabia.

headline: Kuki man found dead day after abduction
content: A DAY after he was allegedly abducted from his field in Kangpokpi district of Manipur, a 71-year-old Kuki man was on Sunday found dead with his hands tied behind his back in a nearby forest, sources said. The man was identified as Hemjang Haokip of Khunkho Kuki village near Leimakhong. He was reported missing after his field hut was set ablaze on Saturday. Haokips farm trousers, shirt and sweater were recovered during a search on Sunday, following which security forces deployed sniffer dogs and intensified the operation to trace him. His body was subsequently found in a nearby forest. The circumstances surrounding Haokips death and the identity of those responsible were not immediately known. According to initial reports, heavy rainfall on Saturday had kept many villagers away from their fields, and the incident came to light only in the evening. Haokip was known to frequently spend the night at his field hut. After learning that the hut had been burnt and Haokip was missing, villagers launched a search that continued until dark but failed to locate him. The Kuki Youth Organisation (KYO), Leimakhong block, had earlier demanded Haokips immediate and safe return and urged the authorities and security agencies to intensify the search and take action against those responsible. The Khunkho Kuki Village Authority had also condemned the abduction and issued a 24-hour ultimatum for Haokips safe and unconditional release, warning of widespread democratic protests if he was not released. The Committee on Tribal Unity, Sadar Hills, had separately appealed for Haokips safe release. Meanwhile, the Ariang (Khunkhu) Naga Village Authority, in a clarification issued on Sunday, expressed solidarity with Haokips family and said neither the village nor its residents had any involvement in his disappearance. The Naga village authority appealed against unverified allegations and speculation, warning that such claims could create unnecessary distrust and tension between the two villages, which it said had maintained peaceful and cordial relations for decades. The incident comes against the backdrop of renewed Kuki-Naga tensions in Manipur, particularly in parts of Kangpokpi district and neighbouring areas.

headline: CBI arrests DGCA official, firm director in bribery case
content: THE CBI has arrested Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Deputy Director (Airworthiness) Sushil Kumar Garg, posted in Chennai, and Director of Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt Ltd Sushil Kumar Garg in connection with an alleged bribery case. The agency has alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs. 2.5 lakh for extending undue favours in the airworthiness certification of the aircraft operated by the private firm. According to sources, the payment was linked to regulatory clearances concerning the airworthiness of aircraft operated by Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt. Ltd. Airworthiness certification is a key regulatory process intended to ensure that aircraft meet prescribed safety and operational standards. Besides Garg and Bhane, the CBI has also named the company and other unknown persons in the case, officials said. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the role of other individuals in the case and to examine whether the purported exchange of money was part of a wider arrangement involving aviation-related approvals, the agency said. The CBI had received inputs about the alleged bribe demand, following which an FIR was registered and a raid was conducted, sources said. According to officials, Garg accepted the Rs. 2.5 lakh bribe, after which he and Bhane were arrested. The agency will move court seeking transit remand of the accused officer to bring him to the national capital for questioning, they said.

headline: Mecca Pact To Be Activated Soon? Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Meet On Houthi Threat
content: The meeting comes after a fresh wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The newly formed Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is set for its first major test, with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkeys Strategic Political and Defence Committee scheduled to meet in Riyadh on Monday amid a sharp escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemens Iran-backed Houthis. The emergency meeting will bring together the foreign ministers, defence ministers and army chiefs of the three countries to discuss the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the pacts operational mechanism and the next steps towards fully institutionalising the alliance. - White House Urges Saudi Arabia, UAE To Bridge Rift As Houthis Gain Ground In Yemen: Report - Pakistan Plans To Deploy Up To 25,000 Troops In Saudi Arabia Amid Rising Houthi Threat | Exclusive - Riyadh Private Schools Move Classes Online Amid Rising Houthi Strikes - Trump Brags Saudi Arabia, Israel Would Be 'Wiped Off The Planet' If He Weren't President The meeting comes after a fresh wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The group on Saturday claimed it had targeted an Aramco facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, while Saudi Arabia has reported intercepting multiple missiles and drones in recent days. Why Are Houthis Suddenly A Mecca Pact Priority? The immediate concern is the sharp escalation in the Saudi-Houthi conflict. Saudi Arabia is backing Yemens internationally recognised government, while the Iran-aligned Houthis control large parts of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. After months of relatively lower-intensity fighting, the conflict has escalated sharply in recent weeks, with Houthi forces making territorial gains around the Red Sea and stepping up attacks targeting Saudi cities and energy infrastructure. Saudi Arabia is now considering and pursuing a broader military response against the group. The timing is significant because Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7. The pact provides for collective defence, with an armed attack on one of the three countries to be treated as an attack on all three. The three countries have since been working on the alliances institutional and military structure. Pakistan has already signalled that it considers the agreement binding. Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif said Islamabad would make whatever means" available to defend Saudi Arabia under the pact, although he stopped short of confirming direct Pakistani military involvement in operations against the Houthis. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is a collective security pact signed on August 7, 2026, by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, stating that an armed attack on one member is treated as an attack on all three.

Its very easy to get disoriented and not know if youre turning, climbing, descending, etc." Transport Canada said it was coordinating with authorities involved in the search and rescue operation. The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information about the incident and had not immediately confirmed whether it would investigate. The Canadian-registered Gulfstream G100 air ambulance jet experienced electrical problems and dropped sharply from 24,000 feet to about 10,000 feet in two minutes before disappearing. The pilot declared an emergency and reported coming in blind as a storm approached the Nantucket coast.

headline: Ethiopia controls Tigray capital as regional rivals meet in Egypt
content: Ethiopian federal forces were in full control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, a local journalist said on Sunday (October 4, 2026), while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces began fighting again on September 23, sparking fears of a return to the devastating civil war of 2020-2022. The presidents of Egypt, Somalia, Sudan and Eritrea all of whom have difficult relations with Ethiopia were set to meet in the Egyptian city of Alamein on Sunday (October 4) to discuss the conflict. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of directly backing the Tigray rebels, with the added support of Sudan and Egypt, which all three countries deny. A counter-offensive has seen Ethiopian forces push deep into rebel-held territory, entering the regional capital, Mekelle, on Saturday without a fight, as TPLF leaders and troops abandoned the city. Federal troops were patrolling Mekelle and manning key institutions on Sunday, a local journalist told AFP, as communications were restored for the first time in more than a week. "We have taken control of Mekelle and we are marching forward," a commander with a pro-government militia told AFP. Businesses and shops remained closed, with owners moving stock to safer locations ahead of time, fearing looting and vandalism. "There are no police. Last night, we had to organise ourselves and take care of security," one resident told AFP, like others speaking on condition of anonymity because of the uncertainty of the situation. Egypt mini-summit The mini-summit in Alamein on the sidelines of an African Business Forum was set to bring together Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki, Somalian President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. Before the talks, Mr. Sisi urged "dialogue, not confrontation", as concerns grow that Ethiopia's escalating violence could spill across borders. Eritrea, which shares a long border with the Tigray region, is most directly involved in the conflict. It accuses landlocked Ethiopia of planning to invade and seize access to its coastline. Analysts say it has backed the rebels in Ethiopia in a bid to keep the conflict away from its border. The TPLF has long been the dominant force in Tigray, ousting a government-appointed administration this year. The rebels' leader Debretsion Gebremichael implied this week that the group would continue guerrilla-style attacks as they did when Mekelle fell to government forces in 2020 during the last war. Their insurgent campaign ultimately led to the TPLF retaking the city the following year. "We operate under a strategy to strike the enemy wherever we choose," Mr. Debretsion said. 'Cooperation, not competition' Addressing the African Union's mid-year coordination summit, Sisi said Egypt opposed foreign interference in African states and called for relations to be based on "mutual respect, good neighbourliness, dialogue and consultation, far from unilateral policies or narrow interests". He said cross-border challenges "require cooperation, not competition, and dialogue, not confrontation", including in managing natural resources and transboundary rivers in accordance with international law. The remarks come against the backdrop of Egypt's long-running dispute with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on the Blue Nile. The TPLF ruled all of Ethiopia from 1991 until 2018, when it was marginalised with the rise of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who hails from the Oromia region. The tensions led to a civil war from 2020 to 2022 that left more than 600,000 dead, according to the African Union, making it one of the deadliest conflicts in the world in recent times. The Pretoria peace agreement of 2022, brokered by African institutions and Washington, was never fully implemented but still helped keep a degree of peace until last year.

headline: China says 'divergent opinions' contributed to lack of G20 consensus
content: China said on Sunday (October 4, 2026) that "divergent opinions" fuelled by U.S. tariffs contributed to the lack of agreement on overcapacity and forced labour at the G20. The United States holds the rotating presidency of the Group of 20 major economies this year, which also includes China, India, France, Germany and Japan. Trade ministers held two days of talks this week in Milwaukee, but failed to reach agreements on countering overcapacity and forced labour, criticisms commonly aimed at China. A draft ministerial statement against excess capacity, seen as driving costs down unfairly, "was supported by all but a handful of members", top U.S. trade official Jamieson Greer said after the talks. The draft called on all countries to move to eliminate structural excess capacity in their economies, among other actions. "Issues such as overcapacity and forced labor have been highly controversial since their inception," China's Ministry of Commerce said in a statement on Sunday (October 4). It said G20 members are subject to tariffs related to forced labour and are "frequently targets" of investigations concerning overcapacity. "Against this backdrop, many members expressed differing views from various viewpoints regarding the presidency's decision to table these issues and push for the issuance of a joint statement and the establishment of cooperation mechanisms," it said. "... due to divergent opinions among the majority of members, the meeting failed to produce an outcome document on these topics," it said. "China has noted that the post-meeting Chair's Statement mentioned that the U.S. side, together with two other G20 nations, issued a statement outside the G20 framework on the issue of forced labor," it added. The statement did not specify which countries opposed it. A G20 leaders' summit will be held at a golf resort in Miami owned by U.S. President Donald Trump in mid-December.

headline: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all Houthi territory
content: Yemen's leader announced on Sunday (October 4, 2026) the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city. The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost large swathes of the country's Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab Strait a chokepoint for international shipping after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis. Yemen's government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital yet again on Sunday (October 4). "I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen's presidential council, said in a statement. Mr. Alimi called on all the armed forces "to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia". The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government's interim capital Aden, according to four security sources. The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city. "We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station," a police source in the area told AFP. Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. The military sources added that fighting in the area was ongoing. Taiz itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen's long-running civil war. "They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it," Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP. Muslimi also downplayed expectations over what the coming government offensive might accomplish. "In my opinion, it's meaningless, he added. Following several years of relative calm, Yemen's civil war reignited in July against the backdrop of the wider conflict in the West Asia. It has also drawn in Saudi Arabia leader of an anti-Houthi military coalition since 2015 with the group regularly claiming attacks on the kingdom's territory in recent weeks and declaring a blockade of its ships in the Red Sea. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Sunday said the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy giant Aramco's sites in Riyadh and in the oil-rich Khurais area in the east. "The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites," Mr. Saree said on X. Saudi oil exports were already under pressure thanks to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf. The Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded. They came a day after Yemen's government said its forces struck Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the southwest. The Yemeni government's air capabilities, however, are limited, and the Saudi-led coalition has long been the primary force carrying out airstrikes against the Houthis. Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes as well. Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014. That year the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of much of the country's north, with Riyadh's international coalition intervening the following year.

headline: Trump names national intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force
content: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (October 4, 2026) tapped Jay Clayton, his director of national intelligence, to lead a new government task force on artificial intelligence. Trump is calling it the Super Intelligence Force, because he has tried to rebrand AI as super intelligence. The announcement comes after Trump hosted top executives of AI companies at the White House last week and said they had signed a voluntary accord that would effectively self-police the development of the technology. The task force will coordinate the federal effort "to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans, Trump in a post on social media Sunday. The task force will reach out to consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and AI companies, the Republican president said. Others on the task force include the Federal Trade Commission's chairman, Andrew Ferguson; Emil Michael, the Pentagons chief technology officer; and Scott Kupor, the director of the Office of Personnel Management. The group will report to Mr. Trump and his chief of staff, Susie Wiles.

headline: City govt colleges seek new courses such as data science, AI and defence studies to attract toppers
content: To attract toppers, govt colleges in the city sought approval from the govt to start trendingcourses such as data science, artificial intelligence, defence studies and business management courses at the undergraduate level.Most of the city colleges have filled more than 90% of their intake for the 2026-27 academic year. However, colleges said courses such as history, economics and maths could not attract students as students are interested in studying emerging technologies even in the arts and science stream.Govt Arts College in Nandanam has filled more than 90% of seats of its 1,430 sanctioned strength for the 2026-27 academic year.We have attracted more top-ranking students after the college became co-ed last year. We wanted to offer courses such as data science, AI and defence studies to attract top rankers, a professor who involved in admissions in the college said.The college has submitted a proposal to govt on new courses.As of now, only two govt colleges, including Dr Ambedkar Arts College at Vyasarpadi, are offering a defence studies course which is very popular across the state. The defence course attracted more than 4,000 applications for 50 seats. Students who want to join the armed forces are interested in defence studies. However, there are no permanent faculty member to offer the programme. The college employed guest faculty through PTA, a faculty member from the college said.Presidency College, which has attracted more than 45,000 applications against a sanctioned intake of 2,380, also plans to start new courses such as BBA, defence studies and communication courses for the next academic year.The state govt should start courses such as BA defence studies with new faculty members in more govt colleges. There is a demand for courses such as sociology, public administration and microbiology as well, said S Suresh, general secretary, Tamil Nadu Govt Collegiate Teachers Association (TNGCTA).According to the data from the Directorate of Collegiate Education, 97,244 seats out of 1,26,959 seats were filled in 181 colleges for the 2026-27 academic year.

headline: 'Went out to play': 4 school students found dead in Thiruneermalai lake near Chennai
content: Four school students who went missing on October 3 were found dead in Thiruneermalai lake near Chromepet on Sunday, police said.The deceased, all residents of Krishna Street in Lakshmipuram, were identified as Pooja, 13, Khushi, 13, K Devadarshan, 12, and Yuvanesh, 10.The two girls were studying in Class VIII, while the boys were in Classes VII and VI, respectively, police told news agency PTI.The children had gone out to play in their neighbourhood on Saturday but did not return home.Their parents and relatives searched for them and circulated their photographs in local WhatsApp groups, but could not trace them.Separate missing-person complaints were subsequently filed at Chromepet police station late Saturday night.Around 10am on Sunday, residents spotted four bodies floating in Thiruneermalai Periya Eri and alerted the authorities.Personnel from the Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services (TNFRS) reached the spot and recovered the bodies, police said.A preliminary investigation suggested that the children may have entered the lake to bathe and drowned after getting trapped in the slush, police said.Family members identified the bodies, which were then sent to the Tambaram District Government Hospital mortuary for postmortem examination.Police have registered a case, and further investigation is underway.(With agency inputs)

headline: We are in talks with both Russia and Ukraine: Jaishankar
content: Disclosing that India has gone beyond advocacy to be a little more involved in the efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war raging since February 2022, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said Sunday that Delhi has been in conversations with both Moscow and Kyiv, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. His remarks, at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, came days after Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said India had put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war for the first time. Jaishankar said, We are seeing today an unfortunate conflict. Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict, and we believe that this will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months, we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. So we have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities. So those are ongoing conversations right now. He said India and Russia have historically had very good relations, particularly since the 1950s, and that history is not forgotten. For us, Russia and the Soviet Union before that was a country that stood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threat. And at a time when, you know, much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us, Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are obviously shaped in many ways by that legacy. Today, the relationship has widened beyond that. You know, it is again, the world has changed. We have changed. Our own relationships are not what they were in the 70s and 80s. Neither is the case with Russias, he said. So, like any relationship, it is refreshed. It undergoes a change. New issues come. Old issues sometimes get rebalanced. So it is very much more today an economic relationship as well. So there is a military component. Theres a nuclear component. There are space issues, but there is a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries, and of course, energy and resources as well. So, any country would, when you view another country, you judge it from our experiences I cant expect Europe, for example, to look at the world and say, okay, what does India think? And my view should be based on Indias experience. Europe will base its judgement on Europes experience. India will base its judgment on Indias experience. So Indias experience has been, frankly, quite positive and consistently positive, he said. On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He said Ukraine is prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and is also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea.

headline: India's resilience to global shocks built on broad reforms: Shaktikanta Das
content: Speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave, Das said that reforms such as flexible inflation targeting, the goods and services tax, digital payments and banking sector reforms were not designed as one-off measures but as buffers that allow the economy to absorb disruptions and recover rapidly. Indias resilience is not accidental. It is the outcome of broad and mutually reinforcing reforms, said Das, who served as the 25th governor of the Reserve Bank of India for six years until December 2024. Das also stressed that Indias strategy is no longer simply to grow rapidly, but to grow sustainably and resiliently over the long term. Das's remarks resonate with the recent assessment by Moodys Ratings, which raised its forecast for Indias real gross domestic product (GDP) growth in FY27 to 7% from 6%, citing the economys resilience to external shocks, stronger domestic demand and investment. He said that the countrys policy focus on fiscal consolidation and sustainable debt should also be viewed against the backdrop of high public debt in many advanced economies, where debt levels average close to 110% of GDP. Such high debt levels are contributing to rising bond yields and limiting the fiscal space available to deal with future shocks, he said. Despite a difficult global environment marked by wars, geopolitical fragmentation, unilateralism, technological restrictions, energy price volatility and rising inflation, India's real GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter of the current financial year, Das said. He added that average annual GDP growth during the five years after the pandemic, from FY2021-22 to FY2025-26, was 7.9%. Das identified strengthening governance and state capacity, building macroeconomic stability, and investing in long-term productive capacity as three broad pillars behind India's economic resilience. On governance, he highlighted improvements in public infrastructure, sanitation, financial inclusion, housing, electrification, digital services and welfare delivery. These measures, he said, have strengthened citizen-state engagement and confidence in institutions. Indias digital public infrastructure, including the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) framework, played a particularly important role during the Covid-19 pandemic by enabling rapid transfers of financial benefits, he said. Direct benefit transfers have also reduced leakages in welfare schemes, with estimated savings of around 5.1 trillion, Das said. The second pillar, macroeconomic stability, is based on five areas such as inflation control, sound government spending, tax reforms, a stable financial sector and careful management of the external sector, he added. Das said that the flexible inflation-targeting framework adopted in 2016 helped India navigate successive shocks, including the pandemic and the war in Ukraine. He also pointed to the governments roadmap to reduce the government debt-to-GDP ratio to 50% by March 2031. The goods and services tax (GST), introduced in 2017, created an integrated national market, reduced the cascading effect of taxes, expanded the tax base and improved compliance and formalisation, Das said. He also described the restoration of financial-sector health as a defining feature of Indias recent economic resilience. Gross non-performing assets of banks had fallen to 1.68% in June 2026, while bank profitability had improved significantly, he said. Indias external sector has also remained broadly resilient, supported by export diversification, free-trade agreements, a sustained surplus in services trade and steady remittance inflows. The current account deficit in FY2025-26 stood at 0.6% of GDP. The third pillar is investment in long-term productive capacity, including infrastructure and logistics, energy and manufacturing. Das highlighted initiatives such as Gati Shakti, the National Logistics Policy, Sagarmala, Jal Jeevan Mission and Udan, saying they had helped improve connectivity, logistics efficiency and market integration. Indias ranking in the World Banks Logistics Performance Index improved from 54 in 2014 to 38 in 2023, he said, with the country aiming to enter the top 25 by 2030. Indias diversification of energy sources across fossil fuels, renewables, biofuels and nuclear energy has also improved its ability to withstand external energy shocks, Das said. Solar energy capacity has reached 165 GW, while more than 50 lakh households have installed rooftop solar systems under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, he said. On manufacturing, Das said that production-linked incentive schemes, PM MITRA and Skill India were helping strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem. India has emerged as the worlds second-largest mobile phone manufacturer, while semiconductor manufacturing has also begun gaining ground, he said. Looking ahead, Das identified five areas that would shape Indias next phase of development: harnessing artificial intelligence, deepening the financial sector, promoting strategic self-reliance, pursuing sustainable development and investing in human capital. He said that AI could improve productivity, public service delivery, scientific research, healthcare and education, but India would also need to address issues around data governance, cybersecurity, concentration of technological power, algorithmic bias and AI safety. Deepening the financial sector would require greater development of corporate bond markets, pension and insurance funds, municipal finance, infrastructure financing and green and transition finance, Das said. On self-reliance, he stressed that Atmanirbharta should not mean isolation. Rather, it should involve building domestic capabilities while remaining integrated with global markets and pursuing more free-trade agreements. He identified global supply chains, strategic manufacturing, defence production and critical technologies as areas requiring greater domestic capability. Das also called for greater emphasis on sustainable development through green hydrogen, electric mobility, energy-efficient infrastructure, sustainable agriculture and circular-economy practices.

headline: Two students killed in road accident in Tiruvannamalai
content: Two college students were killed in a road accident when the two-wheeler they were riding hit a median on the ChittoorCuddalore Highway at Ethal village in Tiruvannamalai on Sunday. The deceased were identified as S. Krithik, 20, and M. Priyadarshan, 20. They were both residents of Chennai, and were studying at a private deemed university in the city. An initial inquiry revealed that they were returning to Chennai after offering worship at the Parvathamalai Temple near Arani when Krithik lost control of the vehicle as he tried to avoid hitting another two-wheeler and ended up crashing into the median. In the impact, he and Priyadarshan were thrown off the vehicle. Other motorists and passers-by admitted them to the Government Taluk Hospital in Vandavasi, where they were declared brought dead. A case was registered by the Vadavanakkampadi police, and a probe is under way.

headline: Clogged canals raise waterlogging concerns in western suburbs
content: With the northeast monsoon nearing, stretches of the canal network running through Porur, Iyyappanthangal, Kummananchavadi and Kolathuvanchery show signs of a system under pressure sections of the waterways are narrow, with silt, plastic and other solid waste accumulating along the bed, thereby reducing flow. The network is a crucial drainage route for excess water from the western suburbs towards Adyar river.The main interconnected waterways along this corridor include Thanthikal Channel, Porur Lake surplus course/Manapakkam Canal and Ramapuram Canal, besides the adjoining feeder and link channels. Thanthikal Channel, about 2.5-km long, carries surplus water from Chembarambakkam reservoir to Porur Lake. From Porur Lake, surplus water moves through the canal system via Moulivakkam, Madanandapuram, Mugalivakkam and Manapakkam before reaching Adyar.The 6.9km Manapakkam Canal passes through densely developed areas, making its carrying capacity particularly important during heavy rain. A metrowater inspection identified 20 sewage outfalls along the canal, with several found carrying sewage during the inspection. Experts say that with sewage outfalls, silt and solid waste, intense rainfall could increase the discharge of polluted water into adjoining low-lying residential areas. Previous flood-management reports have also recorded the vulnerability of the Porur-Iyyappanthangal-Kolathuvanchery belt when surplus-water routes are obstructed.Residents allege encroachments and developments along the banks of the canal have reduced its width by around 5-6 ft in some stretches over the past five years. S Vimala, secretary of Pasumai Karangal and a Porur resident, said the canals required regular maintenance and not just pre-monsoon cleaning. These channels are treated as isolated stretches, when in reality, they form a connected drainage system. If one portion is narrow or blocked, the impact is felt upstream, particularly in low-lying residential areas. Desilting should be followed by regular inspections to ensure the carrying capacity is maintained, she said.K Jayakumar of Kolathuvanchery said the 2023 floods exposed the areas vulnerability. During Michaung rains, several streets were badly affected, and residents struggled to move around until the water receded. Last year, rainfall was comparatively subdued, but the drainage problems did not disappear. Waterlogging remains a concern even without extreme rainfall, showing that the issue is improper drainage system and not the intensity of rain, he said. Kanchipuram district collector D Sneha said necessary action would be taken to survey the clogged canals and undertake desilting in the affected areas.

headline: Expulsion, suspension, reflection papers: How Cornell University punished seven accused in frat house rape case
content: How Cornell University punished seven accused in frat house rape case An alleged rape case of a woman at Cornell University in 2024 has shaken the campus, leading to severe to lightest punishment of writing "reflection papers.' According to The New York Times, the university has imposed varying disciplinary measures on the seven fraternity members who were accused by a woman of sexual assault following an October 2024 gathering at the Chi Phi fraternity house. The accused men have denied wrongdoing. While none of them has been criminally charged, Cornell University has reportedly levied some punishments for each one of them, depending on their involvement. The accused men are following: Matthew Ingalls: Ingalls has been reportedly expelled from Cornell after the university's panel found him responsible for the sexual assault. According to the report, the panel concluded that he had manipulated, exploited and endangered the woman (alias Jane Doe) for his own interests and the entertainment of others. Jonathan Newell: Newell has been reportedly expelled from Cornell. He was accused of sexual assault. The university's disciplinary summary found him responsible for conduct warranting expulsion, according to The New York Times. Winston Lee: Lee has been suspended for two years, followed by several semesters of disciplinary probation upon his return, added the report. He was reportedly ordered not to contact the woman, study sexual harassment and write reflection papers. Gillio Lopes: Unlike others, Lopes has been suspended for only three semesters, followed by two years of disciplinary probation. It is reported that he was also barred from contacting the victim and required to study sexual harassment and write reflection papers. Diego Sarabia: Sarabia has been reportedly barred from Cornell's campus for three years under a persona non grata order. It is said that he had already graduated when the disciplinary panel issued its ruling. Scott Norris: Norris is believed to have been placed under disciplinary measures that included a no-contact order, along with requirements to study sexual harassment, social media use and bystander intervention and also write reflection papers. Scott Kretzschmar: Kretzschmar has received similar disciplinary measures, including a no-contact order, educational requirements and more reflection papers, as per the news outlet. Reportedly, the university did not find him responsible for sexual assault but found him responsible for attempted sexual exploitation. The rape case was filed by a woman, identified anonymously as Jane Doe in court documents. Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September and alleged that she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house at the university. She also said that Cornell University didn't protect her or punish the accused appropriately. Following the allegations, Cornell shut down the fraternity. The university also temporarily suspended the accused while some of them were later expelled. The incident has drawn heavy backlash against the Ivy League institution as well as New York prosecutors for not filing any criminal charges against the accused men. Amid this, The president of Cornell University extended support for an external review of his institution. Sneha Biswas specialises in covering entertainment and pop culture, with a specialisation on Bollywood, Hollywood, OTT platforms, K-pop, K-dramas, and major developments in the US entertainment industry. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

headline: Why did AAP suspend one of their own in Punjab? All you need to know about MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana's row
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana on Saturday slammed the party leadership and Punjab government, alleging that they had failed to resolve the shortage of teachers at some government schools in his constituency. The AAP, however, dismissed the allegations and suspended Maiserkhana over what it described as "anti-party activities and indiscipline". In a Facebook Live earlier in the day, Maiserkhana, who represents the Maur constituency in Bathinda district, said he decided to raise the matter publicly after repeated efforts to address the teacher shortage failed to yield a solution. Challenging the AAP government's claims about improvements in Punjab's school education system, the MLA alleged that conditions on the ground did not reflect the picture presented by the party. The MLA became emotional while speaking about the issue, saying that his own son attends a government School of Eminence where, he claimed, teachers are also in short supply. He further alleged that he is the only legislator from the ruling party whose children attend a government school. "I am going live after feeling sad. I kept demanding the filling of teacher posts, but it has not been done yet," the AAP MLA said, while directing his criticism at the government led by his own party. He said that after bringing the teacher shortage to the party leadership's attention, he was informed that the chief minister wanted to meet him. "But he did not meet me," he claimed, further stating, "How long will I tolerate? What did I do wrong to the party?" The AAP legislator stated he was aware that the party could deny him a ticket in the forthcoming elections, but maintained that this would not stop him from raising issues affecting people. "But I will continue to fight for people," he said. He said he had approached the party's senior leadership with his concerns but claimed that no solution had been found. "Tell me where I am wrong," he said. The MLA also said he was worried that an FIR could be registered against him over his criticism. According to him, the school principal had even told his son to ask him to ensure that vacant teaching positions were filled. My fight is for schools. If nothing is done in schools, then what will one do with such education? Among all MLAs, only my children study in a government school," he added. Following the MLA's public criticism, Punjab AAP general secretary Harchand Singh Barsat announced that Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana had been suspended from the party with immediate effect. Issuing the suspension, Barsat stated, It has come to the notice of the party that you have been found involved in anti-party activities and indiscipline. In view of the above, your primary membership from the party is suspended with immediate effect. Opposition parties seized on the AAP MLA's allegations to attack the Punjab government and called for Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann to step down. Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh said Maiserkhana's allegations had vindicated the Congress' criticism of the AAP government's education policies over the past four-and-a-half years. He alleged that the party's claims of an education revolution were driven by publicity and accused the government of adopting a dictatorial approach. Singh also said Maiserkhana was the only AAP MLA to have enrolled his children in a government school. He claimed that, like many people in Punjab, the legislator had initially been persuaded by the AAP's Delhi model and its claims about transforming the education system. Today, the MLA himself has tearfully brought to light the reality of teachers and facilities in schools and the reality of ignoring his demands for the schools, Singh wrote in a post on X. The BJP's Punjab unit said Maiserkhana's account has "punctured the 'education revolution' narrative" promoted by the ruling party in the state. "A sitting AAP MLA, Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana, says he has repeatedly raised basic issues like repairing schools and appointing teachers, yet nobody listened. "Now, he says that despite being a sitting MLA of the ruling party, he cannot even get an appointment with the chief minister. If an AAP MLA cannot even meet his own chief minister, then what does that say about the ordinary people who are trying to be heard?" Congress leader Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said. Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal also targeted the AAP government, saying its "fake" 'Sikhya Kranti' has been "exposed" by its own MLA. "Four years on, they can't even provide teachers in classrooms. What is the point of renaming schools as 'Schools of Eminence' when there are no basic facilities? Their own MLA says his children complain about the lack of teachers; principals come begging, but the government doesn't listen. Instead of wasting crores of rupees in the advertisement of these schools, they should have recruited the staff,"

headline: French student protests escalate: Up to 500 schools to remain closed on Monday, 5 October
content: Up to 500 schools to remain closed on Monday, 5 October Trisha Bhattacharya Up to 500 high schools across France will be partly or completely closed on Monday, 5 October, as a nationwide student protest movement over deteriorating school conditions continues to escalate. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said on Sunday that lessons would be totally or partly suspended at between 400 and 500 schools because security conditions could not be guaranteed. The figure is broadly in line with Friday, when about 400 high schools were closed amid blockades and clashes. Geffray also said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked since the movement began. The minister said 78 education staff had been injured during the unrest, according to French newspaper Le Parisien. The closures come after protests that began in the Paris region spread rapidly across France. Teenagers have blocked school entrances, disrupted lessons and gathered outside campuses, with some demonstrations turning into confrontations with riot police. Authorities say the unrest has involved fires, vandalism and attacks on police and school staff. Reuters reported that around 5,000 people, most of them teenagers, had been arrested nationwide since Monday, while more than 600 police officers had also been injured. The protests, however, did not begin with demands for confrontation. Students have been raising concerns about the conditions in which they are expected to study. Their grievances include overcrowded classrooms, a shortage of teachers and substitute staff, ageing or poorly maintained school buildings and long school days. Students have also complained about uncomfortable classroom temperatures during heatwaves and the pressures created by Frances university admissions system. Reuters reported that pupils in disadvantaged areas have particularly highlighted inequalities in education. Some students said they had been forced to sit exams despite missing lessons because teachers were unavailable. The government has acknowledged that several of the students complaints are legitimate but has drawn a firm distinction between peaceful demonstrations and the violence that has accompanied some of the protests. French officials have condemned what they describe as urban violence, while authorities have also alleged that outside groups, including elements of the hard-left, are exploiting or attempting to take control of the movement. Representatives of the France Unbowed party have rejected those accusations. The government has urged parents to prevent their children from taking part in violent protests. Paris police chief Patrice Faure said the movement had become out of control and called for a return to peaceful demonstrations. Despite the escalation, student unions are planning further demonstrations this week, while teachers unions have also announced industrial action. The continued unrest is therefore expected to put further pressure on President Emmanuel Macrons government to address concerns over school conditions while restoring order around affected institutions. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Camps to enrol first-time voters to electoral rolls to be held in the Nilgiris
content: Special camps will be held across the three Assembly constituencies in the Nilgiris to enrol first-time voters in the electoral rolls, the district administration has said. The district administration said in a statement, The Election Commission of India, vide its communication dated 29.09.2026, has directed that in States/UTs where the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has already been completed, a special drive will be undertaken by the Chief Electoral Officer, District Election Officers and EROs for the enrolment of left out and young/first-time eligible electors under the process of continuous updation. Declaration Form attached with Form 6 will be used during SIR phase only. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Camps will be conducted through the Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers of the three Assembly Constituencies in the Nilgiris for the enrolment of the names in the electoral roll, it added.

headline: Raised drain, uneven road hinder two-wheeler movement in Perambur
content: A 1.5-foot-high stormwater drain and an uneven road surface at the junction of Venkatraman Canal Street and Perambur High Road are making it difficult for two-wheeler riders to cross the busy stretch. Workers laid the road without milling it and raised the stormwater drain by about 1.5 feet, leaving a sharp level difference between the road and the drain, they said. Two-wheeler riders, especially those turning from the narrow Venkatraman Canal Street onto Perambur High Road, struggle to negotiate the junction.Following complaints, the zonal officer in charge of Thiru Vi Ka Nagar Zone visited the spot and met residents.The official assured us that a proper gradient would be provided to facilitate a smooth transition from Venkatraman Canal Street to Perambur High Road, said Perambur Neighbourhood Development Forum convener C Raghukumar . Instead of immediately rectifying the problem, debris was dumped at the location overnight, making the situation worse and further obstructing the movement of vehicles, he said.Residents said two-wheelers still struggle with the sudden change in level and that authorities have not addressed the issue. They urged Greater Chennai Corporation to provide a proper gradient and remove the debris before an accident occurs. Who will take responsibility if an accident occurs due to the road condition? The public is the one suffering. Authorities should act before an accident rather than after one, said T Yugaraj, a Perambur resident.When contacted, Thiru Vi Ka Nagar Zone zonal officer-in-charge Sathish said the stormwater drain and road surface were at the same level along Perambur High Road, a bus route, while the residential street lay lower. The drain may have a slope, but there would not be any issue for commuters or residents, he said.

headline: Want to be Argentine citizen? There are 2 routes: ₹3.37 crore payment or ₹7.71 crore bond | 'Golden Passport' Explained
content: Kanishka Singharia Argentina has introduced a citizenship-by-investment programme, popularly known as a golden passport, as President Javier Mileis government seeks to bring more foreign capital into the country. The programme was unveiled in Paris on Friday and is expected to come into effect in the fourth quarter. Argentina will become the first South American country to offer citizenship through an investment programme and, by population and size, the largest country in the world to introduce such a scheme. Under the new programme, foreign applicants will have two investment routes to obtain Argentine citizenship. The first option requires the main applicant to make a non-refundable payment of $350,000 ( 3.37 crore) to Argentinas national treasury. Applicants can include their families by paying an additional $100,000 ( 96.33 lakh) for a spouse and $25,000 ( 24.08 lakh) for each child below the age of 18. This means a family of four would need to invest a total of $500,000 ( 4.82 crore), according to a statement issued by Argentinas Economy Ministry on Friday. The second route involves purchasing an $800,000 ( 7.71 crore) government bond that will be specially issued for the citizenship programme. According to the government, money raised through either option will be used to continue strengthening the fiscal and financial position of the Argentine . Applicants will not automatically receive citizenship after making the investment. The government said every application will go through a rigorous evaluation process designed to preserve national security, the integrity of the financial system and the international prestige of Argentine citizenship. The authorities have not yet said how long the approval process will take. The programme will also include safeguards aimed at preventing money laundering. The new citizenship scheme could face criticism from Mileis political opponents, particularly with Argentinas presidential election due next year and nationalist sentiment growing in the country. The government recently faced resistance over a proposal aimed at making it easier for foreigners to buy farmland in Argentina. The bill had to be significantly diluted before it was passed by lawmakers. The arrival of billionaire tech investor Peter Thiel has also triggered protests and speculation. Thiel, who bought a home in Buenos Aires, has faced questions over whether wealthy foreign residents could gain influence over the presidents policy agenda. The citizenship programme is the latest step in Mileis broader effort to make Argentina more attractive to foreign businesses and investors. His government has introduced corporate tax incentives and legal protections for large companies, while also passing major labour reforms and moving towards greater trade and deregulation. However, capital controls and political uncertainty remain concerns for businesses considering investment in the country, particularly ahead of next years elections. (With inputs from news agency Bloomberg)

headline: India hikes deepwater gas price ceiling to $9.89 for difficult fields; Reliance-BP's KG-D6 to benefit
content: The government has raised the ceiling price for natural gas produced from difficult fields such as the KG-D6 block of Reliance Industries and BP to USD 9.89 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) for the six months beginning October 1, from USD 8.90 previously, while keeping the ceiling for gas produced from the legacy fields of state-run ONGC and Oil India Ltd at USD 7 per MMBtu. The new ceiling for gas from deepwater, ultra-deepwater and high-pressure, high-temperature discoveries is applicable for the period October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, according to a notification by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell of the oil ministry. Gas produced from such difficult areas enjoys marketing and pricing freedom under the government's policy, but is subject to a government-notified ceiling. The higher ceiling could provide some relief to producers developing India's more technically challenging offshore gas resources, where production costs are generally higher than those from mature onshore and legacy fields. For gas produced by ONGC and OIL from their nomination fields, the government has notified an APM price of USD 11.22 per MMBtu for October, but the actual price remains capped at USD 7 per MMBtu, according to PPAC. The APM gas price applies to gas produced from the legacy fields of state-owned ONGC and OIL and is used by priority sectors including city gas distribution, fertiliser and power. For gas produced from new wells of ONGC and OIL in their nomination blocks, the government allows a 10 per cent premium over the prevailing APM gas price, subject to the applicable ceiling. With the APM price for October capped at USD 7 per MMBtu, the effective price for new-well gas would accordingly be up to USD 7.70 per MMBtu. The higher price for new-well gas is aimed at incentivising ONGC and OIL to invest in developing additional reserves and bringing new production on stream, while maintaining the existing ceiling for gas from their older, legacy fields. India follows separate pricing mechanisms for gas from legacy fields of national oil companies and newer discoveries in difficult areas. In April 2023, the government shifted pricing of gas from legacy fields to a formula linked to 10 per cent of the monthly average crude oil import price, subject to a floor and ceiling. The ceiling was initially fixed at USD 6.50 per MMBtu and was subsequently raised by USD 0.25 annually after a two-year freeze. The APM ceiling was raised to USD 6.75 per MMBtu from April 2025 and moved to USD 7 in April this year. Before the 2023 reform, APM gas prices were revised every six months based on international gas benchmarks and had fluctuated sharply, ranging from USD 1.79 per MMBtu in 2021 to USD 8.57 in the six months ended March 2023. The separate regime for deepwater and other difficult fields was introduced to encourage investment in India's technically challenging hydrocarbon resources by allowing producers greater pricing and marketing flexibility. Reliance Industries and its partner BP produce gas from the KG-D6 block in the Krishna-Godavari basin, one of India's key deepwater gas-producing areas. Natural gas is a key feedstock for fertiliser production and is also used in power generation and by city gas distributors to supply compressed natural gas (CNG) and piped natural gas (PNG). Changes in domestic gas prices can therefore affect input costs across these sectors.

headline: AI Alerts to 'Plan Bee': How Railways saved 255 elephants from train collisions in northeast
content: Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) has used AI-based alerts, speed restrictions, enhanced patrolling and its Plan Bee system to prevent train-elephant collisions. It helped in saving 255 elephants between January and September 2026. According to Kapinjal Kishore Sharma, Chief Public Relations Officer, NFR, the elephants were saved across four divisions Alipurduar, Rangiya, Lumding and Tinsukia through timely interventions and coordination with the Forest Department. Timely interventions by NFR personnel helped save 255 elephants across its divisions, including 106 in Alipurduar Division, 14 in Rangiya, 122 in Lumding and 15 in Tinsukia Division, Sharma said. How AI alerts are helping detect elephants near railway tracks - AI-based Intrusion Detection System One of the key measures adopted by NFR is an AI-based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) that uses Distributed Acoustic System (DAS) technology. It provides real-time alerts when elephant movement is detected near railway tracks. This allows railway personnel to take timely preventive action and alert train crews in vulnerable sections. The zonal railway is also using other measures, including temporary speed restrictions and night-time speed restrictions when elephant movement is reported. Elephants near railway tracks in the Northeast, where Railways are using technology and other measures to reduce collision risks. (Image: NFR) - Plan Bee used to keep elephants away from tracks The railway has also installed the Plan Bee system at vulnerable locations. The system uses amplified honeybee sounds to discourage elephants from approaching railway tracks. NFR has also taken up the construction of underpasses at identified locations to provide safer routes for wildlife and reduce the need for elephants to cross railway tracks. Along with these measures, railway teams are carrying out regular patrolling, clearing vegetation at vulnerable locations and installing cautionary signs. - Train crews and passengers being sensitised The Railways is also focusing on preventing human activities that could attract elephants towards railway tracks. According to Sharma, railway staff, train crews, pantry car personnel and passengers are being sensitised against throwing food waste near tracks, as discarded food can attract elephants and other animals. The railway is also maintaining continuous communication with the Forest Department. Continuous coordination and real-time communication with the Forest Department further enable timely action whenever elephant movement is detected, he said. AI alerts, speed restrictions and Plan Bee are being used to keep elephants away from railway tracks (Image: NFR) Probe of train-elephant collisions The CPRO also added that all cases involving train-elephant collisions are treated seriously and investigated according to prescribed safety procedures. All cases involving trainelephant dashing are treated with utmost seriousness and investigated as per the prescribed safety procedures. NFR continues to strengthen technology-based monitoring, frontline vigilance and coordination with wildlife authorities to protect elephants while ensuring safe and efficient train operations across the Northeast, he said in a statement.

headline: Prime London Homes Are Increasingly on Frontlines of Extreme Weather
content: Bloomberg) -- More than a decade into a downturn caused by tax hikes, economic and political shocks, Londons high-end housing market has a new villain to contend with intractable heat and flood risks. The assessment comes from Prime Purchase, the branch of Savills UK that represents property buyers in the top end of the real estate market. Guy Meacock, a director at Prime Purchase, says too many premium homes in the UK capital are ill-equipped to deal with the fallout of increasingly frequent extreme-weather shocks. If London gets a reputation for having architecture thats fundamentally not fit for purpose, then its not ludicrous to think that it will have as far reaching an impact on property values as anything else, Meacock said in an interview. The development follows a summer during which Londons vulnerability to extreme heat was laid bare. Air conditioning remains a rarity, existing in less than 10% of properties countrywide. Even basic cooling features such as shutters and awnings have proved hard to get for some of Londons priciest real estate. More worrying still, perhaps, is the citys flood risk as freak downpours fueled by climate change leave a growing number of properties including those with luxury mega-basements more difficult to insure. The concerns add to the list of headwinds facing the UK property market, which is already under pressure from high borrowing costs. Nationwide, house prices fell in August on an annual basis for the first time since 2023, according to the latest figures from Lloyds Banking Group. Prime central London property values are down 26% from a 2014 peak, according to Savills. Heat in particular is growing more relevant for some of Londons priciest boroughs, according to Meacock. He says international buyers are deterred not only by the lack of features to protect properties from weather-related risks, but also by what they perceive as fiendishly complex planning rules that would complicate any efforts to upgrade homes. We are dealing with a lot of American buyers at the moment and the subject of air conditioning for them comes up every single time, he said. Buyers are staggered to learn how unusual AC is in high-end London homes, so your pool of potential properties suddenly shrinks. Climate change is leaving a significant footprint on the UK capital. The governments Environment Agency estimated in July that close to 320,000 London-based homes and businesses are now at high risk of surface-water flooding. In August, the office of the Mayor of London warned that extreme heat has become a major and growing public health threat in the city, with 86% of Londoners surveyed complaining of overheating in their homes. The impact of climate change is having a profound effect on peoples mindset, Meacock said. And although its not yet having a really material impact on values, that is going to be the likely pathway. He says Londons so-called golden postcodes, which are in the borough of Kensington and Chelsea, as well as parts of Westminster and its surrounding areas, are particularly vulnerable to shifts in sentiment from international buyers. With roughly half the buyers investing in such properties coming from outside the UK, sellers cant rely purely on domestic wealth, especially not with the current tax climate, Meacock said. A major concern is the receding availability of insurance, which is tied to how likely the UKs insurer of last resort Flood Re is to provide a backstop. The state-backed program applies only to homes built before 2009. In July, Flood Re unveiled a plan to ensure the program doesnt disproportionately favor wealthy home owners, which means commercial insurers with multimillion-pound properties on their books wont enjoy the same public support they used to. That change is expected to come into force from 2028. Flats in buildings with more than three properties also dont qualify for Flood Re. Tracey Garrett, chief executive of the National Flood Forum, a nonprofit that advises homeowners, says the groups helpline often hears from London residents who cant get affordable coverage. They just manage without flood insurance, she said. That means they end up covering the cost of flood damage themselves. And even though they may well be asset rich, theyre not necessarily day-to-day wealthy, Garrett said. At insurance broker Howden Group, staff are already fielding calls from clients worried they wont be able to sell high-end properties due to a lack of coverage. George Seatter, client director at Howden Private Clients, says he was called earlier this year by an agent representing the sellers of a 2 million property built in 2019 in Buckinghamshire, west of London. The propertys location close to the river Thames, combined with the fact that its not covered by Flood Re, initially left the buyers unable to find insurance. Commercial insurers would have mapped the property, theyd have seen that it was in a perceived high-risk area for flood, Seatter said. Theyd have looked at the fact that it was going to be a second home and built after 2009. Theyd have known that they couldnt cede it to Flood Re, and that wouldve been the end of the conversation. In the event, Seatter says Howden was able to arrange a policy backed by a US insurer. Howdens analysis of the site found that its precise location in relation to the river wasnt a disqualifying risk. Seatter says insurers who invest in more detailed analyses are picking up business from competitors spooked by the broader trend. From a flood risk perspective, were doing this all the time, he said. There are more and more properties that are in flood affected areas, and as an insurer, if you can then remove it from your books, so to speak, and you can pass on the cost to the client, almost, why wouldnt you? More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com 2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: India's Kusum Group pharma plant in Ukraine comes under attack, says report: What to know
content: A Pharma plant in Ukraine has been attacked by Russian drones amid conflicts between the two nations, as per reports. The plant is said to belong to India's Kusum group. According to a report by , the incident has caused an overall loss of 400 crore, leaving one dead and several injured. The main structure of the plant in Ukraine's Sumy has been largely destroyed, said officials to . Reportedly, the number of casualties and injured is subject to change as rescue operations are said to be underway. Several visuals from the attack have now emerged on X. In them, a large plume of smoke was seen rising from the plant area where the drones allegedly struck. The Kusum Group, identified as a Ukrainian pharmaceutical company, started in 1994. It operates as a distributor exporting Indian medicines to Ukraine. In 2002, the company began distributing its own brands. It moved its manufacturing, opening plants in India in 2007, followed by the one in Ukraine in 2009. It also has two more facilities in India. The group produces more than 50 generic products. All of these are supplied for sale in countries like Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and the Philippines. Kusum Group is headed by India's Rajeev Gupta. Reacting to the alleged attack, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky shared a post on X, calling it the Russian attack. He also extended condolences to the family and loved ones of the one who died in the incident. "This morning, the Russians once again struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv with a drone. They attacked an ordinary pharmaceutical warehouse in Sumy with drones. Tragically, one person was killed. My condolences to the family and loved ones. In Dnipro, they struck a communications facility. Six people were injured as a result of these attacks," Zelensky said. "Overnight, the Russians launched 135 attack drones against Ukraine, more than 50 of them jet-powered. Kyiv, the Dnipro, Kharkiv, Donetsk, Sumy, and Zaporizhzhia regions came under attack. And among the main targets of these terrorists, as always, are ordinary residential buildings, critical infrastructure everything that makes up normal everyday life. There are power outages in some communities. Our services are working at the impact sites. "It is important that Ukraine is not left alone against this terror. This week alone, the Russians have used more than 1,900 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs, and 25 missiles against Ukraine. More than 800 of the drones were jet-powered, and Russia must be held accountable for this escalation. Today, Friedrich Merz @bundeskanzler Federal Chancellor of Germany is visiting Kyiv. A leader of a country that consistently demonstrates leadership in protecting the lives of Ukrainians from Russian strikes. We are grateful for all the support, and today we are preparing decisions to give us in Ukraine, and all of Europe, greater capabilities to defend ourselves. There will be important agreements between Ukraine and Germany. Russia must be stopped together. Thank you to everyone who is helping," he added.
