headline: In a first, Ladakh grows saffron on a large scale: Why are Iranian corms being tested on barren land? Know importance
content: altitude cold desert of Ladakh is witnessing a large-scale experiment in saffron cultivation, as the Union Territory administration looks to turn previously barren land into productive farmland and explore new sources of income for local communities, according to news agency PTI. Around 800 kg of premium Iranian saffron corms, numbering nearly 90,000, have been planted across 4,000 square metres at Spituk Pharka in Leh, Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena said on Friday. The cultivation is taking place on land restored under Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative focused on improving water availability and bringing degraded land back into agricultural use in the mountainous region. I am pleased to announce an ambitious experiment of introducing saffron cultivation to Ladakh, for the very first time, on a large scale, Saxena said in a post on X. The administration hopes the high-value crop could help expand the regions agricultural options and generate additional livelihood opportunities for farmers, young people and self-help groups. According to Saxena, the Iranian saffron corms were chosen after considering their ability to adapt to Ladakhs high-altitude agro-climatic conditions. The experiment follows nearly two years of efforts by the Ladakh administration and scientific institutions to determine whether saffron can be grown successfully in the region. Trials for saffron cultivation in Ladakh have already been underway. In March 2025, the administration said the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (CSIR-IIIM) was conducting cultivation trials in the region. The administration had also proposed working with CSIR-IIIM to examine whether saffron cultivation could be economically viable and determine which varieties would be best suited to Ladakhs local conditions. Kargil has emerged as another potential location for the crop. In September 2025, the Agriculture Department, along with CSIR-IIIM, provided saffron corms to progressive farmers in the district and conducted training programmes covering scientific cultivation and post-harvest practices. The Leh experiment is part of a wider effort to make agriculture more viable in an area where farming is challenged by limited rainfall, a short cultivation window and extreme weather conditions. Launched in April, Project Him Sarovar aims to conserve water from snowfall and glacial melt by developing water bodies that can support irrigation and strengthen long-term water security. A water body constructed at Spituk Pharka was inaugurated in June at an altitude of about 11,500 feet. The administration said the project would help provide irrigation and enable agricultural activity on land that had remained barren. If the experiment proves successful, saffron could become another high-value agricultural crop for Ladakh, while supporting the administration's efforts to diversify farming and create new livelihood opportunities. headline: New GRAP Rules in Delhi; Restrictions in NCR October 2026: How your car's year of purchase will decide entry in capital
content: NCR's revised Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) has tightened restrictions on certain vehicles as the region prepares for annual worsening of air quality during winter months. The new measures notified by Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has made many changes from the earlier restrictions. For car owners, however, the question this year is not how old the vehicle is or when it was purchased but the vehicle's fuel type and BS emission standard. While there are no restrictions in first two stages of GRAP, under Stage III, strict restrictions will apply to BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel light motor vehicles (LMVs) in Delhi and five NCR districts: Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar. So, as a car owner in Delhi-NCR, what do these new rules mean for you? Here is what you need to know. The first thing that matters to you is whether you own a petrol variant car or diesel variant. This matters because the Stage III restrictions specifically target BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel LMVs. Unlike earlier guidelines, the revised GRAP rules does not impose the same restriction on all petrol and diesel cars. Therefore, simply owning an older car does not by itself establish whether the vehicle is covered by the Stage III restriction. As owners, you need to check the vehicle's BS emission standard. Under the revised GRAP rules, BS-III petrol cars and BS-IV diesel cars fall under the Stage III restriction on light motor vehicles. The restriction not only applies in Delhi but also in Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar. This means that as a car owner you should check the BS category mentioned in the vehicle documents and not assume eligibility purely from the vehicle's age. The year of purchase alone does not determine the vehicle's BS category in the revised GRAP document. According to the CAQM notification, the restrictions apply because of BS emission standard and not by purchase year. Therefore, the safest way for a car owner to establish whether the vehicle falls under the restriction is to check its BS emission classification in the relevant vehicle documents. You can also check the information on government's Parivahan portal. There by following some simple steps you can check your vehicle's status. If restrictions under Stage III of GRAP is invoked, the governments in NCR cities and the Delhi government will be required to impose strict restrictions on: BS-III petrol LMVs and BS-IV diesel LMVs. The restriction applies in Delhi as well as in high-vehicle-density districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar. The revised GRAP document defines Stage III as AQI 401-450. The amended GRAP plan also allows measures to be invoked in advance based on weather and air-quality forecasts. Yes, depending on the type of vehicle. For private LMVs, the Stage III provision specifically covers Delhi and the five identified high-vehicle-density districts. The document separately contains restrictions based on registration for certain goods vehicles. For example, Delhi-registered diesel BS-IV and below-standard medium goods vehicles face restrictions in Delhi, while such vehicles registered outside Delhi will not be permitted to enter Delhi. Diesel BS-IV and below-standard light goods vehicles registered outside Delhi are also barred from entering Delhi under Stage III. So private car owners should not automatically apply the goods-vehicle rules to their vehicles. The revised rules specifically include Gautam Buddha Nagar, which covers Noida, along with Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat and Ghaziabad in the Stage III restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel LMVs. So when Stage III is in force and you own one of these vehicles, then you need to take into account restrictions not only in Delhi but also in these specified NCR districts. The revised GRAP schedule provides for strict restrictions on plying of these vehicles once Stage III is invoked. It does not provide a general exemption simply because the owner needs to travel into Delhi. Therefore, if you own one of these vehicles then you need to check whether Stage III has been invoked before planning to drive in the restricted areas. It is also important to remember that GRAP restrictions are cumulative, meaning when a higher stage is invoked, restrictions from the earlier stages continue as well. There is a specific exemption for persons with disabilities. The revised GRAP document says BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel LMVs may be used by persons with disabilities provided the vehicles have been specifically adapted for them and are used only for their personal use. A valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate is important, but it does not override the separate BS-standard-based restrictions under Stage III. The revised GRAP plan requires authorities to strictly enforce PUC norms from Stage I, including action against visibly polluting vehicles through impounding and/or penalties. It also calls for enforcement of existing restrictions on overaged petrol and diesel vehicles. So having a valid PUC should not be interpreted as an exemption from a GRAP restriction that applies to the vehicle's BS category. The revised GRAP document calls for strict restrictions and enforcement against vehicles covered by the relevant provisions. It also specifies enforcement agencies including transport authorities and traffic police. However, it does not specify a separate penalty amount for driving a BS-III petrol or BS-IV diesel LMV in violation of the Stage

headline: Narcotic drug offences: Bail can be denied even after one year of incarceration, says Madras HC
content: In a case booked for possession of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, courts can deny bail even after one year of incarceration if there were reasonable grounds to believe that the accused could be guilty of the offence, the Madras High Court has held. Justice N. Ramesh said the right to speedy trial of an accused must be read alongside and not in displacement of Section 37 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, which imposes restrictions on grant of bail to the accused booked under the Act. The judge refused to grant bail to Muneer Sheik, who was arrested along with his co-accused Javeed, by the Manavala Nagar police in Tiruvallur district on October 14, 2025, for being in possession of 55 grams of methamphetamine, a stimulant that affects the central nervous system. On inquiry, the accused had reportedly told the police to have purchased 45 grams from a Nigerian national and the rest of 10 grams from absconding accused Kayum Bhai of Dharavi in Mumbai. The Forensic Sciences Department had confirmed the seized substance was indeed methamphetamine. Any quantity above 50 grams had been classified as commercial quantity under the NDPS Act and hence the petitioner, if convicted for the offence, would have to suffer rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years and the sentence could be extended even up to 20 years under Section 22(c), the judge said. The petitioners counsel sought bail on the ground of long duration of incarceration, but Government Advocate (criminal side) M.M.I. Khaleel vehemently opposed the plea and contended the police had already filed a charge sheet against the accused before a special court for NDPS Act cases in Chennai. After hearing both of them, the judge pointed out that Section 37 of the NDPS Act categorically states every offence punishable under the Act shall be cognisable and no person accused of an offence under it shall be released on bail unless the public prosecutor had been given an opportunity of hearing. Further, Section 37(1)(b)(ii) mandates that when a public prosecutor opposes a bail application, the Court should not grant bail unless it was satisfied there were reasonable grounds for believing the petitioner was not guilty of such offence and that he was not likely to commit any offence while on bail. In the present case, the period of incarceration undergone by the petitioner does not, at this stage, outweigh the bar under Section 37 of the NDPS Act. I am not satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the petitioner is not guilty of the offence alleged, the judge said and dismissed the bail plea.

headline: Sergey Brin may be asked to pay $13 billion wealth tax: Google co-founder spends $102 million to avoid paying it
content: founder Sergey Brin has spent $102 million so far to oppose Californias proposed billionaire wealth tax. According to Fortune, campaign filings show that he is the biggest individual contributor opposing the proposal. His donations went to Building a Better California, a political funding and advocacy group. It opposes the tax and supports business policies, affordable housing and infrastructure. Total funding against the proposal has crossed $187 million. Supporters have raised about $32 million. Proposition 40 will appear on the ballot in November. It proposes a one-time 5% tax on Californias 200 billionaires. Around 90% of the money would support the states healthcare programme. The remaining 10% would fund education, food assistance and administration. Brins wealth is nearly $260 billion. He could therefore face a tax bill of about $13 billion. The debate reflects Californias sharp gap between rich and poor residents. Its economy is worth $4 trillion, roughly matching the United Kingdoms economy. Yet, 18% of its residents live below the poverty line. This is the countrys highest share, partly because living costs are high. Former Google chief Eric Schmidt and PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel have also funded opposition groups. Brin linked his concerns to his familys escape from the Soviet Union in 1979. He said he had feared California could face similar conditions. Governor Gavin Newsom also opposes the measure. He argues that losing wealthy taxpayers could reduce the money available for public services. These include education, childcare, policing and firefighting. Meanwhile, some billionaires have moved business interests outside California. State records now list Brin as a Nevada resident. He reportedly bought a $51 million home near Miami Beach in March. Google co-founder Larry Page moved several assets outside the state. His family office, Koop, was incorporated in Delaware in December 2025. Oceankind, founded by his wife Lucy Southworth, was incorporated there around the same time. However, the financial impact of billionaire departures remains unclear. Six billionaires expected to leave could have contributed about $27 billion under the proposal. The measure is expected to raise $100 billion over five years. A May research paper offered another perspective. Californias billionaires paid $4.1 billion in income tax last year, according to Fortune. That represented about 0.2% of their combined $2 trillion wealth. Even universal departures would take about 25 years to offset the projected tax collection. If one-quarter is left, the lost income tax would take a century to match it, Fortune added. Researchers have described the proposed tax as small compared with billionaires wealth gains. They called it large compared with their existing tax payments. The debate continues until November. headline: UAE shared details about FlyDubai flight with Israel, including pilots' names, nationalities
content: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates shared with Israel a list of passengers and crew ahead of the FlyDubai flight on which a pilot attempted to seize control of the Israel-bound aircraft and crash it, regional officials said on Sunday (October 4, 2026), raising new questions over how the attacker evaded detection. While the investigation continues, preliminary details about the incident have highlighted several major security lapses. Officials already have said the Omani co-pilot had been barred from flying by his own country because of concerns about his extremist views. It also remains unclear how a citizen of Oman, an Arab country that has no diplomatic relations with Israel, was allowed to fly a planeload of Israelis to Tel Aviv. The United Arab Emirates, which is leading the investigation, said the co-pilot attacked the flight's captain with the cockpit's crash ax and tried to take control of the plummeting plane in a terrorist attack Wednesday. His actions nearly crashed the flight with 182 people on board before the Indian captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and others to rush in and subdued the attacker. The regional officials said Emirati authorities had shared information about the passengers and crew, including their nationalities. Israel hadn't raised red flags on any passenger or member of the crew, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to reporters about the probe. The passengers who halted the attack and helped regain control of the aircraft have been hailed as heroes in Israel. But officials have begun to raise difficult questions and trade accusations about the security blunders that could have led to a major disaster. The Shin Bet, Israel's domestic security agency, said the Transportation Ministry is responsible for vetting passenger lists from foreign flights. Transportation Minister Miri Regev told Israel's public broadcaster Kan that the security agencies are responsible for flight security and that her ministry wasn't given a list of passengers or any warnings. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Thursday that Israel has long-standing agreements with foreign carriers to keep pilots from flying into the country if they are citizens of nations that don't maintain diplomatic relations with Israel. It also remains unclear how FlyDubai, a low-cost Emirati airline that operates flights between Israel and the UAE, had failed to identify the Omani pilot as a security risk. Philip Baum, a visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University in England who wrote a book about aircraft hijackings and bombings, said background check systems differ from country to country and there are limits on what types of information can be shared. In terms of aviation security itself, obviously we want to have as robust background checks as possible. But there are huge limitations on doing background checks in any case, especially in cross-border checks, he said.

headline: BJP fields Dinesh Arya from Uttarakhand, Koel Mallick from Bengal
content: The BJP Sunday announced Dinesh Arya and former Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader and actor Rukmini alias Koel Mallick as its candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections from Uttarakhand and West Bengal, respectively. Biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, are scheduled for October 16, alongside a bypoll in West Bengal. Mallick will contest the West Bengal bypoll to retain the seat after joining the BJP following the TMCs defeat in the Assembly elections. Arya, an organisational leader with ties to both the RSS and Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, currently serves as vice chairperson of the states Water Resources Management and Regulatory Commission, a position equivalent to a state Cabinet minister. TMC split and Mallicks nomination Mallick, a prominent figure in Bengali cinema, was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the TMC in April. She subsequently resigned and joined the BJP in July as part of a split within TMC ranks, during which 18 MPs separated, merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), and extended support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government. With the October 6 deadline for filing nominations approaching, BJP leaders held discussions at the party headquarters in New Delhi to finalise candidates for the remaining seats, particularly in Uttar Pradesh. Party sources said the BJP is prioritising women candidates and experienced organisational workers as it seeks to expand its current tally of 116 seats in the 245-member House. In Uttar Pradesh, 10 seats are falling vacant, eight of which are currently held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) hold one each. The single seat falling vacant in Uttarakhand is held by BJP MP Naresh Bansal. While BJP leaders expressed confidence in retaining all eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, party insiders noted that one seat could be contested. With 256 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, the party falls slightly short of the required first-preference votes (37 per seat) to secure all eight seats outright without opposition. Currently, the BJP-led NDA holds 150 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, while non-NDA parties account for just over 100 seats.

headline: Jharkhand woman still in detention centre despite court order. Now HC asks, 'under what law?'
content: A Jamtara woman, then in her early 20s, was arrested in an alleged child kidnapping case in 2018. Sentenced to two years in prison, she was supposed to walk out free in 2020. Instead, she ended up becoming the first and, for a while, the only detainee at the Foreigners Holding Centre in Hazaribag over 190 kilometres from her hometown. Police accused her of being a Bangladeshi national and, for the next several years, she remained at the centre inside the Hazaribag prison. In June 2025, the woman, after allegedly being sexually assaulted multiple times by a constable, escaped from the centre with two other detainees. On July 20 this year, an Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court convicted her of escaping from custody but acquitted her of the charge under the Foreigners Act. However, on completion of her sentence, instead of being released from the prison, she was sent back to the detention centre. On October 1, the Jharkhand High Court asked a question that has followed the woman since she completed her first sentence in 2020: under what law is she still being detained? A division bench of Justices Sujit Narayan Prasad and Akhil Kumar questioned under what authority of law the woman was continuing to be kept at the detention centre after the completion of her sentence. Hazaribag SP told the HC that an inquiry would be initiated into the matter. According to social worker and lawyer Apurva Vivek, who filed a habeas corpus petition on the 30-year-olds behalf in the HC, the woman told her that she had been sexually assaulted multiple times by a police constable. The ordeal had caused her severe mental distress and was part of the circumstances behind her decision to escape. Ordeal began in 2018 Married young after her fathers death, the womans life took a turn when she was arrested on February 2, 2018, relating to the alleged kidnapping of a child. The same year, in December, she was convicted under Section 363 of the IPC and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment, with the period already spent in custody set off against the sentence. On February 4, 2020, the woman completed the sentence. But instead of being released, she was shifted to the foreigners holding centre at the Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan Central Jail (also known as JP Central Jail) campus in Hazaribag. It was there that authorities began treating her as a Bangladeshi national. For several years, the woman remained at the holding centre. According to the chronology placed before the HC, she was initially the only detainee there. In November 2024, another woman, Nina Akter alias Khushi, was brought to the centre. On June 10, 2025, the duo along with another detainee escaped. They were apprehended the following day at Dhanbad railway station. A fresh case was registered at Lohsinghna police station in connection with the escape. It is at this point that Vivek noticed something odd. Instead of the womans real name, she was registered in case records as someone from the minority community. Her fathers name was also found to be different that what it is in her original records. The case subsequently came before the Hazaribag court. The prosecution accused the three women of escaping from the foreigners holding camp and invoked Section 14 of the Foreigners Act. On July 20, the trial court stated that the prosecution had proved the charge relating to escape from custody and convicted all three accused under Section 262 read with Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). But the Foreigners Act charge did not stand, and the court acquitted the Jamtara woman. The judgment recorded several gaps, including the absence of authenticated cross-border records, original travel documents or validated nationality verification material establishing their foreign status. The investigating officer also admitted that documents including an Aadhaar card and SIM allegedly connected to the woman had not been verified with the issuing authorities. The court, therefore, while convicting her of the escape, acquitted her of the Foreigners Act offence. In its October 1 judgment, the court made a broader observation on personal liberty: We are living in the era of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the inherent liberty conferred upon a human being cannot be taken away without any authority of law. The court directed the Hazaribag District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) to record the womans statement. It also sought an inquiry by the Hazaribag Superintendent of Police (SP) into the allegation against the constable and directed the Inspector General of Prisons to participate in the proceedings. The SP told the court that a thorough inquiry into the allegation would be initiated. The Home Secretary of Jharkhand has been directed to appear before the court on October 5. Reports from the DLSA and the SP have also been sought. SP, Hazaribag, could not be contacted for comment despite attempts.

headline: India is going 'beyond advocacy' on the Russia-Ukraine conflict: Jaishankar
content: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Sunday (October 4, 2026) that India is going beyond advocacy on the Russia-Ukraine conflict, on Black sea safety, and grain export agreements. Talking on Indias stand on the conflict, he said, Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict, and we believe that this will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. Mr. Jaishankar was delivering a speech on From New Delhi to New Momentum: Opportunities for Emerging and Middle Power Cooperation at the Munich Leaders Meeting in Delhi on Sunday (October 4, 2026). He said, we have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities. So those are ongoing conversations right now. Commenting on ties with Russia, Mr. Jaishankar said, For us, Russia and Soviet Union before that was a country that stood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threat, and at a time when you know much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us. He added that Russia was a country with which Indias interests aligned. We are obviously shaped in many ways by our legacy, said Mr. Jaishankar Mr. Jaishankar said the government seeks a restoration of uninterrupted flows of energy, trade, and mobility, noting that India is paying the price in many ways for distant conflicts in which it has no stake. He further said, The change in the global landscape is underpinned by the changes in the U.S.s attitude to the world and the rise of China, as well as the weaponisation of every leverage.

headline: Germany's Merz in Kyiv for talks with Zelenskyy
content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, on Sunday (October 4, 2026) on an unannounced visit in a show of support for the country in its war with Russia. Kyiv is under increasing attack from Russian missiles and drones, which are targeting key infrastructure, including the energy sector vital for power and heating as winter approaches. "I travelled to Kyiv today because Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks," Mr. Merz said in a statement issued after his arrival. "If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us." Mr. Merz, whose country is among Ukraine's largest supporters, has been joined on the trip by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche, according to government sources. He was met off the train by Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, who said he would hold talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy "on all matters of our bilateral, European, and international agenda." "Ukraine and Germany have built a strong strategic partnership, and we are determined to deepen it further," Mr. Sybiga wrote on X. Mr. Merz said in his statement that he would tell Ukraine's leader: "You can continue to count on our help." The statement also touted cooperation between German and Ukrainian companies. The German Chancellor earlier this week called for unity within NATO, Europe and his own country, where the far-right and Moscow-friendly Alternative for Germany (AfD) opposition is on the rise. On Saturday, Russia warned foreigners and diplomats to leave Kyiv, saying "massive" new airstrikes would hit the city. The Russian Foreign Ministry declared in a statement that "responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning." Moscow had issued a similar warning in May, but leaders from countries supporting Ukraine have defied the Russian warnings and continued to make visits. Kyiv has faced heavy airstrikes and has repeatedly pleaded for additional air defence munitions to counter Russian drone and missile attacks. In recent days, Russia has attacked several bridges across the Dnipro river that divides the city, causing traffic gridlock and transport disruption. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Friday that the city, which is far from the front line of fighting between soldiers, was in a "very dramatic situation" and should now be on a war footing.

headline: Brazil Elections 2026: Lula vs Bolsonaro — How a Left or Right win could shape ties with US, China | Explained
content: As Brazil goes to the polls on Sunday (October 3), will the country join the "rightward shift" seen in Latin America in recent years? The election in Brazil has been deemed "deeply polarising" as voters choose between two starkly different visions for the country proposed by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Incumbent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and his challenger, Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, are the frontrunners in Brazil's presidential election on Sunday. Polls showed Lula and Flavio in a neck-and-neck fight. Reuters reported that an October 25 runoff is likely. In Brazil, Lula's victory is expected to keep the country a major leftist bastion in the region, alongside Mexico, while a Flavio Bolsonaro win would see the country join the rightward-shifting tide. The battle in Brazil comes as Latin America has swung sharply to the right in recent years. Right-wing candidates and conservative allies of US President Donald Trump won seven major presidential elections in Latin America in the past few years, most of them since Trump's inauguration in January 2025. Here is a look at the Latin American countries that elected conservative presidents recently: Trump-endorsed Abelardo de la Espriella secured a narrow victory in Colombia's June presidential election. A lawyer and business owner, Espriella pledged to reduce the size of the state, broaden the tax base, cut corporate taxes and restart oil exploration. De la Espriella is nicknamed The Tiger." His election marked a pivotal moment for Colombia, which was governed for the past four years by a former member of a rebel group, who was critical of the Trump administrations immigration and anti-drug policies, the Associated Press reported. In Peru, Conservative Keiko Fujimori secured victory in a razor-thin June race. Ratings agency Moody's said a Fujimori government would preserve policy continuity, bolster investor confidence and boost economic growth. A business-friendly conservative politician who campaigned on a tough-on-crime platform, Fujimori is the daughter of late former President Alberto Fujimori, whose government defeated the Shining Path violent extremist group in the 1990s but also took an authoritarian turn. She took office in July. According to AP, she promised to build four new prisons, including a mega-prison modeled after El Salvadors CECOT facility, militarise Perus borders to curb drug trafficking and deport migrants working in the country without legal residency. Javier Milei, nicknamed The Lion, won Argentinas presidential election in November 2023 by promising to slash government spending and tackle the South American nations decades-long inflation problem. An economist and television commentator, Milei has reportedly stopped the nations central bank from printing money to finance the government deficit and has cut government spending by firing civil servants and halting investment in public infrastructure programs, while reducing subsidies for public utility bills. Daniel Noboa winning the election in Ecuador with 56 percent of the vote, and was reelected to a four-year term in April 2025. A member of one of Ecuadors wealthiest families, Noboa has given the military a more prominent role in providing security in coastal cities overrun by drug gangs fighting over the control of ports and drug trafficking routes. But the strategy has not substantially reduced homicide rates. Under her watch, Ecuadors military started to conduct joint operations against drug traffickers with the US Noboa also pushed for the reopening of a US military base in Ecuador, but the proposal was struck down in a referendum last year. Nasry Asfura narrowly won the presidential election in Honduras in November, defeating his closest rival by less than a percentage point. A real estate investor and former city mayor of the National Party, Asfura belongs to the same party as former President Juan Orlando Hernndez, who was pardoned by Trump for a drug trafficking conviction. Asfura was endorsed by the US president, who threatened to cut off aid to the small Central American country if Asfura was not elected. Jos Antonio Kast, a conservative and a devout Catholic, won Chiles presidential election in December 2025, defeating a progressive government that had been in power for the previous four years. In his campaigns, Kast capitalised on fears over increasing crime rates in Chile and said he would expel migrants from countries like Venezuela and Haiti who had been working in Chile without residency permits. One of his first moves after taking office has been to expand a trench along Chiles borders with Peru and Bolivia in a bid, his government says, to stop drug trafficking and migration. Laura Fernndez won Costa Ricas election in February with 48 percent of the vote, defeating her closest rival by 15 percentage points and surpassing the 40 percent of votes needed to avoid a runoff election. She was an economy minister under conservative ex-President Rodrigo Chaves. The winner of the Brazilian elections will determine Brazil's foreign policy. Flavio Bolsonaro's father and far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro is an ally of US President Donald Trump. Meanwhile, Lula, who at 80 is one of the world's oldest heads of state, is running in his seventh presidential election and has strengthened Brazil's ties with China. Notably, Lula has accused the Trump administration of using tariffs and other means to interfere with Brazilian affairs. Bolsonaro has portrayed Trump as an ally, and is expected to strengthen ties with Washington if elected. The Trump administration has imposed tariffs on Brazilian products and sanctions on judges and other officials. If Leftist Lula wins, Washington will likely continue resorting to threats and targeted tariffs to curb ties with China, Regiane Bressan, a professor of International Relations at the Federal University of Sao Paulo, told AFP. The US is Brazil's second-largest trading partner, behind China. A Flavio Bolsonaro presidency would have more alignment with Washington, "at least rhetorically," said Bressan. The latest Latinobarmetro poll, taken in 17 countries and published exclusively by The Economist, showed that Latin Americans views of the United States have soured since Trump came to power. The share with a favourable opinion fell from 73 percent in 2024 to 63 percent, the report published on September 30, 2026, claimed. The poll revealed that, for the first time in a historically pro-American region, Latin Americans view Chinas influence in a better light than Americas: 65% call it positive, compared with 57% for the United States. This reflects Mr Trumps aggressive stance towards a region he believes his country should dominate, the report added. Will this mean Leftist Lula's comeback in the 2026 Brazilian elections? The next president will be known once the results of the ongoing polls are released. The electoral court (TSE) will start publishing results at 5 pm Braslia time on Sunday, October 4, 2026, as soon as polling places close. A runoff between both is expected on October 25, if neither passes 50 percent of votes. Sundays results will offer the first real measure of the candidates support beyond polls.

The Americans, who say something different in the media, have recently put forward proposals through a mediator. But they must understand that the period of dragging out the process and dictating one-sided demands is over," Mr. Qalibaf was quoted as saying. "The position of the Islamic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met," he said.

headline: Iran's Foreign Minister tells U.S. there is no military solution to their conflict
content: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday (October 4, 2026) that there was no military solution to his country's conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse. A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the U.S. and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure. "If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Mr. Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors. "There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding that "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict. The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at providing a framework for a permanent resolution, but the deal collapsed, largely due to disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has sought to impose control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, and has attacked vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation. Iranian and U.S. officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait. Mr. Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations. The United States has not struck Iran since September 1. U.S. media outlet Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday (October 2) to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

headline: Ruling TVK is obsessed with purchasing MLAs: M.K. Stalin tells voters
content: M.K. Stalin tells voters DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Sunday (September 4, 2026) appealed to voters in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies to vote for the DMK candidates, alleging the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was more interested in "purchasing" MLAs to protect its government. In a speech posted on his social media page, Mr. Stalin alleged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was not concerned about pressing issues but was interested in constructing a new Secretariat on the advice of an astrologer. "He is least bothered about the protests by fishermen and farmers. Instead, he will visit London to watch a car race. When murders have become the order of the day, he will be busy releasing reels about the 'Singapen' force," Mr. Stalin said. He appealed to voters who had "chased away" the ruling party's candidates when they came seeking votes to defeat them in the byelections. "You should disappoint the TVK, which seeks to cheat people by releasing reels and projecting false claims as achievements. There will be no betrayal of voters in the future only if you teach a lesson to the ruling party and its candidate who defected to it," he said. Mr. Stalin asked voters to consider why a byelection had become necessary in their constituencies barely four months after the Assembly election. "While MLAs in other constituencies are studying the requirements of their constituencies, the MLAs whom you thought would be loyal to you have come back to seek your votes. Is there any justification for their act? Do they have even an iota of concern for your welfare?" he asked. He alleged the MLAs from the two constituencies had "sold the self-respect" of the voters by "selling themselves" in the "horse race" of the ruling party. "Are you ready to believe their lies and false stories?" he asked. Mr. Stalin alleged the MLAs, after receiving "boxes" from the ruling party, were claiming they could serve the people only by becoming members of the ruling party. "Is it true? If only the ruling party can do good for the people, all MLAs belonging to other parties should have resigned and joined the ruling party. A government cannot afford to ignore a constituency merely because it is represented by an Opposition MLA," he said. Mr. Stalin also rejected as "untrue" the claim that the DMK and the AIADMK had planned to come together to form the government. He said the byelection had been necessitated by the "betrayal" of a political party by its own MLA.

headline: Pakistan braces for protest by ex-PM Imran Khan supporters after talks with government fail
content: PM Imran Khan supporters after talks with government fail Pakistan on Sunday (October 4, 2026) braced for a protest by supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan and his political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf after it decided to proceed with a long march following the failure of negotiations with the government. The talks focused on key demands of Mr. Khan's party, including an immediate meeting with its jailed founder and his transfer to a hospital where his personal doctors could examine and treat him. The first round of talks was held on Friday (October 2, 2026), with the two sides exchanging their positions and agreeing to continue negotiations, but without reaching an agreement. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf sought Mr. Khan's transfer to a hospital, while the government wanted the party to call off its October 4 protest. The second round of talks between government negotiators and Mr. Khan's party leaders began shortly before 5 pm on Saturday (October 3, 2026) and continued for several hours before ending in a deadlock early Sunday (October 4, 2026). The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf had announced plans for a long march to Islamabad on September 27, but later postponed it to October 4 amid government measures to prevent the protest. The 73-year-old former cricketer-turned-politician has been incarcerated since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption and charges related to inciting violence. He is lodged at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. Mr. Khan's party has also demanded the release of his sisters and supporters arrested ahead of the protest, a proper medical check-up for Mr. Khan's wife Bushra Bibi, and that their cases be heard without interference. On August 18, Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered that Mr. Khan be shifted to a private hospital in Islamabad for medical examination and treatment following concerns over his health, particularly his eyesight. The government challenged the order and later filed a review petition. Meanwhile, preparations were made to take Mr. Khan to Shifa International Hospital, but when he was moved from Adiala jail during the night of August 20-21, he was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS). The government said the change was made on security grounds. Mr. Khan was examined at PIMS and the government said he was medically fit before he was returned to jail early on August 21. His sister was present during the examination, while his personal physician, who had been waiting at Shifa, was not allowed to participate. Mr. Khan's family and party colleagues objected, arguing that the government had failed to implement the Supreme Court's order, and subsequently sought contempt proceedings against senior officials. On September 16, however, the Supreme Court deferred the proceedings for three weeks after the Federal Constitutional Court summoned the records of cases concerning Mr. Khan's transfer to Shifa International Hospital, leading to a dispute over the two courts' respective jurisdiction. The unresolved dispute over the implementation of the Supreme Court's order has remained central to Mr. Khan's supporters' demand that he be treated at a private hospital by his own doctor. Pakistans Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the federal government delegation that held discussions with Mr. Khan's party members, said on Sunday (October 4, 2026) that the talks failed primarily because the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government could not assure the Centre that it would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the province. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a northwestern province, is governed by Mr. Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, and the party's planned long march is scheduled to begin from there. The province has long faced militant violence, particularly from the Pakistani Taliban, with militants operating across the Afghanistan-Pakistan border and carrying out attacks. The second round of talks remained deadlocked over access to Mr. Khan, with the government insisting that Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf first announce the cancellation of the protest and that the issue of a meeting with its jailed leader would be decided later, according to sources. The party, however, demanded a meeting with Mr. Khan before deciding on the protest, the sources said. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi announced at 12:46 a.m. that the protest would go ahead. He said in a message on X that party supporters from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu, and Lakki Marwat would join the long march from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1 p.m. on Sunday (October 4, 2026). The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where participants will depart at 12:30 p.m. the next day and stay overnight near Kohat. At 12 p.m. on October 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani. Meanwhile, political adviser to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Rana Sanaullah, said protesters would not be allowed to enter Islamabad. The federal government had earlier deployed additional security personnel and placed shipping containers on roads leading to the capital to prevent the protesters from entering Islamabad.

headline: GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL: Which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation?
content: Which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation? Why This Matters The waitinglist number is not the only thing passengers should look at when booking a train ticket. The type of waitlist can also affect the chances of confirmation. Knowing the waitlist type can therefore help passengers make a better decision - whether to book the ticket, look for another train or consider an alternative travel option. GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL: Which waitlist has the best chance? The train ticket confirmation depends on several factors. Speaking to .com, a senior railway official said the actual movement of a waiting list depends on factors such as cancellations and the release of unutilised quota. Indian Railways reservation rules shows that these are not merely different names for the same waiting list. They represent different reservation quotas and different pools of accommodation. Consequently, their movement towards confirmation can also be very different, the official said. - GNWL: Usually the strongest position GNWL stands for General Waiting List and is associated with the general quota. Among the commonly seen waitlist categories, it generally offers the strongest position for confirmation. The official said that GNWL generally has an advantage because it draws from the main pool of accommodation and benefits from cancellations and release of certain unused quotas. Railway reservation material specifically states that RLWL and PQWL are confirmed after the General Waiting List, giving GNWL an important structural advantage over these smaller quota-based waiting lists, the official noted. The official, however, added that this does not mean GNWL 100 is automatically better than RLWL 2. The actual waiting-list number, train, class, journey sector, day of travel and expected cancellations still matter. But when comparable waiting-list numbers are being considered, GNWL is generally the more favourable category to hold, the official told .com. - RLWL stands for Remote Location Waiting List When a passenger books a train from an important intermediate station rather than the originating station, the ticket may be placed under the RLWL quota. Indian Railways keeps a separate quota for certain remote or important stations on a route. The key difference is that RLWL has a smaller, separate pool of seats. Its confirmation therefore depends largely on cancellations or the availability of accommodation in that particular quota. Railway reservation rules also place RLWL behind the General Waiting List in the confirmation order. Railway reservation instructions make the hierarchy clearer: RLWL is cleared after the General Waiting List. This explains why an apparently small RLWL number should not automatically be treated as equivalent to the same GNWL number, the official explained. - PQWL stands for Pooled Quota Waiting List This quota is meant for passengers travelling between certain intermediate stations on a route. The available seats are shared among these station combinations. Because the number of seats in this pool is limited, PQWL may move more slowly than the General Waiting List. Its confirmation depends on cancellations and the availability of seats in the pooled quota. Railway reservation rules also place PQWL after the General Waiting List for confirmation. Thus, a passenger comparing two otherwise similar booking options should not assume that WL 10 means exactly the same thing under GNWL and PQWL, the official said. - TQWL means Tatkal Quota Waiting List Tatkal Waitlist applies when the seats available under the Tatkal quota have already been booked and further Tatkal bookings are placed on the waiting list. It is a separate quota meant mainly for passengers making last-minute travel plans. This means TQWL follows a different confirmation pattern from the General Waiting List. The chances of a TQWL ticket getting confirmed depend on factors such as cancellations and the availability of berths under the Tatkal quota. For passengers, the practical lesson is straightforward: TQWL should not be treated as having the same confirmation dynamics as GNWL merely because its numerical waiting-list position is smaller, the official added. GNWL, RLWL, PQWL & TQWL WHICH WAITLIST CONFIRMS FASTER? General Waiting List Main/general quota largest accommodation pool Strongest position. Confirmed first, ahead of RLWL and PQWL; benefits most from cancellations and released quota. Remote Location Waiting List Quota reserved for specific intermediate/remote stations Confirmed only after GNWL. Smaller, restricted quota pool movement is slower and depends on that station's own cancellations. Pooled Quota Waiting List Shared quota for specific intermediate station-pairs (not full route) Confirmed only after GNWL. Limited shared pool a given WL number here is weaker than the same number in GNWL. Tatkal Quota Waiting List Separate Tatkal quota, for last-minute bookings Appears once Tatkal quota is exhausted. Confirmation tied strictly to Tatkal availability and cancellations not comparable to GNWL dynamics. - No fixed confirmation percentages exist. Websites quoting fixed rates (e.g. "GNWL has 8090% chance") are estimates, not official Railways figures. - Hierarchy only, not a guarantee: GNWL clears before RLWL and PQWL, but a large GNWL number (e.g. GNWL 120) isn't automatically safer than a small RLWL number (e.g. RLWL 2). - Confirmation depends on: train, class, route, day/season, cancellations, quota releases, extra coaches and time left before departure. - AI prediction is now the better guide: Indian Railways' RailOne app gives an AI-based confirmation prediction, with accuracy improved from 53% to 94% (per Ministry of Railways). It remains an estimate, not a guarantee. Indian Railways waiting ticket confirmation prediction When asked about the actual confirmation percentages, the official said Indian Railways has previously informed Parliament that confirmation and cancellation trends vary depending on factors such as peak and lean travel periods, the type of train, journey details and passenger demand. A GNWL 25 on one train may therefore clear comfortably while GNWL 10 on another heavily booked service during a festival rush may remain uncertain. Other variables include the class of travel, day of the week, boarding and destination stations, cancellations by confirmed passengers, quota releases, additional coaches and the time remaining before departure, the official replied. The railway official also explained that GNWL generally has the strongest position for confirmation. RLWL and PQWL depend on smaller quota pools and are cleared after the General Waiting List, while TQWL follows the Tatkal quota and depends on available berths and cancellations. However, the waitlist number also matters. A GNWL 120 cannot automatically be described as safer than RLWL 2 simply because GNWL has higher priority. There is no mathematically valid comparison without looking at that trains historical and current booking pattern, the official said. Indian Railways waitlist prediction AI Indian Railways RailOne application provides an AI-based prediction of whether a wait-listed ticket is likely to be confirmed or not. According to the national transporter, the accuracy of its waitlist confirmation prediction has increased from 53 per cent earlier to 94 per cent now. The concept itself is not entirely new. Indian Railways introduced a machine-learning-based confirmation prediction facility years ago, using historical PNR data to identify booking and cancellation patterns. The prediction remains an estimate rather than a guarantee. Indian Railways own PNR enquiry system warns passengers that prediction is indicative and based on current and past trends, and that the actual status can differ, the official said.

headline: Election Commission SIR 2026: Meet 5 retired SC, HC judges on panel examining legality, impact on voters
content: The Lawyers' Association for Constitution (LAFC) has set up a panel of former Supreme Court and high court judges to examine the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll undertaken by the Election Commission (EC). The panel will consist of five members and will be chaired by former Supreme Court judge Madan B Lokur, the lawyers' association said in a press release dated October 2, 2026. Besides Lokur, the panel will comprise former Supreme Court judge A K Patnaik, former chief justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court Badar Durrez Ahmad and former judges Rekha Sharma and Anjana Prakash. The move came in the wake of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after an India Express investigation revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken in the Commissions name without their knowledge, including the change to Form 6, deletion of voters and ECINET, the online portal where the electoral roll now sits. Who are these five judges? Know all about their education and career here. Education: Born on December 31, 1953, Justice Madan Bhimarao Lokur studied in Modern School, New Delhi, till 1968. He passed the ISCE examination in 1970-71 from St. Joseph's Collegiate, Allahabad. He Graduated in History (Hons) from St. Stephens College, University of Delhi in 1974. He obtained an LLB degree from the Faculty of Law, Delhi University in 1977. Career: Justice Madan B. Lokur enrolled as an advocate in July 1977. He practiced in the Supreme Court of India and the Delhi High Court. He was appointed as the Additional Solicitor General of India in July 1998, and later served as an Additional Judge of Delhi High Court in February 1999. He was appointed as the permanent judge of that High Court on in July 1999. Justice Madan B. Lokur also served as the Acting Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court from February 13, 2010 to May 21, 2010. He was appointed as the judge of the Supreme Court on June 4, 2012. He retired as the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court on December 30, 2018. As a judge of the non-resident panel of the Supreme court of Fiji, he became, by far, the first Indian judge to become a judge of a foreign country. Education: Justice Ananga Kumar (AK) Patnaik was born on June 3, 1949. He is the son of late Gopal Chandra Patnaik, a leading businessman with great repute in Odisha. He pursued higher education from Delhi University with Honours in Political Science and earned a Law Degree from Madhusudan Law College, Cuttack, according to his profile on the Supreme Court's website. Career: He was enrolled with the State Bar Council of Orissa on March 28, 1974, and practised in the high court, subordinate courts and tribunals in Orissa. He was elevated to the post of Additional Judge of the High Court of Orissa on January 13, 1994. He assumed charge as Additional Judge of the Gauhati High Court on February 7, 1994. He became a permanent Judge of the Gauhati High Court in 1995. After rendering valuable services for eight years as a Judge in the Gauhati High Court, he again assumed charge as a Judge of the Orissa High Court on April 15, 2002. Justice AK Patnaik was appointed as Chief Justice of the High Court of Chhattisgarh on March 14, 2005. He was transferred as the Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court on October 2, 2005. He was appointed as the judge of the Supreme Court in 2009 and retired in 2014. 3. Justice Badar Durrez Ahmad (former Chief Justice, Jammu & Kashmir High Court) Education: Born on March 16, 1956, in Shillong (Meghalaya), Justice Ahmad studied in St Edmund's College, Shillong, (1962-1966) and St Columba's High School, New Delhi (1966-1971). He graduated from St Stephen's College, Delhi University in 1975. He was a lecturer in Economics for BA (Hons) Second and final-year students at St Stephen's College, Delhi (1977-1979). At the same time, he was also studying for the LLB Degree, which he received in 1980 from Delhi University. Career: Justice Badar Durrez Ahmad enrolled as an advocate on September 5, 1980, with the Bar Council of Delhi and started practice in the Supreme Court of India and the Delhi High Court. According to the Delhi High Court's website, Justice Badar Durrez Ahmad has a keen interest in personal laws, including Muslim Personal Law, and has written several articles on the subject. He was elevated as an additional Judge of the Delhi High Court on December 20, 2002. He was appointed as the Acting Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court on June 10, 2013, and served till September 2, 2013. He was again appointed as the Acting Chief Justice on February 17, 2014. He was elevated as the Chief Justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court on April 1, 2017. Education: Born on July 31, 1949, Justice Rekha Sharma pursued her graduation from Miranda House, University of Delhi, Delhi. She studied law at the Faculty of Law, University of Delhi, and was enrolled as an Advocate with the Bar Council of Delhi in 1972. Career: She practised mainly in the Delhi High Court on Constitutional, Civil and Criminal matters. She was appointed as central government counsel for the Delhi High Court from 1977 to 1988. She served as an Additional District Judge in January 1988 and was appointed as District & Sessions Judge on October 1, 2004. She was elevated as Additional Judge of Delhi High Court on February 23, 2005 and became a permanent judge on February 22, 2006. She retired on July 30, 2011. Education: Justice Anjana Prakash was an alumna of Patna Women's College and studied law at Bhagalpur University, according to a report in the Leaflet. Career: Justice Anjana Prakash was appointed as a judge of the Patna High Court on June 13, 2009, and served until her retirement on July 17, 2016. She was the first woman to be elevated to the position of senior advocate at the Patna High Court, along with Justice Seema Ali Khan, the Leaflet reported. She established herself as one of the topmost criminal lawyers at the Patna High Court and holds the distinction of being the first woman to be elevated to the rank of Senior Advocate at that court. Following her retirement from the bench in 2016, she resumed legal practice as a Senior Advocate at the Supreme Court of India, the report added. The LAFC said the commission has been formed in response to growing concerns raised by citizens regarding the "design, implementation, and consequences" of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll undertaken by the Election Commission of India. It said the panel will examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology and overall impact of the exercise to revise the voter list. "The newly-formed independent commission of former judges on the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral roll will function with complete autonomy to examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology and overall impact of the SIR exercise on eligible voters," the statement read. The commission will examine, among other issues, whether eligible citizens were retained on the electoral roll and whether ineligible entries were appropriately excluded, the release said. As part of its inquiry, the commission plans to hold public hearings across the country, with full and regional benches travelling to different locations to record the views and testimonies of affected citizens, civil society organisations and experts. Besides, a dedicated Research Wing will collate and analyse the data regarding voter roll additions/deletions across the country and present it before the Commission. "A Legal Support Team will review relevant legislation, notifications, and verification processes to assess compliance with constitutional safeguards," the association said in the press release. The LAFC said the commission would have the final responsibility for its findings and recommendations. The Commission aims to complete its inquiry on an intensive schedule, with a target to release its final report to the public by December 2026. It said a number of senior lawyers, including Kapil Sibal, Prashant Bhushan, Chander Uday Singh, Prashanto Chandra Sen, Raju Ramachandran, Rebecca Mammen John, Warisha Farasat and Vrinda Grover, would provide strategic legal advice to

headline: Two captive-bred great Indian bustards released in Rajasthan national park
content: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Wildlife Institute of India (WII) scientists released two male great Indian bustards (GIB) in Rajasthans Desert National Park on Sunday morning, marking the first step in rewilding captive-bred GIBs raised at two conservation breeding centres at Ramdevra and Sam, Jaisalmer, under Project GIB. The project is being implemented for the long-term recovery of the critically endangered bird. Only about 150 GIBs remain in the wild. Rajasthan Minister of Forest, Environment, and Climate Change Sanjay Sharma was also present on the occasion. In a milestone move, released two male Great Indian Bustards in Sam, Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, today morning. This landmark success has been made possible by the nearly decade-long unwavering dedication of our scientists, researchers and ground staff who have spent years to ensure GIB reclaims the deserts of Rajasthan, Yadav wrote on X. The conservation breeding centres were established to raise a founder population of GIBs that could be rewilded, a measure against the declining wild population. From 2019 onwards, wild-collected eggs were incubated artificially, and chicks were hand-reared. Later, these hand-reared birds mated in captivity. At present, there are 98 such captive-bred birds in these facilities. Around 86 of them are being maintained for captive reproduction, and 11 have been earmarked for release into the wild. Of these 11, two birds were released into the wild at Desert National Park today. Captive reproduction has resulted in 24 live chicks in 2025 and 29 in 2026. Species recovery programme The release of captive-bred GIBs represents the next critical step in the species recovery programme and will provide important scientific learnings for progressively developing and refining protocols for reintroduction of captive-bred birds into their natural habitat, the environment ministry stated in a press release issued Saturday, after the initiation of the rewilding process. Yadav said Saturday that the GIB was important for grassland conservation, land degradation neutrality, and working as an important stopover for migratory birds that travel from the Central Asia flyway. The Central Asian flyway is a large migratory corridor stretching across 30 countries from North to South Asia, connecting the Arctic and Indian Oceans. Besides captive breeding, the project also includes habitat restoration by the Rajasthan forest department, including the establishment of around 200 square kilometres of fenced grassland enclosures inside the Desert National Park. Long-term telemetry studies by WII have identified these enclosures as prime breeding habitats for the species.

headline: Declare 'Vettri Payanam' scheme unconstitutional, urges private bus operator before Madras High Court
content: A writ petition has been filed in the Madras High Court challenging the constitutional validity of Tamil Nadu governments Vettri Payanam (victorious travel) scheme which offers no-fare travel for women and transwomen passengers in 12,695 government buses across the State. A private bus operator N. Kalamani from Bhavani Taluk in Erode district has approached the Court complaining the scheme would severely affect private transporters who may suffer heavy losses and have no option but to wind up their business. The petitioner claimed private bus operators would not only stand to lose women passengers but also the men because families would naturally prefer to travel together in government buses in which the women need not pay any fare. The writ petition, urging the Court to declare the Vettri Payanam scheme as unconstitutional, has been listed for hearing before the first Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan on Monday (October 5, 2026). Explaining her case in detail, the petitioner said, she was a widow who had two daughters to take care of. She held permits to operate buses on the 47-km route from Erode to Vellithiruppur and another 88-km route from Kakapalayam to Andhiyur. The petitioner had employed about 15 people and their families too were dependant on her transport business. She feared hardly any passenger would step into her buses on the two routes since significant number of government buses were operated in those routes. She said, the State government had come forward to spend a whopping amount of 6,000 crore a year for compensating the State transport corporations towards the Vettri Payanam scheme aimed at benefitting 84.32 lakh women on a daily basis. However, a request made by the Federation of Bus Operators Associations of Tamil Nadu to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on July 22, 2026 for extending the scheme to private bus operators too did not yield the desired result, she claimed. Ms. Kalamani said, not collecting any fare from women passengers in government buses alone would go against the principle of ensuring a level playing field in the bus transport sector and thereby violate Article 14 (right to equality) of the Constitution. Though Vettri Payanam was an expansion of the existing Vidiyal Payanam scheme introduced by the previous DMK regime, the petitioner said, the previous scheme was limited in its scope and did not affect the private operators to a great extent. The petitioner also relied upon various provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as well as the Tamil Nadu Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 to contend that collection of fare from the passengers was mandatory and that the government could not announce no-fare travel. Further, claiming the scheme had been implemented on the basis of an announcement made by the Chief Minister under Rule 110 in the Legislative Assembly and without issuing any Government Order, the petitioner said, such act offends Article 161 of the Constitution. She urged the Court to declare the Chief Ministers announcement, published by the Information and Public Relations Department (DIPR) on August 24, 2026 as unconstitutional and also grant an interim stay to it until the disposal of her writ petition.

headline: Man killed in suspected leopard attack near Hasanur
content: A 35-year-old man was killed, reportedly by a carnivore suspected to be a leopard, near Hasanur in Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve (STR) on Saturday (October 3, 2026) night. The deceased was identified as Periasamy of Bungalowthotti village under Hasanur panchayat. According to Forest Department officials, the incident occurred around 1 a.m. near a restaurant building on NH 948. After Periasamy was reported missing, villagers searched for him and found his body near the forest fringe close to the spot where the incident had occurred. Villagers staged a protest and initially refused to allow the body to be taken, demanding deployment of more Forest Department personnel for protection, enhanced compensation for the victims family, and a visit by a senior Forest Department officer to hold talks with them. They also pointed to previous instances of cattle being killed by a carnivore in the area. After nearly two hours of protest, the villagers allowed the body to be taken for post-mortem examination. A senior Forest Department official said the Department could confirm whether the animal was a leopard or another carnivore only after the post-mortem examination and further investigation. Requests for additional personnel and enhanced protection measures had already been submitted to the government, the official said. A grievance meeting with the villagers would also be arranged, the official added.

headline: Only Governor, not government can grant sanction to conduct investigation against me in ₹100-crore fraud case, Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi claims before Madras High Court
content: Former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi has contended before the Madras High Court that a First Information Report (FIR) registered against him by the Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) police, in the over 100 crore fraud case, was not sustainable since the sanction had been obtained from the State government and not the Governor. Also Read: Mandatory attachment, confiscation essential to combat vice of corruption, says Madras High Court In his FIR quash plea, the former Minister contended only the Governor was the competent authority to grant sanction under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 before the police could commence investigation into any alleged offence by a public servant in discharge of official functions or duties. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan on Monday (September 28, 2026) allowed an application filed by the Minister to dispense with the production of the original copy of the FIR registered against him so that the Registry could number the main case which seeks to quash the FIR on multiple grounds including the ground of sanction. In the petition filed through his counsel Richardson Wilson, Mr. Poyyamozhi said, the sanction that had been granted by the Public department by way of a government letter on June 23, 2026 should be considered as non est in law and incapable of sustaining the FIR as well as the subsequent investigation. Even otherwise, the FIR does not disclose any specific act of dishonest or fraudulent conduct attributable to the petitioner personally besides being vague and also vitiated by inordinate, unexplained delay of over four years from the date of the original complaint, he argued. The haste in registering the FIR post regime change in the State of Tamil Nadu and a reading of the FIR would show that petitioner is being subjected to this biased investigation as a part of regime revenge, which ought not to be countenanced by this court, the former Ministers petition read. He also brought it to the notice of the High Court that the CCB had included the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by filing an FIR alteration report before a metropolitan magistrates court at Egmore on September 9, 2026. The alteration report claimed that material collected during the course of investigation disclosed the role of the present petitioner in relation to certain demands. However, the petitioner contended the alteration report does not state that any kind of illegal gratification was paid to him by any of the private school managements in the State for the purpose of upgrading their schools or obtaining permanent recognition and so on. The alteration report does not speak about any overt act done by this petitioner, or any illegal gratification received by the petitioner. Thus, the sum and substance of the witness statements seem to be that some persons have allegedly collected money using this petitioners name, he added.

headline: What happens to her next after botched execution? Will she be freed or serve life sentence?
content: The fate of a 50-year-old Tennessee woman remains undecided after she survived a botched execution attempt. Christa Pike, who was administered two doses of a lethal injection drug, was due to be executed on Wednesday. However, the botched execution attempt landed her in the hospital in critical condition, where she was receiving "life-saving medical care," according to reports. Following the botched execution, the Tennessee governor halted all executions for 2026. Pike, now 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 after being convicted of murdering 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. In January 1995, Pike, then 18, and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, lured Slemmer to a wooded area, where they tortured and killed her. The case drew widespread public attention after details of the brutal killing emerged. A pentagram was carved into Slemmer's chest, an act Shipp later admitted to. Pike delivered the fatal blow by smashing Slemmer's skull and later kept a piece of the victim's skull. Both Pike and Shipp confessed and were convicted of first-degree murder in 1996. While Pike was sentenced to death, Shipp, who was 17 at the time and therefore ineligible for the death penalty, received life imprisonment with the possibility of parole. On Wednesday, Pike, who would have been the first woman in over 200 years to be put to death in Tennessee and the only woman on a state's death row, was injected with two doses of pentobarbital. However, despite this, she remained alive, her lawyers said, reported. On Thursday, Randy Spivey told reporters, "Last night, the execution team attempted to establish an IV line for an hour," and added, "I counted at least seven needles used in her left arm alone, one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her arm after an unsuccessful attempt." Pike's legal team is now urging the state governor to commute her sentence to life imprisonment, a request that was previously denied. Stephen Ferrell, another of Pike's lawyers, added that her team was also looking at other legal options. Ferrell said, "We want to think this through, and we want to make sure that Christa recovers and has some input in what she wants." However, it remains unclear what will happen next, as Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions for this year and called for a detailed, third-party review. He said, "There are a lot of questions," and added, "The people of our state deserve to have those questions answered, and that's what this investigation is for."
