headline: 'Debris field' found from medical flight missing over Atlantic en route to Boston
content: Searchers found a debris field off the coast of Nantucket, Massachusetts, from an air ambulance that was carrying six people when it vanished over the Atlantic on Saturday (October 3, 2026) during a flight from Bermuda to Boston, the U.S. Coast Guard said. There were four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals aboard, and their next of kin were notified as the search continued, the Coast Guard said in a statement. It added that one of its cutters would continue searching the water overnight and into Sunday (October 4, 2026). Air traffic audio indicates that the medical transport may have been coming in blind with electrical problems when a storm loomed ahead shortly before it vanished very early Saturday (October 3, 2026). The pilot reported electrical problems and declared an emergency as the jet approached the coast, according to air traffic control audio posted by LiveATC.net. Roger, you said you're coming in blind. Is that what you said? a controller can be heard asking the pilot. That makes Mary Schiavo, who is a former Inspector General of the Transportation Department, think the plane may have lost its navigational instruments just as a storm moved across its path on radar. The plane also descended sharply from its cruising altitude of around 24,000 feet to around 10,000 feet, according to preliminary data from flight tracking site FlightRadar24. Something bad happened with this big drop, and they flew into this big storm. It's a terrible place to have a loss of your instruments and be flying blind, said Ms. Schiavo, who is an aviation attorney. It's very easy to get disoriented and not know if you're turning, climbing, descending, etc. Spatial orientation hits pretty quickly. The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers aboard when it departed Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport for the nighttime flight to Massachusetts, according to a statement from the Bermuda airport's operator, Skyport. Transport Canada was closely monitoring and working with authorities on search and rescue efforts, the country's Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said on the social platform X. The Coast Guard said the Federal Aviation Administration reported that the Gulfstream G100 lost contact very early Saturday (October 3, 2026) morning. The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information about the situation, but it did not say immediately if it would investigate.

headline: Aged 71, a Chennai resident travels to top-tier international sports events, freezing iconic sporting moments
content: In cricket, one regularly comes across teams that shift to a whole new lane in the second innings, with surprising progress, eclipsing their first-innings performance. And in that process, they bring immense joy and wonder to spectators. Seshadri Sukumar has pulled off something similar to that. Here are the details of 71-year-old Seshadris second innings: a Press Information Bureau-accredited international sports photographer from Chennai and a Canon EOS Ambassador. He now has a reputation for checking into major international sporting events. As this article is being written, he is shooting images of sporting excellence at the 20th Asian Games, unfolding at Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya in Japan. Also Read: Asian Games 2026: India finishes fourth with 85 medals, late gold rush seals campaign Before zooming in on what he is doing now, a quick run of his first innings: Sukumar had been working in the banking sector, being an official photographer with Indian Overseas Bank (IOB). He always had an intense desire to be a sports photographer, but that remained a desire for a drearily long time. When retirement from his corporate career was looming large, Sukumar took the plunge and started pursuing sports photography full steam ahead. After Sukumar had been years into sports photography, in 2021, Sukumars nephew shared a story about his uncles passion for sports photography online. Sukumar was 66 years old then and covering the Tokyo Olympic Games. And the story of how someone is flourishing in a career kickstarted mid-life caught the worlds imagination. Sukuamars portfolio includes multiple Olympic Games, FIFA World Cups (including the most recent edition), ICC World Cups, Grand Slam tournaments, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, NBA events, FINA World Championships, FIDE World Cups and MotoGP, among several other major sporting events. Among his iconic photographs is one of the Rio Olympics, one that captured the contrasting emotions of the winner and the loser; the photograph won him a gold medal from the Photographic Society of America (PSA). Sukumars professional photographs have been distributed through international wire services and stock photography libraries, including Alamy, Zuma Press, IMAGO Images, SOPA Images and Reuters Connect. Sukumars life and career are a reminder that it is never too late to start afresh.

headline: Jantar Mantar row explained: Journalist alleges sexual assault by Delhi cop, protesters demand FIR
content: Journalist alleges sexual assault by Delhi cop, protesters demand FIR An allegation of sexual assault against a Delhi Police officer during a protest at Jantar Mantar has triggered protests outside Parliament Street Police Station, with journalists, protesters and lawyers demanding action on the complaint. The allegation was made by an independent journalist who said she was covering the detention of AISA activist Neha Bora when the incident allegedly took place. The allegations against the police officer have not been independently verified. Here is what happened and what is known about the controversy so far. In a video message posted by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, the journalist alleged that ACP Vivek Bhagat groped and pushed her while she was covering the detention at Jantar Mantar. "It's been more than three hours that I have been sitting inside Parliament Street Police Station," she said. She alleged that Bhagat "groped me and then pushed me". The journalist said she had gone to Parliament Street Police Station to lodge a complaint but had been waiting for several hours without an FIR being registered. The allegations against the officer have not been independently verified. Delhi Police has now said that complaints of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers during the October 3 protest in New Delhi. In a post on X, Delhi Police said: "On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers." "New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch for fair and impartial enquiry," the police said. The police statement does not detail the allegations made in the three complaints or identify the officers named in them. The allegation prompted hundreds of journalists to gather outside Parliament Street Police Station in support of the journalist. CJP member Saurav Das said journalists, protesters and lawyers would return to the police station and demand a copy of the FIR. "We will tell the police that time's up and now we want the copy of the FIR over Rosie's complaint," he said. Das alleged that Delhi Police was protecting the officer named in the complaint and said police had sought time to examine video footage of the incident. "The police have said that they just need a little time to look at the video footage and so on," he said. He argued that a complaint of sexual assault should result in immediate police action. "But the police, the Delhi police, are protecting their predator. We will absolutely not tolerate this," Das said. He said protesters had nevertheless agreed to give police time to examine the footage. "Whereas it does not take more than half an hour to watch the video," he said. "But even then we want to give the Delhi police the time they want to take." The allegation has also drawn criticism from Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. In a post on X, Gandhi questioned why an FIR had not been registered after hours of protests. "A female journalist has accused a police officer of misconduct at Jantar Mantar. For hours, hundreds of journalists have been sitting there with just one demand: that an FIR be registered. Isn't that the police's basic duty? They haven't even done that," Gandhi wrote. Gandhi also referred to allegations that protesters had been detained at Jantar Mantar, women protesters had faced misconduct and journalists had been dragged and had their cameras snatched. "Women across Delhi, students, are gripped by fear for their safety, staging satyagraha but the very police responsible for protecting women are raising hands against them. And a government that fears registering even one woman's complaint what exactly is it protecting?" he added. He also questioned Union Home Minister Amit Shah, noting that Delhi Police comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs. "Amit Shah ji, where are you? You have to answer for this," he wrote. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka said hundreds of journalists were protesting outside Parliament Street Police Station over allegations against Delhi Police officials. "100s of journalists are protesting outside Parliamentary street police station, alleging harassment and assault by @DelhiPolice officials," he wrote. CJP member Ratna Singh separately alleged that a woman had been sexually harassed by a male police official and claimed that a Delhi Police DCP had asked her not to escalate the matter. The controversy unfolded during demonstrations near Jantar Mantar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police detained several protesters, including AISA president Neha Bora. Senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal were also among those who attempted to move beyond police barricades during the protest. Delhi Police registered three FIRs in connection with the wider protest two at Parliament Street Police Station and one at Connaught Place Police Station. The controversy came amid a wider political dispute over the Election Commission's handling of electoral-roll revision. The Election Commission rejected the suggestion that these objections amounted to institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process. The ECI said decisions on the SIR schedule were unanimous. The immediate focus is on the complaint made by the journalist against the police officer and the demand by protesters for an FIR. The police response, including the examination of video footage cited by officials, is likely to remain central to the dispute. For now, the allegations against the officer remain allegations and have not been

headline: 'One last fight left in me': Smit Machchhar details cockpit attack, struggle to open door
content: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who survived a violent assault by his Omani co-pilot inside a Flydubai cockpit and averted a catastrophic crash on September 30, revealed harrowing details of the incident during a phone conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday night. Recovering at a hospital in Abu Dhabi, Machchhar recounted how he fought through blurred vision and severe disorientation to unlock the cockpit door from the inside, allowing crew members to intervene. Omani pilot asks to pray It just was a normal flight, and the co-pilot wanted to pray, which a lot of locals do pray, and which is not out of the ordinary. But while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back. Omani pilot started hitting from behind And suddenly, after I think I would say about 4-5 minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft, and something is not right. But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and thats when I realised that its not the aircraft; its the other guy who was in the cockpit with me. Machchhar was disoriented I did try to stop him, but because of his initial blows, my vision was almost like nothing, and I was completely blurred out, and at that point, the next thought I had was that the aircraft was sharply going down. So my memory is still in bits and pieces right now, but this is what I remember from that time. Machchhar tried to open the door And I did try to; I did try and manage to open the door once, but I think he shut it back. And at this point, I remember I was lying down on the cockpit floor, and I felt the aircraft and the whooshing sound and people screaming. And as I was telling the ambassador here that I had that one last fight left in me. That, you know, call it personal or call it for people. But lets say I did it. That if I dont do it, Im gonna die. And thats when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had, and just went for the door and opened the door. And thankfully, people were waiting to pounce back and take over the control, and the rest is what you know, sir. Omani pilot did not allow the crew to open the door The door from the inside has a twist-to-open mechanism, and from the outside it cannot. It can only be opened with a code. So my colleagues from outside were trying to. but the guy was not allowing. Machchhar finally managed to open the door And the only way to open the door was to reach the knob, and like any other knob, just to twist it open, and it opens on its own. So there is no pin, but yes, the door. It was a short, quick twist, but the point was to reach that place, and once I had my hand on the knob, I guess I twisted it, and I opened it. Flydubai attack Flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on September 30 with 174 people on board, most of them Israelis. Midway through the flight, the Boeing 737 Max dropped sharply after the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain. Passengers and other crew took back control of the cockpit, and the plane landed in Tabuk, in northwest Saudi Arabia. Authorities in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are now investigating. Netanyahu has invited Machchhar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Israel for the countrys Independence Day, and called the pilot a hero of Israel, India and the world. He has also said the co-pilot went through Islamist radical indoctrination. The UAE is looking into the facts, the motive and whether the attack was planned or linked to terrorism. Meanwhile, in his call with PM Modi, from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he was lying on the cockpit floor when he knew that if he did not get up, the passengers could die. He said he was fighting for his own life, but would not let others die. He also said he recited the Hanuman Chalisa during the attack and that it gave him courage.

headline: Abandon Pattinapakkam Assembly-cum-Secretariat complex project, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court
content: Secretariat complex project, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court The Madras High Court is all set to hear on Monday (October 5, 2026) a public interest litigation petition which has sought a direction to the Tamil Nadu government to abandon its plan to construct a new Legislative Assembly-cum-Secretariat complex on 25.55 acres at Pattinappakkam (Foreshore Estate) in Chennai. The PIL plea has been listed for admission before the First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan. Chennai-based advocate R.S. Tamilvendan had filed the PIL petition. The petitioner said he was shocked to come across news reports that the State government had given in-principle approval for the construction of the Assembly-cum-Secretariat complex on the 25.55-acre land belonging to the Tamil Nadu Housing Board, which was basically meant for constructing low-cost flats for the people. Mr. Tamilvendan said that the Assembly-cum-Secretariat located right now at Fort St. George was the most ideal location since it was close to the Puatchi Thalaivar M.G. Ramachandran Central Railway Station, the Madras High Court buildings, Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital and many other public facilities. He brought to the notice of the court that both the Legislative Assembly and the Secretariat had been functioning from Fort St. George for decades. Although the DMK government, between 2006 and 2011, built a new complex on Anna Salai, the subsequent AIADMK government converted it into a government hospital. Claiming that the existing buildings at Fort St. George could be renovated instead of spending 1,200 crore on a new complex, especially at a time when the government was facing a severe financial crisis, the petitioner said the interests of the fishermen residing in and around Pattinapakkam could also be saved if the proposal was dropped. He also told the court that the construction of the new complex at Pattinapakkam could lead to heavy traffic congestion in the locality and said that a representation made by him to the government authorities in this regard on September 12, 2026, was considered. He urged the court to stay the construction until the disposal of the PIL petition.

headline: The old world within a busy market
content: The wholesale market in Vellore district is always bustling. Vehicles honk as they make their way through the narrow lanes, while people navigate the crowded paths lined with vendors selling vegetables, fruits, and other essential commodities. Yet, within the crowded market are shops that seem to belong to a bygone era. A watch repairman continues his work in the heart of the city. A gas lantern seller has his wares on display. A harmonium repairman tends to musical instruments, while an old tailor works in a shop surrounded by vegetable sellers. Some of these traders have been doing business here for generations, carrying on trades that have survived alongside the changing market. The market itself dates back to the 19th century. It was established in 1868, two years after the Vellore Municipality was formed, right in front of the 16th-century Vellore Fort. The site had earlier served as a stable, where horses from the fort were tethered, according to historians. After the municipality was established in 1866, the market opened with no less than 200 shops. Over the years, it grew in popularity, attracting traders and customers from across the region. Fruits, vegetables, millet varieties, flowers and greens arrive here in bulk from neighbouring States such as Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, before being dispatched to various destinations. Today, the market has more than 700 permanent shops and 300 temporary shops. It remains a lifeline for many, serving the everyday needs of the city. Where old meets new Its history is also visible in the structures that remain. A clock tower, installed in 1911 to commemorate the coronation of King George V and Queen Mary in Delhi, now serves as one of the main entrances to the market. The eastern gate has another historical marker. Its foundation stone was laid on April 6, 1914, by the then British Collector Marjoribanks Esquire and Municipal Council chairman Khan Bahadur Habibullah Sahib. An inscription on the clock tower records that 277 men from the village went to fight in the First World War between 1914 and 1919, and that 14 of them died in battle. Named after freedom fighter Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose by office-bearers of the Vellore Town Vegetable Merchants Association, the market has an oblong-shaped main entrance facing east, with 16 entrances on all four sides. While the market has adapted into the modern era with ease, slices of an older Vellore can be seen at odd corners, basking in nostalgia. G. Arumugam, a third-generation trader, rents out lanterns at Lang Bazaar, continuing a family business that has survived for generations. Brief respite: A worker takes a nap as his colleagues unload sacks of onions at the market. Photo:venkatachalapathy.c/ Above the bazaar: An aerial view of the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Market, the bustling wholesale market in the heart of Vellore. Old ground: Vegetable stalls occupy the site that once served as a stable where horses from the Vellore Fort were tethered. Time stands: The oblong-shaped eastern entrance is marked by a clock tower installed in 1911. Before dawn: Labourers carry boxes of flowers to shops in the middle of the night. headline: 8.5 lakh books, 135 years of history: Supreme Court to hear case on relocation of Central Secretariat Library on Monday
content: The Supreme Court reportedly took suo motu cognisance of the proposed relocation of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library (CSL) in Delhi amid reports that no room has been allocated for it in the new Central Vista Plan, Live Law reported. The library houses more than 8.5 lakh books. A bench comprising Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva is scheduled to hear the matter on Monday (October 5). The suo motu case titled "In Re: 135-Yr-Old Library 8.5 Lakh Books And No Room In The New Central Vista Plan" was registered on October 3, the report added. Why has SC stepped in? The Supreme Court's move comes amid reports that the library, currently housed in Shastri Bhawan, may face relocation in view of the proposed demolition of the building as part of the Central Vista redevelopment plan. Concerns have reportedly been raised about the availability of suitable accommodation for the 135-year-old library and the preservation of its extensive collection. The MoHUA had ordered all Ministries to vacate Shastri Bhawan by the end of September to pave the way for its demolition and redevelopment, the report added. The library, originally set up as the Imperial Secretariat Library in Kolkata in 1891, was moved to Delhi when the British shifted the capital in 1911. It was moved to North Block after its construction in the 1930s and finally to Shastri Bhawan in 1969. It spans four floors and includes 8.5 lakh books, the report claimed. Meanwhile, the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) said that space for the Central Secretariat Library has been earmarked under the Kartavya Path redevelopment plan. "Contrary to a few reports, it is clarified that space for the Central Secretariat Library has been provided for in the Kartavya Path redevelopment plan. The necessary process for construction of the library is underway," the Ministry said in a post on X. The Culture Ministry wrote back on February 26 that the space allotted was inadequate to accommodate the full collection and facilities and that complete relocation is not feasible.

headline: Nolo becomes Category 3 Hurricane in remote Pacific Ocean
content: Nolo strengthened into a major hurricane on Saturday (October 3, 2026) far out in the Pacific Ocean, well to the west of Hawaiis main islands. The storms maximum sustained winds rapidly intensified to 115 mph (185 kph), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center reported, meaning it was a Category 3 hurricane. Nolo was located about 210 miles (335 kilometres) south-southwest of Maro Reef and moving westward at 17 mph (28 kph). A tropical storm warning was issued for the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument a massive and remote federally protected area with islands, atolls, seamounts, shoals and coral reefs from Maro Reef to Lisianski Island. The hurricane centre said large surf associated with Nolo will likely inundate some of the low-lying atolls. No threat was in the forecast for any populated islands, however. The hurricane centre said Nolo was expected to cross the international date line on Sunday (October 4, 2026). Nolo skirted Hawaii as a hurricane a week ago. It then lost some of its punch and became a tropical storm before regaining hurricane strength on Friday (October 2, 2026). Meanwhile, another Pacific hurricane, Category 1 Rachel, continued heading westward on a path away from the west coast of Mexico. Dangerous swells were forecast through the weekend for the coast of west-central Mexico and through Monday (October 5, 2026) for the Baja California Peninsula, according to the hurricane centre.

headline: Flydubai co-pilot who attacked Smit Machchhar to carry out a terrorist attack studied at a UK university: Report
content: Omani national Hamam al Hammami, the Flydubai pilot who allegedly tried to carry out a terrorist attack by nearly crashing a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, had completed a course at a UK university. Buckinghamshire New University's spokesperson, in a statement, said: "Our thoughts are with the injured pilot, crew and passengers involved in this incident," and added, "Hamam al Hammami previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management. He did not undertake any pilot training at the University," Sky News reported. The latest development comes as investigations into the Omani pilot gather pace, with fresh details emerging every day. Quick answers to key questions 1What led to the attempted terrorist attack on Flydubai flight FZ1073? The attempted terrorist attack was led by co-pilot Hamam al Hammami, who attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with an axe while trying to take control of the aircraft, aiming to crash it during a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight. 2Why was Hamam al Hammami banned from flying in Oman? Hamam al Hammami was banned from flying in Oman due to concerns that he had adopted extremist views prior to being hired by Flydubai. 3How did Captain Smit Machchhar manage to prevent a worse disaster during the cockpit attack? Captain Smit Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door amid the attack, allowing crew and passengers to intervene, which helped stabilize the aircraft and prevent a potential catastrophe. 4What were the circumstances surrounding the emergency landing of Flydubai flight FZ1073? The aircraft, after losing more than 17,000 feet of altitude due to the attack, made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where crew members and off-duty pilots assisted in safely bringing it down. 5What investigations are being conducted regarding the Flydubai cockpit attack? Investigators are examining whether Hamam al Hammami acted as a lone wolf or if he had connections to extremist groups, along with determining the motive behind the incident. Hamad Saif al Shamsi, the United Arab Emirates (UAE)'s prosecutor general, said Hamam al Hammami attacked Smit Machchhar with an axe inside the cockpit and tried to take control of the aircraft to commit a "terrorist attack". According to AP, Al Hammami, who was born in the UAE and has a Syrian mother, was banned from flying by Oman over fears that he had adopted extremist views before he was hired by the UAE-based airline. Citing a source, the report added that investigations were underway to determine whether Al Hammami acted as a "lone wolf" or had any connection to an extremist group. Investigators are also trying to determine the motive behind the incident and the circumstances that led to Al Hammami nearly crashing the flight with Israelis on board. Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot of the Tel Aviv-bound flight, is being hailed as a hero and lauded for his extraordinary courage after he fought to open the cockpit door when Al Hammami stabbed him in mid-air. The deputy leader of the UAE visited Machchhar in the hospital. In a post on X, Hamdan bin Mohammed posted a series of pictures of himself with the Flydubai captain as he was being treated for his injuries. The UAE deputy leader noted that Capt Machchhar's actions "embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life", adding that the pilot was "part of the story of our nation and part of what the UAE stands for". Crediting Machchhar for preventing a catastrophe, UAE senior diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash on Friday called the incident a "terrorist attack". In a video message released on Friday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination", and it appeared "very likely that he was going to down the plane." He added, "We are now investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price." Further, US President Donald Trump told reporters that early information he received had suggested links between the Flydubai attack and Iran, warning Tehran that if Iranian agents were to blame, the US would "hit them very hard." The incident occurred on Wednesday aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board. Flight-tracking data showed the plane losing more than 17,000 feet of altitude before the situation was brought under control. The aircraft also sent an emergency signal at 1:32 am ET (11:02 am IST). headline: More trouble for Gyanesh Kumar? Keralam orders probe in 2006 case linked to Malaysian man's suicide: What we know so far
content: State Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a Vigilance investigation into the case involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, news agency ANI reported on Sunday. The move comes against the backdrop of protests by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), the INDIA bloc, and student leaders against the CEC over alleged irregularities in the Special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The case concerns allegations of irregularities during Kumar's tenure as the states Public Works Department Secretary in 2006. It pertains to the death by suicide of Malaysian civil engineer Lee See Been, who was associated with the PATI-BEL consortium involved in the upgradation of MC Road under the Kerala State Transport Project (KSTR). His suicide note reportedly mentioned Gyanesh Kumar. The investigation is being initiated following allegations that external pressure was exerted and the original inquiry was derailed, a statement from the home minister's office read. State Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has directly instructed the Vigilance Director to conduct a thorough inquiry into allegations of external influence in the case involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and take appropriate action based on the findings, the statement added. On October 1, The New reported that the Kerala home department summoned files pertaining to the vigilance bureaus preliminary inquiry against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in 2006, when he was serving as the Public Works Department (PWD) secretary in Keralam. The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau had carried out a preliminary probe against Gyanesh Kumar following the suicide of a Malaysian civil engineer two decades ago. According to the report, Lee See Been had served as chief project manager for PATI-BEL, an Indo-Malaysian consortium involved in upgrading the MC Road under the multi-billion Kerala State Transport Project. Lee died by suicide in Kuala Lumpur, apparently after his bid to get bills cleared were stone-walled by government officials, the report claimed. Gyanesh Kumar, the 1998-batch IAS officer, got dragged into the row after Lees suicide note mentioned his name. Lees notes testified about the systemic corruption that plagued the project implementation. The note reportedly contained allegations concerning corruption and harassment by PWD officials. Lee's death triggered a massive row, prompting the LDF government of the time to announce a vigilance inquiry. However, the vigilance soon lost steam and the enquiry was reportedly stalled, The New reported. Sources told the outlet that most of the documents connected to the case could not be retrieved in the initial search. headline: Tennessee's prisons chief is resigning after failed execution of Christa Pike
content: The head of Tennessee's prison system is resigning, Governor Bill Lee announced Saturday (October 3, 2026), the first major staff shake-up since Christa Pike's stunning failed execution left her unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital. Frank Strada, commissioner of the Department of Correction, will step down this month, Mr. Lee said. Some of the Governor's fellow Republicans and other elected officials had been urging a change in leadership. It was the second time since May that Tennessee had not been able to execute a prisoner who was seemingly moments away from death. The Governor also announced that former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton would lead a review of what happened in Pike's death chamber. Stanton was previously named to conduct a review after Lee called off a different execution in 2022; he found in that case that Tennessee had not complied with its own lethal injection process. Mr. Strada said in a statement that resigning was in the best interest of Tennesseans while Stanton's review is conducted. The state failed to execute Pike despite administering two doses of a lethal drug, pentobarbital. Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, in a jealous rage in 1995. She became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row. There was no immediate response from Pike's lawyers for an update on Saturday (October 3, 2026) on her condition at a hospital. They had disclosed on Friday (October 2, 2026) that she was on a ventilator and unconscious in the hours following the execution attempt and that hospital staff were trying to clear the two doses of pentobarbital. The shocking failure has left both sides of the death penalty debate demanding answers. Mr. Lee has ordered an independent review and halted any new executions. Mr. Strada said he believes the state carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol. Pike's legal team welcomed Mr. Strada's departure but said it does nothing to help Christa now. What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person, the four-lawyer team said. We hope the governors call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessees entire death penalty system. Pikes attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream. Pike was extraordinarily cooperative with the execution team, even instructing them to please try here, please try here as they tried to insert lines, lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters Thursday (October 1, 2026). In May, Tennessee stopped the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff placed an IV into his right arm but couldnt get a secondary IV line. The Governor ordered officials to wait at least a year before trying to execute him again. Mr. Strada took over the Correction Department in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee was changing its lethal injection protocol and would use only pentobarbital. Four people have been executed in Tennessee since 2025, according to the Correction Department. Court filings show that Mr. Strada's job included overseeing executions in Arizona when they resumed in 2022 following an eight-year break. Clarence Dixon was the first that year. The medical team had trouble finding a vein to administer the lethal drugs and finally made an incision in his groin area. The process took about 25 minutes. That same year in Arizona, medical staff preparing Frank Atwood for execution initially could not locate a vein in his right arm but inserted the IV in his right hand at Mr. Atwoods suggestion, said Henry Brean, an Arizona Daily Star reporter who was a witness. Mr. Strada announced Murray Hooper's execution by lethal injection, the third in 2022. There was an unsuccessful attempt to insert an IV line in his right arm. The IV in Hooper's leg was inserted into his femoral artery. When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee, his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known, said Kit Thomas, an attorney who has represented people on Tennessee's death row.

headline: The sal and the beetle: Why Madhya Pradesh is cutting 1.4 lakh trees to save the forest
content: Why Madhya Pradesh is cutting 1.4 lakh trees to save the forest The trees in Dindori forests are witnessing a major infestation of the sal heartwood borer this year, compelling the government and local communities to undertake a mega exercise to tackle the pest At first light, the most noticeable sound in the sal forests off the Dindori-Mandla road in Madhya Pradesh these days is of feet on dry leaves. Villagers fan out toward trees that were felled and stripped of bark three days earlier, its sap drawn out. And there it lies, exposed on the trunks, their culprit the sal heartwood borer, a longhorn beetle that has been a bane for these trees for over a century. The villagers pick them by hand, drop them into bags or jars, and later turn them into necklaces the beetles long feelers aiding the braiding process. The necklaces are not for any ornamental reason but to make it convenient for the villagers to carry them to eight collection centres in the district. Each beetle is worth Rs. 2. So far, this season, 19,25,118 of them have been collected, generating a bill of Rs. 38.5 lakh for the states forest department. Hoplocerambyx spinicornis, commonly known as the sal heartwood borer, is a destructive pest first recorded as a threat to the trees in 1897. Now, it is at the centre of one of the largest sal-tree felling operations in Dindori in recent years following a major infestation. A couple of weeks ago, Centre approved the felling of 1.47 lakh infected sal trees. Sal, or Shorea robusta, is among the dominant tree species of central Indias dry deciduous forests, forming the backbone of tracts that run across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand and parts of Uttar Pradesh. Its canopy makes up much of the habitat inside tiger reserves, such as Kanha and Pench. Sal timber has historically been prized for construction and for railway sleepers because of its strength and resistance to decay. The tree continues to support a range of non-timber produce on which forest-dwelling and tribal communities depend sal seed, pressed for oil and used in cooking and in the soap and confectionery industries; sal leaves, stitched into plates and bowls sold across local markets; and resin tapped from the trunk, used as dhoop in religious offerings. In much of central India, sal groves also carry cultural and religious significance for tribal communities. It is this combination of ecological weight and economic dependence that gives a sal-borer epidemic consequences beyond the forest departments felling ledger. Over 21 epidemics recorded so far The insect does not attack indiscriminately: it tends to target weaker, less vigorous trees, though it becomes capable of killing sal of varying ages once a trees girth exceeds 20 cm. Mortality is largely concentrated among trees between 91 and 150 cm in girth, and the highest losses recorded is in the 121-150 cm range precisely the mature, canopy-forming trees that anchor a sal forests structure and constitute the greatest share of its timber and non-timber yield. More than 21 sal-borer epidemics have been documented across India to date. MP and neighbouring Chhattisgarh experienced a major outbreak between 1997 and 2000, during which roughly 3 lakh hectares of sal forest were affected out of the regions 16.84 lakh hectare cover. Mandla the district adjoining Dindori, and part of the same forest landscape now under felling orders was the worst-hit at the time, with around 8 lakh trees damaged. Dindori Divisional Forest Officer Ashok Solanki said, We are dealing with a substantial number of affected trees. Working in tandem The trapping and the felling are two distinct interventions running in tandem. The insect-collection campaign, carried out through what the department calls trap trees, is organised to pull adult borers out of the population before they can lay eggs and multiply. The felling of already-infected standing trees is a separate, larger sanitation operation, aimed at removing wood that is beyond saving and could otherwise seed further infestation. Dindori SDO Forest Surendra Jatav explained the method in detail. When the rains start, we start the trapping operation, he said. Selected trees are felled and debarked to draw the insect out. It comes and feeds on the sap and becomes exposed at night, Jatav said. The trees are left for three days before villagers return to collect the insects that have surfaced. When they come out after sunrise, around 5-6 in the morning, we go and catch them by hand and put them in a bag, he said. The felling of infected standing trees, Jatav said, is being carried out manually with axes, through an agency, with villagers doing the actual cutting. The operation is expected to take around four months. The felled wood goes to the timber market, said Jatav. The scale of the current outbreak, according to Jatav, is unusual but not without precedent. It is an epidemic-type cycle. It repeats every 30 years, he said, describing how infestation levels can swing sharply from one year to the next. Last year it was very low; this year it has become very high, he said. Unusually high rainfall a factor Dr Uday Homkar, Senior Research Officer and in-charge of the Conservation Division at the State Forest Research Institute (SFRI), Jabalpur, has tracked sal borer outbreaks in MP for more than a decade. He pointed to weather as one contributing factor behind this years spike. He said that unusually high rainfall in the Dindori-Mandla region last year had helped create conditions favourable to the insect. According to Homkar, the first and most decisive step in controlling an outbreak is catching it early. As soon as the infection develops, it has to be detected, he said. We practise this detection. Once a tree is confirmed infected, removing it becomes necessary to prevent the infestation from spreading to its neighbours. But, he cautioned, control should not begin only when large numbers of trees were already affected preventive trapping needs to continue year-round. Homkar said researchers have also studied whether biological control introducing natural predators of the borer instead of relying primarily on felling and trapping could offer a more sustainable path. Large-scale rearing and release have been studied, but their side-effects have not been studied enough.

headline: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing', pledges greater transparency
content: Cornell's president called the alleged gang rape of a student at a fraternity house in 2024 deeply disturbing Saturday (October 3, 2026), said it would weigh on the university for years to come and pledged greater transparency amid mounting outrage over the schools handling of the case. In an eight-minute video message to the Cornell community, Michael Kotlikoff described the past week as one of the most difficult in the universitys history and acknowledged troubling questions about the investigations that followed the allegations. My heart aches when I think of what she experienced, Mr. Kotlikoff said. It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanisation, and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use. Mr. Kotlikoff reaffirmed his commitment to supporting an independent review of Cornell's handling of the case called for by New York Governor Kathy Hochul and said the school's Board of Trustees would announce details next week. He also expressed support for Ms. Hochuls decision to turn the criminal investigation over to the state attorney general. I want to acknowledge something that can be difficult for an institution to say, Mr. Kotlikoff said. We dont have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves. Scrutiny has mounted in recent days over Cornells response to allegations that the woman was sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, has sued the university and seven former students. During a student assembly hearing Thursday (Octover 1, 2026) that allowed students to voice concerns and discuss proposals to improve Cornells response to sexual assault, several speakers called for Mr. Kotlikoffs resignation. Ms. Hochul, asked at a news conference Friday (October 2, 2026) whether she believed Mr. Kotlikoff should resign over the universitys handling of the case, declined to take a position, saying she did not yet have enough information. Mr. Kotlikoff acknowledged frustration that Cornell has not communicated enough, saying that it has led to distrust. While citing real legal and privacy limits on what the university can disclose, he pledged greater transparency and more opportunities for students, parents and others to engage with university leaders. He also committed Cornells support to legislative efforts to change New Yorks sexual assault laws. The case has renewed scrutiny of a state law that makes it difficult to prosecute sexual assaults involving people who voluntarily consume alcohol or drugs, even if they become too intoxicated to consent. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten cited the law in defending his initial decision not to pursue charges, saying the womans original statement to police described voluntary drug use and sexual activity. Critics have long sought to close what they call the voluntary intoxication loophole, which distinguishes between people incapacitated by drugs administered without their consent and those who voluntarily became intoxicated. Ms Hochul has pledged to push for legal changes. Mr. Kotlikoff also called for a serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life, saying Cornell would engage students, alumni and others in examining how to preserve the benefits of Greek life while strengthening accountability and transparency. Being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility for our own actions, for how we treat others or for speaking up when someone may be at risk, he said.

headline: Lula ahead in polls for Brazil's first-round vote; runoff likely
content: A series of polls on Saturday (October 3, 2026) showed Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva slightly ahead of Senator Flavio Bolsonaro before Sundays first-round vote, and a close race in a likely runoff between the leftist incumbent and his right-wing challenger. If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes which exclude blank and null ballots on Sunday (October 4, 2026), the two frontrunners advance to a second-round runoff on October 25. First round (valid votes): Lula 47.8%, Bolsonaro 42.1%, Augusto Cury 3.6%, Ronaldo Caiado 3.4%, Renan Santos 1.7%, Romeu Zema 0.9% Runoff: Lula 47.3%, Bolsonaro 43.1%. MDA surveyed 2,007 people from September 30 to October 2; margin of error of 2.2% points. First round (valid votes): Lula 45%, Bolsonaro 42%, Caiado 4%, Santos 3%, Cury 3%, Zema 1%. Runoff: Lula 47%, Bolsonaro 46%. Datafolha surveyed 4,006 people from October 2-3; margin of error 2% points. First round (valid votes): Lula 46%, Bolsonaro 45%, Cury 3%, Santos 3%, Caiado 3%. Runoff: Bolsonaro 44%, Lula 42%. Quaest surveyed 3,702 people from October 2-3; margin of error 2% points.
