headline: North Korea says it conducted intermediate-range strategic missile drill
content: range strategic missile drill range missile in a test overseen by leader Kim Jong Un, state media KCNA reported on Sunday (October 4, 2026). KCNA said the missile was launched on Saturday (October 3, 2026) from eastern North Korea and hit a target 1,000 km (621 miles) in the sea off the countrys east coast. It said the drill was intended to train troops operating a hypersonic strategic weapon system and to assess the reliability, efficiency and mobility of the countrys war deterrent. The launch was the latest in a series of North Korean weapons tests this year and came as tensions on the Korean peninsula escalated over a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone last month that wounded South Korean soldiers. The KCNA report provided additional details about the missile launch disclosed on Saturday by Kim Yo Jong, the sister of Kim Jong Un and a senior official in the ruling Workers Party. Kim Yo Jong said South Korea and Japan had failed to track the weapons flight, saying a special wave-like trajectory mode had exposed limitations in their tracking capabilities. South Koreas military said on Saturday (October 3, 2026) it had detected a ballistic missile launch by North Korea and assessed the missile had flown more than 700 km toward the sea off its eastern coast. According to KCNA on Sunday (October 4, 2026), Kim Jong Un said Pyongyang must continue efforts to make its enemies recognise the reliability and fatality of its strategic offensive weapons and reaffirmed that developing its nuclear war deterrent remained essential for national security. The test came amid heightened tensions after Kim Yo Jong issued a sharply worded statement on Friday (October 2, 2026) rejecting Seouls demand for an apology over the landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone that seriously wounded South Korean soldiers. South Korea has blamed North Korea for planting the mines and called for an apology. Kim Yo Jong called Seouls accusation groundless and said North Korea had not deliberately laid mines targeting South Korean troops. North Korea has carried out more than 10 missile tests this year.

headline: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
content: aligned Houthis said on Saturday (October 3, 2026) they had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemens Sanaa and other provinces. A large plume of smoke and fire was seen rising in the vicinity of an Aramco facility in Riyadh earlier on Saturday (October 3, 2026), a witness told Reuters. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an attack on an Aramco facility. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reported attack comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure. The Houthis said last week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu with missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said at the time that it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Taif and the Yanbu area, but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

headline: Tariffs, sanctions becoming policy instruments, sometimes weaponised: P K Mishra
content: The Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, P K Mishra, on Saturday said tariffs, export controls and other restrictions are increasingly being used not only for conventional commercial objectives but also for strategic purposes, and these instruments of economic policy are sometimes even weaponised. He said the future will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful, and ambitious without being nave, and India intends to be such a country. Speaking at a session on A World Priced for Risk during the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, Mishra said, We are increasingly confronted, not merely with risk, but also with uncertainty The events of this decade have brought this distinction into sharp focus. We have seen a pandemic disrupting production and mobility across the world, wars disrupting energy and food markets. Shipping routes and geographical chokepoints become sources of economic vulnerability. Export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy, even sometimes they are weaponised. Critical minerals, technologies and even financial infrastructure require a new strategic significance Discussing risks associated with energy availability, Mishra said, For decades the principal question for an energy importing country or energy importing economy was often price of energy. Today, there is another question will the energy be available or can it reach us? A disruption in a major shipping route can affect the price of crude oil thousands of kilometres away. Geography has, therefore, become an economic variableThe economic logic of globalisation was built around specialisation produce where costs are lowest and move the goods efficiently across borders. The logic remains relevant and even powerful, but the experience of the pandemic, geopolitical conflict and more recent disruptions have highlighted another consideration: the cost of interruption. A supply chain that is efficient in normal times may be fragile if the single-node supplier or geography becomes unavailable, he said. We are seeing similar development in critical minerals. Lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other minerals are essential to batteries, electronics, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing, but their extraction, processing and refining are highly concentrated geographically. Geography, we thought technology has made it irrelevant, but it has returned to the centre of the table, and it is not only oil, the minerals of energy transition are held in very few hands. For nearly all of them, a single country does most of the refining. So, the clean energy future, which was meant to free us from oil dependence, risks creating new ones, Mishra said. The result is a world in which economic policy and geographical considerations are becoming more closely intertwined. The question before policymakers is therefore not whether globalisation has ended. It has not. The question is how we preserve the gains from openness, while making economies less vulnerable to concentrated and unpredicted shocks. On Indias response to global supply chain shocks in the wake of disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, Mishra said, India is a major energy importer and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely. Indias response has combined several layers of protection. We have maintained substantial stocks, increased domestic production and ensured that alternative supply routes and suppliers are available. For example, the number of countries from which we import crude oil has increased from 27 to 43, which is very large, he said. He said India has also responded through greater diversification of our external economic relationships. An open economy will always depend on other economies. The objective is not to eliminate that dependence, but to avoid excessive concentration. Indias recent trade policy illustrates this approach. India now has a broader network of trade agreements, including agreements with the UAE, Australia, AIFTA [ASEANIndia Free Trade Area] and more recently, the United Kingdom, Oman, New Zealand and the European Union. There is one more form of resilience that is perhaps less visible, and that is macroeconomic resilience, he said. I believe the world that is coming will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful and ambitious without being nave. India intends to be such a country. I hope that together we can help build such a world.

headline: India can be called a developed economy if development is inclusive: V-P C P Radhakrishnan
content: PRESIDENT C P Radhakrishnan on Saturday underlined the importance of consensus and inclusivity, saying India could call itself a developed economy only if its development was inclusive. Speaking at the inauguration of Kautilya Economic Conclave, 2026, Radhakrishnan said India was moving towards becoming a developed economy and that development should reach every section of society. We can call ourselves a developed economy if it is an inclusive development of everyone, he said. He emphasised the importance of policymakers understanding the ground realities of both micro and macroeconomic situations, saying China had understood the same. If we understand the ground realities of the village, we can know what we should do for the development of that village When you want to make macroeconomic policies, then you have to understand the ground realities of the globe. That is where the success story of the Chinese is well-established. They understand the ground realities of both, and they have brought their nation to be the second largest economy of the worldPolicymakers should always understand the ground realities Speaking of the challenges being faced by economies today, he said consensus was important. In these times of flux, we need decisiveness embedded in consensus. We have to debate, we have to discuss and we have to come to a conclusion that is acceptable to everyone. Referring to the reforms undertaken by the Narendra Modi government over the past decade, including Jan Dhan accounts, direct benefit transfer and Goods and Services Tax, he highlighted financial inclusion. History proves the process of consensus-building helps reforms go forwardThe process may sometimes be gradual and sometimes we may lose our patience also, but we should never show it outside Indias experience of the last decade shows how inclusiveness is important Inclusion can itself become an instrument of resilience, he said.

headline: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle turn heads with a sweet and cosy date night at a Cotswolds pub
content: Trisha Bhattacharya Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have been photographed together in Britain for the first time since returning to the UK with their children in August, choosing a low-key pub lunch in the Cotswolds for their latest public appearance. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were seen holding hands as they arrived at The Falkland Arms in Great Tew, Oxfordshire, on Thursday, 1 October. Photographs published by The Sun showed the couple dressed casually as they walked towards the pub, with both wearing sunglasses. The outing was notable because, although Harry and Meghan have each made appearances in Britain since their return, they had not previously been photographed together in public. PEOPLE reported that the couple's family returned to England in late August, with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, beginning school in the UK. The family continues to maintain its home in Montecito, California, while the location of their UK residence has been kept private. For the pub visit, Meghan wore a black jumper with dark trousers and white trainers. Harry was seen in jeans, a jacket and a Santa Barbara Fire Department baseball cap, a detail that offered a reminder of the couple's continuing connection to their California home. According to The Sun, Meghan ordered gluten-free beer-battered haddock and chips with mushy peas and tartare sauce, while Harry had chicken, ham and leek pie with seasonal vegetables, mashed potatoes and gravy. A source at the pub told The Sun that the couple were treated in the same way as other customers. When they visited, Harry and Meghan just acted like locals, the source said, adding that visitors to the pub are treated alike regardless of who they are. The choice of a local pub also offered a markedly different setting from some of Harry's recent appearances in Britain. Since the family's return, he has attended charity and public events, including the WellChild Awards and a London gala supporting Ukraine. Meghan, meanwhile, has largely stayed out of the public spotlight while the family adjusts to life in Britain. She has continued working on her lifestyle brand, As Ever, while also sharing occasional glimpses of the family's life in the UK. The couple's return to Britain has not been without complications. Their children's schooling became a particular concern after photographers were reportedly seen around the perimeter of their school. PEOPLE reported that two men were observed by school staff and private security monitoring the school grounds. One was later identified by police as an international photographer working for a European press agency. The Sussexes' spokesperson described the incident as an unacceptable intrusion into the children's privacy. The children subsequently changed schools shortly after starting the new term, with the couple's spokesperson saying the decision followed discussions with their security team about the practicalities of their arrangements. Against that backdrop, Harry and Meghan's quiet pub outing provides one of the clearest public glimpses yet of their return to everyday life in Britain. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Trump's latest announcement: $90 Medicare payments for 20 mn seniors ahead of midterm polls; eligibility, exclusions
content: Trisha Bhattacharya US President Donald Trump has announced a one-time Medicare payment for millions of seniors, with the administration saying the money is intended to help cover Part B premiums as the US heads towards November's midterm elections. The payment will be $90 per eligible beneficiary and is being drawn from the Medicare Improvement Fund, according to the Centres for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). The agency said the rebate will go to 20.8 million people enrolled in Original Medicare Part B who meet its eligibility conditions. Most eligible beneficiaries are expected to receive the money automatically. CMS said payments will generally arrive by direct deposit around 8 October, while people without direct deposit will receive a paper cheque later in October. The rebate is not available to everyone enrolled in Medicare. CMS said eligible beneficiaries must be enrolled in Original Medicare Part B and living in United States. They must also not be receiving premium assistance through Medicaid and must not be paying an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount, or IRMAA, on their Part B premiums. People enrolled in Medicare Advantage are also excluded from the rebate. the payment is designed to offset the October B premium. CMS lists the standard Part B premium for 2026 at $202.90 a month. Trump announced the initiative on Friday through Truth Social, describing it as a way to help seniors manage healthcare costs. The White House has framed the move as part of its broader effort to reduce expenses for Medicare beneficiaries. The announcement has also drawn attention because it comes weeks before the November midterm elections. The Wall Street Journal described it as another financial promise from Trump ahead of the vote, alongside his separate proposal for $5,000 payments to adult Americans in Republicans retain control of Congress. That proposal is distinct from the Medicare rebate and would require congressional action. The Journal reported that the broader payment plan could face significant legislative and economic hurdles. The Medicare payments, by contrast, are being issued through the existing Medicare Improvement Fund. The White House and the CMS say the fund contains money intended for improvements for Medicare's fee-for-service programme. The administration has also begun separate $500 refunds to people it says were overcharged for Affordable Care Act coverage. That programme is not connected to the Medicare rebate. The latest payment therefore has a narrower scope than some of Trump's other proposals. It is targeted at a defined group of Medicare beneficiaries, does not apply to Medicare Advantage enrollees and is intended specifically to offset Part B premium costs. For eligible seniors, the payment is expected to arrive automatically, either through direct deposit or by post. For those outside the eligibility criteria, however, no Medicare rebate is due under the programme. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Maduro Not Immune to Prosecution in Narco-Terror Case, US Says
content: Terror Case, US Says Nicols Maduro is not entitled to immunity from criminal charges, US prosecutors said, countering the former Venezuelan presidents bid to toss the USs narco-terrorism case against him. Maduro and Cilia Flores Maduros wife who also faces charges are former rogue officials of a formerly rogue state with no entitlement to immunity, the US argued in a filing in Manhattan federal court late Friday. His defense team argued last month that he is immune to prosecution in the US as the head of a sovereign country. President Donald Trumps decision to withdraw official recognition of Maduro as Venezuelas head of state in 2019 is entitled to absolute deference by the courts under US law, the government argued. The US recognizes interim President Delcy Rodriguez as Venezuelas head of state and her government has not sought immunity for Maduro, prosecutors said. Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, were captured by the US military in a Jan. 3 raid and were subsequently charged with cocaine importation conspiracy, narco-terrorism conspiracy, and possession of machine guns and destructive devices. Federal prosecutors alleged that Maduro and others partnered with groups designated by the US as foreign terrorist organizations and that he sought to enrich himself while holding positions in Venezuelas government for more than a quarter of a century. If convicted, he and his wife could spend the rest of their lives in prison. Both have pleaded not guilty and last month they asked the judge to dismiss the case. Maduro and Flores are being held in a federal lockup in Brooklyn, New York, while awaiting trial. A judge in Manhattan will hear Flores request to be released on bond on Thursday. The case is US v. Maduro, 11-cr-00205, US District Court, Southern District of New York . This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: 'Co-pilot got up to pray, then.': Indian pilot Machchhar reveals new details of flydubai cockpit attack to Netanyahu
content: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar has revealed a new and chilling detail about the flydubai cockpit attack, telling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that his co-pilot asked for time to pray before allegedly launching the assault. Smit Machchhar said he turned away out of respect while the co-pilot prayed. Around four to five minutes later, he felt a heavy blow to the back of his head. The captain's account emerged during a phone conversation with Netanyahu on Saturday (October 4), as Machchhar continued to recover in an Abu Dhabi hospital. Quick answers to key questions 1What did Captain Smit Machchhar reveal about the flydubai cockpit attack? Captain Smit Machchhar revealed that his co-pilot asked for time to pray before launching an attack on him in the cockpit, which he initially mistook for catastrophic damage to the aircraft. 2How did Captain Machchhar manage to regain control during the flydubai attack? Despite being attacked, Machchhar fought back to open the cockpit door, allowing crew members and passengers to intervene and help stabilize the aircraft during the emergency. 3What was the co-pilot's identity and background in the flydubai incident? The co-pilot has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national previously grounded over concerns regarding extremist views, and he has been arrested and described by authorities as attempting a terrorist act. 4Why did Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu call Captain Machchhar a hero? Netanyahu referred to Machchhar as a hero because of his courageous actions during the cockpit attack, which helped save numerous lives on board the flight. 5What emergency measures were taken during the flydubai flight FZ1073 incident? The aircraft rapidly lost more than 17,000 feet in altitude, transmitting emergency signals before safely landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after the intervention of crew and passengers. Machchhar told Netanyahu that his first reaction to the blow was that something catastrophic had happened to the aircraft. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right, he said. But the blows continued. Thats when I realised that its not the aircraft, its the other guy who was in the cockpit with me, Machchhar said. He said his memory was not completely clear because of his injuries, but he recalled trying to open the cockpit door while under attack. I had that one last fight left in me, he said, explaining that he believed he would die if he failed to get the door open. Thats when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door, and thankfully people were waiting, he said. The incident occurred aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board. UAE authorities have said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act, attacking Machchhar with the aircraft's emergency axe and trying to take control of the plane. As the struggle unfolded, the aircraft went into a rapid descent. Flight-tracking data showed the plane losing more than 17,000 feet of altitude before the situation was brought under control. Machchhar's opening of the cockpit door allowed passengers and crew to intervene. Other crew members then helped stabilise the aircraft before it made an emergency landing at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu praised Machchhar during the call and said his actions had saved numerous lives. You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world, Netanyahu told him. The Israeli prime minister also invited Machchhar to Israel as a guest of honour. Netanyahu said he wanted Machchhar and Prime Minister Narendra Narendra Modi to light a flame at Israel's national Independence Day ceremony next May an honour generally reserved for Israeli citizens. The co-pilot is in custody in the UAE. UAE investigators have described the incident as an attempted terrorist act, but a final motive has not been established. The suspect has been identified by multiple media outlets as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami. Reports citing people familiar with the matter have alleged that Omani authorities had previously barred him from flying amid concerns over extremist views. Those claims remain part of the broader investigation and should be distinguished from the UAE's confirmed preliminary findings. Netanyahu has also alleged that the suspect had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination and attempted to crash the aircraft. Investigators are continuing to examine his background, motives and whether anyone else was involved.

headline: Planning a Disneyland Paris trip? Here's what you need to know before you go during Halloween season
content: Trisha Bhattacharya Guests arriving at Disneyland Paris over the busy autumn period have been met with an unwelcome message: the parks are full. Both Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World reached capacity on Saturday, 3 October, according to a report by Inside the Magic, with the resorts official availability calendar showing no registration availability for guests holding undated admission. This means visitors who hoped to make a more spontaneous trip may find themselves unable to enter. The situation is particularly significant for people travelling to the resort without a dated ticket or confirmed reservation. Disneyland Paris does not publish a live figure for the number of visitors inside its parks, so there is no official public headcount for the day. However, capacity restrictions were in effect, and access for some categories of guests was no longer available. Inside the Magic also reported that both parks had been full during September, suggesting that the latest restriction is part of a wider period of heavy demand rather than an isolated occurrence. Disneyland Paris itself has been warning visitors that its parks are full on many dates because of high demand. According to the resorts official guidance, guests with dated tickets can enter on the specified date, subject to the conditions attached to their admission. Those holding undated tickets, Annual Passes or Disneyland Passes must register their visit in advance, with admission dependent on availability. The resort also makes clear that tickets are not sold at the park entrances. That distinction is important because having a ticket does not necessarily mean that every visitor can simply arrive at the gates and enter. For certain ticket types, registration is required before the visit, and Disney says availability depends on park capacity. Disneyland Paris explains that its maximum capacity is based on the number of visitors the parks can accommodate while maintaining satisfactory conditions. The threshold can vary depending on factors including the attractions available and the parks operating hours. The latest capacity pressure comes as Disneyland Paris enters one of its busiest seasonal periods. The Disney Halloween Festival began on 26 September and is scheduled to continue through 1 November. The resort has introduced seasonal decorations, Disney Villains, special character appearances and the return of Mickeys Halloween Celebration at Disneyland Park. Disney Fanatic previously reported that the parks reached capacity on the opening day of the Halloween Festival, with visitors encountering signs warning that the parks were full unless they had the required ticket and reservation. The resort is also operating with a significantly changed second park this year. The former Walt Disney Studios Park has been transformed into Disney Adventure World, with the new World of Frozen forming one of its major attractions. The combination of new experiences and seasonal entertainment has made advance planning increasingly important for visitors, particularly those travelling from outside the Paris region. For families who have already arranged hotels, trains and other parts of a holiday around a Disneyland Paris visit, discovering that park access is unavailable only after reaching the entrance can be especially disruptive. The resorts advice is therefore straightforward: visitors should check availability before travelling and make sure they have the correct dated admission or registration required for their ticket. The recent capacity restrictions do not mean every ticket holder has been turned away. Disneyland Paris own rules distinguish between different forms of admission, and guests with valid dated tickets or qualifying hotel packages can have different entry conditions. For visitors planning an autumn trip, however, the message from the resorts recent warnings is clear: checking park availability is now an essential part of the visit, rather than something to leave until arrival. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: Who was Mad Sandhu? Popular LGBTQ influencer, makeup artist shot dead in Amritsar; found lying on road, blood-soaked
content: Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants in Amritsar on Saturday evening (October 4), police said. Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was attacked on Loharka Road at around 6 pm. According to police, the attackers opened fire at Sandhu and fled the scene on a motorcycle. He was rushed to a hospital but succumbed to his injuries. Who was Mad Sandhu? Mad Sandhu was a familiar face on Punjabi social media and digital platforms, where he spoke openly about makeup artistry, the film industry, fashion and gender issues. The LGBTQ influencer had built a substantial following on Instagram, with around 2.26 lakh followers. Sandhu was also known for appearing on podcasts, where he discussed his experiences in the makeup and entertainment industries and spoke candidly about issues related to gender and identity. Sandhu had also acted in the Punjabi film Oye Bhole Oye. His outspoken online presence and distinctive fashion and makeup choices had attracted both support and criticism on social media. Mad Sandhu shot at close range The shooting took place when Sandhu went to a shop to collect his car, which he had given for washing, police said. Two unidentified men on a motorcycle allegedly opened fire at him. Around two to three rounds were fired, according to police. An eyewitness said Sandhu was shot at close range. A purported video circulating on social media showed Sandhu lying on the road in a pool of blood while some people attempted to lift him. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the shooting. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sirivennela said investigators had some leads and would apprehend the accused soon. The motive behind the killing has not yet been established. Police said they were investigating the case from multiple angles. Sandhu had faced backlash over social media content Sandhu had previously faced criticism and backlash over his social media content, clothing and fashion choices. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had publicly objected to Sandhu's content and clothing, telling him that his videos could have a negative influence on young people.

headline: Madurantakam by-election: Will the AIADMK 'bastion' fall to TVK's growing popularity?
content: Will the AIADMK bastion fall to TVKs growing popularity? In the 2021 Assembly Elections, the ruling AIADMK was swept away by a DMK wave in the KTCC districts (Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, and Chennai), barring one single seat Madurantakam. Maragatham Kumaravel, a seasoned AIADMK leader and a Lok Sabha member for the party during 2014-19 period, stood tall among the ruins. She regained the seat in the 2026 elections amid a TVK wave in the region, giving rise to claims that it was an AIADMK bastion. Then came the twist. Barely three weeks after the declaration of results, Ms. Maragatham, along with five of her colleagues, resigned from the Assembly and joined the TVK. She is now recast as the TVK candidate for the Madurantakam by-election scheduled for October 6. On Friday, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay held a four-and-a-half-hour-long roadshow in the constituency. People lined up in large numbers all along the route, which crisscrossed the constituency touching about three dozen villages. If the turnout of people translates to votes for the party, the TVK would win. But often, what is apparent isnt real, warns Ashok, a grocery store owner in Ayyanar Nagar. Not all those who gather at Vijays rallies would vote for TVK. I went there too to catch a glimpse of him but I may not vote for them, he states. In course of a chat, he lets out a crucial fact that could well decide the fate of the election: the PMKs position. The party had announced that it would stay neutral during the by-elections after a fallout with its alliance partner AIADMK over the choice of candidates. While there are unconfirmed reports of possible backchannel negotiations between the PMK and the TVK, Mr. Ashok says that the supporters on ground arent aware of what the partys stand is as yet. Last two elections (2021 and 2026), PMK was in alliance with AIADMK and the candidate won. So, whoever the PMK supports will have an advantage, he asserts. There may be some meat in this argument, especially since Vanniyars, the prime support base of the PMK, constitute more than 30% of the electorate. They are the largest group after the Scheduled Caste communities, which constitute a little over 40% of the electorate. Madurantakam is a constituency reserved for Scheduled Caste (SC) candidates. As campaigning draws to a close on Sunday evening, the opposition candidates seem to have strung a common tune: the election has been forced down upon the people of Madurantakam. P. Suganthi, the CPI(M) candidate, said that people voted for the TVK with the hope of a change, but the switch-over of AIADMK MLAs soon after election showed that the party wasnt much different from the BJP at the Centre. On her campaign trail on Friday, she encountered unsavoury comments from DMK supporters in Athimanam village, perhaps an indication of tensions between the two former alliance partners. Taking a similar stand, B. Valarmathi, former AIADMK minister, said that people of the constituency felt betrayed with the resignation of Ms. Maragatham within 21 days of the declaration of results. S. Kanitha Sampath, the AIADMK candidate, recalled the days when she helped Ms. Maragatham during her electoral debut in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections and said that people will respond to her betrayal on October 6. I. Paranthamen, the DMK candidate, said this was an unnecessary election thrust on the people in an undemocratic way and they would respond wisely. People are angry. They are reeling from price rise, increase in electricity tariff, and change of terms of the rural employment guarantee scheme, he maintained. Close to the bus stand, a group of white-clad individuals, adorning red stoles, went about distributing pamphlets. They were members of the United Communist Party of India (UCPI) and were canvassing votes for the DMK. Though from the Left ecosystem, we are not with the CPI and the CP(M) and believe that DMK is the only powerful ally to take on the might of communal forces in Tamil Nadu, said Bhaskaran, its State secretary. While campaigning was in its last leg, 72-year-old Babyamma sat under a banyan tree in Mettupalayam watching the rigmarole pass by. Asked who would she vote for, she said that she hasnt made up her mind, although she had voted for irattai ilai (two leaves, the poll symbol of AIADMK) in the past. Asked if she liked Chief Minister Vijay, she replied, He came [to power] and prices went up.

headline: Loop Road fishermen to hold black flag protest on Sunday
content: Fishermen of villages from Nochikuppam to Srinivasapuram will stage a black flag agitation on Sunday, expressing their strong opposition to the proposed Secretariat at Foreshore Estate. The fishermen have asked all the villages to hold peaceful protests, demanding that the State government return the lands belonging to Mullikuppam and Mullimanagar to the villages and earmark them for future expansion of their villages. Demand for new houses They also demand the construction of houses for fishermen living along the Marina Loop Road, as most of their houses were built 40 to 50 years ago. The fishermen have submitted their demands to the Chief Ministers Special Cell. We hope the government will take a positive decision on the issue. Since we are the stakeholders who matter the most, we request the government to appoint someone to listen to our grievances before taking such a major decision. We are holding protests only because nobody has discussed the issue with us, said fishermen leaders G.R. Vijayan and K. Bharathi. Fishermen of villages such as Nochikuppam, Bhavanikuppam, Domingkuppam, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, Mullikuppam/Srinivasapuram, Mullimanagar, Nambikai Nagar, Selvarajpuram and Irudayapuram have planned to hold a series of protests to attract the attention of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.

headline: 'Co-Pilot Got Up To Pray, Then Hit Me On The Head': Smit Machchhar Reveals New Details Of Flydubai Incident
content: pilot stood up to pray, before landing a sharp blow at his head and preventing him from opening the cockpit door.

headline: Paris police chief says student protest movement out of control, urges peaceful action
content: The student protest movement that has spread across France is now out of control, the Paris police chief said on Saturday, urging demonstrators to return to peaceful action and warning that authorities would respond firmly to violence and vandalism. Riot police clashed with high school students across France on Friday (October 2, 2026) and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macrons government battled to contain increasingly violent protests over classroom conditions and funding. Since Monday (September 28, 2026), around 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested nationwide and dozens injured. Agathe Foucault, a spokesperson for the national police, told RTL radio on Saturday (October 3, 2026) that more than 600 police officers had also been injured. Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the tens of millions of euros. Paris police chief Patrice Faure, in an open letter published on X ahead of planned renewed protests from next Tuesday (October 6, 2026), said those who had launched the movement no longer controlled it and called on students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest. It is time to return to peaceful forms of action, Faure wrote, saying parents also had a responsibility to steer their children away from what he described as the influence of professional rioters and their supporters. Student unions have called for a national day of demonstrations on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). Security officials fear that an organised protest in central Paris in particular could see further violence amid concerns that far-left anarchist groups could hijack the movement. The students blockading high schools have voiced anger over overcrowding in classrooms, regular shortages of teachers and dilapidated buildings, blaming years of underinvestment.

headline: TVK moves ECI against Stalin over 'body-shaming' remarks on Dharapuram candidate
content: TVK general secretary (election management) and PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna, along with the partys legal wing, has approached the Election Commission of India seeking action against DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin for allegedly violating the model code of conduct by making derogatory, body-shaming remarks about TVKs Dharapuram candidate P Sathyabama.In his complaint, Arjuna urged the ECI to withdraw Stalins star campaigner status and direct the district returning officer to register an FIR against him under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, 1998. He also sought measures to ensure Sathyabamas fearless participation in the electoral process.Talking to mediapersons at the Secretariat, Arjuna warned that legal action would be initiated against Stalin and Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin if they continued making derogatory remarks against women. We respect the DMK leader, but Stalin has increasingly resorted to denigrating women at a level unseen in the past five years. We are planning to file a formal criminal complaint against the DMK chief, Arjuna said.In a separate representation, the TVK advocates wing urged the ECI to immediately direct Stalin to refrain from making such remarks and, if necessary, impose restrictions on his election campaign.The wing sought registration of an FIR under the relevant provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Representation of the People Act. It also called for a lawful investigation and penal action. The video and audio recordings, along with media reports of the meeting, may be immediately seized and preserved. Details of the action taken on this complaint may be communicated to us, the representation said.

headline: With poor upkeep and no class time, TN's flagship spoken English scheme loses its voice
content: Mozhigal was launched three years ago to improve students spoken English through games, video modules and frequently asked questions Chennai: Poor maintenance of hi-tech labs and the lack of dedicated class periods have left the states flagship spoken English programme for Classes VI to VIII largely defunct in govt schools. Spearheaded by Tamil Nadu State Council for Educational Research and Training, Mozhigal was launched three years ago to improve students spoken English through games, video modules and frequently asked questions. Teachers accessed the portal through their EMIS login IDs from computer labs in schools.However, school heads said that while the portal remains active, classes are rarely held. In the first two years, there were dedicated periods for the subject, and students and teachers were keen on taking them. In the past year, there is no allocated period and the classes are taken for students during the hi-tech lab period. But there are several other activities and assignments that students take during these periods, a headmaster said.Teachers said that after L&Ts contract to maintain the hi-tech labs ended last year, several systems were left non-functional. There are connectivity issues and inadequate number of UPS. Several students use the same computer, making it difficult for them to learn, said a govt school teacher.SCERT director N Latha did not respond to queries. An SCERT faculty member said new modules had not been uploaded to the portal and that chief educational officers and district educational officers had not raised the issue. There are plans to make the window more interactive. But there has been no update, he said.Teachers also called for making spoken English compulsory to prompt greater departmental attention. Students should be graded for spoken English too. The subject should at least be made part of internal assessments. Additionally, the respective block education officers should carry out regular inspections to see if the classes are progressing smoothly, said M Ramalakshmi, a retired school head.

headline: Govt forced bypolls through horse trading: Stalin
content: The chief minister, who once boasted that even his five-minute address would shake the world, is now doing somersaults to win votes in a single constituency, said DMK president M K Stalin. Campaigning in the Madurantakam assembly constituency on Saturday for the partys bypoll candidate I Paranthamen, the former chief minister exhorted the voters to make Oct 6 the day that ends arrogance and betrayal.It is rare for chief ministers to campaign for a byelection. Why is our CM so tense? He himself has no confidence in his govt. In the 2026 general election, he would not have held even 10 campaign meetings in total. Look at his condition now! He is parading through every nook and corner of Madurantakam. I like your fear, CM sir, Stalin said.The former CM said the bypoll should have been avoided. It is an election imposed upon you. Four months ago, you elected someone. But to provide crutches to this govt, which lacks a majority, they resigned and are now shamelessly seeking votes again on a different symbol. Has an MLA ever resigned immediately after winning an election in Tamil Nadu? Never! This election is happening because of blatant horse-trading, he said.Do you know how arrogantly the ruling party people are speaking? They say, even if we field a dog on behalf of TVK, people will vote for it. What a despicable mindset! Such things are disgusting and shameful to hear in Tamil Nadu. You must curb this arrogance. Will you do it? he asked the voters.Stalin acknowledged that DMK had made the mistake of not considering TVK as a major force before the assembly elections. Back then, we did not think of them as a serious force. We fought against our ideological opponents, and ignored this circus of clowns. In addition, several lakh peoples voting rights were taken away due to the SIR of electoral rolls. For these few reasons, we lost in the polls, he said.Cheap minister sir I will call him cheap minister from now on, because he himself has come down in stature. Going through shortcuts, stealing MLAs, kidnapping an AMMK member to get a support letter. We do not need such shortcuts to topple your govt. The people will end your govt through the right path, he said.Stalin also spoke on the law and order situation, violent crimes, drug trafficking, power outages, and shortages of essential commodities such as Aavin milk and basic groceries in the state.Earlier in a video post on X, Stalin urged voters of the Thattanchavady constituency in Puducherry to reject both the AINRC-BJP front and the Congress, and appealed to them to support the DMK candidate to bring genuine administrative accountability and raise the statehood demand. He said that despite making grand campaign promises to secure full statehood for Puducherry, the AINRC-BJP alliance failed to take meaningful steps once in power.Puducherry is now becoming a kolai cherry (a region of murders). Law and order has collapsed, transforming the territory into a crime hub with frequent daylight crimes, he said. Stalin alleged that during the previous elections, the Congress betrayed the DMK by fielding candidates against official DMK nominees. He called upon the electorate to ensure the Congress candidate forfeits his deposit.

headline: TVK govt is the worst regime in the country: EPS
content: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Saturday launched a scathing attack on the TVK and its leadership, alleging that the state was witnessing the worst regime in the country and claiming that the ruling dispensation would not survive.Addressing a campaign meeting at Madurantakam, Palaniswami said the by-election had been necessitated after the MLA elected on an AIADMK ticket resigned and joined the TVK. This is a murder of democracy. The voters mandate has been sold, he alleged, asking voters whether the former MLA should be punished to deter similar defections in the future.Rejecting TVK leader Vijays claim that his party represented a transparent and pure force (Thooya Sakthi), Palaniswami said the party had become a force of theft (Thiruttu Sakthi) after allegedly poaching MLAs.The AIADMK leader also said allegations by the Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK, that cash was being offered to voters during door-to-door campaigning showed that the party was not clean. The govt would collapse if its allies raised their voices even slightly. It is a party that deceives the people. We do not have to do anything; the govt will fall on its own, he said.The former chief minister alleged that the state govt failed to control inflation and maintain law and order. He claimed that GST revenue had declined while the states borrowings had increased, warning that the states debt burden could reach nearly Rs. 20 lakh crore over the next five years if the trend continued. He also accused the government of adopting a double standard on land acquired for the now-abandoned Parandur airport project, alleging that its position had changed after it came to power.

headline: Premium Scotch May Get 10-15% Cheaper In Delhi Soon. Here's Why
content: Delhi's excise officials said the department is studying the provisions of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, or CETA. They are also examining how the lower customs duty should be reflected in prices in the capital.

headline: Gang held in connection with murder of VCK functionary
content: Four youths were arrested by Kalavai police on Saturday, in connection with the murder of a local VCK functionary. The police said the arrested persons were identified as R. Kaviarasu, 21, B. Mani, 22, G. Sarathi, 21, and S. Dinesh, 21. They were childhood friends near Kalavai town in the district. The victim was K. Sivakumar, 60, a VCK functionary in the area. Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, Sivakumar was returning to his house near Kalavai town on Thursday, when a gang on two-wheelers allegedly hacked him to death. On being informed, the Kalavai police inspected the spot and sent the body to Government Medical College Hospital in Vellore for postmortem. Relatives and residents in the village staged a protest to arrest the suspects. Superintendent of Police P. Sibin pacified agitated residents, who dispersed after assurance from revenue officials and the police that they would arrest the suspects. Special teams were formed who analysed CCTV camera footage along the route. The teams also analysed reels posted on social media, in which the gang claimed to take revenge on local political functionaries. The police said the teams traced the location of the gang to a hideout near Arani town in Tiruvannamalai and nabbed them. The gang, led by the key suspect, Sivakumar told the police that he had a dispute over borrowed money from the victim, who allegedly threatened him with dire consequences. Angered by threats, he allegedly hacked the victim to death, along with his friends. A case was registered. Arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore, and a probe is under way.

headline: A month after mass fish death, Ennore fishers flag inaction by authorities; plan on plugging sewage intrusion points with sand bags
content: Fishermen from eight Ennore hamlets plan to block sewage entry points into the creek and Kosasthalaiyar river by dumping sandbags, saying authorities have not acted after mass fish deaths a month ago.More than 8,000 fishermen agreed to plug about 10 suspected sewage-intrusion points next week. The sites are along the creek near Katukkupam, Mugathuvarakuppam and Thazhankuppam, and along Buckingham Canal. This is our way of protesting against the govt, said R L Srinivasan, a fisher leader. A Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) report said sewage contamination caused fish deaths, yet no action has been taken to solve the issue. We have suffered for years because industries and civic agencies discharged treated effluent and sewage into the river, he said, adding, People are now afraid to consume fish from Ennore.About three tonnes of fish died in Kosasthalaiyar and Ennore creek in Aug, forcing fishers to stop work for three weeks. TNPCB found dissolved oxygen levels of 4mg per litre at five locations, pointing to sewage contamination. A fisheries department committee too concluded that sewage, and not industrial effluent, caused the fish deaths. The report was submitted. Civic agencies know the points where sewage enters the waterbody, said a TNPCB official.A Metrowater official, however, said the report had not conclusively established the cause of the fish deaths. Metrowater managing director T Anand said the agency had plugged most sewage outfalls through schemes including Vada Chennai Valarchi Thittam. There are no fresh outfall points as of now. Ongoing schemes and proposals will address the remaining issues, he said.Fishermen said the govt had not paid the relief it promised them in the wake of the incident. We were assured compensation by the legislator. Our men stopped work for more than 20 days and lost between 2,000 and 10,000 a day. The govt must address this, said S Kumaresan, a Katukuppam resident. Environment minister V K Rajeev and MLA Senthilkumar did not respond to calls for comment.

headline: Constitutional rights can't be denied for delayed minority certificate: HC
content: Madras high court has held that a candidates constitutional rights under the minority category to be considered for admission under the special category to educational courses could not be completely denied merely because of the delay in producing the minority certificate.Justice Krishnan Ramaswamy has directed the directorate of medical admission and the state selection committee to consider the application of R Vikasini for the 2026-27 MBBS course under the management quota under the linguistic minority category, though she got the certificate after two rounds of counselling.While the modality of availing such benefits may differ, the petitioners application can be considered, subject to the availability of seats, the court said. Such being the case, the court directed the authorities to permit the petitioner to participate in future rounds of counselling upon the production of the original linguistic minority certificate, in the event any seats are available under the linguistic minority category and the petitioner is otherwise eligible, the judge said.According to the petitioner, she scored 195 marks in NEET 2026 and applied for MBBS under the management quota. While filling up the online application, she marked No under the linguistic minority category as she hadnt received the certificate at that point of time.However, subsequently, she was issued with the Telugu linguistic minority certificate dated Sept 22. Therefore, the petitioner addressed an email to the selection committee requesting permission to correct the application and to consider her under the linguistic minority category.Since the committee neither granted the correction nor communicated a decision, the case has been filed. Disposing of the plea, the court passed the order.

headline: TVK scared of defeat, says EPS
content: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said TVK was afraid of defeat in the bypoll and hence enacted a drama to create sympathy among voters.At a TVK campaign, a candidate wept and chief minister C Joseph Vijay consoled her. This is more dramatic than cinema. Who are they trying to fool with this drama? They are afraid of defeat in Dharapuram and Madurantakam, he said during his campaign at Dharapuram.Palaniswami alleged that Vijay lacked gratitude. He said that when he was CM, Vijay had once gone to meet him and waited three hours at his home. He said Vijay sought his intervention when one of his films faced release hurdles.AIADMK stood by him then, but he lacks basic gratitude. He deliberately avoided naming our party in his speeches, dismissing us as matrum palar (others), he said. He alleged that TVK govt had not only failed to fulfil poll promises, but had also mismanaged the economy and stunted welfare programmes.On the other hand, AIADMK executed multiple welfare projects, Palaniswami said. We introduced Amma Mini Clinics, but neither the previous govt nor this one has paid attention to them. I established a govt medical college hospital in Tirupur at 400 crore and a veterinary research centre in Udumalpet at 125 crore, he said.

headline: HC cannot order closure of Tasmac shops beyond prohibited distance
content: Madras high court has categorically held that closure of a Tasmac shop located beyond the distance prescribed by law cannot be ordered by the court. However, it is open to Tamil Nadu govt to take an appropriate decision in accordance with law, the court said.Justice Hemanth Chandangoudar passed the order while disposing of a plea moved by T S Sridhar who wanted the court to direct Tasmac administration to close its shops at Sukurama Street, Parrys, Post Office Street, Prakasam Salai, Broadway (Near Mannady Metro), Jaffar Sarang Lane, opposite to Harbour and Wall Tax Road.The petitioner, represented by his counsel R S Raveendhren, said on the basis of govts policy decision to close retail liquor outlets situated within 500m of places of worship and educational institutions, he submitted a representation seeking closure of the Tasmac outlets in question.Opposing the plea, Tasmac said the outlets in question are beyond the prescribed distance from the places of worship and educational institutions. Since the outlets are within the limits of a municipal corporation, the restriction under Rule 8(1) of the Tamil Nadu Liquor Retail Vending (in Shops and Bars) Rules, 2003, is not applicable, he said.To this, Raveendhern said the policy decision is irrational since govt says that only 717 shops identified by it violate the norm of 500m, which has not been notified, and other shops in the state which are actually within 500m norm are not chosen for closure. Recording the submissions, the court said, A division bench of this court has rejected a similar prayer, holding that no mandamus could be issued for closure of a Tasmac outlet when the outlet was situated beyond the prohibited distance prescribed under the applicable rules.The bench further said that if the govt decides to change or revisit its policy, it is open to the govt to take an appropriate decision, the judge said, and disposed of the plea.

headline: Chennai PG doctors show gaps in reporting blood reactions
content: Postgraduate doctors at a city college hospital had a good understanding of blood components and transfusion indications, but showed gaps in recognising and reporting adverse transfusion reactions, according to a study published in BMJ Open, a peer-reviewed journal.The gap could lead to under-reporting, limiting hospitals ability to investigate lapses, identify patterns and prevent similar harm to future patients. The researchers assessed the knowledge, attitudes and practices related to haemovigilance among 150 postgraduate doctors. Haemovigilance is a system used to monitor, document and analyse adverse events associated with blood transfusions. Indias programme, launched in 2012, collects information on adverse reactions related to blood transfusions to help hospitals investigate the cause of such reactions, improve transfusion procedures and strengthen patient safety. Both serious and non-serious reactions are meant to be reported.Nearly all participants were aware of different blood components. A similar number identified the blood products used to treat anaemia and thrombocytopenia, or low platelet count. All participants agreed that health institutions should enrol in the haemovigilance programme and report transfusion reactions. About 26%, or 39 of the 150 doctors, said they had formally reported a transfusion reaction, and 21.3%, or about 32 doctors, had attended a haemovigilance-specific education programme or workshop. The study found that, despite familiarity with blood components and transfusion indications, awareness of the national haemovigilance programme and the Transfusion Reaction Reporting Form remained limited. Theoretical awareness alone is not enough, said Akilandeeshwari K, the studys first author from Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research. Doctors in training are often among the first to assess patients who develop fever, chills, breathing difficulty, rashes or other symptoms during or after a transfusion. Not every symptom is caused by a transfusion, but suspected reactions need prompt clinical assessment and reporting. Such documentation can help hospitals identify patterns, examine whether an error occurred and prevent recurrence.The researchers found that doctors with stronger knowledge tended to have better reporting practices. The association was stronger among those with favourable attitudes towards haemovigilance. It must become a part of routine clinical practice, not an activity undertaken only after a serious event, said Dr Anusha Dakshinamoorthi, the studys corresponding author. Structured teaching, hands-on exposure and a clear reporting pathway can make it easier for doctors to act when a transfusion reaction is suspected.The authors recommended focused haemovigilance training for postgraduate doctors, refresher programmes, greater awareness of reporting forms and hospital systems that make reporting easier. Blood banks and hospital transfusion committees, they said, could help embed these practices into everyday clinical work.

headline: DGP asks Avadi police to prevent crimes, speed up probes
content: Director General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal reviewed the law and order and crime situation in Avadi police commissionerate on Saturday and issued directions to officers on preventing serious crimes and improving investigations.The meeting, held at the commissionerate office, was attended by the commissioner of police, joint commissioner, and deputy commissioners. Aggarwal reviewed the investigation of murder cases and crimes against women and children and directed officers to take steps to curb the movement of contraband, including ganja and gutka.He reviewed measures to prevent road accidents and tackle cybercrime. Directions were issued to freeze bank accounts linked to fraudsters and strengthen financial investigations in cybercrime cases. The DGP reviewed the monitoring of history-sheeted offenders and the status of cases pending against them. He instructed officers to initiate steps for cancellation of bail in important cases and ensure the execution of non-bailable warrants.Aggarwal also reviewed the disposal of public petitions, foot patrols, and the functioning of village vigilance committees. He presented appreciation certificates to 20 police officers and personnel of Avadi commissionerate in recognition of their exemplary work. He heard grievances from police personnel and received their petitions.

headline: IMD to replace Chennai Port weather radar in 2027, add four new units in Tamil Nadu
content: band Doppler weather radar at Chennai Port, which has been working for more than two decades, will be replaced in 2027 even as it has been restored and kept operational ahead of the Oct-Dec northeast monsoon. India Meteorological Department, in collaboration with the state govt, will install four new Doppler weather radars in interior Tamil Nadu to strengthen coverage.IMD director general of meteorology Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said an order to replace the ageing radar was placed six months ago. The existing one is fixed and is currently working. We can turn it on whenever we want. We will manage with it until we replace it, he said.Imported from Germany, the Port radar has been operational since 2002 and has faced mechanical problems, including wear and tear in its antenna system and pedestal. Its bull gear, which rotates the antenna, had to be replaced, with Isro helping refurbish it as spare parts for the phased-out model were unavailable. The radar used to earlier be operated for a few hours when required because of these issues.The S-band radar has a range of about 500km and is important for tracking cyclones and other large weather systems, besides monitoring rain-bearing clouds. It provides information on rainfall structure, precipitation accumulation, wind speed and direction, cloud development and movement, and wind shear. A Doppler weather radar transmits electromagnetic waves and measures energy backscattered by water or ice particles in the atmosphere.Mohapatra said radars at Karaikal, Sriharikota and Thiruvananthapuram can provide coverage over Tamil Nadu if the Port radar fails, providing redundancy. The city also has an X-band radar at the NIOT campus in Pallikaranai, with a range of about 150km, used mainly for localised weather monitoring and nowcasting.You cannot assure that all radars will work well. Every time 30% radars will be down. There will be some problems. But we should have redundancy that we are ensuring, he said.The four new radars will be installed in Yercaud, Trichy, Kanyakumari and Ramanathapuram, according to IMD. The expansion is part of a national plan to add 16 radars by March 2027, taking the network from 52 to 68, Mohapatra said. About 91% of the country is covered so far.The focus is on ensuring redundancy, while creating a denser radar network along the coast and strengthening coverage in hilly and urban areas, he said.

headline: Meenambakkam inspector shunted out; kept without posting
content: Meenambakkam crime wing inspector C Mahesh Kumar, who during his stint in Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) had investigated the child rape case against granite baron R Veeramani in 2025, was shunted out and kept without posting on Saturday. An order issued by Chennai city commissioner of police said the transfer, which would take immediate effect, had been done on administrative grounds.The order directed the joint commissioner of police, south zone, to relieve Mahesh from duty with an instruction that he report to Chennai city police control room.Mahesh had served as an AVS inspector in 2025 when an NGO submitted a complaint against Veeramani along with a pen drive containing a video clip showing Veeramani raping a child.

headline: 'We Were Suspicious': Israeli Passengers Claim Flydubai Crew Asked Them To Untie 'Terrorist' Co-Pilot
content: Two Israeli passengers who helped restrain the Flydubai co pilot have described a tense confrontation with crew members who allegedly asked them to release him

headline: Two from Bihar arrested for cheating & robbing passengers in Chennai by posing as railway staff
content: Two men from Bihar, Ajit Bhagat, 21, and Sanjeev Kumar, 32, were arrested for posing as railway officials and cheating train passengers from North Indian states.Police said Rupesh Kumar, 24, from Bihar, who worked at a private dal company in Andhra Pradesh, had arrived at Perambur railway station on Sept 4 to travel to Bihar. The two men approached him and offered to arrange a reserved ticket to his native place. They took him to the Bandar Garden area in Perambur, where they snatched 2g of gold, worth 2.5 lakh, a mobile phone and 7,000 in cash before fleeing.Based on Rupeshs complaint, police registered a case and arrested the duo. Inquiries revealed that the accused had used the same method to rob another person of 10,000 and a mobile phone.Police said the duo had targeted passengers from northern states in more than four such incidents. The arrested duo was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.

headline: GCC races to finish work on key drains in south Chennai before northeast monsoon
content: Greater Chennai Corporation is racing to complete key stormwater drain projects, including a new 660m-long drain that will carry rainwater from IIT Madras, Guindy National Park and Raj Bhavan to south Buckingham Canal, within the next 20 days.The project is intended to improve drainage across about 102ha around Raj Bhavan, 250ha at IIT Madras and 125ha of forest area. An existing 350m lined drain inside IIT Madras will be connected to a double-vent, cut-and-cover stormwater drain leading to south Buckingham Canal.The project has been divided into two packages, said GCC commissioner G S Sameeran. In the first package, 40m of work remains. Top slab concreting work is underway, and will be completed in 10 days, he said. The second package will take another 20 days. Its highly complex because we have to cross Old Mahabalipuram Road, which is also the entry point for Chennai Metro Rail Limiteds underground station tunnel boring machine, Sameeran said.A 90m stretch is yet to be built to connect the drain to south Buckingham Canal. The commissioner said work on the first 45m would be completed in 15 days. Since work in OMR can be carried out only at night, it is causing a delay, he said. Another major stormwater project is under way to divert excess water from the Arasankazhani canal to south Buckingham Canal and reduce pressure on Okkiyam Maduvu. This work too is expected to be completed within the next 20 days, Sameeran said.Last month, chief secretary M Sai Kumar directed all departments to complete northeast monsoon preparedness work by Sept 30.

headline: Texas hasn't elected a Democrat to US Senate since 1988: Two polls show Republican candidate trailing in midterms
content: Democrat James Talarico has opened a narrow lead over Republican Ken Paxton in the race for a US Senate seat in Texas, an unusual development in a state where Republicans have dominated statewide elections for decades. Lloyd Bentsen, a Democrat, was re-elected to the Senate from Texas in 1988 and after that no candidate from the party could win from the state. A Fox News poll of Texas likely voters conducted from September 24 to 28 showed Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 49%. The two-point advantage is within the poll's margin of error of three percentage points. Among registered voters, however, Talarico's lead widened to seven points, compared with a three-point advantage in July. A separate New York Times/Siena University poll conducted from September 21 to 30 put Talarico six points ahead of Paxton. The result has renewed questions over whether Democrats could break their long drought in statewide Texas politics in the 2026 midterms. The polling does not necessarily indicate that Texas has turned Democratic. Instead, the numbers point to a combination of Paxton's weaknesses, divisions within the Republican electorate, Talarico's support among key voter groups and a difficult political environment for Republicans. One of the clearest differences between the two candidates is their personal ratings. Talarico has a net positive rating of eight points, with 52% of likely voters viewing him favourably and 44% unfavourably. Paxton, meanwhile, has a net negative rating of 18 points, with 40% favourable and 58% unfavourable ratings. The Fox News poll also found that Republicans were six times more likely to view Paxton unfavourably than Democrats were to view Talarico unfavourably. The Republican nominee's support is also affected by divisions within the party. Non-MAGA Republicans were more than five times as likely as MAGA Republicans to support Talarico, at 22% versus 4%. The poll found that 20% of likely voters who supported Republican Senator John Cornyn in the March primary now back Talarico. Talarico's advantage extends beyond the Democratic base. The Fox poll found strong support for the Democrat among moderates, with 65% backing him. He also led among Hispanic voters at 64%, voters under 35 at 62% and Black voters at 79%. Paxton's strongest groups included White evangelical Christians, White men without a college degree, rural voters and people aged 65 and above. The polling suggests that Paxton's challenge is not simply holding the Republican base together but also winning over voters who are less firmly aligned with the GOP. Trump won Texas by nearly 14 percentage points in 2024, but his current approval rating in the state is underwater, according to the Fox poll. The survey found 44% of Texans approving of Trump's performance and 55% disapproving. While 15% of voters who disapprove of Trump still support Paxton, only 9% of those who approve of Trump support Talarico. The New York Times also reported that a September Texas Southern University survey put Trump's approval rating seven points underwater in the state. The Fox survey found that seven in 10 Texans consider the cost of living extremely important to their Senate vote. Twice as many voters said they were falling behind financially as said they were getting ahead -- 35% versus 16%. Those who said they were falling behind financially backed Talarico by 32 points, while voters who said they were getting ahead favoured Paxton by 48 points. Talarico also held leads among voters who considered the cost of living, artificial intelligence and Trump extremely important to their Senate vote. headline: 'Baseless': India rejects Pakistan's claim over Ferozepur border incident, summons envoy
content: India on Saturday summoned the Charg dAffaires of the Pakistan High Commission and lodged a strong protest over what it described as the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) also rejected the baseless and motivated allegations by Pakistan regarding an incident in Punjabs Ferozepur sector along the International Border on Friday. According to the MEA, three individuals infiltrated into Indian territory and continued moving towards the border fence despite multiple warnings from the Border Security Force (BSF) to return to Pakistan. The ministry said the BSF was compelled to engage the three individuals after they posed an imminent security threat. New Delhi said the incident highlighted a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan. The Pakistani government was urged to investigate the cross-border infiltration and drug smuggling activities, as well as the alleged complicity of Pakistans border guarding forces. The MEA also called on Pakistan to take appropriate remedial measures and ensure respect for the sanctity of the International Border. India further urged Pakistan to strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and direct its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorised movement from its side.

headline: 'Pashu seva bhi prabhu seva hai': Reliance Executive Director Anant Ambani's farmers-first message from Andhra Pradesh
content: Trisha Bhattacharya Reliance Industries Executive Director Anant Ambani has called for a new approach to farming in Andhra Pradesh, saying young people need better skills, technology and entrepreneurial opportunities if agriculture is to become a career they actively choose. Speaking at the foundation stone-laying ceremony for the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub and Indian School of Agriculture (ISA) in Madanapalle on Friday, Ambani said many young people were moving away from farming because of uncertain incomes and limited opportunities. Too many young people leave farming because incomes are uncertain and opportunities seem limited. Let us give them the skills, technology and enterprise to build successful futures in their own villages, he said. The event was attended by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan and state minister Nara Lokesh. The horticulture hub is part of a wider initiative aimed at developing Rayalaseemas agricultural economy. Ambani said Reliance Industries would establish and manage the Indian School of Agriculture, which he described as an institution that could help make farming a profession that young Indians pursue with pride. The proposed school is expected to focus on modern agricultural practices while combining technology with the experience and traditional knowledge of Indian farmers. Artificial intelligence, drones, robotics and cloud computing could all have practical applications, Ambani said. He gave the example of AI systems that could alert farmers to pest attacks before they spread, drones that could assess crop health and guide the use of water and nutrients, and robotics that could reduce physically demanding farm work and crop losses. The broader horticulture project is planned across 10 districts, with development structured through 201 clusters covering 303 mandals and thousands of villages. The initiative is being implemented in phases and has an estimated investment of 1 lakh crore. Ambani said Reliance Jio would work with the Indian School of Agriculture to take training modules to farmers in Indian languages through interactive virtual classrooms in villages. The idea, he said, is to take agricultural education beyond the campus and directly into farming communities. Educated rural youth could also work as digitally enabled extension workers, helping farmers put the lessons into practice. He pointed to Reliances Jio Krishi platform and said the company had developed products intended to support farmers. Ambani also spoke about price intelligence, saying technology could help farmers determine when and where to sell their produce. Water management was another focus. Cloud-based advice and technology, he said, could help farmers work towards the governments Per Drop More Crop objective, while greenhouse technology could allow cultivation to continue through more of the year. Ambani also linked his agricultural vision to animal welfare, describing himself as a pashu sevak, or someone dedicated to serving animals. Pashu seva bhi prabhu seva hai, he said, stressing his belief in technology-driven animal husbandry. He referred to Vantara in Jamnagar, the animal welfare and conservation initiative associated with the Reliance Foundation, and said work had begun towards what he described as a global university for wildlife and veterinary sciences. His comments placed animal welfare alongside farming and clean energy as parts of the wider vision he outlined in Andhra Pradesh. Ambani also announced that Reliance Industries plans to invest 1 lakh crore in Andhra Pradesh to establish compressed biogas (CBG) plants. According to PTI reporting, the investment is expected to create more than three lakh jobs and generate nearly 60,000 crore in revenue for the state over the coming decades. This 1 lakh crore commitment is separate from the 1 lakh crore estimated investment attached to the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub. Ambani said the CBG projects would help connect agriculture with energy production, while creating another potential source of income and employment in rural areas. Ambani also made a personal appeal to the people of the state, asking them to consider him a son of Andhra and guide him on how he could contribute to its development. Today, I request you to treat me as a son of Andhra and direct me as to what I can contribute to your beautiful state. Nannu Andhra bidde ga bhavinchandi, he said. He added that the foundation stone ceremony was about more than construction, saying the projects were intended to lay the groundwork for stronger villages, rural enterprise and improved livelihoods for farmers. The Rayalaseema initiative is being positioned by the Andhra Pradesh government as a major push to expand horticulture through irrigation, technology, processing and market infrastructure. The project is expected to promote crops including mango, banana, tomato and pomegranate across the region. Trisha Bhattacharya Trisha Bhattacharya is a Senior Content Producer

headline: TVK formally joins INDIA bloc; set to join demonstrations against BJP and EC
content: The various Tamil Nadu leaders of the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) met at the Tamil Nadu Congress Committees (TNCC) headquarters in Chennai on Saturday and formally welcomed the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) into the alliance, led by the Congress nationally. The meeting was chaired by TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore. At the meeting, it was also decided that Save Democracy protests would be organised at the district headquarters across Tamil Nadu on October 13 and 14 to highlight the issues surrounding the breakdown of democracy in India. Additionally, a protest will be held on October 15, in which INDIA bloc leaders will participate in Chennai. Mr. Tagore said the TVKs general secretary (Election Management) and PWD Minister Aadhav Arjuna; MDMK chief Vaiko; VCK chief Thol. Thirumavalavan; CPI(M)s State secretary P. Shanmugam; IUMLs K.A.M. Muhammed Abubacker; and CPI(ML) leader Chandra Mohan participated in the meeting. Other leaders, such as State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson; Congress leaders K.V. Thangkabalu and K.S. Alagiri; State Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan; VCK treasurer S.S. Balaji; Congress MP Praveen Chakravarty; Tiruvallur MP Sasikanth Senthil; and Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert were also present. Asked if the DMK was invited to be a part of the meeting, Mr. Tagore said, Everyone fighting the RSS-BJPs rule can be a part of the INDIA bloc. We need to have a political understanding that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are destroying the democracy in India. Our leaders have reached out to parties who should have come today, but I cannot talk about those who did not attend. You have been asking why the TVK was not participating in INDIA bloc meetings. Now, it has joined the alliance. Its leaders have said that they are ready to protest and burn the effigy of Gyanesh Kumar, he said. INDIA bloc is strong in Tamil Nadu. We are going to oppose the RSS, BJP, and Gyanesh Kumar, he added.
