headline: 'Next year could be bad': Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath endorses grave warning for startup funding
content: Sounak Mukhopadhyay It all started with an X user predicting the future of Indias startup scene in 2027. The post has now gone viral, probably after Nikhil Kamaths approval. The user wrote, If you are a startup or a company looking to raise capital. Raise soon. This is probably the best time to do so. And get a lot of cash to keep you comfortable for a year or two. Be diligent in spending. The cash too can be invested into some liquid assets. Next year could be bad. The Zerodha co-founder replied with a 100 emoji, indicating that the prediction was 100% correct. Now, the reason why the prediction deserves more attention is that the user, whose X handle is @aravind, is known for his uncanny ability to predict the future. On 2 April 2025, he predicted, I can predict, once the Russia-Ukraine peace deal is done, Trump will go after Venezuela hard with sanctions and try to take out Maduro. If everything fails, a false flag and direct bombing-invasion will happen. Why will the US do it? The answer is below for you. The answer that he referred to was a map, showing Venezuela holding more than 302 billion barrels of oil. The tweet got viral after, under US President Donald Trumps command, US forces captured Nicols Maduro and his wife in January 2026. Maduro now faces charges of narco-terrorism in US courts. Nikhil Kamath is one of many people who responded to the startup prediction. When asked for advice for the common man, Aravind posted this: Don't spend more than what you can afford. Live within your means. Don't take unnecessary loans. Try not to be in debt too much. Don't make risky investments. One user asked, What is driving the expectation that next year could be bad....funding availability, valuations, or the broader macro environment?? Aravind blamed it on the broader macro environment. According to him, fund-raising may turn hostile before the end of the next year. One user asked if 2027 would see an AI market correction or even a bubble burst. In 2027, there could be some geopolitical events that could set off selling in the markets, but blame it on AI. This will cause panic-selling and a crash in AI and tech stocks. Tech startups, that too the ones relying on AI, won't be able to raise easy money like now, Aravind replied. Aravinds X bio says that he talks about issues long before they happen. It also says that he sometimes gets into the higher consciousness, Turiya. I post conspiracies, and nothing I say is real. Don't believe anything I post, the bio cautions. Disclosure: Social media posts have been lightly edited for clarity and comprehension. Sounak Mukhopadhyay Sounak Mukhopadhyay covers trending news, sports and entertainment for LiveMint. His reporting focuses on fast-moving stories, box office performance, digital culture and major cricket developments. He combines real-time updates with clear context for everyday readers. Sounak brings newsroom experience across breaking news, explainers and long-form features. He has a strong emphasis on accuracy, verification and responsible storytelling. His work tracks audience behaviour, celebrity influence and the business of sport and cinema. He helps readers understand why a story matters beyond the headline. Sounak has contributed to widely read digital publications. He continues to build a body of journalism shaped by consistency, speed and editorial clarity. He is particularly interested in the intersection of media, popular culture and public conversation in contemporary India.

headline: Parliamentary Committees reshuffle: TMC loses both chairperson posts
content: TMC loses both chairperson posts In a major reshuffle of chairpersons of six of the 24 Standing Parliamentary Committees, the Trinamool Congress on Saturday lost both its chairperson berths owing to a group of their MPs switching camps after the recently concluded West Bengal Assembly elections. Soon after the BJP swept the West Bengal Assembly elections in May, a group of TMC MPs led by Dastidar approached the Speaker, claiming that they had merged with the NCPI, a Tripura-based outfit, and sought to be recognised as a separate bloc in Lok Sabha. A decision on the breakaway factions fate is pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. Reacting strongly to the reshuffle, TMC Parliamentary Leader Derek OBrien wrote a letter to Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan, saying that the Parliament is being turned into a deep, dark chamber. The leader of the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction maintained that theirs is the third largest party in the Upper House, but is being deprived of a chairperson berth. In Rajya Sabha, the BJP is the largest party, followed by the INC (second largest) and AITC (third largest). And yet, the Chairpersonship, which we held in 2024-25 and 2025-26, has been taken away. This is not the first time we have been treated in this manner! In 2019, when we were also the third largest party in Rajya Sabha, we were deprived. That was rectified a few years later and now it is back to square one, said the TMC leader in his letter. Other panel chief changes Other changes announced by Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Saturday include Congress Rajya Sabha member Digvijaya Singh being replaced by party colleague Mukul Wasnik to head the committee on education. Meanwhile, the BJP has reshuffled three of its committee chairpersons, with party MP Brij Lal being replaced by party colleague Sujeet Kumar to head the committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice. Rajya Sabha member Brij Lals term in the Upper House is set to end in November. The BJP has replaced Lok Sabha MP Basavaraj Bommai with Shashank Mani to head the Labour, Textiles and Skill Development Committee. The third change that the BJP has made is in the Committee on Railways, with the party appointing its MP Sudhir Gupta instead of C M Ramesh. Among those who have retained their chairpersonships include DMK MPs Tiruchi Siva and K Kanimozhi who will continue to head the Parliamentary Committee on Industry, and the Committee on Food, Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution, respectively. Congress MPs Shashi Tharoor and Charanjit Singh Channi, have also been retained as chairpersons of Committees on External Affairs, and Agriculture, respectively. Meanwhile, party MP Mukul Wasnik will continue to head the Committee on Education, Women, Children and Youth. Samajwadi Partys Ram Gopal Yadav has also been retained as the chairperson of the Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The leaders of some key BJP allies such as the JD(U), Shiv Sena and TDP have also been retained as heads of different Parliamentary Committees. The Parliament has a total of 24 department-related Standing Committees with members from both the Houses; while eight come under the Rajya Sabha Chairman, the other 16 are under the Lok Sabha Speaker. The Committees serve a one-year term, after which they are reconstituted.

headline: Popular Mobilisation Forces | Iraq's militias within the military
content: Iraqs militias within the military On June 13, 2014, Grand Ayatollah Ali Sistani, Iraqs top Shia cleric, issued a fatwa asking Iraqis to join the fight against terrorism. The nature of the situation and the dangers facing Iraq and its people at the present time require defending the country, its people and the honour of its citizens, said the cleric in his edict, which was read out by his representative Sheikh Abdul-Mahdi al-Karbalai, during Friday prayers in Karbala. Mr. Sistanis call came amid the rapid territorial advances made by the Islamic State (IS), a Sunni-jihadist group, in Iraq. On June 10, IS militants captured Mosul, Iraqs second-largest city. After consolidating in the north, they started moving south towards Baghdad, while also threatening Shia holy places such as Najaf and Karbala. In the north, the Iraqi military collapsed in the face of IS advance. There was panic in Baghdad, where Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki was scrambling to arrest the jihadist surge. This defence is considered a wajib kifai [collective obligation] upon a sufficient number of citizens as is needed to fulfil the task, Mr. Sistani said in his fatwa. Hence, the citizens who are able to bear arms and fight the terrorists in defence of their country, their people and their sanctities must volunteer to join the army and the security forces to achieve this sacred objective. The edict triggered the mobilisation of hundreds of thousands of Iraqi youth to fight the Islamic State. But the mobilisation did not remain confined to the army and police. Shia militias expanded and new armed groups emerged, eventually forming the core of the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMFs, or Hashd al-Shaabi). The Iraqi state, shaken by the loss of Mosul, encouraged the militias to expand their footprint, while Iran, equally invested in defeating the IS, provided money, weapons and training to the militias. Seven groups were already operating in Iraq Badr Organisation; Asaib Ahl al-Haq; Kataib Hezbollah; Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada; Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba; Kataib Jund al-Imam; and Kataib al-Imam Ali. Several new groups also sprang up. All these forces were brought under the PMF umbrella for better coordination in the fight against the Islamic State. The PMF factions, which fought alongside the Iraqi military under U.S. air cover, played a key role in defeating the IS. But the battle against the jihadist group also led to the institutionalisation of the militias, which refused to disarm even after the IS was defeated and its militants were driven out of most Iraqi cities, including Mosul. Calling themselves resistance forces, the prominent factions in the PMF demanded complete American withdrawal from Iraq. The killing of Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis, the deputy chairman of the PMF and leader of Kataib Hezbollah, in January 2020, along with Irans Qassem Soleimani, in Baghdad by a U.S. air strike opened a new phase of attritional conflict between the PMF and U.S. forces in Iraq. This conflict escalated further after the U.S. launched its war on Iran this year. On September 30, when U.S. troops completed their withdrawal from Iraq, 23 years after the invasion started, the PMF, unsurprisingly, called it a historic victory. The PMF now comprises more than three dozen militias, with an estimated total strength of 240,000 fighters and an annual budget of $3.4 billion. Historically, the PMF contained three broad currents: Iran-aligned factions, Sistani-aligned shrine units and the Sadrist Saraya al-Salam. The Sistani-aligned shrine units (Abbas Combat Division, Liwa Ali al-Akbar and Imam Ali Combat Division) subsequently broke away from the PMF structure in 2020 and came under the direct authority of the commander-in-chief. Badr Organisation, originally the armed wing of the Supreme Council for the Islamic Revolution in Iraq; Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba are the prominent Iran-backed factions within the PMF fold. They are also the most powerful among the militias. The most prominent Sadrist militia is Saraya al-Salam (Peace Brigades), which is aligned with the PMF but maintains a tense relationships with its command. Muqtada al-Sadr, a Shia cleric, is one of the most influential religious-political figures in post-war Iraq. He had commanded the now-dissolved Mahdi Army that resisted U.S. troops in the early days of the invasion. The Mahdi Army had received support from Iran, but Mr. Sadr later distanced himself from Iranian influence and projected Saraya al-Salam as an Iraqi nationalist militia. The U.S. had repeatedly demanded that the Iraqi state demobilise the militias, some of which, such as Kataib Hezbollah, have been designated as terrorist groups. But both mainstream Iraqi politicians and militia commanders have resisted such calls. In 2016, the Iraqi Parliament passed the PMF commission law, which institutionalised the PMF as an independent organisation within the Iraqi armed forces. But they continued to maintain their independent command structures. The prominent members of the PMF also formed political parties and started contesting elections. In 2018, Badr Organization, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Kataib Hezbollah and Kataib al-Imam Ali all came together to form the Fatah Alliance, a political coalition to represent the militias in the general elections (the alliance was later disbanded). Besides, the Sadrist movement has a separate political organisation, the National Shia Movement. In the current Iraqi parliament, Badr Organisation has 18 seats, while Sadiqoun Movement, another PMF-linked political bloc, has 27 seats. The war on Iran After the U.S. and Israel started bombing Iran on February 28, 2026, the Iran-aligned militias in the PMF started attacking American military and diplomatic facilities in Iraq. According to U.S. officials, they carried out some 600 attacks since the war broke out and the U.S. launched air strikes targeting these groups. But the U.S. found it increasingly difficult to deter PMF factions whose decentralised operational tactics and geographical spread worked in their favour. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi had said earlier that the militias would be demobilised by September 30, the deadline for U.S. troops withdrawal. After the U.S. troops completed their pullback, Mr. Zaidi said the process of demobilisation had begun, and pushed the deadline to June 2027. Some militias such as Kataib Imam Ali and Saraya al-Salam have reached an understanding with the government to hand over weapons and regularise their status. But the more powerful ones such as Kataib Hezbollah and Nujaba have resisted the calls for disarmament, saying the Islamic resistance would continue as long as American military presence in the region continues. Both the U.S. and the militias have agreed to refrain from attacking each other for 90 days following the withdrawal of U.S. troops, according to Iraqi officials. But with the war on Iran unresolved and some PMF factions deeply entangled with Iran, any escalation between Tehran and Washington could have a direct impact on Iraq.

headline: Dharapuram farmers unhappy over T.N. government's approach on crop loan waiver
content: The State governments approach towards the implementation of the waiver scheme of crop loans extended by primary agricultural cooperative societies has left many farmers in Dharapuram of Tiruppur district unhappy. K.M. Ramasamy, a senior functionary of an association of farmers which, according to him, does not owe allegiance to any political party, complains that the governments couple of changes in the waiver scheme has only created more confusion among the agriculturists and, unnecessarily, created false expectations among the farming community, even though he appreciates that the government has its own constraints. In contrast to the electoral promise of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam that a 100% waiver would be given to small and marginal farmers (up to five acres of land) who took loans from primary agricultural cooperative societies and 50% waiver to others, the TVK regime had, initially, announced a full waiver to 50,000 and a 50% waiver for small farmers on loans up to Rs. 50,000. Subsequently, it revised the waiver for the loans up to 75,000 availed by farmers, irrespective of the size of their landholdings. One more change was made by providing a maximum waiver of 75,000 for those who had obtained loans in the range of 75,000-1,00,000 and a maximum waiver of 35,000 for those who took loans exceeding 1 lakh. Referring to the coverage of the loans given between May 2025 and February 2026, Mr Ramasamy wonders about the exclusion of March 2026 as it is, invariably, during the month that a large number of crop loan gets sanctioned. Besides, those who repaid loans up to June 19 have not been given any relief. All pensioners of the Central and State governments have been excluded from the coverage and this norm should be changed by introducing an income limit. N. Natarajan, another farmer of the constituency, points out that in the western districts, farmers take loans for the purchase of milch cows. The loan waiver scheme should include such farmers also, as animal husbandry and dairy sectors come under the overall agricultural sector. Senior government officials, looking after policy formulation, have not replied to the messages sent by on the issues raised by the farmers.

headline: Crorepati woman owning luxury cars is also entitled to maintenance from estranged partner: HC
content: Owning properties worth several crores and luxury cars does not deny a woman lawful maintenance from her estranged partner, Madras high court has said. The court observed while confirming an order of a family court directing payment of 1 lakh as maintenance to a woman who owned a flat worth 1.7 crore and 1.5 lakh to her child.Justice Sunder Mohan passed the order while dismissing revision petition moved by the womans partner challenging the family court order.According to the man, a film producer, his relationship with the woman, who was a model was not solmonised as a valid marriage and that he already has a legally married wife. Therefore, a woman who he was in live-in relationship was not entitled to maintenance.He added that he was lured by the woman and taking advantage of a weak moment, got conceived to gain unlawfully. He had also stated that he was willing to pay maintenance to the child but not to the woman.Pointing out that the woman has alleged that the petitioner suppressed the existence of a legal marriage by stating that he was divorced, the court said, in such circumstances, the petitioner ought to have established that he never made such a representation and that the earlier marriage is subsisting. The petitioner has not let in evidence to counter the evidence let in by the woman on this aspect. Though the Supreme Court had held that a second wife, whose marriage is void on account of the existence of an earlier legal marriage, is not entitled to maintenance, the apex court had also held that the burden is on the husband to establish that the earlier marriage was in subsistence, the court said.It is the case of the petitioner that the woman has sufficient means to maintain herself and owns a flat worth Rs. 1.7 crore and has two luxury cars. These facts are not in dispute.But the evidence reveals that after the childs birth, the woman did not have a regular source of income. No evidence to the contrary has been let in by the petitioner. The findings of the family court, which is based on the evidence, cannot be faulted, the court said.

headline: A corporate mafia government has been ruling the State, alleges Stalin
content: DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Saturday alleged that a corporate mafia government, controlled by an unidentified individual, was ruling Tamil Nadu. Really, it is a mysterious government. There is no transparency and everything is being decided behind the scenes, he said while campaigning for DMK candidate I. Paranthaman in the Madurantakam Assembly constituency. Mr. Stalin said the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which had promised to provide a clean government, had inducted former AIADMK Ministers facing corruption cases into the party after washing them in washing machines. Can a government that cancelled the Parandur Airport Project be called a clean government? They sought to hand over Chennai airport to private operators and covered up the letter written to the Prime Minister. Is this a clean government? he asked. He alleged that a mafia had taken control of the government with the intention of diverting investments to Andhra Pradesh. Mr. Stalin also criticised Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for not taking a position on the demand by several political parties, barring the BJP and its allies, for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and their protests over the issue. Over 13 crore people have been denied their voting rights, and in many States, the outcome of the election has been stolen. Can a person who does not express his opinion on these issues be called a political leader? Even the leaders of his alliance parties are asking the same question, he said. Mr. Stalin said the real face of the TVK would soon be exposed and people would come to know who was in a secret alliance with the BJP at the Centre. Those who had joined the TVK too would eventually be left in the lurch, he said. He asserted that the DMKs only mistake was that it had failed to take the TVK seriously. We fought our ideological enemies and remained indifferent to the crowd of clowns, he said. He also attributed the DMKs defeat in the Assembly election to the loss of votes caused by the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Lakhs of people lost their votes because of the SIR. We lost because of these reasons, he said. Mr. Stalin rejected the claim that there had been a wave in favour of the TVK. If there had been a wave, it could have won at least 150 seats. It could not secure even 118 seats and formed the government with the support of political parties that were part of the DMK alliance, he said. The Chief Minister might speak in a high pitch, but he should acknowledge that the government had been formed with votes polled in favour of the DMK, Mr. Stalin said. Instead of relying on its allies, Mr. Vijay had purchased AIADMK MLAs and fielded them again in the byelection to increase the TVKs tally, he alleged. Calling upon voters to remain vigilant, Mr. Stalin said they had been taken for a ride by the candidate they had elected. In the name of change, the voters got only disappointment, he added.

headline: Airlines reject 33% cut in international slots at Mumbai airport T2 from Oct 25: Report
content: off between Mumbai airport operator Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) and airlines has intensified, with carriers rejecting the proposed temporary reduction of international departure slots at Terminal 2 (T2) from October 25, according to a CNBC-TV18 report. MIAL, controlled of Adani Group, has proposed temporarily discontinuing 265 of 770 weekly international departure slots at T2, representing a 33% reduction. The move is linked to the planned redevelopment of Terminal 1 (T1), which is currently used for domestic operations. According to PTI, MIAL has communicated the proposed reduction to 46 airlines operating international services from T2. The vacated capacity will be used to accommodate domestic traffic as T1 is closed for redevelopment. Airlines have formally rejected the proposed reduction, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing sources familiar with their response to MIAL's communication. The carriers have said they support the refurbishment and redevelopment of T1 but argued that this should not be treated as consent to flight cancellations or a reduction in T2 operations. Airlines have also raised concerns over the lack of what they consider meaningful consultation on the proposed 33% reduction, its operational implications and the specific flights that could be affected. The timing of the proposed reduction is a major concern for airlines. According to CNBC-TV18, airlines have pointed out that the winter schedule was approved in June 2026, and carriers have already planned their networks, aircraft deployment and passenger commitments accordingly. They have argued that any reduction in approved capacity should follow a transparent consultation and coordination process because of its potential impact on flight schedules, aircraft deployment and passengers. The airlines have also said they have not consented to the proposed slot cancellations and that the reduction should not be imposed unilaterally. MIAL's proposed schedule would require IndiGo to temporarily discontinue 74 weekly international departure slots from Mumbai, while Air India would face a reduction of 33 weekly slots. PTI reported that IndiGo currently operates 224 weekly international flights from Mumbai, while Air India operates 100. Other airlines facing reductions include: Akasa Air - 11 weekly international flights; Air India Express - 7; SpiceJet - 5; Etihad Airways - 10; Emirates - 10. Etihad and Emirates currently operate 28 weekly services each from Mumbai. MIAL has said the reduction is part of the transition linked to the redevelopment of T1. According to CNBC-TV18, the airport operator has given airlines until October 6 to identify the specific slots they want to temporarily discontinue. If airlines do not respond, MIAL has said it will determine the slots itself. MIAL plans to begin reallocating the vacated T2 infrastructure from October 26, including check-in counters, baggage belts, boarding gates and operational office space, to scheduled domestic operators. The objective is to facilitate the movement of around 5 million passengers a year from T1 to T2. With MIAL proceeding with the T1 redevelopment plan and the proposed T2 flight reductions, airlines are seeking intervention from the Civil Aviation Ministry. The airlines want a detailed stakeholder meeting on the T1 redevelopment plan and have asked the government to ensure that operational measures are not implemented unilaterally without airline agreement. They have also raised concerns about the impact on passengers, particularly where bookings may already have been made for flights included in the approved winter schedule.

headline: Palaniswami slams TVK regime for claiming to be corruption-free
content: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Saturday questioned the claim of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government about providing a corruption-free regime. Addressing electors at Achirapakkam in Madurantakam Constituency, where a bypoll is scheduled to be held on October 6, Mr. Palaniswami alleged that 70 per bag of paddy was being collected at direct purchase centres. Referring to searches conducted by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) at many government offices in the last five months, he contended that the DVAC itself had gone on record, saying that unaccounted for money to the tune of 1.7 crore had been seized. Given this backdrop, he asked whether the current dispensation was a clean regime. While gross collections of GST rose in September at the national level, Tamil Nadu had recorded a decline in collections. How is the government going to correct the situation? Already, the loans outstanding have reached 10 lakh crore. As the revenue collections have gone down, the burden of loans will go up, for which taxes will have to be levied on people, he said. Mr. Palaniswami asked the people whether such an incompetent government should remain in office.

headline: GCC audits 417 schools for safety, infrastructure gaps
content: Greater Chennai Corporations Gender Policy Lab is conducting safety audits at its 417 schools to identify infrastructure gaps, assess physical and environmental risks, and recommend improvements.The exercise follows reports of shortcomings in some schools, including girls being asked to leave class while menstruating, poor toilet facilities and limited awareness of menstrual health. The audit, which began last month, assesses child protection systems and students psychosocial safety too. This is a continuous process, not a one-time inspection, said K A N Legis, head of the Gender Policy Lab.The lab is conducting the audit with the Singappen Special Force and departments including social welfare and child protection. Its 95-point checklist covers structural safety, classroom ventilation, electrical wiring and fittings, accessibility features such as ramps and handrails, toilet hygiene, sports equipment, and functioning CCTV cameras.The review examines whether schools have functional Child Protection Committees and prominently display womens helpline and emergency contact numbers. GCC schools have gender clubs that conduct activities intended to promote gender sensitivity and awareness 140 middle schools and 81 high and higher secondary schools. In one recent inspection, officials found construction debris dumped inside a school campus and noted that workers could enter the premises, Legis said. The problem was addressed immediately. GCC assistant engineers and school staff are open to our suggestions, so many issues we identify are being resolved quickly, she said.For safety concerns beyond school grounds, the lab seeks support from the Singappen Special Force. Officials have identified poorly lit areas near schools and asked students whether they feel safe on the journey home. If there are people causing trouble in those areas, the Singappen Special Force carries out regular patrols there, Legis said.

headline: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels abandon regional capital as government advances
content: Tigray rebels were abandoning their regional capital in northern Ethiopia on Saturday (October 3, 2026), a local journalist and residents told AFP, as pro-government forces advanced on the city. Fighting erupted on September 23 in northern Ethiopia as the rebel Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launched attacks into neighbouring states, raising fears of a return to the devastating 2020-2022 civil war. But federal forces and pro-government militias have pushed them back in recent days and were heading north towards the regional capital, Mekelle. "TPLF militants and leaders are leaving Mekelle," the journalist said, adding that federal forces had not yet been seen inside the city. He said government offices and police stations had been left without security personnel. "I am concerned that government and public property could be exposed to looting because there are no security forces in the city," a local resident told AFP. "Lawlessness could spread in the city, and I am also afraid for my life. I want us to quickly return to law and order," added another resident. In a separate development, a diplomatic source told AFP that a mini-summit on Sunday (October 4) would bring together the presidents of Egypt, Eritrea and Somalia, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, as well as the head of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), Abdel Fattah al-Burhane, in Alamein, Egypt, on the sidelines of an African Business Forum. The TPLF has long been the dominant force in Tigray, and kicked out a government-appointed administration earlier this year. In a video message on Thursday, its leader Debretsion Gebremichael implied the TPLF would continue guerrilla-style attacks as they did when Mekelle fell to government forces in 2020 during the early stages of the last war. Their insurgent campaign ultimately led to the TPLF retaking the city in mid-2021. "We operate under a strategy to strike the enemy wherever we choose," Mr. Debretsion said. Regional tensions The conflict has triggered a breakdown in Ethiopia's relations with Eritrea and Egypt, which Ethiopia accuses of supporting the rebels. Ethiopia expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats and shut its embassy in Asmara on Thursday, while Eritrea responded that it would "sever all diplomatic ties". Eritrea accuses landlocked Ethiopia of planning to invade and seize access to its coastline. The TPLF's Debretsion said in his video message that "the war is regional and it is a war to control the Red Sea". Ethiopia also expelled an Egyptian diplomat without explanation, prompting a reciprocal move by Cairo. Counter-offensive The rebels initially made advances in neighbouring Afar and Amhara states, working alongside local militias. But they were pushed back this week, and the government launched a counter-offensive into Tigrayan territory along three axes towards Mekelle, according to the Critical Threats Project, part of the American Enterprise Institute think tank. There were reports that Mekelle's airport, on the southern approach to the city, had fallen to a pro-government militia on Friday. But social media accounts are difficult to verify. Media access is heavily restricted and there have been significant communications blackouts. Earlier, a humanitarian source told AFP on condition of anonymity that the TPLF had been entirely pushed out of Afar. The TPLF ruled all of Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018, when it was marginalised with the rise of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who hails from the Oromia region. The tensions led to a civil war from 2020 to 2022 one of the deadliest in the world in recent times that left more than 600,000 dead, according to the African Union. The Pretoria peace agreement of 2022, brokered by African institutions and Washington, maintained an uneasy calm until last year, but was never fully implemented.

headline: A forest through the eyes of the deaf
content: Tt is so quiet out here, was what one of the hearing impaired participants observed, on taking a walk through Nanmangalam forest. It was 7am and there was just the chirping of birds and insects to be heard. For people with hearing impairment who use hearing aids, the urban soundscape can sometimes become overwhelmingly loud, says Anjana Venkatecan of Care Earth Trust, which collaborated with the Deaf Artists Collective (DFC) to conduct the nature walk recently, along with the Tamil Nadu forest department. Being able to access a peaceful place and experience the sounds of nature was a big deal for them, she says.DFC, a creative community initiative under Madras Photo Bloggers, aims to bridge the accessibility gap by creating meaningful and dignified opportunities for deaf people to explore various spaces. Though they have had photo walks before, this is the first exclusive nature walk for the deaf to be conducted with their communication needs in mind. When it is primarily a photo walk, participants may be more interested in photography than in learning about the environment, says Anjana. Having sign language interpretation and a deaf-friendly environment made it easier for them to participate, learn, connect with others and enjoy the experience without worrying about communication barriers.Srivatsan Sankaran, founder of Madras Photo Bloggers, says many deaf people do not always get opportunities to experience and capture nature because of communication and accessibility barriers. Most outdoor activities and nature experiences are designed around hearing-based communication. Information may be given verbally, instructions may be announced without visual alternatives, and sign language interpretation may not be available. We wanted participants to explore and experience nature through photography.Nanmangalam is a forested area and so spotting birds was difficult, says Anjana. That gave us an opportunity to talk more about its flora. The walk was more geared towards insects. We saw a lot of butterflies, stick insects, weaver ants and other insects.The sign-language interpreter is crucial to the experience. From our side, we had to slightly change our approach to accommodate the interpretation, slow down and factor in the additional time required for signing, says Anjana.DFC will continue creating more of such inclusive nature walks and photography experiences for the deaf community in different environments, says Srivatsan.

headline: Plant based menus take seed at colleges
content: Canteens are increasingly adding recipes without meat, fish or dairy products. Starting 2027, future chefs at SRM Institute of Hotel Management in Kattankulathur will spend a fifth of their coursework learning to cook without meat, fish, eggs or dairy. The institute has also cut animal products in its dining halls and hostels by 30%, as part of a growing push for plant-based food on Indian campuses.The institution recently collaborated with Humane World for Animals India, which sent professionals to campus to train faculty in plant-based food preparation. It covered the fundamentals of plant-based cooking, ingredient substitution, menu planning and preparation of dishes without meat, fish, eggs and dairy products, says Lalitha Shri, vice principal. We reduced animal products in campus dining and hostels to align practical dining hall practices with classroom learning.They are not the only ones. Pondicherry University serves plant-based food in its campus canteens and hostels on Tuesdays, so does Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research (BIHER), Chennai. The German International School in Chennai, one of the first to make a move in this direction, had announced in 2017 that they would serve 100% plant-based meals to their students and avoid using animal products on campus. Student chefs at SRM Institute of Hotel Management At BITS Pilani, Hyderabad, there is a separate vegan counter within the mess, says Parth Gupta, a third year student, and joint secretary of the Club for Animal Rights and Equality. In our case, nearly half the mess menu was plant-based. It took some time to convince the administration, but eventually they agreed to introduce such an alternative. The mess vendors were willing to prepare vegan alternatives for curries with milk or other dairy products such as soya chunks or cashew-based cream, says Parth.In India, especially in South India, much of vegetarian food is plant-based. However, turning a govt institutions canteen plant-based is still problematic owing to the political colours it might take on, says Naman Dedhia, of the organisation Plant Based Treaty, which works with educational institutions across the world to teach them about plant-based cuisine. But there is definitely a movement among private institutions in India.The dishes are not as bland or unappetising as many imagine, says Sheetal Ahuja, director of Vision International School of Excellence, Ankleshwar, Gujarat, where the canteen went vegan three years ago. We worked closely with a nutritionist and put a lot of thought into the menu. We experimented with different combinations and cuisines to ensure that the children received good sources of protein, essential amino acids, fibre and other nutrients.In order to not make children feel that something had been taken away from them, they adapted familiar foods. We marinated tofu to give it a paneer-like texture. We introduced soy curd, soy lassi, almond milk, kheer and several other nutritious and tasty desserts, she says. We talk to children about the compassion behind these choices. Many of them are happy that in their own small way, they can contribute to creating a better world for animals.At SRM, the practical sessions exposed students to ingredients such as vegetables, fruits, grains, pulses, legumes, nuts, seeds, coconut and plant-based dairy alternatives. Students learn how familiar dishes can be recreated using plant-based ingredients while retaining flavour, texture, presentation and nutritional value. The focus is also on techniques rather than recipes. Students are encouraged to understand how ingredients behave, how flavour can be developed using herbs and spices, how plant proteins can be incorporated into menus, and how locally available produce can be used creatively, says Lalitha Shri. Vegan cuisine is not simply about removing animal-based ingredients; it is about reimagining food with creativity, nutrition and sustainability at its heart. The future of hospitality lies in creating food that is delicious, innovative and mindful of both people and the planet.While plant-based diets are beneficial for the gut and are fibre-rich, Vitamin B12 deficiencies are often not found, which might have to be addressed through supplements, says Mumtaz Khalid Ismael, consultant clinical dietician.There are also significant environmental benefits, says Sridhar A, environmental researcher. Introducing more plant-based meals in schools and colleges as a dietary choice, is an opportunity to reduce the environmental footprint of the food system while shaping sustainable and ethical habits among young people. Food systems contribute more than one third of global greenhouse gas emissions, and evidence shows that diets with less animal-based food can substantially reduce pressures on land, water, biodiversity and climate.Beyond health and environmental concerns, there is the ethical question, says Sai Vignesh, vegan advocate and founder of the Chennai-based organisation Almighty Animal Care Trust. If human beings can thrive on a plant-based diet, why should we continue consuming animals? I would say the ethical aspect should remain at the forefront.

headline: Crorepati woman owning luxury cars is also entitled to maintenance from estranged partner: Madras high court
content: Owning properties worth several crores of rupees and luxury cars does not deny a woman lawful maintenance from her estranged partner, Madras high court has said. The court made the observation while confirming an order of a family court directing payment of Rs. 1 lakh as maintenance to a woman, who owned a flat worth Rs. 1.7 crore,and Rs. 1.5 lakh to her child.Justice Sunder Mohan passed the order while dismissing a revision petition moved by the womans partner challenging the family court order.According to the man, a film producer, his relationship with the woman, who was a model was not solmonised as a valid marriage and that he already has a legally married wife. Therefore, a woman who he was in a live-in relationship with was not entitled to maintenance.He added that he was lured by the woman and taking advantage of a weak moment, got conceived to gain unlawfully. He had stated that he was willing to pay maintenance to the child but not to the woman.Pointing out that the woman had alleged that the petitioner suppressed the existence of a legal marriage by stating that he was divorced, the court said, in such circumstances, the petitioner ought to have established that he never made such a representation and that the earlier marriage is subsisting. The petitioner has not let in evidence to counter the evidence let in by the woman on this aspect. Though the Supreme Court had held that a second wife, whose marriage is void on account of the existence of an earlier legal marriage, is not entitled to maintenance, the apex court had also held that the burden is on the husband to establish that the earlier marriage was in subsistence, the court said.It is the case of the petitioner that the woman has sufficient means to maintain herself and owns a flat worth Rs. 1.7 crore and has two luxury cars. These facts are not in dispute.But the evidence reveals that after the childs birth, the woman did not have a regular source of income. No evidence to the contrary has been let in by the petitioner. The findings of the family court, which is based on the evidence, cannot be faulted, the court said.

headline: Nine fishermen from Rameswaram held by SL Navy on poaching charge
content: In a fresh incident, nine fishermen from Thangachimadam here in Ramanathapuram district, who had ventured into the sea for fishing, were arrested by Sri Lankan Navy personnel on charges of poaching on Saturday. Fisheries department officials said that they had issued tokens to 339 mechanised trawlers. On Saturday, the Sri Lankan Navy personnel who were on surveillance claimed that a mechanised trawler, in which there were nine fishermen, had indulged in poaching. After interrogation at mid-sea, they detained the vessel and nine fishermen with the catch and proceeded to the Naval Port in the island nation. As the news reached the coastal habitation here, the fishermen families were shocked. The fishermen leader Jesu Raja said that the Union government should immediately prevail upon the Sri Lankan government and ensure that the fishermen were released forthwith. The names of the arrested fishermen were given as Mathias (22), Mobis (21), Abisten (27), Antony Bruts (42), Episton (29), Steevenson (22), John Jason (24), Antony Pradeep (26) and Subartan (24). The boat owners name was given as Edin.

headline: U.S.-Russia talks on Ukraine involve multi-billion dollar oil deal: report
content: report The Trump administrations talks with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine have expanded to include a multibillion-dollar oil deal that would benefit West Asian business executives with ties to U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the New York Times reported on Saturday (October 3, 2026). The deal, which is contingent on approval from the U.S. government and the Kremlin, involves a sprawling set of oil fields, refineries and gas stations around the world owned by Russian energy group Lukoil, according to the report. The White House, the U.S. Treasury Department and Lukoil didnt respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours. The group pursuing the deal includes US investor and billionaire Todd Boehly, two West Asian groups that have done business with Mr. Kushner or Mr. Witkoffs family, and an arm of the U.S. government, the newspaper said. Russian President Vladimir Putin raised the deal during a September 5 meeting with Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner at the Kremlin, the NYT said, citing people familiar with the meeting. Mr. Putin proposed completing the deal as a way to show Russians they could do business with the United States, one of the people said.

headline: Fifth child rape case registered against Veeramani
content: Yet another child rape case, fifth in the series, has been registered against Gem Granite owner R Veeramani, 84, based on a complaint filed by a Chennai resident. The special investigation team (SIT) probing the cases against Veeramani registered the latest case on Friday.Another woman, who hails from Tiruvannamalai, has also approached SIT alleging that Veeramani had sexually harassed her after promising her a job when she came to Chennai as a child. SIT was verifying the complaint.Veeramani, who was arrested on Aug 29 along with two of his associates -- Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan -- after a video of a child rape came to light, has since been detained under the Goondas Act. The case triggered public and political outcry after it came to light that police in Feb 2026 filed a closure report in the special court for Pocso Act cases saying further action dropped. The court, in Aug 2026, however, disallowed the closure and ordered further inquiry, leading to four arrests and five cases of child rape so far.The fifth case was registered after SIT received the complaint on its dedicated WhatsApp number, 9345319676. Police said complaints from affected women and their relatives continued to be received. Some of the women who had approached the authorities were now married and living with their families. Police said five more actionable pieces of information had been received through the number and that they were being verified.

headline: ABVP seeks Ashoka Chakra for Captain Smit Machchhar
content: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), after its All-India Office Bearers Meeting in Itanagar on Saturday, called on the Indian government to honour Captain Smit Machchhar with the Ashoka Chakra, for his exemplary courage in averting a catastrophic mid-air disaster earlier this week. Machchhar, an Indian commercial pilot, was commanding flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the aircrafts co-pilot allegedly attacked him in an attempt to hijack or crash the plane. During the violent struggle, the Boeing 737 MAX plummeted nearly 14,000 ft in less than 30 seconds. Despite his injuries, the 39-year-old fought back and managed to unlock the cockpit door, allowing alert passengers and crew to storm in and overpower the attacker. Two off-duty flydubai pilots, who were travelling as passengers, then helped level the aircraft, which was carrying 174 passengers, and diverted it for an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The incident had made headlines across the world and Machchhar was hailed globally as a hero for averting a disaster and saving hundreds of lives. The Ashoka Chakra is Indias top peacetime award for extreme bravery and self-sacrifice away from the battlefield. Civilians are eligible for the decoration and there is no requirement that the act of gallantry take place in India. Incidentally, there are historical precedents for Indian civilian aviation personnel receiving the Ashoka Chakra during emergencies abroad. In 1987, Pan Am flight attendant Neerja Bhanot was posthumously awarded the Ashoka Chakra for her actions during the hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 at Karachi the previous year. D N Jatar, captain of the Air India-chartered Kashmir Princess, was awarded the Ashoka Chakra after the aircraft was bombed in 1955 while flying from Hong Kong to Jakarta. Jatar, who died in the crash, was among the earliest civilian recipients of the award. The ABVP meeting, held on October 2 and 3, was its first All India Office Bearers Meeting in Itanagar. A substantial part of it dwelled on the recent student elections, wherein ABVP made significant gains, most notably, at Delhi and Panjab Universities, where it won the presidents post. In Uttarakhand, the organisation emerged victorious in 64 of the 92 colleges that went to polls there, securing the presidents post in 54 of them; and at Haryana University, 33 of the 38 seats. The student wing of the RSS, ABVP also claimed a clean sweep of all 14 seats at Sanskrit College in Kerala, and won three seats at Gauhati University. ABVP National General Secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said, Indias Gen-Z is rooted in values, has a nationalist outlook and believes in social harmony. ABVPs success at Panjab University, Delhi University, Kerala, Uttarakhand and various other campuses reflects the active participation of this young generation, Solanki said. The discussions also covered the state of hostels in Arunachal Pradesh and the Northeast, scholarships, student union elections, the organisations All India Student Hostel Survey 2026, and upcoming campaigns.

headline: Iran executes man linked to anti-government protests
content: government protests Iran said on Saturday (October 3, 2026) it had executed a man convicted of a raft of charges including firing a military-grade weapon at police officers during anti-government protests earlier this year. Siavash Jamshidi was accused of targeting security personnel during mass demonstrations that peaked in January, in which thousands of people were killed. Since that time, Iranian authorities have stepped up executions of convicts linked to the unrest. "Jamshidi was sentenced to death on charges of moharebeh through brandishing and firing a firearm, as well as conspiracy and collusion against national security," Iran's judiciary said, using the legal term moharebeh to mean "waging war against God". The judiciary's Mizan Online website said he was also found guilty of offences not related to the protests, including "fraud, making threats, theft, possession and carrying of an illegal military-grade weapon". Other charges included "complicity in kidnapping, brandishing a weapon to intimidate, and intentional infliction of bodily harm". Mizan said Jamshidi was "active" during the demonstrations, which were sparked in December last year by grievances over living costs in Iran, but peaked on January 8 and 9 with huge rallies. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths in the unrest, attributing the violence to "terrorist acts" orchestrated by the United States and Israel. Foreign-based NGOs however maintain that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. U.S. President Donald Trump threatened at the time to intervene militarily in Iran. Weeks later, in late February, the United States and Israel launched a joint attack on the Islamic , triggering the Middle East war. Since then, arrests and executions have multiplied in Iran, linked both to the war and the protests. In 2025, Iran executed at least 1,639 people, the largest number in any year since 1989, according to the NGOs Iran Human Rights and Together Against the Death Penalty. Amnesty International says Iran carries out more executions than any country except China.

headline: 'Proud he is part of our nation's story': Dubai Crown Prince praises Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar's courage
content: Dubai Crown Prince and UAE Deputy Prime Minister Hamdan bin Mohammed has praised Indian flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his courage, saying he had demonstrated the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. Hamdan shared a photograph from his visit to Smit Machchhar, who is receiving treatment in hospital, and said the UAE leadership extends its appreciation and praise to the pilot. In a post on X, Hamdan said Smit Machchhar had become part of the UAEs national story and praised his contribution in protecting lives. Quick answers to key questions 1What incident occurred aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 involving Captain Smit Machchhar? On September 30, during flydubai Flight FZ1073, Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured by his co-pilot in an alleged attack that resulted in a rapid descent of the aircraft before emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. 2Why is Captain Smit Machchhar being praised by leaders and the public? Captain Machchhar is being praised for his remarkable courage and quick thinking during the cockpit attack, which allowed crew members and passengers to intervene and avert a potential disaster. 3How did Captain Machchhar respond during the cockpit attack? Despite sustaining serious injuries, Machchhar managed to unlock the cockpit door, enabling crew and passengers to subdue the co-pilot and ultimately make an emergency landing. 4What recognition has Captain Smit Machchhar received for his actions during the incident? Captain Machchhar has received praise from various public figures, including Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bollywood stars like Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan, acknowledging his bravery. 5What health updates have been provided regarding Captain Smit Machchhar's recovery? As of the latest updates, Captain Machchhar is under medical care and is recovering well, with the Indian Embassy confirming they are in contact with his family and supporting his recovery. We are proud that he is part of our team part of the story of our nation Hamdan wrote, adding that Machchhar was also part of the UAEs human experience. He concluded the message by describing the UAE as a a nation of compassion a nation of peace and a nation of life. Smit Machchhar was seriously injured during an alleged attack inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Despite his injuries, the pilot was able to respond during the confrontation, while crew members and passengers intervened. The aircraft subsequently made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar remains under medical care as authorities investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Indian Embassy in the UAE said Machchhar remains under medical care and is recovering well. Indian braveheart Capt. Smit remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well, the embassy said on X, adding that it remains in contact with his family and local authorities. Machchhar was initially treated in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, before being transferred to Abu Dhabi for further treatment. The incident took place on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 carrying 170 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv.. The aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing in Tabuk after a violent confrontation inside the cockpit. According to UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft. The UAE has described the incident as an attempted terrorist act. Investigators are continuing to establish the circumstances and motive. Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door. Passengers and crew then intervened and subdued the co-pilot, while two off-duty pilots helped operate the aircraft before it landed safely in Tabuk. The plane reportedly lost more than 16,000 feet during the incident. The co-pilot has been identified by multiple reports as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national. He had previously been grounded in Oman amid concerns over alleged extremist views. Investigations involving UAE and Saudi authorities are continuing, with authorities examining the circumstances and possible motive behind the cockpit attack.

headline: 2.26 lakh teachers await special TET results as deadline looms
content: Nearly three months after taking the special Teachers Eligibility Test, and two days after Madras High Court lifted an interim stay on the declaration of results, lakhs of in-service teachers in Tamil Nadu are still awaiting their results, with time running out to meet a Supreme Court deadline.Around 2.26 lakh in-service teachers took the test conducted by the Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) in July this year in the wake of a Sept 2025 Supreme Court order mandating teachers with more than five years of service to clear the test by Aug 31, 2028. Teachers are required to clear the test (papers 1 and 2) to be considered eligible to teach Classes 1-8.While the school education department announced that it would conduct special TETs thrice a year to give several attempts to around 3.2 lakh teachers yet to clear the test, only one such test has happened so far. SC directive came in Sept last year; it took the govt until July to hold the first exam. Three months have passed without results. Teachers jobs are at stake. We submitted a representation to the secretary and other officials, but there is no clarity on when the results will be out. The govts top priority now must be to release the results and hold the next exam, said TN Elementary Grade Teachers Association state general secretary R Doss. An official from the TRB said that efforts were underway to get the results soon. Initially, the Madras high court had ordered an interim stay in July over petitions from teachers associations to reduce the qualifying marks and add marks based on service. Now that the stay has been lifted, the results are being processed. There will be another special TET in Dec this year. The notification for the exam will be released along with the results, the official said.Teachers, however, said high court stay should not have led to further delay. The high court only ordered a stay in July to publish the results, not to keep them ready. The govt should have been ready with the results at least by Aug and could have released it when the court lifted the stay, said S Natramizhan from Secondary Grade Teachers Association.

headline: Russian attacks kill six in Ukraine, damage Kyiv's Northern Bridge
content: Russian attacks in Ukraine killed at least six people and damaged Kyiv's Northern Bridge, suspending traffic and causing tailbacks for a third day in Moscow's latest effort to disrupt life in the Ukrainian capital. The strike came after two days of Russian assaults forced the full or partial closure of three of Kyiv's six road bridges over the Dnipro River. Previously, Russia has hit apartment blocks, supermarket warehouses, gas stations and data centres, among other targets. Russia invaded its neighbour more than 4 years ago, and there are no concrete signs that a peace settlement might be possible. Fighting along the roughly 1,250-kilometre (780-mile) front line snaking through northern, eastern and southern Ukraine has been virtually deadlocked in recent months. Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said the strike on the bridge damaged the road surface and trolleybus cables, forcing traffic to be suspended. There were no casualties reported. Russia's Defence Ministry on Saturday confirmed it was behind the latest attack, claiming the bridge is used to facilitate troop movements and the logistics of military cargo deliveries for Ukraine's armed forces. Videos circulating on social media appeared to show the moment of impact as vehicles crossed the bridge, including footage purportedly recorded by a driver's dashcam. Moldova expresses concern over the war spillover The aerial war has intensified, with Kyiv striking Russia's oil industry and businesses while Moscow has menaced Ukrainian cities with hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones. Moldovan President Maia Sandu said Saturday that the war is dangerously reaching her country, following a spate of airspace incursions. I condemn Russia's attack on Ukraine this morning. Its war is dangerously reaching Moldova, she said in a post on X, adding that five Russian air attack weapons, including Banderol missiles and drones, violated our airspace and exploded on our soil. Moscow is putting lives at risk across Europe and must be stopped, she added. Ukraine's air force said that Moscow overnight launched Banderol cruise missiles -- low-cost, jet-powered loitering munitions that Russia uses to overwhelm Ukrainian air defences -- at the Odesa region, which shares a long land border with Moldova. A loitering munition is designed to hover over an area, search for targets, and detonate while crashing into them. Meanwhile, people were injured after Ukrainian drones overnight struck the city of Kaluga in western Russia, damaging apartment buildings, according to regional Gov. Vladislav Shapsha. He did not immediately give any figures, but reported that 13 drones were shot down over the region during the night. Russian and Ukrainian attacks leave 9 dead, and scores wounded Russia attacked Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, and nearby areas with drones and guided bombs on Friday and overnight, killing five people and wounding over 40, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov. In nearby Izyum, Russian drone strikes wounded three people, according to the local military administration. It said a drone slammed into an industrial warehouse, while another damaged homes. In Ukraine's Odesa region, home to multiple Black Sea ports, a sailor was killed and three others wounded after Russian forces struck a civilian cargo ship on Saturday, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority reported. It said the ship was flying the Liberian flag. In eastern Ukraine, in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region, Ukrainian drones killed two people and wounded two others, according to Kremlin-installed regional head Leonid Pasechkin. Pasechkin said the drones attacked a truck and passenger car driving along a highway, adding all victims were civilians. In Russia, Ukrainian drone strikes killed a civilian and wounded two more in the Belgorod region, in villages just kilometres (miles) from the Ukrainian border, local authorities said Saturday (October 3).

headline: Israeli strike kills five, including four women, in Gaza, health officials say
content: An Israeli airstrike killed at least five Palestinians, including four women, in an apartment building in Gaza City early on Saturday (October 3, 2026), health and civil defense service officials said. Among the dead were a Christian mother and her daughter, medics said. There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military. The strike destroyed the apartment building and started a fire. We were asleep and suddenly heard continuous strikes, and heavy explosions, the children woke up startled and started running and screaming, said eyewitness Ahmed Al-Dahdouh. We ran out and found that our neighbours house was struck and there were dismembered martyrs, women, men and children, we started to pull them out, they were scattered under the rubble, he told Reuters. Last years U.S.-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. We are Muslims and these are our Christian brethren, who are not involved in anything, they are peaceful people, and everybody loves them, and now we pulled out their bodies, a mother and her daughter, said Dahdouh. Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal. Gaza health officials have said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since last Octobers ceasefire. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.

headline: Ukraine ready to consider India's ceasefire proposal: FM Sybiha
content: has described India's proposal for a possible ceasefire with Russia as the "broadest" among four offers received by Kyiv, with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha saying it is ready to consider a truce covering energy infrastructure and the Black Sea. We have four proposals. The broadest one is Indias proposal. We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in this combination, Mr. Sybiha told reporters in Kyiv on Friday (October 2, 2026), according to the European Pravda newspaper. The Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year, has killed thousands of civilians, displaced millions and caused widespread destruction of homes and critical infrastructure. The comments came a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has very good ideas for finding a mutually acceptable settlement to the Ukraine conflict. Mr. Sybiha said the proposals for a possible ceasefire had come from India, Turkiye, Egypt and the United States. He said Kyiv was ready to consider different formats for a truce, but any agreement should cover not only combat operations but also attacks on energy and port infrastructure and the situation in the Black Sea. Mr. Putin on Thursday (October 1) said Mr. Modi, despite their close ties, constantly raises the issue of ending the conflict and brings it up at every meeting between the two leaders. He has very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions, Mr. Putin said at the annual meeting of the Valdai International Discussion Club, according to state-run TASS news agency. Ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi last month, Mr. Putin and Mr. Modi held talks during which the Russian leader briefed the Prime Minister on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing peace initiatives. A few days earlier, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia would welcome peace efforts by India to resolve the Ukraine conflict and that Moscow's position was aligned with New Delhi's emphasis on dialogue and diplomacy. Ukraine's latest proposal comes amid intensified Russian aerial attacks on the country. Mr. Sybiha said Ukraine agrees to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations but also attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea. The Black Sea is currently one of the world's most dangerous commercial shipping zones due to the intensive escalation of missile and drone strikes by both Russia and Ukraine targeting ports, infrastructure and merchant vessels. Mr. Sybiha has repeated Ukraine's call for an unconditional ceasefire along the front line. Moscow has rejected such a ceasefire, saying a comprehensive peace agreement should be reached instead. The war, which began with Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, has continued despite repeated diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.

headline: North Korea says it test-fired an intermediate-range missile as tensions grow over mine blasts
content: range missile as tensions grow over mine blasts North Korea said Saturday (October 3, 2026) it test-fired an intermediate-range ballistic missile that it claimed has manoeuvrable flight capabilities designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan. The latest test comes amid heightened tensions between the two Koreas over border land mine blasts. Also Read | North Korea launches ballistic missiles toward sea after military drill it sees as threat Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said her brother supervised the test of the missile, which she described as strategic, implying it was designed to deliver nuclear weapons. She also said it could change its flight trajectory at low altitudes and was equipped with unspecified artificial intelligence capabilities that she claimed would make it highly difficult to intercept. Japan's military said the missile landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone. The South Korean military, which often accuses North Korea of exaggerating its military capabilities, did not immediately comment on Kim's claims. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said early Saturday (October 3) it detected the North Korean missile being launched from the eastern coastal Wonsan area and flying more than 700 kilometres (435 miles). Japan's Defence Ministry later said it detected the missile flying about 680 kilometres (422 miles). Ms. Kim argued in her statement that the differing flight details between the neighbouring U.S. allies proved they couldn't properly track the missile in flight. Whenever we applied the wavelike trajectory mode to missiles, the enemy failed to track the targets from their first skip points, she said. There is no way to avoid this attack. The launch came a day after she ridiculed South Korean demands for the North to apologise over the Sept. 21 land mine blasts, which occurred about 10 meters (11 yards) south of the countries' military demarcation line, injuring three South Korean soldiers. South Korea said a joint inspection of the site with the U.S.-led United Nations Command found that the blasts were caused by mines planted by North Korea. The command later determined that the North Korea violated the armistice agreement that ended fighting in the 1950-53 Korean War. The South has also called on the North to halt its recent border fortification efforts, including the installation of mines and anti-tank barriers, which have accelerated after Kim Jong Un in 2024 abandoned his government's long-standing goal of reconciliation with the South and declared Seoul a permanent adversary. Kim Yo Jong, possibly the second-most powerful figure in Pyongyang, dismissed Seoul's demands over the mine blasts as utterly pathetic on Friday, saying the North intends to cut ties with the South forever. In a statement on Sept. 30, she denied North Korean responsibility for the blasts and threatened to retaliate if South Korea fires on North Korean troops fortifying the border.

headline: New GRAP Rules in Delhi; restrictions in NCR October 2026: Is your car allowed? Check eligibility here from govt PDF
content: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has modified the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) framework for Delhi-NCR, with changes affecting vehicles, construction activity and the implementation of pollution-control measures. The revised government framework, announced on September 29, 2026, divides GRAP into four stages based on Delhi's air quality. The measures under successive stages are cumulative. This means that a restriction under Stage I will continue under Stage II and so on. Restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below-standard light motor vehicles (LMVs) under GRAP Stage III have been extended to Sonipat apart from Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar. Now vehicles from three Haryana and two Uttar Pradesh districts will be under restrictions. So, here's what the new GRAP framework means for your vehicle if you are from these places. While restrictions under the old rules have been retained, certain new vehicle-related restrictions have been made added. Under the new framework, restrictions on certain inter-city and inter-state buses have been brought under GRAP Stage I, instead of Stage II. Buses from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and adjoining states, including Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir, will not be permitted to ply in Delhi-NCR unless they are EV, CNG or BS-VI diesel buses, according to the new changes. Another major change is the extension of CAQM's directions on construction and demolition activities to a wider set of areas, including urban, controlled and development areas, industrial areas and zones, and highway corridor zones in NCR states. The CAQM has also removed the earlier exemption for BS-IV and below goods vehicles carrying essential commodities under GRAP Stages III and IV. The revised government document classifies GRAP into four stages: According to the framework announced by CAQM, measures under various stages of GRAP can be taken in advance if forecasts indicate that an AQI threshold is likely to be reached. If pollution unexpectedly crosses a threshold because of extreme meteorological or other episodic conditions, the corresponding measures can be imposed immediately. Whether a private car can ply in the region depends on the GRAP stage, fuel type, BS emission standard, vehicle category and location. There is no blanket ban on all private cars throughout Delhi-NCR under the framework. At Stage I, authorities will be ordered to strictly enforce PUC norms for the vehicles. Vehicles flouting the norms or those visibly polluting can be impounded and/or face penalty. During the Stage I framework restrictions on the entry of certain inter-city and inter-state buses into Delhi-NCR, although EV, CNG and BS-VI diesel buses are permitted. The revised framework does not prescribe a blanket ban on private cars under Stage II, instead, it calls for a higher parking fees to discourage private transport and encourages the use of public transport. At this stage, certain vehicles face restrictions. Under Stage III, NCR states and the Delhi government will have to impose strict restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel LMVs (four-wheelers) and lower-standard vehicles. The restriction covers Gurugram, Faridabad and Sonipat districts of Haryana, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar from Uttar Pradesh apart from Delhi. Noida, which falls within Gautam Buddha Nagar district, will also face restrictions in this stage. Stage IV further tightens the restrictions on goods vehicles but does not recommend for the introduction of blanket ban on all private cars. In this stage no heavy goods vehicle (HGV) other than LNG, CNG, electric and BS-VI diesel trucks can enter the national capital. Delhi-registered diesel BS-IV and below HGVs are also prohibited from plying in Delhi. After Stage III of GRAP comes into effect, BS-III petrol LMVs and BS-IV diesel LMVs face restrictions in Delhi and the specified high-vehicle-density NCR districts. Outside-Delhi registered diesel BS-IV and below light goods vehicles are also not permitted to enter Delhi under the Stage III provisions. Yes. The Stage III provision specifically allows persons with disabilities to ply BS-III petrol/BS-IV diesel LMVs where the vehicles have been specifically adapted for their personal use. For heavy goods vehicles under Stage IV, LNG, CNG, electric and BS-VI diesel trucks are exempted from the general restriction on entry into Delhi. Earlier exemption for BS-IV and below goods vehicles carrying essential commodities under Stages III and IV has also been removed. Not automatically, but the revised framework says that under Stage IV, state governments may consider additional emergency measures, including allowing vehicles to run on an odd-even basis according to registration numbers. So, the invocation of Stage IV itself does not mean an odd-even scheme automatically comes

headline: RTI panel rejects plea saying there is no public interest, and may affect routine work
content: Tamil Nadu Information Commission has rejected an RTI appeal seeking information under 90 heads, holding that the request had no public interest element and that providing such voluminous information could affect the day-to-day functioning of a government office.State information commissioner V P R Ilamparithi said the information sought related to a third party and that the appellant had sought excessive details concerning an official from the School Education Department. The Commission said such a request, in the circumstances, attracted Section 7(9) of the Right to Information Act, as it could affect the resources of the public authority required for its routine functioning.The case concerned an RTI application filed by Mohan S Thamizhkumaran seeking information under 90 heads about V Rameshkumar, who was serving as a block educational officer in Palani union of Dindigul district. The information included details of the union to which Rameshkumar was first appointed as a block educational officer and disciplinary action, if any, taken against him.The application was initially transferred between various authorities under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act. The public information officer (PIO) subsequently furnished information through a letter dated Jan 3, 2024. The appellant, dissatisfied with the response, filed a first appeal and later approached the Commission with a second appeal under Section 19(3).During the hearing last week, the PIO submitted that the information sought had already been furnished through registered post. The officer also told the Commission that the appellant had sought an excessive amount of information, which could affect routine office work, and that there was no public interest involved in the request.The officer further submitted that the information was being sought for reasons of personal animosity or other unnecessary purposes.After examining the application and response, the Commission found that the appellant had sought an excessive amount of information, all of which related to a third party. It also recorded that sufficient information had already been furnished by the PIO.The Commission accordingly disposed of the second appeal and advised the appellant to seek only information required by him, specify his requests clearly and pursue them with a public-interest objective without causing hindrance to the day-to-day functioning of the public authority and the Commission.
