headline: Scoot flight to Singapore aborted as pilot detects glitch while taxiing
content: A Scoot Airlines flight from Chennai to Singapore was cancelled after its pilot detected an engine problem while the aircraft was taxiing for take-off at Chennai airport in the early hours of Saturday.The flight, carrying 310 passengers and 12 crew members, was scheduled to depart from Chennai around midnight. After all passengers boarded and the aircraft began moving towards the runway, the pilot detected an engine problem and stopped the aircraft.The pilot informed the Chennai airport control room, following which the aircraft was towed back to the parking area. Engineers subsequently examined the aircraft and attempted to rectify the problem.The passengers were deboarded and accommodated in the airports rest areas while efforts were made to repair the aircraft. However, the problem could not be rectified by 5am, following which the airline cancelled the flight.Buses then took the 310 passengers to various hotels in Chennai. The airline told passengers the aircraft would be repaired and that the flight was expected to depart for Singapore on Saturday night.The timely detection of the technical problem by the pilot prevented the aircraft from taking off with the snag, officials said.

headline: Government approves 5 Centres of Excellence to support Classical languages
content: The Ministry of Education Saturday approved the establishment of five Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for studies in five Classical languages, namely Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit. The establishment of these five Centres marks a significant step towards strengthening the institutional ecosystem for the study, research and preservation of Indias Classical Languages, the Ministry said in a statement The Centres will focus on four broad areas providing dedicated institutional platforms for advanced research, scholarly work and academic engagement; preservation and digitisation; wider dissemination of Classical Language heritage; and strengthening regional academic ecosystems. The Centre of Excellence for classical Assamese will be established at Tezpur University, Assam; for classical Bengali at Visva-Bharati University, West Bengal; for classical Marathi at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, Pune, Maharashtra; for classical Pali at Central University of Odisha, Odisha; and for classical Prakrit at Central University of Gujarat, Gujarat. The initiative reinforces the governments efforts to preserve and promote Indias rich linguistic and literary heritage while strengthening institutions of higher education as centres of research and scholarship, the Ministrys statement further read.

headline: George Soros family's $102 million Democratic funding push ahead of 2026 US midterms - Details here
content: linked organisations have contributed $102 million to Democracy PAC, a political action committee founded by billionaire investor George Soros in 2019, Fortune reported citing Federal Election Commission records. About half of the contribution came from Geosor Corp, a private investment company owned by Soros, while the remainder came from the Fund for Policy Reform, a nonprofit within Soros Open Society Foundations, according to the news outlet. The foundations board is chaired by Soros son, Alex Soros. Geosor Corp, which is owned by billionaire George Soros, contributed $62 million to Democracy PAC, an allied super PAC that serves as a major channel for the family's political contributions, Business Insider reported. Another $50 million came from the Fund for Democracy, a Soros-aligned organisation. Separately, George Soros has directly donated under $1 million so far to the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) and the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC), the Democratic Party's two principal national fundraising organisations for congressional races, according to the news outlet. Alex Soros, who assumed leadership of the Soros family's Open Society Foundation in 2023, has directly contributed about $125,000 so far, the report said. The largest recipient of his direct contributions has been a joint fundraising committee led by Senator Raphael Warnock, a Georgia Democrat, according to Business Insider. Another Jonathan Soros has directly contributed more than $325,000 during the current election cycle. The largest recipients of his contributions include the Alaska and Iowa Democratic state parties, the report said. The development comes as Democrats seek to strengthen their campaign finances ahead of the November 2026 congressional elections. The $102 million contribution also puts the Soros family on pace to exceed George Soros $128 million in Democratic political giving during the 2022 midterm cycle. The 2026 congressional elections are the first midterm cycle since George Soros transferred control of his political operation to his son Alex Soros in 2023. Democracy PAC had earlier raised more than $81 million in 2020 and nearly $72 million in 2024, according to reports. George Soros, now 96, has financially supported Democratic candidates and political organisations for more than two decades. The fundraising comes as recent polling shows Democrats holding an advantage on the generic congressional ballot. According to Fortune, an Emerson College national poll conducted on September 21-22 among 1,000 likely voters showed Democrats leading Republicans 53% to 42%. Separately, a Cook Political Report survey of 1,052 likely voters across 37 competitive House districts found Democrats at 49%, compared with 47% for Republicans. The survey, conducted from September 8-11, covered districts that had backed Donald Trump by an average of five percentage points in the 2024 election.

headline: IAF needs 36-40 jets annually; Pakistan's fifth-gen jet plan worrying: Air Chief
content: He also highlighted the ongoing efforts of the IAF to develop a robust beyond-visual-range (BVR) combat capability through the planned induction of the indigenous ASTRA and its variants of BVR air-to-air missiles, along with additional batches of foreign missiles offering longer ranges. The IAF Chief made the remarks while addressing the media ahead of the 94th Air Force Day, which will be observed on October 8. Responding to a question about the IAFs fighter squadron strength, Air Chief Marshal Singh said the force could begin inducting 30 to 35 fighter jets annually if things go as planned. Referring to Hindustan Aeronautics Limiteds target of delivering up to 24 LCA Mk1A aircraft to the IAF annually, he said even if HAL produces 20 aircraft a year and the Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) contract is finalised by the end of this year, the total annual induction would add up to approximately 32 aircraft. The MRFA programme, under which the IAF would receive around 12 aircraft annually, involves the proposed acquisition of 114 Rafale jets. He said if the proposed contract to acquire 12 additional Su-30 aircraft is included, with six jets delivered each year, the annual induction could rise to between 30 and 35-40 aircraft, provided all the plans move forward as expected. So, we are hoping that these things will happen and that we will be able to achieve the pace of growth we have set for ourselves, he said. The IAF Chief said it is prudent to have a mix of three to four types of fighter jets in the forces inventory, so that they can perform different roles effectively. He said in the near future, the IAF will have a healthy mix of LCA Tejas Mk 1A, LCA Mk 2, the French Rafales and the indigenous fifth-generation fighter jet Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). Talking about reports of Pakistan moving to acquire Chinas fifth-generation J-35 stealth fighter jet, Air Chief Marshal Singh said it is a cause for worry. Is it a no-go situation? I wouldnt agree with that. We possess the necessary capabilities it is not just about a single platform, but about how it is integrated into the entire system. Pakistan has possessed other platforms in the past, yet they havent been able to achieve anything significant with them during Operation Sindoor. Similarly, if we effectively integrate the platforms we are purchasing and inducting, we should be able to counter this threat at least for the time being, until they fully integrate these new aircraft into their own systems. He also said there is a need to push the AMCA programme and take alternative decisions in case there is a delay in that. He also clarified that Russia has offered the Su-57, but no decision has been taken yet, even as he emphasised the need to consider the need for a fifth-generation aircraft if our adversaries are getting a fifth-generation aircraft. The Astra BVRAAM is already in production, while the Mk2 variant is midway through its R&D and the Mk 3 is in the initial stages of R&D, progressing through research and development. He said the IAF is also making efforts to procure additional batches of missiles with longer ranges from foreign sources. India has been reportedly looking at procuring Russian R-37M ultra-long-range air-to-air missiles and additional batches of French Meteor Missiles. Augmenting the BVR capability of the IAF has been in focus since Operation Sindoor was conducted in May last year. ACM Singh said the Astra, its variants and the additional foreign missiles will fulfil the immediate requirements of the IAF, adding that the development of the Astra Mk2 and Mk3 variants is progressing in the right direction, particularly in terms of ranges. The first in the family, ASTRA Mk 1, has a range of 80 to 110 km. A more advanced version of the ASTRA Mk 1 the ASTRA Mk 2 has an enhanced range of 200 km, up from the earlier decided range of around 160 km. Earlier this year, the DRDO had conducted a flight test of its Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology for the ASTRA Mk 3, which could have a range of over 350 km. He also said that while the IAF is growing the number of drones and loitering munitions, there is no need for a separate drone force. The IAF Chief said that other elements of comprehensive national power of any nation rest on a strong military. Military power becomes the ultimate, and without adequate military power, any state remains vulnerable to coercion, and if we have to do things our way, if we have to follow the path that we want to follow, we have to have a strong military, he said. And when we talk about a strong military, in the recent conflicts we have seen that it is the air power which has come to the fore, which has come out as the cutting edge of military power, and it is one instrument on which any nation relies to meet its objectives, he said. He highlighted that whether it is advanced fighter aircraft, long-range precision weapons, integrated air command and control, or unmanned aerial systems it is all very clear that they all reflect that military power is concentrated around the aerospace domain. Separately, the IAF Chief praised Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhars bravery during the incident involving an Israel-bound flight. He showed great physical and mental resolve. It is a lesson for us, he said.

headline: CJP's Shivaji Park protest triggers FIR: Mumbai Police name organisers, 400-500 others
content: Mumbai Police have registered an FIR against the organisers of the Cockroach Janta Partys (CJP) protest at Shivaji Park, along with 400-500 unidentified people who attended the demonstration on October 2. The case was registered at Shivaji Park police station on Saturday under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Maharashtra Police Act. The charges include unlawful assembly and disobedience of a lawful order issued by a public servant, among other offences, a police official said. The FIR followed a complaint by a resident of the Shivaji Park area. Mumbai Police have not made any arrests in connection with the case so far, and further investigation is underway. The CJP, founded by Abhijeet Dipke, had held the October 2 demonstration at Shivaji Park demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The party has alleged irregularities in the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police had denied permission for the protest before it was held. Authorities had cited restrictions governing the use of Shivaji Park, as well as concerns over noise and traffic disruption in the residential area. Earlier on Friday, Siddhi Deolekar, a resident and advocate, said she lodged a complaint at Shivaji Park Police Station against Cockroach Janata Party activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Ratna Singh for allegedly proceeding with the Shivaji Park protest despite denial of permission. In a post on X, Deolekar said the complaint was filed against CJP leaders Dipke, Ranka, Das and Ratna Singh, the legal affairs head of the Cockroach Janata Party, and others for allegedly proceeding with the protest and gathering a large crowd despite an express denial of permission. "As a responsible Shivaji Park citizen, I have lodged a complaint against @abhijeet_dipke, @AshutoshRanka, @Saurav Dassss and @whattalawyer at Shivaji Park Police Station for allegedly attempting to proceed with the Shivaji Park Protest and gathering a huge crowd despite express denial of permission and the restrictions flowing from the Hon'ble Bombay High Court's judgment in PIL 116/2009 dated 04.01.2013 and the subsequent Maharashtra Government order," she said. She also referred to restrictions arising from the Bombay High Court's judgment in PIL 116/2009 dated January 4, 2013, and a subsequent Maharashtra government order. "This is not 'peaceful protest'. This is an attempt to defy the law under the cover of a political protest," Deolekar said. Delhi Police detained several members of the All India Students' Association (AISA) on Saturday during a protest near Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, as demonstrations over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls continued in the capital. The protesters, including AISA president Neha Bora and senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal, tried to move past police barricades set up near Jantar Mantar. Bora later praised those who took part in the demonstration in a post on X, sharing photographs with Sibal, Bhushan and other protesters. Our Heroes! I hope that when we are your age, we are as strong and steadfast as you all! she wrote. AISA also posted footage from the protest on social media, saying the group would return to the streets. The Saturday action came amid continued protests over the SIR exercise, which has triggered demonstrations in Delhi and other parts of the country. headline: Flames, smoke at Aramco facility south of Saudi capital
content: Flames and smoke were seen rising from a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco south of the kingdoms capital Riyadh on Saturday (October 3, 2026), an AFP journalist said. The circumstances remained unclear but in recent weeks Aramco, majority-owned by the Saudi state, has come under attack from the Houthi group targeting the kingdom as part of the war in Yemen where Riyadh is backing the internationally recognised government. Aramco remains the flagship company of the Saudi economy and one of the largest firms in the world by market capitalisation. Last month, the Houthis said that they launched strikes targeting sensitive sites in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in the kingdoms port city of Yanbu. In August they also targeted an airport and a facility belonging to Aramco in Saudi Arabias southern Najran region. In July the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and raising questions about Riyadhs continued ability to deliver vast quantities of crude to international markets. Yemen, one of the worlds poorest nations, has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war. On Saturday (October 3, 2026) loud explosions were heard in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa, AFP correspondents in the city said, while the Houthis reported airstrikes in the area by Saudi-backed government forces.

headline: Dubai Crown Prince praises Indian pilot Machchhar
content: Captain Machchhar was stabbed and seriously injured in the cockpit of flydubai flight FZ1073 on Wednesday (September 30) while it was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Crown Prince Hamdan visited Mr. Machchhar at the hospital, where he is undergoing treatment and posted photographs from the meeting on X. Mr. Hamdan, who is also the UAE's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, said the flydubai pilot had embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise, he said. We are proud that he is part of our team part of the story of our nation and part of what the UAE stands for a nation of compassion a nation of peace and a nation of life, the crown prince added. The Indian Embassy in the UAE earlier said Mr. Machchhar was recovering well and remained under medical care. Indian braveheart Capt. Smit remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well. We are in touch with his family & local authorities, extending support for a speedy recovery, the embassy said in a post on X on Saturday (October 3). The embassy also thanked the UAE government for providing medical care to Mr. Machchhar and said it joined well-wishers in praying for his recovery. The UAE, which is leading the investigation, said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act on Wednesday (September 30). UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said the co-pilot used a crash axe to attack Machchhar and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the state-run WAM news agency reported. Mr. Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door despite his injuries, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot, according to earlier reports. The co-pilot who attacked Mr. Machchhar has been identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, the Wall Street Journal reported, quoting people familiar with the matter. The flight, carrying 174 passengers, transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet from an altitude of 34,000 feet before making an emergency landing at Prince Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Airport in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk. After receiving initial treatment in Tabuk, Mr. Machchhar was shifted to Abu Dhabi for continued medical care.

headline: Three workers die of suffocation in Ariyalur, police detain house owner
content: The police have detained the owner of an under construction house where three workers died of suffocation while removing wooden planks / supporting framework from a newly constructed septic tank at Sendurai in Ariyalur district on Friday. Ariyalur District Collector N. Mirunalini has said that steps would be taken to provide compensation to the bereaved families. Police identified the victims as K. Bhaskar, 42, of Srinivasapuram in Tiruvarur district; K. Dhinakaran, 60, of Alivalam village in Tiruvarur district and K. Ramachandran, 45, of Nakkampadi village in Ariyalur district. Police sources said the three were engaged by M. Subramanian for the construction of his house at Vallalar Nagar in Sendurai. Bhaskar and Dhinakaran had been working as masons at the house while Ramachandran was engaged for carpentry work. An eight-foot deep septic tank had been constructed behind the building. On Friday morning, the three victims entered the septic tank and fell unconscious one after the other, said police sources. The sources said Subramanian informed the police and firefighters to rescue the three labourers. Firefighters rescued the three from the septic tank and took them to the Government Hospital, Sendurai. The duty doctor declared that all the three persons had died after examining them. The bodies were later sent for autopsy to the Government Hospital at Ariyalur. The Sendurai police have registered a case under Sections 290 of BNS and detained Subramanian. Meanwhile, the Tamil Nadu AITUC has demanded the State government to provide 30 lakh as compensation to each of the three bereaved families. In a statement, AITUC Tamil Nadu general secretary M. Radhakrishnan said action should be taken against those responsible for negligence leading to the three deaths.

headline: 'A hero of our times': Mankind Pharma to give ₹1 crore to FlyDubai Capt Smit Machchhar
content: Mankind Pharma has announced 1 crore contribution to Captain Smit Machchhar and his family, describing the gesture as an expression of gratitude for his courage and leadership during what the company called an "unimaginable crisis". The pharmaceutical company announced it through a statement on LinkedIn. Along with the post, it also shared a letter from its Vice Chairman and Managing Director Rajeev Juneja, in which he praised Machchhar for putting his crew and passengers before himself. "Some acts of courage stay with an entire nation," Mankind Pharma said. "In a moment of unimaginable crisis, showed composure and responsibility, and put his crew and every passenger before himself." Quick answers to key questions 1Why did Mankind Pharma contribute 1 crore to Captain Smit Machchhar? Mankind Pharma contributed 1 crore as a gesture of gratitude for Machchhar's courage and leadership during a crisis when he prioritized the safety of his crew and passengers. 2How did Captain Smit Machchhar manage to save the flight during the attack? Captain Machchhar was injured but successfully opened the cockpit door, allowing crew members and passengers to overpower the co-pilot who attacked him, thus preventing a potential disaster. 3What did Mankind Pharma's Vice Chairman say about Machchhar's actions? Rajeev Juneja praised Machchhar as 'a hero of our times,' highlighting his composure and responsibility in a moment of extreme crisis, which served as an inspiration to many. 4What recognition did Captain Smit Machchhar receive from the Indian Prime Minister? Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Captain Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the FlyDubai incident, calling it a moment of national pride. 5What was the context of the FlyDubai incident involving Captain Machchhar? On a FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Captain Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot in an apparent hijack attempt, which he thwarted through a courageous response. The company said the contribution was its "humble expression of gratitude" and added, "Capt. Smit, you have made India proud. We salute you." Juneja, while reposting Mankind Pharma's statement, wrote that the company believed that pride and appreciation should translate into meaningful action. "When we witness an act of extraordinary courage and our hearts are filled with pride, we have a choice: let that emotion pass with time, or turn it into meaningful action," Juneja said. He said the company decided to support Machchhar after seeing news about his actions, adding that Mankind wanted to go beyond praising his courage and "stand behind our words with meaningful action". "Because emotions fade, but actions leave a lasting impact," Juneja said. According to Juneja, the 1 crore contribution is Mankind Pharma's way of conveying that it recognises Machchhar's courage and stands with him and his family. In the letter addressed to Machchhar, Juneja described him as "a hero of our times" and said his courage, composure and sense of responsibility had touched people in India and around the world. Juneja said Machchhar demonstrated leadership at a time when fear and pressure were high and the lives of passengers and crew depended on his decisions. "A leader is not tested when everything is going well. The real test comes in a moment of extreme crisis, when fear is natural, pressure is immense, and the lives of so many people depend on your decisions," he wrote. He said Machchhar had thought about his crew and passengers and taken responsibility for the lives entrusted to him. "No amount of money can ever equal the value of the lives you protected or the inspiration you have given to millions," Juneja wrote, describing the 1 crore contribution as a "small expression" of the company's respect, gratitude and admiration. He concluded the letter by thanking Machchhar for putting others before himself and for "reminding all of us that, even in the most difficult moments, humanity must always come first". Machchhar was reportedly stabbed with a knife by his co-pilot on the FlyDubai flight from UAE to Israel on Wednesday in an apparent act of hijack. Despite being seriously injured, Machchhar was able to open the cockpit door by activating the door release. This allowed the crew members and passengers to enter the cockpit and overpower the attacker. The flight carrying 174 passengers was later diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also had a telephonic conversation with Machchhar on Friday. PM Modi praised his courage and presence of mind during the incident.

headline: Guwahati railway network set for major upgrade: New lines, 2nd Saraighat Bridge, stations and more
content: New lines, 2nd Saraighat Bridge, stations and more According to Kapinjal Kishore Sharma, Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO) of NFR, several projects are now being developed to meet the growing demand and improve connectivity across Guwahati and the Northeast. - New third railway line between Kamakhya and Guwahati The Kamakhya-Guwahati third line project is being developed over 5.74 km at a sanctioned cost of Rs. 467 crore. This new railway line will increase capacity on the busy section, reduce congestion and help trains operate more smoothly. The project is targeted for completion by 2028. - Second Saraighat Bridge to improve connectivity The railway official said that another major project is the Agthori-Kamakhya double line project, which includes the second Saraighat Rail-cum-Road Bridge. The project has been sanctioned at a cost of Rs. 1,474 crore and covers 7.20 km. The new Saraighat Bridge will have a double-line railway track and a three-lane road. The 1.3-km-long bridge will provide additional rail and road capacity across the Brahmaputra. The project is expected to ease pressure on the existing Saraighat Bridge and improve connectivity between Guwahati, North Guwahati and other parts of the Northeast. It will also support more train services. - Mega Coaching Complex coming up at New Guwahati To improve train maintenance and terminal capacity, NFR is developing a Mega Coaching Complex at New Guwahati at a cost of Rs. 227 crore. The complex will have three pit lines, four stabling lines and two automatic coach-washing plants. It will allow more trains to be handled and maintained, helping improve the efficiency and safety of railway operations. - Redevelopment of Guwahati and Kamakhya stations The passenger facilities are also being improved through the redevelopment of Guwahati and Kamakhya railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme (ABSS). Guwahati railway station is being developed as a modern facility with an IT park and a focus on green-building features. The redevelopment includes provisions for solar power generation, waste management and water management. The CPRO added that a second entry to Guwahati railway station is also under construction. The additional entry will give passengers another way to access the station and is expected to help reduce traffic congestion around the station. The newly inaugurated Panbazar Road Over Bridge is also supporting smoother traffic movement and station redevelopment work. The redevelopment of Kamakhya railway station is also progressing with upgraded passenger facilities and improved amenities. - Kamakhya-Azara elevated railway corridor The Kamakhya-Azara Elevated Corridor is another important project in the region. An elevated viaduct is being constructed along the stretch, including the section passing through Deepor Beel, to facilitate safe and uninterrupted movement of wildlife, including elephants, while ensuring efficient railway connectivity. The remaining 13.25-km-long Azara-Kamakhya double-line stretch is targeted for completion by July 2028, the CPRO said. - Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal (GCT) at Baihata The zonal railway is also expanding freight and logistics infrastructure in the region. The Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal (GCT) at Baihata, near Guwahati, has been completed. The terminal will improve freight handling and logistics capacity. The rail connectivity between Jogighopa station yard and the Multi Modal Logistics Park (MMLP) GCT siding has also been completed. This connectivity will further strengthen Jogighopas potential as a major logistics hub and facilitate seamless multimodal movement of goods across the Northeast, Sharma added. What these projects mean for passengers Together, these projects are aimed at increasing railway capacity and improving connectivity in and around Guwahati. The new railway lines and second Saraighat Bridge will help handle more train traffic, while the Mega Coaching Complex will strengthen train maintenance facilities. For passengers, station redevelopment, a second station entry and improved amenities are expected to make access and travel more convenient. At the same time, the elevated rail infrastructure will support railway connectivity while addressing wildlife movement concerns.

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani POCSO case in Tamil Nadu: a compilation
content: Distressing reports of heinous crimes against minor girls have surfaced in Tamil Nadu in September 2026 with a powerful business tycoon 84-year-old Gem Granites founder R. Veeramani at the centre of the allegations. Veeramani, who, along with two others, was arrested late August for the sexual assault of a minor girl visuals of which were in the possession of the Chennai police as early as October 2025 following a complaint by a child rights activist is now facing multiple allegations of child sexual abuse, with several survivors (all of whom were aged 12-15 at the time of the incidents) having come forward and recorded their statements. The Chennai police, meanwhile, are under fire for failing to take timely action against Veeramani and his co-accused Shanthi, 55, and Mahendra Simhan, 60 whose bunglow was allegedly used by Veeramani to commit the crime and filing a report before a court, recommending that further action be dropped. The report, however, was rejected by the court, resulting in the current investigation. The TVK-led government has consequently removed two senior IPS officers from their posts A. Arun, ADGP, Tamil Nadu Police Academy, and N. Kannan, Commissioner of Police, Coimbatore who were at the helm of the Chennai Police Commissionerate when the complaint first surfaced. A special investigation team (SIT), comprising women officials, has also been set up to probe the crime and related matters. has been closely following the case, dubbed as Tamil Nadus Epstein Files. headline: Cauvery bridge on Tiruchi-Chennai Bypass to be reopened for traffic by October 15
content: Chennai Bypass to be reopened for traffic by October 15 The repair and maintenance work under way on the Cauvery bridge on the Chennai-TiruchiMadurai National Highway would be completed by October 15, according to Tiruchi Member of Parliament Durai Vaiko and sources in the National Highways Authority of India. The reopening of the bridge for traffic would bring a huge relief to commuters as the Tiruchi-Chennai Trunk Road in Srirangam has been facing severe traffic congestion ever since the bridge was closed for repair work. Built in 1963, the bridge is undergoing extensive repairs at an estimated cost of 10 crore. It was closed on June 25 to facilitate repairs by the NHAIs concessionaire maintaining the section and traffic has been diverted via the other carriageway between Sanjeevi Nagar Junction and Kondayampettai. The closure of the bridge had resulted in a large number of drivers using the Tiruchi-Chennai Trunk Road which runs across Srirangam to and from the NH. Residents of Srirangam have been complaining of harrowing experiences during their daily commute in recent months because of severe traffic congestion on the Tiruchi-Chennai Trunk Road between No. 1 Tollgate and the Anna Statue Junction. Traffic hold-ups had become common right from the Chinthamani traffic signal and on the old Cauvery bridge in the city, the overbridge at Thiruvanaikovil and the Kollidam bridge right through the day. Bumper-to-bumper traffic has become the order of the day on most days. Chaos prevailed at the automatic traffic signal at Mambazhasalai, complain residents. The NHAI authorities had earlier informed me that the work would be completed by October 10. But they needed more time due to some additional work. Given the heavy traffic congestion in the alternative routes and the approaching Deepavali festival season, I had requested the NHAI officials to complete the work without any delay. The NHAI officials have assured me the work would be completed fully by October 15, Mr. Durai Vaiko said. The repair work includes replacing 120 bridge bearings, maintaining 14 support pillars, repairing 16 strip-seal expansion joints, and carrying out structural strengthening measures. The bridge was last repaired in 2010. Sources in the NHAI told that all the 120 bearings had been replaced and repairs on 15 of the 16 expansion joints had been completed. At present, work was under way on the final expansion joint and repairs to the pedestrian pathway. All the work would be completed by October 15, they added.

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani booked in second POCSO Act case
content: The Chennai police have registered a fresh case against Gem Granites R. Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, police sources said on Monday (September 28, 2026). The second case was registered based on a complaint lodged by a woman alleging that her daughter, a minor, was sexually abused by the businessman. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has taken up probe in the case. The police booked Veeramani (85) under the POCSO Act and are likely to formally arrest the granite baron, who is already lodged in the Puzhal prison in connection with a different POCSO Act case. The police are investigating the statements given by three other women who claimed they were subjected to sexual abuse by the businessman in the past, sources added. Investigators were also probing a complaint lodged by a woman who alleged her daughter who was abused by Veeramani had ended her life. The incident occurred many years ago. The complaint said though she lodged a complaint with the local police then no action was taken, the sources said. Appeal to public The Chennai Police said those willing to lodge complaints relating to the above cases or share any information could call or send details via WhatsApp at 9345319676. The identity of the sender would be kept confidential. Summon CM, Minister for questioning: T.R. Baalu In a related development, DMK treasurer T.R. Baalu on Monday submitted a petition to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case, urging it to summon Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and his Cabinet colleagues Aadhav Arjuna and C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar and seek the evidence supporting their allegations against the DMK in the case. In his petition, Mr. Baalu recalled Mr. Arjunas allegation that the DMK had protected Mr. Veeramani and closed the case against him. Mr. Nirmal Kumar alleged that the DMK received 500 crore from the industrialist. The allegations are false and have been made to defame DMK leaders. If the two Ministers possess evidence in this case, why have they not handed it over to the officials probing the case, he asked. Mr. Baalu said details from the case diary had been made available unofficially and were being circulated outside. The allegations made by the Chief Minister and his Cabinet colleagues are directly connected with the case. The SIT should obtain the details and evidence from them, he added. headline: Tamil Nadu Ministers Aadhav Arjuna, Nirmal Kumar urge Madras High Court to dismiss DMK's defamation suit
content: a counter affidavit filed through senior counsel Vijay Narayan, the Law Minister denied all allegations of having made false and defamatory statements against DMK in connection with the child sexual abuse case. He also contended that the suit in its present form was not maintainable for want of adherence to procedures prescribed under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). Considering the limited scope of adjudication in the present application seeking leave to sue, I am not traversing upon the correctness/tenability of the plea of alleged defamation. Suffice it to state that the said statements, which were made by me in discharge of my duties rendered in my official capacity, do not constitute defamation by any stretch of imagination under law or in fact, his counter read. He said a reading of the averments made by DMK in its plaint makes it crystal clear that the party was seeking to proceed against him and Mr. Arjuna in respect of their acts in discharge of their official capacities. As a necessary corollary, I am advised to state that the procedure spelt out under Section 80 of the CPC ought to have been followed prior to the filing of the proposed plaint, he added. The Minister contended that DMK ought to have served notices upon him and Mr. Arjuna as contemplated under Section 80(1) of the CPC before filing the suit or it ought to have obtained the leave of the High Court under Section 80(2) of CPC to dispense with the mandatory requirement under Section 80(1). Since neither of it had been done, the maintainability of the suit itself would stand vitiated, he said. His counter also stated that having chosen to sue me as a Minister, having described my statements as made while holding and purporting to speak from the public office, and having founded the jurisdiction of this Honble Court on that very office, it is not open to the applicant (DMK) to subsequently contend that I have been sued in my personal capacity in order to escape the rigour of Section 80 of the CPC. Stating that the statements attributed to him were made in the course of the media interactions since he, as a Minister, was answerable to the people at large especially on serious issues concerning child sexual abuse, Mr. Kumar said, he would have explained his position clearly if the DMK had served notice upon him as required under Section 80 of the CPC. He urged the court to dismiss DMKs application with exemplary costs. Mr. Arjuna too filed a similar counter affidavit through senior counsel Satish Parasaran, assisted by advocates Dixita Gohil and Pranjal Agarwal. The case is expected to be listed for hearing before Justice K. Govindarajan Thilakavadi on Wednesday (September 30, 2026).

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani POCSO case: SIT to file charge sheet
content: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the POCSO case against Gem Granites Veeramani is likely to file its charge sheet before the Special Court for POCSO cases next week, police sources said. The case was initially registered in October 2025 following a complaint from a child rights activist who received a pen drive from an unidentified person containing a video purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a minor girl. Police had subsequently filed a closure report, citing difficulties in identifying the girl. The Special POCSO Court, however, rejected the closure report and ordered further investigation. Subsequently, the case was reinvestigated and the police arrested Veeramani, 84 and his abettors - Shanthi, 60 and her husband Mahendra Simhan, 63. One Ganesh who was an assistant for 23 years with Gem Granites was also arrested. Police identified the victim in the video and more than victims came forward to lodge their complaints. The Special Investigation Team was constituted under Additional Commissioner P.C. Thenmozhi on September 24, 2026 to conduct further investigation into the case and related matters. As part of the probe, the SIT recorded the survivors statement before a judicial magistrate and collected statements from her parents besides other documents and material relevant to the case. The SIT is now completing the remaining procedural formalities before filing the charge sheet before the Special POCSO Court, sources added.

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani booked for abetting suicide of minor in 2004
content: The Greater Chennai Police have booked Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani on charges of abetting the suicide of a minor in 2004, police sources said on Tuesday (September 29, 2026). Investigators also invoked provisions under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against the octogenarian businessmen, his associate Shanti and others, the sources said. The death of the minor girl came to light recently when police accessed a message sent by Shanti to Veeramani asking if he remembered his involvement in the death of a girl. Victim identified A special team formed to investigate the veracity of the message conducted inquiries and identified the victim. Her mother lodged a complaint alleging her daughter was sexually abused by Veeramani and died by suicide. She claimed that though the family lodged a complaint with the local police at that time no action was taken. There is an information that the accused gave 1 lakh to the family or their close relatives on two occasions. We are verifying this claim, a police officer said. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) comprising senior women police officers was expediting investigation and charge sheets were expected to be filed next month in the designated court. City Police Commissioner A. Amalraj reviewed the progress made in the case with SIT officers on Wednesday evening. Police were probing the financial transactions of the accused and others suspected to be involved in the case to check if there was any proceeds of crime angle in the offences. In one of the cases, a bank balance of more than 20 crore was found in the account of a suspect and steps were taken to freeze it, the officer said without going into details. (Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the States health helpline 104 and Snehas suicide prevention helpline 044-2464 0050)

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani case: Police officer in SIT requests recusal; BJP seeks transfer of probe to CBI
content: BJP spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) said that the Tamil Nadu government must transfer the probe into the sexual assault case involving Gem Granites R. Veeramani, to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). In a social media post, he said one of the officers in the all-woman Special Investigation Team (SIT) handling the sexual assault case involving Veeramani V.V. Geethanjali, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Crime Against Women and Children, Greater Chennai Police, Chennai has requested to recuse herself from the team. The officer requested to be exempted from the panel, citing her prior involvement in the initial investigation of this case conducted under the supervision of the then Chennai Police Commissioner A. Arun during her tenure with the Central Crime Branch. Given the possibility that various high-ranking police officials may have played a role in diluting or prematurely concluding this case, it would be proper and fair for the investigation to be handed over to the CBI. The Tamil Nadu government must immediately request a CBI inquiry into this matter," Mr. Thirupathy said.

headline: Tamil Nadu police do not have crystal ball or magic wand to solve cases in a jiffy: Madras High Court
content: The Tamil Nadu police do not have a crystal ball or a magic wand for people to expect the investigators to solve even sensitive cases such as the child sexual abuse case booked against R. Veeramani of Gem Granites within four days of formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), the Madras High Court wrote on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). Justice V. Lakshminarayanan made the observation in an interim order passed in a writ petition filed by R. Varaaki seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the case booked under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. The petitioner had apprehended that the State police might not probe the case properly. When the judge wanted to know the basis for such an apprehension, the petitioners counsel replied the Tamil Nadu government had recently kept two Indian Police Service (IPS) officers on compulsory wait following complaints of them having attempted to cover up the crime during the previous regime. Immediately, the judge retorted: Then, it means, the government is taking action. He went to tell the counsel: It is a very sensitive matter. You people are not realising that this is not an area to play politics. I am concerned more about the children. You are not serious of what happened at all. There are other cases in which you can gain publicity. Please dont interfere in this case. Lot of children belonging to the Scheduled Castes are the victims in this case. However, the petitioners counsel replied that the cause of concern was the suspected involvement of some senior IPS officers in hushing up the crime in the past. Justice Lakshminarayanan said, the SIT would have to necessarily investigate that angle too and that the petitioner or any other person, in possession of information regarding the case, could share it with the team. On the counsels insistence that an independent agency must probe the case because it involves allegations of cover up against serving IPS officers, the judge said: Then, lets transfer it to the FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation). They are totally independent. They have nothing to do with India at all. The CBI too has IPS officers, where do they come from? Later, the judge directed State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan, assisted by Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani, to make sure confidentiality was maintained with respect to all those who share information with the SIT in connection with the POCSO case and file a status report before the court by October 7, 2026 on the investigation conducted so far. He recorded the submission of the writ petitioner that he too would appear before the SIT on Thursday (October 1, 2026) and share all the information available with him with respect to the case.

headline: Veeramani POCSO Act case: Let SIT work in peace, says Madras High Court judge while hearing DMK's plea
content: Let SIT work in peace, says Madras High Court judge while hearing DMKs plea Observing that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing a child sexual abuse case involving R. Veeramani of Gem Granites must be allowed to work in peace, the Madras High Court on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) adjourned by four weeks a petition filed by DMK to inquire Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar too in connection with the case. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan took the decision after Advocate General Vijay Narayan pointed out that the DMK had not only filed the current petition but had also initiated a separate defamation suit against the two Ministers for reportedly alleging that the party shielded the accused during its previous tenure. When the judge said, a sensitive issue such as child sexual abuse should not be politicised, senior counsel J. Ravindran replied that it was exactly the stand of DMK too. He said, the political party was also highly interested in getting the perpetrators of the crime punished and delivering justice to the child victims. However, it was being falsely accused of having shielded the offenders, he complained. In its present petition, the DMK had insisted upon the SIT to act upon its September 27, 2026 representation to summon the Chief Minister and the two Ministers for inquiry and find out if they had any material in their possession to prove the charges levelled against it. In the defamation suit, it had sought damages of 1 crore from the two Ministers for having levelled false accusations against it. The suit was filed along with an application seeking the leave of the court to institute it in Chennai though multi-national corporations X Corp, Meta Platforms, and YouTube were located outside its territorial jurisdiction. In the suit, the party had sought a direction to the social media giants to take down the false and defamatory posts and hence they too had been included as defendants. Opposing the application to grant leave, the two Ministers told the court that DMK had failed to issue prior notices to them as required under Section 80(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) despite having made them as defendants in their official capacity as Ministers and hence the suit itself was not maintainable in law.

headline: 'Gem Granites' Veeramani, his two accomplices in POCSO Act case detained under Goondas Act
content: Greater Chennai City Police Commissioner A. Amalraj has ordered the detention of POCSO Act case accused and Gem Granites founder R. Veeramani (84) and his associates, Shanthi (60) and her husband Mahendra Simhan (63), under the Goondas Act for allegedly engaging in repeated criminal activities and disturbing public order. Veeramani was arrested by the Immoral Trafficking Prevention Unit (ITPU) on August 29, 2026 on charges of sexually assaulting minor girls. Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan were also arrested for abetting him. They were remanded in judicial custody and lodged at Central Prison, Puzhal. Subsequently, the police registered two more cases against Veeramani for driving minor girls to end their lives. A press release from the office of Commissioner said the action was taken as part of the polices efforts to curb the activities of habitual offenders. Four cases booked so far, financial transactions being probed Meanwhile, the police released an update on further action in cases involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls by Veeramani and said that investigation is under way into suspicious financial transactions made by the businessman. The police said that so far, four cases have been registered under various provisions of the law based on complaints, including those lodged by the minor girls and their relatives. The cases are under investigation, the police said, adding that they continued to receive complaints against Veeramani and the other accused. A WhatsApp number, 9345319676, has been introduced for sharing information about the affected minor girls. So far, five useful pieces of information have been received through the number and are being verified and investigated, the police said. 11 detained under Goondas Act Separately, the Commissioner invoked provisions of the Goondas Act and detained 11 others, including Sathish Kumar (26), Manikandan (20), Hariharan (20), Paranitharan (20), and Rakesh (20), who were arrested in connection with the murder of a person named Kannan in Vannanthurai in Shastri Nagar on September 5. The police said all 14 accused had been arrested in their respective cases and remanded in judicial custody before the detention orders were issued. The detention orders were issued by the Commissioner against persons who were allegedly involved in offences including murder, attempt to murder, narcotics offences, and sexual offences, which the police said posed a threat to public order. headline: What is the 'Gem Granites' Veeramani POCSO Act case all about? | Explained
content: On August 29, 2026, the Greater Chennai Police arrested well known industrialist R. Veeramani (84), a pioneer in the granite business and founder of GEM Group of Companies, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of sexually assaulting minor girls over a period of time. The police also arrested his suspected accomplices Shanthi (60) and her husband Mahendra Simhan (63) the latter a senior employee of GEM Group. On October 1, 2026, the Greater Chennai Commissioner of Police Amalraj issued an order detaining the trio under the Goondas Act. According to a police press note, on October 6, 2025, a volunteer of a Chennai-based NGO lodged a complaint with the Inspector of Police, Immoral Trafficking Prevention Unit (ITPU), Greater Chennai Police. The complainant said a man had visited her office and handed over a pen drive, claiming it contained video recordings of Veeramani sexually abusing a minor girl at Shanthis house in Chennai.

headline: Chennai's monsoon test
content: Northeast monsoon is at Chennais doorstep. This year, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted normal Northeast monsoon rainfall, with a strong El Nio likely to strengthen it further towards the end of the year. Historically, November and December have, for long, been months to remember in the city, where rains can be unpredictable. With the monsoon getting shorter and more intense over the past few years, successive Dravidian governments had grappled with mitigation measures, only to be overwhelmed time and again by the ferocity of nature. Is the new Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government prepared to face the monsoon, or will Chennai have to brace for another deluge? R. Aishwaryaa takes a deeper look.
