headline: CPI(M) urges Tamil Nadu government to boycott High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes
content: The CPI(M) has urged the Tamil Nadu government to boycott the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes constituted by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. Strongly condemning the move, CPI(M) State secretary P. Shanmugam said in a statement on Friday that the 35-point questionnaire formulated by this panel exposes the anti-minority agenda of the RSS and the BJP. The CPI(M) alleged that setting up such an extra-legal committee to gather data while the official Census remains pending demonstrates the BJPs malicious intent. The party further accused the committee of acting purely with political motives by seeking religion-wise data from states on faith-based school enrollments, land ownership transfers, and religious conversions among tribal populations. In particular, he pointed out that the committees collection of religious details regarding voters deleted from electoral rolls, coupled with the fact that it does not include even a single demographer, clearly reveals the BJPs underlying motives. He emphasised that to safeguard State autonomy, the Tamil Nadu government must reject the committees questionnaire, openly oppose its motives, and refuse to cooperate by denying any data to the panel.

headline: Don't miss this Saturn show on Oct 4!
content: Saturn will put on one of its best shows of 2026 on Oct 4, when it reaches oppositionthe point at which Earth lies between the Sun and Saturngiving skywatchers an opportunity to see the ringed planet through most of the night.The alignment will occur at 5.30pm, when Saturn will be about 126,000,000km from Earth. It will rise around sunset and remain visible until sunrise.Saturn will shine at a magnitude of 0.3, a scale in which brighter objects have smaller magnitudes. It can be seen as a dot without optical aid, while a telescope will reveal its rings and some of its moons.NASA said Oct 4 will give skywatchers one of the years best opportunities to see Saturn.Earth travels around the sun once a year, while saturn takes about 29.5 years to orbit the sun once. Earths orbit is smaller, and it moves faster than saturn. So once a year, earth passes between saturn and the sun. Astronomers call this opposition, explained S Soundararaja Perumal, former executive director of Birla Planetarium.Saturn opposition happens every 378 days. The previous event was on Sep 21, 2025, and the next will be on Oct 16, 2027. Opposition is not unique to saturn. Perumal said the outer planets mars, jupiter, saturn, uranus and neptune can all reach opposition. Jupiter does so roughly every 399 days, while mars takes about 780 days. Uranus and neptune also reach opposition, but are not visible to the unaided eye.Earth and saturn follow elliptical orbits, so distance between them changes. Exceptionally close saturn oppositions recur on a roughly 30-year cycle. The 2003 opposition was particularly close; the next comparable event is expected in 2032, he said.Astrophotographer Srilakshmi N, who captured images during previous oppositions, said the changing appearance of saturns rings is due to the changing viewing angle as the planet moves around the sun. The rings can therefore appear differently from earth from year to year.She said the ring-plane crossing occurs roughly every 15 years, when the rings appear almost edge-on and can seem to disappear. The last such crossing occurred in 2025 and the next is expected in 2038.

headline: Chennai youths' raison d'etre in Post-it notes on display at IIT-M
content: Today, a wall of hope built of 20,000 Post-it notes, each carrying a young persons raison detre, will come together at IIT Madras Research Park in Taramani. To become an IAS officer, says a yellow 3x3 inch note from a 15-year-old. For my younger brother, says another. There is no one to care for him.The initiative was launched in Oct 2025 as part of a year-long youth-led initiative of the Schizophrenia Research Foundation (SCARF) and its department of youth mental health.Messages were collected from adolescents and young adults at 23 colleges, four schools, five youth spaces and one scientific conference in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and West Bengal.In clinical practice, hopelessness is known to precede suicidal behaviour, and addressing it is central to therapy, says psychiatrist Dr Shiva Prakash Srinivasan of SCARF.Research shows that many people hesitate to speak about suicide directly but are more open to discussing hope and well-being. Getting them to write down their hopes was a way of building optimism and connection, and a pathway to help-seeking. The campaign was led by 400 trained youth ambassadors.The reasons for living that people wrote down, says Dr Shiva Prakash, were relationships and commitments; education, career and financial goals; personal growth and self-development; pursuit of happiness; and holistic life purpose. But we also identified voices of struggle, he adds.About 400 of the 20,000 messages expressed distress or suicidal thoughts, says Aravind. Some were vague, while others were direct statements about not wanting to live or not belonging. It is the start of a conversation, not by a mental health professional or counsellor, but by a peer.With Tamil Nadu recording the second-highest number of suicides in the country, and young people being among the groups most affected, Dr Shiva Prakash says that, as a continuing activity, he hopes to see it integrated into other mental health awareness activities at academic institutions.The anonymity of a small colourful note, says Aravind, gave people with nowhere else to turn a safe space to express themselves.The team did not offer therapy. We only wanted to give them the message that if they are struggling, help is available. We would direct those in distress to counsellors if needed, he said.

headline: A fierce battle on in Dharapuram among three leading contenders
content: The Dharapuram Assembly constituency, which has 2.23 lakh electors and where a byelection is scheduled for October 6, is witnessing a fierce battle among three major parties: the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK). In all likelihood, this will be reflected in the outcome, regardless of the winner, says K.M. Ramasamy, a veteran farmer in the constituency. The three major parties nominees are P. Sathyabama (TVK), who defected from the AIADMK after winning from the constituency in the April-May election; S. Suganya of the DMK; and K. Bhanumathi of the AIADMK. The Left has fielded P. Lakshmanan of the Communist Party of India (CPI) and the Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) has put up M. Karthika. Leaders of the three parties are making last-minute outreach to the people, even as Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, who covered the constituency once, is planning to visit it again on October 4. Former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin of the DMK and Edappadi K. Palaniswami of the AIADMK conducted roadshows on Friday. Mr. Palaniswami had visited the area twice. All the three parties have drafted many of their senior functionaries for the election work. The TVKs campaign is being spearheaded by Revenue Minister K.A. Sengottaiyan, while the DMK and the AIADMK have entrusted the work to former Ministers, including Vellakoil M.P. Saminathan and Thangam Thennarasu, of the DMK, and Pollachi V. Jayaraman and Dindigul C. Sreenivasan, of the AIADMK. However, in contrast to the vibrant atmosphere that can be felt all the time at the offices of the TVK and the DMK on Dharapuram towns main road, the AIADMKs office wears a sober look. Though Dharapuram has been set apart for the Scheduled Castes (SCs) since 1967, the Kongu Vellala Gounders, according to an estimate, constitute 42% of the population, followed by the SCs with 32%. Chettiars and Nadars account for 3.7% each, while the shares of Muslims and Christians are 4% and 1.8%. The fledgling TVK, being the ruling party, enjoys goodwill among certain sections, especially women. But some volunteers of the party say that if the party had put up someone else instead of Ms. Sathyabama, there is no need for Mr. Vijay to campaign personally. They concede that their partys nominee did face hostile treatment in some villages because of her decision to seek re-election within such a short period on a weak ground. But Keerthana, a young homemaker of Manakadavu village, feels the ruling party deserves to be given a fair chance and the criticism that the government has not fulfilled many of the electoral promises does not hold water as every other party, which was in power till now, took its own time to implement its assurances. The DMK, which represented the constituency during 2021-26, is contesting virtually single-handedly, as most of its allies have deserted it, and are backing the TVK. The Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) is an exception, and its general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant was in the constituency a few days ago. However, the DMK is taking no chances. Its fieldwork has been acknowledged by a functionary of the AIADMK, who is from Coimbatore. Our workers are working vigorously and the upset we suffered in the general election has only prompted them to work much more fiercely than what it would have been otherwise, says I.P. Senthilkumar, three-time legislator and son of the DMKs face in Dindigul district I. Periyasamy. The AIADMK, which may appear to be weak, is no pushover as it continues to have considerable hold in the constituency, according to a cross-section of the people. A resident of the town, who is a mechanical engineer, says that traditionally, the DMK is stronger in urban areas and the AIADMK in the villages. The entry of the TVK has upset the applecart. Mr. Ramasamy, the farmer, says the ruling party appears to have grown at the cost of the AIADMK, something that the DMK feels will work to its advantage. Mr. Jayaraman, the former Minister, says those who had voted for the TVK in the general election have started realising that the TVK does not mean what it had promised, and it cannot be taken seriously. The AIADMK being the only credible alternative to the DMK, the voters will elect our candidate once again, he says. Irrespective of the party that is bagging the seat this time, the winner should take steps for resolving water shortage in our constituency where most of the farmland is rain-fed, says N. Natarajan, another farmer who lives near Dasanaickenpatti village. He adds that he has submitted a project proposal to Mr. Sengottaiyan for groundwater recharge. Mr. Ramasamy points out that the farmers have been buying water for farming and feeding the cattle and the poultry. For 24,000 litres, they had paid 5,000 in the last three-four months, because of the failure of the Southwest monsoon, he recalls. It remains to be seen whether the result, to be declared on October 9, will make a meaningful difference to the electors who struggle for water.

headline: CPM lashes out at political landscape in TN, Pondy, accuses parties of distributing cash
content: CPM Tamil Nadu state secretary P Shanmugam on Friday lashed out at the political landscape in TN and the Union territory of Puducherry, accusing major political partiesincluding the TVKof distributing cash for votes in ongoing assembly byelections.Speaking to reporters in Puducherry, Shanmugam targeted TVK founder and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, questioning how a party claiming to represent a pure political force (Thooya Sakthi) could indulge in unhesitating voter bribery. He said TVKs on-the-ground actions contradict its claims of principled politics. The widespread distribution of money to voters completely erases TVKs self-proclaimed identity as a pure force. He said Vijay must answer to the public regarding these double standards.He claimed that alliances led by TVK, DMK, and AIADMK are fearlessly distributing money to voters, leaving the CPM as the only political party refraining from cash inducements. He alleged that the election officials are largely absent on the ground and have turned a blind eye to widespread violations and illegal cash flow despite prior warnings. He pointed out that Vijay, who cancelled more public rallies than he addressed ahead of 2026 assembly polls, has now desperately launched door-to-door campaigns and resorted to street-by-street canvassing across 39 locations in Madurantakam. He attributed this shift to severe competition and an unfavourable electoral ground. He termed the by-elections as an unnecessary burden imposed on the public due to the irresponsible resignations of former representatives, leading to widespread public resentment against returning candidates.Shanmugam criticised Puducherry chief minister and AINRC founder president N Rangasamy for failing to bring tangible development to the Union territory or push effectively for full statehood for the territory. He emphasised that Left parties remain the sole voice raising core public issues inside the legislative assembly.

headline: BHEL celebrates Gandhi Jayanthi in Ranipet
content: The Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) in Ranipet celebrated the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi at its campus here on Friday. According to a press release, K. Saketh Raman, General Manager, Quality, BHEL, garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi and paid floral tributes. Students of DAV and SRK schools sang patriotic songs highlighting Gandhijis principles and contribution to the nation. On the eve of the special day as part of Swachhatha Hi Seva Special Campaign 2026, S. Leela, General Manager (Human Resources), BHEL, inaugurated a procession of school students and staff of BHEL in the campus. A cleaning drive was also organised to observe Swachotsav. Senior officials, representatives of unions and associations were also present, the release said.

headline: Gang held for possession of two elephant tusks in Vellore
content: The Forest Department has arrested a gang of three persons for smuggling two large tusks near Gudiyatham town in Vellore. The arrested persons were identified as K. Thiruvengadam, 38, a native of Chittoor (A.P.), and his relatives G. Munusamy, 49, and S. Govindaraj, residents of Anaicut in Vellore. Based on a tip off, a team of forest officials led by S. Pradeep Kumar, Forest Range Officer (Gudiyatham), stopped a two-wheeler, on which the gang were proceeding, when they were checking vehicles at the bus depot on GudiyathamPallikonda Main Road. Forest officials said that the gang gave contradictory answers when they were asked about the purpose of the visit. The team seized the tusks from a gunny bag that was carried by the gang. Forest officials said that the trio visited Tirumala temple in Tirupati and went to a local temple near Papavinasanam reservoir, where they chopped off the tusks from the carcass of an elephant. Each tusk, on an average, measures around 64 centimeters in length. They decided to sell the tusks to prospective buyers in Vellore, but the gang was intercepted by forest officials in Gudiyatham. A case was registered, and they were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way.

headline: Two workers killed in soil collapse during farm well construction in Tiruvannamalai
content: Two labourers were killed and two others were rescued after soil collapsed during the construction of a farm well at Kasthambadi village near Arani town in Tiruvannamalai. Police said the deceased persons were identified as B. Selvamani, 36, and V. Ravindran, 50. They are residents of Karungalikuppam village near the town. Initial inquiry revealed that Selvamani and Ravindran were hired by R. Thanchi, 62, a retired Army man, with other workers Dakshanamurthy, 40, and E. Babu, 35, to dig a 40 feet deep well to irrigate his 20 acre farmland. The four workers were working to remove a huge load of soil from the pit. As they were removing loads of mud, a portion of the mud collapsed on them. Police said the region had witnessed regular rain, and as a result, the soil loosened. Other workers and farmers managed to pull out Babu and Dhakshamurthy safely but Selvamani and Ravidran got trapped in the mud. The deceased were digging the floor of the under-construction farm well. Based on an alert, firefighters and the Kalambur police rushed to the spot, and retrieved the bodies of the deceased workers from the well. The injured persons were admitted to the Government Medical College Hospital in Vellore. A case was registered, and further probe is under way.

headline: CMC opens Paediatric Speciality Centre at its Ranipet campus
content: Quess Block was inaugurated at the Christian Medical College (CMC) campus in Ranipet on Friday. According to a press release, the new 346-bedded centre, which was built at a cost of 420 crore, marks a significant milestone in the institutions continuing commitment to provide comprehensive, compassionate and advanced healthcare for children. Around 12 departments including Paediatric Neurology, Paediatric Rheumatology, Paediatric Nephrology, Paediatric Respiratory Medicine and Paediatric Oncology are being shifted from CMCs Vellore campus to the new centre. The new facility is expected to be commissioned in January 2027, with the transition and commencement of functioning of the clinical departments planned in phases during February and March 2027. The project has been made possible through the generous support of Fairfax (through the Vellore CMC Foundation) and Quess Corp, along with contributions from other donors and well-wishers, the release said.

headline: Nepal plans to drain four glacial lakes after deadly floods
content: stakes effort this fiscal year to drain four glacial lakes perched high in the mountains, as it scrambles to reduce flood risks, officials said, after a recent disaster that killed more than 1,400. Rescuers are still searching for more than 5,000 people missing in the border region with China after Augusts glacier collapse unleashed landslides and a flash flood that tore through valleys. Our aim is to lower the risk of the lakes breaching their natural dams and reduce the risk of downstream floods, said Subash Tuladhar, an expert with a government research centre tasked with overseeing the new project. Canals will drain water into nearby rivers in a regulated way, he said, adding that workers faced health risks as a result of the lengthy periods of high-altitude work required, in addition to the dangers of sudden flooding. Design work and detailed studies targeting the central and eastern lakes of Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu II, will begin in the fiscal year that runs until mid-July 2027, authorities said. The lakes, at heights ranging from 4,050 m to 5,483 m (13,280 ft to 18,000 ft), rank among Nepals most potentially dangerous, the United Nations Development Programme and the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) said in a 2020 report. Nepal had the skills and experience required for the $50-million project to be funded by the Green Climate Fund, the UNDP and the government, added Tuladhar, of Nepals Centre for Hydrology and Water Resources Research. Draining project could take six years The work of draining through gated structures will start after a detailed study, and could take up to six years to complete, said Sanjeeb Baral, the Centres executive director. It will encompass installation of sensors, a flood forecasting and warning system, and efforts to build downstream resilience and prepare communities for the risks. In similar previous efforts, Nepal lowered by 3 m (10 ft) the level of the central Himalayan glacial lake of Tsho Rolpa by in 2000 and that of Imja in the vicinity of Mount Everest, the worlds tallest peak, 10 years ago. Urgency after recent floods Nepals disaster served as a warning to the world, Prime Minister Balendra Shah, 36, told the United Nations in an impassioned speech last month that blamed climate change despite his countrys negligible emissions. Retreating glaciers, unstable mountain slopes and increasingly unpredictable rivers showed Nepal was paying a heavy price, he added. Nepal, which has reported about 26 Glacial Lake Outburst Flood events in the past four decades, loses more than 300 lives and property worth millions of dollars to extreme climate events annually on average. The latest floods devastated a dozen hydroelectric plants, roads, bridges, farms and settlements. Cash-strapped Nepal would need nearly $5 billion for early recovery, officials have said. Climate scientists say as temperatures rise glaciers in the Himalayas retreat, leaving behind unstable glacial lakes held back by little more than loose rock and ice, above valleys home to millions. Lowering the lakes by 3 m (10 ft) would significantly reduce the threat, said Samjwal Ratna Bajracharya, a retired ICIMOD expert on glaciers, glacial lakes and outburst floods. They are growing fast, are high up in the Himalayas and could cause outbursts any time, due to earthquakes, avalanches, climatic conditions and unplanned human-induced activity, he told Reuters.

headline: Pakistan government holds talks with Imran Khan's party to defuse tensions ahead of long march to Islamabad
content: The federal government and leaders of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan held talks on Friday (October 2, 2026) to defuse political tensions ahead of the Opposition party's planned long march to Islamabad. The developments come a week after the party announced that its long march to Islamabad would start on October 4, postponing it by a week. The negotiations were being held in the chamber of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, who was facilitating the dialogue between the two sides. A six-member government delegation, led by Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, is participating in the talks. The delegation also includes Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam. The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) is represented by Syed Naveed Qamar, Sherry Rehman and Aijaz Jakhrani. The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) delegation includes party Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan; Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas; General Secretary Salman Akram Raja; former National Assembly Speaker Asad Qaiser and lawmaker Aamir Dogar. Zulfiqar Bukhari, the party's international spokesman, confirmed that talks with the government are underway. He said that the government has mandated a team to initiate talks with PTI, and it was holding talks with the party, primarily aimed at defusing the current political situation surrounding PTIs planned march/protest toward Islamabad on October 4. Bukhari said the party's key demands include an immediate meeting with Khan and a decision to take him to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him. The party also demanded the release of Mr. Khan's sisters and others arrested ahead of the protest, a proper medical check-up of his wife Bushra Bibi and that their cases be heard properly without interference. Government sources said the PTI's planned long march would be the main issue during the negotiations, while the party's other demands would also be discussed. Speaking to the media before the meeting, Sanaullah said that protests do not resolve issues and that the solution to all problems lies in negotiation. He emphasised that the courts, not the government, would make decisions regarding the cases against Khan. Separately, Gohar expressed hope that the negotiations between the government and the opposition would succeed. Bukhari said the long march would begin from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, with its first stop in Karak and the second in Kohat on October 5, before entering Peshawar district. "The Long March will set off from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat. The first stop will be in Karak, and the second stop on 5 October will be in Kohat. After that, the Long March will enter District Peshawar, he said. Bukhari said he would share any development emerging from the negotiations with the media but added that so far the call for long march is intact. The government has stepped up security arrangements, with shipping containers placed on roads leading to Islamabad and mobilisation of additional police personnel. Containers blocking routes into Islamabad have disrupted freight movement.

headline: Netanyahu warns 'very heavy price' if any power behind flydubai incident
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Friday (October 2, 2026) that Israel would impose a "very heavy price" on any power behind the flydubai incident, without offering evidence that any country was responsible. Also read: Flydubai incident | Complete coverage "As time passes, the picture is becoming clearer: The attacker underwent Islamist radicalisation. He came to crash the plane with all passengers on board," Mr. Netanyahu said in a statement. "We are investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price," Mr. Netanyahu said of the co-pilot assailant. Mr. Netanyahu did not identify any country as a potential culprit, but for years has been quick to point the finger at Iran, which Israel and the United States attacked in February. U.S. President Donald Trump, who in April reached a ceasefire with Iran that is now in tatters, said Thursday (October 1) in response to a question that he was "hearing" that Iran was involved and that the country will "be hit very hard" if so. Israel and the United States have linked Iran's Shia clerical state to numerous attacks around the world since the Islamic was founded in 1979. But it has little-known connection to hijackings, hallmarks of Al-Qaeda during the September 11, 2001 attacks and of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine in the 1960s and 1970s. Mr. Netanyahu has previously said the pilot was from Oman and earlier left open the possibility that he was experiencing mental problems. Israeli officials and witnesses say the co-pilot of the Tel Aviv-bound flight on Wednesday stabbed the Indian pilot, who let passengers come into the cockpit to overpower the attacker. The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia with no deaths.

headline: Russian aerial strikes snarl traffic on three Kyiv bridges in a new disruption tactic
content: Russian aerial attacks forced the partial closure on Friday (October 2, 2026) of three bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital's mayor said, in Moscow's latest effort to disrupt life in the city. Meanwhile, Ukraine's top diplomat said officials have received separate proposals for a partial truce with Russia from the United States, India, Turkey and Egypt. The proposals envision halting attacks on energy infrastructure, which have caused fuel shortages in Russia and power outages in Ukraine, and on Black Sea shipping needed to get vital grain exports to world markets. The Russian strikes forcing the full or partial closure of three of Kyiv's six road bridges caused traffic jams and appeared to be a new tactic in its campaign to torment the city's residents. Previously, Russia has hit apartment blocks, supermarket warehouses, gas stations and data centres, among other targets, in an escalation of attacks. Civilians are bearing the brunt of this war, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Trk, said in Geneva on Friday (October 2). The war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe that is growing and intensifying by the week, causing unfathomable pain to civilians, he said. Across Ukraine, people are living in constant dread. While the aerial war has intensified in recent months, fighting along the roughly 1,250-kilometre front line snaking through northern, eastern and southern Ukraine has been virtually deadlocked. Russia invaded its neighbour more than 4 years ago, and there are no concrete signs that a peace settlement might be possible. However, Ukraine has this year made some progress against Russia's bigger army, according to the Institute for the Study of War. Russian forces lost control over almost 300 square kilometres (116 square miles) of Ukraine between March and September, the Washington-based think tank said in a report late Thursday. It also said that the Russian military suffered over 46,000 casualties in September, the highest monthly number this year. It did not say how many Ukrainian troops were killed or wounded. President Zelenskyy says sanctions can stop Russian drones and missiles Russia fired more than 100 drones at Ukraine overnight, striking Kyiv and eight other regions, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Almost half of the drones were the jet-powered type that are especially hard to stop, he said. A drone hit a high-rise apartment block in Kyiv, killing one person, he said. At least four people were reported wounded elsewhere. Mr. Zelenskyy repeated his appeal for foreign countries to close loopholes in international sanctions on Russia and to add more restrictions on its trade. He said Russia's drones and missiles are critically dependent on foreign components. Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line, Mr. Zelenskyy said in a post on X. Ukraine has also bombarded Russia with the long-range drones and missiles it now produces, aiming at military manufacturing plants and oil refineries. The Russian Defence Ministry said Friday (October 2) that its air defences overnight downed 646 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions, occupied Crimea, the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. One person was wounded in Russia's southwestern Volgograd region, Gov. Andrei Bocharov said. The attack targeted industrial infrastructure, he said, without providing details. Ukraine is ready for a truce on energy strikes and the Black Sea Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the partial truce proposals presented to Kyiv by four countries were the first time India has offered to play a role. India is trying to balance its ties with Russia against its growing partnerships with the United States and other Western powers. A new U.S. sanctions package on Russia could impose up to 100% tariffs on New Delhi as a major importer of Russian oil. Sybiha said Kyiv is ready to accept a ceasefire if it stops Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid as well as Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and on cargo vessels exporting grain and other farm products through the Black Sea. We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in that combination. Energy and a ceasefire in the Black Sea, Sybiha told reporters Thursday (October 1), in comments embargoed until Friday. He repeated Ukraine's offer of an unconditional ceasefire on the front line. But Moscow has rejected a ceasefire, saying a comprehensive peace deal must be agreed rather than a temporary truce. Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Friday (October 2) that Ukraine attacked four Russian oil refineries overnight, but air defences fended off the attacks and key equipment wasn't damaged. The government and companies have worked hard to improve protection of refineries, he said. Russian President Vladimir Putin decreed in August that the state can temporarily seize control of critical infrastructure facilities if private owners fail to protect them or rebuild them after Ukrainian strikes. It wasn't possible to verify either side's claims. Russia is stockpiling ballistic missiles, Ukraine says Sybiha said Ukraine is requesting some 300 Patriot missiles from partner countries because intelligence services estimate that Russia is holding 600 ballistic missiles in reserve and can produce up to 140 ballistic missiles per month. The U.S.-made Patriot air defence systems can effectively defend against ballistic missiles, which fly fast and drop steeply, but they are in short supply due to the war with Iran. Ukraine needs more funding and quickly, Foreign Minister says Ukraine urgently needs funding in order to contract future drone production, so there are no gaps in supply at the beginning of next year, Sybiha said. Kyiv faces a projected budget deficit of roughly $27 billion this year, although the European Union has promised to help meet its financial requirements. The European Commission announced Friday (October 2) that it had disbursed euros 2.9 billion ($3.3 billion) to Ukraine in its latest batch of financing. Mr. Zelenskyy said the amount would help Ukraine's financial stability and strengthen its defence. Russia is also facing economic and financial challenges due to high military spending and debt.

headline: Ahead of UP polls, Aradhana Mishra replaces Ajay Rai as state unit chief
content: Uttar Pradesh Legislature Party leader Aradhana Mishra has been appointed the partys state chief, replacing Ajay Rai. Imran Masood, Congress MP from Saharanpur, has been appointed working president. The changes are part of the Congresss restructuring of its organisational strategy in the state months before the Assembly elections. Aradhana is the MLA from Rampur Khas in Pratapgarh district. She is the daughter of veteran UP Congress leader Pramod Tiwari, who had made a record of sorts by winning Rampur Khas constituency 9 times from 1980 to 2012. In 2014, when he became the MP, Aradhana had won this seat in a bypoll. In the 2017 polls, she won the seat for the second consecutive time, defeating the BJPs Nagesh Pratap Singh by nearly 17,000 votes. The Congress then made her its Legislature Party leader in the state Assembly. Considered to be close to Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, Aradhana had accompanied her during her visits to the houses of women and other victims of various atrocities in several districts including Hathras, Unnao, Umbha, Sidharthanagar and Lakhimpur Kheri in recent years. In the run-up to the 2022 Assembly polls, she had accompanied Priyanka across the state on her women-centred campaign, called Larki hun, lar sakti hun (I am a girl, and I can fight). She has a Bachelors degree in Commerce and Masters in Business Administration, and had served as a block pramukh for three terms since 2001. Rai, a Bhumihar leader from eastern UP, was appointed in August 2023. He had replaced Dalit leader Brijlal Khabri ahead of the 2024 elections. Rai contested the last two parliamentary elections against Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Varanasi. In 2024, he succeeded in reducing Modis victory margin. Series of changes In July, the All India Congress Committee (AICC) had replaced Avinash Pande as the general secretary in charge of Uttar Pradesh with Rajendra Pal Gautam, the national chairman of the partys Scheduled Castes Department and a prominent Dalit leader. Last month, the Congress appointed Kunwar Singh Nishad as chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committees Media and Publicity Department. According to party sources, Nishad, who hails from Mathura, was earlier associated with the BJP, and joined the Congress during Priyanka Gandhi Vadras campaign in Uttar Pradesh in 2022. He had since been serving as a Congress spokesperson in the state. These two appointments came as the Congress seeks to expand its outreach among Dalits and Most Backward Classes (MBCs).

headline: State Cabinet should comprise 50% women Ministers, says Annamalai
content: Former BJP leader K. Annamalai, who has floated the We The Leaders movement, on Friday called for women to constitute half of the State Cabinet. He was addressing an event where he presented the Kamarajar Awards to 10 women from across Tamil Nadu at Narada Gana Sabha in Chennai. While appreciating the TVK-led government for giving Cabinet berths to more women than previous governments, Mr. Annamalai said he aspired to form a Cabinet with 50% women when his movement came to power. Sister Rosily (from Kanniyakumari district), founder-trustee of Alert NGO Kala Balasundaram (Coimbatore district), mountaineer Muthamilselvi Narayanan (Virudhunagar district), information technology professional-turned organic farmer Jeevitha (Cuddalore district), Villupattu artist M. Madhavi (Tenkasi district), founder of Populars Sevak Trust A. Fathima (Tirunelveli district), student-palymra tree climber P. Harris Karishma (Villupuram district), Carnatic classical violinist C.S. Chinmayi (Chennai), yoga instructor R. Punitha Valli (Chennai), and aerospace engineering student Dhaanvi Karthikeyan (Chennai) were presented the awards. P. Krishnaveni, former president of the Thalaiyuthu panchayat in Tirunelveli district from the Dalit community, who was brutally attacked by a gang, was chosen to receive the WTLs Kamarajar Award. However, as she could not receive it in person, she had sent a recorded video message. During his speech, Mr. Annamalai said initially there was only one woman in the Cabinet and it had gradually increased. There should be at least 17-18 women in the State Cabinet, he said, adding that an all-women team was set to be trained in his Kalam Centre on October 15. Mr. Annamalai underlined the significance of training women for politics.

headline: CJP targets CEC, says ready for 3-month stir; AAP, Left lead protest in Delhi, over 500 detained
content: Thousands joined protests in Mumbai and Delhi on Friday to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar amid questions over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. While the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) led the demonstration in Mumbais Shivaji Park, which went off peacefully, 550 people were detained in the national Capital as Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders, Left student outfits, and civil society members tried to make their way to Jantar Mantar. In Mumbai, CJP national convener Abhijeet Dipke was joined by Hindi film industry personalities such as actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, singer Vishal Dadlani, and director Vishal Bhardwaj. Mahatma Gandhis great-grandson Tushar Gandhi was also present at the protest. Targeting the BJP-led Central government, Dipke said it was so incompetent that the CJP had to launch a second protest in just over two months since the Jantar Mantar agitation against the NEET exam paper leak, which resulted in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister. We wont protest for three days, but for three months, Dipke said. This was just the trailer and now Delhi remains, Dipke said. These protests will continue till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Jantar Mantar 2.0 is loading; Amit Shah should not make the mistake that he did before. We request people to participate in large numbers. The CJP convener criticised the SIR exercise and invoked Mahatma Gandhi, B R Ambedkar, and Jawaharlal Nehru to emphasise the importance of Constitutional rights and the right to vote. If Gandhi is the soul of India, Ambedkar is the backbone, and Nehru the mind, he said. Dipke dared Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to send the protesters to jail. The Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) led by Raj Thackeray have a significant support base in the Dadar area, where Shivaji Park is located, and extended support to the CJP protest. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka also targeted the Centre, asking if citizens who do not support the BJP should have their voting rights taken away. Dadlani sang Mera rang de basanti chola before modifying the lyrics to call on the CEC to step down. Both Dipke and Dadlani thanked the police for their cooperation. The police said 300 personnel from the Mumbai Police and other additional forces were deployed. No one was detained as a precautionary measure; all the roads leading towards Shivaji Park were blocked. The roads were cleared after the protest ended in the evening. The situation is peaceful, said the police. Among those at the protest was 34-year-old Pune resident Kushal Gupte who said he travelled to Mumbai because he believes public trust in the electoral system has taken a hit. The system has failed everyone and the trust in the Election Commission has been totally lost. To regain trust, Gyanesh Kumar should resign, he said. A teenager from Kurla in Mumbai, who was at the protest with her father and sister, said she was participating because of concerns about the future of democracy and the rights of women and other vulnerable groups. While the Mumbai protest went ahead despite the police denying permission for the demonstration, Delhi Police detained 550 protesters after refusing permission for a protest at Jantar Mantar. The police imposed prohibitory orders in the area, while Delhi Metro temporarily closed entry and exit at 12 stations in central Delhi. The police said all protesters were released by evening. While a source in the police said no case had been filed yet, they are investigating the role of the protesters. The police denied manhandling any of them. Among those detained were AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi, and Sanjay Singh; Rashtriya Janata Dal MP Manoj Jha, AISA leader Neha Bora, Swaraj India member Yogendra Yadav, and activists from CPI(M)s student outfit SFI and Congresss student wing NSUI. Before the protesters started gathering and making their way towards Jantar Mantar in the morning, the police sealed off the area around the Parliament Street police station and Jantar Mantar. Officials said more than 4,000 police personnel were deployed in the area, which was divided into multiple zones, each headed by a DCP-rank officer. Drones were also used to monitor the protest site. Bharadwaj arrived around 10.30 am and told reporters, Protesting is our democratic right. But the police are telling us permission for the demonstration has not been granted even though six days ago the AAP applied for permission here for a peaceful demonstration. The police detained him soon afterwards. In a video shared on X from a police station after being detained, Atishi said, We were protesting peacefully at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi Police picked AAP leaders and workers with barbarism and brutality. Over the next five hours, protesters arriving from Ashoka Road, Janpath, and Tolstoy Road were loaded into buses and taken to Fatehpur Beri and Badarpur police stations. By the time Bora arrived, flanked by Yogendra Yadav and RTI activist Nikhil Dey, hundreds had already been detained. The three were detained soon afterwards and were loaded into a bus. The protest is against Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission. But I feel theres a larger context. The resignation of CEC Gyanesh isnt the only thing. People are upset over SIR. This is about disenfranchisement of millions of voters, said Pawan, a 36-year-old IT professional based in Andhra Pradesh.

headline: Carnatic percussionist Tiruchi R. Thayumanavan passes away
content: Tiruchi R. Thayumanavan, an exponent of the mridangam, kanjira, and konakkol, died after a brief illness in the city on Friday at the age of 95. Family sources told that the vidwan had not been keeping well since early this year and had been recently admitted to hospital for treatment. Born in Kottaiyur, Kumbakonam, on September 11, 1931 as the third of four sons to violin exponent S. Raju and Thaiyyalnayagi, the young Thayumanavan showed an early aptitude for rhythm (layam). He insisted on learning the mridangam rather than become a singer or violinist like his brothers R. Govindaswamy, R. Thangavelu, and R. Balasundaram. After training under Narayanaswamy Iyer and his brother Kumbakonam Rajappa Iyer, Thayumanavan was taken under the wing of Pudukottai M. V. Dakshinamoorthy Achariyar in 1945. As his skill grew, Thayumanavan accompanied many famous vocalists like Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar, Chittoor Subramanya Pillai, Alathur Brothers, M.K. Thyagaraja Baghavathar, and K.B. Sundarambal. The bond between Thayumanavan and his guru became deeper when Dakshinamoorthy Achariyar decided to get his second daughter Kanagambujam married to his star pupil in 1953. He built a memorial temple for his guru in Pudukkottai and released a book, The Life History of Dhakshinamoorthy Pillai, in 1987. Thayumanavan received the Kalaimamani award in 1994 for his skill in Konakkol, a kind of note recitation that produces the effect of verbal percussion. The final rites are to be held on Saturday.

headline: A trip down memory lane for Australian grandson of Pudukottai's former Diwan
content: chance query on Facebook brought Australian national Ian Kendall this week to Pudukottai, where his grandfather Sir Alexander Robert Loftus Tottenham served as the erstwhile princely states Administrator and Diwan from 1934 until his demise in 1946. We were overwhelmed by the friendly manner in which we were received in Pudukottai, and to find out about the work of Sir Alexander. We were not aware that he was so warmly appreciated by the people here, Mr. Kendall told over phone on Friday. Over the past few days, Mr. Kendall, 73, and his wife Helen, visited Sir Alexanders grave in Machuvadi and the Collectorate premises in Pudukottai. The couple attended the birth anniversary programme of Rani Rama Devi Tondaiman, the erstwhile Rajmatha of the then Pudukottai Samasthanam, hosted by her son Vijaykumar Tondaiman on October 1. Among Mr. Kendalls cherished memories of the Pudukottai visit is being photographed with the portrait of Sir Alexander at the Collectors Bungalow. An obituary of Sir Alexander Tottenham published by on December 14, 1946, records that he joined the Indian Civil Service (ICS) in Madras Presidency in 1897 and remained there until 1923. He served as a member of the Central Board of Revenue and took an active interest in the archaeology of the Pudukottai state. After retiring from the Indian Civil Service, he became an Administrator of the Pudukottai during the minority of Rajagopala Tondaiman. When the ruler assumed full powers in 1944, he was assigned as the Diwan and continued in administration until 1946. Paying tribute to Sir Alexander in a press communique, in 1946, the then Pudukottah Durbar said, But for a spell of 10 months in England during these 13 years, he was always in Pudukottah and he had such love and affection for the people of Pudukottah that he was often saying that he would lay his bones only here. He was known for his work to reclaim lands affected by soil erosion, and the maintenance of irrigation systems in Pudukottai. The Tottenham filing system of official correspondence that he introduced is still in use in government offices in India, with an upgraded computerised version. The Kendalls came to know of Sir Alexander Tottenham while trying to gather details about Mr. Ians father Robert, who migrated to Australia in the 1940s, and formalise the family tree. While official records state that Sir Alexander was a bachelor, other biographical accounts of British administrators in India suggest that he had an Anglo-Indian spouse and two sons, Robert and Ginger. Vijaykumar [Tondaiman] replied to my niece Simones query about Sir Alexander on Facebook, and sent her a book that had some of his history related to my father and his brother. Thats when we decided to visit Pudukottai. We feel quite humbled that we got so much attention in the short time that we were here, said Mr. Kendall. Alexander Tottenham had left an endowment of 10,000 that he had wished to be used for charitable work after his demise. This has been administered by our family over several years. We observe December 13 as Tottenham Day in Pudukottai with a special prayer service in his memory and by rendering assistance to people in need, Mr. Tondaiman added.

headline: Pilot averted potential catastrophe, says UAE top official as Trump sends Iran a warning
content: Praising flydubais Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his courage and responsibility in averting a potential catastrophe, the UAE Friday called the attack in the cockpit of the passenger aircraft headed to Tel Aviv from Dubai a serious terrorist incident. Machchhar was airlifted to the UAE from Saudi Arabia where the plane had landed Wednesday. Seriously injured in the attack by the co-pilot, he is being treated in a hospital in Abu Dhabi. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE President, said Machchhar deserves the highest praise. In confronting a serious terrorist incident and a potential catastrophe, he embodied courage and responsibility, Gargash said in a post in Arabic on X, according to Gulf News. His professionalism and moral conviction in the darkest of circumstances make him a true hero. Gargash also cautioned that vigilance was essential to confronting future possible acts of extremism and terrorism, and warned against promoting conspiracy theories about the attack. The Associated Press said Israel will begin repatriation flights Friday to bring back passengers stranded in the UAE after commercial travel between the two countries was suspended in the wake of the attack. Authorities in Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and beyond are grappling with the fallout from the incident on board the flydubai flight from Dubai. According to the AP report, Israels Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated his claim Friday that the co-pilot, identified by Israeli officials as an Omani citizen, had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination but provided no evidence to back the assertion. We are now investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price, Netanyahu said in a video message. US President Donald Trump told reporters that early information he has received suggests there are links between the attack and Tehran but did not elaborate. Trump also said that if it is determined that Iranian agents were behind the attack, the United States will hit them very hard. Israeli investigators are involved in the probe but the Emiratis are in the lead, the AP quoted an official speaking on the condition of anonymity.

headline: 'Heritage, Once Lost, Cannot Be Recreated': HC Flags Threat To Jaipur's UNESCO Status
content: Rajasthan HC warned that Jaipurs Walled City could risk its UNESCO World Heritage status over illegal construction, encroachments and poor heritage protection.

headline: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, boost for Trump
content: The Group of Seven industrial nations said they agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil, starting with substantial amounts of diesel after the fuel recently hit record high prices in the United States, where U.S. President Donald Trump said the diesel release would happen immediately." Mr. Trump and his Republican Party face pressure to address surging prices ahead of November's midterm elections. Mr. Trump announced the action Friday (October 2) on social media, saying, "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately. The President faces lagging approval ratings as the Iran war and his trade battles have increased U.S. prices for oil and other goods. Gas prices in the U.S. and abroad have soared during the eight-month-long war, a cost Mr. Trump has repeatedly said is worth it for making sure Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons. Trump has insisted prices will come down after the war, though there's no end in sight. The national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. was $6.37 on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on September 22. Trump had a conversation overnight with French President Emmanuel Macron, the chair of the G7, about the need to address rising fuel prices and the availability of petroleum products, according to the French Embassy in the U.S.. Mr. Macron then chaired a video conference of G7 leaders to discuss the issue. France holds the rotating presidency of the G7 group and made the announcement in a statement released after video-conference talks that Macron presided over. The International Energy Agency will coordinate the effort to combat soaring fuel prices. We will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels (MB) to begin immediately over 4 months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners, the statement said. A new AP-NORC poll found that a majority of U.S. adults blame Mr. Trump for higher prices, and approval on his handling of the economy hit a new low. headline: Hit by Bihar floods, man waiting under helicopter dies as 'relief material falls on him'
content: hit resident of Bihars Saran district died on Friday, police said. While some residents of Parshurampur village said the man was injured after relief material fell on him, others say he died of a heart attack. Police said the exact cause of the death would be established after a post-mortem examination. Police said another person got injured after being hit by portions of some structure that got blown away due to the downdraft caused by the relief helicopter. The deceased was identified as 58-year-old Anil Kumar Singh, also known as Appu Singh. A large number of villagers have been affected in the Gandak River flood, and dry ration was being dropped from a helicopter for them, officials said. The deceaseds body has no external injury marks, Kumar said, adding local residents have given two accounts of the incident. Some said relief material dropped from the helicopter had fallen on Singh, while others said the material landed nearby and Singh died of a heart attack. The body has been sent for post-mortem. The report will clarify why he died, he added. The SHO said the helicopter was flying at a low altitude and that the downdraft also blew away tin sheds and structures nearby. One person was hit by the material and sustained injuries, he said. The injured person received preliminary treatment near the relief camp and was subsequently taken to Amnour Hospital. His injuries were not severe, according to Kumar. 170 villages hit by flood The incident occurred as the district administration stepped up relief operations amid widespread flooding. According to officials, floods have affected 170 villages in 33 panchayats across six blocks of Saran, impacting around 3.32 lakh people and 75,286 families. So far, 43,400 people have been moved to safer locations. Fourteen relief centres are sheltering around 40,000 people, while 46 community kitchens have provided meals to 50,550 people. Some 2,540 boats are operating in affected areas and 2,650 food and dry-ration packets have been distributed. Twenty medical camps and five mobile medical teams are providing healthcare, while eight veterinary camps have treated 370 animals. The administration has also reported distribution of 153.5 quintals of animal fodder. Forty-eight NDRF and SDRF teams are currently engaged in rescue and relief work, with 11 additional teams due to arrive. District officials claimed health teams also helped facilitate four safe deliveries among pregnant women in flood-affected areas, while three other pregnant women were rescued and moved to safety with the help of SDRF and NDRF teams. Meanwhile, the Water Resources Department has intensified night patrolling of embankments affected by the Gandak flash flood and increased water pressure. Officials have been instructed to monitor seepage, erosion and other damage, with flood-fighting preparations strengthened at vulnerable locations, including Revaghat. The air-drop operation had begun a day earlier on the instructions of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary after the Saran administration sought additional ration packets. According to sources, a helicopter was arranged from Gorakhpur to deliver the packets to flood-affected areas.

headline: Ebola treatment centre was burned down as death toll in Congo passes 4,000
content: Congo's Ebola outbreak has recorded more than 4,000 deaths, authorities said, as they struggle to contain the spread of the virus. The latest figures released by the Health Ministry on Thursday (October 1, 2026) showed that 4,018 people have died, making up nearly half of the 8,300 confirmed cases, in what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Congo announced an outbreak on May 15, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no known treatment or vaccine. Some health workers gathered in Bunia, the capital of northeastern Ituri province, the heart of the outbreak. They were demanding payment for wages owed but were quickly dispersed by officials. The protesting workers included surveillance team members, who identify people exposed to infected patients. They waved placards saying, No money, no data! and No payment for months. Front-line workers have gone on strike several times since the outbreak began, further hampering efforts to contain the disease. A senior UN official said that an Ebola-hit camp housing a transit centre for infected patients was burned by soldiers earlier this week as they were looking for weapons in Kigonze, on the outskirts of Bunia, forcing 19,000 people in the camp to flee. The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province, the United Nations said. Julien Harneis, the UN senior Ebola coordinator, said creating Ebola transit and treatment centres has been a struggle, requiring money and staff, all of which are in short supply. When we lose a centre, that means we lose capacity, we lose investment, and we have to start again. And above all, it means that people do not get access to the care that they really need, Harneis said. Infected aid worker evacuated to Netherlands An aid worker with Mdecins Sans Frontieres, known in English as Doctors Without Borders, was infected with Ebola while working in Congo, the group said in a statement. The worker arrived late Thursday night after being flown to the Netherlands on a special medical flight and was transferred to a high-level isolation unit, the Leiden University Medical Centre said in a statement. The human cost of this crisis is unprecedented in the DRC, with communities facing the largest Ebola disease outbreak ever recorded in the country, MSF said. More than 50 health workers have died after contracting the virus. Insecurity and community resistance are hampering containment efforts The World Health Organisation has recently raised the alarm about the virus' rapid spread into new health zones, stretching limited resources. Africa CDC said in its latest news conference that the number of newly confirmed cases is falling, but that could be attributed to insecurity and challenges in getting communities to cooperate in some of the hot spots. While the spread of the disease has slowed down in some areas, it has accelerated in others, creating what experts see as a delicate situation. Confirmed cases have slowed in recent weeks, from around 850 cases and 470 deaths a week in mid-July to an average of 490 cases and 230 deaths in September. Overall, the outbreak also saw a similar jump of 33 per cent in both confirmed cases and deaths through September. A Congolese politician was attacked and beaten to death earlier this week for defending government measures in dealing with the outbreak, highlighting tensions that have stretched both the health community and local resources. The attack on Marie-Clestin Karondwa, a local official with Congo's ruling Union for Democracy and Social Progress party, took place on Sunday at his home in Butembo, an Ebola hot spot in eastern North Kivu province. His house was set on fire afterwards, and he died at a hospital from his injuries. Widespread mistrust of health workers and the authorities has hampered efforts to slow the Central African nation's 17th Ebola outbreak. Authorities last month launched a village-centred approach, but those efforts face resistance from residents who dismiss Ebola as a hoax. There is also deep distrust in the country's government for reasons ranging from how it's managed past Ebola outbreaks to chronic corruption.

headline: Booth-less toll fee collection at Tamil Nadu's Paranur: how does the multi-lane free flow system work?
content: Highway, on September 30, 2026, became Tamil Nadus first booth-less facility to collect toll fee from motor vehicle users through the multi-lane free flow (MLFF) system. MLFF, an advanced contactless and barrierless tolling system, eliminates the need for vehicles to stop at toll plazas by using advanced technologies based on FASTag, radio-frequency identification (RFID) technology, and ANPR technology for seamless electronic toll collection. Why the shift to MLFF? The primary factor is uninterrupted traffic flow. Vehicles no longer need to stop or slow down at toll plazas, thus leading to smoother traffic movement and reduced congestion. Second, operational efficiency and cost savings. Reduced reliance on toll booth infrastructure and manpower results in lower operating costs. And finally, environmental benefits. Smoother traffic flow reduces vehicular idling, cutting down emissions and contributing to cleaner air near tolling points. How does MLFF work? While conventional fee plazas rely on physical booths, gates, and lane infrastructure, under the MLFF system, high-performance RFID readers detect the FASTag affixed on vehicles at high speeds. At the same time, ANPR cameras capture license plate data while radar and LiDAR systems accurately detect and classify vehicles. MLFF equipment creates a toll transaction by reading the FASTag as well as the vehicle number plate and deducts the fee from the FASTag. It also captures evidence of vehicles where payment fails. The MLFF system works across all weather and lighting conditions, round the clock. MLFF thus delivers a fast, transparent, and high-integrity revenue process replacing the traditional toll collection system that cause delays and frustration. What should a vehicle user do? A motor vehicle user travelling on roads should maintain an active FASTag with sufficient balance and ensure that high security registration plates (HSRP) license plates are clearly visible. Vehicles without the tags or with insufficient balance will be issued challans. If a vehicle fails to pay the applicable user fee while crossing an MLFF plaza, an electronic notice or e-notice shall be issued for recovery of the unpaid fee. As per Rule 14 of the National Highway Fee Determination of Rates and Collection Rules 2008, e-notice will be sent via SMS to the registered mobile number of the vehicle owner, as per Vaahan database, and also to the mobile number linked to the FASTag of the vehicle, as per issuer banks records. e-notice amount shall be twice the applicable user fee. However, if payment is made within 72 hours of issuance, a 50% discount shall apply. After 72 hours, the road user shall be required to pay the full e-notice amount. Suspension of FASTag If the road user takes no action within the stipulated time period, related Vaahan services such as No Objection Certificate (NOC), Transfer of Ownership, National Permit, and Fitness Certification will be restricted as per CMVR 1989. Until all e-notices are cleared, the FASTag will remain suspended and will be non-functional at all toll plazas, including State fee plazas and parking facilities across India. e-notice grievance redressal Any aggrieved road user may raise a grievance along with supporting evidence through the National Informatics Centre (NIC) portal within 72 hours of issuance of e-notice, following which the grievance is forwarded to the fee plaza or bank for review and necessary action. The fee plaza will have five days to review the grievance and either accept or reject it. If the fee plaza takes no action within the stipulated time, the claim of the fee plaza to the unpaid user fee shall cease and the grievance will be automatically deemed accepted in favor of road user. If the grievance is accepted, the e-notice will be revoked, but if rejected, the road user shall have to pay the e-notice amount. Road safety measures NHAIs Project Implementation Unit (PIU) will ensure there is proper illumination at the MLFF equipment location, which will enhance the efficiency of the equipment and associated toll revenue with it. Other road safety aspects like closure of medians, illumination at the existing toll plaza, road marking, and signages, will be thoroughly examined. As the MLFF tolling involves high-speed movement of the vehicles near the MLFF toll plazas as in the case of other sections of the highway, NHAI will ensure the MLFF toll plaza, gantry location, etc., are thoroughly audited by the road safety auditor of the PIU.

headline: Woman tracked husband, his companion through hotel QR payment. Then, a crime
content: It was a payment made to the hotels QR code that allegedly exposed their whereabouts. This week, Thrissur Police arrested six people in connection with the alleged sexual assault of a woman from Malappuram in Keralam and the assault of her male friend from Tamil Nadu, after investigators said the latters wife allegedly tracked them down through a payment made to a hotel and allegedly sent a gang to pursue them. The six people arrested include the mans wife, who is from Tiruppur in Tamil Nadu. Others arrested are Thomas Priyadarsan Dev, a 27-year-old native of Nilgiris; Regupathi Raja, a 20-year-old from Dindugal; Sankar, a 20-year-old from Karur; and Balraj, a 31-year-old from Kadavur. A magistrate court in Thrissur remanded them to judicial custody for two weeks. Assistant Police Commissioner T R Rajesh said the wife, whom police have identified as the chief suspect in the case, had known about her taxi-driver husbands affair for eight years and had him followed. The gang members were all taxi drivers. On the morning of September 22, the victims checked into a hotel while reportedly returning from a trip to Wayanad. Since he needed money, he contacted his wife and shared the hotels merchant payment QR code. She paid money to the hotels account from her UPI app, which enabled her to locate her husband, said the assistant commissioner. Police said the woman then alerted one of the gang. Four others joined him, and they rushed to Thrissur, some 170 km away, and introduced themselves to the hotel as a police team looking for a man from Tamil Nadu who they claimed had stolen 65 sovereigns of gold. Having gained entry, they allegedly stormed into the victims room, abducted them and took them back to Tiruppur, where police said the woman was sexually assaulted. The next day, the woman managed to escape while the group was relocating her. En route, when the car was stopped somewhere, two passersby grew suspicious when they saw a woman with torn clothes sitting in the car. As the gang fled, the locals helped her reach the nearest railway station and return to Keralam, the officer said. Upon reaching Keralam, the woman lodged a complaint with her home district Malappuram police, who in turn transferred the case to Thrissur. The duo (the victims) met in Ernakulam during the taxi drivers trip to Keralam. The Tamil Nadu mans wife had been having them for some time. We are checking whether the arrested gang has any recorded criminal antecedents, one officer.

headline: World shares mixed after global bond sell-off deepens, ahead of U.S. jobs data
content: off deepens, ahead of U.S. jobs data Global stocks were mixed, and European shares edged higher on Friday (October 2, 2026) after a global bond sell-off deepened and ahead of a U.S. monthly jobs report due later in the day. Oil prices declined even as the U.S. sent another aircraft carrier and more troops to the West Asia, and as President Donald Trump threatened more possible escalations against Iran. In early European trading, Britain's FTSE 100 climbed 0.5% to 10,485.00. France's CAC 40 rose 0.6% to 7,883.49, while Germany's DAX was up 0.8% to 25,129.78. That came a day after Europe's benchmark stock indexes fell sharply as government bond yields shot up. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.9% to 68,309.46. South Korea's Kospi added 0.5% to 7,003.74. Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost 2.6% to 23,972.29, hitting the lowest level since July. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.8% to 8,682.10. Taiwan's Taiex advanced 0.3%. Markets in mainland China were closed for a holiday. U.S. futures edged up after U.S. Treasury yields held steadier early Friday (October 2, 2026). In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury was at around 5.24%, after it reached 5.34% on Thursday (October 1, 2026), the highest since 2002. It crossed the 5% mark last month, as inflationary pressure from the global energy shock driven by the Iran war and rising U.S. government debt pushed investors to demand higher returns. The 5% level on the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield has been an important psychological threshold for investors, David Clewell, a portfolio manager at T. Rowe Price, said in a commentary this week. Factoring in the U.S.'s resilient economic growth, there is a credible likelihood that the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield can rise toward 5.5% to 6%, Mr. Clewell suggested. Ballooning bond yields have been putting downward pressure on stock markets, as higher borrowing costs can undercut stock returns. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 added 0.2%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up less than 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite rose less than 0.1%. Investors and traders are monitoring closely the U.S. monthly jobs report for September to be released on Friday (October 2, 2026), as the data could provide more insight into the likelihood of an October interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, after the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years. Oil prices declined early Friday (October 2, 2026) as uncertainties surrounding the prospect of a de-escalation between the U.S. and Iran dragged on. The US military is deploying thousands of troops aboard a group of ships, including a third aircraft carrier, to the West Asia, according to a U.S. official on Thursday (October 1, 2026), after Mr. Trump on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) threatened to blow them up or make a deal, referring to Iran, in an exchange with reporters. Brent crude, the international standard, lost 2.3% to below $100 a barrel, at $99.95, after advancing on Thursday (October 1, 2026). That's still well above the approximately $72 per barrel level in late February before the war. The U.S. dollar fell to 157.63 Japanese yen from 158.09 yen. The euro was trading at $1.1255, up from $1.1244.

headline: Taiwan gender-row boxer Lin Yu-ting wins 'monumental' Asian Games gold
content: ting wins 'monumental' Asian Games gold ting won a "monumental" Asian Games gold on Friday (October 2, 2026) and said she was "grateful for making it through" after considering quitting following a major gender row at the Paris Olympics. Also Read: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally The 30-year-old beat China's Yang Chengyu 5-0 in the women's 60kg final in Nagoya, giving her a second Asian Games gold after winning in the 57kg class in Hangzhou three years ago. Lin told AFP before the Games that she had considered retiring after winning gold at the Paris Olympics but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility. She said after her victory in Nagoya that she had been "waiting for that moment when the light breaks through". "It was really not easy at all," she said. "It's rare to finally reach that point where you see the dawn, and I'm just so grateful to myself for making it through." Lin and Imane Khelif of Algeria found themselves in the middle of a major gender row at the 2024 Olympics, with Donald Trump, Elon Musk and author J.K. Rowling among those wading in. The two boxers had been disqualified from the 2023 world championships by the International Boxing Association (IBA) after the organisation said they failed unspecified gender eligibility tests. However, the IOC allowed them to compete in Paris, saying they were victims of "a sudden and arbitrary decision" by the widely discredited IBA. Both went on to win gold. 'Not afraid to die' Lin said winning at the Asian Games was different from her Olympic victory, adding that its "significance is monumental". "I basically just felt like packing up my things and rushing back home that was the kind of mindset I had," she said of her past experience. "I didn't hold on to any hope any more. I am so grateful to the coach for always believing in me and always believing that good things would happen." Lin was backed by a small pocket of vocal Taiwanese supporters in the cosy Nishio Gymnasium. Towering over her opponent, she used her superior reach to take control of the bout and had a clear advantage heading into the third and final round. She held off a late assault from Yang to take gold, celebrating with the minimum of fuss. Lin said she decided to compete in a heavier weight class at the Asian Games because she was "not afraid to die". "People are like that you want to see a different version of yourself," she said. "Since I already had a really solid track record at 57kg, I also wanted to give myself a different challenge and see just how far I could go." Lin refused to confirm whether she planned to defend her Olympic title at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. "I believe that in the future, we can also put on an even better performance, persevere all the way and laugh until the end," she said. China's Olympic champion Wu Yu also won gold, defending her Asian Games title in the women's 51kg. Wu beat Vietnam's Nguyen Thi Tam 5-0. Japan's Rui Yamaguchi gave the home crowd something to cheer about when he took gold in the men's 55kg class. Yamaguchi won by split decision, 3-2 over the Philippines' Carlo Paalam, a silver medallist at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021.
