content: The Consulate of Israel launched a public awareness campaign across major roadways in Mumbai to express gratitude to honour Captain Machchhar's valour. Billboards have been put up at the Warden Road and Napean Sea Road junction, near the Prabodhankar Thackeray flyover on the Western Express Highway in Bandra East, the BKC-Sion connector, the Andheri-Jogeshwari flyover, and Tulsi Pipeline Road near Mahim, bearing the message, "Thank You, Captain Smit, For Saving Israeli Lives! Wishing You a Speedy Recovery." Consul General Yaniv Revach, present at the display on the Western Express Highway in Bandra, said, "Captain Smit activated emergency alerts and successfully opened the cockpit door despite sustaining severe wounds to his neck and hands. The State of Israel and its citizens are deeply grateful to Captain Smit and 4 Israeli passengers on board who saved 174 lives. Captain Smit has become a hero in both India and Israel. Our immediate priority is his complete recovery, after which we look forward to welcoming him to Israel to officially honour his courage." According to the media release, Mr. Revach drew a parallel with the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, when Sandra Samuel, an Indian nanny, saved young Moshe Holtzberg, saying this reflected a shared cultural value placed on preserving innocent life in Indian and Jewish traditions. He said the situation could have precipitated a "complex diplomatic crisis" had Captain Machchhar been unable to open the cockpit door, and cautioned against what he called speculative narrative-building by some media outlets that might misrepresent facts or strain relations among Israel, the UAE and India, naming Qatar and Al Jazeera as examples he said were inciting public opinion against Israel and Jewish people. Mr. Revach also said, according to the release, that the UAE government had invited Israeli authorities to join the investigation. "We trust that a thorough investigation will bring full clarity to the events, though the possibility of a lone-wolf attack cannot be ruled out," he said, adding that joint efforts remained crucial in addressing online and media-driven radicalisation. He said he had personally conveyed his wishes and prayers to Captain Machchhar's family, and that the act of bravery had deepened the bond of friendship between the people of India and Israel. On Wednesday (September 30, 2026), a flydubai Boeing 737-8 MAX flight, FZ 1073, had an in-flight incident while en route from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv, Israel, a sector of more than 2,100 km, usually covered in three hours. The aircraft was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia and landed safely despite extensive damage. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that one pilot stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the plane. Most of the 174 passengers on board were Israelis, including 27 children. Flydubai suspended all flights to and from Israel, and an investigation has begun. The pilot who was attacked, an Indian national, was identified as Captain Smit Machchhar. He had joined the aviation industry with SpiceJet in June 2011 and worked there for more than 11 years, before joining flydubai as a captain in 2022, according to his LinkedIn profile. Media reports said an altercation broke out between the two flight crew members, with one pilot stabbed. Amid the commotion on the flight deck, the aircraft squawked the transponder codes 7700 and 7500, used globally to signal an emergency and a possible hijacking or unlawful interference, which may have prompted Saudi Arabia and Israel to scramble fighter jets. The Boeing 737, flying at about 34,000 feet, made a sudden descent to about 19,000 feet before levelling off at about 15,000 feet, about two and a half hours into the flight. The jet briefly entered Jordanian airspace before looping back to Saudi Arabia and landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk, a civil-military airfield that is also the base of the Royal Saudi Air Force Wing 7. Ground images showed the aircrafts rudder was substantially damaged, with a large part of it missing; passengers were seen deboarding using a step ladder from Saudi Ground Services, the ground handling agency. Flydubai incident | Complete coverage According to Israeli officials, Captain Machchhar, covered in blood on the cockpit floor, managed to activate the release to open the cockpit door. This allowed passengers to enter and overpower his co-pilot, while two off-duty flydubai pilots who were travelling as passengers helped secure the aircraft and carry out the landing. Briefs by Reuters and The Times of Israel, attributing the account to a Netanyahu spokesperson, Doron Spielman, said the captain, who was bloodied and lying on the floor, had drawn on the last moments of his energy to click open the release on the cockpit door, after which passengers who realised something was wrong rushed in and found the co-pilot standing over the control panel, bashing the control panel. Some reports cited a pocket 8as the weapon used; others cited the flight decks crash axe. A senior Boeing pilot told the crash axe, a mandatory aircrew safety tool normally stored near the pilot seats for emergency use, is in plain sight and meant to be accessed quickly. A video clip from aviation sources, shared with , showed both pilots on the cabin floor, bleeding profusely, with bloodstains on the cabin wall; one pilot was seen in a blood-soaked shirt with epaulettes, the other with an oxygen mask, as some passengers nearby asked for the filming to stop. The passengers later reached Tel Avivs Ben Gurion Airport aboard a replacement aircraft. In a video released by Mr. Netanyahus office, he was seen hugging a passenger identified as Yaniv, who helped steady the situation after the stabbing and the sudden drop in altitude; Yaniv was quoted by i24NEWS as crediting his intervention to having watched the Canadian television series Mayday (also known as Air Crash Investigation), which documents air mishaps. Captain Machchhar has been hailed as a hero by leaders including President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mr. Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump. Mr. Modi, in a post on X on October 1, 2026, said, Captain Smit Machchhar is a HERO. In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others... India is proud of Captain Machchhar. Mr. Netanyahu, also on X, said, My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery... He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals... He is a true hero. An All India Radio bulletin on October 1, 2026, said Saudi authorities had arrested the Omani co-pilot. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh, in a post on X, said its mission and the Consulate in Jeddah had been following the health condition of Mr. Smit Machchhar, who was admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and is receiving necessary medical attention, and was reported to be in stable condition, with a full health update awaited. Flydubai, in three statements shared with , confirmed the incident, said the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk Airport and all passengers are safe and accounted for, and that an altercation in the flight deck was resolved by on-duty crew who diverted and landed the aircraft safely. The airline said two replacement aircraft were deployed to Tabuk, that the incident had no impact on other scheduled operations, and urged against premature speculation while the cause remained under formal investigation. It later said flights to and from Israel would be suspended while the investigation continued, and that it remained in close coordination with government authorities, regulators and airport stakeholders. Flydubai, owned by the Dubai Aviation Corporation, began operations in June 2009, flies to more than 125 destinations including India, and operates a single aircraft type, the Boeing 737; it announced an extensive partnership with Emirates in 2017. The incident has drawn comparisons to earlier cases of unlawful interference, including Japan Airlines flight 350 (1982), Royal Air Maroc flight 630 (1994), Silk Air flight 185 (1997), EgyptAir flight 990 (1999), LAM Mozambique Airlines flight 47 (2013) and the Germanwings flight 9525 crash (2015). Israeli authorities are reported to have opened an investigation against the first officer, while Saudi Arabias National Transport Safety Centre and the UAEs General Civil Aviation Authority have also begun investigations. Some reports have referred to undefined threats against Israel ahead of the anniversary of the October 7, 2023, attacks, though the reasons for the incident remain speculative pending a full investigation. Israel has decided to step up security checks on all pilots flying into the country, a Reuters report said, quoting a spokesperson for the Prime Ministers office.

headline: UP girl dies amid 'loud DJ music': Allahabad High Court takes up noise pollution menace
content: Following the death of a Class 2 student allegedly due to loud music during a procession in Uttar Pradeshs Balrampur district last month, the Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the incident, asking who is responsible for enforcing rules on loudspeakers and other sound systems. The girl had collapsed in her classroom on September 22 while the procession was passing outside the school. The child was rushed to the hospital where she was declared dead on arrival. The school authority had lodged an FIR alleging high decibel DJ music was being played, causing the childs death. The DJ owner, operator were arrested and the local police outpost in-charge was suspended. Hearing a bunch of PILs related to noise pollution, a division bench of Justices Rajan Roy and Manjive Shukla, in its September 28 order, stated that it has not drawn any conclusion on what caused the childs death. But the fact that loudspeakers or music instruments were being played at a very high pitch and immediately thereafter, the child collapsed in the classroom, persuades us to take cognizance of the matter as noise pollution is now becoming a menace. In spite of this menace having been noticed and acknowledged by the legislature under the Environment Protection Act, 1986, and the rule-making authority under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, it seems to continue unabated, the court said. The bench observed that noise pollution violations occur every day on the streets. It is common knowledge. The question to be considered is who is responsible for curbing and curtailing this menace and what is being done in this regard? If, in spite of steps taken, this menace is not being curtailed, stopped or curbed, as the case may be, some mechanism needs to be put in place with regular monitoring [for] compliance of statutory provisions, it said. The bench observed that this will also entail spreading awareness among citizens as lack of it is one of the main reasons for violations. How to do it, is the job of the government for which we require its assistance and that of its authorities, the bench said. If violations continue despite measures being taken, then they have to be made accountable. Rules, 2000, provides for a penalty which could be imposed in terms of the Act, 1986, the bench observed. Listing the matter for October 12, the bench directed that the heads of the UP Home Department, Transport, Forest and Environment, Housing and Urban Planning, and Urban Development departments, be arrayed as opposite parties. It included the Director General of Police, Police Commissioner (Central), UP Pollution Control Board, Lucknow Police, and Municipal Commissioners, Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority, and the District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police and Chief Medical Officer of Balrampur district as parties. The court also directed that the school authorities be made an opposite party so they can assist it in examining the circumstances surrounding the childs death. The court issued a caution in its order, stating, we hope and trust that the parents of the child and school authorities will not be pressured and the functioning of the school shall not be interfered unnecessarily by any person or authority of the State.

headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak records more than 4,000 deaths
content: The latest figures were released by the health ministry on Thursday (October 1, 2026). They show that 4,018 people have died from among 8,300 confirmed cases, making up for nearly half of the confirmed cases in what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Congo announced an outbreak on May 15, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no known treatment or vaccine. The World Health Organization has recently raised the alarm regarding the rapid geographical spread of the virus into new health zones, stretching limited resources. The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said in its latest news conference that the number of confirmed cases is falling, but that could be attributed to insecurity and challenges in getting communities to cooperate in some of the hotspots. A Congolese politician was attacked and beaten to death earlier this week for defending government measures in dealing with the outbreak, highlighting tensions that have stretched both the health community and local resources. Widespread mistrust of health workers and the authorities has hampered efforts to slow the Central African nations 17th Ebola outbreak. Authorities last month launched a village-centered approach but those efforts are battling beliefs by some residents who dismiss Ebola as a hoax. There is also deep distrust in the countrys government for reasons ranging from how its managed past Ebola outbreaks to chronic corruption.

headline: Six men with snakes caught asking money from passengers onboard Jansewa Express in Bihar
content: Six men carrying snakes were caught asking passengers for money by displaying them inside a general coach of the Jansewa Express in Bihar on October 2, 2026. The incident took place on train number 14618 Jansewa Express under the Sonpur Division of East Central Railway (ECR). The six men were caught during an RPF check and were deboarded from the train at Dighwara station. RailMadad complaint leads to RPF check The action followed information received through RailMadad. RPF personnel from Sonpur Outpost, Dighwara, including Sub-Inspector Shamsher Kumar and Assistant Sub-Inspector Vijay Kumar, were monitoring the train. After the train left Chhapra station, the RPF team checked the general coaches and found six people displaying snakes while asking passengers for money. Six men deboarded at Bihars Dighwara According to Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO) of ECR, the RPF personnel informed the men about their conduct and deboarded all six at Dighwara station, which was the next scheduled halt of the train. During questioning, the apprehended persons did not clearly disclose their names and addresses. They gave different information regarding their place of residence, including Lucknow and Himachal Pradesh. Verification of their names and addresses is underway, the railway official said. The matter has also been coordinated with the Forest Department and necessary legal action is being taken under the applicable provisions. The national transporter has appealed to passengers to remain alert and report such activities at the earliest. The railway said that asking for money by displaying snakes on trains is illegal. Passengers are advised to report any such activity at the earliest so that timely and appropriate action can be taken, the CPRO said in a statement.

headline: New islands appear after Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano erupts
content: Two new islands have emerged in the waters surrounding Mount Anak Krakatau following a major eruption last month that grounded flights for days, the Head of Indonesia's Volcano Monitoring Agency said on Friday (October 2, 2026). The islands were spotted in satellite images of the water-filled caldera in which Anak Krakatau stands, Rita Susilawati of the PVMBG Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation told AFP. "Based on an evaluation of Sentinel satellite imagery, two formations resembling small islands can be seen around Mount Anak Krakatau" in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra islands, she added. Sentinel is a fleet of Earth observation spacecraft developed by the European Space Agency. One of the islands was located about 760 metres northwest of Mount Anak Krakatau, the other about 495 metres southwest. Ms. Rita said it was too early to refer to the islands as "children" of Mount Anak Krakatau which itself was formed by an underwater eruption in the caldera or depression left behind after the massive 1883 blowout of the original Krakatau volcano. "Anak" means child in Bahasa Indonesia. Ms. Rita said further research was needed to determine if the new islands were emerging from the base of the caldera in a similar way than Anak Krakatau did, or whether they were formed by deposits of volcanic material. In the case of Anak Krakatau, several landmasses briefly emerged starting in 1927 and then disappeared due to erosion before an enduring island formed in 1930, she added. The two new islands may similarly be eroded away over time. Mount Anak Krakatau erupted for 25 hours non-stop in September, blanketing cities in volcanic ash and prompting multiple airports to close. More than 300,000 passengers were left stranded. Ms. Rita said Anak Krakatau was at alert Level 2, the second lowest out of four danger categories. People are advised not to approach within three kilometres (1.86 miles) of the eruption centre. Five journalists on a mission to cover the September eruption were declared presumed dead with three boat crew nearly two weeks after the vessel they were travelling in disappeared without trace. Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where the meeting of continental plates causes high volcanic and seismic activity.

headline: Questions over botched lethal injection protocol after Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike
content: U.S. death row convict Christa Pike remained alive after surviving the lethal injection during her execution in Tennessee on Wednesday night (September 30, 2026). While the 50-year-old remained in critical condition and was receiving treatment at a hospital, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered a stay on all executions for the year. The case has raised several questions about lethal injection protocols, which are the primary method employed for executions in the U.S. What is the case? Pike was found guilty and sentenced to death in 1996 for the killing of another woman, 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. She was 18 years old at the time of the incident. The case invited intense scrutiny because she was a teenager when she committed the crime, and supporters argued that her mental illness and childhood abuse should be taken into account. Also read: How lethal injection is used in death penalty She was scheduled to be executed on Wednesday night (September 30, 2026) after the Supreme Court overturned a last-minute stay ordered by a federal appeals court over allegations that her childhood abuse was not fully considered during sentencing. Pike would have been the first woman in more than 200 years to be executed in Tennessee. What happened during the execution? Pike was administered two doses of pentobarbital, a drug used in several lethal injection protocols in the U.S. Pentobarbital is a drug that doctors often use to treat seizures. It slows down the body, especially the brain and the nervous system. It can be used as part of a combination of drugs or by itself for lethal injections. Witnesses at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, Tennessee, told the media that the injection failed to stop Pikes heart and that she could be heard snoring after the doses were administered. The curtains to the death chamber were closed many times, and the witnesses could often hear only sounds. Pike reportedly spoke a few times during the procedure. She could be heard breathing when the witnesses were removed from the facility more than an hour into the procedure. After the execution failed, she was reportedly taken to a hospital for treatment. What went wrong? Tennessee officials have not given any explanations for the failed execution. Offering more details about the execution, Pikes lawyers said that authorities were working for almost an hour to insert an IV line, and at least seven needles were used while trying to find a vein in her arm. Pike, according to her lawyers, even suggested trying to find a vein a little higher in her arm, and she also asked them if her arm was supposed to feel that way during the process. Tonight the State of Tennessee once again failed to carry out a lawful execution. We take no pleasure in being right, but the concerns raised by Pike proved to be true: difficult vein access, blown veins, degraded pentobarbital, no emergency medical care available when things inevitably go wrong, all under a protocol that remains veiled in secrecy, her lawyers said in a statement. Medical experts suspect that the drug may not have entered the bloodstream and may have leaked into her tissues instead. Although Pike did not die, the drugs may have caused permanent damage, they opined. Pikes lawyers had earlier raised concerns that the procedure would be too painful for her due to her small veins and a blood disorder that made it difficult to insert needles into her veins. What are the officials saying and whats next? Tennessee officials have stood by their actions during the execution. They insisted that every step of the States lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney Generals Office was followed. The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening, they told The Tennessean. Terming the botched execution deeply disturbing and pausing all executions for the year, the Governor has announced a third-party review into the incident. Meanwhile, Pikes lawyers have asked for a commutation of her death sentence. She remains in critical condition in the hospital. Has this happened before? This is the second execution in Tennessee in 2026 that did not go according to plan. Earlier this year, the execution of Tony Carruthers was called off after staff had trouble finding a vein to administer the lethal injection. He was later granted a reprieve for a year. The Death Penalty Information Center, a U.S.-based non-profit organisation working on issues concerning capital punishment, said it has documented seven people who survived failed execution attempts when staff were unable to establish IV lines. However, Pike was the first person to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs. This failed attempt is the worst weve ever seen and unlike any other botched execution in the modern era, said Robin M. Maher, DPI Executive Director.

headline: Pakistan Army presents man it claims India 'wrongly identified' as militant killed in Kashmir
content: Pakistan Army on Thursday (October 1, 2026) disputed Indias claims regarding the killing of a retired havaldar from its elite Special Services Group (SSG) in central Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district. Mohd Asif alias Hashim Moosa was neutralised in a joint operation by the Indian Army and other security forces in Budgam district Tuesday (September 29, 2026) night. He once served in former President Pervez Musharraf's security convoy, Indian officials have said. They said Asif was a top terrorist of the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba and was involved in high-profile attacks, especially in the last three years, which saw a surge in targeted ambushes and strikes against both military personnel and civilian hubs. Pakistani Army spokesperson Lt. Gen. Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry called the Indian account as fabricated during a televised news conference. Then the spokesman paraded a man and identified him as Asif, who he said was a resident of Attock district in Punjab, and a former Pakistani soldier who retired in 2023. "So here is that superman. You can see this superman. Please, come, my brother. Tell us about these achievements of yours, what all you have been doing, Lt. Gen. Chaudhry said, referring to claims regarding his involvement in various terrorist incidents. The man, in brief talks, said that a day ago some friends called him and told him about reports on social media that he was killed "by the Indian Army in Kashmir. I was surprised by whatever was happening as I was sitting in my home, said the man, who identified himself as Asif. The man claimed that he joined the Pakistan Army in 2000. In 2005, I joined the SSG, performed my duty with courage for 18 years, and retired in 2023. He said that he had worked for a private security company for three years. For the past three or four months, I have been living with my family in our home in Rawalpindi.

headline: In a first, Jammu-Srinagar Vande Bharat crosses 100 kmph on Chenab and Anji Bridges
content: Srinagar Vande Bharat train has achieved a new milestone. For the first time, the train ran at 100 kmph while crossing the Chenab Bridge, the worlds highest railway arch bridge. Standing 359 metres above the riverbed, the Chenab Rail Bridge is 35 metres taller than the Eiffel Tower. Stretching 1,315 metres across the Chenab River, the massive steel arch bridge has been built to withstand the regions challenging terrain and extreme weather conditions. It can withstand wind speeds of up to 260 kmph and has a designed lifespan of 120 years. The train also crossed the Anji Bridge at 100 kmph. The Anji Bridge is Indias first cable-stayed railway bridge and is another major structure on the USBRL (Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link) route. It spans the deep Anji River valley, south of the Chenab, connecting the Katra-Banihal section. Located around 80 km from Jammu city, the Anji Bridge towers 331 metres above the riverbed and stretches 725 metres across the valley. The bridge is supported by 96 high-tensile cables, with an inverted Y-shaped pylon rising 193 metres above its foundation. 653 km of cable strands has been used in the construction of the bridge. Vande Bharat runs at 100 kmph The increased speed was successfully tested using Vande Bharat Express train numbers 26401/26404. The speed test was carried out on October 2 after the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section was increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph. The latest speed enhancement is expected to make train operations on the Katra-Banihal section smoother and help reduce travel time. The Katra-Banihal section is an important part of the USBRL project connecting the Jammu region with the Kashmir Valley. Sharing a post on X, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the development, calling it a historic day for the rail network in Jammu and Kashmir. Vande Bharat train in Kashmir Currently, two pairs of Vande Bharat services are operating on the 266-km corridor. The service was initially introduced with eight coaches. However, due to high passenger demand, 16 additional coaches were added earlier this year, taking the total coach count to 20. Developed by Chennai-based Integral Coach Factory, the Vande Bharat trains in Kashmir Valley can operate in temperatures as low as minus 20 degrees Celsius.

headline: University of Madras financially stable, has own funds to pay salaries till December: Registrar
content: After spending years in serious financial doldrums, the University of Madras (UoM) has made considerable progress towards financial stability and had been meeting salary and pension payments from its own revenue, according to Rita John, Registrar. From April 2026 onwards, the University has been meeting its salary and pension obligations through its own revenue and has set aside funds to meet the expenses till December. Furthermore, based on our anticipated revenue, expenditure projections, and strategic financial planning, we are working towards sustaining these commitments through our resources until March 2027, Dr. Rita said at UoM Legacy 170, the initiation ceremony of the Universitys 170th year celebrations. The University, she said, has worked itself out from a tight financial situation and has managed to finish printing 5.5 lakh certificates to clear all the backlogs over the past years. It has managed to enrol full strength in Mathematics and Physics departments this year, she said. Also, the Ramanujam Institute of Advanced Study in Mathematics is all set to get a new building soon with four of its alumni coming forward to fund the rebuild. An MoU will be signed with the alumni members soon and the foundation stone will be laid before the start of construction. This year also happens to be the 100th year of the establishment of the Institute. Dr. Rita said that during the 170th year celebrations, the university seeks to strengthen its bond with the alumni and will be reaching out to them pro-actively. She also sought 100 crore from the government to renovate the Senate House. Dheeraj Kumar, Higher Education Secretary, said that UoM was the mother of all universities of South India and had organic linkages with most of them. It boasts of six Presidents of the country and two Nobel laureates as its alumni.

A possible crash was averted after a passenger and crew members entered the cockpit and managed to stabilise the aircraft. The jet had plunged more than 14,000 feet (4,300 metres) in less than 30 seconds, reportedly reaching close to the speed of sound. headline: U.K.-Iranian man held over U.K. airbase incident
content: Iranian citizenship was arrested Thursday (October 1, 2026) over a mysterious "major incident" at an airbase in southwest England as Israel said it had warned London about an attack. The sixth arrest came after British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the there were "strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford", a base used by the U.S. military in its war against Iran. Iran denounced the British government's "baseless accusations" and condemned London for making military bases and facilities under its jurisdiction "available for the planning and execution of the U.S.-Israeli military aggression against Iran". Counter Terrorism Policing said in a statement Thursday that a "25-year-old man, a dual UK/Iranian national, was arrested" in Westminster in central London "on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts". Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, speaking to Fox News late Wednesday (September 30, 2026), said Israel had tipped off Britain about a plot. "We gave the Brits the intel that there was going to be an attack, and it's an Iranian-sponsored attack," he said. Police were called to the base in the Cotswolds early Sunday, triggering an evacuation of the nearby village and the declaration of a "major incident". A farmer living in the village of Whelford near the airbase called the police after seeing vans blocking a road and a group of masked men. Police arrested five London-based Britons, all men in their mid-20s, at the scene and examined several vehicles. The men were then released on bail on Monday (September 28, 2026), a move criticised by Washington. Police then revealed no explosives were found at the scene and the nature of the threat has not been explained by officials. Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects but police have not commented on the reports. Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said in a statement Thursday that the investigation is "hugely complex" and police are looking at "all possible angles including possible foreign state involvement". Iran's embassy in London earlier said it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" speculation it was involved while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Mr. Burnham was "barking up the wrong tree". Britain gave the U.S. the greenlight to use RAF Fairford for defensive strikes against Iran, drawing Tehran's ire and unease from some residents in the Gloucestershire countryside where the base is located.

headline: Madras High Court reserves judgment on plea to defer bypolls in five Tamil Nadu constituencies
content: The Madras High Court on Thursday (October 1, 2026) reserved its judgment on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition that seeks to restrain the Election Commission of India (ECI) from notifying byelections in the Tiruchi East, Ambasamudram, Perundurai, Viralimalai, and Karur constituencies until the disposal of election petitions related to those constituencies. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan deferred their verdict after senior counsel Dama Sheshadri Naidu, assisted by ECI standing counsel Niranjan Rajagopalan, said that the role of the Commission in the present case was non-adversarial and that it would act in whichever way the court interprets the law. When the judges asked whether the ECI had taken a decision either in favour of conducting the bypolls or against it, Mr. Naidu replied: No MiLords. We have not taken any decision formally. Under Section 151A (of the Representation of the People Act, 1951), we have six months time. Before we could take the decision, the petitioner has knocked the doors of this court. The PIL petition was filed by K. Venkatachalapathy of Tirunelveli, through his counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan, who stated that the Tiruchi East constituency fell vacant because Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had won from two seats and resigned from this seat after retaining Perambur. Pursuant to the resignation, DMK candidate S. Inigo Irudayaraj had filed an election petition challenging the Chief Ministers victory from Tiruchi East. The other four constituencies fell vacant because the MLAs had resigned. Nevertheless, election petitions had been filed in respect to all those four constituencies and hence, bypolls should not be conducted for them in order to avoid an anomalous situation of each of those constituencies being represented by two candidates if the election petitions get allowed after the conduct of bypolls, he argued.

headline: PM Modi speaks to flydubai pilot: 'Indians are not those who take lives'
content: Indians are not those who take lives Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to flydubai airline Captain Smit Machchhar, who foiled an attempt by his co-pilot to allegedly crash the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight. During the telephonic conversation, PM Modi enquired about Machchaars health and lauded his courage during the incident. PM Modi said the whole country is praying for the pilot and wished him a quick recovery. PM Modi said the country can proudly say that Indians are not those who take lives, but those who are willing to risk their lives to save others. He added that Machchhar is a hero whose valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. PM Modi speaks to flydubai pilot: Indians are not those who take lives Your courage, valour and quick thinking saved the lives of so many people. Today, the entire country can say this with pride that we Indians are not the one who takes lives, but one who save lives, PM Modi said during the call. Captain Smit became emotional during the video call with the Prime Minister and said it is a very special moment for him to speak with PM Modi. He told the prime minister, You are my biggest idol. You called me and encouraged me, I am feeling very proud. While giving details of how he gathered courage in a tense situation, Captain Smit Machchhar told PM Modi that he kept reciting the Hanuman Chalisa. PM Modi also spoke about Smits mother, Geeta Ben and said she had raised him with the values and teachings of the Bhagavad Gita. PM Modi earlier spoke to the pilots wife and parents and applauded his bravery during the call. While addressing on Thursday, the PM said Machchhar showed great patience, acumen and bravery. And like Israeli PM (Benjamin Netanyahu) today said that this Indian thwarted 9/11 (like attack). For every Indian, Smits bravery fills our heart with pride, he said. On Wednesday, Smit Machchhar was attacked by his own co-pilot, an Omani national, and was severely injured even as the plane dropped 14,000 feet in 29 seconds. Despite facing stab injuries, Machchhar unlocked the flight deck door, thus allowing passengers to overpower the co-pilot and foiling the crash attempt. The plane made an emergency landing in Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. All 174 passengers on board were safe.

headline: Trump says Iran will be hit 'very hard' if it is behind copilot who tried to crash flight to Israel
content: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (October 1, 2026) that if Iran is linked to the copilot who tried to crash an Israel-bound flight, the Islamic would be struck "very hard" for the attempt on the lives of more than 180 people aboard the jet. Mr. Trump issued the warning as investigators worked to determine why the copilot stabbed the flight's captain, causing the FlyDubai plane to plummet before others on board stopped the attack and landed the airliner in Saudi Arabia. Asked by reporters at the White House whether he had been briefed about any links between the pilot behind the attack and Tehran, Mr. Trump said, "We're working on it right now." "I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes, but we're working on it right now," he said, without elaborating on why he suspected Iran might be involved. Asked if the U.S. would retaliate against Tehran if it was behind the attack, Mr. Trump said, "Oh they'll be hit, very hard, don't worry. You just ask them. They know what happened. They'll be hit very hard." His remarks came as diplomatic efforts to end the war appeared to have stalled. Iranian officials indicated on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) that they had received an official U.S. response to Tehran's latest proposal to end the seven-month war, which Mr. Trump had publicly rejected just days earlier. The officials did not say what the response contained, or whether it was a rejection. Mr. Trump said in a Time magazine interview published Thursday (October 1, 2026) that he would not accept proposals from Iran that "he wouldn't have approved a year ago," and left open the possibility of resuming bombing after the November 3, 2026, election in the U.S. Meanwhile, the American military has dispatched about 9,000 troops aboard a group of ships to West Asia, a U.S. official said on Thursday (October 1, 2026). That could mean three carriers will be in the region as soon as late October, according to the official, who spoke to AP on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations. Despite Mr. Trump's public rebuff, mediators have continued working with Iran and the U.S. to try to broker a deal to end the fighting and open the Strait of Hormuz, according to officials who were not authorised to comment publicly. Passengers got into cockpit to take control of jet Passengers on the plane, which was carrying 182 people, mostly Israelis, from the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv, described how the bloodied Indian captain managed to open the cockpit door to let them in, before they grappled with the copilot and stabilised a descent so sharp that the plane's rudder was torn away. "We felt helpless, suspended in midair, and I didn't know who to turn to. But it was all instinct to survive," Asaf Rajuan, who was among those who intervened, said in a statement shared by Israel's presidency. A regional official briefed on the investigation said the suspect, an Omani citizen, was under arrest, and confirmed that Saudi authorities were working with countries, including Israel, to determine a motive. The UAE, the U.S. and Oman were also involved, the official said. Saudi Arabia said the copilot had been handed over to the UAE. "All possible scenarios, from terrorism to mental disorders, are being looked into. Nothing is ruled out for now," the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss an ongoing investigation. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, without giving details, claimed the attacker had undergone Islamist indoctrination. Asked who had helped radicalise him, the Prime Minister told Fox News's "Fox and Friends" that he did not know. When asked by AP how the Prime Minister knew the copilot had undergone indoctrination, Mr. Netanyahu's office said it would not comment. Mr. Netanyahu told Fox News that the suspect apparently got through a loophole in Israeli aviation rules that normally bar pilots from flying to Israel if they are from countries that do not have diplomatic relations with Israel, which Oman does not. The copilot has not been publicly identified. Video shot inside the plane by Dr. Shota Musayev, a dentist who treated the captain, shows the copilot on his knees, with his hands tied behind his back. Captain Smit Machchhar, widely praised as one of the heroes of the flight, was recovering in Abu Dhabi, the Emirati capital, the Indian government said on Thursday (October 1, 2026). It was not clear what weapon the copilot had used. Israeli investigators will join the interrogation of the copilot Israeli intelligence and security officials were in Saudi Arabia to help investigate the copilot, according to another regional official who spoke on condition of anonymity. Israel has requested that the copilot be sent to Israel for the investigation, though it was unclear if that request would be granted, the official said. Saudi Arabia does not have formal diplomatic ties with Israel, but the countries have long cooperated on security and intelligence matters through alternative channels. The UAE government said its own investigation team had begun looking into the attack and "whether it was linked to any terrorist purpose," noting that Emirati authorities had jurisdiction because the plane was registered there and UAE law applies to crimes committed on board. Asked if there was any indication of Iranian involvement, Mr. Netanyahu told Fox News it was "too early to say." He said he had also spoken with the UAE's President, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who agreed that Israel would join the interrogation of the suspect. On Wednesday (September 30, 2026), Mr. Trump told reporters at the White House that he and Mr. Netanyahu had discussed the incident "at length" by phone. He said it seemed as though the copilot "was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job." Oman's government has not commented. Mr. Netanyahu had warned in recent days of heightened security threats, though he told CNN that Israel had received no specific warning. The country is a week away from the anniversary of the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack on Israel, which triggered the war in Gaza, and weeks away from an election. The Israeli Foreign Ministry said most of the people aboard the flight were from Israel, along with others from India and the UAE. The U.S. State Department said four passengers held American citizenship. Someone in cockpit sent out discreet distress codes Someone in the cockpit sent out two four-digit codes to discreetly signal distress while the plane flew erratically near the Jordanian border with Saudi Arabia, according to Flightradar24.com. The first code was "7700," the universal "squawk" signal for an emergency, followed by "7500," which indicates unlawful interference, including a possible hijacking. The codes are used by pilots when it is impossible or dangerous for them to speak over the radio. FlyDubai said on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) that the jet was secured by on-duty crew members "who diverted and landed the aircraft safely." A regional official said the crew members were pilots in training. In the chaos that began about two and a half hours after take-off, the Boeing 737 MAX 8 descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet in about a minute, before making an erratic circle close to the Jordanian border and landing in Tabuk, according to Flightradar24.

headline: Madras High Court dismisses case over transfer of five juvenile elephants from Assam to Tamil Nadu
content: The Madras High Court on Thursday (October 1, 2026) dismissed a writ petition, which sought a direction to a Supreme Court-appointed high-powered committee in New Delhi to examine the legality of the transfer of juvenile elephants from Assam to various temples in Tamil Nadu. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan pointed out that the petitioner, Mridula Gopalakrishnan, of Chennai, had rushed to the court the very next day of submitting her representation to the high-powered committee. The petitioner approached this court less than 24 hours after submitting her representation to the administrative authorities, without affording the competent authority even a single business day to examine, evaluate, or act upon the request, the judges wrote. The Bench said that the High Courts had been empowered to issue a writ of mandamus under Article 226 of the Constitution to enforce the performance of a public duty where a statutory authority, despite being formally called upon to act, had either expressly refused performance or by inaction demonstrated an unmistakable failure to perform its statutory obligation. A prerequisite for seeking mandamus is the existence of a prior demand for justice and its subsequent denial or inaction within a reasonable timeframe... In the absence of an actual or implied refusal, the essential prerequisite for invoking Article 226 of the Constitution of India remains unfulfilled. Flinging a representation to an authority one day and filing a writ petition the very next morning degrades the judicial process into a routine post-office exercise, the judges said. They went on to add that the authorities concerned must be given reasonable lead time to apply their technical expertise especially when complex factual and statutory evaluations such as verifying provenance, conducting genetic profiling, and determining ownership status of the captive animals had to be done. Approaching the court prematurely bypasses this established statutory mechanism and asks the Court to assume the role of a primary tribunal of fact before the expert body has even had an opportunity to open the file. It deprives executive agencies of the statutory window required to process administrative applications on their merits. Premature litigation of this nature adds unnecessary burden to the court docket and cannot be entertained, the Bench concluded.

headline: USTR Greer says he does not think "something is imminent" on trade deal with India
content: U.S. trade deal are nearing the end, the deal itself is not imminent, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer indicated on Friday (October 2, 2026) India time. His comments followed a constructive conversation with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal in the U.S. on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministerial conference. We had a very constructive conversation, Minister Goyal and myself, Mr. Greer said at a press conference. Our staff is meeting right now, since theyre in the country and were here. We are continually trying to finish the trade deal with India. I would characterise it, as we say in the U.S., were in the short strokes, he added. So I think were toward the end of it. At the same time, I dont think theres something imminent. Modi, Trump remain engaged Mr. Greer said that the two sides had identified the universe of items that are sticking points for both sides and are working diligently to address them. He added that U.S. President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a constructive call on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) and said that there may be another call between the two leaders very soon to assess progress on the deal. The India-U.S. trade deal has been heavily delayed ever since it was announced by Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump in February 2025 due to various tariff actions taken by the U.S. since then. The larger Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) was supposed to have been concluded by Fall 2025 (October-November 2025). Subsequently, talks on a mini deal addressing only tariffs also failed to fructify. In February 2026, the two leaders once again issued a joint statement committing to finalising an interim agreement on trade and continuing negotiating the BTA. The interim agreement was to have been finalised by March-April 2026. Neither the interim deal nor the BTA have so far been finalised. On Indias part, Mr. Goyal has been vocal in saying that India will not sign a deal until it is made clear that it will receive a comparative advantage over its competitors, as was agreed to in February 2026. The U.S., on the other hand, has already levied an additional tariff of 10% on India for not doing enough to prevent the import of goods made using forced labour. It is in the process of finalising further tariffs relating to excess capacity. Meanwhile, the U.S. has also passed into law an Act that could see tariffs of up to 100% being levied on India over and above the other tariffs for its import of Russian oil. All of these issues remain substantial roadblocks to the deal.

headline: Christa Pike botched execution: How lethal injection is used in death penalty
content: How lethal injection is used in death penalty Christa Gail Pike, now 50 years old, was convicted of the murder of her classmate Colleen Slemmer when she was just 18. She was scheduled for execution in Tennessee, which has also garnered significant attention, since this would have been the states first execution of a woman in at least 200 years. However, Pike miraculously survived the lethal execution attempt even after administering two doses of pentobarbital. What is Pentobarbital and how is death penalty injection administered? Pentobarbital is a barbiturate (anaesthetic) used in lethal injection protocols in several U.S. states, including Tennessee. The drug is intended to induce unconsciousness, followed by paralysis and cardiac arrest, which then leads to death. The procedure typically involves administering a three-drug cocktail, but some states have opted to use pentobarbital as the sole agent for execution. Also read: No end to inhumanity As the most common form of punishment in the country, lethal injection is the primary method employed for this purpose by the federal government, the U.S. military and 31 states that authorise it. There have been 1,492 executions carried out since 1976 through this method in the U.S., according to Death Penalty Information Center, a not-for-profit organisation. Due to resistance from drug manufacturers to supplying the drugs commonly used in lethal injections, some states now permit the use of alternative methods when lethal injection is not feasible. As it has become increasingly difficult to legally obtain the drugs typically used in executions, some states have also begun experimenting with new drugs and alternative drug combinations. This has led to prolonged executions in which prisoners have shown signs of pain and distress. Several states turned to sourcing untested and illegal drugs from compounding pharmacies that are not regulated by the FDA. What happened during Christa Pikes failed execution? Just one hour before her execution was set to happen, a federal appeals court intervened to review allegations of childhood sexual abuse and rape that Pike claimed were not fully considered during her sentencing. However, later on Wednesday (September 30, 2026), the U.S. Supreme Court intervened, lifted the stay and cleared the way for the State of Tennessee to proceed with the execution. Pikes condition following the execution attempt was not immediately made known, and it was not clear after she was taken for medical treatment from the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville what legal avenues her lawyers or the state might pursue next. Journalists who witnessed the attempted execution described snoring, loud exhales, gasps and complaints from Pike about pain, as well as her kicking her feet so often that she knocked off the sheets laid on her, according to NBC News. At times, the curtain was closed and journalists could only hear sounds. What happens next? The Tennessee Department of Correction defended its handling of the high-profile execution, which had been opposed by human rights experts due to Pikes age at the time of the crime, her history as the victim of childhood sexual abuse and untreated mental illness. The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the states lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney Generals Office, the agency said in a statement. The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility, the statement concluded. Pikes lawyers filed a federal court motion during the process seeking to halt her execution, citing witnesses accounts that executioners had injected both syringes of lethal injection chemicals and Pike is still alive and snoring, NBC News reported. Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a wooded area where they tortured and killed her. The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victims chest and taking a chunk of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time. (With Reuters and AP inputs)

headline: 'Mohammad' Deepak arrested after businessman alleges assault, threats in Kotdwar
content: A day after his arrest following a complaint by a businessman alleging that he had abused, assaulted and threatened him, Kotdwar gym owner Deepak Kumar alias Mohammad Deepak was released after executing a bond on Friday evening, police officials said. The development comes a day after businessman Sanjeev Tonk lodged a complaint against Deepak at Kotdwar Kotwali, alleging that the two had an altercation following an interaction on a social media post, which the complainant claims was on the partial demolition of a mosque in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. The arrest and allegations against Deepak have also been reported by other outlets. However, people close to Deepak gave a different account of what led to Thursdays confrontation, alleging that Tonk had been harassing Deepak since the January incident. According to a person close to Deepak, Tonk and Deepak had known each other for several years. The source said that after the January incident when Deepak came into the spotlight following a confrontation with members of the Bajrang Dal in Kotdwar Tonk began maintaining distance from him because of differences over their ideas and ideology. The source further alleged that since January, Tonk had been passing comments about Deepak. According to the source, the confrontation on Thursday morning began when Deepak was on his way to his mothers tea shop, located on the same street as Tonks garment shop. Tonk heckled him. That is when Deepak stopped and went to him and requested him to stop passing comments, the source alleged. Tonk, however, has denied the allegation, saying his interaction with Deepak never went beyond exchanging greetings over the years. He also claimed his first interaction with Deepak was over the social media post. This, he claimed, was followed by a tussle. On Thursday morning, after the interaction on the post, I was at my garment shop in Kotdwar with my friends. Deepak came and yelled at me and manhandled me, Tonk alleged. After that, I felt unsafe and went to the police on Thursday afternoon and filed a complaint. What the complaint says In his handwritten complaint to police on October 1, Tonk alleged that Deepak came to his shop and abused and threatened him following the dispute. Police initially registered a case under Sections 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). They later added Section 115 (voluntarily causing hurt) and Section 196 (promoting enmity between different groups). Deepak was arrested under Section 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) as a preventive measure, with police citing the possibility of a disturbance to peace and law and order. Police also carried out a flag march in Kotdwar on Thursday evening. Deepak first came into the spotlight in January after confronting members of the Bajrang Dal during a dispute involving an elderly Muslim shopkeeper in Kotdwar. The confrontation was reportedly over the use of the word Baba in the name of the shopkeepers establishment. During the confrontation, Deepak identified himself as Mohammad Deepak. A video of the incident subsequently went viral on social media, after which he came to be known by that name, police have said. Police have said they would continue taking action against those attempting to take the law into their own hands, issuing threats, spreading animosity or disturbing peace. The police have maintained that maintaining peace, security and harmony in the district is the polices highest priority.

headline: Indian Railways reservation: Can you book a train ticket after chart preparation?
content: Can you book a train ticket after chart preparation? The passengers can book train tickets through both online and offline modes under different reservation options, including the Advance Reservation Period (ARP) and Tatkal booking. However, getting a ticket can become difficult when demand is high, with many trains showing a long waiting list. But what happens if you check the same train after the reservation chart has been prepared? Can you still book a ticket? Speaking to .com, a senior railway official said that IR has a facility known as Current Booking, under which vacant accommodation available after chart preparation can be booked. IRCTC describes Current Booking as booking against vacant accommodation after charting. Can you book a train ticket after chart preparation? The preparation of the first reservation chart does not necessarily mean that ticket booking for that train has completely ended. The railway official said that if seats or berths are still available after chart preparation, they can be offered for booking under the Current Booking facility, however, it is subject to the applicable railway rules and booking window. There is, however, an important difference between normal advance reservation and Current Booking. Only confirmed tickets are issued under Current Booking. A passenger will not get a RAC or wait-listed ticket through this facility. This means that a passenger who checks availability after chart preparation may sometimes find a confirmed seat or berth even if the train was showing a waiting list earlier. CURRENT BOOKING (BOOKING AGAINST VACANT ACCOMMODATION AFTER CHARTING) GUIDELINES |Booking is allowed for all types of users (Normal & Agent). |Only E-Ticket booking is allowed. |Only Confirmed tickets shall be booked during current booking. |Only senior citizen and disabled concession shall be allowed. |Current booking is allowed after charting within the existing booking time limit specified by Railways. |Boarding point change is not allowed for current booking. |Name/age/gender change is not allowed for current booking PNR. |Booking in Premium & Suvidha train will be allowed with the last booking fare. How can a seat become available after chart preparation? The official explained that the availability of accommodation can change during the reservation process. During the charting process, the reservation system takes these changes into account. RAC (Reservation Against Cancellation) and waiting-list passengers are processed according to the applicable rules, while accommodation that becomes available through cancellations or other adjustments is also considered. Even after this process, some seats or berths may remain vacant for a particular journey segment. Such vacant accommodation can then be offered under Current Booking. This serves two purposes: a last-minute passenger gets an opportunity to travel, while the Railways avoids running with accommodation that could otherwise remain vacant. A train showing not available earlier may therefore become bookable later, the official told .com. For example, a passenger may check a train several hours before departure and find that it has a long waiting list. The passenger may decide not to book the ticket. After chart preparation, however, cancellations or other changes in accommodation may result in a confirmed seat or berth becoming available for a particular journey segment. If that accommodation is offered under Current Booking, the passenger may be able to book it. However, availability is dynamic and depends on the train, journey date and journey segment. Current Booking does not create additional seats. It only allows passengers to book accommodation that is actually available. Indian Railways Current Booking time Indian Railways provides for booking of available accommodation after the first reservation chart and close to departure, however it is subject to the applicable booking and charting rules. Railway rules have historically provided for reservation activity between the first and final charts, with the final reservation exercise taking place close to departure. Passengers should therefore check live availability rather than assuming that chart preparation automatically closes booking. The precise usable window can depend on the trains charting and reservation schedule, the official said. Indian Railways Chart Preparation time The timing of reservation chart preparation has also changed. Indian Railways has moved towards preparing reservation charts earlier than the earlier system, under which the first chart was generally prepared around four hours before departure. The Ministry has said advance reservation charting is intended to reduce uncertainty for wait-listed passengers, allowing them more time to make alternative arrangements if their tickets do not confirm. Recent Railway reforms have placed advance chart preparation considerably earlier in the range of around 9 to 18 hours before departure in the revised system, depending on the trains departure schedule. This makes Current Booking particularly relevant for passengers checking availability after the first chart has been prepared. For example, for trains departing between 05:01 hrs and 14:00 hrs, the first reservation chart will be prepared preferably by 20:00 hrs on the previous day. Meanwhile, for trains with departure times between 14:01 hrs and 23:59 hrs, as well as those departing between 00:00 hrs and 05:00 hrs, the first reservation chart will be prepared preferably at least 10 hours in advance. First Chart Preparation By 20:00 hours of the previous day First Chart Preparation At least 10 hours in advance of departure Source: Ministry of Railways Express InfoGenIE However, the second reservation chart is prepared around 30 minutes before the scheduled departure of the train. Thus, a chart preparation does not always mean the end of ticket booking. If vacant accommodation remains and the booking window is open, passengers may still be able to book a confirmed ticket.

headline: chasing system change
content: The mass uprising in Sri Lanka in the summer of 2022 had one unifying chant Gota go home, reflecting the protesting citizens chief demand that then President Gotabaya Rajapaksa resign. It was one of many diverse chants, their tone ranging from witty irreverence to daring dissent, that captured the spirit of the Janata Aragalaya, or peoples struggle. The protesters were emphatic in their rejection of Mr. Gotabaya, whom they held responsible for the countrys bankruptcy and their endless wait in queues amid acute shortages. They were unafraid to voice their anger with the Rajapaksa clan and their frustration with the entire political class. But in that watershed moment, they were thirsty for something else, something new system change, their posters screamed. Once the Rajapaksas grudgingly quit office and Ranil Wickremesinghe took charge, with the Rajapaksas party backing him in an urgent parliamentary vote, the protests fizzled out. The many fragments of the movement had varied reactions to Mr. Wickremesinghes rule. To some, he was an experienced leader capable of facing the challenge of fixing the countrys battered economy. Others, however, saw him as embodying a continuation of the Rajapaksa rule, except in a suit. It was far from the political and systemic overhaul they had sought. That is why Anura Kumara Dissanayakes campaign in 2024, promising to change the corrupt political system, found resonance with voters. It was the first election held since the economic crisis. Although led by the leftist Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP), a party tainted by its history of brutal violence, the broader National Peoples Power (NPP) coalition Mr. Dissanayake founded (in 2019) and built up in the subsequent years emerged as a new force offering rare promise. Voters who had until then switched between one of two legacy political formations alternating at the countrys helm felt they had a real choice. Short of a clear majority in the three-cornered presidential race he secured 42.31 % of the votes Mr. Dissanayake made it with his tally of preferential votes. His impressive win propelled the NPP to a historic supermajority in the general elections that soon followed. Citizens who seemed torn or tentative in the September presidential polls were certain in November 2024. They were going to give AKD and his government a real chance. I am not a magician; I am not a miracle-worker. There are things I know and dont know, Mr. Dissanayake said soon after being sworn in on September 23, 2024. But I will commit to always doing the right thing, and to lead a collective effort to rebuild our nation, the new President said in his first address to the country. Last week, President Dissanayake completed two years in office. He has been addressing rallies across the country as part of a series titled Peoples Rule Two Years Strong. Progress for All. Leading a country struggling to recover from a financial crash was never going to be easy. A year into forming government, the Dissanayake administration faced the deadliest natural disaster the country had witnessed since the Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004. Cyclone Ditwah claimed nearly 700 lives and displaced several thousand people, even as nearly 1,200 landslides swallowed villages in the islands hilly regions in late 2025. Within months, the West Asian crisis began, resulting in volatile fuel prices in the global market. Wasting no time after it came to power, the NPP government prioritised economic stability and recovery. The government opted to go ahead with the International Monetary Fund programme finalised by its predecessors, staunchly pursued fiscal discipline and macroeconomic stability as the IMF spelled them out, and achieved or even surpassed crucial targets set by the Fund. While the ruling administration initially referred to the IMF programme as a compulsion in the economic and social circumstances in the country, it gradually began following through with conviction. Meanwhile, studies have found that poor families are eating less, as they struggle to cope with crushing austerity. We surpassed the target revenue last year and cut down on unnecessary state expenses. It was because of this discipline that we were able to respond to Cyclone Ditwah and the West Asian crisis without passing on the burden to the public, says Nihal Abeysinghe, General Secretary of the NPP and Member of Parliament. Speaking to at the JVP party headquarters on the NPP administrations performance, Dr. Abeysinghe said it has changed the political culture. The Dissanayake government has made a series of high-profile arrests, especially of notorious suspects in the narcotics underworld and prominent politicians and bureaucrats accused of grand corruption. The arrest of a former intelligence chief in connection with the ongoing probe into the 2019 Easter terror bombings raised eyebrows. Law enforcement is the same for all, whether it is a former president or anyone else, Dr. Abeysinghe says. Pending promises According to him, the government will focus on the Provincial Council elections and drafting a new constitution in the three years that remain of its term. Both were among the key promises the NPP made to Tamil voters. While the conduct of the provincial polls remains stuck with a parliamentary committee, there has been no movement yet on the promised new constitution. The governments efforts to bring about legislative changes remain in sharp focus for both its eagerness in some respects and its lethargy in others. Its recent move to introduce a constitutional amendment extending judges retirement age drew flak from the political opposition and legal community, which accused the government of using the judiciary to serve its political interests. The NPPs pledge to repeal Sri Lankas draconian anti-terror legislation and abolish the executive presidency, too, remains only in the manifesto. Rights defenders have slammed draft legislation replacing and not only repealing the Prevention of Terrorism Act for falling short of international human rights standards. Mixed report card Offering a mixed report card for the NPP rule over the last two years, Pradeep Peiris, a political scientist at the University of Colombo, says he is 100% pleased that the country finally has a civilised, dignified polity. All the same, he is frustrated that an important turning point increasingly looks like another lost opportunity to address structural issues in our democracy. The NPP government, in his view, looks more like a government of good governance, rather than one of transformation. We must remember that 2024 was not just any other election, with its outcome bringing about a regime change. After 1948 [Independence], it was the first time citizens felt they could negotiate a new political structure. Observing that the Aragalaya popularised a democratic imagination, Mr. Peiris adds: While voters rejected the old political class in the 2024 election, it was not really a baptism of a new political class. The electorates verdict, he cautions, was more a rejection of old politics than affirmation of the NPPs programme. While the country was very clear about what it did not want, it is not as clear about what it wants, and even less clear about how to get there. The NPP government needs to initiate a robust, inclusive conversation on renegotiating a new social contract with citizens. Contending that a cultural project is necessary for real political transformation, he notes that such a project is yet to take off. In that sense, I feel instead of utilising this historic moment for system change, the NPP has simply become better rulers in the same system they inherited. In such a situation, the risk of the old political order returning always lingers, he notes. There is every indication that the NPP is hoping for a second term in office. The opposition is weak, divided, and has no clear work plan. We dont have a real political challenge yet, and we wont until a new force better than us emerges, Dr. Abeysinghe says with confidence. Meanwhile, the NPP knows that it has its task cut out for it to ensure that its supporters across the country hold on to the hope they felt in 2024. Weeks before he was elected President, Mr. Dissanayake seemed fully aware of the challenge that awaited him if he won. The people have very high expectations now, he told at the time.

headline: Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat train inaugural run: Check route, stops and timings
content: Check route, stops and timings Udaipur Vande Bharat train launch: The new Vande Bharat train between Surat and Udaipur is set to commence its inaugural run today. This new semi-high-speed train will further improve connectivity between Gujarat and Rajasthan. It will not only reduce the travel time between two cities by more than four hours but also enhanced the travel experience for passengers. This new train will be operated and maintained by the Western Railway (WR) zone. Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express inaugural run: Train number, route, distance, travel time On its inaugural run today, the Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express will run as train number 09103. The train will run via Asarva. It will cover a distance of around 690 km in 07:30 hrs. It can run up to a maximum speed of 160 kmph. Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express inaugural run: Stoppages The Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express will stop at nine railway stations. These are: Bharuch, Vadodara, Anand, Maninagar, Asarva, Himmatnagar, Shamlaji Road, Dungarpur and Zawar. Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express inaugural run: Coach composition The Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express is composed of eight coaches. It will have two types of seating category: Executive Chair Car and AC Chair Car coaches. Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express inaugural run: Timings On its inaugural run today, the Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express will depart from Surat at 10 am and arrive at Udaipur City at 5:40 pm. Along the route, the train will halt at Bharuch at 10:41 am, Vadodara at 11:30 am, Anand at 12:01 pm, Maninagar at 12:41 pm, Asarva at 1:10 pm, Himmatnagar at 2:38 pm, Shamlaji Road at 3:08 pm, Dungarpur at 3:47 pm and Zawar at 4:50 pm. Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat train features The Surat-Udaipur Vande Bharat Express trains have following features: - Fitted with KAVACH. - Jerk Free Semi-Permanent couplers. - Centrally controlled Automatic Plug Doors and Fully Sealed wider gangways. - Emergency Alarm Push buttons and Talk Back Units on all Coaches. - Improved fire safety Aerosol based fire detection and suppression system in electrical cabinets and lavatories. - Higher acceleration with design/operating speed of 180/160 KMPH. - Driver-Guard communication with voice recording facility & Crash hardened memory. - Air conditioning units with indigenously developed UV-C lamp based disinfection system. - Better Ride Comfort. - CCTVs in all Coaches. - For Divyangjan passengers special lavatory in the driving coaches on each end. - Coach condition monitoring System (CCMS) display with remote monitoring.

headline: French school protests spread as fires, blockades deepen unrest
content: French students set fire to bins and erected blockades outside schools in several cities, protesting overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and crumbling facilities. Several school principals were injured, harassed or assaulted during blockades at high schools on Thursday (October 1, 2026), according to reports from regional education authorities, prefectures and union representatives. Police have already detained hundreds of protesters at the lyces, which students aged 15 to 18 attend for their final three years of secondary education in France. The Interior Ministry said police and gendarmes had made 1,949 arrests on Thursday (October 1, 2026), while 305 officers had been injured. According to Interior Ministry figures, 1,027 lycees of the 3,700 across France had been affected by the movements actions, with blockades at 222 of them. The authorities in the Paris region said around 50 schools had been the scene of violence, clashes and damage. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez condemned what he described as unbridled violence. The office of Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the demonstrations had become urban violence and cited the intelligence service to justify claims that it had been organised by the radical left. Manuel Bompard, a leading figure in the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI), quickly dismissed the claim, accusing the government of sinking into conspiratorial thinking in comments to AFP. LFI leader Jean-Luc Melenchon demanded to know which arm of the intelligence service had said that. This latest wave of social unrest comes with tensions already running high over inflation, particularly soaring fuel prices and just seven months away from Frances presidential election, where opinion polls suggest far-right leader Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner. School staff targeted Since last week, pupils have staged protests outside schools over a range of grievances. They range from timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers to overheated classrooms during this years heatwaves. The protests have spread across the country from the Paris suburbs. Riot police have lined up against the students, and the force has launched internal probes after accusations of brutality against three pupils, said Interior Minister Laurent Nunez. University students also joined in Thursday (October 1, 2026), blocking access to around 30 campuses, a student union said. Among reports of school staff being targeted was one incident in the southern port city of Marseille when a school principal and his deputy were splashed with petrol. A journalist with TV channel M6 was attacked at the same school, local officials said. In the northwestern city of Nantes, firefighters had to intervene to extinguish a fire in the entrance of a high school following a gathering marked by violence towards staff, the regional education board said. Authorities reported violence near high schools, mainly in Nantes, blaming violent individuals who join the students to carry out acts of vandalism. In the northeastern city of Strasbourg, trams were ordered to halt to restrict the movements of rioters and demonstrators, the regional prefect said. Conditions unbearable Raphael, a 17-year-old who did not give his surname for fear of reprisals, was among the protesters outside a school in Strasbourg, where some used barriers to obstruct the nearby tramway tracks. There are 35 of us per classroom. With 35C in summer, its unbearable. There arent enough toilets, and there are water leaks in some rooms, Raphael said. The building is falling apart, the cafeteria is too small. Theres zero budget, zero resources, not enough supervisors, he said. Nearby, students took photos of themselves in front of burning rubbish bins, holding up the sign with their schools name ripped off the tram stop. In the southern city of Toulouse, hundreds of young people flooded the tram tracks, some toppling trash cans and starting fires, hurling projectiles or smashing bus shelters, AFP journalists said. In the northern city of Lille, AFP reporters saw young people wearing black hoodies destroy the glass of a bus stop. Firefighters intervened to put out the flames on upturned dustbins set on fire. The government has accused the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of encouraging the protests. But LFIs candidate for the 2027 presidential election, Jean-Luc Melenchon, said on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) that his party called for non-violent methods of struggle. In neighbouring Belgium, there were protests and damage at a handful of schools in the eastern city of Liege, police said.
