Part of preparing the pashmina for dyeing, Hussain says, is coating it with a layer of glue, after which, it becomes like paper. The shawls are then steamed for hours before they can take the dyes permanently. While the inaugural exhibition took place in Srinagar, Kadri is also planning to take it outside the Valley now.

headline: Wishy-washy statement, Election Commission in damage-control mode, says Congress
content: THE CONGRESS on Saturday termed the Election Commissions statement on concerns over SIR exercise as wishy-washy and said the poll panel was in a damage-control mode after causing massive damage to democracy. Congress MP and general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X: It (EC) has just issued a wishy-washy Press Note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility. Ramesh said the EC does not directly deny the () story or its findings. It makes a defensive attempt to downplay the same in paragraph 3(i) and 3(ii) but does not say that the allegations are baseless, said Ramesh in a statement on behalf of the Congress. WATCH | Election Commission Investigation: Ritika Chopra Answers All Your Questions On ECI Investigation Second, in the case of Goa [where 97 voters names had been deleted despite them being eligible for inclusion], after having been caught out, the EC has sheepishly stated that Form 6 has already been filled out for inclusion by 81 of the 97 deleted voters. To put this another way, you disenfranchise voters through a broken and corrupt system, and when caught, you say that they are being added back, said the Congress MP. In his third point, Ramesh said the EC statement seeks to justify the Commissions actions by appealing to the Order of the Supreme Court dated May 27, 2026. Citing the ECs decision to extend deadlines for voter registration in Delhi and Maharashtra, he asked what about the voters of Karnataka, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal. Do the voters of these and other states who were deleted due to one mans corruption not deserve answers? Ramesh also said the EC avoided questions regarding the deliberate targeting of Gen Z voters. The ECI has no answer for its targeted disenfranchisement, beginning mid-July 2026 through wholly illegal changes made to Form 6 (unseen and unapproved by Parliament) which placed an unfair burden on them to find and disclose their parents and/or grandparents details, read the statement. The Congress said the CEC thinks he can hide behind bureaucratise and protocol. He (Gyanesh Kumar) stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable. Congress head of media and publicity department Pawan Khera said: The ECIs press note is too lame, too little, too late. Khera said the EC statement still leaves several questions unanswered, even as it does not address the objections raised by two ECs on alterations in Form 6 for new voters. That objection was not resolved then And this mother of all objections has still not been addressed even after todays so-called unanimous meeting. So until the ECI answers this specific legal objection, no length of press notes, no claim of unanimity or any other clownery can save Gyanesh Kumar Guptas face, Khera said on X. It is still not too late for him. He should resign and turn approver, or prepare for jail, he said. Amid calls for the removal of the CEC, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday alleged that the poll panel chief was made in-charge of match-fixing Indias elections by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. WATCH | Sukhbir Singh Sandhu & Vivek Joshi: Who Are The 2 ECs Who Objected To SIR? Gandhi levelled this allegation after sharing a post from Kerala Congress, which cited media reports claiming that Kumar, a former IAS officer, had told a former Kerala chief secretary to contest on a BJP ticket after his retirement. First, Gyanesh Kumar then a serving IAS officer was used to recruit for the BJP Then Modi and Shah made him the umpire and put him in charge of match-fixing Indias elections, Gandhi alleged in a post on X. There was no immediate response from CEC Kumar on the claims made by Gandhi or Kerala Congress.

headline: CJI Surya Kant defends confidentiality of Collegium dissent at CNLU interaction
content: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has defended keeping dissenting views recorded within the Supreme Court Collegium out of the public domain, saying disclosure could put judges and candidates under consideration in a publicly compromised position. Justice Kant was responding to questions from law students during an open-house interaction at Chanakya National Law University (CNLU) in Patna on Friday evening, where he also spoke about the right to peaceful protest, financial support for first-generation lawyers, access to the profession and proposed changes to legal education. The interaction was reportedly organised at the initiative of CNLU students to provide a direct forum for their questions. Asked why dissenting opinions in the Collegium are formally minuted but not made public, the CJI said transparency had to operate within defined institutional boundaries, particularly where the dignity and professional reputation of individuals under consideration were concerned. Public disclosure, he said, could place candidates and judges in an untenable position. The interaction also saw students raise concerns over police action during campus protests. Responding to a question from student Vertika, Justice Kant reaffirmed the judiciarys commitment to protecting the fundamental freedom of peaceful protest and said constitutional courts would not look the other way when lawful student expression was stifled. On another issue concerning access to the legal profession, Justice Kant acknowledged the financial and professional difficulties faced by first-generation advocates entering practice. Referring to the Sarika Tyagi case, he advocated the creation of a dedicated professional assistance corpus, arguing that early financial support should be treated as a structural necessity rather than charity or patronage. Students also flagged rising tuition fees and inadequate scholarship support across national law universities. Justice Kant assured them that the issue of financial exclusion would be proactively addressed. A substantial part of the interaction focused on reforming legal education. CNLU Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Faizan Mustafa proposed replacing the existing five-year integrated law programme with four years of academic study followed by a mandatory, full-time year of court apprenticeship. The proposal would effectively eliminate the separate one-year bar practice requirement currently mandated for judicial service examinations in Bhumika Trust v. Union of India. Justice Kant responded favourably, describing the proposal as a new, welcome idea, and said it would integrate classroom learning with practical litigation experience rather than shorten legal education. Patna High Court Chief Justice and CNLU Chancellor Justice V. Kameswar Rao supported wider changes in practical legal training, calling for judicial clerkships at the High Courts and Supreme Court to become more competitive, prestigious and financially rewarding. He also highlighted the need for better stipends and research infrastructure to attract young legal talent to judicial work, and to make judicial service more competitive with opportunities at elite corporate lawfirms. Prof. Mustafa, while addressing the gathering, spoke about the practical impact of constitutional education. Referring to Article 21, he said students taught about constitutional liberties would later invoke those same rights while making arguments before the university administration, which he described as a source of professional satisfaction.

headline: 'Consequences': India warns Pakistan on terror after Sharif's 'act of war' threat
content: Hours after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif raked up the Kashmir issue and told the United Nations General Assembly that any attempt to alter the status of the Indus Waters Treaty would be considered an act of war, India reacted sharply Saturday, warning Pakistan of consequences over its export of terror, and drawing the world bodys attention to the killings and violence in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Islamabads treatment of minorities. Exercising Indias right to reply after Sharifs address, Petal Gahlot, First Secretary at Indias Permanent Mission to the UN, while referring to Sharif as the representative of Pakistan, rejected his allegations and underlined that Jammu and Kashmir was an integral and inalienable part of India and would remain so. She reminded the world how Pakistan harboured Osama bin Laden, the mastermind of the 9/11 attacks in New York, where the UNGA session was being held. This afternoon, the General Assembly heard some bizarre remarks from the representative of Pakistan. This happens just a fortnight after New York City and the world marked the 25th anniversary of the horrendous 9/11 terrorist attack Its mastermind, Osama bin Laden, was living right on the doorstep of the Pakistani Armys premier academy. They claim to uphold security during the day; they actually carry out terrorism at night The world knows how minorities are treated in Pakistan. No pious platitude can mislead it, she said. Responding to Sharifs remarks on Kashmir, Gahlot said, References were made to the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. This is an integral and inalienable part of my country and will always remain so. But if we must talk about Kashmir, let us turn our attention to Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Ask the people of Rawalakot about the wanton killings, the brutal violence and the denial of basic rights that they have long experienced. Elections to the so-called PoK Assembly were scheduled last month but violent clashes and security crackdowns, and the killing of dozens of protesters, led to the indefinite postponement of polling for several seats Earlier, Sharif, in his address to the UNGA, raised the Kashmir issue and said the people there had been waiting for the United Nations to fulfil its commitment to a plebiscite under its auspices. He alleged that there had been attempts to alter the legal status of Jammu and Kashmir through demographic changes and other measures. Speaking on the issue of Indus waters India put the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance in the wake of the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025 Sharif said that any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistans share of the waters of the Indus river system would be treated as an act of war. He again praised US President Donald Trumps resolute and visionary leadership and thanked him for his timely intervention in saving millions of lives in South Asia. In her response, Gahlot referred to cross-border terror emanating from Pakistan and to Indias Operation Sindoor after the terror attack in Pahalgam. At the heart of the issue is the long-standing practice of cross-border terrorism by Pakistan. We demonstrated last year that terrorists will have nowhere to run and nowhere to hide. Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised and continued. Terrorism by Pakistan will have consequences, she said. We are confident that this Assembly will recognise Pakistan and its policies for what they really are, not what its representative mendaciously projects it to be. Reiterating falsehoods year after year does not make them true. Pakistans terrorism, deceit and duplicity will neither benefit it nor the world, she said. India has made clear that the Indus Waters Treaty will be kept in abeyance until Pakistan credibly stops cross-border terrorism.

headline: Udhayanidhi welcomes T.N.'s decision on Navodaya schools, seeks special Assembly session to reiterate State's stand
content: Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Friday welcomed the governments decision to adhere to the established two-language policy in Tamil Nadu and not permit Navodaya schools in the State. Mr. Udhayanidhi also urged the State government to continue putting forth strong arguments in the ongoing case in the Supreme Court in support of Tamil Nadus position on establishing Navodaya schools. He also suggested convening a special session of the Tamil Nadu Assembly, if required, to adopt a resolution reiterating the States position on this matter. In a statement, Mr. Udhayanidhi said the State was not opposed to any language, including Hindi. Allowing each State to follow the language policy of its choice would further strengthen the unity of India, he said. During every difficult situation faced by our country, be it the Indo-China War, the Bangladesh Liberation War, the Kargil War or the Gujarat earthquake, Tamils have demonstrated their patriotism in no way less than people of other States. Therefore, merely saying we do not want the imposition of Hindi cannot be taken to mean that Tamils want to function as a separate country. There is no connection between learning Hindi and patriotism, he said. He also pointed out the State, which follows the two-language policy, is a leader in India across various sectors, including higher education enrolment and womens workforce participation. From producing Nobel laureates to leading scientists at ISRO, Tamils have achieved distinction without knowing Hindi, Mr. Udhayanidhi further said. Tamil Nadu has not suffered any setback because its people do not know Hindi. On the contrary, Tamil Nadu has achieved better development than other States and is a growth engine for India, he added.

headline: U.S. Treasury's Bessent plans to discuss AI and rare earths with China's He: report
content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent plans to discuss AI, trade, rare earths and economic issues when he meets with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York City this weekend, according to a source familiar with his plans. The discussions are significant because the U.S. and China are the two major forces driving development of advanced AI tools and the global adoption of the technology. Rare earths play a crucial role in the manufacturing of technology. Mr. Bessent and Mr. He will meet ahead of a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on September 24 in Washington. Mr. Bessent said in a statement that he expects the discussions to cover both open- and closed-weight models. Open-weight models are AI systems with publicly accessible core elements. Users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks. Chinese open-weight models are becoming more popular with U.S. companies because they can be cheaper than so-called closed-weight AI tools, such as those developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and other U.S. companies. Chinese AI models have even been used by the U.S. government. Reuters reported on Thursday (September 17, 2026) that a U.S. government website employed an AI model from a Chinese company to allow users to search proposed federal regulations even though the FBI accused the models developer, Alibaba, of malicious copying of Anthropics technology.

Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.

content: The Pentagon's public casualty database currently lists 18 US military deaths since the conflict began on February 28.

headline: Pachaiyappa's Trust gets new board members after election
content: After several years of delay amid litigation, the Pachaiyappas Trust has a new set of board members after elections were held earlier this month in pursuance of the order of the Madras High Court. The newly-constituted Board had its presidential elections subsequently and S. Jayachandran has been elected the President of the Pachaiyappas Trust Board. The Board also nominated S. Paramasivam as Financial Trustee and appointed R. Prabhaakaran as Member Secretary of the Board. The following members were elected to the Board: C. Saravanan and Sinora P.S. Ashok were elected under Members Senate University of Madras constituency; S. Jayachandran and R. Prabhaakaran were elected under the Pachaiyappas Trust College Council constituency; K. Hemanath and V. Ramanathan were elected under Approved Teachers constituency; and S. Paramasivam, Kaattur G. Sampath, and S. Suresh were elected under the Registered Graduate constituency. The Board has now officially commenced proceedings to oversee regular administrative activities.

headline: Students should remain connected with peers, faculty to enrich themselves, says Deputy High Commissioner of Bangladesh
content: Engineering students should always remain connected with their peer groups and faculty members as a lifelong exercise to enrich themselves in the competitive world, said Md. Alimuzzaman, Deputy High Commissioner of Bangladesh, in Chennai. In his inaugural address at the annual 17th edition techno management festival, Gravitas 26, which was organised by VIT at its campus in Vellore, Mr. Alimuzzaman, said that students should compete in a passionate manner in such technical festivals that will help them sharpen their engineering skills. Students should always think beyond classroom learning and competitions. They should acquire skills to contribute for the welfare of society and protect the environment, he said. The Deputy High Commissioner highlighted the importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing various problems in society. Students should use AI technology to solve human problems. Once they are able to do it, students can use AI technology as their business venture. In that way, the Gravitas Festival will help them to gain knowledge and expertise, he said. In his presidential address, G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT, said that modern technologies should be used as a developmental tool for the upliftment of the society rather than for destructive purposes. For example, drones are used more often on the battlefield than in agriculture. In this context, Bangladesh, despite its political upheavals, has been steadily progressing economically so far. The country (Bangladesh) is the largest exporter of textiles in the world, he said. The Chancellor noted that Bangladesh was able to progress economically better than its big neighbour, India, in terms of per capita income. In a decade, Bangladesh has a per capita income of $2,900, compared with India ($2,800) and Pakistan ($1,700), he said. The three-day fest fest will feature a total of 227 events, with more than 40,000 students expected to take part. Of these, 76 events have already been conducted, while the remaining 151 will be held during graVITas. The total prize pool is estimated at around Rs. 25 lakh in cash and Rs. 1.5 crore worth of prizes in kind. On the occasion, Pawan Vadapalli, Corporate Vice President and Global Head of Digital Business Services at HCLTech, and Prince Jayakumar, Executive Vice President and Global Head of Talent Acquisition at HCLTech, Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, were present.

headline: Four persons killed in road accidents in Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai
content: Four persons, including a father and daughter, were killed in two separate road accidents near Sholinghur and Chetpet towns in Ranipet and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday. Police said the deceased victims were identified as R. Suresh Babu, 48, S. Madhumita, 21, B. Sundaram, 33, and J. Thangaraj, 34. In the first incident, Suresh Babu, who works at a private firm, was going to his hometown in Tiruttani town with her daughter Madhumita on a two-wheeler from their house in Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh. Initial inquiry revealed that Babu and Madhumita were on their way to a function at a relatives house in Tiruttani. Babu lost control of the vehicle and hit a government bus in Pillanji village, near Sholinghur town, in Ranipet. The bus was proceeding towards Sholinghur town. In the impact, the duo were thrown from the two-wheeler. Immediately, passersby and other motorists shifted them to Government Taluk Hospital in Sholinghur, where doctors said they were brought dead. A case was registered. In a separate accident, Sundaram, 36, Thangaraj, 36, and Selvaraj, 36, from Kanthapalayam village near Arani, were returning to their hometown after dropping their friend K. Satyamurthy, 35, at Chennai airport. Sundaram, who was driving the car, lost control and hit a lorry coming from Salem on the VandavasiChetpet Main Road. The car got crushed in the impact and Sundaram was killed on the spot. Thangaraj died on the way to Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town, and Selvaraj is under treatment. Police arrested the lorry driver, K. Anbu, a native of Salem. Chetpet police registered a case, and further probe is underway.

headline: British era railway stations at Vellore Cantonment, Tiruvannamalai, Arakkonam, Vaniyambadi get bridges with lifts for commuters
content: The Southern Railway has completed the installation of lifts with newly built steel foot over bridge (FOBs) to connect platforms at British-era railway stations in Vellore Cantonment, Tiruvannamalai, Arakkonam, Ambur and Vaniyambadi Railway officials said that the construction of new bridges with lifts in identified railway stations on Chennai-Bengaluru and VillupuramTirupati routes is part of restoration work under the Station Redevelopment Project. These stations are also getting better passenger amenities like separate arrival and departure corridors, bright LED illumination, hassle-free access to platforms through lifts, and a rainwater harvesting system. Work to construct new steel bridges with lifts in these railway stations has been completed. The facility will help senior citizens and women safely travel between platforms in the railway station. The new lifts will be operated in the coming weeks, said a railway official. As per design, the new bridge has at least 20 staircases on each side along the service lane of the stretch. Each facility, on an average, costs around 1.5 crore including lifts (around 70 lakh). Shelters have been provided on the bridge with lights and CCTV cameras. Both sides of the bridge have been fenced to prevent any accidental fall on the track below the new facility. Ramps have been provided for persons with disabilities. Steel bridges with lifts will help to reach platforms to board express trains especially during rush hour. Adequate safety measures like power backup should be ensure for operating the new lifts, said B. Sugan, a commuter. Railway officials said that installation of lifts remains the major component of the project. Each lift, on an average, can accommodate at least 10 persons. Unlike escalators, lifts are cost effective and occupy less space. It also consumes less electricity. Tucked between major railway junctions like Arakkonam and Jolarpet, most of these railway stations are located along Palar river on Chennai-Bengaluru-Coimbatore route. On an average, each railway station where new lifts with steel bridges are installed handles over 150 trains, mostly express and passenger trains, every day. More than 3,000 commuters board trains at each of these railway stations daily. At present, bridges with lifts are available at railway stations in Katpadi (escalators and lifts) and Ambur on the route. Railway officials said that the total distance of each bridge in these railway stations could not be the same because of the variation in number of platforms in these railway stations. For example, Walajah railway station has a distance of 83 metres, covering seven platforms whereas the railway station at Gudiyatham is only 12 metres with three platforms.

headline: Verification of community certificate can be done even after retirement: HC
content: Madras high court has reiterated that community certificate of an employee can be scrutinised even after the employee has retired and that such verification is not barred merely because the certificate or appointment dates back to before 1995.The law is settled that protecting service benefits merely because the employee has attained superannuation is akin to allowing the thief to retain stolen property and perpetrating constitutional fraud, Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy said citing a judgment passed by a full bench of the court. As such, the matter is no longer res integra (untouched), the judge added.The court made the observations while dismissing two petitions moved by A Jegannathan who was appointed as a Mazdoor at the Chennai Port Trust and retired as a section superintendent in 2013. The appoint was made on the basis of a Scheduled Tribe community certificate issued to the petitioner in 1980.On retirement, in view of pending proceedings relating to the verification of his community certificate, the petitioner was granted only a provisional pension, and the full pension, gratuity, and all other terminal benefits payable to the petitioner were withheld prompting him to approach the court.Refusing any relief, the court pointed out that the vigilance report and independent verification reports of all the authorities, on the basis of the overwhelming positive evidence, had been shown that the petitioner did not fall under Schedule Tribe category. The petitioner started his line of litigation from 1985 and successfully stalled the obvious till 2021, and the same can no longer be permitted. It is a settled legal position that the principles of natural justice are not a straitjacket formula and will depend on the facts and circumstances of the case, and fraud is an anathema to the principle, the court said.

headline: Chennai homebuyers look beyond core city as suburbs gain ground, plots emerge as favourite
content: beyond the citys core. Metro connectivity, industrial corridor development, arterial road development (Outer Ring Road expansion and upcoming Peripheral Ring Road), coupled with relatively affordable price points, are creating new growth corridors. Developers said that there is a 50 % growth in the size of plots purchased by customers - mainly IT employees.According to Colliers Homebuying Sentiment Survey 2026, the strong preference for plots stands out in the city-wise property-type data. Among the respondents surveyed, plots/land accounted for 90% of preferences, compared with 10% for 2/2.5-BHK apartments.Developers said that suburban and peripheral locations continue to offer contiguous land parcels allowing developers to cater to the growing demand beyond apartment projects. Residential activity is supported by ongoing infrastructure upgrades, enhancing connectivity and improving social amenities.In the North aras such as Madhavaram, Ponneri, Minjur, in the south - Padur, Kelamabakkam, Mambakkam, Guduvanchery, Vandalur and West localities including Sriperumbudur, Thirumazhisai, Kuthambakkam are seeing good traction.In the south, localities benefit from their proximity to key office micro-markets along the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) stretch, Pallavaram Thoraipakkam Road (PTR), and Grand Southern Trunk (GST) Road. Industrial and logistics growth are supporting large-scale township projects, planned developments, and middle-income housing in western and northern peripheral areas such as Sriperumbudur, Oragadam, and surrounding localities. Madhavaram in the northern part of the city is also one of the prominent Transit-oriented Development (TOD) nodes in the upcoming Chennai Metro Phase II project, said Vimal Nadar, National Director and Head of Research, Colliers India.Viswajit Naveen, Managing Director of Navins, said that there is a 50 % increase in the size of plots. Earlier, many used to buy in 600 sqft plots as an investment, but werent able to build a proper house due to size constraints. Now many are opting for 1,500 sqft so that they can construct a house with some frontage, he explained.Meanwhile, apartments are also seeing good traction. According to Anarocks H1 2026 Real Estate Homebuyer Survey, Chennai homebuyers are preferring 3BHKs. Chennai is among the markets where 3BHK demand crossed 50%, highlighting the continued preference for spacious homes. Developer credibility, timely delivery, construction quality and customer reputation have emerged as key considerations, particularly as buyers increasingly enter projects at the launch stage.

headline: GCC to desilt Mambalam Canal ahead of NEM
content: Greater Chennai Corporation will desilt the 5.7km-long Mambalam Canal at a cost of 46.7 lakhs ahead of the northeast Monsoon.The civic body has floated tenders and the contractor will be finalised soon. The tender specs entail contractor to deepen the waterway by four feet and it will cover key spots including T Nagar, West Mambalam, Nandanam and Saidapet.GCC will remove silt and remove blockages in culverts at Venkatnaraya Road and CIT Nagar to make waterflow faster. The project also will widen the outfall point of the canal in Adyar River next to YMCA.The contractor has to deploy multiple robotic excavators starting from Valluvar Kottam. Around 300m will be cleared. The canal is also the most narrowest at this spot at just three metres, and works will simultaneously proceed at Bazullah Road and Venkatnarayana Road. Officials said metro too will aid in desilting the stretch where they are constructing the Panagal Park-Nandanam underground line.Officials said about nine encroachments still exist on the canal, particularly, a temple across the Theagaraya Road part of the canal. Notices will be issued, an official from the Teynampet zone said.Officials said the plan is to increase the carrying capacity to 500 cusecs from the existing 200 cusecs. Earlier, the flow capacity was at 138 cusecs and they removed some encroachments in MGR Salai and GN Chetty Road which pushed to flow to 200. Still major works are yet to be done, the official said.The smart city CAG report placed in the Tamil Nadu assembly two weeks ago flagged that 59.4 crore was spent to restore the Mambalam Canal and yet, works fully werent completed and the civic body too did not penalise the contractor.

headline: Drone Hits Cooling Tower At Russia's Nuclear Plant, Says UN Nuclear Watchdog
content: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) "has been informed that the cooling tower of a reactor unit of the Kursk Nuclear Power Plant in the Russian Federation was hit by a drone early on Thursday".

headline: 'Higher Education Dept. will prioritise recruiting teachers to courses with high student enrolment'
content: The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department will prioritise filling up vacancies in those programmes with high student enrolment at State-run universities, Higher Education Secretary Dheeraj Kumar told the University of Madras (UoM) Senate on Friday. The Department has sought department-wise lists of vacancies in all State-run universities, along with the teacher-student ratio, Mr. Kumar said in response to queries raised by professors at the Senate meeting that he chaired. The government has policy clarity now, and this will be done. We want to give priority to such departments so that when there are crucial shortages, they get addressed immediately through regular faculty intake, he clarified. S.S. Sundaram, Head, Department of History, said the 170-year-old university had a sanctioned strength of 540 faculty members, but less than 175 were employed. No recruitment drive was held to fill up the vacancies for the past 12 years and more than 20 departments were functioning with a single faculty member. Pointing out that the university had presented a deficit budget to the Senate, V. Chandra Kumar, Head, Department of Library and Information Science, said 77 crore had been pulled out of its corpus fund earlier this year to settle the terminal benefits of retired employees, thereby diminishing the fund to a little over 300 crore. He sought additionality grant from the government to meet day-to-day expenses of salary and pension benefits of the staff and faculty. In response, the Higher Education Secretary said the UoM, as an autonomous body, should explore avenues to increase its income. He invited the members to write to the Finance Officer or the Registrar with ideas. In case of a shortfall, however, the government will come forward to solve it, he said. C. Murugan, Head, Department of Sanskrit, sought a one-time grant of 500 crore to bail the University out of its financial hardships. He also raised the issue of inordinate delay in extending benefits of the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) to teachers in universities. Redundant process E. Murugan, Head, Department of Physical Chemistry, said the CAS files go through several stages of approval, even though the competent authorities have stamped them. The process was redundant. The Higher Education Secretary said past experiences were fraught with orders of recovery, which werent pleasant for either side. He said that the process has begun in right earnest and will be expedited. S. Santhosh Baboo, Principal, DG Vaishnav College, wanted the university to expedite the process of extending affiliation to colleges. D. Anand, Associate Professor, Department of Botany, Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College, wanted the government to implement the Tamil Nadu Assured Pension Scheme soon and place a proposal to the effect in the next Syndicate meeting.

headline: After a year's delay, foot-overbridge work begins on Velachery Main Road
content: Commuters stepping out of the Velachery MRTS station wont have to walk 800m along the busy 100-Ft Road to cross safely, or jump the median braving speeding vehicles. The Chennai Metropolitan Development Plan (CMDP) wing of state highways department has finally started work on a foot-overbridge (FOB) near Nalli Silks on Velachery Main Road after a year of delay.The 14-crore FOB is being built as a fully enclosed structure with escalators, lifts and gently inclined staircases to make it accessible to elderly people, children and persons with disabilities. Officials said the project was delayed after bidders quoted rates higher than the tender amount. The proposal was then placed before the Commissionerate of Tenders (CoT) for approval, which delayed the launch of work.Geetha Ganesh, secretary of the AGS Colony Residents Welfare Association in Velachery, said the FOB would provide a much-needed safe link between west and east Velachery. With a school and several commercial establishments nearby, students and residents are forced to cross the busy road at great risk. Accidents have also occurred at this junction, she said.A traffic police officer posted in the area said violations such as wrong-side driving, jaywalking, and signal jumping continued despite measures including median barricading, personnel deployment, and periodic removal of encroachments. Better coordination between the highways department and other agencies, along with greater civic discipline, is needed to prevent such violations, the officer said.Palanivel, chief engineer, state highways, said, The delay was due to pending approval from other departments. Now that construction has started, the FOB is expected to be completed by the end of this year.

headline: 17-year-old boy kills drunk dad for attacking his mother
content: A 17-year-old boy killed his father with a log after the drunk man attacked his mother at Periya Karumbur near Baluchettychatram.The deceased, Kumar, a daily wage labourer, lived at Mariamman Koil Street in Periya Karumbur village. He had two wives, Vanitha, 43, and Ramila, 36. Though both families lived on the same street, Kumar usually stayed with his first wife, Vanitha.Around 7.30pm on Thursday, a drunk Kumar picked a quarrel with Ramila, saying she bought a moped without informing him. On seeing Kumar attack his mother, their 17-year-old son, an ITI student, intervened. He picked up a log and struck his father repeatedly on the head, arms, and legs.Kumar was taken to Kancheepuram Government Headquarters Hospital and later shifted to Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital. Following a complaint from Vanitha, Baluchettychatram police registered a case on Friday morning and detained the boy.Meanwhile, Kumar succumbed to his injuries. Police said the case would be altered to murder. The boy was sent to a juvenile observation home in Chengalpet. Further investigation is on.

headline: Collapsed complaint mechanism, power generation deficit, overstretched distribution network cause frequent power cuts in Chennai
content: Hundreds of people taking to the streets to vent frustration over frequent and long power cuts, particularly at night, was not common even in the peak summer months in previous years. Yet, it has become the order of the day in Sept this year.Hardly any neighbourhood is spared from unscheduled power cuts and fluctuations since July. Residents of Washermenpet and Royapuram were the latest to join the series of protests. On Thursday night, they thronged the local section offices and quarrelled with officers. The problem lies in both generation and distribution. Making matters worse, the grievance redressal mechanism has collapsed, meaning consumers are suffering on all three crucial aspects.Generation fumblesThe extended summer has caught the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation (TNPDCL) off guard. The unprecedented surge in power demand, limited generation from the states own plants, and indecisiveness over alternative arrangements have led to the sorry state of affairs in the state. While releasing the white paper on the energy department in July, electricity and law minister R Nirmalkumar said the previous DMK govt bought high-cost power through short-term agreements. Two months later, TNPDCL has again opted for short-term agreements and purchases from exchanges, as no new long or medium-term agreements have been signed.S Neelakanta Pillai, a retired TNEB engineer, said the state-owned thermal plants were generating power well below their installed capacity. The 800MW supercritical thermal plant NCTPS Stage III has been producing power to the extent of 46%, whereas both the 600MW units of Stage II are also generating power at 42% and 46%, he said.TN power generation corporation officials said some plants could not achieve their full potential as they were due for annual maintenance. They still generate power to tide over the crisis. The maintenance is necessary to ensure their availability next summer, said the official.Distribution glitchesThe constant excuse given for power cuts in Chennai and suburban neighbourhoods is failure of the distribution network, including damage to underground cables and tripping of feeders.Poor coordination of NPDCL officials with contractors of other agencies such as MAWS and GCC, despite multiple interagency meetings, also led to outages in several pockets of the city. TNPDCL recently lodged a police complaint against Torrent Gas for damaging an underground cable, which left Avadi and Pattabiram residents in darkness. The electricity minister on Friday said the officers had been directed to lodge police complaints against agencies that cause damage to TNPDCL properties.Complaint mechanism defunctMinnagam, the centralised call centre set up to receive electricity-related complaints from across the state via the dedicated phone number 94987-94987, is the principal channel through which consumers report electricity complaints. But it often falls dead, making it impossible for consumers to report grievances.Minnagam is equipped to take at least 60 calls at a time and forward the complaints to the section concerned for quick redressal.The recently revived Fuse Off Call system for each assistant engineers office also failed to bridge the gap, as all numbers had to be replaced after a dispute with the telecom provider. The consumers are now left in the dark about the new numbers.TNPDCL has not publicised the new numbers. It should have sent an SMS to all consumers about the change. At least, rerouting calls to the new numbers would have helped consumers, said Satish Galley of Semmanchery. T Sadagopan of Pattabiram, a consumer activist, said, TNPDCLs WhatsApp chatbot is still at a nascent stage and does not respond well.However, minister Nirmalkumar said the power crisis in Tamil Nadu is well under control compared to states such as Punjab, where outages last up to 14 hours. For consumer grievance redressal, we are developing an advanced AI tool, and it will be launched in two months, he said.

headline: Seven more girls testify against granite baron Veeramani
content: At least seven more minor girls have testified against the arrested granite baron R Veeramani, 84, stating that he had exploited and sexually abused them over the years.A senior police officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, said police teams had identified the victims and recorded their statements before the special court trying Pocso cases.The Pocso special court judge, Padma Shanmugasundaram, sent Veeramani to a three-day police custody on Thursday. The interrogation was completed by Friday evening.Veeramani, chairperson of Gem Group and head of Gem Granites, was arrested on Aug 29 after a USB drive containing a video clip that purportedly showed a juvenile girl being sexually assaulted by him in Oct 2025.The case came to public knowledge after the special court refused to close it and instead ordered further investigation. A special team led by assistant commissioner Rajalakshmi was formed following the courts direction. Police said they identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019. Her statement was subsequently recorded before a court trying Pocso cases. Along with Veeramani, police also arrested Shanti, 60, and her husband Mahendra Simhan, 63, in connection with the case.Meanwhile, Child Welfare Committee (CWC) member Sheela Jayanthi said the committee was yet to receive a report from the city police. Sheela Jayanthi said, We are closely watching the developments in the case and discussing them with the District Child Protection officers. As the girl was sexually abused when she was a minor and is now a major, there is no need for intervention by CWC officials.

headline: Anbil Mahesh questioned for 8 hours by CCB
content: Former school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi was questioned by the Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) on Friday over allegations that more than 100 crore was collected from private school managements for govt approvals when the DMK was in power.Anbil walked into the CCB office around 10.45am and walked out more than eight hours later. He told reporters that officials asked him 246 questions and that he had answered them all. He said he had denied all the allegations.Officials said the CCB would continue to examine the seized documents, financial records, and electronic evidence to establish the role of each person connected with the case.The case was registered over a complaint alleging that private school managements were promised permanent recognition, upgradation, DTCP approval, and other govt clearances for a consideration. B T Arasakumar, who ran an unrecognised association of private schools, was arrested along with his two associates in connection with the case. After their arrests, at least 177 private schools lodged complaints, saying bribes were demanded and paid when DMK was in power.The CCB registered a case against Anbil under the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act on Sept 16, and also raided his premises in Chennai and Tiruchi. Officials said they seized 118 items, including property documents, bank records, mobile phones, laptops, computers, pen drives and other electronic devices during the raids.Subsequently, Anbil was issued a summons under Section 35(3) of the BNSS requiring him to appear before the CCB for questioning.Investigators questioned him about his alleged links with Arasakumar and other accused persons, his interactions with private-school managements, the collection of money described in the investigation as party funds, and related bank accounts and financial transactions. Questions were also based on documents and electronic evidence seized during the searches.

headline: 31 Conditions On Rahul Gandhi's Indore Event, Rajiv Gandhi Killing Cited
content: Congress city president Chintu Choukse was handed the conditions along with police permission on Thursday, after the party fulfilled five conditions stipulated by the Indore Development Authority for using its ground opposite Regional Park.

headline: Udhayanidhi Stalin defends Tamil Nadu's two-language policy, opposes Navodaya schools
content: A day after Supreme Court asked Tamil Nadu govt to change its mindset against Hindi and Navodaya Schools, leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Friday said Tamil Nadu was not against any language and did not function as a separate country. He said the state did not want Navodaya schools and, if necessary, a special assembly session could be convened to pass a resolution against them.Tamil Nadu follows a two-language policy and has remained at the forefront in several areas, including higher education enrolment and womens participation in the workforce. Without learning Hindi, many Tamilians have carved a niche for themselves, from winning Nobel Prizes to becoming eminent scientists at ISRO. This clearly indicates that Tamil Nadu is not at a disadvantage because of not knowing or learning Hindi, Udhayanidhi said in a statement.Citing the SCs recent observations in connection with Navodaya schools, Udhayanidhi said the TVK govt was also following the states two-language policy and had rejected the three-language policy.The seed of the two-language policy was sown by Perarignar Anna (C N Annadurai) in this (Tamil) land. Cutting across political lines, we all should come together to uphold the states policy in the SC and stop the Navodaya schools that impose the three-language policy, he said.

headline: No support for any party in Assembly bypoll: PMK
content: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Friday said his party will not support any alliance in the upcoming Madurantakam (SC) and Dharapuram (SC) Assembly bypolls. "I would like to inform you that after consultations with the state executives of the PMK and the executives of the districts comprising the two constituencies, it has been decided not to support any party," he said in a statement. The decision of the party comes at a time when the PMK and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam have exhibited closeness on several occasions since the election results on May 4. While the PMK's floor leader Sowmiya Anbumani and Dr. Anbumani Ramadoss met with the Water Resources minister and TVK general secretary, N Anand, to discuss various water projects, Dr. Anbumani also was seen playing badminton recently with PWD minister, Aadhav Arjuna. The announcement is seen as a blow to the prospects of the AIADMK, especially in the Madurantakam seat, in which PMK reportedly has a strong support base.

headline: Massive Fire At Jaipur's UNESCO-Recognised Parkota Bazar
content: The fire started around 7 am, and there were no casualties. During daytime hours, the market is normally packed with thousands of people and many foreign tourists; had the fire occurred then, it could have caused major loss of life.

headline: 'We Are Not Intimidated': Macron Warns Of Growing Russian 'Hybrid' Threat Across Europe
content: Macron said France would continue supporting Ukraine despite the growing threats and warned that attacks linked to Russia would not go unanswered.

headline: Funds will be released in a couple of days for Malaysia-based PhD scholar: Minister
content: The govt will release the pending scholarship funds within a couple of days for Malaysia-based dalit PhD scholar Bharathidasan, who is pursuing his doctoral studies under the Annal Ambedkar Overseas Higher Education Scholarship Scheme, assured social justice minister Vanni Arasu. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the observation of the death anniversary of late social reformer Rettamalai Srinivasan at Tindivanam in Villupuram district on Friday, the minister appealed to one and all not to politicise the issue.He said the social welfare and adi dravidar welfare department had already submitted a report outlining the assistance provided so far. The tuition fees for the current academic year, along with other expenses, have already been disbursed. The remaining financial allocation will be transferred in a couple of days. The govt is committed to supporting the education so that he can complete his studies successfully, he said.Referring to Bharathidasan as his younger brother, the minister affirmed that the govt stands firmly by dalit students to safeguard their educational aspirations. Highlighting the govts achievements in supporting dalit students studying abroad, he shared details comparing past and current statistics. He noted that out of 437 applicants received this year, 365 students have been sent abroad, with a total budgetary allocation of 131 crore. Last year, although 601 out of 609 applicants were selected, only 181 students were sent abroad under an allocated budget of 84.89 crore, he said.The minister noted that after assuming charge, he pursued the matter with the finance secretary to secure additional funding, breaking past benchmarks. He dismissed charges levelled by the opposition leaders, including DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin and appealed to them not to use the issue for political gain.

headline: Tiger trapped in Gudalur to reach Chennai today
content: A 12-year-old male tiger that was caught on Friday morning for the suspected killing of two people in Gudalur, Nilgiris district, is being transported to Arignar Anna Zoological Park at Vandalur in Chennai.Forest officials said the tiger will reach the rehabilitation centre at Vandalur zoo in the wee hours of Saturday. Based on an examination and recommendation of technical guidance committee constituted, in accordance with the guidelines of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), it has been determined that the tigers canine teeth have worn down and it is in a weakened physical condition. Therefore, it has been found that there are no possibilities of releasing it back into the wild, a release said.The last man-eating tiger that was relocated to Vandalur was MTRT 37 in 2025. The adult tiger had killed a 65-year-old tribal woman.This tiger was trapped in a cage near Gudalur in the early hours of Friday, after a 28-day search operation by forest officials, involving significant manpower, camera traps, cages, kumki elephants and drone cameras. It was taken to Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, where it was confirmed to be behind the deaths of M Balakrishnan on Aug 9 and K Ravikumar on Aug 21. During the operation, two leopards were trapped and subsequently released back in the reserve forest area.

headline: PMK not to extend support to any party in Madurantakam, Dharapuram bypolls: Anbumani
content: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss announced that the party will not support any political party in the upcoming byelections for the Madurantakam (SC) and Dharapuram (SC) assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu.In a statement on Friday, Anbumani said that PMK had earlier announced that it would not field candidates in the bypolls. Subsequently, extensive consultations were held with state executives and district functionaries overseeing the two constituencies to decide on the partys stance, he said. Following detailed discussions, the party unanimously decided to remain neutral and refrain from extending support to any political party for the bypolls, he said.The announcement has come as a setback to AIADMK, which had allied with PMK in the recently concluded assembly elections. The support of PMK was particularly crucial in Madurantakam, a region where it wields considerable influence. With PMK abstaining from the polls, votes of the party cadres may be split.Two days ago, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami and AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran had expressed hope that PMK would support the AIADMK candidates.

headline: Governor Arlekar approves 12 Tamil Nadu bills, seeks clarification on private universities
content: Governor R V Arlekar has given assent to 12 of the 13 bills tabled in the recently concluded assembly session, while seeking clarification on certain sections of Private Universities Bill.Private Universities Bill reduced the land and endowment fund requirements for private education institutions to become private universities. The bill faced opposition from legislators of some opposition parties, who said that it would lead to commercialisation of education institutions.Arlekar, according to govt sources, sought an explanation on certain sections of the bill and reserved it without taking a further decision. Governors office has hinted that he would forward the bill to Presidents office for her nod.The approved bills include the one empowering Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC) to recruit personnel for urban local bodies aimed at establishing a common mechanism and transparent recruitment framework along with Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Bill, Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation (Amendment) Bill, Tamil Nadu Payment of Salaries (Amendment) Bill and Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax (second amendment) Bill.

headline: Assad-era Syrian official jailed for 60 years by U.S. court
content: A former Syrian government official who headed the Damascus Central Prison under ousted President Bashar al-Assad and was convicted of torture by a U.S. federal jury has been sentenced to 60 years in prison by a U.S. judge, federal prosecutors said. Samir Ousman Alsheikh, 74, was charged in 2024 and convicted in March this year on three counts of torture and one count of conspiracy to commit torture for his involvement in the abuse of prisoners at Adra Prison in Damascus. Alsheikh was also convicted of lying to U.S. immigration authorities about his commission of the crimes, fraudulently obtaining a green card and attempting to naturalise as a U.S. citizen, the U.S. Department of Justice said. Thursdays (September 18) sentence was handed down by U.S. District Judge Hernan Vera in Los Angeles. Prosecutors said Alsheikh ordered subordinates to inflict physical and mental pain on prisoners to deter opposition to Mr Assads government and was sometimes personally involved in such incidents. The U.S. Justice Department said Alsheikh, who held positions in the state security apparatus, was the highest-ranking former member of Mr Assads government to be tried and convicted in person outside Syria so far. Alsheikhs legal team had asked for a five-year sentence. In March, they said they were disappointed by his conviction. Alsheikh, who headed Adra Prison from 2005 to 2008, had previously pleaded not guilty. Khaled Abdul Malek, a witness in the case who was detained and tortured at Adra prison, said in a written statement shared with reporters that the sentencing showed that even when justice is delayed, it will always come. This trial is not the end, but the first step on the road toward accountability and justice for everyone whose hands have been stained with the blood of innocent people, he said. Syrian rebels put an end to more than 50 years of rule by the Assad family in late 2024 following a lightning advance. Hundreds of thousands died in a civil war that lasted more than a decade, unleashed a global refugee crisis, and left cities across the country in ruins. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, a former al-Qaeda commander, took over after Mr Assads ouster and has worked to improve ties with the West. Last month, a Syrian court sentenced Mr Assad, who resides in Russia, in absentia to death after convicting him of crimes including killings, torture, and arbitrary arrest during the countrys war.

headline: Kancheepuram admin denies release certificate to deceased irula woman's family
content: The Kancheepuram district administration has refused to issue a release certificate to the family of a 44-year-old irula tribal woman, Thenmozhi, who died along with her newborn during childbirth at a worksite in Vellaicate village on Sept 8.A release certificate recognises that a person has been rescued from bonded labour. It enables survivors to access central and state welfare schemes and financial assistance aimed at rehabilitation and preventing re-bondage. The revenue department recently recognised the certificate as valid identity proof for accessing services through e-seva centres.The rejection of the RC came despite the district legal services authority (DLSA) recommending that revenue authorities issue the document after an inquiry confirmed that the woman and her family were held as bonded labourers. DLSA identified key indicators of bonded labour such as advance payment given to the family, long working hours, low wages and restrictions on movement.We found elements of bonded labour during our inquiry. Based on our findings, we communicated to the sub-collector recommending him to issue the certificate, said an official.However, Kancheepuram sub-collector T Bhuvanesh Ram responded that the woman and her family were not bonded labourers. Asked why the certificate was rejected, Bhuvanesh said the inquiry report had been submitted to higher authorities and its findings could not be disclosed.According to a complaint filed by the womans husband, Anand, the family had taken an advance payment of 20,000 from the employer Arumugam. Anand, Thenmozhi, their daughter Kaviya and son-in-law Muthu allegedly worked from 7am until late evening and lived in a tarpaulin shed at the worksite for six months.Anand alleged that Arumugam refused to let him take Thenmozhi to hospital when she went into labour, telling him not to leave without settling the advance. When Anand returned to the shed around 2pm on Sept 8, he found Thenmozhi and the newborn dead.There are sufficient indicators to establish that the victim and her family were bonded labourers. Officials are not accepting it. This is shocking, said a member of the one-stop crisis team.

headline: US-based Walgreens enters India, to set up global capability centre in Chennai
content: headquartered Walgreens India Private Limited to establish its first-ever global capability centre (GCC) at DLF Downtown complex, Taramani. The initiative is expected to generate 250 jobs.The MoU was signed in the presence of chief minister C Joseph Vijay at the secretariat, industries minister S Keerthana, chief secretary M Sai Kumar, additional chief secretary for the industries, investment promotion and commerce S Vijaykumar and senior bureaucrats. The development comes a day after Vijay returned from his maiden foreign trip to London to attract investments.The state govt said the proposed investment would deliver an economic boost to Tamil Nadu by creating 250 high-value, specialised employment opportunities in its first year. With provisions for future expansion, the centre will generate skilled job opportunities for local talent across technology, healthcare services and operational domains. It would accelerate the states industrial growth, said a statement from govt. Securing Walgreens first Indian facility highlights TNs growing reputation as a preferred destination for multinational corporations and foreign investors, govt said. The development directly supports the state govts targeted policy to attract high-value capability centres, strengthening the local digital ecosystem, driving innovation and reinforcing the states position as a premier global hub for technology and business services, said the release. During the interaction, Vijay appealed to the representatives of the US firm to provide high-value jobs to youngsters from Tier II and Tier III cities in TN.

headline: EPS leaves out Velumani, Shanmugam from AIADMK star campaigners list
content: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami has left out senior leaders S P Velumani and C Ve Shanmugam from the partys list of 40 star campaigners submitted to ECI for the Oct 6 bypolls.This comes after Palaniswami expressed displeasure that Velumani and Shanmugam were functioning as a separate entity within and outside the assembly. He has kept them away from key party activities.Velumani was in charge of Tirupur district, where Dharapuram assembly segment is located, during the April 23 polls, and Shanmugam is an influential AIADMK leader in northern TN. Former ministers K P Anbazhagan, P Thangamani and K C Veeramani, along with several other functionaries associated with their camp, were left out of the list too.The composition of the star campaigners list suggests that Palaniswami has not sought to broaden the role of the dissident camp in the bypoll campaign.

headline: IIT Madras, SCU set up high-altitude atmospheric observatory in Ladakh
content: altitude atmospheric observatory in Ladakh Chennai: Researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras), in collaboration with Sindhu Central University (SCU), have established a high-altitude atmospheric observatory at SCUs campus in Khaltse, Ladakh, at an elevation of 3,450m, to study air chemistry and climate processes in the Himalayan region.The observatory uses a Proton Transfer Reaction Mass Spectrometer (PTR-MS) to measure volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the air online and in real time, even at concentrations of parts per trillion. It means it can detect one molecule of a VOC among one trillion air molecules. A Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer (SMPS) measures the number and sizes of aerosol particles. A black carbon instrument is also being installed, with more advanced instruments planned.The idea is to understand how the ecosystem responds to human activities, and determine whether the changes we observe are driven by human influence, natural processes or a combination of both, said Prof Sachin S Gunthe, Centre for Atmospheric and Climate Sciences (CACS), department of civil engineering, IIT Madras.VOCs drive regional atmospheric chemistry, and understanding how this chemistry differs in the Himalayas could reveal its implications for the region, he said. The observatory will study pristine Himalayan air chemistry, aerosol formation and growth, and long-range transport of pollutants. It will also provide insights into climate change impacts on the fragile Himalayan ecosystem, CACS said in an online post.The whole idea is to start better understanding the Himalayan climate, Gunthe said, adding that the research would examine how climate affects atmospheric chemistry and how atmospheric chemistry, in turn, influences climate.Aerosols are tiny particles suspended in the atmosphere that can influence cloud formation, sunlight reaching the Earth and rainfall. Measurements from the observatory will help scientists investigate these processes and their links to regional climate.The facility is among Indias northernmost measurements of its kind and one of the countrys highest-altitude atmospheric composition studies. Gunthe said its location near Kargil, further north than existing Himalayan research sites such as Hanle, offered a distinct advantage.Globally, high-altitude atmospheric research facilities include the Sphinx Observatory at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps, at 3,580 metres, and the Testa Grigia Observatory in the western Alps on the Italian-Swiss border, at 3,480 metres. The Ladakh facility will add atmospheric observations from a high-altitude site in the tropics.

headline: Pakistan court blocks expulsion of Afghan medical college students
content: A Pakistan court blocked on Friday (September 18, 2026) an order by the country's medical board for dozens of Afghans studying to be doctors to be expelled from colleges and universities and sent home. "The Lahore High Court has extended the stay order preventing the expulsion of over a hundred Afghan medical students from medical colleges until the next hearing," a Lahore court decision seen by AFP said. Pakistan orders medical institutions to expel Afghan students, halt fresh admissions The judge, Justice Khalid Ishaq, did not fix a date for the next hearing. Earlier this month, the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) said in a letter to academic institutes that no "form of facilitation of Afghan nationals is permitted for the current academic session". The PMDC letter to college deans said: "Afghans previously enrolled in medical or dental programs in Pakistan are required to return to Afghanistan." The letter, a copy of which was seen by AFP, did not say on whose authority the medical council was acting, but said: "The matter is of highest priority and relates to national policy directions." Speaking after Friday's (September 18, 2026) hearing, final-year Lahore student Mubin Ulfati told AFP: "We were predicting this, because in a view of human rights, education is our primary right, so we were 100% sure that this was going to happen." The 24-year-old, who had just returned from a hospital shift in July when he was given 24 hours to leave the country, added: "Everything is still in a desperate situation, and we don't know what to do." A similar court petition has already been rejected by officials in Balochistan province, while another is under way in Sindh. Relations between neighbours Pakistan and Afghanistan have plummeted since the Taliban government's return to power in Kabul in 2021, and escalated into weeks of war earlier this year. More than 2.5 million Afghans -- many who spent decades living as refugees in Pakistan -- have been expelled or left voluntarily over the past three years, according to UN data, as part of a deportation drive by Islamabad. Human Rights Watch urged authorities to reverse the PMDC order, highlighting the plight of women who are banned from studying in Afghanistan. Amnesty International slammed the move as "discriminatory and arbitrary". Among the Lahore petitioners was a 23-year-old who was just days away from finishing her second-year studies when she was told she must "go back and leave everything". A judge suspended the expulsion order at the provincial level on September 11, but the student said her records have already been expunged from the university's online platform. 'Never give up' The undergraduate, who requested anonymity for security reasons, was forced to end her medical studies in Afghanistan after Taliban authorities banned women from universities. She said she was one of about 20 Afghan women out of 30,000 applicants to win a scholarship in Pakistan. "I will never give up... I learned from this journey that sadness doesn't bring anything," she told an AFP journalist in Kabul by phone. Asad Jamal, one of several lawyers representing the students in Lahore, criticised the PMDC orders, which he said failed to provide medics with "any opportunity to be heard". The PMDC did not respond to AFP's request for comment. Mr. Jamal said even if the students lose their Lahore petition, the case could still be taken to Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court. Some Afghan medics had been deported even before the PMDC order, such as a fourth-year student who tried unsuccessfully for more than a year to renew his visa. "We are only students. We are not political people," said the medic, who was specialising in ophthalmology and requested anonymity. The 33-year-old was pulled out of the operating theatre and expelled within two days. "Please, let us finish our studies," he said. "We will finish, and we will go back to our country."

headline: Tamil Nadu set to get back 40 vacant super speciality seats
content: After surrendering 151 unfilled super speciality seats for the second round of All India Quota counselling, Tamil Nadu is set to get 40 of them back. Nearly 100 in-service candidates are waiting for these seats and new applications are expected to be invited soon as the Centre has informed the Supreme Court that the qualifying score for NEET-Super Speciality is being lowered from the 50th percentile to the 30th percentile. The State had to surrender the unfilled seats meant for Tamil Nadus in-service candidates in line with a Supreme Court direction. Now, 40 of these seats that remained vacant after round two of All India Quota counselling are being reverted to the State. Fresh applications Officials said there are around 100 eligible candidates, but they would have to call for applications again after receiving the court orders. The application window will depend on the duration stipulated by the court. M. Akilan, State secretary, Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association (TNMOA), said in a statement that after the Supreme Court ordered on May 29 that the vacant in-service super speciality seats be surrendered to the All India pool, it filed an independent fresh writ petition before the court, representing the rights and interests of in-service doctors in super speciality education. The court later directed that the vacant seats be surrendered to the All India pool and if the qualifying cut-off was reduced in subsequent rounds of counselling, 50% of the remaining unfilled Tamil Nadu seats should be reverted to the State. Interlocutory Application TNMOA said it continued its legal efforts and subsequently filed another Interlocutory Application seeking the full reversion of the remaining unfilled Tamil Nadu in-service seats to the State. At the hearing on Thursday (September 17, 2026), the Medical Counselling Committee informed the court that the NEET-SS qualifying percentile would be reduced to the 30th percentile. All remaining unfilled in-service seats would be reverted to the State. Dr. Akilan said that 111 candidates were already waiting and that new applicants would come in. Last year, Tamil Nadu surrendered 145 seats to the All India Quota and 39 were reverted. Some senior government doctors expressed dissatisfaction. First, the cut-off was kept at the 50th percentile. Then, 151 unfilled high-value super speciality seats were taken away for non-service All India candidates. Now, the cut-off percentile has been reduced to 30, and 40 seats have been reverted. These seats often belong to neglected disciplines. This is a sabotage of the Directorate-General of Health Services. The solution will be removal of the eligibility cut-off in the prospectus and running a fair counselling for service candidates at least from next year, a doctor said. Another doctor added that the vacant seats would not have many takers. Lack of financial and promotional opportunities had brought the interest down, he said.

headline: Yemen conflict displaces 1,12,000 people inside country, thousands flee to Djibouti, UN migration agency says
content: At least 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen within the last two weeks as fighting continues along the countrys west coast amid a renewed conflict, while nearly 3,000 have fled by sea to Djibouti, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday (September 18, 2026). Yemens Iran-aligned Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure while advancing along Yemens Red Sea coast towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route. Nearly 3,000 people have crossed the Gulf of Aden to Djibouti in the Horn of Africa in less than a week as escalating violence has forced more families to flee, Sandrine Desamours, the representative for the UNs refugee agency, UNHCR, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Djibouti. The government of Djibouti is preparing for the arrival of up to 10,000 refugees - which will add acute pressure on the countrys health care and education services, she said. The UN International Organization for Migration said people are fleeing on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water. Most fleeing are Yemeni families seeking refuge in Djibouti, but IOM is also beginning to see a small number of migrants, mainly from Ethiopia, heading in the same direction. Additionally, authorities in Somaliland and Puntland have also reported increased arrivals from Yemen, including Yemeni refugees and Somali refugee returnees, though numbers remain in the hundreds for now, UNHCR said. UN agencies described the latest fighting as being a crisis on top of multiple crises, as the countrys health services and economy have been shattered amid a long civil war between forces of the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed administration and the Houthis, creating one of the worlds biggest humanitarian crises. The Houthi advance along Yemens Red Sea coast is bolstering Tehrans hand in its conflict with the U.S., as the group tightens its control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic chokepoint for global oil and commodities shipping, more than six months after U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran.

headline: 'Tamil Nadu not against Hindi': Udhayanidhi Stalin responds to Supreme Court remark, rejects Navodaya schools
content: A day after Supreme Court asked Tamil Nadu govt to change its mindset against Hindi and observed that the state could not function like a separate country, Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Friday said Tamil Nadu was not against any language and did not function like a separate country.He said the state did not want Navodaya schools and, if necessary, a special assembly session could be convened to pass a resolution against them.Tamil Nadu follows a two-language policy and has remained at the forefront in several areas, including higher education enrolment and womens participation in the workforce.Without learning Hindi, many Tamilians have carved a niche for themselves, from winning Nobel Prizes to becoming eminent scientists at ISRO. This clearly indicates that Tamil Nadu is not at a disadvantage because of not knowing or learning Hindi, Udhayanidhi said in a statement. Citing the SCs recent observations in connection with Navodaya schools, Udhayanidhi said the present TVK govt was also following the states two-language policy and had rejected the three-language policy.The seed of the two-language policy was sown by Perarignar Anna in this (Tamil) land. Cutting across political lines, we all should come together to uphold the states policy in the SC and stop the Navodaya schools that impose the three-language policy, he said.

headline: Former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh questioned by CCB Police
content: The Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) police on Friday questioned former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in connection with a fraud case involving alleged collection of money from private school managements on the promise of securing government approvals from the School Education Department. Based on a complaint lodged with the Greater Chennai Police Commissioner, the CCB registered a case and commenced an investigation. Three accused persons B.T. Arasakumar, Suresh and Raja were arrested. The investigation has so far established that around 18 crore was allegedly collected from private schools in the name of securing government approvals, resulting in a breach of trust and financial fraud. Based on the evidence collected during the investigation, action was initiated against Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi under provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. On September 16, the CCB conducted searches at nine locations, including four premises belonging to Mr. Anbil Mahesh in Chennai and Tiruchi and premises linked to his aides Valadi Karthik, Arun Prakash and Prakash. Property documents, bank details, cheques and electronic devices were seized during the searches. Further investigation is underway. Acting on a notice issued under Section 35(3) of the BNSS directing him to appear for enquiry, Mr. Anbil Mahesh appeared before the CCB at the Police Commissionerate in Vepery around 11 a.m. on Friday. Police questioned him in detail about his alleged links with Arasakumar, Muthukumar and private school managements, the alleged collection of party fund from school managements, bank accounts identified in connection with the transactions and various financial dealings. During the enquiry, the police questioned him on the alleged events on a case-by-case basis and confronted him with documentary evidence. His responses and explanations were recorded as part of his statement. The enquiry continued until the evening. Further investigation into the case is underway.
