headline: Hundreds of thousands attend Iran's biggest government-organised rally since the war began
content: Iran's government has sought to rally the people and stress national unity, even as the economy worsens under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and new U.S. sanctions. On Friday (September 18, 2026), it claimed another attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway it has sought to control since the start of the war. Estimates varied on the number of people volunteering to receive limited military training and defend the country in an effort described as Janfaday-e Iran, or the ones who sacrifice their lives for Iran. They marched through downtown Tehran in combat uniform, carrying flags, as onlookers cheered. For days, state media have encouraged Iranians to join the campaign, saying training with assault rifles would begin soon. The volunteers would be an additional layer of security for the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard and the Basij militia, which has played a key role in quashing anti-government protests. Bogged down: On the U.S.-Iran conflict escalation Tehrans Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 people had registered to participate, with over 1 million expected to take part in the training. On Friday morning (September 18, 2026), the broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people were on the streets. The new head of the Basij, Hossein Taeb, declared in a speech as the rally began that the volunteers will be ready for full-fledged defense and similar rallies will take place in other cities soon. The new trainees will make a nightmare for Iran's enemies, Taeb added, as President Masoud Pezeshkian, military commanders and other senior officials watched the march. Some participants trampled flags of the U.S. and Israel. Others chanted Death to America and Death to Israel. I am here to tell [U.S. President Donald] Trump that we Iranians have no fear of his threats against our homeland, said Marzieh Afaghi, 24, who attended the rally with her toddler and husband. No one in history could invade Iran and remain there. The rally was also a chance for Iran to show off military hardware. Anti-aircraft batteries were on display, while female Guard members in black headscarves sat with truck-mounted machine guns. The Guard displayed drones that have been used against ships in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's attacks and threats have severely affected the Gulf regions shipments of oil and natural gas to the rest of the world. Iran said it had attacked a Togo-flagged oil tanker, the Trend, for what it called an illegal attempt to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, the state broadcaster reported. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations centre said a tanker was hit by a projectile, sparking a fire on board that was extinguished. The UKMTO, in a separate update, said ship transits facilitated by the U.S. military off Oman have averaged 24 a day over the past week but overall traffic remains about 90% lower than before the war. Friday's (September 18, 2026) events also suggested that hard-liners like Taeb among Iran's leadership will be more prepared to suppress any future demonstration against the theocracy. In January, shortly before the war, Iran saw some of its largest nationwide protests in history, which began over the struggling economy and turned into wider grievances. Activists have said a crackdown killed over 7,000 people and saw tens of thousands detained. In May, government officials said more than 30 million people in Iran which has a total population of some 90 million had volunteered via an online form or at public gatherings to lay down their lives for the theocracy. The Associated Press could not independently confirm that.

headline: T.N. government writes to PM Modi seeking to change the operator of Chennai airport
content: In a significant development, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking to change the operator of the Chennai airport. Unhappy with a few aspects of the airport, the State has asked the Centre to bring in an operator other than the Airports Authority of India (AAI), sources said. In the letter sent in August, the State government has said Tamil Nadu has been industry-friendly, making consistent efforts to attract business and investment; hence, better management of the airport is of paramount importance, sources said. The letter has highlighted that be it passenger volume, aircraft movement, or cargo volume, the Chennai airport needs significant improvement. Such a business-friendly State needs an excellent airport. The State government hence wants a change in the operator, a source said. The move, essentially an attempt to privatise the airport, comes on the heels of the States decision to drop the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur in Kancheepuram district and its plans to expand the existing airport. We have sent the letter. Now, we hope the Centre takes it up on priority and initiates work to privatise the airport, another source said. The State has shortlisted two sites Cheyyur and Gummidipoondi for the second airport. However, since it will take several years to build it, the immediate priority seems to be not only to expand the existing airport but also to privatise it. Air passengers have been demanding the privatisation of the airport for long, arguing that it will bring in better upkeep, connectivity to more destinations, and enhanced ambience. Their displeasure also stems from the fact that some of the infrastructure projects, such as the cab pick-up point, were inordinately delayed before they were opened and that the T3 Terminal is still under construction. Many significant decisions have to be vetted by the AAI headquarters in New Delhi and this process consumes time, thus affecting the operations of the airport, though a lot of efforts is being made by the airport staff, the sources said.

headline: Nigeria police fire tear gas at protesters over deaths of 37 miners in custody
content: Police in Nigeria fired tear gas at dozens of people who gathered Friday (September 18, 2026) to protest the deaths of 37 miners while they were in custody. Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago said on Thursday (September 17, 2026) that the miners, who were arrested earlier in the week on suspicion of illegal mining by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, died in custody. The civil defence corps said they died as a result of a suspected disease outbreak, but survivors told The Associated Press that the miners died of suffocation. Dozens of young people, including miners and their relatives, gathered near the civil defence corps' office on Friday (September 18). Police officers cordoned off the area and attempted to disperse protesters by firing tear gas canisters. The protesters claim the miners were killed in retaliation for earlier attacks by some miners on the corps officers. The Nigerian government suspended the commandant of Niger State's civil defence corps on Friday (September 18). It is an unfortunate incident; however, a full investigation will be conducted while the commandant under whose watch this happened remains suspended, the Minister of Interior said in a statement. Illegal mining is a serious problem in Nigeria, where analysts say it funds activities of armed groups, some of whom control the mines.

headline: Russia begins 3 days of voting in a parliamentary election set to cement the Kremlin's power
content: Russians on Friday (September 18, 2026) began three days of voting in the countrys first wartime parliamentary election, which features virtually no opposition and is all but certain to secure the Kremlins political dominance. Authorities spread the election over the weekend, ending Sunday (September 20, 2026), in a bid to boost turnout among the 111 million eligible voters, and they even allowed electronic balloting. The Kremlin wants the parliamentary election the first since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to underline public support for the war and give a veneer of legitimacy to its actions. It has sought to avoid any political risks by stamping out even the slightest sign of dissent. Your choice and resolve will once again demonstrate that millions of people stand behind our fighters, that we are a united people, bound by shared values, historical memory, and love for the Motherland, President Vladimir Putin told the nation before the vote. Russian state news agencies reported that Mr. Putin voted online Friday (September 18, 2026) and released a video of him in front of a computer screen. The main Kremlin party, United Russia, is all but assured of retaining its overwhelming control of the lower house, the State Duma. Several smaller parties of the systemic opposition that vote in sync with the government on all key issues are also expected to retain their presence. Voters cast two separate ballots, filling half of the Dumas 450 seats by selecting political parties listed on the ballot. The rest are contested in single-seat constituencies, with voters choosing individual candidates. Russians interviewed by The Associated Press expressed different expectations from the election. Dmitry Kirillin in Moscow said earlier this week that he would like to see some changes. To see a different party at the helm. But Muscovite Alexander Vertukhin believed what United Russia and the communists are doing is quite sufficient; their platforms cover everything. Speaking at a Moscow polling station Friday (September 18, 2026), pensioner Galina Vavilova said she thought ending the war in Ukraine is the main thing, of course. That is the most important thing right now. Everyone wants peace; thats what it comes down to. So that our guys are safe and sound, she said. Another pensioner, Lyudmila Kalinina, wished for life to stabilise for the better and for an end to the big divide between the ultra-rich and the extremely poor, because, after all, many people don't live a very sweet life. Vladimir Chubarev, a 72-year-old professor, expressed hope for all the important initiatives our government is undertaking to succeed, adding: And, of course, for victory. The liberal Yabloko party, the only registered political entity that dared to criticise the war, was removed from the ballot last month by Russias Supreme Court and only has a few dozen candidates in the single-constituency races. Additionally, some anti-war politicians have been imprisoned or forced to flee abroad ahead of the campaign. The election follows a summer of Ukraines long-range drone strikes on oil refineries that triggered a widespread fuel crisis. Warehouses belonging to online retailers Wildberries and Ozon were also attacked. The damage has exacerbated problems for the Russian economy and brought the war home for millions. In Russia's Black Sea resort of Sochi, polling stations were briefly closed because of a threat of a drone attack, local officials said. One polling station in the Krasnodar region had to be set up in a different venue after a drone shattered windows there, said Central Election Commission head Ella Pamfilova. For the first time, the parliamentary election includes residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began but still doesn't fully control. Voting is also taking place in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that was illegally annexed by Russia in 2014. Voters dropped their ballots in a box at one polling station in the Russian-held part of the Donetsk region of eastern Ukraine as an armed Russian soldier stood nearby and watched. In the Russian-held Luhansk region, 14 polling stations were using backup power sources after Ukrainian drones damaged electrical lines, Pamfilova said. Separately, Russian officials said Ukrainian attacks earlier this week killed a polling station chief and wounded another in the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia region. There was no immediate comment from Ukraine on the accusation. Authorities in Kyiv denounced the voting in the Russian-held areas as illegal and urged foreign governments and international organisations not to recognise the election, warning Ukrainians that taking part in organising the balloting could carry criminal liability. European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand also called the voting in Russian-held regions illegal and said the European Union condemns it. These so-called elections represent yet another blatant violation of international law. The European Union does not, and will never, recognise either the holding of these so-called elections, sham elections, in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine or their results," he said. Mr. Wigand said the way the elections are held underscores the continued and deepening erosion of democracy in Russia," and that the Kremlin deprives voters in Russia of a genuine choice about the future of their country. He also noted that Russia decided not to invite observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, disregarding its commitments. He vowed that the EU will continue to support Russian civil society organizations, human rights groups and independent media.

headline: Saudi Aramco halts October crude deliveries to some European refiners after pipeline attack, says report
content: Oil company Saudi Aramco has told at least two European refining customers they will receive no crude oil next month following an attack on Saudi Arabias key pipeline to the Red Sea, Bloomberg News reported on Friday (September 18, 2026), citing people familiar with the matter. European refiners typically buy Saudi crude under term contracts that guarantee monthly supplies, but Aramco has informed customers that next months deliveries will not proceed, the report said. Saudi Arabia earlier informed European customers that some crude cargoes would be cancelled after drone attacks forced the shutdown of its East-West pipeline, damaging three pumping stations and disrupting oil loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The disruption has prompted customers, including Polands Orlen, to seek alternative crude supplies, with traders saying the refiner bought North Sea grades to replace disrupted Saudi imports. Reuters could not verify the report. Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours. Aramco is working to partially restart the pipeline within days and return it to full capacity within six weeks, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Separately, Saudi Aramco has boosted crude exports from the Gulf through ship-to-ship transfers off Omans Sohar port to help offset volumes lost from reduced Red Sea shipments.

headline: At JD(U) orientation, the message as Nitish Kumar's son takes stage
content: The Janata Dal (United)s day-long orientation programme on Friday turned into a platform for its scion Nishant Kumar, as the Bihar health minister invoked his father Nitish Kumars legacy and urged party workers to carry it forward. In his first-ever address to Janata Dal (United) workers, Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar, son of former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, praised Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for following the ideals and governance model of his predecessor and party chief Nitish Kumar, and urged JD-U workers to do the same. You all should follow the ideals of our partys supreme leader and former CM, Nitish Kumar. Speak to the people about what he has done for Bihar since 2005. Highlight his policies, programmes, and governance schemes, Nishant urged party legislators, adding: Current CM Samrat Choudhary is also following in the footsteps of Nitish Kumar ji You should gather feedback from the public and flag any concerns of the people and party workers with party leadership. This is Nishant Kumars first official address to party legislators. While the orientation programme originally organised to train legislators in legislative practices and procedures had several senior leaders in attendance, only one other leader besides Nishant, JD(U) National Working President Sanjay Kumar Jha, addressed the gathering. Significantly, the function served to indicate one thing how the partys politics could shift towards him in the near future. While former chief minister Nitish Kumar inaugurated the function, he left shortly after the ceremonial lamp lighting. Senior leaders, including deputy chief ministers Bijendra Prasad Yadav and Vijay Kumar Choudhary, and JD(U) Legislature Party Leader and Minister Shravan Kumar, attended the event. Union Minister and former JD(U) National President Rajiv Ranjan Singh (alias Lalan Singh) was conspicuously missing, with unofficial remarks from several legislators highlighting this absence. Speaking to reporters later, Sanjay Kumar Jha stated: We discussed budget practices, the economy, major road network expansions, and how electricity access has improved over the last two decades. We also discussed what more needs to be done, along with best legislative practices from other states. He downplayed Lalan Singhs absence, noting that the orientation programme was not intended for MPs. The meeting made no official mention of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC). However, some leaders said the party should maintain its longstanding stance on the issue. Now that Article 370 and the Ram Temple issues have been resolved, our distinct stand on the UCC is what separates us from the BJPs ideology, one legislator noted. Nitish Kumar always ensured social cohesion. Bihar should avoid anything that could disturb social harmony.

headline: IIT Madras, SCU set up high-altitude atmospheric observatory in Ladakh
content: altitude atmospheric observatory in Ladakh CHENNAI: Researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras), in collaboration with Sindhu Central University (SCU), have established a high-altitude atmospheric observatory at SCUs campus in Khaltse, Ladakh, at an elevation of 3,450m, to study air chemistry and climate processes in the Himalayan region.The observatory uses a Proton Transfer Reaction Mass Spectrometer (PTR-MS) to measure volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the air online and in real time, even at concentrations of parts per trillion. It means it can detect one molecule of a VOC among one trillion air molecules. A Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer (SMPS) measures the number and sizes of aerosol particles. A black carbon instrument is also being installed, with more advanced instruments planned.The idea is to understand how the ecosystem responds to human activities, and determine whether the changes we observe are driven by human influence, natural processes or a combination of both, said Prof Sachin S Gunthe, Centre for Atmospheric and Climate Sciences (CACS), department of civil engineering, IIT Madras.VOCs drive regional atmospheric chemistry, and understanding how this chemistry differs in the Himalayas could reveal its implications for the region, he said. The observatory will study pristine Himalayan air chemistry, aerosol formation and growth, and long-range transport of pollutants. It will also provide insights into climate change impacts on the fragile Himalayan ecosystem, CACS said in an online post.The whole idea is to start better understanding the Himalayan climate, Gunthe said, adding that the research would examine how climate affects atmospheric chemistry and how atmospheric chemistry, in turn, influences climate.Aerosols are tiny particles suspended in the atmosphere that can influence cloud formation, sunlight reaching the Earth and rainfall. Measurements from the observatory will help scientists investigate these processes and their links to regional climate.The facility is among Indias northernmost measurements of its kind and one of the countrys highest-altitude atmospheric composition studies. Gunthe said its location near Kargil, further north than existing Himalayan research sites such as Hanle, offered a distinct advantage.Globally, high-altitude atmospheric research facilities include the Sphinx Observatory at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps, at 3,580 metres, and the Testa Grigia Observatory in the western Alps on the Italian-Swiss border, at 3,480 metres. The Ladakh facility will add atmospheric observations from a high-altitude site in the tropics.

headline: How Chennai's GCC expansion could reshape its real estate market
content: Tamil Nadu has been home to Global Capability Centres (GCCs), but the pace of expansion has accelerated in recent years, with several prominent global companies choosing Chennai as their GCC hub. The previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) government placed a strong emphasis on building the States GCC ecosystem, and now the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government is continuing to pursue investments in the sector through a series of MoUs. It has also made new announcements for the sector. As the GCC footprint expands, the ripple effect is expected to be felt across Chennais commercial real estate market, driving demand for Grade A office space and fuelling leasing activity. This mirrors the impact of the IT boom on office and residential development in the late 90s and early 2000s. To attract the next generation of GCCs, Tamil Nadus Industries Minister S. Keerthana recently said that the Tamil Nadu GCC Corridor and Growth Plan will be introduced along the Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road, Mount-Poonamallee High Road and Rajiv Gandhi Salai. She said these zones would have higher FSI, along with improved common and shared infrastructure facilities, to attract more GCCs to Chennai. The Tamil Nadu GCC Corridor and Growth Plan is a strategic initiative to unlock expansion capacity for multinational Global Capability Centres already operating in ChennaiDeepak JacobManaging director and CEO of Guidance, a nodal agency located in Chennai Rather than piecemeal project approvals, the government is treating three established commercial corridors as integrated zones with coordinated planning and infrastructure development, adds Jacob. The Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road was chosen because it already hosts established IT infrastructure and serves as a critical north-south connector for the southern GCC cluster, with direct connectivity to Chennai International Airport via the Pallavaram Flyover, says Jacob. Mount-Poonamallee High Road (SH-55) is an emerging commercial corridor with proven GCC presence and benefits from upcoming Poonamallee Metro Line development, making it a gateway for multinational entry. Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR) is the established premier IT corridor with the highest GCC concentration and proven demand from banking and financial services (BFSI), automotive and professional services sectors. FSI enhancement The core game plan involves enhancing Floor Space Index (FSI) in eligible zones to allow existing GCC campuses to expand vertically without additional land acquisition, while upgrading common infrastructure. The increased FSI will enable developers to build greater floor area and leasable space and it can also support in redesigning projects to higher densities, generating greater development returns and improved margins without needing to purchase additional land, benefitting developers, property owners and investors, says Jerry Kingsley, head of research, India, and city lead for capital markets, JLL Chennai, a commercial real estate solutions. Kingsley adds that by targeting GCCs, which require Grade A infrastructure, the corridor ensures sustained demand for premium office space. The resulting influx of skilled professionals will drive residential development across mid-to-premium segments, triggering new housing projects. Growth broadens According to Kanchana Krishnan, city head and executive director, Anarock, a real estate consultancy, GCCs accounted for around 55% of Chennais office leasing in the first half of 2026, up from 49% in 2025. GCCs bring high-quality employment, which creates demand for housing, retail, hospitality, schools, healthcare and other social infrastructure. The impact can extend beyond the office market, creating a broader employment-led real estate ecosystemKanchana KrishnanCity head and executive director, Anarock Currently, Tamil Nadu is home to over 465 Global Capability Centres, representing approximately 10%-15% of Indias entire GCC ecosystem. The State has 4.5 lakh GCC-ready professionals and added roughly 65,000 GCC jobs in the financial year 2025. Chennai accounts for 405 of these GCCs. Tamil Nadus emerging cities such as Coimbatore, Madurai and Tiruchi, house over 60 GCCs. This showcases the distributed growth of the State. According to a study by Colliers, a commercial real estate services firm, although Bengaluru and Hyderabad have collectively driven over 60% of GCC leasing since 2021, demand from capability centres in India is becoming broad-based. Other Tier I cities continue to leverage competitive costs and specialised industry ecosystems to attract global firms. While Bengaluru and Hyderabad are likely to continue to be preferred by technology GCCs, Mumbai and Pune will anchor BFSI operations. Similarly, Chennai is likely to increasingly attract GCCs from the engineering and manufacturing sectors. MoUs to drive growth The TVK government has signed a slew of MoUs in the GCC space at the Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave. To cite an example, Bosch Global Software Technologies and TIDCO signed an MoU to establish a Global Software Development Centre focused on automotive software and autonomous systems, with R&D and engineering operations. It is expected to come up either along OMR or the Mount-Poonamallee corridor. Chubb, a global insurance company, signed an MoU in July to expand its insurance operations through a GCC in Chennai. The new centre will handle claims processing, AI-driven underwriting, fraud detection and captive operations serving Chubbs Asia-Pacific portfolio. Nordex, the German wind turbine manufacturer and a global leader in renewable energy technology, signed an MoU to establish a significant GCC in Chennai focused on product engineering and technology innovation. More recently, during his visit to the United Kingdom, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay signed an agreement with Ernst & Young (EY) to establish a GCC in Tamil Nadu, entailing an investment of 1,000 crore. Those tracking the real estate sector say these investments will lead to significant growth in leasing activity in the coming months. Jacob says these GCCs are not support centres or back-office operations, but encompass much more. For instance, existing GCCs such as Ford design powertrains for cars sold in 150 countries; Bosch develops autonomous driving technology; Standard Chartered runs mission-critical, 24/7 banking operations; KLAs algorithms advance global semiconductor manufacturing; and AstraZeneca discovers medicines with a global reach. These are strategic, high-innovation functions that multinational enterprises cannot outsource. Tamil Nadu has also been attracting first-time India GCC entrants companies establishing their first India operations in the State. SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation), Japans second-largest bank, established a significant GCC in Chennai focused on trade finance, banking operations and technology infrastructure for Asia-Pacific clients. HD Supply, a leading industrial and construction distributor, chose Chennai for its India GCC to optimise supply chain operations and develop digital commerce platforms serving Indias infrastructure and construction sectors. SES (Socit Europenne des Satellites), the Luxembourg-based satellite and space technology company, has set up a technology centre in Chennai for satellite communications, IoT solutions and space technology applications serving Asia-Pacific markets. Demand and pricing GCCs are looking for spaces starting from 30,000 sq.ft. and going up to several lakh sq.ft. In Chennai, most moderate-sized GCCs typically opt for conventional office spaces between 30,000 and 50,000 sq.ft., seeking stability and tailored infrastructure for their business needs. Meanwhile, smaller-scale GCCs entering Chennai favour flex spaces, which provide reduced upfront costs, shorter commitments and the ability to scale during their early operational phase, Kingsley adds. Chennais Grade A rents are still around 76 to 78 per sq.ft., which gives it a significant cost advantage over markets such as Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Improvement in infrastructure With GCC corridors being proposed, industry stakeholders have urged the government to strengthen infrastructure in these regions. One key concern is the need to expedite Metro Rail projects, as roads in several areas remain in poor condition due to ongoing digging work. Last-mile connectivity and public transport also need to be improved. Beyond office space, GCC clusters require good schools, hospitals, hotels, serviced apartments, restaurants, retail and recreational facilities. The government should consider developing this supporting infrastructure alongside GCC hubs. Drainage, water supply and flood mitigation should be treated as core infrastructure. Krishnan said there is evidence of an employment-led real estate multiplier effect, although it is difficult to attribute price appreciation entirely to GCCs. The pattern was evident during the IT revolution in locations such as OMR in Chennai, Whitefield in Bengaluru and Gachibowli in Hyderabad. A similar trend is now emerging in Chennai, she said. Average residential capital values increased from around 4,935 per sq.ft. in 2020 to 7,100 per sq.ft. in 2025, an increase of about 44%. South Chennai, including the OMR/ GST growth belt, accounted for around 78% of residential launches and 66% of sales in 2025.

headline: IIIT-Hyderabad cancels screening of Umar Khalid documentary
content: A day after the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) flagged a proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at The International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad (IIIT-H), stating that publicly exhibiting an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained, the institute has cancelled the programme. The Institute has made it clear that no public or private screening of the film will be permitted in any Institute space, including classrooms, laboratories or offices, IIIT-Hyderabad said in a statement, adding that it has promptly cancelled the screening as soon as it was made aware of the unauthorised event. Stating that the IIIT-H has taken note of the proposed screening of the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present on the Institute campus, which has not been certified by the CBFC, it added that an informal student group had proposed the screening in a campus lecture hall on September 18. It has no link to IIIT-H officially in any way, it said, adding: Since no official permission was taken for this, nor were any of the required protocols followed, the Institute promptly cancelled the screening as soon as it was made aware of such an unauthorised event. IIIT Hyderabad reiterates that the proposed screening was not an Institute-organised or authorised event as has been erroneously reported in some instances, it noted. Neither the Institute nor any of its recognised student clubs, cells or bodies were involved in any way with the proposed screening. The Institute has long-established processes governing official events and activities on campus, and no permission for this film screening has been obtained from the competent authorities. IIIT Hyderabad has no association with the proposed screening, which was not an Institute-organised or authorised event and does not represent the views or position of the Institute, it further noted. It said that as an academic institution, IIIT Hyderabad has a large and diverse student community. Students and faculty may, in their individual capacity, meet or interact with people from all walks of life. Such personal interaction should not be construed as Institute-organised events, nor do they represent the views or activities of the Institute. The Institute expects all members of its community to follow established procedures and applicable legal and institutional requirements while organising or announcing activities on campus, it added. The documentary, Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, is directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani. It was scheduled to be shown by a group of students at the institutes KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. The cancellation of the screening took place after the CBFC flagged it on X, stating that public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act. Earlier, a planned screening of the documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru was postponed following objections from the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), which claimed that allowing the screening would amount to using the campus for political propaganda. The student committee postponed the screening, citing logistical and security considerations, while adding that it would be held later in the trimester.

headline: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
content: The White House said Thursday (September 18, 2026) that it was withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Donald Trumps domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer. Schroyer, who has little experience in immigration, is close to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a former U.S. senator from Oklahoma. The White House offered no comment in a brief statement. The latest setback comes as the agency remains under withering scrutiny over its handling of enforcement operations. Critics have questioned how ICE has recruited and trained officers as it raced to hire thousands to carry out President Trumps promise of mass deportations. Officers have shot and killed multiple people, including two American citizens in Minneapolis earlier this year. Senator Rand Paul, the chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, had refused to hold a hearing on the nominee until DHS provided him with information he had been seeking about civilian deaths during ICE enforcement operations. I dont have a concern with who the nominee was. I had asked them to give me an update on the internal investigation into civilian deaths, Mr Paul, R-Ky., told The Associated Press. And Im still waiting. When Mullin took over DHS in March, he pledged a lower-profile approach to immigration enforcement, pulling back on the aggressive, tumultuous crackdown on the streets of large cities that sparked widespread public condemnation. Arrests have continued to accelerate, reaching nearly 51,000 in August, the highest single monthly arrest total during the second Trump administration. Mr Paul said he intended to hold a hearing on Schroyers nomination, but it never came to that. He only heard about the nomination being withdrawn when the White House made it public Thursday (September 17). ICE has not had a Senate-confirmed leader since the Obama administration. David Venturella, a former executive at a private prison operator, returned to the agency as acting director earlier this year after Todd Lyons resigned. When Mr Trump nominated Schroyer in June, Mr Trump said on his Truth Social platform that his pick was a PATRIOT with real operational experience and a proven leader with DECADES of experience locking up the worst of the worst. The administration did not indicate when it might announce another pick for the position.

headline: BEML secures Rs 5,400 crore order for Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project
content: BEML Limited has secured an order worth more than Rs. 5,400 crore from the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) Corridor. According to an exchange filing, the order covers the supply and maintenance of high-speed rolling stock and allied works for the 508-km-long high-speed rail project. BEML has been developing and manufacturing the countrys first bullet train, the B28, at its Aditya High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru. The trainsets are being built for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. The facility was inaugurated by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on April 25, 2026. B28 bullet train to be ready by March 2027 The Ministry of Railways has set a target to manufacture the countrys first bullet train, B28, by March 2027. The defence PSU was awarded the contract in October 2024 by Chennai-based Integral Coach Factory (ICF) to design, manufacture and commission two high-speed trainsets. B28 bullet train route Initially, the national transporter has planned to roll out the B28 bullet train between Surat and Vapi. The 97-km-long stretch is part of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project, which the Railways aims to make operational by August 2027. A decision has been taken to start the operation using B28. Efforts are underway to start operation using B28 (Bharat made Bullet, 280 kmph) for Surat to Vapi (97km) in Aug 2027, the Ministry of Railways said in an earlier statement. B28 high speed train: Speed According to the Railways, the B28 (Bharat-made bullet trainset) indicates a design speed of 280 kmph, while its operational speed will be 250 kmph. The high-speed trainset will feature a fully air-conditioned, Chair Car configuration coach. The Bharat made Bullet trainset will also offer modern passenger amenities such as reclining and rotatable seats, special provisions for passengers with restricted mobility and onboard infotainment systems.

headline: Prominent dissidents left out of AIADMK's bypoll campaign programmes
content: Members of Legislative Assembly (MLA), S.P. Velumani, C.Ve. Shanmugam and Natham R. Viswanathan, in its official programmes of by-poll campaign in Madurantakam and Dharapuram assembly constituencies. There are 13 sitting legislators including general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami who have figured in the list of star campaigners. The purpose of the party providing its list to the election authorities is to ensure that expenses borne on account of the travel of the campaigners are not considered for calculating election expenses of the partys candidates. Former Minister of Power, Mr Thangamani, also a key figure in the dissidents camp, has also been excluded in the list. So are his colleagues K.P. Anbalagan, P. Balakrishna Reddy and K.C. Veeramani. However, R. Kamaraj, who represents Nannilam in the Assembly, and G. Hari (Tirutanni) , are back in the good books of the party establishment, though they were also in the rebels camp at one point of time. But, Mr Thangamani, breaking ranks with his rebel-colleagues, participated in the protest in Salem about a month ago. The stir was held as part of the partys State-wide demonstrations on a host of issues concerning farmers including the Cauvery. The former Minister, who lost in in his traditional seat of Kumarapalayam in the Assembly election during April-May, had even told the agitators that Mr. Palaniswami would soon become the Chief Minister again. In the partys agitation last month, Mr Viswanathan, Mr Velumani and Mr Anbalagan skipped the events despite being named to lead the stir in different places. However, Mr Reddy and Mr Veeramani took part in the programme. The friction began in the party four months ago following the action of 25 legislators voting in favour of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government in the Assembly during the trust motion.. This led to Mr Palaniswami sacking 26 district secretaries, many of whom are now part of the dissidents camp. Some others had joined the TVK. In fact, this process of churning in the Dravidian major has necessitated the by-elections, as the TVKs nominees, Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama, were originally from the AIADMK, and, after supporting the TVK regime, they joined the ruling party. After removing several of the dissidents from the powerful position of district secretaries, Mr Palaniswami had offered them alternative positions such as deputy general secretary to Mr Velumani and Mr Viswanathan and organisation secretary to many others. But, most of the dissidents did not accept the offer. They also did not take part in the consultations chaired by Mr Palaniswami to review the partys performance in the Assembly polls. Among those who made it to the list are deputy general secretary K.P. Munusamy, treasurer Dindigul C. Sreenivasan, propaganda secretary M. Thambi Durai and Nagapattinam district secretary O.S. Manian.

headline: Governor Arlekar seeks clarifications from T.N. govt. on Tamil Nadu Private Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026
content: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought clarifications from the Tamil Nadu government regarding some of the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Private Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which was recently passed by the Assembly. Sources told that the Bill is still under the consideration of the Governor and he has sought a briefing from the government on some provisions. The sources clarified this amidst reports that Mr. Arlekar has reserved the Bill for consideration by the President of India. In the recently concluded Budget Session of the Tamil Nadu Assembly, a total of 13 Bills were passed. Of these, the Tamil Nadu Private Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, attracted severe criticism from the Opposition. Barring this Bill, the Governor has accorded assent to the 12 other Bills. What does the Bill say? The Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019, mandates that not less than 100 acres of contiguous land is required for the establishment of a private university in the State. The Act also mandates the sponsoring body to establish a permanent endowment fund of at least 50 crore. The amendment Bill sought to reduce the minimum land requirement for establishing a private university to 12 acres in the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) area, 18 acres in other municipal corporations and municipal councils, and 25 acres in other areas. It also proposed to reduce the permanent endowment fund requirement to 25 crore. Some Opposition parties alleged the Bill would lead to the commercialisation of education. However, Minister for Higher Education P. Viswanathan had recently said the objective behind the amendment Bill was to facilitate the establishment of world-class private universities in Tamil Nadu.

headline: India, Bhutan commend progress in bilateral development cooperation
content: India and Bhutan reviewed all aspects of bilateral ties and commended progress in development cooperation during External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankars visit to the country. Mr. Jaishankar arrived in Bhutan on Wednesday (September 18, 2026) on a two-day official visit aiming to further strengthen the bilateral ties and cooperation between the two countries. During the visit, Mr. Jaishankar received an audience with King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, called on Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay, and held talks with his Bhutanese counterpart D. N. Dhungyel. "Honoured to receive an audience with His Majesty Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, The King of Bhutan, in Thimphu today. Deeply value his guidance to further deepen the unique friendship between India and Bhutan," Mr. Jaishankar posted on X after meeting the King on Thursday (September 17, 2026). The two sides reviewed all aspects of bilateral cooperation, as well as other regional and international issues of mutual importance, according to a joint press release issued on Friday (September 18, 2026). They appreciated the progress in strengthening the special and multi-faceted India-Bhutan partnership. The two sides commended the progress in bilateral development cooperation, it said. Mr. Jaishankar reaffirmed Indias support for Bhutans developmental goals and priorities, while Bhutan appreciated Indias support for wide-ranging programmes under its 13th Five Year Plan (2024-29). The E.A.M. discussed advancing multifaceted engagement in development partnership, energy, trade, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties with his Bhutanese counterpart. He inaugurated several projects during his visit, including the 65-bed Gyaltsuen Jetsun Pema Mother and Child Hospital in Mongar. He also laid the foundation stone for the 500 KW Lunana Hydropower Project in Gasa, northern Bhutan. Mr. Jaishankar handed over 43 Jersey cows from India to the National Cattle Breeding Centre in Bumthang and 54 electric vehicles to the Royal Government of Bhutan. The two ministers welcomed the operationalisation of a Unified Payments Interface (UPI)-based facility that will enable Bhutanese nationals to make digital payments in India using Bhutanese mobile applications. The two sides also discussed ongoing cooperation in the space sector and encouraged engagement on satellite data applications in areas such as monitoring glaciers, forest resources, floods and agriculture. Mr. Jaishankar reaffirmed the Government of Indias support for the Bhutanese Kings vision for the Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), with the two sides agreeing to continue efforts to develop collaboration on GMC-related issues. The ministers also expressed satisfaction at the implementation of the Joint Vision on Energy Partnership of March 2024. They welcomed the signing of an agreement on a concessional Line of Credit of 4,000 crore for energy projects in Bhutan and commended the active engagement of Indian companies in hydropower projects in the country, saying it was adding dynamism to existing energy cooperation. India reaffirmed its commitment to establish an Immigration Check Post at Hatisar in Assam to facilitate the movement of investors and visitors to Gelephu, as announced during Prime Minister Narendra Modis state visit to Bhutan in November 2025. The two sides welcomed the recent operationalisation of a new Land Customs Station in Samrang, Assam, reflecting joint efforts to expand cross-border connectivity, infrastructure and facilities. They reviewed progress on the establishment of cross-border rail links between Gelephu and Kokrajhar and Samtse and Banarhat. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments and recognised the significance of close bilateral ties amid the complex international environment. India thanked Bhutan for its support for its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for the 2028-2029 term. It also appreciated Bhutans ratification of the Framework Agreement of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA). Mr. Jaishankars visit was in line with the longstanding tradition of close engagement and cooperation between the two countries, according to the release. Mr. Jaishankar invited Dhungyel to visit India at his earliest convenience.

headline: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman, a post he has held since 1970
content: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. Mr. Buffett, 96, will become chairman emeritus and will take on his new role immediately, the company said Friday (September 19, 2026). His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman. Howard Buffett has been on the Berkshire Hathaway board since 1993. Warren Buffett will remain a director. He had served as Berkshire Hathaway's chairman since 1970. Mr. Buffett stepped down as CEO of the company late last year. He was succeeded by Greg Abel. I have served Berkshire since 1965," Mr. Buffett said in a letter to shareholders. Sixty-plus years in, I still have the best job in the world. That is not something many people my age can say, and I have never felt better about what comes next. Mr. Buffett said that he is confident in Abel and his son Howard leading Berkshire Hathaway. Greg runs the company; Howard will guard its culture and values both worth more than anything on our balance sheet, he said. Think of Howard as a policy the shareholders own and hope never to claim against. Buffett's fortune has been amassed through Berkshire Hathaway stock. It was worth more than $140 billion in July 2026. He has already given away roughly $66 billion worth of stock since 2006.

headline: Blast rips through mosque during Friday prayers in northwest Pakistan; 16 killed, dozens injured
content: At least 16 people were killed and dozens injured in a powerful suicide blast during Friday prayers (September 18, 2026) at a mosque near police lines in Kohat district in northwest Pakistan, officials said. The blast occurred at the mosque located near the old Police Lines in Kohat district, around 60 kilometres southwest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's capital Peshawar, they said. At least 16 people, including five police personnel and 11 civilians, were killed in the suicide blast at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province during Friday prayers, provincial Police Chief Zulfiqar Hameed said. No group or individual has claimed responsibility for the attack. Citing District Headquarters Hospital's MS Tahir Ali Shah, Geo News reported that 15 bodies were brought to the hospital along with over 50 injured following the blast. Most of those wounded were worshippers, police said, adding that the blast caused a crater outside the mosque. According to Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi, rescue teams reached the site shortly after receiving the information and launched a rescue operation. He said several of those injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for initial medical treatment. The spokesperson said rescue teams were present at the scene and assessing the situation.

headline: Bones behind the bungalow: How the Nithari serial killing case unravelled
content: How the Nithari serial killing case unravelled In 2006, a drain behind the Nithari house in Noidas Sector 31 revealed a horrific sight human skulls, skeletal remains, and fragments of clothes of 19 missing girls were found stuffed in gunny bags. (Express Photo by Tashi Tobgyal) Local police have been circumspect so far, and have refused to comment beyond confirming the identity. Reports said Koli moved to Haridwar his family is from Almora, roughly 300km away a few months ago Why? That is unclear at this time. The Nithari serial killings Between 2005 and 2006 a killer stalked Nithari, a small urban village in Noida. Girls and young women kept vanishing 19 of them and their families were left chasing whispers and shadows in a quest just to be heard. But one by one they were turned away; the police shrugged, apparently either unwilling or unable to help. She ran away or she must have eloped were some of the responses. It wasnt till May 2006 and the disappearance of Payal Sarkar that the horror story came to light. And it wasnt till December of that year that the bodies were found. They were found dismembered and decomposed, some of them worn down by time to skeletal remains in the drains behind a bungalow in Noidas Sector 31. Media reports from that time read like a horror story. From the drains behind and between that house and its neighbour, the police began pulling out skulls, bone fragments, torn dresses, and childrens toys. A school bag dirty and torn and faded, roiled in mud bore silent witness. Surendra Koli was a Dalit from the Almora district of Uttarakhand. (Express Photo/File) Moninder Singh Pandher owned the house D-5, Sector 31, Noida. Koli was his domestic help. The Express spoke to Jhabbu Lal a dhobi who sat opposite D-5 and who used to sometimes chat with Pandher. His daughter Jyoti, 10, was among the victims. He recalled one instance when Koli gave him one of Pandhers shirts, it was blood-stained. He (Koli) said it was from sahab slaughtering a chicken By Christmas of 2007 Pandher and Koli were arrested, and Koli confessed. NITHARI CASE TIMELINE The Nithari Case: From Vanished Girls To A Death In Haridwar Girls who vanished Years Koli was in custody Cases he was acquitted in Phase One The Disappearances Girls and young women start vanishing from Nithari, a small urban village in Noida 19 in total. Families chasing answers are turned away: "she ran away", "she must have eloped". Payal Sarkar disappears. Her case is the one that finally brings the horror to public attention. Bodies are found. Skulls, bone fragments, torn dresses and children's toys are pulled from the drains behind D-5, Sector 31 the house of Moninder Singh Pandher. Pandher and his domestic help, Surendra Koli, are arrested. Koli reportedly "confesses" while in custody. Early January, in the weeks after The CBI takes over the case. More skeletal remains a skull, a torso and parts of a leg are found. Phase Two Convictions And Death Sentences First conviction. Pandher and Koli are convicted of murdering 14-year-old Rimpa Haldar and sentenced to death. Koli is found guilty of killing seven-year-old Arti Prasad. Koli is found guilty of murdering nine-year-old Rachna Lal. The Supreme Court upholds the death sentence. President Pranab Mukherjee rejects a mercy plea. A death warrant is issued against Koli. Koli is convicted in the murder of five-year-old Kavita his fifth death sentence. September 12, 2014 Koli's execution is scheduled for this date. Phase Three The Case Unravels Acquittal. The Allahabad High Court acquits Koli in all 12 cases against him, and Pandher in the two he faced calling the investigation "casual and perfunctory". The Supreme Court dismisses the state's appeals, calling the earlier verdict a "manifest miscarriage of justice". By now Koli has spent 19 years in custody, Pandher over a decade. September 2026 Friday Koli is found dead near a Haridwar tea stall, apparently by suicide a few months after moving from his family's home in Almora, roughly 300km away. Police confirmed his identity but have declined further comment. Neither Koli nor Pandher, the courts eventually said, had anything to do with the deaths. The case leaves one question officially unanswered: who killed the 19 girls of Nithari? Angry with the police for having dragged their feet for months in which time more girls were raped and killed there were violent clashes between residents and cops. The police were corrupt, the grief-stricken families raged. Six cops were sacked amid claims some had colluded with Pandher. But then, two years later, Sub-Inspector Simarjeet Kaur then in charge of the police outpost in the village got her job back. She spent time in jail for allegedly accepting a bribe. There were rumours also of human trafficking, that the girls were being abducted and killed for their organs. There was a doctor who lived near Pandher whom the police suspected in an unrelated illegal kidney transplant racket. Was he in on this? What Police Found Behind The Nithari House In the drains behind and between D-5, Sector 31, Noida the house owned by Moninder Singh Pandher and its neighbour. Recovered From The Scene Pulled from the drains behind the house, among the first remains found. Some remains had been worn down by time to skeletal fragments. Clothing belonging to some of the victims, recovered from the debris. Children's toys Found alongside the remains and clothing in the drains. A torn school bag Dirty, faded and mud-roiled it "bore silent witness", Express reporters noted. A blood-stained shirt Koli gave it to a local dhobi to iron, saying it was from "sahab" Pandher "slaughtering a chicken". A knife and an axe 'Recovered' from the house this evidence was later dropped amid doubts over the investigation. More remains, later After the CBI took over: a skull, a torso, and parts of a leg. Media reports from the time read like a horror story. What began as a search for missing girls became a years-long reckoning with how the case against Koli and Pandher was built and how it eventually fell apart. Pandhers maid Maya was questioned too. Did she lure some of the girls? There were even rumours of cannibalism. The web of suspicion and unease spread relentlessly. Much was claimed but little was proven. The strained relationship between Pandher and his family was a dead end. Old kidnapping cases in Chandigarh, his hometown, were dug out of storage and a link was sought. Then they were dropped. In early January the Central Bureau of Investigation took over the case, and more skeletal remains were found: this time a skull, a torso, and parts of a leg. The convictions On paper it seemed an open-and-shut case. Nineteen girls missing, a house of secrets and horror, and a confession. The verdict that opened the floodgates came in February 2009. Pandher and Koli were convicted of murdering 14-year-old Rimpa Haldar, and sentenced to death. In May 2010 Koli was found guilty of killing seven-year-old Arti Prasad. In September, he was found guilty of murdering nine-year-0ld Rachna Lal. The verdicts kept coming. The death sentences piled up. By the December 2012 verdict in the murder of Kavita, 5, he was to have been put to death five times. In February 2011 the Supreme Court agreed. In July the President of India then Pranab Mukherjee rejected a plea. In September a death warrant was issued. Koli was to be hanged on September 12, 2014. And then it fell apart Questions over flawed investigation protocols and poor record-keeping counted against the police. A knife and axe recovered from the Nithari house were dropped. Questions over the police failing to properly investigate the neighbour the doctor and disregard for some evidence, including how the bodies were cut, were flagged. And questions over when exactly Koli was taken into custody December 27 or December 29, added to the confusion. The difference was key; it meant Koli may have been illegally detained by the police before being produced in court. NITHARI CASE HOW IT UNRAVELLED How The Case Against Surendra Koli Collapsed A 'confession', a custody-date discrepancy, and evidence that didn't hold 19 years after his arrest, the courts found the case against him fell apart. A KEY DISCREPANCY December 27 or December 29? Questions over flawed investigation protocols and poor record-keeping counted against the police from the start. Chief among them: when exactly was Koli taken into custody December 27 or December 29, 2007? The difference was not a technicality. It meant Koli may have been illegally detained by the police before being produced in court which is illegal under law. That single unresolved date became the thread that, pulled on, began to unravel the case. THE 'CONFESSION' Recorded under duress, Koli alleged The confession that anchored the prosecution's case was, Koli later alleged, extracted through torture not given freely. Electric shocks and beating Koli said he was reportedly tortured, including being subjected to electric shocks and beaten, then told what to say. Burns and pulled fingernails He claimed his genitals were burned and his fingernails pulled out during interrogation. The story that began to emerge was not of a killer but a Dalit man cast as a depraved villain, underlining systemic, socio-cultural inequalities that remain today. THE PROSECUTION'S CASE What didn't hold up Beyond the confession, the physical case against Koli and Pandher thinned under scrutiny. The knife and axe were dropped A knife and axe 'recovered' from the Nithari house once part of the case were dropped as evidence. ? The neighbour-doctor angle, unexamined Questions were raised over the police failing to properly investigate a neighbouring doctor suspected in an unrelated illegal kidney transplant racket and over disregard for evidence, including how the bodies were cut. Years Koli spent in custody Cases he was acquitted in Years Pandher spent in custody Allahabad High Court acquits both men The court acquitted Koli in all 12 cases against him, and Pandher in the two he had faced. It was left "disheartened" by the prosecution's handling of the arrest, confession and evidence recovery calling it all "casual and perfunctory". Supreme Court dismisses the state's appeal The top court called the earlier conviction a "manifest miscarriage of justice". Neither Koli nor Pandher, the courts eventually said, had anything to do with the deaths. Who killed the 19 girls of Nithari remains officially unanswered. Nithari killingsSurendra KoliMoninder Singh PandherAllahabad High CourtSupreme Court Under law that is illegal. And the case against Koli started to break down. The confession was allegedly recorded under duress he was reportedly tortured, including being subject to electric shocks, and beaten, and then told what to say. He claimed his genitals were burned and fingernails pulled out. The story that began to emerge was not of a killer but a Dalit man cast as a depraved villain, underlining systemic, socio-cultural inequalities that remain today. By October 2023, the Allahabad High Court acquitted Koli in all 12 cases against him, and Pandher in the two that he had faced. The court was left disheartened by the prosecutions handling of the arrest, confession and evidence recovery. It was all in a casual and perfunctory manner, the court complained. The states appeals against the acquittals were dismissed by the Supreme Court in July 2025. The top court called the earlier verdict a manifest miscarriage of justice. By then Koli had spent 19 years in custody. Pandher spent over a decade. Neither, the courts eventually said, had anything to do with the deaths. But then who killed the 19 girls? headline: Walgreens to set up Global Capability Centre in Chennai, create over 250 jobs in first year
content: Tamil Nadus growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem continues to attract companies, with Walgreens, one of the leading healthcare and pharmacy companies in the U.S. setting up a new GCC in Chennai. An MoU regarding this was signed with Walgreens India Private Limited on Friday (September 18, 2026), in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Industries Minister S. Keerthana. The proposed GCC will focus on technology and business services and is expected to create more than 250 employment opportunities in its first year, with further expansion planned over the coming years. The centre will be located at DLF Downtown, Taramani, in Chennais emerging GCC ecosystem. The investment comes on the heels of the State government announcing the Tamil Nadu Global Capability Centres Corridor and Development Programme in the Assembly recently, covering key employment corridors across Chennai and aimed at enabling the next generation of GCCs to establish, expand, and scale in the State. According to a statement, the centre will enable Walgreens to build critical technology and business capabilities from Chennai to support its enterprise operations, while creating high-value employment opportunities for the States skilled workforce.

headline: Tiger that killed two people in O'Valley in Gudalur captured
content: After a 29-day-long effort involving significant manpower, kumki elephants, drone cameras, and 14 strategically placed cages around Gudalur, the tiger that is believed to have killed two people at Lauriston in OValley, Gudalur, was trapped in one of the cages placed at the Silver Cloud Estate on Friday (September 18, 2026) morning. Following its capture, the animal was taken to the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR), where Forest Department officials verified whether the animal that they had captured was, in fact, the same one that had killed two persons over a two-week period in OValley in August. They used hair samples collected at the scenes of the incidents, besides comparing the images captured by a camera trap, for the verification process. The male tiger was then transported to the Arignar Anna Zoological Park in Chennai, where it is to live out the rest of its life in captivity.

headline: The making of Madurai's greatest landmark
content: Goddess Meenakshi is revered by the people of Madurai as their queen (Maduraiyin Rani or Arasi in Tamil), but what draws thousands of devotees from across the world to the Meenakshi-Sundareswarar Temple each day is its audacious architecture. Far more than a place of worship, the sprawling complex is a marvel of sacred design. It boasts 14 gopurams, including four towering raja gopurams at its eastern, western, southern and northern entrances; gold-plated vimanas above the sanctums of Sundareswarar and Meenakshi; the famed Golden Lotus Tank; and a train of magnificent mandapams. Built of granite, these halls are grand edifices supported by massive pillars and adorned with life-size sculptures, intricate carvings, friezes, murals and, most importantly, inscriptions. Equally striking is the Indra Vimanam above Sundareswarars sanctum, held aloft by eight silver-coated elephant sculptures. The Cholas, the Pandyas, the Vijayanagara rulers and the Nayaks contributed to transforming the Meenakshi-Sundareswarar Temple into the spectacular complex it is today. The Nayaks, who presided over the temples final great phase of architectural expansion, left the most visible imprint. Viswanatha Nayak, the dynastys founder, Tirumalai Nayak and Rani Mangammal renovated and extended the temple, building several mandapams and introducing the distinctive composite pillars featuring yalis and human figures. The inscriptions recording the Cholas contributions, however, were lost during later Nayak-era renovations. Interestingly, epigraphist and scholar C. Santhalingam points out that none of the Chola kings are known to have entered the temple, though the reason remains unknown. There was intense hostility between the Cholas and the Pandyas for about 200 years. One of the most striking features of the temple are its mandapams Ashta Shakti, Meenakshi Nayak, Mudali Pillai, Unjal, Veerappa Nayak, Veera Vasantha Raya, Kalyana, 16-pillared, 1000-pillared, Sangathar, 63-Nayanmars, Nagara and Pudhu mandapams. Among these, the 1000-pillared and Pudhu Mandapams are renowned for their extraordinary architecture and breath-taking sculptures. The Ashta Shakti Mandapam, located on the eastern side, serves as the main entrance to the temple. Apart from featuring the sculptures of dwarapalakis and eight forms of Shakti, it also houses sculptures of Tirumalai Nayak and his two wives, Rudrapathi Ammal and Dhoni Ammal, who built the mandapam. According to Porchelvi Jeyapraksh, a scholar on the temple, the mandapam was built when the Shakti cult was dominant in Tamizhagam. There is no temple, other than this one, which has a mandapam dedicated to Ashta Sakti, she says. As you walk out of the Mudali Pillai Mandapam, the Golden Lotus Tank (Potramarai kulam) confronts you. The tank is 200 ft long and 148 ft wide, with a total water spread area of 29,600 sq ft. Who excavated the tank is a mystery. Legend has it that, the tank served as the sacred site for many of Shivas 64 divine games knowns as Tiruvilaiyadalgal. He enacted these to bless his devotees, test their faith and establish righteousness. Though Meenakshi translates to the fish-eyed one, the temple tank has no fish, and it is attributed to Shivas boon to a devoted stork. The pillars on the northern corridor have intricate stone carvings of Sangam-age poets, holding palm leaf manuscripts and a stylus. It also features sculptures of Viswanatha Nayak, and Perumal, who built the corridor. On the western side of the tank is the Unjal Mandapam, built in 1653 by Chettiappa Nayak. Its ceiling and walls are decorated with exquisite murals, created during the rule of Rani Mangammal. Says S. Kannan, former associate professor of History, Annamalai University, Chidambaram, the paintings are based on three themes: The wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar witnessed by Rani Mangammal, her minister Ramappaiyer and grandson Vijayaranga Chokkanathar; Rani Mangammal receiving the royal sceptre from the goddess; and Parvatis dik vijayam. One then reaches the sanctum of Goddess Meenakshi, which, according to C. Santhalingam, was built in the 12th century CE during the reign of Kulasekhara Pandya. Until then, Meenakshi did not have a separate shrine. During the 7th century CE, when the famous Saivite saint Thirugnanasambandar visited and sang verses (Tevaram) praising the deity, Meenakshi did not have her own shrine. Instead, an idol of Angayarkanni (the one with fish-like eyes) was installed in the sanctum of Alavay Annal, as Sambandar called Chokkar or Shiva. The temple is believed to be about 1,800 years old. While Sangam-age works such as Madurai Kanchi and Purananooru, as well as the post-Sangam Paripadal, refer to a Shiva temple in Madurai, none mentions the present Meenakshi-Sundareswarar Temple. (The Sangam era was extant from third century BCE to third century CE). It is Sambandar, who, in his Madurai decads (Madurai Padhigams) describes the temples architectual layout, its location on the southern bank of the Vaigai river, and the long compound wall (neel madhil). He also talks about the Pandya king Ninraseer Nedumaran, his queen Mangayarkarasi and his minister Kulachirayar worshipping at the shrine of Alavay Annal. Tirunavukkarasar alias Appar, another revered Saivite saint and a contemporary of Sambandar, too has sung decads about this temple. From a simple brick structure with a couple of towers in the 7th century CE, the Meenakshi-Sundareswarar temple has today metamorphosed into a massive temple complex over 15.37 acres. Besides the main sanctums, it also now has separate shrines for Mukkuruni Vinayagar, Nataraja (depicted in a rare posture with his right leg raised and balancing on his left), Ellam Valla Siddhar, Bhikshatana, Saraswati and Subrahmanya. To appreciate its grand architecture, mention should be made about the Kambathadi Mandapam, in front of Sundareswarars sanctum. Built by Nattukkottai Chettiars or Nagarathars in 1870, on its eight pillars are a large panel depicting the Sundareswarar-Meenakshi marriage, with Vishnu, her brother, consecrating the wedding. There are 25 sculptures of Shiva on these pillars representing his anugraha, samhara and nritta aspects. Their iconography is distinct from Nayak-period sculptures. The Kambathadi sculptures are heavily ornamented and characterised by cleft chins, razor-sharp shin bones and bulging kneecaps, adds Prof. Kannan. The temple had faced debilitating vicissitudes from three Delhi Sultanate invasions by Malik Kafur in 1311, Khusroo Khan in 1314 and Ulugh Khan in 1323. Parakrama Pandya, who built the west raja gopuram, valiantly fought the invaders but fled to Kalaiyar Kovil during the third invasion. The invaders ransacked and looted the Madurai, Srirangam and Chidambaram temples. The Meenakshi-Sundareswar temple was shut down for 48 years from 1323 to 1371. The Vijayanagara army commander, Kumara Kampanna, arrived in Madurai in 1378 and drove out the invaders. Madurai was liberated and worship revived in the temple, whose mahakumbabishekam was performed yesterday after a gap of 17 years.

headline: Elections to 7,405 primary cooperative societies to be held in first phase in T.N.
content: The Tamil Nadu State Cooperative Societies Election Commission is considering holding elections to 7,405 primary cooperative societies across 38 zones in the first phase of the electoral process. In a recent letter to the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Dayanand Kataria, Commissioner of the Tamil Nadu State Cooperative Societies Election Commission (TNSCSEC), said the Commission had decided to hold elections to 7,405 primary cooperative societies in the 38 zones in Phase I in four stages. The Commission also sought district-wise details of these societies. It also sought details of the cooperative societies for which elections would be conducted in Phases II to V. According to official sources, last time, elections were held to 18,244 cooperative societies, and 1,88,400 board members were elected in 2018. After the five-year term of the board members expired in 2023, administrators were appointed to the cooperative societies.

headline: Taiwan holds first joint drill using multiple attack drones in modernisation push
content: Taiwan's military carried out its first joint combat exercise using multiple types of attack drones this week, President Lai Ching-te said on Friday (September 18, 2026) showed how the armed forces were adapting to the needs of modern warfare. Mr. Lai has made defence modernisation a key part of his agenda given the rising threat from China, including developing drones and spending more on defence, something U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly pressed the countrys allies to do. Overseeing the drills in the far south of Taiwan, which also included launches of domestically developed Hsiung Feng III anti-ship missiles and Lockheed Martin-made HIMARS rockets, Mr. Lai said precision firing exercises are crucial for testing weapon effectiveness. In particular, this marks the first time the military has incorporated multiple types of attack drones into joint combat exercises, Mr. Lai said, according to a transcript of his comments to officers provided by the presidential office. The coordinated use of unmanned vehicles with conventional weapons reflects the adaptation to modern warfare, he added. The statement from his office did not say what types of drones were used during the three days of drills and only provided images of the missiles. Drones, which are very low of cost, have become central to combat operations both in the war between Ukraine and Russia and in the West Asia, and Taiwan has been keen to learn lessons from those conflicts for its contingency planning. Mr. Lai said the military is accelerating its combat capabilities to show Taiwan has the confidence and capability to defend national sovereignty and fulfil its responsibility for regional peace and stability. Mr. Lai was accompanied not only by Defence Minister Wellington Koo and other senior security officials, but also by Kuan Bi-ling, head of Taiwans Ocean Affairs Council, during his visit. Also Read | China warns of consequences for Taiwan after Taipei envoys attend Pacific leaders summit The government has been working to better integrate the Coast Guard into overall defence planning, given it would have an auxiliary role to the navy during a war. During Taiwans main annual war games in August, a Coast Guard ship was fitted with anti-ship missiles. Mr. Lai and his government reject Beijings sovereignty claims, saying only Taiwans people can decide their future.

headline: F-16 fighter jet crashes during training in Michigan; pilot ejects safely
content: 16 fighter jet from Texas crashed in rural Michigan during a routine training exercise on Thursday (September 17, 2026), and the pilot ejected safely, a military spokesman said. Sgt Derek Gutierrez, a public affairs specialist with the 149th Fighter Wing, said the pilot was receiving medical treatment at a local hospital. Mr. Gutierrez declined to release details about the pilots identity or any injuries, citing military policy. The plane was participating in training exercises at a National Guard base in Alpena, about 190 miles (305 kilometres) north of Detroit. Witnesses reported hearing a loud crash, while images posted on social media showed a dark plume of smoke in the air. Wendy Sobeck said she and her husband heard a very loud crash down the road, minutes from their rural home. We thought there was a car accident outside our house. We saw big billowing black smoke. We couldnt tell what it was, so my husband got into his pickup truck and saw what happened, Ms. Sobeck said. You could see the plane debris in the field. Explosions kept happening. Fred Sobeck (65) said he drove down the road and saw a big fireball in the field near a house and a camper, which were not hit. Police told me to get out of there because of explosions, he said. The jet was one of several F-16 aircraft from Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, taking part in the Michigan training exercises, Sgt. Gutierrez said. The military began flying the first F-16s in 1979. There have been at least 14 Class A mishaps involving F-16s since 2000, according to the Air Force Safety Center. The Class A mishap designation is generally used when the damage totals more than $2 million, when an aircraft is destroyed or when a service member is killed. In December last year, an F-16C Fighting Falcon with the Air Forces elite Thunderbirds demonstration squadron crashed in the Southern California desert, and the pilot in that crash was also able to eject safely.
