She said the current situation highlighted the need for North Korea to take responsive measures proportional or more offensive in its nature and warned that the countrys armed forces would mobilize all means available if its security or national interests were violated. The statement was Ms. Kims second in two days. On Thursday (September 17, 2026), she rejected renewed calls for North Koreas denuclearisation at an International Atomic Energy Agency conference and reiterated Pyongyangs position that its status as a nuclear weapons state is irreversible. Pacific Vanguard 2026, a multilateral exercise led by the U.S. Navy and involving the navies of South Korea, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Japan in the vicinity of Guam, ran from August 29 to September 10, according to Japans Maritime Self-Defence Force.

headline: Before court today, Sir Sobha Singh Trust plea against RSS affiliate over rent dues of '15 years'
content: A petition by the Sir Sobha Singh Public Charitable Trust over alleged non-payment of rent by RSS-affiliated trade outfit Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS), among others, for four of its properties is coming up for a hearing before the Tis Hazari Court on Friday. The rented premises comprise four rooms across two floors of the Sir Sobha Singh Building, located near the New Delhi Railway Station, which was once the headquarters of the Bharatiya Jan Sangh, the precursor to the BJP. The BMS occupies the four premises as its Delhi headquarters now. The four matters related to the four portions are in court. In its petition, which was filed in 2021, the Sir Sobha Singh Trust has said that the respondents have been in continuous rent default for 15 years and continue to occupy the premises without authorisation. Cases have been filed against Deshraj Gupta over three portions, and Jagdish Prasad Mathur over one (both Deshraj and Mathur are no more). Deshraj was the son of Hansraj Gupta, the late mayor of Delhi. The three other sons of Hansraj Shiv Raj (also deceased), Rajendra (ex-Mayor and former Delhi minister) and Mahendra are also named as respondents, as is the BMS. Hansraj served as the Delhi Prant Sangh Chalak of the RSS for years and was mayor of Delhi Nagar Nigam from 1967 to 1972, as a Jan Sangh candidate. Mathur was an RSS pracharak who worked with the Jan Sangh and later with the BJP for decades. Court records suggest that with none of the other respondents turning up in court, the BMS alone is fighting the legal battle. On January 28 this year, the BMS offered to pay the arrears, says its advocate Adarsh Tiwari. Our case is solid. A certain rent amount is outstanding, and that we will pay. While the advocate of the Trust, Anand Singh, declined to comment, a source said: They (the tenants) have been occupying the building unauthorisedly and not paying rent for several years. The BMS was founded in 1955 by Dattopant Thengdi. When the Jan Sangh started functioning from the building, it was a struggling outfit, and found its feet after 1967, when it became a part of coalition governments in a few states. A nearby building is now owned by the BJP and is still being used by it. The Trust claims it has received no rent from the tenants since January 2006, with the arrears standing at more than Rs. 1.27 lakh as of February 28, 2021. According to the Trusts petition, the tenancy was created around 1951 in the name of Hansraj, who was also an industrialist, with the premises to be used as a personal office linked to his work with both the BMS and Jan Sangh. Records show that the rent for one of the four portions was Rs. 849.20 per month in 2013. The Trust says rent and house tax were paid till 2005, with the last recorded payment of Rs. 1,281 received by cheque dated January 24, 2006, for one of the portions. As per the petition, on April 23, 2013, trustee Preminder Singh sent a notice seeking Rs. 54,393 in arrears and invoking Section 6A of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, which allows a 10% rent increase every three years. By that calculation, the monthly rent for a portion was Rs. 772 in June 2013. Again, on August 14, 2020, the Trust sent a notice to Guptas four sons and the BMS. The notice gave 15 days to pay the dues of Rs. 2.48 lakh, with 15% interest, as well as to restore the premises and vacate. The Trust has cited unauthorised subletting and structural damage as a second ground for eviction. As per its petition, a site inspection on July 14, 2020, showed the Gupta brothers no longer possessed the building and it was solely occupied by the BMS. And that the open balcony and verandah in front of the tenanted area had been enclosed and an unauthorised shed erected. The Sir Sobha Singh Public Charitable Trust was created in March 1961 by Sardar Bahadur Sir Sobha Singh, with an initial endowment of Rs. 5,000. Sir Sobha Singh was one of the principal contractors for Lutyens New Delhi, and behind the construction of historic buildings such as the South Block, the National Museum and parts of Connaught Place and India Gate. The Trusts original trustees included S Ujjal Singh (later Governor of Punjab and Tamil Nadu), S Bhagwan Singh, writer Khushwant Singh, S Daljit Singh and R B Nathu Ram.

headline: CBI names 2 BHEL officials in FIR regarding missing 31 kg silver
content: According to the FIR, the disappearance of 31.65 kg of silver from a locker at the Amorphous Silicon Solar Cell Plant of BHEL came to light during an inspection in 2024. The missing silver, at the prevailing rate, is valued at around Rs. 71 lakh. A Central public sector undertaking, BHEL manufactures photovoltaic cells, which require silver. The Gurugram plant also functions as BHELs dedicated industrial research and development centre for photovoltaics. The CBIs preliminary inquiry into the matter on February 26 found prima facie commission of cognizable offences by the plants Additional General Manager and head Dr Bharat Kumar Pant, and the plants then manager-cum-material management section in-charge Ashish Kumar. The inquiry disclosed that nearly 35.6 kg of Silver Targets/ Recyclable Silver belonging to MNRE-funded assets were available at ASSCP, BHEL, Gurugram, until 2016-17 and the same continued to be reflected in records/ audit observations until 2020. However, during physical verification conducted on 06.02.2024, the quantity of Silver was found available as 6.23 kg (3.98 kg silver target and 2.25 kg scrap) in the Godrej Safe, thereby revealing that around 31.65 kg silver was found unaccounted for, the CBI sub-inspector in-charges complaint read. The CBI registered the FIR on July 8 on the basis of the complaint of its sub-inspector under Indian Penal Code (IPC) sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence) and 409 (criminal breach of trust by public servants) and Section 13 (criminal misconduct by public servant) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. While the FIR names Pant, who remains the AGM and head of the plant, and Kumar, who is now a manager at the BHEL corporate office in Delhi, it also says that the roles of three others Ajay Yadav, Vinayan Bhardwaj and Ajai Kumar should also be looked into. Yadav was then the manager for finance and human resources at the plant and is now the Joint General Manager (Finance) at Noida Metro Rail Corporation, while Bhardwaj and Ajai Kumar were manager and engineer, respectively, at the plant then and are now posted in the BHELs corporate office in Delhi. BHEL and Noida Metro Rail Corporation did not respond to emails sent seeking comment. An email sent to Dr Pant went unanswered. The CBIs inquiry found that annual physical verification of the silver was conducted regularly until 2018, but from 2019, when Pant took over as the head of the plant, it was stopped. Further, inventory verification reports and stock registers pertaining to crucial years were also found missing. No proper system for recording consumption, movement or custody of silver was maintained at BHEL, ASSCP, Gurugram. The internal control mechanism relating to custody and verification of silver was systematically weakened, thereby facilitating unauthorised access and gradual removal of silver over a period of time without detection, the complaint says. It adds that the officials examined during the enquiry gave contradictory statements regarding physical verification of the silver, the custody of keys to the safe, the existence of records, and opening of cartons and files. This, it said, indicated concealment and suppression of material facts. The complaint says that Ashish Kumar, Yadav, Bhardwaj and Ajai Kumar had participated in the physical verification of the silver on March 31, 2022, when 35.6kg of silver was found. After that, the silver was placed in the custody of the material management section of the plant, it says. It adds that the four officials did not reveal this during their examination in the inquiry. The inquiry also revealed that Ashish Kumar, Ajay Yadav and Vinayan Bhardwaj also participated in the process of physical verification of silver targets on 06.02.2024 during which, out of 35.6 kg of silver, only 6.23 kg of silver was found available. Despite having knowledge of earlier inventory figures, they also failed to raise objections regarding the substantial shortage of silver and signed the physical verification report dated 06.02.2024. Their statements were found contradictory to documentary evidence collected during enquiry, it says.

headline: Uttarakhand's spiritual solution to stem migration – Rudraksh farming
content: What makes Rudraksh a viable option is that it addresses a number of problems that mar other crops: It is not eaten by wildlife, requires little maintenance, and has a large domestic and export market. However, it is not without its challenges. For a state touted as Dev Bhoomi (land of the Gods), Uttarakhand is not alien to the significance of Rudraksh the seed used to make prayer beads and is revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Now, the state government has plans to channelise these very beads to stem a problem that it has been battling for decades: Migration, especially from the hill districts. The Uttarakhand government has directed its Horticulture Department to draw up a formal cultivation policy for Rudraksh, as part of an effort to create new income sources in these districts. The instruction came in a notification on August 31. Signed by Under Secretary Sandeep Sharma of the states Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department, and addressed to the Director of Horticulture and Food Processing, the letter instructed the officials to study a proposal on cultivation methods, farm management, post-harvest processing, marketing and soil suitability. It asked the department to submit a clear proposal to the government as soon as possible. The letter follows a request from Tehri MLA Kishore Upadhyay to Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, and a four-member government delegations visit to Nepal in March to study Rudraksh cultivation there. The delegation included Upadhyay, Rudraksh expert Prince Agrawal, and Ramesh Singh Pal, a senior agricultural scientist. The groups findings are laid out in a 197-page technical report and an accompanying presentation, Strategic Introduction of Rudraksha Cultivation in Uttarakhand, presented to CM Dhami, in July. The migration problem Uttarakhands hill districts have long been losing residents to Dehradun, Delhi and other cities a trend the states own migration commission has tracked and attributed, in part, to a lack of viable income from agriculture, crop damage from wildlife, and fragmented landholdings. The expert teams presentation to the government frames the wildlife menace, fragmented, low-yield holdings and lack of cash-generating assets as the core drivers of migration from the hills. It describes Rudraksh as a crop that addresses each of these problems: It is not eaten by wildlife, requires little maintenance once established, and has a large, and mostly unmet, domestic and export market. The China market Much of the case for the project rests on demand from China, which the presentation identifies as the worlds largest importer of Rudraksh. Citing customs data, the report states that China accounts for 63.7% of total recorded Rudraksh exports, followed by the United States at 19.3%. A table in the presentation estimates Chinas 2025 Rudraksha imports, sourced mainly from Nepals collector and raw-bead trade, at $100,800,000 roughly five times Indias own import bill of $20,140,000, more than 95% of which, the presentation states, comes from Indonesia and Nepal. Pal stated a specific example from the delegations trip to illustrate the scale of that market: We went to Nepal and saw a 29-mukhi Rudraksh there ourselves. Referring to the bead with 29 lobes or ridges a rare variety, he said, A single piece is for about Rs. 1.5 crore. China imports more of this than India does. The presentation notes that large-scale commercial production of Rudraksh is currently dominated by Nepal and Indonesia, and argues that Uttarakhand, which shares similar soil and climate conditions with Nepals growing regions, has not yet captured any share of that trade. China is buying a lot of Rudraksh because it has both religious and medicinal uses there. There are different rituals and traditions in which Rudraksh is used, and people also wear it as a necklace, considering it sacred. They have their own traditions and monasteries where it is believed in and used, said scientist Pal. It also has medicinal value in Ayurveda. Some people believe that using water in which Rudraksh has been soaked helps with skin ailments and other health problems, said Pal. Besides China, the bead is in demand in Singapore and Japan. Followers believe it brings prosperity and well being, said Singh. Lessons from Nepal trip The team visited Bhetedhar and Dingla in Nepals Bhojpur district from March 23 to 29 and collected soil samples for comparison against sites in Tehri Garhwal, Rishikesh, Haridwars Chilla forest range, and the Mansa Devi and Manokamna temple areas of Uttarakhand. According to the presentation, Nepals Rudraksh belt sits between 600 and 2,000 metres in altitude, with average temperatures of 25-30C and annual rainfall of 1,500-2,500mm. Uttarakhands proposed growing zone 500 to 1,800 metres high with 2235C average temperature, and 1,0002,200mm of rainfall falls within a comparable range. The comparative soil analysis indicates that Uttarakhand soils are largely suitable for Rudraksh cultivation and comparable to Nepalese growing regions, the presentation said. Based on those findings, the presentation listed Pauri, Tehri, Rudraprayag, Chamoli, Almora and Bageshwar as high potential districts for plantation, and Nainital, Champawat, Pithoragarh and the hill areas of Dehradun as that of moderate potential. Not without challenges Pal also raised concerns about problems that have affected earlier, less organised attempts to grow Rudraksh in the state. He said a similar-looking but different species, known as Bhadraksh, is often mistaken for or substituted for genuine Rudraksh. The two are entirely different species same genus, but Bhadraksh grows in Rudrakshs place in a lot of areas. In the early stage, the sapling looks exactly like a Rudraksh plant. Its only later, after fruiting starts, two or four years in, that you can tell the difference, he added. Herein lies another problem that the report also acknowledges: Rudraksh trees do not begin fruiting for six to eight years, and take about 10 years to reach peak production stage. The report estimates that a hill migrant working in a city typically saves Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 15,000 a month. By comparison, it states, a single mature Rudraksh tree can produce 1,000 to 2,000 beads a year, which, at a conservative wholesale price of Rs. 10-20 per bead for the common five-faced variety, would generate Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 40,000 annually per tree. A family managing 20 mature trees could earn Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 8 lakh a year, according to the report. To cover the years before the trees begin bearing fruit, the plan proposes using the Centres rural employment guarantee scheme to fund labour for digging pits, planting and fencing for the first three years. The Horticulture Department would supply saplings for free or at subsidised rates for the purpose, it adds. A later phase calls for training womens self-help groups in cleaning, grading and oiling harvested beads, and training young people in stringing prayer beads, silver-capping and packaging work that, according to the report, pays significantly more than selling raw beads. The report sets a target of 10,000 hectares under Rudraksh cultivation by 2047, with 10 million trees planted, 50,000 to 70,000 farmers involved, and up to 150,000 rural jobs created.

headline: Six months after docking, Iranian navy ship still in Kochi, with some crew members
content: The Lavan and Dena had come to India in February to participate in the International Fleet Review and the MILAN 2026 multilateral naval exercises in Visakhapatnam. Six months after the outbreak of the war in West Asia, Iranian Navy landing ship IRIS Lavan, which docked in Kochi on March 4, the day the frigate IRIS Dena was sunk by a US submarine in the waters near Sri Lanka, remains at the port city with part of its crew. The Lavan and Dena had come to India in February to participate in the International Fleet Review and the MILAN 2026 multilateral naval exercises in Visakhapatnam. As the ships set out for home after the exercise, the war began. A third Iranian Navy ship, the fleet supply vessel IRIS Bushehr, sought refuge in Sri Lanka on March 5. India allowed the Lavan to dock at Kochi on March 4 on humanitarian grounds after the vessel reported technical issues. The crew was hosted at Indian naval facilities. It is learnt that over two dozen essential crew members of the Lavan are still in Kochi, a long with the ship. The guardianship of the vessel has now been transferred to the Cochin Port Authority, sources said. The Lavan had 183 crew members on board when it docked at Kochi in March. A month later, India repatriated the non-essential crew members. It is learnt that over 50 crew members are still in Kochi. On March 7, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar had said that India allowed the Lavan to dock in Kochi on humanitarian grounds. You had these ships, and we got a message from the Iranian side that one of the ships, which presumably was closest to our waters at that point of time wanted to come into our port. They were reporting that they were having problems. And so, my recollection is this was on the 28th (February). And on the 1st (March), we said, okay, you can come in, he said. It took them a few days to sail in, and then they docked in Kochi. And the ship is there. And obviously, the people on the ship, a lot of them young cadets They have disembarked. They are, you know, in a nearby facility When they set out and came here, the situation was totally different. They were coming in for a fleet review, and then they got, in a way, caught on the wrong side of events. So for us, when this ship wanted to come in, and that too in difficulties, I think it was the humane thing to do, Jaishankar said.

headline: Poland warns Russia planning drone or rocket strikes on NATO territory, says attacks will be called 'accidental'
content: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned on Thursday (September 17, 2026) that Russia is planning hybrid strikes with drones or rockets on European countries supporting Ukraine, among them Poland. Russia will pretend the attacks are accidental in order to paralyze or at least weaken the motivation of NATO countries" to rush to the defence of the member state coming under attack, Mr. Tusk said in a speech to the Polish Parliament. There is a real risk that drones or other types of projectiles will enter the territory of one or several countries on the eastern flank and even cause destruction," PM Tusk warned. The official narration will be that it's an accident and there is no reason for NATO to think about a response, he added. He said Russia was more dangerous because it was increasingly using jet-powered drones, which fly higher and faster and thus are more difficult to detect by air defense before reaching their targets. Mr. Tusk has been for months warning that Russia might be preparing a more serious hybrid attack against a NATO country. His warnings have gotten increasingly specific as he received intelligence from NATO, Ukrainian and U.S. secret services, including the CIA, he said. In recent days, Mr. Tusk has said Russia was now focusing on attacking border crossings between Ukraine and its European neighbors in order to disrupt delivery lines to Ukraine. Four such incidents happened on Poland's border with Ukraine in the past week and several others took place in the last weeks on Ukraine's border with Moldova. Mr. Tusk said at the moment Russia was not ready for any peace talks without the total capitulation of Ukraine. They are convinced the winter will be tragically critical for Ukraine. He said last winter Poland stepped in with deliveries when Ukraine's energy infrastructure came under attack, but if border crossings are destroyed, it will be much harder for Warsaw to offer such help this upcoming winter. Russia's goal is to destroy as much as possible the economy and logistics of Ukraine, Mr. Tusk said, adding that intelligence indicates continuous attacks of very high frequency and intensity on six main Ukrainian cities should be expected in the near future. Mr. Tusk announced he would travel to Ukraine overnight to Friday (September 18, 2026), in what can be seen as an act of defiance against Russia after European leaders narrowly escaped a drone strike on a train near the Polish-Ukrainian border on Sunday (September 13, 2026). Officials usually keep their travel plans to Ukraine secret for security reasons. In Kyiv, he said he would discuss with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy how to defend against the new types of drones as well as discuss with partners including Slovakia about further sanctions against Russia. On Thursday (September 17, 2026), U.S. President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that major progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland after a US delegation was in Poland last week to visit several possible locations. If this happens, the location will be announced very soon, Mr. Trump wrote. This will be a historic step for our Great US/Polish Alliance. Poland has for years sought to host a permanent US base as a strong guarantee of its security in the face of the rising Russian threat. Poland's high defence spending and major U.S. arms purchases have persuaded the Trump administration to consider putting a permanent base in Poland even as it reorganises and reduces its overall military presence in Europe. In May, the U.S. unexpectedly withdrew troops from the total of around 10,000 stationed in Poland, causing confusion among European allies and nervousness in Warsaw. But officials in both Poland and the U.S. soon said the withdrawal was temporary and Poland was not expected to suffer from the U.S. troop reorganisation.

headline: 'No Doubt': Pakistan General Vows To Defend Saudi Arabia 'To Any Extent' Amid Houthi Attacks
content: Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan's pledge covered more than territorial defence, extending specifically to the protection of Makkah and Madinah.

headline: Togo-flagged tanker stuck in Strait of Hormuz: Iran Guards
content: Irans Revolutionary Guards Navy said it struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker which was attempting to make an illegal passage through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media said early on Friday (September 18, 2026). The tanker which was attacked on Thursday (September 17, 2026) came to a halt after catching fire, the Revolutionary Guards Navy added.

headline: Hiranandani-backed Greenbase to develop 5mn sqft in TN with ₹2k cr investment
content: backed industrial and warehouse infrastructure venture, plans to develop about five million sqft industrial and logistics park in the outskirts of Chennai with an investment of Rs. 2,000 crore. The company said it has completed land acquisition and is developing a 215-acre parcel in key industrial corridors near Oragadam and Gummudipoondin to meet growing demand. The project will be financed by a mix of equity and debt.The company has about 160 acres in Palur, near Oragadam and 55 acres in Arani, near Gummudipoondi and expects the development to complete in two years. The company targets to develop about 9 million to 10 million sqft of Grade A industrial infrastructure across the country, out of which around 50%- 60% will be Tamil Nadu. Other projects in Pune and Mumbai (MMRDA/Bhiwandi-Vada region). The total outlay is around Rs. 3,500 crore spread over three to five years.N Sridhar, CEO, Greenbase the company is identifying opportunities in Coimbatore and Hosur and evaluating in Tutucorin with growing interest from multi-nationals setting up facilities. Three more locations in Southern market will cumulatively take up to another 100 acres of development.Sridhar said apart from macro and structural factors such as Make in India and Oragadam corridor, the company is witnessing demand from companies in high-tech manufacturing and emerging sectors such as battery energy storage systems, electric vehicle, defence and electronics. Clean energy and battery storage systems are among the new categories of industries driving demand prominently. We see a lot of interest from the EV ecosystem, including motors, battery, components, electronics manufacturing, ESDM, industrial automation, robotics, defense production and advanced manufacturing, along with automotive and auto components, heavy engineering, third party logistics, he said.The Arani facility is located closer to Gummudipoondi, where large scale battery and energy storage systems and industrial electronics facilities are expected to be established under the union govts electronic manufacturing cluster 2.0. He said the company has finalized talks with notable anchor companies, including a few in Gummudipoondi.Greenbase is joint venture between Hiranandani group and private equity company Blackstone with about 5 million sqft and existing parks at Oragadam, Chennai and Talegaon, Pune. The company calls this second phase Greenbase 2.0 and pursues primarily with its own capital.Niranjan Hiranandani, chairperson of the Hiranandani group, was quoted as saying, Global manufacturers are looking for dependable ecosystems, faster execution, sustainability and infrastructure that can support scale over the long term.

headline: Prince Harry makes first public appearances 'back on British soil'
content: Britains Prince Harry made his first public appearance on Thursday (September 17, 2026) since he and his wife Meghan returned to Britain after six years in California, saying, Its good to be back on British soil. Prince Harry, the younger son of King Charles, relocated last month with Ms. Meghan and their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, surprising even their close family. The royal attended the inaugural Invictus Spirit Awards in London, which are linked to the Invictus Games, the sporting competition for wounded, injured and sick military veterans that he founded. Earlier, Prince Harry spoke at an event focused on improving the care of children wounded in conflict hosted by charity Save the Children and Imperial College London. His appearances came on a busy day for Britains royals, with King Charles hosting a conference for AI leaders amid criticism in a forthcoming book by the brother of his late first wife, Diana. The book by Charles Spencer is being serialised in the Daily Mail. In the latest extracts published on Thursday (September 17, 2026), Charles Spencer said King Charles sounded like a lottery winner after the death of Diana.

headline: CBFC flags screening of Umar Khalid documentary at IIIT-Hyderabad
content: A PROPOSED screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad has likely been cancelled after the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) flagged the programme, stating that publicly exhibiting an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained. The documentary, Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, is directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani. It was scheduled to be shown by a group of students at the institutes KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act, the CBFC posted on X. It also tagged IIIT-Hyderabad, stating the institutes authorities may take note for necessary action. Citing sources, PTI reported that the students have decided to cancel the screening. The invitation for the screening said it was planned on the occasion of Political Prisoners Day. It also referred to the death anniversary of Jatindra Nath Das, a comrade of Bhagat Singh, who died after a prolonged hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929. The development follows the postponement of a planned screening of the documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru. This decision came after objections were raised by the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), which claimed that allowing the screening would amount to using the campus for political propaganda. The student committee postponed the screening, citing logistical and security considerations, while adding that it would be held later in the trimester. Prisoner No. 626710 is Present is based on former JNU research scholar Khalid. He was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots. Khalid was charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.

headline: U.S. approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia
content: The United States has approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes and related equipment to Saudi Arabia, the U.S. State Department announced on Thursday (September 17, 2026), in a significant boost to the kingdom's forces. Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel the only country in the region to operate the jets have voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push for the kingdom to normalise relations. "The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia's capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defense, and improving interoperability with US forces," the State Department said in a statement. It "will also augment Saudi Arabia's operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defense capability," it added. The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of U.S. lawmakers.

headline: Nepal flash flood death toll surges to 1,410; over 6,100 still missing
content: The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,410 on Thursday (September 17, 2026), with over 6,100 people still missing, according to the country's disaster management authorities. Flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects. According to the data issued by Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority(NDRRMA) on Thursday evening, 1,410 people have been killed in the floods so far, with 6,145 people still missing. According to NDRRMA, 364 dead bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 232 from Nawalparasi East, 222 from Nawalparasi West, and 203 from Nuwakot. Similarly, 199 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 78 bodies from Gorkha, 72 bodies from Dhading and 38 bodies from Tanahu. Two flood victims died in Kathmandu hospitals while undergoing treatment. So far, 13,756 people have been rescued from the flood-affected areas. The joint command of security personnel continues to carry out search and rescue operations in the flood-affected areas.

headline: Russia, China veto U.S. proposal for UN experts to keep monitoring sanctions on Iran
content: Russia and China vetoed a United Nations resolution on Thursday (September 17, 2026) that would have authorised UN experts to keep monitoring sanctions that were reimposed against Iran last year over its nuclear program. The UN Security Council sanctions are still in effect, which freeze Iran's assets abroad, halt arms deals with Tehran and penalize any development of Iran's ballistic missile program, among other measures. Using a provision in the 2015 nuclear deal between Iran and major powers France, Germany and the United Kingdom triggered the snapback mechanism, which reimposed the sanctions on September 27, 2025. It restored the Security Council sanctions committee and authorised a panel of UN experts to monitor implementation. The United States drafted a resolution to extend the UN expert panel's mandate for a year, coming as America also pursues a wider campaign to isolate Tehran from its remaining economic partners as the more than six-month-old war in Iran has hit a stalemate. The proposal was defeated by a vote of 11-2, with Somalia and Pakistan abstaining, because of the Russian and Chinese vetoes. Since Israel and the U.S. struck Iran's nuclear sites in June 2025, UN nuclear inspectors have been unable to verify the status of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium. According to the UN nuclear watchdog, Iran maintained a stockpile of 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium enriched up to 60 per cent purity a short, technical step away from weapons-grade levels of 90 per cent. Iran's UN mission thanked China and Russia for vetoing the resolution, saying on social media that the countries prevented yet another cynical attempt by the United States and its allies to abuse the Security Council for their political purposes. U.S. Deputy Ambassador to the UN Jennifer Locetta said the United States wasn't surprised by the vetoes because the experts would have shined the light" on prohibited cooperation between Iran and its partners. She said the vetoes are part of a broader effort to prevent expert monitoring of sanctions, and even the appointment of panel members, to stifle reporting that implicates their own activities in support of rogue regimes. In March 2024, a Russian veto ended UN monitoring of sanctions against North Korea over its nuclear program. In Mali, sanctions were terminated, and Locetta said that in Yemen and the Central African expert appointments have been delayed or refused. While the panel of experts for Iran was authorized a year ago and Secretary-General Antonio Guterres proposed members, they were never approved. Without an independent panel of experts, this council loses its principal source of impartial, evidence-based reporting on sanctions violations, creating a monitoring gap that only benefits the Iranian regime and those who profit from evading those measures, Ms. Locetta warned. Russian UN Ambassador Vassily Nebenzia reiterated Moscow's claim that the snapback of sanctions against Iran was illegal, and therefore the resolution to extend the mandate of the panel of experts was deeply flawed and did not have any legal basis. Russia and China had strongly urged the U.S. and its allies not to put the resolution to a vote, which would only increase tensions in the council, Nebenzia said, but Washington decided to opt for confrontation. French UN Ambassador Jerome Bonnafont, the current council president, said implementing sanctions is a crucial instrument to encourage Iran to return to its nuclear obligations. France will study how to ensure sanctions are enforced, he said. One possibility would be to follow what happened after the North Korea panel of experts was abolished: establishing a monitoring team that includes France, Germany, the UK and the United States.

headline: 'I'm Back': WikiLeaks Founder Julian Assange Returns To X After Two-Year Silence
content: The WikiLeaks founder's personal account had once been central to the campaign pushing for his freedom, but fell silent on 28 June 2024.

headline: Two U.S.-bound vessels apparently compromised by hackers: officials
content: U.S. Coast Guard and FBI personnel boarded two commercial vessels bound for the United States in the Gulf of Mexico last month after indications that hackers had broken into their computer networks, the agencies said on Thursday (September 17, 2026). The unusual operation, carried out on August 21 and August 24 aboard two foreign-flagged ships, comes as U.S. authorities grapple with a series of cyber incidents that media reports have linked to Iran since the outbreak of conflict between Washington and Tehran. The FBI said a joint Coast Guard-FBI team boarded the vessels after receiving indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised. The Coast Guard, which referred only to the August 21 boarding, said that foreign cyber actors were involved but did not identify them. Neither agency provided further details about the incidents or explained the discrepancies between their accounts. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency referred questions back to the Coast Guard. Corey Ranslem, CEO of maritime security group Dryad Global, said that his firm had confirmed that one of the ships was the Liberian-flagged VL Prosperity. The vessel is currently anchored in waters around Galveston in Texas, according to LSEG and MarineTraffic ship tracking data. Liberias flag registry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Irans Mehr news agency reported on August 20 that VL Prosperity had suffered what it called a major cyberattack while transiting through the Strait of Gibraltar and that its communications had been knocked out for 30 hours. Citing an unnamed crew member, Mehr reported that hackers had also infiltrated the engine-room systems, reduced the engines cooling flow, increased the engine speed, and disabled the ships fuel and engine-oil tank. The Iranian news agency did not say who was thought to be behind the alleged attack. Although dramatic in its effects, a ship-centered cyberattack is not that difficult to pull off, Mr. Ranslem said. We are expecting these types of attacks to continue and will expand in the very near future, he said.

headline: Prasanna Kumar Acharya is new CMD of NLCIL
content: According to a press release, Mr. Acharya has nearly three decades of experience in the power, mining and infrastructure sectors. He has held key positions in organisations including GRIDCO, NTPC and Tata Power. He had made significant contributions to major infrastructure initiatives, including the Phase - II project of Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL). During his tenure at NLCIL, Mr. Acharya had led several initiatives in digital transformation and governance reforms, including ERP modernisation, centralisation of various finance functions, AI-enabled systems and introduction of a vendor Invoice Management System. Mr. Acharya also played an important role in steering joint ventures with various State utilities and in supporting NLCILs ambitious growth roadmap, which envisages achieving more than 20 GW of power generation capacity and over 100 MTPA of mining capacity by 2030, while progressing towards its vision of becoming a Maharatna enterprise.

headline: State Finance Commission chairman calls for authority, greater fiscal autonomy for local bodies
content: Local bodies should be given authority, greater fiscal autonomy and resources, Chairman of the Tamil Nadu government-constituted Seventh State Finance Commission (SSFC) K. Allaudin said on Thursday. If we could achieve this decentralisation, we will cease to be a mere Constitutional promise and we will become a lived reality of Indian democracy, he said. In his presidential address in the national seminar on Strengthening Local Body Governance and Finances organised by the SSFC and the Madras Institute of Development Studies in Chennai, Mr. Allaudin said that no institution can exercise meaningful autonomy and discharge its functions without adequate and predictable financial resources. Local governments continue to depend substantially on transfers from the Union and State governments, he said. Gagandeep Singh Bedi, Secretary of the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department pointed out that the own sources of revenue (OSR) for rural local bodies in many States through property and professional taxes, rentals and charges, among others, ranged between 1% to 8%. While the collection of property tax in OECD countries was about 1.1% of the GDP, it was only 0.2% in India, he said and added: If we want our cities, villages to be better developed, then we have to do something more. We also have to, perhaps, pay more property tax, etc. As for functions of the local bodies, Mr. Bedi also flagged the issue of spouses of elected women representatives in local bodies attempting to take over their role informally, despite 50% reservation of seats for women in local bodies in some States. Though it is decreasing, I think we should empower the women elected representatives, he said. Mr. Bedi called for GIS-based tax collection and focus on solid waste management, user charges, parking fees, among others to augment the revenue. Dharmendra Pratap Yadav, Secretary, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department referred to the State governments initiative for rural empowerment, specifically through Tamil Nadu Village Empowerment, Transformation and Rejuvenation Initiative (TN-VETRI). He also underlined the importance of providing authority to rural local bodies for levy and collection of taxes. Calling for autonomy to local bodies, Mr. Yadav was critical of the bureaucratic environment and pointed out that bureaucracy was not accountable to the people. He was against depending too much on the bureaucracy and called for faith on the self-government models. Mr. Yadav also said that the Rural Development Department has requested for increasing the devolution funds from 10% to 12%. In his inaugural address, former Director of National Institute of Public Finance and Policy M. Govinda Rao underlined the issues concerning decentralisation and explained how to make systems work successfully. Calling for clarity on the functions of the local bodies, Mr. Rao explained the need for autonomy for local bodies to raise revenue. MIDS Director M. Suresh Babu, Joint Secretary in SSFC V. Anbazhagan also spoke.

headline: Driver brings bus to a halt before dying of cardiac arrest in Vellore
content: A 59-year-old bus driver died of cardiac arrest after safely bringing the vehicle to a stop by the roadside near Gudiyatham town on Thursday, ensuring the safety of around 25 commuters. The deceased, identified as K. Venkatesan, a resident of Katpadi, was driving the bus from Pernambut to Salem through the bypass road when he experienced severe chest pain. The police said that Mr. Venketasan managed to halt the bus before collapsing on the steering wheel. Commuters immediately rushed towards him and found him unconscious. They shifted him to the Government Taluk Hospital in Gudiyatham, where doctors declared him brought dead. A probe is under way.

headline: RPF seize 32 kg ganja at Jolarpet railway station
content: The Railway Protection Force (RPF) seized a consignment of 32 kg of ganja from a bag inside an express train at Jolarpet railway station on Thursday. The police said that as part of a special drive against the illegal transportation of narcotic substances and inflammable articles on trains, a team of RPF personnel was conducting surprise checks at the railway station. The team searched the train that had halted on platform 2 en route to Chennai, and found two bags abandoned in its general compartment. On opening the bag, they found bundles of ganja inside. Initial inquiry revealed that three persons had abandoned the consignment and fled the spot when they noticed the police team. The Jolarpet RPF has registered a case and analysed the CCTV footage to nab the gang that was involved in ganja smuggling. A probe is under way.

headline: KICL forays into FMCG sector targeting healthy beverage
content: Kothari Industrial Corporation (KICL), part of the DC Kothari group, on Thursday said its entering into the fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector through the launch of its beverage portfolio called Chusip, based on tender coconut water. It was priced at Rs. 50 for 200ml.The company plans to introduce a wide choice of flavours and aims to distribute them through traditional channels in southern parts of the country. The company plans to later expand geographically, including to international markets and introduce them in ecommerce platforms. Jinnah Rafiq Ahamed, executive director of KICL said this is the first step towards building a portfolio that is focused on nature, health and trust. Our research findings show there is a trend emerging in India of consumers moving towards healthy, natural and authentic choices. We strongly believe this is the right time to bring back the purity of nature in the form of coconut water sourced from the finest coconut farms. KICL aims to build a Rs. 2,500 crore beverage business by 2035, he said.

headline: Guest worker from Bihar murdered; 5 suspects on the run
content: A 27-year-old guest worker from Bihar was stabbed to death when he tried to save his friend during a clash with another group from Assam near Somangalam in Kancheepuram district on Wednesday night. Police have launched a search for five men in connection with the murder.Police identified the deceased as Gulshan Kumar, 27, who was staying near Kattarambakkam with his friend Nitish Kumar, 25. Both were employed at a factory in the Sriperumbudur area. Police said a group of workers from Assam, including Tobo, 24, Bapkon, Vikas, and Akash, also lived and worked in the locality. The two groups got into quarrels earlier.On Wednesday night, Tobo and his friends were sitting at Kattarambakkam junction when Nitish and Gulshan arrived. An argument broke out between the two groups and soon escalated into a clash. Tobo pulled out a knife and attempted to slash Nitish on the neck. Gulshan stepped in to protect his friend and was stabbed in the neck instead, police said. He collapsed at the spot with severe injuries.The assailants fled immediately after the attack. Gulshan was rushed to a private hospital at Thandalam, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.Somangalam police registered a murder case and sent the body to Sriperumbudur Government Hospital for postmortem. Special teams have been formed to trace Tobo and four others who are absconding.

headline: CM, other leaders mark Periyar's birth anniversary with social justice oath
content: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay, DMK president M K Stalin, leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami, and other political leaders paid homage to social reformer E V R Periyar on his birth anniversary on Thursday.Vijay visited the secretariat and paid floral tributes to a portrait of Periyar. Later, he took the Social Justice Day oath along with cabinet colleagues and govt staff. In a post on X, he urged people to follow Periyars principles.M K Stalin and senior DMK leaders took a similar oath at the party headquarters, Anna Arivalayam. Udhayanidhi garlanded Periyars statue on Anna Salai and said, We will uphold Periyars principles - we will protect social justice.Social justice minister Vanni Arasu praised Periyars uncompromising approach to eradicating Sanatana, male dominance, and caste discrimination. After paying tributes at Periyars memorial in Periyar Thidal, he said, On his birth anniversary, lets take an oath to eradicate Sanatana and uphold the states rights. He also urged people to safeguard the identities of the state and country.DMK MP Kanimozhi Rajathi Karunanidhi posted a short video on X, which took a dig at those who depend on astrologers all the while but use Periyar whenever required for the sake of politics.

headline: Woman kills mother-in-law after bathroom fall
content: What initially appeared to be the death of a 61-year-old woman after she fell unconscious in her bathroom turned out to be a murder after a postmortem revealed that she had been strangled. Police arrested her daughter-in-law, who allegedly strangled the woman while she lay unconscious after the fall.The deceased, Perundevi, lived on Periyathatham Mettu Street in Chengalpet with her son Venkatesan, 34, daughter-in-law Indhuja, 28, and grandchildren. Police said Perundevi slipped and fell in the bathroom on Tuesday night and lost consciousness. She was rushed to Chengalpet Government Hospital, but died.Chengalpet Town police initially registered a case of natural death. However, the postmortem examination conducted on Thursday found signs of strangulation, prompting police to question Indhuja.Police said Perundevi and Indhuja had been at loggerheads for the past five years over family issues. During questioning, Indhuja admitted to strangling her mother-in-law after finding her unconscious following the fall, police said. Indhuja told police that she believed the strangulation would go undetected and that Perundevis death would be attributed to the fall. She also claimed that her mother-in-law frequently abused her and found fault with the way she handled household chores.Police subsequently altered the case to murder and arrested Indhuja. She was produced before a court in Chengalpet and remanded in judicial custody at Puzhal womens prison.

headline: Mere delay can't can't be reason to stop disciplinary proceeding: HC
content: A mere delay in conducting disciplinary proceedings against an employee will not automatically become fatal to the entire proceedings, Madras high court has said, adding, Courts must examine the reasons for the delay and the circumstances in which the alleged misconduct was discovered.A division bench of Justice S M Subramaniam and Justice Krishnaswamy Govindarajan further emphasised that the natural-justice inquiry focuses on whether the delinquent employee received a fair opportunity to defend himself, rather than mechanically determining whether a particular number of notices were issued.The court made the observations while upholding the termination of S Sukumar, an employee of the Dharapuram Public Servants Co-operative Thrift and Credit Society, over allegations of misappropriation of the societys funds.According to Sukumar, the alleged incident occurred between 1995-97, but the charge memorandum was issued in 2011. Due to the long delay in framing the charges, a single judge of the court quashed the termination order. Aggrieved, the management of the society moved the present appeal.Allowing the appeal, the court pointed out that the delay in issuing the charge memo was due to an interim order passed by a single judge of the court. Therefore, the delay cannot be attributed against the management of the society for initiation of departmental disciplinary proceedings, the court said.Mere delays per se would not be sufficient to quash the entire charge memorandum in all cases. Each case has to be decided by considering the facts, the nature of the allegations, the mitigating circumstances, and the cause for the delay in initiating the departmental disciplinary proceedings, the court said.As to the allegation of violation of natural justice, the court said, It is not about issuance of show cause notices, but whether a fair opportunity was afforded to the delinquent officer. The test to be applied is whether the principles of natural justice has been complied with by affording a fair opportunity to the delinquent officer.

headline: Dengue cases cross 16,000 in TN, health dept says rise not abnormal
content: Tamil Nadu has recorded 16,334 dengue cases and nine deaths between Jan 1 and Sept 16 this year. Health department said rise in cases is not abnormal compared with corresponding period last year. The state had recorded 15,688 dengue cases and 13 deaths between Jan and Sept 2025, while 2024 saw 34,339 cases and 13 deaths during the same period. Officials said the figures do not indicate an unusual or alarming spread of dengue and that seasonal fluctuations in cases are expected during the monsoon.Cases rise with changes in weather that create favourable breeding conditions for Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit the disease, said Dr A Somasundaram, director of public health and preventive medicine. We see increased breeding between Oct and Dec. We have intensified surveillance and preventive measures across TN, he said. Officials have been deployed to coordinate prevention and control activities, while campaigns are being conducted to educate the public about preventing mosquito breeding. The health department is coordinating with other departments to implement preventive measures, he added.The city has recorded 3,404 fever cases in two weeks, with hospitals reporting surge in outpatients seeking treatment. In Aug, fever cases reported was 4,520. From Sept 1 to 16, numbers have crossed 3,000. Primary health centres have sufficient stocks of medicines. We have intensified fever-control measures for which 3,697 workers have been engaged. Fever surveillance has also been strengthened at hospitals and through house-to-house visits by health workers to identify cases at community level, said GCC commissioner GS Sameeran.Doctors said symptoms include fever, body ache, muscle pain, fatigue and headache. Since last month, we saw more than 3,000 people with fever, of whom around 150 had dengue, said Dr Prabha G, senior consultant, general medicine of SRM Prime Hospital.

headline: Veeramani brought in for questioning
content: Gem Granites owner R Veeramani, 84, was taken into the three-day custody by the Central Crime Branchs Anti-Vice Squad on Thursday for questioning in connection with a case of rape of a minor girl. Citing his age and health condition, an Egmore magistrate directed police to question him within the court premises.Veeramani was among three people arrested in the case, along with Shanthi and her husband Mahendra Simhan. The case was registered in Oct 2025 after police received a pen drive containing a video that purportedly showed a minor girl being sexually assaulted. Police subsequently identified Veeramani as the man seen in the footage, according to investigators.The police had earlier sought to close the case after they could not identify or locate the girl. A special POCSO court rejected the closure report on Aug 19 and ordered further investigation. The fresh probe led to the arrests of Veeramani and the couple.During the present questioning, police prepared a questionnaire containing around 100 questions. Investigators were examining details provided by Shanthi, including the circumstances surrounding the alleged offence and the possible involvement of others. Police said the survivor had subsequently been identified and her statement was recorded before a magistrate in Egmore on Wednesday. Investigators were also examining whether any other minor girls had been subjected to similar assault.Veeramani had earlier told the magistrate that his health condition had worsened while he was in Puzhal prison. Following representations from his counsel, police took him to a govt hospital for a medical assessment before questioning him in the court premises.An investigating officer said Veeramani would be permitted to meet his lawyer once a day in accordance with the courts directions.

headline: S Jayachandran elected Pachaiyappa's Trust Board president
content: S Jayachandran was unanimously elected president of the newly constituted Pachaiyappas Trust Board after elections were held on September 6 and votes counted on September 7.The nine trustees were elected from four constituencies University of Madras Senate members, Pachaiyappas Trust College Council, approved teachers and registered graduates. The Madras High Court accepted the election results and the new board assumed administrative duties from September 16.The board subsequently appointed S Paramasivam as Financial Trustee and Dr R Prabhaakaran as Member Secretary. It has begun functioning and passed resolutions concerning the welfare of teachers and other employees.

headline: Putting The 'Ant' In Restaur'ant', Gangnam Style: Michelin-Starred Seoul Eatery Fined Over 'Creepy' Dessert
content: A routine inspection by municipal food safety officials revealed that the restaurant was incorporating live or dried black ants into its high-end tasting menu

headline: No NOC required to get power supply for houses on poromboke land
content: The state govt has exempted people living on poromboke land from getting a no-objection certificate (NOC) from govt departments to get an electricity connection. However, they must fulfil certain criteria, including the house size, payment of necessary charges as well as an undertaking that they are aware they could be evicted at any time.The GO dated Sept 16, issued by the energy department, said houses built on lands classified as water course, mandaiveli, and meikal poromboke, as well as lands belonging to temples, cantonment, railways, and forest departments, will not be eligible for electricity services.Also, the houses built on permitted poromboke lands should not exceed 250sqft in built-up area. Until now, these houses needed an NOC from the authority concerned for getting power supply. This has been done away now as there is a huge pendency of such applications, said an official. In the written undertaking, the applicant should state that the new electricity service does not confer any right on the land on which they have built the house and that they are liable to be evicted and to have power supply disconnected if the govt requires the land.The GO has made it clear that the section officer concerned should inspect and ensure that applicants under the LT-1A(3) category have not built houses on prohibited poromboke or other categories of land before effecting the service. The chairman and managing director of TNPDCL should also submit a district and taluk-wise status report of such services to the govt every three months and ensure that the facility is not misused.These connections will be classified as a separate consumer category low tension - 1A (3) to distinguish them from the regular domestic category, though they would be charged the same tariff as the domestic category (LT-1A). The billing software is being updated to accommodate such services, and the information technology team is working on processing such applications online. These connections require double the security deposit. Other charges for this consumer category are also being worked out, added the official.

headline: Cooum Check dams could help track and tackle pollution: study
content: Check dams across the Cooum basin could serve as strategic points to monitor and tackle pollution, a study into one of its tributaries has found.Researchers said the structures trapped organic matter, nutrients, salts and plastics, while diatoms (algae) shifted from types that thrive in cleaner water to pollution-tolerant types, as water slowed down in these spots, allowing material to settle in sediment.Published in Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, researchers from the National Taiwan Ocean University and the University of Madras examined 12 sites along an upper-midreach tributary in Tiruvallur district, covering Kannapalayam, Avadi, Paruthipattu and Thiruverkadu, before it joins the main Cooum.A key finding was that upstream water was relatively clean, with diatoms associated with better water quality, while pollution increased and sediment accumulated pollutants and plastics towards the urban check dam .Diatoms are good indicators of pollution because different types survive under different water conditions. Our findings show that the check dams are also retaining pollutants in the sediment. These pollutants could affect groundwater in surrounding localities, said Prof Nagaraj Subramani, corresponding author. He said the check dams could be intervention points because they are located before the tributary joins the Cooum. Pollution stopped here means cleaner water flowing into the main river, he said, adding that cleaning feeder streams should be part of Cooum restoration.A partial recovery in diatom diversity was found in a free-flowing middle stretch, linked to better water movement, before pollution-tolerant types increased again downstream.At the urban check dam, conductivity was 1,766 microsiemens per centimetre, compared with 748 upstream, indicating high pollution. Total dissolved solids were 1,236 mg/l against 524 mg/l, while chloride was 200 mg/l against 104 mg/l.Two sediment cores up to 35cm and 20cm deep that were studied contained organic matter, phosphorus, and chloride, while plastic material was found in several layers. The rural core showed plastic deposition at one level.The urban sediment core had more microplastics than the rural site, likely because sewage brings them into the river and slower water at check-dams allows them to settle, said Sagaya John Paul Joseph, first author.Environmental activist G Sundarrajan said pollution must be stopped at source. Around 10 years ago, a march along the Cooum identified about 880 sewage inflow points. The first priority must be to stop sewage from entering the river. We have spent thousands of crores on making Chennai beautiful, but we are still not getting the results. We need delivery on the ground, not more projects on paper.

headline: Tamil Nadu's mission to repair the hills of Tiruvannamalai
content: A nwardeen I grew up among the hills of Tiruvannamalai, and while their majesty never ceased to amaze him as child, their increasing vulnerability to landslides began to worry him. Which is why Anwardeen, now director of the Green Tamil Nadu Mission has set about to solve the problem.The sacred hills of Tiruvannamalai are now set for an ecological restoration that promises to fix the damage caused by soil erosion, poor drainage, forest fires, disappearing vegetation, and silt-clogged water bodies around the temple town.Tiruvannamalai has seen devastation from landslides, he says. A massive landslide triggered by heavy rain from Cyclone Fengal on December 1, 2024, resulted in the deaths of seven members of a family. The cyclone loosened soil and caused a massive boulder and mud to crash into their house. We took samples from the Annamalaiyar Hills to assess the likelihood of further landslides in the area.The project will cover 962 hectares of hillside. Weve broken them up into 16 zones or micro-watersheds, says Anwardeen. We plan to follow a ridge-to-valley approach, meaning work starts at the top of the hills and moves down toward the valleys. Satellite mapping, drone surveys and detailed studies of the land, water flow, and landslide risk are being used to decide where and how to intervene.Work will happen in stages. In the first phase, the most vulnerable areas will be stabilised. Teams will then move on to treating the wider watershed and repairing water-harvesting structures. The final phase will involve large-scale restoration of the natural ecology.Five ponds will be repaired by clearing silt, fixing overflow channels and embankments, and treating the streams that feed them. This should add about 3,341 cubic metres of extra water storage, helping the area hold and absorb more rainwater, all of which will help prevent landslides.Anwardeen says that once completed, the project could turn Tiruvannamalai hills into a eco-model for how Tamil Nadu can protect and restore fragile hill areas, combining ecological repair, biodiversity protection, water security, and disaster preparedness in one integrated programme.The project is expected to cost `10 crore and will begin soon. The biggest share, `2.5 crore, will go toward planting native trees and restoring the ecology. Another `2 crore is set aside for building structures like check dams and trenches to control water runoff, while `3 crore will fund fire-prevention work and the repair of ponds and water bodies. Smaller amounts have been allocated for restoring grasslands, stabilising slopes using natural methods, conducting surveys, involving local communities, and maintaining the work once its done.Green Tamil Nadu Mission has launched several initiatives in Tamil Nadu to expand the states green cover, ranging from urban afforestation to large-scale ecological restoration, says Anwardeen. We have partnered with the municipal administration and water supply department to implement greening projects in urban local bodies, to strengthen urban greening programmes. The initiative has also been extended to state and national highways, where green corridors are being developed along linear infrastructure.We are also working to improve urban biodiversity and carry out tree census across the state, says Anwardeen.Whats On The Cards?A programme is under way to green the Eastern Ghats across nine districts, focusing on ecological restoration and tribal livelihoodsIn Dharmapuri district, a bamboo restoration project has been taken up, combining ecological restoration with sustainable resource development and livelihood generationState govt has proposed restoring and creating mangroves across 2,500 hectares through Green Tamil Nadu Mission, a move expected to enhance the resilience of coastal ecosystemsRestoration of the Buckingham Canal through mangrove-based ecological interventions, which is expected to demonstrate the use of nature-based solutions in degraded urban-coastal landscapes is also underwayOther initiatives include sandalwood restoration, large-scale agro-forestry programmes, development of community nature parks, improved clonal planting materials and palmyra restoration

headline: Kanimozhi meets Mamata Banerjee as DMK works on third front
content: DMK has started working on the formation of a prospective third front by trying to wean away some of the INDIA bloc constituents.DMK deputy general secretary and MP Kanimozhi Rajathi Karunanidhi met Trinamool Congress chief and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee at her Kalighat residence in Kolkata on Thursday. This came after Kanimozhis meetings with Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackerey and NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule in Mumbai on Sept 12.DMK broke all ties with Congress since the latter walked out of its alliance to join the TVK-led govt in Tamil Nadu in May. A DMK leader said Kanimozhi has been tasked with reaching out to opposition leaders.We are exploring the possibility of a third front without Congress, the leader said.Kanimozhis discussions with these leaders have predominantly been on the proposed delimitation, though the broader idea is to bring them on board. Mamata has been particularly unhappy with Congress after the latter rejected her seat-sharing offer for the Oct 6 Nandigram and Rejinagar byelections.A senior Trinamool MP said, Mamata Banerjee shares an excellent relationship with DMK chief M K Stalin. She also maintains very good ties with non-NDA parties and remains close to INDIA bloc members that are not allied with Congress. Todays discussion was strictly between her and Kanimozhi. Anything said beyond that would be speculation.NCP (SP) sources said the party leadership remains non-committal to DMKs proposal. DMK floated the idea of a third front, and a preliminary meeting was held. DMK is testing the waters with opposition parties with which it has a good equation, unlike Congress, a senior NCP leader said.Meanwhile, chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sept 9 named the TVK-led combine as Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance (SSJVA), which includes erstwhile DMK allies Congress, VCK and IUML. The new alliance will take on DMK and AIADMK in the upcoming local body elections in Tamil Nadu.(With inputs from Saibal Sen in Kolkata and Anurag Bende in Pune)

headline: Many parts of T.N., including Chennai, see summer-like heat this September
content: like in parts of Tamil Nadu, with maximum temperatures remaining above normal in several places. Officials of the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, attributed elevated temperatures in the interior parts and coastal areas such as Chennai to the weak Southwest monsoon and lack of cloud cover so far this month. While there have been similar instances at various stations in the past, this September has been unusually hot in many places. Places such as Erode, Palayamkottai, Vellore, Tiruchi, and Madurai have been among the hottest places in the State this month. The day temperature has crossed 40C at some weather stations in these locations earlier this month. On Thursday, several places sizzled with the mercury level soaring to 4C or 5C above normal. For the third consecutive day, Tiruchi recorded the highest day temperature of 39.5C in the State. Nungambakkam in Chennai recorded 38.1C, making it the decades second highest September maximum temperature recorded in the city. The citys all-time September record is 38.9C, registered in 1883. In Meenambakkam, the highest day temperature measured was 38.5C this month, which set the record for second highest temperature this decade in the city. However, the RMC has predicted a change in weather conditions as increased rainfall activity particularly in north and interior Tamil Nadu would cool down sweltering heat gradually from Friday. Pointing out that most parts of Tamil Nadu experienced unusually hot weather for September, officials said El Nio, a global weather phenomenon, had influenced the September weather conditions in Tamil Nadu too. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said the current wet spell would be triggered by a trough extending up to the Gulf of Mannar and not essentially because of monsoon influence. It would bring cloud cover and rainfall only to specific regions. The absence of cloud cover and prevailing wind patterns contributed to such high temperatures. The flow of relatively dry southerly winds over the State and lack of adequate thundercloud development sustained the rise in temperature, he said. With the trough expected to shift its position, rainfall is expected to increase in north Tamil Nadu, including Chennai and Vellore and interior parts, from Friday and bring down the temperature, he said. Meteorologists said September usually brought considerable rainfall to Tamil Nadu. Y.E.A. Raj, former deputy Director-General of Meteorology, said the break in monsoon conditions with the southwesterly component and wind convergence, which helped thundercloud development, did not occur significantly this season. Rainfall over the next few weeks may narrow the rainfall deficit. Officials added that weather models were being monitored and radars were undergoing maintenance as part of monsoon preparedness measures.

headline: Canada's Carney pushes 'new alliance' with EU despite Trump threats
content: Canadas Prime Minister Mark Carney shrugged off a threat of U.S. retaliation on Thursday (September 17, 1016) as he pitched a new alliance with Europe as a bulwark against outside pressures, in a closely watched address to the European Parliament. Mr. Carneys speech came after EU chief Ursula von der Leyen suggested Canada could become the 27-nation blocs first associate member in her own address to EU lawmakers on Wednesday (September 16, 1016). Europe and Canada are stronger together, the Prime Minister said, in a speech that drew a standing ovation, saying his country welcomed the EU proposal and wanted deeper cooperation on issues from artificial intelligence to defence and energy. The Canadian leader pushed back afterwards at U.S. President Donald Trumps threat to cut trade with the EU should the plan go ahead telling reporters: No one is going to dictate our culture, or with whom we can strike agreements internationally. Mr. Carney has been pursuing closer ties with Europe, as his country gets drawn ever deeper into a trade war with the United States. EU-U.S. relations have also been badly strained by tariffs and territorial threats. We are pursuing resilience so no one, no one can control our open markets, impair our sovereignty, threaten our territorial integrity, or undermine our freedoms, our democracies, our rule of law, Mr. Carney said. Ms. Von der Leyens proposal drew an irritated rebuke from Mr. Trump, who slammed it as laughable and told reporters it could be seen as an hostile act. If its a bad intention, well put very heavy tariffs on Europe, he said. Better manners The contours of the associate member pitch were not immediately clear, as EU treaties do not envisage such a possibility but Carney said Canada welcomes this ambition. Ms. Von der Leyen had emphasised the partnership was not against anyone else and Carney likewise sought to reassure Washington the alliance would not be antagonistic but a positive initiative. A stronger, more resilient Canada will be a more effective partner with the United States, he told reporters. Mr. Carneys visit to Strasbourg was meant to act as a catalyst ahead of an EU-Canada summit in Montreal next month. Canada could help Europe secure supplies of critical raw materials and contribute towards its energy needs with liquefied natural gas and hydrogen, Mr. Carney said, also offering partnership on AI, compute, space and payments. The two parties should move towards seamless digital trade and allow their young people to work and study on either side of the Atlantic, he said. On Wednesday (September 16, 2026), Ms. von der Leyen had similarly talked about forming a tech alliance, integrating defence industrial bases and making the Arctic a flagship joint project. Whats in a name? The idea of creating a new associate status short of full membership was first floated by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz this year for Ukraine. Under that plan Kyiv would have benefited from parts of the EU budget, attended the blocs summits and had a representative in the European Commission but no full voting rights. Terminology aside, Mr. Carney told reporters: What matters is the substance what are we actually building together? EU rules demand that member states approve any form of partnership with a non-EU country, and it was unclear how much support Ms. von der Leyens proposal would receive from capitals. Spains leader Pedro Sanchez appeared to back the idea Thursday, posting on social media the image of a red maple leaf -- Canadas symbol sitting just outside the circle of golden stars on the EUs flag. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Paris backed ever-closer ties with Canada but that the plan would have to be debated, scrutinised and analysed. The EU and Canada already have the CETA free-trade agreement, which abolished almost all tariffs. Trade in goods and services has jumped more than 80% since 2016. And this year Canada became the first non-EU country to join a flagship defence loan programme. One EU official said the bloc needed to be realistic and pragmatic about what more it could achieve. But a European diplomat speaking on condition of anonymity said EU countries were keen to keep strengthening ties with Canada, regardless of what they called their alliance. Carney came here to strengthen his cards vis a vis the US. Ursula helped him, the diplomat said. Trumps reaction shows they already won.

headline: China opposes U.S. sanctions bill, says will not accept 'long-arm jurisdiction'
content: China on Thursday (September 17, 2026) rejected the U.S. long-arm jurisdiction to impose tariffs on purchases of Russian oil and gas, saying its normal trade and economic cooperation with other countries should not be subject to interference or coercion by third parties. The U.S. House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026 that authorises Mr. Trump to impose sanctions on Russia and steep tariffs on its leading trading partners such as India and China. Asked about the bill, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told a media briefing in Beijing that China opposes any action that lacks UN Security Council authorisation. China engages in normal economic and trade cooperation with other countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit, Mr. Guo said. Such cooperation does not target any third party and shall be free from disruption or coercion from any third party. China opposes long-arm jurisdiction and unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate, he said. China reiterated its opposition to any tariff linkages to buying oil and gas from Russia ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinpings planned visit to Washington next week for a summit meeting with Mr. Trump. The summit, expected to be held from September 24-25, will be their second summit this year. Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May this year and held extensive talks with Xi. Meanwhile, the Chinese Commerce Ministry on Thursday (September 17, 2026) said Beijing and Washington are in talks to reach an agreement on a reciprocal tariff regime. China and the U.S. are holding consultations on a reciprocal tariff reduction framework arrangement that would cover $30 billion worth of products from each side, the ministry said. Economic and trade teams from both countries are earnestly carrying out the consensus reached by the two heads of state during their meeting in Beijing. The aim of the consultations is to reach a reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement at the earliest possible date, ministry spokesperson Huang Ling was quoted as saying by state-run Xinhua news agency. Beijing has repeatedly opposed unilateral sanctions. It also defied U.S. sanctions against buying oil from Iran. China, along with India, is one of the largest buyers of oil and gas from Russia. Much of China's imports are transported through pipelines crossing its land border. According to official data, Chinas imports of Russian oil and gas amounted to $64 billion last year, and its imports from January to August this year crossed over $70 billion. The bill passed by the U.S. Senate last month was approved by the House in a 262-159 vote on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) and will now go to Mr. Trump to be signed into law. It aims to punish Russia for continuing the war against Ukraine.
