headline: Country's growth should be based on economic justice: Prof. Shanmugasundaram
content: India emerges as one of the major economies of the world, among the greatest challenges it faces is that the growth that is taking place is not based on economic justice, Vedagiri Shanmugasundaram, former Vice-Chancellor of Manonmaniam Sundaranar University, said on Wednesday. In his acceptance speech at his centenary celebrations at D.G. Vaishnav College here, Prof. Shanmugasundaram said that Indias growth was primary based on economic strength and not economic justice. The strength should lead to justice and fairness, which is not happening, he said. He said that a recent phenomenon an envy of the world but a matter of deep concern was the rapid increase in the number of billionaires in India. Their emergence is not to be despised, for after all, wealth creation is the basic purpose of Economics. But in the process of wealth creation, sometimes poverty on a large scale may happen. That process of wealth creation should be checked. For this, deep knowledge of economics is required, Prof. Shanmugasundaram said. The subject of Economics itself has undergone major changes, with the advent of macroeconomics, microeconomics, regional economics, and even national economics. But economics as a discipline the study of mankind in the ordinary business of life is essentially the study of the ordinary man, not only the persons who are captains of industry, agriculture, and business, he added. He appealed to G. Viswanathan, Founder and Chancellor of Vellore Institute of Technology, to help develop certain types of research in economics, like economics of India, economics of Tamil Nadu, economics of districts of India, and economics of different classes of people, so that our country will not be in the list of poor countries but in the list of rich countries of the world rich countries of a new kind that share the wealth of creation with everybody. Dr. Viswanathan, who was also the chairperson of the centenary celebrations organising committee, said that Prof. Shanmugasundaram and his wife Yasodha Shanmugasundaram, former Vice-Chancellor of Mother Teresa Womens University, were the only husband-wife duo known to him who have been Vice-Chancellors and are admired across the academic community. The irony, he said, was the current scarcity of Vice-Chancellors in the State, as 17 of the 22 public universities in Tamil Nadu do not have Vice-Chancellors. At the centenary celebrations of Prof. Shanmugasundaram, I request both the Central and State governments to put your issues aside for a moment, focus on the students, focus on their education, he added. Elder statesman C. Rangarajan, former Governor, Reserve Bank of India, described Prof. Shanmugasundaram as the elder statesman of the profession of economics in Tamil Nadu. He classified his contribution to economics into three categories: as an economist and a teacher, as one who helped organise various organisations such as the Indian Economics Association, and as a contributor to policy-making in Tamil Nadu through his writings and his 15-year stint at the State Planning Commission. With the expansion of specialisations of economics, the education system in Tamil Nadu should introduce appropriate changes in the school system so that teaching of mathematics becomes an integral part, he added. A biography of Prof. Shanmugasundaram authored by Prof. Yasodha was released on the occasion. Among those who offered felicitations were K. Veeramani, President, Dravidar Kazhagam; Thamizhachi Thangapandian, DMK MP; Thol. Thirumavalavan, VCK MP; Vaiko, MDMK leader; R. Mutharasan, former State president of CPI; K.V. Thangkabalu, former Union Minister; Agri S.S. Krishnamurthy, MLA; A.D.N. Bajpai, former Vice-Chancellor and president of IEA, A. Kanagaraj, Chairman, Jaya Educational Trust; A.C. Shanmugam, Founder Chancellor, Dr. MGR Educational and Research Institute University; K. Chockalingam, former Vice-Chancellor, Manonmaniam Sundaranar University, S. Santhosh Baboo, Principal, DG Vaishnav College, and Dr. Yasodha Shanmugasundaram.

headline: 'Muslim Warrior', secure app and WhatsApp groups: 19-year-old coding expert held in Coimbatore over Al Qaida link
content: terrorism squads (ATS) of Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh arrested a 19-year-old youth from UP in Coimbatore on Sept 14 on charges of attempting to radicalise youth.The youth, identified as Maqsood Ali, son of Abdul Kuthus of Madhwapur in UPs Siddharthnagar district, was secured from the Hope College area in Coimbatore hours before he was to leave for Bengaluru.Maqsood was arrested based on the information provided by another suspect from Azamgarh, identified as Mohammad Nabeel, who was nabbed on Sept 12.Police said he was part of an online module linked to Al Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS).According to Tamil Nadu ATS, Maqsood had been working for a Bengaluru-based manpower agency run by Safiqul, a native of Bihar. He, along with a few others, arrived in Coimbatore on Sept 7 to work at Codissia Trade Fair Complex and stayed at a hotel near Hope College.Acting on an alert from UP ATS, TN police tracked down Maqsoods location within an hour and detained him. The Coimbatore ATS team handed him over to the UP ATS who produced him before a local court and took him to Uttar Pradesh on a prisoner transit warrant. Preliminary investigations revealed that he operated an Instagram handle called Muslim Warrior. The agency said Maqsood developed a secure application called Captain M Network with the motto One Platform, One Motive Unity, Plan and Action, which was allegedly used to radicalise youth. He was also said to have operated two WhatsApp accounts and was allegedly linked to groups named UU Entry Gate, United Ummah, Gazwa-e-Hind, Team Black Hat and Lashkar-e-Mehndi. ATS claimed the groups included Pakistani numbers and carried discussions on secure messaging tools and extremist content.Investigators said around 12 Pakistani nationals were part of the Ghazwa-e-Hind group. ATS alleged Maqsood, Nabeel and others were part of a conspiracy to carry out violent jihadist activities. Investigators alleged Maqsood had come into contact with Pakistani hackers and was attempting to develop hacking tools, having learned Python, Java, coding and hacking skills through online resources including Instagram, YouTube, Telegram and WhatsApp groups.Maqsood, who studied up to Class IX, was learning coding and artificial intelligence online. We seized his mobile phone. He remained largely uncooperative during questioning, a senior officer said. While Maqsood claimed he was innocent and merely browsed reels, officials scanned CCTV footage from the hotel and the venue, confirming he did not meet any local contacts.His employer Safiqul, told TOI that he was unaware of Maqsoods background, having hired him barely ten days earlier through an acquaintance.Investigators said the two suspects were purportedly influenced by the ideology of Al Qaida-linked preacher Anwar al-Awlaki and used WhatsApp groups to recruit youths. They allegedly planned to train recruits as mujahids, including imparting weapons-related training and fundraising, ATS claimed.The agency said the network operated across multiple states and maintained links with foreign contacts. An FIR was registered under sections 152 and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with sections 18 and 38 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

headline: Power cuts have become the norm in State: Anbumani Ramadoss
content: Anbumani Ramadoss PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Wednesday said that though the State government has said that steps have been taken to purchase 2000 MW of power to reduce power cuts, there has been no progress on the ground. In a statement, he pointed to an incident wherein Revenue minister K.A. Sengottaiyan had to give a media interview with the help of a mobile phone torch due to a sudden power cut in Vellore and said it illustrated how unannounced power cuts have become a norm across the State. Tamil Nadu's power demand, which reached a peak of 20,500 MW21,000 MW during the summer, continues to remain at the same level even now because temperatures have not come down. This is 4,000 MW higher compared to September last year. The reason for the power cuts is that the Tamil Nadu government has not made adequate arrangements for electricity to meet this additional demand, he said. He added, People have been holding protests against the power cuts being implemented everywhere from Chennai to the southern districts of Tamil Nadu. However, the power cuts have still not been withdrawn. Normally, officials ensure that power cuts do not occur in areas where ministers are participating in programmes. But if power supply is being disrupted despite the efforts of officials, it means that there is a shortage of electricity that is beyond their ability to manage.

headline: Fire breaks out in apartment complex in Thaiyur due to gas leak
content: A major fire broke out at the 11th floor of an apartment complex in Thaiyur near Kelambakkam on OMR on Wednesday night following an LPG leak. No casualties were reported.The complex has around 1,500 flat sacross 18 floors, with more than 4,000 residents. Around 9pm, residents of a flat on the 11th floor noticed a gas leak. The occupants immediately rushed out before it caught fire. The flames soon spread to neighbouring flats and the gas cylinder exploded triggering panic. Fire tenders from Tiruporur, Siruseri and Kovalam were rushed to the complex and firefighters battled the blaze before bringing it under control.Residents of the affected and neighbouring flats were evacuated. Fire and rescue personnel are assessing the extent of damage.

headline: Decades-old tradition: Tirupati temple umbrellas taken out in procession in Chennai
content: Tirupati temple umbrellas taken out in procession in Chennai Eleven white silken umbrellas meant for the annual Brahmotsavam at the Tirumala Tirupati Temple were flagged off on Wednesday evening from the Tirupati Umbrella Charities at Kandappa Chetty Street. According to S. Varadharajulu, the tradition of sending umbrellas by his family began at least five generations ago. "We have been sending them for over 170 years now. Devotees living along Audiappa Naicken Street, Govindappa Naicker Street, NSC Bose Road, and Varada Muthiappan Street watched the procession of the umbrellas that will reach Tirumala on September 19.

headline: City traders oppose 0.4% UPI MDR, large retailers absorb fee
content: A day after the announcement of a 0.4% MDR on select UPI transactions, city traders expressed concern that the cost could eventually be passed on to customers.Large retailers said they could absorb it as the charge was too small to affect prices. Retailers in some sectors, however, said they were awaiting clarity on how the new rules would apply to them.A M Vikramaraja, president of the Federation of Tamil Nadu Traders Association, said the new charge would add to the financial pressure on traders already struggling with multiple regulatory and operating costs. We will not pay the tax from our pocket. We will recover it from customers. We will stop encouraging digital payments and insist that they pay in cash, he said.Vikramaraja said traders were already facing pressure from compliance requirements, including GST, FSSAI, city corporation regulations and labour department rules. We are already on the verge of surrendering to corporates. Today, the government says there is no charge for UPI transactions up to 2,000. What is the guarantee that smaller transactions will not be charged in the future? How are small traders expected to do business? he asked. Large retailers, however, said the 0.4% MDR was too small to warrant passing the cost on to customers. They pointed out that UPI, along with credit and debit cards, had become deeply embedded in retail transactions after demonetisation and had since spread to smaller towns.We do not have the right to ask a customer to use another mode of payment if they prefer UPI. The MDR of 0.4% is too small to have an impact. We will absorb it; it will not be passed on to customers, said Ramesh Pothy, managing director, Pothys.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) announced on Sept 15 a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for select UPI transactions. From Oct 15, a 0.4% MDR will apply to person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above 2,000, subject to a maximum charge of 300 per transaction. The framework keeps person-to-person payments free, while small merchants covered under the P2PM category will continue to enjoy zero MDR. The charge is a fee within the digital payments ecosystem, not a tax collected by the govt. The govt has also said customers should not be charged separately for making UPI payments.M Ravi, president of the Chennai Hotels Association, said the impact would be felt by businesses of different sizes, even as hotels preferred UPI because payments went directly into their bank accounts.When customers pay in cash, we have to take it to the bank the next day. UPI is convenient because the money goes directly into our accounts. But we already pay around 2% when purchasing a UPI machine, apart from GST. Why should there be another charge? This will affect many businesses, he said. The government sometimes takes decisions without considering the difficulties faced by businesses, he said.Some retailers said they were yet to understand the details of the announcement. Most of our customers prefer card payments. This is a new announcement, and I do not know the details yet, said Nalli Kuppuswami Chetti, chairman, Nalli Silks.

headline: Burglars decamp with 20 sovereigns of gold, ₹60,000 cash from farmer's house in Tiruvannamalai
content: decamped with 20 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects, and around 60,000 cash from the house of a farmer in Thachambadi village near Chetpet town in Tiruvannamalai on Wednesday. V. Kannappan, 68, a farmer, his wife Chinna Kulathai, 62, were returning from their farm when they noticed damage to the main door of the house. The couple checked the cupboard and found vaulables missing. On being informed, Chetpet police reached the house with forensic experts. Fingerprints were taken. The police also took CCTV camera footage. Superintendent of Police (SP) M. Sudhakar formed special teams to nab the culprits. A case was registered and a probe is under way.

headline: VCK joined the alliance for Ministerial post: Premallatha
content: Premallatha Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant on Wednesday hit back at VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan for his recent comments that the sudden inclusion of DMDK in the erstwhile DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance before the Assembly elections were one of the reasons for its loss. Speaking after the district secretaries meeting in Chennai, Ms. Premallatha said, I have a lot of respect for Thirumavalavan. He is a straightforward person. But the truth is that he has changed his position, and since they have a Minister, they have joined the alliance. Why didnt he support the government from outside like the Communists? Why couldnt he say he did not want a Ministry? You wished for a Ministerial post and joined the alliance why are you dragging in the DMDK unnecessarily? She also said that the DMDK would support the DMK in the upcoming byelections.

headline: GCC to procure 260 tonnes of bituminous cold mix ahead of Northeast monsoon
content: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) is set to procure 260 tonnes of bituminous cold mix at an estimated cost of 59.41 lakh to fix potholes on bus route and interior roads across all its 15 zones. The procurement comes ahead of the Northeast monsoon, amid complaints about damaged roads and delays in road relaying work. The tender for the procurement was published on September 15. Deputy Mayor M. Magesh Kumaar questioned the use of cold mix for road repairs. He said the material often failed to provide a lasting solution. He suggested that the GCC award annual, zone-wise road maintenance contracts covering identified damaged roads instead. Wastage is high while procuring cold mix materials. The Chennai Corporation previously had its own unit for proper bitumen mixing, which was dismantled. Contractors are not applying the mix correctly. Instead of cleaning the pothole, applying a bitumen layer (tar), and then filling it, they are simply dumping the mix directly into the potholes, which fails to hold, Mr. Kumaar further said. The Deputy Mayor said a zone-wise annual maintenance arrangement, similar to that followed for electrical works, would enable contractors to attend to potholes, road cuts, and other damage throughout the year. Instead of piecemeal patch jobs, the Corporation should adopt an Annual Maintenance Contract model similar to the one followed by the State Highways Department. Contracts should be awarded per zone or ward to handle all road cuts, damages, and general maintenance for the year, he said. He cited the condition of Thanikachalam Road, where he said his car fell into a pothole recently, following which wet mix was used for temporary repair. He also referred to the damaged stretches on Jones Road, Jafferkhanpet Road and several interior roads. According to the GCCs Roads Department, patches arising from road cuts and rainwater inundation were repaired using bituminous cold mix, cement concrete, and hot mix.

headline: Four injured as autorickshaw tumbles inside unfinished drain
content: Four people suffered minor injuries after an autorickshaw overturned into an unfinished rainwater drain on Valasaravakkam-Arcot Road on Sunday night.The injured were identified as autorickshaw driver Murugan, 40, of Choolaimedu, and his relatives, Gopi, Revathi and Selva. Murugan had travelled to Porur with his family to attend a relatives wedding reception. After the function, he was returning to Choolaimedu with his relatives when the autorickshaw fell into a pit dug for the unfinished drain on Valasaravakkam-Arcot Road.Passersby rescued the four occupants, who were trapped inside the autorickshaw. They were taken to the Government Peripheral Hospital in KK Nagar for treatment. Valasaravakkam police registered a case. Police said they were examining the circumstances that led to the accident and the condition of the unfinished drain.

headline: 15 special centres to help motorists clear pending e-challans
content: challans can approach 15 special centres operated by Greater Chennai Traffic Police (GCTP) from Sept 21 to 30. Officials will also contact vehicle owners to alert them about unpaid fines. The centres will function daily from 9am to 7pm.Police said this has been launched because many motorists are unaware of e-challans generated for violations detected through automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras, traffic regulation observation zones (TROZ) and other enforcement systems. Some motorists also avoid opening links sent by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), suspecting them to be fraudulent.At the centres, personnel will inform motorists about pending challans and fine amounts and assist those making inquiries over phone or in person. Bulk SMS alerts will also be sent to motorists with unpaid challans.The centres will function at ICF annexure police booth in Ayanavaram, Music Academy police booth in Royapettah, Greenways junction police booth in Abiramapuram, Tower Clock junction police booth on Anna Salai, Anna Nagar Roundana, Anna Arch traffic police booth, Maduravoyal traffic police station, Madhavaram Roundana, Elephant Gate police station, New Washermenpet police station, Sembium police station, Mambalam police station, Adyar police station, Traffic Mount subdivision campus beneath Kathipara flyover and the ITMS headquarters at the police commissioners office in Vepery. Motorists can also verify pending challans through the official Parivahan e-Challan portal or NextGen e-Challan. Fines can be paid online through NextGen e-Challan, Paytm, post offices or Tamil Nadu e-Sevai centres. Drunk-driving fines can be paid through courts.Police have given motorists a week to check and clear pending fines. Repeat offenders booked multiple times for the same violation could face enhanced fines and further action, including suspension or cancellation of their driving licence, an official release said.

headline: IMD forecasts moderate rain for Chennai and north Tamil Nadu this week
content: After several days of short, isolated spells, rain activity may intensify over the city and neighbouring districts in the coming days. The IMD has forecast moderate rain at one or two places in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengelpet, Kancheepuram and other north Tamil Nadu and interior districts on Thursday and Friday. Heavy rain has also been forecast over Tiruvallur on Saturday.V R Durai, director, Area Cyclone Warning Centre, IMD, said an upper-air circulation over south coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining Rayalaseema, along with a trough extending from north interior Karnataka to the Gulf of Mannar, may bring rain to the city, neighbouring districts and other parts of Tamil Nadu.An upper-air circulation is an area where winds rotate around a region of relatively low pressure several kilometres above the ground. It can draw moisture into the atmosphere and encourage air to rise. As the moist air rises, it cools and condenses into clouds, which may produce rain when conditions are favourable. A trough is an elongated zone of relatively low pressure that can also bring winds together, supporting rising air and cloud formation.It may not be widespread rain in the city, but moderate spells are possible in some areas till Sept 20, Durai said. On Sept 17 and 18, thunderstorms and lightning, accompanied by gusty winds reaching 40-50kmph, may occur in some areas. On Thursday, the city and suburbs may receive light to moderate rain during the evening and night, with partly cloudy skies. Daytime temperatures may be 35-36C, while nighttime temperatures may remain around 27-28C.Since June 1, Chennai has recorded 361.4mm of rain, around 2% below normal. Nungambakkam recorded 392.7mm, about 10.7mm above normal, while Meenambakkam received 422.4mm, around 6.1mm below normal. Tiruvallur has recorded 86.3mm, 22% below normal; Kancheepuram, 264.6mm, 33% below normal; and Chengalpet, 154.5mm, 54% below normal.

headline: Premallatha hits out at Thirumavalavan over seat-share remarks
content: DMDK general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant on Wednesday hit out at VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan for his remarks expressing displeasure over allocation of 10 seats to DMDK in DMK-led front for the assembly poll.Premallatha said VCK changed its political stand for the sake of a ministerial post, but was blaming DMK and DMDK for the disintegration of the DMK-led alliance. If VCK decided to back TVK govt only to prevent governors rule, why didnt the party choose to extend outside support to TVK as the Left parties did, she asked. The reason was simple as VCK wanted the ministerial post, she said.She said DMK had increased VCKs allocation from six to eight seats during the assembly election. She questioned Thirumavalavan for unwantedly dragging DMDK into controversies and asked whether VCK was scared of her party.She also criticised DMK leader A Raja for his controversial remark against minister R Nirmalkumar and said that politicians should watch their words. Who gave the rights to demean women in the family of the political rivals, she asked.

headline: Arappor questions TN govt's claim on Tambaram tender controversy
content: A day after shunting out Tambaram corporation commissioner S Balachandar over irregularities in two tenders an Ashoka Pillar statue and a Save Water concept statue, together valued at 46 lakh the anti-corruption NGO, Arappor Iyakkam questioned the govts claim that the issue was only a procedural lapse. It, instead, cited serious discrepancies in the govts narrative on how the work was conceived and executed.Welcoming the transfer of S Balachander out of the commissioner post, Arappor coordinator Jayaram Venkatesan said the govts explanation that the work had already been executed using CSR funds and that a subsequent tender for the same work constituted a procedural lapse raised several questions.As for the claim that the administrative approval was obtained at a council meeting on July 14, Arappor said no council meeting was held in July and that the meeting after June 11 was held only on Aug 30. It also sought details of the company that allegedly wrote to the corporation on July 24, a day after the tender notice was issued on July 23, offering to execute the work through CSR funds. It asked when the corporation approved the proposal.Even if the approval was issued immediately on July 25, how could the company fabricate and install the Ashoka Pillar within three days and inaugurate it on July 29? Arappor asked. It also questioned why the company had neither displayed its name around the structure nor publicised its CSR contribution.The organisation questioned why the tender floated on Aug 6 was described as a procedural lapse when it was cancelled only on Sept 15, that too after Arappor flagged it. Seeking verification of the CSR contribution, Arappor asked if a backdated company letter was inserted into records.A senior official, however, said Tambaram mayor K Vasanthakumari had approved the project through a resolution by circulation on July 14.

headline: HC directs Centre to process sanction to prosecute IAS officers
content: Madras high court on Wednesday directed the Union govt to complete, within two months, the process of granting sanction to prosecute two IAS officers - K S Kandhasamy and M K Vijaya Karthikeyan in connection with the alleged tender irregularities case involving former AIADMK minister S P Velumani.Justice N Anand Venkatesh passed the interim order on a contempt of court petition moved by anti-corruption NGO Arappor Iyakkam.When the plea came up for hearing, the court questioned Sushil Kumar Patil, joint secretary, department of personnel and training (DoPT), who appeared through video conference, about the delay in granting sanction to prosecute the two officers.The officer submitted that a large volume of documents relating to the case had to be examined and that the documents be forwarded to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) for its views. A response from the commission is expected the following week, he said.After receiving the CVCs response, the relevant documents would be forwarded to the prime ministers office, which has the authority to take the decision on granting sanction for prosecution in the case, the officer said.He added that the entire process would require approximately two months, and assured the court that there would be no further delay. He also stated that priority would be given to completing the sanction process.Recording the submission, the court directed the Union govt to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken from Nov 2025 till date in relation to the proposal to grant sanction for prosecuting the two IAS officers.The court further directed the Union govt to complete the sanction process within two months and communicate its decision to the Tamil Nadu govt and adjourned the hearing to Nov 12.

headline: Elected MLAs can resign, but what about rights of voters, asks Madras HC
content: While an elected MLA has an absolute right to resign, the rights of the voter cannot be violated, observed Madras high court, adding that elected MLAs resigning and then contesting immediately on another partys symbol is a problem.A division bench of justices S M Subramaniam and K Govindarajan made the observations on Wednesday, when a public interest writ petition moved by advocate K Suthan seeking to restrain Election Commission of India (ECI) from holding byelections to fill the vacancies in Madurantakam and Dharapuram assembly constituencies, came up for hearing.The bench directed ECI to come up with steps to protect the constitutional rights of a voter who elected the MLAs, and asked it to explain whether there are guidelines to deal with the peculiar situation of an MLA resigning the post soon after being elected and seeking re-election in the bypolls which is necessitated by the very resignation. The court, refusing to pass an interim order stalling the byelection, observed that courts cannot interfere in the election process once it is set in motion.The petitioner wanted the court to direct ECI to examine and initiate necessary legislative and regulatory measures to create a mechanism to ensure financial accountability of elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from their seats without legally recognised compelling circumstances. He suggested introduction of election expenditure security to recover the cost of the resultant byelections and to examine and initiate necessary legislative measures to introduce a statutory disqualification or a reasonable cooling-off period to prevent elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from contesting subsequent elections for a prescribed period.As to the notified byelection to the two constituencies, the petitioner wanted the court to direct ECI to mandate payment of election expenditure security by Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama who resigned from Maduranthakam and Dharapuram constituencies immediately after election. The deposit must be made as a pre-condition for filing nomination papers for the byelection, the petitioner said.

headline: Avadi corporation to upgrade access roads to 4 railway stations
content: strewn, poorly lit, unsafe and slushy roads to better-lit, motorable and more pedestrian-friendly approaches - Avadi Corporation is planning a makeover of access roads to four railway stations in its jurisdiction-Avadi, Pattabiram, Thirumullaivoyal and Annanur.The initiative is part of a larger plan to strengthen public transport connectivity in the corporation limits. Suburban network is the lifeline of Avadi and surrounding areas. These four major stations see good footfall. But some issues persist on access roads to these stations. We will be improving it, said R Saranya, Commissioner of the Avadi City Municipal Corporation.The corporation will prepare detailed project report (DPR) and decide on the feasibility of this project. The focus will be on improving motorability of the roads, many of which are currently in poor condition and become slushy during the monsoon. The plan will also include beautification and improved illumination, with the latter aimed at addressing safety concerns, particularly for women using the station approaches, said a corporation official.This project becomes pertinent as the localities are seeing a real estate boom and more people are moving into these areas. Out of these four stations - Avadi and Annanur have two Tasmac shops each near them. This poses as a security threat for women passengers who return late from work, said Kathiresan, a resident of Annanur.T Sadagopan, President, Tamil Nadu Progressive Consumer Centre, said that there is no proper pedestrian path to reach station. There is no proper safety for the commuters. The North Bazaar entrance needs a lot of improvement. We have been appealing to officials, but there has been no response, he said.The project is envisaged as the first step towards creating better links between the railway stations and other public transport infrastructure. The main idea is to remove the load from the road and encourage public transport especially with metro connectivity planned to Avadi and the upcoming Avadi bus terminus being developed by CMDA. Access and last mile connectivity has to be improved to achieve this, added the Avadi corporation official.

headline: TN govt zeroes in on Cheyyur for Chennai's second airport
content: Cheyyur in Chengalpet district is likely to be the first choice of the Tamil Nadu govt to develop the proposed second airport, govt sources told TOI.The govt is also discussing ways to return the acquired parcels of land at Parandur to their earlier owners. On Aug 24, chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced the cancellation of the Parandur airport project, for which the previous govt had acquired 1,802 acres out of the 3,874 acres of patta land identified.Manellore in Gummidipoondi, Tiruvallur district, is another site recently shortlisted by the state govt for the Airports Authority of Indias pre-feasibility study.In Cheyyur, 90km from Chennai, the govt has 623 acres earlier acquired for a power project by Union govt through Tamil Nadu Power Finance Corporation. There are also about 300 acres of poramboke land. The power project was shelved towards the end of the previous AIADMK govt. So Cheyyur is being considered for the airport project, a govt official said.Manellore, which is an alternative option, may raise environment concerns due to its proximity to Pulicat lake, officials said. The final picture, however, will emerge only after AAI submits its pre-feasibility study report. A senior airport official said the existing airport is capable of handling the projected traffic for a few more years, but further expansion is not possible.Chennai airport has an annual passenger-handling capacity of 30 million. The development of Terminal 3 is expected to raise the overall capacity to 35 million passengers a year. AAI has also proposed a satellite terminal with an additional capacity of 20 million passengers annually.Since the satellite terminal would be built within the existing airport premises, it would not require additional land acquisition. We are planning an elevated express corridor for approach from a national highway, the airport official said.

headline: Point Calimere Sanctuary Delivers Tanker Water Amid Drought
content: Every day, dozens of water tankers roll into Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary in Kodiyakarai, Nagapattinam district, carrying thousands of litres of water for animals.There has been no rainfall in the region since Feb and temperatures are soaring on account of El Nino, says Nagapattinam district forest officer D Rameshwaran.The wetlands within the reserve forest areas including swamps, mudflats and salt marshes that normally hold water have dried up.We are buying thousands of litres of water from various sources, transporting it by tanker and filling troughs for the animals, says the DFO.The sanctuary, a Ramsar site and wetland complex covering 21sqkm, supports a variety of herbivores such as blackbucks, chital (spotted deer) and black-naped hares; carnivores including golden jackals, monitor lizards, Indian grey mongooses and jungle cats; omnivores such as bonnet macaques, wild boar and small Indian civets; and frugivores like the short-nosed fruit bat.It is also home to hundreds of feral horses, which are neither native to the sanctuary nor classified as wildlife. An adult feral horse needs about 40l of water a day, says a sanctuary staffer. They account for the largest share of water consumption.About 20 drinking-water points serve wildlife in and around the sanctuary. Some sites also have storage tanks, sumps and bore wells from which water is pumped daily, although the groundwater table has fallen. The department has also placed plastic saucer-type water tanks at various spots and along roadsides. These are regularly filled with 15,000 litres of water delivered by tankers.We are facing some difficulty in maintaining water supply. Because of the heat water evaporates fast. Also, the feral horses deposit large quantities of dung in the troughs, says A Joseph Daniel, Vedaranyam forest range officer.In dry periods, spotted deer and feral horses enter nearby villages in search of water. There they risk being hit by vehicles or attacked by stray dogs. We have stepped up patrolling in the villages to keep track of animals that wander outside the sanctuary, says Rameshwaran.The sanctuary ranks among the states most important bird-arrival sites, but we dont see many migratory birds now because of the drought, says wildlife biologist I Arivu. Muniyappan lake, one of the largest water bodies and a key congregation point for wildlife and birds, has dried up. Migratory bird numbers will increase once it starts raining, says Arivu.

headline: Whose Periyar? How the rationalist leader's legacy shapes Tamil Nadu politics across party lines
content: E V Ramasamy never contested an election. Yet, five decades after his death, his name surfaces in the context of every election in Tamil Nadu. Parties across the states political spectrum, parties that share little else in common continue to publicly invoke the rationalist leader.When C Joseph Vijay launched TVK a couple of years ago, he named Periyar as one of partys ideological guiding lights. DMK and AIADMK have always maintained their core ideologies have been influenced by Periyar. CPI endorses Periyars social reform movement especially his views on inter-caste marriages.Whether adapt or adopt, embrace or challenge, uphold or contest, every party stakes a claim to the legacy of the rationalist leader. But on their own terms.In June, after he became chief minister, Vijay made it clear in the assembly that while TVK had embraced Periyars social principles, it did not share his views on atheism. We took Periyars teachings but also made it clear we are believers in God, he said.In March, former BJP state president Tamilisai Soundararajan justified the removal of a Periyar photo from the entrance of an NDA meeting in Madurai. Yet, she credits Periyars agitation for womens rights for the independence they enjoy today. The party does not accept the phrase Periyar mann (Periyars soil). Its the soil of Periyalvaar (one of the 12 alvar saints of South India) and Andal (the only female Tamil saint) too. Religion and spirituality are just as important as social justice, says Tamilisai.Periyar, says political historian and biographer Kannan R, remains an enduring ideological benchmark. He can never be a vote-catching name. He did not seek electoral office. But C N Annadurai, who spent years in his movement, took elements of that social reform politics into electoral mobilisation through DMK. Invoking Periyar does not mean accepting his entire ideology. Parties do it to establish that their politics belongs within the social and political history of Tamil Nadu, even when their ideological positions differ from his, says Kannan.Much like Congress invokes Gandhi, parties in Tamil Nadu that cast aside his atheism and radical ideas invoke Periyar as a symbol to anchor their political identity and Tamils-first legitimacy. It is why Periyar became an ideological reference point even after the movement entered electoral politics.Political strategists say the influence traces back to the caste hierarchies of the early 20th century, when there was disproportionate representation in govt employment, education and administrative positions. The Justice Party, formed in 1916, laid the ground to fix the imbalance, but Periyar, who supported the movement, took it further by launching the Self-Respect Movement in 1925 to challenge caste, patriarchy and religious orthodoxy.Justice Party passed the first communal GO in 1921, which aimed to increase proportion of posts held by non-brahmin communities in provincial govt services. After Supreme Court struck down the communal GO in 1950, Periyar led agitations demanding it be restored. The political pressure led to the First Constitutional Amendment in 1951, which inserted Article 15(4) allowing reservations for socially backward classes, Christians, Muslims, dalits and tribal communities.For V Kumaresan, DKs treasurer, this achievement is one of the main reasons parties cannot escape Periyar. What began as communal representation became social justice. From then on, whichever party came to power could not afford to neglect social justice. It became the core of the Dravidian movement, he says.But the rationalist leaders influence was not limited to policy demands. He changed the language through which political demands were made, says political historian Rajan Kurai Krishnan.Periyar believed self-respect and questioning were synonymous. Periyar said: You are equal to everybody. Respect yourself. This became a political value, he says. His legacy goes beyond Dravidian parties that emerged from his movement. Parties do not have to agree with all of Periyars ideas to engage with the political space he created.DMK continues to identify closely with Periyars principles but, like many parties, does not insist on atheism as a condition for accepting them. We follow Periyars ideology of equality and equanimity, says DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan. The only idea we do not propagate as strongly as Periyar did is atheism. Party leaders may personally be atheists, but we do not preach it.AIADMK links itself to Periyar through social justice and equality while invoking Annadurais position on religion. Periyar upheld atheism and rejected the existence of God. Anna advocated ondre kulam, oruvane devan (one community, one God), says AIADMK spokesperson D Jayakumar.For PMK, Periyars legacy is in its campaign for caste-based data and reservation. Periyar saw reservation as an important way to address caste inequalities. We have been demanding a caste census in Tamil Nadu and India for many years, says president Anbumani Ramadoss.CPI identifies with another aspect of his social reform movement. We believe in Periyars views on inter-caste and inter-religious marriages. We conduct such marriages, says S K Siva, the partys South Chennai district secretary. He says the party has recommended a law against caste-based crimes.Periyar defined the vocabulary around which the states politics developed. Thats why every party wants to invoke him in some way, says Jenny S, a political consultant, who worked with DMK and AIADMK. That does not make every party a Periyarist, she says.But the questions he raised are important even today. Who gets representation? How do we address caste inequality? How do we protect dignity and equality?Sept 17, 2026, marks Periyars 147th birth anniversary.

headline: Armed Russian drone found near Polish beach: officials
content: officials 2 drone armed with explosives was found in the sea off northern Poland this week, officials said Wednesday (September 16, 2026). "The aerial craft was secured and it was established that it was armed" after it was found on Monday (September 14), military affairs prosecutor Bartosz Okoniewski told journalists. "It contained a warhead with a detonator," he said, without providing further information. The drone will undergo further examination by the military to determine where it came from and what its intended target was. Defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said on Monday (September 14) that the military had located the drone near the village of Rusinowo in northwestern Poland and recovered it from the sea. He added that the drone was thought to have been lost by Russia during test manoeuvres over the Baltic Sea. The military affairs department of the district prosecutor's office in the northwestern city of Szczecin launched proceedings over the incident. Okoniewski said the department was investigating a suspected charge of "causing an incident that endangers the life or health of many people and property of great value". Poland, a NATO and EU member state bordering both Ukraine and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, has faced repeated drone incursions into its territory since the beginning of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

headline: EU chief von der Leyen calls for a joint mechanism to counter drones, sabotage
content: like mechanism to better respond to drone incidents, acts of sabotage and cyberattacks across Europe, many of them blamed on Russia, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026). "Europe needs its own counter-hybrid playbook. We urgently need a consensus on how to respond to certain incidents, Ms. von der Leyen said, particularly for acts that fall below armed aggression but clearly threaten our national security. Officials in Germany, Denmark, and Poland have in recent weeks accused Russia of involvement in drone incursions, sabotage, arson, surveillance of defence facilities and planning to use a drone carrying explosives to attack an airport. Italian fighter jets working with NATO shot down a drone over EU member Lithuania earlier this week, the first time one has been downed in its airspace. It was believed to have entered from Russia's ally, Belarus. But Europe and NATO are struggling to know how best to respond to acts that fall short of outright aggression. Ms. von der Leyen said that the system should be similar to Article 4 of NATO's founding treaty, which allows countries believing that their territory is under threat to convene emergency meetings. When triggered by one member state, all member states would convene to coordinate a European response, to deter further escalation, and to mitigate the impact, she said. NATO's Article 4 is separate from Article 5, the collective security guarantee that obliges all member countries to come to the aid of an ally under attack. Ms. von der Leyen also said that the EU Commission will set out our ideas to make a European Security Council a reality. It would involve other international partners like Britain, Canada, Norway and Ukraine, she said. No details were provided.

headline: Trust takes small loans on behalf of tribespeople, 'fails' to repay them
content: The Tamil Nadu Tribal Peoples Association has alleged that around 60 families in Gudalur have been defrauded by people running a trust, which procured loans for them but misappropriated the repayment. Association district organiser K. Mahendran, along with the affected residents, petitioned the Superintendent of Police on Tuesday, demanding action against those responsible. They alleged that the trust met tribeswomen from the Kattunayakan and Paniya communities in Devarshola, Nellakottai and Sri Madurai panchayats, offering to arrange loans for them through the Indian Bank branches at Gudalur and Devarshola. The loans were arranged for the beneficiaries through a joint liability group system, with each person receiving loans ranging from 50,000 to 1 lakh. They alleged that trust representatives visited the women every month and collected loan instalments but misappropriated the money instead of repaying the loans at the bank. Moreover, the trust representatives collected the instalment amount even after the 30-month repayment period ended, the complainants said. Since the collected amount was not properly deposited in the bank, the bank accounts of members of the groups were frozen, alleged Mr. Mahendran. They also leveled allegations of fraud against the bank itself, saying that the bank seized the money deposited into the womens accounts for government housing schemes. The tribespeople in these areas generally earn their livelihood by seasonally collecting and selling pepper, honey and areca nuts, and by working occasionally in plantations. Some also work as labourers in estates. They do not have continuous employment opportunities. A large number of the men are reportedly addicted to alcohol. In such circumstances, the group loans have caused additional problems within the families, said Mr. Mahendran. The association demanded action against the chairman of the trust, its secretary, co-ordinator and others and demand that a case be registered against them under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

headline: UPI MDR fee hike explained in 10 points: No rollback, Rahul Gandhi vs Centre
content: There will be no rollback of the proposed 0.4 per cent fee on person-to-business UPI transactions worth more than Rs. 2,000, government sources told news agency PTI on Wednesday. Asked if the government had considered withdrawing the MDR, or merchant discount rate, order, an official said there is no question of reversing it. But the Unified Payment Interface fee hike expected to take effect from October 15 already faces a potential legal challenge after a plea was filed in the Supreme Court this afternoon. The 0.4 per cent UPI MDR fee has also been criticised by the opposition. The government has responded to the criticism, with the Finance Ministry and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman issuing statements. 'Modi prostrated himself': Rahul Gandhi on UPI fee Rahul Gandhi has been leading this charge; in a searing video message posted earlier today the Congress MP accused the Narendra Modi government of having prostrated himself in front of United States President Donald Trump. Gandhi's attack came a day after the National Payments Corporation of India - a government body facilitating digital payments - confirmed a revised merchant pricing framework that revolves around the levy of 0.4 per cent MDR. 'No foreign pressure': Centre on UPI transaction fee However, in the light of Gandhi's criticism and the opposition's red flags about the poorer sections of society being squeezed, the government has said 'external pressure' played no role in its decision to set a MDR for certain transactions. The charge is to be borne fully by the merchant in each case, the Finance Ministry said in an explainer infographic on X, and will be capped at Rs. 300 for transactions of Rs. 75,000 and above. Person-to-person UPI transfers will remain free. 'Transcend sectoral interests': FM Sitharaman Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday said tax reforms must look beyond 'sectoral interests' and focus on Indias wider economic needs, including creating a fair, predictable system that promotes investment and innovation. Speaking at the Eighth International Tax Conference in Bengaluru, she called for independent tax policy research in public discourse and urged tax professionals to 'put the nation first'. She also highlighted efforts to rationalise TDS and TCS provisions, reduce unnecessary criminal consequences and renegotiate tax treaties with Mauritius, Singapore and Cyprus to restore Indias right to tax capital gains at source. What is MDR? MDR is the fee merchants must pay to banks and payment service providers for processing digital payments. This fee is also used to help maintain the payments infrastructure, which includes cloud storage, the payment app itself, and customer support features. The fee is shared between banks and payment service providers involved in processing the transaction. Credit cards, for instance, face an MDR of one to three per cent of transaction value, while it is up to 0.9 per cent for debit cards. UPI has operated under a zero-MDR regime since January 2020, i.e., as the Covid pandemic was worsening and the need for social distancing became paramount. What is the UPI fee hike? The new framework - announced Tuesday - ends six years of free UPI transactions. Under it the 0.4 per cent MDR will apply from October 15 to merchants above Rs. 2,000. Person-to-person transfers and small payments will remain free. The decision to levy an MDR - a practice followed in several other countries - was taken when the UPI system was introduced in 2020. The new framework, sources explained, is aimed at 'making UPI financially self-sustainable'. Why do we need UPI fee hike? More than 55 crore people use UPI now and 703 entities - from banks to payment service providers - are involved in facilitating its transactions. But there are costs involved in maintaining the digital payments infrastructure, and these have been borne by banks and payment service providers for years. This may be as high as Rs. 20,000 crore every year. Why does UPI fee hike matter? First, because it is the consumer who could end up facing the fee. In the case of credit cards, for instance, small merchants have been known to pass on the MDR amount to the consumers. The same may happen with UPI. However, the government did say on Tuesday that it had 'advised' banks to ensure merchants do not pass on the additional MDR cost to consumers. Second, such a fee would affect a significant chunk of UPI transactions. While transactions above Rs. 2,000 accounted for only four per cent of person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI payments by volume in 2025-26, these made up around two-thirds of UPI payments by value. In 2025-26, over 24,000 crore UPI transactions worth Rs. 314 lakh crore were made. Government sources said the move had been introduced in the 'broader interests of the UPI ecosystem', particularly to strengthen its safety and security. Parliament concern over UPI fee hike The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had earlier raised concerns about the sustainability of the zero-MDR model. In its 32nd report, the panel said the regime 'puts pressure on government finances' and warned that 'establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the government exchequer'. The committee also noted the government is currently spending roughly Rs. 2,000 crore annually to fund the incentive scheme associated with the zero-MDR policy. What about micro-merchants, small vendors? Small merchants, including street vendors, receiving up to Rs. 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes into their personal bank accounts will not be subjected to MDR charges. These merchants are part of a special category - Person-to-Person-Merchant - and, according to the NPCI, small merchants arent required to replace or re-register their QR codes under the new MDR framework. History of UPI in India The technology was developed by the RBI-regulated NPCI and the Indian Banks Association. Work on it started as long back as 2012-13, with the payment systems 'vision document' for 2012-15 making noteworthy points.

headline: CMC organises annual conference on brachytherapy
content: The Department of Radiation Oncology at Christian Medical College (CMC) has organised the 16th Annual Conference of the Indian Brachytherapy Society (IBSCON 2026) at its campus in Vellore. According to a press release, the conference, which was inaugurated by Vijay Anand Reddy, senior consultant and director, Apollo Cancer Hospital, Chennai, was centred on the theme Re-imagining Brachytherapy in Comprehensive Cancer Care: Precision, Personalisation, and Compassion. The scientific programme featured a series of lectures, expert panel discussions, debates, and interactive sessions highlighting recent advances and innovations in brachytherapy. Delegates actively participated by presenting original research, challenging clinical cases, and innovative treatment approaches, fostering a vibrant exchange of knowledge and professional networking. A hands-on cadaveric workshop focused on brachytherapy techniques for head and neck cancers and soft tissue sarcomas provided participants with practical, experience-based learning under expert guidance. The conference brought together 287 delegates, faculty members, and trainees from across India, including office-bearers of the Indian Brachytherapy Society, the release said.

headline: EU to ban social media for under 13s, curb access until 15
content: The European Union will ban social media for children under 13 and allow only limited, supervised access until the age of 15 under plans unveiled Wednesday (September 16, 2026) by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen. A global backlash against social media has piled pressure on policymakers, with a rising body of evidence showing negative impacts on children's physical and mental health. Australia last year became the first country to ban social media for under-16s, triggering a wave of similar moves elsewhere. The 27-country bloc would take a "gradual" approach, Ms. von der Leyen confirmed during her annual keynote address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France. "Each age has its own sensitivities. And therefore, each will have its own tailored protection level," she said. "No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15," she said. "That means from 13 to under 15, only mini accounts, set up and supervised by parents or guardians, with limited features and time restriction to one hour a day." "And between 15 and 18, safe design will be an obligation for the platforms." Before she outlined the EU's approach, Ms. von der Leyen paid tribute to a 14-year-old girl in Belgium, named Olea, who ended her life one month ago after being bullied, and whose mother she quoted as saying: "I am convinced that without these omnipresent networks, my daughter would still be here." Ms. von der Leyen made no reference to online games or AI chatbots, which according to draft legislation seen by AFP would also be hit by the restrictions. The European Commission president and tech chief Henna Virkkunen will formally present the proposed "KIDS Act", including the tiered age limits in Strasbourg, France on Thursday (September 16, 2026). The EU will also ban addictive design features such as so-called infinite scrolling where children are concerned, according to a draft document. If platforms break the rules, they face fines of up to 6% of annual turnover, draft details show. "Europe has the power to act. It is we who decide our rules, not big tech," Ms. von der Leyen said. "We do not have to accept addictive features," she warned, saying "platforms will have to prove that they are safe". "It is not about our minors accessing social media. It is about when and how do we allow social media to access minors," Ms. von der Leyen added. The "risk" is not limited to children, she noted. "Addictive design, for example, is harming everyone," she said, telling EU lawmakers that Europe needed more rules that will be proposed in the autumn. Pressure from EU states Among those listening in the grand chamber was Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney whose country has also moved to curb social media for under-16s. Ms. von der Leyen had faced pressure from member states including France, Denmark and Greece for action across the 27-nation bloc to limit online harms for children. The EU has sought for years to rein in Big Tech, empowering itself with a strengthened legal armoury that it now believes is not sufficient. The bloc has already told Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram as well as TikTok to change their "addictive" design through its content law known as the Digital Services Act, but changes have taken longer than Brussels wants. Digital and children's rights groups have raised concerns over how the new social media curbs will work in practice, as well as over a related age-check app the EU is preparing to roll out. "Age verification is not a silver bullet and would raise serious privacy and data protection concerns," said European consumer organisation BEUC's Agustin Reyna. Thursday's (September 17, 2026) proposal will only become law after negotiations on a final text between EU capitals and the European Parliament, which could take months.

headline: 10 get death sentence in 2013 Maoist attack on Chhattisgarh Congress leaders
content: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Jagdalpur city in Bastar district on Wednesday convicted 10 Maoists and awarded them death on charges of criminal conspiracy and murder for their alleged involvement in the Jhiram Ghati attack. In the 2013 attack, armed cadres of the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist) had surrounded and launched an attack on a Congress convoy, killing at least 27 people and almost wiping out the state party leadership. As many as 38 people had suffered injuries. NIA judge Ajay Singh Rajput convicted the accused under several sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act. The death sentence was awarded for criminal conspiracy (120 B) and murder (section 302) of the IPC. The 10 who have been convicted are Pramila Modiyam, Chaitu Lekam alias Munna, Sumita alias Punem Modiyam, Mukka Mandvi, Kosa Kavasi alias Kosaram, Aayata Markam, Madkami Deva, Joga Madkami, Banjami Sanna alias Chamru and Mahadev Nag. An 11th accused died during trial while another 28, named in the chargesheet as accused, have been listed as wanted. Among the prominent Maoists chargesheeted in the case but shown as wanted accused are Thippiri Tirupathi alias Devuji, a CPI (Maoist) politburo member who surrendered in Telangana in February this year; Barse Deva, who succeeded Madvi Hidma as commander of the PLGA Battalion 1, and surrendered in January this year; and Ganesh Uikey, a CPI (Maoist) central committee member who was killed in a December 2025 encounter in Odisha. Man behind Salwa Judum among those killed The Jhiram Ghati attack took place on May 25, 2013, when over 150 Maoists ambushed a Congress Parivartan Rally convoy and killed several people, including Mahendra Karma, who was instrumental in founding the banned anti-Maoist militia Salwa Judum; state Congress chief Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh; and senior party leader and former MLA Uday Mudliyar. According to investigators, the attack near the inter-district border of Bastar and Sukma districts was primarily aimed at Karma. According to the NIA chargesheet, the attack was meticulously planned as part of the banned CPI (Maoist)s Tactical Counter Offensive Campaign (TCOC). Maoist commanders conspired during meetings in early 2013 to target class enemies, specifically targeting Karma, it added. The Maoists triggered a landmine blast beneath a red Bolero vehicle, creating a 5-foot-deep crater and blocking the road with a stalled truck. Surrounding hilltops were used to rain indiscriminate gunfire and throw grenades on the trapped 20-vehicle convoy for nearly two hours. The 27 people who were killed included 10 security personnel. Police records show that the Maoists also looted a 9 mm pistol with two magazines and 20 rounds, two AK-47 rifles with 14 magazines and 455 rounds, 10 hand grenades and communication sets. The NIA took over the investigation two days after the attack. On September 25, 2014, it filed a chargesheet against nine arrested accused before the NIA Special Court in Jagdalpur. On September 28, 2015, it filed a supplementary chargesheet against another 30 accused. A total of 11 accused were arrested in the case but one of them died during trial. At least 28 more accused who were chargesheeted are wanted in the case. The trial lasted more than a decade, with at least 294 hearings. After final arguments were completed this month, the NIA court delivered its judgment on September 5 followed by quantum of punishment on Wednesday.

headline: 'No rethink' on 0.4% fee for UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Report
content: The government is not considering any rollback of the proposed 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions above Rs. 2,000, government sources told news agency PTI on Wednesday. A senior official, responding to questions on whether the MDR charge, scheduled to take effect from October 15, could be withdrawn, said the decision had already been taken and there was no question of reversing it, PTI reported. The new framework, announced on Tuesday, ends nearly six years of completely free UPI payments. Under it, a 0.4 per cent MDR will apply to merchant payments above Rs. 2,000. Person-to-person transfers and smaller payments will remain outside the charge. According to government sources, the move has been introduced in the broader interest of the UPI ecosystem, particularly to strengthen its safety and security. They said the decision to levy MDR, a practice followed in several other countries, was taken when the UPI system was introduced in 2020. The new framework, they added, is aimed at making UPI financially self-sustainable, according to the report. No foreign influence: Finance Ministry Earlier in the day, the government rubbished claims of foreign influence in its decision to impose the fee. In an X post the Finance Ministry said: Some claims suggest the change is due to foreign influence. This is false. Indias UPI policy decisions are made independently, with the clear goal of building a self-sustaining, inclusive, and affordable digital payments ecosystem. The statement comes as the move faced opposition from traders, shopkeepers and political parties, with critics referring to it as the Modi Tax. Some Opposition parties, including the Congress, have also alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave in to pressure from the US. The Congress alleged that the government surrendered to a demand by the United States and in a particularly stinging attack, Rahul Gandhi declared PM Modi had decided to lie down straight and prostrate himself in front of US President Donald Trump. The Finance Ministry said: UPI continues to be free for customers. Sending money to friends, paying at shops, or scanning a QR code all remain without charges. It also issued a detailed note on the new charges, including assuring lakhs of UPI users across the country that everyday payments are safe, pointing out that over 95 per cent of merchant transactions are below the Rs. 2,000 threshold that will invite the 0.4 per cent fee. Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI. It added, MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments. The ministry also said individuals would retain unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions. Vendors making up to Rs. 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes will continue to enjoy zero charges and that small merchants are protected, the government added. The government underlined that only larger merchant transactionsthat is, those over Rs. 2,000would be subject to the tax, which will be covered by the merchants. In yet another crucial clarification, the government stated that payments for necessities like fuel, telecom, and train tickets will be subject to a fixed cost of Rs. 5 for each transaction exceeding Rs. 2,000. Put nation first: FM Sitharaman In a response to the opposition, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman Wednesday stated that the discussion of tax reform must transcend sectoral interests and concentrate on the more general needs of Indias economy, such as developing a system that is equitable, predictable, and encouraging of investment and innovation. Speaking at the Eighth International Tax Conference on New Age Taxation in Bengaluru, the Finance Ministry called for independent tax policy research to become part of public discourse and urged tax professionals to rise above sectoral interests and put the nation first, while highlighting steps to rationalise Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) and Tax Collected at Source (TCS) provisions and reduce unnecessary criminal consequences. She said India had renegotiated tax treaties with Mauritius, Singapore and Cyprus to restore its right to tax capital gains at source, and noted that the country faced its own unique challenges on the path to growth and development. The government on Tuesday had defended the decision, saying incentives would be provided to encourage further expansion of UPI in rural and semi-urban regions while preserving its competitiveness. It also maintained that the vast majority of payments would continue to remain free. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had earlier raised concerns about the sustainability of the zero-MDR model. In its 32nd report, the panel said the regime puts pressure on government finances and warned that establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the government exchequer. The committee also noted that the government was spending around Rs. 2,000 crore annually to fund the incentive scheme associated with the zero-MDR policy. The change marks a shift after years of zero-cost UPI transactions, with a petition challenging the order is reportedly filed in the Supreme Court. (With Inputs from PTI)
