headline: Left parties to contest in Tamil Nadu bypolls; CPI to field candidate in Dharapuram, CPI(M) in Madurantakam
content: The two Left parties Communist Party of India (CPI) and Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI(M)) have decided to contest the ensuing byelections to the Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies without aligning with any other formations. CPI will contest the Dharapuram seat, while the CPI(M) will contest Madurantakam, said CPI State secretary M. Veerapandian on Sunday (September 13, 2026). With the Left parties decision to contest as a separate front, the upcoming bypolls have become a five-cornered contest. The alliances led by the TVK, the DMK and the AIADMK have already announced their candidates while Seeman-led Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) is to face the byelections alone. Speaking to reporters at Balan Illam, the CPI State headquarters in Chennai, Mr. Veerapandian said the candidates of the Left front would be announced on September 15. In the prevailing political situation in Tamil Nadu, the CPI had already decided not to be part of any alliance. At the executive committee meeting held on Saturday and Sunday, there was also a strong view that the same stand should continue, he said. Respecting the verdict given by the people, the Left parties extended outside support to the TVK to form the government, to avoid Governors rule and, indirectly, the BJPs rule. We are neither a part of the Cabinet nor a part of the alliance, he said. According to him, the upcoming bypolls in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram constituencies are not normal byelections, but what he termed as byelections imposed on people. It has been decided that the Left parties will face this election from the position we have already taken, that is, the position of not being part of any alliance. The CPI will contest in Dharapuram and the CPI (M) will contest in Madurantakam. We appeal to various democratic forces to extend their support to the Left parties, he said. We believe that students and youngsters are intellectually strong, aware of what is happening around the world and politically conscious. We believe that the Left will have a place among them, he added. Outside support will continue CPI(M) State secretary P. Shanmugam said that though the two Left parties had decided to contest alone in the upcoming bypolls, the CPI(M) would continue to extend outside support to the TVK-led government. Speaking to journalists after the State executive committee meeting of the CPI(M) that was held in Tiruchi to discuss in detail the stand to be taken for the forthcoming bypolls. Mr. Shanmugam said the Left parties had already decided that they would function independently. The forthcoming bypolls were neither a general election nor intended for a regime change. Hence, it was decided that the CPI(M) and the CPI would contest in one Assembly seat each, he said. Asked whether the CPI(M)s decision to contest would indirectly provide strength to the DMK, Mr. Shanmugam categorically reiterated that his partys outside support to the ruling TVK-led government would continue. The political stand taken by the CPI(M) for the bypolls would not endanger the present government. It would be wrong to say that the CPI(M) had taken the stand to support the DMK, he said, adding that his party would field its candidate against the three fronts. Wrong decision The candidates selected by the TVK to contest in the two Assembly constituencies had won as AIADMK candidates in the 2026 Assembly election. Within days of their victory, the two MLAs resigned from the AIADMK and joined the TVK. However, they could not cite any fair reason for this move. The CPI(M) had made it clear then that it was a wrong decision, as it went against the peoples sentiments, Mr. Shanmugam said. Asked whether the support to the TVK government on the one hand and contesting alone in the byelections on the other would confuse the people, he said the Left parties would clarify their political stand during the course of the campaign for the byelections. The byelections to Madurantakam and Dharapuram are scheduled to be held on October 6.

headline: Jaywalking a menace on OMR, motorists say
content: Motorists on Rajiv Gandhi Salai are complaining about jaywalking on various stretches, including Thoraipakkam, Sholinganallur, and Navalur especially at night, making driving in the dark more difficult. G. Gurumurthy of Thoraipakkam said, At Kottivakkam, if one is not careful, hit and run cases could almost become the norm at night. The lighting was improved a few days ago, but it is not effective. The lighting on the road has not improved despite the Tamil Nadu Road Development Companys promise of providing lights in sections that have been handed over to them by the Chennai Metro Rail, pointed out Harsha Koda, Co-founder, Federation of OMR Residents Welfare Associations. The height of the median in many places is not as tall as it should be. Since there are no proper zebra crossings and foot overbridges at necessary spots, the public is forced to clamber up the medians and jump over. Lamp posts have not yet been installed along the road and lights sitting atop the CMRL structures are inadequate to light up the road. Sridevi Kothandapani of Thazhambur said that the blue-grey steel shutters can be moved, and when people want to cross the road, they move it and create gaps in the shutters. Recently, when I was trying to cross the road at night and was holding on to one shutter, it moved and I fell on the road. Luckily for me, there was no vehicle on the road at that time, she said.

headline: Bridge to replace part of Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road on Pallikaranai marshland
content: Thoraipakkam Radial Road on Pallikaranai marshland In the near future, there will be a time when a 2-km stretch of Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam Radial Road from Chennai One to Kamakshi Hospital junction will cease to exist. The Pallikaranai marshland will take over the seven hectares of space earlier occupied by the road, and flood waters will be able to flow without any hindrance. An elevated bridge running to a length of 2 km will be constructed in its place. The detailed project report (DPR) for the project is getting its final touches. The proposal is to construct a six-lane elevated facility that will take off ahead of Chennai One on the Thoraipakkam side and land 100 metres ahead of the flyover at Kamakshi Hospital junction, said sources in the Highways department. The elevated bridge will have 200 metres long spans so that the number of piers holding up the super structure will be less. Each of the piers will be 2.5 metres diametre. The civil cost of the structure alone will be around 450 crore and will take two years to construct since there is no land acquisition involved in the proposal. All that will be needed is traffic diversion during construction. The road that connects Rajiv Gandhi Salai with Velachery, Pallikaranai, Madipakkam, Kilkattalai and the GST Road, at present carries around 1.25 lakh vehicles a day. Removal of the road will bring some relief to residents of Ram Nagar, Velachery, and Madipakkam, that get flooded every year. A total of 15,000 cusecs of water has to run to the Okkiyam Maduvu. At present, in the entire 2100 metres of road only 90 mts has culverts, which is hardly enough to permit free flow of flood waters. This is perhaps the first time that an existing road is being removed for the sake of the environment, explained another source. A retired Highways engineer explained that this road and others including Pallavaram Kundrathur Road, OMR, portions of ECR, Sholinganallur Kudimiyanthoppu Road, Kodambakkam Sriperumbudur Road and Chennai Bypass were all planned through the Madras Area Traffic Study Unit that was formed by the CMDA. At least 15 roads were identified and maps drawn. Land acquisition too was taken up. In 1998- 1999, a separate chief engineers wing was formed to construct these roads. The radial road was formed using building debris and even some garbage. We had no idea how the marsh will behave, so some sections caved in and had to be strengthened. In those days we had no idea of the environment, he recalled.

headline: Long-awaited cab pick-up plaza at Chennai airport opened after two-year delay
content: up plaza at Chennai airport was thrown open for air passengers on Sunday morning. Minister of Civil Aviation Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, who inaugurated the facility virtually, said, the plaza is set to reduce congestion and streamline vehicle movement. Looking at the significant improvement the facility can bring to passenger convenience, we have decided that its inauguration should not be delayed because of the ongoing BRICS summit, he said. He was to open the plaza in-person but could not come due to the summit. Developed at a cost of 22.88 crore, the plaza is situated nearly 30 metres from the T1 Domestic Terminal and can handle 28 vehicles at a time in two pickup lanes. The plaza has a seating capacity of 150. While lane A and B have been earmarked as passenger pick-up points, lane C will serve as the exit. Initially, Ola, Uber, Rapido, Fastrack, Red Taxi and prepaid taxis will be allowed inside the plaza and eventually, it will be extended to other yellow board vehicles. Mr. Naidu said he was particularly concerned about the experience of the arrival passengers at Chennai airport for some time. We were getting a lot of feedback, a lot of articles were also there in newspapers [that] passengers with heavy baggage, elderly passengers, families with young children, they had to walk [to] the multi-level car parking, and then [to] the second floor. So, we came up with this solution, which is the dedicated cab pick-up plaza, located 30 metres in front of the terminal. The moment you step out of the terminal, the cab is waiting for you, he said. Mr. Naidu said as Chennai has grown, so has the pressure of the infrastructure around it. With Chennai being a space constrained airport and sitting in the heart of the city, and on top of that [there is a] growing passenger footfall. It has presented us with some unique challenges, he noted. The Minister also said that the T3 Terminal construction is progressing across multiple fronts and will be ready in April 2027. We are continuously monitoring from the Ministry to ensure this time it is not delayed anymore and gets completed on time, he assured. The terminal is expected to increase the passenger handling capacity of Chennai airport, from around 20 million passengers to 35 million passengers a year. Despite several operational constraints, including the presence of operational terminals on either side of the construction site, and disruptions in supply chain due to the West Asia crisis [the delay occurred], a lot of efforts are being put to see that the timelines are being met, he said. T5 in planning stage Terminal 5 for Chennai airport is now in the planning stage, and the Ministry will engage with the State government to see how to expand the capacity, Mr. Naidu said. Completion of T5 Terminal will take the overall capacity of Chennai airport to approximately 55 million passengers per annum, he added. Some of the early users of the plaza said it was way more convenient than the previous arrangement to go to the parking area. Saji Mathew, who landed from Bengaluru, said he was pleasantly surprised and glad to see the new cab pick-up point.

headline: Temple tenants urge CM to implement G.O. fixing rents
content: Tenants of temple properties have urged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to intervene and implement the G.O. fixing rents, issued by the previous government for residential properties. An estimated 20 lakh families would be directly impacted by this G.O. 85 issued on 17.2.2026. That order was issued after much deliberation. The present government can go into the pros and cons of it before taking a call. It would save much time and energy and ensure that the temples get the revenue on time, said V. A. Balasubramanian, president, Tamil Nadu Koil Saarndhu/Saaradha Manaiyil Kudiyuruppor Sanga Koottamaippu. D. Sasikumar, a committee member of the Sangam, said that though the order in question was issued a few months before the Assembly elections, it was not implemented by the respective temples. It was issued after tenants complained that the previous order issued in 2016 stipulated rent rates that were too steep. Since there is no rule that fixes the rates of rent or lease due to the respective deities, the fixation of rents kept changing with every government. Only a Section of Religious and Charitable Endowments Act says rents ought to be collected. Mr. Balasubramanian also said that the temples must allow repairs to buildings and should not stipulate that the tenants should sign a gift deed to get a change in the name of the tenant. Rents were fixed the last time based on prevailing rents on the respective areas. But we objected to this too as properties constructed by private individuals by providing drinking water, sewage and electricity connections on lands that they owned cannot be equated to temple properties where the super structure was constructed by the tenants. Mr. Sasikumar, who is also the president of the Thiruvalleswarar Nagar Welfare Association, a temple property, also suggested that the temples must undertake an exercise to identify sub-let and sub-sold properties and bring them into the rental fold. This would bring an increase in revenue to temples. At present, nobody collects rents from these enjoying these properties, he added.

headline: BJP opposes circular on breakfast scheme
content: BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran on Sunday criticised a reported circular, as per which the Tamil Nadu government issued an advisory for headmasters to bear the expenses to be incurred for the expansion of the breakfast scheme for school students. In a social media post, he said while the expansion of the scheme was welcome, it was shocking that it had been planned without proper financial allocation. Referring to the circular, Mr. Nagenthran said it was mounting pressure on the headmasters. Teachers are there to impact education and guide students, not to share the governments financial burden, he added.

headline: Stolen emerald idol recovered from an abandoned quarry in TN's Chengalpet
content: A chance conversation about the value of emerald artefacts led three cash-strapped friends to go through video-sharing platforms in search of temples housing emerald idols, scouting shrines, disabling security systems and eventually stealing a 2.5-foot emerald idol from the Nadupalani temple in Chengalpet district.The gang, however, did not realise that footage of them prior to dismantling the CCTV cameras had already been recorded during their recce. Investigators who retrieved the footage, found crucial clues about their movements.Their heist unravelled 12 days later when police spotted them near an abandoned quarry where they had buried the idol.The accused G Manikandan, 27, E Elavazhakan, 26 and D Jayapal, 20 from Ariyalur, were arrested on Sunday. Police recovered the idol and silver articles stolen from the Nadupalani Balamurugan Maragatha Thandayuthapani Temple at Perunkaranai near Madurantakam.Police said Manikandan struck upon the idea when he overheard a trader he met in connection with cashew business, speaking about emerald articles fetching huge sums owing to their rarity and value.After Manikandan told this to his friends, the trio began searching online for temples with emerald idols. They found one in Sivagangai, one in Ramanathapuram and another in Perunkaranai in Chengalpet district.They visited all three but dropped plans to target the first two after finding they had stronger security and larger idols, which would be difficult to remove.They zeroed in on Perunkaranai temple, located atop a hill. Its presiding deity is a 2.5-foot idol carved entirely from emerald, and the shrine draws large crowds, particularly during festivals. The trio posed as devotees and visited it on Aug 28 to study the layout, security arrangements, CCTV cameras and burglar alarms.On the night of Sept 1, they entered the temple after dismantling 16 CCTV cameras around the premises and disabling three burglar alarms that formed part of a three-tier security system.Police said the alarms were loud enough to alert residents of nearby villages in the event of a security breach. After disabling the security systems, the trio removed the emerald idol and stole silver articles. They took the idol to an abandoned quarry about a kilometre away and buried it there.When priests and temple staff discovered the theft on Sept 2, they alerted Sithamur police, who registered a case. Six special teams were formed to trace the burglars and recover the idol. Investigators scrutinised footage from more than 100 CCTV cameras and questioned over 20 previous offenders involved in temple thefts and similar crimes.A team headed by Sithamu Inspector S Mahalingam pieced together footage and other clues to narrow down the suspects. Police said the trio also had previous criminal cases against them.The breakthrough came on Sunday morning when the police team noticed suspicious activity near the abandoned quarry. The three men were found there and taken in for questioning.Based on information obtained from them, police recovered the emerald idol from the spot where it had been buried, along with the stolen silver articles.The recovered idol was handed over to the Madurantakam Revenue Divisional Officers office.Police are investigating whether anyone else was involved in the theft and whether the trio had approached prospective buyers to dispose of the idol. Further investigation is on.

headline: Procession of silk umbrellas leaves for Tirupati from Chennai
content: The procession of 11 white silk decorated umbrellas, meant for the annual Brahmotsavam of the Tirupati Venkatachalapathi Temple at Tirumala, started from the Chenna Kesava Perumal Temple in Flower Bazaar on Sunday. The umbrella procession was flagged off by Sri Raghuvarendra Swami of Sri Bheemanna Ghatte Math and R. R. Gopaljee of Dharmartha Samithi. After being accorded special pujas by devotees in various areas, the umbrellas will reach Tirumala on September 18 for the Garuda Sevai, said a press release.

headline: There is no such thing as a 'UN map with borders': UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres
content: Days after India pointed out anomalies in a world map that was used during the passing of the Correct the Map resolution at the United Nations General Assembly, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said that the UN has not published any map with borders. In an exclusive interview with , Mr. Guterres insisted that its not for the UN to define borders. Earlier, had reported that a map was published by the UN Geospatial and used during the consultation process for the Correct the Map resolution, depicted Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin without the specified Indian and Chinese claim lines that previous UN maps had used.

headline: RPF rescues two teens from Nagaland near Katpadi
content: Two 17-year-old boys from Nagaland were rescued by the Railway Protection Force (Katpadi) in Ammor village on Sunday. The police said the rescued boys were identified as T. Nagampha and A. Tsemtun Kanyak. The teens were stranded in a remote forest area near a railway track between Walajah Road and Mukundarayapuram railway stations past midnight. A railway patrol team comprising assistant sub-inspector P.R. Murali and head constable G. Gopalakrishnan found the teens. We got an alert from our counterpart in Nagaland that two teens were missing from their houses and were headed towards Kerala. Despite heavy rain, our patrol team was looking for the boys in the area, said K. Prabhu, inspector, RPF (Katpadi). The police said that the two boys had left their homes in search for jobs in Keralam. The boys had initially travelled by train and reportedly alighted at Samalkot Railway Station near Kakinada in A.P to attend natures call. They had briefly alighted at Samalkot Railway Station and before they could re-board, the train departed. They subsequently purchased fresh tickets and boarded another train, the Gurudev Express, bound for Thiruvananthapuram. However, overcome with anxiety, the boys got down near Katpadi and were walking aimlessly when they were found by the patrol team. After their rescue, the boys were provided with suitable clothing, food, and necessary medical assistance. They were found to be in good health. Necessary arrangements were also initiated for their safe reunion with their family. After informing the Child Welfare Committee, the boys were handed over to the Child Helpline for Safe Custody at the Collectorate.

headline: New Vellore Corporation Commissioner assumes charge
content: A. Catherine Saranya assumed charge as the Commissioner for Vellore Corporation. According to a press release, Ms. Saranya, a civil servant, earlier served as executive director, State Industries Promotion Corporation (SIPCOT) before she was transferred.

headline: Minnagam helpline goes powerless often with poor backup system, leaves consumers stranded
content: The helpline meant to report power cuts is itself going off the grid. Minnagam, the grievance redressal number 94987 94987 used by consumers to report power cuts, low voltage, billing issues and other problems, has been going out of reach, leaving frustrated callers with little more than a beep when they desperately try to register a complaint.TNPDCL itself is to be blamed for Minnagams going out of reach because it could not provide a reliable power supply to its call centre. Inquiries with officials reveal that the power backup for such a helpline is only for 10 minutes. Minnagam call centre is powered by Mylapore 230kV substation. Whenever the substation develops a glitch, the helpline goes offline after the issue is not restored within 10 minutes, said an official.TNPDCL replaced the mobile numbers of field officers, but did not publicise it much. Many consumers are unaware of officers new numbers and fuse-off call numbers remain unreachable. Minnagam is then the go-to helpline, receiving 3,000 calls every day.Meanwhile, contrary to electricity and law minister R Nirmalkumars claims that power supply position was stabilised in Tamil Nadu since Saturday, unscheduled power cuts were reported. As per TNPDCLs own declaration, power cuts lasting more than an hour were reported in 56 different regions across Chennai and neighbouring districts 24 hours till Sunday morning. On Sunday too, residents of Pulianthope, Palavakkam complained of three-hour long power cuts due to failure as well as fault in the underground cables.Social activist T Sadagopan said it is unacceptable for TNPDCL to say that they were not prepared for the summer-like weather in Sept. There is lack of coordination among various govt agencies which results in peoples suffering due to unscheduled power cuts. Industries have also started fleeing the pinch of power cuts. This cannot go on, he said.

headline: Trump says 'very negative forces' raising exaggerated concerns over AI
content: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (September 13, 2026) likened critics of artificial intelligence to "very negative forces" bringing up scenarios that will not happen, and said he wanted to make sure that the U.S. remains the industry leader. "We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins," Mr. Trump told reporters at his Ireland golf course when asked if the AI industry should slow down or be more regulated. "We could put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen." Mr. Trump has resisted stirring concerns about AI. The public debate about AI has heated up in the U.S. after two Anthropic researchers issued warnings that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future. In his second term, Mr. Trump's administration has largely embraced AI firms. These AI leaders and other technology companies have also supported Mr. Trump's initiatives. AI executives have poured money into the midterm campaign ahead of the November 3 election that will determine control of Congress. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's super PAC, America PAC, has already spent millions backing Republican candidates and is expected to play a major role in voter turnout efforts this fall. The Pentagon this year warned of risks from Anthropic's model. After the researcher warnings, some AI CEOs are pushing for slowing advancement of the models. On Saturday (September 12), Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a three-step framework intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks.The proposal immediately received endorsements from several other executives at major AI companies, including Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. In an interview that aired Sunday (September 12) on the CBS program "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Mr. Amodei said the competition between U.S. and Chinese AI companies was the "toughest dilemma" in trying to establish a "speed limit" on the rate of AI development. "We shouldn't kid ourselves, because the incentives to pull ahead and the military advantage that you get from that are so large that the ability to check that the other side isn't cheating has to be ironclad," he said. "So I think that's going to be the work of years, and honestly, I don't know if it's possible." Jacob Coxon, one of the Anthropic researchers who resigned and then issued the warnings, pushed for the U.S. to work with other countries to ensure pace. "I feel we need international coordination, or else we risk running the same race with China, which could be equally dangerous," Mr. Coxon said on NBC.

headline: India steps up Africa outreach as Modi holds talks with leaders from the continent
content: Africa Forum Summit because of the Ebola crisis, New Delhi has started a broad-based dialogue with African countries, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi engaging multiple African leaders on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit that concluded on Sunday (September 12, 2026). Mr. Modi hosted Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali on Saturday (September 12, 2026), during which the two leaders discussed regional and global developments, and he met South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on Sunday. At the meeting between the Prime Ministers of India and Ethiopia, the External Affairs Ministry said, The two leaders held discussions aimed at further strengthening the bilateral Strategic Partnership. They reviewed progress across key sectors, including economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. In his remarks at the BRICS Summit, the Ethiopian Prime Minister had pitched his country as a frontrunner in digital public infrastructure in Africa and urged the world to prepare to deal with disruptions. He said, Africa should help build the next generation of AI. That requires research, computing capacity, skills and institutions able to lead that work. BRICS Summit 2026 September 13 updates Mr. Modi met President Ramaphosa of South Africa on Sunday (September 13, 2026) and reviewed the state of bilateral relations between their two countries. The New Delhi Declaration issued on Saturday (September 12, 2026) had taken note of the racial injustice that Africans have suffered historically, and also of the Brazilian-South African plan to start an international panel on inequality. The declaration also referred to decolonisation and Asian-African solidarity as displayed in the Bandung conference of 1955. It also particularly mentioned the South Africa-initiated legal process at the International Court of Justice against Israel for its military campaign in the Gaza Strip. Acknowledging South Africas leading role in holding Israel accountable, the New Delhi Declaration said the proceedings reaffirmed Israels legal obligation to ensure the provision of humanitarian aid in Gaza. In his discussion with Mr. Ramaphosa, Mr. Modi reviewed the multi-faceted strategic partnership between India and Africa. The two leaders exchanged views on a range of global issues of mutual interest and agreed to maintain close coordination in multilateral fora, said the External Affairs Ministry in a statement. India-Africa Forum India had also invited the President of Burundi, Evariste Ndayishimiye, in his capacity as the Chairperson of the African Union, to the BRICS Summit, and Mr. Modi hosted him for talks on Sunday (September 13, 2026) and discussed the possibility of hosting the India-Africa Forum Summit early. A statement issued by the External Affairs Ministry said the two sides acknowledged India-African Union partnership is a key pillar of cooperation within the Global South. President Ndayishimiye acknowledged Indias assistance to African health authorities in dealing with the Ebola crisis, and Prime Minister Modi appreciated Africas successful handling of the outbreak. The Ministry said that agricultural modernisation, healthcare and capacity-building initiatives were discussed during the meeting. Mr. Modi on Sunday (September 13, 2026) also met dignitaries from Uganda and Nigeria both invited to the New Delhi BRICS summit as partner countries. He met Vice President of Uganda Jessica Rose Epel Alupo and reaffirmed Indias support for the countrys Vision 2040 for a prosperous Uganda. The discussion covered technology partnerships, capacity building, investment facilitation, and private sector collaboration between the two sides. Mr. Modi also met the Vice-President of Nigeria, Kashim Shettima Mustapha and discussed initiatives in trade, defence, agriculture, health and digital technologies.

headline: Russia strikes Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train: Ukraine, Poland
content: Warsaw passenger train near the Polish border on Sunday (September 13, 2026) but caused no casualties, Ukraine and Poland said, as Moscow steps up attacks in the fifth year of its invasion. The strike, just two kilometres (1.2 miles) from the Polish border, came days after U.S. envoys visited Kyiv and Moscow, hoping to revive Washington-led talks on ending Europe's worst conflict since World War II, without securing a breakthrough. NATO member Poland said a second drone struck near a border crossing, prompting Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski to accuse Russian President Vladimir Putin of "escalating" the conflict. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow struck the train "deliberately" and accused Russia of attacking rail and energy infrastructure as well as civilian buildings across the country, including in the west. "It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand," Zelensky said. Putin is escalating "Putin is escalating," Polish Foreign Minister Sikorski said on social media. The country's PKP Intercity rail service said the train was travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw with 206 passengers onboard. With Ukrainian airspace closed, trains to neighbouring Poland have been one of the main routes out of the war-torn country, often carrying refugees and packed with women and children. Neither country reported casualties and Intercity said the service was delayed by more than six hours but would travel on to Warsaw after border checks were completed. Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said one drone struck near the Dorohusk-Yagodyn border crossing, while the other hit the passenger train. "We are treating these events with the utmost seriousness. The situation is being monitored on an ongoing basis," Mr. Kierwinski said. Russian attacks killed at least two people on Sunday, both in the frontline city of Kramatorsk. Twenty people, including two children, were also wounded in a second day of attacks on the southern port city of Odesa, Ukrainian officials said. Three-way talks The Kremlin, meanwhile, said three-way negotiations with Ukraine and the US on ending the war could take place in October. "We do not rule out such a possibility; we are talking about the foreseeable future," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told journalists, cited by Russia's Ria and Tass news agencies. Several previous rounds of negotiations have failed, while U.S.-led efforts stalled during the Middle East war. In an interview released on Saturday, Mr. Zelenskyy said he would be willing to meet Mr. Putin at the G20 summit in Miami in December for talks. But Peskov immediately said that was "impossible", speaking to AFP in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12), repeating Moscow's demand that a meeting could only take place in the Russian capital. Mr. Putin has repeatedly rejected offers for a face-to-face sit-down with Zelensky aimed at brokering an end to the conflict and has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine. On Sunday (September 13), Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov told journalists, including those from AFP, that there was still no "coordinated package" on which negotiations could be based. "At present, there is the idea that we need to reach an agreement on the territorial issue. But there are also many other questions," he added.

headline: A Raja regrets remarks against C T R Nirmalkumar after backlash
content: A day after facing a severe backlash, DMK MP A Raja expressed regret over his controversial remarks against TVK minister C T R Nirmalkumar and said he had no hesitation in taking back his words.I regret questioning the identity and truth behind the person who mocked and deliberately slandered a leader who is epitome of sacrifice, Raja said in a statement on X. Raja however warned that those who do not correct their ways would be forced to mend themselves.The response came after DMK MP M Kanimozhi posted a Thirukkural couplet, without naming Raja, which cautioned that everyone needs to watch their words.The backlash was for Rajas remarks made at a DMK protest in Chennais Saidapet on Saturday. After Raja criticised chief minister C Joseph Vijay for his assembly speech `taunting DMK president M K Stalin, he targeted Nirmalkumar for alleging that the DMK leader was imprisoned for `dubious activities and not for his opposition to Emergency. He questioned Nirmalkumars parentage, a remark which drew widespread condemnation, including from the CPM. It is unbearable that some DMK leaders continue to demean women while cadres cheer them, CPM state secretary P Shanmugham said. Condemn what minister Nirmalkumar said. But how can the DMK president silently watch when Nirmalkumars mother is insulted? Shanmugham asked.He said some DMK members continued to stray from dignity and hoped Stalin would perform his duty to restore discipline.Raja said he was driven by emotion when he made the speech and wanted the person (Nirmal Kumar) who triggered the emotion to feel the same pain.Responding on X, Nirmalkumar said obscene and vulgar language was always used as weapon by DMK men whenever they stare at failure. Is putting up a stage and getting people to speak obscenely about me and our leader your last weapon? he asked Stalin.He said Saturdays protest had shocked people, particularly women. He accused the DMK of resorting to violence or obscene speech whenever questioned over corruption, betrayal and lies. Can you show such low-grade speeches by DMK members to the women and children in their own homes? he asked.He said TVK would answer through honest politics, predicted voters would end the DMKs political run, and invoked MGRs description of the party as an evil force.

headline: Sailing beyond the classroom: Air India pilot takes children to sea to learn life skills
content: Air India pilot takes children to sea to learn life skills Chennai: For a group of children, a Sunday evening at sea turned into an unusual classroom, as they learnt sailing, teamwork and responsibility through a 90-minute experiential programme organised by Explorers Club at the Royal Madras Yacht Club.The initiative, led by Air India Senior Commander and Trainer Pilot Capt Soniya Jain, brought together children aged between eight and 15 with the aim of giving them an opportunity to learn through real-world experiences rather than just textbooks.Soniya Jain, who has two decades of aviation experience and served in the Vande Bharat Mission during the Covid-19 pandemic, said children needed opportunities to experience the world and step outside their comfort zones. She has also been associated with organisations including Yi, GDC Club, IWPA, RCC Magnum and JITO.The programme introduced the children to the basics of sailing, including how boats balance, wind directions and the importance of coordination. They also learnt different knots and took part in rope-based activities, including making their own wind catchers.For the young participants, the experience turned out to be very different from the simple boat ride some had expected. Pehel Ranka, 14, said, I thought it would be a simple sailing session where we would just go on the boat, sail for a while and return. I did not expect to learn much, Pehel said.Another participant, Darsh Khemka,14, described it as an adventurous Sunday that began with learning different types of knots and making a wind catcher before heading out to sea. The children were also given passports to collect stamps for future challenges.For Shreya Punamiya,13, who had earlier attended an NCC camp at AMET, the sailing experience offered something different. She recalled seeing cargo ships, jellyfish, and enthusiastic fellow participants, describing the day as an unforgettable experience.The initiative is built around Soniya Jains larger belief that experiential learning can help children develop confidence, discipline, independence, responsibility and teamwork in ways that traditional classroom learning may not always achieve.

headline: Krishna water supply to Chennai set to stop as Kandaleru storage dips
content: The discharge of Krishna water from Andhra Pradeshs Kandaleru reservoir to Chennai will stop within the next two to three days, as the reservoir's water storage has fallen sharply.Currently, only 40 cusecs of water are being released towards Chennai, a fraction of the usual supply. The city received around 3 TMC of Krishna water between May and September, compared with the usual 4-5 TMC during the period. This has raised concerns over the reduced inflow to Chennais reservoirs.To augment Chennais water storage, the neighbouring state began releasing water from the Kandaleru reservoir on Feb 25, which reached Poondi reservoir on March 4. However, the discharge was temporarily halted on March 29 due to maintenance work on water bodies in Andhra Pradesh. The supply resumed on May 15, with 180-200 cusecs being released, and the same level of outflow was maintained until July 10.In July, the neighbouring state increased the release of Krishna water to 455 cusecs despite low storage in the reservoir. The same level of outflow was maintained until the first week of Sept.Since there was no rainfall in Andhra Pradesh and water storage in the Kandaleru reservoir was only 17 TMC, the state had to meet its requirements for the second crop cultivation. So, the outflow to Chennai was reduced. From Sept 10, only 100 cusecs were discharged, which gradually came down to 40 cusecs. The supply is expected to stop temporarily in the next two to three days, said a senior WRD official.However, officials have assured that the outflow could resume if the reservoir receives adequate inflows following rainfall in the catchment areas in the coming days.At present, Chennais reservoirs have around 5 TMC of water, which is expected to meet the citys requirements for the next five months. In addition, the 3 TMC of Krishna water received so far could meet the requirement for another three months, taking the supply up to Feb 2027. However, officials said a deficient northeast monsoon could lead to water shortages during the summer of 2027.

headline: Nearly 86,000 flee fighting in Yemen: UN
content: Flaring fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has displaced nearly 86,000 people, the United Nations said Sunday, with the number surging by 10,000 from a day earlier. Tens of thousands have taken flight in the wake of a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen's Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, cementing their hold on the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. "Displacement in Yemen, the Arab world's poorest country, has now reached 85,818 people," the International Organization for Migration said in a statement, a day after putting the number of people displaced since July at 76,000. The UN agency stressed that more than 82,000 of those displaced had been forced to flee their homes since the start of September, when the Houthis, who have for years controlled large parts of northern Yemen, launched their large-scale offensive against Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. The displacements had happened across the west coast and Taiz areas, the IOM said. Taiz was the hardest-hit, it said, with some 9,280 households, or nearly 56,000 people, displaced from districts in that province alone. And now, some of those displaced have begun fleeing Yemen altogether, IOM said, pointing out that more than 2,000 people had reached Djibouti. The UN body told AFP that the first arrivals landed on Thursday evening (September 10, 2026). Djibouti lies opposite Yemen across the Bab al-Mandab strait, which has become an important artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports after Iran began its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the West Asia war. Those arriving in Djibouti many of them women and young children had been transported to a site in Obock where they were receiving assistance, IOM said, warning that "more are expected to flee as fighting intensifies". "Behind every number is a family who's lost everything," IOM chief Amy Pope said in the statement. "Many have been displaced multiple times. People are crossing the sea with nothing because they have no other choice left," she said. Ms. Pope highlighted that Yemen was a "country torn by poverty and conflict, and it cannot carry this crisis alone". "I call on donors to scale up support now, for those arriving in Djibouti and for the communities in Obock receiving them."

headline: Malaysian PM sings Kishore Kumar song, wins hearts online
content: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is winning hearts on the Internet after breaking into the famous song rendered by Kishore Kumar, Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat, a video of which he shared on Saturday (September 12, 2026) night on social media platform X. The song is from the 1960s Dev Anand-starrer Teen Devian. Dressed in a crisp grey suit, he sings to a piano tune being played by an accompanist. The clip has garnered over a million views and is being shared widely. It was not immediately known exactly when or where the video was taken. Mr. Ibrahim attended the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, hosted by India on September 12 and 13 at the Bharat Mandapam complex in New Delhi. "Prime Minister Ibrahim has in the past confessed to being a fan of Lata Mangeshkar and Kishore Kumar, both Indian singing legends," Shahrizan Salian, editor with Malaysia's New Straits Times, who is in India to cover the BRICS Summit, told the PTI. Mr. Ibrahim does not know Hindi, yet he managed to sing along to a piano tune without any visual aid to the lyrics. "It all came from his heart. Music has no language," Mr. Salian said.

headline: It was good conversation, we agreed to put past behind us: Pezeshkian on meeting with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince
content: A day after holding a rare meeting with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday (September 13, 2026) described it as a "good conversation" and said that both sides agreed to put the past behind. Mr. Pezeshkian held talks with Sheikh Khaled on the sidelines of the BRICS summit that was seen as some kind of ice-breaker between the two sides. "We had a good conversation with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, and agreed to put the past behind us and look to the future," Pezeshkian said on Sunday (September 13, 2026), according to the Iranian embassy. Relations between the two countries came under severe strain after Iran targeted many U.S. bases in the UAE in the last few months as part of its retaliation for the U.S. attacks on Iranian installations. The meeting assumed greater significance as it came two days ahead of talks between Iran and members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) in Oman. The Iran-GCC meeting will take place on September 14 to discuss an agreement on transit through the Strait of Hormuz. It will be the first such meeting since the start of the West Asia conflict. Mr. Pezeshkian also said that he had held discussions with the Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. "We also had discussions with the Presidents of Russia and China, which were mostly brief exchanges. A promising outlook for the expansion of economic cooperation is taking shape," he said. Mr. Pezeshkian also said that the BRICS member nations have condemned attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities and civilian infrastructure, stressing the need for restraint and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of West Asian countries. The Iranian President said the declaration of the summit reflected opposition to such attacks, as well as broader concern over "unilateralism, occupation and violations of international law." He said the participating countries emphasised the need to strengthen multilateralism and work toward a multipolar world, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency. Mr. Pezeshkian said the summit produced promising prospects for investment, financial exchanges and broader economic cooperation.

headline: Dear minister, you are not the king of England
content: On Aug 28, a Madras high court judge asked counsel for Tamil Nadu finance minister N Marie Wilson a question: Are you the King of England? The minister was facing criminal proceedings before a Judicial Magistrate in Puducherry. His counsel sought exemption from personal appearance, citing ministerial responsibilities and the assembly session. The judge was unimpressed. He pointed out that even former Prime Minister P V Narasimha Rao had appeared before a court while holding office, and questioned why a serving minister should expect different treatment merely because of his position. Then came the line: Are you the King of England?Instead of making the king of England statement, the judge could have expressed the point in simpler language: You are not above the law.Instead, he reached for an image from another constitutional age. That makes the question more powerful. The British constitutional system historically placed the Crown at the apex of the legal order. The question reaches back into English constitutional history, particularly the maxim rex non potest peccare, meaning the King can do no wrong. The maxim did not mean that the monarch was incapable of making a moral or factual mistake. It described a constitutional and legal position in which the Crown occupied a distinct status and enjoyed immunities that ordinary subjects did not. Historically, the Crown stood apart from the ordinary conception of the defendant before the law.A minister in India occupies no such position. He is a constitutional functionary, not a sovereign. He exercises public power under a written Constitution, and that power is subject to constitutional and judicial limits. He enjoys no personal immunity from criminal proceedings merely because he holds ministerial office. That, in essence, is what the judges question conveyed: what is it about holding ministerial office that places you beyond the ordinary operation of the law?Independent India did not merely inherit the constitutional order of the British Crown. It replaced it. Article 14 guarantees equality before law. The Constitution does recognise specific immunities for certain high constitutional offices. Article 361, for instance, protects the President and governors from criminal proceedings during their term of office and imposes special conditions concerning certain civil proceedings. That is a constitutional immunity expressly created by the Constitution. No equivalent provision exists for ministers, nor should the position of ministers be confused with the institutional safeguards surrounding serving judges of Supreme Court and high courts.In K Veeraswami vs Union of India (1991), Supreme Court recognised procedural safeguards concerning criminal proceedings against serving judges. Judicial protocol also ordinarily protects judges from being unnecessarily required to appear personally in other courts. These safeguards serve an institutional purpose: protecting judicial independence and the functioning of the judiciary. They do not confer sovereign status. A minister has neither the constitutional immunity of the President or governor nor the institutional protection afforded to the judiciary. The reference sometimes made to Section 133 of the Code of Civil Procedure is of limited relevance. That provision concerns personal appearance in civil proceedings. It cannot be invoked as a general exemption from personal appearance in a criminal case.None of this means that an accused must invariably appear personally before a criminal court. The law has always recognised circumstances in which personal attendance may appropriately be dispensed with. Sections 205 and 317 of the old Code of Criminal Procedure enabled a magistrate, in appropriate circumstances, to permit an accused to appear through counsel. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, continues the principle in Section 228. The magistrate may excuse personal attendance for sufficient reason and may subsequently require the accused to appear personally. Supreme Court has repeatedly emphasised that such discretion must be exercised sensibly and in appropriate cases. In Maneka Sanjay Gandhi vs Rani Jethmalani (1979), the Court recognised the need for a liberal and pragmatic approach where circumstances warrant exemption. The principle is not that personal attendance is invariably mandatory; nor is it that exemption follows automatically from social or political status. The crucial distinction is between immunity from the process and exemption from personal attendance. The former is a matter of constitutional or statutory law. The latter is a matter of judicial discretion.Judicial discretion must be exercised judiciously, by considering relevant circumstances, the interests of justice and the needs of the proceedings. The Narasimha Rao episode illustrates the distinction. While serving as Prime Minister, Rao faced criminal proceedings and appeared before the courts. When security and official responsibilities created practical difficulties, the Court accommodated him with orders permitting representation through counsel. The lesson is not simply that even the Prime Minister had to appear. It is more nuanced: high office does not confer immunity from judicial process, but legitimate practical difficulties may justify judicial accommodation.(The writer is an advocate in Madras high court)

headline: 1 Indian seafarer missing after attack on Panama-flagged tanker off Oman
content: An Indian seafarer is reportedly missing after the vessel he was on, a Panama-flagged oil tanker, was attacked off the coast of Oman on Sunday. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has condemned the attack, adding that efforts are underway to rescue the other 13 Indian crew members of MT El Gaia. We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman earlier today. Of the 14 Indian crew onboard, 13 Indians have been rescued so far, it said. Search and rescue operations for the missing Indian national are continuing. Our embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the situation and proactively coordinating with the Omani authorities in the ongoing search and rescue operation, the MEA said in a statement. Our statement on the attack on a commercial vessel off the coast of Oman Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) September 13, 2026 The Indian side thanked Omani authorities for their support in rescuing the Indian seafarers. We reiterate our call for immediate de-escalation of tensions and pursuance of dialogue and diplomacy to bring peace to the region, the MEA further said, adding, The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable. New Delhi has been concerned over attacks on commercial shipping as most of the vessels usually have Indian seafarers. Speaking at the BRICS summit on Saturday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed the creation of a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to safeguard them from security risks due to regional conflicts. Ten Indian seafarers are among the 16 Indians killed so far in the West Asia conflict, while another five Indian seafarers have died in strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea.

headline: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
content: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesnt restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis. Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday (September 11, 2026), Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay off-line. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing. Saudi Arabias government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbours. The worlds biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day around 4% of global supply to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea. But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports. Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypts ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said. Yanbu storage capacity stands at around 35 million barrels, according to industry estimates, with Ain Sukhna and Sidi Kerir able to store 18 million and 20 million barrels respectively. Stocks are not full and will ultimately run out without the east-west pipeline resuming operations, the four sources said. Saudi oil supply has already fallen to a more than three-decade low in August on reduced flows via Hormuz and the Red Sea, the International Energy Agency said on Friday (September 11, 2026). World oil supply will decline this year by 5.7 million bpd, or about 6%, the IEA, which coordinates Western energy policies, said. In addition to the attack on the pipeline, Houthi fighters in Yemen, who have threatened Saudi oil shipments, seized an island on Friday (September 11) in the mouth of the Red Sea. West Asia supplied around 22 million barrels per day of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed to just 6 million to 9 million bpd, industry sources say. Saudi Arabia told OPEC last week that its oil production had dropped to just 6.2 million bpd in August from 10.9 million bpd in February before the start of the war.

headline: Minor girl abducted, sexually assaulted in Coimbatore; police shoot in the leg of one accused
content: The police on Sunday (September 13, 2026) arrested two persons, who allegedly abducted a 14-year-old girl and sexually assaulted her in a house in Coimbatore on Saturday (September 12, 2026). The police shot in the leg of one of the accused, after he allegedly attacked a woman police officer with a sickle. According to the police, Santhosh (24) of Mettur near Vellalore and Thavasi (28) of Kanjikonampalayam, both daily wage workers, abducted the minor girl on a two-wheeler on Saturday evening. They took her to Thavasis house at Kanjikonampalayam and sexually assaulted her, before releasing her. The girl returned to her residence and lodged a complaint at the All Women Police Station, Coimbatore South, along with her parents around 7.30 p.m. The survivor was provided counselling and she was taken to the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital (CMCH) for a medical examination. The police registered a case under different Sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and launched an investigation. They apprehended Santhosh and Thavasi on Sunday, after analysing surveillance cameras visuals and other evidence. Thavasi, during interrogation, told the police that a sickle, which they allegedly used to threaten the minor girl while committing the crime, was hidden at a graveyard in the locality. A police team led by Inspector I. Sornavalli took Thavasi to the graveyard to recover the weapon. The police stated that the accused retrieved the hidden sickle and attacked the Inspector, causing her an injury on her shoulder. According to the police, Thavasi attempted to escape and tried to assault the Inspector further, following which Sub-Inspector Silambarasan shot on his leg with a service pistol. He was rushed to CMCH for treatment. Ms. Sornavalli, who was also hospitalised, is recovering.

headline: Putin seeks BRICS grain trade, insurance to fight curbs
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Sunday (September 13, 2026) proposed a new insurance mechanism and a collaborative grain market among BRICS nations, urging the group to adopt a holistic approach to combat global challenges. Mr. Putin proposed the new initiatives for economic growth among the BRICS member nations as well as the Global South nations amid crippling sanctions imposed by the Western powers on Moscow for its war on Ukraine. The G-7 countries, the European Union, and the U.K. prohibited Western companies from insuring any ship transporting Russian crude unless the oil was purchased at or below a specified price cap. Sanctions on the insurance sector have adversely impacted Russian crude oil exports. The Russian President pitched for setting up a dedicated platform for economic growth with the BRICS. We have independent routes for moving capital, labour and technologies. In fact, we can operate regardless of outside pressure, Mr. Putin said at the concluding session of the BRICS summit. We have some promising initiatives going forward, such as creating an insurance mechanism and a grain market. These are Russian proposals, and we invite all other member states to make use of those, he said without elaborating. Mr. Putin complimented the New Development Bank (NDB), saying it is handling projects worth $140 billion. The NDB is a multilateral development bank established by the BRICS nations. As global challenges keep surfacing, we should adopt a holistic approach to address both the symptoms and root causes, he said. Global South countries should jointly advance better [global] governance structure and tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats, he said. The Russian President said the global stature of BRICS is rising as it has been focusing on charting an independent course to combat pressing global challenges. The broad participation in todays meeting confirms that international interest in BRICS continues to grow. Many around the world find our core values and ideals appealing, including our commitment to charting an independent course and a desire to resolve problems collectively, guided by international law and the key provisions of the UN Charter, Mr. Putin said. The concluding session of the BRICS Summit was attended by the blocs full member nations and partner countries. This format opens the door to direct, candid dialogue between full-fledged BRICS members and partner countries, as well as other states and multilateral organisations keen to work with our group, Mr. Putin said. Highlighting the importance of greater intra-BRICS economic cooperation, Mr. Putin said a common platform for better trade and investment ties will be helpful to all the member nations. We have great new horizons for investment, cooperation and partnership between markets. We're talking about forming a joint platform for growth within BRICS that would combine the competitive advantages of all members of the group, he said. This platform must be built on the principles of openness and availability, not just for the partners of BRICS, but to all of our friends, he said. BRICS, originally comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, with Indonesia joining in 2025. Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam became BRICS partner countries last year. BRICS has emerged as an influential grouping as it brings together 11 major emerging economies of the world, representing around 49.5% of the global population, around 40% of the global GDP, and around 26% of the global trade.

headline: Electricity demand peaks this September, unscheduled power cuts return to Tamil Nadu
content: As many parts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, are going through an extended summer this September, resulting in searing heat conditions, unscheduled power cuts have returned to the State. The power demand remained steady in the past few months, at 20,500 MW, as against 16,000 MW-17,000 MW during this time last year. With the shortage of over 3,000 MW, Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has had to purchase 2,000 MW to tide over the crisis. The power demand in Chennai, which breached the 5,000-MW mark in June this year, is in the range of 4,200 MW to 4,500 MW. Normally, the citys power demand during this period of the year was 3,500 MW to 3,800 MW, TNPDCL officials said. Unscheduled power cuts led to protests across the State last week. In Tirunelveli, Tiruchi, and Ambasamudram, residents staged a protest to highlight the regular power cuts at night. Protest in Royapuram People took to the streets at Royapuram and Tiruvallur against the power cuts at night. Pattabhiram residents faced regular power cuts in the past one week. At Tiruvallur, the residents blocked a road after they faced a power cut on the night of Thursday (September 10, 2026). Residents in Chennai, including at Madipakkam and Tambaram, have been suffering from power disruptions. Residents of areas like Velachery and Anna Nagar have also complained about the regular maintenance shutdown not being published properly. Residents of Thandurai village faced a power cut for more than eight hours a day, initially owing to the damage caused to the underground cable near Paruthipattu. Though electricity officials restored the supply last week, the residents continue to face intermittent disruptions. A senior official of TNPDCL said steps were taken to ensure a steady and uninterrupted supply across the State. In Chennai, a team of high-ranking officials were monitoring the power grid and the distribution status round the clock and taking prompt action in case of complaints, he added.

headline: Tamil Nadu to set up university for emerging technologies
content: Tamil Nadu higher education department plans to set up a new university for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, biotechnology, climate technology and space technology.Named Periyar Institute of Emerging Technology, it will first be launched as an autonomous institute under Anna University, which is tasked with preparing the detailed project report.The institute will start its academic session within the next five months as part of Anna University, said higher education secretary Dheeraj Kumar said. Our ultimate goal is to convert this into an independent university for emerging technologies and collaborate with leading universities and institutes across the world.The institute would conduct high-end application-oriented research and have degree-awarding powers. This will be the first such institute in the country for emerging technologies. Anna University will partner with globally reputable institutions and industry for research, and design the curriculum for degree programmes, an official from Anna University said. The institute would aim to produce young talent in advanced technologies. The higher education department also plans to introduce new legislation to establish an institute of excellence in basic sciences this academic year. We want this institute to be developed on the lines of Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru, with the power to award degrees, Dheeraj Kumar said.There are about 30 renowned institutions for basic science research in the country. After Kerala and Odisha, Tamil Nadu will be the third state to establish its own research institute for basic sciences.It will focus only on PG programmes, PhDs and post-doctoral research in physics, chemistry, math and computational biology. We will tie up with internationally renowned institutions such as International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Italy to meet international standards, a senior official from Tamil Nadu State Council for Higher Education said.Easing norms to establish new private universities, Tamil Nadu govt also brought down land requirement from 100 acres to 12 acres in Chennai and to 18 acres in other corporations. It also brought down the endowment fund from Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 25 crore.

headline: 25-year-old techie arrested for attempting to steal from pawn shop

With the help of locals, Mangalsandh caught the accused and informed the police.The police registered a case and seized a mobile phone, a cutting machine, hammer, drilling machine and a screwdriver from the accused. Police said that Sriram, a native of Nellore in Andhra Pradesh, worked at an IT firm in Perungudi.Sriram was produced before the court on Saturday and remanded to prison.

headline: Chennai airport's cab pickup point finally is back to where it should have always been
content: Passengers arriving at Chennai airports domestic Terminal 1 can now walk out of Gate A2 and board their pre-booked cabs at a new pickup point right outside the terminal, instead of taking a buggy to the multi-level car park (MLCP). On its first day on Sunday, however, many passengers were unaware of the new facility due to lack of signage and people on ground.The new facility marks the end of a 26-month wait for passengers to access cabs directly from Terminal 1. Earlier, passengers had to wait for a buggy and travel nearly a kilometre to the MLCP to board their cabs. Union civil aviation minister K Rammohan Naidu virtually inaugurated the cab pickup plaza and the adjoining pickup point on Sunday.Though ground staff were available, many flyers appeared unsure at the terminal. Meanwhile, a few passengers watched others get into cabs and followed suit, finding out about the new pickup arrangement in the process.Around 5.30pm, K Sumesh and his family walked out of Gate A2, crossed the kerbside road and boarded their pre-booked cab after seeing others do so. We were not aware of this facility. There should be more signage about this new facility. Earlier, this was a hectic process. No other airport was as torturous as Chennai. The buggies used to come quickly, but the wait for the elevator at the MLCP was tiring, explained Sumesh.The cab pick-up point was shifted to the newly constructed multi-level car parking lot on July 29, 2024, forcing passengers to walk or use buggies to access the parking premises to board cabs. After relentless criticism, AAI decided to reopen the pick-up point near T1 and after prolonged delays, the plaza finally saw the light of day on Sunday.Some passengers welcomed the move, but said a few minor tweaks could further improve the experience. A lot of vehicles remain parked in front of the A2 gate, and they should be regulated. Passengers boarding private vehicles at the kerbside could also be allowed to exit through the A3 gate, so that these vehicles do not remain parked in front of A2 and hinder passenger movement, said Pradeep Krishnan, a passenger who arrived in Chennai from Trichy.Chennai airport director M Raja Kishore said that at least 50% of passengers arriving at T1 terminal use cabs, and the plaza will make their experience better. AAI has made A2 Gate, located right in front of the Plaza entry, the main exit gate instead of A3 Gate to make it easier to spot the plaza and reach pickup point. Apart from stairs, there are ramps on both side for push trolleys.The two vehicle pick-up bays have been further divided into seven segments with dedicated points for each cab aggregator. The first lane has been allotted to Ola, Uber and Fastrack, while the second bay has been allotted to prepaid taxis, Rapido, WTi cabs and Redtaxi. The respective aggregators have set up kiosks at the plaza to help passengers book cabs.To reach the plaza, cabs can enter only at Meenambakkam end and should go around the Aerohub mall. Similarly, to exit the airport, two different bays have been set up - one for personal vehicles and another for cabs. Personal vehicles are charged only at the exit, whereas fixed charges are collected from cabs. With a dedicated lane, cabs can exit faster, said an official. Also, buggies are operated from T4 to T1 via T2, as well as to the multi-level car parking lot, where they can continue to board cabs.

headline: Iran, UAE agree to 'put past behind'. Trump 'doesn't care'
content: and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have agreed to put the past behind us and look to the future, President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Sunday. This declaration from New Delhi, after the conclusion of the BRICS Summit 2026, came a day after a meeting between Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Thousands of kilometres away, US President Donald Trump said he doesnt care if Gulf nations meet with Iran, asserting its up to them. In New Delhi, Pezeshkian said he held brief exchanges with the presidents of Russia and China, and that there was a promising outlook for expanding economic cooperation. Iranian Embassy in India posted this update on their X handle. The UAE has made no similar announcement as yet. President Pezeshkian, at the conclusion of his visit to India: We had a good conversation with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, and agreed to put the past behind us and look to the future. Iran in India (@Iran_in_India) September 13, 2026 A day earlier, the embassy had posted about the meeting between the top leaders of the two countries. Iran in India (@Iran_in_India) September 12, 2026 What Trump said Trump asserted again that Iran was calling constantly for peace talks, something that that Tehran has dismissed in the past. Iran wants to make a deal badly, he told reporters and added that he doesnt care if Gulf nations meet with Iranthats up to them. The Republican leaders also gave a timeline on the West Asia conflict. Iran will end right after maybe before but itll end right after the midterms. Gasolines going to drop like a rock, Trump told reporters at the Irish Open golf championship. I will tell you this: Iran wants to make a deal so bad. They are calling constantly. They want to make a deal. Theyve got to make the right deal. Im not going to make a deal thats no good, he said. Why Iran-UAE development matters Iran and the UAE have found themselves on either side during the ongoing West Asia conflict that began with missile decapitation strikes by the United States and Israel against Tehran. Last month, the UAE had suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran after accusing the countrys military forces of launching two ballistic missiles towards it. Iran had denied this claim. The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in a statement, said the decision was taken in response to escalations that undermine peace and security in the region and all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran had been halted until further notice, Al Jazeera reported. Multiple UAE tankers have been hit in alleged Iranian attacks, with a few Indians also losing their lives. The defence ministry of the UAE had then said that two tankers were targeted by two Iranian cruise missiles while transiting the southern shipping lane of the Strait of Hormuz, within Omani territorial waters. Abu Dhabi National Oil Companys shipping arm ADNOC L&S said the vessels had sustained significant damage.

headline: City walls get a wildlife makeover as GCC ties up with EFI
content: From pictures of Indian blackbucks to herons, moorhens and coastal life, the citys walls are getting a colourful makeover. The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has partnered with the Environmentalist Foundation of India (EFI) to beautify dull walls into vibrant public spaces.Called the Wall.E - BlueGreen Chennai initiative, local residents, youth, and street artists are roped in to paint the walls depicting flourishing wildlife, wetlands and urban nature.The project serves a dual purpose -- beautification of neighborhoods as well as educating citizens on the urgent need to protect the citys natural heritage. It also prevents defacement of public spaces caused by illegal postering, graffiti and littering, said Arun Krishnamoorthy, EFI.At present, the work has commenced in southern areas of the city, including Greenways Road, Adyar and RA Puram. Paintings of Coppersmith Barbet, ducks and goose decked up the wall up to 500 metres along the Thiru Vi Ka bridge. Sholinganallur, Tambaram, Keezhkattalai, Chetpet and Kovalam are among the areas that will be covered subsequently, and completed in the next one month.The corporation will also expand the initiative to other zones of the city soon after completing the first set of areas, GCC Commissioner G S Sameeran said. Officials involved in the project said that the initiative was also a way of reclaiming public spaces through community art. Already, the corporation has taken efforts to paint school walls in several zones of the city. When people or students see local bird species, marine life, and green landscapes painted in their daily spaces, it creates a sense of pride and ownership in them to keep the city clean and green, an official from GCC south zone said.

headline: Al-Mokha is not a storm in a coffee cup
content: every sip of a mocha, caffeine fiends ingest a slice of history, just as alive and kicking as the delectable brew with heady coffee filling much of the cup. Such is the provenance of the drink: its name comes from Al-Mokha, a Red Sea port city steeped in trade in the late Middle Ages and still contested today, as the Houthis, or Ansar Allah, who control northern and northwestern Yemen, hold onto this strategic redoubt. Yemen, in the present times, may be known for the cultivation of khat, a plant infamous for its psychoactive properties. But once, the land was redolent with the aroma of coffee, long before produce from India reached the high tables of Europe. Therein lies a tale, apocryphal for some but the only truth for coffee aficionados who like to have their drink spiked with myth and legend. Yemen is where the worlds first coffee farms came up, writes Jonathan Morris in his book, Coffee: A Global History. Ethiopia remained the sole source of coffee until the 1540s, but as supplies dwindled due to internal conflict, coffee started being cultivated in the highlands of the Yemeni interior between the coastal plain of Tihama and the capital city of Sanaa, he says. The Yemeni rulers jealously guarded their coffee and allowed no fertile seed to leave the port of Al-Mokha so that cultivation spreading elsewhere would deny their country a golden goose. While returning to India from his Haj pilgrimage, the Sufi saint Baba Budan travelled through the port and hatched a plan to smuggle a few seeds to India. He hid seven seeds inside his flowing beard to escape scrutiny of the port inspectors. Back in India, he planted these seeds in the Chandragiri Hills in Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka. There begins a tale that changed the history of the coffee trade forever. India connection The India connection started even earlier, as Al-Mokha had been a bustling port through which the worlds trade transited. The coffee would then pass through various intermediaries before ending up in the major wholesale market of Bayt al-Faqih located on the coastal plain. Here, it was bought by merchants and held in warehouses, prior to being transported by camel train to the ports of Al-Makha [otherwise known as Al-Mocha, Al-Mokka and, to Europeans, Mocha] and Hudaydah for shipping. Most of these merchants were Banyans, members of a diaspora that spread from the Gujarat port of Surat to dominate trade around the Indian Ocean. They also controlled the Yemeni credit networks, making it likely they were the chief financiers and effective initiators of coffee cultivation, Mr. Morris writes in his book. Brazil is now the country that produces the most coffee, followed by Vietnam, Colombia, Indonesia, and yes, Ethiopia. India ranks seventh, and the country is now a Robusta nation, though what Baba Budan planted in Chikkamagaluru was Arabica. Yemen still produces coffee despite the khat proliferation, but just the dregs of a lucrative trade. Al-Mokha first became synonymous with coffee, as the shortened mocha was coffee back then. Now mocha, across the world, is a lip-smacking comfort drink with spoonfuls of chocolate stirred in. The British East India Company opened a depot in Al-Mocha as early as 1618, over 30 years before coffee became available in Britain. And mocha continues to delight coffee fans.
